verses.text: In  the beginning God created heaven, and earth.
verses.textLatin: In principio creavit Deus cælum et terram.

verses.text: And the earth was void and empty, and darkness was upon the face of the deep; and the spirit of God moved over the waters.
verses.textLatin: Terra autem erat inanis et vacua, et tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi: et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.

verses.text: And God said: Be light made. And light was made.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus: Fiat lux. Et facta est lux.

verses.text: And God saw the light that it was good; and he divided the light from the darkness.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Deus lucem quod esset bona: et divisit lucem a tenebris.

verses.text: And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night; and there was evening and morning one day.
verses.textLatin: Appellavitque lucem Diem, et tenebras Noctem: factumque est vespere et mane, dies unus.

verses.text: And God said: Let there be a firmament made amidst the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Deus: Fiat firmamentum in medio aquarum: et dividat aquas ab aquis.

verses.text: And God made a firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those that were above the firmament, and it was so.
verses.textLatin: Et fecit Deus firmamentum, divisitque aquas, quæ erant sub firmamento, ab his, quæ erant super firmamentum. Et factum est ita.

verses.text: And God called the firmament, Heaven; and the evening and morning were the second day.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Deus firmamentum, Cælum: et factum est vespere et mane, dies secundus.

verses.text: God also said: Let the waters that are under the heaven, be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: Dixit vero Deus: Congregentur aquæ, quæ sub cælo sunt, in locum unum: et appareat arida. Et factum est ita.

verses.text: And God called the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit Deus aridam Terram, congregationesque aquarum appellavit Maria. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

verses.text: And he said: Let the earth bring forth the green herb, and such as may seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, which may have seed in itself upon the earth. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Germinet terra herbam virentem, et facientem semen, et lignum pomiferum faciens fructum juxta genus suum, cujus semen in semetipso sit super terram. Et factum est ita.

verses.text: And the earth brought forth the green herb, and such as yieldeth seed according to its kind, and the tree that beareth fruit, having seed each one according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.textLatin: Et protulit terra herbam virentem, et facientem semen juxta genus suum, lignumque faciens fructum, et habens unumquodque sementem secundum speciem suam. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

verses.text: And the evening and the morning were the third day.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies tertius.

verses.text: And God said: Let there be lights made in the firmament of heaven, to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Deus: Fiant luminaria in firmamento cæli, et dividant diem ac noctem, et sint in signa et tempora, et dies et annos:

verses.text: To shine in the firmament of heaven, and to give light upon the earth. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: ut luceant in firmamento cæli, et illuminent terram. Et factum est ita.

verses.text: And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day; and a lesser light to rule the night: and the stars.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque Deus duo luminaria magna: luminare majus, ut præesset diei: et luminare minus, ut præesset nocti: et stellas.

verses.text: And he set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et posuit eas in firmamento cæli, ut lucerent super terram,

verses.text: And to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
verses.textLatin: et præessent diei ac nocti, et dividerent lucem ac tenebras. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

verses.text: And the evening and morning were the fourth day.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies quartus.

verses.text: God also said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping creature having life, and the fowl that may fly over the earth under the firmament of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Dixit etiam Deus: Producant aquæ reptile animæ viventis, et volatile super terram sub firmamento cæli.

verses.text: And God created the great whales, and every living and moving creature, which the waters brought forth, according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.textLatin: Creavitque Deus cete grandia, et omnem animam viventem atque motabilem, quam produxerant aquæ in species suas, et omne volatile secundum genus suum. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum.

verses.text: And he blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters of the sea: and let the birds be multiplied upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Benedixitque eis, dicens: Crescite, et multiplicamini, et replete aquas maris: avesque multiplicentur super terram.

verses.text: And the evening and morning were the fifth day.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est vespere et mane, dies quintus.

verses.text: And God said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, according to their kinds. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Deus: Producat terra animam viventem in genere suo, jumenta, et reptilia, et bestias terræ secundum species suas. Factumque est ita.

verses.text: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, and cattle, and every thing that creepeth on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.textLatin: Et fecit Deus bestias terræ juxta species suas, et jumenta, et omne reptile terræ in genere suo. Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum,

verses.text: And he said: Let us make man to our image and likeness: and let him have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and the beasts, and the whole earth, and every creeping creature that moveth upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Faciamus hominem ad imaginem et similitudinem nostram: et præsit piscibus maris, et volatilibus cæli, et bestiis, universæque terræ, omnique reptili, quod movetur in terra.

verses.text: And God created man to his own image: to the image of God he created him: male and female he created them.
verses.textLatin: Et creavit Deus hominem ad imaginem suam: ad imaginem Dei creavit illum, masculum et feminam creavit eos.

verses.text: And God blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and all living creatures that move upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Benedixitque illis Deus, et ait: Crescite et multiplicamini, et replete terram, et subjicite eam, et dominamini piscibus maris, et volatilibus cæli, et universis animantibus, quæ moventur super terram.

verses.text: And God said: Behold I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the earth, and all trees that have in themselves seed of their own kind, to be your meat:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus: Ecce dedi vobis omnem herbam afferentem semen super terram, et universa ligna quæ habent in semetipsis sementem generis sui, ut sint vobis in escam:

verses.text: And to all beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: et cunctis animantibus terræ, omnique volucri cæli, et universis quæ moventur in terra, et in quibus est anima vivens, ut habeant ad vescendum. Et factum est ita.

verses.text: And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good. And the evening and morning were the sixth day.
verses.textLatin: Viditque Deus cuncta quæ fecerat, et erant valde bona. Et factum est vespere et mane, dies sextus.

verses.text: So  the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them.
verses.textLatin: Igitur perfecti sunt cæli et terra, et omnis ornatus eorum.

verses.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
verses.textLatin: Complevitque Deus die septimo opus suum quod fecerat: et requievit die septimo ab universo opere quod patrarat.

verses.text: And he blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.
verses.textLatin: Et benedixit diei septimo, et sanctificavit illum, quia in ipso cessaverat ab omni opere suo quod creavit Deus ut faceret.

verses.text: These are the generations of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth:
verses.textLatin: Istæ sunt generationes cæli et terræ, quando creata sunt, in die quo fecit Dominus Deus cælum et terram,

verses.text: And every plant of the field before it sprung up in the earth, and every herb of the ground before it grew: for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth; and there was not a man to till the earth.
verses.textLatin: et omne virgultum agri antequam oriretur in terra, omnemque herbam regionis priusquam germinaret: non enim pluerat Dominus Deus super terram, et homo non erat qui operaretur terram:

verses.text: But a spring rose out of the earth, watering all the surface of the earth.
verses.textLatin: sed fons ascendebat e terra, irrigans universam superficiem terræ.

verses.text: And the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
verses.textLatin: Formavit igitur Dominus Deus hominem de limo terræ, et inspiravit in faciem ejus spiraculum vitæ, et factus est homo in animam viventem.

verses.text: And the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure from the beginning: wherein he placed man whom he had formed.
verses.textLatin: Plantaverat autem Dominus Deus paradisum voluptatis a principio, in quo posuit hominem quem formaverat.

verses.text: And the Lord God brought forth of the ground all manner of trees, fair to behold, and pleasant to eat of: the tree of life also in the midst of paradise: and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
verses.textLatin: Produxitque Dominus Deus de humo omne lignum pulchrum visu, et ad vescendum suave lignum etiam vitæ in medio paradisi, lignumque scientiæ boni et mali.

verses.text: And a river went out of the place of pleasure to water paradise, which from thence is divided into four heads.
verses.textLatin: Et fluvius egrediebatur de loco voluptatis ad irrigandum paradisum, qui inde dividitur in quatuor capita.

verses.text: The name of the one is Phison: that is it which compasseth all the land of Hevilath, where gold groweth.
verses.textLatin: Nomen uni Phison: ipse est qui circuit omnem terram Hevilath, ubi nascitur aurum:

verses.text: And the gold of that land is very good: there is found bdellium, and the onyx stone.
verses.textLatin: et aurum terræ illius optimum est; ibi invenitur bdellium, et lapis onychinus.

verses.text: And the name of the second river is Gehon: the same is it that compasseth all the land of Ethiopia.
verses.textLatin: Et nomen fluvii secundi Gehon; ipse est qui circumit omnem terram Æthiopiæ.

verses.text: And the name of the third river is Tigris: the same passeth along by the Assyrians. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
verses.textLatin: Nomen vero fluminis tertii, Tigris: ipse vadit contra Assyrios. Fluvius autem quartus, ipse est Euphrates.

verses.text: And the Lord God took man, and put him into the paradise of pleasure, to dress it, and to keep it.
verses.textLatin: Tulit ergo Dominus Deus hominem, et posuit eum in paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur, et custodiret illum:

verses.text: And he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat:
verses.textLatin: præcepitque ei, dicens: Ex omni ligno paradisi comede;

verses.text: But of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat. For in what day soever thou shalt eat of it, thou shalt die the death.
verses.textLatin: de ligno autem scientiæ boni et mali ne comedas: in quocumque enim die comederis ex eo, morte morieris.

verses.text: And the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus Deus: Non est bonum esse hominem solum: faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi.

verses.text: And the Lord God having formed out of the ground all the beasts of the earth, and all the fowls of the air, brought them to Adam to see what he would call them: for whatsoever Adam called any living creature the same is its name.
verses.textLatin: Formatis igitur Dominus Deus de humo cunctis animantibus terræ, et universis volatilibus cæli, adduxit ea ad Adam, ut videret quid vocaret ea: omne enim quod vocavit Adam animæ viventis, ipsum est nomen ejus.

verses.text: And Adam called all the beasts by their names, and all the fowls of the air, and all the cattle of the field: but for Adam there was not found a helper like himself.
verses.textLatin: Appellavitque Adam nominibus suis cuncta animantia, et universa volatilia cæli, et omnes bestias terræ: Adæ vero non inveniebatur adjutor similis ejus.

verses.text: Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam: and when he was fast asleep, he took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh for it.
verses.textLatin: Immisit ergo Dominus Deus soporem in Adam: cumque obdormisset, tulit unam de costis ejus, et replevit carnem pro ea.

verses.text: And the Lord God built the rib which he took from Adam into a woman: and brought her to Adam.
verses.textLatin: Et ædificavit Dominus Deus costam, quam tulerat de Adam, in mulierem: et adduxit eam ad Adam.

verses.text: And Adam said: This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, because she was taken out of man.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Adam: Hoc nunc os ex ossibus meis, et caro de carne mea: hæc vocabitur Virago, quoniam de viro sumpta est.

verses.text: Wherefore a man shall leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem relinquet homo patrem suum, et matrem, et adhærebit uxori suæ: et erunt duo in carne una.

verses.text: And they were both naked: to wit, Adam and his wife: and were not ashamed.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem uterque nudus, Adam scilicet et uxor ejus: et non erubescebant.

verses.text: Now  the serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth which the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman: Why hath God commanded you, that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?
verses.textLatin: Sed et serpens erat callidior cunctis animantibus terræ quæ fecerat Dominus Deus. Qui dixit ad mulierem: Cur præcepit vobis Deus ut non comederetis de omni ligno paradisi?

verses.text: And the woman answered him, saying: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit mulier: De fructu lignorum, quæ sunt in paradiso, vescimur:

verses.text: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God hath commanded us that we should not eat; and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.
verses.textLatin: de fructu vero ligni quod est in medio paradisi, præcepit nobis Deus ne comederemus, et ne tangeremus illud, ne forte moriamur.

verses.text: And the serpent said to the woman: No, you shall not die the death.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem serpens ad mulierem: Nequaquam morte moriemini.

verses.text: For God doth know that in what day soever you shall eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as Gods, knowing good and evil.
verses.textLatin: Scit enim Deus quod in quocumque die comederitis ex eo, aperientur oculi vestri, et eritis sicut dii, scientes bonum et malum.

verses.text: And the woman saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave to her husband who did eat.
verses.textLatin: Vidit igitur mulier quod bonum esset lignum ad vescendum, et pulchrum oculis, aspectuque delectabile: et tulit de fructu illius, et comedit: deditque viro suo, qui comedit.

verses.text: And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons.
verses.textLatin: Et aperti sunt oculi amborum; cumque cognovissent se esse nudos, consuerunt folia ficus, et fecerunt sibi perizomata.

verses.text: And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise at the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God, amidst the trees of paradise.
verses.textLatin: Et cum audissent vocem Domini Dei deambulantis in paradiso ad auram post meridiem, abscondit se Adam et uxor ejus a facie Domini Dei in medio ligni paradisi.

verses.text: And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where art thou?
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Dominus Deus Adam, et dixit ei: Ubi es?

verses.text: And he said: I heard thy voice in paradise; and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait: Vocem tuam audivi in paradiso, et timui, eo quod nudus essem, et abscondi me.

verses.text: And he said to him: And who hath told thee that thou wast naked, but that thou hast eaten of the tree whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat?
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit: Quis enim indicavit tibi quod nudus esses, nisi quod ex ligno de quo præceperam tibi ne comederes, comedisti?

verses.text: And Adam said: The woman, whom thou gavest me to be my companion, gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Adam: Mulier, quam dedisti mihi sociam, dedit mihi de ligno, et comedi.

verses.text: And the Lord God said to the woman: Why hast thou done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I did eat.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus Deus ad mulierem: Quare hoc fecisti? Quæ respondit: Serpens decepit me, et comedi.

verses.text: And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because thou hast done this thing, thou art cursed among all cattle, and beasts of the earth: upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat all the days of thy life.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus Deus ad serpentem: Quia fecisti hoc, maledictus es inter omnia animantia, et bestias terræ: super pectus tuum gradieris, et terram comedes cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.

verses.text: I will put enmities between thee and the woman, and thy seed and her seed: she shall crush thy head, and thou shalt lie in wait for her heel.
verses.textLatin: Inimicitias ponam inter te et mulierem, et semen tuum et semen illius: ipsa conteret caput tuum, et tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus.

verses.text: To the woman also he said: I will multiply thy sorrows, and thy conceptions: in sorrow shalt thou bring forth children, and thou shalt be under thy husband’s power, and he shall have dominion over thee.
verses.textLatin: Mulieri quoque dixit: Multiplicabo ærumnas tuas, et conceptus tuos: in dolore paries filios, et sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui.

verses.text: And to Adam he said: Because thou hast hearkened to the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldst not eat, cursed is the earth in thy work; with labour and toil shalt thou eat thereof all the days of thy life.
verses.textLatin: Adæ vero dixit: Quia audisti vocem uxoris tuæ, et comedisti de ligno, ex quo præceperam tibi ne comederes, maledicta terra in opere tuo: in laboribus comedes ex ea cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.

verses.text: Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herbs of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Spinas et tribulos germinabit tibi, et comedes herbam terræ.

verses.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread till thou return to the earth, out of which thou wast taken: for dust thou art, and into dust thou shalt return.
verses.textLatin: In sudore vultus tui vesceris pane, donec revertaris in terram de qua sumptus es: quia pulvis es et in pulverem reverteris.

verses.text: And Adam called the name of his wife Eve: because she was the mother of all the living.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit Adam nomen uxoris suæ, Heva: eo quod mater esset cunctorum viventium.

verses.text: And the Lord God made for Adam and his wife, garments of skins, and clothed them.
verses.textLatin: Fecit quoque Dominus Deus Adæ et uxori ejus tunicas pelliceas, et induit eos:

verses.text: And he said: Behold Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Ecce Adam quasi unus ex nobis factus est, sciens bonum et malum: nunc ergo ne forte mittat manum suam, et sumat etiam de ligno vitæ, et comedat, et vivat in æternum.

verses.text: And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.
verses.textLatin: Et emisit eum Dominus Deus de paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur terram de qua sumptus est.

verses.text: And he cast out Adam; and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubims, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
verses.textLatin: Ejecitque Adam: et collocavit ante paradisum voluptatis cherubim, et flammeum gladium, atque versatilem, ad custodiendam viam ligni vitæ.

verses.text: And  Adam knew Eve his wife: who conceived and brought forth Cain, saying: I have gotten a man through God.
verses.textLatin: Adam vero cognovit uxorem suam Hevam, quæ concepit et peperit Cain, dicens: Possedi hominem per Deum.

verses.text: And again she brought forth his brother Abel. And Abel was a shepherd, and Cain a husbandman.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque peperit fratrem ejus Abel. Fuit autem Abel pastor ovium, et Cain agricola.

verses.text: And it came to pass after many days, that Cain offered, of the fruits of the earth, gifts to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem post multos dies ut offerret Cain de fructibus terræ munera Domino.

verses.text: Abel also offered of the firstlings of his flock, and of their fat: and the Lord had respect to Abel, and to his offerings.
verses.textLatin: Abel quoque obtulit de primogenitis gregis sui, et de adipibus eorum: et respexit Dominus ad Abel, et ad munera ejus.

verses.text: But to Cain and his offerings he had no respect: and Cain was exceedingly angry, and his countenance fell.
verses.textLatin: Ad Cain vero, et ad munera illius non respexit: iratusque est Cain vehementer, et concidit vultus ejus.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Why art thou angry? and why is thy countenance fallen?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Quare iratus es? et cur concidit facies tua?

verses.text: If thou do well, shalt thou not receive? but if ill, shall not sin forthwith be present at the door? but the lust thereof shall be under thee, and thou shalt have dominion over it.
verses.textLatin: nonne si bene egeris, recipies: sin autem male, statim in foribus peccatum aderit? sed sub te erit appetitus ejus, et tu dominaberis illius.

verses.text: And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go forth abroad. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and slew him.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Cain ad Abel fratrem suum: Egrediamur foras. Cumque essent in agro, consurrexit Cain adversus fratrem suum Abel, et interfecit eum.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Cain: Where is thy brother Abel? And he answered, I know not: am I my brother’s keeper?
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus ad Cain: Ubi est Abel frater tuus? Qui respondit: Nescio: num custos fratris mei sum ego?

verses.text: And he said to him: What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth to me from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eum: Quid fecisti? vox sanguinis fratris tui clamat ad me de terra.

verses.text: Now, therefore, cursed shalt thou be upon the earth, which hath opened her mouth and received the blood of thy brother at thy hand.
verses.textLatin: Nunc igitur maledictus eris super terram, quæ aperuit os suum, et suscepit sanguinem fratris tui de manu tua.

verses.text: When thou shalt till it, it shall not yield to thee its fruit: a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Cum operatus fueris eam, non dabit tibi fructus suos: vagus et profugus eris super terram.

verses.text: And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than that I may deserve pardon.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Cain ad Dominum: Major est iniquitas mea, quam ut veniam merear.

verses.text: Behold thou dost cast me out this day from the face of the earth, and I shall be hidden from thy face, and I shall be a vagabond and a fugitive on the earth: every one, therefore, that findeth me, shall kill me.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ejicis me hodie a facie terræ, et a facie tua abscondar, et ero vagus et profugus in terra: omnis igitur qui invenerit me, occidet me.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: No, it shall not be so: but whosoever shall kill Cain, shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, that whosoever found him should not kill him.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei Dominus: Nequaquam ita fiet: sed omnis qui occiderit Cain, septuplum punietur. Posuitque Dominus Cain signum, ut non interficeret eum omnis qui invenisset eum.

verses.text: And Cain went out from the face of the Lord, and dwelt as a fugitive on the earth, at the east side of Eden.
verses.textLatin: Egressusque Cain a facie Domini, habitavit profugus in terra ad orientalem plagam Eden.

verses.text: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived, and brought forth Henoch: and he built a city, and called the name thereof by the name of his son Henoch.
verses.textLatin: Cognovit autem Cain uxorem suam, quæ concepit, et peperit Henoch: et ædificavit civitatem, vocavitque nomen ejus ex nomine filii sui, Henoch.

verses.text: And Henoch begot Irad, and Irad begot Maviael, and Maviael begot Mathusael, and Mathusael begot Lamech:
verses.textLatin: Porro Henoch genuit Irad, et Irad genuit Maviaël, et Maviaël genuit Mathusaël, et Mathusaël genuit Lamech.

verses.text: Who took two wives: the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the other Sella.
verses.textLatin: Qui accepit duas uxores, nomen uni Ada, et nomen alteri Sella.

verses.text: And Ada brought forth Jabel: who was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of herdsmen.
verses.textLatin: Genuitque Ada Jabel, qui fuit pater habitantium in tentoriis, atque pastorum.

verses.text: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of them that play upon the harp and the organs.
verses.textLatin: Et nomen fratris ejus Jubal: ipse fuit pater canentium cithara et organo.

verses.text: Sella also brought forth Tubalcain, who was a hammerer and artificer in every work of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubalcain was Noema.
verses.textLatin: Sella quoque genuit Tubalcain, qui fuit malleator et faber in cuncta opera æris et ferri. Soror vero Tubalcain, Noëma.

verses.text: And Lamech said to his wives Ada and Sella: Hear my voice, ye wives of Lamech, hearken to my speech: for I have slain a man to the wounding of myself, and a stripling to my own bruising.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Lamech uxoribus suis Adæ et Sellæ: Audite vocem meam, uxores Lamech; auscultate sermonem meum: quoniam occidi virum in vulnus meum, et adolescentulum in livorem meum.

verses.text: Sevenfold vengeance shall be taken for Cain: but for Lamech seventy times sevenfold.
verses.textLatin: Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain: de Lamech vero septuagies septies.

verses.text: Adam also knew his wife again: and she brought forth a son, and called his name Seth, saying: God hath given me another seed, for Abel whom Cain slew.
verses.textLatin: Cognovit quoque adhuc Adam uxorem suam: et peperit filium, vocavitque nomen ejus Seth, dicens: Posuit mihi Deus semen aliud pro Abel, quem occidit Cain.

verses.text: But to Seth also was born a son, whom he called Enos; this man began to call upon the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sed et Seth natus est filius, quem vocavit Enos: iste cœpit invocare nomen Domini.

verses.text: This  is the book of the generation of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him to the likeness of God.
verses.textLatin: Hic est liber generationis Adam. In die qua creavit Deus hominem, ad similitudinem Dei fecit illum.

verses.text: He created them male and female; and blessed them: and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
verses.textLatin: Masculum et feminam creavit eos, et benedixit illis: et vocavit nomen eorum Adam, in die quo creati sunt.

verses.text: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begot a son to his own image and likeness, and called his name Seth.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Adam centum triginta annis: et genuit ad imaginem et similitudinem suam, vocavitque nomen ejus Seth.

verses.text: And the days of Adam, after he begot Seth, were eight hundred years: and he begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt dies Adam, postquam genuit Seth, octingenti anni: genuitque filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the time that Adam lived came to nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est omne tempus quod vixit Adam, anni nongenti triginta, et mortuus est.

verses.text: Seth also lived a hundred and five years, and begot Enos.
verses.textLatin: Vixit quoque Seth centum quinque annis, et genuit Enos.

verses.text: And Seth lived after he begot Enos, eight hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Seth, postquam genuit Enos, octingentis septem annis, genuitque filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Seth nongentorum duodecim annorum, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Enos lived ninety years, and begot Cainan.
verses.textLatin: Vixit vero Enos nonaginta annis, et genuit Cainan.

verses.text: After whose birth he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Post cujus ortum vixit octingentis quindecim annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Factique sunt omnes dies Enos nongenti quinque anni, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Cainan lived seventy years, and begot Malaleel.
verses.textLatin: Vixit quoque Cainan septuaginta annis, et genuit Malaleel.

verses.text: And Cainan lived after he begot Malaleel, eight hundred and forty years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit Cainan, postquam genuit Malaleel, octingentis quadraginta annis, genuitque filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Cainan nongenti decem anni, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Malaleel lived sixty-five years, and begot Jared.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Malaleel sexaginta quinque annis, et genuit Jared.

verses.text: And Malaleel lived after he begot Jared, eight hundred and thirty years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit Malaleel, postquam genuit Jared, octingentis triginta annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Malaleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Malaleel octingenti nonaginta quinque anni, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Jared lived a hundred and sixty-two years, and begot Henoch.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Jared centum sexaginta duobus annis, et genuit Henoch.

verses.text: And Jared lived after he begot Henoch, eight hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit Jared, postquam genuit Henoch, octingentis annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Jared nongenti sexaginta duo anni, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Henoch lived sixty-five years, and begot Mathusala.
verses.textLatin: Porro Henoch vixit sexaginta quinque annis, et genuit Mathusalam.

verses.text: And Henoch walked with God: and lived after he begot Mathusala, three hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et ambulavit Henoch cum Deo: et vixit, postquam genuit Mathusalam, trecentis annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Henoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Henoch trecenti sexaginta quinque anni.

verses.text: And he walked with God, and was seen no more: because God took him.
verses.textLatin: Ambulavitque cum Deo, et non apparuit: quia tulit eum Deus.

verses.text: And Mathusala lived a hundred and eighty-seven years, and begot Lamech.
verses.textLatin: Vixit quoque Mathusala centum octoginta septem annis, et genuit Lamech.

verses.text: And Mathusala lived after he begot Lamech, seven hundred and eighty-two years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit Mathusala, postquam genuit Lamech, septingentis octoginta duobus annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Mathusala were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Mathusala nongenti sexaginta novem anni, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And Lamech lived a hundred and eighty-two years, and begot a son.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Lamech centum octoginta duobus annis, et genuit filium:

verses.text: And he called his name Noe, saying: This same shall comfort us from the works and labours of our hands on the earth, which the Lord hath cursed.
verses.textLatin: vocavitque nomen ejus Noë, dicens: Iste consolabitur nos ab operibus et laboribus manuum nostrarum in terra, cui maledixit Dominus.

verses.text: And Lamech lived after he begot Noe, five hundred and ninety-five years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Lamech, postquam genuit Noë, quingentis nonaginta quinque annis, et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And all the days of Lamech came to seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died. And Noe, when he was five hundred years old, begot Sem, Cham, and Japheth.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt omnes dies Lamech septingenti septuaginta septem anni, et mortuus est. Noë vero cum quingentorum esset annorum, genuit Sem, Cham et Japheth.

verses.text: And  after that men began to be multiplied upon the earth, and daughters were born to them,
verses.textLatin: Cumque cœpissent homines multiplicari super terram, et filias procreassent,

verses.text: The sons of God seeing the daughters of men, that they were fair, took to themselves wives of all which they chose.
verses.textLatin: videntes filii Dei filias hominum quod essent pulchræ, acceperunt sibi uxores ex omnibus, quas elegerant.

verses.text: And God said: My spirit shall not remain in man for ever, because he is flesh, and his days shall be a hundred and twenty years.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus: Non permanebit spiritus meus in homine in æternum, quia caro est: eruntque dies illius centum viginti annorum.

verses.text: Now giants were upon the earth in those days. For after the sons of God went in to the daughters of men, and they brought forth children, these are the mighty men of old, men of renown.
verses.textLatin: Gigantes autem erant super terram in diebus illis: postquam enim ingressi sunt filii Dei ad filias hominum, illæque genuerunt, isti sunt potentes a sæculo viri famosi.

verses.text: And God seeing that the wickedness of men was great on the earth, and that all the thought of their heart was bent upon evil at all times,
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Deus quod multa malitia hominum esset in terra, et cuncta cogitatio cordis intenta esset ad malum omni tempore,

verses.text: It repented him that he had made man on the earth. And being touched inwardly with sorrow of heart,
verses.textLatin: pœnituit eum quod hominum fecisset in terra. Et tactus dolore cordis intrinsecus,

verses.text: He said: I will destroy man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth, from man even to beasts, from the creeping thing even to the fowls of the air, for it repenteth me that I have made them.
verses.textLatin: Delebo, inquit, hominem, quem creavi, a facie terræ, ab homine usque ad animantia, a reptili usque ad volucres cæli: pœnitet enim me fecisse eos.

verses.text: But Noe found grace before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Noë vero invenit gratiam coram Domino.

verses.text: These are the generations of Noe: Noe was a just and perfect man in his generations, he walked with God.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt generationes Noë: Noë vir justus atque perfectus fuit in generationibus suis; cum Deo ambulavit.

verses.text: And he begot three sons, Sem, Cham, and Japheth.
verses.textLatin: Et genuit tres filios, Sem, Cham et Japheth.

verses.text: And the earth was corrupted before God, and was filled with iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Corrupta est autem terra coram Deo, et repleta est iniquitate.

verses.text: And when God had seen that the earth was corrupted (for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth,)
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset Deus terram esse corruptam (omnis quippe caro corruperat viam suam super terram),

verses.text: He said to Noe: The end of all flesh is come before me, the earth is filled with iniquity through them, and I will destroy them with the earth.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad Noë: Finis universæ carnis venit coram me: repleta est terra iniquitate a facie eorum, et ego disperdam eos cum terra.

verses.text: Make thee an ark of timber planks: thou shalt make little rooms in the ark, and thou shalt pitch it within and without.
verses.textLatin: Fac tibi arcam de lignis lævigatis; mansiunculas in arca facies, et bitumine linies intrinsecus et extrinsecus.

verses.text: And thus shalt thou make it: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits: the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
verses.textLatin: Et sic facies eam: trecentorum cubitorum erit longitudo arcæ, quinquaginta cubitorum latitudo, et triginta cubitorum altitudo illius.

verses.text: Thou shalt make a window in the ark, and in a cubit shalt thou finish the top of it: and the door of the ark thou shalt set in the side: with lower, middle chambers, and third stories shalt thou make it.
verses.textLatin: Fenestram in arca facies, et in cubito consummabis summitatem ejus: ostium autem arcæ pones ex latere; deorsum, cœnacula et tristega facies in ea.

verses.text: Behold I will bring the waters of a great flood upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, under heaven. All things that are in the earth shall be consumed.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego adducam aquas diluvii super terram, ut interficiam omnem carnem, in qua spiritus vitæ est subter cælum: universa quæ in terra sunt, consumentur.

verses.text: And I will establish my covenant with thee, and thou shalt enter into the ark, thou and thy sons, and thy wife, and the wives of thy sons with thee.
verses.textLatin: Ponamque fœdus meum tecum: et ingredieris arcam tu et filii tui, uxor tua, et uxores filiorum tuorum tecum.

verses.text: And of every living creature of all flesh, thou shalt bring two of a sort into the ark, that they may live with thee: of the male sex, and the female.
verses.textLatin: Et ex cunctis animantibus universæ carnis bina induces in arcam, ut vivant tecum: masculini sexus et feminini.

verses.text: Of fowls according to their kind, and of beasts in their kind, and of every thing that creepeth on the earth according to its kind; two of every sort shall go in with thee, that they may live.
verses.textLatin: De volucribus juxta genus suum, et de jumentis in genere suo, et ex omni reptili terræ secundum genus suum: bina de omnibus ingredientur tecum, ut possint vivere.

verses.text: Thou shalt take unto thee of all food that may be eaten, and thou shalt lay it up with thee: and it shall be food for thee and them.
verses.textLatin: Tolles igitur tecum ex omnibus escis, quæ mandi possunt, et comportabis apud te: et erunt tam tibi, quam illis in cibum.

verses.text: And Noe did all things which God commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Fecit igitur Noë omnia quæ præceperat illi Deus.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to him: Go in thou and all thy house into the ark: for thee I have seen just before me in this generation.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Ingredere tu et omnis domus tua in arcam: te enim vidi justum coram me in generatione hac.

verses.text: Of all clean beasts take seven and seven, the male and the female.
verses.textLatin: Ex omnibus animantibus mundis tolle septena et septena, masculum et feminam: de animantibus vero immundis duo et duo, masculum et feminam.

verses.text: But of the beasts that are unclean two and two, the male and the female. Of the fowls also of the air seven and seven, the male and the female: that seed may be saved upon the face of the whole earth.
verses.textLatin: Sed et de volatilibus cæli septena et septena, masculum et feminam: ut salvetur semen super faciem universæ terræ.

verses.text: For yet a while, and after seven days, I will rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and I will destroy every substance that I have made, from the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc enim, et post dies septem ego pluam super terram quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus: et delebo omnem substantiam, quam feci, de superficie terræ.

verses.text: And Noe did all things which the Lord had commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ergo Noë omnia quæ mandaverat ei Dominus.

verses.text: And he was six hundred years old, when the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.
verses.textLatin: Eratque sexcentorum annorum quando diluvii aquæ inundaverunt super terram.

verses.text: And Noe went in and his sons, his wife and the wives of his sons with him into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.
verses.textLatin: Et ingressus est Noë et filii ejus, uxor ejus et uxores filiorum ejus cum eo in arcam propter aquas diluvii.

verses.text: And of beasts clean and unclean, and of fowls, and of every thing that moveth upon the earth,
verses.textLatin: De animantibus quoque mundis et immundis, et de volucribus, et ex omni quod movetur super terram,

verses.text: Two and two went in to Noe into the ark, male and female, as the Lord had commanded Noe.
verses.textLatin: duo et duo ingressa sunt ad Noë in arcam, masculus et femina, sicut præceperat Dominus Noë.

verses.text: And after the seven days were passed, the waters of the flood overflowed the earth.
verses.textLatin: Cumque transissent septem dies, aquæ diluvii inundaverunt super terram.

verses.text: In the six hundredth year of the life of Noe, in the second month, in the seventeenth day of the month, all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the flood gates of heaven were opened:
verses.textLatin: Anno sexcentesimo vitæ Noë, mense secundo, septimodecimo die mensis, rupti sunt omnes fontes abyssi magnæ, et cataractæ cæli apertæ sunt:

verses.text: And the rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
verses.textLatin: et facta est pluvia super terram quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus.

verses.text: In the selfsame day Noe, and Sem, and Cham, and Japheth his sons: his wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, went into the ark:
verses.textLatin: In articulo diei illius ingressus est Noë, et Sem, et Cham, et Japheth filii ejus; uxor illius, et tres uxores filiorum ejus cum eis in arcam:

verses.text: They and every beast according to its kind, and all the cattle in their kind, and every thing that moveth upon the earth according to its kind, and every fowl according to its kind, all birds, and all that fly,
verses.textLatin: ipsi et omne animal secundum genus suum, universaque jumenta in genere suo, et omne quod movetur super terram in genere suo, cunctumque volatile secundum genus suum, universæ aves, omnesque volucres,

verses.text: Went in to Noe into the ark, two and two of all flesh, wherein was the breath of life.
verses.textLatin: ingressæ sunt ad Noë in arcam, bina et bina ex omni carne, in qua erat spiritus vitæ.

verses.text: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the Lord shut him in on the outside.
verses.textLatin: Et quæ ingressa sunt, masculus et femina ex omni carne introierunt, sicut præceperat ei Deus: et inclusit eum Dominus deforis.

verses.text: And the flood was forty days upon the earth, and the waters increased, and lifted up the ark on high from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Factumque est diluvium quadraginta diebus super terram: et multiplicatæ sunt aquæ, et elevaverunt arcam in sublime a terra.

verses.text: For they overflowed exceedingly: and filled all on the face of the earth: and the ark was carried upon the waters.
verses.textLatin: Vehementer enim inundaverunt, et omnia repleverunt in superficie terræ: porro arca ferebatur super aquas.

verses.text: And the waters prevailed beyond measure upon the earth: and all the high mountains under the whole heaven were covered.
verses.textLatin: Et aquæ prævaluerunt nimis super terram: opertique sunt omnes montes excelsi sub universo cælo.

verses.text: The water was fifteen cubits higher than the mountains which it covered.
verses.textLatin: Quindecim cubitis altior fuit aqua super montes, quos operuerat.

verses.text: And all flesh was destroyed that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beasts, and of all creeping things that creep upon the earth: and all men.
verses.textLatin: Consumptaque est omnis caro quæ movebatur super terram, volucrum, animantium, bestiarum, omniumque reptilium, quæ reptant super terram: universi homines,

verses.text: And all things wherein there is the breath of life on the earth, died.
verses.textLatin: et cuncta, in quibus spiraculum vitæ est in terra, mortua sunt.

verses.text: And he destroyed all the substance that was upon the earth, from man even to beast, and the creeping things and fowls of the air: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noe only remained, and they that were with him in the ark.
verses.textLatin: Et delevit omnem substantiam quæ erat super terram, ab homine usque ad pecus, tam reptile quam volucres cæli: et deleta sunt de terra. Remansit autem solus Noë, et qui cum eo erant in arca.

verses.text: And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.
verses.textLatin: Obtinueruntque aquæ terram centum quinquaginta diebus.

verses.text: And  God remembered Noe, and all the living creatures, and all the cattle which were with him in the ark, and brought a wind upon the earth, and the waters were abated.
verses.textLatin: Recordatus autem Deus Noë, cunctorumque animantium, et omnium jumentorum, quæ erant cum eo in arca, adduxit spiritum super terram, et imminutæ sunt aquæ.

verses.text: The fountains also of the deep, and the flood gates of heaven were shut up, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
verses.textLatin: Et clausi sunt fontes abyssi, et cataractæ cæli: et prohibitæ sunt pluviæ de cælo.

verses.text: And the waters returned from off the earth going and coming: and they began to be abated after a hundred and fifty days.
verses.textLatin: Reversæque sunt aquæ de terra euntes et redeuntes: et cœperunt minui post centum quinquaginta dies.

verses.text: And the ark rested in the seventh month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, upon the mountains of Armenia.
verses.textLatin: Requievitque arca mense septimo, vigesimo septimo die mensis, super montes Armeniæ.

verses.text: And the waters were going and decreasing until the tenth month: for in the tenth month, the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
verses.textLatin: At vero aquæ ibant et decrescebant usque ad decimum mensem: decimo enim mense, primo die mensis, apparuerunt cacumina montium.

verses.text: And after that forty days were passed, Noe, opening the window of the ark which he had made, sent forth a raven:
verses.textLatin: Cumque transissent quadraginta dies, aperiens Noë fenestram arcæ, quam fecerat, dimisit corvum,

verses.text: Which went forth and did not return, till the waters were dried up upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: qui egrediebatur, et non revertebatur, donec siccarentur aquæ super terram.

verses.text: He sent forth also a dove after him, to see if the waters had now ceased upon the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Emisit quoque columbam post eum, ut videret si jam cessassent aquæ super faciem terræ.

verses.text: But she, not finding where her foot might rest, returned to him into the ark: for the waters were upon the whole earth: and he put forth his hand, and caught her, and brought her into the ark.
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum non invenisset ubi requiesceret pes ejus, reversa est ad eum in arcam: aquæ enim erant super universam terram: extenditque manum, et apprehensam intulit in arcam.

verses.text: And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.
verses.textLatin: Expectatis autem ultra septem diebus aliis, rursum dimisit columbam ex arca.

verses.text: And she came to him in the evening, carrying a bough of an olive tree, with green leaves, in her mouth. Noe therefore understood that the waters were ceased upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: At illa venit ad eum ad vesperam, portans ramum olivæ virentibus foliis in ore suo: intellexit ergo Noë quod cessassent aquæ super terram.

verses.text: And he stayed yet other seven days: and he sent forth the dove, which returned not any more unto him.
verses.textLatin: Expectavitque nihilominus septem alios dies: et emisit columbam, quæ non est reversa ultra ad eum.

verses.text: Therefore in the six hundredth and first year, the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were lessened upon the earth, and Noe opening the covering of the ark, looked, and saw that the face of the earth was dried.
verses.textLatin: Igitur sexcentesimo primo anno, primo mense, prima die mensis, imminutæ sunt aquæ super terram: et aperiens Noë tectum arcæ, aspexit, viditque quod exsiccata esset superficies terræ.

verses.text: In the second month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth was dried.
verses.textLatin: Mense secundo, septimo et vigesimo die mensis arefacta est terra.

verses.text: And God spoke to Noe, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est autem Deus ad Noë, dicens:

verses.text: Go out of the ark, thou and thy wife, thy sons, and the wives of thy sons with thee.
verses.textLatin: Egredere de arca, tu et uxor tua, filii tui et uxores filiorum tuorum tecum.

verses.text: All living things that are with thee of all flesh, as well in fowls as in beasts, and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, bring out with thee, and go ye upon the earth: increase and multiply upon it.
verses.textLatin: Cuncta animantia, quæ sunt apud te, ex omni carne, tam in volatilibus quam in bestiis et universis reptilibus, quæ reptant super terram, educ tecum, et ingredimini super terram: crescite et multiplicamini super eam.

verses.text: So Noe went out, he and his sons: his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.
verses.textLatin: Egressus est ergo Noë, et filii ejus: uxor illius, et uxores filiorum ejus cum eo.

verses.text: And all living things, and cattle, and creeping things that creep upon the earth, according to their kinds, went out of the ark.
verses.textLatin: Sed et omnia animantia, jumenta, et reptilia quæ reptant super terram, secundum genus suum, egressa sunt de arca.

verses.text: And Noe built an altar unto the Lord: and taking of all cattle and fowls that were clean, offered holocausts upon the altar.
verses.textLatin: Ædificavit autem Noë altare Domino: et tollens de cunctis pecoribus et volucribus mundis, obtulit holocausta super altare.

verses.text: And the Lord smelled a sweet savour, and said: I will no more curse the earth for the sake of man: for the imagination and thought of man’s heart are prone to evil from his youth: therefore I will no more destroy every living soul as I have done.
verses.textLatin: Odoratusque est Dominus odorem suavitatis, et ait: Nequaquam ultra maledicam terræ propter homines: sensus enim et cogitatio humani cordis in malum prona sunt ab adolescentia sua: non igitur ultra percutiam omnem animam viventem sicut feci.

verses.text: All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not cease.
verses.textLatin: Cunctis diebus terræ, sementis et messis, frigus et æstus, æstas et hiems, nox et dies non requiescent.

verses.text: And  God blessed Noe and his sons. And he said to them: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.
verses.textLatin: Benedixitque Deus Noë et filiis ejus. Et dixit ad eos: Crescite, et multiplicamini, et replete terram.

verses.text: And let the fear and dread of you be upon all the beasts of the earth, and upon all the fowls of the air, and all that move upon the earth: all the fishes of the sea are delivered into your hand.
verses.textLatin: Et terror vester ac tremor sit super cuncta animalia terræ, et super omnes volucres cæli, cum universis quæ moventur super terram: omnes pisces maris manui vestræ traditi sunt.

verses.text: And every thing that moveth and liveth shall be meat for you: even as the green herbs have I delivered them all to you:
verses.textLatin: Et omne, quod movetur et vivit, erit vobis in cibum: quasi olera virentia tradidi vobis omnia.

verses.text: Saving that flesh with blood you shall not eat.
verses.textLatin: Excepto, quod carnem cum sanguine non comedetis.

verses.text: For I will require the blood of your lives at the hand of every beast, and at the hand of man, at the hand of every man, and of his brother, will I require the life of man.
verses.textLatin: Sanguinem enim animarum vestrarum requiram de manu cunctarum bestiarum: et de manu hominis, de manu viri, et fratris ejus requiram animam hominis.

verses.text: Whosoever shall shed man’s blood, his blood shall be shed: for man was made to the image of God.
verses.textLatin: Quicumque effuderit humanum sanguinem, fundetur sanguis illius: ad imaginem quippe Dei factus est homo.

verses.text: But increase you and multiply, and go upon the earth, and fill it.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem crescite et multiplicamini, et ingredimini super terram, et implete eam.

verses.text: Thus also said God to Noe, and to his sons with him,
verses.textLatin: Hæc quoque dixit Deus ad Noë, et ad filios ejus cum eo:

verses.text: Behold I will establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you:
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego statuam pactum meum vobiscum, et cum semine vestro post vos:

verses.text: And with every living soul that is with you, as well in all birds as in cattle and beasts of the earth, that are come forth out of the ark, and in all the beasts of the earth.
verses.textLatin: et ad omnem animam viventem, quæ est vobiscum, tam in volucribus quam in jumentis et pecudibus terræ cunctis, quæ egressa sunt de arca, et universis bestiis terræ.

verses.text: I will establish my covenant with you, and all flesh shall be no more destroyed with the waters of a flood, neither shall there be from henceforth a flood to waste the earth.
verses.textLatin: Statuam pactum meum vobiscum, et nequaquam ultra interficietur omnis caro aquis diluvii, neque erit deinceps diluvium dissipans terram.

verses.text: And God said: This is the sign of the covenant which I give between me and you, and to every living soul that is with you, for perpetual generations.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus: Hoc signum fœderis quod do inter me et vos, et ad omnem animam viventem, quæ est vobiscum in generationes sempiternas:

verses.text: I will set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be the sign of a covenant between me, and between the earth.
verses.textLatin: arcum meum ponam in nubibus, et erit signum fœderis inter me et inter terram.

verses.text: And when I shall cover the sky with clouds, my bow shall appear in the clouds:
verses.textLatin: Cumque obduxero nubibus cælum, apparebit arcus meus in nubibus:

verses.text: And I will remember my covenant with you, and with every living soul that beareth flesh: and there shall no more be waters of a flood to destroy all flesh.
verses.textLatin: et recordabor fœderis mei vobiscum, et cum omni anima vivente quæ carnem vegetat: et non erunt ultra aquæ diluvii ad delendum universam carnem.

verses.text: And the bow shall be in the clouds, and I shall see it, and shall remember the everlasting covenant, that was made between God and every living soul of all flesh which is upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Eritque arcus in nubibus, et videbo illum, et recordabor fœderis sempiterni quod pactum est inter Deum et omnem animam viventem universæ carnis quæ est super terram.

verses.text: And God said to Noe: This shall be the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus ad Noë: Hoc erit signum fœderis, quod constitui inter me et omnem carnem super terram.

verses.text: And the sons of Noe who came out of the ark, were Sem, Cham, and Japheth: and Cham is the father of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Erant ergo filii Noë, qui egressi sunt de arca, Sem, Cham et Japheth: porro Cham ipse est pater Chanaan.

verses.text: These three are the sons of Noe: and from these was all mankind spread over the whole earth.
verses.textLatin: Tres isti filii sunt Noë: et ab his disseminatum est omne genus hominum super universam terram.

verses.text: And Noe, a husbandman, began to till the ground, and planted a vineyard,
verses.textLatin: Cœpitque Noë vir agricola exercere terram, et plantavit vineam.

verses.text: And drinking of the wine was made drunk, and was uncovered in his tent.
verses.textLatin: Bibensque vinum inebriatus est, et nudatus in tabernaculo suo.

verses.text: Which when Cham the father of Chanaan had seen, to wit, that his father’s nakedness was uncovered, he told it to his two brethren without.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidisset Cham, pater Chanaan, verenda scilicet patris sui esse nudata, nuntiavit duobus fratribus suis foras.

verses.text: But Sem and Japheth put a cloak upon their shoulders, and going backward, covered the nakedness of their father: and their faces were turned away, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.
verses.textLatin: At vero Sem et Japheth pallium imposuerunt humeris suis, et incedentes retrorsum, operuerunt verenda patris sui: faciesque eorum aversæ erant, et patris virilia non viderunt.

verses.text: And Noe awaking from the wine, when he had learned what his younger son had done to him,
verses.textLatin: Evigilans autem Noë ex vino, cum didicisset quæ fecerat ei filius suus minor,

verses.text: He said: Cursed be Chanaan, a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.
verses.textLatin: ait: Maledictus Chanaan, servus servorum erit fratribus suis.

verses.text: And he said: Blessed be the Lord God of Sem, be Chanaan his servant.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque: Benedictus Dominus Deus Sem, sit Chanaan servus ejus.

verses.text: May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Sem, and Chanaan be his servant.
verses.textLatin: Dilatet Deus Japheth, et habitet in tabernaculis Sem, sitque Chanaan servus ejus.

verses.text: And Noe lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years:
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Noë post diluvium trecentis quinquaginta annis.

verses.text: And all his days were in the whole nine hundred and fifty years: and he died.
verses.textLatin: Et impleti sunt omnes dies ejus nongentorum quinquaginta annorum: et mortuus est.

verses.text: These  are the generations of the sons of Noe: Sem, Cham, and Japheth: and unto them sons were born after the flood.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt generationes filiorum Noë, Sem, Cham et Japheth: natique sunt eis filii post diluvium.

verses.text: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Thubal, and Mosoch, and Thiras.
verses.textLatin: Filii Japheth: Gomer, et Magog, et Madai, et Javan, et Thubal, et Mosoch, et Thiras.

verses.text: And the sons of Gomer: Ascenez and Riphath and Thogorma.
verses.textLatin: Porro filii Gomer: Ascenez et Riphath et Thogorma.

verses.text: And the sons of Javan: Elisa and Tharsis, Cetthim and Dodanim.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Javan: Elisa et Tharsis, Cetthim et Dodanim.

verses.text: By these were divided the islands of the Gentiles in their lands, every one according to his tongue and their families, in their nations.
verses.textLatin: Ab his divisæ sunt insulæ gentium in regionibus suis, unusquisque secundum linguam suam et familias suas in nationibus suis.

verses.text: And the Sons of Cham: Chus, and Mesram, and Phuth, and Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Cham: Chus, et Mesraim, et Phuth, et Chanaan.

verses.text: And the sons of Chus: Saba, and Hevila, and Sabatha, and Regma, and Sabatacha. The sons of Regma: Saba and Dadan.
verses.textLatin: Filii Chus: Saba, et Hevila, et Sabatha, et Regma, et Sabatacha. Filii Regma: Saba et Dadan.

verses.text: Now Chus begot Nemrod: he began to be mighty on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Porro Chus genuit Nemrod: ipse cœpit esse potens in terra,

verses.text: And he was a stout hunter before the Lord. Hence came a proverb: Even as Nemrod the stout hunter before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et erat robustus venator coram Domino. Ob hoc exivit proverbium: Quasi Nemrod robustus venator coram Domino.

verses.text: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, and Arach, and Achad, and Chalanne in the land of Sennaar.
verses.textLatin: Fuit autem principium regni ejus Babylon, et Arach et Achad, et Chalanne, in terra Sennaar.

verses.text: Out of that land came forth Assur, and built Ninive, and the streets of the city, and Chale.
verses.textLatin: De terra illa egressus est Assur, et ædificavit Niniven, et plateas civitatis, et Chale.

verses.text: Resen also between Ninive and Chale: this is the great city.
verses.textLatin: Resen quoque inter Niniven et Chale: hæc est civitas magna.

verses.text: And Mesraim begot Ludim, and Anamim, and Laabim, Nepthuim,
verses.textLatin: At vero Mesraim genuit Ludim, et Anamim et Laabim, Nephthuim,

verses.text: And Phetrusim, and Chasluim; of whom came forth the Philistines, and the Capthorim.
verses.textLatin: et Phetrusim, et Chasluim: de quibus egressi sunt Philisthiim et Caphtorim.

verses.text: And Chanaan begot Sidon, his firstborn, the Hethite,
verses.textLatin: Chanaan autem genuit Sidonem primogenitum suum. Hethæum,

verses.text: And the Jebusite, and the Amorrhite, and the Gergesite,
verses.textLatin: et Jebusæum, et Amorrhæum, Gergesæum,

verses.text: The Hevite and the Aracite: the Sinite,
verses.textLatin: Hevæum, et Aracæum: Sinæum,

verses.text: And the Aradian, the Samarite, and the Hamathite: and afterwards the families of the Chanaanites were spread abroad.
verses.textLatin: et Aradium, Samaræum, et Amathæum: et post hæc disseminati sunt populi Chananæorum.

verses.text: And the limits of Chanaan were from Sidon as one comes to Gerara even to Gaza, until thou enter Sodom and Gomorrha, and Adama, and Seboim even to Lesa.
verses.textLatin: Factique sunt termini Chanaan venientibus a Sidone Geraram usque Gazam, donec ingrediaris Sodomam et Gomorrham, et Adamam, et Seboim usque Lesa.

verses.text: These are the children of Cham in their kindreds, and tongues, and generations, and lands, and nations.
verses.textLatin: Hi sunt filii Cham in cognationibus, et linguis, et generationibus, terrisque et gentibus suis.

verses.text: Of Sem also, the father of all the children of Heber, the elder brother of Japheth, sons were born.
verses.textLatin: De Sem quoque nati sunt, patre omnium filiorum Heber, fratre Japheth majore.

verses.text: The sons of Sem: Elam and Assur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.
verses.textLatin: Filii Sem: Ælam, et Assur, et Arphaxad, et Lud, et Aram.

verses.text: The sons of Aram: Us and Hull, and Gether: and Mess.
verses.textLatin: Filii Aram: Us, et Hul, et Gether, et Mes.

verses.text: But Arphaxad begot Sale, of whom was born Heber.
verses.textLatin: At vero Arphaxad genuit Sale, de quo ortus est Heber.

verses.text: And to Heber were born two sons: the name of the one was Phaleg, because in his days the earth was divided: and his brother’s name Jectan.
verses.textLatin: Natique sunt Heber filii duo: nomen uni Phaleg, eo quod in diebus ejus divisa sit terra: et nomen fratris ejus Jectan.

verses.text: Which Jectan begot Elmodad, and Saleph, and Asarmoth, Jare,
verses.textLatin: Qui Jectan genuit Elmodad, et Saleph, et Asarmoth, Jare,

verses.text: And Aduram, and Uzal, and Decla,
verses.textLatin: et Aduram, et Uzal, et Decla,

verses.text: And Ebal, and Abimael, Saba,
verses.textLatin: et Ebal, et Abimaël, Saba,

verses.text: And Ophir, and Hevila, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Jectan.
verses.textLatin: et Ophir, et Hevila, et Jobab: omnes isti, filii Jectan.

verses.text: And their dwelling was from Messa as we go on as far as Sephar, a mountain in the east.
verses.textLatin: Et facta est habitatio eorum de Messa pergentibus usque Sephar montem orientalem.

verses.text: These are the children of Sem according to their kindreds and tongues, and countries in their nations.
verses.textLatin: Isti filii Sem secundum cognationes, et linguas, et regiones in gentibus suis.

verses.text: These are the families of Noe, according to their peoples and nations. By these were the nations divided on the earth after the flood.
verses.textLatin: Hæ familiæ Noë juxta populos et nationes suas. Ab his divisæ sunt gentes in terra post diluvium.

verses.text: And  the earth was of one tongue, and of the same speech.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem terra labii unius, et sermonum eorumdem.

verses.text: And when they removed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Sennaar, and dwelt in it.
verses.textLatin: Cumque proficiscerentur de oriente, invenerunt campum in terra Sennaar, et habitaverunt in eo.

verses.text: And each one said to his neighbour: Come, let us make brick, and bake them with fire. And they had brick instead of stones, and slime instead of mortar.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque alter ad proximum suum: Venite, faciamus lateres, et coquamus eos igni. Habueruntque lateres pro saxis, et bitumen pro cæmento:

verses.text: And they said: Come, let us make a city and a tower, the top whereof may reach to heaven: and let us make our name famous before we be scattered abroad into all lands.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt: Venite, faciamus nobis civitatem et turrim, cujus culmen pertingat ad cælum: et celebremus nomen nostrum antequam dividamur in universas terras.

verses.text: And the Lord came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of Adam were building.
verses.textLatin: Descendit autem Dominus ut videret civitatem et turrim, quam ædificabant filii Adam,

verses.text: And he said: Behold, it is one people, and all have one tongue: and they have begun to do this, neither will they leave off from their designs, till they accomplish them in deed.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Ecce, unus est populus, et unum labium omnibus: cœperuntque hoc facere, nec desistent a cogitationibus suis, donec eas opere compleant.

verses.text: Come ye, therefore, let us go down, and there confound their tongue, that they may not understand one another’s speech.
verses.textLatin: Venite igitur, descendamus, et confundamus ibi linguam eorum, ut non audiat unusquisque vocem proximi sui.

verses.text: And so the Lord scattered them from that place into all lands, and they ceased to build the city.
verses.textLatin: Atque ita divisit eos Dominus ex illo loco in universas terras, et cessaverunt ædificare civitatem.

verses.text: And therefore the name thereof was called Babel, because there the language of the whole earth was confounded: and from thence the Lord scattered them abroad upon the face of all countries.
verses.textLatin: Et idcirco vocatum est nomen ejus Babel, quia ibi confusum est labium universæ terræ: et inde dispersit eos Dominus super faciem cunctarum regionum.

verses.text: These are the generations of Sem: Sem was a hundred years old when he begot Arphaxad, two years after the flood.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt generationes Sem: Sem erat centum annorum quando genuit Arphaxad, biennio post diluvium.

verses.text: And Sem lived after he begot Arphaxad, five hundred years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Sem, postquam genuit Arphaxad, quingentis annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Arphaxad lived thirty-five years, and begot Sale.
verses.textLatin: Porro Arphaxad vixit triginta quinque annis, et genuit Sale.

verses.text: And Arphaxad lived after he begot Sale, three hundred and three years; and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Arphaxad, postquam genuit Sale, trecentis tribus annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: Sale also lived thirty years, and begot Heber.
verses.textLatin: Sale quoque vixit triginta annis, et genuit Heber.

verses.text: And Sale lived after he begot Heber, four hundred and three years; and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Sale, postquam genuit Heber, quadringentis tribus annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Heber lived thirty-four years, and begot Phaleg.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Heber triginta quatuor annis, et genuit Phaleg.

verses.text: And Heber lived after he begot Phaleg, four hundred and thirty years: and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit Heber postquam genuit Phaleg, quadringentis triginta annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: Phaleg also lived thirty years, and begot Reu.
verses.textLatin: Vixit quoque Phaleg triginta annis, et genuit Reu.

verses.text: And Phaleg lived after he begot Reu, two hundred and nine years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Phaleg, postquam genuit Reu, ducentis novem annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Reu lived thirty-two years, and begot Sarug.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Reu triginta duobus annis, et genuit Sarug.

verses.text: And Reu lived after he begot Sarug, two hundred and seven years, and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixit quoque Reu, postquam genuit Sarug, ducentis septem annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Sarug lived thirty years, and begot Nachor.
verses.textLatin: Vixit vero Sarug triginta annis, et genuit Nachor.

verses.text: And Sarug lived after he begot Nachor, two hundred years: and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Sarug, postquam genuit Nachor, ducentis annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Nachor lived nine and twenty years, and begot Thare.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Nachor viginti novem annis, et genuit Thare.

verses.text: And Nachor lived after he begot Thare, a hundred and nineteen years: and begot sons and daughters.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Nachor, postquam genuit Thare, centum decem et novem annis: et genuit filios et filias.

verses.text: And Thare lived seventy years, and begot Abram, and Nachor, and Aran.
verses.textLatin: Vixitque Thare septuaginta annis, et genuit Abram, et Nachor, et Aran.

verses.text: And these are the generations of Thare: Thare begot Abram, Nachor, and Aran. And Aran begot Lot.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt autem generationes Thare: Thare genuit Abram, Nachor et Aran. Porro Aran genuit Lot.

verses.text: And Aran died before Thare his father, in the land of his nativity in Ur of the Chaldees.
verses.textLatin: Mortuusque est Aran ante Thare patrem suum, in terra nativitatis suæ, in Ur Chaldæorum.

verses.text: And Abram and Nachor married wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai: and the name of Nachor’s wife, Melcha, the daughter of Aran, father of Melcha, and father of Jescha.
verses.textLatin: Duxerunt autem Abram et Nachor uxores: nomen uxoris Abram, Sarai: et nomen uxoris Nachor, Melcha filia Aran, patris Melchæ, et patris Jeschæ.

verses.text: And Sarai was barren, and had no children.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Sarai sterilis, nec habebat liberos.

verses.text: And Thare took Abram, his son, and Lot the son of Aran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter in law, the wife of Abram his son, and brought them out of Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Chanaan: and they came as far as Haran, and dwelt there.
verses.textLatin: Tulit itaque Thare Abram filium suum, et Lot filium Aran, filium filii sui, et Sarai nurum suam, uxorem Abram filii sui, et eduxit eos de Ur Chaldæorum, ut irent in terram Chanaan: veneruntque usque Haran, et habitaverunt ibi.

verses.text: And the days of Thare were two hundred and five years, and he died in Haran.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt dies Thare ducentorum quinque annorum, et mortuus est in Haran.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Abram: Go forth out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and out of thy father’s house, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Abram: Egredere de terra tua, et de cognatione tua, et de domo patris tui, et veni in terram quam monstrabo tibi.

verses.text: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Faciamque te in gentem magnam, et benedicam tibi, et magnificabo nomen tuum, erisque benedictus.

verses.text: I will bless them that bless thee, and curse them that curse thee, and IN THEE shall all the kindred of the earth be blessed:
verses.textLatin: Benedicam benedicentibus tibi, et maledicam maledicentibus tibi, atque in te benedicentur universæ cognationes terræ.

verses.text: So Abram went out as the Lord had commanded him, and Lot went with him: Abram was seventy-five years old when he went forth from Haran.
verses.textLatin: Egressus est itaque Abram sicut præceperat ei Dominus, et ivit cum eo Lot: septuaginta quinque annorum erat Abram cum egrederetur de Haran.

verses.text: And he took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the substance which they had gathered, and the souls which they had gotten in Haran: and they went out to go into the land of Chanaan. And when they were come into it,
verses.textLatin: Tulitque Sarai uxorem suam, et Lot filium fratris sui, universamque substantiam quam possederant, et animas quas fecerant in Haran: et egressi sunt ut irent in terram Chanaan. Cumque venissent in eam,

verses.text: Abram passed through the country into the place of Sichem, as far as the noble vale: now the Chanaanite was at that time in the land.
verses.textLatin: pertransivit Abram terram usque ad locum Sichem, usque ad convallem illustrem: Chananæus autem tunc erat in terra.

verses.text: And the Lord appeared to Abram, and said to him: To thy seed will I give this land. And he built there an altar to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
verses.textLatin: Apparuit autem Dominus Abram, et dixit ei: Semini tuo dabo terram hanc. Qui ædificavit ibi altare Domino, qui apparuerat ei.

verses.text: And passing on from thence to a mountain, that was on the east side of Bethel, he there pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Hai on the east; he built there also an altar to the Lord, and called upon his name.
verses.textLatin: Et inde transgrediens ad montem, qui erat contra orientem Bethel, tetendit ibi tabernaculum suum, ab occidente habens Bethel, et ab oriente Hai: ædificavit quoque ibi altare Domino, et invocavit nomen ejus.

verses.text: And Abram went forward, going, and proceeding on to the south.
verses.textLatin: Perrexitque Abram vadens, et ultra progrediens ad meridiem.

verses.text: And there came a famine in the country; and Abram went down into Egypt, to sojourn there: for the famine was very grievous in the land.
verses.textLatin: Facta est autem fames in terra: descenditque Abram in Ægyptum, ut peregrinaretur ibi: prævaluerat enim fames in terra.

verses.text: And when he was near to enter into Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife: I know that thou art a beautiful woman:
verses.textLatin: Cumque prope esset ut ingrederetur Ægyptum, dixit Sarai uxori suæ: Novi quod pulchra sis mulier:

verses.text: And that when the Egyptians shall see thee, they will say: She is his wife: and they will kill me, and keep thee.
verses.textLatin: et quod cum viderint te Ægyptii, dicturi sunt: Uxor ipsius est: et interficient me, et te reservabunt.

verses.text: Say, therefore, I pray thee, that thou art my sister: that I may be well used for thee, and that my soul may live for thy sake.
verses.textLatin: Dic ergo, obsecro te, quod soror mea sis: ut bene sit mihi propter te, et vivat anima mea ob gratiam tui.

verses.text: And when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians saw the woman that she was very beautiful.
verses.textLatin: Cum itaque ingressus esset Abram Ægyptum, viderunt Ægyptii mulierem quod esset pulchra nimis.

verses.text: And the princes told Pharao, and praised her before him: and the woman was taken into the house of Pharao.
verses.textLatin: Et nuntiaverunt principes Pharaoni, et laudaverunt eam apud illum: et sublata est mulier in domum Pharaonis.

verses.text: And they used Abram well for her sake. And he had sheep and oxen, and he asses, and menservants and maidservants, and she asses, and camels.
verses.textLatin: Abram vero bene usi sunt propter illam: fueruntque ei oves et boves et asini, et servi et famulæ, et asinæ et cameli.

verses.text: But the Lord scourged Pharao and his house with most grievous stripes for Sarai, Abram’s wife.
verses.textLatin: Flagellavit autem Dominus Pharaonem plagis maximis, et domum ejus, propter Sarai uxorem Abram.

verses.text: And Pharao called Abram, and said to him: What is this that thou hast done to me? Why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Pharao Abram, et dixit ei: Quidnam est hoc quod fecisti mihi? quare non indicasti quod uxor tua esset?

verses.text: For what cause didst thou say, she was thy sister, that I might take her to my wife? Now, therefore, there is thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
verses.textLatin: quam ob causam dixisti esse sororem tuam, ut tollerem eam mihi in uxorem? Nunc igitur ecce conjux tua, accipe eam, et vade.

verses.text: And Pharao gave his men orders concerning Abram: and they led him away, and his wife, and all that he had.
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque Pharao super Abram viris: et deduxerunt eum, et uxorem illius, et omnia quæ habebat.

verses.text: And  Abram went up out of Egypt, he and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the south.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit ergo Abram de Ægypto, ipse et uxor ejus, et omnia quæ habebat, et Lot cum eo, ad australem plagam.

verses.text: And he was very rich in possession of gold and silver.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem dives valde in possessione auri et argenti.

verses.text: And he returned by the way that he came, from the south to Bethel, to the place where before he had pitched his tent between Bethel and Hai:
