verses.textLatin: Reversusque est per iter, quo venerat, a meridie in Bethel, usque ad locum ubi prius fixerat tabernaculum inter Bethel et Hai,

verses.text: In the place of the altar which he had made before; and there he called upon the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: in loco altaris quod fecerat prius: et invocavit ibi nomen Domini.

verses.text: But Lot also, who was with Abram, had flocks of sheep, and herds of beasts, and tents.
verses.textLatin: Sed et Lot qui erat cum Abram, fuerunt greges ovium, et armenta, et tabernacula.

verses.text: Neither was the land able to bear them, that they might dwell together: for their substance was great, and they could not dwell together.
verses.textLatin: Nec poterat eos capere terra, ut habitarent simul: erat quippe substantia eorum multa, et nequibant habitare communiter.

verses.text: Whereupon also there arose a strife between the herdsmen of Abram and of Lot. And at that time the Chanaanite and the Pherezite dwelled in that country.
verses.textLatin: Unde et facta est rixa inter pastores gregum Abram et Lot. Eo autem tempore Chananæus et Pherezæus habitabant in terra illa.

verses.text: Abram therefore said to Lot: Let there be no quarrel, I beseech thee, between me and thee, and between my herdsmen and thy herdsmen: for we are brethren.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Abram ad Lot: Ne quæso sit jurgium inter me et te, et inter pastores meos et pastores tuos: fratres enim sumus.

verses.text: Behold the whole land is before thee: depart from me I pray thee: if thou wilt go to the left hand, I will take the right: if thou choose the right hand, I will pass to the left.
verses.textLatin: Ecce universa terra coram te est: recede a me, obsecro: si ad sinistram ieris, ego dexteram tenebo: si tu dexteram elegeris, ego ad sinistram pergam.

verses.text: And Lot, lifting up his eyes, saw all the country about the Jordan, which was watered throughout, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha, as the paradise of the Lord, and like Egypt as one comes to Segor.
verses.textLatin: Elevatis itaque Lot oculis, vidit omnem circa regionem Jordanis, quæ universa irrigabatur antequam subverteret Dominus Sodomam et Gomorrham, sicut paradisus Domini, et sicut Ægyptus venientibus in Segor.

verses.text: And Lot chose to himself the country about the Jordan, and he departed from the east: and they were separated one brother from the other.
verses.textLatin: Elegitque sibi Lot regionem circa Jordanem, et recessit ab oriente: divisique sunt alterutrum a fratre suo.

verses.text: Abram dwelt in the land of Chanaan; and Lot abode in the towns that were about the Jordan, and dwelt in Sodom.
verses.textLatin: Abram habitavit in terra Chanaan; Lot vero moratus est in oppidis, quæ erant circa Jordanem, et habitavit in Sodomis.

verses.text: And the men of Sodom were very wicked, and sinners before the face of the Lord, beyond measure.
verses.textLatin: Homines autem Sodomitæ pessimi erant, et peccatores coram Domino nimis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Abram, after Lot was separated from him: Lift up thy eyes, and look from the place wherein thou now art, to the north and to the south, to the east and to the west.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Abram, postquam divisus est ab eo Lot: Leva oculos tuos et vide a loco, in quo nunc es, ad aquilonem et meridiem, ad orientem et occidentem.

verses.text: All the land which thou seest, I will give to thee, and to thy seed for ever.
verses.textLatin: Omnem terram, quam conspicis, tibi dabo, et semini tuo usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: if any man be able to number the dust of the earth, he shall be able to number thy seed also.
verses.textLatin: Faciamque semen tuum sicut pulverem terræ: si quis potest hominum numerare pulverem terræ, semen quoque tuum numerare poterit.

verses.text: Arise and walk through the land in the length, and in the breadth thereof: for I will give it to thee.
verses.textLatin: Surge, et perambula terram in longitudine et in latitudine sua: quia tibi daturus sum eam.

verses.text: So Abram removing his tent came and dwelt by the vale of Mambre, which is in Hebron: and he built there an altar to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Movens igitur tabernaculum suum Abram, venit, et habitavit juxta convallem Mambre, quæ est in Hebron: ædificavitque ibi altare Domino.

verses.text: And  it came to pass at that time, that Amraphel king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Pontus, and Chodorlahomor king of the Elamites, and Thadal king of nations,
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem in illo tempore, ut Amraphel rex Sennaar, et Arioch rex Ponti, et Chodorlahomor rex Elamitarum, et Thadal rex gentium

verses.text: Made war against Bara king of Sodom, and against Bersa king of Gomorrha, and against Sennaab king of Adama, and against Semeber king of Seboim, and against the king of Bala, which is Segor.
verses.textLatin: inirent bellum contra Bara regem Sodomorum, et contra Bersa regem Gomorrhæ, et contra Sennaab regem Adamæ, et contra Semeber regem Seboim, contraque regem Balæ, ipsa est Segor.

verses.text: All these came together into the woodland vale, which now is the salt sea.
verses.textLatin: Omnes hi convenerunt in vallem Silvestrem, quæ nunc est mare salis.

verses.text: For they had served Chodorlahomor twelve years, and in the thirteenth year they revolted from him.
verses.textLatin: Duodecim enim annis servierunt Chodorlahomor, et tertiodecimo anno recesserunt ab eo.

verses.text: And in the fourteenth year came Chodorlahomor, and the kings that were with him: and they smote the Raphaim in Astarothcarnaim, and the Zuzim with them, and the Emim in Save of Cariathaim.
verses.textLatin: Igitur quartodecimo anno venit Chodorlahomor, et reges qui erant cum eo: percusseruntque Raphaim in Astarothcarnaim, et Zuzim cum eis, et Emim in Save Cariathaim,

verses.text: And the Chorreans in the mountains of Seir, even to the plains of Pharan, which is in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: et Chorræos in montibus Seir, usque ad Campestria Pharan, quæ est in solitudine.

verses.text: And they returned, and came to the fountain of Misphat, the same is Cades: and they smote all the country of the Amalecites, and the Amorrhean that dwelt in Asasonthamar.
verses.textLatin: Reversique sunt, et venerunt ad fontem Misphat, ipsa est Cades: et percusserunt omnem regionem Amalecitarum, et Amorrhæum, qui habitabat in Asasonthamar.

verses.text: And the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrha, and the king of Adama, and the king of Seboim, and the king of Bala, which is Segor, went out: and they set themselves against them in battle array in the woodland vale:
verses.textLatin: Et egressi sunt rex Sodomorum, et rex Gomorrhæ, rexque Adamæ, et rex Seboim, necnon et rex Balæ, quæ est Segor: et direxerunt aciem contra eos in valle Silvestri:

verses.text: To wit, against Chodorlahomor king of the Elamites, and Thadal king of nations, and Amraphel king of Sennaar, and Arioch king of Pontus: four kings against five.
verses.textLatin: scilicet adversus Chodorlahomor regem Elamitarum, et Thadal regem Gentium, et Amraphel regem Sennaar, et Arioch regem Ponti: quatuor reges adversus quinque.

verses.text: Now the woodland vale had many pits of slime. And the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrha turned their backs and were overthrown there: and they that remained fled to the mountain.
verses.textLatin: Vallis autem Silvestris habebat puteos multos bituminis. Itaque rex Sodomorum, et Gomorrhæ, terga verterunt, cecideruntque ibi: et qui remanserant, fugerunt ad montem.

verses.text: And they took all the substance of the Sodomites, and Gomorrhites, and all their victuals, and went their way:
verses.textLatin: Tulerunt autem omnem substantiam Sodomorum et Gomorrhæ, et universa quæ ad cibum pertinent, et abierunt:

verses.text: And Lot also, the son of Abram’s brother, who dwelt in Sodom, and his substance.
verses.textLatin: necnon et Lot, et substantiam ejus, filium fratris Abram, qui habitabat in Sodomis.

verses.text: And behold one that had escaped told Abram the Hebrew, who dwelt in the vale of Mambre the Amorrhite, the brother of Escol, and the brother of Aner: for these had made league with Abram.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce unus, qui evaserat, nuntiavit Abram Hebræo, qui habitabat in convalle Mambre Amorrhæi, fratris Escol, et fratris Aner: hi enim pepigerant fœdus cum Abram.

verses.text: Which when Abram had heard, to wit, that his brother Lot was taken, he numbered of the servants born in his house, three hundred and eighteen well appointed: and pursued them to Dan.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Abram, captum videlicet Lot fratrem suum, numeravit expeditos vernaculos suos trecentos decem et octo: et persecutus est usque Dan.

verses.text: And dividing his company, he rushed upon them in the night: and defeated them, and pursued them as far as Hoba, which is on the left hand of Damascus.
verses.textLatin: Et divisis sociis, irruit super eos nocte: percussitque eos, et persecutus est eos usque Hoba, quæ est ad lævam Damasci.

verses.text: And he brought back all the substance, and Lot his brother, with his substance, the women also and the people.
verses.textLatin: Reduxitque omnem substantiam, et Lot fratrem suum cum substantia illius, mulieres quoque et populum.

verses.text: And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after he returned from the slaughter of Chodorlahomor, and of the kings that were with him in the vale of Save, which is the king’s vale.
verses.textLatin: Egressus est autem rex Sodomorum in occursum ejus postquam reversus est a cæde Chodorlahomor, et regum qui cum eo erant in valle Save, quæ est vallis regis.

verses.text: But Melchisedech the king of Salem, bringing forth bread and wine, for he was the priest of the most high God,
verses.textLatin: At vero Melchisedech rex Salem, proferens panem et vinum, erat enim sacerdos Dei altissimi,

verses.text: Blessed him, and said: Blessed be Abram by the most high God, who created heaven and earth.
verses.textLatin: benedixit ei, et ait: Benedictus Abram Deo excelso, qui creavit cælum et terram:

verses.text: And blessed be the most high God, by whose protection the enemies are in thy hands. And he gave him the tithes of all.
verses.textLatin: et benedictus Deus excelsus, quo protegente, hostes in manibus tuis sunt. Et dedit ei decimas ex omnibus.

verses.text: And the king of Sodom said to Abram: Give me the persons, and the rest take to thyself.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem rex Sodomorum ad Abram: Da mihi animas, cetera tolle tibi.

verses.text: And he answered him: I lift up my hand to the Lord God the most high, the possessor of heaven and earth,
verses.textLatin: Qui respondit ei: Levo manum meam ad Dominum Deum excelsum possessorem cæli et terræ,

verses.text: That from the very woof thread unto the shoe latchet, I will not take of any things that are thine, lest thou say I have enriched Abram:
verses.textLatin: quod a filo subtegminis usque ad corigiam caligæ, non accipiam ex omnibus quæ tua sunt, ne dicas: Ego ditavi Abram:

verses.text: Except such things as the young men have eaten, and the shares of the men that came with me, Aner, Escol, and Mambre: these shall take their shares.
verses.textLatin: exceptis his, quæ comederunt juvenes, et partibus virorum, qui venerunt mecum, Aner, Escol et Mambre: isti accipient partes suas.

verses.text: Now  when these things were done, the word of the Lord came to Abram by a vision, saying: Fear not, Abram, I am thy protector, and thy reward exceeding great.
verses.textLatin: His itaque transactis, factus est sermo Domini ad Abram per visionem dicens: Noli timere, Abram: ego protector tuus sum, et merces tua magna nimis.

verses.text: And Abram said: Lord God, what wilt thou give me? I shall go without children: and the son of the steward of my house is this Damascus Eliezer.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Abram: Domine Deus, quid dabis mihi? ego vadam absque liberis, et filius procuratoris domus meæ iste Damascus Eliezer.

verses.text: And Abram added: But to me thou hast not given seed: and lo my servant, born in my house, shall be my heir.
verses.textLatin: Addiditque Abram: Mihi autem non dedisti semen, et ecce vernaculus meus, hæres meus erit.

verses.text: And immediately the word of the Lord came to him, saying : He shall not be thy heir: but he that shall come out of thy bowels, him shalt thou have for thy heir.
verses.textLatin: Statimque sermo Domini factus est ad eum, dicens: Non erit hic hæres tuus, sed qui egredietur de utero tuo, ipsum habebis hæredem.

verses.text: And he brought him forth abroad, and said to him: Look up to heaven and number the stars, if thou canst. And he said to him: So shall thy seed be.
verses.textLatin: Eduxitque eum foras, et ait illi: Suspice cælum, et numera stellas, si potes. Et dixit ei: Sic erit semen tuum.

verses.text: Abram believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice.
verses.textLatin: Credidit Abram Deo, et reputatum est illi ad justitiam.

verses.text: And he said to him: I am the Lord who brought thee out from Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land, and that thou mightest possess it.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eum: Ego Dominus qui eduxi te de Ur Chaldæorum ut darem tibi terram istam, et possideres eam.

verses.text: But he said: Lord God, whereby may I know that I shall possess it?
verses.textLatin: At ille ait: Domine Deus, unde scire possum quod possessurus sim eam?

verses.text: And the Lord answered, and said: Take me a cow of three years old, and a she goat of three years, and a ram of three years, a turtle also, and a pigeon.
verses.textLatin: Et respondens Dominus: Sume, inquit, mihi vaccam triennem, et capram trimam, et arietem annorum trium, turturem quoque et columbam.

verses.text: And he took all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid the two pieces of each one against the other; but the birds he divided not.
verses.textLatin: Qui tollens universa hæc, divisit ea per medium, et utrasque partes contra se altrinsecus posuit; aves autem non divisit.

verses.text: And the fowls came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
verses.textLatin: Descenderuntque volucres super cadavera, et abigebat eas Abram.

verses.text: And when the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a great and darksome horror seized upon him.
verses.textLatin: Cumque sol occumberet, sopor irruit super Abram, et horror magnus et tenebrosus invasit eum.

verses.text: And it was said unto him: Know thou beforehand that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land not their own, and they shall bring them under bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.
verses.textLatin: Dictumque est ad eum: Scito prænoscens quod peregrinum futurum sit semen tuum in terra non sua, et subjicient eos servituti, et affligent quadringentis annis.

verses.text: But I will judge the nation which they shall serve, and after this they shall come out with great substance.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen gentem, cui servituri sunt, ego judicabo: et post hæc egredientur cum magna substantia.

verses.text: And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace, and be buried in a good old age.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem ibis ad patres tuos in pace, sepultus in senectute bona.

verses.text: But in the fourth generation they shall return hither: for as yet the iniquities of the Amorrhites are not at the full until this present time.
verses.textLatin: Generatione autem quarta revertentur huc: necdum enim completæ sunt iniquitates Amorrhæorum usque ad præsens tempus.

verses.text: And when the sun was set, there arose a dark mist, and there appeared a smoking furnace and a lamp of fire passing between those divisions.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo occubuisset sol, facta est caligo tenebrosa, et apparuit clibanus fumans, et lampas ignis transiens inter divisiones illas.

verses.text: That day God made a covenant with Abram, saying: To thy seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt even to the great river Euphrates.
verses.textLatin: In illo die pepigit Dominus fœdus cum Abram, dicens: Semini tuo dabo terram hanc a fluvio Ægypti usque ad fluvium magnum Euphraten,

verses.text: The Cineans and Cenezites, the Cedmonites,
verses.textLatin: Cinæos, et Cenezæos, Cedmonæos,

verses.text: And the Hethites, and the Pherezites, the Raphaim also,
verses.textLatin: et Hethæos, et Pherezæos, Raphaim quoque,

verses.text: And the Amorrhites, and the Chanaanites, and the Gergesites, and the Jebusites.
verses.textLatin: et Amorrhæos, et Chananæos, et Gergesæos, et Jebusæos.

verses.text: Now  Sarai the wife of Abram, had brought forth no children; but having a handmaid, an Egyptian, named Agar,
verses.textLatin: Igitur Sarai, uxor Abram, non genuerat liberos: sed habens ancillam ægyptiam nomine Agar,

verses.text: She said to her husband: Behold, the Lord hath restrained me from bearing: go in unto my handmaid, it may be I may have children of her at least. And when he agreed to her request,
verses.textLatin: dixit marito suo: Ecce, conclusit me Dominus, ne parerem. Ingredere ad ancillam meam, si forte saltem ex illa suscipiam filios. Cumque ille acquiesceret deprecanti,

verses.text: She took Agar the Egyptian her handmaid, ten years after they first dwelt in the land of Chanaan, and gave her to her husband to wife.
verses.textLatin: tulit Agar ægyptiam ancillam suam post annos decem quam habitare cœperant in terra Chanaan: et dedit eam viro suo uxorem.

verses.text: And he went in to her. But she, perceiving that she was with child, despised her mistress.
verses.textLatin: Qui ingressus est ad eam. At illa concepisse se videns, despexit dominam suam.

verses.text: And Sarai said to Abram: Thou dost unjustly with me: I gave my handmaid into thy bosom, and she perceiving herself to be with child, despiseth me. The Lord judge between me and thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Sarai ad Abram: Inique agis contra me: ego dedi ancillam meam in sinum tuum, quæ videns quod conceperit, despectui me habet: judicet Dominus inter me et te.

verses.text: And Abram made answer, and said to her: Behold thy handmaid is in thy own hand, use her as it pleaseth thee. And when Sarai afflicted her, she ran away.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondens Abram: Ecce, ait, ancilla tua in manu tua est, utere ea ut libet. Affligente igitur eam Sarai, fugam iniit.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord having found her, by a fountain of water in the wilderness, which is in the way to Sur in the desert,
verses.textLatin: Cumque invenisset eam angelus Domini juxta fontem aquæ in solitudine, qui est in via Sur in deserto,

verses.text: He said to her: Agar, handmaid of Sarai, whence comest thou? and whither goest thou? And she answered: I flee from the face of Sarai, my mistress.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad illam: Agar ancilla Sarai, unde venis? et quo vadis? Quæ respondit: A facie Sarai dominæ meæ ego fugio.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord said to her: Return to thy mistress, and humble thyself under her hand.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei angelus Domini: Revertere ad dominam tuam, et humiliare sub manu illius.

verses.text: And again he said: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, and it shall not be numbered for multitude.
verses.textLatin: Et rursum: Multiplicans, inquit, multiplicabo semen tuum, et non numerabitur præ multitudine.

verses.text: And again: Behold, said he, thou art with child, and thou shalt bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name Ismael, because the Lord hath heard thy affliction.
verses.textLatin: Ac deinceps: Ecce, ait, concepisti, et paries filium: vocabisque nomen ejus Ismaël, eo quod audierit Dominus afflictionem tuam.

verses.text: He shall be a wild man: his hand will be against all men, and all men’s hands against him: and he shall pitch his tents over against all his brethren.
verses.textLatin: Hic erit ferus homo: manus ejus contra omnes, et manus omnium contra eum: et e regione universorum fratrum suorum figet tabernacula.

verses.text: And she called the name of the Lord that spoke unto her: Thou the God who hast seen me. For she said: Verily here have I seen the hinder parts of him that seeth me.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem nomen Domini qui loquebatur ad eam: Tu Deus qui vidisti me. Dixit enim: Profecto hic vidi posteriora videntis me.

verses.text: Therefore she called that well, The well of him that liveth and seeth me. The same is between Cades and Barad.
verses.textLatin: Propterea appellavit puteum illum Puteum viventis et videntis me. Ipse est inter Cades et Barad.

verses.text: And Agar brought forth a son to Abram: who called his name Ismael.
verses.textLatin: Peperitque Agar Abræ filium: qui vocavit nomen ejus Ismaël.

verses.text: Abram was fourscore and six years old when Agar brought him forth Ismael.
verses.textLatin: Octoginta et sex annorum erat Abram quando peperit ei Agar Ismaëlem.

verses.text: And  after he began to be ninety and nine years old, the Lord appeared to him: and said unto him: I am the Almighty God: walk before me, and be perfect.
verses.textLatin: Postquam vero nonaginta et novem annorum esse cœperat, apparuit ei Dominus, dixitque ad eum: Ego Deus omnipotens: ambula coram me, et esto perfectus.

verses.text: And I will make my covenant between me and thee: and I will multiply thee exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Ponamque fœdus meum inter me et te, et multiplicabo te vehementer nimis.

verses.text: Abram fell flat on his face.
verses.textLatin: Cecidit Abram pronus in faciem.

verses.text: And God said to him: I AM, and my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be a father of many nations.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei Deus: Ego sum, et pactum meum tecum, erisque pater multarum gentium.

verses.text: Neither shall thy name be called any more Abram: but thou shalt be called Abraham: because I have made thee a father of many nations.
verses.textLatin: Nec ultra vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, sed appellaberis Abraham: quia patrem multarum gentium constitui te.

verses.text: And I will make thee increase, exceedingly, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.
verses.textLatin: Faciamque te crescere vehementissime, et ponam te in gentibus, regesque ex te egredientur.

verses.text: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee, and between thy seed after thee in their generations, by a perpetual covenant: to be a God to thee, and to thy seed after thee.
verses.textLatin: Et statuam pactum meum inter me et te, et inter semen tuum post te in generationibus suis, fœdere sempiterno: ut sim Deus tuus, et seminis tui post te.

verses.text: And I will give to thee, and to thy seed, the land of thy sojournment, all the land of Chanaan for a perpetual possession, and I will be their God.
verses.textLatin: Daboque tibi et semini tuo terram peregrinationis tuæ, omnem terram Chanaan in possessionem æternam, eroque Deus eorum.

verses.text: Again God said to Abraham: And thou therefore shalt keep my covenant, and thy seed after thee in their generations.
verses.textLatin: Dixit iterum Deus ad Abraham: Et tu ergo custodies pactum meum, et semen tuum post te in generationibus suis.

verses.text: This is my covenant which you shall observe, between me and you, and thy seed after thee: All the male kind of you shall be circumcised:
verses.textLatin: Hoc est pactum meum quod observabitis inter me et vos, et semen tuum post te: circumcidetur ex vobis omne masculinum:

verses.text: And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, that it may be for a sign of the covenant between me and you.
verses.textLatin: et circumcidetis carnem præputii vestri, ut sit in signum fœderis inter me et vos.

verses.text: An infant of eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations: he that is born in the house, as well as the bought servant shall be circumcised, and whosoever is not of your stock:
verses.textLatin: Infans octo dierum circumcidetur in vobis, omne masculinum in generationibus vestris: tam vernaculus, quam emptitius circumcidetur, et quicumque non fuerit de stirpe vestra:

verses.text: And my covenant shall be in your flesh for a perpetual covenant.
verses.textLatin: eritque pactum meum in carne vestra in fœdus æternum.

verses.text: The male, whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be destroyed out of his people: because he hath broken my covenant.
verses.textLatin: Masculus, cujus præputii caro circumcisa non fuerit, delebitur anima illa de populo suo: quia pactum meum irritum fecit.

verses.text: God said also to Abraham: Sarai thy wife thou shalt not call Sarai, but Sara.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Deus ad Abraham: Sarai uxorem tuam non vocabis Sarai, sed Saram.

verses.text: And I will bless her, and of her I will give thee a son, whom I will bless, and he shall become nations, and kings of people shall spring from him.
verses.textLatin: Et benedicam ei, et ex illa dabo tibi filium cui benedicturus sum: eritque in nationes, et reges populorum orientur ex eo.

verses.text: Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, saying in his heart: Shall a son, thinkest thou, be born to him that is a hundred years old? and shall Sara that is ninety years old bring forth?
verses.textLatin: Cecidit Abraham in faciem suam, et risit, dicens in corde suo: Putasne centenario nascetur filius? et Sara nonagenaria pariet?

verses.text: And he said to God: O that Ismael may live before thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Deum: Utinam Ismaël vivat coram te.

verses.text: And God said to Abraham: Sara thy wife shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name Isaac, and I will establish my covenant with him for a perpetual covenant, and with his seed after him.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Deus ad Abraham: Sara uxor tua pariet tibi filium, vocabisque nomen ejus Isaac, et constituam pactum meum illi in fœdus sempiternum, et semini ejus post eum.

verses.text: And as for Ismael I have also heard thee. Behold, I will bless him, and increase, and multiply him exceedingly: he shall beget twelve chiefs, and I will make him a great nation.
verses.textLatin: Super Ismaël quoque exaudivi te: ecce, benedicam ei, et augebo, et multiplicabo eum valde: duodecim duces generabit, et faciam illum in gentem magnam.

verses.text: But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sara shall bring forth to thee at this time in the next year.
verses.textLatin: Pactum vero meum statuam ad Isaac, quem pariet tibi Sara tempore isto in anno altero.

verses.text: And when he had left off speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.
verses.textLatin: Cumque finitus esset sermo loquentis cum eo, ascendit Deus ab Abraham.

verses.text: And Abraham took Ismael his son, and all that were born in his house: and all whom he had bought, every male among the men of his house: and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin forthwith the very same day, as God had commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Tulit autem Abraham Ismaël filium suum, et omnes vernaculos domus suæ, universosque quos emerat, cunctos mares ex omnibus viris domus suæ: et circumcidit carnem præputii eorum statim in ipsa die, sicut præceperat ei Deus.

verses.text: Abraham was ninety and nine years old, when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
verses.textLatin: Abraham nonaginta et novem erat annorum quando circumcidit carnem præputii sui.

verses.text: And Ismael his son was full thirteen years old at the time of his circumcision.
verses.textLatin: Et Ismaël filius tredecim annos impleverat tempore circumcisionis suæ.

verses.text: The selfsame day was Abraham circumcised and Ismael his son.
verses.textLatin: Eadem die circumcisus est Abraham et Ismaël filius ejus:

verses.text: And all the men of his house, as well they that were born in his house, as the bought servants and strangers were circumcised with him.
verses.textLatin: et omnes viri domus illius, tam vernaculi, quam emptitii et alienigenæ pariter circumcisi sunt.

verses.text: And  the Lord appeared to him in the vale of Mambre as he was sitting at the door of his tent, in the very heat of the day.
verses.textLatin: Apparuit autem ei Dominus in convalle Mambre sedenti in ostio tabernaculi sui in ipso fervore diei.

verses.text: And when he had lifted up his eyes, there appeared to him three men standing near him: and as soon as he saw them he ran to meet them from the door of his tent, and adored down to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevasset oculos, apparuerunt ei tres viri stantes prope eum: quos cum vidisset, cucurrit in occursum eorum de ostio tabernaculi, et adoravit in terram.

verses.text: And he said: Lord, if I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away from thy servant:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Domine, si inveni gratiam in oculis tuis, ne transeas servum tuum:

verses.text: But I will fetch a little water, and wash ye your feet, and rest ye under the tree.
verses.textLatin: sed afferam pauxillum aquæ, et lavate pedes vestros, et requiescite sub arbore.

verses.text: And I will set a morsel of bread, and strengthen ye your heart, afterwards you shall pass on: for therefore are you come aside to your servant. And they said: Do as thou hast spoken.
verses.textLatin: Ponamque buccellam panis, et confortate cor vestrum: postea transibitis: idcirco enim declinastis ad servum vestrum. Qui dixerunt: Fac ut locutus es.

verses.text: Abraham made haste into the tent to Sara, and said to her: Make haste, temper together three measures of flour, and make cakes upon the hearth.
verses.textLatin: Festinavit Abraham in tabernaculum ad Saram, dixitque ei: Accelera, tria sata similæ commisce, et fac subcinericios panes.

verses.text: And he himself ran to the herd, and took from thence a calf very tender and very good, and gave it to a young man: who made haste and boiled it.
verses.textLatin: Ipse vero ad armentum cucurrit, et tulit inde vitulum tenerrimum et optimum, deditque puero: qui festinavit et coxit illum.

verses.text: He took also butter and milk, and the calf which he had boiled, and set before them: but he stood by them under the tree.
verses.textLatin: Tulit quoque butyrum et lac, et vitulum quem coxerat, et posuit coram eis: ipse vero stabat juxta eos sub arbore.

verses.text: And when they had eaten, they said to him: Where is Sara thy wife? He answered: Lo, she is in the tent.
verses.textLatin: Cumque comedissent, dixerunt ad eum: Ubi est Sara uxor tua? Ille respondit: Ecce in tabernaculo est.

verses.text: And he said to him: I will return and come to thee at this time, life accompanying, and Sara thy wife shall have a son. Which when Sara heard, she laughed behind the door of the tent.
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit: Revertens veniam ad te tempore isto, vita comite, et habebit filium Sara uxor tua. Quo audito, Sara risit post ostium tabernaculi.

verses.text: Now they were both old, and far advanced in years, and it had ceased to be with Sara after the manner of women.
verses.textLatin: Erant autem ambo senes, provectæque ætatis, et desierant Saræ fieri muliebria.

verses.text: And she laughed secretly, saying: After I am grown old and my lord is an old man, shall I give myself to pleasure?
verses.textLatin: Quæ risit occulte dicens: Postquam consenui, et dominus meus vetulus est, voluptati operam dabo?

verses.text: And the Lord said to Abraham: Why did Sara laugh, saying: Shall I who am an old woman bear a child indeed?
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Abraham: Quare risit Sara, dicens: Num vere paritura sum anus?

verses.text: Is there any thing hard to God? according to appointment I will return to thee at this same time, life accompanying, and Sara shall have a son.
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deo quidquam est difficile? juxta condictum revertar ad te hoc eodem tempore, vita comite, et habebit Sara filium.

verses.text: Sara denied, saying: I did not laugh: for she was afraid. But the Lord said, Nay: but thou didst laugh:
verses.textLatin: Negavit Sara, dicens: Non risi, timore perterrita. Dominus autem: Non est, inquit, ita: sed risisti.

verses.text: And when the men rose up from thence, they turned their eyes towards Sodom: and Abraham walked with them, bringing them on the way.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo surrexissent inde viri, direxerunt oculos contra Sodomam: et Abraham simul gradiebatur, deducens eos.

verses.text: And the Lord said: Can I hide from Abraham what I am about to do:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus: Num celare potero Abraham quæ gesturus sum:

verses.text: Seeing he shall become a great and mighty nation, and in him all the nations of the earth shall be blessed?
verses.textLatin: cum futurus sit in gentem magnam, ac robustissimam, et benedicendæ sint in illo omnes nationes terræ?

verses.text: For I know that he will command his children, and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord, and do judgment and justice: that for Abraham’s sake the Lord may bring to effect all the things he hath spoken unto him.
verses.textLatin: Scio enim quod præcepturus sit filiis suis, et domui suæ post se ut custodiant viam Domini, et faciant judicium et justitiam: ut adducat Dominus propter Abraham omnia quæ locutus est ad eum.

verses.text: And the Lord said: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrha is multiplied, and their sin is become exceedingly grievous.
verses.textLatin: Dixit itaque Dominus: Clamor Sodomorum et Gomorrhæ multiplicatus est, et peccatum eorum aggravatum est nimis.

verses.text: I will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry that is come to me: or whether it be not so, that I may know.
verses.textLatin: Descendam, et videbo utrum clamorem qui venit ad me, opere compleverint; an non est ita, ut sciam.

verses.text: And they turned themselves from thence, and went their way to Sodom: but Abraham as yet stood before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Converteruntque se inde, et abierunt Sodomam: Abraham vero adhuc stabat coram Domino.

verses.text: And drawing nigh he said: Wilt thou destroy the just with the wicked?
verses.textLatin: Et appropinquans ait: Numquid perdes justum cum impio?

verses.text: If there be fifty just men in the city, shall they perish withal? and wilt thou not spare that place for the sake of the fifty just, if they be therein?
verses.textLatin: si fuerint quinquaginta justi in civitate, peribunt simul? et non parces loco illi propter quinquaginta justos, si fuerint in eo?

verses.text: Far be it from thee to do this thing, and to slay the just with the wicked, and for the just to be in like case as the wicked, this is not beseeming thee: thou who judgest all the earth, wilt not make this judgment.
verses.textLatin: Absit a te ut rem hanc facias, et occidas justum cum impio, fiatque justus sicut impius, non est hoc tuum: qui judicas omnem terram, nequaquam facies judicium hoc.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: If I find in Sodom fifty just within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Si invenero Sodomis quinquaginta justos in medio civitatis, dimittam omni loco propter eos.

verses.text: And Abraham answered, and said: Seeing I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord, whereas I am dust and ashes.
verses.textLatin: Respondensque Abraham, ait: Quia semel cœpi, loquar ad Dominum meum, cum sim pulvis et cinis.

verses.text: What if there be five less than fifty just persons? wilt thou for five and forty destroy the whole city? And he said: I will not destroy it, if I find five and forty.
verses.textLatin: Quid si minus quinquaginta justis quinque fuerint? delebis, propter quadraginta quinque, universam urbem? Et ait: Non delebo, si invenero ibi quadraginta quinque.

verses.text: And again he said to him: But if forty be found there, what wilt thou do? He said: I will not destroy it for the sake of forty.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque locutus est ad eum: Sin autem quadraginta ibi inventi fuerint, quid facies? Ait: Non percutiam propter quadraginta.

verses.text: Lord, saith he, be not angry, I beseech thee, if I speak: What if thirty shall be found there? He answered: I will not do it, if I find thirty there.
verses.textLatin: Ne quæso, inquit, indigneris, Domine, si loquar: quid si ibi inventi fuerint triginta? Respondit: Non faciam, si invenero ibi triginta.

verses.text: Seeing, saith he, I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord. What if twenty be found there? He said: I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.
verses.textLatin: Quia semel, ait, cœpi loquar ad Dominum meum: quid si ibi inventi fuerint viginti? Ait: Non interficiam propter viginti.

verses.text: I beseech thee, saith he, be not angry, Lord, if I speak yet once more: What if ten should be found there? And he said: I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.
verses.textLatin: Obsecro, inquit, ne irascaris, Domine, si loquar adhuc semel: quid si inventi fuerint ibi decem? Et dixit: Non delebo propter decem.

verses.text: And the Lord departed, after he had left speaking to Abraham: and Abraham returned to his place.
verses.textLatin: Abiitque Dominus, postquam cessavit loqui ad Abraham: et ille reversus est in locum suum.

verses.text: And  the two angels came to Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gate of the city. And seeing them, he rose up and went to meet them: and worshipped prostrate to the ground,
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque duo angeli Sodomam vespere, et sedente Lot in foribus civitatis. Qui cum vidisset eos, surrexit, et ivit obviam eis: adoravitque pronus in terram,

verses.text: And said: I beseech you, my lords, turn in to the house of your servant, and lodge there: wash your feet, and in the morning you shall go on your way. And they said: No, but we will abide in the street.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Obsecro, domini, declinate in domum pueri vestri, et manete ibi: lavate pedes vestros, et mane proficiscemini in viam vestram. Qui dixerunt: Minime, sed in platea manebimus.

verses.text: He pressed them very much to turn in unto him: and when they were come in to his house, he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread and they ate:
verses.textLatin: Compulit illos oppido ut diverterent ad eum: ingressisque domum illius fecit convivium, et coxit azyma, et comederunt.

verses.text: But before they went to bed, the men of the city beset the house both young and old, all the people together.
verses.textLatin: Prius autem quam irent cubitum, viri civitatis vallaverunt domum a puero usque ad senem, omnis populus simul.

verses.text: And they called Lot, and said to him: Where are the men that came in to thee at night? bring them out hither that we may know them:
verses.textLatin: Vocaveruntque Lot, et dixerunt ei: Ubi sunt viri qui introierunt ad te nocte? educ illos huc, ut cognoscamus eos.

verses.text: Lot went out to them, and shut the door after him, and said:
verses.textLatin: Egressus ad eos Lot, post tergum occludens ostium, ait:

verses.text: Do not so, I beseech you, my brethren, do not commit this evil.
verses.textLatin: Nolite, quæso, fratres mei, nolite malum hoc facere.

verses.text: I have two daughters who as yet have not known man: I will bring them out to you, and abuse you them as it shall please you, so that you do no evil to these men, because they are come in under the shadow of my roof.
verses.textLatin: Habeo duas filias, quæ necdum cognoverunt virum: educam eas ad vos, et abutimini eis sicut vobis placuerit, dummodo viris istis nihil mali faciatis, quia ingressi sunt sub umbra culminis mei.

verses.text: But they said: Get thee back thither. And again: Thou camest in, said they, as a stranger, was it to be a judge? therefore we will afflict thee more than them. And they pressed very violently upon Lot: and they were even at the point of breaking open the doors.
verses.textLatin: At illi dixerunt: Recede illuc. Et rursus: Ingressus es, inquiunt, ut advena; numquid ut judices? te ergo ipsum magis quam hos affligemus. Vimque faciebant Lot vehementissime: jamque prope erat ut effringerent fores.

verses.text: And behold the men put out their hand, and drew in Lot unto them, and shut the door:
verses.textLatin: Et ecce miserunt manum viri, et introduxerunt ad se Lot, clauseruntque ostium:

verses.text: And them that were without, they struck with blindness from the least to the greatest, so that they could not find the door.
verses.textLatin: et eos, qui foris erant, percusserunt cæcitate a minimo usque ad maximum, ita ut ostium invenire non possent.

verses.text: And they said to Lot: Hast thou here any of thine? son in law, or sons, or daughters, all that are thine bring them out of this city:
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt autem ad Lot: Habes hic quempiam tuorum? generum, aut filios, aut filias, omnes, qui tui sunt, educ de urbe hac:

verses.text: For we will destroy this place, because their cry is grown loud before the Lord, who hath sent us to destroy them.
verses.textLatin: delebimus enim locum istum, eo quod increverit clamor eorum coram Domino, qui misit nos ut perdamus illos.

verses.text: So Lot went out, and spoke to his sons in law that were to have his daughters, and said: Arise: get you out of this place, because the Lord will destroy this city. And he seemed to them to speak as it were in jest.
verses.textLatin: Egressus itaque Lot, locutus est ad generos suos qui accepturi erant filias ejus, et dixit: Surgite, egredimini de loco isto: quia delebit Dominus civitatem hanc. Et visus est eis quasi ludens loqui.

verses.text: And when it was morning, the angels pressed him, saying: Arise, take thy wife, and the two daughters which thou hast: lest thou also perish in the wickedness of the city.
verses.textLatin: Cumque esset mane, cogebant eum angeli, dicentes: Surge, tolle uxorem tuam, et duas filias quas habes: ne et tu pariter pereas in scelere civitatis.

verses.text: And as he lingered, they took his hand, and the hand of his wife, and of his two daughters, because the Lord spared him.
verses.textLatin: Dissimulante illo, apprehenderunt manum ejus, et manum uxoris, ac duarum filiarum ejus, eo quod parceret Dominus illi.

verses.text: And they brought him forth, and set him without the city: and there they spoke to him, saying: Save thy life: look not back, neither stay thou in all the country about: but save thyself in the mountain, lest thou be also consumed.
verses.textLatin: Eduxeruntque eum, et posuerunt extra civitatem: ibique locuti sunt ad eum, dicentes: Salva animam tuam: noli respicere post tergum, nec stes in omni circa regione: sed in monte salvum te fac, ne et tu simul pereas.

verses.text: And Lot said to them: I beseech thee my Lord,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Lot ad eos: Quæso, domine mi,

verses.text: Because thy servant hath found grace before thee, and thou hast magnified thy mercy, which thou hast shewn to me, in saving my life, and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest some evil seize me, and I die:
verses.textLatin: quia invenit servus tuus gratiam coram te, et magnificasti misericordiam tuam quam fecisti mecum, ut salvares animam meam, nec possum in monte salvari, ne forte apprehendat me malum, et moriar:

verses.text: There is this city here at hand, to which I may flee, it is a little one, and I shall be saved in it: is it not a little one, and my soul shall live?
verses.textLatin: est civitas hæc juxta, ad quam possum fugere, parva, et salvabor in ea: numquid non modica est, et vivet anima mea?

verses.text: And he said to him: Behold also in this, I have heard thy prayers, not to destroy the city for which thou hast spoken.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eum: Ecce etiam in hoc suscepi preces tuas, ut non subvertam urbem pro qua locutus es.

verses.text: Make haste and be saved there, because I cannot do any thing till thou go in thither. Therefore the name of that city was called Segor.
verses.textLatin: Festina, et salvare ibi: quia non potero facere quidquam donec ingrediaris illuc. Idcirco vocatum est nomen urbis illius Segor.

verses.text: The sun was risen upon the earth, and Lot entered into Segor.
verses.textLatin: Sol egressus est super terram, et Lot ingressus est Segor.

verses.text: And the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord out of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Dominus pluit super Sodomam et Gomorrham sulphur et ignem a Domino de cælo:

verses.text: And he destroyed these cities, and all the country about, all the inhabitants of the cities, and all things that spring from the earth.
verses.textLatin: et subvertit civitates has, et omnem circa regionem, universos habitatores urbium, et cuncta terræ virentia.

verses.text: And his wife looking behind her, was turned into a statue of salt.
verses.textLatin: Respiciensque uxor ejus post se, versa est in statuam salis.

verses.text: And Abraham got up early in the morning, and in the place where he had stood before with the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Abraham autem consurgens mane, ubi steterat prius cum Domino,

verses.text: He looked towards Sodom and Gomorrha, and the whole land of that country: and he saw the ashes rise up from the earth as the smoke of a furnace.
verses.textLatin: intuitus est Sodomam et Gomorrham, et universam terram regionis illius: viditque ascendentem favillam de terra quasi fornacis fumum.

verses.text: Now when God destroyed the cities of that country, remembering Abraham, he delivered Lot out of the destruction of the cities wherein he had dwelt.
verses.textLatin: Cum enim subverteret Deus civitates regionis illius, recordatus Abrahæ, liberavit Lot de subversione urbium in quibus habitaverat.

verses.text: And Lot went up out of Segor, and abode in the mountain, and his two daughters with him, (for he was afraid to stay in Segor,) and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters with him.
verses.textLatin: Ascenditque Lot de Segor, et mansit in monte, duæ quoque filiæ ejus cum eo (timuerat enim manere in Segor) et mansit in spelunca ipse, et duæ filiæ ejus cum eo.

verses.text: And the elder said to the younger: Our father is old, and there is no man left on the earth, to come in unto us after the manner of the whole earth.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque major ad minorem: Pater noster senex est, et nullus virorum remansit in terra, qui possit ingredi ad nos juxta morem universæ terræ.

verses.text: Come, let us make him drunk with wine, and let us lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.
verses.textLatin: Veni, inebriemus eum vino, dormiamusque cum eo, ut servare possimus ex patre nostro semen.

verses.text: And they made their father drink wine that night: and the elder went in and lay with her father: but he perceived not neither when his daughter lay down, nor when she rose up.
verses.textLatin: Dederunt itaque patri suo bibere vinum nocte illa. Et ingressa est major, dormivitque cum patre; at ille non sensit, nec quando accubuit filia, nec quando surrexit.

verses.text: And the next day the elder said to the younger: Behold I lay last night with my father, let us make him drink wine also to night, and thou shalt lie with him, that we may save seed of our father.
verses.textLatin: Altera quoque die dixit major ad minorem: Ecce dormivi heri cum patre meo, demus ei bibere vinum etiam hac nocte, et dormies cum eo, ut salvemus semen de patre nostro.

verses.text: They made their father drink wine that night also, and the younger daughter went in, and lay with him: and neither then did he perceive when she lay down, nor when she rose up.
verses.textLatin: Dederunt etiam et illa nocte patri suo bibere vinum, ingressaque minor filia, dormivit cum eo: et ne tunc quidem sensit quando concubuerit, vel quando illa surrexerit.

verses.text: So the two daughters of Lot were with child by their father.
verses.textLatin: Conceperunt ergo duæ filiæ Lot de patre suo.

verses.text: And the elder bore a son, and she called his name Moab: he is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
verses.textLatin: Peperitque major filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Moab: ipse est pater Moabitarum usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: The younger also bore a son, and she called his name Ammon, that is, the son of my people: he is the father of the Ammonites unto this day.
verses.textLatin: Minor quoque peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Ammon, id est, Filius populi mei: ipse est pater Ammonitarum usque hodie.

verses.text: Abraham  removed from thence to the south country, and dwelt between Cades and Sur, and sojourned in Gerara.
verses.textLatin: Profectus inde Abraham in terram australem, habitavit inter Cades et Sur: et peregrinatus est in Geraris.

verses.text: And he said of Sara his wife: She is my sister. So Abimelech the king of Gerara sent, and took her.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque de Sara uxore suo: Soror mea est. Misit ergo Abimelech rex Geraræ, et tulit eam.

verses.text: And God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and he said to him: Lo thou shalt die for the woman thou hast taken: for she hath a husband.
verses.textLatin: Venit autem Deus ad Abimelech per somnium nocte, et ait illi: En morieris propter mulierem quam tulisti: habet enim virum.

verses.text: Now Abimelech had not touched her, and he said: Lord, wilt thou slay a nation, that is ignorant and just?
verses.textLatin: Abimelech vero non tetigerat eam, et ait: Domine, num gentem ignorantem et justam interficies?

verses.text: Did not he say to me: She is my sister: and she say, He is my brother? in the simplicity of my heart, and cleanness of my hands have I done this.
verses.textLatin: nonne ipse dixit mihi: Soror mea est: et ipsa ait: Frater meus est? In simplicitate cordis mei, et munditia manuum mearum feci hoc.

verses.text: And God said to him: And I know that thou didst it with a sincere heart: and therefore I withheld thee from sinning against me, and I suffered thee not to touch her.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eum Deus: Et ego scio quod simplici corde feceris: et ideo custodivi te ne peccares in me, et non dimisi ut tangeres eam.

verses.text: Now therefore restore the man his wife, for he is a prophet: and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: but if thou wilt not restore her, know that thou shalt surely die, thou and all that are thine.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo redde viro suo uxorem, quia propheta est: et orabit pro te, et vives: si autem nolueris reddere, scito quod morte morieris tu, et omnia quæ tua sunt.

verses.text: And Abimelech forthwith rising up in the night, called all his servants: and spoke all these words in their hearing, and all the men were exceedingly afraid.
verses.textLatin: Statimque de nocte consurgens Abimelech, vocavit omnes servos suos: et locutus est universa verba hæc in auribus eorum, timueruntque omnes viri valde.

verses.text: And Abimelech called also for Abraham, and said to him: What hast thou done to us? what have we offended thee in, that thou hast brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done to us what thou oughtest not to do.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem Abimelech etiam Abraham, et dixit ei: Quid fecisti nobis? quid peccavimus in te, quia induxisti super me et super regnum meum peccatum grande? quæ non debuisti facere, fecisti nobis.

verses.text: And again he expostulated with him, and said, What sawest thou, that thou hast done this?
verses.textLatin: Rursumque expostulans, ait: Quid vidisti, ut hoc faceres?

verses.text: Abraham answered: I thought with myself, saying: Perhaps there is not the fear of God in this place: and they will kill me for the sake of my wife:
verses.textLatin: Respondit Abraham: Cogitavi mecum, dicens: Forsitan non est timor Dei in loco isto: et interficient me propter uxorem meam:

verses.text: Howbeit, otherwise also she is truly my sister, the daughter of my father, and not the daughter of my mother, and I took her to wife.
verses.textLatin: alias autem et vere soror mea est, filia patris mei, et non filia matris meæ, et duxi eam in uxorem.

verses.text: And after God brought me out of my father’s house, I said to her: Thou shalt do me this kindness: In every place, to which we shall come, thou shalt say that I am thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem eduxit me Deus de domo patris mei, dixi ad eam: Hanc misericordiam facies mecum: in omni loco, ad quem ingrediemur, dices quod frater tuus sim.

verses.text: And Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and gave to Abraham: and restored to him Sara, his wife.
verses.textLatin: Tulit igitur Abimelech oves et boves, et servos et ancillas, et dedit Abraham: reddiditque illi Saram uxorem suam,

verses.text: And said: The land is before you, dwell wheresoever it shall please thee.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Terra coram vobis est, ubicumque tibi placuerit habita.

verses.text: And to Sara he said: Behold I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: this shall serve thee for a covering of thy eyes to all that are with thee, and whithersoever thou shalt go: and remember thou wast taken.
verses.textLatin: Saræ autem dixit: Ecce mille argenteos dedi fratri tuo, hoc erit tibi in velamen oculorum ad omnes qui tecum sunt, et quocumque perrexeris: mementoque te deprehensam.

verses.text: And when Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bore children:
verses.textLatin: Orante autem Abraham, sanavit Deus Abimelech et uxorem, ancillasque ejus, et pepererunt:

verses.text: For the Lord had closed up every womb of the house of Abimelech on account of Sara, Abraham’s wife.
verses.textLatin: concluserat enim Dominus omnem vulvam domus Abimelech propter Saram uxorem Abrahæ.

verses.text: And  the Lord visited Sara, as he had promised: and fulfilled what he had spoken.
verses.textLatin: Visitavit autem Dominus Saram, sicut promiserat: et implevit quæ locutus est.

verses.text: And she conceived and bore a son in her old age, at the time that God had foretold her.
verses.textLatin: Concepitque et peperit filium in senectute sua, tempore quo prædixerat ei Deus.

verses.text: And Abraham called the name of his son, whom Sara bore him, Isaac.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Abraham nomen filii sui, quem genuit ei Sara, Isaac:

verses.text: And he circumcised him the eighth day, as God had commanded him,
verses.textLatin: et circumcidit eum octavo die, sicut præceperat ei Deus,

verses.text: When he was a hundred years old: for at this age of his father was Isaac born.
verses.textLatin: cum centum esset annorum: hac quippe ætate patris, natus est Isaac.

verses.text: And Sara said: God hath made a laughter for me: whosoever shall hear of it will laugh with me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Sara: Risum fecit mihi Deus: quicumque audierit, corridebit mihi.

verses.text: And again she said: Who would believe that Abraham should hear that Sara gave suck to a son, whom she bore to him in his old age.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque ait: Quis auditurus crederet Abraham quod Sara lactaret filium, quem peperit ei jam seni?

verses.text: And the child grew and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast on the day of his weaning.
verses.textLatin: Crevit igitur puer, et ablactatus est: fecitque Abraham grande convivium in die ablactationis ejus.

verses.text: And when Sara had seen the son of Agar the Egyptian playing with Isaac her son, she said to Abraham:
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset Sara filium Agar Ægyptiæ ludentem cum Isaac filio suo, dixit ad Abraham:

verses.text: Cast out this bondwoman, and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.
verses.textLatin: Ejice ancillam hanc, et filium ejus: non enim erit hæres filius ancillæ cum filio meo Isaac.

verses.text: Abraham took this grievously for his son.
verses.textLatin: Dure accepit hoc Abraham pro filio suo.

verses.text: And God said to him: Let it not seem grievous to thee for the boy, and for thy bondwoman: in all that Sara hath said to thee, hearken to her voice: for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit Deus: Non tibi videatur asperum super puero, et super ancilla tua: omnia quæ dixerit tibi Sara, audi vocem ejus: quia in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen.

verses.text: But I will make the son also of the bondwoman a great nation, because he is thy seed.
verses.textLatin: Sed et filium ancillæ faciam in gentem magnam, quia semen tuum est.

verses.text: So Abraham rose up in the morning, and taking bread and a bottle of water, put it upon her shoulder, and delivered the boy, and sent her away. And she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Bersabee.
verses.textLatin: Surrexit itaque Abraham mane, et tollens panem et utrem aquæ, imposuit scapulæ ejus, tradiditque puerum, et dimisit eam. Quæ cum abiisset, errabat in solitudine Bersabee.

verses.text: And when the water in the bottle was spent, she cast the boy under one of the trees that were there.
verses.textLatin: Cumque consumpta esset aqua in utre, abjecit puerum subter unam arborum, quæ ibi erant.

verses.text: And she went her way, and sat over against him a great way off as far as a bow can carry, for she said: I will not see the boy die: and sitting over against, she lifted up her voice and wept.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit, seditque e regione procul quantum potest arcus jacere: dixit enim: Non videbo morientem puerum: et sedens contra, levavit vocem suam et flevit.

verses.text: And God heard the voice of the boy: and an angel of God called to Agar from heaven, saying: What art thou doing, Agar? fear not: for God hath heard the voice of the boy, from the place wherein he is.
verses.textLatin: Exaudivit autem Deus vocem pueri: vocavitque angelus Dei Agar de cælo, dicens: Quid agis Agar? noli timere: exaudivit enim Deus vocem pueri de loco in quo est.

verses.text: Arise, take up the boy, and hold him by the hand: for I will make him a great nation.
verses.textLatin: Surge, tolle puerum, et tene manum illius: quia in gentem magnam faciam eum.

verses.text: And God opened her eyes: and she saw a well of water, and went and filled the bottle, and gave the boy to drink.
verses.textLatin: Aperuitque oculos ejus Deus: quæ videns puteum aquæ, abiit, et implevit utrem, deditque puero bibere.

verses.text: And God was with him: and he grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became a young man, an archer.
verses.textLatin: Et fuit cum eo: qui crevit, et moratus est in solitudine, factusque est juvenis sagittarius.

verses.text: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Pharan, and his mother took a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Habitavitque in deserto Pharan, et accepit illi mater sua uxorem de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: At the same time Abimelech, and Phicol the general of his army said to Abraham: God is with thee in all that thou dost.
verses.textLatin: Eodem tempore dixit Abimelech, et Phicol princeps exercitus ejus, ad Abraham: Deus tecum est in universis quæ agis.

verses.text: Swear therefore by God, that thou wilt not hurt me, nor my posterity, nor my stock: but according to the kindness that I have done to thee, thou shalt do to me, and to the land wherein thou hast lived a stranger.
verses.textLatin: Jura ergo per Deum, ne noceas mihi, et posteris meis, stirpique meæ: sed juxta misericordiam, quam feci tibi, facies mihi, et terræ in qua versatus es advena.

verses.text: And Abraham said: I will swear.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Abraham: Ego jurabo.

verses.text: And he reproved Abimelech for a well of water, which his servants had taken away by force.
verses.textLatin: Et increpavit Abimelech propter puteum aquæ quem vi abstulerunt servi ejus.

verses.text: And Abimelech answered: I knew not who did this thing: and thou didst not tell me, and I heard not of it till to day.
verses.textLatin: Responditque Abimelech: Nescivi quis fecerit hanc rem: sed et tu non indicasti mihi, et ego non audivi præter hodie.

verses.text: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them to Abimelech: and both of them made a league.
verses.textLatin: Tulit itaque Abraham oves et boves, et dedit Abimelech: percusseruntque ambo fœdus.

verses.text: And Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs of the flock.
verses.textLatin: Et statuit Abraham septem agnas gregis seorsum.

verses.text: And Abimelech said to him: What mean these seven ewe lambs which thou hast set apart?
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit Abimelech: Quid sibi volunt septem agnæ istæ, quas stare fecisti seorsum?

verses.text: But he said: Thou shalt take seven ewe lambs at my hand: that they may be a testimony for me, that I dug this well.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Septem, inquit, agnas accipies de manu mea: ut sint mihi in testimonium, quoniam ego fodi puteum istum.

verses.text: Therefore that place was called Bersabee: because there both of them did swear.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco vocatus est locus ille Bersabee: quia ibi uterque juravit.

verses.text: And they made a league for the well of oath.
verses.textLatin: Et inierunt fœdus pro puteo juramenti.

verses.text: And Abimelech, and Phicol the general of his army arose and returned to the land of the Palestines. But Abraham planted a grove in Bersabee, and there called upon the name of the Lord God eternal.
verses.textLatin: Surrexit autem Abimelech, et Phicol princeps exercitus ejus, reversique sunt in terram Palæstinorum. Abraham vero plantavit nemus in Bersabee, et invocavit ibi nomen Domini Dei æterni.

verses.text: And he was a sojourner in the land of the Palestines many days.
verses.textLatin: Et fuit colonus terræ Palæstinorum diebus multis.

verses.text: After  these things, God tempted Abraham, and said to him: Abraham, Abraham. And he answered: Here I am.
verses.textLatin: Quæ postquam gesta sunt, tentavit Deus Abraham, et dixit ad eum: Abraham, Abraham. At ille respondit: Adsum.

verses.text: He said to him: Take thy only begotten son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and go into the land of vision: and there thou shalt offer him for an holocaust upon one of the mountains which I will shew thee.
verses.textLatin: Ait illi: Tolle filium tuum unigenitum, quem diligis, Isaac, et vade in terram visionis, atque ibi offeres eum in holocaustum super unum montium quem monstravero tibi.

verses.text: So Abraham rising up in the night, saddled his ass: and took with him two young men, and Isaac his son: and when he had cut wood for the holocaust he went his way to the place which God had commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Abraham de nocte consurgens, stravit asinum suum, ducens secum duos juvenes, et Isaac filium suum: cumque concidisset ligna in holocaustum, abiit ad locum quem præceperat ei Deus.

verses.text: And on the third day, lifting up his eyes, he saw the place afar off.
verses.textLatin: Die autem tertio, elevatis oculis, vidit locum procul:

verses.text: And he said to his young men: Stay you here with the ass: I and the boy will go with speed as far as yonder, and after we have worshipped, will return to you.
verses.textLatin: dixitque ad pueros suos: Expectate hic cum asino: ego et puer illuc usque properantes, postquam adoraverimus, revertemur ad vos.

verses.text: And he took the wood for the holocaust, and laid it upon Isaac his son: and he himself carried in his hands fire and a sword. And as they two went on together,
verses.textLatin: Tulit quoque ligna holocausti, et imposuit super Isaac filium suum: ipse vero portabat in manibus ignem et gladium. Cumque duo pergerent simul,

verses.text: Isaac said to his father: My father. And he answered: What wilt thou, son? Behold, saith he, fire and wood: where is the victim for the holocaust?
verses.textLatin: dixit Isaac patri suo: Pater mi. At ille respondit: Quid vis, fili? Ecce, inquit, ignis et ligna: ubi est victima holocausti?

verses.text: And Abraham said: God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust, my son. So they went on together.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Abraham: Deus providebit sibi victimam holocausti, fili mi. Pergebant ergo pariter.

verses.text: And they came to the place which God had shewn him, where he built an altar, and laid the wood in order upon it: and when he had bound Isaac his son, he laid him on the altar upon the pile of wood.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt ad locum quem ostenderat ei Deus, in quo ædificavit altare, et desuper ligna composuit; cumque alligasset Isaac filium suum, posuit eum in altare super struem lignorum.

verses.text: And he put forth his hand and took the sword, to sacrifice his son.
verses.textLatin: Extenditque manum, et arripuit gladium, ut immolaret filium suum.

verses.text: And behold an angel of the Lord from heaven called to him, saying: Abraham, Abraham. And he answered: Here I am.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce angelus Domini de cælo clamavit, dicens: Abraham, Abraham. Qui respondit: Adsum.

verses.text: And he said to him: Lay not thy hand upon the boy, neither do thou any thing to him: now I know that thou fearest God, and hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei: Non extendas manum tuam super puerum, neque facias illi quidquam: nunc cognovi quod times Deum, et non pepercisti unigenito filio tuo propter me.

verses.text: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw behind his back a ram amongst the briers sticking fast by the horns, which he took and offered for a holocaust instead of his son.
verses.textLatin: Levavit Abraham oculos suos, viditque post tergum arietem inter vepres hærentem cornibus, quem assumens obtulit holocaustum pro filio.

verses.text: And he called the name of that place, The Lord seeth. Whereupon even to this day it is said: In the mountain the Lord will see.
verses.textLatin: Appellavitque nomen loci illius, Dominus videt. Unde usque hodie dicitur: In monte Dominus videbit.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord called to Abraham a second time from heaven, saying:
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem angelus Domini Abraham secundo de cælo, dicens:

verses.text: By my own self have I sworn, saith the Lord: because thou hast done this thing, and hast not spared thy only begotten son for my sake:
verses.textLatin: Per memetipsum juravi, dicit Dominus: quia fecisti hanc rem, et non pepercisti filio tuo unigenito propter me:

verses.text: I will bless thee, and I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand that is by the sea shore: thy seed shall possess the gates of their enemies.
verses.textLatin: benedicam tibi, et multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas cæli, et velut arenam quæ est in littore maris: possidebit semen tuum portas inimicorum suorum,

verses.text: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because thou hast obeyed my voice.
verses.textLatin: et benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ, quia obedisti voci meæ.

verses.text: Abraham returned to his young men, and they went to Bersabee together, and he dwelt there.
verses.textLatin: Reversus est Abraham ad pueros suos, abieruntque Bersabee simul, et habitavit ibi.

verses.text: After these things, it was told Abraham that Melcha also had borne children to Nachor his brother.
verses.textLatin: His ita gestis, nuntiatum est Abrahæ quod Melcha quoque genuisset filios Nachor fratri suo:

verses.text: Hus the firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Camuel the father of the Syrians,
verses.textLatin: Hus primogenitum, et Buz fratrem ejus, et Camuel patrem Syrorum,

verses.text: And Cased, and Azau, and Pheldas, and Jedlaph,
verses.textLatin: et Cased, et Azau, Pheldas quoque et Jedlaph,

verses.text: And Bathuel, of whom was born Rebecca: These eight did Melcha bear to Nachor Abraham’s brother.
verses.textLatin: ac Bathuel, de quo nata est Rebecca: octo istos genuit Melcha, Nachor fratri Abrahæ.

verses.text: And his concubine, named Roma, bore Tabee, and Gaham, and Tahas, and Maacha.
verses.textLatin: Concubina vero illius, nomine Roma, peperit Tabee, et Gaham, et Thahas, et Maacha.

verses.text: And  Sara lived a hundred and twenty-seven years.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Sara centum viginti septem annis.

verses.text: And she died in the city of Arbee which is Hebron, in the land of Chanaan: and Abraham came to mourn and weep for her.
verses.textLatin: Et mortua est in civitate Arbee, quæ est Hebron, in terra Chanaan: venitque Abraham ut plangeret et fleret eam.

verses.text: And after he rose up from the funeral obsequies, he spoke to the children of Heth, saying:
verses.textLatin: Cumque surrexisset ab officio funeris, locutus est ad filios Heth, dicens:

verses.text: I am a stranger and sojourner among you: give me the right of a burying place with you, that I may bury my dead.
verses.textLatin: Advena sum et peregrinus apud vos: date mihi jus sepulchri vobiscum, ut sepeliam mortuum meum.

verses.text: The children of Heth answered, saying:
verses.textLatin: Responderunt filii Heth, dicentes:

verses.text: My Lord, hear us, thou art a prince of God among us: bury thy dead in our principal sepulchres: and no man shall have power to hinder thee from burying thy dead in his sepulchre.
verses.textLatin: Audi nos, domine: princeps Dei es apud nos: in electis sepulchris nostris sepeli mortuum tuum, nullusque te prohibere poterit quin in monumento ejus sepelias mortuum tuum.

verses.text: Abraham rose up, and bowed down to the people of the land, to wit the children of Heth:
verses.textLatin: Surrexit Abraham, et adoravit populum terræ, filios videlicet Heth:

verses.text: And said to them: If it please your soul that I should bury my dead, hear me, and intercede for me to Ephron the son of Seor.
verses.textLatin: dixitque ad eos: Si placet animæ vestræ ut sepeliam mortuum meum, audite me, et intercedite pro me apud Ephron filium Seor:

verses.text: That he may give me the double cave, which he hath in the end of his field: for as much money as it is worth he shall give it me before you, for a possession of a buryingplace.
verses.textLatin: ut det mihi speluncam duplicem, quam habet in extrema parte agri sui: pecunia digna tradat eam mihi coram vobis in possessionem sepulchri.

verses.text: Now Ephron dwelt in the midst of the children of Heth. And Ephron made answer to Abraham in the hearing of all that went in at the gate of the city, saying:
verses.textLatin: Habitabat autem Ephron in medio filiorum Heth. Responditque Ephron ad Abraham, cunctis audientibus qui ingrediebantur portam civitatis illius, dicens:

verses.text: Let it not be so, my lord, but do thou rather hearken to what I say: The field I deliver to thee, and the cave that is therein, in the presence of the children of my people, bury thy dead.
verses.textLatin: Nequaquam ita fiat, domine mi, sed tu magis ausculta quod loquor. Agrum trado tibi, et speluncam quæ in eo est, præsentibus filiis populi mei; sepeli mortuum tuum.

verses.text: Abraham bowed down before the people of the land,
verses.textLatin: Adoravit Abraham coram populo terræ.

verses.text: And he spoke to Ephron, in the presence of the people: I beseech thee to hear me: I will give money for the field: take it, and so I will bury my dead in it.
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est ad Ephron circumstante plebe: Quæso ut audias me: dabo pecuniam pro agro: suscipe eam, et sic sepeliam mortuum meum in eo.

verses.text: And Ephron answered:
verses.textLatin: Responditque Ephron:

verses.text: My lord, hear me. The ground which thou desirest, is worth four hundred sicles of silver: this is the price between me and thee: but what is this? bury thy dead.
verses.textLatin: Domine mi, audi me: terra, quam postulas, quadringentis siclis argenti valet: istud est pretium inter me et te: sed quantum est hoc? sepeli mortuum tuum.

verses.text: And when Abraham had heard this, he weighed out the money that Ephron had asked, in the hearing of the children of Heth, four hundred sicles of silver of common current money.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Abraham, appendit pecuniam, quam Ephron postulaverat, audientibus filiis Heth, quadringentos siclos argenti probatæ monetæ publicæ.

verses.text: And the field that before was Ephron’s, wherein was the double cave, looking towards Mambre, both it and the cave, and all the trees thereof in all its limits round about,
verses.textLatin: Confirmatusque est ager quondam Ephronis, in quo erat spelunca duplex, respiciens Mambre, tam ipse, quam spelunca, et omnes arbores ejus in cunctis terminis ejus per circuitum,

verses.text: Was made sure to Abraham for a possession, in the sight of the children of Heth, and of all that went in at the gate of his city.
verses.textLatin: Abrahæ in possessionem, videntibus filiis Heth, et cunctis qui intrabant portam civitatis illius.

verses.text: And so Abraham buried Sara his wife, in a double cave of the field, that looked towards Mambre, this is Hebron in the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Atque ita sepelivit Abraham Saram uxorem suam in spelunca agri duplici, quæ respiciebat Mambre. Hæc est Hebron in terra Chanaan.

verses.text: And the field was made sure to Abraham, and the cave that was in it, for a possession to bury in, by the children of Heth.
verses.textLatin: Et confirmatus est ager, et antrum quod erat in eo, Abrahæ in possessionem monumenti a filiis Heth.

verses.text: Now  Abraham was old; and advanced in age: and the Lord had blessed him in all things.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Abraham senex, dierumque multorum: et Dominus in cunctis benedixerat ei.

verses.text: And he said to the elder servant of his house, who was ruler over all he had: Put thy hand under my thigh,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad servum seniorem domus suæ, qui præerat omnibus quæ habebat: Pone manum tuam subter femur meum,

verses.text: That I may make thee swear by the Lord the God of heaven and earth, that thou take not a wife for my son, of the daughters of the Chanaanites, among whom I dwell:
verses.textLatin: ut adjurem te per Dominum Deum cæli et terræ, ut non accipias uxorem filio meo de filiabus Chananæorum, inter quos habito:

verses.text: But that thou go to my own country and kindred, and take a wife from thence for my son Isaac.
verses.textLatin: sed ad terram et cognationem meam proficiscaris et inde accipias uxorem filio meo Isaac.

verses.text: The servant answered: If the woman will not come with me into this land, must I bring thy son back again to the place, from whence thou camest out?
verses.textLatin: Respondit servus: Si noluerit mulier venire mecum in terram hanc, numquid reducere debeo filium tuum ad locum, de quo egressus es?

verses.text: And Abraham said: Beware thou never bring my son back again thither.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Abraham: Cave nequando reducas filium meum illuc.

verses.text: The Lord God of heaven, who took me out of my father’s house, and out of my native country, who spoke to me, and swore to me, saying: To thy seed will I give this land: he will send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take from thence a wife for my son.
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus cæli, qui tulit me de domo patris mei, et de terra nativitatis meæ, qui locutus est mihi, et juravit mihi, dicens: Semini tuo dabo terram hanc: ipse mittet angelum suum coram te, et accipies inde uxorem filio meo:

verses.text: But if the woman will not follow thee, thou shalt not be bound by the oath; only bring not my son back thither again.
verses.textLatin: sin autem mulier noluerit sequi te, non teneberis juramento: filium meum tantum ne reducas illuc.

verses.text: The servant therefore put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord, and swore to him upon his word.
verses.textLatin: Posuit ergo servus manum sub femore Abraham domini sui, et juravit illi super sermone hoc.

verses.text: And he took ten camels of his master’s herd, and departed, carrying something of all his goods with him, and he set forward and went on to Mesopotamia to the city of Nachor.
verses.textLatin: Tulitque decem camelos de grege domini sui, et abiit, ex omnibus bonis ejus portans secum, profectusque perrexit in Mesopotamiam ad urbem Nachor.

verses.text: And when he had made the camels lie down without the town near a well of water in the evening, at the time when women are wont to come out to draw water, he said:
verses.textLatin: Cumque camelos fecisset accumbere extra oppidum juxta puteum aquæ vespere, tempore quo solent mulieres egredi ad hauriendam aquam, dixit:

verses.text: O Lord the God of my master Abraham, meet me to day, I beseech thee, and shew kindness to my master Abraham.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus domini mei Abraham, occurre, obsecro, mihi hodie, et fac misericordiam cum domino meo Abraham.

verses.text: Behold I stand nigh the spring of water, and the daughters of the inhabitants of this city will come out to draw water.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego sto prope fontem aquæ, et filiæ habitatorum hujus civitatis egredientur ad hauriendam aquam.

verses.text: Now, therefore, the maid to whom I shall say: Let down thy pitcher that I may drink: and she shall answer, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let it be the same whom thou hast provided for thy servant Isaac: and by this I shall understand, that thou hast shewn kindness to my master.
verses.textLatin: Igitur puella, cui ego dixero: Inclina hydriam tuam ut bibam: et illa responderit: Bibe, quin et camelis tuis dabo potum: ipsa est quam præparasti servo tuo Isaac: et per hoc intelligam quod feceris misericordiam cum domino meo.

verses.text: He had not yet ended these words within himself, and behold Rebecca came out, the daughter of Bathuel, son of Melcha, wife to Nachor the brother of Abraham, having a pitcher on her shoulder:
verses.textLatin: Necdum intra se verba compleverat, et ecce Rebecca egrediebatur, filia Bathuel, filii Melchæ uxoris Nachor fratris Abraham, habens hydriam in scapula sua:

verses.text: An exceeding comely maid, and a most beautiful virgin, and not known to man: and she went down to the spring, and filled her pitcher and was coming back.
verses.textLatin: puella decora nimis, virgoque pulcherrima, et incognita viro: descenderat autem ad fontem, et impleverat hydriam, ac revertebatur.

verses.text: And the servant ran to meet her, and said: Give me a little water to drink of thy pitcher.
verses.textLatin: Occurritque ei servus, et ait: Pauxillum aquæ mihi ad bibendum præbe de hydria tua.

verses.text: And she answered: Drink, my lord. And quickly she let down the pitcher upon her arm, and gave him drink.
verses.textLatin: Quæ respondit: Bibe, domine mi: celeriterque deposuit hydriam super ulnam suam, et dedit ei potum.

verses.text: And when he had drunk, she said: I will draw water for thy camels also, till they all drink.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ille bibisset, adjecit: Quin et camelis tuis hauriam aquam, donec cuncti bibant.

verses.text: And pouring out the pitcher into the troughs, she ran back to the well to draw water: and having drawn she gave to all the camels.
verses.textLatin: Effundensque hydriam in canalibus, recurrit ad puteum ut hauriret aquam: et haustam omnibus camelis dedit.

verses.text: But he musing beheld her with silence, desirous to know whether the Lord had made his journey prosperous or not.
verses.textLatin: Ipse autem contemplabatur eam tacitus, scire volens utrum prosperum iter suum fecisset Dominus, an non.

verses.text: And after that the camels had drunk, the man took out golden earrings, weighing two sicles: and as many bracelets of ten sicles weight.
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem biberunt cameli, protulit vir inaures aureas, appendentes siclos duos, et armillas totidem pondo siclorum decem.

verses.text: And he said to her: Whose daughter art thou? tell me: is there any place in thy father’s house to lodge?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eam: Cujus es filia? indica mihi, est in domo patris tui locus ad manendum?

verses.text: And she answered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the son of Melcha, whom she bore to Nachor.
verses.textLatin: Quæ respondit: Filia sum Bathuelis, filii Melchæ, quem peperit ipsi Nachor.

verses.text: And she said moreover to him: We have good store of both straw and hay, and a large place to lodge in.
