verses.textLatin: Et addidit, dicens: Palearum quoque et fœni plurimum est apud nos, et locus spatiosus ad manendum.

verses.text: The man bowed himself down, and adored the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Inclinavit se homo, et adoravit Dominum,

verses.text: Saying: Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who hath not taken away his mercy and truth from my master, and hath brought me the straight way into the house of my master’s brother.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Benedictus Dominus Deus domini mei Abraham, qui non abstulit misericordiam et veritatem suam a domino meo, et recto itinere me perduxit in domum fratris domini mei.

verses.text: Then the maid ran, and told in her mother’s house, all that she had heard.
verses.textLatin: Cucurrit itaque puella, et nuntiavit in domum matris suæ omnia quæ audierat.

verses.text: And Rebecca had a brother named Laban, who went out in haste to the man, to the well.
verses.textLatin: Habebat autem Rebecca fratrem nomine Laban, qui festinus egressus est ad hominem, ubi erat fons.

verses.text: And when he had seen the earrings and bracelets in his sister’s hands, and had heard all that she related, saying: Thus and thus the man spoke to me: he came to the man who stood by the camels, and near to the spring of water,
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset inaures et armillas in manibus sororis suæ, et audisset cuncta verba referentis: Hæc locutus est mihi homo: venit ad virum qui stabat juxta camelos, et prope fontem aquæ:

verses.text: And said to him: Come in, thou blessed of the Lord: why standest thou without? I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels.
verses.textLatin: dixitque ad eum: Ingredere, benedicte Domini: cur foris stas? præparavi domum, et locum camelis.

verses.text: And he brought him in into his lodging: and he unharnessed the camels and gave straw and hay, and water to wash his feet, and the feet of the men that were come with him.
verses.textLatin: Et introduxit eum in hospitium: ac destravit camelos, deditque paleas et fœnum, et aquam ad lavandos pedes ejus, et virorum qui venerant cum eo.

verses.text: And bread was set before him. But he said: I will not eat, till I tell my message. He answered him: Speak.
verses.textLatin: Et appositus est in conspectu ejus panis. Qui ait: Non comedam, donec loquar sermones meos. Respondit ei: Loquere.

verses.text: And he said: I am the servant of Abraham:
verses.textLatin: At ille: Servus, inquit, Abraham sum:

verses.text: And the Lord hath blessed my master wonderfully, and he is become great: and he hath given him sheep and oxen, silver and gold, menservants and womenservants, camels and asses.
verses.textLatin: et Dominus benedixit domino meo valde, magnificatusque est: et dedit ei oves et boves, argentum et aurum, servos et ancillas, camelos et asinos.

verses.text: And Sara my master’s wife hath borne my master a son in her old age, and he hath given him all that he had.
verses.textLatin: Et peperit Sara uxor domini mei filium domino meo in senectute sua, deditque illi omnia quæ habuerat.

verses.text: And my master made me swear, saying: Thou shalt not take a wife for my son of the Chanaanites, in whose land I dwell:
verses.textLatin: Et adjuravit me dominus meus, dicens: Non accipies uxorem filio meo de filiabus Chananæorum, in quorum terra habito:

verses.text: But thou shalt go to my father’s house, and shalt take a wife of my own kindred for my son:
verses.textLatin: sed ad domum patris mei perges, et de cognatione mea accipies uxorem filio meo.

verses.text: But I answered my master: What if the woman will not come with me?
verses.textLatin: Ego vero respondi domino meo: Quid si noluerit venire mecum mulier?

verses.text: The Lord, said he, in whose sight I walk, will send his angel with thee, and will direct thy way: and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my own kindred, and of my father’s house.
verses.textLatin: Dominus, ait, in cujus conspectu ambulo, mittet angelum suum tecum, et diriget viam tuam: accipiesque uxorem filio meo de cognatione mea, et de domo patris mei.

verses.text: But thou shalt be clear from my curse, when thou shalt come to my kindred, if they will not give thee one.
verses.textLatin: Innocens eris a maledictione mea, cum veneris ad propinquos meos, et non dederint tibi.

verses.text: And I came to day to the well of water, and said: O Lord God of my master Abraham, if thou hast prospered my way, wherein I now walk,
verses.textLatin: Veni ergo hodie ad fontem aquæ, et dixi: Domine Deus domini mei Abraham, si direxisti viam meam, in qua nunc ambulo,

verses.text: Behold I stand by the well of water, and the virgin, that shall come out to draw water, who shall hear me say: Give me a little water to drink of thy pitcher:
verses.textLatin: ecce sto juxta fontem aquæ, et virgo, quæ egredietur ad hauriendam aquam, audierit a me: Da mihi pauxillum aquæ ad bibendum ex hydria tua:

verses.text: And shall say to me: Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman, whom the Lord hath prepared for my master’s son.
verses.textLatin: et dixerit mihi: Et tu bibe, et camelis tuis hauriam: ipsa est mulier, quam præparavit Dominus filio domini mei.

verses.text: And whilst I pondered these things secretly with myself, Rebecca appeared coming with a pitcher, which she carried on her shoulder: and she went down to the well and drew water. And I said to her: Give me a little to drink.
verses.textLatin: Dumque hæc tacitus mecum volverem, apparuit Rebecca veniens cum hydria, quam portabat in scapula: descenditque ad fontem, et hausit aquam. Et aio ad eam: Da mihi paululum bibere.

verses.text: And she speedily let down the pitcher from her shoulder, and said to me: Both drink thou, and to thy camels I will give drink. I drank, and she watered the camels.
verses.textLatin: Quæ festinans deposuit hydriam de humero, et dixit mihi: Et tu bibe, et camelis tuis tribuam potum. Bibi, et adaquavit camelos.

verses.text: And I asked her, and said: Whose daughter art thou? And she answered: I am the daughter of Bathuel, the son of Nachor, whom Melcha bore to him. So I put earrings on her to adorn her face, and I put bracelets on her hands.
verses.textLatin: Interrogavique eam, et dixi: Cujus es filia? Quæ respondit: Filia Bathuelis sum, filii Nachor, quem peperit ei Melcha. Suspendi itaque inaures ad ornandam faciem ejus, et armillas posui in manibus ejus.

verses.text: And falling down I adored the Lord, blessing the Lord God of my master Abraham, who hath brought me the straight way to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
verses.textLatin: Pronusque adoravi Dominum, benedicens Domino Deo domini mei Abraham, qui perduxit me recto itinere, ut sumerem filiam fratris domini mei filio ejus.

verses.text: Wherefore if you do according to mercy and truth with my master, tell me: but if it please you otherwise, tell me that also, that I may go to the right hand, or to the left.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem si facitis misericordiam et veritatem cum domino meo, indicate mihi: sin autem aliud placet, et hoc dicite mihi, ut vadam ad dextram, sive ad sinistram.

verses.text: And Laban and Bathuel answered: The word hath proceeded from the Lord, we cannot speak any other thing to thee but his pleasure.
verses.textLatin: Responderuntque Laban et Bathuel: A Domino egressus est sermo: non possumus extra placitum ejus quidquam aliud loqui tecum.

verses.text: Behold Rebecca is before thee, take her and go thy way, and let her be the wife of thy master’s son, as the Lord hath spoken.
verses.textLatin: En Rebecca coram te est, tolle eam, et proficiscere, et sit uxor filii domini tui, sicut locutus est Dominus.

verses.text: Which when Abraham’s servant heard, falling down to the ground he adored the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset puer Abraham, procidens adoravit in terram Dominum.

verses.text: And bringing forth vessels of silver and gold, and garments, he gave them to Rebecca for a present. He offered gifts also to her brothers, and to her mother.
verses.textLatin: Prolatisque vasis argenteis, et aureis, ac vestibus, dedit ea Rebeccæ pro munere: fratribus quoque ejus et matri dona obtulit.

verses.text: And a banquet was made, and they ate and drank together, and lodged there. And in the morning, the servant arose, and said: Let me depart, that I may go to my master.
verses.textLatin: Inito convivio, vescentes pariter et bibentes manserunt ibi. Surgens autem mane, locutus est puer: Dimitte me, ut vadam ad dominum meum.

verses.text: And her brother and mother answered: Let the maid stay at least ten days with us, and afterwards she shall depart.
verses.textLatin: Responderuntque fratres ejus et mater: Maneat puella saltem decem dies apud nos, et postea proficiscetur.

verses.text: Stay me not, said he, because the Lord hath prospered my way: send me away, that I may go to my master.
verses.textLatin: Nolite, ait, me retinere, quia Dominus direxit viam meam: dimittite me ut pergam ad dominum meum.

verses.text: And they said: Let us call the maid, and ask her will.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt: Vocemus puellam, et quæramus ipsius voluntatem.

verses.text: And they called her, and when she was come, they asked: Wilt thou go with this man? She said: I will go.
verses.textLatin: Cumque vocata venisset, sciscitati sunt: Vis ire cum homine isto? Quæ ait: Vadam.

verses.text: So they sent her away, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his company,
verses.textLatin: Dimiserunt ergo eam, et nutricem illius, servumque Abraham, et comites ejus,

verses.text: Wishing prosperity to their sister, and saying: Thou art our sister, mayst thou increase to thousands of thousands, and may thy seed possess the gates of their enemies.
verses.textLatin: imprecantes prospera sorori suæ, atque dicentes: Soror nostra es, crescas in mille millia, et possideat semen tuum portas inimicorum suorum.

verses.text: So Rebecca and her maids, being set upon camels, followed the man: who with speed returned to his master.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Rebecca et puellæ illius, ascensis camelis, secutæ sunt virum: qui festinus revertebatur ad dominum suum.

verses.text: At the same time Isaac was walking along the way to the well which is called Of the living and the seeing: for he dwelt in the south country.
verses.textLatin: Eo autem tempore deambulabat Isaac per viam quæ ducit ad puteum, cujus nomen est Viventis et videntis: habitabat enim in terra australi:

verses.text: And he was gone forth to meditate in the field, the day being now well spent: and when he had lifted up his eyes, he saw camels coming afar off.
verses.textLatin: et egressus fuerat ad meditandum in agro, inclinata jam die: cumque elevasset oculos, vidit camelos venientes procul.

verses.text: Rebecca also, when she saw Isaac, lighted off the camel,
verses.textLatin: Rebecca quoque, conspecto Isaac, descendit de camelo,

verses.text: And said to the servant: Who is that man who cometh towards us along the field? And he said to her: That man is my master. But she quickly took her cloak, and covered herself.
verses.textLatin: et ait ad puerum: Quis est ille homo qui venit per agrum in occursum nobis? Dixitque ei: Ipse est dominus meus. At illa tollens cito pallium, operuit se.

verses.text: And the servant told Isaac all that he had done.
verses.textLatin: Servus autem cuncta, quæ gesserat, narravit Isaac.

verses.text: Who brought her into the tent of Sara his mother, and took her to wife: and he loved her so much, that it moderated the sorrow which was occasioned by his mother’s death.
verses.textLatin: Qui introduxit eam in tabernaculum Saræ matris suæ, et accepit eam uxorem: et in tantum dilexit eam, ut dolorem, qui ex morte matris ejus acciderat, temperaret.

verses.text: And  Abraham married another wife named Cetura:
verses.textLatin: Abraham vero aliam duxit uxorem nomine Ceturam:

verses.text: Who bore him Zamran, and Jecsan, and Madan, and Madian, and Jesboc, and Sue.
verses.textLatin: quæ peperit ei Zamran et Jecsan, et Madan, et Madian, et Jesboc, et Sue.

verses.text: Jecsan also begot Saba and Dadan. The children of Dadan were Assurim, and Latusim and Loomin.
verses.textLatin: Jecsan quoque genuit Saba et Dadan. Filii Dadan fuerunt Assurim, et Latusim, et Loomin.

verses.text: But of Madian was born Epha, and Opher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaa: all these were the children of Cetura.
verses.textLatin: At vero ex Madian ortus est Epha, et Opher, et Henoch, et Abida, et Eldaa: omnes hi filii Ceturæ.

verses.text: And Abraham gave all his possessions to Isaac.
verses.textLatin: Deditque Abraham cuncta quæ possederat, Isaac:

verses.text: And to the children of the concubines he gave gifts, and separated them from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, to the east country.
verses.textLatin: filiis autem concubinarum largitus est munera, et separavit eos ab Isaac filio suo, dum adhuc ipse viveret, ad plagam orientalem.

verses.text: And the days of Abraham’s life were a hundred and seventy-five years.
verses.textLatin: Fuerunt autem dies vitæ Abrahæ, centum septuaginta quinque anni.

verses.text: And decaying he died in a good old age, and having lived a long time, and being full of days: and was gathered to his people.
verses.textLatin: Et deficiens mortuus est in senectute bona, provectæque ætatis et plenus dierum: congregatusque est ad populum suum.

verses.text: And Isaac and Ismael his sons buried him in the double cave, which was situated in the field of Ephron the son of Seor the Hethite, over against Mambre;
verses.textLatin: Et sepelierunt eum Isaac et Ismaël filii sui in spelunca duplici, quæ sita est in agro Ephron filii Seor Hethæi, e regione Mambre,

verses.text: Which he had bought of the children of Heth: there was he buried, and Sara his wife.
verses.textLatin: quem emerat a filiis Heth: ibi sepultus est ipse, et Sara uxor ejus.

verses.text: And after his death, God blessed Isaac his son, who dwelt by the well named Of the living and seeing.
verses.textLatin: Et post obitum illius benedixit Deus Isaac filio ejus, qui habitabat juxta puteum nomine Viventis et videntis.

verses.text: These are the generations of Ismael the son of Abraham, whom Agar the Egyptian, Sara’s servant, bore unto him:
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt generationes Ismaël filii Abrahæ, quem peperit ei Agar Ægyptia, famula Saræ: et

verses.text: And these are the names of his children according to their calling and generations. The firstborn of Ismael was Nabajoth, then Cedar, and Adbeel, and Mabsam.
verses.textLatin: hæc nomina filiorum ejus in vocabulis et generationibus suis. Primogenitus Ismaëlis Nabaioth, deinde Cedar, et Adbeel, et Mabsam,

verses.text: And Masma, and Duma, and Massa,
verses.textLatin: Masma quoque, et Duma, et Massa,

verses.text: Hadar, and Thema, and Jethur, and Naphis, and Cedma.
verses.textLatin: Hadar, et Thema, et Jethur, et Naphis, et Cedma.

verses.text: These are the sons of Ismael: and these are their names by their castles and towns, twelve princes of their tribes.
verses.textLatin: Isti sunt filii Ismaëlis: et hæc nomina per castella et oppida eorum, duodecim principes tribuum suarum.

verses.text: And the years of Ismael’s life were a hundred and thirty-seven, and decaying he died, and was gathered unto his people.
verses.textLatin: Et facti sunt anni vitæ Ismaëlis centum triginta septem, deficiensque mortuus est, et appositus ad populum suum.

verses.text: And he dwelt from Hevila as far as Sur, which looketh towards Egypt, to them that go towards the Assyrians. He died in the presence of all his brethren.
verses.textLatin: Habitavit autem ab Hevila usque Sur, quæ respicit Ægyptum introëuntibus Assyrios; coram cunctis fratribus suis obiit.

verses.text: These also are the generations of Isaac the son of Abraham: Abraham begot Isaac:
verses.textLatin: Hæ quoque sunt generationes Isaac filii Abraham: Abraham genuit Isaac:

verses.text: Who when he was forty years old, took to wife Rebecca the daughter of Bathuel the Syrian of Mesopotamia, sister to Laban.
verses.textLatin: qui cum quadraginta esset annorum, duxit uxorem Rebeccam filiam Bathuelis Syri de Mesopotamia, sororem Laban.

verses.text: And Isaac besought the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; and he heard him, and made Rebecca to conceive.
verses.textLatin: Deprecatusque est Isaac Dominum pro uxore sua, eo quod esset sterilis: qui exaudivit eum, et dedit conceptum Rebeccæ.

verses.text: But the children struggled in her womb: and she said: If it were to be so with me, what need was there to conceive? And she went to consult the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sed collidebantur in utero ejus parvuli; quæ ait: Si sic mihi futurum erat, quid necesse fuit concipere? perrexitque ut consuleret Dominum.

verses.text: And he answering said:Two nations are in thy womb, and two peoples shall be divided out of thy womb, and one people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger.
verses.textLatin: Qui respondens ait: Duæ gentes sunt in utero tuo, et duo populi ex ventre tuo dividentur, populusque populum superabit, et major serviet minori.

verses.text: And when her time was come to be delivered, behold twins were found in her womb.
verses.textLatin: Jam tempus pariendi advenerat, et ecce gemini in utero ejus reperti sunt.

verses.text: He that came forth first was red, and hairy like a skin: and his name was called Esau. Immediately the other coming forth, held his brother’s foot in his hand, and therefore he was called Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Qui prior egressus est, rufus erat, et totus in morem pellis hispidus: vocatumque est nomen ejus Esau. Protinus alter egrediens, plantam fratris tenebat manu: et idcirco appellavit eum Jacob.

verses.text: Isaac was threescore years old when the children were born unto him.
verses.textLatin: Sexagenarius erat Isaac quando nati sunt ei parvuli.

verses.text: And when they were grown up, Esau became a skilful hunter, and a husbandman: but Jacob a plain man dwelt in tents.
verses.textLatin: Quibus adultis, factus est Esau vir gnarus venandi, et homo agricola: Jacob autem vir simplex habitabat in tabernaculis.

verses.text: Isaac loved Esau, because he ate of his hunting: and Rebecca loved Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Isaac amabat Esau, eo quod de venationibus illius vesceretur: et Rebecca diligebat Jacob.

verses.text: And Jacob boiled pottage: to whom Esau, coming faint out of the field,
verses.textLatin: Coxit autem Jacob pulmentum: ad quem cum venisset Esau de agro lassus,

verses.text: Said: Give me of this red pottage, for I am exceeding faint. For which reason his name was called Edom.
verses.textLatin: ait: Da mihi de coctione hac rufa, quia oppido lassus sum. Quam ob causam vocatum est nomen ejus Edom.

verses.text: And Jacob said to him: Sell me thy first birthright.
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit Jacob: Vende mihi primogenita tua.

verses.text: He answered: Lo I die, what will the first birthright avail me.
verses.textLatin: Ille respondit: En morior, quid mihi proderunt primogenita?

verses.text: Jacob said: Swear therefore to me. Esau swore to him, and sold his first birthright.
verses.textLatin: Ait Jacob: Jura ergo mihi. Juravit ei Esau et vendidit primogenita.

verses.text: And so taking bread and the pottage of lentils, he ate, and drank, and went his way; making little account of having sold his first birthright.
verses.textLatin: Et sic, accepto pane et lentis edulio, comedit et bibit, et abiit, parvipendens quod primogenita vendidisset.

verses.text: And  when a famine came in the land, after that barrenness which had happened in the days of Abraham, Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Palestines to Gerara.
verses.textLatin: Orta autem fame super terram post eam sterilitatem, quæ acciderat in diebus Abraham, abiit Isaac ad Abimelech regem Palæstinorum in Gerara.

verses.text: And the Lord appeared to him and said: Go not down into Egypt, but stay in the land that I shall tell thee.
verses.textLatin: Apparuitque ei Dominus, et ait: Ne descendas in Ægyptum, sed quiesce in terra quam dixero tibi,

verses.text: And sojourn in it, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee: for to thee and to thy seed I will give all these countries, to fulfill the oath which I swore to Abraham thy father.
verses.textLatin: et peregrinare in ea: eroque tecum, et benedicam tibi: tibi enim et semini tuo dabo universas regiones has, complens juramentum quod spopondi Abraham patri tuo.

verses.text: And I will multiply thy seed like the stars of heaven: and I will give to thy posterity all these countries: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Et multiplicabo semen tuum sicut stellas cæli: daboque posteris tuis universas regiones has: et benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ,

verses.text: Because Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my precepts and commandments, and observed my ceremonies and laws.
verses.textLatin: eo quod obedierit Abraham voci meæ, et custodierit præcepta et mandata mea, et cæremonias legesque servaverit.

verses.text: So Isaac abode in Gerara.
verses.textLatin: Mansit itaque Isaac in Geraris.

verses.text: And when he was asked by the men of that place, concerning his wife, he answered: She is my sister; for he was afraid to confess that she was his wife, thinking lest perhaps they would kill him because of her beauty.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum interrogaretur a viris loci illius super uxore sua, respondit: Soror mea est: timuerat enim confiteri quod sibi esset sociata conjugio, reputans ne forte interficerent eum propter illius pulchritudinem.

verses.text: And when very many days were passed, and he abode there, Abimelech king of the Palestines looking out through a window, saw him playing with Rebecca his wife.
verses.textLatin: Cumque pertransissent dies plurimi, et ibidem moraretur, prospiciens Abimelech rex Palæstinorum per fenestram, vidit eum jocantem cum Rebecca uxore sua.

verses.text: And calling for him, he said: It is evident she is thy wife: why didst thou feign her to be thy sister? He answered: I feared lest I should die for her sake.
verses.textLatin: Et accersito eo, ait: Perspicuum est quod uxor tua sit: cur mentitus es eam sororem tuam esse? Respondit: Timui ne morerer propter eam.

verses.text: And Abimelech said: Why hast thou deceived us? Some man of the people might have lain with thy wife, and thou hadst brought upon us a great sin. And he commanded all the people, saying:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Abimelech: Quare imposuisti nobis? potuit coire quispiam de populo cum uxore tua, et induxeras super nos grande peccatum. Præcepitque omni populo, dicens:

verses.text: He that shall touch this man’s wife, shall surely be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Qui tetigerit hominis hujus uxorem, morte morietur.

verses.text: And Isaac sowed in that land, and he found that same year a hundredfold: and the Lord blessed him.
verses.textLatin: Sevit autem Isaac in terra illa, et invenit in ipso anno centuplum: benedixitque ei Dominus.

verses.text: And the man was enriched, and he went on prospering and increasing, till he became exceeding great:
verses.textLatin: Et locupletatus est homo, et ibat proficiens atque succrescens, donec magnus vehementer effectus est:

verses.text: And he had possessions of sheep and of herds, and a very great family. Wherefore the Palestines envying him,
verses.textLatin: habuit quoque possessiones ovium et armentorum, et familiæ plurimum. Ob hoc invidentes ei Palæstini,

verses.text: Stopped up at that time all the wells, that the servants of his father Abraham had digged, filling them up with earth:
verses.textLatin: omnes puteos, quos foderant servi patris illius Abraham, illo tempore obstruxerunt, implentes humo:

verses.text: Insomuch that Abimelech himself said to Isaac: Depart from us, for thou art become much mightier than we.
verses.textLatin: in tantum, ut ipse Abimelech diceret ad Isaac: Recede a nobis, quoniam potentior nobis factus es valde.

verses.text: So he departed and came to the torrent of Gerara, to dwell there:
verses.textLatin: Et ille discedens, ut veniret ad torrentem Geraræ, habitaretque ibi,

verses.text: And he digged again other wells, which the servants of his father Abraham had digged, and which, after his death, the Palestines had of old stopped up: and he called them by the same names by which his father before had called them.
verses.textLatin: rursum fodit alios puteos, quos foderant servi patris sui Abraham, et quos, illo mortuo, olim obstruxerant Philisthiim: appellavitque eos eisdem nominibus quibus ante pater vocaverat.

verses.text: And they digged in the torrent, and found living water.
verses.textLatin: Foderuntque in torrente, et repererunt aquam vivam.

verses.text: But there also the herdsmen of Gerara strove against the herdsmen of Isaac, saying: It is our water. Wherefore he called the name of the well, on occasion of that which had happened, Calumny.
verses.textLatin: Sed et ibi jurgium fuit pastorum Geraræ adversus pastores Isaac, dicentium: Nostra est aqua, quam ob rem nomen putei ex eo, quod acciderat, vocavit Calumniam.

verses.text: And they digged also another; and for that they quarrelled likewise, and he called the name of it, Enmity.
verses.textLatin: Foderunt autem et alium: et pro illo quoque rixati sunt, appellavitque eum Inimicitias.

verses.text: Going forward from thence, he digged another well, for which they contended not: therefore he called the name thereof, Latitude, saying: Now hath the Lord given us room, and made us to increase upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Profectus inde fodit alium puteum, pro quo non contenderunt: itaque vocavit nomen ejus Latitudo, dicens: Nunc dilatavit nos Dominus, et fecit crescere super terram.

verses.text: And he went up from that place to Bersabee,
verses.textLatin: Ascendit autem ex illo loco in Bersabee,

verses.text: Where the Lord appeared to him that same night, saying: I am the God of Abraham thy father; do not fear, for I am with thee: I will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.
verses.textLatin: ubi apparuit ei Dominus in ipsa nocte, dicens: Ego sum Deus Abraham patris tui: noli timere, quia ego tecum sum: benedicam tibi, et multiplicabo semen tuum propter servum meum Abraham.

verses.text: And he built there an altar: and called upon the name of the Lord, and pitched his tent: and commanded his servants to dig a well.
verses.textLatin: Itaque ædificavit ibi altare: et invocato nomine Domini, extendit tabernaculum, præcepitque servis suis ut foderent puteum.

verses.text: To which place when Abimelech, and Ochozath his friend, and Phicol chief captain of his soldiers came from Gerara,
verses.textLatin: Ad quem locum cum venissent de Geraris Abimelech, et Ochozath amicus illius, et Phicol dux militum,

verses.text: Isaac said to them: Why are ye come to me, a man whom you hate, and have thrust out from you?
verses.textLatin: locutus est eis Isaac: Quid venistis ad me, hominem quem odistis, et expulistis a vobis?

verses.text: And they answered: We saw that the Lord is with thee, and therefore we said: Let there be an oath between us, and let us make a covenant,
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Vidimus tecum esse Dominum, et idcirco nos diximus: Sit juramentum inter nos, et ineamus fœdus,

verses.text: That thou do us no harm, as we on our part have touched nothing of thine, nor have done any thing to hurt thee: but with peace have sent thee away increased with the blessing of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ut non facias nobis quidquam mali, sicut et nos nihil tuorum attigimus, nec fecimus quod te læderet: sed cum pace dimisimus auctum benedictione Domini.

verses.text: And he made them a feast, and after they had eaten and drunk:
verses.textLatin: Fecit ergo eis convivium, et post cibum et potum

verses.text: Arising in the morning, they swore one to another: and Isaac sent them away peaceably to their own home.
verses.textLatin: surgentes mane, juraverunt sibi mutuo: dimisitque eos Isaac pacifice in locum suum.

verses.text: And behold the same day the servants of Isaac came, telling him of a well which they had digged, and saying: We have found water.
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem venerunt in ipso die servi Isaac annuntiantes ei de puteo, quem foderant, atque dicentes: Invenimus aquam.

verses.text: Whereupon he called it Abundance: and the name of the city was called Bersabee, even to this day.
verses.textLatin: Unde appellavit eum Abundantiam: et nomen urbi impositum est Bersabee, usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: And Esau being forty years old, married wives, Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hethite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon of the same place.
verses.textLatin: Esau vero quadragenarius duxit uxores, Judith filiam Beeri Hethæi, et Basemath filiam Elon ejusdem loci:

verses.text: And they both offended the mind of Isaac and Rebecca.
verses.textLatin: quæ ambæ offenderant animum Isaac et Rebeccæ.

verses.text: Now  Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, and he could not see: and he called Esau, his elder son, and said to him: My son? And he answered: Here I am.
verses.textLatin: Senuit autem Isaac, et caligaverunt oculi ejus, et videre non poterat: vocavitque Esau filium suum majorem, et dixit ei: Fili mi? Qui respondit: Adsum.

verses.text: And his father said to him: Thou seest that I am old, and know not the day of my death.
verses.textLatin: Cui pater: Vides, inquit, quod senuerim, et ignorem diem mortis meæ.

verses.text: Take thy arms, thy quiver, and bow, and go abroad: and when thou hast taken some thing by hunting,
verses.textLatin: Sume arma tua, pharetram, et arcum, et egredere foras: cumque venatu aliquid apprehenderis,

verses.text: Make me savoury meat thereof, as thou knowest I like, and bring it, that I may eat: and my soul may bless thee before I die.
verses.textLatin: fac mihi inde pulmentum sicut velle me nosti, et affer ut comedam: et benedicat tibi anima mea antequam moriar.

verses.text: And when Rebecca had heard this, and he was gone into the field to fulfil his father’s commandment,
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Rebecca, et ille abiisset in agrum ut jussionem patris impleret,

verses.text: She said to her son Jacob: I heard thy father talking with Esau thy brother, and saying to him:
verses.textLatin: dixit filio suo Jacob: Audivi patrem tuum loquentem cum Esau fratre tuo, et dicentem ei:

verses.text: Bring me of thy hunting, and make me meats that I may eat, and bless thee in the sight of the Lord, before I die.
verses.textLatin: Affer mihi de venatione tua, et fac cibos ut comedam, et benedicam tibi coram Domino antequam moriar.

verses.text: Now, therefore, my son, follow my counsel:
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, fili mi, acquiesce consiliis meis:

verses.text: And go thy way to the flock, bring me two kids of the best, that I may make of them meat for thy father, such as he gladly eateth:
verses.textLatin: et pergens ad gregem, affer mihi duos hædos optimos, ut faciam ex eis escas patri tuo, quibus libenter vescitur:

verses.text: Which when thou hast brought in, and he hath eaten, he may bless thee before he die.
verses.textLatin: quas cum intuleris, et comederit, benedicat tibi priusquam moriatur.

verses.text: And he answered her: Thou knowest that Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am smooth.
verses.textLatin: Cui ille respondit: Nosti quod Esau frater meus homo pilosus sit, et ego lenis:

verses.text: If my father shall feel me, and perceive it, I fear lest he will think I would have mocked him, and I shall bring upon me a curse instead of a blessing.
verses.textLatin: si attrectaverit me pater meus, et senserit, timeo ne putet me sibi voluisse illudere, et inducam super me maledictionem pro benedictione.

verses.text: And his mother said to him: Upon me be this curse, my son: only hear thou my voice, and go, fetch me the things which I have said.
verses.textLatin: Ad quem mater: In me sit, ait, ista maledictio, fili mi: tantum audi vocem meam, et pergens, affer quæ dixi.

verses.text: He went, and brought, and gave them to his mother. She dressed meats, such as she knew his father liked.
verses.textLatin: Abiit, et attulit, deditque matri. Paravit illa cibos, sicut velle noverat patrem illius.

verses.text: And she put on him very good garments of Esau, which she had at home with her:
verses.textLatin: Et vestibus Esau valde bonis, quas apud se habebat domi, induit eum:

verses.text: And the little skins of the kids she put about his hands, and covered the bare of his neck.
verses.textLatin: pelliculasque hædorum circumdedit manibus, et colli nuda protexit:

verses.text: And she gave him the savoury meat, and delivered him bread that she had baked.
verses.textLatin: deditque pulmentum, et panes, quos coxerat, tradidit.

verses.text: Which when he had carried in, he said: My father? But he answered: I hear. Who art thou, my son?
verses.textLatin: Quibus illatis, dixit: Pater mi? At ille respondit: Audio. Quis es tu, fili mi?

verses.text: And Jacob said: I am Esau thy firstborn: I have done as thou didst command me: arise, sit, and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Jacob: Ego sum primogenitus tuus Esau: feci sicut præcepisti mihi: surge, sede, et comede de venatione mea, ut benedicat mihi anima tua.

verses.text: And Isaac said to his son: How couldst thou find it so quickly, my son? He answered: It was the will of God that what I sought came quickly in my way.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque Isaac ad filium suum: Quomodo, inquit, tam cito invenire potuisti, fili mi? Qui respondit: Voluntas Dei fuit ut cito occurreret mihi quod volebam.

verses.text: And Isaac said: Come hither, that I may feel thee, my son, and may prove whether thou be my son Esau, or not.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Isaac: Accede huc, ut tangam te, fili mi, et probem utrum tu sis filius meus Esau, an non.

verses.text: He came near to his father, and when he had felt him, Isaac said: The voice indeed is the voice of Jacob; but the hands are the hands of Esau.
verses.textLatin: Accessit ille ad patrem, et palpato eo, dixit Isaac: Vox quidem, vox Jacob est: sed manus, manus sunt Esau.

verses.text: And he knew him not, because his hairy hands made him like to the elder. Then blessing him,
verses.textLatin: Et non cognovit eum, quia pilosæ manus similitudinem majoris expresserant. Benedicens ergo illi,

verses.text: He said: Art thou my son Esau? He answered: I am.
verses.textLatin: ait: Tu es filius meus Esau? Respondit: Ego sum.

verses.text: Then he said: Bring me the meats of thy hunting, my son, that my soul may bless thee. And when they were brought, and he had eaten, he offered him wine also, which after he had drunk,
verses.textLatin: At ille: Affer mihi, inquit, cibos de venatione tua, fili mi, ut benedicat tibi anima mea. Quos cum oblatos comedisset, obtulit ei etiam vinum. Quo hausto,

verses.text: He said to him: Come near me, and give me a kiss, my son.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad eum: Accede ad me, et da mihi osculum, fili mi.

verses.text: He came near, and kissed him. And immediately as he smelled the fragrant smell of his garments, blessing him, he said: Behold the smell of my son is as the smell of a plentiful field, which the Lord hath blessed.
verses.textLatin: Accessit, et osculatus est eum. Statimque ut sensit vestimentorum illius fragrantiam, benedicens illi, ait: Ecce odor filii mei sicut odor agri pleni, cui benedixit Dominus.

verses.text: God give thee the dew of heaven, and of the fatness of the earth, abundance of corn and wine.
verses.textLatin: Det tibi Deus de rore cæli et de pinguedine terræ abundantiam frumenti et vini.

verses.text: And let peoples serve thee, and tribes worship thee: be thou lord of thy brethren, and let thy mother’s children bow down before thee. Cursed be he that curseth thee: and let him that blesseth thee be filled with blessings.
verses.textLatin: Et serviant tibi populi, et adorent te tribus: esto dominus fratrum tuorum, et incurventur ante te filii matris tuæ: qui maledixerit tibi, sit ille maledictus, et qui benedixerit tibi, benedictionibus repleatur.

verses.text: Isaac had scarce ended his words, when Jacob being now gone out abroad, Esau came,
verses.textLatin: Vix Isaac sermonem impleverat, et egresso Jacob foras, venit Esau,

verses.text: And brought in to his father meats made of what he had taken in hunting, saying: Arise, my father, and eat of thy son’s venison; that thy soul may bless me.
verses.textLatin: coctosque de venatione cibos intulit patri, dicens: Surge, pater mi, et comede de venatione filii tui, ut benedicat mihi anima tua.

verses.text: And Isaac said to him: Why! who art thou? He answered: I am thy firstborn son Esau.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque illi Isaac: Quis enim es tu? Qui respondit: Ego sum filius tuus primogenitus Esau.

verses.text: Isaac was struck with fear, and astonished exceedingly: and wondering beyond what can be believed, said: Who is he then that even now brought me venison that he had taken, and I ate of all before thou camest? and I have blessed him, and he shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Expavit Isaac stupore vehementi: et ultra quam credi potest admirans, ait: Quis igitur ille est qui dudum captam venationem attulit mihi, et comedi ex omnibus priusquam tu venires; benedixique ei, et erit benedictus?

verses.text: Esau having heard his father’s words, roared out with a great cry: and being in a great consternation, said: Bless me also, my father.
verses.textLatin: Auditis Esau sermonibus patris, irrugiit clamore magno: et consternatus, ait: Benedic etiam et mihi, pater mi.

verses.text: And he said: Thy brother came deceitfully and got thy blessing.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait: Venit germanus tuus fraudulenter, et accepit benedictionem tuam.

verses.text: But he said again: Rightly is his name called Jacob; for he hath supplanted me lo this second time: my first birthright he took away before, and now this second time he hath stolen away my blessing. And again he said to his father: Hast thou not reserved me also a blessing?
verses.textLatin: At ille subjunxit: Juste vocatum est nomen ejus Jacob: supplantavit enim me en altera vice: primogenita mea ante tulit, et nunc secundo surripuit benedictionem meam. Rursumque ad patrem: Numquid non reservasti, ait, et mihi benedictionem?

verses.text: Isaac answered: I have appointed him thy lord, and have made all his brethren his servants: I have established him with corn and wine, and after this, what shall I do more for thee, my son?
verses.textLatin: Respondit Isaac: Dominum tuum illum constitui, et omnes fratres ejus servituti illius subjugavi; frumento et vino stabilivi eum: et tibi post hæc, fili mi, ultra quid faciam?

verses.text: And Esau said to him: Hast thou only one blessing, father? I beseech thee bless me also. And when he wept with a loud cry,
verses.textLatin: Cui Esau: Num unam, inquit, tantum benedictionem habes, pater? mihi quoque obsecro ut benedicas. Cumque ejulatu magno fleret,

verses.text: Isaac being moved, said to him: In the fat of the earth, and in the dew of heaven from above,
verses.textLatin: motus Isaac, dixit ad eum: In pinguedine terræ, et in rore cæli desuper,

verses.text: Shall thy blessing be. Thou shalt live by the sword and shalt serve thy brother: and the time shall come, when thou shalt shake off and loose his yoke from thy neck.
verses.textLatin: erit benedictio tua. Vives in gladio, et fratri tuo servies: tempusque veniet, cum excutias et solvas jugum ejus de cervicibus tuis.

verses.text: Esau therefore always hated Jacob for the blessing wherewith his father had blessed him: and he said in his heart: The days will come of the mourning of my father, and I will kill my brother Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Oderat ergo semper Esau Jacob pro benedictione qua benedixerat ei pater: dixitque in corde suo: Venient dies luctus patris mei, et occidam Jacob fratrem meum.

verses.text: These things were told to Rebecca: and she sent and called Jacob her son, and said to him: Behold Esau thy brother threateneth to kill thee.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiata sunt hæc Rebeccæ: quæ mittens et vocans Jacob filium suum, dixit ad eum: Ecce Esau frater tuus minatur ut occidat te.

verses.text: Now therefore, my son, hear my voice: arise and flee to Laban my brother to Haran:
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, fili mi, audi vocem meam, et consurgens fuge ad Laban fratrem meum in Haran:

verses.text: And thou shalt dwell with him a few days, till the wrath of thy brother be assuaged,
verses.textLatin: habitabisque cum eo dies paucos, donec requiescat furor fratris tui,

verses.text: And his indignation cease, and he forget the things thou hast done to him: afterwards I will send, and bring thee from thence hither. Why shall I be deprived of both my sons in one day?
verses.textLatin: et cesset indignatio ejus, obliviscaturque eorum quæ fecisti in eum: postea mittam, et adducam te inde huc: cur utroque orbabor filio in uno die?

verses.text: And Rebecca said to Isaac: I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the stock of this land, I choose not to live.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Rebecca ad Isaac: Tædet me vitæ meæ propter filias Heth: si acceperit Jacob uxorem de stirpe hujus terræ, nolo vivere.

verses.text: And  Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, saying: Take not a wife of the stock of Chanaan:
verses.textLatin: Vocavit itaque Isaac Jacob, et benedixit eum, præcepitque ei dicens: Noli accipere conjugem de genere Chanaan:

verses.text: But go, and take a journey to Mesopotamia of Syria, to the house of Bathuel thy mother’s father, and take thee a wife thence of the daughters of Laban thy uncle.
verses.textLatin: sed vade, et proficiscere in Mesopotamiam Syriæ, ad domum Bathuel patris matris tuæ, et accipe tibi inde uxorem de filiabus Laban avunculi tui.

verses.text: And God almighty bless thee, and make thee to increase, and multiply thee: that thou mayst be a multitude of people.
verses.textLatin: Deus autem omnipotens benedicat tibi, et crescere te faciat, atque multiplicet, ut sis in turbas populorum.

verses.text: And give the blessings of Abraham to thee, and to thy seed after thee: that thou mayst possess the land of thy sojournment, which he promised to thy grandfather.
verses.textLatin: Et det tibi benedictiones Abrahæ, et semini tuo post te: ut possideas terram peregrinationis tuæ, quam pollicitus est avo tuo.

verses.text: And when Isaac had sent him away, he took his journey and went to Mesopotamia of Syria to Laban the son of Bathuel the Syrian, brother to Rebecca his mother.
verses.textLatin: Cumque dimisisset eum Isaac, profectus venit in Mesopotamiam Syriæ ad Laban filium Bathuel Syri, fratrem Rebeccæ matris suæ.

verses.text: And Esau seeing that his father had blessed Jacob, and had sent him into Mesopotamia of Syria, to marry a wife thence; and that after the blessing he had charged him, saying: Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Chanaan:
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Esau quod benedixisset pater suus Jacob, et misisset eum in Mesopotamiam Syriæ, ut inde uxorem duceret; et quod post benedictionem præcepisset ei, dicens: Non accipies uxorem de filiabus Chanaan:

verses.text: And that Jacob obeying his parents was gone into Syria:
verses.textLatin: quodque obediens Jacob parentibus suis isset in Syriam:

verses.text: Experiencing also that his father was not well pleased with the daughters of Chanaan:
verses.textLatin: probans quoque quod non libenter aspiceret filias Chanaan pater suus:

verses.text: He went to Ismael, and took to wife, besides them he had before, Maheleth the daughter of Ismael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nabajoth.
verses.textLatin: ivit ad Ismaëlem, et duxit uxorem absque iis, quas prius habebat, Maheleth filiam Ismaël filii Abraham, sororem Nabaioth.

verses.text: But Jacob being departed from Bersabee, went on to Haran.
verses.textLatin: Igitur egressus Jacob de Bersabee, pergebat Haran.

verses.text: And when he was come to a certain place, and would rest in it after sunset, he took of the stones that lay there, and putting under his head, slept in the same place.
verses.textLatin: Cumque venisset ad quemdam locum, et vellet in eo requiescere post solis occubitum, tulit de lapidibus qui jacebant, et supponens capiti suo, dormivit in eodem loco.

verses.text: And he saw in his sleep a ladder standing upon the earth, and the top thereof touching heaven: the angels also of God ascending and descending by it;
verses.textLatin: Viditque in somnis scalam stantem super terram, et cacumen illius tangens cælum: angelos quoque Dei ascendentes et descendentes per eam,

verses.text: And the Lord leaning upon the ladder, saying to him: I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac; the land, wherein thou sleepest, I will give to thee and to thy seed.
verses.textLatin: et Dominum innixum scalæ dicentem sibi: Ego sum Dominus Deus Abraham patris tui, et Deus Isaac: terram, in qua dormis, tibi dabo et semini tuo.

verses.text: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth: thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and IN THEE and thy seed all the tribes of the earth SHALL BE BLESSED.
verses.textLatin: Eritque semen tuum quasi pulvis terræ: dilataberis ad occidentem, et orientem, et septentrionem, et meridiem: et benedicentur in te et in semine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ.

verses.text: And I will be thy keeper whithersoever thou goest, and will bring thee back into this land: neither will I leave thee, till I shall have accomplished all that I have said.
verses.textLatin: Et ero custos tuus quocumque perrexeris, et reducam te in terram hanc: nec dimittam nisi complevero universa quæ dixi.

verses.text: And when Jacob awaked out of sleep, he said: Indeed the Lord is in this place, and I knew it not.
verses.textLatin: Cumque evigilasset Jacob de somno, ait: Vere Dominus est in loco isto, et ego nesciebam.

verses.text: And trembling he said: How terrible is this place! this is no other but the house of God, and the gate of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Pavensque, Quam terribilis est, inquit, locus iste! non est hic aliud nisi domus Dei, et porta cæli.

verses.text: And Jacob, arising in the morning, took the stone, which he had laid under his head, and set it up for a title, pouring oil upon the top of it.
verses.textLatin: Surgens ergo Jacob mane, tulit lapidem quem supposuerat capiti suo, et erexit in titulum, fundens oleum desuper.

verses.text: And he called the name of the city Bethel, which before was called Luza.
verses.textLatin: Appellavitque nomen urbis Bethel, quæ prius Luza vocabatur.

verses.text: And he made a vow, saying: If God shall be with me, and shall keep me in the way by which I walk, and shall give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
verses.textLatin: Vovit etiam votum, dicens: Si fuerit Deus mecum, et custodierit me in via, per quam ego ambulo, et dederit mihi panem ad vescendum, et vestimentum ad induendum,

verses.text: And I shall return prosperously to my father’s house: the Lord shall be my God:
verses.textLatin: reversusque fuero prospere ad domum patris mei: erit mihi Dominus in Deum,

verses.text: And this stone, which I have set up for a title, shall be called the house of God: and of all things that thou shalt give to me, I will offer tithes to thee.
verses.textLatin: et lapis iste, quem erexi in titulum, vocabitur Domus Dei: cunctorumque quæ dederis mihi, decimas offeram tibi.

verses.text: Then  Jacob went on in his journey, and came into the east country.
verses.textLatin: Profectus ergo Jacob venit in terram orientalem.

verses.text: And he saw a well in the field, and three flocks of sheep lying by it: for the beasts were watered out of it, and the mouth thereof was closed with a great stone.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit puteum in agro, tres quoque greges ovium accubantes juxta eum: nam ex illo adaquabantur pecora, et os ejus grandi lapide claudebatur.

verses.text: And the custom was, when all the sheep were gathered together, to roll away the stone, and after the sheep were watered, to put it on the mouth of the well again.
verses.textLatin: Morisque erat ut cunctis ovibus congregatis devolverent lapidem, et refectis gregibus rursum super os putei ponerent.

verses.text: And he said to the shepherds: Brethren, whence are you? They answered: Of Haran.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad pastores: Fratres, unde estis? Qui responderunt: De Haran.

verses.text: And he asked them, saying: Know you Laban the son of Nachor? They said: We know him.
verses.textLatin: Quos interrogans, Numquid, ait, nostis Laban filium Nachor? Dixerunt: Novimus.

verses.text: He said: Is he in health? He is in health, say they: and behold Rachel his daughter cometh with his flock.
verses.textLatin: Sanusne est? inquit. Valet, inquiunt: et ecce Rachel filia ejus venit cum grege suo.

verses.text: And Jacob said: There is yet much day remaining, neither is it time to bring the flocks into the folds again: first give the sheep drink, and so lead them back to feed.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Jacob: Adhuc multum diei superest, nec est tempus ut reducantur ad caulas greges: date ante potum ovibus, et sic eas ad pastum reducite.

verses.text: They answered: We cannot, till all the cattle be gathered together, and we remove the stone from the well’s mouth, that we may water the flocks.
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Non possumus, donec omnia pecora congregentur, et amoveamus lapidem de ore putei, ut adaquemus greges.

verses.text: They were yet speaking, and behold Rachel came with her father’s sheep: for she fed the flock.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc loquebantur, et ecce Rachel veniebat cum ovibus patris sui: nam gregem ipsa pascebat.

verses.text: And when Jacob saw her, and knew her to be his cousin-german, and that they were the sheep of Laban, his uncle: he removed the stone wherewith the well was closed.
verses.textLatin: Quam cum vidisset Jacob, et sciret consobrinam suam, ovesque Laban avunculi sui, amovit lapidem quo puteus claudebatur.

verses.text: And having watered the flock, he kissed her: and lifting up his voice, wept.
verses.textLatin: Et adaquato grege, osculatus est eam: et elevata voce flevit,

verses.text: And he told her that he was her father’s brother, and the son of Rebecca: but she went in haste and told her father.
verses.textLatin: et indicavit ei quod frater esset patris sui, et filius Rebeccæ: at illa festinans nuntiavit patri suo.

verses.text: Who, when he heard that Jacob his sister’s son was come, ran forth to meet him; and embracing him, and heartily kissing him, brought him into his house. And when he had heard the causes of his journey,
verses.textLatin: Qui cum audisset venisse Jacob filium sororis suæ, cucurrit obviam ei: complexusque eum, et in oscula ruens, duxit in domum suam. Auditis autem causis itineris,

verses.text: He answered: Thou art my bone and my flesh. And after the days of one month were expired,
verses.textLatin: respondit: Os meum es, et caro mea. Et postquam impleti sunt dies mensis unius,

verses.text: He said to him: Because thou art my brother, shalt thou serve me without wages? Tell me what wages thou wilt have.
verses.textLatin: dixit ei: Num quia frater meus es, gratis servies mihi? dic quid mercedis accipias.

verses.text: Now he had two daughters, the name of the elder was Lia: and the younger was called Rachel.
verses.textLatin: Habebat vero duas filias: nomen majoris Lia, minor vero appellabatur Rachel.

verses.text: But Lia was blear eyed: Rachel was well favoured, and of a beautiful countenance.
verses.textLatin: Sed Lia lippis erat oculis: Rachel decora facie, et venusto aspectu.

verses.text: And Jacob being in love with her, said: I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
verses.textLatin: Quam diligens Jacob, ait: Serviam tibi pro Rachel filia tua minore, septem annis.

verses.text: Laban answered: It is better that I give her to thee than to another man; stay with me.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Laban: Melius est ut tibi eam dem quam alteri viro: mane apud me.

verses.text: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel: and they seemed but a few days, because of the greatness of his love.
verses.textLatin: Servivit ergo Jacob pro Rachel septem annis: et videbantur illi pauci dies præ amoris magnitudine.

verses.text: And he said to Laban: Give me my wife; for now the time is fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Laban: Da mihi uxorem meam: quia jam tempus impletum est, ut ingrediar ad illam.

verses.text: And he, having invited a great number of his friends to the feast, made the marriage.
verses.textLatin: Qui vocatis multis amicorum turbis ad convivium, fecit nuptias.

verses.text: And at night he brought in Lia his daughter to him,
verses.textLatin: Et vespere Liam filiam suam introduxit ad eum,

verses.text: Giving his daughter a handmaid, named Zelpha. Now when Jacob had gone in to her according to custom, when morning was come he saw it was Lia:
verses.textLatin: dans ancillam filiæ, Zelpham nomine. Ad quam cum ex more Jacob fuisset ingressus, facto mane vidit Liam:

verses.text: And he said to his father in law: What is it that thou didst mean to do? did not I serve thee for Rachel? why hast thou deceived me?
verses.textLatin: et dixit ad socerum suum: Quid est quod facere voluisti? nonne pro Rachel servivi tibi? quare imposuisti mihi?

verses.text: Laban answered: It is not the custom in this place, to give the younger in marriage first.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Laban: Non est in loco nostro consuetudinis, ut minores ante tradamus ad nuptias.

verses.text: Make up the week of days of this match: and I will give thee her also, for the service that thou shalt render me other seven years.
verses.textLatin: Imple hebdomadam dierum hujus copulæ: et hanc quoque dabo tibi pro opere quo serviturus es mihi septem annis aliis.

verses.text: He yielded to his pleasure: and after the week was past, he married Rachel:
verses.textLatin: Acquievit placito: et hebdomada transacta, Rachel duxit uxorem:

verses.text: To whom her father gave Bala for her servant.
verses.textLatin: cui pater servam Balam tradiderat.

verses.text: And having at length obtained the marriage he wished for, he preferred the love of the latter before the former, and served with him other seven years.
verses.textLatin: Tandemque potitus optatis nuptiis, amorem sequentis priori prætulit, serviens apud eum septem annis aliis.

verses.text: And the Lord seeing that he despised Lia, opened her womb, but her sister remained barren.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Dominus quod despiceret Liam, aperuit vulvam ejus, sorore sterili permanente.

verses.text: And she conceived and bore a son, and called his name Ruben, saying: The Lord saw my affliction: now my husband will love me.
verses.textLatin: Quæ conceptum genuit filium, vocavitque nomen ejus Ruben, dicens: Vidit Dominus humilitatem meam: nunc amabit me vir meus.

verses.text: And again she conceived and bore a son, and said: Because the Lord heard that I was despised, he hath given this also to me: and she called his name Simeon.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque concepit et peperit filium, et ait: Quoniam audivit me Dominus haberi contemptui, dedit etiam istum mihi; vocavitque nomen ejus Simeon.

verses.text: And she conceived the third time, and bore another son: and said: Now also my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons: and therefore she called his name Levi.
verses.textLatin: Concepitque tertio, et genuit alium filium: dixitque: Nunc quoque copulabitur mihi maritus meus: eo quod pepererim ei tres filios: et idcirco appellavit nomen ejus Levi.

verses.text: The fourth time she conceived and bore a son, and said: now will I praise the Lord: and for this she called him Juda. And she left bearing.
verses.textLatin: Quarto concepit, et peperit filium, et ait: Modo confitebor Domino, et ob hoc vocavit eum Judam: cessavitque parere.

verses.text: And  Rachel, seeing herself without children, envied her sister, and said to her husband: Give me children, otherwise I shall die.
verses.textLatin: Cernens autem Rachel quod infecunda esset, invidit sorori suæ, et ait marito suo: Da mihi liberos, alioquin moriar.

verses.text: And Jacob being angry with her, answered: Am I as God, who hath deprived thee of the fruit of thy womb?
verses.textLatin: Cui iratus respondit Jacob: Num pro Deo ego sum, qui privavit te fructu ventris tui?

verses.text: But she said: I have here my servant Bala: go in unto her, that she may bear upon my knees, and I may have children by her.
verses.textLatin: At illa: Habeo, inquit, famulam Balam: ingredere ad illam, ut pariat super genua mea, et habeam ex illa filios.

verses.text: And she gave him Bala in marriage: who,
verses.textLatin: Deditque illi Balam in conjugium: quæ,

verses.text: When her husband had gone in unto her, conceived and bore a son.
verses.textLatin: ingresso ad se viro, concepit, et peperit filium.

verses.text: And Rachel said: The Lord hath judged for me, and hath heard my voice, giving me a son, and therefore she called his name Dan.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Rachel: Judicavit mihi Dominus, et exaudivit vocem meam, dans mihi filium, et idcirco appellavit nomen ejus Dan.

verses.text: And again Bala conceived and bore another,
verses.textLatin: Rursumque Bala concipiens, peperit alterum,

verses.text: For whom Rachel said: God hath compared me with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called him Nephtali.
verses.textLatin: pro quo ait Rachel: Comparavit me Deus cum sorore mea, et invalui: vocavitque eum Nephthali.

verses.text: Lia, perceiving that she had left off bearing, gave Zelpha her handmaid to her husband.
verses.textLatin: Sentiens Lia quod parere desiisset, Zelpham ancillam suam marito tradidit.

verses.text: And when she had conceived and brought forth a son,
verses.textLatin: Qua post conceptum edente filium,

verses.text: She said: Happily. And therefore called his name Gad.
verses.textLatin: dixit: Feliciter, et idcirco vocavit nomen ejus Gad.

verses.text: Zelpha also bore another.
verses.textLatin: Peperit quoque Zelpha alterum.

verses.text: And Lia said: This is for my happiness: for women will call me blessed. Therefore she called him Aser.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Lia: Hoc pro beatitudine mea: beatam quippe me dicent mulieres: propterea appellavit eum Aser.

verses.text: And Ruben, going out in the time of the wheat harvest into the field, found mandrakes: which he brought to his mother Lia. And Rachel said: Give me part of thy son’s mandrakes.
verses.textLatin: Egressus autem Ruben tempore messis triticeæ in agrum, reperit mandragoras, quas matri Liæ detulit. Dixitque Rachel: Da mihi partem de mandragoris filii tui.

verses.text: She answered: Dost thou think it a small matter, that thou hast taken my husband from me, unless thou take also my son’s mandrakes? Rachel said: He shall sleep with thee this night, for thy son’s mandrakes.
verses.textLatin: Illa respondit: Parumne tibi videtur quod præripueris maritum mihi, nisi etiam mandragoras filii mei tuleris? Ait Rachel: Dormiat tecum hac nocte pro mandragoris filii tui.

verses.text: And when Jacob returned at even from the field, Lia went out to meet him, and said: Thou shalt come in unto me, because I have hired thee for my son’s mandrakes. And he slept with her that night.
verses.textLatin: Redeuntique ad vesperam Jacob de agro, egressa est in occursum ejus Lia, et Ad me, inquit, intrabis: quia mercede conduxi te pro mandragoris filii mei. Dormivitque cum ea nocte illa.

verses.text: And God heard her prayers: and she conceived and bore the fifth son,
verses.textLatin: Et exaudivit Deus preces ejus, concepitque et peperit filium quintum,

verses.text: And said: God hath given me a reward, because I gave my handmaid to my husband. And she called his name Issachar.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Dedit Deus mercedem mihi, quia dedi ancillam meam viro meo: appellavitque nomen ejus Issachar.

verses.text: And Lia conceived again, and bore the sixth son,
verses.textLatin: Rursum Lia concipiens, peperit sextum filium,

verses.text: And said: God hath endowed me with a good dowry: this turn also my husband will be with me, because I have borne him six sons: and therefore she called his name Zabulon.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Dotavit me Deus dote bona: etiam hac vice mecum erit maritus meus, eo quod genuerim ei sex filios: et idcirco appellavit nomen ejus Zabulon.

verses.text: After whom she bore a daughter, named Dina.
verses.textLatin: Post quem peperit filiam, nomine Dinam.

verses.text: The Lord also remembering Rachel, heard her, and opened her womb.
verses.textLatin: Recordatus quoque Dominus Rachelis, exaudivit eam, et aperuit vulvam ejus.

verses.text: And she conceived, and bore a son, saying: God hath taken away my reproach.
verses.textLatin: Quæ concepit, et peperit filium, dicens: Abstulit Deus opprobrium meum.

verses.text: And she called his name Joseph, saying: The Lord give me also another son.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit nomen ejus Joseph, dicens: Addat mihi Dominus filium alterum.

verses.text: And when Joseph was born, Jacob said to his father in law: Send me away that I may return into my country, and to my land.
verses.textLatin: Nato autem Joseph, dixit Jacob socero suo: Dimitte me ut revertar in patriam, et ad terram meam.

verses.text: Give me my wives, and my children, for whom I have served thee, that I may depart: thou knowest the service that I have rendered thee.
verses.textLatin: Da mihi uxores, et liberos meos, pro quibus servivi tibi, ut abeam: tu nosti servitutem qua servivi tibi.

verses.text: Laban said to him: Let me find favour in thy sight: I have learned by experience, that God hath blessed me for thy sake:
verses.textLatin: Ait illi Laban: Inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo, experimento didici, quia benedixerit mihi Deus propter te:

verses.text: Appoint thy wages which I shall give thee.
verses.textLatin: constitue mercedem tuam quam dem tibi.

verses.text: But he answered: Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how great thy possession hath been in my hands.
verses.textLatin: At ille respondit: Tu nosti quomodo servierim tibi, et quanta in manibus meis fuerit possessio tua.

verses.text: Thou hadst but little before I came to thee, and now thou art become rich: and the Lord hath blessed thee at my coming. It is reasonable therefore that I should now provide also for my own house.
verses.textLatin: Modicum habuisti antequam venirem ad te, et nunc dives effectus es: benedixitque tibi Dominus ad introitum meum. Justum est igitur ut aliquando provideam etiam domui meæ.

verses.text: And Laban said: What shall I give thee? But he said: I require nothing: but if thou wilt do what I demand, I will feed, and keep thy sheep again.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Laban: Quid tibi dabo? At ille ait: Nihil volo: sed si feceris quod postulo, iterum pascam, et custodiam pecora tua.

verses.text: Go round through all thy flocks, and separate all the sheep of divers colours, and speckled: and all that is brown and spotted, and of divers colours, as well among the sheep, as among the goats, shall be my wages.
verses.textLatin: Gyra omnes greges tuos, et separa cunctas oves varias, et sparso vellere; quodcumque furvum, et maculosum, variumque fuerit, tam in ovibus quam in capris, erit merces mea.

verses.text: And my justice shall answer for me to morrow before thee when the time of the bargain shall come: and all that is not of divers colours, and spotted, and brown, as well among the sheep as among the goats, shall accuse me of theft.
verses.textLatin: Respondebitque mihi cras justitia mea, quando placiti tempus advenerit coram te: et omnia quæ non fuerint varia, et maculosa, et furva, tam in ovibus quam in capris, furti me arguent.

verses.text: And Laban said: I like well what thou demandest.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Laban: Gratum habeo quod petis.

verses.text: And he separated the same day the she goats, and the sheep, and the he goats, and the rams of divers colours, and spotted: and all the flock of one colour, that is, of white and black fleece, he delivered into the hands of his sons.
verses.textLatin: Et separavit in die illa capras, et oves, et hircos, et arietes varios, atque maculosos: cunctum autem gregem unicolorem, id est albi et nigri velleris, tradidit in manu filiorum suorum.

verses.text: And he set the space of three days’ journey betwixt himself and his son in law, who fed the rest of his flock.
verses.textLatin: Et posuit spatium itineris trium dierum inter se et generum, qui pascebat reliquos greges ejus.

verses.text: And Jacob took green rods of poplar, and of almond, and of plane trees, and pilled them in part: so when the bark was taken off, in the parts that were pilled, there appeared whiteness: but the parts that were whole remained green: and by this means the colour was divers.
verses.textLatin: Tollens ergo Jacob virgas populeas virides, et amygdalinas, et ex platanis, ex parte decorticavit eas: detractisque corticibus, in his, quæ spoliata fuerant, candor apparuit: illa vero quæ integra fuerant, viridia permanserunt: atque in hunc modum color effectus est varius.

verses.text: And he put them in the troughs, where the water was poured out: that when the flocks should come to drink, they might have the rods before their eyes, and in the sight of them might conceive.
verses.textLatin: Posuitque eas in canalibus, ubi effundebatur aqua: ut cum venissent greges ad bibendum, ante oculos haberent virgas, et in aspectu earum conciperent.

verses.text: And it came to pass that in the very heat of coition, the sheep beheld the rods, and brought forth spotted, and of divers colours, and speckled.
verses.textLatin: Factumque est ut in ipso calore coitus, oves intuerentur virgas, et parerent maculosa, et varia, et diverso colore respersa.

verses.text: And Jacob separated the flock, and put the rods in the troughs before the eyes of the rams: and all the white and the black were Laban’s: and the rest were Jacob’s, when the flocks were separated one from the other.
verses.textLatin: Divisitque gregem Jacob, et posuit virgas in canalibus ante oculos arietum: erant autem alba et nigra quæque, Laban; cetera vero, Jacob, separatis inter se gregibus.

verses.text: So when the ewes went first to ram, Jacob put the rods in the troughs of water before the eyes of the rams, and of the ewes, that they might conceive while they were looking upon them:
verses.textLatin: Igitur quando primo tempore ascendebantur oves, ponebat Jacob virgas in canalibus aquarum ante oculos arietum et ovium, ut in earum contemplatione conciperent:

verses.text: But when the latter coming was, and the last conceiving, he did not put them. And those that were lateward, became Laban’s: and they of the first time, Jacob’s.
verses.textLatin: quando vero serotina admissura erat, et conceptus extremus, non ponebat eas. Factaque sunt ea quæ erant serotina, Laban: et quæ primi temporis, Jacob.

verses.text: And the man was enriched exceedingly, and he had many flocks, maidservants and menservants, camels and asses.
verses.textLatin: Ditatusque est homo ultra modum, et habuit greges multos, ancillas et servos, camelos et asinos.

verses.text: But  after that he heard the words of the sons of Laban, saying: Jacob hath taken away all that was our father’s, and being enriched by his substance is become great:
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem audivit verba filiorum Laban dicentium: Tulit Jacob omnia quæ fuerunt patris nostri, et de illius facultate ditatus, factus est inclytus:

verses.text: And perceiving also that Laban’s countenance was not towards him as yesterday and the other day,
verses.textLatin: animadvertit quoque faciem Laban, quod non esset erga se sicut heri et nudiustertius,

verses.text: Especially the Lord saying to him: Return into the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred, and I will be with thee.
verses.textLatin: maxime dicente sibi Domino: Revertere in terram patrum tuorum, et ad generationem tuam, eroque tecum.

verses.text: He sent, and called Rachel and Lia into the field, where he fed the flocks,
verses.textLatin: Misit, et vocavit Rachel et Liam in agrum, ubi pascebat greges,

verses.text: And said to them: I see your father’s countenance is not towards me as yesterday and the other day: but the God of my father hath been with me.
verses.textLatin: dixitque eis: Video faciem patris vestri quod non sit erga me sicut heri et nudiustertius: Deus autem patris mei fuit mecum.

verses.text: And you know that I have served your father to the uttermost of my power.
verses.textLatin: Et ipsæ nostis quod totis viribus meis servierim patri vestro.

verses.text: Yea, your father also hath overreached me, and hath changed my wages ten times: and yet God hath not suffered him to hurt me.
verses.textLatin: Sed et pater vester circumvenit me et mutavit mercedem meam decem vicibus: et tamen non dimisit eum Deus ut noceret mihi.

verses.text: If at any time he said: The speckled shall be thy wages: all the sheep brought forth speckled: but when he said on the contrary: Thou shalt take all the white ones for thy wages: all the flocks brought forth white ones.
verses.textLatin: Si quando dixit: Variæ erunt mercedes tuæ: pariebant omnes oves varios fœtus; quando vero e contrario, ait: Alba quæque accipies pro mercede: omnes greges alba pepererunt.

verses.text: And God hath taken your father’s substance, and given it to me.
verses.textLatin: Tulitque Deus substantiam patris vestri, et dedit mihi.

verses.text: For after that time came of the ewes conceiving, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in my sleep that the males which leaped upon the females were of divers colours, and spotted, and speckled.
verses.textLatin: Postquam enim conceptus ovium tempus advenerat, levavi oculos meos, et vidi in somnis ascendentes mares super feminas, varios et maculosos, et diversorum colorum.

verses.text: And the angel of God said to me in my sleep: Jacob? And I answered: Here I am.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque angelus Dei ad me in somnis: Jacob? Et ego respondi: Adsum.

verses.text: And he said: Lift up thy eyes, and see that all the males leaping upon the females, are of divers colours, spotted, and speckled. For I have seen all that Laban hath done to thee.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait: Leva oculos tuos, et vide universos masculos ascendentes super feminas, varios, maculosos, atque respersos. Vidi enim omnia quæ fecit tibi Laban.

verses.text: I am the God of Bethel, where thou didst anoint the stone, and make a vow to me. Now therefore arise, and go out of this land, and return into thy native country.
verses.textLatin: Ego sum Deus Bethel, ubi unxisti lapidem, et votum vovisti mihi. Nunc ergo surge, et egredere de terra hac, revertens in terram nativitatis tuæ.

verses.text: And Rachel and Lia answered: Have we any thing left among the goods and inheritance of our father’s house?
verses.textLatin: Responderuntque Rachel et Lia: Numquid habemus residui quidquam in facultatibus et hæreditate domus patris nostri?

verses.text: Hath he not counted us as strangers and sold us, and eaten up the price of us?
verses.textLatin: nonne quasi alienas reputavit nos, et vendidit, comeditque pretium nostrum?

verses.text: But God hath taken our father’s riches, and delivered them to us, and to our children: wherefore do all that God hath commanded thee.
verses.textLatin: Sed Deus tulit opes patris nostri, et eas tradidit nobis, ac filiis nostris: unde omnia quæ præcepit tibi Deus, fac.

verses.text: Then Jacob rose up, and having set his children and wives upon camels, went his way.
verses.textLatin: Surrexit itaque Jacob, et impositis liberis ac conjugibus suis super camelos, abiit.

verses.text: And he took all his substance, and flocks, and whatsoever he had gotten in Mesopotamia, and went forward to Isaac his father to the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Tulitque omnem substantiam suam, et greges, et quidquid in Mesopotamia acquisierat, pergens ad Isaac patrem suum in terram Chanaan.

verses.text: At that time Laban was gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole away her father’s idols.
verses.textLatin: Eo tempore ierat Laban ad tondendas oves, et Rachel furata est idola patris sui.

verses.text: And Jacob would not confess to his father in law that he was flying away.
verses.textLatin: Noluitque Jacob confiteri socero suo quod fugeret.

verses.text: And when he was gone, together with all that belonged to him, and having passed the river, was going on towards mount Galaad,
verses.textLatin: Cumque abiisset tam ipse quam omnia quæ juris sui erant, et amne transmisso pergeret contra montem Galaad,

verses.text: It was told Laban on the third day that Jacob fled.
verses.textLatin: nuntiatum est Laban die tertio quod fugeret Jacob.

verses.text: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days; and overtook him in the mount of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Qui, assumptis fratribus suis, persecutus est eum diebus septem: et comprehendit eum in monte Galaad.

verses.text: And he saw in a dream God saying to him: Take heed thou speak not any thing harshly against Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Viditque in somnis dicentem sibi Deum: Cave ne quidquam aspere loquaris contra Jacob.

verses.text: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain: and when he with his brethren had overtaken him, he pitched his tent in the same mount of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Jamque Jacob extenderat in monte tabernaculum: cumque ille consecutus fuisset eum cum fratribus suis, in eodem monte Galaad fixit tentorium.

verses.text: And he said to Jacob: Why hast thou done thus, to carry away, without my knowledge, my daughters, as captives taken with the sword.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad Jacob: Quare ita egisti, ut clam me abigeres filias meas quasi captivas gladio?

verses.text: Why wouldst thou run away privately and not acquaint me, that I might have brought thee on the way with joy, and with songs, and with timbrels, and with harps?
verses.textLatin: cur ignorante me fugere voluisti, nec indicare mihi, ut prosequerer te cum gaudio, et canticis, et tympanis, et citharis?

verses.text: Thou hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and daughters: thou hast done foolishly: and now, indeed,
verses.textLatin: Non es passus ut oscularer filios meos et filias: stulte operatus es: et nunc quidem

verses.text: It is in my power to return thee evil: but the God of your father said to me yesterday: Take heed thou speak not any thing harshly against Jacob.
verses.textLatin: valet manus mea reddere tibi malum: sed Deus patris vestri heri dixit mihi: Cave ne loquaris contra Jacob quidquam durius.

verses.text: Suppose thou didst desire to go to thy friends, and hadst a longing after thy father’s house: why hast thou stolen away my gods?
verses.textLatin: Esto, ad tuos ire cupiebas, et desiderio erat tibi domus patris tui: cur furatus es deos meos?

verses.text: Jacob answered: That I departed unknown to thee, it was for fear lest thou wouldst take away thy daughters by force.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Jacob: Quod inscio te profectus sum, timui ne violenter auferres filias tuas.

verses.text: But whereas thou chargest me with theft: with whomsoever thou shalt find thy gods, let him be slain before our brethren. Search, and if thou find any of thy things with me, take them away. Now when he said this, he knew not that Rachel had stolen the idols.
verses.textLatin: Quod autem furti me arguis: apud quemcumque inveneris deos tuos, necetur coram fratribus nostris: scrutare, quidquid tuorum apud me inveneris, et aufer. Hæc dicens, ignorabat quod Rachel furata esset idola.

verses.text: So Laban went into the tent of Jacob, and of Lia, and of both the handmaids, and found them not. And when he was entered into Rachel’s tent,
verses.textLatin: Ingressus itaque Laban tabernaculum Jacob, et Liæ, et utriusque famulæ, non invenit. Cumque intrasset tentorium Rachelis,

verses.text: She in haste hid the idols under the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them: and when he had searched all the tent, and found nothing,
verses.textLatin: illa festinans abscondit idola subter stramenta cameli, et sedit desuper: scrutantique omne tentorium, et nihil invenienti,

verses.text: She said: Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee, because it has now happened to me, according to the custom of women. So his careful search was in vain.
verses.textLatin: ait: Ne irascatur dominus meus quod coram te assurgere nequeo: quia juxta consuetudinem feminarum nunc accidit mihi: sic delusa sollicitudo quærentis est.

verses.text: And Jacob being angry, said in a chiding manner: For what fault of mine, and for what offence on my part hast thou so hotly pursued me,
verses.textLatin: Tumensque Jacob, cum jurgio ait: Quam ob culpam meam, et ob quod peccatum meum sic exarsisti post me,

verses.text: And searched all my household stuff? What hast thou found of all the substance of thy house? lay it here before my brethren, and thy brethren, and let them judge between me and thee.
verses.textLatin: et scrutatus es omnem supellectilem meam? quid invenisti de cuncta substantia domus tuæ? pone hic coram fratribus meis, et fratribus tuis, et judicent inter me et te.

verses.text: Have I therefore been with thee twenty years? thy ewes and goats were not barren, the rams of thy flocks I did not eat:
verses.textLatin: Idcirco viginti annis fui tecum? oves tuæ et capræ steriles non fuerunt, arietes gregis tui non comedi:

verses.text: Neither did I shew thee that which the beast had torn, I made good all the damage: whatsoever was lost by theft, thou didst exact it of me:
verses.textLatin: nec captum a bestia ostendi tibi, ego damnum omne reddebam: quidquid furto peribat, a me exigebas:

verses.text: Day and night was I parched with heat, and with frost, and sleep departed from my eyes.
verses.textLatin: die noctuque æstu urebar, et gelu, fugiebatque somnus ab oculis meis.

verses.text: And in this manner have I served thee in thy house twenty years, fourteen for thy daughters, and six for thy flocks: thou hast changed also my wages ten times.
verses.textLatin: Sicque per viginti annos in domo tua servivi tibi, quatuordecim pro filiabus, et sex pro gregibus tuis: immutasti quoque mercedem meam decem vicibus.

verses.text: Unless the God of my father Abraham, and the fear of Isaac had stood by me, peradventure now thou hadst sent me away naked: God beheld my affliction and the labour of my hands, and rebuked thee yesterday.
verses.textLatin: Nisi Deus patris mei Abraham, et timor Isaac affuisset mihi, forsitan modo nudum me dimisisses: afflictionem meam et laborem manuum mearum respexit Deus, et arguit te heri.

verses.text: Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and thy flocks, and all things that thou seest are mine: what can I do to my children, and grandchildren?
verses.textLatin: Respondit ei Laban: Filiæ meæ et filii, et greges tui, et omnia quæ cernis, mea sunt: quid possum facere filiis et nepotibus meis?

verses.text: Come therefore, let us enter into a league: that it may be for a testimony between me and thee.
verses.textLatin: Veni ergo, et ineamus fœdus, ut sit in testimonium inter me et te.

verses.text: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a title:
verses.textLatin: Tulit itaque Jacob lapidem, et erexit illum in titulum:

verses.text: And he said to his brethren: Bring hither stones. And they gathering stones together, made a heap, and they ate upon it.
verses.textLatin: dixitque fratribus suis: Afferte lapides. Qui congregantes fecerunt tumulum, comederuntque super eum:
