verses.text: And Laban called it The witness heap: and Jacob, The hillock of testimony; each of them according to the propriety of his language.
verses.textLatin: quem vocavit Laban Tumulum testis: et Jacob, Acervum testimonii, uterque juxta proprietatem linguæ suæ.

verses.text: And Laban said: This heap shall be a witness between me and thee this day, and therefore the name thereof was called Galaad, that is, The witness heap.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Laban: Tumulus iste erit testis inter me et te hodie, et idcirco appellatum est nomen ejus Galaad, id est, Tumulus testis.

verses.text: The Lord behold and judge between us when we shall be gone one from the other.
verses.textLatin: Intueatur et judicet Dominus inter nos quando recesserimus a nobis,

verses.text: If thou afflict my daughters, and if thou bring in other wives over them: none is witness of our speech but God, who is present and beholdeth.
verses.textLatin: si afflixeris filias meas, et si introduxeris alias uxores super eas: nullus sermonis nostri testis est absque Deo, qui præsens respicit.

verses.text: And he said again to Jacob: Behold this heap, and the stone which I have set up between me and thee,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque rursus ad Jacob: En tumulus hic, et lapis quem erexi inter me et te,

verses.text: Shall be a witness: this heap, I say, and the stone, be they for a testimony, if either I shall pass beyond it going towards thee, or thou shalt pass beyond it, thinking harm to me.
verses.textLatin: testis erit: tumulus, inquam, iste et lapis sint in testimonium, si aut ego transiero illum pergens ad te, aut tu præterieris, malum mihi cogitans.

verses.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nachor, the God of their father, judge between us. And Jacob swore by the fear of his father Isaac.
verses.textLatin: Deus Abraham, et Deus Nachor, judicet inter nos, Deus patris eorum. Juravit ergo Jacob per timorem patris sui Isaac:

verses.text: And after he had offered sacrifices in the mountain, he called his brethren to eat bread. And when they had eaten, they lodged there:
verses.textLatin: immolatisque victimis in monte, vocavit fratres suos ut ederent panem. Qui cum comedissent, manserunt ibi:

verses.text: But Laban arose in the night, and kissed his sons, and daughters, and blessed them: and returned to his place.
verses.textLatin: Laban vero de nocte consurgens, osculatus est filios, et filias suas, et benedixit illis: reversusque est in locum suum.

verses.text: Jacob  also went on the journey he had begun: and the angels of God met him.
verses.textLatin: Jacob quoque abiit itinere quo cœperat: fueruntque ei obviam angeli Dei.

verses.text: And when he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God, and he called the name of that place Mahanaim, that is, Camps.
verses.textLatin: Quos cum vidisset, ait: Castra Dei sunt hæc: et appellavit nomen loci illius Mahanaim, id est, Castra.

verses.text: And he sent messengers before him to Esau his brother to the land of Seir to the country of Edom:
verses.textLatin: Misit autem et nuntios ante se ad Esau fratrem suum in terram Seir, in regionem Edom:

verses.text: And he commanded them, saying: Thus shall ye speak to my lord Esau: Thus saith thy brother Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban, and have been with him until this day.
verses.textLatin: præcepitque eis, dicens: Sic loquimini domino meo Esau: Hæc dicit frater tuus Jacob: Apud Laban peregrinatus sum, et fui usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: I have oxen, and asses, and sheep, and menservants, and womenservants: and now I send a message to my lord, that I may find favour in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: Habeo boves, et asinos, et oves, et servos, et ancillas: mittoque nunc legationem ad dominum meum, ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo.

verses.text: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: We came to Esau thy brother, and behold he cometh with speed to meet thee with four hundred men.
verses.textLatin: Reversique sunt nuntii ad Jacob, dicentes: Venimus ad Esau fratrem tuum, et ecce properat tibi in occursum cum quadringentis viris.

verses.text: Then Jacob was greatly afraid; and in his fear divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and the sheep, and the oxen, and the camels, into two companies,
verses.textLatin: Timuit Jacob valde: et perterritus divisit populum qui secum erat, greges quoque et oves, et boves, et camelos, in duas turmas,

verses.text: Saying: If Esau come to one company and destroy it, the other company that is left shall escape.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Si venerit Esau ad unam turmam, et percusserit eam, alia turma, quæ relicta est, salvabitur.

verses.text: And Jacob said: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Lord, who saidst to me: Return to thy land and to the place of thy birth, and I will do well for thee,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Jacob: Deus patris mei Abraham, et Deus patris mei Isaac: Domine qui dixisti mihi: Revertere in terram tuam, et in locum nativitatis tuæ, et benefaciam tibi:

verses.text: I am not worthy of the least of all thy mercies, and of thy truth which thou hast fulfilled to thy servant. With my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I return with two companies.
verses.textLatin: minor sum cunctis miserationibus tuis, et veritate tua quam explevisti servo tuo. In baculo meo transivi Jordanem istum: et nunc cum duabus turmis regredior.

verses.text: Deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am greatly afraid of him: lest perhaps he come, and kill the mother with the children.
verses.textLatin: Erue me de manu fratris mei Esau, quia valde eum timeo: ne forte veniens percutiat matrem cum filiis.

verses.text: Thou didst say that thou wouldst do well by me, and multiply my seed like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.
verses.textLatin: Tu locutus es quod benefaceres mihi, et dilatares semen meum sicut arenam maris, quæ præ multitudine numerari non potest.

verses.text: And when he had slept there that night, he set apart, of the things which he had, presents for his brother Esau,
verses.textLatin: Cumque dormisset ibi nocte illa, separavit de his quæ habebat, munera Esau fratri suo,

verses.text: Two hundred she goats, twenty he goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams,
verses.textLatin: capras ducentas, hircos viginti, oves ducentas, et arietes viginti,

verses.text: Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty kine, and twenty bulls, twenty she asses, and ten of their foals.
verses.textLatin: camelos fœtas cum pullis suis triginta, vaccas quadraginta, et tauros viginti, asinas viginti et pullos earum decem.

verses.text: And he sent them by the hands of his servants, every drove by itself, and he said to his servants: Go before me, and let there be a space between drove and drove.
verses.textLatin: Et misit per manus servorum suorum singulos seorsum greges, dixitque pueris suis: Antecedite me, et sit spatium inter gregem et gregem.

verses.text: And he commanded the first, saying: If thou meet my brother Esau, and he ask thee: Whose art thou? or whither goest thou? or whose are these before thee?
verses.textLatin: Et præcepit priori, dicens: Si obvium habueris fratrem meum Esau, et interrogaverit te: Cujus es? aut, Quo vadis? aut, Cujus sunt ista quæ sequeris?

verses.text: Thou shalt answer: Thy servant Jacob’s: he hath sent them as a present to my lord Esau: and he cometh after us.
verses.textLatin: respondebis: Servi tui Jacob, munera misit domino meo Esau, ipse quoque post nos venit.

verses.text: In like manner he commanded the second and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying: Speak ye the same words to Esau, when ye find him.
verses.textLatin: Similiter dedit mandata secundo, et tertio, et cunctis qui sequebantur greges, dicens: Iisdem verbis loquimini ad Esau cum inveneritis eum.

verses.text: And ye shall add: Thy servant Jacob himself also followeth after us; for he said: I will appease him with the presents that go before, and afterwards I will see him, perhaps he will be gracious to me.
verses.textLatin: Et addetis: Ipse quoque servus tuus Jacob iter nostrum insequitur. Dixit enim: Placabo illum muneribus quæ præcedunt, et postea videbo illum: forsitan propitiabitur mihi.

verses.text: So the presents went before him, but himself lodged that night in the camp.
verses.textLatin: Præcesserunt itaque munera ante eum, ipse vero mansit nocte illa in castris.

verses.text: And rising early he took his two wives, and his two handmaids, with his eleven sons, and passed over the ford of Jaboc.
verses.textLatin: Cumque mature surrexisset, tulit duas uxores suas, et totidem famulas cum undecim filiis, et transivit vadum Jaboc.

verses.text: And when all things were brought over that belonged to him,
verses.textLatin: Traductisque omnibus quæ ad se pertinebant,

verses.text: He remained alone: and behold a man wrestled with him till morning.
verses.textLatin: mansit solus: et ecce vir luctabatur cum eo usque mane.

verses.text: And when he saw that he could not overcome him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and forthwith it shrank.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum videret quod eum superare non posset, tetigit nervum femoris ejus, et statim emarcuit.

verses.text: And he said to him: Let me go, for it is break of day. He answered: I will not let thee go except thou bless me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eum: Dimitte me: jam enim ascendit aurora. Respondit: Non dimittam te, nisi benedixeris mihi.

verses.text: And he said: What is thy name? He answered: Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Ait ergo: Quod nomen est tibi? Respondit: Jacob.

verses.text: But he said: Thy name shall not be called Jacob, but Israel: for if thou hast been strong against God, how much more shalt thou prevail against men?
verses.textLatin: At ille: Nequaquam, inquit, Jacob appellabitur nomen tuum, sed Israël: quoniam si contra Deum fortis fuisti, quanto magis contra homines prævalebis?

verses.text: Jacob asked him, Tell me by what name art thou called? He answered: Why dost thou ask my name? And he blessed him in the same place.
verses.textLatin: Interrogavit eum Jacob: Dic mihi, quo appellaris nomine? Respondit: Cur quæris nomen meum? Et benedixit ei in eodem loco.

verses.text: And Jacob called the name of the place Phanuel, saying: I have seen God face to face, and my soul has been saved.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Jacob nomen loci illius Phanuel, dicens: Vidi Deum facie ad faciem, et salva facta est anima mea.

verses.text: And immediately the sun rose upon him, after he was past Phanuel; but he halted on his foot.
verses.textLatin: Ortusque est ei statim sol, postquam transgressus est Phanuel: ipse vero claudicabat pede.

verses.text: Therefore the children of Israel, unto this day, eat not the sinew, that shrank in Jacob’s thigh: because he touched the sinew of his thigh and it shrank.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob causam non comedunt nervum filii Israël, qui emarcuit in femore Jacob, usque in præsentem diem: eo quod tetigerit nervum femoris ejus, et obstupuerit.

verses.text: And  Jacob lifting up his eyes, saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men; and he divided the children of Lia, and of Rachel, and of the two handmaids:
verses.textLatin: Elevans autem Jacob oculos suos, vidit venientem Esau, et cum eo quadringentos viros: divisitque filios Liæ et Rachel, ambarumque famularum:

verses.text: And he put both the handmaids and their children foremost: and Lia and her children in the second place: and Rachel and Joseph last.
verses.textLatin: et posuit utramque ancillam, et liberos earum, in principio: Liam vero, et filios ejus, in secundo loco: Rachel autem et Joseph novissimos.

verses.text: And he went forward and bowed down with his face to the ground seven times until his brother came near.
verses.textLatin: Et ipse progrediens adoravit pronus in terram septies, donec appropinquaret frater ejus.

verses.text: Then Esau ran to meet his brother, and embraced him: and clasping him fast about the neck, and kissing him, wept.
verses.textLatin: Currens itaque Esau obviam fratri suo, amplexatus est eum: stringensque collum ejus, et osculans flevit.

verses.text: And lifting up his eyes, he saw the women and their children, and said: What mean these? And do they belong to thee? He answered: They are the children which God hath given to me thy servant.
verses.textLatin: Levatisque oculis, vidit mulieres et parvulos earum, et ait: Quid sibi volunt isti? et si ad te pertinent? Respondit: Parvuli sunt quos donavit mihi Deus servo tuo.

verses.text: Then the handmaids and their children came near, and bowed themselves.
verses.textLatin: Et appropinquantes ancillæ et filii earum, incurvati sunt.

verses.text: Lia also with her children came near, and bowed down in like manner, and last of all Joseph and Rachel bowed down.
verses.textLatin: Accessit quoque Lia cum pueris suis: et cum similiter adorassent, extremi Joseph et Rachel adoraverunt.

verses.text: And Esau said: What are the droves that I met? He answered: That I might find favour before my lord.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Esau: Quænam sunt istæ turmæ quas obviam habui? Respondit: Ut invenirem gratiam coram domino meo.

verses.text: But he said: I have plenty, my brother, keep what is thine for thyself.
verses.textLatin: At ille ait: Habeo plurima, frater mi, sint tua tibi.

verses.text: And Jacob said: Do not so I beseech thee, but if I have found favour in thy eyes, receive a little present at my hands: for I have seen thy face, as if I should have seen the countenance of God: be gracious to me,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Jacob: Noli ita, obsecro: sed si inveni gratiam in oculis tuis, accipe munusculum de manibus meis. Sic enim vidi faciem tuam, quasi viderim vultum Dei: esto mihi propitius,

verses.text: And take the blessing, which I have brought thee, and which God hath given me, who giveth all things. He took it with much ado at his brother’s earnest pressing him,
verses.textLatin: et suscipe benedictionem quam attuli tibi, et quam donavit mihi Deus tribuens omnia. Vix fratre compellente, suscipiens,

verses.text: And said: Let us go on together, and I will accompany thee in thy journey.
verses.textLatin: ait: Gradiamur simul, eroque socius itineris tui.

verses.text: And Jacob said: My lord, thou knowest that I have with me tender children, and sheep, and kine with young: which if I should cause to be overdriven, in one day all the flocks will die.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Jacob: Nosti, domine mi, quod parvulos habeam teneros, et oves, et boves fœtas mecum: quas si plus in ambulando fecero laborare, morientur una die cuncti greges.

verses.text: May it please my lord to go before his servant: and I will follow softly after him, as I shall see my children to be able, until I come to my lord in Seir.
verses.textLatin: Præcedat dominus meus ante servum suum: et ego sequar paulatim vestigia ejus, sicut videro parvulos meos posse, donec veniam ad dominum meum in Seir.

verses.text: Esau answered: I beseech thee, that some of the people at least, who are with me, may stay to accompany thee in the way. And he said: There is no necessity: I want nothing else but only to find favour, my lord, in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Esau: Oro te, ut de populo qui mecum est, saltem socii remaneant viæ tuæ. Non est, inquit, necesse: hoc uno tantum indigeo, ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo, domine mi.

verses.text: So Esau returned, that day, the way that he came, to Seir.
verses.textLatin: Reversus est itaque illo die Esau itinere quo venerat in Seir.

verses.text: And Jacob came to Socoth: where having built a house, and pitched tents, he called the name of the place Socoth, that is, Tents.
verses.textLatin: Et Jacob venit in Socoth: ubi ædificata domo et fixis tentoriis appellavit nomen loci illius Socoth, id est, Tabernacula.

verses.text: And he passed over to Salem, a city of the Sichemites, which is in the land of Chanaan, after he returned from Mesopotamia of Syria: and he dwelt by the town:
verses.textLatin: Transivitque in Salem urbem Sichimorum, quæ est in terra Chanaan, postquam reversus est de Mesopotamia Syriæ: et habitavit juxta oppidum.

verses.text: And he bought that part of the field, in which he pitched his tents, of the children of Hemor, the father of Sichem for a hundred lambs.
verses.textLatin: Emitque partem agri, in qua fixerat tabernacula, a filiis Hemor patris Sichem centum agnis.

verses.text: And raising an altar there, he invoked upon it the most mighty God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et erecto ibi altari, invocavit super illud fortissimum Deum Israël.

verses.text: And  Dina the daughter of Lia went out to see the women of that country.
verses.textLatin: Egressa est autem Dina filia Liæ ut videret mulieres regionis illius.

verses.text: And when Sichem the son of Hemor the Hevite, the prince of that land, saw her, he was in love with her: and took her away, and lay with her, ravishing the virgin.
verses.textLatin: Quam cum vidisset Sichem filius Hemor Hevæi, princeps terræ illius, adamavit eam: et rapuit, et dormivit cum illa, vi opprimens virginem.

verses.text: And his soul was fast knit unto her, and whereas she was sad, he comforted her with sweet words.
verses.textLatin: Et conglutinata est anima ejus cum ea, tristemque delinivit blanditiis.

verses.text: And going to Hemor his father, he said: Get me this damsel to wife.
verses.textLatin: Et pergens ad Hemor patrem suum: Accipe, inquit, mihi puellam hanc conjugem.

verses.text: But when Jacob had heard this, his sons being absent, and employed in feeding the cattle, he held his peace till they came back.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Jacob absentibus filiis, et in pastu pecorum occupatis, siluit donec redirent.

verses.text: And when Hemor the father of Sichem was come out to speak to Jacob,
verses.textLatin: Egresso autem Hemor patre Sichem ut loqueretur ad Jacob,

verses.text: Behold his sons came from the field: and hearing what had passed, they were exceeding angry, because he had done a foul thing in Israel, and committed an unlawful act, in ravishing Jacob’s daughter.
verses.textLatin: ecce filii ejus veniebant de agro: auditoque quod acciderat, irati sunt valde, eo quod fœdam rem operatus esset in Israël et, violata filia Jacob, rem illicitam perpetrasset.

verses.text: And Hemor spoke to them: The soul of my son Sichem has a longing for your daughter: give her him to wife:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est itaque Hemor ad eos: Sichem filii mei adhæsit anima filiæ vestræ: date eam illi uxorem:

verses.text: And let us contract marriages one with another: give us your daughters and take you our daughters,
verses.textLatin: et jungamus vicissim connubia: filias vestras tradite nobis, et filias nostras accipite,

verses.text: And dwell with us: the land is at your command, till, trade, and possess it.
verses.textLatin: et habitate nobiscum: terra in potestate vestra est: exercete, negotiamini, et possidete eam.

verses.text: Sichem also said to her father and to her brethren: Let me find favour in your sight: and whatsoever you shall appoint I will give.
verses.textLatin: Sed et Sichem ad patrem et ad fratres ejus ait: Inveniam gratiam coram vobis: et quæcumque statueritis, dabo:

verses.text: Raise the dowry, and ask gifts, and I will gladly give what you shall demand: only give me this damsel to wife.
verses.textLatin: augete dotem, et munera postulate, et libenter tribuam quod petieritis: tantum date mihi puellam hanc uxorem.

verses.text: The sons of Jacob answered Sichem and his father deceitfully, being enraged at the deflowering of their sister:
verses.textLatin: Responderunt filii Jacob Sichem et patri ejus in dolo, sævientes ob stuprum sororis:

verses.text: We cannot do what you demand, nor give our sister to one that is uncircumcised, which with us is unlawful and abominable.
verses.textLatin: Non possumus facere quod petitis, nec dare sororem nostram homini incircumciso: quod illicitum et nefarium est apud nos.

verses.text: But in this we may be allied with you, if you will be like us, and all the male sex among you be circumcised:
verses.textLatin: Sed in hoc valebimus fœderari, si volueritis esse similes nostri, et circumcidatur in vobis omne masculini sexus;

verses.text: Then will we mutually give and take your daughters, and ours: and we will dwell with you, and will be one people:
verses.textLatin: tunc dabimus et accipiemus mutuo filias vestras ac nostras: et habitabimus vobiscum, erimusque unus populus.

verses.text: But if you will not be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart:
verses.textLatin: Si autem circumcidi nolueritis, tollemus filiam nostram, et recedemus.

verses.text: Their offer pleased Hemor, and Sichem his son:
verses.textLatin: Placuit oblatio eorum Hemor, et Sichem filio ejus,

verses.text: And the young man made no delay, but forthwith fulfilled what was required, for he loved the damsel exceedingly, and he was the greatest man in all his father’s house.
verses.textLatin: nec distulit adolescens quin statim quod petebatur expleret: amabat enim puellam valde, et ipse erat inclytus in omni domo patris sui.

verses.text: And going into the gate of the city they spoke to the people:
verses.textLatin: Ingressique portam urbis, locuti sunt ad populum:

verses.text: These men are peaceable and willing to dwell with us: let them trade in the land, and till it, which being large and wide wanteth men to till it: we shall take their daughters for wives, and we will give them ours.
verses.textLatin: Viri isti pacifici sunt, et volunt habitare nobiscum: negotientur in terra, et exerceant eam, quæ spatiosa et lata cultoribus indiget: filias eorum accipiemus uxores, et nostras illis dabimus.

verses.text: One thing there is for which so great a good is deferred: We must circumcise every male among us, following the manner of the nation.
verses.textLatin: Unum est quo differtur tantum bonum: si circumcidamus masculos nostros, ritum gentis imitantes.

verses.text: And their substance, and cattle, and all that they possess, shall be ours: only in this let us condescend, and by dwelling together, we shall make one people.
verses.textLatin: Et substantia eorum, et pecora, et cuncta quæ possident, nostra erunt: tantum in hoc acquiescamus, et habitantes simul, unum efficiemus populum.

verses.text: And they all agreed, and circumcised all the males.
verses.textLatin: Assensique sunt omnes, circumcisis cunctis maribus.

verses.text: And behold the third day, when the pain of the wound was greatest, two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, taking their swords, entered boldly into the city, and slew all the men:
verses.textLatin: Et ecce, die tertio, quando gravissimus vulnerum dolor est: arreptis duo filii Jacob, Simeon et Levi fratres Dinæ, gladiis, ingressi sunt urbem confidenter: interfectisque omnibus masculis,

verses.text: And they killed also Hemor and Sichem, and took away their sister Dina, out of Sichem’s house.
verses.textLatin: Hemor et Sichem pariter necaverunt, tollentes Dinam de domo Sichem sororem suam.

verses.text: And when they were gone out, the other sons of Jacob came upon the slain; and plundered the city in revenge of the rape.
verses.textLatin: Quibus egressis, irruerunt super occisos ceteri filii Jacob: et depopulati sunt urbem in ultionem stupri.

verses.text: And they took their sheep and their herds and their asses, wasting all they had in their houses and in the fields.
verses.textLatin: Oves eorum, et armenta, et asinos, cunctaque vastantes quæ in domibus et in agris erant,

verses.text: And their children and wives they took captive,
verses.textLatin: parvulos quoque eorum et uxores duxerunt captivas.

verses.text: And when they had boldly perpetrated these things, Jacob said to Simeon and Levi: You have troubled me, and made me hateful to the Chanaanites and Pherezites, the inhabitants of this land: we are few: they will gather themselves together and kill me; and both I, and my house, shall be destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Quibus patratis audacter, Jacob dixit ad Simeon et Levi: Turbastis me, et odiosum fecistis me Chananæis, et Pherezæis habitatoribus terræ hujus: nos pauci sumus; illi congregati percutient me, et delebor ego, et domus mea.

verses.text: They answered: Should they abuse our sister as a strumpet?
verses.textLatin: Responderunt: Numquid ut scorto abuti debuere sorore nostra?

verses.text: In  the mean time God said to Jacob: Arise, and go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make there an altar to God, who appeared to thee when thou didst flee from Esau thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Interea locutus est Deus ad Jacob: Surge, et ascende Bethel, et habita ibi, facque altare Deo qui apparuit tibi quando fugiebas Esau fratrem tuum.

verses.text: And Jacob having called together all his household, said: Cast away the strange gods that are among you, and be cleansed and change your garments.
verses.textLatin: Jacob vero convocata omni domo sua, ait: Abjicite deos alienos qui in medio vestri sunt, et mundamini, ac mutate vestimenta vestra.

verses.text: Arise, and let us go up to Bethel, that we may make there an altar to God: who heard me in the day of my affliction, and accompained me in my journey.
verses.textLatin: Surgite, et ascendamus in Bethel, ut faciamus ibi altare Deo: qui exaudivit me in die tribulationis meæ, et socius fuit itineris mei.

verses.text: So they gave him all the strange gods they had, and the earrings which were in their ears: and he buried them under the turpentine tree, that is behind the city of Sichem.
verses.textLatin: Dederunt ergo ei omnes deos alienos quos habebant, et inaures quæ erant in auribus eorum: at ille infodit ea subter terebinthum, quæ est post urbem Sichem.

verses.text: And when they were departed, the terror of God fell upon all the cities round about, and they durst not pursue after them as they went away.
verses.textLatin: Cumque profecti essent, terror Dei invasit omnes per circuitum civitates, et non sunt ausi persequi recedentes.

verses.text: And Jacob came to Luza, which is in the land of Chanaan, surnamed Bethel: he and all the people that were with him.
verses.textLatin: Venit igitur Jacob Luzam, quæ est in terra Chanaan, cognomento Bethel: ipse et omnis populus cum eo.

verses.text: And he built there an altar, and called the name of that place, The house of God: for there God appeared to him when he fled from his brother.
verses.textLatin: Ædificavitque ibi altare, et appellavit nomen loci illius, Domus Dei: ibi enim apparuit ei Deus cum fugeret fratrem suum.

verses.text: At the same time Debora the nurse of Rebecca died, and was buried at the foot of Bethel under an oak: and the name of that place was called, The oak of weeping.
verses.textLatin: Eodem tempore mortua est Debora nutrix Rebeccæ, et sepulta est ad radices Bethel subter quercum: vocatumque est nomen loci illius, Quercus fletus.

verses.text: And God appeared again to Jacob, after he returned from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he blessed him,
verses.textLatin: Apparuit autem iterum Deus Jacob postquam reversus est de Mesopotamia Syriæ, benedixitque ei

verses.text: Saying: Thou shalt not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name. And he called him Israel.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Non vocaberis ultra Jacob, sed Israël erit nomen tuum. Et appellavit eum Israël,

verses.text: And said to him: I am God Almighty, increase thou and be multiplied. Nations and peoples of nations shall be from thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins.
verses.textLatin: dixitque ei: Ego Deus omnipotens: cresce, et multiplicare: gentes et populi nationum ex te erunt, reges de lumbis tuis egredientur,

verses.text: And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to thee, and to thy seed after thee.
verses.textLatin: terramque quam dedi Abraham et Isaac, dabo tibi et semini tuo post te.

verses.text: And he departed from him.
verses.textLatin: Et recessit ab eo.

verses.text: But he set up a monument of stone, in the place where God had spoken to him: pouring drink offerings upon it, and pouring oil thereon:
verses.textLatin: Ille vero erexit titulum lapideum in loco quo locutus fuerat ei Deus: libans super eum libamina, et effundens oleum:

verses.text: And calling the name of that place Bethel.
verses.textLatin: vocansque nomen loci illius Bethel.

verses.text: And going forth from thence, he came in the springtime to the land which leadeth to Ephrata: wherein when Rachel was in travail,
verses.textLatin: Egressus autem inde, venit verno tempore ad terram quæ ducit Ephratam: in qua cum parturiret Rachel,

verses.text: By reason of her hard labour she began to be in danger, and the midwife said to her: Fear not, for thou shalt have this son also.
verses.textLatin: ob difficultatem partus periclitari cœpit. Dixitque ei obstetrix: Noli timere, quia et hunc habebis filium.

verses.text: And when her soul was departing for pain, and death was now at hand, she called the name of her son Benoni, that is, The son of my pain: but his father called him Benjamin, that is, The son of the right hand.
verses.textLatin: Egrediente autem anima præ dolore, et imminente jam morte, vocavit nomen filii sui Benomi, id est, Filius doloris mei: pater vero appellavit eum Benjamin, id est, Filius dextræ.

verses.text: So Rachel died, and was buried in the highway that leadeth to Ephrata, this is Bethlehem.
verses.textLatin: Mortua est ergo Rachel, et sepulta est in via quæ ducit Ephratam, hæc est Bethlehem.

verses.text: And Jacob erected a pillar over her sepulchre: this is the pillar of Rachel’s monument, to this day.
verses.textLatin: Erexitque Jacob titulum super sepulchrum ejus: hic est titulus monumenti Rachel, usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: Departing thence, he pitched his tent beyond the Flock tower.
verses.textLatin: Egressus inde, fixit tabernaculum trans Turrem gregis.

verses.text: And when he dwelt in that country, Ruben went, and slept with Bala, the concubine of his father: which he was not ignorant of. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.
verses.textLatin: Cumque habitaret in illa regione, abiit Ruben, et dormivit cum Bala concubina patris sui: quod illum minime latuit. Erant autem filii Jacob duodecim.

verses.text: The sons of Lia: Ruben the firstborn, and Simeon, and Levi, and Juda, and Issachar, and Zabulon.
verses.textLatin: Filii Liæ: primogenitus Ruben, et Simeon, et Levi, et Judas, et Issachar, et Zabulon.

verses.text: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.textLatin: Filii Rachel: Joseph et Benjamin.

verses.text: The sons of Bala, Rachel’s handmaid: Dan and Nephtali.
verses.textLatin: Filii Balæ ancillæ Rachelis: Dan et Nephthali.

verses.text: The sons of Zelpha, Lia’s handmaid: Gad and Aser: these are the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
verses.textLatin: Filii Zelphæ ancillæ Liæ: Gad et Aser: hi sunt filii Jacob, qui nati sunt ei in Mesopotamia Syriæ.

verses.text: And he came to Isaac his father in Mambre, the city of Arbee, this is Hebron: wherein Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
verses.textLatin: Venit etiam ad Isaac patrem suum in Mambre, civitatem Arbee, hæc est Hebron, in qua peregrinatus est Abraham et Isaac.

verses.text: And the days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years.
verses.textLatin: Et completi sunt dies Isaac centum octoginta annorum.

verses.text: And being spent with age he died, and was gathered to his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
verses.textLatin: Consumptusque ætate mortuus est: et appositus est populo suo senex et plenus dierum: et sepelierunt eum Esau et Jacob filii sui.

verses.text: And  these are the generations of Esau, the same is Edom.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt autem generationes Esau, ipse est Edom.

verses.text: Esau took wives of the daughters of Chanaan: Ada the daughter of Elon the Hethite, and Oolibama the daughter of Ana, the daughter of Sebeon the Hevite:
verses.textLatin: Esau accepit uxores de filiabus Chanaan: Ada filiam Elon Hethæi, et Oolibama filiam Anæ filiæ Sebeon Hevæi:

verses.text: And Basemath the daughter of Ismael, sister of Nabajoth.
verses.textLatin: Basemath quoque filiam Ismaël sororem Nabaioth.

verses.text: And Ada bore Eliphaz: Basemath bore Rahuel:
verses.textLatin: Peperit autem Ada Eliphaz: Basemath genuit Rahuel:

verses.text: Oolibama bore Jehus and Ihelon and Core. These are the sons of Esau, that were born to him in the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Oolibama genuit Jehus et Ihelon et Core. Hi filii Esau qui nati sunt ei in terra Chanaan.

verses.text: And Esau took his wives and his sons and daughters, and every soul of his house, and his substance, and cattle, and all that he was able to acquire in the land of Chanaan: and went into another country, and departed from his brother Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Tulit autem Esau uxores suas et filios et filias, et omnem animam domus suæ, et substantiam, et pecora, et cuncta quæ habere poterat in terra Chanaan: et abiit in alteram regionem, recessitque a fratre suo Jacob.

verses.text: For they were exceeding rich, and could not dwell together: neither was the land in which they sojourned able to bear them, for the multitude of their flocks.
verses.textLatin: Divites enim erant valde, et simul habitare non poterant: nec sustinebat eos terra peregrinationis eorum præ multitudine gregum.

verses.text: And Esau dwelt in mount Seir: he is Edom.
verses.textLatin: Habitavitque Esau in monte Seir, ipse est Edom.

verses.text: And these are the generations of Esau the father of Edom in mount Seir,
verses.textLatin: Hæ autem sunt generationes Esau patris Edom in monte Seir,

verses.text: And these the names of his sons: Eliphaz the son of Ada the wife of Esau: and Rahuel the son of Basemath his wife.
verses.textLatin: et hæc nomina filiorum ejus: Eliphaz filius Ada uxoris Esau: Rahuel quoque filius Basemath uxoris ejus.

verses.text: And Eliphaz had sons: Theman, Omar, Sepho, and Gatham, and Cenez.
verses.textLatin: Fueruntque Eliphaz filii: Theman, Omar, Sepho, et Gatham, et Cenez.

verses.text: And Thamna was the concubine of Eliphaz the son of Esau: and she bore him Amalech. These are the sons of Ada the wife of Esau.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Thamna concubina Eliphaz filii Esau: quæ peperit ei Amalech. Hi sunt filii Ada uxoris Esau.

verses.text: And the sons of Rahuel were Nahath and Zara, Samma and Meza. These were the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Rahuel: Nahath et Zara, Samma et Meza: hi filii Basemath uxoris Esau.

verses.text: And these were the sons of Oolibama, the daughter of Ana, the daughter of Sebeon, the wife of Esau, whom she bore to him, Jehus, and Ihelon, and Core.
verses.textLatin: Isti quoque erant filii Oolibama filiæ Anæ filiæ Sebeon, uxoris Esau, quos genuit ei, Jehus et Ihelon et Core.

verses.text: These were dukes of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: duke Theman, duke Omar, duke Sepho, duke Cenez,
verses.textLatin: Hi duces filiorum Esau: filii Eliphaz primogeniti Esau: dux Theman, dux Omra, dux Sepho, dux Cenez,

verses.text: Duke Core, duke Gatham, duke Amalech: these are the sons of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, and these the sons of Ada.
verses.textLatin: dux Core, dux Gathan, dux Amalech. Hi filii Eliphaz in terra Edom, et hi filii Ada.

verses.text: And these were the sons of Rahuel, the son of Esau: duke Nahath, duke Zara, duke Samma, duke Meza. And these are the dukes of Rahuel, in the land of Edom: these the sons of Basemath the wife of Esau.
verses.textLatin: Hi quoque filii Rahuel filii Esau: dux Nahath, dux Zara, dux Samma, dux Meza: hi autem duces Rahuel in terra Edom: isti filii Basemath uxoris Esau.

verses.text: And these the sons of Oolibama the wife of Esau: duke Jehus, duke Ihelon, duke Core. These are the dukes of Oolibama, the daughter of Ana, and wife of Esau.
verses.textLatin: Hi autem filii Oolibama uxoris Esau: dux Jehus, dux Ihelon, dux Core: hi duces Oolibama filiæ Anæ uxoris Esau.

verses.text: These are the sons of Esau, and these the dukes of them: the same is Edom.
verses.textLatin: Isti sunt filii Esau, et hi duces eorum: ipse est Edom.

verses.text: These are the sons of Seir the Horrite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Sobal, and Sebeon, and Ana,
verses.textLatin: Isti sunt filii Seir Horræi, habitatores terræ: Lotan, et Sobal, et Sebeon, et Ana,

verses.text: And Dison, and Eser, and Disan. These are dukes of the Horrites, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom.
verses.textLatin: et Dison, et Eser, et Disan: hi duces Horræi, filii Seir in terra Edom.

verses.text: And Lotan had sons: Hori and Heman. And the sister of Lotan was Thamna.
verses.textLatin: Facti sunt autem filii Lotan: Hori et Heman. Erat autem soror Lotan, Thamna.

verses.text: And these the sons of Sobal: Alvan and Manahat, and Ebal, and Sepho, and Oman.
verses.textLatin: Et isti filii Sobal: Alvan et Manahat et Ebal, et Sepho et Onam.

verses.text: And these the sons of Sebeon: Aia and Ana. This is Ana that found the hot waters in the wilderness, when he fed the asses of Sebeon his father:
verses.textLatin: Et hi filii Sebeon: Aja et Ana. Iste est Ana qui invenit aquas calidas in solitudine, cum pasceret asinos Sebeon patris sui:

verses.text: And he had a son Dison, and a daughter Oolibama.
verses.textLatin: habuitque filium Dison, et filiam Oolibama.

verses.text: And these were the sons of Dison: Hamdan, and Eseban, and Jethram, and Charan.
verses.textLatin: Et isti filii Dison: Hamdan, et Eseban, et Jethram, et Charan.

verses.text: These also were the sons of Eser: Balaan, and Zavan, and Acan.
verses.textLatin: Hi quoque filii Eser: Balaan, et Zavan, et Acan.

verses.text: And Dison had sons: Hus, and Aram.
verses.textLatin: Habuit autem filios Disan: Hus et Aram.

verses.text: These were dukes of the Horrites: duke Lotan, duke Sobal, duke Sebeon, duke Ana,
verses.textLatin: Hi duces Horræorum: dux Lotan, dux Sobal, dux Sebeon, dux Ana,

verses.text: Duke Dison, duke Eser, duke Disan: these were dukes of the Horrites that ruled in the land of Seir.
verses.textLatin: dux Dison, dux Eser, dux Disan: isti duces Horræorum qui imperaverunt in terra Seir.

verses.text: And the kings that ruled in the land of Edom, before the children of Israel had a king, were these:
verses.textLatin: Reges autem qui regnaverunt in terra Edom antequam haberent regem filii Israël, fuerunt hi:

verses.text: Bela the son of Beor, and the name of his city Denaba.
verses.textLatin: Bela filius Beor, nomenque urbis ejus Denaba.

verses.text: And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zara of Bosra reigned in his stead.
verses.textLatin: Mortuus est autem Bela, et regnavit pro eo Jobab filius Zaræ de Bosra.

verses.text: And when Jobab was dead, Husam of the land of the Themanites reigned in his stead.
verses.textLatin: Cumque mortuus esset Jobab, regnavit pro eo Husam de terra Themanorum.

verses.text: And after his death, Adad the son of Badad reigned in his stead, who defeated the Madianites in the country of Moab: and the name of his city was Avith.
verses.textLatin: Hoc quoque mortuo, regnavit pro eo Adad filius Badad, qui percussit Madian in regione Moab: et nomen urbis ejus Avith.

verses.text: And when Adad was dead, there reigned in his stead, Semla of Masreca.
verses.textLatin: Cumque mortuus esset Adad, regnavit pro eo Semla de Masreca.

verses.text: And he being dead, Saul of the river Rohoboth, reigned in his stead.
verses.textLatin: Hoc quoque mortuo regnavit pro eo Saul de fluvio Rohoboth.

verses.text: And when he also was dead, Balanan the son of Achobor succeeded to the kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Cumque et hic obiisset, successit in regnum Balanan filius Achobor.

verses.text: This man also being dead, Adar reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Phau: and his wife was called Meetabel, the daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezaab.
verses.textLatin: Isto quoque mortuo regnavit pro eo Adar, nomenque urbis ejus Phau: et appellabatur uxor ejus Meetabel, filia Matred filiæ Mezaab.

verses.text: And these are the names of the dukes of Esau in their kindreds, and places, and callings: duke Thamna, duke Alva, duke Jetheth,
verses.textLatin: Hæc ergo nomina ducum Esau in cognationibus, et locis, et vocabulis suis: dux Thamna, dux Alva, dux Jetheth,

verses.text: Duke Oolibama, duke Ela, duke Phinon,
verses.textLatin: dux Oolibama, dux Ela, dux Phinon,

verses.text: Duke Cenez, duke Theman, duke Mabsar,
verses.textLatin: dux Cenez, dux Theman, dux Mabsar,

verses.text: Duke Magdiel, duke Hiram: these are the dukes of Edom dwelling in the land of their government; the same is Esau the father of the Edomites.
verses.textLatin: dux Magdiel, dux Hiram: hi duces Edom habitantes in terra imperii sui, ipse est Esau pater Idumæorum.

verses.text: And  Jacob dwelt in the land of Chanaan wherein his father sojourned.
verses.textLatin: Habitavit autem Jacob in terra Chanaan, in qua pater suus peregrinatus est.

verses.text: And these are his generations: Joseph, when he was sixteen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren, being but a boy: and he was with the sons of Bala and of Zelpha his father’s wives: and he accused his brethren to his father of a most wicked crime.
verses.textLatin: Et hæ sunt generationes ejus: Joseph cum sedecim esset annorum, pascebat gregem cum fratribus suis adhuc puer: et erat cum filiis Balæ et Zelphæ uxorum patris sui: accusavitque fratres suos apud patrem crimine pessimo.

verses.text: Now Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, because he had him in his old age: and he made him a coat of divers colours.
verses.textLatin: Israël autem diligebat Joseph super omnes filios suos, eo quod in senectute genuisset eum: fecitque ei tunicam polymitam.

verses.text: And his brethren seeing that he was loved by his father, more than all his sons, hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him.
verses.textLatin: Videntes autem fratres ejus quod a patre plus cunctis filiis amaretur, oderant eum, nec poterant ei quidquam pacifice loqui.

verses.text: Now it fell out also that he told his brethren a dream, that he had dreamed: which occasioned them to hate him the more.
verses.textLatin: Accidit quoque ut visum somnium referret fratribus suis: quæ causa majoris odii seminarium fuit.

verses.text: And he said to them: Hear my dream which I dreamed.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eos: Audite somnium meum quod vidi:

verses.text: I thought we were binding sheaves in the field: and my sheaf arose as it were, and stood, and your sheaves standing about, bowed down before my sheaf.
verses.textLatin: putabam nos ligare manipulos in agro: et quasi consurgere manipulum meum, et stare, vestrosque manipulos circumstantes adorare manipulum meum.

verses.text: His brethren answered: Shalt thou be our king? or shall we be subject to thy dominion? Therefore this matter of his dreams and words ministered nourishment to their envy and hatred.
verses.textLatin: Responderunt fratres ejus: Numquid rex noster eris? aut subjiciemur ditioni tuæ? Hæc ergo causa somniorum atque sermonum, invidiæ et odii fomitem ministravit.

verses.text: He dreamed also another dream, which he told his brethren, saying: I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars worshipping me.
verses.textLatin: Aliud quoque vidit somnium, quod narrans fratribus, ait: Vidi per somnium, quasi solem, et lunam, et stellas undecim adorare me.

verses.text: And when he had told this to his father and brethren, his father rebuked him, and said: What meaneth this dream that thou hast dreamed? shall I and thy mother, and thy brethren worship thee upon the earth?
verses.textLatin: Quod cum patri suo, et fratribus retulisset, increpavit eum pater suus, et dixit: Quid sibi vult hoc somnium quod vidisti? num ego et mater tua, et fratres tui adorabimus te super terram?

verses.text: His brethren therefore envied him: but his father considered the thing with himself.
verses.textLatin: Invidebant ei igitur fratres sui: pater vero rem tacitus considerabat.

verses.text: And when his brethren abode in Sechem feeding their father’s flocks,
verses.textLatin: Cumque fratres illius in pascendis gregibus patris morarentur in Sichem,

verses.text: Israel said to him: Thy brethren feed the sheep in Sichem: come, I will send thee to them. And when he answered:
verses.textLatin: dixit ad eum Israël: Fratres tui pascunt oves in Sichimis: veni, mittam te ad eos. Quo respondente,

verses.text: I am ready: he said to him: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren, and the cattle: and bring me word again what is doing. So being sent from the vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:
verses.textLatin: Præsto sum, ait ei: Vade, et vide si cuncta prospera sint erga fratres tuos, et pecora: et renuntia mihi quid agatur. Missus de valle Hebron, venit in Sichem:

verses.text: And a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he sought.
verses.textLatin: invenitque eum vir errantem in agro, et interrogavit quid quæreret.

verses.text: But he answered: I seek my brethren; tell me where they feed the flocks.
verses.textLatin: At ille respondit: Fratres meos quæro: indica mihi ubi pascant greges.

verses.text: And the man said to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let us go to Dothain. And Joseph went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei vir: Recesserunt de loco isto: audivi autem eos dicentes: Eamus in Dothain. Perrexit ergo Joseph post fratres suos, et invenit eos in Dothain.

verses.text: And when they saw him afar off, before he came nigh them, they thought to kill him.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum vidissent eum procul, antequam accederet ad eos, cogitaverunt illum occidere:

verses.text: And said one to another: Behold the dreamer cometh.
verses.textLatin: et mutuo loquebantur: Ecce somniator venit:

verses.text: Come, let us kill him, and cast him into some old pit: and we will say: Some evil beast hath devoured him: and then it shall appear what his dreams avail him:
verses.textLatin: venite, occidamus eum, et mittamus in cisternam veterem: dicemusque: Fera pessima devoravit eum: et tunc apparebit quid illi prosint somnia sua.

verses.text: And Ruben hearing this, endeavoured to deliver him out of their hands, and said:
verses.textLatin: Audiens autem hoc Ruben, nitebatur liberare eum de manibus eorum, et dicebat:

verses.text: Do not take away his life, nor shed his blood: but cast him into this pit, that is in the wilderness, and keep your hands harmless: now he said this, being desirous to deliver him out of their hands and to restore him to his father.
verses.textLatin: Non interficiatis animam ejus, nec effundatis sanguinem: sed projicite eum in cisternam hanc, quæ est in solitudine, manusque vestras servate innoxias: hoc autem dicebat, volens eripere eum de manibus eorum, et reddere patri suo.

verses.text: And as soon as he came to his brethren, they forthwith stript him of his outside coat, that was of divers colours:
verses.textLatin: Confestim igitur ut pervenit ad fratres suos, nudaverunt eum tunica talari et polymita:

verses.text: And cast him into an old pit, where there was no water.
verses.textLatin: miseruntque eum in cisternam veterem, quæ non habebat aquam.

verses.text: And sitting down to eat bread, they saw some Ismaelites on their way coming from Galaad, with their camels, carrying spices, and balm, and myrrh to Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et sedentes ut comederent panem, viderunt Ismaëlitas viatores venire de Galaad, et camelos eorum portantes aromata, et resinam, et stacten in Ægyptum.

verses.text: And Juda said to his brethren: What will it profit us to kill our brother, and conceal his blood?
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Judas fratribus suis: Quid nobis prodest si occiderimus fratrem nostrum, et celaverimus sanguinem ipsius?

verses.text: It is better that he be sold to the Ismaelites, and that our hands be not defiled: for he is our brother and our flesh. His brethren agreed to his words.
verses.textLatin: melius est ut venundetur Ismaëlitis, et manus nostræ non polluantur: frater enim et caro nostra est. Acquieverunt fratres sermonibus illius.

verses.text: And when the Madianite merchants passed by, they drew him out of the pit, and sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver: and they led him into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et prætereuntibus Madianitis negotiatoribus, extrahentes eum de cisterna, vendiderunt eum Ismaëlitis, viginti argenteis: qui duxerunt eum in Ægyptum.

verses.text: And Ruben, returning to the pit, found not the boy:
verses.textLatin: Reversusque Ruben ad cisternam, non invenit puerum:

verses.text: And rending his garments he went to his brethren, and said: The boy doth not appear and whither shall I go?
verses.textLatin: et scissis vestibus pergens ad fratres suos, ait: Puer non comparet, et ego quo ibo?

verses.text: And they took his coat, and dipped it in the blood of a kid, which they had killed:
verses.textLatin: Tulerunt autem tunicam ejus, et in sanguine hædi, quem occiderant, tinxerunt:

verses.text: Sending some to carry it to their father, and to say: This we have found: see whether it be thy son’s coat, or not.
verses.textLatin: mittentes qui ferrent ad patrem, et dicerent: Hanc invenimus: vide utrum tunica filii tui sit, an non.

verses.text: And the father acknowledging it, said: It is my son’s coat, an evil wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath devoured Joseph.
verses.textLatin: Quam cum agnovisset pater, ait: Tunica filii mei est: fera pessima comedit eum, bestia devoravit Joseph.

verses.text: And tearing his garments, he put on sackcloth, mourning for his son a long time.
verses.textLatin: Scissisque vestibus, indutus est cilicio, lugens filium suum multo tempore.

verses.text: And all his children being gathered together to comfort their father in his sorrow, he would not receive comfort, but said: I will go down to my son into hell, mourning. And whilst he continued weeping,
verses.textLatin: Congregatis autem cunctis liberis ejus ut lenirent dolorem patris, noluit consolationem accipere, sed ait: Descendam ad filium meum lugens in infernum. Et illo perseverante in fletu,

verses.text: The Madianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Putiphar, an eunuch of Pharao, captain of the soldiers.
verses.textLatin: Madianitæ vendiderunt Joseph in Ægypto Putiphari eunucho Pharaonis, magistro militum.

verses.text: At  that time Juda went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Odollamite, named Hiras.
verses.textLatin: Eodem tempore, descendens Judas a fratribus suis, divertit ad virum Odollamitem, nomine Hiram.

verses.text: And he saw there the daughter of a manof Chanaan, called Sue: and taking her to wife, he went in unto her.
verses.textLatin: Viditque ibi filiam hominis Chananæi, vocabulo Sue: et accepta uxore, ingressus est ad eam.

verses.text: And she conceived, and bore a son, and called his name Her.
verses.textLatin: Quæ concepit, et peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Her.

verses.text: And conceiving again, she bore a son, and called him Onan.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque concepto fœtu, natum filium vocavit Onan.

verses.text: She bore also a third: whom she called Sela. After whose birth, she ceased to bear any more.
verses.textLatin: Tertium quoque peperit: quem appellavit Sela; quo nato, parere ultra cessavit.

verses.text: And Juda took a wife for Her his firstborn, whose name was Thamar.
verses.textLatin: Dedit autem Judas uxorem primogenito suo Her, nomine Thamar.

verses.text: And Her, the firstborn of Juda, was wicked in the sight of the Lord: and was slain by him.
verses.textLatin: Fuit quoque Her primogenitus Judæ nequam in conspectu Domini: et ab eo occisus est.

verses.text: Juda therefore said to Onan his son: Go in to thy brother’s wife and marry her, that thou mayst raise seed to thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Judas ad Onan filium suum: Ingredere uxorem fratris tui, et sociare illi, ut suscites semen fratri tuo.

verses.text: He knowing that the children should not be his, when he went in to his brother’s wife, spilled his seed upon the ground, lest children should be born in his brother’s name.
verses.textLatin: Ille sciens non sibi nasci filios, introiens ad uxorem fratris sui, semen fundebat in terram, ne liberi fratris nomine nascerentur.

verses.text: And therefore the Lord slew him, because he did a detestable thing.
verses.textLatin: Et idcirco percussit eum Dominus, quod rem detestabilem faceret.

verses.text: Wherefore Juda said to Thamar his daughter in law: Remain a widow in thy father’s house, till Sela my son grow up: for he was afraid lest he also might die, as his brethren did. She went her way and dwelt in her father’s house.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem dixit Judas Thamar nurui suæ: Esto vidua in domo patris tui, donec crescat Sela filius meus: timebat enim ne et ipse moreretur, sicut fratres ejus. Quæ abiit, et habitavit in domo patris sui.

verses.text: And after many days were past, the daughter of Sue the wife of Juda died: and when he had taken comfort after his mourning, he went up to Thamnas, to the shearers of his sheep, he and Hiras the Odollamite the shepherd of his flock.
verses.textLatin: Evolutis autem multis diebus, mortua est filia Sue uxor Judæ: qui, post luctum consolatione suscepta, ascendebat ad tonsores ovium suarum, ipse et Hiras opilio gregis Odollamites, in Thamnas.

verses.text: And it was told Thamar that her father in law was come up to Thamnas to shear his sheep.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiatumque est Thamar quod socer illius ascenderet in Thamnas ad tondendas oves.

verses.text: And she put off the garments of her widowhood, and took a veil: and changing her dress, sat in the cross way, that leadeth to Thamnas: because Sela was grown up, and she had not been married to him.
verses.textLatin: Quæ, depositis viduitatis vestibus, assumpsit theristrum: et mutato habitu, sedit in bivio itineris, quod ducit Thamnam: eo quod crevisset Sela, et non eum accepisset maritum.

verses.text: When Juda saw her, he thought she was a harlot: for she had covered her face, lest she should be known.
verses.textLatin: Quam cum vidisset Judas, suspicatus est esse meretricem: operuerat enim vultum suum, ne agnosceretur.

verses.text: And going to her, he said: Suffer me to lie with thee: for he knew her not to be his daughter in law. And she answered: What wilt thou give me to enjoy my company?
verses.textLatin: Ingrediensque ad eam, ait: Dimitte me ut coëam tecum: nesciebat enim quod nurus sua esset. Qua respondente: Quid dabis mihi ut fruaris concubitu meo?

verses.text: He said: I will send thee a kid out of the flock. And when she said again: I will suffer what thou wilt, if thou give a pledge, till thou send what thou promisest,
verses.textLatin: dixit: Mittam tibi hædum de gregibus. Rursumque illa dicente: Patiar quod vis, si dederis mihi arrhabonem, donec mittas quod polliceris.

verses.text: Juda said: What wilt thou have for a pledge? She answered: Thy ring and bracelet, and the staff which thou holdest in thy hand. The woman therefore at one copulation conceived.
verses.textLatin: Ait Judas: Quid tibi vis pro arrhabone dari? Respondit: Annulum tuum, et armillam, et baculum quem manu tenes. Ad unum igitur coitum mulier concepit,

verses.text: And she arose and went her way: and putting off the apparel which she had taken, put on the garments of her widowhood.
verses.textLatin: et surgens abiit: depositoque habitu quem sumpserat, induta est viduitatis vestibus.

verses.text: And Juda sent a kid by his shepherd, the Odollamite, that he might receive the pledge again, which he had given to the woman: but he, not finding her,
verses.textLatin: Misit autem Judas hædum per pastorem suum Odollamitem, ut reciperet pignus quod dederat mulieri: qui cum non invenisset eam,

verses.text: Asked the men of that place: Where is the woman that sat in the cross way? And when they all made answer: There was no harlot in this place,
verses.textLatin: interrogavit homines loci illius: Ubi est mulier quæ sedebat in bivio? Respondentibus cunctis: Non fuit in loco ista meretrix.

verses.text: He returned to Juda, and said to him: I have not found her; moreover the men of that place said to me, that there never sat a harlot there.
verses.textLatin: Reversus est ad Judam, et dixit ei: Non inveni eam: sed et homines loci illius dixerunt mihi, numquam sedisse ibi scortum.

verses.text: Juda said: Let her take it to herself; surely she cannot charge us with a lie: I sent the kid which I promised: and thou didst not find her.
verses.textLatin: Ait Judas: Habeat sibi, certe mendacii arguere nos non potest, ego misi hædum quem promiseram: et tu non invenisti eam.

verses.text: And behold after three months they told Juda, saying: Thamar, thy daughter in law hath played the harlot, and she appeareth to have a big belly. And Juda said: Bring her out that she may be burnt.
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem post tres menses nuntiaverunt Judæ, dicentes: Fornicata est Thamar nurus tua, et videtur uterus illius intumescere. Dixitque Judas: Producite eam ut comburatur.

verses.text: But when she was led to execution, she sent to her father in law, saying: By the man, to whom these things belong, I am with child. See whose ring, and bracelet, and staff this is.
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum duceretur ad pœnam, misit ad socerum suum, dicens: De viro, cujus hæc sunt, concepi: cognosce cujus sit annulus, et armilla, et baculus.

verses.text: But he acknowledging the gifts, said: She is juster than I: because I did not give her to Sela my son. However, he knew her no more.
verses.textLatin: Qui, agnitis muneribus, ait: Justior me est: quia non tradidi eam Sela filio meo. Attamen ultra non cognovit eam.

verses.text: And when she was ready to be brought to bed, there appeared twins in her womb: and in the very delivery of the infants, one put forth a hand, whereon the midwife tied a scarlet thread, saying:
verses.textLatin: Instante autem partu, apparuerunt gemini in utero: atque in ipsa effusione infantium unus protulit manum, in qua obstetrix ligavit coccinum, dicens:

verses.text: This shall come forth the first.
verses.textLatin: Iste egredietur prior.

verses.text: But he drawing back his hand, the other came forth: and the woman said: Why is the partition divided for thee? and therefore called his name Phares.
verses.textLatin: Illo vero retrahente manum, egressus est alter: dixitque mulier: Quare divisa est propter te maceria? et ob hanc causam, vocavit nomen ejus Phares.

verses.text: Afterwards his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread: and she called him Zara.
verses.textLatin: Postea egressus est frater ejus, in cujus manu erat coccinum: quem appellavit Zara.

verses.text: And  Joseph was brought into Egypt, and Putiphar an eunuch of Pharao, chief captain of the army, an Egyptian, bought him of the Ismaelites, by whom he was brought.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Joseph ductus est in Ægyptum, emitque eum Putiphar eunuchus Pharaonis, princeps exercitus, vir ægyptius, de manu Ismaëlitarum, a quibus perductus erat.

verses.text: And the Lord was with him, and he was a prosperous man in all things: and he dwelt in his master’s house,
verses.textLatin: Fuitque Dominus cum eo, et erat vir in cunctis prospere agens: habitavitque in domo domini sui,

verses.text: Who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
verses.textLatin: qui optime noverat Dominum esse cum eo, et omnia, quæ gerebat, ab eo dirigi in manu illius.

verses.text: And Joseph found favour in the sight of his master, and ministered to him: and being set over all by him, he governed the house committed to him, and all things that were delivered to him:
verses.textLatin: Invenitque Joseph gratiam coram domino suo, et ministrabat ei: a quo præpositus omnibus gubernabat creditam sibi domum, et universa quæ ei tradita fuerant:

verses.text: And the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian for Joseph’s sake, and multiplied all his substance, both at home, and in the fields.
verses.textLatin: benedixitque Dominus domui Ægyptii propter Joseph, et multiplicavit tam in ædibus quam in agris cunctam ejus substantiam:

verses.text: Neither knew he any other thing, but the bread which he ate. And Joseph was of a beautiful countenance, and comely to behold.
verses.textLatin: nec quidquam aliud noverat, nisi panem quo vescebatur. Erat autem Joseph pulchra facie, et decorus aspectu.

verses.text: And after many days his mistress cast her eyes on Joseph, and said: Lie with me.
verses.textLatin: Post multos itaque dies injecit domina sua oculos suos in Joseph, et ait: Dormi mecum.

verses.text: But he, in no wise consenting to that wicked act, said to her: Behold, my master hath delivered all things to me, and knoweth not what he hath in his own house:
verses.textLatin: Qui nequaquam acquiescens operi nefario, dixit ad eam: Ecce dominus meus, omnibus mihi traditis, ignorat quid habeat in domo sua:

verses.text: Neither is there any thing which is not in my power, or that he hath not delivered to me, but thee, who art his wife: how then can I do this wicked thing, and sin against my God?
verses.textLatin: nec quidquam est quod non in mea sit potestate, vel non tradiderit mihi, præter te, quæ uxor ejus es: quomodo ergo possum hoc malum facere, et peccare in Deum meum?

verses.text: With such words as these day by day, both the woman was importunate with the young man, and he refused the adultery.
verses.textLatin: Hujuscemodi verbis per singulos dies, et mulier molesta erat adolescenti: et ille recusabat stuprum.

verses.text: Now it happened on a certain day, that Joseph went into the house, and was doing some business without any man with him:
verses.textLatin: Accidit autem quadam die ut intraret Joseph domum, et operis quippiam absque arbitris faceret:

verses.text: And she catching the skirt of his garment, said: Lie with me. But he leaving the garment in her hand, fled, and went out.
verses.textLatin: et illa, apprehensa lacinia vestimenti ejus, diceret: Dormi mecum. Qui relicto in manu ejus pallio fugit, et egressus est foras.

verses.text: And when the woman saw the garment in her hands, and herself disregarded,
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset mulier vestem in manibus suis, et se esse contemptam,

verses.text: She called to her the men of her house, and said to them: See, he hath brought in a Hebrew, to abuse us: he came in to me, to lie with me: and when I cried out,
verses.textLatin: vocavit ad se homines domus suæ, et ait ad eos: En introduxit virum hebræum, ut illuderet nobis: ingressus est ad me, ut coiret mecum: cumque ego succlamassem,

verses.text: And he heard my voice, he left the garment that I held, and got him out.
verses.textLatin: et audisset vocem meam, reliquit pallium quod tenebam, et fugit foras.

verses.text: For a proof therefore of her fidelity, she kept the garment, and shewed it to her husband when he returned home:
verses.textLatin: In argumentum ergo fidei retentum pallium ostendit marito revertenti domum,

verses.text: And said: The Hebrew servant, whom thou hast brought, came to me to abuse me.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Ingressus est ad me servus hebræus quem adduxisti, ut illuderet mihi:

verses.text: And when he heard me cry, he left the garment which I held, and fled out.
verses.textLatin: cumque audisset me clamare, reliquit pallium quod tenebam, et fugit foras.

verses.text: His master hearing these things, and giving too much credit to his wife’s words, was very angry.
verses.textLatin: His auditis dominus, et nimium credulus verbis conjugis, iratus est valde:

verses.text: And cast Joseph into the prison, where the king’s prisoners were kept, and he was there shut up.
verses.textLatin: tradiditque Joseph in carcerem, ubi vincti regis custodiebantur, et erat ibi clausus.

verses.text: But the Lord was with Joseph, and having mercy upon him gave him favour in the sight of the chief keeper of the prison:
verses.textLatin: Fuit autem Dominus cum Joseph, et misertus illius dedit ei gratiam in conspectu principis carceris.

verses.text: Who delivered into his hand all the prisoners that were kept in custody: and whatsoever was done was under him.
verses.textLatin: Qui tradidit in manu illius universos vinctos qui in custodia tenebantur: et quidquid fiebat, sub ipso erat.

verses.text: Neither did he himself know any thing, having committed all things to him: for the Lord was with him, and made all that he did to prosper.
verses.textLatin: Nec noverat aliquid, cunctis ei creditis: Dominus enim erat cum illo, et omnia opera ejus dirigebat.

verses.text: After  this, it came to pass, that two eunuchs, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, offended their lord.
verses.textLatin: His ita gestis, accidit ut peccarent duo eunuchi, pincerna regis Ægypti, et pistor, domino suo.

verses.text: And Pharao being angry with them (now the one was chief butler, the other chief baker)
verses.textLatin: Iratusque contra eos Pharao (nam alter pincernis præerat, alter pistoribus),

verses.text: He sent them to the prison of the commander of the soldiers, in which Joseph also was prisoner,
verses.textLatin: misit eos in carcerem principis militum, in quo erat vinctus et Joseph.

verses.text: But the keeper of the prison delivered them to Joseph, and he served them. Some little time passed, and they were kept in custody.
verses.textLatin: At custos carceris tradidit eos Joseph, qui et ministrabat eis: aliquantulum temporis fluxerat, et illi in custodia tenebantur.

verses.text: And they both dreamed a dream the same night, according to the interpretation agreeing to themselves:
verses.textLatin: Videruntque ambo somnium nocte una, juxta interpretationem congruam sibi:

verses.text: And when Joseph was come in to them in the morning, and saw them sad,
verses.textLatin: ad quos cum introisset Joseph mane, et vidisset eos tristes,

verses.text: He asked them, saying: Why is your countenance sadder today than usual?
verses.textLatin: sciscitatus est eos, dicens: Cur tristior est hodie solito facies vestra?

verses.text: They answered: We have dreamed a dream, and there is nobody to interpret it to us. And Joseph said to them: Doth not interpretation belong to God? Tell me what you have dreamed.
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Somnium vidimus, et non est qui interpretetur nobis. Dixitque ad eos Joseph: Numquid non Dei est interpretatio? referte mihi quid videritis.

verses.text: The chief butler first told his dream: I saw before me a vine,
verses.textLatin: Narravit prior, præpositus pincernarum, somnium suum: Videbam coram me vitem,

verses.text: On which were three branches, which by little and little sent out buds, and after the blossoms brought forth ripe grapes:
verses.textLatin: in qua erant tres propagines, crescere paulatim in gemmas, et post flores uvas maturescere:

verses.text: And the cup of Pharao was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into the cup which I held, and I gave the cup to Pharao.
verses.textLatin: calicemque Pharaonis in manu mea: tuli ergo uvas, et expressi in calicem quem tenebam, et tradidi poculum Pharaoni.

verses.text: Joseph answered: This is the interpretation of the dream: The three branches are yet three days:
verses.textLatin: Respondit Joseph: Hæc est interpretatio somnii: tres propagines, tres adhuc dies sunt:

verses.text: After which Pharao will remember thy service, and will restore thee to thy former place: and thou shalt present him the cup according to thy office, as before thou wast wont to do.
verses.textLatin: post quos recordabitur Pharao ministerii tui, et restituet te in gradum pristinum: dabisque ei calicem juxta officium tuum, sicut ante facere consueveras.

verses.text: Only remember me, when it shall be well with thee, and do me this kindness: to put Pharao in mind to take me out of this prison:
verses.textLatin: Tantum memento mei, cum bene tibi fuerit, et facias mecum misericordiam: ut suggeras Pharaoni ut educat me de isto carcere:

verses.text: For I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here without any fault was cast into the dungeon.
verses.textLatin: quia furto sublatus sum de terra Hebræorum, et hic innocens in lacum missus sum.

verses.text: The chief baker seeing that he had wisely interpreted the dream, said: I also dreamed a dream, That I had three baskets of meal upon my head:
verses.textLatin: Videns pistorum magister quod prudenter somnium dissolvisset, ait: Et ego vidi somnium: quod tria canistra farinæ haberem super caput meum:

verses.text: And that in one basket which was uppermost, I carried all meats that are made by the art of baking, and that the birds ate out of it.
verses.textLatin: et in uno canistro quod erat excelsius, portare me omnes cibos qui fiunt arte pistoria, avesque comedere ex eo.

verses.text: Joseph answered: This is the interpretation of the dream: The three baskets are yet three days:
verses.textLatin: Respondit Joseph: Hæc est interpretatio somnii: tria canistra, tres adhuc dies sunt:

verses.text: After which Pharao will take thy head from thee, and hang thee on a cross, and the birds shall tear thy flesh.
verses.textLatin: post quos auferet Pharao caput tuum, ac suspendet te in cruce, et lacerabunt volucres carnes tuas.

verses.text: The third day after this was the birthday of Pharao: and he made a great feast for his servants, and at the banquet remembered the chief butler, and the chief baker.
verses.textLatin: Exinde dies tertius natalitius Pharaonis erat: qui faciens grande convivium pueris suis, recordatus est inter epulas magistri pincernarum, et pistorum principis.

verses.text: And he restored the one to his place to present him the cup:
verses.textLatin: Restituitque alterum in locum suum, ut porrigeret ei poculum:

verses.text: The other he hanged on a gibbet, that the truth of the interpreter might be shewn.
verses.textLatin: alterum suspendit in patibulo, ut conjectoris veritas probaretur.

verses.text: But the chief butler, when things prospered with him, forgot his interpreter.
verses.textLatin: Et tamen succedentibus prosperis, præpositus pincernarum oblitus est interpretis sui.

verses.text: After  two years Pharao had a dream. He thought he stood by the river,
verses.textLatin: Post duos annos vidit Pharao somnium. Putabat se stare super fluvium,

verses.text: Out of which came up seven kine, very beautiful and fat: and they fed in marshy places.
verses.textLatin: de quo ascendebant septem boves, pulchræ et crassæ nimis: et pascebantur in locis palustribus.

verses.text: Other seven also came up out of the river, ill favoured, and leanfleshed: and they fed on the very bank of the river, in green places:
verses.textLatin: Aliæ quoque septem emergebant de flumine, fœdæ confectæque macie: et pascebantur in ipsa amnis ripa in locis virentibus:

verses.text: And they devoured them, whose bodies were very beautiful and well conditioned. So Pharao awoke.
verses.textLatin: devoraveruntque eas, quarum mira species et habitudo corporum erat. Expergefactus Pharao,

verses.text: He slept again, and dreamed another dream: Seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk full and fair:
verses.textLatin: rursum dormivit, et vidit alterum somnium: septem spicæ pullulabant in culmo uno plenæ atque formosæ:

verses.text: Then seven other ears sprung up thin and blasted,
verses.textLatin: aliæ quoque totidem spicæ tenues, et percussæ uredine oriebantur,

verses.text: And devoured all the beauty of the former. Pharao awaked after his rest:
verses.textLatin: devorantes omnium priorum pulchritudinem. Evigilans Pharao post quietem,

verses.text: And when morning was come, being struck with fear, he sent to all the interpreters of Egypt, and to all the wise men: and they being called for, he told them his dream, and there was not any one that could interpret it.
verses.textLatin: et facto mane, pavore perterritus, misit ad omnes conjectores Ægypti, cunctosque sapientes, et accersitis narravit somnium, nec erat qui interpretaretur.

verses.text: Then at length the chief butler remembering, said: I confess my sin:
verses.textLatin: Tunc demum reminiscens pincernarum magister, ait: Confiteor peccatum meum:

verses.text: The king being angry with his servants, commanded me and the chief baker to be cast into the prison of the captain of the soldiers:
verses.textLatin: iratus rex servis suis, me et magistrum pistorum retrudi jussit in carcerem principis militum:

verses.text: Where in one night both of us dreamed a dream foreboding things to come.
verses.textLatin: ubi una nocte uterque vidimus somnium præsagum futurorum.

verses.text: There was there a young man a Hebrew, servant to the same captain of the soldiers: to whom we told our dreams,
verses.textLatin: Erat ibi puer hebræus, ejusdem ducis militum famulus: cui narrantes somnia,

verses.text: And we heard what afterwards the event of the thing proved to be so. For I was restored to my office: and he was hanged upon a gibbet.
verses.textLatin: audivimus quidquid postea rei probavit eventus; ego enim redditus sum officio meo, et ille suspensus est in cruce.

verses.text: Forthwith at the king’s command, Joseph was brought out of the prison, and they shaved him, and changing his apparel, brought him in to him.
verses.textLatin: Protinus ad regis imperium eductum de carcere Joseph totonderunt: ac veste mutata obtulerunt ei.

verses.text: And he said to him: I have dreamed dreams, and there is no one that can expound them: now I have heard that thou art very wise at interpreting them.
verses.textLatin: Cui ille ait: Vidi somnia, nec est qui edisserat: quæ audivi te sapientissime conjicere.

verses.text: Joseph answered: Without me, God shall give Pharao a prosperous answer.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Joseph: Absque me Deus respondebit prospera Pharaoni.

verses.text: So Pharao told what he had dreamed: Methought I stood upon the bank of the river,
verses.textLatin: Narravit ergo Pharao quod viderat: Putabam me stare super ripam fluminis,

verses.text: And seven kine came up out of the river exceeding beautiful and full of flesh: and they grazed on green places in a marshy pasture.
verses.textLatin: et septem boves de amne conscendere, pulchras nimis, et obesis carnibus: quæ in pastu paludis virecta carpebant.

verses.text: And behold, there followed these, other seven kine, so very ill favoured and lean, that I never saw the like in the land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Et ecce, has sequebantur aliæ septem boves, in tantum deformes et macilentæ, ut numquam tales in terra Ægypti viderim:

verses.text: And they devoured and consumed the former,
verses.textLatin: quæ, devoratis et consumptis prioribus,

verses.text: And yet gave no mark of their being full: but were as lean and ill favoured as before. I awoke, and then fell asleep again,
verses.textLatin: nullum saturitatis dedere vestigium: sed simili macie et squalore torpebant. Evigilans, rursus sopore depressus,

verses.text: And dreamed a dream: Seven ears of corn grew upon one stalk, full and very fair.
verses.textLatin: vidi somnium. Septem spicæ pullulabant in culmo uno plenæ atque pulcherrimæ.

verses.text: Other seven also thin and blasted, sprung of the stock:
verses.textLatin: Aliæ quoque septem tenues et percussæ uredine, oriebantur e stipula:

verses.text: And they devoured the beauty of the former: I told this dream to the conjecturers, and there is no man that can expound it.
verses.textLatin: quæ priorum pulchritudinem devoraverunt. Narravi conjectoribus somnium, et nemo est qui edisserat.

verses.text: Joseph answered: The king’s dream is one: God hath shewn to Pharao what he is about to do.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Joseph: Somnium regis unum est: quæ facturus est Deus, ostendit Pharaoni.

verses.text: The seven beautiful kine, and the seven full ears, are seven years of plenty: and both contain the same meaning of the dream.
verses.textLatin: Septem boves pulchræ, et septem spicæ plenæ, septem ubertatis anni sunt: eamdemque vim somnii comprehendunt.

verses.text: And the seven lean and thin kine that came up after them, and the seven thin ears that were blasted with the burning wind, are seven years of famine to come:
verses.textLatin: Septem quoque boves tenues atque macilentæ, quæ ascenderunt post eas, et septem spicæ tenues, et vento urente percussæ, septem anni venturæ sunt famis.

verses.text: Which shall be fulfilled in this order:
verses.textLatin: Qui hoc ordine complebuntur:

verses.text: Behold, there shall come seven years of great plenty in the whole land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: ecce septem anni venient fertilitatis magnæ in universa terra Ægypti,

verses.text: After which shall follow other seven years of so great scarcity, that all the abundance before shall be forgotten: for the famine shall consume all the land,
verses.textLatin: quos sequentur septem anni alii tantæ sterilitatis, ut oblivioni tradatur cuncta retro abundantia: consumptura est enim fames omnem terram,

verses.text: And the greatness of the scarcity shall destroy the greatness of the plenty.
verses.textLatin: et ubertatis magnitudinem perditura est inopiæ magnitudo.

verses.text: And for that thou didst see the second time a dream pertaining to the same thing: it is a token of the certainty, and that the word of God cometh to pass, and is fulfilled speedily.
verses.textLatin: Quod autem vidisti secundo ad eamdem rem pertinens somnium: firmitatis indicium est, eo quod fiat sermo Dei, et velocius impleatur.

verses.text: Now therefore let the king provide a wise and industrious man, and make him ruler over the land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo provideat rex virum sapientem et industrium, et præficiat eum terræ Ægypti:

verses.text: That he may appoint overseers over all the countries: and gather into barns the fifth part of the fruits, during the seven fruitful years,
verses.textLatin: qui constituat præpositos per cunctas regiones: et quintam partem fructuum per septem annos fertilitatis,

verses.text: That shall now presently ensue: and let all the corn be laid up under Pharao’s hands, and be reserved in the cities.
verses.textLatin: qui jam nunc futuri sunt, congreget in horrea: et omne frumentum sub Pharaonis potestate condatur, serveturque in urbibus.

verses.text: And let it be in readiness, against the famine of seven years to come, which shall oppress Egypt, and the land shall not be consumed with scarcity.
verses.textLatin: Et præparetur futuræ septem annorum fami, quæ oppressura est Ægyptum, et non consumetur terra inopia.

verses.text: The counsel pleased Pharao and all his servants.
verses.textLatin: Placuit Pharaoni consilium et cunctis ministris ejus:

verses.text: And he said to them: Can we find such another man, that is full of the spirit of God?
verses.textLatin: locutusque est ad eos: Num invenire poterimus talem virum, qui spiritu Dei plenus sit?

verses.text: He said therefore to Joseph: Seeing God hath shewn thee all that thou hast said, can I find one wiser and one like unto thee?
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo ad Joseph: Quia ostendit tibi Deus omnia quæ locutus es, numquid sapientiorem et consimilem tui invenire potero?

verses.text: Thou shalt be over my house, and at the commandment of thy mouth all the people shall obey: only in the kingly throne will I be above thee.
verses.textLatin: Tu eris super domum meam, et ad tui oris imperium cunctus populus obediet: uno tantum regni solio te præcedam.

verses.text: And again Pharao said to Joseph: Behold, I have appointed thee over the whole land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque rursus Pharao ad Joseph: Ecce, constitui te super universam terram Ægypti.
