verses.text: And he took his ring from his own hand, and gave it into his hand: and he put upon him a robe of silk, and put a chain of gold about his neck.
verses.textLatin: Tulitque annulum de manu sua, et dedit eum in manu ejus: vestivitque eum stola byssina, et collo torquem auream circumposuit.

verses.text: And he made him go up into his second chariot, the crier proclaiming that all should bow their knee before him, and that they should know he was made governor over the whole land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque eum ascendere super currum suum secundum, clamante præcone, ut omnes coram eo genu flecterent, et præpositum esse scirent universæ terræ Ægypti.

verses.text: And the king said to Joseph: I am Pharao; without thy commandment no man shall move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque rex ad Joseph: Ego sum Pharao: absque tuo imperio non movebit quisquam manum aut pedem in omni terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And he turned his name, and called him in the Egyptian tongue, The saviour of the world. And he gave him to wife Aseneth the daughter of Putiphare priest of Heliopolis. Then Joseph went out to the land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Vertitque nomen ejus, et vocavit eum, lingua ægyptiaca, Salvatorem mundi. Deditque illi uxorem Aseneth filiam Putiphare sacerdotis Heliopoleos. Egressus est itaque Joseph ad terram Ægypti

verses.text: (Now he was thirty years old when he stood before king Pharao) and he went round all the countries of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: (triginta autem annorum erat quando stetit in conspectu regis Pharaonis), et circuivit omnes regiones Ægypti.

verses.text: And the fruitfulness of the seven years came: and the corn being bound up into sheaves was gathered together into the barns of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Venitque fertilitas septem annorum: et in manipulos redactæ segetes congregatæ sunt in horrea Ægypti.

verses.text: And all the abundance of grain was laid up in every city.
verses.textLatin: Omnis etiam frugum abundantia in singulis urbibus condita est.

verses.text: And there was so great abundance of wheat, that it was equal to the sand of the sea, and the plenty exceeded measure.
verses.textLatin: Tantaque fuit abundantia tritici, ut arenæ maris coæquaretur, et copia mensuram excederet.

verses.text: And before the famine came, Joseph had two sons born: whom Aseneth the daughter of Putiphare priest of Heliopolis bore unto him.
verses.textLatin: Nati sunt autem Joseph filii duo antequam veniret fames: quos peperit ei Aseneth filia Putiphare sacerdotis Heliopoleos.

verses.text: And he called the name of the firstborn Manasses, saying: God hath made me to forget all my labours, and my father’s house.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque nomen primogeniti Manasses, dicens: Oblivisci me fecit Deus omnium laborum meorum, et domus patris mei.

verses.text: And he named the second Ephraim, saying: God hath made me to grow in the land of my poverty.
verses.textLatin: Nomen quoque secundi appellavit Ephraim, dicens: Crescere me fecit Deus in terra paupertatis meæ.

verses.text: Now when the seven years of the plenty that had been in Egypt were past:
verses.textLatin: Igitur transactis septem ubertatis annis, qui fuerant in Ægypto,

verses.text: The seven years of scarcity, which Joseph had foretold, began to come: and the famine prevailed in the whole world, but there was bread in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: cœperunt venire septem anni inopiæ, quos prædixerat Joseph: et in universo orbe fames prævaluit, in cuncta autem terra Ægypti panis erat.

verses.text: And when there also they began to be famished, the people cried to Pharao for food. And he said to them: Go to Joseph: and do all that he shall say to you.
verses.textLatin: Qua esuriente, clamavit populus ad Pharaonem, alimenta petens. Quibus ille respondit: Ite ad Joseph: et quidquid ipse vobis dixerit, facite.

verses.text: And the famine increased daily in all the land: and Joseph opened all the barns, and sold to the Egyptians: for the famine had oppressed them also.
verses.textLatin: Crescebat autem quotidie fames in omni terra: aperuitque Joseph universa horrea, et vendebat Ægyptiis: nam et illos oppresserat fames.

verses.text: And all provinces came into Egypt, to buy food, and to seek some relief of their want.
verses.textLatin: Omnesque provinciæ veniebant in Ægyptum, ut emerent escas, et malum inopiæ temperarent.

verses.text: And  Jacob hearing that food was sold in Egypt, said to his sons: Why are ye careless?
verses.textLatin: Audiens autem Jacob quod alimenta venderentur in Ægypto, dixit filiis suis: Quare negligitis?

verses.text: I have heard that wheat is sold in Egypt: go ye down, and buy us necessaries, that we may live, and not be consumed with want.
verses.textLatin: audivi quod triticum venundetur in Ægypto: descendite, et emite nobis necessaria, ut possimus vivere, et non consumamur inopia.

verses.text: So the ten brethren of Joseph went down, to buy corn in Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Descendentes igitur fratres Joseph decem, ut emerent frumenta in Ægypto,

verses.text: Whilst Benjamin was kept at home by Jacob, who said to his brethren: Lest perhaps he take any harm in the journey.
verses.textLatin: Benjamin domi retento a Jacob, qui dixerat fratribus ejus: Ne forte in itinere quidquam patiatur mali:

verses.text: And they entered into the land of Egypt with others that went to buy. For the famine was in the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: ingressi sunt terram Ægypti cum aliis qui pergebant ad emendum. Erat autem fames in terra Chanaan.

verses.text: And Joseph was governor in the land of Egypt, and corn was sold by his direction to the people. And when his brethren had bowed down to him,
verses.textLatin: Et Joseph erat princeps in terra Ægypti, atque ad ejus nutum frumenta populis vendebantur. Cumque adorassent eum fratres sui,

verses.text: And he knew them, he spoke as it were to strangers somewhat roughly, asking them: Whence came you? They answered: From the land of Chanaan, to buy necessaries of life.
verses.textLatin: et agnovisset eos, quasi ad alienos durius loquebatur, interrogans eos: Unde venistis? Qui responderunt: De terra Chanaan, ut emamus victui necessaria.

verses.text: And though he knew his brethren, he was not known by them.
verses.textLatin: Et tamen fratres ipse cognoscens, non est cognitus ab eis.

verses.text: And remembering the dreams, which formerly he had dreamed, he said to them: You are spies. You are come to view the weaker parts of the land.
verses.textLatin: Recordatusque somniorum, quæ aliquando viderat, ait ad eos: Exploratores estis: ut videatis infirmiora terræ venistis.

verses.text: But they said: It is not so, my lord, but thy servants are come to buy food.
verses.textLatin: Qui dixerunt: Non est ita, domine, sed servi tui venerunt ut emerent cibos.

verses.text: We are all the sons of one man: we are come as peaceable men, neither do thy servants go about any evil.
verses.textLatin: Omnes filii unius viri sumus: pacifici venimus, nec quidquam famuli tui machinantur mali.

verses.text: And he answered them: It is otherwise: you are come to consider the unfenced parts of this land.
verses.textLatin: Quibus ille respondit: Aliter est: immunita terræ hujus considerare venistis.

verses.text: But they said: We thy servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Chanaan: the youngest is with our father, the other is not living.
verses.textLatin: At illi: Duodecim, inquiunt, servi tui, fratres sumus, filii viri unius in terra Chanaan: minimus cum patre nostro est, alius non est super.

verses.text: He saith: This is it that I said: You are spies.
verses.textLatin: Hoc est, ait, quod locutus sum: exploratores estis.

verses.text: I shall now presently try what you are: by the health of Pharao you shall not depart hence, until your youngest brother come.
verses.textLatin: Jam nunc experimentum vestri capiam: per salutem Pharaonis non egrediemini hinc, donec veniat frater vester minimus.

verses.text: Send one of you to fetch him: and you shall be in prison, till what you have said be proved, whether it be true or false: or else by the health of Pharao you are spies.
verses.textLatin: Mittite ex vobis unum, et adducat eum: vos autem eritis in vinculis, donec probentur quæ dixistis utrum vera an falsa sint: alioquin per salutem Pharaonis exploratores estis.

verses.text: So he put them in prison three days.
verses.textLatin: Tradidit ergo illos custodiæ tribus diebus.

verses.text: And the third day he brought them out of prison, and said: Do as I have said, and you shall live: for I fear God.
verses.textLatin: Die autem tertio eductis de carcere, ait: Facite quæ dixi, et vivetis: Deum enim timeo.

verses.text: If you be peaceable men, let one of your brethren be bound in prison: and go ye your ways and carry the corn that you have bought, unto your houses.
verses.textLatin: Si pacifici estis, frater vester unus ligetur in carcere: vos autem abite, et ferte frumenta quæ emistis, in domos vestras,

verses.text: And bring your youngest brother to me, that I may find your words to be true, and you may not die. They did as he had said.
verses.textLatin: et fratrem vestrum minimum ad me adducite, ut possim vestros probare sermones, et non moriamini. Fecerunt ut dixerat,

verses.text: And they talked one to another: We deserve to suffer these things, because we have sinned against our brother, seeing the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear: therefore is this affliction come upon us.
verses.textLatin: et locuti sunt ad invicem: Merito hæc patimur, quia peccavimus in fratrem nostrum, videntes angustiam animæ illius, dum deprecaretur nos, et non audivimus: idcirco venit super nos ista tribulatio.

verses.text: And Ruben, one of them, said: Did not I say to you: Do not sin against the boy: and you would not hear me? Behold his blood is required.
verses.textLatin: E quibus unus Ruben, ait: Numquid non dixi vobis: Nolite peccare in puerum: et non audistis me? en sanguis ejus exquiritur.

verses.text: And they knew not that Joseph understood, because he spoke to them by an interpreter.
verses.textLatin: Nesciebant autem quod intelligeret Joseph, eo quod per interpretem loqueretur ad eos.

verses.text: And he turned himself away a little while, and wept: and returning he spoke to them.
verses.textLatin: Avertitque se parumper, et flevit: et reversus locutus est ad eos.

verses.text: And taking Simeon, and binding him in their presence, he commanded his servants to fill their sacks with wheat, and to put every man’s money again in their sacks, and to give them besides provisions for the way: and they did so.
verses.textLatin: Tollensque Simeon, et ligans illis præsentibus, jussit ministris ut implerent eorum saccos tritico, et reponerent pecunias singulorum in sacculis suis, datis supra cibariis in viam: qui fecerunt ita.

verses.text: But they having loaded their asses with the corn, went their way.
verses.textLatin: At illi portantes frumenta in asinis suis, profecti sunt.

verses.text: And one of them opening his sack, to give his beast provender in the inn, saw the money in the sack’s mouth;
verses.textLatin: Apertoque unus sacco, ut daret jumento pabulum in diversorio, contemplatus pecuniam in ore sacculi,

verses.text: And said to his brethren: My money is given me again, behold it is in the sack. And they were astonished, and troubled, and said to one another: What is this that God hath done unto us?
verses.textLatin: dixit fratribus suis: Reddita est mihi pecunia, en habetur in sacco. Et obstupefacti, turbatique, mutuo dixerunt: Quidnam est hoc quod fecit nobis Deus?

verses.text: And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Chanaan, and they told him all things that had befallen them, saying:
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque ad Jacob patrem suum in terram Chanaan, et narraverunt ei omnia quæ accidissent sibi, dicentes:

verses.text: The lord of the land spoke roughly to us, and took us to be spies of the country.
verses.textLatin: Locutus est nobis dominus terræ dure, et putavit nos exploratores esse provinciæ.

verses.text: And we answered him: We are peaceable men, and we mean no plot.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondimus: Pacifici sumus, nec ullas molimur insidias.

verses.text: We are twelve brethren born of one father: one is not living, the youngest is with our father in the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Duodecim fratres uno patre geniti sumus: unus non est super, minimus cum patre nostro est in terra Chanaan.

verses.text: And he said to us: Hereby shall I know that you are peaceable men: Leave one of your brethren with me, and take ye necessary provision for your houses, and go your ways.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait nobis: Sic probabo quod pacifici sitis: fratrem vestrum unum dimittite apud me, et cibaria domibus vestris necessaria sumite, et abite,

verses.text: And bring your youngest brother to me, that I may know you are not spies: and you may receive this man again, that is kept in prison: and afterwards may have leave to buy what you will.
verses.textLatin: fratremque vestrum minimum adducite ad me, ut sciam quod non sitis exploratores: et istum, qui tenetur in vinculis, recipere possitis: ac deinceps quæ vultis, emendi habeatis licentiam.

verses.text: When they had told this, they poured out their corn, and every man found his money tied in the mouth of his sack: and all being astonished together,
verses.textLatin: His dictis, cum frumenta effunderent, singuli repererunt in ore saccorum ligatas pecunias, exterritisque simul omnibus,

verses.text: Their father Jacob said: You have made me to be without children: Joseph is not living, Simeon is kept in bonds, and Benjamin you will take away: all these evils are fallen upon me.
verses.textLatin: dixit pater Jacob: Absque liberis me esse fecistis: Joseph non est super, Simeon tenetur in vinculis, et Benjamin auferetis: in me hæc omnia mala reciderunt.

verses.text: And Ruben answered him: Kill my two sons, if I bring him not again to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will restore him to thee.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Ruben: Duos filios meos interfice, si non reduxero illum tibi: trade illum in manu mea, et ego eum tibi restituam.

verses.text: But he said: My son shall not go down with you: his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if any mischief befall him in the land to which you go, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to hell.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Non descendet, inquit, filius meus vobiscum: frater ejus mortuus est, et ipse solus remansit: si quid ei adversi acciderit in terra ad quam pergitis, deducetis canos meos cum dolore ad inferos.

verses.text: In  the mean time the famine was heavy upon all the land.
verses.textLatin: Interim fames omnem terram vehementer premebat.

verses.text: And when they had eaten up all the corn, which they had brought out of Egypt, Jacob said to his sons: Go again and buy us a little food.
verses.textLatin: Consumptisque cibis quos ex Ægypto detulerant, dixit Jacob ad filios suos: Revertimini, et emite nobis pauxillum escarum.

verses.text: Juda answered: The man declared unto us with the attestation of an oath, saying: You shall not see my face, unless you bring your youngest brother with you.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Judas: Denuntiavit nobis vir ille sub attestatione jurisjurandi, dicens: Non videbitis faciem meam, nisi fratrem vestrum minimum adduxeritis vobiscum.

verses.text: If therefore thou wilt send him with us, we will set out together, and will buy necessaries for thee.
verses.textLatin: Si ergo vis eum mittere nobiscum, pergemus pariter, et ememus tibi necessaria:

verses.text: But if thou wilt not, we will not go: for the man, as we have often said, declared unto us, saying: You shall not see my face without your youngest brother.
verses.textLatin: sin autem non vis, non ibimus: vir enim, ut sæpe diximus, denuntiavit nobis, dicens: Non videbitis faciem meam absque fratre vestro minimo.

verses.text: Israel said to them: You have done this for my misery in that you told him you had also another brother.
verses.textLatin: Dixit eis Israël: In meam hoc fecistis miseriam, ut indicaretis ei et alium habere vos fratrem.

verses.text: But they answered: The man asked us in order concerning our kindred: if our father lived: if we had a brother: and we answered him regularly, according to what he demanded: could we know that he would say: Bring hither your brother with you?
verses.textLatin: At illi responderunt: Interrogavit nos homo per ordinem nostram progeniem: si pater viveret: si haberemus fratrem: et nos respondimus ei consequenter juxta id quod fuerat sciscitatus: numquid scire poteramus quod dicturus esset: Adducite fratrem vestrum vobiscum?

verses.text: And Juda said to his father: Send the boy with me, that we may set forward, and may live: lest both we and our children perish.
verses.textLatin: Judas quoque dixit patri suo: Mitte puerum mecum, ut proficiscamur, et possimus vivere: ne moriamur nos et parvuli nostri.

verses.text: I take the boy upon me, require him at my hand: unless I bring him again, and restore him to thee, I will be guilty of sin against thee for ever.
verses.textLatin: Ego suscipio puerum: de manu mea require illum: nisi reduxero, et reddidero eum tibi, ero peccati reus in te omni tempore.

verses.text: If delay had not been made, we had been here again the second time.
verses.textLatin: Si non intercessisset dilatio, jam vice alter venissemus.

verses.text: Then Israel said to them: If it must needs be so, do what you will: take of the best fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down presents to the man, a little balm, and honey, and storax, myrrh, turpentine, and almonds.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Israël pater eorum dixit ad eos: Si sic necesse est, facite quod vultis: sumite de optimis terræ fructibus in vasis vestris, et deferte viro munera, modicum resinæ, et mellis, et storacis, stactes, et terebinthi, et amygdalarum.

verses.text: And take with you double money, and carry back what you found in your sacks, lest perhaps it was done by mistake.
verses.textLatin: Pecuniam quoque duplicem ferte vobiscum: et illam, quam invenistis in sacculis, reportate, ne forte errore factum sit:

verses.text: And take also your brother, and go to the man.
verses.textLatin: sed et fratrem vestrum tollite, et ite ad virum.

verses.text: And may my almighty God make him favourable to you; and send back with you your brother, whom he keepeth, and this Benjamin: and as for me I shall be desolate without children.
verses.textLatin: Deus autem meus omnipotens faciat vobis eum placabilem: et remittat vobiscum fratrem vestrum quem tenet, et hunc Benjamin: ego autem quasi orbatus absque liberis ero.

verses.text: So the men took the presents, and double money, and Benjamin: and went down into Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.textLatin: Tulerunt ergo viri munera, et pecuniam duplicem, et Benjamin: descenderuntque in Ægyptum, et steterunt coram Joseph.

verses.text: And when he had seen them, and Benjamin with them, he commanded the steward of his house, saying: Bring in the men into the house, and kill victims, and prepare a feast: because they shall eat with me at noon.
verses.textLatin: Quos cum ille vidisset et Benjamin simul, præcepit dispensatori domus suæ, dicens: Introduc viros domum, et occide victimas, et instrue convivium: quoniam mecum sunt comesturi meridie.

verses.text: He did as he was commanded, and brought the men into the house.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ille quod sibi fuerat imperatum, et introduxit viros domum.

verses.text: And they being much afraid, said there one to another: Because of the money, which we carried back the first time in our sacks, we are brought in: that he may bring upon us a false accusation, and by violence make slaves of us and our asses.
verses.textLatin: Ibique exterriti, dixerunt mutuo: Propter pecuniam, quam retulimus prius in saccis nostris, introducti sumus: ut devolvat in nos calumniam, et violenter subjiciat servituti et nos, et asinos nostros.

verses.text: Wherefore going up to the steward of the house, at the door,
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem in ipsis foribus accedentes ad dispensatorem domus,

verses.text: They said: Sir, we desire thee to hear us. We came down once before to buy food:
verses.textLatin: locuti sunt: Oramus, domine, ut audias nos. Jam ante descendimus ut emeremus escas:

verses.text: And when we had bought, and come to the inn, we opened our sacks, and found our money in the mouths of the sacks: which we have now brought again in the same weight.
verses.textLatin: quibus emptis, cum venissemus ad diversorium, aperuimus saccos nostros, et invenimus pecuniam in ore saccorum: quam nunc eodem pondere reportavimus.

verses.text: And we have brought other money besides, to buy what we want: we cannot tell who put it in our bags.
verses.textLatin: Sed et aliud attulimus argentum, ut emamus quæ nobis necessaria sunt: non est in nostra conscientia quis posuerit eam in marsupiis nostris.

verses.text: But he answered: Peace be with you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father hath given you treasure in your sacks. For the money, which you gave me, I have for good. And he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.textLatin: At ille respondit: Pax vobiscum, nolite timere: Deus vester, et Deus patris vestri, dedit vobis thesauros in saccis vestris: nam pecuniam, quam dedistis mihi, probatam ego habeo. Eduxitque ad eos Simeon.

verses.text: And having brought them into the house, he fetched water, and they washed their feet, and he gave provender to their asses.
verses.textLatin: Et introductis domum, attulit aquam, et laverunt pedes suos, deditque pabulum asinis eorum.

verses.text: But they made ready the presents, against Joseph came at noon: for they had heard that they should eat bread there.
verses.textLatin: Illi vero parabant munera, donec ingrederetur Joseph meridie: audierant enim quod ibi comesturi essent panem.

verses.text: Then Joseph came into his house, and they offered him the presents holding them in their hands, and they bowed down with their face to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Igitur ingressus est Joseph domum suam, obtuleruntque ei munera, tenentes in manibus suis: et adoraverunt proni in terram.

verses.text: But he, courteously saluting them again, asked them, saying: Is the old man your father in health, of whom you told me? Is he yet living?
verses.textLatin: At ille, clementer resalutatis eis, interrogavit eos, dicens: Salvusne est pater vester senex, de quo dixeratis mihi? adhuc vivit?

verses.text: And they answered: Thy servant our father is in health, he is yet living. And bowing themselves they made obeisance to him.
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Sospes est servus tuus pater noster, adhuc vivit. Et incurvati, adoraverunt eum.

verses.text: And Joseph lifting up his eyes, saw Benjamin his brother, by the same mother, and said: Is this your young brother, of whom you told me? And he said: God be gracious to thee, my son.
verses.textLatin: Attollens autem Joseph oculos, vidit Benjamin fratrem suum uterinum, et ait: Iste est frater vester parvulus, de quo dixeratis mihi? Et rursum: Deus, inquit, misereatur tui, fili mi.

verses.text: And he made haste because his heart was moved upon his brother, and tears gushed out: and going into his chamber he wept.
verses.textLatin: Festinavitque, quia commota fuerant viscera ejus super fratre suo, et erumpebant lacrimæ: et introiens cubiculum flevit.

verses.text: And when he had washed his face, coming out again, he refrained himself, and said: Set bread on the table.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque lota facie egressus, continuit se, et ait: Ponite panes.

verses.text: And when it was set on, for Joseph apart, and for his brethren apart, for the Egyptians also that ate with him, apart, (for it is unlawful for the Egyptians to eat with the Hebrews, and they think such a feast profane:)
verses.textLatin: Quibus appositis, seorsum Joseph, et seorsum fratribus, Ægyptiis quoque qui vescebantur simul, seorsum (illicitum est enim Ægyptiis comedere cum Hebræis, et profanum putant hujuscemodi convivium)

verses.text: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his age. And they wondered very much:
verses.textLatin: sederunt coram eo, primogenitus juxta primogenita sua, et minimus juxta ætatem suam. Et mirabantur nimis,

verses.text: Taking the messes which they received of him: and the greater mess came to Benjamin, so that it exceeded by five parts. And they drank, and were merry with him.
verses.textLatin: sumptis partibus quas ab eo acceperant: majorque pars venit Benjamin, ita ut quinque partibus excederet. Biberuntque et inebriati sunt cum eo.

verses.text: And  Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying: Fill their sacks with corn, as much as they can hold: and put the money of every one in the top of his sack.
verses.textLatin: Præcepit autem Joseph dispensatori domus suæ, dicens: Imple saccos eorum frumento, quantum possunt capere: et pone pecuniam singulorum in summitate sacci.

verses.text: And in the mouth of the younger’s sack put my silver cup, and the price which he gave for the wheat. And it was so done.
verses.textLatin: Scyphum autem meum argenteum, et pretium quod dedit tritici, pone in ore sacci junioris. Factumque est ita.

verses.text: And when the morning arose, they were sent away with their asses.
verses.textLatin: Et orto mane, dimissi sunt cum asinis suis.

verses.text: And when they were now departed out of the city, and had gone forward a little way; Joseph sending for the steward of his house, said: Arise, and pursue after the men: and when thou hast overtaken them, say to them: Why have you returned evil for good?
verses.textLatin: Jamque urbem exierant, et processerant paululum: tunc Joseph accersito dispensatore domus, Surge, inquit, et persequere viros: et apprehensis dicito: Quare reddidistis malum pro bono?

verses.text: The cup which you have stolen is that in which my lord drinketh, and in which he is wont to divine: you have done a very evil thing.
verses.textLatin: scyphus, quem furati estis, ipse est in quo bibit dominus meus, et in quo augurari solet: pessimam rem fecistis.

verses.text: He did as he had commanded him. And having overtaken them, he spoke to them the same words.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ille ut jusserat: et apprehensis per ordinem locutus est.

verses.text: And they answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Quare sic loquitur dominus noster, ut servi tui tantum flagitii commiserint?

verses.text: The money, that we found in the top of our sacks, we brought back to thee from the land of Chanaan: how then should it be that we should steal out of thy lord’s house, gold or silver?
verses.textLatin: pecuniam, quam invenimus in summitate saccorum, reportavimus ad te de terra Chanaan: et quomodo consequens est ut furati simus de domo domini tui aurum vel argentum?

verses.text: With whomsoever of thy servants shall be found that which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of my lord.
verses.textLatin: apud quemcumque fuerit inventum servorum tuorum quod quæris, moriatur, et nos erimus servi domini nostri.

verses.text: And he said to them: Let it be according to your sentence: with whomsoever it shall be found, let him be my servant, and you shall be blameless.
verses.textLatin: Qui dixit eis: Fiat juxta vestram sententiam: apud quemcumque fuerit inventum, ipse sit servus meus, vos autem eritis innoxii.

verses.text: Then they speedily took down their sacks to the ground, and every man opened his sack.
verses.textLatin: Itaque festinato deponentes in terram saccos, aperuerunt singuli.

verses.text: Which when he had searched, beginning at the eldest and ending at the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin’s sack.
verses.textLatin: Quos scrutatus, incipiens a majore usque ad minimum, invenit scyphum in sacco Benjamin.

verses.text: Then they rent their garments, and loading their asses again, returned into the town.
verses.textLatin: At illi, scissis vestibus, oneratisque rursum asinis, reversi sunt in oppidum.

verses.text: And Juda at the head of his brethren went in to Joseph, (for he was not yet gone out of the place,) and they altogether fell down before him on the ground.
verses.textLatin: Primusque Judas cum fratribus ingressus est ad Joseph (necdum enim de loco abierat) omnesque ante eum pariter in terram corruerunt.

verses.text: And he said to them: Why would you do so? know you not that there is no one like me in the science of divining.
verses.textLatin: Quibus ille ait: Cur sic agere voluistis? an ignoratis quod non sit similis mei in augurandi scientia?

verses.text: And Juda said to him: What shall we answer my lord? or what shall we say, or be able justly to allege? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are all bondmen to my lord, both we, and he with whom the cup was found.
verses.textLatin: Cui Judas: Quid respondebimus, inquit, domino meo? vel quid loquemur, aut juste poterimus obtendere? Deus invenit iniquitatem servorum tuorum: en omnes servi sumus domini mei, et nos, et apud quem inventus est scyphus.

verses.text: Joseph answered: God forbid that I should do so: he that stole the cup, he shall be my bondman: and go you away free to your father.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Joseph: Absit a me ut sic agam: qui furatus est scyphum, ipse sit servus meus: vos autem abite liberi ad patrem vestrum.

verses.text: Then Juda coming nearer, said boldly: I beseech thee, my lord, let thy servant speak a word in thy ears, and be not angry with thy servant: for after Pharao thou art.
verses.textLatin: Accedens autem propius Judas, confidenter ait: Oro, domine mi, loquatur servus tuus verbum in auribus tuis, et ne irascaris famulo tuo: tu es enim post Pharaonem

verses.text: My lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother?
verses.textLatin: dominus meus. Interrogasti prius servos tuos: Habetis patrem aut fratrem?

verses.text: And we answered thee, my lord: We have a father an old man, and a young boy, that was born in his old age; whose brother by the mother is dead: and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him tenderly.
verses.textLatin: et nos respondimus tibi domino meo: Est nobis pater senex, et puer parvulus, qui in senectute illius natus est: cujus uterinus frater mortuus est: et ipsum solum habet mater sua, pater vero tenere diligit eum.

verses.text: And thou saidst to thy servants: Bring him hither to me, and I will set my eyes on him.
verses.textLatin: Dixistique servis tuis: Adducite eum ad me, et ponam oculos meos super illum.

verses.text: We suggested to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father: for if he leave him, he will die.
verses.textLatin: Suggessimus domino meo: Non potest puer relinquere patrem suum: si enim illum dimiserit, morietur.

verses.text: And thou saidst to thy servants: Except your youngest brother come with you, you shall see my face no more.
verses.textLatin: Et dixisti servis tuis: Nisi venerit frater vester minimus vobiscum, non videbitis amplius faciem meam.

verses.text: Therefore when we were gone up to thy servant our father, we told him all that my lord had said.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo ascendissemus ad famulum tuum patrem nostrum, narravimus ei omnia quæ locutus est dominus meus.

verses.text: And our father said: Go again, and buy us a little wheat.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit pater noster: Revertimini, et emite nobis parum tritici.

verses.text: And we said to him: We cannot go: if our youngest brother go down with us, we will set out together: otherwise, without him we dare not see the man’s face.
verses.textLatin: Cui diximus: Ire non possumus: si frater noster minimus descenderit nobiscum, proficiscemur simul: alioquin illo absente, non audemus videre faciem viri.

verses.text: Whereunto he answered: You know that my wife bore me two.
verses.textLatin: Ad quæ ille respondit: Vos scitis quod duos genuerit mihi uxor mea.

verses.text: One went out, and you said: A beast devoured him: and hitherto he appeareth not.
verses.textLatin: Egressus est unus, et dixistis: Bestia devoravit eum: et hucusque non comparet.

verses.text: If you take this also, and any thing befall him in the way, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow unto hell.
verses.textLatin: Si tuleritis et istum, et aliquid ei in via contigerit, deducetis canos meos cum mœrore ad inferos.

verses.text: Therefore if I shall go to thy servant our father, and the boy be wanting, (whereas his life dependeth upon the life of him,)
verses.textLatin: Igitur si intravero ad servum tuum patrem nostrum, et puer defuerit (cum anima illius ex hujus anima pendeat),

verses.text: And he shall see that he is not with us, he will die, and thy servants shall bring down his gray hairs with sorrow unto hell.
verses.textLatin: videritque eum non esse nobiscum, morietur, et deducent famuli tui canos ejus cum dolore ad inferos.

verses.text: Let me be thy proper servant, who took him into my trust, and promised, saying: If I bring him not again, I will be guilty of sin against my father for ever.
verses.textLatin: Ego proprie servus tuus sim qui in meam hunc recepi fidem, et spopondi dicens: Nisi reduxero eum, peccati reus ero in patrem meum omni tempore.

verses.text: Therefore I thy servant will stay instead of the boy in the service of my lord, and let the boy go up with his brethren.
verses.textLatin: Manebo itaque servus tuus pro puero in ministerio domini mei, et puer ascendat cum fratribus suis.

verses.text: For I cannot return to my father without the boy, lest I be a witness of the calamity that will oppress my father.
verses.textLatin: Non enim possum redire ad patrem meum, absente puero: ne calamitatis, quæ oppressura est patrem meum, testis assistam.

verses.text: Joseph  could no longer refrain himself before many that stood by: whereupon he commanded that all should go out, and no stranger be present at their knowing one another.
verses.textLatin: Non se poterat ultra cohibere Joseph multis coram astantibus: unde præcepit ut egrederentur cuncti foras, et nullus interesset alienus agnitioni mutuæ.

verses.text: And he lifted up his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians and all the house of Pharao heard.
verses.textLatin: Elevavitque vocem cum fletu, quam audierunt Ægyptii, omnisque domus Pharaonis.

verses.text: And he said to his brethren: I am Joseph: is my father yet living? His brethren could not answer him, being struck with exceeding great fear.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit fratribus suis: Ego sum Joseph: adhuc pater meus vivit? Non poterant respondere fratres nimio terrore perterriti.

verses.text: And he said mildly to them: Come nearer to me. And when they were come near him, he said: I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Ad quos ille clementer: Accedite, inquit, ad me. Et cum accessissent prope: Ego sum, ait, Joseph, frater vester, quem vendidistis in Ægyptum.

verses.text: Be not afraid, and let it not seem to you a hard case that you sold me into these countries: for God sent me before you into Egypt for your preservation.
verses.textLatin: Nolite pavere, neque vobis durum esse videatur quod vendidistis me in his regionibus: pro salute enim vestra misit me Deus ante vos in Ægyptum.

verses.text: For it is two years since the famine began to be upon the land, and five years more remain, wherein there can be neither ploughing nor reaping.
verses.textLatin: Biennium est enim quod cœpit fames esse in terra: et adhuc quinque anni restant, quibus nec arari poterit, nec meti.

verses.text: And God sent me before, that you may be preserved upon the earth, and may have food to live.
verses.textLatin: Præmisitque me Deus ut reservemini super terram, et escas ad vivendum habere possitis.

verses.text: Not by your counsel was I sent hither, but by the will of God: who hath made me as it were a father to Pharao, and lord of his whole house, and governor in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Non vestro consilio, sed Dei voluntate huc missus sum: qui fecit me quasi patrem Pharaonis, et dominum universæ domus ejus, ac principem in omni terra Ægypti.

verses.text: Make haste, and go ye up to my father, and say to him: Thus saith thy son Joseph: God hath made me lord of the whole land of Egypt: come down to me, linger not.
verses.textLatin: Festinate, et ascendite ad patrem meum, et dicetis ei: Hæc mandat filius tuus Joseph: Deus fecit me dominum universæ terræ Ægypti: descende ad me, ne moreris,

verses.text: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Gessen: and thou shalt be near me, thou and thy sons, and thy sons’ sons, thy sheep, and thy herds, and all things that thou hast.
verses.textLatin: et habitabis in terra Gessen: erisque juxta me tu, et filii tui, et filii filiorum tuorum, oves tuæ, et armenta tua, et universa quæ possides:

verses.text: And there I will feed thee, (for there are yet five years of famine remaining,) lest both thou perish, and thy house, and all things that thou hast.
verses.textLatin: ibique te pascam (adhuc enim quinque anni residui sunt famis) ne et tu pereas, et domus tua, et omnia quæ possides.

verses.text: Behold, your eyes, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my mouth that speaketh to you.
verses.textLatin: En oculi vestri, et oculi fratris mei Benjamin, vident quod os meum loquatur ad vos.

verses.text: You shall tell my father of all my glory, and all things that you have seen in Egypt: make haste and bring him to me.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiate patri meo universam gloriam meam, et cuncta quæ vidistis in Ægypto: festinate, et adducite eum ad me.

verses.text: And falling upon the neck of his brother Benjamin, he embraced him and wept: and Benjamin in like manner wept also on his neck.
verses.textLatin: Cumque amplexatus recidisset in collum Benjamin fratris sui, flevit: illo quoque similiter flente super collum ejus.

verses.text: And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept upon every one of them: after which they were emboldened to speak to him.
verses.textLatin: Osculatusque est Joseph omnes fratres suos, et ploravit super singulos: post quæ ausi sunt loqui ad eum.

verses.text: And it was heard, and the fame was abroad in the king’s court: The brethren of Joseph are come: and Pharao with all his family was glad.
verses.textLatin: Auditumque est, et celebri sermone vulgatum in aula regis: Venerunt fratres Joseph: et gavisus est Pharao, atque omnis familia ejus.

verses.text: And he spoke to Joseph that he should give orders to his brethren, saying: Load your beasts, and go into the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Joseph ut imperaret fratribus suis, dicens: Onerantes jumenta, ite in terram Chanaan,

verses.text: And bring away from thence your father and kindred, and come to me: and I will give you all the good things of Egypt, that you may eat the marrow of the land.
verses.textLatin: et tollite inde patrem vestrum et cognationem, et venite ad me: et ego dabo vobis omnia bona Ægypti, ut comedatis medullam terræ.

verses.text: Give orders also that they take wagons out of the land of Egypt, for the carriage of their children and their wives: and say: Take up your father, and make haste to come with all speed:
verses.textLatin: Præcipe etiam ut tollant plaustra de terra Ægypti, ad subvectionem parvulorum suorum ac conjugum: et dicito: Tollite patrem vestrum, et properate quantocius venientes.

verses.text: And leave nothing of your household stuff: for all the riches of Egypt shall be yours.
verses.textLatin: Nec dimittatis quidquam de supellectili vestra: quia omnes opes Ægypti vestræ erunt.

verses.text: And the sons of Israel did as they were bid. And Joseph gave them wagons according to Pharao’s commandment: and provisions for the way.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque filii Israël ut eis mandatum fuerat. Quibus dedit Joseph plaustra, secundum Pharaonis imperium, et cibaria in itinere.

verses.text: He ordered also to be brought out for every one of them two robes: but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver with five robes of the best:
verses.textLatin: Singulis quoque proferri jussit binas stolas: Benjamin vero dedit trecentos argenteos cum quinque stolis optimis:

verses.text: Sending to his father as much money and raiment, adding besides ten he asses to carry off all the riches of Egypt, and as many she asses, carrying wheat and bread for the journey.
verses.textLatin: tantumdem pecuniæ et vestium mittens patri suo, addens et asinos decem, qui subveherent ex omnibus divitiis Ægypti, et totidem asinas, triticum in itinere, panesque portantes.

verses.text: So he sent away his brethren, and at their departing said to them: Be not angry in the way.
verses.textLatin: Dimisit ergo fratres suos, et proficiscentibus ait: Ne irascamini in via.

verses.text: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Chanaan to their father Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Qui ascendentes ex Ægypto, venerunt in terram Chanaan ad patrem suum Jacob.

verses.text: And they told him, saying: Joseph thy son is living: and he is ruler in all the land of Egypt. Which when Jacob heard, he awaked as it were out of a deep sleep, yet did not believe them.
verses.textLatin: Et nuntiaverunt ei, dicentes: Joseph filius tuus vivit: et ipse dominatur in omni terra Ægypti. Quo audito Jacob, quasi de gravi somno evigilans, tamen non credebat eis.

verses.text: They, on the other side, told the whole order of the thing. And when he saw the wagons and all that he had sent his spirit revived,
verses.textLatin: Illi e contra referebant omnem ordinem rei. Cumque vidisset plaustra et universa quæ miserat, revixit spiritus ejus,

verses.text: And he said: It is enough for me, if Joseph my son be yet living: I will go and see him before I die.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Sufficit mihi si adhuc Joseph filius meus vivit: vadam, et videbo illum antequam moriar.

verses.text: And  Israel taking his journey, with all that he had, came to the well of the oath, and killing victims there to the God of his father Isaac,
verses.textLatin: Profectusque Israël cum omnibus quæ habebat, venit ad Puteum juramenti: et mactatis ibi victimis Deo patris sui Isaac,

verses.text: He heard him by a vision in the night calling him, and saying to him: Jacob, Jacob. And he answered him: Lo, here I am.
verses.textLatin: audivit eum per visionem noctis vocantem se, et dicentem sibi: Jacob, Jacob. Cui respondit: Ecce adsum.

verses.text: God said to him: I am the most mighty God of thy father: fear not, go down into Egypt, for I will make a great nation of thee there.
verses.textLatin: Ait illi Deus: Ego sum fortissimus Deus patris tui: noli timere, descende in Ægyptum, quia in gentem magnam faciam te ibi.

verses.text: I will go down with thee thither, and will bring thee back again from thence: Joseph also shall put his hands upon thy eyes.
verses.textLatin: Ego descendam tecum illuc, et ego inde adducam te revertentem: Joseph quoque ponet manus suas super oculos tuos.

verses.text: And Jacob rose up from the well of the oath: and his sons took him up, with their children and wives in the wagons, which Pharao had sent to carry the old man,
verses.textLatin: Surrexit autem Jacob a Puteo juramenti: tuleruntque eum filii cum parvulis et uxoribus suis in plaustris quæ miserat Pharao ad portandum senem,

verses.text: And all that he had in the land of Chanaan, and he came into Egypt with all his seed:
verses.textLatin: et omnia quæ possederat in terra Chanaan: venitque in Ægyptum cum omni semine suo,

verses.text: His sons, and grandsons, daughters, and all his offspring together.
verses.textLatin: filii ejus, et nepotes, filiæ, et cuncta simul progenies.

verses.text: And these are the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Egypt, he and his children. His firstborn Ruben,
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt autem nomina filiorum Israël, qui ingressi sunt in Ægyptum, ipse cum liberis suis. Primogenitus Ruben.

verses.text: The sons of Ruben: Henoch and Phallu, and Hesron and Charmi.
verses.textLatin: Filii Ruben: Henoch et Phallu et Hesron et Charmi.

verses.text: The sons of Simeon: Jamuel and Jamin and Ahod, and Jachin and Sohar, and Saul the son of a woman of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Filii Simeon: Jamuel et Jamin et Ahod, et Jachin et Sohar, et Saul filius Chanaanitidis.

verses.text: The sons of Levi: Gerson and Caath and Merari.
verses.textLatin: Filii Levi: Gerson et Caath et Merari.

verses.text: The sons of Juda: Her and Onan and Sela and Phares and Zara. And Her and Onan died in the land of Chanaan. And sons were born to Phares: Hesron and Hamul.
verses.textLatin: Filii Juda: Her et Onan et Sela et Phares et Zara; mortui sunt autem Her et Onan in terra Chanaan. Natique sunt filii Phares: Hesron et Hamul.

verses.text: The sons of Issachar: Thola and Phua and Job and Semron.
verses.textLatin: Filii Issachar: Thola et Phua et Job et Semron.

verses.text: The sons of Zabulon: Sared and Elon and Jahelel.
verses.textLatin: Filii Zabulon: Sared et Elon et Jahelel.

verses.text: These are the sons of Lia, whom she bore in Mesopotamia of Syria, with Dina his daughter. All the souls of her sons and daughters, thirty-three.
verses.textLatin: Hi filii Liæ quos genuit in Mesopotamia Syriæ cum Dina filia sua: omnes animæ filiorum ejus et filiarum, triginta tres.

verses.text: The sons of Gad: Sephian and Haggi and Suni and Esebon and Heri and Arodi and Areli.
verses.textLatin: Filii Gad: Sephion et Haggi et Suni et Esebon et Heri et Arodi et Areli.

verses.text: The sons of Aser: Jamne and Jesua and Jessuri and Beria, and Sara their sister. The sons of Beria: Heber and Melchiel.
verses.textLatin: Filii Aser: Jamne et Jesua et Jessui et Beria, Sara quoque soror eorum. Filii Beria: Heber et Melchiel.

verses.text: These are the sons of Zelpha, whom Laban gave to Lia his daughter. And these she bore to Jacob, sixteen souls.
verses.textLatin: Hi filii Zelphæ, quam dedit Laban Liæ filiæ suæ: et hos genuit Jacob sedecim animas.

verses.text: The sons of Rachel Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.textLatin: Filii Rachel uxoris Jacob: Joseph et Benjamin.

verses.text: And sons were born to Joseph, in the land of Egypt, whom Aseneth the daughter of Putiphare priest of Heliopolis bore him: Manasses and Ephraim.
verses.textLatin: Natique sunt Joseph filii in terra Ægypti, quos genuit ei Aseneth filia Putiphare sacerdotis Heliopoleos: Manasses et Ephraim.

verses.text: The sons of Benjamin: Bela and Bechor and Asbel and Gera and Naaman and Echi and Ross and Mophim and Ophim and Ared.
verses.textLatin: Filii Benjamin: Bela et Bechor et Asbel et Gera et Naaman et Echi et Ros et Mophim et Ophim et Ared.

verses.text: These are the sons of Rachel, whom she bore to Jacob: all the souls, fourteen.
verses.textLatin: Hi filii Rachel quos genuit Jacob: omnes animæ, quatuordecim.

verses.text: The sons of Dan: Husim.
verses.textLatin: Filii Dan: Husim.

verses.text: The sons of Nephtali: Jaziel and Guni and Jeser and Sallem.
verses.textLatin: Filii Nephthali: Jasiel et Guni et Jeser et Sallem.

verses.text: These are the sons of Bala, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter: and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls, seven.
verses.textLatin: Hi filii Balæ, quam dedit Laban Racheli filiæ suæ: et hos genuit Jacob: omnes animæ, septem.

verses.text: All the souls that went with Jacob into Egypt, and that came out of his thigh, besides his sons’ wives, sixty-six.
verses.textLatin: Cunctæ animæ, quæ ingressæ sunt cum Jacob in Ægyptum, et egressæ sunt de femore illius, absque uxoribus filiorum ejus, sexaginta sex.

verses.text: And the sons of Joseph, that were born to him in the land of Egypt, two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Egypt, were seventy.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Joseph, qui nati sunt ei in terra Ægypti, animæ duæ. Omnes animæ domus Jacob, quæ ingressæ sunt in Ægyptum, fuere septuaginta.

verses.text: And he sent Juda before him to Joseph, to tell him; and that he should meet him in Gessen.
verses.textLatin: Misit autem Judam ante se ad Joseph, ut nuntiaret ei, et occurreret in Gessen.

verses.text: And when he was come thither, Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet his father, in the same place: and seeing him, he fell upon his neck, and embracing him wept.
verses.textLatin: Quo cum pervenisset, juncto Joseph curro suo, ascendit obviam patri suo ad eumdem locum: vidensque eum, irruit super collum ejus, et inter amplexus flevit.

verses.text: And the father said to Joseph: Now shall I die with joy, because I have seen thy face, and leave thee alive.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque pater ad Joseph: Jam lætus moriar, quia vidi faciem tuam, et superstitem te relinquo.

verses.text: And Joseph said to his brethren, and to all his father’s house: I will go up, and will tell Pharao, and will say to him: My brethren and my father’s house, that were in the land of Chanaan, are come to me:
verses.textLatin: At ille locutus est ad fratres suos, et ad omnem domum patris sui: Ascendam, et nuntiabo Pharaoni, dicamque ei: Fratres mei, et domus patris mei, qui erant in terra Chanaan, venerunt ad me:

verses.text: And the men are shepherds, and their occupation is to feed cattle: their flocks and herds, and all they have, they have brought with them.
verses.textLatin: et sunt viri pastores ovium, curamque habent alendorum gregum: pecora sua, et armenta, et omnia quæ habere potuerunt, adduxerunt secum.

verses.text: And when he shall call you, and shall say: What is your occupation?
verses.textLatin: Cumque vocaverit vos, et dixerit: Quod est opus vestrum?

verses.text: You shall answer: We thy servants are shepherds, from our infancy until now, both we and our fathers. And this you shall say, that you may dwell in the land of Gessen, because the Egyptians have all shepherds in abomination.
verses.textLatin: respondebitis: Viri pastores sumus servi tui, ab infantia nostra usque in præsens, et nos et patres nostri. Hæc autem dicetis, ut habitare possitis in terra Gessen: quia detestantur Ægyptii omnes pastores ovium.

verses.text: Then  Joseph went in and told Pharao, saying: My father and brethren, their sheep and their herds, and all that they possess, are come out of the land of Chanaan: and behold they stay in the land of Gessen.
verses.textLatin: Ingressus ergo Joseph nuntiavit Pharaoni, dicens: Pater meus et fratres, oves eorum et armenta, et cuncta quæ possident, venerunt de terra Chanaan: et ecce consistunt in terra Gessen.

verses.text: Five men also the last of his brethren, he presented before the king:
verses.textLatin: Extremos quoque fratrum suorum quinque viros constituit coram rege:

verses.text: And he asked them: What is your occupation? They answered: We thy servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.
verses.textLatin: quos ille interrogavit: Quid habetis operis? Responderunt: Pastores ovium sumus servi tui, et nos et patres nostri.

verses.text: We are come to sojourn in thy land, because there is no grass for the flocks of thy servants, the famine being very grievous in the land of Chanaan: and we pray thee to give orders that we thy servants may be in the land of Gessen.
verses.textLatin: Ad peregrinandum in terra tua venimus: quoniam non est herba gregibus servorum tuorum, ingravescente fame in terra Chanaan: petimusque ut esse nos jubeas servos tuos in terra Gessen.

verses.text: The king therefore said to Joseph: Thy father and thy brethren are come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixit itaque rex ad Joseph: Pater tuus et fratres tui venerunt ad te.

verses.text: The land of Egypt is before thee: and make them dwell in the best place, and give them the land of Gessen. And if thou knowest that there are industrious men among them, make them rulers over my cattle.
verses.textLatin: Terra Ægypti in conspectu tuo est: in optimo loco fac eos habitare, et trade eis terram Gessen. Quod si nosti in eis esse viros industrios, constitue illos magistros pecorum meorum.

verses.text: After this Joseph brought in his father to the king, and presented him before him: and he blessed him.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc introduxit Joseph patrem suum ad regem, et statuit eum coram eo: qui benedicens illi,

verses.text: And being asked by him: How many are the days of the years of thy life?
verses.textLatin: et interrogatus ab eo: Quot sunt dies annorum vitæ tuæ?

verses.text: He answered: The days of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years, few, and evil, and they are not come up to the days of the pilgrimage of my fathers.
verses.textLatin: respondit: Dies peregrinationis meæ centum triginta annorum sunt, parvi et mali, et non pervenerunt usque ad dies patrum meorum quibus peregrinati sunt.

verses.text: And blessing the king, he went out.
verses.textLatin: Et benedicto rege, egressus est foras.

verses.text: But Joseph gave a possession to his father and his brethren in Egypt, in the best place of the land, in Ramesses, as Pharao had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Joseph vero patri et fratribus suis dedit possessionem in Ægypto in optimo terræ loco, Ramesses, ut præceperat Pharao.

verses.text: And he nourished them, and all his father’s house, allowing food to every one.
verses.textLatin: Et alebat eos, omnemque domum patris sui, præbens cibaria singulis.

verses.text: For in the whole world there was want of bread, and a famine had oppressed the land: more especially of Egypt and Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: In toto enim orbe panis deerat, et oppresserat fames terram, maxime Ægypti et Chanaan.

verses.text: Out of which he gathered up all the money for the corn which they bought, and brought it into the king’s treasure.
verses.textLatin: E quibus omnem pecuniam congregavit pro venditione frumenti, et intulit eam in ærarium regis.

verses.text: And when the buyers wanted money, all Egypt came to Joseph, saying: Give us bread: why should we die in thy presence, having now no money.
verses.textLatin: Cumque defecisset emptoribus pretium, venit cuncta Ægyptus ad Joseph, dicens: Da nobis panes: quare morimur coram te, deficiente pecunia?

verses.text: And he answered them: Bring me your cattle, and for them I will give you food, if you have no money.
verses.textLatin: Quibus ille respondit: Adducite pecora vestra, et dabo vobis pro eis cibos, si pretium non habetis.

verses.text: And when they had brought them, he gave them food in exchange for their horses, and sheep, and oxen, and asses: and he maintained them that year for the exchange of their cattle.
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum adduxissent, dedit eis alimenta pro equis, et ovibus, et bobus, et asinis: sustentavitque eos illo anno pro commutatione pecorum.

verses.text: And they came the second year, and said to him: We will not hide from our lord, how that our money is spent, and our cattle also are gone: neither art thou ignorant that we have nothing now left but our bodies and our lands.
verses.textLatin: Venerunt quoque anno secundo, et dixerunt ei: Non celabimus dominum nostrum quod deficiente pecunia, pecora simul defecerunt: nec clam te est, quod absque corporibus et terra nihil habeamus.

verses.text: Why therefore shall we die before thy eyes? we will be thine, both we and our lands: buy us to be the king’s servants, and give us seed, lest for want of tillers the land be turned into a wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Cur ergo moriemur te vidente? et nos et terra nostra tui erimus: eme nos in servitutem regiam, et præbe semina, ne pereunte cultore redigatur terra in solitudinem.

verses.text: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt, every man selling his possessions, because of the greatness of the famine. And he brought it into Pharao’s hands:
verses.textLatin: Emit igitur Joseph omnem terram Ægypti, vendentibus singulis possessiones suas præ magnitudine famis. Subjecitque eam Pharaoni,

verses.text: And all its people from one end of the borders of Egypt, even to the other end thereof,
verses.textLatin: et cunctos populos ejus a novissimis terminis Ægypti usque ad extremos fines ejus,

verses.text: Except the land of the priests, which had been given them by the king: to whom also a certain allowance of food was given out of the public stores, and therefore they were not forced to sell their possessions.
verses.textLatin: præter terram sacerdotum, quæ a rege tradita fuerat eis: quibus et statuta cibaria ex horreis publicis præbebantur, et idcirco non sunt compulsi vendere possessiones suas.

verses.text: Then Joseph said to the people: Behold as you see, both you and your lands belong to Pharao: take seed and sow the fields,
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Joseph ad populos: En ut cernitis, et vos et terram vestram Pharao possidet: accipite semina, et serite agros,

verses.text: That you may have corn. The fifth part you shall give to the king: the other four you shall have for seed, and for food for your families and children.
verses.textLatin: ut fruges habere possitis. Quintam partem regi dabitis: quatuor reliquas permitto vobis in sementem, et in cibum familiis et liberis vestris.

verses.text: And they answered: Our life is in thy hand: only let my lord look favourably upon us, and we will gladly serve the king.
verses.textLatin: Qui responderunt: Salus nostra in manu tua est: respiciat nos tantum dominus noster, et læti serviemus regi.

verses.text: From that time unto this day, in the whole land of Egypt, the fifth part is paid to the king, and it is become as a law, except the land of the priests, which was free from this covenant.
verses.textLatin: Ex eo tempore usque in præsentem diem, in universa terra Ægypti regibus quinta pars solvitur, et factum est quasi in legem, absque terra sacerdotali, quæ libera ab hac conditione fuit.

verses.text: So Israel dwelt in Egypt, that is, in the land of Gessen, and possessed it: and grew, and was multiplied exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Habitavit ergo Israël in Ægypto, id est, in terra Gessen, et possedit eam: auctusque est, et multiplicatus nimis.

verses.text: And he lived in it seventeen years: and all the days of his life came to a hundred and forty-seven years.
verses.textLatin: Et vixit in ea decem et septem annis: factique sunt omnes dies vitæ illius, centum quadraginta septem annorum.

verses.text: And when he saw that the day of his death drew nigh, he called his son Joseph, and said to him: If I have found favour in thy sight, put thy hand under my thigh; and thou shalt shew me this kindness and truth, not to bury me in Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Cumque appropinquare cerneret diem mortis suæ, vocavit filium suum Joseph, et dixit ad eum: Si inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, pone manum tuam sub femore meo: et facies mihi misericordiam et veritatem, ut non sepelias me in Ægypto:

verses.text: But I will sleep with my fathers, and thou shalt take me away out of this land, and bury me in the buryingplace of my ancestors. And Joseph answered him: I will do what thou hast commanded.
verses.textLatin: sed dormiam cum patribus meis, et auferas me de terra hac, condasque in sepulchro majorum meorum. Cui respondit Joseph: Ego faciam quod jussisti.

verses.text: And he said: Swear then to me. And as he was swearing, Israel adored God, turning to the bed’s head.
verses.textLatin: Et ille: Jura ergo, inquit, mihi. Quo jurante, adoravit Israël Deum, conversus ad lectuli caput.

verses.text: After  these things, it was told Joseph that his father was sick: and he set out to go to him, taking his two sons Manasses and Ephraim.
verses.textLatin: His ita transactis, nuntiatum est Joseph quod ægrotaret pater suus: qui, assumptis duobus filiis Manasse et Ephraim, ire perrexit.

verses.text: And it was told the old man: Behold thy son Joseph cometh to thee. And being strengthened he sat on his bed.
verses.textLatin: Dictumque est seni: Ecce filius tuus Joseph venit ad te. Qui confortatus sedit in lectulo.

verses.text: And when Joseph was come in to him, he said: God Almighty appeared to me at Luza, which is in the land of Chanaan: and he blessed me,
verses.textLatin: Et ingresso ad se ait: Deus omnipotens apparuit mihi in Luza, quæ est in terra Chanaan: benedixitque mihi,

verses.text: And he said: I will cause thee to increase and multiply, and I will make of thee a multitude of people: and I will give this land to thee, and to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Ego te augebo et multiplicabo, et faciam te in turbas populorum: daboque tibi terram hanc, et semini tuo post te in possessionem sempiternam.

verses.text: So thy two sons who were born to thee in the land of Egypt before I came hither to thee, shall be mine: Ephraim and Manasses shall be reputed to me as Ruben and Simeon.
verses.textLatin: Duo ergo filii tui, qui nati sunt tibi in terra Ægypti antequam huc venirem ad te, mei erunt: Ephraim et Manasses, sicut Ruben et Simeon reputabuntur mihi.

verses.text: But the rest whom thou shalt have after them, shall be thine, and shall be called by the name of their brethren in their possessions.
verses.textLatin: Reliquos autem quos genueris post eos, tui erunt, et nomine fratrum suorum vocabuntur in possessionibus suis.

verses.text: For, when I came out of Mesopotamia, Rachel died from me in the land of Chanaan in the very journey, and it was springtime: and I was going to Ephrata, and I buried her near the way of Ephrata, which by another name is called Bethlehem.
verses.textLatin: Mihi enim, quando veniebam de Mesopotamia, mortua est Rachel in terra Chanaan in ipso itinere, eratque vernum tempus: et ingrediebar Ephratam, et sepelivi eam juxta viam Ephratæ, quæ alio nomine appellatur Bethlehem.

verses.text: Then seeing his sons, he said to him: Who are these?
verses.textLatin: Videns autem filios ejus dixit ad eum: Qui sunt isti?

verses.text: He answered: They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said: Bring them to me that I may bless them.
verses.textLatin: Respondit: Filii mei sunt, quos donavit mihi Deus in hoc loco. Adduc, inquit, eos ad me, ut benedicam illis.

verses.text: For Israel’s eyes were dim by reason of his great age, and he could not see clearly. And when they were brought to him, he kissed and embraced them.
verses.textLatin: Oculi enim Israël caligabant præ nimia senectute, et clare videre non poterat. Applicitosque ad se, deosculatus et circumplexus eos,

verses.text: And said to his son: I am not deprived of seeing thee: moreover God hath shewed me thy seed.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad filium suum: Non sum fraudatus aspectu tuo: insuper ostendit mihi Deus semen tuum.

verses.text: And when Joseph had taken them from his father’s lap, he bowed down with his face to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Cumque tulisset eos Joseph de gremio patris, adoravit pronus in terram.

verses.text: And he set Ephraim on his right hand, that is, towards the left hand of Israel; but Manasses on his left hand, to wit, towards his father’s right hand, and brought them near to him.
verses.textLatin: Et posuit Ephraim ad dexteram suam, id est, ad sinistram Israël: Manassen vero in sinistra sua, ad dexteram scilicet patris, applicuitque ambos ad eum.

verses.text: But he stretching forth his right hand, put it upon the head of Ephraim the younger brother; and the left upon the head of Manasses who was the elder, changing his hands.
verses.textLatin: Qui extendens manum dexteram, posuit super caput Ephraim minoris fratris: sinistram autem super caput Manasse qui major natu erat, commutans manus.

verses.text: And Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and said: God, in whose sight my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, God that feedeth me from my youth until this day;
verses.textLatin: Benedixitque Jacob filiis Joseph, et ait: Deus, in cujus conspectu ambulaverunt patres mei Abraham, et Isaac; Deus qui pascit me ab adolescentia mea usque in præsentem diem:

verses.text: The angel that delivereth me from all evils, bless these boys: and let my name be called upon them, and the names of my fathers Abraham, and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: angelus, qui eruit me de cunctis malis, benedicat pueris istis: et invocetur super eos nomen meum, nomina quoque patrum meorum Abraham et Isaac, et crescant in multitudinem super terram.

verses.text: And Joseph seeing that his father had put his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, was much displeased: and taking his father’s hand he tried to lift it from Ephraim’s head, and to remove it to the head of Manasses.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Joseph quod posuisset pater suus dexteram manum super caput Ephraim, graviter accepit: et apprehensam manum patris levare conatus est de capite Ephraim, et transferre super caput Manasse.

verses.text: And he said to his father: It should not be so, my father: for this is the firstborn, put thy right hand upon his head.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad patrem: Non ita convenit, pater: quia hic est primogenitus, pone dexteram tuam super caput ejus.

verses.text: But he refusing, said: I know, my son, I know: and this also shall become peoples, and shall be multiplied: but this younger brother shall be greater than he: and his seed shall grow into nations.
verses.textLatin: Qui renuens, ait: Scio, fili mi, scio: et iste quidem erit in populos, et multiplicabitur: sed frater ejus minor, major erit illo: et semen illius crescet in gentes.

verses.text: And he blessed them at that time, saying: In thee shall Israel be blessed, and it shall be said: God do to thee as to Ephraim, and as to Manasses. And he set Ephraim before Manasses.
verses.textLatin: Benedixitque eis in tempore illo, dicens: In te benedicetur Israël, atque dicetur: Faciat tibi Deus sicut Ephraim, et sicut Manasse. Constituitque Ephraim ante Manassen.

verses.text: And he said to Joseph his son: Behold I die, and God will be with you, and will bring you back into the land of your fathers.
verses.textLatin: Et ait ad Joseph filium suum: En ego morior, et erit Deus vobiscum, reducetque vos ad terram patrum vestrorum.

verses.text: I give thee a portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorrhite with my sword and bow.
verses.textLatin: Do tibi partem unam extra fratres tuos, quam tuli de manu Amorrhæi in gladio et arcu meo.

verses.text: And  Jacob called his sons, and said to them: Gather yourselves together that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem Jacob filios suos, et ait eis: Congregamini, ut annuntiem quæ ventura sunt vobis in diebus novissimis.

verses.text: Gather yourselves together, and hear, O ye sons of Jacob, hearken to Israel your father:
verses.textLatin: Congregamini, et audite, filii Jacob, audite Israël patrem vestrum:

verses.text: Ruben, my firstborn, thou art my strength, and the beginning of my sorrow: excelling in gifts, greater in command.
verses.textLatin: Ruben, primogenitus meus, tu fortitudo mea, et principium doloris mei; prior in donis, major in imperio.

verses.text: Thou art poured out as water, grow thou not: because thou wentest up to thy father’s bed, and didst defile his couch.
verses.textLatin: Effusus es sicut aqua, non crescas: quia ascendisti cubile patris tui, et maculasti stratum ejus.

verses.text: Simeon and Levi brethren: vessels of iniquity, waging war.
verses.textLatin: Simeon et Levi fratres vasa iniquitatis bellantia.

verses.text: Let not my soul go into their counsel, nor my glory be in their assembly: because in their fury they slew a man, and in their selfwill they undermined a wall.
verses.textLatin: In consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, et in cœtu illorum non sit gloria mea: quia in furore suo occiderunt virum, et in voluntate sua suffoderunt murum.

verses.text: Cursed be their fury, because it was stubborn: and their wrath because it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and will scatter them in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax: et indignatio eorum, quia dura: dividam eos in Jacob, et dispergam eos in Israël.

verses.text: Juda, thee shall thy brethren praise: thy hands shall be on the necks of thy enemies: the sons of thy father shall bow down to thee.
verses.textLatin: Juda, te laudabunt fratres tui: manus tua in cervicibus inimicorum tuorum, adorabunt te filii patris tui.

verses.text: Juda is a lion’s whelp: to the prey, my son, thou art gone up: resting thou hast couched as a lion, and as a lioness, who shall rouse him?
verses.textLatin: Catulus leonis Juda: ad prædam, fili mi, ascendisti: requiescens accubuisti ut leo, et quasi leæna: quis suscitabit eum?

verses.text: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.
verses.textLatin: Non auferetur sceptrum de Juda, et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est, et ipse erit expectatio gentium.

verses.text: Tying his foal to the vineyard, and his ass, O my son, to the vine. He shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape.
verses.textLatin: Ligans ad vineam pullum suum, et ad vitem, o fili mi, asinam suam, lavabit in vino stolam suam et in sanguine uvæ pallium suum.

verses.text: His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
verses.textLatin: Pulchriores sunt oculi ejus vino, et dentes ejus lacte candidiores.

verses.text: Zabulon shall dwell on the sea shore, and in the road of ships, reaching as far as Sidon.
verses.textLatin: Zabulon in littore maris habitabit, et in statione navium pertingens usque ad Sidonem.

verses.text: Issachar shall be a strong ass lying down between the borders.
verses.textLatin: Issachar asinus fortis accubans inter terminos.

verses.text: He saw rest that it was good: and the land that it was excellent: and he bowed his shoulder to carry, and became a servant under tribute.
verses.textLatin: Vidit requiem, quod esset bona et terram, quod optima: et supposuit humerum suum ad portandum, factusque est tributis serviens.

verses.text: Dan shall judge his people like another tribe in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Dan judicabit populum suum sicut et alia tribus in Israël.

verses.text: Let Dan be a snake in the way, a serpent in the path, that biteth the horse’s heels that his rider may fall backward.
verses.textLatin: Fiat Dan coluber in via, cerastes in semita, mordens ungulas equi, ut cadat ascensor ejus retro.

verses.text: I will look for thy salvation, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Salutare tuum expectabo, Domine.

verses.text: Gad, being girded, shall fight before him: and he himself shall be girded backward.
verses.textLatin: Gad, accinctus præliabitur ante eum: et ipse accingetur retrorsum.

verses.text: Aser, his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield dainties to kings.
verses.textLatin: Aser, pinguis panis ejus, et præbebit delicias regibus.

verses.text: Nephtali, a hart let loose, and giving words of beauty.
verses.textLatin: Nephthali, cervus emissus, et dans eloquia pulchritudinis.

verses.text: Joseph is a growing son, a growing son and comely to behold; the daughters run to and fro upon the wall.
verses.textLatin: Filius accrescens Joseph, filius accrescens et decorus aspectu: filiæ discurrerunt super murum.

verses.text: But they that held darts provoked him, and quarrelled with him, and envied him.
verses.textLatin: Sed exasperaverunt eum et jurgati sunt, invideruntque illi habentes jacula.

verses.text: His bow rested upon the strong, and the bands of his arms and his hands were loosed, by the hands of the mighty one of Jacob: thence he came forth a pastor, the stone of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Sedit in forti arcus ejus, et dissoluta sunt vincula brachiorum et manuum illius per manus potentis Jacob: inde pastor egressus est, lapis Israël.

verses.text: The God of thy father shall be thy helper, and the Almighty shall bless thee with the blessings of heaven above, with the blessings of the deep that lieth beneath, with the blessings of the breasts and of the womb.
verses.textLatin: Deus patris tui erit adjutor tuus, et omnipotens benedicet tibi benedictionibus cæli desuper, benedictionibus abyssi jacentis deorsum, benedictionibus uberum et vulvæ.

verses.text: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren.
verses.textLatin: Benedictiones patris tui confortatæ sunt benedictionibus patrum ejus, donec veniret desiderium collium æternorum: fiant in capite Joseph, et in vertice Nazaræi inter fratres suos.

verses.text: Benjamin a ravenous wolf, in the morning shall eat the prey, and in the evening shall divide the spoil.
verses.textLatin: Benjamin lupus rapax, mane comedat prædam, et vespere dividet spolia.

verses.text: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: these things their father spoke to them, and he blessed every one, with their proper blessings.
verses.textLatin: Omnes hi in tribubus Israël duodecim: hæc locutus est eis pater suus, benedixitque singulis benedictionibus propriis.

verses.text: And he charged them, saying: I am now going to be gathered to my people: bury me with my fathers in the double cave, which is in the field of Ephron the Hethite,
verses.textLatin: Et præcepit eis, dicens: Ego congregor ad populum meum: sepelite me cum patribus meis in spelunca duplici quæ est in agro Ephron Hethæi,

verses.text: Over against Mambre in the land of Chanaan, which Abraham bought together with the field of Ephron the Hethite for a possession to bury in.
verses.textLatin: contra Mambre in terra Chanaan, quam emit Abraham cum agro ab Ephron Hethæo in possessionem sepulchri.

verses.text: There they buried him, and Sara his wife: there was Isaac buried with Rebecca his wife: there also Lia doth lie buried.
verses.textLatin: Ibi sepelierunt eum, et Saram uxorem ejus: ibi sepultus est Isaac cum Rebecca conjuge sua: ibi et Lia condita jacet.

verses.text: And when he had ended the commandments, wherewith he instructed his sons, he drew up his feet upon the bed, and died: and he was gathered to his people.
verses.textLatin: Finitisque mandatis quibus filios instruebat, collegit pedes suos super lectulum, et obiit: appositusque est ad populum suum.

verses.text: And  when Joseph saw this, he fell upon his father’s face weeping and kissing him.
verses.textLatin: Quod cernens Joseph, ruit super faciem patris, flens et deosculans eum.

verses.text: And he commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father.
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque servis suis medicis ut aromatibus condirent patrem.

verses.text: And while they were fulfilling his commands, there passed forty days: for this was the manner with bodies that were embalmed, and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.
verses.textLatin: Quibus jussa explentibus, transierunt quadraginta dies: iste quippe mos erat cadaverum conditorum: flevitque eum Ægyptus septuaginta diebus.

verses.text: And the time of the mourning being expired, Joseph spoke to the family of Pharao: If I have found favour in your sight, speak in the ears of Pharao:
verses.textLatin: Et expleto planctus tempore, locutus est Joseph ad familiam Pharaonis: Si inveni gratiam in conspectu vestro, loquimini in auribus Pharaonis:

verses.text: For my father made me swear to him, saying: Behold I die: thou shalt bury me in my sepulchre which I have digged for myself in the land of Chanaan. So I will go up and bury my father, and return.
verses.textLatin: eo quod pater meus adjuraverit me dicens: En morior: in sepulchro meo, quod fodi mihi in terra Chanaan, sepelies me. Ascendam igitur, et sepeliam patrem meum, ac revertar.

verses.text: And Pharao said to him: Go up and bury thy father according as he made thee swear.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei Pharao: Ascende, et sepeli patrem tuum sicut adjuratus es.

verses.text: So he went up, and there went with him all the ancients of Pharao’s house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.textLatin: Quo ascendente, ierunt cum eo omnes senes domus Pharaonis, cunctique majores natu terræ Ægypti:

verses.text: And the house of Joseph with his brethren, except their children, and their flocks and herds, which they left in the land of Gessen.
verses.textLatin: domus Joseph cum fratribus suis, absque parvulis, et gregibus atque armentis, quæ dereliquerant in terra Gessen.

verses.text: He had also in his train chariots and horsemen: and it was a great company.
verses.textLatin: Habuit quoque in comitatu currus et equites: et facta est turba non modica.

verses.text: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is situated beyond the Jordan: where celebrating the exequies with a great and vehement lamentation, they spent full seven days.
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque ad Aream Atad, quæ sita est trans Jordanem: ubi celebrantes exequias planctu magno atque vehementi impleverunt septem dies.

verses.text: And when the inhabitants of Chanaan saw this, they said: This is a great mourning to the Egyptians. And therefore the name of that place was called, The mourning of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidissent habitatores terræ Chanaan, dixerunt: Planctus magnus est iste Ægyptiis. Et idcirco vocatum est nomen loci illius, Planctus Ægypti.

verses.text: So the sons of Jacob did as he had commanded them.
verses.textLatin: Fecerunt ergo filii Jacob sicut præceperat eis:

verses.text: And carrying him into the land of Chanaan, they buried him in the double cave which Abraham had bought together with the field for a possession of a buryingplace, of Ehpron the Hethite over against Mambre.
verses.textLatin: et portantes eum in terram Chanaan, sepelierunt eum in spelunca duplici, quam emerat Abraham cum agro in possessionem sepulchri ab Ephron Hethæo, contra faciem Mambre.

verses.text: And Joseph returned into Egypt with his brethren, and all that were in his company, after he had buried his father.
verses.textLatin: Reversusque est Joseph in Ægyptum cum fratribus suis, et omni comitatu, sepulto patre.

verses.text: Now he being dead, his brethren were afraid, and talked one with another: Lest perhaps he should remember the wrong he suffered, and requite us all the evil that we did to him.
verses.textLatin: Quo mortuo, timentes fratres ejus, et mutuo colloquentes: Ne forte memor sit injuriæ quam passus est, et reddat nobis omne malum quod fecimus,

verses.text: And they sent a message to him, saying: Thy father commanded us before he died,
verses.textLatin: mandaverunt ei dicentes: Pater tuus præcepit nobis antequam moreretur,

verses.text: That we should say thus much to thee from him: I beseech thee to forget the wickedness of thy brethren, and the sin and malice they practised against thee: we also pray thee, to forgive the servants of the God of thy father this wickedness. And when Joseph heard this, he wept.
verses.textLatin: ut hæc tibi verbis illius diceremus: Obsecro ut obliviscaris sceleris fratrum tuorum, et peccati atque malitiæ quam exercuerunt in te: nos quoque oramus ut servis Dei patris tui dimittas iniquitatem hanc. Quibus auditis flevit Joseph.

verses.text: And his brethren came to him: and worshipping prostrate on the ground they said: We are thy servants.
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque ad eum fratres sui: et proni adorantes in terram, dixerunt: Servi tui sumus.

verses.text: And he answered them: Fear not: can we resist the will of God?
verses.textLatin: Quibus ille respondit: Nolite timere: num Dei possumus resistere voluntati?
