verses.text: You thought evil against me: but God turned it into good, that he might exalt me, as at present you see, and might save many people.
verses.textLatin: Vos cogitastis de me malum: sed Deus vertit illud in bonum, ut exaltaret me, sicut in præsentiarum cernitis, et salvos faceret multos populos.

verses.text: Fear not: I will feed you and your children. And he comforted them, and spoke gently and mildly.
verses.textLatin: Nolite timere: ego pascam vos et parvulos vestros: consolatusque est eos, et blande ac leniter est locutus.

verses.text: And he dwelt in Egypt with all his father’s house: and lived a hundred and ten years. And he saw the children of Ephraim to the third generation. The children also of Machir the son of Maasses were born on Joseph’s knees.
verses.textLatin: Et habitavit in Ægypto cum omni domo patris sui: vixitque centum decem annis. Et vidit Ephraim filios usque ad tertiam generationem. Filii quoque Machir filii Manasse nati sunt in genibus Joseph.

verses.text: After which he told his brethren: God will visit you after my death, and will make you go up out of this land, to the land which he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Quibus transactis, locutus est fratribus suis: Post mortem meam Deus visitabit vos, et ascendere vos faciet de terra ista ad terram quam juravit Abraham, Isaac et Jacob.

verses.text: And he made them swear to him, saying: God will visit you, carry my bones with you out of this place:
verses.textLatin: Cumque adjurasset eos atque dixisset: Deus visitabit vos, asportate ossa mea vobiscum de loco isto:

verses.text: And he died being a hundred and ten years old. And being embalmed he was laid in a coffin in Egypt.
verses.textLatin: mortuus est, expletis centum decem vitæ suæ annis. Et conditus aromatibus, repositus est in loculo in Ægypto.

verses.text: These  are the names of the children of Israel, that went into Egypt with Jacob: they went in, every man with his household:
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt nomina filiorum Israël qui ingressi sunt in Ægyptum cum Jacob: singuli cum domibus suis introierunt:

verses.text: Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Juda,
verses.textLatin: Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Judas,

verses.text: Issachar, Zabulon, and Benjamin,
verses.textLatin: Issachar, Zabulon et Benjamin,

verses.text: Dan, and Nephtali, Gad and Aser.
verses.textLatin: Dan et Nephthali, Gad et Aser.

verses.text: And all the souls that came out of Jacob’s thigh, were seventy: but Joseph was in Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Erant igitur omnes animæ eorum qui egressi sunt de femore Jacob, septuaginta: Joseph autem in Ægypto erat.

verses.text: After he was dead, and all his brethren, and all that generation,
verses.textLatin: Quo mortuo, et universis fratribus ejus, omnique cognatione illa,

verses.text: The children of Israel increased, and sprung up into multitudes, and growing exceedingly strong they filled the land.
verses.textLatin: filii Israël creverunt, et quasi germinantes multiplicati sunt: ac roborati nimis, impleverunt terram.

verses.text: In the mean time there arose a new king over Egypt, that knew not Joseph:
verses.textLatin: Surrexit interea rex novus super Ægyptum, qui ignorabat Joseph.

verses.text: And he said to his people: Behold the people of the children of Israel are numerous and stronger than we.
verses.textLatin: Et ait ad populum suum: Ecce, populus filiorum Israël multus, et fortior nobis est.

verses.text: Come, let us wisely oppress them, lest they multiply: and if any war shall rise against us, join with our enemies, and having overcome us, depart out of the land.
verses.textLatin: Venite, sapienter opprimamus eum, ne forte multiplicetur: et si ingruerit contra nos bellum, addatur inimicis nostris, expugnatisque nobis egrediatur de terra.

verses.text: Therefore he set over them masters of the works, to afflict them with burdens, and they built for Pharao cities of tabernacles, Phithom, and Ramesses.
verses.textLatin: Præposuit itaque eis magistros operum, ut affligerent eos oneribus: ædificaveruntque urbes tabernaculorum Pharaoni, Phithom et Ramesses.

verses.text: But the more they oppressed them, the more they were multiplied, and increased:
verses.textLatin: Quantoque opprimebant eos, tanto magis multiplicabantur, et crescebant:

verses.text: And the Egyptians hated the children of Israel, and afflicted them and mocked them:
verses.textLatin: oderantque filios Israël Ægyptii, et affligebant illudentes eis,

verses.text: And they made their life bitter with hard works in clay, and brick, and with all manner of service, wherewith they were overcharged in the works of the earth.
verses.textLatin: atque ad amaritudinem perducebant vitam eorum operibus duris luti et lateris, omnique famulatu, quo in terræ operibus premebantur.

verses.text: And the king of Egypt spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews: of whom one was called Sephora, the other Phua,
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem rex Ægypti obstetricibus Hebræorum, quarum una vocabatur Sephora, altera Phua,

verses.text: Commanding them: When you shall do the office of midwives to the Hebrew women, and the time of delivery is come: if it be a man child, kill it: if a woman, keep it alive.
verses.textLatin: præcipiens eis: Quando obstetricabitis Hebræas, et partus tempus advenerit: si masculus fuerit, interficite eum: si femina, reservate.

verses.text: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded, but saved the men children.
verses.textLatin: Timuerunt autem obstetrices Deum, et non fecerunt juxta præceptum regis Ægypti, sed conservabant mares.

verses.text: And the king called for them and said: What is that you meant to do, that you would save the men children?
verses.textLatin: Quibus ad se accersitis, rex ait: Quidnam est hoc quod facere voluistis, ut pueros servaretis?

verses.text: They answered: The Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women: for they themselves are skilful in the office of a midwife; and they are delivered before we come to them.
verses.textLatin: Quæ responderunt: Non sunt Hebreæ sicut ægyptiæ mulieres: ipsæ enim obstetricandi habent scientiam, et priusquam veniamus ad eas, pariunt.

verses.text: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied and grew exceedingly strong.
verses.textLatin: Bene ergo fecit Deus obstetricibus: et crevit populus, confortatusque est nimis.

verses.text: And because the midwives feared God, he built them houses.
verses.textLatin: Et quia timuerunt obstetrices Deum, ædificavit eis domos.

verses.text: Pharao therefore charged all his people, saying: Whatsoever shall be born of the male sex, ye shall cast into the river: whatsoever of the female, ye shall save alive.
verses.textLatin: Præcepit ergo Pharao omni populo suo, dicens: Quidquid masculini sexus natum fuerit, in flumen projicite: quidquid feminini, reservate.

verses.text: After  this there went a man of the house of Levi; and took a wife of his own kindred.
verses.textLatin: Egressus est post hæc vir de domo Levi: et accepit uxorem stirpis suæ.

verses.text: And she conceived, and bore a son; and seeing him a goodly child, hid him three months.
verses.textLatin: Quæ concepit, et peperit filium: et videns eum elegantem, abscondit tribus mensibus.

verses.text: And when she could hide him no longer, she took a basket made of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and pitch: and put the little babe therein, and laid him in the sedges by the river’s brink,
verses.textLatin: Cumque jam celare non posset, sumpsit fiscellam scirpeam, et linivit eam bitumine ac pice: posuitque intus infantulum, et exposuit eum in carecto ripæ fluminis,

verses.text: His sister standing afar off, and taking notice what would be done.
verses.textLatin: stante procul sorore ejus, et considerante eventum rei.

verses.text: And behold the daughter of Pharao came down to wash herself in the river: and her maids walked by the river’s brink. And when she saw the basket in the sedges, she sent one of her maids for it: and when it was brought,
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem descendebat filia Pharaonis ut lavaretur in flumine: et puellæ ejus gradiebantur per crepidinem alvei. Quæ cum vidisset fiscellam in papyrione, misit unam e famulabus suis: et allatam

verses.text: She opened it and seeing within it an infant crying, having compassion on it she said: This is one of the babes of the Hebrews.
verses.textLatin: aperiens, cernensque in ea parvulum vagientem, miserta ejus, ait: De infantibus Hebræorum est hic.

verses.text: And the child’s sister said to her: Shall I go and call to thee a Hebrew woman, to nurse the babe?
verses.textLatin: Cui soror pueri: Vis, inquit, ut vadam, et vocem tibi mulierem hebræam, quæ nutrire possit infantulum?

verses.text: She answered: Go. The maid went and called her mother.
verses.textLatin: Respondit: Vade. Perrexit puella et vocavit matrem suam.

verses.text: And Pharao’s daughter said to her: Take this child and nurse him for me: I will give thee thy wages. The woman took, and nursed the child: and when he was grown up, she delivered him to Pharao’s daughter.
verses.textLatin: Ad quam locuta filia Pharaonis: Accipe, ait, puerum istum, et nutri mihi: ego dabo tibi mercedem tuam. Suscepit mulier, et nutrivit puerum: adultumque tradidit filiæ Pharaonis.

verses.text: And she adopted him for a son, and called him Moses, saying: Because I took him out of the water.
verses.textLatin: Quem illa adoptavit in locum filii, vocavitque nomen ejus Moyses, dicens: Quia de aqua tuli eum.

verses.text: In those days after Moses was grown up, he went out to his brethren: and saw their affliction, and an Egyptian striking one of the Hebrews his brethren.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis postquam creverat Moyses, egressus est ad fratres suos: viditque afflictionem eorum, et virum ægyptium percutientem quemdam de Hebræis fratribus suis.

verses.text: And when he had looked about this way and that way, and saw no one there, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
verses.textLatin: Cumque circumspexisset huc atque illuc, et nullum adesse vidisset, percussum Ægyptium abscondit sabulo.

verses.text: And going out the next day, he saw two Hebrews quarrelling: and he said to him that did the wrong: Why strikest thou thy neighbour?
verses.textLatin: Et egressus die altero conspexit duos Hebræos rixantes: dixitque ei qui faciebat injuriam: Quare percutis proximum tuum?

verses.text: But he answered: Who hath appointed thee prince and judge over us: wilt thou kill me, as thou didst yesterday kill the Egyptian? Moses feared, and said: How is this come to be known?
verses.textLatin: Qui respondit: Quis te constituit principem et judicem super nos? num occidere me tu vis, sicut heri occidisti Ægyptium? Timuit Moyses, et ait: Quomodo palam factum est verbum istud?

verses.text: And Pharao heard of this word and sought to kill Moses: but he fled from his sight, and abode in the land of Madian, and he sat down by a well.
verses.textLatin: Audivitque Pharao sermonem hunc, et quærebat occidere Moysen: qui fugiens de conspectu ejus, moratus est in terra Madian, et sedit juxta puteum.

verses.text: And the priest of Madian had seven daughters, who came to draw water: and when the troughs were filled, desired to water their father’s flocks.
verses.textLatin: Erant autem sacerdoti Madian septem filiæ, quæ venerunt ad hauriendam aquam: et impletis canalibus adaquare cupiebant greges patris sui.

verses.text: And the shepherds came and drove them away: and Moses arose, and defending the maids, watered their sheep.
verses.textLatin: Supervenere pastores, et ejecerunt eas: surrexitque Moyses, et defensis puellis, adaquavit oves earum.

verses.text: And when they returned to Raguel their father, he said to them: Why are ye come sooner than usual?
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum revertissent ad Raguel patrem suum, dixit ad eas: Cur velocius venistis solito?

verses.text: They answered: A man of Egypt delivered us from the hands of the shepherds: and he drew water also with us, and gave the sheep to drink.
verses.textLatin: Responderunt: Vir ægyptius liberavit nos de manu pastorum: insuper et hausit aquam nobiscum, potumque dedit ovibus.

verses.text: But he said: Where is he? why have you let the man go? call him that he may eat bread.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Ubi est? inquit: quare dimisistis hominem? vocate eum ut comedat panem.

verses.text: And Moses swore that he would dwell with him. And he took Sephora his daughter to wife:
verses.textLatin: Juravit ergo Moyses quod habitaret cum eo. Accepitque Sephoram filiam ejus uxorem:

verses.text: And she bore him a son, whom he called Gersam, saying: I have been a stranger in a foreign country. And she bore another, whom he called Eliezer, saying: For the God of my father, my helper hath delivered me out of the hand of Pharao.
verses.textLatin: quæ peperit ei filium, quem vocavit Gersam, dicens: Advena fui in terra aliena. Alterum vero peperit, quem vocavit Eliezer, dicens: Deus enim patris mei adjutor meus eripuit me de manu Pharaonis.

verses.text: Now after a long time the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel groaning, cried out because of the works: and their cry went up unto God from the works.
verses.textLatin: Post multum vero tempore mortuus est rex Ægypti: et ingemiscentes filii Israël, propter opera vociferati sunt: ascenditque clamor eorum ad Deum ab operibus.

verses.text: And he heard their groaning, and remembered the covenant which he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit gemitum eorum, ac recordatus est fœderis quod pepigit cum Abraham, Isaac et Jacob.

verses.text: And the Lord looked upon the children of Israel, and he knew them.
verses.textLatin: Et respexit Dominus filios Israël et cognovit eos.

verses.text: Now  Moses fed the sheep of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Madian: and he drove the flock to the inner parts of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, Horeb.
verses.textLatin: Moyses autem pascebat oves Jethro soceri sui sacerdotis Madian: cumque minasset gregem ad interiora deserti, venit ad montem Dei Horeb.

verses.text: And the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he saw that the bush was on fire and was not burnt.
verses.textLatin: Apparuitque ei Dominus in flamma ignis de medio rubi: et videbat quod rubus arderet, et non combureretur.

verses.text: And Moses said: I will go and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Moyses: Vadam, et videbo visionem hanc magnam, quare non comburatur rubus.

verses.text: And when the Lord saw that he went forward to see, he called to him out of the midst of the bush, and said: Moses, Moses. And he answered: Here I am.
verses.textLatin: Cernens autem Dominus quod pergeret ad videndum, vocavit eum de medio rubi, et ait: Moyses, Moyses. Qui respondit: Adsum.

verses.text: And he said: Come not nigh hither, put off the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Ne appropies, inquit, huc: solve calceamentum de pedibus tuis: locus enim, in quo stas, terra sancta est.

verses.text: And he said: I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Moses hid his face: for he durst not look at God.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Ego sum Deus patris tui, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob. Abscondit Moyses faciem suam: non enim audebat aspicere contra Deum.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the rigour of them that are over the works:
verses.textLatin: Cui ait Dominus: Vidi afflictionem populi mei in Ægypto, et clamorem ejus audivi propter duritiam eorum qui præsunt operibus:

verses.text: And knowing their sorrow, I am come down to deliver them out of the hands of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land into a good and spacious land, into a land that floweth with milk and honey, to the places of the Chanaanite, and Hethite, and Amorrhite, and Pherezite, and Hevite, and Jebusite.
verses.textLatin: et sciens dolorem ejus, descendi ut liberem eum de manibus Ægyptiorum, et educam de terra illa in terram bonam, et spatiosam, in terram quæ fluit lacte et melle, ad loca Chananæi et Hethæi, et Amorrhæi, et Pherezæi, et Hevæi, et Jebusæi.

verses.text: For the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have seen their affliction, wherewith they are oppressed by the Egyptians.
verses.textLatin: Clamor ergo filiorum Israël venit ad me: vidique afflictionem eorum, qua ab Ægyptiis opprimuntur.

verses.text: But come, and I will send thee to Pharao, that thou mayst bring forth my people, the children of Israel out of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Sed veni, et mittam te ad Pharaonem, ut educas populum meum, filios Israël, de Ægypto.

verses.text: And Moses said to God: Who am I that I should go to Pharao, and should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad Deum: Quis sum ego ut vadam ad Pharaonem, et educam filios Israël de Ægypto?

verses.text: And he said to him: I will be with thee: and this thou shalt have for a sign, that I have sent thee: When thou shalt have brought my people out of Egypt, thou shalt offer sacrifice to God upon this mountain.
verses.textLatin: Qui dixit ei: Ego ero tecum: et hoc habebis signum, quod miserim te: cum eduxeris populum meum de Ægypto, immolabis Deo super montem istum.

verses.text: Moses said to God: Lo, I shall go to the children of Israel, and say to them: The God of your fathers hath sent me to you. If they should say to me: What is his name? what shall I say to them?
verses.textLatin: Ait Moyses ad Deum: Ecce ego vadam ad filios Israël, et dicam eis: Deus patrum vestrorum misit me ad vos. Si dixerint mihi: Quod est nomen ejus? quid dicam eis?

verses.text: God said to Moses: I AM WHO AM. He said: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: HE WHO IS, hath sent me to you.
verses.textLatin: Dixit Deus ad Moysen: Ego sum qui sum. Ait: Sic dices filiis Israël: Qui est, misit me ad vos.

verses.text: And God said again to Moses: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me to you: This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque iterum Deus ad Moysen: Hæc dices filiis Israël: Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob, misit me ad vos: hoc nomen mihi est in æternum, et hoc memoriale meum in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: Go, gather together the ancients of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared to me, saying: Visiting I have visited you: and I have seen all that hath befallen you in Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Vade, et congrega seniores Israël, et dices ad eos: Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum apparuit mihi, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob, dicens: Visitans visitavi vos: et vidi omnia quæ acciderunt vobis in Ægypto.

verses.text: And I have said the word to bring you forth out of the affliction of Egypt, into the land of the Chanaanite, the Hethite, and the Amorrhite, and Pherezite, and Hevite, and Jebusite, to a land that floweth with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi ut educam vos de afflictione Ægypti in terram Chananæi, et Hethæi, et Amorrhæi, et Pherezæi, et Hevæi, et Jebusæi, ad terram fluentem lacte et melle.

verses.text: And they shall hear thy voice: and thou shalt go in, thou and the ancients of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and thou shalt say to him: The Lord God of the Hebrews hath called us: we will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, to sacrifice unto the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Et audient vocem tuam: ingredierisque tu, et seniores Israël, ad regem Ægypti, et dices ad eum: Dominus Deus Hebræorum vocavit nos: ibimus viam trium dierum in solitudinem, ut immolemus Domino Deo nostro.

verses.text: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go, but by a mighty hand.
verses.textLatin: Sed ego scio quod non dimittet vos rex Ægypti ut eatis nisi per manum validam.

verses.text: For I will stretch forth my hand, and will strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst of them: after these he will let you go.
verses.textLatin: Extendam enim manum meam, et percutiam Ægyptum in cunctis mirabilibus meis, quæ facturus sum in medio eorum: post hæc dimittet vos.

verses.text: And I will give favour to this people, in the sight of the Egyptians: and when you go forth, you shall not depart empty:
verses.textLatin: Daboque gratiam populo huic coram Ægyptiis: et cum egrediemini, non exibitis vacui:

verses.text: But every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that is in her house, vessels of silver and of gold, and raiment: and you shall put them on your sons and daughters, and shall spoil Egypt.
verses.textLatin: sed postulabit mulier a vicina sua et ab hospita sua, vasa argentea et aurea, ac vestes: ponetisque eas super filios et filias vestras, et spoliabitis Ægyptum.

verses.text: Moses  answered and said: They will not believe me, nor hear my voice, but they will say: The Lord hath not appeared to thee.
verses.textLatin: Respondens Moyses ait: Non credent mihi, neque audient vocem meam, sed dicent: Non apparuit tibi Dominus.

verses.text: Then he said to him: What is that thou holdest in thy hand? He answered: A rod.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo ad eum: Quid est quod tenes in manu tua? Respondit: Virga.

verses.text: And the Lord said: Cast it down upon the ground. He cast it down, and it was turned into a serpent: so that Moses fled from it.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus: Projice eam in terram. Projecit, et versa est in colubrum, ita ut fugeret Moyses.

verses.text: And the Lord said: Put out thy hand and take it by the tail. He put forth his hand, and took hold of it, and it was turned into a rod.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus: Extende manum tuam, et apprehende caudam ejus. Extendit, et tenuit, versaque est in virgam.

verses.text: That they may believe, saith he, that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ut credant, inquit, quod apparuerit tibi Dominus Deus patrum suorum, Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob.

verses.text: And the Lord said again: Put thy hand into thy bosom. And when he had put it into his bosom, he brought it forth leprous as snow.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus rursum: Mitte manum tuam in sinum tuum. Quam cum misisset in sinum, protulit leprosam instar nivis.

verses.text: And he said: Put back thy hand into thy bosom. He put it back, and brought it out again, and it was like the other flesh.
verses.textLatin: Retrahe, ait, manum tuam in sinum tuum. Retraxit, et protulit iterum, et erat similis carni reliquæ.

verses.text: If they will not believe thee, saith he, nor hear the voice of the former sign, they will believe the word of the latter sign.
verses.textLatin: Si non crediderint, inquit, tibi, neque audierint sermonem signi prioris, credent verbo signi sequentis.

verses.text: But if they will not even believe these two signs, nor hear thy voice: take of the river water, and pour it out upon the dry land, and whatsoever thou drawest out of the river shall be turned into blood.
verses.textLatin: Quod si nec duobus quidem his signis crediderint, neque audierint vocem tuam: sume aquam fluminis, et effunde eam super aridam, et quidquid hauseris de fluvio, vertetur in sanguinem.

verses.text: Moses said: I beseech thee, Lord, I am not eloquent from yesterday and the day before: and since thou hast spoken to thy servant, I have more impediment and slowness of tongue.
verses.textLatin: Ait Moyses: Obsecro, Domine, non sum eloquens ab heri et nudiustertius: et ex quo locutus es ad servum tuum, impeditioris et tardioris linguæ sum.

verses.text: The Lord said to him: Who made man’s mouth? or who made the dumb and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? did not I?
verses.textLatin: Dixit Dominus ad eum: Quis fecit os hominis? aut quis fabricatus est mutum et surdum, videntem et cæcum? nonne ego?

verses.text: Go therefore, and I will be in thy mouth: and I will teach thee what thou shalt speak.
verses.textLatin: Perge, igitur, et ego ero in ore tuo: doceboque te quid loquaris.

verses.text: But he said: I beseech thee, Lord, send whom thou wilt send.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Obsecro, inquit, Domine, mitte quem missurus es.

verses.text: The Lord being angry at Moses, said: Aaron the Levite is thy brother, I know that he is eloquent: behold he cometh forth to meet thee, and seeing thee shall be glad at heart.
verses.textLatin: Iratus Dominus in Moysen, ait: Aaron frater tuus Levites, scio quod eloquens sit: ecce ipse egreditur in occursum tuum, vidensque te lætabitur corde.

verses.text: Speak to him, and put my words in his mouth: and I will be in thy mouth, and in his mouth, and will shew you what you must do.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad eum, et pone verba mea in ore ejus: et ego ero in ore tuo, et in ore illius, et ostendam vobis quid agere debeatis.

verses.text: He shall speak in thy stead to the people, and shall be thy mouth: but thou shalt be to him in those things that pertain to God.
verses.textLatin: Ipse loquetur pro te ad populum, et erit os tuum: tu autem eris ei in his quæ ad Deum pertinent.

verses.text: And take this rod in thy hand, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.
verses.textLatin: Virgam quoque hanc sume in manu tua, in qua facturus es signa.

verses.text: Moses went his way, and returned to Jethro his father in law and said to him: I will go and return to my brethren into Egypt, that I may see if they be yet alive. And Jethro said to him: Go in peace.
verses.textLatin: Abiit Moyses, et reversus est ad Jethro socerum suum, dixitque ei: Vadam et revertar ad fratres meos in Ægyptum, ut videam si adhuc vivant. Cui ait Jethro: Vade in pace.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses, in Madian: Go, and return into Egypt: for they are all dead that sought thy life.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Dominus ad Moysen in Madian: Vade, et revertere in Ægyptum, mortui sunt enim omnes qui quærebant animam tuam.

verses.text: Moses therefore took his wife, and his sons, and set them upon an ass: and returned into Egypt, carrying the rod of God in his hand.
verses.textLatin: Tulit ergo Moyses uxorem suam, et filios suos, et imposuit eos super asinum: reversusque est in Ægyptum, portans virgam Dei in manu sua.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him as he was returning into Egypt: See that thou do all the wonders before Pharao, which I have put in thy hand: I shall harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei Dominus revertenti in Ægyptum: Vide ut omnia ostenta quæ posui in manu tua, facias coram Pharaone: ego indurabo cor ejus, et non dimittet populum.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Israel is my son, my firstborn.
verses.textLatin: Dicesque ad eum: Hæc dicit Dominus: Filius meus primogenitus Israël.

verses.text: I have said to thee: Let my son go, that he may serve me, and thou wouldst not let him go: behold I will kill thy son, thy firstborn.
verses.textLatin: Dixi tibi: Dimitte filium meum ut serviat mihi; et noluisti dimittere eum: ecce ego interficiam filium tuum primogenitum.

verses.text: And when he was in his journey, in the inn, the Lord met him, and would have killed him.
verses.textLatin: Cumque esset in itinere, in diversorio occurrit ei Dominus, et volebat occidere eum.

verses.text: Immediately Sephora took a very sharp stone, and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and touched his feet, and said: A bloody spouse art thou to me.
verses.textLatin: Tulit idcirco Sephora acutissimam petram, et circumcidit præputium filii sui, tetigitque pedes ejus, et ait: Sponsus sanguinum tu mihi es.

verses.text: And he let him go after she had said: A bloody spouse art thou to me, because of the circumcision.
verses.textLatin: Et dimisit eum postquam dixerat: Sponsus sanguinum ob circumcisionem.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: Go into the desert to meet Moses. And he went forth to meet him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Aaron: Vade in occursum Moysi in desertum. Qui perrexit obviam ei in montem Dei, et osculatus est eum.

verses.text: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord, by which he had sent him, and the signs that he had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Narravitque Moyses Aaron omnia verba Domini quibus miserat eum, et signa quæ mandaverat.

verses.text: And they came together, and they assembled all the ancients of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque simul, et congregaverunt cunctos seniores filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And Aaron spoke all the words which the Lord had said to Moses: and he wrought the signs before the people,
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Aaron omnia verba quæ dixerat Dominus ad Moysen: et fecit signa coram populo,

verses.text: And the people believed. And they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel: and that he had looked upon their affliction: and falling down they adored.
verses.textLatin: et credidit populus. Audieruntque quod visitasset Dominus filios Israël, et respexisset afflictionem illorum: et proni adoraverunt.

verses.text: After  these things Moses and Aaron went in, and said to Pharao: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: Let my people go that they may sacrifice to me in the desert.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc ingressi sunt Moyses et Aaron, et dixerunt Pharaoni: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Israël: Dimitte populum meum ut sacrificet mihi in deserto.

verses.text: But he answered: Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voice, and let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go.
verses.textLatin: At ille respondit: Quis est Dominus, ut audiam vocem ejus, et dimittam Israël? nescio Dominum, et Israël non dimittam.

verses.text: And they said: The God of the Hebrews hath called us, to go three days’ journey into the wilderness and to sacrifice to the Lord our God: lest a pestilence or the sword fall upon us.
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque: Deus Hebræorum vocavit nos, ut eamus viam trium dierum in solitudinem, et sacrificemus Domino Deo nostro: ne forte accidat nobis pestis aut gladius.

verses.text: The king of Egypt said to them: Why do you Moses and Aaron draw off the people from their works? Get you gone to your burdens.
verses.textLatin: Ait ad eos rex Ægypti: Quare Moyses et Aaron sollicitatis populum ab operibus suis? ite ad onera vestra.

verses.text: And Pharao said: The people of the land is numerous: you see that the multitude is increased: how much more if you give them rest from their works?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Pharao: Multus est populus terræ: videtis quod turba succreverit: quanto magis si dederitis eis requiem ab operibus?

verses.text: Therefore he commanded the same day the overseers of the works, and the taskmasters of the people, saying:
verses.textLatin: Præcepit ergo in die illo præfectis operum et exactoribus populi, dicens:

verses.text: You shall give straw no more to the people to make brick, as before: but let them go and gather straw.
verses.textLatin: Nequaquam ultra dabitis paleas populo ad conficiendos lateres, sicut prius: sed ipsi vadant, et colligant stipulas.

verses.text: And you shall lay upon them the task of bricks, which they did before, neither shall you diminish any thing thereof: for they are idle, and therefore they cry, saying: Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
verses.textLatin: Et mensuram laterum, quam prius faciebant, imponetis super eos, nec minuetis quidquam: vacant enim, et idcirco vociferantur, dicentes: Eamus, et sacrificemus Deo nostro.

verses.text: Let them be oppressed, with works, and let them fulfil them: that they may not regard lying words.
verses.textLatin: Opprimantur operibus, et expleant ea: ut non acquiescant verbis mendacibus.

verses.text: And the overseers of the works and the taskmasters went out and said to the people: Thus saith Pharao, I allow you no straw:
verses.textLatin: Igitur egressi præfecti operum et exactores ad populum, dixerunt: Sic dicit Pharao: Non do vobis paleas:

verses.text: Go, and gather it where you can find it: neither shall any thing of your work be diminished.
verses.textLatin: ite, et colligite sicubi invenire poteritis, nec minuetur quidquam de opere vestro.

verses.text: And the people was scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather straw.
verses.textLatin: Dispersusque est populus per omnem terram Ægypti ad colligendas paleas.

verses.text: And the overseers of the works pressed them, saying: Fulfil your work every day as before you were wont to do when straw was given you.
verses.textLatin: Præfecti quoque operum instabant, dicentes: Complete opus vestrum quotidie, ut prius facere solebatis quando dabantur vobis paleæ.

verses.text: And they that were over the works of the children of Israel were scourged by Pharao’s taskmasters, saying: Why have you not made up the task of bricks both yesterday and to day as before?
verses.textLatin: Flagellatique sunt qui præerant operibus filiorum Israël, ab exactoribus Pharaonis, dicentibus: Quare non impletis mensuram laterum sicut prius, nec heri, nec hodie?

verses.text: And the officers of the children of Israel came, and cried out to Pharao, saying: Why dealest thou so with thy servants?
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque præpositi filiorum Israël, et vociferati sunt ad Pharaonem dicentes: Cur ita agis contra servos tuos?

verses.text: Straw is not given us, and bricks are required of us as before: behold we thy servants are beaten with whips, and thy people is unjustly dealt withal.
verses.textLatin: paleæ non dantur nobis, et lateres similiter imperantur: en famuli tui flagellis cædimur, et injuste agitur contra populum tuum.

verses.text: And he said: You are idle, and therefore you say: Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait: Vacatis otio, et idcirco dicitis: Eamus, et sacrificemus Domino.

verses.text: Go therefore, and work: straw shall not be given you, and you shall deliver the accustomed number of bricks.
verses.textLatin: Ite ergo, et operamini: paleæ non dabuntur vobis, et reddetis consuetum numerum laterum.

verses.text: And the officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in evil case, because it was said to them: There shall not a whit be diminished of the bricks for every day.
verses.textLatin: Videbantque se præpositi filiorum Israël in malo, eo quod diceretur eis: Non minuetur quidquam de lateribus per singulos dies.

verses.text: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood over against them as they came out from Pharao:
verses.textLatin: Occurreruntque Moysi et Aaron, qui stabant ex adverso, egredientibus a Pharaone:

verses.text: And they said to them: The Lord see and judge, because you have made our savour to stink before Pharao and his servants, and you have given him a sword to kill us.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt ad eos: Videat Dominus et judicet, quoniam fœtere fecistis odorem nostrum coram Pharaone et servis ejus, et præbuistis ei gladium, ut occideret nos.

verses.text: And Moses returned to the Lord, and said: Lord, why hast thou afflicted this people? wherefore hast thou sent me?
verses.textLatin: Reversusque est Moyses ad Dominum, et ait: Domine, cur afflixisti populum istum? quare misisti me?

verses.text: For since the time that I went in to Pharao to speak in thy name, he hath afflicted thy people: and thou hast not delivered them.
verses.textLatin: ex eo enim quo ingressus sum ad Pharaonem ut loquerer in nomine tuo, afflixit populum tuum: et non liberasti eos.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Now thou shalt see what I will do to Pharao: for by a mighty hand shall he let them go, and with a strong hand shall he cast them out of his land.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Nunc videbis quæ facturus sim Pharaoni: per manum enim fortem dimittet eos, et in manu robusta ejiciet illos de terra sua.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen dicens: Ego Dominus

verses.text: That appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, by the name of God Almighty; and my name ADONAI I did not shew them.
verses.textLatin: qui apparui Abraham, Isaac et Jacob in Deo omnipotente: et nomen meum Adonai non indicavi eis.

verses.text: And I made a covenant with them, to give them the land of Chanaan, the land of their pilgrimage wherein they were strangers.
verses.textLatin: Pepigique fœdus cum eis, ut darem eis terram Chanaan, terram peregrinationis eorum, in qua fuerunt advenæ.

verses.text: I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, wherewith the Egyptians have oppressed them: and I have remembered my covenant.
verses.textLatin: Ego audivi gemitum filiorum Israël, quo Ægyptii oppresserunt eos: et recordatus sum pacti mei.

verses.text: Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord who will bring you out from the work prison of the Egyptians, and will deliver you from bondage: and redeem you with a high arm, and great judgments.
verses.textLatin: Ideo dic filiis Israël: Ego Dominus qui educam vos de ergastulo Ægyptiorum, et eruam de servitute, ac redimam in brachio excelso et judiciis magnis.

verses.text: And I will take you to myself for my people, I will be your God: and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the work prison of the Egyptians.
verses.textLatin: Et assumam vos mihi in populum, et ero vester Deus: et scietis quod ego sum Dominus Deus vester qui eduxerim vos de ergastulo Ægyptiorum,

verses.text: And brought you into the land, concerning which I lifted up my hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: and I will give it you to possess, I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et induxerim in terram, super quam levavi manum meam ut darem eam Abraham, Isaac et Jacob: daboque illam vobis possidendam. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: And Moses told all this to the children of Israel: but they did not hearken to him, for anguish of spirit, and most painful work.
verses.textLatin: Narravit ergo Moyses omnia filiis Israël: qui non acquieverunt ei propter angustiam spiritus, et opus durissimum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Go in, and speak to Pharao king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.textLatin: Ingredere, et loquere ad Pharaonem regem Ægypti, ut dimittat filios Israël de terra sua.

verses.text: Moses answered before the Lord: Behold the children of Israel do not hearken to me; and how will Pharao hear me, especially as I am of uncircumcised lips?
verses.textLatin: Respondit Moyses coram Domino: Ecce filii Israël non audiunt me: et quomodo audiet Pharao, præsertim cum incircumcisus sim labiis?

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and he gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharao the king of Egypt, that they should bring forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, et dedit mandatum ad filios Israël, et ad Pharaonem regem Ægypti ut educerent filios Israël de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: These are the heads of their houses by their families. The sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel: Henoch and Phallu, Hesron and Charmi.
verses.textLatin: Isti sunt principes domorum per familias suas. Filii Ruben primogeniti Israëlis: Henoch et Phallu, Hesron et Charmi:

verses.text: These are the kindreds of Ruben. The sons of Simeon: Jamuel, and Jamin, and Ahod, and Jachin, and Soar, and Saul the son of a Chanaanitess: these are the families of Simeon.
verses.textLatin: hæ cognationes Ruben. Filii Simeon: Jamuel, et Jamin, et Ahod, et Jachin, et Soar, et Saul filius Chananitidis: hæ progenies Simeon.

verses.text: And these are the names of the sons of Levi by their kindreds: Gerson, and Caath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were a hundred and thirty-seven.
verses.textLatin: Et hæc nomina filiorum Levi per cognationes suas: Gerson, et Caath, et Merari. Anni autem vitæ Levi fuerunt centum triginta septem.

verses.text: The sons of Gerson: Lobni and Semei, by their kindreds.
verses.textLatin: Filii Gerson: Lobni et Semei, per cognationes suas.

verses.text: The sons of Caath: Amram, and Isaar, and Hebron, and Oziel. And the years of Caath’s life were a hundred and thirty-three.
verses.textLatin: Filii Caath: Amram, et Isaar, et Hebron, et Oziel; anni quoque vitæ Caath, centum triginta tres.

verses.text: The sons of Merari: Moholi and Musi. These are the kindreds of Levi by their families.
verses.textLatin: Filii Merari: Moholi et Musi: hæ cognationes Levi per familias suas.

verses.text: And Amram took to wife Jochabed his aunt by the father’s side: and she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of Amram’s life were a hundred and thirty-seven.
verses.textLatin: Accepit autem Amram uxorem Jochabed patruelem suam: quæ peperit ei Aaron et Moysen. Fueruntque anni vitæ Amram, centum triginta septem.

verses.text: The sons also of Isaar: Core, and Nepheg, and Zechri.
verses.textLatin: Filii quoque Isaar: Core, et Nepheg, et Zechri.

verses.text: The sons also of Oziel: Mizael, and Elizaphan, and Sethri.
verses.textLatin: Filii quoque Oziel: Misaël, et Elisaphan, et Sethri.

verses.text: And Aaron took to wife Elizabeth the daughter of Aminadab, sister of Nahason, who bore him Nadab, and Abiu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.textLatin: Accepit autem Aaron uxorem Elisabeth filiam Aminadab, sororem Nahason, quæ peperit ei Nadab, et Abiu, et Eleazar, et Ithamar.

verses.text: The sons also of Core: Aser, and Elcana, and Abiasaph. These are the kindreds of the Corites.
verses.textLatin: Filii quoque Core: Aser, et Elcana, et Abiasaph: hæ sunt cognationes Coritarum.

verses.text: But Eleazar the son of Aaron took a wife of the daughters of Phutiel: and she bore him Phinees. These are the heads of the Levitical families by their kindreds.
verses.textLatin: At vero Eleazar filius Aaron accepit uxorem de filiabus Phutiel: quæ peperit ei Phinees. Hi sunt principes familiarum Leviticarum per cognationes suas.

verses.text: These are Aaron and Moses, whom the Lord commanded to bring forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.
verses.textLatin: Iste est Aaron et Moyses, quibus præcepit Dominus ut educerent filios Israël de terra Ægypti per turmas suas.

verses.text: These are they that speak to Pharao king of Egypt, in order to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron,
verses.textLatin: Hi sunt, qui loquuntur ad Pharaonem regem Ægypti, ut educant filios Israël de Ægypto: iste est Moyses et Aaron,

verses.text: In the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: in die qua locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord: speak thou to Pharao king of Egypt all that I say to thee.
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens: Ego Dominus: loquere ad Pharaonem regem Ægypti, omnia quæ ego loquor tibi.

verses.text: And Moses said before the Lord: Lo I am of uncircumcised lips, how will Pharao hear me?
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses coram Domino: En incircumcisus labiis sum, quomodo audiet me Pharao?

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Behold I have appointed thee the God of Pharao: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Ecce constitui te Deum Pharaonis: et Aaron frater tuus erit propheta tuus.

verses.text: Thou shalt speak to him all that I command thee; and he shall speak to Pharao, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.textLatin: Tu loqueris ei omnia quæ mando tibi: et ille loquetur ad Pharaonem, ut dimittat filios Israël de terra sua.

verses.text: But I shall harden his heart, and shall multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,
verses.textLatin: Sed ego indurabo cor ejus, et multiplicabo signa et ostenta mea in terra Ægypti,

verses.text: And he will not hear you: and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and will bring forth my army and my people the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, by very great judgments.
verses.textLatin: et non audiet vos: immittamque manum meam super Ægyptum, et educam exercitum et populum meum filios Israël de terra Ægypti per judicia maxima.

verses.text: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, who have stretched forth my hand upon Egypt, and have brought forth the children of Israel out of the midst of them.
verses.textLatin: Et scient Ægyptii quia ego sum Dominus qui extenderim manum meam super Ægyptum, et eduxerim filios Israël de medio eorum.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded: so did they.
verses.textLatin: Fecit itaque Moyses et Aaron sicut præceperat Dominus: ita egerunt.

verses.text: And Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three, when they spoke to Pharao.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Moyses octoginta annorum, et Aaron octoginta trium, quando locuti sunt ad Pharaonem.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron:

verses.text: When Pharao shall say to you, Shew signs: thou shalt say to Aaron: Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharao, and it shall be turned into a serpent.
verses.textLatin: Cum dixerit vobis Pharao, Ostendite signa: dices ad Aaron: Tolle virgam tuam, et projice eam coram Pharaone, ac vertetur in colubrum.

verses.text: So Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharao, and did as the Lord had commanded. And Aaron took the rod before Pharao, and his servants, and it was turned into a serpent.
verses.textLatin: Ingressi itaque Moyses et Aaron ad Pharaonem, fecerunt sicut præceperat Dominus: tulitque Aaron virgam coram Pharaone et servis ejus, quæ versa est in colubrum.

verses.text: And Pharao called the wise men and the magicians: and they also by Egyptian enchantments and certain secrets did in like manner.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem Pharao sapientes et maleficos: et fecerunt etiam ipsi per incantationes ægyptiacas et arcana quædam similiter.

verses.text: And they every one cast down their rods, and they were turned into serpents: but Aaron’s rod devoured their rods.
verses.textLatin: Projeceruntque singuli virgas suas, quæ versæ sunt in dracones: sed devoravit virga Aaron virgas eorum.

verses.text: And Pharao’s heart was hardened, and he did not hearken to them, as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Induratumque est cor Pharaonis, et non audivit eos, sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Pharao’s heart is hardened, he will not let the people go.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Ingravatum est cor Pharaonis: non vult dimittere populum.

verses.text: Go to him in the morning, behold he will go out to the waters: and thou shalt stand to meet him on the bank of the river: and thou shalt take in thy hand the rod that was turned into a serpent.
verses.textLatin: Vade ad eum mane, ecce egredietur ad aquas: et stabis in occursum ejus super ripam fluminis: et virgam quæ conversa est in draconem, tolles in manu tua.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to him: The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to thee, saying: Let my people go to sacrifice to me in the desert: and hitherto thou wouldst not hear.
verses.textLatin: Dicesque ad eum: Dominus Deus Hebræorum misit me ad te, dicens: Dimitte populum meum ut sacrificet mihi in deserto: et usque ad præsens audire noluisti.

verses.text: Thus therefore saith the Lord: In this thou shalt know that I am the Lord: behold I will strike with the rod, that is in my hand, the water of the river, and it shall be turned into blood.
verses.textLatin: Hæc igitur dicit Dominus: In hoc scies quod sim Dominus: ecce percutiam virga, quæ in manu mea est, aquam fluminis, et vertetur in sanguinem.

verses.text: And the fishes that are in the river shall die, and the waters shall be corrupted, and the Egyptians shall be afflicted when they drink the water of the river.
verses.textLatin: Pisces quoque, qui sunt in fluvio, morientur, et computrescent aquæ, et affligentur Ægyptii bibentes aquam fluminis.

verses.text: The Lord also said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch forth thy hand upon the waters of Egypt, and upon their rivers, and streams and pools, and all the ponds of waters, that they may be turned into blood: and let blood be in all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and of stone.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen: Dic ad Aaron: Tolle virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super aquas Ægypti, et super fluvios eorum, et rivos ac paludes, et omnes lacus aquarum, ut vertantur in sanguinem: et sit cruor in omni terra Ægypti, tam in ligneis vasis quam in saxeis.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded: and lifting up the rod he struck the water of the river before Pharao and his servants: and it was turned into blood.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque Moyses et Aaron sicut præceperat Dominus: et elevans virgam percussit aquam fluminis coram Pharaone et servis ejus: quæ versa est in sanguinem.

verses.text: And the fishes that were in the river died: and the river corrupted, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river, and there was blood in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et pisces, qui erant in flumine, mortui sunt: computruitque fluvius, et non poterant Ægyptii bibere aquam fluminis, et fuit sanguis in tota terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And the magicians of the Egyptians with their enchantments did in like manner: and Pharao’s heart was hardened, neither did he hear them, as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque similiter malefici Ægyptiorum incantationibus suis: et induratum est cor Pharaonis, nec audivit eos, sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: And he turned himself away and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to it this time also.
verses.textLatin: Avertitque se, et ingressus est domum suam, nec apposuit cor etiam hac vice.

verses.text: And all the Egyptians dug round about the river for water to drink: for they could not drink of the water of the river.
verses.textLatin: Foderunt autem omnes Ægyptii per circuitum fluminis aquam ut biberent: non enim poterant bibere de aqua fluminis.

verses.text: And seven days were fully ended, after that the Lord struck the river.
verses.textLatin: Impletique sunt septem dies, postquam percussit Dominus fluvium.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao, and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen: Ingredere ad Pharaonem, et dices ad eum: Hæc dicit Dominus: Dimitte populum meum, ut sacrificet mihi:

verses.text: But if thou wilt not let them go behold I will strike all thy coasts with frogs.
verses.textLatin: sin autem nolueris dimittere, ecce ego percutiam omnes terminos tuos ranis,

verses.text: And the river shall bring forth an abundance of frogs: which shall come up, and enter into thy house, and thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the houses of thy servants, and to thy people, and into thy ovens, and into the remains of thy meats;
verses.textLatin: et ebulliet fluvius ranas: quæ ascendent, et ingredientur domum tuam, et cubiculum lectuli tui, et super stratum tuum, et in domos servorum tuorum, et in populum tuum, et in furnos tuos, et in reliquias ciborum tuorum:

verses.text: And the frogs shall come in to thee, and to thy people, and to all thy servants.
verses.textLatin: et ad te, et ad populum tuum, et ad omnes servos tuos intrabunt ranæ.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch forth thy hand upon the streams and upon the rivers and the pools, and bring forth frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Dic ad Aaron: Extende manum tuam super fluvios ac super rivos et paludes, et educ ranas super terram Ægypti.

verses.text: And Aaron stretched forth his hand upon the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et extendit Aaron manum super aquas Ægypti, et ascenderunt ranæ, operueruntque terram Ægypti.

verses.text: And the magicians also by their enchantments did in like manner, and they brought forth frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Fecerunt autem et malefici per incantationes suas similiter, eduxeruntque ranas super terram Ægypti.

verses.text: But Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Pray ye to the Lord to take away the frogs from me and from my people; and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem Pharao Moysen et Aaron, et dixit eis: Orate Dominum ut auferat ranas a me et a populo meo, et dimittam populum ut sacrificet Domino.

verses.text: And Moses said to Pharao: Set me a time when I shall pray for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, that the frogs may be driven away from thee and from thy house, and from thy servants, and from thy people: and may remain only in the river.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad Pharaonem: Constitue mihi quando deprecer pro te, et pro servis tuis, et pro populo tuo, ut abigantur ranæ a te, et a domo tua, et a servis tuis, et a populo tuo: et tantum in flumine remaneant.

verses.text: And he answered: To morrow. But he said: I will do according to thy word; that thou mayst know that there is none like to the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Qui respondit: Cras. At ille: Juxta, inquit, verbum tuum faciam: ut scias quoniam non est sicut Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy house, and from thy servants, and from thy people; and shall remain only in the river.
verses.textLatin: Et recedent ranæ a te, et a domo tua, et a servis tuis, et a populo tuo: et tantum in flumine remanebunt.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron went forth from Pharao: and Moses cried to the Lord for the promise, which he had made to Pharao concerning the frogs.
verses.textLatin: Egressique sunt Moyses et Aaron a Pharaone: et clamavit Moyses ad Dominum pro sponsione ranarum quam condixerat Pharaoni.

verses.text: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses: and the frogs died out of the houses, and out of the villages, and out of the fields:
verses.textLatin: Fecitque Dominus juxta verbum Moysi: et mortuæ sunt ranæ de domibus, et de villis, et de agris.

verses.text: And they gathered them together into immense heaps, and the land was corrupted.
verses.textLatin: Congregaveruntque eas in immensos aggeres, et computruit terra.

verses.text: And Pharao seeing that rest was given, hardened his own heart, and did not hear them, as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Pharao quod data esset requies, ingravavit cor suum, et non audivit eos, sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch forth thy rod, and strike the dust of the earth: and may there be sciniphs in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Loquere ad Aaron: Extende virgam tuam, et percute pulverem terræ: et sint sciniphes in universa terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And they did so. And Aaron stretched forth his hand, holding the rod: and he struck the dust of the earth, and there came sciniphs on men and on beasts: all the dust of the earth was turned into sciniphs through all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque ita. Et extendit Aaron manum, virgam tenens: percussitque pulverem terræ, et facti sunt sciniphes in hominibus, et in jumentis: omnis pulvis terræ versus est in sciniphes per totam terram Ægypti.

verses.text: And the magicians with their enchantments practised in like manner, to bring forth sciniphs, and they could not: and there were sciniphs as well on men as on beasts.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque similiter malefici incantationibus suis, ut educerent sciniphes, et non potuerunt: erantque sciniphes tam in hominibus quam in jumentis.

verses.text: And the magicians said to Pharao: This is the finger of God. And Pharao’s heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt malefici ad Pharaonem: Digitus Dei est hic; induratumque est cor Pharaonis, et non audivit eos sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord also said to Moses: Arise early, and stand before Pharao: for he will go forth to the waters: and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen: Consurge diluculo, et sta coram Pharaone: egredietur enim ad aquas: et dices ad eum: Hæc dicit Dominus: Dimitte populum meum ut sacrificet mihi.

verses.text: But if thou wilt not let them go, behold I will send in upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy houses all kind of flies: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with flies of divers kinds, and the whole land wherein they shall be.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non dimiseris eum, ecce ego immittam in te, et in servos tuos, et in populum tuum, et in domos tuas, omne genus muscarum: et implebuntur domus Ægyptiorum muscis diversi generis, et universa terra in qua fuerint.

verses.text: And I will make the land of Gessen wherein my people is, wonderful in that day, so that flies shall not be there: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord in the midst of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Faciamque mirabilem in die illa terram Gessen, in qua populus meus est, ut non sint ibi muscæ: et scias quoniam ego Dominus in medio terræ.

verses.text: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: to morrow shall this sign be.
verses.textLatin: Ponamque divisionem inter populum meum et populum tuum: cras erit signum istud.

verses.text: And the Lord did so. And there came a very grievous swarm of flies into the houses of Pharao and of his servants, and into all the land of Egypt: and the land was corrupted by this kind of flies.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque Dominus ita. Et venit musca gravissima in domos Pharaonis et servorum ejus, et in omnem terram Ægypti: corruptaque est terra ab hujuscemodi muscis.

verses.text: And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Go, and sacrifice to your God in this land.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Pharao Moysen et Aaron, et ait eis: Ite et sacrificate Deo vestro in terra hac.

verses.text: And Moses said: It cannot be so: for we shall sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God: now if we kill those things which the Egyptians worship, in their presence, they will stone us.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: Non potest ita fieri: abominationes enim Ægyptiorum immolabimus Domino Deo nostro: quod si mactaverimus ea quæ colunt Ægyptii coram eis, lapidibus nos obruent.

verses.text: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness: and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.
verses.textLatin: Viam trium dierum pergemus in solitudinem: et sacrificabimus Domino Deo nostro, sicut præcepit nobis.

verses.text: And Pharao said: I will let you go to sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness: but go no farther: pray for me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Pharao: Ego dimittam vos ut sacrificetis Domino Deo vestro in deserto: verumtamen longius ne abeatis, rogate pro me.

verses.text: And Moses said: I will go out from thee, and will pray to the Lord: and the flies shall depart from Pharao, and from his servants, and from his people to morrow: but do not deceive any more, in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: At ait Moyses: Egressus a te, orabo Dominum: et recedet musca a Pharaone, et a servis suis, et a populo ejus cras: verumtamen noli ultra fallere, ut non dimittas populum sacrificare Domino.

verses.text: So Moses went out from Pharao, and prayed to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Egressusque Moyses a Pharaone, oravit Dominum.

verses.text: And he did according to his word: and he took away the flies from Pharao, and from his servants, and from his people: there was not left so much as one.
verses.textLatin: Qui fecit juxta verbum illius, et abstulit muscas a Pharaone, et a servis suis, et a populo ejus: non superfuit ne una quidem.

verses.text: And Pharao’s heart was hardened, so that neither this time would he let the people go.
verses.textLatin: Et ingravatum est cor Pharaonis, ita ut nec hac quidem vice dimitteret populum.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao, and speak to him: Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Ingredere ad Pharaonem, et loquere ad eum: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Hebræorum: Dimitte populum meum ut sacrificet mihi.

verses.text: But if thou refuse, and withhold them still:
verses.textLatin: Quod si adhuc renuis, et retines eos,

verses.text: Behold my hand shall be upon thy fields: and a very grievous murrain upon thy horses, and asses, and camels, and oxen, and sheep.
verses.textLatin: ecce manus mea erit super agros tuos, et super equos, et asinos, et camelos, et boves, et oves, pestis valde gravis.

verses.text: And the Lord will make a wonderful difference between the possessions of Israel and the possessions of the Egyptians, that nothing at all shall die of those things that belong to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et faciet Dominus mirabile inter possessiones Israël et possessiones Ægyptiorum, ut nihil omnino pereat ex eis quæ pertinent ad filios Israël.

verses.text: And the Lord appointed a time, saying: To morrow will the Lord do this thing in the land.
verses.textLatin: Constituitque Dominus tempus, dicens: Cras faciet Dominus verbum istud in terra.

verses.text: The Lord therefore did this thing the next day: and all the beasts of the Egyptians died, but of the beasts of the children of Israel there died not one.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ergo Dominus verbum hoc altera die: mortuaque sunt omnia animantia Ægyptiorum; de animalibus vero filiorum Israël, nihil omnino periit.

verses.text: And Pharao sent to see: and there was not any thing dead of that which Israel possessed. And Pharao’s heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Pharao ad videndum: nec erat quidquam mortuum de his quæ possidebat Israël. Ingravatumque est cor Pharaonis, et non dimisit populum.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take to you handfuls of ashes out of the chimney, and let Moses sprinkle it in the air in the presence of Pharao.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron: Tollite plenas manus cineris de camino, et spargat illum Moyses in cælum coram Pharaone.

verses.text: And be there dust upon all the land of Egypt: for there shall be boils and swelling blains both in men and beasts, in the whole land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Sitque pulvis super omnem terram Ægypti: erunt enim in hominibus et jumentis ulcera, et vesicæ turgentes in universa terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And they took ashes out of the chimney, and stood before Pharao, and Moses sprinkled it in the air: and there came boils with swelling blains in men and beasts.
verses.textLatin: Tuleruntque cinerem de camino, et steterunt coram Pharaone, et sparsit illum Moyses in cælum: factaque sunt ulcera vesicarum turgentium in hominibus et jumentis:

verses.text: Neither could the magicians stand before Moses for the boils that were upon them, and in all the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: nec poterant malefici stare coram Moyse propter ulcera quæ in illis erant, et in omni terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, and he hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
verses.textLatin: Induravitque Dominus cor Pharaonis, et non audivit eos, sicut locutus est Dominus ad Moysen.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Arise in the morning, and stand before Pharao, and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Mane consurge, et sta coram Pharaone, et dices ad eum: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Hebræorum: Dimitte populum meum ut sacrificet mihi.

verses.text: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thy heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people: that thou mayst know there is none like me in all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Quia in hac vice mittam omnes plagas meas super cor tuum, et super servos tuos, et super populum tuum: ut scias quod non sit similis mei in omni terra.

verses.text: For now I will stretch out my hand to strike thee, and thy people with pestilence, and thou shalt perish from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Nunc enim extendens manum percutiam te, et populum tuum peste, peribisque de terra.

verses.text: And therefore have I raised thee, that I may shew my power in thee, and my name may be spoken of throughout all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco autem posui te, ut ostendam in te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra.

verses.text: Dost thou yet hold back my people: and wilt thou not let them go?
verses.textLatin: Adhuc retines populum meum, et non vis dimittere eum?

verses.text: Behold I will cause it to rain to morrow at this same hour, an exceeding great hail: such as hath not been in Egypt from the day that it was founded, until this present time.
verses.textLatin: En pluam cras hac ipsa hora grandinem multam nimis, qualis non fuit in Ægypto a die qua fundata est, usque in præsens tempus.

verses.text: Send therefore now presently, and gather together thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field: for men and beasts, and all things that shall be found abroad, and not gathered together out of the fields, which the hail shall fall upon, shall die.
verses.textLatin: Mitte ergo jam nunc, et congrega jumenta tua, et omnia quæ habes in agro: homines enim, et jumenta, et universa quæ inventa fuerint foris, nec congregata de agris, cecideritque super ea grando, morientur.

verses.text: He that feared the word of the Lord among Pharao’s servants, made his servants and his cattle flee into houses:
verses.textLatin: Qui timuit verbum Domini de servis Pharaonis, facit confugere servos suos et jumenta in domos:

verses.text: But he that regarded not the word of the Lord, left his servants and his cattle in the fields:
verses.textLatin: qui autem neglexit sermonem Domini, dimisit servos suos et jumenta in agris.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand towards heaven, that there may be hail in the whole land of Egypt, upon men, and upon beasts, and upon every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam in cælum, ut fiat grando in universa terra Ægypti super homines, et super jumenta, et super omnem herbam agri in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod towards heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning running along the ground: and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Extenditque Moyses virgam in cælum, et Dominus dedit tonitrua, et grandinem, ac discurrentia fulgura super terram: pluitque Dominus grandinem super terram Ægypti.

verses.text: And the hail and fire mixed with it drove on together: and it was of so great bigness, as never before was seen in the whole land of Egypt since that nation was founded.
verses.textLatin: Et grando et ignis mista pariter ferebantur: tantæque fuit magnitudinis, quanta ante numquam apparuit in universa terra Ægypti ex quo gens illa condita est.

verses.text: And the hail destroyed through all the land of Egypt all things that were in the fields, both man and beast: and the hail smote every herb of the field, and it broke every tree of the country.
verses.textLatin: Et percussit grando in omni terra Ægypti cuncta quæ fuerunt in agris, ab homine usque ad jumentum: cunctamque herbam agri percussit grando, et omne lignum regionis confregit.

verses.text: Only in the land of Gessen, where the children of Israel were, the hail fell not.
verses.textLatin: Tantum in terra Gessen, ubi erant filii Israël, grando non cecidit.

verses.text: And Pharao sent and called Moses and Aaron, saying to them: I have sinned this time also; the Lord is just: I and my people are wicked.
verses.textLatin: Misitque Pharao, et vocavit Moysen et Aaron, dicens ad eos: Peccavi etiam nunc: Dominus justus; ego et populus meus, impii.

verses.text: Pray ye to the Lord, that the thunderings of God and the hail may cease: that I may let you go, and that you may stay here no longer.
verses.textLatin: Orate Dominum ut desinant tonitrua Dei, et grando: ut dimittam vos, et nequaquam hic ultra maneatis.

verses.text: Moses said: As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will stretch forth my hands to the Lord, and the thunders shall cease, and the hail shall be no more: that thou mayst know that the earth is the Lord’s.
verses.textLatin: Ait Moyses: Cum egressus fuero de urbe, extendam palmas meas ad Dominum, et cessabunt tonitrua, et grando non erit, ut scias quia Domini est terra:

verses.text: But I know that neither thou, nor thy servants do yet fear the Lord God.
verses.textLatin: novi autem quod et tu et servi tui necdum timeatis Dominum Deum.

verses.text: The flax therefore and the barley were hurt, because the barley was green, and the flax was now bolled:
verses.textLatin: Linum ergo et hordeum læsum est, eo quod hordeum esset virens, et linum jam folliculos germinaret:

verses.text: But the wheat, and other winter corn were not hurt, because they were lateward.
verses.textLatin: triticum autem et far non sunt læsa, quia serotina erant.

verses.text: And when Moses was gone from Pharao out of the city, he stretched forth his hands to the Lord: and the thunders and the hail ceased, neither did there drop any more rain upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Egressusque Moyses a Pharaone ex urbe, tetendit manus ad Dominum: et cessaverunt tonitrua et grando, nec ultra stillavit pluvia super terram.

verses.text: And Pharao seeing that the rain and the hail, and the thunders were ceased, increased his sin.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Pharao quod cessasset pluvia, et grando, et tonitrua, auxit peccatum:

verses.text: And his heart was hardened, and the heart of his servants, and it was made exceeding hard: neither did he let the children of Israel go, as the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses.
verses.textLatin: et ingravatum est cor ejus, et servorum illius, et induratum nimis: nec dimisit filios Israël, sicut præceperat Dominus per manum Moysi.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao; for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants: that I may work these my signs in him.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Ingredere ad Pharaonem: ego enim induravi cor ejus, et servorum illius, ut faciam signa mea hæc in eo:

verses.text: And thou mayest tell in the ears of thy sons, and of thy grandsons, how often I have plagued the Egyptians, and wrought my signs amongst them: and you may know that I am the Lord:
verses.textLatin: et narres in auribus filii tui, et nepotum tuorum, quoties contriverim Ægyptios, et signa mea fecerim in eis: et sciatis quia ego Dominus.

verses.text: Therefore Moses and Aaron went in to Pharao, and said to him: Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews: How long refusest thou to submit to me? let my people go, to sacrifice to me.
verses.textLatin: Introierunt ergo Moyses et Aaron ad Pharaonem, et dixerunt ei: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Hebræorum: Usquequo non vis subjici mihi? dimitte populum meum, ut sacrificet mihi.

verses.text: But if thou resist, and wilt not let them go, behold I will bring in to morrow the locust into thy coasts:
verses.textLatin: Sin autem resistis, et non vis dimittere eum: ecce ego inducam cras locustam in fines tuos:

verses.text: To cover the face of the earth that nothing thereof may appear, but that which the hail hath left may be eaten: for they shall feed upon all the trees that spring in the fields.
verses.textLatin: quæ operiat superficiem terræ, ne quidquam ejus appareat, sed comedatur quod residuum fuerit grandini: corrodet enim omnia ligna quæ germinant in agris.

verses.text: And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of thy servants, and of all the Egyptians: such a number as thy fathers have not seen, nor thy grandfathers, from the time they were first upon the earth, until this present day. And he turned himself away, and went forth from Pharao.
verses.textLatin: Et implebunt domos tuas, et servorum tuorum, et omnium Ægyptiorum, quantam non viderunt patres tui, et avi, ex quo orti sunt super terram, usque in præsentem diem. Avertitque se, et egressus est a Pharaone.

verses.text: And Pharao’s servants said to him: How long shall we endure this scandal? let the men go to sacrifice to the Lord their God. Dost thou not see that Egypt is undone?
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt autem servi Pharaonis ad eum: Usquequo patiemur hoc scandalum? dimitte homines, ut sacrificent Domino Deo suo; nonne vides quod perierit Ægyptus?

verses.text: And they called back Moses, and Aaron to Pharao: and he said to them: Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God: who are they that shall go?
verses.textLatin: Revocaveruntque Moysen et Aaron ad Pharaonem: qui dixit eis: Ite, sacrificate Domino Deo vestro: quinam sunt qui ituri sunt?

verses.text: Moses said: We will go with our young and old, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and herds: for it is the solemnity of the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Ait Moyses: Cum parvulis nostris, et senioribus pergemus, cum filiis et filiabus, cum ovibus et armentis: est enim solemnitas Domini Dei nostri.

verses.text: And Pharao answered: So be the Lord with you, as I shall let you and your children go: who can doubt but that you intend some great evil?
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Pharao: Sic Dominus sit vobiscum, quomodo ego dimittam vos, et parvulos vestros, cui dubium est quod pessime cogitetis?

verses.text: It shall not be so: but go ye men only, and sacrifice to the Lord: for this yourselves also desired. And immediately they were cast out from Pharao’s presence.
verses.textLatin: non fiet ita, sed ite tantum viri, et sacrificate Domino: hoc enim et ipsi petistis. Statimque ejecti sunt de conspectu Pharaonis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand upon the land of Egypt unto the locust, that it come upon it, and devour every herb that is left after the hail.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam super terram Ægypti ad locustam, ut ascendat super eam, et devoret omnem herbam quæ residua fuerit grandini.

verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod upon the land of Egypt: and the Lord brought a burning wind all that day, and night: and when it was morning, the burning wind raised the locusts:
verses.textLatin: Et extendit Moyses virgam super terram Ægypti: et Dominus induxit ventum urentem tota die illa et nocte: et mane facto, ventus urens levavit locustas.

verses.text: And they came up over the whole land of Egypt: and rested in all the coasts of the Egyptians innumerable, the like as had not been before that time, nor shall be hereafter.
verses.textLatin: Quæ ascenderunt super universam terram Ægypti: et sederunt in cunctis finibus Ægyptiorum innumerabiles, quales ante illud tempus non fuerant, nec postea futuræ sunt.

verses.text: And they covered the whole face of the earth, wasting all things. And the grass of the earth was devoured, and what fruits soever were on the trees, which the hail had left: and there remained not any thing that was green on the trees, or in the herbs of the earth in all Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Operueruntque universam superficiem terræ, vastantes omnia. Devorata est igitur herba terræ, et quidquid pomorum in arboribus fuit, quæ grando dimiserat: nihilque omnino virens relictum est in lignis et in herbis terræ, in cuncta Ægypto.

verses.text: Wherefore Pharao in haste called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem festinus Pharao vocavit Moysen et Aaron, et dixit eis: Peccavi in Dominum Deum vestrum, et in vos.

verses.text: But now forgive me my sin this time also, and pray to the Lord your God, that he take away from me this death.
verses.textLatin: Sed nunc dimittite peccatum mihi etiam hac vice, et rogate Dominum Deum vestrum, ut auferat a me mortem istam.

verses.text: And Moses going forth from the presence of Pharao, prayed to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Egressusque Moyses de conspectu Pharaonis, oravit Dominum.

verses.text: And he made a very strong wind to blow from the west, and it took the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea: there remained not so much as one in all the coasts of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Qui flare fecit ventum ab occidente vehementissimum, et arreptam locustam projecit in mare Rubrum: non remansit ne una quidem in cunctis finibus Ægypti.

verses.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, neither did he let the children of Israel go.
verses.textLatin: Et induravit Dominus cor Pharaonis, nec dimisit filios Israël.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out thy hand towards heaven: and may there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, so thick that it may be felt.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam in cælum: et sint tenebræ super terram Ægypti tam densæ, ut palpari queant.

verses.text: And Moses stretched forth his hand towards heaven: and there came horrible darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.textLatin: Extenditque Moyses manum in cælum: et factæ sunt tenebræ horribiles in universa terra Ægypti tribus diebus.

verses.text: No man saw his brother, nor moved himself out of the place where he was: but wheresoever the children of Israel dwelt there was light.
verses.textLatin: Nemo vidit fratrem suum, nec movit se de loco in quo erat: ubicumque autem habitabant filii Israël, lux erat.

verses.text: And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Go sacrifice to the Lord: let your sheep only, and herds remain; let your children go with you.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Pharao Moysen et Aaron, et dixit eis: Ite, sacrificate Domino: oves tantum vestræ et armenta remaneant, parvuli vestri eant vobiscum.

verses.text: Moses said: Thou shalt give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, to the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Ait Moyses: Hostias quoque et holocausta dabis nobis, quæ offeramus Domino Deo nostro.

verses.text: All the flocks shall go with us: there shall not a hoof remain of them: for they are necessary for the service of the Lord our God: especially as we know not what must be offered, till we come to the very place.
verses.textLatin: Cuncti greges pergent nobiscum; non remanebit ex eis ungula: quæ necessaria sunt in cultum Domini Dei nostri: præsertim cum ignoremus quid debeat immolari, donec ad ipsum locum perveniamus.

verses.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, and he would not let them go.
verses.textLatin: Induravit autem Dominus cor Pharaonis, et noluit dimittere eos.

verses.text: And Pharao said to Moses: Get thee from me, and beware thou see not my face any more: in what day soever thou shalt come in my sight, thou shalt die.
