verses.textLatin: Dixitque Pharao ad Moysen: Recede a me, et cave ne ultra videas faciem meam: quocumque die apparueris mihi, morieris.

verses.text: Moses answered: So shall it be as thou hast spoken, I will not see thy face any more.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Moyses: Ita fiet ut locutus es: non videbo ultra faciem tuam.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses: Yet one plague more will I bring upon Pharao and Egypt, and after that he shall let you go and thrust you out.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Adhuc una plaga tangam Pharaonem et Ægyptum, et post hæc dimittet vos, et exire compellet.

verses.text: Therefore thou shalt tell all the people that every man ask of his friend, and every woman of her neighbour, vessels of silver, and of gold.
verses.textLatin: Dices ergo omni plebi ut postulet vir ab amico suo, et mulier a vicina sua, vasa argentea et aurea.

verses.text: And the Lord will give favour to his people in the sight of the Egyptians. And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharao’s servants, and of all the people.
verses.textLatin: Dabit autem Dominus gratiam populo suo coram Ægyptiis. Fuitque Moyses vir magnus valde in terra Ægypti coram servis Pharaonis et omni populo.

verses.text: And he said: Thus said the Lord: At midnight I will enter into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Hæc dicit Dominus: Media nocte egrediar in Ægyptum:

verses.text: And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die, from the firstborn of Pharao who sitteth on his throne, even to the firstborn of the handmaid that is at the mill, and all the firstborn of beasts.
verses.textLatin: et morietur omne primogenitum in terra Ægyptiorum, a primogenito Pharaonis, qui sedet in solio ejus, usque ad primogenitum ancillæ quæ est ad molam, et omnia primogenita jumentorum.

verses.text: And there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as neither hath been before, nor shall be hereafter.
verses.textLatin: Eritque clamor magnus in universa terra Ægypti, qualis nec ante fuit, nec postea futurus est.

verses.text: But with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise, from man even to beast: that you may know how wonderful a difference the Lord maketh between the Egyptians and Israel.
verses.textLatin: Apud omnes autem filios Israël non mutiet canis ab homine usque ad pecus: ut sciatis quanto miraculo dividat Dominus Ægyptios et Israël.

verses.text: And all these thy servants shall come down to me, and shall worship me, saying: Go forth thou, and all the people that is under thee: after that we will go out.
verses.textLatin: Descendentque omnes servi tui isti ad me, et adorabunt me, dicentes: Egredere tu, et omnis populus qui subjectus est tibi: post hæc egrediemur.

verses.text: And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry. But the Lord said to Moses: Pharao will not hear you, that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit a Pharaone iratus nimis. Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Non audiet vos Pharao ut multa signa fiant in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron did all the wonders that are written, before Pharao. And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, neither did he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.textLatin: Moyses autem et Aaron fecerunt omnia ostenta, quæ scripta sunt, coram Pharaone. Et induravit Dominus cor Pharaonis, nec dimisit filios Israël de terra sua.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron in terra Ægypti:

verses.text: This month shall be to you the beginning of months: it shall be the first in the months of the year.
verses.textLatin: Mensis iste, vobis principium mensium: primus erit in mensibus anni.

verses.text: Speak ye to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: On the tenth day of this month let every man take a lamb by their families and houses.
verses.textLatin: Loquimini ad universum cœtum filiorum Israël, et dicite eis: Decima die mensis hujus tollat unusquisque agnum per familias et domos suas.

verses.text: But if the number be less than may suffice to eat the lamb, he shall take unto him his neighbour that joineth to his house, according to the number of souls which may be enough to eat the lamb.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem minor est numerus ut sufficere possit ad vescendum agnum, assumet vicinum suum qui junctus est domui suæ, juxta numerum animarum quæ sufficere possunt ad esum agni.

verses.text: And it shall be a lamb without blemish, a male, of one year: according to which rite also you shall take a kid.
verses.textLatin: Erit autem agnus absque macula, masculus, anniculus: juxta quem ritum tolletis et hædum.

verses.text: And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month: and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it in the evening.
verses.textLatin: Et servabitis eum usque ad quartamdecimam diem mensis hujus: immolabitque eum universa multitudo filiorum Israël ad vesperam.

verses.text: And they shall take of the blood thereof, and put it upon both the side posts, and on the upper door posts of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.
verses.textLatin: Et sument de sanguine ejus, ac ponent super utrumque postem, et in superliminaribus domorum, in quibus comedent illum.

verses.text: And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted at the fire, and unleavened bread with wild lettuce.
verses.textLatin: Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni, et azymos panes cum lactucis agrestibus.

verses.text: You shall not eat thereof any thing raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted at the fire: you shall eat the head with the feet and entrails thereof.
verses.textLatin: Non comedetis ex eo crudum quid, nec coctum aqua, sed tantum assum igni: caput cum pedibus ejus et intestinis vorabitis.

verses.text: Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning. If there be any thing left, you shall burn it with fire.
verses.textLatin: Nec remanebit quidquam ex eo usque mane; si quid residuum fuerit, igne comburetis.

verses.text: And thus you shall eat it: you shall gird your reins, and you shall have shoes on your feet, holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste: for it is the Phase (that is the Passage) of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sic autem comedetis illum: renes vestros accingetis, et calceamenta habebitis in pedibus, tenentes baculos in manibus, et comedetis festinanter: est enim Phase (id est, transitus) Domini.

verses.text: And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and will kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt both man and beast: and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et transibo per terram Ægypti nocte illa, percutiamque omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti ab homine usque ad pecus: et in cunctis diis Ægypti faciam judicia. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be: and I shall see the blood, and shall pass over you: and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I shall strike the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Erit autem sanguis vobis in signum in ædibus in quibus eritis: et videbo sanguinem, et transibo vos: nec erit in vobis plaga disperdens quando percussero terram Ægypti.

verses.text: And this day shall be for a memorial to you: and you shall keep it a feast to the Lord in your generations with an everlasting observance.
verses.textLatin: Habebitis autem hunc diem in monimentum: et celebrabitis eam solemnem Domino in generationibus vestris cultu sempiterno.

verses.text: Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread: in the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses: whosoever shall eat any thing leavened, from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall perish out of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Septem diebus azyma comedetis: in die primo non erit fermentum in domibus vestris: quicumque comederit fermentatum, peribit anima illa de Israël, a primo die usque ad diem septimum.

verses.text: The first day shall be holy and solemn, and the seventh day shall be kept with the like solemnity: you shall do no work in them, except those things that belong to eating.
verses.textLatin: Dies prima erit sancta atque solemnis, et dies septima eadem festivitate venerabilis: nihil operis facietis in eis, exceptis his, quæ ad vescendum pertinent.

verses.text: And you shall observe the feast of the unleavened bread: for in this same day I will bring forth your army out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day in your generations by a perpetual observance.
verses.textLatin: Et observabitis azyma: in eadem enim ipsa die educam exercitum vestrum de terra Ægypti, et custodietis diem istum in generationes vestras ritu perpetuo.

verses.text: The first month, the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the same month in the evening.
verses.textLatin: Primo mense, quartadecima die mensis ad vesperam, comedetis azyma usque ad diem vigesimam primam ejusdem mensis ad vesperam.

verses.text: Seven days there shall not be found any leaven in your houses: he that shall eat leavened bread, his soul shall perish out of the assembly of Israel, whether he be a stranger or born in the land.
verses.textLatin: Septem diebus fermentum non invenietur in domibus vestris: qui comederit fermentatum, peribit anima ejus de cœtu Israël, tam de advenis quam de indigenis terræ.

verses.text: You shall not eat any thing leavened: in all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.textLatin: Omne fermentatum non comedetis: in cunctis habitaculis vestris edetis azyma.

verses.text: And Moses called all the ancients of the children of Israel, and said to them: Go take a lamb by your families, and sacrifice the Phase.
verses.textLatin: Vocavit autem Moyses omnes seniores filiorum Israël, et dixit ad eos: Ite tollentes animal per familias vestras, et immolate Phase.

verses.text: And dip a bunch of hyssop in the blood that is at the door, and sprinkle the transom of the door therewith, and both the door cheeks: let none of you go out of the door of his house till morning.
verses.textLatin: Fasciculumque hyssopi tingite in sanguine qui est in limine, et aspergite ex eo superliminare, et utrumque postem: nullus vestrum egrediatur ostium domus suæ usque mane.

verses.text: For the Lord will pass through striking the Egyptians: and when he shall see the blood on the transom, and on both the posts, he will pass over the door of the house, and not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses and to hurt you.
verses.textLatin: Transibit enim Dominus percutiens Ægyptios: cumque viderit sanguinem in superliminari, et in utroque poste, transcendet ostium domus, et non sinet percussorem ingredi domos vestras et lædere.

verses.text: Thou shalt keep this thing as a law for thee and thy children for ever.
verses.textLatin: Custodi verbum istud legitimum tibi et filiis tuis usque in æternum.

verses.text: And when you have entered into the land which the Lord will give you as he hath promised, you shall observe these ceremonies.
verses.textLatin: Cumque introieritis terram, quam Dominus daturus est vobis ut pollicitus est, observabitis cæremonias istas.

verses.text: And when your children shall say to you: What is the meaning of this service?
verses.textLatin: Et cum dixerint vobis filii vestri: Quæ est ista religio?

verses.text: You shall say to them: It is the victim of the passage of the Lord, when he passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, striking the Egyptians, and saving our houses. And the people bowing themselves, adored.
verses.textLatin: Dicetis eis: Victima transitus Domini est, quando transivit super domos filiorum Israël in Ægypto, percutiens Ægyptios, et domos nostras liberans. Incurvatusque populus adoravit.

verses.text: And the children of Israel going forth did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Et egressi filii Israël fecerunt sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi et Aaron.

verses.text: And it came to pass at midnight, the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao, who sat on his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive woman that was in the prison, and all the firstborn of cattle.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem in noctis medio, percussit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito Pharaonis, qui in solio ejus sedebat, usque ad primogenitum captivæ quæ erat in carcere, et omne primogenitum jumentorum.

verses.text: And Pharao arose in the night, and all his servants, and all Egypt; and there arose a great cry in Egypt: for there was not a house wherein there lay not one dead.
verses.textLatin: Surrexitque Pharao nocte, et omnes servi ejus, cunctaque Ægyptus: et ortus est clamor magnus in Ægypto: neque enim erat domus in qua non jaceret mortuus.

verses.text: And Pharao calling Moses and Aaron, in the night, said: Arise and go forth from among my people, you and the children of Israel: go, sacrifice to the Lord as you say.
verses.textLatin: Vocatisque Pharao Moyse et Aaron nocte, ait: Surgite et egredimini a populo meo, vos et filii Israël: ite, immolate Domino sicut dicitis.

verses.text: Your sheep and herds take along with you, as you demanded, and departing, bless me.
verses.textLatin: Oves vestras et armenta assumite ut petieratis, et abeuntes benedicite mihi.

verses.text: And the Egyptians pressed the people to go forth out of the land speedily, saying: We shall all die.
verses.textLatin: Urgebantque Ægyptii populum de terra exire velociter, dicentes: Omnes moriemur.

verses.text: The people therefore took dough before it was leavened: and tying it in their cloaks, put it on their shoulders.
verses.textLatin: Tulit igitur populus conspersam farinam antequam fermentaretur: et ligans in palliis, posuit super humeros suos.

verses.text: And the children of Israel did as Moses had commanded: and they asked of the Egyptians vessels of silver and gold, and very much raiment.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque filii Israël sicut præceperat Moyses: et petierunt ab Ægyptiis vasa argentea et aurea, vestemque plurimam.

verses.text: And the Lord gave favour to the people in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them: and they stripped the Egyptians.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem dedit gratiam populo coram Ægyptiis ut commodarent eis: et spoliaverunt Ægyptios.

verses.text: And the children of Israel set forward from Ramesse to Socoth, being about six hundred thousand men on foot, beside children.
verses.textLatin: Profectique sunt filii Israël de Ramesse in Socoth, sexcenta fere millia peditum virorum, absque parvulis.

verses.text: And a mixed multitude without number went up also with them, sheep and herds and beasts of divers kinds, exceeding many.
verses.textLatin: Sed et vulgus promiscuum innumerabile ascendit cum eis, oves et armenta et animantia diversi generis multa nimis.

verses.text: And they baked the meal, which a little before they had brought out of Egypt, in dough: and they made earth cakes unleavened: for it could not be leavened, the Egyptians pressing them to depart, and not suffering them to make any stay: neither did they think of preparing any meat.
verses.textLatin: Coxeruntque farinam, quam dudum de Ægypto conspersam tulerant: et fecerunt subcinericios panes azymos: neque enim poterant fermentari, cogentibus exire Ægyptiis, et nullam facere sinentibus moram: nec pulmenti quidquam occurrerat præparare.

verses.text: And the abode of the children of Israel that they made in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
verses.textLatin: Habitatio autem filiorum Israël qua manserunt in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum.

verses.text: Which being expired, the same day all the army of the Lord went forth out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Quibus expletis, eadem die egressus est omnis exercitus Domini de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: This is the observable night of the Lord, when he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt: this night all the children of Israel must observe in their generations.
verses.textLatin: Nox ista est observabilis Domini, quando eduxit eos de terra Ægypti: hanc observare debent omnes filii Israël in generationibus suis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: This is the service of the Phase: No foreigner shall eat of it.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron: Hæc est religio Phase: omnis alienigena non comedet ex eo.

verses.text: But every bought servant shall be circumcised, and so shall eat.
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem servus emptitius circumcidetur, et sic comedet.

verses.text: The stranger and the hireling shall not eat thereof.
verses.textLatin: Advena et mercenarius non edent ex eo.

verses.text: In one house shall it be eaten, neither shall you carry forth of the flesh thereof out of the house, neither shall you break a bone thereof.
verses.textLatin: In una domo comedetur, nec efferetis de carnibus ejus foras, nec os illius confringetis.

verses.text: All the assembly of the children of Israel shall keep it.
verses.textLatin: Omnis cœtus filiorum Israël faciet illud.

verses.text: And if any stranger be willing to dwell among you, and to keep the Phase of the Lord, all his males shall first be circumcised, and then shall he celebrate it according to the manner: and he shall be as he that is born in the land: but if any man be uncircumcised, he shall not eat thereof.
verses.textLatin: Quod si quis peregrinorum in vestram voluerit transire coloniam, et facere Phase Domini, circumcidetur prius omne masculinum ejus, et tunc rite celebrabit: eritque sicut indigena terræ: si quis autem circumcisus non fuerit, non vescetur ex eo.

verses.text: The same law shall be to him that is born in the land, and to the proselyte that sojourneth with you.
verses.textLatin: Eadem lex erit indigenæ et colono qui peregrinatur apud vos.

verses.text: And all the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque omnes filii Israël sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi et Aaron.

verses.text: And the same day the Lord brought forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.
verses.textLatin: Et eadem die eduxit Dominus filios Israël de terra Ægypti per turmas suas.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Sanctify unto me every firstborn that openeth the womb among the children of Israel, as well of men as of beasts: for they are all mine.
verses.textLatin: Sanctifica mihi omne primogenitum quod aperit vulvam in filiis Israël, tam de hominibus quam de jumentis: mea sunt enim omnia.

verses.text: And Moses said to the people: Remember this day in which you came forth out of Egypt, and out of the house of bondage, for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought you forth out of this place: that you eat no leavened bread.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses ad populum: Mementote diei hujus in qua egressi estis de Ægypto et de domo servitutis, quoniam in manu forti eduxit vos Dominus de loco isto: ut non comedatis fermentatum panem.

verses.text: This day you go forth in the month of new corn.
verses.textLatin: Hodie egredimini mense novarum frugum.

verses.text: And when the Lord shall have brought thee into the land of the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, and the Amorrhite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to thy fathers that he would give thee, a land that floweth with milk and honey, thou shalt celebrate this manner of sacred rites in this month.
verses.textLatin: Cumque introduxerit te Dominus in terram Chananæi, et Hethæi, et Amorrhæi, et Hevæi, et Jebusæi, quam juravit patribus tuis ut daret tibi, terram fluentem lacte et melle, celebrabis hunc morem sacrorum mense isto.

verses.text: Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread: and on the seventh day shall be the solemnity of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Septem diebus vesceris azymis: et in die septimo erit solemnitas Domini.

verses.text: Unleavened bread shall you eat seven days: there shall not be seen any thing leavened with thee, nor in all thy coasts.
verses.textLatin: Azyma comedetis septem diebus: non apparebit apud te aliquid fermentatum, nec in cunctis finibus tuis.

verses.text: And thou shalt tell thy son in that day, saying: This is what the Lord did to me when I came forth out of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Narrabisque filio tuo in die illo, dicens: Hoc est quod fecit mihi Dominus quando egressus sum de Ægypto.

verses.text: And it shall be as a sign in thy hand, and as a memorial before thy eyes: and that the law of the Lord be always in thy mouth, for with a strong hand the Lord hath brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et erit quasi signum in manu tua, et quasi monimentum ante oculos tuos: et ut lex Domini semper sit in ore tuo, in manu enim forti eduxit te Dominus de Ægypto.

verses.text: Thou shalt keep this observance at the set time from days to days.
verses.textLatin: Custodies hujuscemodi cultum statuto tempore a diebus in dies.

verses.text: And when the Lord shall have brought thee into the land of the Chanaanite, as he swore to thee and thy fathers, and shall give it thee:
verses.textLatin: Cumque introduxerit te Dominus in terram Chananæi, sicut juravit tibi et patribus tuis, et dederit tibi eam:

verses.text: Thou shalt set apart all that openeth the womb for the Lord, and all that is first brought forth of thy cattle: whatsoever thou shalt have of the male sex, thou shalt consecrate to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: separabis omne quod aperit vulvam Domino, et quod primitivum est in pecoribus tuis: quidquid habueris masculini sexus, consecrabis Domino.

verses.text: The firstborn of an ass thou shalt change for a sheep: and if thou do not redeem it, thou shalt kill it. And every firstborn of men thou shalt redeem with a price.
verses.textLatin: Primogenitum asini mutabis ove: quod si non redemeris, interficies. Omne autem primogenitum hominis de filiis tuis, pretio redimes.

verses.text: And when thy son shall ask thee to morrow, saying: What is this? thou shalt answer him: With a strong hand did the Lord bring us forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
verses.textLatin: Cumque interrogaverit te filius tuus cras, dicens: Quid est hoc? respondebis ei: In manu forti eduxit nos Dominus de terra Ægypti, de domo servitutis.

verses.text: For when Pharao was hardened, and would not let us go, the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beasts: therefore I sacrifice to the Lord all that openeth the womb of the male sex, and all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.
verses.textLatin: Nam cum induratus esset Pharao, et nollet nos dimittere, occidit Dominus omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, a primogenito hominis usque ad primogenitum jumentorum: idcirco immolo Domino omne quod aperit vulvam masculini sexus, et omnia primogenita filiorum meorum redimo.

verses.text: And it shall be as a sign in thy hand, and as a thing hung between thy eyes, for a remembrance: because the Lord hath brought us forth out of Egypt by a strong hand.
verses.textLatin: Erit igitur quasi signum in manu tua, et quasi appensum quid, ob recordationem, inter oculos tuos: eo quod in manu forti eduxit nos Dominus de Ægypto.

verses.text: And when Pharao had sent out the people, the Lord led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines which is near: thinking lest perhaps they would repent, if they should see wars arise against them, and would return into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Igitur cum emisisset Pharao populum, non eos duxit Deus per viam terræ Philisthiim quæ vicina est: reputans ne forte pœniteret eum, si vidisset adversum se bella consurgere, et reverteretur in Ægyptum.

verses.text: But he led them about by the way of the desert, which is by the Red Sea: and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Sed circumduxit per viam deserti, quæ est juxta mare Rubrum: et armati ascenderunt filii Israël de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And Moses took Joseph’s bones with him: because he had adjured the children of Israel, saying: God shall visit you, carry out my bones from hence with you.
verses.textLatin: Tulit quoque Moyses ossa Joseph secum: eo quod adjurasset filios Israël, dicens: Visitabit vos Deus; efferte ossa mea hinc vobiscum.

verses.text: And marching from Socoth they encamped in Etham in the utmost coasts of the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Profectique de Socoth castrametati sunt in Etham, in extremis finibus solitudinis.

verses.text: And the Lord went before them to shew the way by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire: that he might be the guide of their journey at both times.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem præcedebat eos ad ostendendam viam per diem in columna nubis, et per noctem in columna ignis: ut dux esset itineris utroque tempore.

verses.text: There never failed the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, before the people.
verses.textLatin: Numquam defuit columna nubis per diem, nec columna ignis per noctem, coram populo.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel: Let them turn and encamp over against Phihahiroth which is between Magdal and the sea over against Beelsephon: you shall encamp before it upon the sea.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël: Reversi castrametentur e regione Phihahiroth, quæ est inter Magdalum et mare contra Beelsephon: in conspectu ejus castra ponetis super mare.

verses.text: And Pharao will say of the children of Israel: They are straitened in the land, the desert hath shut them in.
verses.textLatin: Dicturusque est Pharao super filiis Israël: Coarctati sunt in terra; conclusit eos desertum.

verses.text: And I shall harden his heart, and he will pursue you: and I shall be glorified in Pharao, and in all his army: and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord. And they did so.
verses.textLatin: Et indurabo cor ejus, ac persequetur vos: et glorificabor in Pharaone, et in omni exercitu ejus; scientque Ægyptii quia ego sum Dominus. Feceruntque ita.

verses.text: And it was told the king of the Egyptians that the people was fled: and the heart of Pharao and of his servants was changed with regard to the people, and they said: What meant we to do, that we let Israel go from serving us?
verses.textLatin: Et nuntiatum est regi Ægyptiorum quod fugisset populus: immutatumque est cor Pharaonis et servorum ejus super populo, et dixerunt: Quid voluimus facere ut dimitteremus Israël, ne serviret nobis?

verses.text: So he made ready his chariot, and took all his people with him.
verses.textLatin: Junxit ergo currum, et omnem populum suum assumpsit secum.

verses.text: And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots that were in Egypt: and the captains of the whole army.
verses.textLatin: Tulitque sexcentos currus electos, et quidquid in Ægypto curruum fuit: et duces totius exercitus.

verses.text: And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao king of Egypt, and he pursued the children of Israel: but they were gone forth in a mighty hand.
verses.textLatin: Induravitque Dominus cor Pharaonis regis Ægypti, et persecutus est filios Israël: at illi egressi sunt in manu excelsa.

verses.text: And when the Egyptians followed the steps of them who were gone before, they found them encamped at the sea side: all Pharao’s horse and chariots, and the whole army were in Phihahiroth before Beelsephon.
verses.textLatin: Cumque persequerentur Ægyptii vestigia præcedentium, repererunt eos in castris super mare: omnis equitatus et currus Pharaonis, et universus exercitus, erant in Phihahiroth contra Beelsephon.

verses.text: And when Pharao drew near, the children of Israel, lifting up their eyes, saw the Egyptians behind them: and they feared exceedingly, and cried to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Cumque appropinquasset Pharao, levantes filii Israël oculos, viderunt Ægyptios post se, et timuerunt valde: clamaveruntque ad Dominum,

verses.text: And they said to Moses: Perhaps there were no graves in Egypt, therefore thou hast brought us to die in the wilderness: why wouldst thou do this, to lead us out of Egypt?
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt ad Moysen: Forsitan non erant sepulchra in Ægypto, ideo tulisti nos ut moreremur in solitudine: quid hoc facere voluisti, ut educeres nos ex Ægypto?

verses.text: Is not this the word that we spoke to thee in Egypt, saying: Depart from us that we may serve the Egyptians? for it was much better to serve them, than to die in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: nonne iste est sermo, quem loquebamur ad te in Ægypto, dicentes: Recede a nobis, ut serviamus Ægyptiis? multo enim melius erat servire eis, quam mori in solitudine.

verses.text: And Moses said to the people: Fear not: stand and see the great wonders of the Lord, which he will do this day: for the Egyptians, whom you see now, you shall see no more for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses ad populum: Nolite timere: state, et videte magnalia Domini quæ facturus est hodie: Ægyptios enim, quos nunc videtis, nequaquam ultra videbitis usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: The Lord will fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.
verses.textLatin: Dominus pugnabit pro vobis, et vos tacebitis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Why criest thou to me? Speak to the children of Israel to go forward.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Quid clamas ad me? loquere filiis Israël ut proficiscantur.

verses.text: But lift thou up thy rod, and stretch forth thy hand over the sea, and divide it: that the children of Israel may go through the midst of the sea on dry ground.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem eleva virgam tuam, et extende manum tuam super mare, et divide illud: ut gradiantur filii Israël in medio mari per siccum.

verses.text: And I will harden the heart of the Egyptians to pursue you: and I will be glorified in Pharao, and in all his host, and in his chariots, and in his horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem indurabo cor Ægyptiorum ut persequantur vos: et glorificabor in Pharaone, et in omni exercitu ejus, et in curribus et in equitibus illius.

verses.text: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall be glorified in Pharao, and in his chariots and in his horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Et scient Ægyptii quia ego sum Dominus cum glorificatus fuero in Pharaone, et in curribus atque in equitibus ejus.

verses.text: And the angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, removing, went behind them: and together with him the pillar of the cloud, leaving the forepart,
verses.textLatin: Tollensque se angelus Dei, qui præcedebat castra Israël, abiit post eos: et cum eo pariter columna nubis, priora dimittens, post tergum

verses.text: Stood behind, between the Egyptians’ camp and the camp of Israel: and it was a dark cloud, and enlightening the night, so that they could not come at one another all the night.
verses.textLatin: stetit, inter castra Ægyptiorum et castra Israël: et erat nubes tenebrosa, et illuminans noctem, ita ut ad se invicem toto noctis tempore accedere non valerent.

verses.text: And when Moses had stretched forth his hand over the sea, the Lord took it away by a strong and burning wind blowing all the night, and turned it into dry ground: and the water was divided.
verses.textLatin: Cumque extendisset Moyses manum super mare, abstulit illud Dominus flante vento vehementi et urente tota nocte, et vertit in siccum: divisaque est aqua.

verses.text: And the children of Israel went in through the midst of the sea dried up: for the water was as a wall on their right hand and on their left.
verses.textLatin: Et ingressi sunt filii Israël per medium sicci maris: erat enim aqua quasi murus a dextra eorum et læva.

verses.text: And the Egyptians pursuing went in after them, and all Pharao’s horses, his chariots and horsemen through the midst of the sea,
verses.textLatin: Persequentesque Ægyptii ingressi sunt post eos, et omnis equitatus Pharaonis, currus ejus et equites per medium maris.

verses.text: And now the morning watch was come, and behold the Lord looking upon the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, slew their host.
verses.textLatin: Jamque advenerat vigilia matutina, et ecce respiciens Dominus super castra Ægyptiorum per columnam ignis et nubis, interfecit exercitum eorum,

verses.text: And overthrew the wheels of the chariots, and they were carried into the deep. And the Egyptians said: Let us flee from Israel: for the Lord fighteth for them against us.
verses.textLatin: et subvertit rotas curruum, ferebanturque in profundum. Dixerunt ergo Ægyptii: Fugiamus Israëlem: Dominus enim pugnat pro eis contra nos.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand over the sea, that the waters may come again upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots and horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus ad Moysen: Extende manum tuam super mare, ut revertantur aquæ ad Ægyptios super currus et equites eorum.

verses.text: And when Moses had stretched forth his hand towards the sea, it returned at the first break of day to the former place: and as the Egyptians were fleeing away, the waters came upon them, and the Lord shut them up in the middle of the waves.
verses.textLatin: Cumque extendisset Moyses manum contra mare, reversum est primo diluculo ad priorem locum: fugientibusque Ægyptiis occurrerunt aquæ, et involvit eos Dominus in mediis fluctibus.

verses.text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen of all the army of Pharao, who had come into the sea after them, neither did there so much as one of them remain.
verses.textLatin: Reversæque sunt aquæ, et operuerunt currus et equites cuncti exercitus Pharaonis, qui sequentes ingressi fuerant mare: nec unus quidem superfuit ex eis.

verses.text: But the children of Israel marched through the midst of the sea upon dry land, and the waters were to them as a wall on the right hand and on the left:
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Israël perrexerunt per medium sicci maris, et aquæ eis erant quasi pro muro a dextris et a sinistris:

verses.text: And the Lord delivered Israel on that day out of the hands of the Egyptians.
verses.textLatin: liberavitque Dominus in die illa Israël de manu Ægyptiorum.

verses.text: And they saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore, and the mighty hand that the Lord had used against them: and the people feared the Lord, and they believed the Lord, and Moses his servant.
verses.textLatin: Et viderunt Ægyptios mortuos super littus maris, et manum magnam quam exercuerat Dominus contra eos: timuitque populus Dominum, et crediderunt Domino, et Moysi servo ejus.

verses.text: Then  Moses and the children of Israel sung this canticle to the Lord: and said: Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and the rider he hath thrown into the sea.
verses.textLatin: Tunc cecinit Moyses et filii Israël carmen hoc Domino, et dixerunt: Cantemus Domino: gloriose enim magnificatus est, equum et ascensorem dejecit in mare.

verses.text: The Lord is my strength and my praise, and he is become salvation to me: he is my God and I will glorify him: the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
verses.textLatin: Fortitudo mea, et laus mea Dominus, et factus est mihi in salutem: iste Deus meus, et glorificabo eum: Deus patris mei, et exaltabo eum.

verses.text: The Lord is as a man of war, Almighty is his name.
verses.textLatin: Dominus quasi vir pugnator, Omnipotens nomen ejus,

verses.text: Pharao’s chariots and his army he hath cast into the sea: his chosen captains are drowned in the Red Sea.
verses.textLatin: currus Pharaonis et exercitum ejus projecit in mare: electi principes ejus submersi sunt in mari Rubro.

verses.text: The depths have covered them, they are sunk to the bottom like a stone.
verses.textLatin: Abyssi operuerunt eos; descenderunt in profundum quasi lapis.

verses.text: Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength: thy right hand, O Lord, hath slain the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Dextera tua, Domine, magnificata est in fortitudine: dextera tua, Domine, percussit inimicum.

verses.text: And in the multitude of thy glory thou hast put down thy adversaries: thou hast sent thy wrath, which hath devoured them like stubble.
verses.textLatin: Et in multitudine gloriæ tuæ deposuisti adversarios tuos: misisti iram tuam, quæ devoravit eos sicut stipulam.

verses.text: And with the blast of thy anger the waters were gathered together: the flowing water stood, the depths were gathered together in the midst of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Et in spiritu furoris tui congregatæ sunt aquæ: stetit unda fluens, congregata sunt abyssi in medio mari.

verses.text: The enemy said: I will pursue and overtake, I will divide the spoils, my soul shall have its fill: I will draw my sword, my hand shall slay them.
verses.textLatin: Dixit inimicus: Persequar et comprehendam, dividam spolia, implebitur anima mea: evaginabo gladium meum, interficiet eos manus mea.

verses.text: Thy wind blew and the sea covered them: they sunk as lead in the mighty waters.
verses.textLatin: Flavit spiritus tuus, et operuit eos mare: submersi sunt quasi plumbum in aquis vehementibus.

verses.text: Who is like to thee, among the strong, O Lord? who is like to thee, glorious in holiness, terrible and praise-worthy, doing wonders?
verses.textLatin: Quis similis tui in fortibus, Domine? quis similis tui, magnificus in sanctitate, terribilis atque laudabilis, faciens mirabilia?

verses.text: Thou stretchedst forth thy hand, and the earth swallowed them.
verses.textLatin: Extendisti manum tuam, et devoravit eos terra.

verses.text: In thy mercy thou hast been a leader to the people which thou hast redeemed: and in thy strength thou hast carried them to thy holy habitation.
verses.textLatin: Dux fuisti in misericordia tua populo quem redemisti: et portasti eum in fortitudine tua, ad habitaculum sanctum tuum.

verses.text: Nations rose up, and were angry: sorrows took hold on the inhabitants of Philisthiim.
verses.textLatin: Ascenderunt populi, et irati sunt: dolores obtinuerunt habitatores Philisthiim.

verses.text: Then were the princes of Edom troubled, trembling seized on the stout men of Moab: all the inhabitants of Chanaan became stiff.
verses.textLatin: Tunc conturbati sunt principes Edom, robustos Moab obtinuit tremor: obriguerunt omnes habitatores Chanaan.

verses.text: Let fear and dread fall upon them, in the greatness of thy arm: let them become unmoveable as a stone, until thy people, O Lord, pass by: until this thy people pass by, which thou hast possessed.
verses.textLatin: Irruat super eos formido et pavor, in magnitudine brachii tui: fiant immobiles quasi lapis, donec pertranseat populus tuus, Domine, donec pertranseat populus tuus iste, quem possedisti.

verses.text: Thou shalt bring them in, and plant them in the mountain of thy inheritance, in thy most firm habitation which thou hast made, O Lord; thy sanctuary, O Lord, which thy hands have established.
verses.textLatin: Introduces eos, et plantabis in monte hæreditatis tuæ, firmissimo habitaculo tuo quod operatus es, Domine: sanctuarium tuum, Domine, quod firmaverunt manus tuæ.

verses.text: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Dominus regnabit in æternum et ultra.

verses.text: For Pharao went in on horseback with his chariots and horsemen into the sea: and the Lord brought back upon them the waters of the sea: but the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst thereof.
verses.textLatin: Ingressus est enim eques Pharao cum curribus et equitibus ejus in mare: et reduxit super eos Dominus aquas maris: filii autem Israël ambulaverunt per siccum in medio ejus.

verses.text: So Mary the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand: and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and with dances:
verses.textLatin: Sumpsit ergo Maria prophetissa, soror Aaron, tympanum in manu sua: egressæque sunt omnes mulieres post eam cum tympanis et choris,

verses.text: And she began the song to them, saying: Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified, the horse and his rider he hath thrown into the sea.
verses.textLatin: quibus præcinebat, dicens: Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est: equum et ascensorem ejus dejecit in mare.

verses.text: And Moses brought Israel from the Red Sea, and they went forth into the wilderness of Sur: and they marched three days through the wilderness, and found no water.
verses.textLatin: Tulit autem Moyses Israël de mari Rubro, et egressi sunt in desertum Sur: ambulaveruntque tribus diebus per solitudinem, et non inveniebant aquam.

verses.text: And they came into Mara, and they could not drink the waters of Mara, because they were bitter: whereupon he gave a name also agreeable to the place, calling it Mara, that is, bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt in Mara, nec poterant bibere aquas de Mara, eo quod essent amaræ: unde et congruum loco nomen imposuit, vocans illum Mara, id est, amaritudinem.

verses.text: And the people murmured against Moses, saying: What shall we drink?
verses.textLatin: Et murmuravit populus contra Moysen, dicens: Quid bibemus?

verses.text: But he cried to the Lord, and he shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, they were turned into sweetness. There he appointed him ordinances, and judgments, and there he proved him,
verses.textLatin: At ille clamavit ad Dominum, qui ostendit ei lignum: quod cum misisset in aquas, in dulcedinem versæ sunt: ibi constituit ei præcepta, atque judicia, et ibi tentavit eum,

verses.text: Saying: If thou wilt hear the voice of the Lord thy God, and do what is right before him, and obey his commandments, and keep all his precepts, none of the evils that I laid upon Egypt, will I bring upon thee: for I am the Lord thy healer.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Si audieris vocem Domini Dei tui, et quod rectum est coram eo feceris, et obedieris mandatis ejus, custodierisque omnia præcepta illius, cunctum languorem, quem posui in Ægypto, non inducam super te: ego enim Dominus sanator tuus.

verses.text: And the children of Israel came into Elim, where there were twelve fountains of water, and seventy palm trees: and they encamped by the waters.
verses.textLatin: Venerunt autem in Elim filii Israël, ubi erant duodecim fontes aquarum, et septuaginta palmæ: et castrametati sunt juxta aquas.

verses.text: And  they set forward from Elim, and all the multitude of the children of Israel came into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai: the fifteenth day of the second month, after they came out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Profectique sunt de Elim, et venit omnis multitudo filiorum Israël in desertum Sin, quod est inter Elim et Sinai, quintodecimo die mensis secundi, postquam egressi sunt de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Et murmuravit omnis congregatio filiorum Israël contra Moysen et Aaron in solitudine.

verses.text: And the children of Israel said to them: Would to God we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over the flesh pots, and ate bread to the full. Why have you brought us into this desert, that you might destroy all the multitude with famine?
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque filii Israël ad eos: Utinam mortui essemus per manum Domini in terra Ægypti, quando sedebamus super ollas carnium, et comedebamus panem in saturitate: cur eduxistis nos in desertum istud, ut occideretis omnem multitudinem fame?

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Behold I will rain bread from heaven for you: let the people go forth, and gather what is sufficient for every day: that I may prove them whether they will walk in my law, or not.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Ecce ego pluam vobis panes de cælo: egrediatur populus, et colligat quæ sufficiunt per singulos dies: ut tentem eum utrum ambulet in lege mea, an non.

verses.text: But the sixth day let them provide for to bring in: and let it be double to that they were wont to gather every day.
verses.textLatin: Die autem sexto parent quod inferant: et sit duplum quam colligere solebant per singulos dies.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron said to the children of Israel: In the evening you shall know that the Lord hath brought you forth out of the land of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque Moyses et Aaron ad omnes filios Israël: Vespere scietis quod Dominus eduxerit vos de terra Ægypti,

verses.text: And in the morning you shall see the glory of the Lord: for he hath heard your murmuring against the Lord: but as for us, what are we, that you mutter against us?
verses.textLatin: et mane videbitis gloriam Domini: audivit enim murmur vestrum contra Dominum: nos vero quid sumus, quia mussitastis contra nos?

verses.text: And Moses said: In the evening the Lord will give you flesh to eat, and in the morning bread to the full: for he hath heard your murmurings, with which you have murmured against him, for what are we? your murmuring is not against us, but against the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: Dabit vobis Dominus vespere carnes edere, et mane panes in saturitate: eo quod audierit murmurationes vestras quibus murmurati estis contra eum: nos enim quid sumus? nec contra nos est murmur vestrum, sed contra Dominum.

verses.text: Moses also said to Aaron: Say to the whole congregation of the children of Israel: Come before the Lord: for he hath heard your murmuring.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Moyses ad Aaron: Dic universæ congregationi filiorum Israël: Accedite coram Domino: audivit enim murmur vestrum.

verses.text: And when Aaron spoke to all the assembly of the children of Israel, they looked towards the wilderness: and behold the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.
verses.textLatin: Cumque loqueretur Aaron ad omnem cœtum filiorum Israël, respexerunt ad solitudinem: et ecce gloria Domini apparuit in nube.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: I have heard the murmuring of the children of Israel: say to them: In the evening you shall eat flesh, and in the morning you shall have your fill of bread: and you shall know that I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Audivi murmurationes filiorum Israël. Loquere ad eos: Vespere comedetis carnes, et mane saturabimini panibus: scietisque quod ego sum Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: So it came to pass in the evening, that quails coming up, covered the camp: and in the morning a dew lay round about the camp.
verses.textLatin: Factum est ergo vespere, et ascendens coturnix, cooperuit castra: mane quoque ros jacuit per circuitum castrorum.

verses.text: And when it had covered the face of the earth, it appeared in the wilderness small, and as it were beaten with a pestle, like unto the hoar frost on the ground.
verses.textLatin: Cumque operuisset superficiem terræ, apparuit in solitudine minutum, et quasi pilo tusum in similitudinem pruinæ super terram.

verses.text: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another: Manhu! which signifieth: What is this! for they knew not what it was. And Moses said to them: This is the bread, which the Lord hath given you to eat.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidissent filii Israël, dixerunt ad invicem: Manhu? quod significat: Quid est hoc? ignorabant enim quid esset. Quibus ait Moyses: Iste est panis quem Dominus dedit vobis ad vescendum.

verses.text: This is the word, that the Lord hath commanded: Let every one gather of it as much as is enough to eat: a gomor for every man, according to the number of your souls that dwell in a tent, so shall you take of it.
verses.textLatin: Hic est sermo, quem præcepit Dominus: Colligat unusquisque ex eo quantum sufficit ad vescendum: gomor per singula capita, juxta numerum animarum vestrarum quæ habitant in tabernaculo sic tolletis.

verses.text: And the children of Israel did so: and they gathered, one more, another less.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque ita filii Israël: et collegerunt, alius plus, alius minus.

verses.text: And they measured by the measure of a gomor: neither had he more that had gathered more: nor did he find less that had provided less: but every one had gathered, according to what they were able to eat.
verses.textLatin: Et mensi sunt ad mensuram gomor: nec qui plus collegerat, habuit amplius: nec qui minus paraverat, reperit minus: sed singuli juxta id quod edere poterant, congregaverunt.

verses.text: And Moses said to them: Let no man leave thereof till the morning.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad eos: Nullus relinquat ex eo in mane.

verses.text: And they hearkened not to him, but some of them left until the morning, and it began to be full of worms, and it putrefied, and Moses was angry with them.
verses.textLatin: Qui non audierunt eum, sed dimiserunt quidam ex eis usque mane, et scatere cœpit vermibus, atque computruit: et iratus est contra eos Moyses.

verses.text: Now every one of them gathered in the morning, as much as might suffice to eat: and after the sun grew hot, it melted.
verses.textLatin: Colligebant autem mane singuli, quantum sufficere poterat ad vescendum: cumque incaluisset sol, liquefiebat.

verses.text: But on the sixth day they gathered twice as much, that is, two gomors every man: and all the rulers of the multitude came, and told Moses.
verses.textLatin: In die autem sexta collegerunt cibos duplices, id est, duo gomor per singulos homines: venerunt autem omnes principes multitudinis, et narraverunt Moysi.

verses.text: And he said to them: This is what the Lord hath spoken: To morrow is the rest of the sabbath sanctified to the Lord. Whatsoever work is to be done, do it: and the meats that are to be dressed, dress them: and whatsoever shall remain, lay it up until the morning.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait eis: Hoc est quod locutus est Dominus: Requies sabbati sanctificata est Domino cras: quodcumque operandum est, facite, et quæ coquenda sunt coquite: quidquid autem reliquum fuerit, reponite usque in mane.

verses.text: And they did so as Moses had commanded, and it did not putreify, neither was there worm found in it.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque ita ut præceperat Moyses, et non computruit, neque vermis inventus est in eo.

verses.text: And Moses said: Eat it to day, because it is the sabbath of the Lord: to day it shall not be found in the field.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses: Comedite illud hodie, quia sabbatum est Domini: non invenietur hodie in agro.

verses.text: Gather it six days: but on the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord, therefore it shall not be found.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus colligite: in die autem septimo sabbatum est Domini, idcirco non invenietur.

verses.text: And the seventh day came: and some of the people going forth to gather, found none.
verses.textLatin: Venitque septima dies: et egressi de populo ut colligerent, non invenerunt.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: How long will you refuse to keep my commandments, and my law?
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Usquequo non vultis custodire mandata mea et legem meam?

verses.text: See that the Lord hath given you the sabbath, and for this reason on the sixth day he giveth you a double provision: let each man stay at home, and let none go forth out of his place the seventh day.
verses.textLatin: videte quod Dominus dederit vobis sabbatum, et propter hoc die sexta tribuit vobis cibos duplices: maneat unusquisque apud semetipsum; nullus egrediatur de loco suo die septimo.

verses.text: And the people kept the sabbath on the seventh day.
verses.textLatin: Et sabbatizavit populus die septimo.

verses.text: And the house of Israel called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed white, and the taste thereof like to flour with honey.
verses.textLatin: Appellavitque domus Israël nomen ejus Man: quod erat quasi semen coriandri album, gustusque ejus quasi similæ cum melle.

verses.text: And Moses said: This is the word, which the Lord hath commanded: Fill a gomor of it, and let it be kept unto generations to come hereafter, that they may know the bread, wherewith I fed you in the wilderness, when you were brought forth out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Moyses: Iste est sermo, quem præcepit Dominus: Imple gomor ex eo, et custodiatur in futuras retro generationes: ut noverint panem, quo alui vos in solitudine, quando educti estis de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And Moses said to Aaron: Take a vessel, and put manna into it, as much as a gomor can hold: and lay it up before the Lord to keep unto your generations,
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad Aaron: Sume vas unum, et mitte ibi man, quantum potest capere gomor, et repone coram Domino ad servandum in generationes vestras,

verses.text: As the Lord commanded Moses. And Aaron put it in the tabernacle to be kept.
verses.textLatin: sicut præcepit Dominus Moysi. Posuitque illud Aaron in tabernaculo reservandum.

verses.text: And the children of Israel ate manna forty years, till they came to a habitable land: with this meat were they fed, until they reached the borders of the land of Chanaan.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Israël comederunt man quadraginta annis, donec venirent in terram habitabilem: hoc cibo aliti sunt, usquequo tangerent fines terræ Chanaan.

verses.text: Now a gomor is the tenth part of an ephi.
verses.textLatin: Gomor autem decima pars est ephi.

verses.text: Then  all the multitude of the children of Israel setting forward from the desert of Sin, by their mansions, according to the word of the Lord, encamped in Raphidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.textLatin: Igitur profecta omnis multitudo filiorum Israël de deserto Sin per mansiones suas, juxta sermonem Domini, castrametati sunt in Raphidim, ubi non erat aqua ad bibendum populo.

verses.text: And they chode with Moses, and said: Give us water, that we may drink. And Moses answered them: Why chide you with me? Wherefore do you tempt the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Qui jurgatus contra Moysen, ait: Da nobis aquam, ut bibamus. Quibus respondit Moyses: Quid jurgamini contra me? cur tentatis Dominum?

verses.text: So the people were thirsty there for want of water, and murmured against Moses, saying: Why didst thou make us go forth out of Egypt, to kill us and our children, and our beasts with thirst?
verses.textLatin: Sitivit ergo ibi populus præ aquæ penuria, et murmuravit contra Moysen, dicens: Cur fecisti nos exire de Ægypto, ut occideres nos, et liberos nostros, ac jumenta siti?

verses.text: And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: What shall I do to this people? Yet a little more and they will stone me.
verses.textLatin: Clamavit autem Moyses ad Dominum, dicens: Quid faciam populo huic? adhuc paululum, et lapidabit me.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Go before the people, and take with thee of the ancients of Israel: and take in thy hand the rod wherewith thou didst strike the river, and go.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus ad Moysen: Antecede populum, et sume tecum de senioribus Israël: et virgam qua percussisti fluvium, tolle in manu tua, et vade.

verses.text: Behold I will stand there before thee, upon the rock Horeb: and thou shalt strike the rock, and water shall come out of it that the people may drink. Moses did so before the ancients of Israel:
verses.textLatin: En ego stabo ibi coram te, supra petram Horeb: percutiesque petram, et exibit ex ea aqua, ut bibat populus. Fecit Moyses ita coram senioribus Israël:

verses.text: And he called the name of that place Temptation, because of the chiding of the children of Israel, and for that they tempted the Lord, saying: Is the Lord amongst us or not?
verses.textLatin: et vocavit nomen loci illius, Tentatio, propter jurgium filiorum Israël, et quia tentaverunt Dominum, dicentes: Estne Dominus in nobis, an non?

verses.text: And Amalec came, and fought against Israel in Raphidim.
verses.textLatin: Venit autem Amalec, et pugnabat contra Israël in Raphidim.

verses.text: And Moses said to Josue: Choose out men: and go out and fight against Amalec: to morrow I will stand on the top of the hill having the rod of God in my hand.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad Josue: Elige viros: et egressus, pugna contra Amalec: cras ego stabo in vertice collis, habens virgam Dei in manu mea.

verses.text: Josue did as Moses had spoken, and he fought against Amalec; but Moses, and Aaron, and Hur went up upon the top of the hill.
verses.textLatin: Fecit Josue ut locutus erat Moyses, et pugnavit contra Amalec: Moyses autem et Aaron et Hur ascenderunt super verticem collis.

verses.text: And when Moses lifted up his hands, Israel overcame: but if he let them down a little, Amalec overcame.
verses.textLatin: Cumque levaret Moyses manus, vincebat Israël: sin autem paululum remisisset, superabat Amalec.

verses.text: And Moses’ hands were heavy: so they took a stone, and put under him, and he sat on it: and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands on both sides. And it came to pass that his hands were not weary until sunset.
verses.textLatin: Manus autem Moysi erant graves: sumentes igitur lapidem, posuerunt subter eum, in quo sedit: Aaron autem et Hur sustentabant manus ejus ex utraque parte. Et factum est ut manus illius non lassarentur usque ad occasum solis.

verses.text: And Josue put Amalec and his people to flight, by the edge of the sword.
verses.textLatin: Fugavitque Josue Amalec, et populum ejus in ore gladii.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Write this for a memorial in a book, and deliver it to the ears of Josue: for I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Scribe hoc ob monimentum in libro, et trade auribus Josue: delebo enim memoriam Amalec sub cælo.

verses.text: And Moses built an altar: and called the name thereof, The Lord my exaltation, saying:
verses.textLatin: Ædificavitque Moyses altare: et vocavit nomen ejus, Dominus exaltatio mea, dicens:

verses.text: Because the hand of the throne of the Lord, and the war of the Lord shall be against Amalec, from generation to generation.
verses.textLatin: Quia manus solii Domini, et bellum Domini erit contra Amalec, a generatione in generationem.

verses.text: And  when Jethro the priest of Madian, the kinsman of Moses, had heard all the things that God had done to Moses, and to Israel his people, and that the Lord had brought forth Israel out of Egypt,
verses.textLatin: Cumque audisset Jethro, sacerdos Madian, cognatus Moysi, omnia quæ fecerat Deus Moysi, et Israëli populo suo, et quod eduxisset Dominus Israël de Ægypto,

verses.text: He took Sephora the wife of Moses whom he had sent back:
verses.textLatin: tulit Sephoram uxorem Moysi quam remiserat,

verses.text: And her two sons, of whom one was called Gersam, his father saying: I have been a stranger in a foreign country.
verses.textLatin: et duos filios ejus: quorum unus vocabatur Gersam, dicente patre: Advena fui in terra aliena;

verses.text: And the other Eliezer: For the God of my father, said he, is my helper, and hath delivered me from the sword of Pharao.
verses.textLatin: alter vero Eliezer: Deus enim, ait, patris mei adjutor meus, et eruit me de gladio Pharaonis.

verses.text: And Jethro the kinsman of Moses came with his sons and his wife, to Moses into the desert, where he was camped by the mountain of God.
verses.textLatin: Venit ergo Jethro cognatus Moysi, et filii ejus, et uxor ejus ad Moysen in desertum, ubi erat castrametatus juxta montem Dei.

verses.text: And he sent word to Moses, saying: I Jethro thy kinsman come to thee, and thy wife, and thy two sons with her.
verses.textLatin: Et mandavit Moysi, dicens: Ego Jethro cognatus tuus venio ad te, et uxor tua, et duo filii cum ea.

verses.text: And he went out to meet his kinsman, and worshipped and kissed him: and they saluted one another with words of peace. And when he was come into the tent,
verses.textLatin: Qui egressus in occursum cognati sui, adoravit, et osculatus est eum: salutaveruntque se mutuo verbis pacificis. Cumque intrasset tabernaculum,

verses.text: Moses told his kinsman all that the Lord had done to Pharao, and the Egyptians, in favour of Israel: and all the labour which had befallen them in the journey, and that the Lord had delivered them.
verses.textLatin: narravit Moyses cognato suo cuncta quæ fecerat Dominus Pharaoni et Ægyptiis propter Israël: universumque laborem, qui accidisset eis in itinere, et quod liberaverat eos Dominus.

verses.text: And Jethro rejoiced for all the good things that the Lord had done to Israel, because he had delivered them out of the hands of the Egyptians.
verses.textLatin: Lætatusque est Jethro super omnibus bonis, quæ fecerat Dominus Israëli, eo quod eruisset eum de manu Ægyptiorum.

verses.text: And he said: Blessed is the Lord, who hath delivered you out of the hand of Pharao, and out of the hand of the Egyptians, who hath delivered his people out of the hand of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Benedictus Dominus, qui liberavit vos de manu Ægyptiorum, et de manu Pharaonis; qui eruit populum suum de manu Ægypti.

verses.text: Now I know that the Lord is great above all gods: because they dealt proudly against them.
verses.textLatin: Nunc cognovi, quia magnus Dominus super omnes deos: eo quod superbe egerint contra illos.

verses.text: So Jethro the kinsman of Moses offered holocausts and sacrifices to God: and Aaron and all the ancients of Israel came, to eat bread with them before God.
verses.textLatin: Obtulit ergo Jethro cognatus Moysi holocausta et hostias Deo: veneruntque Aaron et omnes seniores Israël, ut comederent panem cum eo coram Deo.

verses.text: And the next day Moses sat, to judge the people, who stood by Moses from morning until night.
verses.textLatin: Altera autem die sedit Moyses ut judicaret populum, qui assistebat Moysi a mane usque ad vesperam.

verses.text: And when his kinsman had seen all things that he did among the people, he said: What is it that thou dost among the people? Why sittest thou alone, and all the people wait from morning till night.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidisset cognatus ejus, omnia scilicet quæ agebat in populo, ait: Quid est hoc quod facis in plebe? cur solus sedes, et omnis populus præstolatur de mane usque ad vesperam?

verses.text: And Moses answered him: The people come to me to seek the judgment of God.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Moyses: Venit ad me populus quærens sententiam Dei:

verses.text: And when any controversy falleth out among them, they come to me to judge between them, and to shew the precepts of God, and his laws.
verses.textLatin: cumque acciderit eis aliqua disceptatio, veniunt ad me ut judicem inter eos, et ostendam præcepta Dei, et leges ejus.

verses.text: But he said: The thing thou dost is not good.
verses.textLatin: At ille: Non bonam, inquit, rem facis.

verses.text: Thou art spent with foolish labour, both thou and this people that is with thee: the business is above thy strength, thou alone canst not bear it.
verses.textLatin: Stulto labore consumeris et tu, et populus iste qui tecum est: ultra vires tuas est negotium; solus illud non poteris sustinere.

verses.text: But hear my words and counsels, and God shall be with thee. Be thou to the people in those things that pertain to God, to bring their words to him:
verses.textLatin: Sed audi verba mea atque consilia, et erit Deus tecum. Esto tu populo in his quæ ad Deum pertinent, ut referas quæ dicuntur ad eum:

verses.text: And to shew the people the ceremonies and the manner of worshipping, and the way wherein they ought to walk, and the work that they ought to do.
verses.textLatin: ostendasque populo cæremonias et ritum colendi, viamque per quam ingredi debeant, et opus quod facere debeant.

verses.text: And provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, in whom there is truth, and that hate avarice, and appoint of them rulers of thousands, and of hundreds, and of fifties, and of tens.
verses.textLatin: Provide autem de omni plebe viros potentes, et timentes Deum, in quibus sit veritas, et qui oderint avaritiam, et constitue ex eis tribunos, et centuriones, et quinquagenarios, et decanos,

verses.text: Who may judge the people at all times: and when any great matter soever shall fall out, let them refer it to thee, and let them judge the lesser matters only: that so it may be lighter for thee, the burden being shared out unto others.
verses.textLatin: qui judicent populum omni tempore: quidquid autem majus fuerit, referant ad te, et ipsi minora tantummodo judicent: leviusque sit tibi, partito in alios onere.

verses.text: If thou dost this, thou shalt fulfil the commandment of God, and shalt be able to bear his precepts: and all this people shall return to their places with peace.
verses.textLatin: Si hoc feceris, implebis imperium Dei, et præcepta ejus poteris sustentare: et omnis hic populus revertetur ad loca sua cum pace.

verses.text: And when Moses heard this, he did all things that he had suggested unto him.
verses.textLatin: Quibus auditis, Moyses fecit omnia quæ ille suggesserat.

verses.text: And choosing able men out of all Israel, he appointed them rulers of the people, rulers over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens.
verses.textLatin: Et electis viris strenuis de cuncto Israël, constituit eos principes populi, tribunos, et centuriones, et quinquagenarios, et decanos.

verses.text: And they judged the people at all times: and whatsoever was of greater difficulty they referred to him, and they judged the easier cases only.
verses.textLatin: Qui judicabant plebem omni tempore: quidquid autem gravius erat, referebant ad eum, faciliora tantummodo judicantes.

verses.text: And he let his kinsman depart: and he returned and went into his own country.
verses.textLatin: Dimisitque cognatum suum: qui reversus abiit in terram suam.

verses.text: In  the third month of the departure of Israel out of the land of Egypt, on this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai:
verses.textLatin: Mense tertio egressionis Israël de terra Ægypti, in die hac venerunt in solitudinem Sinai.

verses.text: For departing out of Raphidim, and coming to the desert of Sinai, they camped in the same place, and there Israel pitched their tents over against the mountain.
verses.textLatin: Nam profecti de Raphidim, et pervenientes usque in desertum Sinai, castrametati sunt in eodem loco, ibique Israël fixit tentoria e regione montis.

verses.text: And Moses went up to God: and the Lord called unto him from the mountain, and said: Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Moyses autem ascendit ad Deum: vocavitque eum Dominus de monte, et ait: Hæc dices domui Jacob, et annuntiabis filiis Israël:

verses.text: You have seen what I have done to the Egyptians, how I have carried you upon the wings of eagles, and have taken you to myself.
verses.textLatin: Vos ipsi vidistis quæ fecerim Ægyptiis, quomodo portaverim vos super alas aquilarum, et assumpserim mihi.

verses.text: If therefore you will hear my voice, and keep my covenant, you shall be my peculiar possession above all people: for all the earth is mine.
verses.textLatin: Si ergo audieritis vocem meam, et custodieritis pactum meum, eritis mihi in peculium de cunctis populis: mea est enim omnis terra:

verses.text: And you shall be to me a priestly kingdom, and a holy nation. These are the words thou shalt speak to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et vos eritis mihi in regnum sacerdotale, et gens sancta. Hæc sunt verba quæ loqueris ad filios Israël.

verses.text: Moses came, and calling together the elders of the people, he declared all the words which the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Venit Moyses: et convocatis majoribus natu populi, exposuit omnes sermones quos mandaverat Dominus.

verses.text: And all the people answered together: All that the Lord hath spoken, we will do. And when Moses had related the people’s words to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Responditque omnis populus simul: Cuncta quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus. Cumque retulisset Moyses verba populi ad Dominum,

verses.text: The Lord said to him: Lo, now will I come to thee in the darkness of a cloud, that the people may hear me speaking to thee, and may believe thee for ever. And Moses told the words of the people to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ait ei Dominus: Jam nunc veniam ad te in caligine nubis, ut audiat me populus loquentem ad te, et credat tibi in perpetuum. Nuntiavit ergo Moyses verba populi ad Dominum.

verses.text: And he said to him: Go to the people, and sanctify them to day, and to morrow, and let them wash their garments.
verses.textLatin: Qui dixit ei: Vade ad populum, et sanctifica illos hodie, et cras, laventque vestimenta sua.

verses.text: And let them be ready against the third day: for on the third day the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon mount Sinai.
verses.textLatin: Et sint parati in diem tertium: in die enim tertia descendet Dominus coram omni plebe super montem Sinai.

verses.text: And thou shalt appoint certain limits to the people round about, and thou shalt say to them: Take heed you go not up into the mount, and that ye touch not the borders thereof: every one that toucheth the mount dying he shall die.
verses.textLatin: Constituesque terminos populo per circuitum, et dices ad eos: Cavete ne ascendatis in montem, nec tangatis fines illius: omnis qui tetigerit montem, morte morietur.

verses.text: No hands shall touch him, but he shall be stoned to death, or shall be shot through with arrows: whether it be beast, or man, he shall not live. When the trumpet shall begin to sound, then let them go up into the mount.
verses.textLatin: Manus non tanget eum, sed lapidibus opprimetur, aut confodietur jaculis: sive jumentum fuerit, sive homo, non vivet: cum cœperit clangere buccina, tunc ascendant in montem.

verses.text: And Moses came down from the mount to the people, and sanctified them. And when they had washed their garments,
verses.textLatin: Descenditque Moyses de monte ad populum, et sanctificavit eum. Cumque lavissent vestimenta sua,

verses.text: He said to them: Be ready against the third day, and come not near your wives.
verses.textLatin: ait ad eos: Estote parati in diem tertium, et ne appropinquetis uxoribus vestris.

verses.text: And now the third day was come, and the morning appeared: and behold thunders began to be heard, and lightning to flash, and a very thick cloud to cover the mount, and the noise of the trumpet sounded exceeding loud, and the people that was in the camp, feared.
verses.textLatin: Jamque advenerat tertius dies, et mane inclaruerat: et ecce cœperunt audiri tonitrua, ac micare fulgura, et nubes densissima operire montem, clangorque buccinæ vehementius perstrepebat: et timuit populus qui erat in castris.

verses.text: And when Moses had brought them forth to meet God from the place of the camp, they stood at the bottom of the mount.
verses.textLatin: Cumque eduxisset eos Moyses in occursum Dei de loco castrorum, steterunt ad radices montis.

verses.text: And all mount Sinai was on a smoke: because the Lord was come down upon it in fire, and the smoke arose from it as out of a furnace: and all the mount was terrible.
verses.textLatin: Totus autem mons Sinai fumabat, eo quod descendisset Dominus super eum in igne: et ascenderet fumus ex eo quasi de fornace, eratque omnis mons terribilis.

verses.text: And the sound of the trumpet grew by degrees louder and louder, and was drawn out to a greater length: Moses spoke, and God answered him.
verses.textLatin: Et sonitus buccinæ paulatim crescebat in majus, et prolixius tendebatur: Moyses loquebatur, et Deus respondebat ei.

verses.text: And the Lord came down upon mount Sinai, in the very top of the mount, and he called Moses unto the top thereof. And when he was gone up thither,
verses.textLatin: Descenditque Dominus super montem Sinai in ipso montis vertice, et vocavit Moysen in cacumen ejus. Quo cum ascendisset,

verses.text: He said unto him: Go down, and charge the people: lest they should have a mind to pass the limits to see the Lord, and a very great multitude of them should perish.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad eum: Descende, et contestare populum: ne forte velit transcendere terminos ad videndum Dominum, et pereat ex eis plurima multitudo.

verses.text: The priests also that come to the Lord, let them be sanctified, lest he strike them.
verses.textLatin: Sacerdotes quoque qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos.

verses.text: And Moses said to the Lord: The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou didst charge, and command, saying: Set limits about the mount, and sanctify it.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad Dominum: Non poterit vulgus ascendere in montem Sinai: tu enim testificatus es, et jussisti, dicens: Pone terminos circa montem, et sanctifica illum.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Go, get thee down: and thou shalt come up, thou and Aaron with thee: but let not the priests and the people pass the limits, nor come up to the Lord, lest he kill them.
verses.textLatin: Cui ait Dominus: Vade, descende: ascendesque tu, et Aaron tecum: sacerdotes autem et populus ne transeant terminos, nec ascendant ad Dominum, ne forte interficiat illos.

verses.text: And Moses went down to the people and told them all.
verses.textLatin: Descenditque Moyses ad populum, et omnia narravit eis.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke all these words:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus cunctos sermones hos:

verses.text: I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
verses.textLatin: Ego sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, de domo servitutis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not have strange gods before me.
verses.textLatin: Non habebis deos alienos coram me.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make to thyself a graven thing, nor the likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or in the earth beneath, nor of those things that are in the waters under the earth.
verses.textLatin: Non facies tibi sculptile, neque omnem similitudinem quæ est in cælo desuper, et quæ in terra deorsum, nec eorum quæ sunt in aquis sub terra.

verses.text: Thou shalt not adore them, nor serve them: I am the Lord thy God, mighty, jealous, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me:
verses.textLatin: Non adorabis ea, neque coles: ego sum Dominus Deus tuus fortis, zelotes, visitans iniquitatem patrum in filios, in tertiam et quartam generationem eorum qui oderunt me:

verses.text: And shewing mercy unto thousands to them that love me, and keep my commandments.
verses.textLatin: et faciens misericordiam in millia his qui diligunt me, et custodiunt præcepta mea.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that shall take the name of the Lord his God in vain.
verses.textLatin: Non assumes nomen Domini Dei tui in vanum: nec enim habebit insontem Dominus eum qui assumpserit nomen Domini Dei sui frustra.

verses.text: Remember that thou keep holy the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Memento ut diem sabbati sanctifices.

verses.text: Six days shalt thou labour, and shalt do all thy works.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus operaberis, et facies omnia opera tua.

verses.text: But on the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: thou shalt do no work on it, thou nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy beast, nor the stranger that is within thy gates.
verses.textLatin: Septimo autem die sabbatum Domini Dei tui est: non facies omne opus in eo, tu, et filius tuus et filia tua, servus tuus et ancilla tua, jumentum tuum, et advena qui est intra portas tuas.

verses.text: For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and the sea, and all things that are in them, and rested on the seventh day: therefore the Lord blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it.
verses.textLatin: Sex enim diebus fecit Dominus cælum et terram, et mare, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, et requievit in die septimo: idcirco benedixit Dominus diei sabbati, et sanctificavit eum.

verses.text: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thou mayest be longlived upon the land which the Lord thy God will give thee.
verses.textLatin: Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, ut sis longævus super terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi.

verses.text: Thou shalt not kill.
verses.textLatin: Non occides.

verses.text: Thou shalt not commit adultery.
verses.textLatin: Non mœchaberis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not steal.
verses.textLatin: Non furtum facies.

verses.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Non loqueris contra proximum tuum falsum testimonium.

verses.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house: neither shalt thou desire his wife, nor his servant, nor his handmaid, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is his.
verses.textLatin: Non concupisces domum proximi tui, nec desiderabis uxorem ejus, non servum, non ancillam, non bovem, non asinum, nec omnia quæ illius sunt.

verses.text: And all the people saw the voices and the flames, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mount smoking: and being terrified and struck with fear, they stood afar off,
verses.textLatin: Cunctus autem populus videbat voces et lampades, et sonitum buccinæ, montemque fumantem: et perterriti ac pavore concussi, steterunt procul,

verses.text: Saying to Moses: Speak thou to us, and we will hear: let not the Lord speak to us, lest we die.
verses.textLatin: dicentes Moysi: Loquere tu nobis, et audiemus: non loquatur nobis Dominus, ne forte moriamur.

verses.text: And Moses said to the people: Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that the dread of him might be in you, and you should not sin.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses ad populum: Nolite timere: ut enim probaret vos venit Deus, et ut terror illius esset in vobis, et non peccaretis.

verses.text: And the people stood afar off. But Moses went to the dark cloud wherein God was.
verses.textLatin: Stetitque populus de longe. Moyses autem accessit ad caliginem in qua erat Deus.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.
verses.textLatin: Dixit præterea Dominus ad Moysen: Hæc dices filiis Israël: Vos vidistis quod de cælo locutus sim vobis.

verses.text: You shall not make gods of silver, nor shall you make to yourselves gods of gold.
verses.textLatin: Non facietis deos argenteos, nec deos aureos facietis vobis.

verses.text: You shall make an altar of earth unto me, and you shall offer upon it your holocausts and peace offerings, your sheep and oxen, in every place where the memory of my name shall be: I will come to thee, and will bless thee.
verses.textLatin: Altare de terra facietis mihi, et offeretis super eo holocausta et pacifica vestra, oves vestras et boves in omni loco in quo memoria fuerit nominis mei: veniam ad te, et benedicam tibi.

verses.text: And if thou make an altar of stone unto me, thou shalt not build it of hewn stones: for if thou lift up a tool upon it, it shall be defiled.
