verses.textLatin: Quod si altare lapideum feceris mihi, non ædificabis illud de sectis lapidibus: si enim levaveris cultrum super eo, polluetur.

verses.text: Thou shalt not go up by steps unto my altar, lest thy nakedness be discovered.
verses.textLatin: Non ascendes per gradus ad altare meum, ne reveletur turpitudo tua.

verses.text: These  are the judgments which thou shalt set before them.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt judicia quæ propones eis.

verses.text: If thou buy a Hebrew servant, six years shall he serve thee: in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.
verses.textLatin: Si emeris servum hebræum, sex annis serviet tibi: in septimo egredietur liber gratis.

verses.text: With what raiment he came in, with the like let him go out: if having a wife, his wife also shall go out with him.
verses.textLatin: Cum quali veste intraverit, cum tali exeat: si habens uxorem, et uxor egredietur simul.

verses.text: But if his master gave him a wife, and she hath borne sons and daughters: the woman and her children shall be her master’s: but he himself shall go out with his raiment.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem dominus dederit illi uxorem, et pepererit filios et filias: mulier et liberi ejus erunt domini sui, ipse vero exibit cum vestitu suo.

verses.text: And if the servant shall say: I love my master and my wife and children, I will not go out free:
verses.textLatin: Quod si dixerit servus: Diligo dominum meum et uxorem ac liberos; non egrediar liber:

verses.text: His master shall bring him to the gods, and he shall be set to the door and the posts, and he shall bore his ear through with an awl: and he shall be his servant for ever.
verses.textLatin: offeret eum dominus diis, et applicabitur ad ostium et postes, perforabitque aurem ejus subula: et erit ei servus in sæculum.

verses.text: If any man sell his daughter to be a servant, she shall not go out as bondwomen are wont to go out.
verses.textLatin: Si quis vendiderit filiam suam in famulam, non egredietur sicut ancillæ exire consueverunt.

verses.text: If she displease the eyes of her master to whom she was delivered, he shall let her go: but he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign nation, if he despise her.
verses.textLatin: Si displicuerit oculis domini sui cui tradita fuerat, dimittet eam: populo autem alieno vendendi non habebit potestatem, si spreverit eam.

verses.text: But if he have betrothed her to his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem filio suo desponderit eam, juxta morem filiarum faciet illi.

verses.text: And if he take another wife for him, he shall provide her a marriage, and raiment, neither shall he refuse the price of her chastity.
verses.textLatin: Quod si alteram ei acceperit, providebit puellæ nuptias, et vestimenta, et pretium pudicitiæ non negabit.

verses.text: If he do not these three things, she shall go out free without money.
verses.textLatin: Si tria ista non fecerit, egredietur gratis absque pecunia.

verses.text: He that striketh a man with a will to kill him, shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit hominem volens occidere, morte moriatur.

verses.text: But he that did not lie in wait for him, but God delivered him into his hands: I will appoint thee a place to which he must flee.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem non est insidiatus, sed Deus illum tradidit in manus ejus, constituam tibi locum in quem fugere debeat.

verses.text: If a man kill his neighbour on set purpose and by lying in wait for him: thou shalt take him away from my altar, that he may die.
verses.textLatin: Si quis per industriam occiderit proximum suum, et per insidias: ab altari meo evelles eum, ut moriatur.

verses.text: He that striketh his father or mother, shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit patrem suum aut matrem, morte moriatur.

verses.text: He that shall steal a man, and sell him, being convicted of the guilt, shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Qui furatus fuerit hominem, et vendiderit eum, convictus noxæ, morte moriatur.

verses.text: He that curseth his father, or mother, shall die the death.
verses.textLatin: Qui maledixerit patri suo, vel matri, morte moriatur.

verses.text: If men quarrel, and the one strike his neighbour with a stone or with his fist, and he die not, but keepeth his bed:
verses.textLatin: Si rixati fuerint viri, et percusserit alter proximum suum lapide vel pugno, et ille mortuus non fuerit, sed jacuerit in lectulo:

verses.text: If he rise again and walk abroad upon his staff, he that struck him shall be quit, yet so that he make restitution for his work, and for his expenses upon the physicians.
verses.textLatin: si surrexerit, et ambulaverit foris super baculum suum, innocens erit qui percusserit, ita tamen ut operas ejus et impensas in medicos restituat.

verses.text: He that striketh his bondman or bondwoman with a rod, and they die under his hands, shall be guilty of the crime.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit servum suum, vel ancillam virga, et mortui fuerint in manibus ejus, criminis reus erit.

verses.text: But if the party remain alive a day or two, he shall not be subject to the punishment, because it is his money.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem uno die vel duobus supervixerit, non subjacebit pœnæ, quia pecunia illius est.

verses.text: If men quarrel, and one strike a woman with child, and she miscarry indeed, but live herself: he shall be answerable for so much damage as the woman’s husband shall require, and as arbiters shall award.
verses.textLatin: Si rixati fuerint viri, et percusserit quis mulierem prægnantem, et abortivum quidem fecerit, sed ipsa vixerit: subjacebit damno quantum maritus mulieris expetierit, et arbitri judicaverint.

verses.text: But if her death ensue thereupon, he shall render life for life.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem mors ejus fuerit subsecuta, reddet animam pro anima,

verses.text: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
verses.textLatin: oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente, manum pro manu, pedem pro pede,

verses.text: Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
verses.textLatin: adustionem pro adustione, vulnus pro vulnere, livorem pro livore.

verses.text: If any man strike the eye of his manservant or maidservant, and leave them but one eye, he shall let them go free for the eye which he put out.
verses.textLatin: Si percusserit quispiam oculum servi sui aut ancillæ, et luscos eos fecerit, dimittet eos liberos pro oculo quem eruit.

verses.text: Also if he strike out a tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he shall in like manner make them free.
verses.textLatin: Dentem quoque si excusserit servo vel ancillæ suæ, similiter dimittet eos liberos.

verses.text: If an ox gore a man or a woman, and they die, he shall be stoned: and his flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox shall be quit.
verses.textLatin: Si bos cornu percusserit virum aut mulierem, et mortui fuerint, lapidibus obruetur: et non comedentur carnes ejus, dominus quoque bovis innocens erit.

verses.text: But if the ox was wont to push with his horn yesterday and the day before, and they warned his master, and he did not shut him up, and he shall kill a man or a woman: then the ox shall be stoned, and his owner also shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Quod si bos cornupeta fuerit ab heri et nudiustertius, et contestati sunt dominum ejus, nec recluserit eum, occideritque virum aut mulierem: et bos lapidibus obruetur, et dominum ejus occident.

verses.text: And if they set a price upon him, he shall give for his life whatsoever is laid upon him.
verses.textLatin: Quod si pretium fuerit ei impositum, dabit pro anima sua quidquid fuerit postulatus.

verses.text: If he have gored a son, or a daughter, he shall fall under the like sentence.
verses.textLatin: Filium quoque et filiam si cornu percusserit, simili sententiæ subjacebit.

verses.text: If he assault a bondman or bondwoman, he shall give thirty sicles of silver to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.
verses.textLatin: Si servum ancillamque invaserit, triginta siclos argenti domino dabit, bos vero lapidibus opprimetur.

verses.text: If a man open a pit, and dig one, and cover it not, and an ox or an ass fall into it,
verses.textLatin: Si quis aperuerit cisternam, et foderit, et non operuerit eam, cecideritque bos aut asinus in eam,

verses.text: The owner of the pit shall pay the price of the beasts: and that which is dead shall be his own.
verses.textLatin: reddet dominus cisternæ pretium jumentorum: quod autem mortuum est, ipsius erit.

verses.text: If one man’s ox gore another man’s ox, and he die: they shall sell the live ox, and shall divide the price, and the carcass of that which died they shall part between them:
verses.textLatin: Si bos alienus bovem alterius vulneraverit, et ille mortuus fuerit: vendent bovem vivum, et divident pretium, cadaver autem mortui inter se dispertient.

verses.text: But if he knew that his ox was wont to push yesterday and the day before, and his master did not keep him in: he shall pay ox for ox, and shall take the whole carcass.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem sciebat quod bos cornupeta esset ab heri et nudiustertius, et non custodivit eum dominus suus: reddet bovem pro bove, et cadaver integrum accipiet.

verses.text: If  any man steal an ox or a sheep, and kill or sell it: he shall restore five oxen for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.
verses.textLatin: Si quis furatus fuerit bovem aut ovem, et occiderit vel vendiderit: quinque boves pro uno bove restituet, et quatuor oves pro una ove.

verses.text: If a thief be found breaking open a house or undermining it, and be wounded so as to die: he that slew him shall not be guilty of blood.
verses.textLatin: Si effringens fur domum sive suffodiens fuerit inventus, et accepto vulnere mortuus fuerit, percussor non erit reus sanguinis.

verses.text: But if he did this when the sun is risen, he hath committed murder, and he shall die. If he have not wherewith to make restitution for the theft, he shall be sold.
verses.textLatin: Quod si orto sole hoc fecerit, homicidium perpetravit, et ipse morietur. Si non habuerit quod pro furto reddat, ipse venundabitur.

verses.text: If that which he stole be found with him, alive, either ox, or ass, or sheep: he shall restore double.
verses.textLatin: Si inventum fuerit apud eum quod furatus est, vivens: sive bos, sive asinus, sive ovis, duplum restituet.

verses.text: If any man hurt a field or a vineyard, and put in his beast to feed upon that which is other men’s: he shall restore the best of whatsoever he hath in his own field, or in his vineyard, according to the estimation of the damage.
verses.textLatin: Si læserit quispiam agrum vel vineam, et dimiserit jumentum suum ut depascatur aliena: quidquid optimum habuerit in agro suo, vel in vinea, pro damni æstimatione restituet.

verses.text: If a fire breaking out light upon thorns, and catch stacks of corn, or corn standing in the fields, he that kindled the fire shall make good the loss.
verses.textLatin: Si egressus ignis invenerit spinas, et comprehenderit acervos frugum, sive stantes segetes in agris, reddet damnum qui ignem succenderit.

verses.text: If a man deliver money, or any vessel unto his friend to keep, and they be stolen away from him that received them: if the thief be found he shall restore double:
verses.textLatin: Si quis commendaverit amico pecuniam aut vas in custodiam, et ab eo, qui susceperat, furto ablata fuerint: si invenitur fur, duplum reddet:

verses.text: If the thief be not known, the master of the house shall be brought to the gods, and shall swear that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbour’s goods,
verses.textLatin: si latet fur, dominus domus applicabitur ad deos, et jurabit quod non extenderit manum in rem proximi sui,

verses.text: To do any fraud, either in ox, or in ass, or sheep, or raiment, or any thing that may bring damage: the cause of both parties shall come to the gods: and if they give judgment, he shall restore double to his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: ad perpetrandam fraudem, tam in bove quam in asino, et ove ac vestimento, et quidquid damnum inferre potest: ad deos utriusque causa perveniet, et si illi judicaverint, duplum restituet proximo suo.

verses.text: If a man deliver ass, ox, sheep, or any beast, to his neighbour’s custody, and it die, or be hurt, or be taken by enemies, and no man saw it:
verses.textLatin: Si quis commendaverit proximo suo asinum, bovem, ovem, et omne jumentum ad custodiam, et mortuum fuerit, aut debilitatum, vel captum ab hostibus, nullusque hoc viderit:

verses.text: There shall be an oath between them, that he did not put forth his hand to his neighbour’s goods: and the owner shall accept of the oath; and he shall not be compelled to make restitution.
verses.textLatin: jusjurandum erit in medio, quod non extenderit manum ad rem proximi sui: suscipietque dominus juramentum, et ille reddere non cogetur.

verses.text: But if it were taken away by stealth, he shall make the loss good to the owner.
verses.textLatin: Quod si furto ablatum fuerit, restituet damnum domino;

verses.text: If it were eaten by a beast, let him bring to him that which was slain, and he shall not make restitution.
verses.textLatin: si comestum a bestia, deferat ad eum quod occisum est, et non restituet.

verses.text: If a man borrow of his neighbour any of these things, and it be hurt or die, the owner not being present, he shall be obliged to make restitution.
verses.textLatin: Qui a proximo suo quidquam horum mutuo postulaverit, et debilitatum aut mortuum fuerit domino non præsente, reddere compelletur.

verses.text: But if the owner be present, he shall not make restitution, especially if it were hired and came for the hire of his work.
verses.textLatin: Quod si impræsentiarum dominus fuerit, non restituet, maxime si conductum venerat pro mercede operis sui.

verses.text: If a man seduce a virgin not yet espoused, and lie with her: he shall endow her, and have her to wife.
verses.textLatin: Si seduxerit quis virginem necdum desponsatam, dormieritque cum ea: dotabit eam, et habebit eam uxorem.

verses.text: If the maid’s father will not give her to him, he shall give money according to the dowry, which virgins are wont to receive.
verses.textLatin: Si pater virginis dare noluerit, reddet pecuniam juxta modum dotis, quam virgines accipere consueverunt.

verses.text: Wizards thou shalt not suffer to live.
verses.textLatin: Maleficos non patieris vivere.

verses.text: Whosoever copulateth with a beast shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Qui coierit cum jumento, morte moriatur.

verses.text: He that sacrificeth to gods, shall be put to death, save only to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui immolat diis, occidetur, præterquam Domino soli.

verses.text: Thou shalt not molest a stranger, nor afflict him: for yourselves also were strangers in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Advenam non contristabis, neque affliges eum: advenæ enim et ipsi fuistis in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: You shall not hurt a widow or an orphan.
verses.textLatin: Viduæ et pupillo non nocebitis.

verses.text: If you hurt them they will cry out to me, and I will hear their cry:
verses.textLatin: Si læseritis eos, vociferabuntur ad me, et ego audiam clamorem eorum:

verses.text: And my rage shall be enkindled, and I will strike you with the sword, and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless.
verses.textLatin: et indignabitur furor meus, percutiamque vos gladio, et erunt uxores vestræ viduæ, et filii vestri pupilli.

verses.text: If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor, that dwelleth with thee, thou shalt not be hard upon them as an extortioner, nor oppress them with usuries.
verses.textLatin: Si pecuniam mutuam dederis populo meo pauperi qui habitat tecum, non urgebis eum quasi exactor, nec usuris opprimes.

verses.text: If thou take of thy neighbour a garment in pledge, thou shalt give it him again before sunset.
verses.textLatin: Si pignus a proximo tuo acceperis vestimentum, ante solis occasum reddes ei.

verses.text: For that same is the only thing wherewith he is covered, the clothing of his body, neither hath he any other to sleep in: if he cry to me, I will hear him, because I am compassionate.
verses.textLatin: Ipsum enim est solum, quo operitur, indumentum carnis ejus, nec habet aliud in quo dormiat: si clamaverit ad me, exaudiam eum, quia misericors sum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not speak ill of the gods, and the prince of thy people thou shalt not curse.
verses.textLatin: Diis non detrahes, et principi populi tui non maledices.

verses.text: Thou shalt not delay to pay thy tithes and thy firstfruits: thou shalt give the firstborn of thy sons to me.
verses.textLatin: Decimas tuas et primitias tuas non tardabis reddere: primogenitum filiorum tuorum dabis mihi.

verses.text: Thou shalt do the same with the firstborn of thy oxen also and sheep: seven days let it be with its dam, the eighth day thou shalt give it to me.
verses.textLatin: De bobus quoque, et ovibus similiter facies: septem diebus sit cum matre sua, die octava reddes illum mihi.

verses.text: You shall be holy men to me: the flesh that beasts have tasted of before, you shall not eat, but shall cast it to the dogs.
verses.textLatin: Viri sancti eritis mihi: carnem, quæ a bestiis fuerit prægustata, non comedetis, sed projicietis canibus.

verses.text: Thou  shalt not receive the voice of a lie: neither shalt thou join thy hand to bear false witness for a wicked person.
verses.textLatin: Non suscipies vocem mendacii, nec junges manum tuam ut pro impio dicas falsum testimonium.

verses.text: Thou shalt not follow the multitude to do evil: neither shalt thou yield in judgment, to the opinion of the most part, to stray from the truth.
verses.textLatin: Non sequeris turbam ad faciendum malum: nec in judicio, plurimorum acquiesces sententiæ, ut a vero devies.

verses.text: Neither shalt thou favour a poor man in judgment.
verses.textLatin: Pauperis quoque non misereberis in judicio.

verses.text: If thou meet thy enemy’s ox or ass going astray, bring it back to him.
verses.textLatin: Si occurreris bovi inimici tui, aut asino erranti, reduc ad eum.

verses.text: If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lie underneath his burden, thou shalt not pass by, but shalt lift him up with him.
verses.textLatin: Si videris asinum odientis te jacere sub onere, non pertransibis, sed sublevabis cum eo.

verses.text: Thou shalt not go aside in the poor man’s judgment.
verses.textLatin: Non declinabis in judicium pauperis.

verses.text: Thou shalt fly lying. The innocent and just person thou shalt not put to death: because I abhor the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Mendacium fugies. Insontem et justum non occides: quia aversor impium.

verses.text: Neither shalt thou take bribes, which even blind the wise, and pervert the words of the just.
verses.textLatin: Nec accipies munera, quæ etiam excæcant prudentes, et subvertunt verba justorum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not molest a stranger, for you know the hearts of strangers: for you also were strangers in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Peregrino molestus non eris. Scitis enim advenarum animas: quia et ipsi peregrini fuistis in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: Six years thou shalt sow thy ground, and shalt gather the corn thereof.
verses.textLatin: Sex annis seminabis terram tuam, et congregabis fruges ejus:

verses.text: But the seventh year thou shalt let it alone, and suffer it to rest, that the poor of thy people may eat, and whatsoever shall be left, let the beasts of the field eat it: so shalt thou do with thy vineyard and thy oliveyard.
verses.textLatin: anno autem septimo dimittes eam, et requiescere facies, ut comedant pauperes populi tui: et quidquid reliquum fuerit, edant bestiæ agri: ita facies in vinea et in oliveto tuo.

verses.text: Six days thou shalt work: the seventh day thou shalt cease, that thy ox and thy ass may rest: and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus operaberis: septimo die cessabis, ut requiescat bos et asinus tuus, et refrigeretur filius ancillæ tuæ, et advena.

verses.text: Keep all things that I have said to you. And by the name of strange gods you shall not swear, neither shall it be heard out of your mouth.
verses.textLatin: Omnia quæ dixi vobis, custodite. Et per nomen externorum deorum non jurabitis, neque audietur ex ore vestro.

verses.text: Three times every year you shall celebrate feasts to me.
verses.textLatin: Tribus vicibus per singulos annos mihi festa celebrabitis.

verses.text: Thou shalt keep the feast of unleavened bread. Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, in the time of the month of new corn, when thou didst come forth out of Egypt: thou shalt not appear empty before me.
verses.textLatin: Solemnitatem azymorum custodies. Septem diebus comedes azyma, sicut præcepi tibi, tempore mensis novorum, quando egressus es de Ægypto: non apparebis in conspectu meo vacuus.

verses.text: And the feast of the harvest of the firstfruits of thy work, whatsoever thou hast sown in the field. The feast also in the end of the year, when thou hast gathered in all thy corn out of the field.
verses.textLatin: Et solemnitatem messis primitivorum operis tui, quæcumque seminaveris in agro: solemnitatem quoque in exitu anni, quando congregaveris omnes fruges tuas de agro.

verses.text: Thrice a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Ter in anno apparebit omne masculinum tuum coram Domino Deo tuo.

verses.text: Thou shalt not sacrifice the blood of my victim upon leaven, neither shall the fat of my solemnity remain until the morning.
verses.textLatin: Non immolabis super fermento sanguinem victimæ meæ, nec remanebit adeps solemnitatis meæ usque mane.

verses.text: Thou shalt carry the firstfruits of the corn of thy ground to the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in the milk of his dam.
verses.textLatin: Primitias frugum terræ tuæ deferes in domum Domini Dei tui. Non coques hædum in lacte matris suæ.

verses.text: Behold I will send my angel, who shall go before thee, and keep thee in thy journey, and bring thee into the place that I have prepared.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego mittam angelum meum, qui præcedat te, et custodiat in via, et introducat in locum quem paravi.

verses.text: Take notice of him, and hear his voice, and do not think him one to be contemned: for he will not forgive when thou hast sinned, and my name is in him.
verses.textLatin: Observa eum, et audi vocem ejus, nec contemnendum putes: quia non dimittet cum peccaveris, et est nomen meum in illo.

verses.text: But if thou wilt hear his voice, and do all that I speak, I will be an enemy to thy enemies, and will afflict them that afflict thee.
verses.textLatin: Quod si audieris vocem ejus, et feceris omnia quæ loquor, inimicus ero inimicis tuis, et affligam affligentes te.

verses.text: And my angel shall go before thee, and shall bring thee in unto the Amorrhite, and the Hethite, and the Pherezite, and the Chanaanite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite, whom I will destroy.
verses.textLatin: Præcedetque te angelus meus, et introducet te ad Amorrhæum, et Hethæum, et Pherezæum, Chananæumque, et Hevæum, et Jebusæum, quos ego conteram.

verses.text: Thou shalt not adore their gods, nor serve them. Thou shalt not do their works, but shalt destroy them, and break their statues.
verses.textLatin: Non adorabis deos eorum, nec coles eos: non facies opera eorum, sed destrues eos, et confringes statuas eorum.

verses.text: And you shall serve the Lord your God, that I may bless your bread and your waters, and may take away sickness from the midst of thee.
verses.textLatin: Servietisque Domino Deo vestro, ut benedicam panibus tuis et aquis, et auferam infirmitatem de medio tui.

verses.text: There shall not be one fruitless nor barren in thy land: I will fill the number of thy days.
verses.textLatin: Non erit infœcunda, nec sterilis in terra tua: numerum dierum tuorum implebo.

verses.text: I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come: and will turn the backs of all thy enemies before thee.
verses.textLatin: Terrorem meum mittam in præcursum tuum, et occidam omnem populum, ad quem ingredieris: cunctorumque inimicorum tuorum coram te terga vertam:

verses.text: Sending out hornets before, that shall drive away the Hevite, and the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, before thou come in.
verses.textLatin: emittens crabrones prius, qui fugabunt Hevæum, et Chananæum, et Hethæum, antequam introëas.

verses.text: I will not cast them out from thy face in one year: lest the land be brought into a wilderness, and the beasts multiply against thee.
verses.textLatin: Non ejiciam eos a facie tua anno uno: ne terra in solitudinem redigatur, et crescant contra te bestiæ.

verses.text: By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, till thou be increased, and dost possess the land.
verses.textLatin: Paulatim expellam eos de conspectu tuo, donec augearis, et possideas terram.

verses.text: And I will set thy bounds from the Red Sea to the sea of the Palestines, and from the desert to the river: I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and will drive them out from before you.
verses.textLatin: Ponam autem terminos tuos a mari Rubro usque ad mare Palæstinorum, et a deserto usque ad fluvium: tradam in manibus vestris habitatores terræ, et ejiciam eos de conspectu vestro.

verses.text: Thou shalt not enter into league with them, nor with their gods.
verses.textLatin: Non inibis cum eis fœdus, nec cum diis eorum.

verses.text: Let them not dwell in thy land, lest perhaps they make thee sin against me, if thou serve their gods: which undoubtedly will be a scandal to thee.
verses.textLatin: Non habitent in terra tua, ne forte peccare te faciant in me, si servieris diis eorum: quod tibi certe erit in scandalum.

verses.text: And  he said to Moses: Come up to the Lord, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abiu, and seventy of the ancients of Israel, and you shall adore afar off.
verses.textLatin: Moysi quoque dixit: Ascende ad Dominum tu, et Aaron, Nadab et Abiu, et septuaginta senes ex Israël, et adorabitis procul.

verses.text: And Moses alone shall come up to the Lord, but they shall not come nigh: neither shall the people come up with him.
verses.textLatin: Solusque Moyses ascendet ad Dominum, et illi non appropinquabunt: nec populus ascendet cum eo.

verses.text: So Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord, and all the judgments: and all the people answered with one voice: We will do all the words of the Lord, which he hath spoken.
verses.textLatin: Venit ergo Moyses et narravit plebi omnia verba Domini, atque judicia: responditque omnis populus una voce: Omnia verba Domini, quæ locutus est, faciemus.

verses.text: And Moses wrote all the words of the Lord: and rising in the morning he built an altar at the foot of the mount, and twelve titles according to the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Scripsit autem Moyses universos sermones Domini: et mane consurgens, ædificavit altare ad radices montis, et duodecim titulos per duodecim tribus Israël.

verses.text: And he sent young men of the children of Israel, and they offered holocausts, and sacrificed pacific victims of calves to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Misitque juvenes de filiis Israël, et obtulerunt holocausta, immolaveruntque victimas pacificas Domino, vitulos.

verses.text: Then Moses took half of the blood, and put it into bowls: and the rest he poured upon the altar.
verses.textLatin: Tulit itaque Moyses dimidiam partem sanguinis, et misit in crateras: partem autem residuam fudit super altare.

verses.text: And taking the book of the covenant, he read it in the hearing of the people: and they said: All things that the Lord hath spoken we will do, we will be obedient.
verses.textLatin: Assumensque volumen fœderis, legit audiente populo: qui dixerunt: Omnia quæ locutus est Dominus, faciemus, et erimus obedientes.

verses.text: And he took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, and he said: This is the blood of the covenant which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.
verses.textLatin: Ille vero sumptum sanguinem respersit in populum, et ait: Hic est sanguis fœderis quod pepigit Dominus vobiscum super cunctis sermonibus his.

verses.text: Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abiu, and seventy of the ancients of Israel went up:
verses.textLatin: Ascenderuntque Moyses et Aaron, Nadab et Abiu, et septuaginta de senioribus Israël:

verses.text: And they saw the God of Israel: and under his feet as it were a work of sapphire stone, and as the heaven, when clear.
verses.textLatin: et viderunt Deum Israël: et sub pedibus ejus quasi opus lapidis sapphirini, et quasi cælum, cum serenum est.

verses.text: Neither did he lay his hand upon those of the children of Israel, that retired afar off, and they saw God, and they did eat and drink.
verses.textLatin: Nec super eos qui procul recesserant de filiis Israël, misit manum suam, videruntque Deum, et comederunt, ac biberunt.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I will give thee tables of stone, and the law, and the commandments which I have written: that thou mayest teach them.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Ascende ad me in montem, et esto ibi: daboque tibi tabulas lapideas, et legem, ac mandata quæ scripsi: ut doceas eos.

verses.text: Moses rose up, and his minister Josue: and Moses going up into the mount of God,
verses.textLatin: Surrexerunt Moyses et Josue minister ejus: ascendensque Moyses in montem Dei,

verses.text: Said to the ancients: Wait ye here till we return to you. You have Aaron and Hur with you: if any question shall arise, you shall refer it to them.
verses.textLatin: senioribus ait: Expectate hic donec revertamur ad vos. Habetis Aaron et Hur vobiscum: si quid natum fuerit quæstionis, referetis ad eos.

verses.text: And when Moses was gone up, a cloud covered the mount.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ascendisset Moyses, operuit nubes montem,

verses.text: And the glory of the Lord dwelt upon Sinai, covering it with a cloud six days: and the seventh day he called him out of the midst of the cloud.
verses.textLatin: et habitavit gloria Domini super Sinai, tegens illum nube sex diebus: septimo autem die vocavit eum de medio caliginis.

verses.text: And the sight of the glory of the Lord was like a burning fire upon the top of the mount, in the eyes of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem species gloriæ Domini quasi ignis ardens super verticem montis in conspectu filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And Moses, entering into the midst of the cloud, went up into the mountain: and he was there forty days, and forty nights.
verses.textLatin: Ingressusque Moyses medium nebulæ, ascendit in montem: et fuit ibi quadraginta diebus, et quadraginta noctibus.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring firstfruits to me: of every man that offereth of his own accord, you shall take them.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, ut tollant mihi primitias: ab omni homine qui offeret ultroneus, accipietis eas.

verses.text: And these are the things you must take: gold, and silver, and brass,
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt autem quæ accipere debeatis: aurum, et argentum, et æs,

verses.text: Violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, and goats’ hair,
verses.textLatin: hyacinthum et purpuram, coccumque bis tinctum, et byssum, pilos caprarum,

verses.text: And rams’ skins dyed red, and violet skins, and setim wood:
verses.textLatin: et pelles arietum rubricatas, pellesque janthinas, et ligna setim:

verses.text: Oil to make lights: spices for ointment, and for sweetsmelling incense:
verses.textLatin: oleum ad luminaria concinnanda: aromata in unguentum, et thymiamata boni odoris:

verses.text: Onyx stones, and precious stones to adorn the ephod and the rational.
verses.textLatin: lapides onychinos, et gemmas ad ornandum ephod, ac rationale.

verses.text: And they shall make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell in the midst of them:
verses.textLatin: Facientque mihi sanctuarium, et habitabo in medio eorum:

verses.text: According to all the likeness of the tabernacle which I will shew thee, and of all the vessels for the service thereof: and thus you shall make it:
verses.textLatin: juxta omnem similitudinem tabernaculi quod ostendam tibi, et omnium vasorum in cultum ejus. Sicque facietis illud:

verses.text: Frame an ark of setim wood, the length whereof shall be of two cubits and a half: the breadth, a cubit and a half: the height, likewise, a cubit and a half.
verses.textLatin: arcam de lignis setim compingite, cujus longitudo habeat duos et semis cubitos: latitudo, cubitum et dimidium: altitudo, cubitum similiter ac semissem.

verses.text: And thou shalt overlay it with the purest gold within and without: and over it thou shalt make a golden crown round about:
verses.textLatin: Et deaurabis eam auro mundissimo intus et foris: faciesque supra, coronam auream per circuitum:

verses.text: And four golden rings, which thou shalt put at the four corners of the ark: let two rings be on the one side, and two on the other.
verses.textLatin: et quatuor circulos aureos, quos pones per quatuor arcæ angulos: duo circuli sint in latere uno, et duo in altero.

verses.text: Thou shalt make bars also of setim wood, and shalt overlay them with gold.
verses.textLatin: Facies quoque vectes de lignis setim, et operies eos auro.

verses.text: And thou shalt put them in through the rings that are in the sides of the ark, that it may be carried on them.
verses.textLatin: Inducesque per circulos qui sunt in arcæ lateribus, ut portetur in eis:

verses.text: And they shall be always in the rings, neither shall they at any time be drawn out of them.
verses.textLatin: qui semper erunt in circulis, nec umquam extrahentur ab eis.

verses.text: And thou shalt put in the ark the testimony which I will give thee.
verses.textLatin: Ponesque in arca testificationem quam dabo tibi.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a propitiatory of the purest gold: the length thereof shall be two cubits and a half, and the breadth a cubit and a half.
verses.textLatin: Facies et propitiatorium de auro mundissimo: duos cubitos et dimidium tenebit longitudo ejus, et cubitum ac semissem latitudo.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also two cherubims of beaten gold, on the two sides of the oracle.
verses.textLatin: Duos quoque cherubim aureos et productiles facies, ex utraque parte oraculi.

verses.text: Let one cherub be on the one side, and the other on the other.
verses.textLatin: Cherub unus sit in latere uno, et alter in altero.

verses.text: Let them cover both sides of the propitiatory, spreading their wings, and covering the oracle, and let them look one towards the other, their faces being turned towards the propitiatory wherewith the ark is to be covered.
verses.textLatin: Utrumque latus propitiatorii tegant expandentes alas, et operientes oraculum, respiciantque se mutuo versis vultibus in propitiatorium quo operienda est arca,

verses.text: In which thou shalt put the testimony that I will give thee.
verses.textLatin: in qua pones testimonium quod dabo tibi.

verses.text: Thence will I give orders, and will speak to thee over the propitiatory, and from the midst of the two cherubims, which shall be upon the ark of the testimony, all things which I will command the children of Israel by thee.
verses.textLatin: Inde præcipiam, et loquar ad te supra propitiatorium, ac de medio duorum cherubim, qui erunt super arcam testimonii, cuncta quæ mandabo per te filiis Israël.

verses.text: Thou shalt make a table also of setim wood, of two cubits in length, and a cubit in breadth, and a cubit and a half in height.
verses.textLatin: Facies et mensam de lignis setim, habentem duos cubitos longitudinis, et in latitudine cubitum, et in altitudine cubitum et semissem.

verses.text: And thou shalt overlay it with the purest gold: and thou shalt make to it a golden ledge round about.
verses.textLatin: Et inaurabis eam auro purissimo: faciesque illi labium aureum per circuitum,

verses.text: And to the ledge itself a polished crown, four inches high: and over the same another little golden crown.
verses.textLatin: et ipsi labio coronam interrasilem altam quatuor digitis: et super illam, alteram coronam aureolam.

verses.text: Thou shalt prepare also four golden rings, and shalt put them in the four corners of the same table over each foot.
verses.textLatin: Quatuor quoque circulos aureos præparabis, et pones eis in quatuor angulis ejusdem mensæ per singulos pedes.

verses.text: Under the crown shall the golden rings be, that the bars may be put through them, and the table may be carried.
verses.textLatin: Subter coronam erunt circuli aurei, ut mittantur vectes per eos, et possit mensa portari.

verses.text: The bars also themselves thou shalt make of setim wood, and shalt overlay them with gold to bear up the table.
verses.textLatin: Ipsos quoque vectes facies de lignis setim, et circumdabis auro ad subvehendam mensam.

verses.text: Thou shalt prepare also dishes, and bowls, censers, and cups, wherein the libations are to be offered of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Parabis et acetabula, ac phialas, thuribula, et cyathos, in quibus offerenda sunt libamina, ex auro purissimo.

verses.text: And thou shalt set upon the table loaves of proposition in my sight always.
verses.textLatin: Et pones super mensam panes propositionis in conspectu meo semper.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a candlestick of beaten work of the finest gold, the shaft thereof, and the branches, the cups, and the bowls, and the lilies going forth from it.
verses.textLatin: Facies et candelabrum ductile de auro mundissimo, hastile ejus, et calamos, scyphos, et sphærulas, ac lilia ex ipso procedentia.

verses.text: Six branches shall come out of the sides, three out of one side, and three out of the other.
verses.textLatin: Sex calami egredientur de lateribus, tres ex uno latere, et tres ex altero.

verses.text: Three cups as it were nuts to every branch, and a bowl withal, and a lily; and three cups, likewise of the fashion of nuts in the other branch, and a bowl withal, and a lily. Such shall be the work of the six branches, that are to come out from the shaft:
verses.textLatin: Tres scyphi quasi in nucis modum per calamos singulos, sphærulaque simul, et lilium: et tres similiter scyphi instar nucis in calamo altero, sphærulaque simul et lilium. Hoc erit opus sex calamorum, qui producendi sunt de hastili:

verses.text: And in the candlestick itself shall be four cups in the manner of a nut, and at every one, bowls and lilies.
verses.textLatin: in ipso autem candelabro erunt quatuor scyphi in nucis modum, sphærulæque per singulos, et lilia.

verses.text: Bowls under two branches in three places, which together make six coming forth out of one shaft.
verses.textLatin: Sphærulæ sub duobus calamis per tria loca, qui simul sex fiunt procedentes de hastili uno.

verses.text: And both the bowls and the branches shall be of the same beaten work of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Et sphærulæ igitur et calami ex ipso erunt, universa ductilia de auro purissimo.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also seven lamps, and shalt set them upon the candlestick, to give light over against.
verses.textLatin: Facies et lucernas septem, et pones eas super candelabrum, ut luceant ex adverso.

verses.text: The snuffers also and where the snuffings shall be put out, shall be made of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Emunctoria quoque, et ubi quæ emuncta sunt extinguantur, fiant de auro purissimo.

verses.text: The whole weight of the candlestick with all the furniture thereof shall be a talent of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Omne pondus candelabri cum universis vasis suis habebit talentum auri purissimi.

verses.text: Look, and make it according to the pattern, that was shewn thee in the mount.
verses.textLatin: Inspice, et fac secundum exemplar quod tibi in monte monstratum est.

verses.text: And  thou shalt make the tabernacle in this manner: Thou shalt make ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, diversified with embroidery.
verses.textLatin: Tabernaculum vero ita facies: decem cortinas de bysso retorta, et hyacintho, ac purpura, coccoque bis tincto, variatas opere plumario facies.

verses.text: The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, the breadth shall be four cubits. All the curtains shall be of one measure.
verses.textLatin: Longitudo cortinæ unius habebit viginti octo cubitos: latitudo, quatuor cubitorum erit. Unius mensuræ fient universa tentoria.

verses.text: Five curtains shall be joined one to another, and the other five shall be coupled together in like manner.
verses.textLatin: Quinque cortinæ sibi jungentur mutuo, et aliæ quinque nexu simili cohærebunt.

verses.text: Thou shalt make loops of violet in the sides and tops of the curtains, that they may be joined one to another.
verses.textLatin: Ansulas hyacinthinas in lateribus ac summitatibus facies cortinarum, ut possint invicem copulari.

verses.text: Every curtain shall have fifty loops on both sides, so set on, that one loop may be against another loop, and one may be fitted to the other.
verses.textLatin: Quinquagenas ansulas cortina habebit in utraque parte, ita insertas ut ansa contra ansam veniat, et altera alteri possit aptari.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also fifty rings of gold wherewith the veils of the curtains are to be joined, that it may be made one tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Facies et quinquaginta circulos aureos quibus cortinarum vela jungenda sunt, ut unum tabernaculum fiat.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also eleven curtains of goats’ hair, to cover the top of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Facies et saga cilicina undecim, ad operiendum tectum tabernaculi.

verses.text: The length of one hair curtain shall be thirty cubits: and the breadth four: the measure of all the curtains shall be equal.
verses.textLatin: Longitudo sagi unius habebit triginta cubitos, et latitudo, quatuor: æqua erit mensura sagorum omnium.

verses.text: Five of which thou shalt couple by themselves, and the six others thou shalt couple one to another, so as to double the sixth curtain in the front of the roof.
verses.textLatin: E quibus quinque junges seorsum, et sex sibi mutuo copulabis, ita ut sextum sagum in fronte tecti duplices.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also fifty loops in the edge of one curtain, that it may be joined with the other: and fifty loops in the edge of the other curtain, that it may be coupled with its fellow.
verses.textLatin: Facies et quinquaginta ansas in ora sagi unius, ut conjungi cum altero queat, et quinquaginta ansas in ora sagi alterius, ut cum altero copuletur.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also fifty buckles of brass, wherewith the loops may be joined, that of all there may be made one covering.
verses.textLatin: Facies et quinquaginta fibulas æneas quibus jungantur ansæ, ut unum ex omnibus operimentum fiat.

verses.text: And that which shall remain of the curtains, that are prepared for the roof, to wit, one curtain that is over and above, with the half thereof thou shalt cover the back parts of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Quod autem superfuerit in sagis quæ parantur tecto, id est unum sagum quod amplius est, ex medietate ejus operies posteriora tabernaculi.

verses.text: And there shall hang down a cubit on the one side, and another on the other side, which is over and above in the length of the curtains, fencing both sides of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Et cubitus ex una parte pendebit, et alter ex altera qui plus est in sagorum longitudine, utrumque latus tabernaculi protegens.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also another cover to the roof, of rams’ skins dyed red; and over that again another cover of violet coloured skins.
verses.textLatin: Facies et operimentum aliud tecto de pellibus arietum rubricatis: et super hoc rursum aliud operimentum de janthinis pellibus.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also the boards of the tabernacle standing upright of setim wood.
verses.textLatin: Facies et tabulas stantes tabernaculi de lignis setim,

verses.text: Let every one of them be ten cubits in length, and in breadth one cubit and a half.
verses.textLatin: quæ singulæ denos cubitos in longitudine habeant, et in latitudine singulos ac semissem.

verses.text: In the sides of the boards shall be made two mortises, whereby one board may be joined to another board: and after this manner shall all the boards be prepared.
verses.textLatin: In lateribus tabulæ, duæ incastraturæ fient, quibus tabula alteri tabulæ connectatur: atque in hunc modum cunctæ tabulæ parabuntur.

verses.text: Of which twenty shall be in the south side southward.
verses.textLatin: Quarum viginti erunt in latere meridiano quod vergit ad austrum.

verses.text: For which thou shalt cast forty sockets of silver, that under every board may be put two sockets at the two corners.
verses.textLatin: Quibus quadraginta bases argenteas fundes, ut binæ bases singulis tabulis per duos angulos subjiciantur.

verses.text: In the second side also the tabernacle that looketh to the north, there shall be twenty boards,
verses.textLatin: In latere quoque secundo tabernaculi quod vergit ad aquilonem, viginti tabulæ erunt,

verses.text: Having forty sockets of silver, two sockets shall be put under each board.
verses.textLatin: quadraginta habentes bases argenteas, binæ bases singulis tabulis supponentur.

verses.text: But on the west side of the tabernacle thou shalt make six boards.
verses.textLatin: Ad occidentalem vero plagam tabernaculi facies sex tabulas,

verses.text: And again other two which shall be erected in the corners at the back of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: et rursum alias duas quæ in angulis erigantur post tergum tabernaculi.

verses.text: And they shall be joined together from beneath unto the top, and one joint shall hold them all. The like joining shall be observed for the two boards also that are to be put in the corners.
verses.textLatin: Eruntque conjunctæ a deorsum usque sursum, et una omnes compago retinebit. Duabus quoque tabulis quæ in angulis ponendæ sunt, similis junctura servabitur.

verses.text: And they shall be in all eight boards, and their silver sockets sixteen, reckoning two sockets for each board.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt simul tabulæ octo, bases earum argenteæ sedecim, duabus basibus per unam tabulam supputatis.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also five bars of setim wood, to hold together the boards on one side of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Facies et vectes de lignis setim quinque ad continendas tabulas in uno latere tabernaculi,

verses.text: And five others on the other side, and as many at the west side:
verses.textLatin: et quinque alios in altero, et ejusdem numeri ad occidentalem plagam:

verses.text: And they shall be put along by the midst of the boards from one end to the other.
verses.textLatin: qui mittentur per medias tabulas a summo usque ad summum.

verses.text: The boards also themselves thou shalt overlay with gold, and shall cast rings of gold to be set upon them, for places for the bars to hold together the boardwork: which bars thou shalt cover with plates of gold.
verses.textLatin: Ipsas quoque tabulas deaurabis, et fundes in eis annulos aureos per quos vectes tabulata contineant: quos operies laminis aureis.

verses.text: And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the pattern that was shewn thee in the mount.
verses.textLatin: Et eriges tabernaculum juxta exemplar quod tibi in monte monstratum est.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a veil of violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen, wrought with embroidered work, and goodly variety:
verses.textLatin: Facies et velum de hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta, opere plumario et pulchra varietate contextum:

verses.text: And thou shalt hang it up before four pillars of setim wood, which themselves also shall be overlaid with gold, and shall have heads of gold, but sockets of silver.
verses.textLatin: quod appendes ante quatuor columnas de lignis setim, quæ ipsæ quidem deauratæ erunt, et habebunt capita aurea, sed bases argenteas.

verses.text: And the veils shall be hanged on with rings, and within it thou shalt put the ark of the testimony, and the sanctuary, and the holy of holies shall be divided with it.
verses.textLatin: Inseretur autem velum per circulos, intra quod pones arcam testimonii, quo et sanctuarium, et sanctuarii sanctuaria dividentur.

verses.text: And thou shalt set the propitiatory upon the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.
verses.textLatin: Pones et propitiatorium super arcam testimonii in Sancto sanctorum,

verses.text: And the table without the veil: and over against the table the candlestick in the south side of the tabernacle: for the table shall stand in the north side.
verses.textLatin: mensamque extra velum, et contra mensam candelabrum in latere tabernaculi meridiano: mensa enim stabit in parte aquilonis.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a hanging in the entrance of the tabernacle of violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen with embroidered work.
verses.textLatin: Facies et tentorium in introitu tabernaculi de hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta, opere plumarii.

verses.text: And thou shalt overlay with gold five pillars of setim wood, before which the hanging shall be drawn: their heads shall be of gold, and the sockets of brass.
verses.textLatin: Et quinque columnas deaurabis lignorum setim, ante quas ducetur tentorium: quarum erunt capita aurea, et bases æneæ.

verses.text: Thou  shalt make also an altar of setim wood, which shall be five cubits long and as many broad, that is, foursquare, and three cubits high.
verses.textLatin: Facies et altare de lignis setim, quod habebit quinque cubitus in longitudine, et totidem in latitudine, id est, quadrum, et tres cubitos in altitudine.

verses.text: And there shall be horns at the four corners of the same: and thou shalt cover it with brass.
verses.textLatin: Cornua autem per quatuor angulos ex ipso erunt: et operies illud ære.

verses.text: And thou shalt make for the uses thereof pans to receive the ashes, and tongs and fleshhooks, and firepans: all its vessels thou shalt make of brass.
verses.textLatin: Faciesque in usus ejus lebetes ad suscipiendos cineres, et forcipes atque fuscinulas, et ignium receptacula; omnia vasa ex ære fabricabis.

verses.text: And a grate of brass in manner of a net: at the four corners of which shall be four rings of brass,
verses.textLatin: Craticulamque in modum retis æneam: per cujus quatuor angulos erunt quatuor annuli ænei.

verses.text: Which thou shalt put under the hearth of the altar: and the grate shall be even to the midst of the altar.
verses.textLatin: Quos pones subter arulam altaris: eritque craticula usque ad altaris medium.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also two bars for the altar of setim wood, which thou shalt cover with plates of brass:
verses.textLatin: Facies et vectes altaris de lignis setim duos, quos operies laminis æneis:

verses.text: And thou shalt draw them through rings, and they shall be on both sides of the altar to carry it.
verses.textLatin: et induces per circulos, eruntque ex utroque latere altaris ad portandum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make it solid, but empty and hollow in the inside, as it was shewn thee in the mount.
verses.textLatin: Non solidum, sed inane et cavum intrinsecus facies illud, sicut tibi in monte monstratum est.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also the court of the tabernacle, in the south side whereof southward there shall be hangings of fine twisted linen of a hundred cubits long for one side.
verses.textLatin: Facies et atrium tabernaculi, in cujus australi plaga contra meridiem erunt tentoria de bysso retorta: centum cubitos unum latus tenebit in longitudine.

verses.text: And twenty pillars with as many sockets of brass, the heads of which with their engraving shall be of silver.
verses.textLatin: Et columnas viginti cum basibus totidem æneis, quæ capita cum cælaturis suis habebunt argentea.

verses.text: In like manner also on the north side there shall be hangings of a hundred cubits long, twenty pillars, and as many sockets of brass, and their heads with their engraving of silver.
verses.textLatin: Similiter et in latere aquilonis per longum erunt tentoria centum cubitorum, columnæ viginti, et bases æneæ ejusdem numeri, et capita earum cum cælaturis suis argentea.

verses.text: But in the breadth of the court, that looketh to the west, there shall be hangings of fifty cubits, and ten pillars, and as many sockets.
verses.textLatin: In latitudine vero atrii, quod respicit ad occidentem, erunt tentoria per quinquaginta cubitos, et columnæ decem, basesque totidem.

verses.text: In that breadth also of the court, which looketh to the east, there shall be fifty cubits.
verses.textLatin: In ea quoque atrii latitudine, quæ respicit ad orientem, quinquaginta cubiti erunt.

verses.text: In which there shall be for one side hangings of fifteen cubits, and three pillars and as many sockets.
verses.textLatin: In quibus quindecim cubitorum tentoria lateri uno deputabuntur, columnæque tres et bases totidem:

verses.text: And in the other side there shall be hangings of fifteen cubits, with three pillars and as many sockets.
verses.textLatin: et in latere altero erunt tentoria cubitos obtinentia quindecim, columnæ tres, et bases totidem.

verses.text: And in the entrance of the court there shall be made a hanging of twenty cubits of violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen, with embroidered work: it shall have four pillars with as many sockets.
verses.textLatin: In introitu vero atrii fiet tentorium cubitorum viginti ex hyacintho et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta, opere plumarii: columnas habebit quatuor, cum basibus totidem.

verses.text: All the pillars of the court round about shall be garnished with plates of silver, silver heads and sockets of brass.
verses.textLatin: Omnes columnæ atrii per circuitum vestitæ erunt argenteis laminis, capitibus argenteis, et basibus æneis.

verses.text: In length the court shall take up a hundred cubits, in breadth fifty, the height shall be of five cubits, and it shall be made of fine twisted linen, and shall have sockets of brass.
verses.textLatin: In longitudine occupabit atrium cubitos centum, in latitudine quinquaginta, altitudo quinque cubitorum erit: fietque de bysso retorta, et habebit bases æneas.

verses.text: All the vessels of the tabernacle for all uses and ceremonies, and the pins both of it, and of the court, thou shalt make of brass.
verses.textLatin: Cuncta vasa tabernaculi in omnes usus et cæremonias, tam paxillos ejus quam atrii, ex ære facies.

verses.text: Command the children of Israel that they bring thee the purest oil of the olives, and beaten with a pestle: that a lamp may burn always,
verses.textLatin: Præcipe filiis Israël ut afferant tibi oleum de arboribus olivarum purissimum, piloque contusum, ut ardeat lucerna semper

verses.text: In the tabernacle of the testimony, without the veil that hangs before the testimony. And Aaron and his sons shall order it, that it may give light before the Lord until the morning. It shall be a perpetual observance throughout their successions among the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: in tabernaculo testimonii, extra velum quod oppansum est testimonio. Et collocabunt eam Aaron et filii ejus, ut usque mane luceat coram Domino. Perpetuus erit cultus per successiones eorum a filiis Israël.

verses.text: Take  unto thee also Aaron thy brother with his sons, from among the children of Israel, that they may minister to me in the priest’s office: Aaron, Nadab, and Abiu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.textLatin: Applica quoque ad te Aaron fratrem tuum cum filiis suis de medio filiorum Israël, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi: Aaron, Nadab, et Abiu, Eleazar, et Ithamar.

verses.text: And thou shalt make a holy vesture for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.
verses.textLatin: Faciesque vestem sanctam Aaron fratri tuo in gloriam et decorem.

verses.text: And thou shalt speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron’s vestments, in which he being consecrated may minister to me.
verses.textLatin: Et loqueris cunctis sapientibus corde quos replevi spiritu prudentiæ, ut faciant vestes Aaron, in quibus sanctificatus ministret mihi.

verses.text: And these shall be the vestments that they shall make: A rational and an ephod, a tunick and a strait linen garment, a mitre and a girdle. They shall make the holy vestments for thy brother Aaron and his sons, that they may do the office of priesthood unto me.
verses.textLatin: Hæc autem erunt vestimenta quæ faciet: rationale et superhumerale, tunicam et lineam strictam, cidarim et balteum. Facient vestimenta sancta fratri tuo Aaron et filiis ejus, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.

verses.text: And they shall take gold, and violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen.
verses.textLatin: Accipientque aurum, et hyacinthum, et purpuram, coccumque bis tinctum, et byssum.

verses.text: And they shall make the ephod of gold, and violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen, embroidered with divers colours.
verses.textLatin: Facient autem superhumerale de auro et hyacintho et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta, opere polymito.

verses.text: It shall have the two edges joined in the top on both sides, that they may be closed together.
verses.textLatin: Duas oras junctas habebit in utroque latere summitatum, ut in unum redeant.

verses.text: The very workmanship also and all the variety of the work shall be of gold, and violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.
verses.textLatin: Ipsa quoque textura et cuncta operis varietas erit ex auro et hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta.

verses.text: And thou shalt take two onyx stones, and shalt grave on them the names of the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Sumesque duos lapides onychinos, et sculpes in eis nomina filiorum Israël:

verses.text: Six names on one stone, and the other six on the other, according to the order of their birth.
verses.textLatin: sex nomina in lapide uno, et sex reliqua in altero, juxta ordinem nativitatis eorum.

verses.text: With the work of an engraver and the graving of a jeweller, thou shalt engrave them with the names of the children of Israel, set in gold and compassed about:
verses.textLatin: Opere sculptoris et cælatura gemmarii, sculpes eos nominibus filiorum Israël, inclusos auro atque circumdatos:

verses.text: And thou shalt put them in both sides of the ephod, a memorial for the children of Israel. And Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord upon both shoulders, for a remembrance.
verses.textLatin: et pones in utroque latere superhumeralis, memoriale filiis Israël. Portabitque Aaron nomina eorum coram Domino super utrumque humerum, ob recordationem.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also hooks of gold.
verses.textLatin: Facies et uncinos ex auro,

verses.text: And two little chains of the purest gold linked one to another, which thou shalt put into the hooks.
verses.textLatin: et duas catenulas ex auro purissimo sibi invicem cohærentes, quas inseres uncinis.

verses.text: And thou shalt make the rational of judgment with embroidered work of divers colours, according to the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.
verses.textLatin: Rationale quoque judicii facies opere polymito juxta texturam superhumeralis, ex auro, hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta.

verses.text: It shall be foursquare and doubled: it shall be the measure of a span both in length and in breadth.
verses.textLatin: Quadrangulum erit et duplex: mensuram palmi habebit tam in longitudine quam in latitudine.

verses.text: And thou shalt set in it four rows of stones: in the first row shall be a sardius stone, and a topaz, and an emerald:
verses.textLatin: Ponesque in eo quatuor ordines lapidum: in primo versu erit lapis sardius, et topazius, et smaragdus:

verses.text: In the second a carbuncle, a sapphire and a jasper.
verses.textLatin: in secundo carbunculus, sapphirus, et jaspis:

verses.text: In the third a ligurius, an agate, and an amethyst:
verses.textLatin: in tertio ligurius, achates, et amethystus:

verses.text: In the fourth a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl. They shall be set in gold by their rows.
verses.textLatin: in quarto chrysolithus, onychinus, et beryllus. Inclusi auro erunt per ordines suos.

verses.text: And they shall have the names of the children of Israel: with twelve names shall they be engraved, each stone with the name of one according to the twelve tribes.
verses.textLatin: Habebuntque nomina filiorum Israël: duodecim nominibus cælabuntur, singuli lapides nominibus singulorum per duodecim tribus.

verses.text: And thou shalt make on the rational chains linked one to another of the purest gold:
verses.textLatin: Facies in rationali catenas sibi invicem cohærentes ex auro purissimo,

verses.text: And two rings of gold, which thou shalt put in the two ends at the top of the rational.
verses.textLatin: et duos annulos aureos, quos pones in utraque rationalis summitate:

verses.text: And the golden chains thou shalt join to the rings, that are in the ends thereof:
verses.textLatin: catenasque aureas junges annulis, qui sunt in marginibus ejus,

verses.text: And the ends of the chains themselves thou shalt join together with two hooks on both sides of the ephod, which is towards the rational.
verses.textLatin: et ipsarum catenarum extrema duobus copulabis uncinis in utroque latere superhumeralis quod rationale respicit.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also two rings of gold which thou shalt put in the top parts of the rational, in the borders that are over against the ephod, and look towards the back parts thereof.
verses.textLatin: Facies et duos annulos aureos, quos pones in summitatibus rationalis, in oris, quæ e regione sunt superhumeralis, et posteriora ejus aspiciunt.

verses.text: Moreover also other two rings of gold, which are to be set on each side of the ephod beneath, that looketh towards the nether joining, that the rational may be fitted with the ephod,
verses.textLatin: Necnon et alios duos annulos aureos, qui ponendi sunt in utroque latere superhumeralis deorsum, quod respicit contra faciem juncturæ inferioris, ut aptari possit cum superhumerali,

verses.text: And may be fastened by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a violet fillet, that the joining artificially wrought may continue, and the rational and the ephod may not be loosed one from the other.
verses.textLatin: et stringatur rationale annulis suis cum annulis superhumeralis vitta hyacinthina, ut maneat junctura fabrefacta, et a se invicem rationale et superhumerale nequeant separari.

verses.text: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the rational of judgment upon his breast, when he shall enter into the sanctuary, a memorial before the Lord for ever.
verses.textLatin: Portabitque Aaron nomina filiorum Israël in rationali judicii super pectus suum, quando ingredietur Sanctuarium, memoriale coram Domino in æternum.

verses.text: And thou shalt put in the rational of judgment doctrine and truth, which shall be on Aaron’s breast, when he shall go in before the Lord: and he shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel on his breast, in the sight of the Lord always.
verses.textLatin: Pones autem in rationali judicii Doctrinam et Veritatem, quæ erunt in pectore Aaron, quando ingredietur coram Domino: et gestabit judicium filiorum Israël in pectore suo, in conspectu Domini semper.

verses.text: And thou shalt make the tunick of the ephod all of violet,
verses.textLatin: Facies et tunicam superhumeralis totam hyacinthinam,

verses.text: In the midst whereof above shall be a hole for the head, and a border round about it woven, as is wont to be made in the outmost parts of garments, that it may not easily be broken.
verses.textLatin: in cujus medio supra erit capitium, et ora per gyrum ejus textilis, sicut fieri solet in extremis vestium partibus, ne facile rumpatur.

verses.text: And beneath at the feet of the same tunick round about, thou shalt make as it were pomegranates, of violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, with little bells set between:
verses.textLatin: Deorsum vero, ad pedes ejusdem tunicæ, per circuitum, quasi mala punica facies, ex hyacintho, et purpura, et cocco bis tincto, mistis in medio tintinnabulis,

verses.text: So that there shall be a golden bell and a pomegranate, and again another golden bell and a pomegranate.
verses.textLatin: ita ut tintinnabulum sit aureum et malum punicum: rursumque tintinnabulum aliud aureum et malum punicum.

verses.text: And Aaron shall be vested with it in the office of his ministry, that the sound may be heard, when he goeth in and cometh out of the sanctuary, in the sight of the Lord, and that he may not die.
verses.textLatin: Et vestietur ea Aaron in officio ministerii, ut audiatur sonitus quando ingreditur et egreditur sanctuarium in conspectu Domini, et non moriatur.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a plate of the purest gold: wherein thou shalt grave with engraver’s work, Holy to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Facies et laminam de auro purissimo, in qua sculpes opere cælatoris, Sanctum Domino.

verses.text: And thou shalt tie it with a violet fillet, and it shall be upon the mitre,
verses.textLatin: Ligabisque eam vitta hyacinthina, et erit super tiaram,

verses.text: Hanging over the forehead of the high priest. And Aaron shall bear the iniquities of those things, which the children of Israel have offered and sanctified, in all their gifts and offerings. And the plate shall be always on his forehead, that the Lord may be well pleased with them.
verses.textLatin: imminens fronti pontificis. Portabitque Aaron iniquitates eorum, quæ obtulerunt et sanctificaverunt filii Israël, in cunctis muneribus et donariis suis. Erit autem lamina semper in fronte ejus, ut placatus sit eis Dominus.

verses.text: And thou shalt gird the tunick with fine linen, and thou shalt make a fine linen mitre, and a girdle of embroidered work.
verses.textLatin: Stringesque tunicam bysso, et tiaram byssinam facies, et balteum opere plumarii.

verses.text: Moreover for the sons of Aaron thou shalt prepare linen tunicks, and girdles and mitres for glory and beauty:
verses.textLatin: Porro filiis Aaron tunicas lineas parabis et balteos ac tiaras in gloriam et decorem:

verses.text: And with all these things thou shalt vest Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him. And thou shalt consecrate the hands of them all, and shalt sanctify them, that they may do the office of priesthood unto me.
verses.textLatin: vestiesque his omnibus Aaron fratrem tuum et filios ejus cum eo. Et cunctorum consecrabis manus, sanctificabisque illos, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.

verses.text: Thou shalt make also linen breeches, to cover the flesh of their nakedness from the reins to the thighs:
verses.textLatin: Facies et feminalia linea, ut operiant carnem turpitudinis suæ, a renibus usque ad femora:

verses.text: And Aaron and his sons shall use them when they shall go in to the tabernacle of the testimony, or when they approach to the altar to minister in the sanctuary, lest being guilty of iniquity they die. It shall be a law for ever to Aaron, and to his seed after him.
verses.textLatin: et utentur eis Aaron et filii ejus quando ingredientur tabernaculum testimonii, vel quando appropinquant ad altare ut ministrent in sanctuario, ne iniquitatis rei moriantur. Legitimum sempiternum erit Aaron, et semini ejus post eum.

verses.text: And  thou shalt also do this, that they may be consecrated to me in priesthood. Take a calf from the herd, and two rams without blemish,
verses.textLatin: Sed et hoc facies, ut mihi in sacerdotio consecrentur. Tolle vitulum de armento, et arietes duos immaculatos,

verses.text: And unleavened bread, and a cake without leaven, tempered with oil, wafers also unleavened anointed with oil: thou shalt make them all of wheaten flour.
verses.textLatin: panesque azymos, et crustulam absque fermento, quæ conspersa sit oleo, lagana quoque azyma oleo lita: de simila triticea cuncta facies.

verses.text: And thou shalt put them in a basket and offer them: and the calf and the two rams.
verses.textLatin: Et posita in canistro offeres: vitulum autem et duos arietes.

verses.text: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony. And when thou hast washed the father and his sons with water,
verses.textLatin: Et Aaron ac filios ejus applicabis ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii. Cumque laveris patrem cum filiis suis aqua,

verses.text: Thou shalt clothe Aaron with his vestments, that is, with the linen garment and the tunick, and the ephod and the rational, which thou shalt gird with the girdle.
verses.textLatin: indues Aaron vestimentis suis, id est, linea et tunica, et superhumerali et rationali, quod constringes balteo.

verses.text: And thou shalt put the mitre upon his head, and the holy plate upon the mitre,
verses.textLatin: Et pones tiaram in capite ejus, et laminam sanctam super tiaram,

verses.text: And thou shalt pour the oil of unction upon his head: and by this rite shall he be consecrated.
verses.textLatin: et oleum unctionis fundes super caput ejus: atque hoc ritu consecrabitur.

verses.text: Thou shalt bring his sons also and shalt put on them the linen tunicks, and gird them with a girdle:
verses.textLatin: Filios quoque illius applicabis, et indues tunicis lineis, cingesque balteo,

verses.text: To wit, Aaron and his children, and thou shalt put mitres upon them: and they shall be priests to me by a perpetual ordinance. After thou shalt have consecrated their hands,
verses.textLatin: Aaron scilicet et liberos ejus, et impones eis mitras: eruntque sacerdotes mihi religione perpetua. Postquam initiaveris manus eorum,

verses.text: Thou shalt present also the calf before the tabernacle of the testimony. And Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon his head,
verses.textLatin: applicabis et vitulum coram tabernaculo testimonii. Imponentque Aaron et filii ejus manus super caput illius,

verses.text: And thou shalt kill him in the sight of the Lord, beside the door of the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.textLatin: et mactabis eum in conspectu Domini, juxta ostium tabernaculi testimonii.

verses.text: And taking some of the blood of the calf, thou shalt put it upon the horns of the altar with thy finger, and the rest of the blood thou shalt pour at the bottom thereof.
verses.textLatin: Sumptumque de sanguine vituli, pones super cornua altaris digito tuo, reliquum autem sanguinem fundes juxta basim ejus.

verses.text: Thou shalt take also all the fat that covereth the entrails, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and shalt offer a burnt offering upon the altar:
verses.textLatin: Sumes et adipem totum qui operit intestina, et reticulum jecoris, ac duos renes, et adipem qui super eos est, et offeres incensum super altare:

verses.text: But the flesh of the calf and the hide and the dung, thou shalt burn abroad, without the camp, because it is for sin.
verses.textLatin: carnes vero vituli et corium et fimum combures foris extra castra, eo quod pro peccato sit.

verses.text: Thou shalt take also one ram upon the head whereof Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands.
verses.textLatin: Unum quoque arietem sumes, super cujus caput ponent Aaron et filii ejus manus.

verses.text: And when thou hast killed him, thou shalt take of the blood thereof, and pour round about the altar:
verses.textLatin: Quem cum mactaveris, tolles de sanguine ejus, et fundes circa altare.

verses.text: And thou shalt cut the ram in pieces, and having washed his entrails and feet, thou shalt put them upon the flesh that is cut in pieces, and upon his head.
verses.textLatin: Ipsum autem arietem secabis in frustra: lotaque intestina ejus ac pedes, pones super concisas carnes, et super caput illius.

verses.text: And thou shalt offer the whole ram for a burnt offering upon the altar: It is an oblation to the Lord, a most sweet savour of the victim of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et offeres totum arietem in incensum super altare: oblatio est Domino, odor suavissimus victimæ Domini.

verses.text: Thou shalt take also the other ram, upon whose head Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands.
verses.textLatin: Tolles quoque arietem alterum, super cujus caput Aaron et filii ejus ponent manus.

verses.text: And when thou hast sacrificed him, thou shalt take of his blood, and put upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, and upon the thumbs and great toes of their right hand and foot, and thou shalt pour the blood upon the altar round about.
verses.textLatin: Quem cum immolaveris, sumes de sanguine ejus, et pones super extremum auriculæ dextræ Aaron et filiorum ejus, et super pollices manus eorum ac pedis dextri, fundesque sanguinem super altare per circuitum.

verses.text: And when thou hast taken of the blood, that is upon the altar, and of the oil of unction, thou shalt sprinkle Aaron and his vesture, his sons and their vestments. And after they and their vestments are consecrated,
verses.textLatin: Cumque tuleris de sanguine qui est super altare, et de oleo unctionis, asperges Aaron et vestes ejus, filios et vestimenta eorum. Consecratisque ipsis et vestibus,

verses.text: Thou shalt take the fat of the ram, and the rump, and the fat that covereth the lungs, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder, because it is the ram of consecration.
verses.textLatin: tolles adipem de ariete, et caudam et arvinam, quæ operit vitalia, ac reticulum jecoris, et duos renes, atque adipem, qui super eos est, armumque dextrum, eo quod sit aries consecrationis:

verses.text: And one roll of bread, a cake tempered with oil, a wafer out of the basket of unleavened bread, which is set in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: tortamque panis unius, crustulam conspersam oleo, laganum de canistro azymorum, quod positum est in conspectu Domini:

verses.text: And thou shalt put all upon the hands of Aaron and of his sons, and shalt sanctify them elevating before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ponesque omnia super manus Aaron et filiorum ejus, et sanctificabis eos elevans coram Domino.

verses.text: And thou shalt take all from their hands, and shalt burn them upon the altar for a holocaust, a most sweet savour in the sight of the Lord, because it is his oblation.
verses.textLatin: Suscipiesque universa de manibus eorum: et incendes super altare in holocaustum, odorem suavissimum in conspectu Domini, quia oblatio ejus est.

verses.text: Thou shalt take also the breast of the ram, wherewith Aaron was consecrated, and elevating it thou shalt sanctify it before the Lord, and it shall fall to thy share.
verses.textLatin: Sumes quoque pectusculum de ariete, quo initiatus est Aaron, sanctificabisque illud elevatum coram Domino, et cedet in partem tuam.

verses.text: And thou shalt sanctify both the consecrated breast, and the shoulder that thou didst separate of the ram,
verses.textLatin: Sanctificabisque et pectusculum consecratum, et armum quem de ariete separasti,

verses.text: Wherewith Aaron was consecrated and his sons, and they shall fall to Aaron’s share and his sons’ by a perpetual right from the children of Israel: because they are the choicest and the beginnings of their peace victims which they offer to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: quo initiatus est Aaron et filii ejus, cedentque in partem Aaron et filiorum ejus jure perpetuo a filiis Israël: quia primitiva sunt et initia de victimis eorum pacificis quæ offerunt Domino.

verses.text: And the holy vesture, which Aaron shall use, his sons shall have after him, that they may be anointed, and their hands consecrated in it.
verses.textLatin: Vestem autem sanctam, qua utetur Aaron, habebunt filii ejus post eum, ut ungantur in ea, et consecrantur manus eorum.

verses.text: He of his sons that shall be appointed high priest in his stead, and that shall enter into the tabernacle of the testimony to minister in the sanctuary, shall wear it seven days.
verses.textLatin: Septem diebus utetur illa qui pontifex pro eo fuerit constitutus de filiis ejus, et qui ingredietur tabernaculum testimonii ut ministret in sanctuario.

verses.text: And thou shalt take the ram of the consecration, and shalt boil the flesh thereof in the holy place:
verses.textLatin: Arietem autem consecrationis tolles, et coques carnes ejus in loco sancto:

verses.text: And Aaron and his sons shall eat it. The loaves also, that are in the basket, they shall eat in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony,
verses.textLatin: quibus vescetur Aaron et filii ejus. Panes quoque, qui sunt in canistro, in vestibulo tabernaculi testimonii comedent,

verses.text: That it may be an atoning sacrifice, and the hands of the offerers may be sanctified. A stranger shall not eat of them, because they are holy.
verses.textLatin: ut sit placabile sacrificium, et sanctificentur offerentium manus. Alienigena non vescetur ex eis, quia sancti sunt.

verses.text: And if there remain of the consecrated flesh, or of the bread till the morning, thou shalt burn the remainder with fire: they shall not be eaten, because they are sanctified.
verses.textLatin: Quod si remanserit de carnibus consecratis, sive de panibus usque mane, combures reliquias igni: non comedentur, quia sanctificata sunt.

verses.text: All that I have commanded thee, thou shalt do unto Aaron and his sons. Seven days shalt thou consecrate their hands:
verses.textLatin: Omnia, quæ præcepi tibi, facies super Aaron et filiis ejus. Septem diebus consecrabis manus eorum:

verses.text: And thou shalt offer a calf for sin every day for expiation. And thou shalt cleanse the altar when thou hast offered the victim of expiation, and shalt anoint it to sanctify it.
verses.textLatin: et vitulum pro peccato offeres per singulos dies ad expiandum. Mundabisque altare cum immolaveris expiationis hostiam, et unges illud in sanctificationem.

verses.text: Seven days shalt thou expiate the altar and sanctify it, and it shall be most holy. Every one that shall touch it shall be holy.
verses.textLatin: Septem diebus expiabis altare, et sanctificabis, et erit Sanctum sanctorum: omnis, qui tetigerit illud, sanctificabitur.

verses.text: This is what thou shalt sacrifice upon the altar: Two lambs of a year old every day continually.
verses.textLatin: Hoc est quod facies in altari: agnos anniculos duos per singulos dies jugiter,

verses.text: One lamb in the morning and another in the evening.
verses.textLatin: unum agnum mane, et alterum vespere,

verses.text: With one lamb a tenth part of flour tempered with beaten oil, of the fourth part of a hin, and wine for libation of the same measure.
verses.textLatin: decimam partem similæ conspersæ oleo tuso, quod habeat mensuram quartam partem hin, et vinum ad libandum ejusdem mensuræ in agno uno.
