verses.text: And the other lamb thou shalt offer in the evening, according to the rite of the morning oblation, and according to what we have said, for a savour of sweetness:
verses.textLatin: Alterum vero agnum offeres ad vesperam juxta ritum matutinæ oblationis, et juxta ea quæ diximus, in odorem suavitatis:

verses.text: It is a sacrifice to the Lord, by perpetual oblation unto your generations, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony before the Lord, where I will appoint to speak unto thee.
verses.textLatin: sacrificium est Domino, oblatione perpetua in generationes vestras, ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii coram Domino, ubi constituam ut loquar ad te.

verses.text: And there will I command the children of Israel, and the altar shall be sanctified by my glory.
verses.textLatin: Ibique præcipiam filiis Israël, et sanctificabitur altare in gloria mea.

verses.text: I will sanctify also the tabernacle of the testimony with the altar, and Aaron with his sons, to do the office of priesthood unto me.
verses.textLatin: Sanctificabo et tabernaculum testimonii cum altari, et Aaron cum filiis suis, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.

verses.text: And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, and will be their God:
verses.textLatin: Et habitabo in medio filiorum Israël, eroque eis Deus,

verses.text: And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who have brought them out of the land of Egypt, that I might abide among them, I the Lord their God.
verses.textLatin: et scient quia ego Dominus Deus eorum, qui eduxi eos de terra Ægypti, ut manerem inter illos, ego Dominus Deus ipsorum.

verses.text: Thou  shalt make also an altar to burn incense, of setim wood.
verses.textLatin: Facies quoque altare ad adolendum thymiama, de lignis setim,

verses.text: It shall be a cubit in length, and another in breadth, that is, foursquare, and two in height. Horns shall go out of the same.
verses.textLatin: habens cubitum longitudinis, et alterum latitudinis, id est, quadrangulum, et duos cubitos in altitudine. Cornua ex ipso procedent.

verses.text: And thou shalt overlay it with the purest gold, as well as the grate thereof, as the walls round about and the horns. And thou shalt make to it a crown of gold round about,
verses.textLatin: Vestiesque illud auro purissimo, tam craticulam ejus, quam parietes per circuitum, et cornua. Faciesque ei coronam aureolam per gyrum,

verses.text: And two golden rings under the crown on either side, that the bars may be put into them, and the altar be carried.
verses.textLatin: et duos annulos aureos sub corona per singula latera, ut mittantur in eos vectes, et altare portetur.

verses.text: And thou shalt make the bars also of setim wood, and shalt overlay them with gold.
verses.textLatin: Ipsos quoque vectes facies de lignis setim, et inaurabis.

verses.text: And thou shalt set the altar over against the veil, that hangeth before the ark of the testimony before the propitiatory wherewith the testimony is covered, where I will speak to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ponesque altare contra velum, quod ante arcum pendet testimonii coram propitiatorio quo tegitur testimonium, ubi loquar tibi.

verses.text: And Aaron shall burn sweet smelling incense upon it in the morning. When he shall dress the lamps, he shall burn it:
verses.textLatin: Et adolebit incensum super eo Aaron, suave fragrans, mane. Quando componet lucernas, incendet illud:

verses.text: And when he shall place them in the evening, he shall burn an everlasting incense before the Lord throughout your generations.
verses.textLatin: et quando collocabit eas ad vesperum, uret thymiama sempiternum coram Domino in generationes vestras.

verses.text: You shall not offer upon it incense of another composition nor oblation, and victim, neither shall you offer libations.
verses.textLatin: Non offeretis super eo thymiama compositionis alterius, nec oblationem, et victimam, nec libabitis libamina.

verses.text: And Aaron shall pray upon the horns thereof once a year, with the blood of that which was offered for sin, and shall make atonement upon it in your generations. It shall be most holy to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et deprecabitur Aaron super cornua ejus semel per annum, in sanguine quod oblatum est pro peccato, et placabit super eo in generationibus vestris. Sanctum sanctorum erit Domino.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: When thou shalt take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, every one of them shall give a price for their souls to the Lord, and there shall be no scourge among them, when they shall be reckoned.
verses.textLatin: Quando tuleris summam filiorum Israël juxta numerum, dabunt singuli pretium pro animabus suis Domino, et non erit plaga in eis, cum fuerint recensiti.

verses.text: And this shall every one give that passeth at the naming, half a sicle according to the standard of the temple. A sicle hath twenty obols. Half a sicle shall be offered to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Hoc autem dabit omnis qui transit ad nomen, dimidium sicli juxta mensuram templi (siclus viginti obolos habet); media pars sicli offeretur Domino.

verses.text: He that is counted in the number from twenty years and upwards, shall give the price.
verses.textLatin: Qui habetur in numero, a viginti annis et supra, dabit pretium.

verses.text: The rich man shall not add to half a sicle, and the poor man shall diminish nothing.
verses.textLatin: Dives non addet ad medium sicli, et pauper nihil minuet.

verses.text: And the money received which was contributed by the children of Israel, thou shalt deliver unto the uses of the tabernacle of the testimony, that it may be a memorial of them before the Lord, and he may be merciful to their souls.
verses.textLatin: Susceptamque pecuniam, quæ collata est a filiis Israël, trades in usus tabernaculi testimonii, ut sit monimentum eorum coram Domino, et propitietur animabus eorum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Thou shalt make also a brazen laver with its foot, to wash in: and thou shalt set it between the tabernacle of the testimony and the altar. And water being put into it,
verses.textLatin: Facies et labrum æneum cum basi sua ad lavandum: ponesque illud inter tabernaculum testimonii et altare. Et missa aqua,

verses.text: Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet in it:
verses.textLatin: lavabunt in ea Aaron et filii ejus manus suas ac pedes,

verses.text: When they are going into the tabernacle of the testimony, and when they are to come to the altar, to offer on it incense to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: quando ingressuri sunt tabernaculum testimonii, et quando accessuri sunt ad altare, ut offerant in eo thymiama Domino,

verses.text: Lest perhaps they die. It shall be an everlasting law to him, and to his seed by successions.
verses.textLatin: ne forte moriantur; legitimum sempiternum erit ipsi, et semini ejus per successiones.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses,
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen,

verses.text: Saying: Take spices, of principal and chosen myrrh five hundred sicles, and of cinnamon half so much, that is, two hundred and fifty sicles, of calamus in like manner two hundred and fifty.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Sume tibi aromata, primæ myrrhæ et electæ quingentos siclos, et cinnamomi medium, id est, ducentos quinquaginta siclos, calami similiter ducentos quinquaginta,

verses.text: And of cassia five hundred sicles by the weight of the sanctuary, of oil of olives the measure hin:
verses.textLatin: casiæ autem quingentos siclos, in pondere sanctuarii, olei de olivetis mensuram hin:

verses.text: And thou shalt make the holy oil of unction, an ointment compounded after the art of the perfumer,
verses.textLatin: faciesque unctionis oleum sanctum, unguentum compositum opere unguentarii,

verses.text: And therewith thou shalt anoint the tabernacle of the testimony, and the ark of the testament,
verses.textLatin: et unges ex eo tabernaculum testimonii, et arcam testamenti,

verses.text: And the table with the vessels thereof, the candlestick and furniture thereof, the altars of incense,
verses.textLatin: mensamque cum vasis suis, et candelabrum, et utensilia ejus, altaria thymiamatis,

verses.text: And of holocaust, and all the furniture that belongeth to the service of them.
verses.textLatin: et holocausti, et universam supellectilem quæ ad cultum eorum pertinet.

verses.text: And thou shalt sanctify all, and they shall be most holy: he that shall touch them shall be sanctified.
verses.textLatin: Sanctificabisque omnia, et erunt Sancta sanctorum; qui tetigerit ea, sanctificabitur.

verses.text: Thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons, and shalt sanctify them, that they may do the office of priesthood unto me.
verses.textLatin: Aaron et filios ejus unges, sanctificabisque eos, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to the children of Israel: This oil of unction shall be holy unto me throughout your generations.
verses.textLatin: Filiis quoque Israël dices: Hoc oleum unctionis sanctum erit mihi in generationes vestras.

verses.text: The flesh of man shall not be anointed therewith, and you shall make none other of the same composition, because it is sanctified, and shall be holy unto you.
verses.textLatin: Caro hominis non ungetur ex eo, et juxta compositionem ejus non facietis aliud, quia sanctificatum est, et sanctum erit vobis.

verses.text: What man soever shall compound such, and shall give thereof to a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people.
verses.textLatin: Homo quicumque tale composuerit, et dederit ex eo alieno, exterminabitur de populo suo.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Take unto thee spices, stacte, and onycha, galbanum of sweet savour, and the clearest frankincense, all shall be of equal weight.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Sume tibi aromata, stacten et onycha, galbanum boni odoris, et thus lucidissimum; æqualis ponderis erunt omnia:

verses.text: And thou shalt make incense compounded by the work of the perfumer, well tempered together, and pure, and most worthy of sanctification.
verses.textLatin: faciesque thymiama compositum opere unguentarii, mistum diligenter, et purum, et sanctificatione dignissimum.

verses.text: And when thou hast beaten all into very small powder, thou shalt set of it before the tabernacle of the testimony, in the place where I will appear to thee. Most holy shall this incense be unto you.
verses.textLatin: Cumque in tenuissimum pulverem universa contuderis, pones ex eo coram tabernaculo testimonii, in quo loco apparebo tibi. Sanctum sanctorum erit vobis thymiama.

verses.text: You shall not make such a composition for your own uses, because it is holy to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Talem compositionem non facietis in usus vestros, quia sanctum est Domino.

verses.text: What man soever shall make the like, to enjoy the smell thereof, he shall perish out of his people.
verses.textLatin: Homo quicumque fecerit simile, ut odore illius perfruatur, peribit de populis suis.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Behold, I have called by name Beseleel the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Juda,
verses.textLatin: Ecce, vocavi ex nomine Beseleel filium Uri filii Hur de tribu Juda,

verses.text: And I have filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom and understanding, and knowledge in all manner of work.
verses.textLatin: et implevi spiritu Dei, sapientia, et intelligentia et scientia in omni opere,

verses.text: To devise whatsoever may be artificially made of gold, and silver, and brass,
verses.textLatin: ad excogitandum quidquid fabrefieri potest ex auro, et argento, et ære,

verses.text: Of marble, and precious stones, and variety of wood.
verses.textLatin: marmore, et gemmis, et diversitate lignorum.

verses.text: And I have given him for his companion Ooliab the son of Achisamech of the tribe of Dan. And I have put wisdom in the heart of every skilful man, that they may make all things which I have commanded thee,
verses.textLatin: Dedique ei socium Ooliab filium Achisamech de tribu Dan. Et in corde omnis eruditi posui sapientiam: ut faciant cuncta quæ præcepi tibi,

verses.text: The tabernacle of the covenant, and the ark of the testimony, and the propitiatory that is over it, and all the vessels of the tabernacle,
verses.textLatin: tabernaculum fœderis, et arcam testimonii, et propitiatorium, quod super eam est, et cuncta vasa tabernaculi,

verses.text: And the table and the vessels thereof, the most pure candlestick with the vessels thereof, and the altars of incense,
verses.textLatin: mensamque et vasa ejus, candelabrum purissimum cum vasis suis, et altaris thymiamatis,

verses.text: And of holocaust, and all their vessels, the laver with its foot,
verses.textLatin: et holocausti, et omnia vasa eorum, labrum cum basi sua,

verses.text: The holy vestments in the ministry for Aaron the priest, and for his sons, that they may execute their office about the sacred things:
verses.textLatin: vestes sanctas in ministerio Aaron sacerdoti, et filiis ejus, ut fungantur officio suo in sacris:

verses.text: The oil of unction, and the incense of spices in the sanctuary, all things which I have commanded thee, shall they make.
verses.textLatin: oleum unctionis, et thymiama aromatum in sanctuario, omnia quæ præcepi tibi, facient.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: See that thou keep my sabbath: because it is a sign between me and you in your generations: that you may know that I am the Lord, who sanctify you.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Videte ut sabbatum meum custodiatis: quia signum est inter me et vos in generationibus vestris: ut sciatis quia ego Dominus, qui sanctifico vos.

verses.text: Keep you my sabbath: for it is holy unto you: he that shall profane it, shall be put to death: he that shall do any work in it, his soul shall perish out of the midst of his people.
verses.textLatin: Custodite sabbatum meum, sanctum est enim vobis: qui polluerit illud, morte morietur; qui fecerit in eo opus, peribit anima illius de medio populi sui.

verses.text: Six days shall you do work: in the seventh day is the sabbath, the rest holy to the Lord. Every one that shall do any work on this day, shall die.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus facietis opus: in die septimo sabbatum est, requies sancta Domino; omnis qui fecerit opus in hac die, morietur.

verses.text: Let the children of Israel keep the sabbath, and celebrate it in their generations. It is an everlasting covenant
verses.textLatin: Custodiant filii Israël sabbatum, et celebrent illud in generationibus suis. Pactum est sempiternum

verses.text: Between me and the children of Israel, and a perpetual sign. For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and in the seventh he ceased from work.
verses.textLatin: inter me et filios Israël, signumque perpetuum; sex enim diebus fecit Dominus cælum et terram, et in septimo ab opere cessavit.

verses.text: And the Lord, when he had ended these words in mount Sinai, gave to Moses two stone tables of testimony, written with the finger of God.
verses.textLatin: Deditque Dominus Moysi, completis hujuscemodi sermonibus in monte Sinai, duas tabulas testimonii lapideas, scriptas digito Dei.

verses.text: And  the people seeing that Moses delayed to come down from the mount, gathering together against Aaron, said: Arise, make us gods, that may go before us: for as to this Moses, the man that brought us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what has befallen him.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem populus quod moram faceret descendendi de monte Moyses, congregatus adversus Aaron, dixit: Surge, fac nobis deos, qui nos præcedant: Moysi enim huic viro, qui nos eduxit de terra Ægypti, ignoramus quid acciderit.

verses.text: And Aaron said to them: Take the golden earrings from the ears of your wives, and your sons and daughters, and bring them to me.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad eos Aaron: Tollite inaures aureas de uxorum, filiorumque et filiarum vestrarum auribus, et afferte ad me.

verses.text: And the people did what he had commanded, bringing the earrings to Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque populus quæ jusserat, deferens inaures ad Aaron.

verses.text: And when he had received them, he fashioned them by founders’ work, and made of them a molten calf. And they said: These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Quas cum ille accepisset, formavit opere fusorio, et fecit ex eis vitulum conflatilem: dixeruntque: Hi sunt dii tui Israël, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And when Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it, and made proclamation by a crier’s voice, saying: To morrow is the solemnity of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidisset Aaron, ædificavit altare coram eo, et præconis voce clamavit dicens: Cras solemnitas Domini est.

verses.text: And rising in the morning, they offered holocausts, and peace victims, and the people sat down to eat, and drink, and they rose up to play.
verses.textLatin: Surgentesque mane, obtulerunt holocausta, et hostias pacificas, et sedit populus manducare, et bibere, et surrexerunt ludere.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Go, get thee down: thy people, which thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, hath sinned.
verses.textLatin: Locutus est autem Dominus ad Moysen, dicens: Vade, descende: peccavit populus tuus, quem eduxisti de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: They have quickly strayed from the way which thou didst shew them: and they have made to themselves a molten calf, and have adored it, and sacrificing victims to it, have said: These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Recesserunt cito de via, quam ostendisti eis: feceruntque sibi vitulum conflatilem, et adoraverunt, atque immolantes ei hostias, dixerunt: Isti sunt dii tui Israël, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And again the Lord said to Moses: See that this people is stiffnecked:
verses.textLatin: Rursumque ait Dominus ad Moysen: Cerno quod populus iste duræ cervicis sit:

verses.text: Let me alone, that my wrath may be kindled against them, and that I may destroy them, and I will make of thee a great nation.
verses.textLatin: dimitte me, ut irascatur furor meus contra eos, et deleam eos, faciamque te in gentem magnam.

verses.text: But Moses besought the Lord his God, saying: Why, O Lord, is thy indignation enkindled against thy people, whom thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, with great power, and with a mighty hand?
verses.textLatin: Moyses autem orabat Dominum Deum suum, dicens: Cur, Domine, irascitur furor tuus contra populum tuum, quem eduxisti de terra Ægypti, in fortitudine magna, et in manu robusta?

verses.text: Let not the Egyptians say, I beseech thee: He craftily brought them out, that he might kill them in the mountains, and destroy them from the earth: let thy anger cease, and be appeased upon the wickedness of thy people.
verses.textLatin: Ne quæso dicant Ægyptii: Callide eduxit eos, ut interficeret in montibus, et deleret e terra: quiescat ira tua, et esto placabilis super nequitia populi tui.

verses.text: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou sworest by thy own self, saying: I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven: and this whole land that I have spoken of, I will give to your seed, and you shall possess it for ever.
verses.textLatin: Recordare Abraham, Isaac, et Israël servorum tuorum, quibus jurasti per temetipsum, dicens: Multiplicabo semen vestrum sicut stellas cæli; et universam terram hanc, de qua locutus sum, dabo semini vestro, et possidebitis eam semper.

verses.text: And the Lord was appeased from doing the evil which he had spoken against his people.
verses.textLatin: Placatusque est Dominus ne faceret malum quod locutus fuerat adversus populum suum.

verses.text: And Moses returned from the mount, carrying the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both sides,
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Moyses de monte, portans duas tabulas testimonii in manu sua, scriptas ex utraque parte,

verses.text: And made by the work of God: the writing also of God was graven in the tables.
verses.textLatin: et factas opere Dei: scriptura quoque Dei erat sculpta in tabulis.

verses.text: And Josue hearing the noise of the people shouting, said to Moses: The noise of battle is heard in the camp.
verses.textLatin: Audiens autem Josue tumultum populi vociferantis, dixit ad Moysen: Ululatus pugnæ auditur in castris.

verses.text: But he answered: It is not the cry of men encouraging to fight, nor the shout of men compelling to flee: but I hear the voice of singers.
verses.textLatin: Qui respondit: Non est clamor adhortantium ad pugnam, neque vociferatio compellentium ad fugam: sed vocem cantantium ego audio.

verses.text: And when he came nigh to the camp, he saw the calf, and the dances: and being very angry, he threw the tables out of his hand, and broke them at the foot of the mount:
verses.textLatin: Cumque appropinquasset ad castra, vidit vitulum, et choros: iratusque valde, projecit de manu tabulas, et confregit eas ad radicem montis:

verses.text: And laying hold of the calf which they had made, he burnt it, and beat it to powder, which he strowed into water, and gave thereof to the children of Israel to drink.
verses.textLatin: arripiensque vitulum quem fecerant, combussit, et contrivit usque ad pulverem, quem sparsit in aquam, et dedit ex eo potum filiis Israël.

verses.text: And he said to Aaron: What has this people done to thee, that thou shouldst bring upon them a most heinous sin?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Aaron: Quid tibi fecit hic populus, ut induceres super eum peccatum maximum?

verses.text: And he answered him: Let not my lord be offended: for thou knowest this people, that they are prone to evil.
verses.textLatin: Cui ille respondit: Ne indignetur dominus meus: tu enim nosti populum istum, quod pronus sit ad malum:

verses.text: They said to me: Make us gods, that may go before us: for as to this Moses, who brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is befallen him.
verses.textLatin: dixerunt mihi: Fac nobis deos, qui nos præcedant: huic enim Moysi, qui nos eduxit de terra Ægypti, nescimus quid acciderit.

verses.text: And I said to them: Which of you hath any gold? and they took and brought it to me: and I cast it into the fire, and this calf came out.
verses.textLatin: Quibus ego dixi: Quis vestrum habet aurum? Tulerunt, et dederunt mihi: et projeci illud in ignem, egressusque est hic vitulus.

verses.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked, (for Aaron had stripped them by occasion of the shame of the filth, and had set them naked among their enemies,)
verses.textLatin: Videns ergo Moyses populum quod esset nudatus (spoliaverat enim eum Aaron propter ignominiam sordis, et inter hostes nudum constituerat),

verses.text: Then standing in the gate of the camp, he said: If any man be on the Lord’s side let him join with me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him:
verses.textLatin: et stans in porta castrorum, ait: Si quis est Domini, jungatur mihi. Congregatique sunt ad eum omnes filii Levi:

verses.text: And he said to them: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: Put every man his sword upon his thigh: go, and return from gate to gate through the midst of the camp, and let every man kill his brother, and friend, and neighbour.
verses.textLatin: quibus ait: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus Israël: Ponat vir gladium super femur suum: ite, et redite de porta usque ad portam per medium castrorum, et occidat unusquisque fratrem, et amicum, et proximum suum.

verses.text: And the sons of Levi did according to the words of Moses, and there were slain that day about three and twenty thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque filii Levi juxta sermonem Moysi, cecideruntque in die illa quasi viginti tria millia hominum.

verses.text: And Moses said: You have consecrated your hands this day to the Lord, every man in his son and in his brother, that a blessing may be given to you.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: Consecrastis manus vestras hodie Domino, unusquisque in filio, et in fratre suo, ut detur vobis benedictio.

verses.text: And when the next day was come, Moses spoke to the people: You have sinned a very great sin: I will go up to the Lord, if by any means I may be able to entreat him for your crime.
verses.textLatin: Facto autem altero die, locutus est Moyses ad populum: Peccastis peccatum maximum: ascendam ad Dominum, si quomodo quivero eum deprecari pro scelere vestro.

verses.text: And returning to the Lord, he said: I beseech thee: this people hath sinned a heinous sin, and they have made to themselves gods of gold: either forgive them this trespass,
verses.textLatin: Reversusque ad Dominum, ait: Obsecro, peccavit populus iste peccatum maximum, feceruntque sibi deos aureos: aut dimitte eis hanc noxam,

verses.text: Or if thou do not, strike me out of the book that thou hast written.
verses.textLatin: aut si non facis, dele me de libro tuo quem scripsisti.

verses.text: And the Lord answered him: He that hath sinned against me, him will I strike out of my book:
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Dominus: Qui peccaverit mihi, delebo eum de libro meo:

verses.text: But go thou, and lead this people whither I have told thee: my angel shall go before thee. And I in the day of revenge will visit this sin also of theirs.
verses.textLatin: tu autem vade, et duc populum istum quo locutus sum tibi: angelus meus præcedet te. Ego autem in die ultionis visitabo et hoc peccatum eorum.

verses.text: The Lord therefore struck the people for the guilt on occasion of the calf which Aaron had made.
verses.textLatin: Percussit ergo Dominus populum pro reatu vituli, quem fecerat Aaron.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Go, get thee up from this place, thou and thy people which thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, into the land concerning which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: To thy seed I will give it.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens: Vade, ascende de loco isto tu, et populus tuus quem eduxisti de terra Ægypti, in terram quam juravi Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, dicens: Semini tuo dabo eam:

verses.text: And I will send an angel before thee, that I may cast out the Chanaanite, and the Amorrhite, and the Hethite, and the Pherezite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite.
verses.textLatin: et mittam præcursorem tui angelum, ut ejiciam Chananæum, et Amorrhæum, et Hethæum, et Pherezæum, et Hevæum, et Jebusæum,

verses.text: That thou mayst enter into the land that floweth with milk and honey. For I will not go up with thee, because thou art a stiffnecked people: lest I destroy thee in the way.
verses.textLatin: et intres in terram fluentem lacte et melle. Non enim ascendam tecum, quia populus duræ cervicis es: ne forte disperdam te in via.

verses.text: And the people hearing these very bad tidings, mourned: and no man put on his ornaments according to custom.
verses.textLatin: Audiensque populus sermonem hunc pessimum, luxit: et nullus ex more indutus est cultu suo.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to the children of Israel: Thou art a stiffnecked people; once I shall come up in the midst of thee, and shall destroy thee. Now presently lay aside thy ornaments, that I may know what to do to thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Loquere filiis Israël: Populus duræ cervicis es: semel ascendam in medio tui, et delebo te. Jam nunc depone ornatum tuum, ut sciam quid faciam tibi.

verses.text: So the children of Israel laid aside their ornaments by Mount Horeb.
verses.textLatin: Deposuerunt ergo filii Israël ornatum suum a monte Horeb.

verses.text: Moses also taking the tabernacle, pitched it without the camp afar off, and called the name thereof, The tabernacle of the covenant. And all the people that had any question, went forth to the tabernacle of the covenant, without the camp.
verses.textLatin: Moyses quoque tollens tabernaculum, tetendit extra castra procul, vocavitque nomen ejus, Tabernaculum fœderis. Et omnis populus, qui habebat aliquam quæstionem, egrediebatur ad tabernaculum fœderis, extra castra.

verses.text: And when Moses went forth to the tabernacle, all the people rose up, and every one stood in the door of his pavilion, and they beheld the back of Moses, till he went into the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Cumque egrederetur Moyses ad tabernaculum, surgebat universa plebs, et stabat unusquisque in ostio papilionis sui, aspiciebantque tergum Moysi, donec ingrederetur tentorium.

verses.text: And when he was gone into the tabernacle of the covenant, the pillar of the cloud came down, and stood at the door, and he spoke with Moses.
verses.textLatin: Ingresso autem illo tabernaculum fœderis, descendebat columna nubis, et stabat ad ostium, loquebaturque cum Moyse,

verses.text: And all saw that the pillar of the cloud stood at the door of the tabernacle. And they stood, and worshipped at the doors of their tents.
verses.textLatin: cernentibus universis quod columna nubis staret ad ostium tabernaculi. Stabantque ipsi, et adorabant per fores tabernaculorum suorum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend. And when he returned into the camp, his servant Josue the son of Nun, a young man, departed not from the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Loquebatur autem Dominus ad Moysen facie ad faciem, sicut solet loqui homo ad amicum suum. Cumque ille reverteretur in castra, minister ejus Josue filius Nun, puer, non recedebat de tabernaculo.

verses.text: And Moses said to the Lord: Thou commandest me to lead forth this people: and thou dost not let me know whom thou wilt send with me, especially whereas thou hast said: I know thee by name, and thou hast found favour in my sight.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Moyses ad Dominum: Præcipis ut educam populum istum: et non indicas mihi quem missurus es mecum, præsertim cum dixeris: Novi te ex nomine, et invenisti gratiam coram me.

verses.text: If therefore I have found favour in thy sight, shew me thy face, that I may know thee, and may find grace before thy eyes: look upon thy people this nation.
verses.textLatin: Si ergo inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, ostende mihi faciem tuam, ut sciam te, et inveniam gratiam ante oculos tuos: respice populum tuum gentem hanc.

verses.text: And the Lord said: My face shall go before thee, and I will give thee rest.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus: Facies mea præcedet te, et requiem dabo tibi.

verses.text: And Moses said: If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: Si non tu ipse præcedas, ne educas nos de loco isto.

verses.text: For how shall we be able to know, I and thy people, that we have found grace in thy sight, unless thou walk with us, that we may be glorified by all people that dwell upon the earth?
verses.textLatin: In quo enim scire poterimus ego et populus tuus invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum, ut glorificemur ab omnibus populis qui habitant super terram?

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: This word also, which thou hast spoken, will I do: for thou hast found grace before me, and thee I have known by name.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Dominus ad Moysen: Et verbum istud, quod locutus es, faciam: invenisti enim gratiam coram me, et teipsum novi ex nomine.

verses.text: And he said: Shew me thy glory.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait: Ostende mihi gloriam tuam.

verses.text: He answered: I will shew thee all good, and I will proclaim in the name of the Lord before thee: and I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me.
verses.textLatin: Respondit: Ego ostendam omne bonum tibi, et vocabo in nomine Domini coram te: et miserebor cui voluero, et clemens ero in quem mihi placuerit.

verses.text: And again he said: Thou canst not see my face: for man shall not see me and live.
verses.textLatin: Rursumque ait: Non poteris videre faciem meam: non enim videbit me homo et vivet.

verses.text: And again he said: Behold there is a place with me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock.
verses.textLatin: Et iterum: Ecce, inquit, est locus apud me, et stabis supra petram.

verses.text: And when my glory shall pass, I will set thee in a hole of the rock, and protect thee with my right hand, till I pass:
verses.textLatin: Cumque transibit gloria mea, ponam te in foramine petræ, et protegam dextera mea, donec transeam:

verses.text: And I will take away my hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face thou canst not see.
verses.textLatin: tollamque manum meam, et videbis posteriora mea: faciem autem meam videre non poteris.

verses.text: And  after this he said: Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the former, and I will write upon them the words which were in the tables, which thou brokest.
verses.textLatin: Ac deinceps: Præcide, ait, tibi duas tabulas lapideas instar priorum, et scribam super eas verba, quæ habuerunt tabulæ quas fregisti.

verses.text: Be ready in the morning, that thou mayst forthwith go up into mount Sinai, and thou shalt stand with me upon the top of the mount.
verses.textLatin: Esto paratus mane, ut ascendas statim in montem Sinai, stabisque mecum super verticem montis.

verses.text: Let no man go up with thee: and let not any man be seen throughout all the mount: neither let the oxen nor the sheep feed over against it.
verses.textLatin: Nullus ascendat tecum, nec videatur quispiam per totum montem: boves quoque et oves non pascantur e contra.

verses.text: Then he cut out two tables of stone, such as had been before: and rising very early he went up into the mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, carrying with him the tables.
verses.textLatin: Excidit ergo duas tabulas lapideas, quales antea fuerant: et de nocte consurgens ascendit in montem Sinai, sicut præceperat ei Dominus, portans secum tabulas.

verses.text: And when the Lord was come down in a cloud, Moses stood with him, calling upon the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Cumque descendisset Dominus per nubem, stetit Moyses cum eo, invocans nomen Domini.

verses.text: And when he passed before him, he said: O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true,
verses.textLatin: Quo transeunte coram eo, ait: Dominator Domine Deus, misericors et clemens, patiens et multæ miserationis, ac verax,

verses.text: Who keepest mercy unto thousands: who takest away iniquity, and wickedness, and sin, and no man of himself is innocent before thee. Who renderest the iniquity of the fathers to the children, and to the grandchildren, unto the third and fourth generation.
verses.textLatin: qui custodis misericordiam in millia; qui aufers iniquitatem, et scelera, atque peccata, nullusque apud te per se innocens est; qui reddis iniquitatem patrum filiis, ac nepotibus in tertiam et quartam progeniem.

verses.text: And Moses making haste, bowed down prostrate unto the earth, and adoring,
verses.textLatin: Festinusque Moyses, curvatus est pronus in terram, et adorans

verses.text: Said: If I have found grace in thy sight: O Lord, I beseech thee, that thou wilt go with us, (for it is a stiffnecked people,) and take away our iniquities and sin, and possess us.
verses.textLatin: ait: Si inveni gratiam in conspectu tuo, Domine, obsecro ut gradiaris nobiscum (populus enim duræ cervicis est) et auferas iniquitates nostras atque peccata, nosque possideas.

verses.text: The Lord answered: I will make a covenant in the sight of all. I will do signs such as were never seen upon the earth, nor in any nations: that this people, in the midst of whom thou art, may see the terrible work of the Lord which I will do.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Dominus: Ego inibo pactum videntibus cunctis: signa faciam quæ numquam visa sunt super terram, nec in ullis gentibus, ut cernat populus iste, in cujus es medio, opus Domini terribile quod facturus sum.

verses.text: Observe all things which this day I command thee: I myself will drive out before thy face the Amorrhite, and the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, and the Pherezite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite.
verses.textLatin: Observa cuncta quæ hodie mando tibi: ego ipse ejiciam ante faciem tuam Amorrhæum, et Chananæum, et Hethæum, Pherezæum quoque, et Hevæum, et Jebusæum.

verses.text: Beware thou never join in friendship with the inhabitants of that land, which may be thy ruin:
verses.textLatin: Cave ne umquam cum habitatoribus terræ illius jungas amicitias, quæ sint tibi in ruinam:

verses.text: But destroy their altars, break their statues, and cut down their groves:
verses.textLatin: sed aras eorum destrue, confringe statuas, lucosque succide:

verses.text: Adore not any strange god. The Lord his name is Jealous, he is a jealous God.
verses.textLatin: noli adorare deum alienum. Dominus zelotes nomen ejus; Deus est æmulator.

verses.text: Make no covenant with the men of those countries lest, when they have committed fornication with their gods, and have adored their idols, some one call thee to eat of the things sacrificed.
verses.textLatin: Ne ineas pactum cum hominibus illarum regionum: ne, cum fornicati fuerint cum diis suis, et adoraverint simulacra eorum, vocet te quispiam ut comedas de immolatis.

verses.text: Neither shalt thou take of their daughters a wife for thy son, lest after they themselves have committed fornication, they make thy sons also to commit fornication with their gods.
verses.textLatin: Nec uxorem de filiabus eorum accipies filiis tuis: ne, postquam ipsæ fuerint fornicatæ, fornicari faciant et filios tuos in deos suos.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make to thyself any molten gods.
verses.textLatin: Deos conflatiles non facies tibi.

verses.text: Thou shalt keep the feast of the unleavened bread. Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee in the time of the month of the new corn: for in the month of the springtime thou camest out from Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Solemnitatem azymorum custodies. Septem diebus vesceris azymis, sicut præcepi tibi, in tempore mensis novorum: mense enim verni temporis egressus es de Ægypto.

verses.text: All of the male kind, that openeth the womb, shall be mine. Of all beasts, both of oxen and of sheep, it shall be mine.
verses.textLatin: Omne quod aperit vulvam generis masculini, meum erit. De cunctis animantibus, tam de bobus, quam de ovibus, meum erit.

verses.text: The firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a sheep: but if thou wilt not give a price for it, it shall be slain. The firstborn of thy sons thou shalt redeem: neither shalt thou appear before me empty.
verses.textLatin: Primogenitum asini redimes ove: sin autem nec pretium pro eo dederis, occidetur. Primogenitum filiorum tuorum redimes: nec apparebis in conspectu meo vacuus.

verses.text: Six days shalt thou work, the seventh day thou shalt cease to plough, and to reap.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus operaberis; die septimo cessabis arare et metere.

verses.text: Thou shalt keep the feast of weeks with the firstfruits of the corn of thy wheat harvest, and the feast when the time of the year returneth that all things are laid in.
verses.textLatin: Solemnitatem hebdomadarum facies tibi in primitiis frugum messis tuæ triticeæ, et solemnitatem, quando redeunte anni tempore cuncta conduntur.

verses.text: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear in the sight of the Almighty Lord the God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Tribus temporibus anni apparebit omne masculinum tuum in conspectu omnipotentis Domini Dei Israël.

verses.text: For when I shall have taken away the nations from thy face, and shall have enlarged thy borders, no man shall lie in wait against thy land when thou shalt go up, and appear in the sight of the Lord thy God thrice in a year.
verses.textLatin: Cum enim tulero gentes a facie tua, et dilatavero terminos tuos, nullus insidiabitur terræ tuæ, ascendente te, et apparente in conspectu Domini Dei tui ter in anno.

verses.text: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice upon leaven: neither shall there remain in the morning any thing of the victim of the solemnity of the Phase.
verses.textLatin: Non immolabis super fermento sanguinem hostiæ meæ: neque residebit mane de victima solemnitatis Phase.

verses.text: The first of the fruits of thy ground thou shalt offer in the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in the milk of his dam.
verses.textLatin: Primitias frugum terræ tuæ offeres in domo Domini Dei tui. Non coques hædum in lacte matris suæ.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Write thee these words by which I have made a covenant both with thee and with Israel.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Scribe tibi verba hæc, quibus et tecum et cum Israël pepigi fœdus.

verses.text: And he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights: he neither ate bread nor drank water, and he wrote upon the tables the ten words of the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Fuit ergo ibi cum Domino quadraginta dies et quadraginta noctes: panem non comedit, et aquam non bibit, et scripsit in tabulis verba fœderis decem.

verses.text: And when Moses came down from the mount Sinai, he held the two tables of the testimony, and he knew not that his face was horned from the conversation of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Cumque descenderet Moyses de monte Sinai, tenebat duas tabulas testimonii, et ignorabat quod cornuta esset facies sua ex consortio sermonis Domini.

verses.text: And Aaron and the children of Israel seeing the face of Moses horned, were afraid to come near.
verses.textLatin: Videntes autem Aaron et filii Israël cornutam Moysi faciem, timuerunt prope accedere.

verses.text: And being called by him, they returned, both Aaron and the rulers of the congregation. And after that he spoke to them.
verses.textLatin: Vocatique ab eo, reversi sunt tam Aaron, quam principes synagogæ. Et postquam locutus est ad eos,

verses.text: And all the children of Israel came to him: and he gave them in commandment all that he had heard of the Lord in mount Sinai.
verses.textLatin: venerunt ad eum etiam omnes filii Israël: quibus præcepit cuncta quæ audierat a Domino in monte Sinai.

verses.text: And having done speaking, he put a veil upon his face.
verses.textLatin: Impletisque sermonibus, posuit velamen super faciem suam.

verses.text: But when he went in to the Lord, and spoke with him, he took it away until he came forth, and then he spoke to the children of Israel all things that had been commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Quod ingressus ad Dominum, et loquens cum eo, auferebat donec exiret, et tunc loquebatur ad filios Israël omnia quæ sibi fuerant imperata.

verses.text: And they saw that the face of Moses when he came out was horned, but he covered his face again, if at any time he spoke to them.
verses.textLatin: Qui videbant faciem egredientis Moysi esse cornutam, sed operiebat ille rursus faciem suam, siquando loquebatur ad eos.

verses.text: And  all the multitude of the children of Israel being gathered together, he said to them: These are the things which the Lord hath commanded to be done.
verses.textLatin: Igitur congregata omni turba filiorum Israël, dixit ad eos: Hæc sunt quæ jussit Dominus fieri.

verses.text: Six days you shall do work: the seventh day shall be holy unto you, the sabbath, and the rest of the Lord: he that shall do any work on it, shall be put to death.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus facietis opus: septimus dies erit vobis sanctus, sabbatum, et requies Domini: qui fecerit opus in eo, occidetur.

verses.text: You shall kindle no fire in any of your habitations on the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Non succendetis ignem in omnibus habitaculis vestris per diem sabbati.

verses.text: And Moses said to all the assembly of the children of Israel: This is the word the Lord hath commanded, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses ad omnem catervam filiorum Israël: Iste est sermo quem præcepit Dominus, dicens:

verses.text: Set aside with you firstfruits to the Lord. Let every one that is willing and hath a ready heart, offer them to the Lord: gold, and silver, and brass,
verses.textLatin: Separate apud vos primitias Domino. Omnis voluntarius et prono animo offerat eas Domino: aurum et argentum, et æs,

verses.text: Violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, goats’ hair,
verses.textLatin: hyacinthum et purpuram, coccumque bis tinctum, et byssum, pilos caprarum,

verses.text: And rams’ skins dyed red, and violet coloured skins, setim wood,
verses.textLatin: pellesque arietum rubricatas, et janthinas, ligna setim,

verses.text: And oil to maintain lights, and to make ointment, and most sweet incense.
verses.textLatin: et oleum ad luminaria concinnanda, et ut conficiatur unguentum, et thymiama suavissimum,

verses.text: Onyx stones, and precious stones, for the adorning of the ephod and the rational.
verses.textLatin: lapides onychinos, et gemmas ad ornatum superhumeralis et rationalis.

verses.text: Whosoever of you is wise, let him come, and make that which the Lord hath commanded:
verses.textLatin: Quisque vestrum sapiens est, veniat, et faciat quod Dominus imperavit:

verses.text: To wit, the tabernacle and the roof thereof, and the cover, the rings, and the board work with the oars, the pillars, and the sockets:
verses.textLatin: tabernaculum scilicet, et tectum ejus, atque operimentum, annulos, et tabulata cum vectibus, paxillos, et bases:

verses.text: The ark and the staves, the propitiatory, and the veil that is drawn before it:
verses.textLatin: arcam et vectes, propitiatorium, et velum, quod ante illud oppanditur:

verses.text: The table with the bars and the vessels, and the loaves of proposition:
verses.textLatin: mensam cum vectibus et vasis, et propositionis panibus:

verses.text: The candlestick to bear up the lights, the vessels thereof and the lamps, and the oil for the nourishing of fires:
verses.textLatin: candelabrum ad luminaria sustentanda, vasa illius et lucernas, et oleum ad nutrimenta ignium:

verses.text: The altar of incense, and the bars, and the oil of unction and the incense of spices: the hanging at the door of the tabernacle:
verses.textLatin: altare thymiamatis, et vectes, et oleum unctionis et thymiama ex aromatibus: tentorium ad ostium tabernaculi:

verses.text: The altar of holocaust, and its grate of brass, with the bars and vessels thereof: the laver and its foot:
verses.textLatin: altare holocausti, et craticulam ejus æneam cum vectibus et vasis suis: labrum et basim ejus:

verses.text: The curtains of the court with the pillars and the sockets, the hanging in the doors of the entry,
verses.textLatin: cortinas atrii cum columnis et basibus, tentorium in foribus vestibuli,

verses.text: The pins of the tabernacle and of the court with their little cords:
verses.textLatin: paxillos tabernaculi et atrii cum funiculis suis:

verses.text: The vestments that are to be used in the ministry of the sanctuary, the vesture of Aaron the high priest, and of his sons, to do the office of priesthood to me.
verses.textLatin: vestimenta, quorum usus est in ministerio sanctuarii, vestes Aaron pontificis ac filiorum ejus, ut sacerdotio fungantur mihi.

verses.text: And all the multitude of the children of Israel going out from the presence of Moses,
verses.textLatin: Egressaque omnis multitudo filiorum Israël de conspectu Moysi,

verses.text: Offered firstfruits to the Lord with a most ready and devout mind, to make the work of the tabernacle of the testimony. Whatsoever was necessary to the service, and to the holy vestments,
verses.textLatin: obtulerunt mente promptissima atque devota primitias Domino, ad faciendum opus tabernaculi testimonii. Quidquid ad cultum et ad vestes sanctas necessarium erat,

verses.text: Both men and women gave bracelets and earrings, rings and tablets: every vessel of gold was set aside to be offered to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: viri cum mulieribus præbuerunt, armillas et inaures, annulos et dextralia: omne vas aureum in donaria Domini separatum est.

verses.text: If any man had violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, fine linen and goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and violet coloured skins,
verses.textLatin: Si quis habebat hyacinthum, et purpuram, coccumque bis tinctum, byssum et pilos caprarum, pelles arietum rubricatas, et janthinas,

verses.text: Metal of silver and brass, they offered it to the Lord, and setim wood for divers uses.
verses.textLatin: argenti, ærisque metalla, obtulerunt Domino, lignaque setim in varios usus.

verses.text: The skilful women also gave such things as they had spun, violet, purple, and scarlet, and fine linen,
verses.textLatin: Sed et mulieres doctæ, quæ neverant, dederunt hyacinthum, purpuram, et vermiculum, ac byssum,

verses.text: And goats’ hair, giving all of their own accord.
verses.textLatin: et pilos caprarum, sponte propria cuncta tribuentes.

verses.text: But the princes offered onyx stones, and precious stones, for the ephod and the rational,
verses.textLatin: Principes vero obtulerunt lapides onychinos, et gemmas ad superhumerale et rationale,

verses.text: And spices and oil for the lights, and for the preparing of ointment, and to make the incense of most sweet savour.
verses.textLatin: aromataque et oleum ad luminaria concinnanda, et ad præparandum unguentum, ac thymiama odoris suavissimi componendum.

verses.text: All both men and women with devout mind offered gifts, that the works might be done which the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses. All the children of Israel dedicated voluntary offerings to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Omnes viri et mulieres mente devota obtulerunt donaria, ut fierent opera, quæ jusserat Dominus per manum Moysi. Cuncti filii Israël voluntaria Domino dedicaverunt.

verses.text: And Moses said to the children of Israel: Behold the Lord hath called by name Beseleel the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad filios Israël: Ecce, vocavit Dominus ex nomine Beseleel filium Uri, filii Hur de tribu Juda,

verses.text: And hath filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom and understanding and knowledge and all learning.
verses.textLatin: implevitque eum spiritu Dei, sapientia et intelligentia, et scientia et omni doctrina,

verses.text: To devise and to work in gold and silver and brass,
verses.textLatin: ad excogitandum, et faciendum opus in auro, et argento, et ære,

verses.text: And in engraving stones, and in carpenters’ work. Whatsoever can be devised artificially,
verses.textLatin: sculpendisque lapidibus, et opere carpentario, quidquid fabre adinveniri potest,

verses.text: He hath given in his heart: Ooliab also the son of Achisamech of the tribe of Dan:
verses.textLatin: dedit in corde ejus: Ooliab quoque filium Achisamech de tribu Dan:

verses.text: Both of them hath he instructed with wisdom, to do carpenters’ work, and tapestry, and embroidery in blue and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, and to weave all things, and to invent all new things.
verses.textLatin: ambos erudivit sapientia, ut faciant opera abietarii, polymitarii, ac plumarii, de hyacintho ac purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso, et texant omnia, ac nova quæque reperiant.

verses.text: Beseleel,  therefore, and Ooliab, and every wise man, to whom the Lord gave wisdom and understanding, to know how to work artificially, made the things that are necessary for the uses of the sanctuary, and which the Lord commanded.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ergo Beseleel, et Ooliab, et omnis vir sapiens, quibus dedit Dominus sapientiam et intellectum, ut scirent fabre operari quæ in usus sanctuarii necessaria sunt, et quæ præcepit Dominus.

verses.text: And when Moses had called them, and every skilful man, to whom the Lord had given wisdom, and such as of their own accord had offered themselves to the making of the work,
verses.textLatin: Cumque vocasset eos Moyses et omnem eruditum virum, cui dederat Dominus sapientiam, et qui sponte sua obtulerant se ad faciendum opus,

verses.text: He delivered all the offerings of the children of Israel unto them. And while they were earnest about the work, the people daily in the morning offered their vows.
verses.textLatin: tradidit eis universa donaria filiorum Israël. Qui cum instarent operi, quotidie mane vota populus offerebat.

verses.text: Whereupon the workmen being constrained to come,
verses.textLatin: Unde artifices venire compulsi,

verses.text: Said to Moses: The people offereth more than is necessary.
verses.textLatin: dixerunt Moysi: Plus offert populus quam necessarium est.

verses.text: Moses therefore commanded proclamation to be made by the crier’s voice: Let neither man nor woman offer any more for the work of the sanctuary. And so they ceased from offering gifts,
verses.textLatin: Jussit ergo Moyses præconis voce cantari: Nec vir, nec mulier quidquam offerat ultra in opere sanctuarii. Sicque cessatum est a muneribus offerendis,

verses.text: Because the things that were offered did suffice, and were too much.
verses.textLatin: eo quod oblata sufficerent et superabundarent.

verses.text: And all the men that were wise of heart, to accomplish the work of the tabernacle, made ten curtains of twisted fine linen, and violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, with varied work, and the art of embroidering:
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque omnes corde sapientes ad explendum opus tabernaculi, cortinas decem de bysso retorta, et hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, opere vario, et arte polymita:

verses.text: The length of one curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the breadth four: all the curtains were of the same size.
verses.textLatin: quarum una habebat in longitudine viginti octo cubitos, et in latitudine quatuor; una mensura erat omnium cortinarum.

verses.text: And he joined five curtains, one to another, and the other five he coupled one to another.
verses.textLatin: Conjunxitque cortinas quinque, alteram alteri, et alias quinque sibi invicem copulavit.

verses.text: He made also loops of violet in the edge of one curtain on both sides, and in the edge of the other curtain in like manner,
verses.textLatin: Fecit et ansas hyacinthinas in ora cortinæ unius ex utroque latere, et in ora cortinæ alterius similiter,

verses.text: That the loops might meet one against another, and might be joined each with the other.
verses.textLatin: ut contra se invicem venirent ansæ, et mutuo jungerentur.

verses.text: Whereupon also he cast fifty rings of gold, that might catch the loops of the curtains, and they might be made one tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Unde et quinquaginta fudit circulos aureos, qui morderent cortinarum ansas, et fieret unum tabernaculum.

verses.text: He made also eleven curtains of goats’ hair, to cover the roof of the tabernacle:
verses.textLatin: Fecit et saga undecim de pilis caprarum ad operiendum tectum tabernaculi:

verses.text: One curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits broad: all the curtains were of one measure.
verses.textLatin: unum sagum in longitudine habebat cubitos triginta, et in latitudine cubitos quatuor: unius mensuræ erant omnia saga:

verses.text: Five of which he joined apart, and the other six apart.
verses.textLatin: quorum quinque junxit seorsum, et sex alia separatim.

verses.text: And he made fifty loops in the edge of one curtain, and fifty in the edge of another curtain, that they might be joined one to another.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque ansas quinquaginta in ora sagi unius, et quinquaginta in ora sagi alterius, ut sibi invicem jungerentur.

verses.text: And fifty buckles of brass wherewith the roof might be knit together, that of all the curtains there might be made one covering.
verses.textLatin: Et fibulas æneas quinquaginta, quibus necteretur tectum, ut unum pallium ex omnibus sagis fieret.

verses.text: He made also a cover for the tabernacle of rams’ skins dyed red: and another cover over that of violet skins.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et opertorium tabernaculi de pellibus arietum rubricatis: aliudque desuper velamentum de pellibus janthinis.

verses.text: He made also the boards of the tabernacle of setim wood standing.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et tabulas tabernaculi de lignis setim stantes.

verses.text: The length of one board was ten cubits: and the breadth was one cubit and a half.
verses.textLatin: Decem cubitorum erat longitudo tabulæ unius: et unum ac semis cubitum latitudo retinebat.

verses.text: There were two mortises throughout every board, that one might be joined to the other. And in this manner he made for all the boards of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Binæ incastraturæ erant per singulas tabulas, ut altera alteri jungeretur. Sic fecit in omnibus tabernaculi tabulis.

verses.text: Of which twenty were at the south side southward,
verses.textLatin: E quibus viginti ad plagam meridianam erant contra austrum,

verses.text: With forty sockets of silver, two sockets were put under one board on the two sides of the corners, where the mortises of the sides end in the corners.
verses.textLatin: cum quadraginta basibus argenteis. Duæ bases sub una tabula ponebantur ex utraque parte angulorum, ubi incastraturæ laterum in angulis terminantur.

verses.text: At that side also of the tabernacle, that looketh toward the north, he made twenty boards.
verses.textLatin: Ad plagam quoque tabernaculi, quæ respicit ad aquilonem, fecit viginti tabulas,

verses.text: With forty sockets of silver, two sockets for every board.
verses.textLatin: cum quadraginta basibus argenteis, duas bases per singulas tabulas.

verses.text: But against the west, to wit, at that side of the tabernacle, which looketh to the sea, he made six boards,
verses.textLatin: Contra occidentem vero, id est, ad eam partem tabernaculi quæ mare respicit, fecit sex tabulas,

verses.text: And two others at each corner of the tabernacle behind:
verses.textLatin: et duas alias per singulos angulos tabernaculi retro:

verses.text: Which were also joined from beneath unto the top, and went together into one joint. Thus he did on both sides at the corners:
verses.textLatin: quæ junctæ erant a deorsum usque sursum, et in unam compaginem pariter ferebantur. Ita fecit ex utraque parte per angulos:

verses.text: So there were in all eight boards, and they had sixteen sockets of silver, to wit, two sockets under every board.
verses.textLatin: ut octo essent simul tabulæ, et haberent bases argenteas sedecim, binas scilicet bases sub singulis tabulis.

verses.text: He made also bars of setim wood, five to hold together the boards of one side of the tabernacle,
verses.textLatin: Fecit et vectes de lignis setim, quinque ad continendas tabulas unius lateris tabernaculi,

verses.text: And five others to join together the boards of the other side: and besides these, five other bars at the west side of the tabernacle towards the sea.
verses.textLatin: et quinque alios ad alterius lateris coaptandas tabulas: et extra hos, quinque alios vectes ad occidentalem plagam tabernaculi contra mare.

verses.text: He made also another bar, that might come by the midst of the boards from corner to corner.
verses.textLatin: Fecit quoque vectem alium, qui per medias tabulas ab angulo usque ad angulum perveniret.

verses.text: And the board works themselves he overlaid with gold, casting for them sockets of silver. And their rings he made of gold, through which the bars might be drawn: and he covered the bars themselves with plates of gold.
verses.textLatin: Ipsa autem tabulata deauravit, fusis basibus earum argenteis. Et circulos eorum fecit aureos, per quos vectes induci possent: quos et ipsos laminis aureis operuit.

verses.text: He made also a veil of violet, and purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, varied and distinguished with embroidery:
verses.textLatin: Fecit et velum de hyacintho, et purpura, vermiculo, ac bysso retorta, opere polymitario, varium atque distinctum:

verses.text: And four pillars of setim wood, which with their heads he overlaid with gold, casting for them sockets of silver.
verses.textLatin: et quatuor columnas de lignis setim, quas cum capitibus deauravit, fusis basibus earum argenteis.

verses.text: He made also a hanging in the entry of the tabernacle of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, with the work of an embroiderer.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et tentorium in introitu tabernaculi ex hyacintho, purpura, vermiculo, byssoque retorta, opere plumarii:

verses.text: And five pillars with their heads, which he covered with gold, and their sockets he cast of brass.
verses.textLatin: et columnas quinque cum capitibus suis, quas operuit auro, basesque earum fudit æneas.

verses.text: And  Beseleel made also the ark of setim wood: it was two cubits and a half in length, and a cubit and a half in breadth, and the height was of one cubit and a half: and he overlaid it with the purest gold within and without.
verses.textLatin: Fecit autem Beseleel et arcam de lignis setim, habentem duos semis cubitos in longitudine, et cubitum ac semissem in latitudine, altitudo quoque unius cubiti fuit et dimidii: vestivitque eam auro purissimo intus ac foris.

verses.text: And he made to it a crown of gold round about,
verses.textLatin: Et fecit illi coronam auream per gyrum,

verses.text: Casting four rings of gold at the four corners thereof: two rings in one side, and two in the other.
verses.textLatin: conflans quatuor annulos aureos per quatuor angulos ejus: duos annulos in latere uno, et duos in altero.

verses.text: And he made bars of setim wood, which he overlaid with gold,
verses.textLatin: Vectes quoque fecit de lignis setim, quos vestivit auro,

verses.text: And he put them into the rings that were at the sides of the ark to carry it.
verses.textLatin: et quos misit in annulos, qui erant in lateribus arcæ ad portandum eam.

verses.text: He made also the propitiatory, that is, the oracle, of the purest gold, two cubits and a half in length, and a cubit and a half in breadth.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et propitiatorium, id est, oraculum, de auro mundissimo, duorum cubitorum et dimidii in longitudine, et cubiti ac semis in latitudine.

verses.text: Two cherubims also of beaten gold, which he set on the two sides of the propitiatory:
verses.textLatin: Duos etiam cherubim ex auro ductili, quos posuit ex utraque parte propitiatorii:

verses.text: One cherub in the top of one side, and the other cherub in the top of the other side: two cherubims at the two ends of the propitiatory,
verses.textLatin: cherub unum in summitate unius partis, et cherub alterum in summitate partis alterius: duos cherubim in singulis summitatibus propitiatorii,

verses.text: Spreading their wings, and covering the propitiatory, and looking one towards the other, and towards it.
verses.textLatin: extendentes alas, et tegentes propitiatorium, seque mutuo et illud respicientes.

verses.text: He made also the table of setim wood, in length two cubits, and in breadth one cubit, and in height it was a cubit and a half.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et mensam de lignis setim in longitudine duorum cubitorum, et in latitudine unius cubiti, quæ habebat in altitudine cubitum ac semissem.

verses.text: And he overlaid it with the finest gold, and he made to it a golden ledge round about.
verses.textLatin: Circumdeditque eam auro mundissimo, et fecit illi labium aureum per gyrum,

verses.text: And to the ledge itself he made a polished crown of gold, of four fingers’ breadth, and upon the same another golden crown.
verses.textLatin: ipsique labio coronam auream interrasilem quatuor digitorum, et super eamdem, alteram coronam auream.

verses.text: And he cast four rings of gold, which he put in the four corners at each foot of the table,
verses.textLatin: Fudit et quatuor circulos aureos, quos posuit in quatuor angulis per singulos pedes mensæ

verses.text: Over against the crown: and he put the bars into them, that the table might be carried.
verses.textLatin: contra coronam: misitque in eos vectes, ut possit mensa portari.

verses.text: And the bars also themselves he made of setim wood, and overlaid them with gold,
verses.textLatin: Ipsos quoque vectes fecit de lignis setim, et circumdedit eos auro.

verses.text: And the vessels for the divers uses of the table, dishes, bowls, and cups, and censers of pure gold, wherein the libations are to be offered.
verses.textLatin: Et vasa ad diversos usus mensæ, acetabula, phialas, et cyathos, et thuribula, ex auro puro, in quibus offerenda sunt libamina.

verses.text: He made also the candlestick of beaten work of the finest gold. From the shaft whereof its branches, its cups, and bowls, and lilies came out:
verses.textLatin: Fecit et candelabrum ductile de auro mundissimo, de cujus vecte calami, scyphi, sphærulæque, ac lilia procedebant:

verses.text: Six on the two sides: three branches on one side, and three on the other.
verses.textLatin: sex in utroque latere, tres calami ex parte una, et tres ex altera:

verses.text: Three cups in manner of a nut on each branch, and bowls withal and lilies; and three cups of the fashion of a nut in another branch, and bowls withal and lilies. The work of the six branches that went out from the shaft of the candlestick was equal.
verses.textLatin: tres scyphi in nucis modum per calamos singulos, sphærulæque simul et lilia: et tres scyphi instar nucis in calamo altero, sphærulæque simul et lilia. Æquum erat opus sex calamorum, qui procedebant de stipite candelabri.

verses.text: And in the shaft itself were four cups after the manner of a nut, and bowls withal at every one, and lilies:
verses.textLatin: In ipso autem vecte erant quatuor scyphi in nucis modum, sphærulæque per singulos simul et lilia:

verses.text: And bowls under two branches in three places, which together make six branches going out from one shaft.
verses.textLatin: et sphærulæ sub duobus calamis per loca tria, qui simul sex fiunt calami procedentes de vecte uno.

verses.text: So both the bowls, and the branches were of the same, all beaten work of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Et sphærulæ igitur, et calami ex ipso erant, universa ductilia ex auro purissimo.

verses.text: He made also the seven lamps with their snuffers, and the vessels where the snuffings were to be put out, of the purest gold.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et lucernas septem cum emunctoriis suis, et vasa ubi ea, quæ emuncta sunt, extinguantur, de auro mundissimo.

verses.text: The candlestick with all the vessels thereof weighed a talent of gold.
verses.textLatin: Talentum auri appendebat candelabrum cum omnibus vasis suis.

verses.text: He made also the altar of incense of setim wood, being a cubit on every side foursquare, and in height two cubits: from the corners of which went out horns.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et altare thymiamatis de lignis setim, per quadrum singulos habens cubitos, et in altitudine duos: e cujus angulis procedebant cornua.

verses.text: And he overlaid it with the purest gold, with its grate and the sides, and the horns.
verses.textLatin: Vestivitque illud auro purissimo cum craticula ac parietibus et cornibus.

verses.text: And he made to it a crown of gold round about, and two golden rings under the crown at each side, that the bars might be put into them, and the altar be carried.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque ei coronam aureolam per gyrum, et duos annulos aureos sub corona per singula latera, ut mittantur in eos vectes, et possit altare portari.

verses.text: And the bars themselves he made also of setim wood, and overlaid them with plates of gold.
verses.textLatin: Ipsos autem vectes fecit de lignis setim, et operuit laminis aureis.

verses.text: He compounded also the oil for the ointment of sanctification, and incense of the purest spices, according to the work of a perfumer.
verses.textLatin: Composuit et oleum ad sanctificationis unguentum, et thymiama de aromatibus mundissimis opere pigmentarii.

verses.text: He  made also the altar of holocaust of setim wood, five cubits square, and three in height:
verses.textLatin: Fecit et altare holocausti de lignis setim, quinque cubitorum per quadrum, et trium in altitudine:

verses.text: The horns whereof went out from the corners, and he overlaid it with plates of brass.
verses.textLatin: cujus cornua de angulis procedebant, operuitque illum laminis æneis.

verses.text: And for the uses thereof, he prepared divers vessels of brass, cauldrons, tongs, fleshhooks, pothooks, and firepans.
verses.textLatin: Et in usus ejus paravit ex ære vasa diversa, lebetes, forcipes, fuscinulas, uncinos, et ignium receptacula.

verses.text: And he made the grate thereof of brass, in manner of a net, and under it in the midst of the altar a hearth,
verses.textLatin: Craticulamque ejus in modum retis fecit æneam, et subter eam in altaris medio arulam,

verses.text: Casting four rings at the four ends of the net at the top, to put in bars to carry it.
verses.textLatin: fusis quatuor annulis per totidem retiaculi summitates, ad immittendos vectes ad portandum:

verses.text: And he made the bars of setim wood, and overlaid them with plates of brass:
verses.textLatin: quos et ipsos fecit de lignis setim, et operuit laminis æneis:

verses.text: And he drew them through the rings that stood out in the sides of the altar. And the altar itself was not solid, but hollow, of boards, and empty within.
verses.textLatin: induxitque in circulos, qui in lateribus altaris eminebant. Ipsum autem altare non erat solidum, sed cavum ex tabulis, et intus vacuum.

verses.text: He made also the laver of brass, with the foot thereof, of the mirrors of the women that watched at the door of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Fecit et labrum æneum cum basi sua de speculis mulierum, quæ excubabant in ostio tabernaculi.

verses.text: He made also the court, in the south side whereof were hangings of fine twisted linen, of a hundred cubits,
verses.textLatin: Fecit et atrium, in cujus australi plaga erant tentoria de bysso retorta, cubitorum centum,

verses.text: Twenty pillars of brass with their sockets, the heads of the pillars, and the whole graving of the work, of silver.
verses.textLatin: columnæ æneæ viginti cum basibus suis, capita columnarum, et tota operis cælatura, argentea.

verses.text: In like manner at the north side the hangings, the pillars, and the sockets and heads of the pillars were of the same measure, and work and metal.
verses.textLatin: Æque ad septentrionalem plagam tentoria columnæ, basesque et capita columnarum ejusdem mensuræ, et operis ac metalli, erant.

verses.text: But on that side that looketh to the west, there were hangings of fifty cubits, ten pillars of brass with their sockets, and the heads of the pillars, and all the graving of the work, of silver.
verses.textLatin: In ea vero plaga, quæ ad occidentem respicit, fuerunt tentoria cubitorum quinquaginta, columnæ decem cum basibus suis æneæ, et capita columnarum, et tota operis cælatura, argentea.

verses.text: Moreover towards the east he prepared hangings of fifty cubits:
verses.textLatin: Porro contra orientem quinquaginta cubitorum paravit tentoria:

verses.text: Fifteen cubits of which were on one side with three pillars, and their sockets:
verses.textLatin: e quibus, quindecim cubitos columnarum trium, cum basibus suis, unum tenebat latus:

verses.text: And on the other side (for between the two he made the entry of the tabernacle) there were hangings equally of fifteen cubits, and three pillars, and as many sockets.
verses.textLatin: et in parte altera (quia inter utraque introitum tabernaculi fecit) quindecim æque cubitorum erant tentoria, columnæque tres, et bases totidem.

verses.text: All the hangings of the court were woven with twisted linen.
verses.textLatin: Cuncta atrii tentoria byssus retorta texuerat.

verses.text: The sockets of the pillars were of brass, and their heads with all their gravings of silver: and he overlaid the pillars of the court also with silver.
verses.textLatin: Bases columnarum fuere æneæ, capita autem earum cum cunctis cælaturis suis argentea: sed et ipsas columnas atrii vestivit argento.

verses.text: And he made in the entry thereof an embroidered hanging of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, that was twenty cubits long, and five cubits high according to the measure of all the hangings of the court.
verses.textLatin: Et in introitu ejus opere plumario fecit tentorium ex hyacintho, purpura, vermiculo, ac bysso retorta, quod habebat viginti cubitos in longitudine, altitudo vero quinque cubitorum erat juxta mensuram, quam cuncta atrii tentoria habebant.

verses.text: And the pillars in the entry were four with sockets of brass, and their heads and gravings of silver.
verses.textLatin: Columnæ autem in ingressu fuere quatuor cum basibus æneis, capitaque earum et cælaturæ argenteæ.

verses.text: The pins also of the tabernacle and of the court round about he made of brass.
verses.textLatin: Paxillos quoque tabernaculi et atrii per gyrum fecit æneos.

verses.text: These are the instruments of the tabernacle of the testimony, which were counted according to the commandment of Moses, in the ceremonies of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest:
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt instrumenta tabernaculi testimonii, quæ enumerata sunt juxta præceptum Moysi in cæremoniis Levitarum per manum Ithamar filii Aaron sacerdotis:

verses.text: Which Beseleel the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Juda had made as the Lord commanded by Moses,
verses.textLatin: quæ Beseleel filius Uri filii Hur de tribu Juda, Domino per Moysen jubente, compleverat,

verses.text: Having for his companion Ooliab the son of Achisamech of the tribe of Dan: who also was an excellent artificer in wood, and worker in tapestry and embroidery in violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.
verses.textLatin: juncto sibi socio Ooliab filio Achisamech de tribu Dan: qui et ipse artifex lignorum egregius fuit, et polymitarius atque plumarius ex hyacintho, purpura, vermiculo et bysso.

verses.text: All the gold that was spent in the work of the sanctuary, and that was offered in gifts was nine and twenty talents, and seven hundred and thirty sicles according to the standard of the sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Omne aurum quod expensum est in opere sanctuarii, et quod oblatum est in donariis, viginti novem talentorum fuit, et septingentorum triginta siclorum ad mensuram sanctuarii.

verses.text: And it was offered by them that went to be numbered, from twenty years old and upwards, of six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men able to bear arms.
verses.textLatin: Oblatum est autem ab his qui transierunt ad numerum a viginti annis et supra, de sexcentis tribus millibus et quingentis quinquaginta armatorum.

verses.text: There were moreover a hundred talents of silver, whereof were cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and of the entry where the veil hangeth.
verses.textLatin: Fuerunt præterea centum talenta argenti e quibus conflatæ sunt bases sanctuarii, et introitus, ubi velum pendet.

verses.text: A hundred sockets were made of a hundred talents, one talent being reckoned for every socket.
verses.textLatin: Centum bases factæ sunt de talentis centum, singulis talentis per bases singulas supputatis.

verses.text: And of the thousand seven hundred and seventy-five he made the heads of the pillars, which also he overlaid with silver.
verses.textLatin: De mille autem septingentis et septuaginta quinque, fecit capita columnarum, quas et ipsas vestivit argento.

verses.text: And there were offered of brass also seventy-two thousand talents, and four hundred sicles besides.
verses.textLatin: Æris quoque oblata sunt talenta septuaginta duo millia, et quadringenti supra sicli,

verses.text: Of which were cast the sockets in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony, and the altar of brass with the grate thereof, and all the vessels that belong to the use thereof.
verses.textLatin: ex quibus fusæ sunt bases in introitu tabernaculi testimonii, et altare æneum cum craticula sua, omniaque vasa quæ ad usum ejus pertinent,

verses.text: And the sockets of the court as well round about as in the entry thereof, and the pins of the tabernacle and of the court round about.
verses.textLatin: et bases atrii tam in circuitu quam in ingressu ejus, et paxilli tabernaculi atque atrii per gyrum.

verses.text: And  he made, of violet and purple, scarlet and fine linen, the vestments for Aaron to wear when he ministered in the holy places, as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: De hyacintho vero et purpura, vermiculo ac bysso, fecit vestes, quibus indueretur Aaron quando ministrabat in sanctis, sicut præcepit Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: So he made an ephod of gold, violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.
verses.textLatin: Fecit igitur superhumerale de auro, hyacintho, et purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta,

verses.text: With embroidered work: and he cut thin plates of gold, and drew them small into threads, that they might be twisted with the woof of the aforesaid colours,
verses.textLatin: opere polymitario: inciditque bracteas aureas, et extenuavit in fila, ut possent torqueri cum priorum colorum subtegmine,

verses.text: And two borders coupled one to the other in the top on either side,
verses.textLatin: duasque oras sibi invicem copulatas in utroque latere summitatum,

verses.text: And a girdle of the same colours, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: et balteum ex eisdem coloribus, sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: He prepared also two onyx stones, fast set and closed in gold, and graven by the art of a lapidary, with the names of the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Paravit et duos lapides onychinos, astrictos et inclusos auro, et sculptos arte gemmaria nominibus filiorum Israël:

verses.text: And he set them in the sides of the ephod for a memorial of the children of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: posuitque eos in lateribus superhumeralis in monimentum filiorum Israël, sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: He made also a rational with embroidered work, according to the work of the ephod, of gold, violet, purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen,
verses.textLatin: Fecit et rationale opere polymito juxta opus superhumeralis, ex auro, hyacintho, purpura, coccoque bis tincto, et bysso retorta:

verses.text: Foursquare, double, of the measure of a span.
verses.textLatin: quadrangulum, duplex, mensuræ palmi.

verses.text: And he set four rows of precious stones in it. In the first row was a sardius, a topaz, an emerald.
verses.textLatin: Et posuit in eo gemmarum ordines quatuor. In primo versu erat sardius, topazius, smaragdus.

verses.text: In the second, a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper.
verses.textLatin: In secundo, carbunculus, sapphirus, et jaspis.

verses.text: In the third, a ligurius, an agate, and an amethyst.
verses.textLatin: In tertio, ligurius, achates, et amethystus.

verses.text: In the fourth, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl, set and enclosed in gold by their rows.
verses.textLatin: In quarto, chrysolithus, onychinus, et beryllus, circumdati et inclusi auro per ordines suos.
