verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses ad Aaron, et ad Eleazar, et Ithamar, filios ejus: Capita vestra nolite nudare, et vestimenta nolite scindere, ne forte moriamini, et super omnem cœtum oriatur indignatio. Fratres vestri, et omnis domus Israël, plangant incendium quod Dominus suscitavit:

verses.text: But you shall not go out of the door of the tabernacle, otherwise you shall perish, for the oil of the holy unction is on you. And they did all things according to the precept of Moses.
verses.textLatin: vos autem non egrediemini fores tabernaculi, alioquin peribitis: oleum quippe sanctæ unctionis est super vos. Qui fecerunt omnia juxta præceptum Moysi.

verses.text: The Lord also said to Aaron:
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Aaron:

verses.text: You shall not drink wine nor any thing that may make drunk, thou nor thy sons, when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony, lest you die: because it is an everlasting precept through your generations:
verses.textLatin: Vinum, et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibetis tu et filii tui, quando intratis in tabernaculum testimonii, ne moriamini: quia præceptum sempiternum est in generationes vestras:

verses.text: And that you may have knowledge to discern between holy and unholy, between unclean and clean:
verses.textLatin: et ut habeatis scientiam discernendi inter sanctum et profanum, inter pollutum et mundum;

verses.text: And may teach the children of Israel all my ordinances which the Lord hath spoken to them by the hand of Moses.
verses.textLatin: doceatisque filios Israël omnia legitima mea quæ locutus est Dominus ad eos per manum Moysi.

verses.text: And Moses spoke to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons that were left: Take the sacrifice that is remaining of the oblation of the Lord, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is holy of holies.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses ad Aaron, et ad Eleazar, et Ithamar, filios ejus, qui erant residui: Tollite sacrificium, quod remansit de oblatione Domini, et comedite illud absque fermento juxta altare, quia Sanctum sanctorum est.

verses.text: And you shall eat it in a holy place: which is given to thee and thy sons of the oblations of the Lord, as it hath been commanded me.
verses.textLatin: Comedetis autem in loco sancto: quod datum est tibi et filiis tuis de oblationibus Domini, sicut præceptum est mihi.

verses.text: The breast also that is offered, and the shoulder that is separated, you shall eat in a most clean place, thou and thy sons, and thy daughters with thee. For they are set aside for thee and thy children, of the victims of peace offerings of the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Pectusculum quoque quod oblatum est, et armum qui separatus est, edetis in loco mundissimo tu et filii tui, et filiæ tuæ tecum: tibi enim ac liberis tuis reposita sunt de hostiis salutaribus filiorum Israël:

verses.text: Because they have elevated before the Lord the shoulder and the breast, and the fat that is burnt on the altar, and they belong to thee and to thy sons by a perpetual law, as the Lord hath commanded.
verses.textLatin: eo quod armum et pectus, et adipes qui cremantur in altari, elevaverunt coram Domino, et pertineant ad te, et ad filios tuos, lege perpetua, sicut præcepit Dominus.

verses.text: While these things were a doing, when Moses sought for the buck goat, that had been offered for sin, he found it burnt: and being angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron that were left, he said:
verses.textLatin: Inter hæc, hircum, qui oblatus fuerat pro peccato, cum quæreret Moyses, exustum reperit: iratusque contra Eleazar et Ithamar filios Aaron, qui remanserant, ait:

verses.text: Why did you not eat in the holy place the sacrifice for sin, which is most holy, and given to you, that you may bear the iniquity of the people, and may pray for them in the sight of the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Cur non comedistis hostiam pro peccato in loco sancto, quæ Sancta sanctorum est, et data vobis ut portetis iniquitatem multitudinis, et rogetis pro ea in conspectu Domini,

verses.text: Especially whereas none of the blood thereof hath been carried within the holy places, and you ought to have eaten it in the sanctuary, as was commanded me?
verses.textLatin: præsertim cum de sanguine illius non sit illatum intra sancta, et comedere debueritis eam in Sanctuario, sicut præceptum est mihi?

verses.text: Aaron answered: This day hath been offered the victim for sin, and the holocaust before the Lord: and to me what thou seest has happened: how could I eat it, or please the Lord in the ceremonies, having a sorrowful heart?
verses.textLatin: Respondit Aaron: Oblata est hodie victima pro peccato, et holocaustum coram Domino: mihi autem accidit quod vides; quomodo potui comedere eam, aut placere Domino in cæremoniis mente lugubri?

verses.text: Which when Moses had heard he was satisfied.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Moyses, recepit satisfactionem.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: Say to the children of Israel: These are the animals which you are to eat of all the living things of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Dicite filiis Israël: Hæc sunt animalia quæ comedere debetis de cunctis animantibus terræ:

verses.text: Whatsoever hath the hoof divided, and cheweth the cud among the beasts, you shall eat.
verses.textLatin: omne quod habet divisam ungulam, et ruminat in pecoribus, comedetis.

verses.text: But whatsoever cheweth indeed the cud, and hath a hoof, but divideth it not, as the camel, and others, that you shall not eat, but shall reckon it among the unclean.
verses.textLatin: Quidquid autem ruminat quidem, et habet ungulam, sed non dividit eam, sicut camelus et cetera, non comedetis illud, et inter immunda reputabitis.

verses.text: The cherogrillus which cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof, is unclean.
verses.textLatin: Chœrogryllus qui ruminat, ungulamque non dividit, immundus est.

verses.text: The hare also: for that too cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof.
verses.textLatin: Lepus quoque: nam et ipse ruminat, sed ungulam non dividit.

verses.text: And the swine, which, though it divideth the hoof, cheweth not the cud.
verses.textLatin: Et sus: qui cum ungulam dividat, non ruminat.

verses.text: The flesh of these you shall not eat, nor shall you touch their carcasses, because they are unclean to you.
verses.textLatin: Horum carnibus non vescemini, nec cadavera contingetis, quia immunda sunt vobis.

verses.text: These are the things that breed in the waters, and which it is lawful to eat. All that hath fins, and scales, as well in the sea, as in the rivers, and the pools, you shall eat.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt quæ gignuntur in aquis, et vesci licitum est: omne quod habet pinnulas et squamas, tam in mari quam in fluminibus et stagnis, comedetis.

verses.text: But whatsoever hath not fins and scales, of those things that move and live in the waters, shall be an abomination to you,
verses.textLatin: Quidquid autem pinnulas et squamas non habet, eorum quæ in aquis moventur et vivunt, abominabile vobis,

verses.text: And detestable: their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall avoid.
verses.textLatin: execrandumque erit: carnes eorum non comedetis, et morticina vitabitis.

verses.text: All that have not fins and scales, in the waters, shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Cuncta quæ non habent pinnulas et squamas in aquis, polluta erunt.

verses.text: Of birds these are they which you must not eat, and which are to be avoided by you: The eagle, and the griffon, and the osprey,
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt quæ de avibus comedere non debetis, et vitanda sunt vobis: aquilam, et gryphem, et haliæetum,

verses.text: And the kite, and the vulture, according to their kind,
verses.textLatin: et milvum ac vulturem juxta genus suum,

verses.text: And all that is of the raven kind, according to their likeness.
verses.textLatin: et omne corvini generis in similitudinem suam,

verses.text: The ostrich, and the owl, and the larus, and the hawk according to its kind.
verses.textLatin: struthionem, et noctuam, et larum, et accipitrem juxta genus suum:

verses.text: The screech owl, and the cormorant, and the ibis,
verses.textLatin: bubonem, et mergulum, et ibin,

verses.text: And the swan, and the bittern, and the porphyrion,
verses.textLatin: et cygnum, et onocrotalum, et porphyrionem,

verses.text: The heron, and the charadroin according to its kind, the houp also, and the bat.
verses.textLatin: herodionem, et charadrion juxta genus suum, upupam quoque, et vespertilionem.

verses.text: Of things that fly, whatsoever goeth upon four feet, shall be abominable to you.
verses.textLatin: Omne de volucribus quod graditur super quatuor pedes, abominabile erit vobis.

verses.text: But whatsoever walketh upon four feet, but hath the legs behind longer, wherewith it hoppeth upon the earth,
verses.textLatin: Quidquid autem ambulat quidem super quatuor pedes, sed habet longiora retro crura, per quæ salit super terram,

verses.text: That you shall eat, as the bruchus in its kind, the attacus, and ophiomachus, and the locust, every one according to their kind.
verses.textLatin: comedere debetis, ut est bruchus in genere suo, et attacus atque ophiomachus, ac locusta, singula juxta genus suum.

verses.text: But of flying things whatsoever hath four feet only, shall be an abomination to you:
verses.textLatin: Quidquid autem ex volucribus quatuor tantum habet pedes, execrabile erit vobis:

verses.text: And whosoever shall touch the carcasses of them, shall be defiled, and shall be unclean until the evening:
verses.textLatin: et quicumque morticina eorum tetigerit, polluetur, et erit immundus usque ad vesperum:

verses.text: And if it be necessary that he carry any of these things when they are dead, he shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until the sun set.
verses.textLatin: et si necesse fuerit ut portet quippiam horum mortuum, lavabit vestimenta sua, et immundus erit usque ad occasum solis.

verses.text: Every beast that hath a hoof, but divideth it not, nor cheweth the cud, shall be unclean: and he that toucheth it, shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Omne animal quod habet quidem ungulam, sed non dividit eam, nec ruminat, immundum erit: et qui tetigerit illud, contaminabitur.

verses.text: That which walketh upon hands of all animals which go on all four, shall be unclean: he that shall touch their carcasses shall be defiled until evening.
verses.textLatin: Quod ambulat super manus ex cunctis animantibus, quæ incedunt quadrupedia, immundum erit: qui tetigerit morticina eorum, polluetur usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: And he that shall carry such carcasses, shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until evening: because all these things are unclean to you.
verses.textLatin: Et qui portaverit hujuscemodi cadavera, lavabit vestimenta sua, et immundus erit usque ad vesperum: quia omnia hæc immunda sunt vobis.

verses.text: These also shall be reckoned among unclean things, of all that move upon the earth, the weasel, and the mouse, and the crocodile, every one according to their kind:
verses.textLatin: Hæc quoque inter polluta reputabuntur de his quæ moventur in terra, mustela et mus et crocodilus, singula juxta genus suum,

verses.text: The shrew, and the chameleon, and the stello, and the lizard, and the mole:
verses.textLatin: mygale, et chamæleon, et stellio, et lacerta, et talpa.

verses.text: All these are unclean. He that toucheth their carcasses shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Omnia hæc immunda sunt. Qui tetigerit morticina eorum, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:

verses.text: And upon what thing soever any of their carcasses shall fall, it shall be defiled, whether it be a vessel of wood, or a garment, or skins or haircloths; or any thing in which work is done, they shall be dipped in water, and shall be unclean until the evening, and so afterwards shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: et super quod ceciderit quidquam de morticinis eorum, polluetur, tam vas ligneum et vestimentum, quam pelles et cilicia: et in quocumque fit opus, tingentur aqua, et polluta erunt usque ad vesperum, et sic postea mundabuntur.

verses.text: But an earthen vessel, into which any of these shall fall, shall be defiled, and therefore is to be broken.
verses.textLatin: Vas autem fictile, in quod horum quidquam intro cecidit, polluetur, et idcirco frangendum est.

verses.text: Any meat which you eat, if water from such a vessel be poured upon it, shall be unclean; and every liquor that is drunk out of any such vessel, shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Omnis cibus, quem comedetis, si fusa fuerit super eum aqua, immundus erit: et omne liquens quod bibitur de universo vase, immundum erit.

verses.text: And upon whatsoever thing any of these dead beasts shall fall, it shall be unclean: whether it be oven, or pots with feet, they shall be destroyed, and shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Et quidquid de morticinis hujuscemodi ceciderit super illud, immundum erit: sive clibani, sive chytropodes, destruentur, et immundi erunt.

verses.text: But fountains and cisterns, and all gatherings together of waters shall be clean. He that toucheth their carcasses shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Fontes vero et cisternæ, et omnis aquarum congregatio munda erit. Qui morticinum eorum tetigerit, polluetur.

verses.text: If it fall upon seed corn, it shall not defile it.
verses.textLatin: Si ceciderit super sementem, non polluet eam.

verses.text: But if any man pour water upon the seed, and afterwards it be touched by the carcasses, it shall be forthwith defiled.
verses.textLatin: Si autem quispiam aqua sementem perfuderit, et postea morticinis tacta fuerit, illico polluetur.

verses.text: If any beast die, of which it is lawful for you to eat, he that toucheth the carcass thereof, shall be unclean until the evening:
verses.textLatin: Si mortuum fuerit animal, quod licet vobis comedere, qui cadaver ejus tetigerit, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:

verses.text: And he that eateth or carrieth any thing thereof, shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: et qui comederit ex eo quippiam, sive portaverit, lavabit vestimenta sua, et immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: All that creepeth upon the earth shall be abominable, neither shall it be taken for meat.
verses.textLatin: Omne quod reptat super terram, abominabile erit, nec assumetur in cibum.

verses.text: Whatsoever goeth upon the breast on four feet, or hath many feet, or traileth on the earth, you shall not eat, because it is abominable.
verses.textLatin: Quidquid super pectus quadrupes graditur, et multos habet pedes, sive per humum trahitur, non comedetis, quia abominabile est.

verses.text: Do not defile your souls, nor touch aught thereof, lest you be unclean,
verses.textLatin: Nolite contaminare animas vestras, nec tangatis quidquam eorum, ne immundi sitis.

verses.text: For I am the Lord your God: be holy because I am holy. Defile not your souls by any creeping thing, that moveth upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester: sancti estote, quia ego sanctus sum. Ne polluatis animas vestras in omni reptili quod movetur super terram.

verses.text: For I am the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God.
verses.textLatin: Ego enim sum Dominus, qui eduxi vos de terra Ægypti, ut essem vobis in Deum. Sancti eritis, quia ego sanctus sum.

verses.text: You shall be holy, because I am holy. This is the law of beasts and fowls, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and creepeth on the earth:
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex animantium ac volucrum, et omnis animæ viventis, quæ movetur in aqua, et reptat in terra,

verses.text: That you may know the differences of the clean, and unclean, and know what you ought to eat, and what to refuse.
verses.textLatin: ut differentias noveritis mundi et immundi, et sciatis quid comedere et quid respuere debeatis.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: If a woman having received seed shall bear a man child, she shall be unclean seven days, according to the days of the separation of her flowers.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Mulier, si suscepto semine pepererit masculum, immunda erit septem diebus juxta dies separationis menstruæ.

verses.text: And on the eighth day the infant shall be circumcised:
verses.textLatin: Et die octavo circumcidetur infantulus:

verses.text: But she shall remain three and thirty days in the blood of her purification. She shall touch no holy thing, neither shall she enter into the sanctuary, until the days of her purification be fulfilled.
verses.textLatin: ipsa vero triginta tribus diebus manebit in sanguine purificationis suæ. Omne sanctum non tanget, nec ingredietur in sanctuarium, donec impleantur dies purificationis suæ.

verses.text: But if she shall bear a maid child, she shall be unclean two weeks, according to the custom of her monthly courses, and she shall remain in the blood of her purification sixty-six days.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem feminam pepererit, immunda erit duabus hebdomadibus juxta ritum fluxus menstrui, et sexaginta sex diebus manebit in sanguine purificationis suæ.

verses.text: And when the days of her purification are expired, for a son, or for a daughter, she shall bring to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, a lamb of a year old for a holocaust, and a young pigeon or a turtle for sin, and shall deliver them to the priest:
verses.textLatin: Cumque expleti fuerint dies purificationis suæ, pro filio sive pro filia, deferet agnum anniculum in holocaustum, et pullum columbæ sive turturem pro peccato, ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii, et tradet sacerdoti,

verses.text: Who shall offer them before the Lord, and shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed from the issue of her blood. This is the law for her that beareth a man child or a maid child.
verses.textLatin: qui offeret illa coram Domino, et orabit pro ea, et sic mundabitur a profluvio sanguinis sui: ista est lex parientis masculum aut feminam.

verses.text: And if her hand find not sufficiency, and she is not able to offer a lamb, she shall take two turtles, or two young pigeons, one for a holocaust, and another for sin: and the priest shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non invenerit manus ejus, nec potuerit offerre agnum, sumet duos turtures vel duos pullos columbarum, unum in holocaustum, et alterum pro peccato: orabitque pro ea sacerdos, et sic mundabitur.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: The man in whose skin or flesh shall arise a different colour or a blister, or as it were something shining, that is, the stroke of the leprosy, shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or any one of his sons.
verses.textLatin: Homo, in cujus cute et carne ortus fuerit diversus color, sive pustula, aut quasi lucens quippiam, id est, plaga lepræ, adducetur ad Aaron sacerdotem, vel ad unum quemlibet filiorum ejus.

verses.text: And if he see the leprosy in his skin, and the hair turned white, and the place where the leprosy appears lower than the skin and the rest of the flesh: it is the stroke of the leprosy, and upon his judgment he shall be separated.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum viderit lepram in cute, et pilos in album mutatos colorem, ipsamque speciem lepræ humiliorem cute et carne reliqua: plaga lepræ est, et ad arbitrium ejus separabitur.

verses.text: But if there be a shining whiteness in the skin, and not lower than the other flesh, and the hair be of the former colour, the priest shall shut him up seven days.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem lucens candor fuerit in cute, nec humilior carne reliqua, et pili coloris pristini, recludet eum sacerdos septem diebus:

verses.text: And the seventh day he shall look on him: and if the leprosy be grown no farther, and hath not spread itself in the skin, he shall shut him up again other seven days.
verses.textLatin: et considerabit die septimo: et si quidem lepra ultra non creverit, nec transierit in cute priores terminos, rursum recludet eum septem diebus aliis.

verses.text: And on the seventh day, he shall look on him: if the leprosy be somewhat obscure, and not spread in the skin, he shall declare him clean, because it is but a scab: and the man shall wash his clothes, and shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: Et die septimo contemplabitur: si obscurior fuerit lepra, et non creverit in cute, mundabit eum, quia scabies est: lavabitque homo vestimenta sua, et mundus erit.

verses.text: But if the leprosy grow again, after he was seen by the priest and restored to cleanness, he shall be brought to him,
verses.textLatin: Quod si postquam a sacerdote visus est, et redditus munditiæ, iterum lepra creverit: adducetur ad eum,

verses.text: And shall be condemned of uncleanness.
verses.textLatin: et immunditiæ condemnabitur.

verses.text: If the stroke of the leprosy be in a man, he shall be brought to the priest,
verses.textLatin: Plaga lepræ si fuerit in homine, adducetur ad sacerdotem,

verses.text: And he shall view him. And when there shall be a white colour in the skin, and it shall have changed the look of the hair, and the living flesh itself shall appear:
verses.textLatin: et videbit eum. Cumque color albus in cute fuerit, et capillorum mutaverit aspectum, ipsa quoque caro viva apparuerit:

verses.text: It shall be judged an inveterate leprosy, and grown into the skin. The priest therefore shall declare him unclean, and shall not shut him up, because he is evidently unclean.
verses.textLatin: lepra vetustissima judicabitur, atque inolita cuti. Contaminabit itaque eum sacerdos, et non recludet, quia perspicuæ immunditiæ est.

verses.text: But if the leprosy spring out running about in the skin, and cover all the skin from the head to the feet, whatsoever falleth under the sight of the eyes,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem effloruerit discurrens lepra in cute, et operuerit omnem cutem a capite usque ad pedes, quidquid sub aspectum oculorum cadit,

verses.text: The priest shall view him, and shall judge that the leprosy which he has is very clean: because it is all turned into whiteness, and therefore the man shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: considerabit eum sacerdos, et teneri lepra mundissima judicabit: eo quod omnis in candorem versa sit, et idcirco homo mundus erit.

verses.text: But when the live flesh shall appear in him,
verses.textLatin: Quando vero caro vivens in eo apparuerit,

verses.text: Then by the judgment of the priest he shall be defiled, and shall be reckoned among the unclean: for live flesh, if it be spotted with leprosy, is unclean.
verses.textLatin: tunc sacerdotis judicio polluetur, et inter immundos reputabitur: caro enim viva, si lepra aspergitur, immunda est.

verses.text: And if again it be turned into whiteness, and cover all the man,
verses.textLatin: Quod si rursum versa fuerit in alborem, et totum hominem operuerit,

verses.text: The priest shall view him, and shall judge him to be clean.
verses.textLatin: considerabit eum sacerdos, et mundum esse decernet.

verses.text: When also there has been an ulcer in the flesh and the skin, and it has been healed,
verses.textLatin: Caro autem et cutis in qua ulcus natum est, et sanatum,

verses.text: And in the place of the ulcer, there appeareth a white scar, or somewhat red, the man shall be brought to the priest:
verses.textLatin: et in loco ulceris cicatrix alba apparuerit, sive subrufa, adducetur homo ad sacerdotem.

verses.text: And when he shall see the place of the leprosy lower than the other flesh, and the hair turned white, he shall declare him unclean, for the plague of leprosy is broken out in the ulcer.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum viderit locum lepræ humiliorem carne reliqua, et pilos versos in candorem, contaminabit eum: plaga enim lepræ orta est in ulcere.

verses.text: But if the hair be of the former colour, and the scar somewhat obscure, and be not lower than the flesh that is near it, he shall shut him up seven days.
verses.textLatin: Quod si pilus coloris est pristini, et cicatrix subobscura, et vicina carne non est humilior, recludet eum septem diebus:

verses.text: And if it spread, he shall judge him to have the leprosy:
verses.textLatin: et si quidem creverit, adjudicabit eum lepræ;

verses.text: But if it stay in its place, it is but the scar of an ulcer, and the man shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: sin autem steterit in loco suo, ulceris est cicatrix, et homo mundus erit.

verses.text: The flesh also and skin that hath been burnt, and after it is healed hath a white or a red scar,
verses.textLatin: Caro autem et cutis, quam ignis exusserit, et sanata albam sive rufam habuerit cicatricem,

verses.text: The priest shall view it, and if he see it turned white, and the place thereof is lower than the other skin: he shall declare him unclean, because the evil of leprosy is broken out in the scar.
verses.textLatin: considerabit eam sacerdos: et ecce versa est in alborem, et locus ejus reliqua cute est humilior, contaminabit eum, quia plaga lepræ in cicatrice orta est.

verses.text: But if the colour of the hair be not changed, nor the blemish lower than the other flesh, and the appearance of the leprosy be somewhat obscure, he shall shut him up seven days,
verses.textLatin: Quod si pilorum color non fuerit immutatus, nec humilior plaga carne reliqua, et ipsa lepræ species fuerit subobscura, recludet eum septem diebus,

verses.text: And on the seventh day he shall view him: if the leprosy be grown farther in the skin, he shall declare him unclean.
verses.textLatin: et die septimo contemplabitur: si creverit in cute lepra, contaminabit eum.

verses.text: But if the whiteness stay in its place, and be not very clear, it is the sore of a burning, and therefore he shall be cleansed, because it is only the scar of a burning.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem in loco suo candor steterit non satis clarus, plaga combustionis est, et idcirco mundabitur, quia cicatrix est combusturæ.

verses.text: If the leprosy break out in the head or the beard of a man or woman, the priest shall see them,
verses.textLatin: Vir, sive mulier, in cujus capite vel barba germinaverit lepra, videbit eos sacerdos.

verses.text: And if the place be lower than the other flesh, and the hair yellow, and thinner than usual: he shall declare them unclean, because it is the leprosy of the head and the beard;
verses.textLatin: Et si quidem humilior fuerit locus carne reliqua, et capillus flavus, solitoque subtilior, contaminabit eos, quia lepra capitis ac barbæ est.

verses.text: But if he perceive the place of the spot is equal with the flesh that is near it, and the hair black: he shall shut him up seven days,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem viderit locum maculæ æqualem vicinæ carni, et capillum nigrum: recludet eum septem diebus,

verses.text: And on the seventh day he shall look upon it. If the spot be not grown, and the hair keep its colour, and the place of the blemish be even with the other flesh:
verses.textLatin: et die septimo intuebitur. Si non creverit macula, et capillus sui coloris est, et locus plagæ carni reliquæ æqualis:

verses.text: The man shall be shaven all but the place of the spot, and he shall be shut up other seven days:
verses.textLatin: radetur homo absque loco maculæ, et includetur septem diebus aliis.

verses.text: If on the seventh day the evil seem to have stayed in its place, and not lower than the other flesh, he shall cleanse him, and his clothes being washed he shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: Si die septimo visa fuerit stetisse plaga in loco suo, nec humilior carne reliqua, mundabit eum: lotisque vestibus suis, mundus erit.

verses.text: But if after his cleansing the spot spread again in the skin,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem post emundationem rursus creverit macula in cute,

verses.text: He shall seek no more whether the hair be turned yellow, because he is evidently unclean.
verses.textLatin: non quæret amplius utrum capillus in flavum colorem sit immutatus, quia aperte immundus est.

verses.text: But if the spot be stayed, and the hair be black, let him know that the man is healed, and let him confidently pronounce him clean.
verses.textLatin: Porro si steterit macula, et capilli nigri fuerint, noverit hominem sanatum esse, et confidenter eum pronuntiet mundum.

verses.text: If a whiteness appear in the skin of a man or a woman,
verses.textLatin: Vir, sive mulier, in cujus cute candor apparuerit,

verses.text: The priest shall view them. If he find that a darkish whiteness shineth in the skin, let him know that it is not the leprosy, but a white blemish, and that the man is clean.
verses.textLatin: intuebitur eos sacerdos. Si deprehenderit subobscurum alborem lucere in cute, sciat non esse lepram, sed maculam coloris candidi, et hominem mundum.

verses.text: The man whose hair falleth off from his head, he is bald and clean:
verses.textLatin: Vir, de cujus capite capilli fluunt, calvus et mundus est:

verses.text: And if the hair fall from his forehead, he is bald before and clean.
verses.textLatin: et si a fronte ceciderint pili, recalvaster et mundus est.

verses.text: But if in the bald head or in the bald forehead there be risen a white or reddish colour,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem in calvitio sive in recalvatione albus vel rufus color fuerit exortus,

verses.text: And the priest perceive this, he shall condemn him undoubtedly of leprosy which is risen in the bald part.
verses.textLatin: et hoc sacerdos viderit, condemnabit eum haud dubiæ lepræ, quæ orta est in calvitio.

verses.text: Now whosoever shall be defiled with the leprosy, and is separated by the judgment of the priest,
verses.textLatin: Quicumque ergo maculatus fuerit lepra, et separatus est ad arbitrium sacerdotis,

verses.text: Shall have his clothes hanging loose, his head bare, his mouth covered with a cloth, and he shall cry out that he is defiled and unclean.
verses.textLatin: habebit vestimenta dissuta, caput nudum, os veste contectum, contaminatum ac sordidum se clamabit.

verses.text: All the time that he is a leper and unclean, he shall dwell alone without the camp.
verses.textLatin: Omni tempore quo leprosus est et immundus, solus habitabit extra castra.

verses.text: A woollen or linen garment that shall have the leprosy
verses.textLatin: Vestis lanea sive linea, quæ lepram habuerit,

verses.text: In the warp, and the woof, or skin, or whatsoever is made of a skin,
verses.textLatin: in stamine atque subtegmine, aut certe pellis, vel quidquid ex pelle confectum est,

verses.text: If it be infected with a white or red spot, it shall be accounted the leprosy, and shall be shewn to the priest.
verses.textLatin: si alba vel rufa macula fuerit infecta, lepra reputabitur, ostendeturque sacerdoti:

verses.text: And he shall look upon it and shall shut it up seven days:
verses.textLatin: qui consideratam recludet septem diebus:

verses.text: And on the seventh day when he looketh on it again, if he find that it is grown, it is a fixed leprosy: he shall judge the garment unclean, and every thing wherein it shall be found:
verses.textLatin: et die septimo rursus aspiciens, si deprehenderit crevisse, lepra perseverans est: pollutum judicabit vestimentum, et omne in quo fuerit inventa:

verses.text: And therefore it shall be burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: et idcirco comburetur flammis.

verses.text: But if he see that it is not grown,
verses.textLatin: Quod si eam viderit non crevisse,

verses.text: He shall give orders, and they shall wash that part wherein the leprosy is, and he shall shut it up other seven days.
verses.textLatin: præcipiet, et lavabunt id in quo lepra est, recludetque illud septem diebus aliis.

verses.text: And when he shall see that the former colour is not returned, nor yet the leprosy spread, he shall judge it unclean, and shall burn it with fire, for the leprosy has taken hold of the outside of the garment, or through the whole.
verses.textLatin: Et cum viderit faciem quidem pristinam non reversam, nec tamen crevisse lepram, immundum judicabit, et igne comburet, eo quod infusa sit in superficie vestimenti, vel per totum, lepra.

verses.text: But if the place of the leprosy be somewhat dark, after the garment is washed, he shall tear it off, and divide it from that which is sound.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem obscurior fuerit locus lepræ, postquam vestis est lota, abrumpet eum, et a solido dividet.

verses.text: And if after this there appear in those places that before were without spot, a flying and wandering leprosy: it must be burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: Quod si ultra apparuerit in his locis, quæ prius immaculata erant, lepra volatilis et vaga, debet igne comburi.

verses.text: If it cease, he shall wash with water the parts that are pure, the second time, and they shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: Si cessaverit, lavabit aqua ea, quæ pura sunt, secundo, et munda erunt.

verses.text: This is the law touching the leprosy of any woollen or linen garment, either in the warp or woof, or any thing of skins, how it ought to be cleansed, or pronounced unclean.
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex lepræ vestimenti lanei et linei, staminis, atque subtegminis, omnisque supellectilis pelliceæ, quomodo mundari debeat, vel contaminari.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: This is the rite of a leper, when he is to be cleansed: he shall be brought to the priest:
verses.textLatin: Hic est ritus leprosi, quando mundandus est. Adducetur ad sacerdotem:

verses.text: Who going out of the camp when he shall find that the leprosy is cleansed,
verses.textLatin: qui egressus de castris, cum invenerit lepram esse mundatam,

verses.text: Shall command him that is to be purified, to offer for himself two living sparrows, which it is lawful to eat, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.
verses.textLatin: præcipiet ei, qui purificatur, ut offerat duos passeres vivos pro se, quibus vesci licitum est, et lignum cedrinum, vermiculumque et hyssopum.

verses.text: And he shall command one of the sparrows to be immolated in an earthen vessel over living waters:
verses.textLatin: Et unum ex passeribus immolari jubebit in vase fictili super aquas viventes:

verses.text: But the other that is alive he shall dip, with the cedar wood, and the scarlet and the hyssop, in the blood of the sparrow that is immolated:
verses.textLatin: alium autem vivum cum ligno cedrino, et cocco et hyssopo, tinget in sanguine passeris immolati,

verses.text: Wherewith he shall sprinkle him that is to be cleansed seven times, that he may be rightly purified: and he shall let go the living sparrow, that it may fly into the field.
verses.textLatin: quo asperget illum, qui mundandus est, septies, ut jure purgetur: et dimittet passerem vivum, ut in agrum avolet.

verses.text: And when the man hath washed his clothes, he shall shave all the hair of his body, and shall be washed with water: and being purified, he shall enter into the camp, yet so that he tarry without his own tent seven days:
verses.textLatin: Cumque laverit homo vestimenta sua, radet omnes pilos corporis, et lavabitur aqua: purificatusque ingredietur castra, ita dumtaxat ut maneat extra tabernaculum suum septem diebus,

verses.text: And on the seventh day he shall shave the hair of his head, and his beard and his eyebrows, and the hair of all his body. And having washed again his clothes, and his body,
verses.textLatin: et die septimo radet capillos capitis, barbamque et supercilia, ac totius corporis pilos. Et lotis rursum vestibus et corpore,

verses.text: On the eighth day he shall take two lambs without blemish, and an ewe of a year old without blemish, and three tenths of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice, and a sextary of oil apart.
verses.textLatin: die octavo assumet duos agnos immaculatos, et ovem anniculam absque macula, et tres decimas similæ in sacrificium, quæ conspersa sit oleo, et seorsum olei sextarium.

verses.text: And when the priest that purifieth the man, hath presented him, and all these things before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony,
verses.textLatin: Cumque sacerdos purificans hominem, statuerit eum, et hæc omnia coram Domino in ostio tabernaculi testimonii,

verses.text: He shall take a lamb, and offer it for a trespass offering with the sextary of oil: and having offered all before the Lord,
verses.textLatin: tollet agnum et offeret eum pro delicto, oleique sextarium: et oblatis ante Dominum omnibus,

verses.text: He shall immolate the lamb, where the victim for sin is wont to be immolated, and the holocaust, that is, in the holy place: for as that which is for sin, so also the victim for a trespass offering pertaineth to the priest: it is holy of holies.
verses.textLatin: immolabit agnum, ubi solet immolari hostia pro peccato, et holocaustum, id est, in loco sancto. Sicut enim pro peccato, ita et pro delicto ad sacerdotem pertinet hostia: Sancta sanctorum est.

verses.text: And the priest taking of the blood of the victim that was immolated for trespass, shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot:
verses.textLatin: Assumensque sacerdos de sanguine hostiæ, quæ immolata est pro delicto, ponet super extremum auriculæ dextræ ejus qui mundatur, et super pollices manus dextræ et pedis:

verses.text: And he shall pour of the sextary of oil into his own left hand,
verses.textLatin: et de olei sextario mittet in manum suam sinistram,

verses.text: And shall dip his right finger in it, and sprinkle it before the Lord seven times.
verses.textLatin: tingetque digitum dextrum in eo, et asperget coram Domino septies.

verses.text: And the rest of the oil in his left hand, he shall pour upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot, and upon the blood that was shed for trespass,
verses.textLatin: Quod autem reliquum est olei in læva manu, fundet super extremum auriculæ dextræ ejus qui mundatur, et super pollices manus ac pedis dextri, et super sanguinem qui effusus est pro delicto,

verses.text: And upon his head.
verses.textLatin: et super caput ejus.

verses.text: And he shall pray for him before the Lord, and shall offer the sacrifice for sin: then shall he immolate the holocaust,
verses.textLatin: Rogabitque pro eo coram Domino, et faciet sacrificium pro peccato: tunc immolabit holocaustum,

verses.text: And put it on the altar with the libations thereof, and the man shall be rightly cleansed.
verses.textLatin: et ponet illud in altari cum libamentis suis, et homo rite mundabitur.

verses.text: But if he be poor, and his hand cannot find the things aforesaid: he shall take a lamb for an offering for trespass, that the priest may pray for him, and a tenth part of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice, and a sextary of oil,
verses.textLatin: Quod si pauper est, et non potest manus ejus invenire quæ dicta sunt pro delicto, assumet agnum ad oblationem, ut roget pro eo sacerdos, decimamque partem similæ conspersæ oleo in sacrificium, et olei sextarium,

verses.text: And two turtles or two young pigeons, of which one may be for sin, and the other for a holocaust:
verses.textLatin: duosque turtures sive duos pullos columbæ, quorum unus sit pro peccato, et alter in holocaustum:

verses.text: And he shall offer them on the eighth day of his purification to the priest, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: offeretque ea die octavo purificationis suæ sacerdoti, ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii coram Domino.

verses.text: And the priest receiving the lamb for trespass, and the sextary of oil, shall elevate them together.
verses.textLatin: Qui suscipiens agnum pro delicto et sextarium olei, levabit simul:

verses.text: And the lamb being immolated, he shall put of the blood thereof upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and the great toe of his right foot:
verses.textLatin: immolatoque agno, de sanguine ejus ponet super extremum auriculæ dextræ illius qui mundatur, et super pollices manus ejus ac pedis dextri:

verses.text: But he shall pour part of the oil into his own left hand,
verses.textLatin: olei vero partem mittet in manum suam sinistram,

verses.text: And dipping the finger of his right hand in it, he shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord:
verses.textLatin: in quo tingens digitum dextræ manus asperget septies coram Domino:

verses.text: And he shall touch the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot, in the place of the blood that was shed for trespass.
verses.textLatin: tangetque extremum dextræ auriculæ illius qui mundatur, et pollices manus ac pedis dextri, in loco sanguinis qui effusus est pro delicto:

verses.text: And the other part of the oil that is in his left hand, he shall pour upon the head of the purified person, that he may appease the Lord for him.
verses.textLatin: reliquam autem partem olei, quæ est in sinistra manu, mittet super caput purificati, ut placet pro eo Dominum:

verses.text: And he shall offer a turtle, or young pigeon,
verses.textLatin: et turturem sive pullum columbæ offeret,

verses.text: One for trespass, and the other for a holocaust, with their libations.
verses.textLatin: unum pro delicto, et alterum in holocaustum cum libamentis suis.

verses.text: This is the sacrifice of a leper, that is not able to have all things that appertain to his cleansing.
verses.textLatin: Hoc est sacrificium leprosi, qui habere non potest omnia in emundationem sui.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: When you shall come into the land of Chanaan, which I will give you for a possession, if there be the plague of leprosy in a house,
verses.textLatin: Cum ingressi fueritis terram Chanaan, quam ego dabo vobis in possessionem, si fuerit plaga lepræ in ædibus,

verses.text: He whose house it is, shall go and tell the priest, saying: It seemeth to me, that there is the plague of leprosy in my house,
verses.textLatin: ibit cujus est domus, nuntians sacerdoti, et dicet: Quasi plaga lepræ videtur mihi esse in domo mea.

verses.text: And he shall command, that they carry forth all things out of the house, before he go into it, and see whether it have the leprosy, lest all things become unclean that are in the house. And afterwards he shall go in to view the leprosy of the house.
verses.textLatin: At ille præcipiet ut efferant universa de domo, priusquam ingrediatur eam, et videat utrum leprosa sit, ne immunda fiant omnia quæ in domo sunt. Intrabitque postea ut consideret lepram domus:

verses.text: And if he see in the walls thereof as it were little dints, disfigured with paleness or redness, and lower than all the rest,
verses.textLatin: et cum viderit in parietibus illius quasi valliculas pallore sive rubore deformes, et humiliores superficie reliqua,

verses.text: He shall go out of the door of the house, and forthwith shut it up seven days,
verses.textLatin: egredietur ostium domus, et statim claudet illam septem diebus.

verses.text: And returning on the seventh day, he shall look upon it. If he find that the leprosy is spread,
verses.textLatin: Reversusque die septimo, considerabit eam: si invenerit crevisse lepram,

verses.text: He shall command, that the stones wherein the leprosy is, be taken out, and cast without the city into an unclean place:
verses.textLatin: jubebit erui lapides in quibus lepra est, et projici eos extra civitatem in locum immundum:

verses.text: And that the house be scraped on the inside round about, and the dust of the scraping be scattered without the city into an unclean place:
verses.textLatin: domum autem ipsam radi intrinsecus per circuitum, et spargi pulverem rasuræ extra urbem in locum immundum,

verses.text: And that other stones be laid in the place of them that were taken away, and the house be plastered with other mortar.
verses.textLatin: lapidesque alios reponi pro his qui ablati fuerint, et luto alio liniri domum.

verses.text: But if, after the stones be taken out, and the dust scraped off, and it be plastered with other earth,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem postquam eruti sunt lapides, et pulvis erasus, et alia terra lita,

verses.text: The priest going in perceive that the leprosy is returned, and the walls full of spots, it is a lasting leprosy, and the house is unclean:
verses.textLatin: ingressus sacerdos viderit reversam lepram, et parietes respersos maculis, lepra est perseverans, et immunda domus:

verses.text: And they shall destroy it forthwith, and shall cast the stones and timber thereof, and all the dust without the town into an unclean place.
verses.textLatin: quam statim destruent, et lapides ejus ac ligna, atque universum pulverem projicient extra oppidum in locum immundum.

verses.text: He that entereth into the house when it is shut, shall be unclean until evening,
verses.textLatin: Qui intraverit domum quando clausa est, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:

verses.text: And he that sleepeth in it, and eateth any thing, shall wash his clothes.
verses.textLatin: et qui dormierit in ea, et comederit quippiam, lavabit vestimenta sua.

verses.text: But if the priest going in perceive that the leprosy is not spread in the house, after it was plastered again, he shall purify it, it being cured,
verses.textLatin: Quod si introiens sacerdos viderit lepram non crevisse in domo, postquam denuo lita fuerit, purificabit eam reddita sanitate:

verses.text: And for the purification thereof he shall take two sparrows, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:
verses.textLatin: et in purificationem ejus sumet duos passeres, lignumque cedrinum, et vermiculum atque hyssopum:

verses.text: And having immolated one sparrow in an earthen vessel over living waters,
verses.textLatin: et immolato uno passere in vase fictili super aquas vivas,

verses.text: He shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living sparrow, and shall dip all in the blood of the sparrow that is immolated, and in the living water, and he shall sprinkle the house seven times:
verses.textLatin: tollet lignum cedrinum, et hyssopum, et coccum, et passerem vivum, et tinget omnia in sanguine passeris immolati, atque in aquis viventibus, et asperget domum septies,

verses.text: And shall purify it as well with the blood of the sparrow, as with the living water, and with the living sparrow, and with the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet.
verses.textLatin: purificabitque eam tam in sanguine passeris quam in aquis viventibus, et in passere vivo, lignoque cedrino et hyssopo atque vermiculo.

verses.text: And when he hath let go the sparrow to fly freely away into the field, he shall pray for the house, and it shall be rightly cleansed.
verses.textLatin: Cumque dimiserit passerem avolare in agrum libere, orabit pro domo, et jure mundabitur.

verses.text: This is the law of every kind of leprosy and stroke.
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex omnis lepræ et percussuræ,

verses.text: Of the leprosy of garments and houses,
verses.textLatin: lepræ vestium et domorum,

verses.text: Of a scar and of blisters breaking out, of a shining spot, and when the colours are diversely changed:
verses.textLatin: cicatricis et erumpentium papularum, lucentis maculæ, et in varias species, coloribus immutatis,

verses.text: That it may be known when a thing is clean or unclean.
verses.textLatin: ut possit sciri quo tempore mundum quid, vel immundum sit.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: The man that hath an issue of seed, shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Loquimini filiis Israël, et dicite eis: Vir, qui patitur fluxum seminis, immundus erit.

verses.text: And then shall he be judged subject to this evil, when a filthy humour, at every moment, cleaveth to his flesh, and gathereth there.
verses.textLatin: Et tunc judicabitur huic vitio subjacere, cum per singula momenta adhæserit carni ejus, atque concreverit fœdus humor.

verses.text: Every bed on which he sleepeth, shall be unclean, and every place on which he sitteth.
verses.textLatin: Omne stratum, in quo dormierit, immundum erit, et ubicumque sederit.

verses.text: If any man touch his bed, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Si quis hominum tetigerit lectum ejus, lavabit vestimenta sua, et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: If a man sit where that man hath sitten, he also shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Si sederit ubi ille sederat, et ipse lavabit vestimenta sua: et lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: He that toucheth his flesh, shall wash his clothes: and being himself washed with water shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Qui tetigerit carnem ejus, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: If such a man cast his spittle upon him that is clean, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Si salivam hujuscemodi homo jecerit super eum qui mundus est, lavabit vestimenta sua: et lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: The saddle on which he hath sitten shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Sagma, super quo sederit, immundum erit:

verses.text: And whatsoever has been under him that hath the issue of seed, shall be unclean until the evening. He that carrieth any of these things, shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: et quidquid sub eo fuerit, qui fluxum seminis patitur, pollutum erit usque ad vesperum. Qui portaverit horum aliquid, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: Every person whom such a one shall touch, not having washed his hands before, shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Omnis, quem tetigerit qui talis est, non lotis ante manibus, lavabit vestimenta sua, et lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: If he touch a vessel of earth, it shall be broken: but if a vessel of wood, it shall be washed with water.
verses.textLatin: Vas fictile quod tetigerit confringetur: vas autem ligneum lavabitur aqua.

verses.text: If he who suffereth this disease be healed, he shall number seven days after his cleansing, and having washed his clothes, and all his body in living water, he shall be clean.
verses.textLatin: Si sanatus fuerit qui hujuscemodi sustinet passionem, numerabit septem dies post emundationem sui, et lotis vestibus et toto corpore in aquis viventibus, erit mundus.

verses.text: And on the eighth day he shall take two turtles, or two young pigeons, and he shall come before the Lord, to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall give them to the priest:
verses.textLatin: Die autem octavo sumet duos turtures, aut duos pullos columbæ, et veniet in conspectum Domini ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii, dabitque eos sacerdoti:

verses.text: Who shall offer one for sin, and the other for a holocaust: and he shall pray for him before the Lord, that he may be cleansed of the issue of his seed.
verses.textLatin: qui faciet unum pro peccato et alterum in holocaustum: rogabitque pro eo coram Domino, ut emundetur a fluxi seminis sui.

verses.text: The man from whom the seed of copulation goeth out, shall wash all his body with water: and he shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Vir de quo egreditur semen coitus, lavabit aqua omne corpus suum: et immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: The garment or skin that he weareth, he shall wash with water, and it shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Vestem et pellem, quam habuerit, lavabit aqua, et immunda erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: The woman, with whom he copulateth, shall be washed with water, and shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Mulier, cum qua coierit, lavabitur aqua, et immunda erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: The woman, who at the return of the month, hath her issue of blood, shall be separated seven days.
verses.textLatin: Mulier, quæ redeunte mense patitur fluxum sanguinis, septem diebus separabitur.

verses.text: Every one that toucheth her, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Omnis qui tetigerit eam, immundus erit usque ad vesperum:

verses.text: And every thing that she sleepeth on, or that she sitteth on in the days of her separation, shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: et in quo dormierit vel sederit diebus separationis suæ, polluetur.

verses.text: He that toucheth her bed shall wash his clothes: and being himself washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Qui tetigerit lectum ejus, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: Whosoever shall touch any vessel on which she sitteth, shall wash his clothes: and himself being washed with water, shall be defiled until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Omne vas, super quo illa sederit, quisquis attigerit, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, pollutus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: If a man copulateth with her in the time of her flowers, he shall be unclean seven days: and every bed on which he shall sleep shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Si coierit cum ea vir tempore sanguinis menstrualis, immundus erit septem diebus: et omne stratum, in quo dormierit, polluetur.

verses.text: The woman that hath an issue of blood many days out of her ordinary time, or that ceaseth not to flow after the monthly courses, as long as she is subject to this disease, shall be unclean, in the same manner as if she were in her flowers.
verses.textLatin: Mulier, quæ patitur multis diebus fluxum sanguinis non in tempore menstruali, vel quæ post menstruum sanguinem fluere non cessat, quamdiu subjacet huic passioni, immunda erit quasi sit in tempore menstruo.

verses.text: Every bed on which she sleepeth, and every vessel on which she sitteth, shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Omne stratum, in quo dormierit, et vas in quo sederit, pollutum erit.

verses.text: Whosoever toucheth them shall wash his clothes: and himself being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Quicumque tetigerit ea, lavabit vestimenta sua: et ipse lotus aqua, immundus erit usque ad vesperam.

verses.text: If the blood stop and cease to run, she shall count seven days of her purification:
verses.textLatin: Si steterit sanguis, et fluere cessaverit, numerabit septem dies purificationis suæ:

verses.text: And on the eighth day she shall offer for herself to the priest, two turtles, or two young pigeons, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:
verses.textLatin: et die octavo offeret pro se sacerdoti duos turtures, aut duos pullos columbarum, ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii:

verses.text: And he shall offer one for sin, and the other for a holocaust, and he shall pray for her before the Lord, and for the issue of her uncleanness.
verses.textLatin: qui unum faciet pro peccato, et alterum in holocaustum, rogabitque pro ea coram Domino, et pro fluxu immunditiæ ejus.

verses.text: You shall teach therefore the children of Israel to take heed of uncleanness, that they may not die in their filth, when they shall have defiled my tabernacle that is among them.
verses.textLatin: Docebitis ergo filios Israël ut caveant immunditiam, et non moriantur in sordibus suis, cum polluerint tabernaculum meum quod est inter eos.

verses.text: This is the law of him that hath the issue of seed, and that is defiled by copulation.
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex ejus, qui patitur fluxum seminis, et qui polluitur coitu,

verses.text: And of the woman that is separated in her monthly times, or that hath a continual issue of blood, and of the man that sleepeth with her.
verses.textLatin: et quæ menstruis temporibus separatur, vel quæ jugi fluit sanguine, et hominis qui dormierit cum ea.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they were slain upon their offering strange fire:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen post mortem duorum filiorum Aaron, quando offerentes ignem alienum interfecti sunt:

verses.text: And he commanded him, saying Speak to Aaron thy brother, that he enter not at all into the sanctuary, which is within the veil before the propitiatory, with which the ark is covered, lest he die, (for I will appear in a cloud over the oracle,)
verses.textLatin: et præcepit ei, dicens: Loquere ad Aaron fratrem tuum, ne omni tempore ingrediatur sanctuarium, quod est intra velum coram propitiatorio quo tegitur arca, ut non moriatur (quia in nube apparebo super oraculum),

verses.text: Unless he first do these things: He shall offer a calf for sin, and a ram for a holocaust.
verses.textLatin: nisi hæc ante fecerit: vitulum pro peccato offeret, et arietem in holocaustum.

verses.text: He shall be vested with a linen tunick, he shall cover his nakedness with linen breeches: he shall be girded with a linen girdle, and he shall put a linen mitre upon his head: for these are holy vestments: all which he shall put on, after he is washed.
verses.textLatin: Tunica linea vestietur, feminalibus lineis verenda celabit: accingetur zona linea, cidarim lineam imponet capiti: hæc enim vestimenta sunt sancta: quibus cunctis, cum lotus fuerit, induetur.

verses.text: And he shall receive from the whole multitude of the children of Israel two buck goats for sin, and one ram for a holocaust.
verses.textLatin: Suscipietque ab universa multitudine filiorum Israël duos hircos pro peccato, et unum arietem in holocaustum.

verses.text: And when he hath offered the calf and prayed for himself, and for his own house,
verses.textLatin: Cumque obtulerit vitulum, et oraverit pro se et pro domo sua,

verses.text: He shall make the two buck goats to stand before the Lord in the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:
verses.textLatin: duos hircos stare faciet coram Domino in ostio tabernaculi testimonii:

verses.text: And casting lots upon them both, one to be offered to the Lord, and the other to be the emissary goat:
verses.textLatin: mittensque super utrumque sortem, unam Domino, alteram capro emissario:

verses.text: That whose lot fell to be offered to the Lord, he shall offer for sin:
verses.textLatin: cujus exierit sors Domino, offeret illum pro peccato:

verses.text: But that whose lot was to be the emissary goat, he shall present alive before the Lord, that he may pour out prayers upon him, and let him go into the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: cujus autem in caprum emissarium, statuet eum vivum coram Domino, ut fundat preces super eo, et emittat eum in solitudinem.

verses.text: After these things are duly celebrated, he shall offer the calf, and praying for himself and for his own house, he shall immolate it:
verses.textLatin: His rite celebratis, offeret vitulum, et rogans pro se, et pro domo sua, immolabit eum:

verses.text: And taking the censer, which he hath filled with the burning coals of the altar, and taking up with his hands the compounded perfume for incense, he shall go in within the veil into the holy place:
verses.textLatin: assumptoque thuribulo, quod de prunis altaris impleverit, et hauriens manu compositum thymiama in incensum, ultra velum intrabit in sancta:

verses.text: That when the perfumes are put upon the fire, the cloud and vapour thereof may cover the oracle, which is over the testimony, and he may not die.
verses.textLatin: ut, positis super ignem aromatibus, nebula eorum et vapor operiat oraculum quod est supra testimonium, et non moriatur.

verses.text: He shall take also of the blood of the calf, and sprinkle with his finger seven times towards the propitiatory to the east.
verses.textLatin: Tollet quoque de sanguine vituli, et asperget digito septies contra propitiatorium ad orientem.

verses.text: And when he hath killed the buck goat for the sin of the people, he shall carry in the blood thereof within the veil, as he was commanded to do with the blood of the calf, that he may sprinkle it over against the oracle,
verses.textLatin: Cumque mactaverit hircum pro peccato populi, inferet sanguinem ejus intra velum, sicut præceptum est de sanguine vituli, ut aspergat e regione oraculi,

verses.text: And may expiate the sanctuary from the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and from their transgressions, and all their sins. According to this rite shall he do to the tabernacle of the testimony, which is fixed among them in the midst of the filth of their habitation.
verses.textLatin: et expiet sanctuarium ab immunditiis filiorum Israël, et a prævaricationibus eorum, cunctisque peccatis. Juxta hunc ritum faciet tabernaculo testimonii, quod fixum est inter eos, in medio sordium habitationis eorum.

verses.text: Let no man be in the tabernacle when the high priest goeth into the sanctuary, to pray for himself and his house, and for the whole congregation of Israel, until he come out.
verses.textLatin: Nullus hominum sit in tabernaculo, quando pontifex sanctuarium ingreditur, ut roget pro se, et pro domo sua, et pro universo cœtu Israël, donec egrediatur.

verses.text: And when he is come out to the altar that is before the Lord, let him pray for himself, and taking the blood of the calf, and of the buck goat, let him pour it upon the horns thereof round about:
verses.textLatin: Cum autem exierit ad altare quod coram Domino est, oret pro se, et sumptum sanguinem vituli atque hirci fundat super cornua ejus per gyrum:

verses.text: And sprinkling with his finger seven times, let him expiate, and sanctify it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: aspergensque digito septies, expiet, et sanctificet illud ab immunditiis filiorum Israël.

verses.text: After he hath cleansed the sanctuary, and the tabernacle, and the altar, then let him offer the living goat:
verses.textLatin: Postquam emundaverit sanctuarium, et tabernaculum, et altare, tunc offerat hircum viventem:

verses.text: And putting both hands upon his head, let him confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their offences and sins: and praying that they may light on its head, he shall turn him out by a man ready for it, into the desert.
verses.textLatin: et posita utraque manu super caput ejus, confiteatur omnes iniquitates filiorum Israël, et universa delicta atque peccata eorum: quæ imprecans capiti ejus, emittet illum per hominem paratum, in desertum.

verses.text: And when the goat hath carried all their iniquities into an uninhabited land, and shall be let go into the desert,
verses.textLatin: Cumque portaverit hircus omnes iniquitates eorum in terram solitariam, et dimissus fuerit in deserto,

verses.text: Aaron shall return into the tabernacle of the testimony, and putting off the vestments, which he had on him before when he entered into the sanctuary, and leaving them there,
verses.textLatin: revertetur Aaron in tabernaculum testimonii, et depositis vestibus, quibus prius indutus erat, cum intraret sanctuarium, relictisque ibi,

verses.text: He shall wash his flesh in the holy place, and shall put on his own garments. And after that he has come out and hath offered his own holocaust, and that of the people, he shall pray both for himself, and for the people:
verses.textLatin: lavabit carnem suam in loco sancto, indueturque vestibus suis. Et postquam egressus obtulerit holocaustum suum, ac plebis, rogabit tam pro se quam pro populo:

verses.text: And the fat that is offered for sins, he shall burn upon the altar.
verses.textLatin: et adipem, qui oblatus est pro peccatis, adolebit super altare.

verses.text: But he that hath let go the emissary goat, shall wash his clothes, and his body with water, and so shall enter into the camp.
verses.textLatin: Ille vero, qui dimiserit caprum emissarium, lavabit vestimenta sua, et corpus aqua, et sic ingredietur in castra.

verses.text: But the calf and the buck goat, that were sacrificed for sin, and whose blood was carried into the sanctuary, to accomplish the atonement, they shall carry forth without the camp, and shall burn with fire, their skins and their flesh, and their dung:
verses.textLatin: Vitulum autem, et hircum, qui pro peccato fuerant immolati, et quorum sanguis illatus est in sanctuarium, ut expiatio compleretur, asportabunt foras castra, et comburent igni tam pelles quam carnes eorum, ac fimum:

verses.text: And whosoever burneth them shall wash his clothes, and flesh with water, and so shall enter into the camp.
verses.textLatin: et quicumque combusserit ea, lavabit vestimenta sua et carnem aqua, et sic ingredietur in castra.

verses.text: And this shall be to you an everlasting ordinance: The seventh month, the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no work, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you.
verses.textLatin: Eritque vobis hoc legitimum sempiternum: mense septimo, decima die mensis, affligetis animas vestras, nullumque opus facietis, sive indigena, sive advena qui peregrinatur inter vos.

verses.text: Upon this day shall be the expiation for you, and the cleansing from all your sins: you shall be cleansed before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: In hac die expiatio erit vestri, atque mundatio ab omnibus peccatis vestris: coram Domino mundabimini.

verses.text: For it is a sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls by a perpetual religion.
verses.textLatin: Sabbatum enim requietionis est, et affligetis animas vestras religione perpetua.

verses.text: And the priest that is anointed, and whose hands are consecrated to do the office of the priesthood in his father’s stead, shall make atonement; and he shall be vested with the linen robe and the holy vestments,
verses.textLatin: Expiabit autem sacerdos, qui unctus fuerit, et cujus manus initiatæ sunt ut sacerdotio fungatur pro patre suo: indueturque stola linea et vestibus sanctis,

verses.text: And he shall expiate the sanctuary and the tabernacle of the testimony and the altar, the priest also and all the people.
verses.textLatin: et expiabit sanctuarium et tabernaculum testimonii atque altare, sacerdotes quoque et universum populum.

verses.text: And this shall be an ordinance for ever, that you pray for the children of Israel, and for all their sins once in a year. He did therefore as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: Eritque vobis hoc legitimum sempiternum, ut oretis pro filiis Israël, et pro cunctis peccatis eorum semel in anno. Fecit igitur sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel, saying to them: This is the word, which the Lord hath commanded, saying:
verses.textLatin: Loquere Aaron et filiis ejus, et cunctis filiis Israël, dicens ad eos: Iste est sermo quem mandavit Dominus, dicens:

verses.text: Any man whosoever of the house of Israel if he kill an ox, or a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or without the camp,
verses.textLatin: Homo quilibet de domo Israël, si occiderit bovem aut ovem, sive capram, in castris vel extra castra,

verses.text: And offer it not at the door of the tabernacle an oblation to the Lord, shall be guilty of blood: as if he had shed blood, so shall he perish from the midst of his people.
verses.textLatin: et non obtulerit ad ostium tabernaculi oblationem Domino, sanguinis reus erit: quasi si sanguinem fuderit, sic peribit de medio populi sui.

verses.text: Therefore the children of Israel shall bring to the priest their victims, which they kill in the field, that they may be sanctified to the Lord before the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and they may sacrifice them for peace offerings to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ideo sacerdoti offerre debent filii Israël hostias suas, quas occident in agro, ut sanctificentur Domino ante ostium tabernaculi testimonii, et immolent eas hostias pacificas Domino.

verses.text: And the priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall burn the fat for a sweet odour to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Fundetque sacerdos sanguinem super altare Domini ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii, et adolebit adipem in odorem suavitatis Domino:

verses.text: And they shall no more sacrifice their victims to devils, with whom they have committed fornication. It shall be an ordinance for ever to them and to their posterity.
verses.textLatin: et nequaquam ultra immolabunt hostias suas dæmonibus, cum quibus fornicati sunt. Legitimum sempiternum erit illis et posteris eorum.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to them: The man of the house of Israel, and of the strangers who sojourn among you, that offereth a holocaust or a victim,
verses.textLatin: Et ad ipsos dices: Homo de domo Israël, et de advenis qui peregrinantur apud vos, qui obtulerit holocaustum sive victimam,

verses.text: And bringeth it not to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, that it may be offered to the Lord, shall perish from among his people.
verses.textLatin: et ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii non adduxerit eam, ut offeratur Domino, interibit de populo suo.

verses.text: If any man whosoever of the house of Israel, and of the strangers that sojourn among them, eat blood, I will set my face against his soul, and will cut him off from among his people:
verses.textLatin: Homo quilibet de domo Israël et de advenis qui peregrinantur inter eos, si comederit sanguinem, obfirmabo faciem meam contra animam illius, et disperdam eam de populo suo,

verses.text: Because the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you, that you may make atonement with it upon the altar for your souls, and the blood may be for an expiation of the soul.
verses.textLatin: quia anima carnis in sanguine est: et ego dedi illum vobis, ut super altare in eo expietis pro animabus vestris, et sanguis pro animæ piaculo sit.

verses.text: Therefore I have said to the children of Israel: No soul of you, nor of the strangers that sojourn among you, shall eat blood.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco dixi filiis Israël: Omnis anima ex vobis non comedet sanguinem, nec ex advenis qui peregrinantur apud vos.

verses.text: Any man whosoever of the children of Israel, and of the strangers that sojourn among you, if by hunting or fowling, he take a wild beast or a bird, which is lawful to eat, let him pour out its blood, and cover it with earth.
verses.textLatin: Homo quicumque de filiis Israël, et de advenis qui peregrinantur apud vos, si venatione atque aucupio ceperit feram, vel avem, quibus vesci licitum est, fundat sanguinem ejus, et operiat illum terra.

verses.text: For the life of all flesh is in the blood: therefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh at all, because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and whosoever eateth it, shall be cut off.
verses.textLatin: Anima enim omnis carnis in sanguine est: unde dixi filiis Israël: Sanguinem universæ carnis non comedetis, quia anima carnis in sanguine est: et quicumque comederit illum, interibit.

verses.text: The soul that eateth that which died of itself, or has been caught by a beast, whether he be one of your own country or a stranger, shall wash his clothes and himself with water, and shall be defiled until the evening: and in this manner he shall be made clean.
verses.textLatin: Anima, quæ comederit morticinum, vel captum a bestia, tam de indigenis, quam de advenis, lavabit vestimenta sua et semetipsum aqua, et contaminatus erit usque ad vesperum: et hoc ordine mundus fiet.

verses.text: But if he do not wash his clothes, and his body, he shall bear his iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non laverit vestimenta sua et corpus, portabit iniquitatem suam.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Ego Dominus Deus vester:

verses.text: You shall not do according to the custom of the land of Egypt, in which you dwelt: neither shall you act according to the manner of the country of Chanaan, into which I will bring you, nor shall you walk in their ordinances.
verses.textLatin: juxta consuetudinem terræ Ægypti, in qua habitastis, non facietis: et juxta morem regionis Chanaan, ad quam ego introducturus sum vos, non agetis, nec in legitimis eorum ambulabitis.

verses.text: You shall do my judgments, and shall observe my precepts, and shall walk in them. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Facietis judicia mea, et præcepta mea servabitis, et ambulabitis in eis. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Keep my laws and my judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Custodite leges meas atque judicia, quæ faciens homo, vivet in eis. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: No man shall approach to her that is near of kin to him, to uncover her nakedness. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Omnis homo ad proximam sanguinis sui non accedet, ut revelet turpitudinem ejus. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother: she is thy mother, thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem patris tui et turpitudinem matris tuæ non discooperies: mater tua est: non revelabis turpitudinem ejus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s wife: for it is the nakedness of thy father.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem uxoris patris tui non discooperies: turpitudo enim patris tui est.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy sister by father or by mother, whether born at home or abroad.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem sororis tuæ ex patre sive ex matre, quæ domi vel foris genita est, non revelabis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy son’s daughter, or thy daughter’s daughter: because it is thy own nakedness.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem filiæ filii tui vel neptis ex filia non revelabis: quia turpitudo tua est.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s wife’s daughter, whom she bore to thy father, and who is thy sister.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem filiæ uxoris patris tui, quam peperit patri tuo, et est soror tua, non revelabis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s sister: because she is the flesh of thy father.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem sororis patris tui non discooperies: quia caro est patris tui.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister: because she is thy mother’s flesh.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem sororis matris tuæ non revelabis, eo quod caro sit matris tuæ.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s brother: neither shalt thou approach to his wife, who is joined to thee by affinity.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem patrui tui non revelabis, nec accedes ad uxorem ejus, quæ tibi affinitate conjungitur.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy daughter in law: because she is thy son’s wife, neither shalt thou discover her shame.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem nurus tuæ non revelabis, quia uxor filii tui est: nec discooperies ignominiam ejus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s wife: because it is the nakedness of thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem uxoris fratris tui non revelabis: quia turpitudo fratris tui est.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy wife and her daughter. Thou shalt not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter, to discover her shame: because they are her flesh, and such copulation is incest.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem uxoris tuæ et filiæ ejus non revelabis. Filiam filii ejus, et filiam filiæ illius non sumes, ut reveles ignominiam ejus: quia caro illius sunt, et talis coitus incestus est.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take thy wife’s sister for a harlot, to rival her, neither shalt thou discover her nakedness, while she is yet living.
verses.textLatin: Sororem uxoris tuæ in pellicatum illius non accipies, nec revelabis turpitudinem ejus adhuc illa vivente.

verses.text: Thou shalt not approach to a woman having her flowers, neither shalt thou uncover her nakedness.
verses.textLatin: Ad mulierem quæ patitur menstrua non accedes, nec revelabis fœditatem ejus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not lie with thy neighbour’s wife, nor be defiled with mingling of seed.
verses.textLatin: Cum uxore proximi tui non coibis, nec seminis commistione maculaberis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not give any of thy seed to be consecrated to the idol Moloch, nor defile the name of thy God: I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: De semine tuo non dabis ut consecretur idolo Moloch, nec pollues nomen Dei tui. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not lie with mankind as with womankind, because it is an abomination.
verses.textLatin: Cum masculo non commiscearis coitu femineo, quia abominatio est.

verses.text: Thou shalt not copulate with any beast, neither shalt thou be defiled with it. A woman shall not lie down to a beast, nor copulate with it: because it is a heinous crime.
verses.textLatin: Cum omni pecore non coibis, nec maculaberis cum eo. Mulier non succumbet jumento, nec miscebitur ei, quia scelus est.

verses.text: Defile not yourselves with any of these things with which all the nations have been defiled, which I will cast out before you,
verses.textLatin: Nec polluamini in omnibus his quibus contaminatæ sunt universæ gentes, quas ego ejiciam ante conspectum vestrum,

verses.text: And with which the land is defiled: the abominations of which I will visit, that it may vomit out its inhabitants.
verses.textLatin: et quibus polluta est terra: cujus ego scelera visitabo, ut evomat habitatores suos.

verses.text: Keep ye my ordinances and my judgments, and do not any of these abominations: neither any of your own nation, nor any stranger that sojourneth among you.
verses.textLatin: Custodite legitima mea atque judicia, et non faciatis ex omnibus abominationibus istis, tam indigena quam colonus qui peregrinantur apud vos.

verses.text: For all these detestable things the inhabitants of the land have done, that were before you, and have defiled it.
verses.textLatin: Omnes enim execrationes istas fecerunt accolæ terræ qui fuerunt ante vos, et polluerunt eam.

verses.text: Beware then, lest in like manner, it vomit you also out, if you do the like things, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
