verses.textLatin: Cavete ergo ne et vos similiter evomat, cum paria feceritis, sicut evomuit gentem, quæ fuit ante vos.

verses.text: Every soul that shall commit any of these abominations, shall perish from the midst of his people.
verses.textLatin: Omnis anima, quæ fecerit de abominationibus his quippiam, peribit de medio populi sui.

verses.text: Keep my commandments. Do not the things which they have done, that have been before you, and be not defiled therein. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Custodite mandata mea. Nolite facere quæ fecerunt hi qui fuerunt ante vos, et ne polluamini in eis. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: The  Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: Be ye holy, because I the Lord your God am holy.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad omnem cœtum filiorum Israël, et dices ad eos: Sancti estote, quia ego sanctus sum, Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Let every one fear his father, and his mother. Keep my sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Unusquisque patrem suum, et matrem suam timeat. Sabbata mea custodite. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Turn ye not to idols, nor make to yourselves molten gods. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Nolite converti ad idola, nec deos conflatiles faciatis vobis. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: If ye offer in sacrifice a peace offering to the Lord, that he may be favourable,
verses.textLatin: Si immolaveritis hostiam pacificorum Domino, ut sit placabilis,

verses.text: You shall eat it on the same day it was offered, and the next day: and whatsoever shall be left until the third day, you shall burn with fire.
verses.textLatin: eo die quo fuerit immolata, comedetis eam, et die altero: quidquid autem residuum fuerit in diem tertium, igne comburetis.

verses.text: If after two days any man eat thereof, he shall be profane and guilty of impiety:
verses.textLatin: Si quis post biduum comederit ex ea, profanus erit, et impietatis reus:

verses.text: And shall bear his iniquity, because he hath defiled the holy thing of the Lord, and that soul shall perish from among his people.
verses.textLatin: portabitque iniquitatem suam, quia sanctum Domini polluit, et peribit anima illa de populo suo.

verses.text: When thou reapest the corn of thy land, thou shalt not cut down all that is on the face of the earth to the very ground: nor shalt thou gather the ears that remain.
verses.textLatin: Cumque messueris segetes terræ tuæ, non tondebis usque ad solum superficiem terræ, nec remanentes spicas colliges,

verses.text: Neither shalt thou gather the bunches and grapes that fall down in thy vineyard, but shalt leave them to the poor and the strangers to take. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: neque in vinea tua racemos et grana decidentia congregabis: sed pauperibus et peregrinis carpenda dimittes. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: You shall not steal. You shall not lie, neither shall any man deceive his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Non facietis furtum. Non mentiemini, nec decipiet unusquisque proximum suum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not swear falsely by my name, nor profane the name of thy God. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non perjurabis in nomine meo, nec pollues nomen Dei tui. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not calumniate thy neighbour, nor oppress him by violence. The wages of him that hath been hired by thee shall not abide with thee until the morning.
verses.textLatin: Non facies calumniam proximo tuo nec vi opprimes eum. Non morabitur opus mercenarii tui apud te usque mane.

verses.text: Thou shalt not speak evil of the deaf, nor put a stumblingblock before the blind: but thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, because I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non maledices surdo, nec coram cæco pones offendiculum: sed timebis Dominum Deum tuum, quia ego sum Dominus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not do that which is unjust, nor judge unjustly. Respect not the person of the poor, nor honour the countenance of the mighty. But judge thy neighbour according to justice.
verses.textLatin: Non facies quod iniquum est, nec injuste judicabis. Non consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis. Juste judica proximo tuo.

verses.text: Thou shalt not be a detractor nor a whisperer among the people. Thou shalt not stand against the blood of thy neighbour. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non eris criminator, nec susurro in populo. Non stabis contra sanguinem proximi tui. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart, but reprove him openly, lest thou incur sin through him.
verses.textLatin: Non oderis fratrem tuum in corde tuo, sed publice argue eum, ne habeas super illo peccatum.

verses.text: Seek not revenge, nor be mindful of the injury of thy citizens. Thou shalt love thy friend as thyself. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non quæras ultionem, nec memor eris injuriæ civium tuorum. Diliges amicum tuum sicut teipsum. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Keep ye my laws. Thou shalt not make thy cattle to gender with beasts of any other kind. Thou shalt not sow thy field with different seeds. Thou shalt not wear a garment that is woven of two sorts.
verses.textLatin: Leges meas custodite. Jumentum tuum non facies coire cum alterius generis animantibus. Agrum tuum non seres diverso semine. Veste, quæ ex duobus texta est, non indueris.

verses.text: If a man carnally lie with a woman that is a bondservant and marriageable, and yet not redeemed with a price, nor made free: they both shall be scourged, and they shall not be put to death, because she was not a free woman.
verses.textLatin: Homo, si dormierit cum muliere coitu seminis, quæ sit ancilla etiam nubilis, et tamen pretio non redempta, nec libertate donata: vapulabunt ambo, et non morientur, quia non fuit libera.

verses.text: And for his trespass he shall offer a ram to the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:
verses.textLatin: Pro delicto autem suo offeret Domino ad ostium tabernaculi testimonii arietem:

verses.text: And the priest shall pray for him and for his sin before the Lord, and he shall have mercy on him, and the sin shall be forgiven.
verses.textLatin: orabitque pro eo sacerdos, et pro peccato ejus coram Domino, et repropitiabitur ei, dimitteturque peccatum.

verses.text: When you shall be come into the land, and shall have planted in it fruit trees, you shall take away the firstfruits of them: the fruit that comes forth shall be unclean to you, neither shall you eat of them.
verses.textLatin: Quando ingressi fueritis terram, et plantaveritis in ea ligna pomifera, auferetis præputia eorum: poma, quæ germinant, immunda erunt vobis, nec edetis ex eis.

verses.text: But in the fourth year, all their fruit shall be sanctified, to the praise of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Quarto autem anno omnis fructus eorum sanctificabitur, laudabilis Domino.

verses.text: And in the fifth year you shall eat the fruits thereof, gathering the increase thereof. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Quinto autem anno comedetis fructus, congregantes poma, quæ proferunt. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: You shall not eat with blood. You shall not divine nor observe dreams.
verses.textLatin: Non comedetis cum sanguine. Non augurabimini, nec observabitis somnia.

verses.text: Nor shall you cut your hair roundwise: nor shave your beard.
verses.textLatin: Neque in rotundum attondebitis comam, nec radetis barbam.

verses.text: You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh, for the dead, neither shall you make in yourselves any figures or marks: I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et super mortuo non incidetis carnem vestram, neque figuras aliquas aut stigmata facietis vobis. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Make not thy daughter a common strumpet, lest the land be defiled, and filled with wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Ne prostituas filiam tuam, ne contaminetur terra et impleatur piaculo.

verses.text: Keep ye my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sabbata mea custodite, et sanctuarium meum metuite. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Go not aside after wizards, neither ask any thing of soothsayers, to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Non declinetis ad magos, nec ab ariolis aliquid sciscitemini, ut polluamini per eos. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man: and fear the Lord thy God. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Coram cano capite consurge, et honora personam senis: et time Dominum Deum tuum. Ego sum Dominus.

verses.text: If a stranger dwell in your land, and abide among you, do not upbraid him:
verses.textLatin: Si habitaverit advena in terra vestra, et moratus fuerit inter vos, non exprobretis ei:

verses.text: But let him be among you as one of the same country: and you shall love him as yourselves: for you were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: sed sit inter vos quasi indigena, et diligetis eum quasi vosmetipsos: fuistis enim et vos advenæ in terra Ægypti. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure.
verses.textLatin: Nolite facere iniquum aliquid in judicio, in regula, in pondere, in mensura.

verses.text: Let the balance be just and the weights equal, the bushel just, and the sextary equal. I am the Lord your God, that brought you out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Statera justa, et æqua sint pondera, justus modius, æquusque sextarius. Ego Dominus Deus vester, qui eduxi vos de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: Keep all my precepts, and all my judgments, and do them. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Custodite omnia præcepta mea, et universa judicia, et facite ea. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: If any man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers, that dwell in Israel, give of his seed to the idol Moloch, dying let him die: the people of the land shall stone him.
verses.textLatin: Hæc loqueris filiis Israël: Homo de filiis Israël, et de advenis qui habitant in Israël, si quis dederit de semine suo idolo Moloch, morte moriatur: populus terræ lapidabit eum.

verses.text: And I will set my face against him: and I will cut him off from the midst of his people, because he hath given of his seed to Moloch, and hath defiled my sanctuary, and profaned my holy name.
verses.textLatin: Et ego ponam faciem meam contra illum: succidamque eum de medio populi sui, eo quod dederit de semine suo Moloch, et contaminaverit sanctuarium meum, ac polluerit nomen sanctum meum.

verses.text: And if the people of the land neglecting, and as it were little regarding my commandment, let alone the man that hath given of his seed to Moloch, and will not kill him:
verses.textLatin: Quod si negligens populus terræ, et quasi parvipendens imperium meum, dimiserit hominem qui dedit de semine suo Moloch, nec voluerit eum occidere:

verses.text: I will set my face against that man, and his kindred, and will cut off both him and all that consented with him, to commit fornication with Moloch, out of the midst of their people.
verses.textLatin: ponam faciem meam super hominem illum, et super cognationem ejus, succidamque et ipsum, et omnes qui consenserunt ei ut fornicarentur cum Moloch, de medio populi sui.

verses.text: The soul that shall go aside after magicians, and soothsayers, and shall commit fornication with them, I will set my face against that soul, and destroy it out of the midst of its people.
verses.textLatin: Anima, quæ declinaverit ad magos et ariolos, et fornicata fuerit cum eis, ponam faciem meam contra eam, et interficiam illam de medio populi sui.

verses.text: Sanctify yourselves, and be ye holy because I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Sanctificamini et estote sancti, quia ego sum Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Keep my precepts, and do them. I am the Lord that sanctify you.
verses.textLatin: Custodite præcepta mea, et facite ea: ego Dominus qui sanctifico vos.

verses.text: He that curseth his father, or mother, dying let him die: he hath cursed his father, and mother, let his blood be upon him.
verses.textLatin: Qui maledixerit patri suo, aut matri, morte moriatur: patri matrique maledixit: sanguis ejus sit super eum.

verses.text: If any man commit adultery with the wife of another, and defile his neighbour’s wife, let them be put to death, both the adulterer and the adulteress.
verses.textLatin: Si mœchatus quis fuerit cum uxore alterius, et adulterium perpetraverit cum conjuge proximi sui, morte moriantur et mœchus et adultera.

verses.text: If a man lie with his stepmother, and discover the nakedness of his father, let them both be put to death: their blood be upon them.
verses.textLatin: Qui dormierit cum noverca sua, et revelaverit ignominiam patris sui, morte moriantur ambo: sanguis eorum sit super eos.

verses.text: If any man lie with his daughter in law, let both die, because they have done a heinous crime: their blood be upon them.
verses.textLatin: Si quis dormierit cum nuru sua, uterque moriatur, quia scelus operati sunt: sanguis eorum sit super eos.

verses.text: If any one lie with a man as with a woman, both have committed an abomination, let them be put to death: their blood be upon them.
verses.textLatin: Qui dormierit cum masculo coitu femineo, uterque operatus est nefas: morte moriantur: sit sanguis eorum super eos.

verses.text: If any man after marrying the daughter, marry her mother, he hath done a heinous crime: he shall be burnt alive with them: neither shall so great an abomination remain in the midst of you.
verses.textLatin: Qui supra uxorem filiam, duxerit matrem ejus, scelus operatus est: vivus ardebit cum eis, nec permanebit tantum nefas in medio vestri.

verses.text: He that shall copulate with any beast or cattle, dying let him die: the beast also ye shall kill.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum jumento et pecore coierit, morte moriatur: pecus quoque occidite.

verses.text: The woman that shall lie under any beast, shall be killed together with the same: their blood be upon them.
verses.textLatin: Mulier, quæ succubuerit cuilibet jumento, simul interficietur cum eo: sanguis eorum sit super eos.

verses.text: If any man take his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother, and see her nakedness, and she behold her brother’s shame: they have committed a crime: they shall be slain, in the sight of their people, because they have discovered one another’s nakedness, and they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Qui acceperit sororem suam filiam patris sui, vel filiam matris suæ, et viderit turpitudinem ejus, illaque conspexerit fratris ignominiam, nefariam rem operati sunt: occidentur in conspectu populi sui, eo quod turpitudinem suam mutuo revelaverint, et portabunt iniquitatem suam.

verses.text: If any man lie with a woman in her flowers, and uncover her nakedness, and she open the fountain of her blood, both shall be destroyed out of the midst of their people.
verses.textLatin: Qui coierit cum muliere in fluxu menstruo, et revelaverit turpitudinem ejus, ipsaque aperuerit fontem sanguinis sui, interficientur ambo de medio populi sui.

verses.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy aunt by thy mother, and of thy aunt by thy father: he that doth this, hath uncovered the shame of his own flesh, both shall bear their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Turpitudinem materteræ et amitæ tuæ non discooperies: qui hoc fecerit, ignominiam carnis suæ nudavit; portabunt ambo iniquitatem suam.

verses.text: If any man lie with the wife of his uncle by the father, or of his uncle by the mother, and uncover the shame of his near akin, both shall bear their sin: they shall die without children.
verses.textLatin: Qui coierit cum uxore patrui vel avunculi sui, et revelaverit ignominiam cognationis suæ, portabunt ambo peccatum suum: absque liberis morientur.

verses.text: He that marrieth his brother’s wife, doth an unlawful thing, he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness: they shall be without children.
verses.textLatin: Qui duxerit uxorem fratris sui, rem facit illicitam: turpitudinem fratris sui revelavit: absque liberis erunt.

verses.text: Keep my laws and my judgments, and do them: lest the land into which you are to enter to dwell therein, vomit you also out.
verses.textLatin: Custodite leges meas, atque judicia, et facite ea: ne et vos evomat terra quam intraturi estis et habitaturi.

verses.text: Walk not after the laws of the nations, which I will cast out before you. For they have done all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.
verses.textLatin: Nolite ambulare in legitimis nationum, quas ego expulsurus sum ante vos. Omnia enim hæc fecerunt, et abominatus sum eas.

verses.text: But to you I say: Possess their land which I will give you for an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who have separated you from other people.
verses.textLatin: Vobis autem loquor. Possidete terram eorum, quam dabo vobis in hæreditatem, terram fluentem lacte et melle. Ego Dominus Deus vester, qui separavi vos a ceteris populis.

verses.text: Therefore do you also separate the clean beast from the unclean, and the clean fowl from the unclean: defile not your souls with beasts, or birds, or any things that move on the earth, and which I have shewn you to be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Separate ergo et vos jumentum mundum ab immundo, et avem mundam ab immunda: ne polluatis animas vestras in pecore, et avibus, et cunctis quæ moventur in terra, et quæ vobis ostendi esse polluta.

verses.text: You shall be holy unto me, because I the Lord am holy, and I have separated you from other people, that you should be mine.
verses.textLatin: Eritis mihi sancti, quia sanctus sum ego Dominus, et separavi vos a ceteris populis, ut essetis mei.

verses.text: A man, or woman, in whom there is a pythonical or divining spirit, dying let them die: they shall stone them: their blood be upon them.
verses.textLatin: Vir, sive mulier, in quibus pythonicus, vel divinationis fuerit spiritus, morte moriantur: lapidibus obruent eos: sanguis eorum sit super illos.

verses.text: The  Lord said also to Moses: Speak to the priests the sons of Aaron, and thou shalt say for them: Let not a priest incur an uncleanness at the death of his citizens:
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen: Loquere ad sacerdotes filios Aaron, et dices ad eos: Ne contaminetur sacerdos in mortibus civium suorum,

verses.text: But only for his kin, such as are near in blood, that is to say, for his father and for his mother, and for his son, and for his daughter, for his brother also,
verses.textLatin: nisi tantum in consanguineis, ac propinquis, id est, super patre et matre, et filio, et filia, fratre quoque,

verses.text: And for a maiden sister, who hath had no husband:
verses.textLatin: et sorore virgine quæ non est nupta viro:

verses.text: But not even for the prince of his people shall he do any thing that may make him unclean.
verses.textLatin: sed nec in principe populi sui contaminabitur.

verses.text: Neither shall they shave their head, nor their beard, nor make incisions in their flesh.
verses.textLatin: Non radent caput, nec barbam, neque in carnibus suis facient incisuras.

verses.text: They shall be holy to their God, and shall not profane his name: for they offer the burnt offering of the Lord, and the bread of their God, and therefore they shall be holy.
verses.textLatin: Sancti erunt Deo suo, et non polluent nomen ejus: incensum enim Domini, et panes Dei sui offerunt, et ideo sancti erunt.

verses.text: They shall not take to wife a harlot or a vile prostitute, nor one that has been put away from her husband: because they are consecrated to their God,
verses.textLatin: Scortum et vile prostibulum non ducent uxorem, nec eam quæ repudiata est a marito: quia consecrati sunt Deo suo,

verses.text: And offer the loaves of proposition. Let them therefore be holy, because I also am holy, the Lord, who sanctify them.
verses.textLatin: et panes propositionis offerunt. Sint ergo sancti, quia et ego sanctus sum, Dominus qui sanctifico eos.

verses.text: If the daughter of a priest be taken in whoredom, and dishonour the name of her father, she shall be burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: Sacerdotis filia si deprehensa fuerit in stupro, et violaverit nomen patris sui, flammis exuretur.

verses.text: The high priest, that is to say, the priest, is the greatest among his brethren, upon whose head the oil of unction hath been poured, and whose hands have been consecrated for the priesthood, and who hath been vested with the holy vestments, shall not uncover his head, he shall not rend his garments:
verses.textLatin: Pontifex, id est, sacerdos maximus inter fratres suos, super cujus caput fusum est unctionis oleum, et cujus manus in sacerdotio consecratæ sunt, vestitusque est sanctis vestibus, caput suum non discooperiet, vestimenta non scindet:

verses.text: Nor shall he go in at all to any dead person: not even for his father, or his mother, shall he be defiled:
verses.textLatin: et ad omnem mortuum non ingredietur omnino: super patre quoque suo et matre non contaminabitur.

verses.text: Neither shall he go out of the holy places, lest he defile the sanctuary of the Lord, because the oil of the holy unction of his God is upon him. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Nec egredietur de sanctis, ne polluat sanctuarium Domini, quia oleum sanctæ unctionis Dei sui super eum est. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: He shall take a virgin unto his wife:
verses.textLatin: Virginem ducet uxorem:

verses.text: But a widow or one that is divorced, or defiled, or a harlot, he shall not take, but a maid of his own people:
verses.textLatin: viduam autem et repudiatam, et sordidam, atque meretricem non accipiet, sed puellam de populo suo:

verses.text: He shall not mingle the stock of his kindred with the common people of his nation: for I am the Lord who sanctify him.
verses.textLatin: ne commisceat stirpem generis sui vulgo gentis suæ: quia ego Dominus, qui sanctifico eum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Say to Aaron: Whosoever of thy seed throughout their families, hath a blemish, he shall not offer bread to his God.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad Aaron: Homo de semine tuo per familias qui habuerit maculam, non offeret panes Deo suo,

verses.text: Neither shall he approach to minister to him: If he be blind, if he be lame, if he have a little, or a great, or a crooked nose,
verses.textLatin: nec accedet ad ministerium ejus: si cæcus fuerit, si claudus, si parvo vel grandi, vel torto naso,

verses.text: If his foot, or if his hand be broken,
verses.textLatin: si fracto pede, si manu,

verses.text: If he be crookbacked, or blear eyed, or have a pearl in his eye, or a continual scab, or a dry scurf in his body, or a rupture:
verses.textLatin: si gibbus, si lippus, si albuginem habens in oculo, si jugem scabiem, si impetiginem in corpore, vel herniosus.

verses.text: Whosoever of the seed of Aaron the priest hath a blemish, he shall not approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor bread to his God.
verses.textLatin: Omnis qui habuerit maculam de semine Aaron sacerdotis, non accedet offerre hostias Domino, nec panes Deo suo:

verses.text: He shall eat nevertheless of the loaves, that are offered in the sanctuary,
verses.textLatin: vescetur tamen panibus qui offeruntur in sanctuario,

verses.text: Yet so that he enter not within the veil, nor approach to the altar, because he hath a blemish, and he must not defile my sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctify them.
verses.textLatin: ita dumtaxat, ut intra velum non ingrediatur, nec accedat ad altare, quia maculam habet, et contaminare non debet sanctuarium meum. Ego Dominus qui sanctifico eos.

verses.text: Moses therefore spoke to Aaron, and to his sons and to all Israel, all the things that had been commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Locutus est ergo Moyses ad Aaron, et ad filios ejus, et ad omnem Israël cuncta quæ fuerant sibi imperata.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus quoque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they beware of those things that are consecrated of the children of Israel, and defile not the name of the things sanctified to me, which they offer. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad Aaron et ad filios ejus, ut caveant ab his quæ consecrata sunt filiorum Israël, et non contaminent nomen sanctificatorum mihi, quæ ipsi offerunt. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Say to them and to their posterity: Every man of your race, that approacheth to those things that are consecrated, and which the children of Israel have offered to the Lord, in whom there is uncleanness, shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Dic ad eos, et ad posteros eorum: Omnis homo qui accesserit de stirpe vestra ad ea quæ consecrata sunt, et quæ obtulerunt filii Israël Domino, in quo est immunditia, peribit coram Domino. Ego sum Dominus.

verses.text: The man of the seed of Aaron, that is a leper, or that suffereth a running of the seed, shall not eat of those things that are sanctified to me, until he be healed. He that toucheth any thing unclean by occasion of the dead, and he whose seed goeth from him as in generation,
verses.textLatin: Homo de semine Aaron, qui fuerit leprosus, aut patiens fluxum seminis, non vescetur de his quæ sanctificata sunt mihi, donec sanetur. Qui tetigerit immundum super mortuo, et ex quo egreditur semen quasi coitus,

verses.text: And he that toucheth a creeping thing, or any unclean thing, the touching of which is defiling,
verses.textLatin: et qui tangit reptile, et quodlibet immundum cujus tactus est sordidus,

verses.text: Shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat those things that are sanctified: but when he hath washed his flesh with water,
verses.textLatin: immundus erit usque ad vesperum, et non vescetur his quæ sanctificata sunt: sed cum laverit carnem suam aqua,

verses.text: And the sun is down, then being purified, he shall eat of the sanctified things, because it is his meat.
verses.textLatin: et occubuerit sol, tunc mundatus vescetur de sanctificatis, quia cibus illius est.

verses.text: That which dieth of itself, and that which was taken by a beast, they shall not eat, nor be defiled therewith. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Morticinum et captum a bestia non comedent, nec polluentur in eis. Ego sum Dominus.

verses.text: Let them keep my precepts, that they may not fall into sin, and die in the sanctuary, when they shall have defiled it. I am the Lord who sanctify them.
verses.textLatin: Custodiant præcepta mea, ut non subjaceant peccato, et moriantur in sanctuario, cum polluerint illud. Ego Dominus qui sanctifico eos.

verses.text: No stranger shall eat of the sanctified things: a sojourner of the priests, or a hired servant, shall not eat of them.
verses.textLatin: Omnis alienigena non comedet de sanctificatis; inquilinus sacerdotis et mercenarius non vescentur ex eis.

verses.text: But he whom the priest hath bought, and he that is his servant, born in his house, these shall eat of them.
verses.textLatin: Quem autem sacerdos emerit, et qui vernaculus domus ejus fuerit, his comedent ex eis.

verses.text: If the daughter of a priest be married to any of the people, she shall not eat of those things that are sanctified, nor of the firstfruits.
verses.textLatin: Si filia sacerdotis cuilibet ex populo nupta fuerit, de his quæ sanctificata sunt, et de primitiis non vescetur.

verses.text: But if she be a widow, or divorced, and having no children return to her father’s house, she shall eat of her father’s meats, as she was wont to do when she was a maid, no stranger hath leave to eat of them.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem vidua, vel repudiata, et absque liberis reversa fuerit ad domum patris sui: sicut puella consueverat, aletur cibis patris sui. Omnis alienigena comedendi ex eis non habet potestatem.

verses.text: He that eateth of the sanctified things through ignorance, shall add the fifth part with that which he ate, and shall give it to the priest into the sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Qui comederit de sanctificatis per ignorantiam, addet quintam partem cum eo quod comedit, et dabit sacerdoti in sanctuarium.

verses.text: And they shall not profane the sanctified things of the children of Israel, which they offer to the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Nec contaminabunt sanctificata filiorum Israël, quæ offerunt Domino:

verses.text: Lest perhaps they bear the iniquity of their trespass, when they shall have eaten the sanctified things. I am the Lord who sanctify them.
verses.textLatin: ne forte sustineant iniquitatem delicti sui, cum sanctificata comederint. Ego Dominus qui sanctifico eos.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man of the house of Israel, and of the strangers who dwell with you, that offereth his oblation, either paying his vows, or offering of his own accord, whatsoever it be which he presenteth for a holocaust of the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad Aaron et filios ejus, et ad omnes filios Israël, dicesque ad eos: Homo de domo Israël, et de advenis qui habitant apud vos, qui obtulerit oblationem suam, vel vota solvens, vel sponte offerens, quidquid illud obtulerit in holocaustum Domini,

verses.text: To be offered by you, it shall be a male without blemish of the beeves, or of the sheep, or of the goats.
verses.textLatin: ut offeratur per vos, masculus immaculatus erit ex bobus, et ovibus, et ex capris:

verses.text: If it have a blemish you shall not offer it, neither shall it be acceptable.
verses.textLatin: si maculam habuerit, non offeretis, neque erit acceptabile.

verses.text: The man that offereth a victim of peace offerings to the Lord, either paying his vows, or offering of his own accord, whether of beeves or of sheep, shall offer it without blemish, that it may be acceptable: there shall be no blemish in it.
verses.textLatin: Homo qui obtulerit victimam pacificorum Domino, vel vota solvens, vel sponte offerens, tam de bobus quam de ovibus, immaculatum offeret ut acceptabile sit: omnis macula non erit in eo.

verses.text: If it be blind, or broken, or have a scar or blisters, or a scab, or a dry scurf: you shall not offer them to the Lord, nor burn any thing of them upon the Lord’s altar.
verses.textLatin: Si cæcum fuerit, si fractum, si cicatricem habens, si papulas, aut scabiem, aut impetiginem: non offeretis ea Domino, nec adolebitis ex eis super altare Domini.

verses.text: An ox or a sheep, that hath the ear and the tail cut off, thou mayst offer voluntarily: but a vow may not be paid with them.
verses.textLatin: Bovem et ovem, aure et cauda amputatis, voluntarie offerre potes, votum autem ex eis solvi non potest.

verses.text: You shall not offer to the Lord any beast that hath the testicles bruised, or crushed, or cut and taken away: neither shall you do any such thing in your land.
verses.textLatin: Omne animal, quod vel contritis, vel tusis, vel sectis ablatisque testiculis est, non offeretis Domino, et in terra vestra hoc omnino ne faciatis.

verses.text: You shall not offer bread to your God, from the hand of a stranger, nor any other thing that he would give: because they are all corrupted, and defiled: you shall not receive them.
verses.textLatin: De manu alienigenæ non offeretis panes Deo vestro, et quidquid aliud dare voluerit, quia corrupta, et maculata sunt omnia: non suscipietis ea.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, they shall be seven days under the udder of their dam: but the eighth day, and thenceforth, they may be offered to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Bos, ovis et capra, cum genita fuerint, septem diebus erunt sub ubere matris suæ: die autem octavo, et deinceps, offerri poterunt Domino.

verses.text: Whether it be a cow, or a sheep, they shall not be sacrificed the same day with their young ones.
verses.textLatin: Sive illa bos, sive ovis, non immolabuntur una die cum fœtibus suis.

verses.text: If you immolate a victim for thanksgiving to the Lord, that he may be favourable,
verses.textLatin: Si immolaveritis hostiam pro gratiarum actione Domino, ut possit esse placabilis,

verses.text: You shall eat it the same day, there shall not any of it remain until the morning of the next day. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: eodem die comedetis eam: non remanebit quidquam in mane alterius diei. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Keep my commandments, and do them. I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Custodite mandata mea, et facite ea. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: Profane not my holy name, that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctify you,
verses.textLatin: Ne polluatis nomen meum sanctum, ut sanctificer in medio filiorum Israël. Ego Dominus qui sanctifico vos,

verses.text: And who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God: I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et eduxi de terra Ægypti, ut essem vobis in Deum. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call holy.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Hæ sunt feriæ Domini, quas vocabitis sanctas.

verses.text: Six days shall ye do work: the seventh day, because it is the rest of the sabbath, shall be called holy. You shall do no work on that day: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your habitations.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus facietis opus: dies septimus, quia sabbati requies est, vocabitur sanctus: omne opus non facietis in eo: sabbatum Domini est in cunctis habitationibus vestris.

verses.text: These also are the holy days of the Lord, which you must celebrate in their seasons.
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt ergo feriæ Domini sanctæ, quas celebrare debetis temporibus suis.

verses.text: The first month, the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the phase of the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Mense primo, quartadecima die mensis ad vesperum, Phase Domini est:

verses.text: And the fifteenth day of the same month is the solemnity of the unleavened bread of the Lord. Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread.
verses.textLatin: et quintadecima die mensis hujus, solemnitas azymorum Domini est. Septem diebus azyma comedetis.

verses.text: The first day shall be most solemn unto you, and holy: you shall do no servile work therein:
verses.textLatin: Dies primus erit vobis celeberrimus, sanctusque: omne opus servile non facietis in eo,

verses.text: But you shall offer sacrifice in fire to the Lord seven days. And the seventh day shall be more solemn, and more holy: and you shall do no servile work therein.
verses.textLatin: sed offeretis sacrificium in igne Domino septem diebus. Dies autem septimus erit celebrior et sanctior: nullumque servile opus facietis in eo.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, and shall reap your corn, you shall bring sheaves of ears, the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest:
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Cum ingressi fueritis terram, quam ego dabo vobis, et messueritis segetem, feretis manipulos spicarum, primitias messis vestræ, ad sacerdotem:

verses.text: Who shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord, the next day after the sabbath, that it may be acceptable for you, and shall sanctify it.
verses.textLatin: qui elevabit fasciculum coram Domino, ut acceptabile sit pro vobis, altero die sabbati, et sanctificabit illum.

verses.text: And on the same day that the sheaf is consecrated, a lamb without blemish of the first year shall be killed for a holocaust of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Atque in eodem die quo manipulus consecratur, cædetur agnus immaculatus anniculus in holocaustum Domini.

verses.text: And the libations shall be offered with it, two tenths of flour tempered with oil, for a burnt offering of the Lord, and a most sweet odour: libations also of wine, the fourth part of a hin.
verses.textLatin: Et libamenta offerentur cum eo, duæ decimæ similæ conspersæ oleo in incensum Domini, odoremque suavissimum: liba quoque vini, quarta pars hin.

verses.text: You shall not eat either bread, or parched corn, or frumenty of the harvest, until the day that you shall offer thereof to your God. It is a precept for ever throughout your generations, and all your dwellings.
verses.textLatin: Panem, et polentam, et pultes non comedetis ex segete, usque ad diem qua offeretis ex ea Deo vestro. Præceptum est sempiternum in generationibus, cunctisque habitaculis vestris.

verses.text: You shall count therefore from the morrow after the sabbath, wherein you offered the sheaf of firstfruits, seven full weeks.
verses.textLatin: Numerabitis ergo ab altero die sabbati, in quo obtulistis manipulum primitiarum, septem hebdomadas plenas,

verses.text: Even unto the morrow after the seventh week be expired, that is to say, fifty days, and so you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: usque ad alteram diem expletionis hebdomadæ septimæ, id est, quinquaginta dies: et sic offeretis sacrificium novum Domino

verses.text: Out of all your dwellings, two loaves of the firstfruits, of two tenths of flour leavened, which you shall bake for the firstfruits of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ex omnibus habitaculis vestris, panes primitiarum duos de duabus decimis similæ fermentatæ, quos coquetis in primitias Domini.

verses.text: And you shall offer with the loaves seven lambs without blemish of the first year, and one calf from the herd, and two rams, and they shall be for a holocaust with their libations for a most sweet odour to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Offeretisque cum panibus septem agnos immaculatos anniculos, et vitulum de armento unum, et arietes duos, et erunt in holocaustum cum libamentis suis, in odorem suavissimum Domini.

verses.text: You shall offer also a buck goat for sin, and two lambs of the first year for sacrifices of peace offerings.
verses.textLatin: Facietis et hircum pro peccato, duosque agnos anniculos hostias pacificorum.

verses.text: And when the priest hath lifted them up with the loaves of the firstfruits before the Lord, they shall fall to his use.
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevaverit eos sacerdos cum panibus primitiarum coram Domino, cedent in usum ejus.

verses.text: And you shall call this day most solemn, and most holy. You shall do no servile work therein. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in all your dwellings and generations.
verses.textLatin: Et vocabitis hunc diem celeberrimum, atque sanctissimum: omne opus servile non facietis in eo. Legitimum sempiternum erit in cunctis habitaculis, et generationibus vestris.

verses.text: And when you reap the corn of your land, you shall not cut it to the very ground: neither shall you gather the ears that remain; but you shall leave them for the poor and for the strangers. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem messueritis segetem terræ vestræ, nec secabitis eam usque ad solum, nec remanentes spicas colligetis: sed pauperibus et peregrinis dimittetis eas. Ego sum Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Say to the children of Israel: The seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall keep a sabbath, a memorial, with the sound of trumpets, and it shall be called holy.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël: Mense septimo, prima die mensis, erit vobis sabbatum, memoriale, clangentibus tubis, et vocabitur sanctum:

verses.text: You shall do no servile work therein, and you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: omne opus servile non facietis in eo, et offeretis holocaustum Domino.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Upon the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the day of atonement, it shall be most solemn, and shall be called holy: and you shall afflict your souls on that day, and shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Decimo die mensis hujus septimi, dies expiationum erit celeberrimus, et vocabitur sanctus: affligetisque animas vestras in eo, et offeretis holocaustum Domino.

verses.text: You shall do no servile work in the time of this day: because it is a day of propitiation, that the Lord your God may be merciful unto you.
verses.textLatin: Omne opus servile non facietis in tempore diei hujus: quia dies propitiationis est, ut propitietur vobis Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Every soul that is not afflicted on this day, shall perish from among his people:
verses.textLatin: Omnis anima, quæ afflicta non fuerit die hac, peribit de populis suis:

verses.text: And every soul that shall do any work, the same will I destroy from among his people.
verses.textLatin: et quæ operis quippiam fecerit, delebo eam de populo suo.

verses.text: You shall do no work therefore on that day: it shall be an everlasting ordinance unto you in all your generations, and dwellings.
verses.textLatin: Nihil ergo operis facietis in eo: legitimum sempiternum erit vobis in cunctis generationibus, et habitationibus vestris.

verses.text: It is a sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls beginning on the ninth day of the month: from evening until evening you shall celebrate your sabbaths.
verses.textLatin: Sabbatum requietionis est, et affligetis animas vestras die nono mensis: a vespera usque ad vesperam celebrabitis sabbata vestra.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Say to the children of Israel: From the fifteenth day of this same seventh month, shall be kept the feast of tabernacles seven days to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël: A quintodecimo die mensis hujus septimi, erunt feriæ tabernaculorum septem diebus Domino.

verses.text: The first day shall be called most solemn and most holy: you shall do no servile work therein. And seven days you shall offer holocausts to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Dies primus vocabitur celeberrimus atque sanctissimus: omne opus servile non facietis in eo.

verses.text: The eighth day also shall be most solemn and most holy, and you shall offer holocausts to the Lord: for it is the day of assembly and congregation: you shall do no servile work therein.
verses.textLatin: Et septem diebus offeretis holocausta Domino. Dies quoque octavus erit celeberrimus, atque sanctissimus, et offeretis holocaustum Domino: est enim cœtus atque collectæ: omne opus servile non facietis in eo.

verses.text: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call most solemn and most holy, and shall offer on them oblations to the Lord, holocausts and libations according to the rite of every day,
verses.textLatin: Hæ sunt feriæ Domini, quas vocabitis celeberrimas atque sanctissimas, offeretisque in eis oblationes Domino, holocausta et libamenta juxta ritum uniuscujusque diei:

verses.text: Besides the sabbaths of the Lord, and your gifts, and those things that you offer by vow, or which you shall give to the Lord voluntarily.
verses.textLatin: exceptis sabbatis Domini, donisque vestris, et quæ offeretis ex voto, vel quæ sponte tribuetis Domino.

verses.text: So from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you shall have gathered in all the fruits of your land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord seven days: on the first day and the eighth shall be a sabbath, that is a day of rest.
verses.textLatin: A quintodecimo ergo die mensis septimi, quando congregaveritis omnes fructus terræ vestræ, celebrabitis ferias Domini septem diebus: die primo et die octavo erit sabbatum, id est, requies.

verses.text: And you shall take to you on the first day the fruits of the fairest tree, and branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Sumetisque vobis die primo fructus arboris pulcherrimæ, spatulasque palmarum, et ramos ligni densarum frondium, et salices de torrente, et lætabimini coram Domino Deo vestro.

verses.text: And you shall keep the solemnity thereof seven days in the year. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in your generations. In the seventh month shall you celebrate this feast.
verses.textLatin: Celebrabitisque solemnitatem ejus septem diebus per annum: legitimum sempiternum erit in generationibus vestris. Mense septimo festa celebrabitis,

verses.text: And you shall dwell in bowers seven days: every one that is of the race of Israel, shall dwell in tabernacles:
verses.textLatin: et habitabitis in umbraculis septem diebus: omnis, qui de genere est Israël, manebit in tabernaculis,

verses.text: That your posterity may know, that I made the children of Israel to dwell in tabernacles, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: ut discant posteri vestri quod in tabernaculis habitare fecerim filios Israël, cum educerem eos de terra Ægypti. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: And Moses spoke concerning the feasts of the Lord to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses super solemnitatibus Domini ad filios Israël.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee the finest and clearest oil of olives, to furnish the lamps continually,
verses.textLatin: Præcipe filiis Israël, ut afferant tibi oleum de olivis purissimum, ac lucidum, ad concinnandas lucernas jugiter,

verses.text: Without the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron shall set them from evening until morning before the Lord, by a perpetual service and rite in your generations.
verses.textLatin: extra velum testimonii in tabernaculo fœderis. Ponetque eas Aaron a vespere usque ad mane coram Domino, cultu rituque perpetuo in generationibus vestris.

verses.text: They shall be set upon the most pure candlestick before the Lord continually.
verses.textLatin: Super candelabrum mundissimum ponentur semper in conspectu Domini.

verses.text: Thou shalt take also fine flour, and shalt bake twelve loaves thereof, two tenths shall be in every loaf:
verses.textLatin: Accipies quoque similam, et coques ex ea duodecim panes, qui singuli habebunt duas decimas:

verses.text: And thou shalt set them six and six one against another upon the most clean table before the Lord:
verses.textLatin: quorum senos altrinsecus super mensam purissimam coram Domino statues:

verses.text: And thou shalt put upon them the clearest frankincense, that the bread may be for a memorial of the oblation of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et pones super eos thus lucidissimum, ut sit panis in monimentum oblationis Domini.

verses.text: Every sabbath they shall be changed before the Lord, being received of the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant:
verses.textLatin: Per singula sabbata mutabuntur coram Domino suscepti a filiis Israël fœdere sempiterno:

verses.text: And they shall be Aaron’s and his sons’, that they may eat them in the holy place: because it is most holy of the sacrifices of the Lord by a perpetual right.
verses.textLatin: eruntque Aaron et filiorum ejus, ut comedant eos in loco sancto: quia Sanctum sanctorum est de sacrificiis Domini jure perpetuo.

verses.text: And behold there went out the son of a woman of Israel, whom she had of an Egyptian, among the children of Israel, and fell at words in the camp with a man of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem egressus filius mulieris Israëlitidis, quem pepererat de viro ægyptio inter filios Israël, jurgatus est in castris cum viro Israëlita.

verses.text: And when he had blasphemed the name, and had cursed it, he was brought to Moses: (now his mother was called Salumith, the daughter of Dabri, of the tribe of Dan:)
verses.textLatin: Cumque blasphemasset nomen, et maledixisset ei, adductus est ad Moysen. (Vocabatur autem mater ejus Salumith, filia Dabri de tribu Dan.)

verses.text: And they put him into prison, till they might know what the Lord would command.
verses.textLatin: Miseruntque eum in carcerem, donec nossent quid juberet Dominus.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses,
verses.textLatin: Qui locutus est ad Moysen,

verses.text: Saying: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let them that heard him, put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Educ blasphemum extra castra, et ponant omnes qui audierunt, manus suas super caput ejus, et lapidet eum populus universus.

verses.text: And thou shalt speak to the children of Israel: the man that curseth his God, shall bear his sin:
verses.textLatin: Et ad filios Israël loqueris: Homo, qui maledixerit Deo suo, portabit peccatum suum;

verses.text: And he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die: all the multitude shall stone him, whether he be a native or a stranger. He that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die.
verses.textLatin: et qui blasphemaverit nomen Domini, morte moriatur: lapidibus opprimet eum omnis multitudo, sive ille civis, sive peregrinus fuerit. Qui blasphemaverit nomen Domini, morte moriatur.

verses.text: He that striketh and killeth a man, dying let him die.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit, et occiderit hominem, morte moriatur.

verses.text: He that killeth a beast, shall make it good, that is to say, shall give beast for beast.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit animal, reddet vicarium, id est, animam pro anima.

verses.text: He that giveth a blemish to any of his neighbours: as he hath done, so shall it be done to him:
verses.textLatin: Qui irrogaverit maculam cuilibet civium suorum, sicut fecit, sic fiet ei:

verses.text: Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, shall he restore. What blemish he gave, the like shall he be compelled to suffer.
verses.textLatin: fracturam pro fractura, oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente restituet: qualem inflixerit maculam, talem sustinere cogetur.

verses.text: He that striketh a beast, shall render another. He that striketh a man shall be punished.
verses.textLatin: Qui percusserit jumentum, reddet aliud. Qui percusserit hominem, punietur.

verses.text: Let there be equal judgment among you, whether he be a stranger, or a native that offends: because I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Æquum judicium sit inter vos, sive peregrinus, sive civis peccaverit: quia ego sum Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought forth him that had blasphemed, without the camp, and they stoned him. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses ad filios Israël: et eduxerunt eum, qui blasphemaverat, extra castra, ac lapidibus oppresserunt. Feceruntque filii Israël sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses in mount Sinai, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen in monte Sinai, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, observe the rest of the sabbath to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Quando ingressi fueritis terram quam ego dabo vobis, sabbatizes sabbatum Domino.

verses.text: Six years thou shalt sow thy field and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and shalt gather the fruits thereof:
verses.textLatin: Sex annis seres agrum tuum, et sex annis putabis vineam tuam, colligesque fructus ejus:

verses.text: But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord: thou shalt not sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.
verses.textLatin: septimo autem anno sabbatum erit terræ, requietionis Domini: agrum non seres, et vineam non putabis.

verses.text: What the ground shall bring forth of itself, thou shalt not reap: neither shalt thou gather the grapes or the firstfruits as a vintage: for it is a year of rest to the land:
verses.textLatin: Quæ sponte gignet humus, non metes: et uvas primitiarum tuarum non colliges quasi vindemiam: annus enim requietionis terræ est:

verses.text: But they shall be unto you for meat, to thee and to thy manservant, to thy maidservant and thy hireling, and to the strangers that sojourn with thee:
verses.textLatin: sed erunt vobis in cibum, tibi et servo tuo, ancillæ et mercenario tuo, et advenæ qui peregrinantur apud te:

verses.text: All things that grow shall be meat to thy beasts and to thy cattle.
verses.textLatin: jumentis tuis et pecoribus, omnia quæ nascuntur præbebunt cibum.

verses.text: Thou shalt also number to thee seven weeks of years, that is to say, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years:
verses.textLatin: Numerabis quoque tibi septem hebdomadas annorum, id est, septies septem, quæ simul faciunt annos quadraginta novem:

verses.text: And thou shalt sound the trumpet in the seventh month, the tenth day of the month, in the time of the expiation in all your land.
verses.textLatin: et clanges buccina mense septimo, decima die mensis, propitiationis tempore, in universa terra vestra.

verses.text: And thou shalt sanctify the fiftieth year, and shalt proclaim remission to all the inhabitants of thy land: for it is the year of jubilee. Every man shall return to his possession, and every one shall go back to his former family:
verses.textLatin: Sanctificabisque annum quinquagesimum, et vocabis remissionem cunctis habitatoribus terræ tuæ: ipse est enim jubilæus. Revertetur homo ad possessionem suam, et unusquisque rediet ad familiam pristinam:

verses.text: Because it is the jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor reap the things that grow in the field of their own accord, neither shall you gather the firstfruits of the vines,
verses.textLatin: quia jubilæus est, et quinquagesimus annus. Non seretis neque metetis sponte in agro nascentia, et primitias vindemiæ non colligetis,

verses.text: Because of the sanctification of the jubilee: but as they grow you shall presently eat them.
verses.textLatin: ob sanctificationem jubilæi: sed statim oblata comedetis.

verses.text: In the year of the jubilee all shall return to their possessions.
verses.textLatin: Anno jubilæi, redient omnes ad possessiones suas.

verses.text: When thou shalt sell any thing to thy neighbour, or shalt buy of him; grieve not thy brother: but thou shalt buy of him according to the number of years from the jubilee.
verses.textLatin: Quando vendes quippiam civi tuo, vel emes ab eo, ne contristes fratrem tuum, sed juxta numerum annorum jubilæi emes ab eo,

verses.text: And he shall sell to thee according to the computation of the fruits.
verses.textLatin: et juxta supputationem frugum vendet tibi.

verses.text: The more years remain after the jubilee, the more shall the price increase: and the less time is counted, so much the less shall the purchase cost. For he shall sell to thee the time of the fruits.
verses.textLatin: Quanto plures anni remanserint post jubilæum, tanto crescet et pretium: et quanto minus temporis numeraveris, tanto minoris et emptio constabit: tempus enim frugum vendet tibi.

verses.text: Do not afflict your countrymen, but let every one fear his God: because I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Nolite affligere contribules vestros, sed timeat unusquisque Deum suum, quia ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Do my precepts, and keep my judgments, and fulfil them: that you may dwell in the land without any fear,
verses.textLatin: Facite præcepta mea, et judicia custodite, et implete ea: ut habitare possitis in terra absque ullo pavore,

verses.text: And the ground may yield you its fruits, of which you may eat your fill, fearing no man’s invasion.
verses.textLatin: et gignat vobis humus fructus suos, quibus vescamini usque ad saturitatem, nullius impetum formidantes.

verses.text: But if you say: What shall we eat the seventh year, if we sow not, nor gather our fruits?
verses.textLatin: Quod si dixeritis: Quid comedemus anno septimo, si non severimus, neque collegerimus fruges nostras?

verses.text: I will give you my blessing the sixth year, and it shall yield the fruits of three years:
verses.textLatin: dabo benedictionem meam vobis anno sexto, et faciet fructus trium annorum:

verses.text: And the eighth year you shall sow, and shall eat of the old fruits, until the ninth year: till new grow up, you shall eat the old store.
verses.textLatin: seretisque anno octavo, et comedetis veteres fruges usque ad nonum annum: donec nova nascantur, edetis vetera.

verses.text: The land also shall not be sold for ever: because it is mine, and you are strangers and sojourners with me.
verses.textLatin: Terra quoque non vendetur in perpetuum, quia mea est, et vos advenæ et coloni mei estis:

verses.text: For which cause all the country of your possession shall be under the condition of redemption.
verses.textLatin: unde cuncta regio possessionis vestræ sub redemptionis conditione vendetur.

verses.text: If thy brother being impoverished sell his little possession, and his kinsman will, he may redeem what he had sold.
verses.textLatin: Si attenuatus frater tuus vendiderit possessiunculam suam, et voluerit propinquus ejus, potest redimere quod ille vendiderat.

verses.text: But if he have no kinsman, and he himself can find the price to redeem it:
verses.textLatin: Sin autem non habuerit proximum, et ipse pretium ad redimendum potuerit invenire,

verses.text: The value of the fruits shall be counted from that time when he sold it: and the overplus he shall restore to the buyer, and so shall receive his possession again.
verses.textLatin: computabuntur fructus ex eo tempore quo vendidit: et quod reliquum est, reddet emptori, sicque recipiet possessionem suam.

verses.text: But if his hands find not the means to repay the price, the buyer shall have what he bought, until the year of the jubilee. For in that year all that is sold shall return to the owner, and to the ancient possessor.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non invenerit manus ejus ut reddat pretium, habebit emptor quod emerat, usque ad annum jubilæum. In ipso enim omnis venditio redibit ad dominum et ad possessorem pristinum.

verses.text: He that selleth a house within the walls of a city, shall have the liberty to redeem it, until one year be expired:
verses.textLatin: Qui vendiderit domum intra urbis muros, habebit licentiam redimendi, donec unus impleatur annus.

verses.text: If he redeem it not, and the whole year be fully out, the buyer shall possess it, and his posterity for ever, and it cannot be redeemed, not even in the jubilee.
verses.textLatin: Si non redemerit, et anni circulus fuerit evolutus, emptor possidebit eam, et posteri ejus in perpetuum, et redimi non poterit, etiam in jubilæo.

verses.text: But if the house be in a village, that hath no walls, it shall be sold according to the same law as the fields: if it be not redeemed before, in the jubilee it shall return to the owner.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem in villa domus, quæ muros non habet, agrorum jure vendetur: si ante redempta non fuerit, in jubilæo revertetur ad dominum.

verses.text: The houses of Levites, which are in cities, may always be redeemed:
verses.textLatin: Ædes Levitarum quæ in urbibus sunt, semper possunt redimi:

verses.text: If they be not redeemed, in the jubilee they shall all return to the owners, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are for their possessions among the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: si redemptæ non fuerint, in jubilæo revertentur ad dominos, quia domus urbium Levitarum pro possessionibus sunt inter filios Israël.

verses.text: But let not their suburbs be sold, because it is a perpetual possession.
verses.textLatin: Suburbana autem eorum non veneant, quia possessio sempiterna est.

verses.text: If thy brother be impoverished, and weak of hand, and thou receive him as a stranger and sojourner, and he live with thee,
verses.textLatin: Si attenuatus fuerit frater tuus, et infirmus manu, et susceperis eum quasi advenam et peregrinum, et vixerit tecum,

verses.text: Take not usury of him nor more than thou gavest: fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee.
verses.textLatin: ne accipias usuras ab eo, nec amplius quam dedisti: time Deum tuum, ut vivere possit frater tuus apud te.

verses.text: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor exact of him any increase of fruits.
verses.textLatin: Pecuniam tuam non dabis ei ad usuram, et frugum superabundantiam non exiges.

verses.text: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might give you the land of Chanaan, and might be your God.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus Deus vester, qui eduxi vos de terra Ægypti, ut darem vobis terram Chanaan, et essem vester Deus.

verses.text: If thy brother constrained by poverty, sell himself to thee, thou shalt not oppress him with the service of bondservants:
verses.textLatin: Si paupertate compulsus vendiderit se tibi frater tuus, non eum opprimes servitute famulorum,

verses.text: But he shall be as a hireling, and a sojourner: he shall work with thee until the year of the jubilee,
verses.textLatin: sed quasi mercenarius et colonus erit: usque ad annum jubilæum operabitur apud te,

verses.text: And afterwards he shall go out with his children, and shall return to his kindred and to the possession of his fathers,
verses.textLatin: et postea egredietur cum liberis suis, et revertetur ad cognationem, ad possessionem patrum suorum.

verses.text: For they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt: let them not be sold as bondmen:
verses.textLatin: Mei enim servi sunt, et ego eduxi eos de terra Ægypti: non veneant conditione servorum:

verses.text: Afflict him not by might, but fear thy God.
verses.textLatin: ne affligas eum per potentiam, sed metuito Deum tuum.

verses.text: Let your bondmen, and your bondwomen, be of the nations that are round about you.
verses.textLatin: Servus et ancilla sint vobis de nationibus quæ in circuitu vestro sunt:

verses.text: And of the strangers that sojourn among you, or that were born of them in your land, these you shall have for servants:
verses.textLatin: et de advenis qui peregrinantur apud vos, vel qui ex his nati fuerint in terra vestra, hos habebitis famulos:

verses.text: And by right of inheritance shall leave them to your posterity, and shall possess them for ever. But oppress not your brethren the children of Israel by might.
verses.textLatin: et hæreditario jure transmittetis ad posteros, ac possidebitis in æternum: fratres autem vestros filios Israël ne opprimatis per potentiam.

verses.text: If the hand of a stranger or a sojourner grow strong among you, and thy brother being impoverished sell himself to him, or to any of his race:
verses.textLatin: Si invaluerit apud vos manus advenæ atque peregrini, et attenuatus frater tuus vendiderit se ei, aut cuiquam de stirpe ejus:

verses.text: After the sale he may be redeemed. He that will of his brethren shall redeem him:
verses.textLatin: post venditionem potest redimi. Qui voluerit ex fratribus suis, redimet eum,

verses.text: Either his uncle, or his uncle’s son, or his kinsman, by blood, or by affinity. But if he himself be able also, he shall redeem himself,
verses.textLatin: et patruus, et patruelis, et consanguineus, et affinis. Sin autem et ipse potuerit, redimet se,

verses.text: Counting only the years from the time of his selling unto the year of the jubilee: and counting the money that he was sold for, according to the number of the years and the reckoning of a hired servant,
verses.textLatin: supputatis dumtaxat annis a tempore venditionis suæ usque ad annum jubilæum: et pecunia, qua venditus fuerat, juxta annorum numerum, et rationem mercenarii supputata.

verses.text: If there be many years that remain until the jubilee, according to them shall he also repay the price.
verses.textLatin: Si plures fuerint anni qui remanent usque ad jubilæum, secundum hos reddet et pretium:

verses.text: If few, he shall make the reckoning with him according to the number of the years, and shall repay to the buyer of what remaineth of the years,
verses.textLatin: si pauci, ponet rationem cum eo juxta annorum numerum, et reddet emptori quod reliquum est annorum,

verses.text: His wages being allowed for which he served before: he shall not afflict him violently in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: quibus ante servivit mercedibus imputatis: non affliget eum violenter in conspectu tuo.

verses.text: And if by these means he cannot be redeemed, in the year of the jubilee he shall go out with his children.
verses.textLatin: Quod si per hæc redimi non potuerit, anno jubilæo egredietur cum liberis suis.

verses.text: For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Mei enim sunt servi filii Israël, quos eduxi de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: I  AM the Lord your God: you shall not make to yourselves any idol or graven thing, neither shall you erect pillars, nor set up a remarkable stone in your land, to adore it: for I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus Deus vester: non facietis vobis idolum, et sculptile, nec titulos erigetis, nec insignem lapidem ponetis in terra vestra, ut adoretis eum. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: Keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Custodite sabbata mea, et pavete ad sanctuarium meum. Ego Dominus.

verses.text: If you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments, and do them, I will give you rain in due seasons.
verses.textLatin: Si in præceptis meis ambulaveritis, et mandata mea custodieritis, et feceritis ea, dabo vobis pluvias temporibus suis,

verses.text: And the ground shall bring forth its increase, and the trees shall be filled with fruit.
verses.textLatin: et terra gignet germen suum, et pomis arbores replebuntur.

verses.text: The threshing of your harvest shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time: and you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land without fear.
verses.textLatin: Apprehendet messium tritura vindemiam, et vindemia occupabit sementem: et comedetis panem vestrum in saturitate, et absque pavore habitabitis in terra vestra.

verses.text: I will give peace in your coasts: you shall sleep, and there shall be none to make you afraid. I will take away evil beasts: and the sword shall not pass through your quarters.
verses.textLatin: Dabo pacem in finibus vestris: dormietis, et non erit qui exterreat. Auferam malas bestias, et gladius non transibit terminos vestros.

verses.text: You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you.
verses.textLatin: Persequemini inimicos vestros, et corruent coram vobis.

verses.text: Five of yours shall pursue a hundred others, and a hundred of you ten thousand: your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
verses.textLatin: Persequentur quinque de vestris centum alienos, et centum de vobis decem millia: cadent inimici vestri gladio in conspectu vestro.

verses.text: I will look on you, and make you increase: you shall be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you.
verses.textLatin: Respiciam vos, et crescere faciam: multiplicabimini, et firmabo pactum meum vobiscum.

verses.text: You shall eat the oldest of the old store, and, new coming on, you shall cast away the old.
verses.textLatin: Comedetis vetustissima veterum, et vetera novis supervenientibus projicietis.

verses.text: I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you, and my soul shall not cast you off.
verses.textLatin: Ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestri, et non abjiciet vos anima mea.

verses.text: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.
verses.textLatin: Ambulabo inter vos, et ero Deus vester, vosque eritis populus meus.

verses.text: I am the Lord your God: who have brought you out of the land of the Egyptians, that you should not serve them, and who have broken the chains of your necks, that you might go upright.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus Deus vester, qui eduxi vos de terra Ægyptiorum, ne serviretis eis: et qui confregi catenas cervicum vestrarum, ut incederetis erecti.

verses.text: But if you will not hear me, nor do all my commandments,
verses.textLatin: Quod si non audieritis me, nec feceritis omnia mandata mea,

verses.text: If you despise my laws, and contemn my judgments so as not to do those things which are appointed by me, and to make void my covenant:
verses.textLatin: si spreveritis leges meas, et judicia mea contempseritis, ut non faciatis ea quæ a me constituta sunt, et ad irritum perducatis pactum meum:

verses.text: I also will do these things to you: I will quickly visit you with poverty, and burning heat, which shall waste your eyes, and consume your lives. You shall sow your seed in vain, which shall be devoured by your enemies.
verses.textLatin: ego quoque hæc faciam vobis: visitabo vos velociter in egestate, et ardore, qui conficiat oculos vestros, et consumat animas vestras. Frustra seretis sementem, quæ ab hostibus devorabitur.

verses.text: I will set my face against you, and you shall fall down before your enemies, and shall be made subject to them that hate you, you shall flee when no man pursueth you.
verses.textLatin: Ponam faciem meam contra vos, et corruetis coram hostibus vestris, et subjiciemini his qui oderunt vos: fugietis, nemine persequente.

verses.text: But if you will not yet for all this obey me: I will chastise you seven times more for your sins,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem nec sic obedieritis mihi, addam correptiones vestras septuplum propter peccata vestra,

verses.text: And I will break the pride of your stubbornness, and I will make to you the heaven above as iron, and the earth as brass:
verses.textLatin: et conteram superbiam duritiæ vestræ. Daboque vobis cælum desuper sicut ferrum, et terram æneam.

verses.text: Your labour shall be spent in vain, the ground shall not bring forth her increase, nor the trees yield their fruit.
verses.textLatin: Consumetur incassum labor vester, non proferet terra germen, nec arbores poma præbebunt.

verses.text: If you walk contrary to me, and will not hearken to me, I will bring seven times more plagues upon you for your sins:
verses.textLatin: Si ambulaveritis ex adverso mihi, nec volueritis audire me, addam plagas vestras in septuplum propter peccata vestra:

verses.text: And I will send in upon you the beasts of the field, to destroy you and your cattle, and make you few in number, and that your highways may be desolate.
verses.textLatin: immittamque in vos bestias agri, quæ consumant vos, et pecora vestra, et ad paucitatem cuncta redigant, desertæque fiant viæ vestræ.

verses.text: And if even so you will not amend, but will walk contrary to me:
verses.textLatin: Quod si nec sic volueritis recipere disciplinam, sed ambulaveritis ex adverso mihi:

verses.text: I also will walk contrary to you, and will strike you seven times for your sins.
verses.textLatin: ego quoque contra vos adversus incedam, et percutiam vos septies propter peccata vestra,

verses.text: And I will bring in upon you the sword that shall avenge my covenant. And when you shall flee into the cities, I will send the pestilence in the midst of you, and you shall be delivered into the hands of your enemies,
verses.textLatin: inducamque super vos gladium ultorem fœderis mei. Cumque confugeritis in urbes, mittam pestilentiam in medio vestri, et trademini in manibus hostium,

verses.text: After I shall have broken the staff of your bread: so that ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and give it out by weight: and you shall eat, and shall not be filled.
verses.textLatin: postquam confregero baculum panis vestri: ita ut decem mulieres in uno clibano coquant panes, et reddant eos ad pondus: et comedetis, et non saturabimini.

verses.text: But if you will not for all this hearken to me, but will walk against me:
verses.textLatin: Sin autem nec per hæc audieritis me, sed ambulaveritis contra me:

verses.text: I will also go against you with opposite fury, and I will chastise you with seven plagues for your sins,
verses.textLatin: et ego incedam adversus vos in furore contrario, et corripiam vos septem plagis propter peccata vestra:

verses.text: So that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and of your daughters.
verses.textLatin: ita ut comedatis carnes filiorum vestrorum et filiarum vestrarum.

verses.text: I will destroy your high places, and break your idols. You shall fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.
verses.textLatin: Destruam excelsa vestra, et simulacra confringam. Cadetis inter ruinas idolorum vestrorum, et abominabitur vos anima mea,

verses.text: Insomuch that I will bring your cities to be a wilderness, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and will receive no more your sweet odours.
verses.textLatin: in tantum ut urbes vestras redigam in solitudinem, et deserta faciam sanctuaria vestra, nec recipiam ultra odorem suavissimum.

verses.text: And I will destroy your land, and your enemies shall be astonished at it, when they shall be the inhabitants thereof.
verses.textLatin: Disperdamque terram vestram, et stupebunt super ea inimici vestri, cum habitatores illius fuerint.

verses.text: And I will scatter you among the Gentiles, and I will draw out the sword after you, and your land shall be desert, and your cities destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem dispergam in gentes, et evaginabo post vos gladium, eritque terra vestra deserta, et civitates vestræ dirutæ.

verses.text: Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths all the days of her desolation: when you shall be
verses.textLatin: Tunc placebunt terræ sabbata sua cunctis diebus solitudinis suæ: quando fueritis

verses.text: In the enemy’s land, she shall keep a sabbath, and rest in the sabbaths of her desolation, because she did not rest in your sabbaths when you dwelt therein.
verses.textLatin: in terra hostili, sabbatizabit, et requiescet in sabbatis solitudinis suæ, eo quod non requieverit in sabbatis vestris quando habitabatis in ea.

verses.text: And as to them that shall remain of you I will send fear in their hearts in the countries of their enemies, the sound of a flying leaf shall terrify them, and they shall flee as it were from the sword: they shall fall, when no man pursueth them,
verses.textLatin: Et qui de vobis remanserint, dabo pavorem in cordibus eorum in regionibus hostium, terrebit eos sonitus folii volantis, et ita fugient quasi gladium: cadent, nullo persequente,

verses.text: And they shall every one fall upon their brethren as fleeing from wars, none of you shall dare to resist your enemies.
verses.textLatin: et corruent singuli super fratres suos, quasi bella fugientes, nemo vestrum inimicis audebit resistere.

verses.text: You shall perish among the Gentiles, and an enemy’s land shall consume you.
verses.textLatin: Peribitis inter gentes, et hostilis vos terra consumet.

verses.text: And if of them also some remain, they shall pine away in their iniquities, in the land of their enemies, and they shall be afflicted for the sins of their fathers, and their own:
verses.textLatin: Quod si et de iis aliqui remanserint, tabescent in iniquitatibus suis, in terra inimicorum suorum, et propter peccata patrum suorum et sua affligentur:

verses.text: Until they confess their iniquities and the iniquities of their ancestors, whereby they have transgressed against me, and walked contrary unto me.
verses.textLatin: donec confiteantur iniquitates suas, et majorum suorum, quibus prævaricati sunt in me, et ambulaverunt ex adverso mihi.

verses.text: Therefore I also will walk against them, and bring them into their enemies’ land until their uncircumcised mind be ashamed: then shall they pray for their sins.
verses.textLatin: Ambulabo igitur et ego contra eos, et inducam illos in terram hostilem, donec erubescat incircumcisa mens eorum: tunc orabunt pro impietatibus suis.

verses.text: And I will remember my covenant, that I made with Jacob, and Isaac, and Abraham. I will remember also the land:
verses.textLatin: Et recordabor fœderis mei, quod pepigi cum Jacob, et Isaac, et Abraham. Terræ quoque memor ero:

verses.text: Which when she shall be left by them, shall enjoy her sabbaths, being desolate for them. But they shall pray for their sins, because they rejected my judgments, and despised my laws.
verses.textLatin: quæ cum relicta fuerit ab eis, complacebit sibi in sabbatis suis, patiens solitudinem propter illos. Ipsi vero rogabunt pro peccatis suis, eo quod abjecerint judicia mea, et leges meas despexerint.

verses.text: And yet for all that when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not cast them off altogether, neither did I so despise them that they should be quite consumed, and I should make void my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God.
verses.textLatin: Et tamen etiam cum essent in terra hostili, non penitus abjeci eos, neque sic despexi ut consumerentur, et irritum facerent pactum meum cum eis. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus eorum,

verses.text: And I will remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, in the sight of the Gentiles, to be their God. I am the Lord. These are the judgments, and precepts, and laws, which the Lord gave between him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.textLatin: et recordabor fœderis mei pristini, quando eduxi eos de terra Ægypti in conspectu gentium, ut essem Deus eorum. Ego Dominus. Hæc sunt judicia atque præcepta et leges quas dedit Dominus inter se et filios Israël in monte Sinai per manum Moysi.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man that shall have made a vow, and promised his soul to God, shall give the price according to estimation.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Homo qui votum fecerit, et spoponderit Deo animam suam, sub æstimatione dabit pretium.

verses.text: If it be a man from twenty years old unto sixty years old, he shall give fifty sicles of silver, after the weight of the sanctuary:
verses.textLatin: Si fuerit masculus a vigesimo anno usque ad sexagesimum annum, dabit quinquaginta siclos argenti ad mensuram sanctuarii:

verses.text: If a woman, thirty.
verses.textLatin: si mulier, triginta.

verses.text: But from the fifth year until the twentieth, a man shall give twenty sicles: a woman ten.
verses.textLatin: A quinto autem anno usque ad vigesimum, masculus dabit viginti siclos: femina, decem.
