verses.textLatin: et in hostias pacificorum boves duos, arietes quinque, hircos quinque, agnos anniculos quinque. Hæc fuit oblatio Salamiel filii Surisaddai.

verses.text: The sixth day the prince of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph the son of Duel,
verses.textLatin: Die sexto princeps filiorum Gad, Eliasaph filius Duel,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles by the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:
verses.textLatin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila conspersa oleo in sacrificum:

verses.text: The seventh day the prince of the sons of Ephraim, Elisama the son of Ammiud,
verses.textLatin: Die septimo princeps filiorum Ephraim, Elisama filius Ammiud,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:

verses.text: The eighth day the prince of the sons of Manasses, Gamaliel the son of Phadassur,
verses.textLatin: Die octavo, princeps filiorum Manasse, Gamaliel filius Phadassur,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles, according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:

verses.text: The ninth day the prince of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan the son of Gedeon,
verses.textLatin: Die nono princeps filiorum Benjamin, Abidan filius Gedeonis,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles by the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:
verses.textLatin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila conspersa oleo in sacrificum:

verses.text: An ox of the herd, and a ram, and a lamb of a year old for a holocaust:
verses.textLatin: bovem de armento, et arietem, et agnum anniculum in holocaustum:

verses.text: The tenth day the prince of the sons of Dan, Ahiezer the son of Ammisaddai,
verses.textLatin: Die decimo princeps filiorum Dan, Ahiezer filius Ammisaddai,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles, according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:
verses.textLatin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila conspersa oleo in sacrificum:

verses.text: The eleventh day the prince of the sons of Aser, Phegiel the son of Ochran,
verses.textLatin: Die undecimo princeps filiorum Aser, Phegiel filius Ochran,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles, according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:
verses.textLatin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila conspersa oleo in sacrificum:

verses.textLatin: mortariolum aureum appendens decem siclos, plenum incenso:

verses.textLatin: bovem de armento, et arietem, et agnum anniculum in holocaustum:

verses.textLatin: et in hostias pacificorum boves duos, arietes quinque, hircos quinque, agnos anniculos quinque. Hæc fuit oblatio Phegiel filii Ochran.

verses.text: The twelfth day the prince of the sons of Nephtali, Ahira the son of Enan,
verses.textLatin: Die duodecimo princeps filiorum Nephthali, Ahira filius Enan,

verses.text: Offered a silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles, a silver bowl of seventy sicles, according to the weight of the sanctuary, both full of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice:
verses.textLatin: obtulit acetabulum argenteum appendens centum triginta siclos, phialam argenteam habentem septuaginta siclos, ad pondus sanctuarii, utrumque plenum simila oleo conspersa in sacrificum:

verses.text: A little mortar of gold weighing ten sicles full of incense:
verses.textLatin: mortariolum aureum appendens decem siclos, plenum incenso:

verses.text: An ox of the herd, and a ram, and a lamb of a year old for a holocaust:
verses.textLatin: bovem de armento, et arietem, et agnum anniculum in holocaustum:

verses.text: And a buck goat for sin:
verses.textLatin: hircumque pro peccato:

verses.text: And for sacrifices of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five buck goats, five lambs of a year old. This was the offering of Ahira the son of Enan.
verses.textLatin: et in hostias pacificorum boves duos, arietes quinque, hircos quinque, agnos anniculos quinque. Hæc fuit oblatio Ahira filii Enan.

verses.text: These were the offerings made by the princes of Israel in the dedication of the altar, in the day wherein it was consecrated. Twelve dishes of silver: twelve silver bowls: twelve little mortars of gold:
verses.textLatin: Hæc in dedicatione altaris oblata sunt a principibus Israël, in die qua consecratum est: acetabula argentea duodecim: phialæ argenteæ duodecim: mortariola aurea duodecim:

verses.text: Each dish weighing a hundred and thirty sicles of silver, and each bowl seventy sicles: that is, putting all the vessels of silver together, two thousand four hundred sicles, by the weight of the sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: ita ut centum triginta siclos argenti haberet unum acetabulum, et septuaginta siclos haberet una phiala: id est, in commune vasorum omnium ex argento sicli duo millia quadringenti, pondere sanctuarii:

verses.text: Twelve little mortars of gold full of incense, weighing ten sicles apiece, by the weight of the sanctuary: that is, in all a hundred and twenty sicles of gold.
verses.textLatin: mortariola aurea duodecim plena incenso, denos siclos appendentia pondere sanctuarii: id est, simul auri sicli centum viginti:

verses.text: Twelve oxen out of the herd for a holocaust, twelve rams, twelve lambs of a year old, and their libations: twelve buck goats for sin.
verses.textLatin: boves de armento in holocaustum duodecim, arietes duodecim, agni anniculi duodecim, et libamenta eorum: hirci duodecim pro peccato.

verses.text: And for sacrifices of peace offerings, oxen twenty-four, rams sixty, buck goats sixty, lambs of a year old sixty. These things were offered in the dedication of the altar, when it was anointed.
verses.textLatin: In hostias pacificorum, boves viginti quatuor, arietes sexaginta, hirci sexaginta, agni anniculi sexaginta. Hæc oblata sunt in dedicatione altaris, quando unctum est.

verses.text: And when Moses entered into the tabernacle of the covenant, to consult the oracle, he heard the voice of one speaking to him from the propitiatory, that was over the ark between the two cherubims, and from this place he spoke to him.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ingrederetur Moyses tabernaculum fœderis, ut consuleret oraculum, audiebat vocem loquentis ad se de propitiatorio quod erat super arcam testimonii inter duos cherubim, unde et loquebatur ei.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Aaron, and thou shalt say to him: When thou shalt place the seven lamps, let the candlestick be set up on the south side. Give orders therefore that the lamps look over against the north, towards the table of the loaves of proposition, over against that part shall they give light, towards which the candlestick looketh.
verses.textLatin: Loquere Aaron, et dices ad eum: Cum posueris septem lucernas, candelabrum in australi parte erigatur. Hoc igitur præcipe ut lucernæ contra boream e regione respiciant ad mensam panum propositionis, contra eam partem, quam candelabrum respicit, lucere debebunt.

verses.text: And Aaron did so, and he put the lamps upon the candlestick, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque Aaron, et imposuit lucernas super candelabrum, ut præceperat Dominus Moysi.

verses.text: Now this was the work of the candlestick, it was of beaten gold, both the shaft in the middle, and all that came out of both sides of the branches: according to the pattern which the Lord had shewn to Moses, so he made the candlestick.
verses.textLatin: Hæc autem erat factura candelabri, ex auro ductili, tam medius stipes, quam cuncta quæ ex utroque calamorum latere nascebantur: juxta exemplum quod ostendit Dominus Moysi, ita operatus est candelabrum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Take the Levites out of the midst of the children of Israel, and thou shalt purify them,
verses.textLatin: Tolle Levitas de medio filiorum Israël, et purificabis eos

verses.text: According to this rite: Let them be sprinkled with the water of purification, and let them shave all the hairs of their flesh. And when they shall have washed their garments, and are cleansed,
verses.textLatin: juxta hunc ritum: aspergantur aqua lustrationis, et radant omnes pilos carnis suæ. Cumque laverint vestimenta sua, et mundati fuerint,

verses.text: They shall take an ox of the herd, and for the offering thereof fine flour tempered with oil: and thou shalt take another ox of the herd for a sin offering:
verses.textLatin: tollent bovem de armentis, et libamentum ejus similam oleo conspersam: bovem autem alterum de armento tu accipies pro peccato:

verses.text: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the covenant, calling together all the multitude of the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: et applicabis Levitas coram tabernaculo fœderis, convocata omni multitudine filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And when the Levites are before the Lord, the children of Israel shall put their hands upon them:
verses.textLatin: Cumque Levitæ fuerint coram Domino, ponent filii Israël manus suas super eos.

verses.text: And Aaron shall offer the Levites, as a gift in the sight of the Lord from the children of Israel, that they may serve in his ministry.
verses.textLatin: Et offeret Aaron Levitas, munus in conspectu Domini a filiis Israël, ut serviant in ministerio ejus.

verses.text: The Levites also shall put their hands upon the heads of the oxen, of which thou shalt sacrifice one for sin, and the other for a holocaust to the Lord, to pray for them.
verses.textLatin: Levitæ quoque ponent manus suas super capita boum, e quibus unum facies pro peccato, et alterum in holocaustum Domini, ut depreceris pro eis.

verses.text: And thou shalt set the Levites in the sight of Aaron and of his sons, and shalt consecrate them being offered to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Statuesque Levitas in conspectu Aaron et filiorum ejus, et consecrabis oblatos Domino,

verses.text: And shalt separate them from the midst of the children of Israel, to be mine.
verses.textLatin: ac separabis de medio filiorum Israël, ut sint mei.

verses.text: And afterwards they shall enter into the tabernacle of the covenant, to serve me. And thus shalt thou purify and consecrate them for an oblation of the Lord: for as a gift they were given me by the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et postea ingredientur tabernaculum fœderis, ut serviant mihi. Sicque purificabis et consecrabis eos in oblationem Domini: quoniam dono donati sunt mihi a filiis Israël.

verses.text: I have taken them instead of the firstborn that open every womb in Israel,
verses.textLatin: Pro primogenitis quæ aperiunt omnem vulvam in Israël, accepi eos.

verses.text: For all the firstborn of the children of Israel, both of men and of beasts, are mine. From the day that I slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, have I sanctified them to myself:
verses.textLatin: Mea sunt enim omnia primogenita filiorum Israël, tam ex hominibus quam ex jumentis. Ex die quo percussi omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti, sanctificavi eos mihi:

verses.text: And I have taken the Levites for all the firstborn of the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: et tuli Levitas pro cunctis primogenitis filiorum Israël,

verses.text: And have delivered them for a gift to Aaron and his sons out of the midst of the people, to serve me for Israel in the tabernacle of the covenant, and to pray for them, lest there should be a plague among the people, if they should presume to approach unto my sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: tradidique eos dono Aaron et filiis ejus de medio populi, ut serviant mihi pro Israël in tabernaculo fœderis, et orent pro eis ne sit in populo plaga, si ausi fuerint accedere ad sanctuarium.

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron and all the multitude of the children of Israel did with the Levites all that the Lord had commanded Moses:
verses.textLatin: Feceruntque Moyses et Aaron et omnis multitudo filiorum Israël super Levitas quæ præceperat Dominus Moysi:

verses.text: And they were purified, and washed their garments. And Aaron lifted them up in the sight of the Lord, and prayed for them,
verses.textLatin: purificatique sunt, et laverunt vestimenta sua. Elevavitque eos Aaron in conspectu Domini, et oravit pro eis,

verses.text: That being purified they might go into the tabernacle of the covenant to do their services before Aaron and his sons. As the Lord had commanded Moses touching the Levites, so was it done.
verses.textLatin: ut purificati ingrederentur ad officia sua in tabernaculum fœderis coram Aaron et filiis ejus. Sicut præceperat Dominus Moysi de Levitis, ita factum est.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: This is the law of the Levites: From twenty-five years old and upwards, they shall go in to minister in the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est lex Levitarum: a viginti quinque annis et supra, ingredientur ut ministrent in tabernaculo fœderis.

verses.text: And when they shall have accomplished the fiftieth year of their age, they shall cease to serve:
verses.textLatin: Cumque quinquagesimum annum ætatis impleverint, servire cessabunt,

verses.text: And they shall be the ministers of their brethren in the tabernacle of the covenant, to keep the things that are committed to their care, but not to do the works. Thus shalt thou order the Levites touching their charge.
verses.textLatin: eruntque ministri fratrum suorum in tabernaculo fœderis, ut custodiant quæ sibi fuerunt commendata: opera autem ipsa non faciant. Sic dispones Levitis in custodiis suis.

verses.text: The  Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai, the second year after they were come out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen in deserto Sinai anno secundo, postquam egressi sunt de terra Ægypti, mense primo, dicens:

verses.text: Let the children of Israel make the phase in its due time,
verses.textLatin: Faciant filii Israël Phase in tempore suo,

verses.text: The fourteenth day of this month in the evening, according to all the ceremonies and justifications thereof.
verses.textLatin: quartadecima die mensis hujus ad vesperam, juxta omnes cæremonias et justificationes ejus.

verses.text: And Moses commanded the children of Israel that they should make the phase.
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque Moyses filiis Israël ut facerent Phase.

verses.text: And they made it in its proper time: the fourteenth day of the month at evening, in mount Sinai. The children of Israel did according to all things that the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.textLatin: Qui fecerunt tempore suo, quartadecima die mensis ad vesperam, in monte Sinai. Juxta omnia quæ mandaverat Dominus Moysi, fecerunt filii Israël.

verses.text: But behold some who were unclean by occasion of the soul of a man, who could not make the phase on that day, coming to Moses and Aaron,
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem quidam immundi super anima hominis, qui non poterant facere Phase in die illo, accedentes ad Moysen et Aaron,

verses.text: Said to them: We are unclean by occasion of the soul of a man. Why are we kept back that we may not offer in its season the offering to the Lord among the children of Israel?
verses.textLatin: dixerunt eis: Immundi sumus super anima hominis: quare fraudamur ut non valeamus oblationem offerre Domino in tempore suo inter filios Israël?

verses.text: And Moses answered them: Stay that I may consult the Lord what he will ordain concerning you.
verses.textLatin: Quibus respondit Moyses: State ut consulam quid præcipiat Dominus de vobis.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Say to the children of Israel: The man that shall be unclean by occasion of one that is dead, or shall be in a journey afar off in your nation, let him make the phase to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël: Homo, qui fuerit immundus super anima, sive in via procul in gente vestra, faciat Phase Domino

verses.text: In the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, they shall eat it with unleavened bread and wild lettuce:
verses.textLatin: in mense secundo, quartadecima die mensis ad vesperam. Cum azymis et lactucis agrestibus comedent illud:

verses.text: They shall not leave any thing thereof until morning, nor break a bone thereof, they shall observe all the ceremonies of the phase.
verses.textLatin: non relinquent ex eo quippiam usque mane, et os ejus non confringent: omnem ritum Phase observabunt.

verses.text: But if any man is clean, and was not on a journey, and did not make the phase, that soul shall be cut off from among his people, because he offered not sacrifice to the Lord in due season: he shall bear his sin.
verses.textLatin: Si quis autem et mundus est, et in itinere non fuit, et tamen non fecit Phase, exterminabitur anima illa de populis suis, quia sacrificium Domino non obtulit tempore suo: peccatum suum ipse portabit.

verses.text: The sojourner also and the stranger if they be among you, shall make the phase to the Lord according to the ceremonies and justifications thereof. The same ordinance shall be with you both for the stranger, and for him that was born in the land.
verses.textLatin: Peregrinus quoque et advena si fuerint apud vos, facient Phase Domino juxta cæremonias et justificationes ejus. Præceptum idem erit apud vos tam advenæ quam indigenæ.

verses.text: Now on the day that the tabernacle was reared up, a cloud covered it. But from the evening there was over the tabernacle, as it were, the appearance of fire until the morning.
verses.textLatin: Igitur die qua erectum est tabernaculum, operuit illud nubes. A vespere autem super tentorium erat quasi species ignis usque mane.

verses.text: So it was always: by day the cloud covered it, and by night as it were the appearance of fire.
verses.textLatin: Sic fiebat jugiter: per diem operiebat illud nubes, et per noctem quasi species ignis.

verses.text: And when the cloud that covered the tabernacle was taken up, then the children of Israel marched forward: and in the place where the cloud stood still, there they camped.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ablata fuisset nubes, quæ tabernaculum protegebat, tunc proficiscebantur filii Israël: et in loco ubi stetisset nubes, ibi castrametabantur.

verses.text: At the commandment of the Lord they marched, and at his commandment they pitched the tabernacle. All the days that the cloud abode over the tabernacle, they remained in the same place:
verses.textLatin: Ad imperium Domini proficiscebantur, et ad imperium illius figebant tabernaculum. Cunctis diebus quibus stabat nubes super tabernaculum, manebant in eodem loco:

verses.text: And if it was so that it continued over it a long time, the children of Israel kept the watches of the Lord, and marched not,
verses.textLatin: et si evenisset ut multo tempore maneret super illud, erant filii Israël in excubiis Domini, et non proficiscebantur

verses.text: For as many days soever as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle. At the commandment of the Lord they pitched their tents, and at his commandment they took them down.
verses.textLatin: quot diebus fuisset nubes super tabernaculum. Ad imperium Domini erigebant tentoria, et ad imperium illius deponebant.

verses.text: If the cloud tarried from evening until morning, and immediately at break of day left the tabernacle, they marched forward: and if it departed after a day and a night, they took down their tents.
verses.textLatin: Si fuisset nubes a vespere usque mane, et statim diluculo tabernaculum reliquisset, proficiscebantur: et si post diem et noctem recessisset, dissipabant tentoria.

verses.text: But if it remained over the tabernacle for two days or a month or a longer time, the children of Israel remained in the same place, and marched not: but immediately as soon as it departed, they removed the camp.
verses.textLatin: Si vero biduo aut uno mense vel longiori tempore fuisset super tabernaculum, manebant filii Israël in eodem loco, et non proficiscebantur: statim autem ut recessisset, movebant castra.

verses.text: By the word of the Lord they pitched their tents, and by his word they marched: and kept the watches of the Lord according to his commandment by the hand of Moses.
verses.textLatin: Per verbum Domini figebant tentoria, et per verbum illius proficiscebantur: erantque in excubiis Domini juxta imperium ejus per manum Moysi.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Make thee two trumpets of beaten silver, wherewith thou mayest call together the multitude when the camp is to be removed.
verses.textLatin: Fac tibi duas tubas argenteas ductiles, quibus convocare possis multitudinem quando movenda sunt castra.

verses.text: And when thou shalt sound the trumpets, all the multitude shall gather unto thee to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Cumque increpueris tubis, congregabitur ad te omnis turba ad ostium tabernaculi fœderis.

verses.text: If thou sound but once, the princes and the heads of the multitude of Israel shall come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Si semel clangueris, venient ad te principes, et capita multitudinis Israël.

verses.text: But if the sound of the trumpets be longer, and with interruptions, they that are on the east side, shall first go forward.
verses.textLatin: Si autem prolixior atque concisus clangor increpuerit, movebunt castra primi qui sunt ad orientalem plagam.

verses.text: And at the second sounding and like noise of the trumpet, they who lie on the south side shall take up their tents. And after this manner shall the rest do, when the trumpets shall sound for a march.
verses.textLatin: In secundo autem sonitu et pari ululatu tubæ, levabunt tentoria qui habitant ad meridiem; et juxta hunc modum reliqui facient, ululantibus tubis in profectionem.

verses.text: But when the people is to be gathered together, the sound of the trumpets shall be plain, and they shall not make a broken sound.
verses.textLatin: Quando autem congregandus est populus, simplex tubarum clangor erit, et non concise ululabunt.

verses.text: And the sons of Aaron the priest shall sound the trumpets: and this shall be an ordinance for ever in your generations.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Aaron sacerdotes clangent tubis: eritque hoc legitimum sempiternum in generationibus vestris.

verses.text: If you go forth to war out of your land against the enemies that fight against you, you shall sound aloud with the trumpets, and there shall be a remembrance of you before the Lord your God, that you may be delivered out of the hands of your enemies.
verses.textLatin: Si exieritis ad bellum de terra vestra contra hostes qui dimicant adversum vos, clangetis ululantibus tubis, et erit recordatio vestri coram Domino Deo vestro, ut eruamini de manibus inimicorum vestrorum.

verses.text: If at any time you shall have a banquet, and on your festival days, and on the first days of your months, you shall sound the trumpets over the holocausts, and the sacrifices of peace offerings, that they may be to you for a remembrance of your God. I am the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: Siquando habebitis epulum, et dies festos, et calendas, canetis tubis super holocaustis, et pacificis victimis, ut sint vobis in recordationem Dei vestri. Ego Dominus Deus vester.

verses.text: The second year, in the second month, the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle of the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Anno secundo, mense secundo, vigesima die mensis, elevata est nubes de tabernaculo fœderis:

verses.text: And the children of Israel marched by their troops from the desert of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Pharan.
verses.textLatin: profectique sunt filii Israël per turmas suas de deserto Sinai, et recubuit nubes in solitudine Pharan.

verses.text: And the first went forward according to the commandment of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
verses.textLatin: Moveruntque castra primi juxta imperium Domini in manu Moysi.

verses.text: The sons of Juda by their troops: whose prince was Nahasson the son of Aminadab.
verses.textLatin: Filii Juda per turmas suas: quorum princeps erat Nahasson filius Aminadab.

verses.text: In the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the prince was Nathanael the son of Suar.
verses.textLatin: In tribu filiorum Issachar fuit princeps Nathanaël filius Suar.

verses.text: In the tribe of Zabulon, the prince was Eliab the son of Helon.
verses.textLatin: In tribu Zabulon erat princeps Eliab filius Helon.

verses.text: And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gerson and Merari set forward, bearing it.
verses.textLatin: Depositumque est tabernaculum, quod portantes egressi sunt filii Gerson et Merari.

verses.text: And the sons of Ruben also marched, by their troops and ranks, whose prince was Helisur the son of Sedeur.
verses.textLatin: Profectique sunt et filii Ruben, per turmas et ordinem suum: quorum princeps erat Helisur filius Sedeur.

verses.text: And in the tribe of Simeon, the prince was Salamiel the son of Surisaddai.
verses.textLatin: In tribu autem filiorum Simeon, princeps fuit Salamiel filius Surisaddai.

verses.text: And in the tribe of Gad, the prince was Eliasaph the son of Duel.
verses.textLatin: Porro in tribu Gad erat princeps Eliasaph filius Duel.

verses.text: Then the Caathites also marched carrying the sanctuary. So long was the tabernacle carried, till they came to the place of setting it up.
verses.textLatin: Profectique sunt et Caathitæ portantes sanctuarium. Tamdiu tabernaculum portabatur, donec venirent ad erectionis locum.

verses.text: The sons of Ephraim also moved their camp by their troops, in whose army the prince was Elisama the son of Ammiud.
verses.textLatin: Moverunt castra et filii Ephraim per turmas suas, in quorum exercitu princeps erat Elisama filius Ammiud.

verses.text: And in the tribe of the sons of Manasses, the prince was Gamaliel the son of Phadassur.
verses.textLatin: In tribu autem filiorum Manasse princeps fuit Gamaliel filius Phadassur.

verses.text: And in the tribe of Benjamin, the prince was Abidan the son of Gedeon.
verses.textLatin: Et in tribu Benjamin erat dux Abidan filius Gedeonis.

verses.text: The last of all the camp marched the sons of Dan by their troops, in whose army the prince was Ahiezer the son of Ammisaddai.
verses.textLatin: Novissimi castrorum omnium profecti sunt filii Dan per turmas suas, in quorum exercitu princeps fuit Ahiezer filius Ammisaddai.

verses.text: And in the tribe of the sons of Aser, the prince was Phegiel the son of Ochran.
verses.textLatin: In tribu autem filiorum Aser erat princeps Phegiel filius Ochran.

verses.text: And in the tribe of the sons of Nephtali, the prince was Ahira the son of Enan.
verses.textLatin: Et in tribu filiorum Nephthali princeps fuit Ahira filius Enan.

verses.text: This was the order of the camps, and marches of the children of Israel by their troops, when they set forward.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt castra, et profectiones filiorum Israël per turmas suas quando egrediebantur.

verses.text: And Moses said to Hobab the son of Raguel the Madianite, his kinsman: We are going towards the place which the Lord will give us: come with us, that we may do thee good: for the Lord hath promised good things to Israel.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses Hobab filio Raguel Madianitæ, cognato suo: Proficiscimur ad locum quem Dominus daturus est nobis: veni nobiscum, ut benefaciamus tibi, quia Dominus bona promisit Israëli.

verses.text: But he answered him: I will not go with thee, but I will return to my country, wherein I was born.
verses.textLatin: Cui ille respondit: Non vadam tecum, sed revertar in terram meam, in qua natus sum.

verses.text: And he said: Do not leave us: for thou knowest in what places we should encamp in the wilderness, and thou shalt be our guide.
verses.textLatin: Et ille: Noli, inquit, nos relinquere: tu enim nosti in quibus locis per desertum castra ponere debeamus, et eris ductor noster.

verses.text: And if thou comest with us, we will give thee what is the best of the riches which the Lord shall deliver to us.
verses.textLatin: Cumque nobiscum veneris, quidquid optimum fuerit ex opibus, quas nobis traditurus est Dominus, dabimus tibi.

verses.text: So they marched from the mount of the Lord three days’ journey, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord went before them, for three days providing a place for the camp.
verses.textLatin: Profecti sunt ergo de monte Domini viam trium dierum, arcaque fœderis Domini præcedebat eos, per dies tres providens castrorum locum.

verses.text: The cloud also of the Lord was over them by day when they marched.
verses.textLatin: Nubes quoque Domini super eos erat per diem cum incederent.

verses.text: And when the ark was lifted up, Moses said: Arise, O Lord, and let thy enemies be scattered, and let them that hate thee, flee from before thy face.
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevaretur arca, dicebat Moyses: Surge, Domine, et dissipentur inimici tui, et fugiant qui oderunt te, a facie tua.

verses.text: And when it was set down, he said: Return, O Lord, to the multitude of the host of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem deponeretur, aiebat: Revertere, Domine, ad multitudinem exercitus Israël.

verses.text: In  the mean time there arose a murmuring of the people against the Lord, as it were repining at their fatigue. And when the Lord heard it he was angry. And the fire of the Lord being kindled against them, devoured them that were at the uttermost part of the camp.
verses.textLatin: Interea ortum est murmur populi, quasi dolentium pro labore, contra Dominum. Quod cum audisset Dominus, iratus est. Et accensus in eos ignis Domini, devoravit extremam castrorum partem.

verses.text: And when the people cried to Moses, Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire was swallowed up.
verses.textLatin: Cumque clamasset populus ad Moysen, oravit Moyses ad Dominum, et absorptus est ignis.

verses.text: And he called the name of that place, The burning: for that the fire of the Lord had been kindled against them.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque nomen loci illius, Incensio: eo quod incensus fuisset contra eos ignis Domini.

verses.text: For a mixt multitude of people, that came up with them, burned with desire, sitting and weeping, the children of Israel also being joined with them, and said: Who shall give us flesh to eat?
verses.textLatin: Vulgus quippe promiscuum, quod ascenderat cum eis, flagravit desiderio, sedens et flens, junctis sibi pariter filiis Israël, et ait: Quis dabit nobis ad vescendum carnes?

verses.text: We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt free cost: the cucumbers come into our mind, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic.
verses.textLatin: recordamur piscium quos comedebamus in Ægypto gratis: in mentem nobis veniunt cucumeres, et pepones, porrique, et cæpe, et allia.

verses.text: Our soul is dry, our eyes behold nothing else but manna.
verses.textLatin: Anima nostra arida est: nihil aliud respiciunt oculi nostri nisi man.

verses.text: Now the manna was like coriander seed, of the colour of bdellium.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem man quasi semen coriandri, coloris bdellii.

verses.text: And the people went about, and gathering it, ground it in a mill, or beat it in a mortar, and boiled it in a pot, and made cakes thereof of the taste of bread tempered with oil.
verses.textLatin: Circuibatque populus, et colligens illud, frangebat mola, sive terebat in mortario, coquens in olla, et faciens ex eo tortulas saporis quasi panis oleati.

verses.text: And when the dew fell in the night upon the camp, the manna also fell with it.
verses.textLatin: Cumque descenderet nocte super castra ros, descendebat pariter et man.

verses.text: Now Moses heard the people weeping by their families, every one at the door of his tent. And the wrath of the Lord was exceedingly enkindled: to Moses also the thing seemed insupportable.
verses.textLatin: Audivit ergo Moyses flentem populum per familias, singulos per ostia tentorii sui. Iratusque est furor Domini valde: sed et Moysi intoleranda res visa est,

verses.text: And he said to the Lord: Why hast thou afflicted thy servant? wherefore do I not find favour before thee? and why hast thou laid the weight of all this people upon me?
verses.textLatin: et ait ad Dominum: Cur afflixisti servum tuum? quare non invenio gratiam coram te? et cur imposuisti pondus universi populi hujus super me?

verses.text: Have I conceived all this multitude, or begotten them, that thou shouldst say to me: Carry them in thy bosom as the nurse is wont to carry the little infant, and bear them into the land, for which thou hast sworn to their fathers?
verses.textLatin: Numquid ego concepi omnem hanc multitudinem, vel genui eam, ut dicas mihi: Porta eos in sinu tuo sicut portare solet nutrix infantulum, et defer in terram, pro qua jurasti patribus eorum?

verses.text: Whence should I have flesh to give to so great a multitude? they weep against me, saying: Give us flesh that we may eat.
verses.textLatin: Unde mihi carnes ut dem tantæ multitudini? flent contra me, dicentes: Da nobis carnes ut comedamus.

verses.text: I am not able alone to bear all this people, because it is too heavy for me.
verses.textLatin: Non possum solus sustinere omnem hunc populum, quia gravis est mihi.

verses.text: But if it seem unto thee otherwise, I beseech thee to kill me, and let me find grace in thy eyes, that I be not afflicted with so great evils.
verses.textLatin: Sin aliter tibi videtur, obsecro ut interficias me, et inveniam gratiam in oculis tuis, ne tantis afficiar malis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Gather unto me seventy men of the ancients of Israel, whom thou knowest to be ancients and masters of the people: and thou shalt bring them to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant, and shalt make them stand there with thee,
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Congrega mihi septuaginta viros de senibus Israël, quos tu nosti quod senes populi sint ac magistri: et duces eos ad ostium tabernaculi fœderis, faciesque ibi stare tecum,

verses.text: That I may come down and speak with thee: and I will take of thy spirit, and will give to them, that they may bear with thee the burden of the people, and thou mayest not be burthened alone.
verses.textLatin: ut descendam et loquar tibi: et auferam de spiritu tuo, tradamque eis, ut sustentent tecum onus populi, et non tu solus graveris.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to the people: Be ye sanctified: to morrow you shall eat flesh: for I have heard you say: Who will give us flesh to eat? it was well with us in Egypt. That the Lord may give you flesh, and you may eat:
verses.textLatin: Populo quoque dices: Sanctificamini (cras comedetis carnes: ego enim audivi vos dicere: Quis dabit nobis escas carnium? bene nobis erat in Ægypto), ut det vobis Dominus carnes, et comedatis:

verses.text: Not for one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, no nor for twenty.
verses.textLatin: non uno die, nec duobus, vel quinque aut decem, nec viginti quidem,

verses.text: But even for a month of days, till it come out at your nostrils, and become loathsome to you, because you have cast off the Lord, who is in the midst of you, and have wept before him, saying: Why came we out of Egypt?
verses.textLatin: sed usque ad mensem dierum, donec exeat per nares vestras, et vertatur in nauseam, eo quod repuleritis Dominum, qui in medio vestri est, et fleveritis coram eo, dicentes: Quare egressi sumus ex Ægypto?

verses.text: And Moses said: There are six hundred thousand footmen of this people, and sayest thou: I will give them flesh to eat a whole month?
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: Sexcenta millia peditum hujus populi sunt: et tu dicis: Dabo eis esum carnium mense integro?

verses.text: Shall then a multitude of sheep and oxen be killed, that it may suffice for their food? or shall the fishes of the sea be gathered together to fill them?
verses.textLatin: numquid ovium et boum multitudo cædetur, ut possit sufficere ad cibum? vel omnes pisces maris in unum congregabuntur, ut eos satient?

verses.text: And the Lord answered him: Is the hand of the Lord unable? Thou shalt presently see whether my word shall come to pass or no.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Dominus: Numquid manus Domini invalida est? jam nunc videbis utrum meus sermo opere compleatur.

verses.text: Moses therefore came, and told the people the words of the Lord, and assembled seventy men of the ancients of Israel, and made them to stand about the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Venit igitur Moyses, et narravit populo verba Domini, congregans septuaginta viros de senibus Israël, quos stare fecit circa tabernaculum.

verses.text: And the Lord came down in a cloud, and spoke to him, taking away of the spirit that was in Moses, and giving to the seventy men. And when the spirit had rested on them they prophesied, nor did they cease afterwards.
verses.textLatin: Descenditque Dominus per nubem, et locutus est ad eum, auferens de spiritu qui erat in Moyse, et dans septuaginta viris. Cumque requievisset in eis spiritus, prophetaverunt, nec ultra cessaverunt.

verses.text: Now there remained in the camp two of the men, of whom one was called Eldad, and the other Medad, upon whom the spirit rested; for they also had been enrolled, but were not gone forth to the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Remanserat autem in castris duo viri, quorum unus vocabatur Eldad, et alter Medad, super quos requievit spiritus. Nam et ipsi descripti fuerant, et non exierant ad tabernaculum.

verses.text: And when they prophesied in the camp, there ran a young man, and told Moses, saying: Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp.
verses.textLatin: Cumque prophetarent in castris, cucurrit puer, et nuntiavit Moysi, dicens: Eldad et Medad prophetant in castris.

verses.text: Forthwith Josue the son of Nun, the minister of Moses, and chosen out of many, said: My lord Moses forbid them.
verses.textLatin: Statim Josue filius Nun, minister Moysi, et electus e pluribus, ait: Domine mi Moyses, prohibe eos.

verses.text: But he said: Why hast thou emulation for me? O that all the people might prophesy, and that the Lord would give them his spirit!
verses.textLatin: At ille: Quid, inquit æmularis pro me? quis tribuat ut omnis populus prophetet, et det eis Dominus spiritum suum?

verses.text: And Moses returned, with the ancients of Israel, into the camp.
verses.textLatin: Reversusque est Moyses, et majores natu Israël in castra.

verses.text: And a wind going out from the Lord, taking quails up beyond the sea brought them, and cast them into the camp for the space of one day’s journey, on every side of the camp round about, and they flew in the air two cubits high above the ground.
verses.textLatin: Ventus autem egrediens a Domino, arreptans trans mare coturnices detulit, et demisit in castra itinere quantum uno die confici potest, ex omni parte castrorum per circuitum, volabantque in aëre duobus cubitis altitudine super terram.

verses.text: The people therefore rising up all that day, and night, and the next day, gathered together of quails, he that did least, ten cores: and they dried them round about the camp.
verses.textLatin: Surgens ergo populus toto die illo, et nocte, ac die altero, congregavit coturnicum: qui parum, decem coros: et siccaverunt eas per gyrum castrorum.

verses.text: As yet the flesh was between their teeth, neither had that kind of meat failed: when behold the wrath of the Lord being provoked against the people, struck them with an exceeding great plague.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc carnes erant in dentibus eorum, nec defecerat hujuscemodi cibus: et ecce furor Domini concitatus in populum, percussit eum plaga magna nimis.

verses.text: And that place was called, The graves of lust: for there they buried the people that had lusted. And departing from the graves of lust, they came unto Haseroth, and abode there.
verses.textLatin: Vocatusque est ille locus, Sepulchra concupiscentiæ: ibi enim sepelierunt populum qui desideraverat. Egressi autem de Sepulchris concupiscentiæ, venerunt in Haseroth, et manserunt ibi.

verses.text: And  Mary and Aaron spoke against Moses, because of his wife the Ethiopian,
verses.textLatin: Locutaque est Maria et Aaron contra Moysen propter uxorem ejus Æthiopissam,

verses.text: And they said: Hath the Lord spoken by Moses only? hath he not also spoken to us in like manner? And when the Lord heard this,
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt: Num per solum Moysen locutus est Dominus? nonne et nobis similiter est locutus? Quod cum audisset Dominus

verses.text: (For Moses was a man exceeding meek above all men that dwelt upon earth)
verses.textLatin: (erat enim Moyses vir mitissimus super omnes homines qui morabantur in terra),

verses.text: Immediately he spoke to him, and to Aaron and Mary: Come out you three only to the tabernacle of the covenant. And when they were come out,
verses.textLatin: statim locutus est ad eum, et ad Aaron et Mariam: Egredimini vos tantum tres ad tabernaculum fœderis. Cumque fuissent egressi,

verses.text: The Lord came down in a pillar of the cloud, and stood in the entry of the tabernacle calling to Aaron and Mary. And when they were come,
verses.textLatin: descendit Dominus in columna nubis, et stetit in introitu tabernaculi, vocans Aaron et Mariam. Qui cum issent,

verses.text: He said to them: Hear my words: if there be among you a prophet of the Lord, I will appear to him in a vision, or I will speak to him in a dream.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad eos: Audite sermones meos: si quis fuerit inter vos propheta Domini, in visione apparebo ei, vel per somnium loquar ad illum.

verses.text: But it is not so with my servant Moses who is most faithful in all my house:
verses.textLatin: At non talis servus meus Moyses, qui in omni domo mea fidelissimus est:

verses.text: For I speak to him mouth to mouth: and plainly, and not by riddles and figures doth he see the Lord. Why then were you not afraid to speak ill of my servant Moses?
verses.textLatin: ore enim ad os loquor ei: et palam, et non per ænigmata et figuras Dominum videt. Quare ergo non timuistis detrahere servo meo Moysi?

verses.text: And being angry with them he went away:
verses.textLatin: Iratusque contra eos, abiit:

verses.text: The cloud also that was over the tabernacle departed: and behold Mary appeared white as snow with a leprosy. And when Aaron had looked on her, and saw her all covered with leprosy,
verses.textLatin: nubes quoque recessit quæ erat super tabernaculum: et ecce Maria apparuit candens lepra quasi nix. Cumque respexisset eam Aaron, et vidisset perfusam lepra,

verses.text: He said to Moses: I beseech thee, my lord, lay not upon us this sin, which we have foolishly committed:
verses.textLatin: ait ad Moysen: Obsecro, domine mi, ne imponas nobis hoc peccatum quod stulte commisimus,

verses.text: Let her not be as one dead, and as an abortive that is cast forth from the mother’s womb. Lo, now one half of her flesh is consumed with the leprosy.
verses.textLatin: ne fiat hæc quasi mortua, et ut abortivum quod projicitur de vulva matris suæ: ecce jam medium carnis ejus devoratum est a lepra.

verses.text: And Moses cried to the Lord, saying: O God, I beseech thee heal her.
verses.textLatin: Clamavitque Moyses ad Dominum, dicens: Deus, obsecro, sana eam.

verses.text: And the Lord answered him: If her father had spitten upon her face, ought she not to have been ashamed for seven days at least? Let her be separated seven days without the camp, and after wards she shall be called again.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Dominus: Si pater ejus spuisset in faciem illius, nonne debuerat saltem septem diebus rubore suffundi? separetur septem diebus extra castra, et postea revocabitur.

verses.text: Mary therefore was put out of the camp seven days: and the people moved not from that place until Mary was called again.
verses.textLatin: Exclusa est itaque Maria extra castra septem diebus: et populus non est motus de loco illo, donec revocata est Maria.

verses.text: And  the people marched from Haseroth, and pitched their tents in the desert of Pharan.
verses.textLatin: Profectusque est populus de Haseroth, fixis tentoriis in deserto Pharan.

verses.text: And there the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Ibique locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Send men to view the land of Chanaan, which I will give to the children of Israel, one of every tribe, of the rulers.
verses.textLatin: Mitte viros, qui considerent terram Chanaan, quam daturus sum filiis Israël, singulos de singulis tribubus, ex principibus.

verses.text: Moses did what the Lord had commanded, sending from the desert of Pharan, principal men, whose names are these:
verses.textLatin: Fecit Moyses quod Dominus imperaverat, de deserto Pharan mittens principes viros, quorum ista sunt nomina.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Ruben, Sammua the son of Zechur.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Ruben, Sammua filium Zechur.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Simeon, Saphat the son of Huri.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Simeon, Saphat filium Huri.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Juda, Caleb the son of Jephone.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Juda, Caleb filium Jephone.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Issachar, Igal filium Joseph.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Osee the son of Nun.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Ephraim, Osee filium Nun.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Phalti the son of Raphu.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Benjamin, Phalti filium Raphu.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Zabulon, Geddiel the son of Sodi.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Zabulon, Geddiel filium Sodi.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Joseph, of the sceptre of Manasses, Gaddi the son of Susi.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Joseph, sceptri Manasse, Gaddi filium Susi.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Dan, Ammiel filium Gemalli.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Aser, Sthur the son of Michael.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Aser, Sthur filium Michaël.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Nephtali, Nahabi the son of Vapsi.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Nephthali, Nahabi filium Vapsi.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Gad, Guel the son of Machi.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Gad, Guel filium Machi.

verses.text: These are the names of the men, whom Moses sent to view the land: and he called Osee the son of Nun, Josue.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt nomina virorum, quos misit Moyses ad considerandam terram: vocavitque Osee filium Nun, Josue.

verses.text: And Moses sent them to view the land of Chanaan, and said to them: Go you up by the south side. And when you shall come to the mountains,
verses.textLatin: Misit ergo eos Moyses ad considerandam terram Chanaan, et dixit ad eos: Ascendite per meridianam plagam. Cumque veneritis ad montes,

verses.text: View the land, of what sort it is: and the people that are the inhabitants thereof, whether they be strong or weak: few in number or many:
verses.textLatin: considerate terram, qualis sit: et populum qui habitator est ejus, utrum fortis sit an infirmus: si pauci numero an plures:

verses.text: The land itself, whether it be good or bad: what manner of cities, walled or without walls:
verses.textLatin: ipsa terra, bona an mala: urbes quales, muratæ an absque muris:

verses.text: The ground, fat or barren, woody or without trees. Be of good courage, and bring us of the fruits of the land. Now it was the time when the firstripe grapes are fit to be eaten.
verses.textLatin: humus, pinguis an sterilis, nemorosa an absque arboribus. Confortamini, et afferte nobis de fructibus terræ. Erat autem tempus quando jam præcoquæ uvæ vesci possunt.

verses.text: And when they were gone up, they viewed the land from the desert of Sin, unto Rohob as you enter into Emath.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ascendissent, exploraverunt terram a deserto Sin, usque Rohob intrantibus Emath.

verses.text: And they went up at the south side, and came to Hebron, where were Achiman and Sisai and Tholmai the sons of Enac. For Hebron was built seven years before Tanis the city of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Ascenderuntque ad meridiem, et venerunt in Hebron, ubi erant Achiman et Sisai et Tholmai filii Enac: nam Hebron septem annis ante Tanim urbem Ægypti condita est.

verses.text: And going forward as far as the torrent of the cluster of grapes, they cut off a branch with its cluster of grapes, which two men carried upon a lever. They took also of the pomegranates and of the figs of that place:
verses.textLatin: Pergentesque usque ad Torrentem botri, absciderunt palmitem cum uva sua, quem portaverunt in vecte duo viri. De malis quoque granatis et de ficis loci illius tulerunt:

verses.text: Which was called Nehelescol, that is to say, the torrent of the cluster of grapes, because from thence the children of Israel had carried a cluster of grapes.
verses.textLatin: qui appellatus est Nehelescol, id est Torrens botri, eo quod botrum portassent inde filii Israël.

verses.text: And they that went to spy out the land returned after forty days, having gone round all the country,
verses.textLatin: Reversique exploratores terræ post quadraginta dies, omni regione circuita,

verses.text: And came to Moses and Aaron and to all the assembly of the children of Israel to the desert of Pharan, which is in Cades. And speaking to them and to all the multitude, they shewed them the fruits of the land:
verses.textLatin: venerunt ad Moysen et Aaron et ad omnem cœtum filiorum Israël in desertum Pharan, quod est in Cades. Locutique eis et omni multitudini ostenderunt fructus terræ:

verses.text: And they related and said: We came into the land to which thou sentest us, which in very deed floweth with milk and honey as may be known by these fruits:
verses.textLatin: et narraverunt, dicentes: Venimus in terram, ad quam misisti nos, quæ revera fluit lacte et melle, ut ex his fructibus cognosci potest:

verses.text: But it hath very strong inhabitants, and the cities are great and walled. We saw there the race of Enac.
verses.textLatin: sed cultores fortissimos habet, et urbes grandes atque muratas. Stirpem Enac vidimus ibi.

verses.text: Amalec dwelleth in the south, the Hethite and the Jebusite and the Amorrhite in the mountains: but the Chanaanite abideth by the sea and near the streams of the Jordan.
verses.textLatin: Amalec habitat in meridie, Hethæus et Jebusæus et Amorrhæus in montanis: Chananæus vero moratur juxta mare et circa fluenta Jordanis.

verses.text: In the mean time Caleb, to still the murmuring of the people that rose against Moses, said: Let us go up and possess the land, for we shall be able to conquer it.
verses.textLatin: Inter hæc Caleb compescens murmur populi, qui oriebatur contra Moysen, ait: Ascendamus, et possideamus terram, quoniam poterimus obtinere eam.

verses.text: But the others, that had been with him, said: No, we are not able to go up to this people, because they are stronger than we.
verses.textLatin: Alii vero, qui fuerant cum eo, dicebant: Nequaquam ad hunc populum valemus ascendere, quia fortior nobis est.

verses.text: And they spoke ill of the land, which they had viewed, before the children of Israel, saying: The land which we have viewed, devoureth its inhabitants: the people, that we beheld, are of a tall stature.
verses.textLatin: Detraxeruntque terræ, quam inspexerant, apud filios Israël, dicentes: Terra, quam lustravimus, devorat habitatores suos: populus, quem aspeximus, proceræ staturæ est.

verses.text: There we saw certain monsters of the sons of Enac, of the giant kind: in comparison of whom, we seemed like locusts.
verses.textLatin: Ibi vidimus monstra quædam filiorum Enac de genere giganteo: quibus comparati, quasi locustæ videbamur.

verses.text: Therefore  the whole multitude crying wept that night.
verses.textLatin: Igitur vociferans omnis turba flevit nocte illa,

verses.text: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: et murmurati sunt contra Moysen et Aaron cuncti filii Israël, dicentes:

verses.text: Would God that we had died in Egypt: and would God we may die in this vast wilderness, and that the Lord may not bring us into this land, lest we fall by the sword, and our wives and children be led away captives. Is it not better to return into Egypt?
verses.textLatin: Utinam mortui essemus in Ægypto: et in hac vasta solitudine utinam pereamus, et non inducat nos Dominus in terram istam, ne cadamus gladio, et uxores ac liberi nostri ducantur captivi. Nonne melius est reverti in Ægyptum?

verses.text: And they said one to another: Let us appoint a captain, and let us return into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque alter ad alterum: Constituamus nobis ducem, et revertamur in Ægyptum.

verses.text: And when Moses and Aaron heard this, they fell down flat upon the ground before the multitude of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Quo audito, Moyses et Aaron ceciderunt proni in terram coram omni multitudine filiorum Israël.

verses.text: But Josue the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephone, who themselves also had viewed the land, rent their garments,
verses.textLatin: At vero Josue filius Nun et Caleb filius Jephone, qui et ipsi lustraverant terram, sciderunt vestimenta sua,

verses.text: And said to all the multitude of the children of Israel: The land which we have gone round is very good:
verses.textLatin: et ad omnem multitudinem filiorum Israël locuti sunt: Terra, quam circuivimus, valde bona est.

verses.text: If the Lord be favourable, he will bring us into it, and give us a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: Si propitius fuerit Dominus, inducet nos in eam, et tradet humum lacte et melle manantem.

verses.text: Be not rebellious against the Lord: and fear ye not the people of this land, for we are able to eat them up as bread. All aid is gone from them: the Lord is with us, fear ye not.
verses.textLatin: Nolite rebelles esse contra Dominum: neque timeatis populum terræ hujus, quia sicut panem ita eos possumus devorare. Recessit ab eis omne præsidium: Dominus nobiscum est, nolite metuere.

verses.text: And when all the multitude cried out, and would have stoned them, the glory of the Lord appeared over the tabernacle of the covenant to all the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Cumque clamaret omnis multitudo, et lapidibus eos vellet opprimere, apparuit gloria Domini super tectum fœderis cunctis filiis Israël.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: How long will this people detract me? how long will they not believe me for all the signs that I have wrought before them?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Moysen: Usquequo detrahet mihi populus iste? quousque non credent mihi, in omnibus signis quæ feci coram eis?

verses.text: I will strike them therefore with pestilence, and will consume them: but thee I will make a ruler over a great nation, and a mightier than this is.
verses.textLatin: Feriam igitur eos pestilentia, atque consumam: te autem faciam principem super gentem magnam, et fortiorem quam hæc est.

verses.text: And Moses said to the Lord: That the Egyptians, from the midst of whom thou hast brought forth this people,
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses ad Dominum: Ut audiant Ægyptii, de quorum medio eduxisti populum istum,

verses.text: And the inhabitants of this land, (who have heard that thou, O Lord, art among this people, and art seen face to face, and thy cloud protecteth them, and thou goest before them in a pillar of a cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night,)
verses.textLatin: et habitatores terræ hujus, qui audierunt quod tu, Domine, in populo isto sis, et facie videaris ad faciem, et nubes tua protegat illos, et in columna nubis præcedas eos per diem, et in columna ignis per noctem:

verses.text: May hear that thou hast killed so great a multitude as it were one man and may say:
verses.textLatin: quod occideris tantam multitudinem quasi unum hominem, et dicant:

verses.text: He could not bring the people into the land for which he had sworn, therefore did he kill them in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Non poterat introducere populum in terram pro qua juraverat: idcirco occidit eos in solitudine?

verses.text: Let then the strength of the Lord be magnified, as thou hast sworn, saying:
verses.textLatin: Magnificetur ergo fortitudo Domini sicut jurasti, dicens:

verses.text: The Lord is patient and full of mercy, taking away iniquity and wickedness, and leaving no man clear, who visitest the sins of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation.
verses.textLatin: Dominus patiens et multæ misericordiæ, auferens iniquitatem et scelera, nullumque innoxium derelinquens, qui visitas peccata patrum in filios in tertiam et quartam generationem.

verses.text: Forgive, I beseech thee, the sins of this people, according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast been merciful to them from their going out of Egypt unto this place.
verses.textLatin: Dimitte, obsecro, peccatum populi hujus secundum magnitudinem misericordiæ tuæ, sicut propitius fuisti egredientibus de Ægypto usque ad locum istum.

verses.text: And the Lord said: I have forgiven according to thy word.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus: Dimisi juxta verbum tuum.

verses.text: As I live: and the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Vivo ego: et implebitur gloria Domini universa terra.

verses.text: But yet all the men that have seen my majesty, and the signs that I have done in Egypt, and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now ten times, and have not obeyed my voice,
verses.textLatin: Attamen omnes homines qui viderunt majestatem meam, et signa quæ feci in Ægypto et in solitudine, et tentaverunt me jam per decem vices, nec obedierunt voci meæ,

verses.text: Shall not see the land for which I swore to their fathers, neither shall any one of them that hath detracted me behold it.
verses.textLatin: non videbunt terram pro qua juravi patribus eorum, nec quisquam ex illis qui detraxit mihi, intuebitur eam.

verses.text: My servant Caleb, who being full of another spirit hath followed me, I will bring into this land which he hath gone round: and his seed shall possess it.
verses.textLatin: Servum meum Caleb, qui plenus alio spiritu secutus est me, inducam in terram hanc, quam circuivit; et semen ejus possidebit eam.

verses.text: For the Amalecite and the Chanaanite dwell in the valleys. To morrow remove the camp, and return into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam Amalecites et Chananæus habitant in vallibus. Cras movete castra, et revertimini in solitudinem per viam maris Rubri.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: How long doth this wicked multitude murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Usquequo multitudo hæc pessima murmurat contra me? querelas filiorum Israël audivi.

verses.text: Say therefore to them: As I live, saith the Lord: According as you have spoken in my hearing, so will I do to you.
verses.textLatin: Dic ergo eis: Vivo ego, ait Dominus: sicut locuti estis audiente me, sic faciam vobis.

verses.text: In the wilderness shall your carcasses lie. All you that were numbered from twenty years old and upward, and have murmured against me,
verses.textLatin: In solitudine hac jacebunt cadavera vestra. Omnes qui numerati estis a viginti annis et supra, et murmurastis contra me,

verses.text: Shall not enter into the land, over which I lifted up my hand to make you dwell therein, except Caleb the son of Jephone, and Josue the son of Nun.
verses.textLatin: non intrabitis terram, super quam levavi manum meam ut habitare vos facerem, præter Caleb filium Jephone, et Josue filium Nun.

verses.text: But your children, of whom you said, that they should be a prey to the enemies, will I bring in: that they may see the land which you have despised.
verses.textLatin: Parvulos autem vestros, de quibus dixistis quod prædæ hostibus forent, introducam, ut videant terram, quæ vobis displicuit.

verses.text: Your carcasses shall lie in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Vestra cadavera jacebunt in solitudine.

verses.text: Your children shall wander in the desert forty years, and shall bear your fornication, until the carcasses of their fathers be consumed in the desert,
verses.textLatin: Filii vestri erunt vagi in deserto annis quadraginta, et portabunt fornicationem vestram, donec consumantur cadavera patrum in deserto,

verses.text: According to the number of the forty days, wherein you viewed the land: a year shall be counted for a day. And forty years you shall receive your iniquities, and shall know my revenge:
verses.textLatin: juxta numerum quadraginta dierum, quibus considerastis terram: annus pro die imputabitur. Et quadraginta annis recipietis iniquitates vestras, et scietis ultionem meam:

verses.text: For as I have spoken, so will I do to all this wicked multitude, that hath risen up together against me: in this wilderness shall it faint away and die.
verses.textLatin: quoniam sicut locutus sum, ita faciam omni multitudini huic pessimæ, quæ consurrexit adversum me: in solitudine hac deficiet, et morietur.

verses.text: Therefore all the men, whom Moses had sent to view the land, and who at their return had made the whole multitude to murmur against him, speaking ill of the land that it was naught,
verses.textLatin: Igitur omnes viri, quos miserat Moyses ad contemplandam terram, et qui reversi murmurare fecerant contra eum omnem multitudinem, detrahentes terræ quod esset mala,

verses.text: Died and were struck in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: mortui sunt atque percussi in conspectu Domini.

verses.text: But Josue the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephone lived, of all them that had gone to view the land.
verses.textLatin: Josue autem filius Nun, et Caleb filius Jephone, vixerunt ex omnibus qui perrexerant ad considerandam terram.

verses.text: And Moses spoke all these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourned exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses universa verba hæc ad omnes filios Israël, et luxit populus nimis.

verses.text: And behold rising up very early in the morning, they went up to the top of the mountain, and said: We are ready to go up to the place, of which the Lord hath spoken: for we have sinned.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce mane primo surgentes ascenderunt verticem montis, atque dixerunt: Parati sumus ascendere ad locum, de quo Dominus locutus est: quia peccavimus.

verses.text: And Moses said to them: Why transgress you the word of the Lord, which shall not succeed prosperously with you?
verses.textLatin: Quibus Moyses: Cur, inquit, transgredimini verbum Domini, quod vobis non cedet in prosperum?

verses.text: Go not up, for the Lord is not with you: lest you fall before your enemies.
verses.textLatin: nolite ascendere: non enim est Dominus vobiscum: ne corruatis coram inimicis vestris.

verses.text: The Amalecite and the Chanaanite are before you, and by their sword you shall fall, because you would not consent to the Lord, neither will the Lord be with you.
verses.textLatin: Amalecites et Chananæus ante vos sunt, quorum gladio corruetis, eo quod nolueritis acquiescere Domino: nec erit Dominus vobiscum.

verses.text: But they being blinded went up to the top of the mountain. But the ark of the testament of the Lord and Moses departed not from the camp.
verses.textLatin: At illi contenebrati ascenderunt in verticem montis. Arca autem testamenti Domini et Moyses non recesserunt de castris.

verses.text: And the Amalecite came down, and the Chanaanite that dwelt in the mountain: and smiting and slaying them pursued them as far as Horma.
verses.textLatin: Descenditque Amalecites et Chananæus, qui habitabat in monte: et percutiens eos atque concidens, persecutus est eos usque Horma.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall be come into the land of your habitation, which I will give you,
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad filios Israël, et dices ad eos: Cum ingressi fueritis terram habitationis vestræ, quam ego dabo vobis,

verses.text: And shall make an offering to the Lord, for a holocaust, or a victim, paying your vows, or voluntarily offering gifts, or in your solemnities burning a sweet savour unto the Lord, of oxen or of sheep:
verses.textLatin: et feceritis oblationem Domino in holocaustum, aut victimam, vota solventes, vel sponte offerentes munera, aut in solemnitatibus vestris adolentes odorem suavitatis Domino, de bobus sive de ovibus:

verses.text: Whosoever immolateth the victim, shall offer a sacrifice of fine flour, the tenth part of an ephi, tempered with the fourth part of a hin of oil:
verses.textLatin: offeret quicumque immolaverit victimam, sacrificium similæ, decimam partem ephi, conspersæ oleo, quod mensuram habebit quartam partem hin:

verses.text: And he shall give the same measure of wine to pour out in libations for the holocaust or for the victim. For every lamb,
verses.textLatin: et vinum ad liba fundenda ejusdem mensuræ dabit in holocaustum sive in victimam. Per agnos singulos

verses.text: And for every ram there shall be a sacrifice of flour of two tenths, which shall be tempered with the third part of a hin of oil:
verses.textLatin: et arietes erit sacrificium similæ duarum decimarum, quæ conspersa sit oleo tertiæ partis hin:

verses.text: And he shall offer the third part of the same measure of wine for the libation, for a sweet savour to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et vinum ad libamentum tertiæ partis ejusdem mensuræ offeret in odorem suavitatis Domino.

verses.text: But when thou offerest a holocaust or sacrifice of oxen, to fulfil thy vow or for victims of peace offerings,
verses.textLatin: Quando vero de bobus feceris holocaustum aut hostiam, ut impleas votum vel pacificas victimas,

verses.text: Thou shalt give for every ox three tenths of flour tempered with half a hin of oil,
verses.textLatin: dabis per singulos boves similæ tres decimas conspersæ oleo, quod habeat medium mensuræ hin:

verses.text: And wine for libations of the same measure, for an offering of most sweet savour to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et vinum ad liba fundenda ejusdem mensuræ in oblationem suavissimi odoris Domino.

verses.text: Thus shalt thou do
verses.textLatin: Sic facies

verses.text: For every ox and ram and lamb and kid.
verses.textLatin: per singulos boves et arietis et agnos et hædos.

verses.text: Both they that are born in the land, and the strangers
verses.textLatin: Tam indigenæ quam peregrini

verses.text: Shall offer sacrifices after the same rite.
verses.textLatin: eodem ritu offerent sacrificia.

verses.text: There shall be all one law and judgment both for you and for them who are strangers in the land.
verses.textLatin: Unum præceptum erit atque judicium tam vobis quam advenis terræ.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them:
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos:

verses.text: When you are come into the land which I will give you,
verses.textLatin: Cum veneritis in terram, quam dabo vobis,

verses.text: And shall eat of the bread of that country, you shall separate firstfruits to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: et comederitis de panibus regionis illius, separabitis primitias Domino

verses.text: Of the things you eat. As you separate firstfruits of your barnfloors:
verses.textLatin: de cibis vestris. Sicut de areis primitias separatis,

verses.text: So also shall you give firstfruits of your dough to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ita et de pulmentis dabitis primitiva Domino.

verses.text: And if through ignorance you omit any of these things, which the Lord hath spoken to Moses,
verses.textLatin: Quod si per ignorantiam præterieritis quidquam horum, quæ locutus est Dominus ad Moysen,

verses.text: And by him hath commanded you, from the day that he began to command and thenceforward,
verses.textLatin: et mandavit per eum ad vos, a die qua cœpit jubere et ultra,

verses.text: And the multitude have forgotten to do it: they shall offer a calf out of the herd, a holocaust for a most sweet savour to the Lord, and the sacrifice and libations thereof, as the ceremonies require, and a buck goat for sin:
verses.textLatin: oblitaque fuerit facere multitudo: offeret vitulum de armento, holocaustum in odorem suavissimum Domino, et sacrificum ejus ac liba, ut cæremoniæ postulant, hircumque pro peccato:

verses.text: And the priest shall pray for all the multitude of the children of Israel: and it shall be forgiven them, because they sinned ignorantly, offering notwithstanding a burnt offering to the Lord for themselves and for their sin and their ignorance:
verses.textLatin: et rogabit sacerdos pro omni multitudine filiorum Israël, et dimittetur eis, quoniam non sponte peccaverunt, nihilominus offerentes incensum Domino pro se et pro peccato atque errore suo:

verses.text: And it shall be forgiven all the people of the children of Israel: and the strangers that sojourn among them: because it is the fault of all the people through ignorance.
verses.textLatin: et dimittetur universæ plebi filiorum Israël, et advenis qui peregrinantur inter eos: quoniam culpa est omnis populi per ignorantiam.

verses.text: But if one soul shall sin ignorantly, he shall offer a she goat of a year old for his sin.
verses.textLatin: Quod si anima una nesciens peccaverit, offeret capram anniculam pro peccato suo:

verses.text: And the priest shall pray for him, because he sinned ignorantly before the Lord: and he shall obtain his pardon, and it shall be forgiven him.
verses.textLatin: et deprecabitur pro ea sacerdos, quod inscia peccaverit coram Domino: impetrabitque ei veniam, et dimittetur illi.

verses.text: The same law shall be for all that sin by ignorance, whether they be natives or strangers.
verses.textLatin: Tam indigenis quam advenis una lex erit omnium, qui peccaverint ignorantes.

verses.text: But the soul that committeth any thing through pride, whether he be born in the land or a stranger (because he hath been rebellious against the Lord) shall be cut off from among his people:
verses.textLatin: Anima vero, quæ per superbiam aliquid commiserit, sive civis sit ille, sive peregrinus (quoniam adversus Dominum rebellis fuit), peribit de populo suo:

verses.text: For he hath contemned the word of the Lord, and made void his precept: therefore shall he be destroyed, and shall bear his iniquity.
verses.textLatin: verbum enim Domini contempsit, et præceptum illius fecit irritum: idcirco delebitur, et portabit iniquitatem suam.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel were in the wilderness, and had found a man gathering sticks on the sabbath day,
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem, cum essent filii Israël in solitudine, et invenissent hominem colligentem ligna in die sabbati,

verses.text: That they brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole multitude.
verses.textLatin: obtulerunt eum Moysi et Aaron et universæ multitudini.

verses.text: And they put him into prison, not knowing what they should do with him.
verses.textLatin: Qui recluserunt eum in carcerem, nescientes quid super eo facere deberent.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Let that man die, let all the multitude stone him without the camp.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Morte moriatur homo iste: obruat eum lapidibus omnis turba extra castra.

verses.text: And when they had brought him out, they stoned him, and he died as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Cumque eduxissent eum foras, obruerunt lapidibus, et mortuus est, sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord also said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt tell them to make to themselves fringes in the corners of their garments, putting in them ribands of blue:
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos ut faciant sibi fimbrias per angulos palliorum, ponentes in eis vittas hyacinthinas:

verses.text: That when they shall see them, they may remember all the commandments of the Lord, and not follow their own thoughts and eyes going astray after divers things,
verses.textLatin: quas cum viderint, recordentur omnium mandatorum Domini, nec sequantur cogitationes suas et oculos per res varias fornicantes,

verses.text: But rather being mindful of the precepts of the Lord, may do them and be holy to their God.
verses.textLatin: sed magis memores præceptorum Domini faciant ea, sintque sancti Deo suo.

verses.text: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus Deus vester, qui eduxi vos de terra Ægypti, ut essem Deus vester.

verses.text: And  behold Core the son of Isaar, the son of Caath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiron the sons of Eliab, and Hon the son of Pheleth of the children of Ruben,
verses.textLatin: Ecce autem Core filius Isaar, filii Caath, filii Levi, et Dathan atque Abiron filii Eliab, Hon quoque filius Pheleth de filiis Ruben,

verses.text: Rose up against Moses, and with them two hundred and fifty others of the children of Israel, leading men of the synagogue, and who in the time of assembly were called by name.
verses.textLatin: surrexerunt contra Moysen, aliique filiorum Israël ducenti quinquaginta viri proceres synagogæ, et qui tempore concilii per nomina vocabantur.

verses.text: And when they had stood up against Moses and Aaron, they said: Let it be enough for you, that all the multitude consisteth of holy ones, and the Lord is among them: Why lift you up yourselves above the people of the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Cumque stetissent adversum Moysen et Aaron, dixerunt: Sufficiat vobis, quia omnis multitudo sanctorum est, et in ipsis est Dominus: cur elevamini super populum Domini?

verses.text: When Moses heard this, he fell flat on his face:
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Moyses, cecidit pronus in faciem:

verses.text: And speaking to Core and all the multitude, he said: In the morning the Lord will make known who belong to him, and the holy he will join to himself: and whom he shall choose, they shall approach to him.
verses.textLatin: locutusque ad Core et ad omnem multitudinem: Mane, inquit, notum faciet Dominus qui ad se pertineant, et sanctos applicabit sibi: et quos elegerit, appropinquabunt ei.

verses.text: Do this therefore: Take every man of you your censers, thou Core, and all thy company.
verses.textLatin: Hoc igitur facite: tollat unusquisque thuribula sua, tu Core, et omne concilium tuum:

verses.text: And putting fire in them to morrow, put incense upon it before the Lord: and whomsoever he shall choose, the same shall be holy: you take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.
verses.textLatin: et hausto cras igne, ponite desuper thymiama coram Domino: et quemcumque elegerit, ipse erit sanctus: multum erigimini filii Levi.

verses.text: And he said again to Core: Hear ye sons of Levi.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque rursum ad Core: Audite, filii Levi:

verses.text: Is it a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath spared you from all the people, and joined you to himself, that you should serve him in the service of the tabernacle, and should stand before the congregation of the people, and should minister to him?
verses.textLatin: num parum vobis est quod separavit vos Deus Israël ab omni populo, et junxit sibi, ut serviretis ei in cultu tabernaculi, et staretis coram frequentia populi, et ministraretis ei?

verses.text: Did he therefore make thee and all thy brethren the sons of Levi to approach unto him, that you should challenge to yourselves the priesthood also,
verses.textLatin: idcirco ad se fecit accedere te et omnes fratres tuos filios Levi, ut vobis etiam sacerdotium vindicetis,

verses.text: And that all thy company should stand against the Lord? for what is Aaron that you murmur against him?
verses.textLatin: et omnis globus tuus stet contra Dominum? quid est enim Aaron ut murmuretis contra eum?

verses.text: Then Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiron the sons of Eliab. But they answered: We will not come.
verses.textLatin: Misit ergo Moyses ut vocaret Dathan et Abiron filios Eliab. Qui responderunt: Non venimus.

verses.text: Is it a small matter to thee, that thou hast brought us out of a land that flowed with milk and honey, to kill us in the desert, except thou rule also like a lord over us?
verses.textLatin: Numquid parum est tibi quod eduxisti nos de terra, quæ lacte et melle manabat, ut occideres in deserto, nisi et dominatus fueris nostri?

verses.text: Thou hast brought us indeed into a land that floweth with rivers of milk and honey, and hast given us possessions of fields and vineyards; wilt thou also pull out our eyes? We will not come.
verses.textLatin: Revera induxisti nos in terram, quæ fluit rivis lactis et mellis, et dedisti nobis possessiones agrorum et vinearum: an et oculos nostros vis eruere? non venimus.

verses.text: Moses therefore being very angry, said to the Lord: Respect not their sacrifices: thou knowest that I have not taken of them so much as a young ass at any time, nor have injured any of them.
verses.textLatin: Iratusque Moyses valde, ait ad Dominum: Ne respicias sacrificia eorum: tu scis quod ne asellum quidem umquam acceperim ab eis, nec afflixerim quempiam eorum.

verses.text: And he said to Core: Do thou and thy congregation stand apart before the Lord to morrow, and Aaron apart.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Core: Tu, et omnis congregatio tua, state seorsum coram Domino, et Aaron die crastino separatim.

verses.text: Take every one of you censers, and put incense upon them, offering to the Lord two hundred and fifty censers: let Aaron also hold his censer.
verses.textLatin: Tollite singuli thuribula vestra, et ponite super ea incensum, offerentes Domino ducenta quinquaginta thuribula: Aaron quoque teneat thuribulum suum.

verses.text: When they had done this, Moses and Aaron standing,
verses.textLatin: Quod cum fecissent, stantibus Moyses et Aaron,
