verses.text: And had drawn up all the multitude against them to the door of the tabernacle, the glory of the Lord appeared to them all.
verses.textLatin: et coacervassent adversum eos omnem multitudinem ad ostium tabernaculi, apparuit cunctis gloria Domini.

verses.text: And the Lord speaking to Moses and Aaron, said:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, ait:

verses.text: Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may presently destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Separamini de medio congregationis hujus, ut eos repente disperdam.

verses.text: They fell flat on their face, and said: O most mighty, the God of the spirits of all flesh, for one man’s sin shall thy wrath rage against all?
verses.textLatin: Qui ceciderunt proni in faciem, atque dixerunt: Fortissime Deus spirituum universæ carnis, num uno peccante, contra omnes ira tua desæviet?

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Command the whole people to separate themselves from the tents of Core and Dathan and Abiron.
verses.textLatin: Præcipe universo populo ut separetur a tabernaculis Core et Dathan et Abiron.

verses.text: And Moses arose, and went to Dathan and Abiron: and the ancients of Israel following him,
verses.textLatin: Surrexitque Moyses, et abiit ad Dathan et Abiron: et sequentibus eum senioribus Israël,

verses.text: He said to the multitude: Depart from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be involved in their sins.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad turbam: Recedite a tabernaculis hominum impiorum, et nolite tangere quæ ad eos pertinent, ne involvamini in peccatis eorum.

verses.text: And when they were departed from their tents round about, Dathan and Abiron coming out stood in the entry of their pavilions with their wives and children, and all the people.
verses.textLatin: Cumque recessissent a tentoriis eorum per circuitum, Dathan et Abiron egressi stabant in introitu papilionum suorum cum uxoribus et liberis, omnique frequentia.

verses.text: And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all things that you see, and that I have not forged them of my own head:
verses.textLatin: Et ait Moyses: In hoc scietis quod Dominus miserit me ut facerem universa quæ cernitis, et non ex proprio ea corde protulerim:

verses.text: If these men die the common death of men, and if they be visited with a plague, wherewith others also are wont to be visited, the Lord did not send me.
verses.textLatin: si consueta hominum morte interierint, et visitaverit eos plaga, qua et ceteri visitari solent, non misit me Dominus:

verses.text: But if the Lord do a new thing, and the earth opening her mouth swallow them down, and all things that belong to them, and they go down alive into hell, you shall know that they have blasphemed the Lord.
verses.textLatin: sin autem novam rem fecerit Dominus, ut aperiens terra os suum deglutiat eos et omnia quæ ad illos pertinent, descenderintque viventes in infernum, scietis quod blasphemaverint Dominum.

verses.text: And immediately as he had made an end of speaking, the earth broke asunder under their feet:
verses.textLatin: Confestim igitur ut cessavit loqui, dirupta est terra sub pedibus eorum:

verses.text: And opening her mouth, devoured them with their tents and all their substance.
verses.textLatin: et aperiens os suum, devoravit illos cum tabernaculis suis et universa substantia eorum,

verses.text: And they went down alive into hell, the ground closing upon them, and they perished from among the people.
verses.textLatin: descenderuntque vivi in infernum operti humo, et perierunt de medio multitudinis.

verses.text: But all Israel, that was standing round about, fled at the cry of them that were perishing: saying: Lest perhaps the earth swallow us up also.
verses.textLatin: At vero omnis Israël, qui stabat per gyrum, fugit ad clamorem pereuntium, dicens: Ne forte et nos terra deglutiat.

verses.text: And a fire coming out from the Lord, destroyed the two hundred and fifty men that offered the incense.
verses.textLatin: Sed et ignis egressus a Domino interfecit ducentos quinquaginta viros, qui offerebant incensum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Command Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers that lie in the burning, and to scatter the fire of one side and the other: because they are sanctified
verses.textLatin: Præcipe Eleazaro filio Aaron sacerdoti ut tollat thuribula quæ jacent in incendio, et ignem huc illucque dispergat: quoniam sanctificata sunt

verses.text: In the deaths of the sinners: and let him beat them into plates, and fasten them to the altar, because incense hath been offered in them to the Lord, and they are sanctified, that the children of Israel may see them for a sign and a memorial.
verses.textLatin: in mortibus peccatorum: producatque ea in laminas, et affigat altari, eo quod oblatum sit in eis incensum Domino, et sanctificata sint, ut cernant ea pro signo et monimento filii Israël.

verses.text: Then Eleazar the priest took the brazen censers, wherein they had offered, whom the burning fire had devoured, and beat them into plates, fastening them to the altar:
verses.textLatin: Tulit ergo Eleazar sacerdos thuribula ænea, in quibus obtulerant hi quos incendium devoravit, et produxit ea in laminas, affigens altari:

verses.text: That the children of Israel might have for the time to come wherewith they should be admonished, that no stranger or any one that is not of the seed of Aaron should come near to offer incense to the Lord, lest he should suffer as Core suffered, and all his congregation, according as the Lord spoke to Moses.
verses.textLatin: ut haberent postea filii Israël, quibus commonerentur ne quis accedat alienigena, et qui non est de semine Aaron ad offerendum incensum Domino, ne patiatur sicut passus est Core, et omnis congregatio ejus, loquente Domino ad Moysen.

verses.text: The following day all the multitude of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Murmuravit autem omnis multitudo filiorum Israël sequenti die contra Moysen et Aaron, dicens: Vos interfecistis populum Domini.

verses.text: And when there arose a sedition, and the tumult increased,
verses.textLatin: Cumque oriretur seditio, et tumultus incresceret,

verses.text: Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. And when they were gone into it, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
verses.textLatin: Moyses et Aaron fugerunt ad tabernaculum fœderis. Quod, postquam ingressi sunt, operuit nubes, et apparuit gloria Domini.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Get you out from the midst of this multitude, this moment will I destroy them. And as they were lying on the ground,
verses.textLatin: Recedite de medio hujus multitudinis, etiam nunc delebo eos. Cumque jacerent in terra,

verses.text: Moses said to Aaron: Take the censer, and putting fire in it from the altar, put incense upon it, and go quickly to the people to pray for them: for already wrath is gone out from the Lord, and the plague rageth.
verses.textLatin: dixit Moyses ad Aaron: Tolle thuribulum, et hausto igne de altari, mitte incensum desuper, pergens cito ad populum, ut roges pro eis: jam enim egressa est ira a Domino, et plaga desævit.

verses.text: When Aaron had done this, and had run to the midst of the multitude which the burning fire was now destroying, he offered the incense:
verses.textLatin: Quod cum fecisset Aaron, et cucurrisset ad mediam multitudinem, quam jam vastabat incendium, obtulit thymiama:

verses.text: And standing between the dead and the living, he prayed for the people, and the plague ceased.
verses.textLatin: et stans inter mortuos ac viventes, pro populo deprecatus est, et plaga cessavit.

verses.text: And the number of them that were slain was fourteen thousand and seven hundred men, besides them that had perished in the sedition of Core.
verses.textLatin: Fuerunt autem qui percussi sunt, quatuordecim millia hominum, et septingenti, absque his qui perierant in seditione Core.

verses.text: And Aaron returned to Moses to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant after the destruction was over.
verses.textLatin: Reversusque est Aaron ad Moysen ad ostium tabernaculi fœderis postquam quievit interitus.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and take of every one of them a rod by their kindreds, of all the princes of the tribes, twelve rods, and write the name of every man upon his rod.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad filios Israël, et accipe ab eis virgas singulas per cognationes suas, a cunctis principibus tribuum, virgas duodecim, et uniuscujusque nomen superscribes virgæ suæ.

verses.text: And the name of Aaron shall be for the tribe of Levi, and one rod shall contain all their families:
verses.textLatin: Nomen autem Aaron erit in tribu Levi, et una virga cunctas seorsum familias continebit:

verses.text: And thou shalt lay them up in the tabernacle of the covenant before the testimony, where I will speak to thee.
verses.textLatin: ponesque eas in tabernaculo fœderis coram testimonio, ubi loquar ad te.

verses.text: Whomsoever of these I shall choose, his rod shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel, wherewith they murmur against you.
verses.textLatin: Quem ex his elegero, germinabit virga ejus: et cohibebo a me querimonias filiorum Israël, quibus contra vos murmurant.

verses.text: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and all the princes gave him rods one for every tribe: and there were twelve rods besides the rod of Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Moyses ad filios Israël: et dederunt ei omnes principes virgas per singulas tribus: fueruntque virgæ duodecim absque virga Aaron.

verses.text: And when Moses had laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony:
verses.textLatin: Quas cum posuisset Moyses coram Domino in tabernaculo testimonii,

verses.text: He returned on the following day, and found that the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi, was budded: and that the buds swelling it had bloomed blossoms, which spreading the leaves, were formed into almonds.
verses.textLatin: sequenti die regressus invenit germinasse virgam Aaron in domo Levi: et turgentibus gemmis eruperant flores, qui, foliis dilatatis, in amygdalas deformati sunt.

verses.text: Moses therefore brought out all the rods from before the Lord to all the children of Israel: and they saw, and every one received their rods.
verses.textLatin: Protulit ergo Moyses omnes virgas de conspectu Domini ad cunctos filios Israël: videruntque, et receperunt singuli virgas suas.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Carry back the rod of Aaron into the tabernacle of the testimony, that it may be kept there for a token of the rebellious children of Israel, and that their complaints may cease from me lest they die.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Refer virgam Aaron in tabernaculum testimonii, ut servetur ibi in signum rebellium filiorum Israël, et quiescant querelæ eorum a me, ne moriantur.

verses.text: And Moses did as the Lord had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Fecitque Moyses sicut præceperat Dominus.

verses.text: And the children of Israel said to Moses: Behold we are consumed, we all perish.
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt autem filii Israël ad Moysen: Ecce consumpti sumus, omnes perivimus.

verses.text: Whosoever approacheth to the tabernacle of the Lord, he dieth. Are we all to a man to be utterly destroyed?
verses.textLatin: Quicumque accedit ad tabernaculum Domini, moritur. Num usque ad internecionem cuncti delendi sumus?

verses.text: And  the Lord said to Aaron: Thou, and thy sons, and thy father’s house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the sins of your priesthood.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Aaron: Tu, et filii tui, et domus patris tui tecum, portabitis iniquitatem sanctuarii: et tu et filii tui simul sustinebitis peccata sacerdotii vestri.

verses.text: And take with thee thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, and the sceptre of thy father, and let them be ready in hand, and minister to thee: but thou and thy sons shall minister in the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.textLatin: Sed et fratres tuos de tribu Levi, et sceptrum patris tui sume tecum, præstoque sint, et ministrent tibi: tu autem et filii tui ministrabitis in tabernaculo testimonii.

verses.text: And the Levites shall watch to do thy commands, and about all the works of the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary nor the altar, lest both they die, and you also perish with them.
verses.textLatin: Excubabuntque Levitæ ad præcepta tua, et ad cuncta opera tabernaculi: ita dumtaxat ut ad vasa sanctuarii et ad altare non accedant, ne et illi moriantur, et vos pereatis simul.

verses.text: But let them be with thee, and watch in the charge of the tabernacle, and in all the ceremonies thereof. A stranger shall not join himself with you.
verses.textLatin: Sint autem tecum, et excubent in custodiis tabernaculi, et in omnibus cæremoniis ejus. Alienigena non miscebitur vobis.

verses.text: Watch ye in the charge of the sanctuary, and in the ministry of the altar: lest indignation rise upon the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Excubate in custodia sanctuarii, et in ministerio altaris: ne oriatur indignatio super filios Israël.

verses.text: I have given you your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel, and have delivered them for a gift to the Lord, to serve in the ministries of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Ego dedi vobis fratres vestros Levitas de medio filiorum Israël, et tradidi donum Domino, ut serviant in ministeriis tabernaculi ejus.

verses.text: But thou and thy sons look ye to the priesthood: and all things that pertain to the service of the altar, and that are within the veil, shall be executed by the priests. If any stranger shall approach, he shall be slain.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem et filii tui custodite sacerdotium vestrum: et omnia quæ ad cultum altaris pertinent, et intra velum sunt, per sacerdotes administrabuntur: si quis externus accesserit, occidetur.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: Behold I have given thee the charge of my firstfruits. All things that are sanctified by the children of Israel, I have delivered to thee and to thy sons for the priestly office, by everlasting ordinances.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Aaron: Ecce dedi tibi custodiam primitiarum mearum. Omnia quæ sanctificantur a filiis Israël, tradidi tibi et filiis tuis pro officio sacerdotali legitima sempiterna.

verses.text: These therefore shalt thou take of the things that are sanctified, and are offered to the Lord. Every offering, and sacrifice, and whatsoever is rendered to me for sin and for trespass, and becometh holy of holies, shall be for thee and thy sons.
verses.textLatin: Hæc ergo accipies de his, quæ sanctificantur et oblata sunt Domino. Omnis oblatio, et sacrificium, et quidquid pro peccato atque delicto redditur mihi, et cedit in Sancta sanctorum, tuum erit, et filiorum tuorum.

verses.text: Thou shalt eat it in the sanctuary: the males only shall eat thereof, because it is a consecrated thing to thee.
verses.textLatin: In sanctuario comedes illud: mares tantum edent ex eo, quia consecratum est tibi.

verses.text: But the firstfruits, which the children of Israel shall vow and offer, I have given to thee, and to thy sons, and to thy daughters, by a perpetual law. He that is clean in thy house, shall eat them.
verses.textLatin: Primitias autem, quas voverint et obtulerint filii Israël, tibi dedi, et filiis tuis, ac filiabus tuis, jure perpetuo: qui mundus est in domo tua, vescetur eis.

verses.text: All the best of the oil, and of the wine, and of the corn, whatsoever firstfruits they offer to the Lord, I have given them to thee.
verses.textLatin: Omnem medullam olei, et vini, ac frumenti, quidquid offerunt primitiarum Domino, tibi dedi.

verses.text: All the firstripe of the fruits, that the ground bringeth forth, and which are brought to the Lord, shall be for thy use: he that is clean in thy house, shall eat them.
verses.textLatin: Universa frugum initia, quas gignit humus, et Domino deportantur, cedent in usus tuos: qui mundus est in domo tua, vescetur eis.

verses.text: Every thing that the children of Israel shall give by vow, shall be thine.
verses.textLatin: Omne quod ex voto reddiderint filii Israël, tuum erit.

verses.text: Whatsoever is firstborn of all flesh, which they offer to the Lord, whether it be of men, or of beasts, shall belong to thee: only for the firstborn of man thou shalt take a price, and every beast that is unclean thou shalt cause to be redeemed,
verses.textLatin: Quidquid primum erumpit e vulva cunctæ carnis, quam offerunt Domino, sive ex hominibus, sive de pecoribus fuerit, tui juris erit: ita dumtaxat ut pro hominis primogenito pretium accipias, et omne animal quod immundum est redimi facias,

verses.text: And the redemption of it shall be after one month, for five sicles of silver, by the weight of the sanctuary. A sicle hath twenty obols.
verses.textLatin: cujus redemptio erit post unum mensem, siclis argenti quinque, pondere sanctuarii. Siclus viginti obolos habet.

verses.text: But the firstling of a cow and of a sheep and of a goat thou shalt not cause to be redeemed, because they are sanctified to the Lord. Their blood only thou shalt pour upon the altar, and their fat thou shalt burn for a most sweet odour to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Primogenitum autem bovis, et ovis, et capræ, non facies redimi, quia sanctificata sunt Domino. Sanguinem tantum eorum fundes super altare, et adipes adolebis in suavissimum odorem Domino.

verses.text: But the flesh shall fall to thy use, as the consecrated breast, and the right shoulder shall be thine.
verses.textLatin: Carnes vero in usum tuum cedent, sicut pectusculum consecratum, et armus dexter: tua erunt.

verses.text: All the firstfruits of the sanctuary which the children of Israel offer to the Lord, I have given to thee and to thy sons and daughters, by a perpetual ordinance. It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, to thee and to thy sons.
verses.textLatin: Omnes primitias sanctuarii, quas offerunt filii Israël Domino, tibi dedi, et filiis, ac filiabus tuis, jure perpetuo. Pactum salis est sempiternum coram Domino, tibi ac filiis tuis.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: You shall possess nothing in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them: I am thy portion and inheritance in the midst of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Aaron: In terra eorum nihil possidebitis, nec habebitis partem inter eos: ego pars et hæreditas tua in medio filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And I have given to the sons of Levi all the tithes of Israel for a possession, for the ministry wherewith they serve me in the tabernacle of the covenant:
verses.textLatin: Filiis autem Levi dedi omnes decimas Israëlis in possessionem, pro ministerio, quo serviunt mihi in tabernaculo fœderis:

verses.text: That the children of Israel may not approach any more to the tabernacle, nor commit deadly sin,
verses.textLatin: ut non accedant ultra filii Israël ad tabernaculum, nec committant peccatum mortiferum,

verses.text: But only the sons of Levi may serve me in the tabernacle, and bear the sins of the people. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in your generations. They shall not possess any other thing,
verses.textLatin: solis filiis Levi mihi in tabernaculo servientibus, et portantibus peccata populi. Legitimum sempiternum erit in generationibus vestris. Nihil aliud possidebunt,

verses.text: But be content with the oblation or tithes, which I have separated for their uses and necessities.
verses.textLatin: decimarum oblatione contenti, quas in usus eorum et necessaria separavi.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Command the Levites, and declare unto them: When you shall receive of the children of Israel the tithes, which I have given you, offer the firstfruits of them to the Lord, that is to say, the tenth part of the tenth:
verses.textLatin: Præcipe Levitis, atque denuntia: Cum acceperitis a filiis Israël decimas, quas dedi vobis, primitias earum offerte Domino, id est, decimam partem decimæ,

verses.text: That it may be reckoned to you as an oblation of firstfruits, as well of the barnfloors as of the winepresses:
verses.textLatin: ut reputetur vobis in oblationem primitivorum, tam de areis quam de torcularibus:

verses.text: And of all the things of which you receive tithes, offer the firstfruits to the Lord, and give them to Aaron the priest.
verses.textLatin: et universis quorum accipitis primitias, offerte Domino, et date Aaron sacerdoti.

verses.text: All the things that you shall offer of the tithes, and shall separate for the gifts of the Lord, shall be the best and choicest things.
verses.textLatin: Omnia quæ offeretis ex decimis, et in donaria Domini separabitis, optima et electa erunt.

verses.text: And thou shalt say to them: If you offer all the goodly and the better things of the tithes, it shall be reckoned to you as if you had given the firstfruits of the barnfloor and the winepress:
verses.textLatin: Dicesque ad eos: Si præclara et meliora quæque obtuleritis ex decimis, reputabitur vobis quasi de area, et torculari dederitis primitias:

verses.text: And you shall eat them in all your places, both you and your families: because it is your reward for the ministry, wherewith you serve in the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.textLatin: et comedetis eas in omnibus locis vestris, tam vos quam familiæ vestræ: quia pretium est pro ministerio, quo servitis in tabernaculo testimonii.

verses.text: And you shall not sin in this point, by reserving the choicest and fat things to yourselves, lest you profane the oblations of the children of Israel, and die.
verses.textLatin: Et non peccabitis super hoc, egregia vobis et pinguia reservantes, ne polluatis oblationes filiorum Israël, et moriamini.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron, dicens:

verses.text: This is the observance of the victim, which the Lord hath ordained. Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee a red cow of full age, in which there is no blemish, and which hath not carried the yoke:
verses.textLatin: Ista est religio victimæ, quam constituit Dominus. Præcipe filiis Israël, ut adducant ad te vaccam rufam ætatis integræ, in qua nulla sit macula, nec portaverit jugum:

verses.text: And you shall deliver her to Eleazar the priest, who shall bring her forth without the camp, and shall immolate her in the sight of all:
verses.textLatin: tradetisque eam Eleazaro sacerdoti, qui eductam extra castra, immolabit in conspectu omnium:

verses.text: And dipping his finger in her blood, shall sprinkle it over against the door of the tabernacle seven times,
verses.textLatin: et tingens digitum in sanguine ejus, asperget contra fores tabernaculi septem vicibus,

verses.text: And shall burn her in the sight of all, delivering up to the fire her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, and her dung.
verses.textLatin: comburetque eam cunctis videntibus, tam pelle et carnibus ejus quam sanguine et fimo flammæ traditis.

verses.text: The priest shall also take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet twice dyed, and cast it into the flame, with which the cow is consumed.
verses.textLatin: Lignum quoque cedrinum, et hyssopum, coccumque bis tinctum sacerdos mittet in flammam, quæ vaccam vorat.

verses.text: And then after washing his garments, and body, he shall enter into the camp, and shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Et tunc demum, lotis vestibus et corpore suo, ingredietur in castra, commaculatusque erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: He also that hath burned her, shall wash his garments, and his body, and shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Sed et ille qui combusserit eam, lavabit vestimenta sua et corpus, et immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the cow, and shall pour them forth without the camp in a most clean place, that they may be reserved for the multitude of the children of Israel, and for a water of aspersion: because the cow was burnt for sin.
verses.textLatin: Colliget autem vir mundus cineres vaccæ, et effundet eos extra castra in loco purissimo, ut sint multitudini filiorum Israël in custodiam, et in aquam aspersionis: quia pro peccato vacca combusta est.

verses.text: And when he that carried the ashes of the cow, hath washed his garments, he shall be unclean until the evening. The children of Israel, and the strangers that dwell among them, shall observe this for a holy thing by a perpetual ordinance.
verses.textLatin: Cumque laverit qui vaccæ portaverat cineres vestimenta sua, immundus erit usque ad vesperum. Habebunt hoc filii Israël, et advenæ qui habitant inter eos, sanctum jure perpetuo.

verses.text: He that toucheth the corpse of a man, and is therefore unclean seven days,
verses.textLatin: Qui tetigerit cadaver hominis, et propter hoc septem diebus fuerit immundus,

verses.text: Shall be sprinkled with this water on the third day, and on the seventh, and so shall be cleansed. If he were not sprinkled on the third day, he cannot be cleansed on the seventh.
verses.textLatin: aspergetur ex hac aqua die tertio et septimo, et sic mundabitur. Si die tertio aspersus non fuerit, septimo non poterit emundari.

verses.text: Every one that toucheth the corpse of a man, and is not sprinkled with this mixture, shall profane the tabernacle of the Lord, and shall perish out of Israel: because he was not sprinkled with the water of expiation, he shall be unclean, and his uncleanness shall remain upon him.
verses.textLatin: Omnis qui tetigerit humanæ animæ morticinum, et aspersus hac commistione non fuerit, polluet tabernaculum Domini et peribit ex Israël: quia aqua expiationis non est aspersus, immundus erit, et manebit spurcitia ejus super eum.

verses.text: This is the law of a man that dieth in a tent: All that go into his tent and all the vessels that are there, shall be unclean seven days.
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex hominis qui moritur in tabernaculo: omnes qui ingrediuntur tentorium illius, et universa vasa quæ ibi sunt, polluta erunt septem diebus.

verses.text: The vessel that hath no cover, nor binding over it, shall be unclean.
verses.textLatin: Vas, quod non habuerit operculum nec ligaturam desuper, immundum erit.

verses.text: If any man in the field touch the corpse of a man that was slain, or that died of himself, or his bone, or his grave, he shall be unclean seven days.
verses.textLatin: Si quis in agro tetigerit cadaver occisi hominis, aut per se mortui, sive os illius, vel sepulchrum, immundus erit septem diebus.

verses.text: And they shall take of the ashes of the burning and of the sin offering, and shall pour living waters upon them into a vessel.
verses.textLatin: Tollentque de cineribus combustionis atque peccati, et mittent aquas vivas super eos in vas:

verses.text: And a man that is clean shall dip hyssop in them, and shall sprinkle therewith all the tent, and all the furniture, and the men that are defiled with touching any such thing:
verses.textLatin: in quibus cum homo mundus tinxerit hyssopum, asperget ex eo omne tentorium, et cunctam supellectilem, et homines hujuscemodi contagione pollutos:

verses.text: And in this manner he that is clean shall purify the unclean on the third and on the seventh day. And being expiated the seventh day, he shall wash both himself and his garments, and be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: atque hoc modo mundus lustrabit immundum tertio et septimo die: expiatusque die septimo, lavabit et se et vestimenta sua, et immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: If any man be not expiated after this rite, his soul shall perish out of the midst of the church: because he hath profaned the sanctuary of the Lord, and was not sprinkled with the water of purification.
verses.textLatin: Si quis hoc ritu non fuerit expiatus, peribit anima illius de medio ecclesiæ: quia sanctuarium Domini polluit, et non est aqua lustrationis aspersus.

verses.text: This precept shall be an ordinance for ever. He also that sprinkled the water, shall wash his garments. Every one that shall touch the waters of expiation, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Erit hoc præceptum legitimum sempiternum. Ipse quoque qui aspergit aquas, lavabit vestimenta sua. Omnis qui tetigerit aquas expiationis, immundus erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: Whatsoever a person toucheth who is unclean, he shall make it unclean: and the person that toucheth any of these things, shall be unclean until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Quidquid tetigerit immundus, immundum faciet: et anima, quæ horum quippiam tetigerit, immunda erit usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: And  the children of Israel, and all the multitude came into the desert of Sin, in the first month: and the people abode in Cades. And Mary died there, and was buried in the same place.
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque filii Israël et omnis multitudo in desertum Sin, mense primo, et mansit populus in Cades. Mortuaque est ibi Maria, et sepulta in eodem loco.

verses.text: And the people wanting water, came together against Moses and Aaron:
verses.textLatin: Cumque indigeret aqua populus, convenerunt adversum Moysen et Aaron:

verses.text: And making a sedition, they said: Would God we had perished among our brethren before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et versi in seditionem, dixerunt: Utinam periissemus inter fratres nostros coram Domino.

verses.text: Why have you brought out the church of the Lord into the wilderness, that both we and our cattle should die?
verses.textLatin: Cur eduxistis ecclesiam Domini in solitudinem, ut et nos et nostra jumenta moriamur?

verses.text: Why have you made us come up out of Egypt, and have brought us into this wretched place which cannot be sowed, nor bringeth forth figs, nor vines, nor pomegranates, neither is there any water to drink?
verses.textLatin: quare nos fecistis ascendere de Ægypto, et adduxistis in locum istum pessimum, qui seri non potest, qui nec ficum gignit, nec vineas, nec malogranata, insuper et aquam non habet ad bibendum?

verses.text: And Moses and Aaron leaving the multitude, went into the tabernacle of the covenant, and fell flat upon the ground, and cried to the Lord, and said: O Lord God, hear the cry of this people, and open to them thy treasure, a fountain of living water, that being satisfied, they may cease to murmur. And the glory of the Lord appeared over them.
verses.textLatin: Ingressusque Moyses et Aaron, dimissa multitudine, tabernaculum fœderis, corruerunt proni in terram, clamaveruntque ad Dominum, atque dixerunt: Domine Deus, audi clamorem hujus populi, et aperi eis thesaurum tuum fontem aquæ vivæ, ut satiati, cesset murmuratio eorum. Et apparuit gloria Domini super eos.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Take the rod, and assemble the people together, thou and Aaron thy brother, and speak to the rock before them, and it shall yield waters. And when thou hast brought forth water out of the rock, all the multitude and their cattle shall drink.
verses.textLatin: Tolle virgam, et congrega populum, tu et Aaron frater tuus, et loquimini ad petram coram eis, et illa dabit aquas. Cumque eduxeris aquam de petra, bibet omnis multitudo et jumenta ejus.

verses.text: Moses therefore took the rod, which was before the Lord, as he had commanded him,
verses.textLatin: Tulit igitur Moyses virgam, quæ erat in conspectu Domini, sicut præceperat ei,

verses.text: And having gathered together the multitude before the rock, he said to them: Hear, ye rebellious and incredulous: Can we bring you forth water out of this rock?
verses.textLatin: congregata multitudine ante petram: dixitque eis: Audite, rebelles et increduli: num de petra hac vobis aquam poterimus ejicere?

verses.text: And when Moses had lifted up his hand, and struck the rock twice with the rod, there came forth water in great abundance, so that the people and their cattle drank,
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevasset Moyses manum, percutiens virga bis silicem, egressæ sunt aquæ largissimæ, ita ut populus biberet et jumenta.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land, which I will give them.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen et Aaron: Quia non credidistis mihi, ut sanctificaretis me coram filiis Israël, non introducetis hos populos in terram, quam dabo eis.

verses.text: This is the Water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove with words against the Lord, and he was sanctified in them.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est aqua contradictionis, ubi jurgati sunt filii Israël contra Dominum, et sanctificatus est in eis.

verses.text: In the mean time Moses sent messengers from Cades to the king of Edom, to say: Thus saith thy brother Israel: Thou knowest all the labour that hath come upon us:
verses.textLatin: Misit interea nuntios Moyses de Cades ad regem Edom, qui dicerent: Hæc mandat frater tuus Israël: Nosti omnem laborem qui apprehendit nos,

verses.text: In what manner our fathers went down into Egypt, and there we dwelt a long time, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers.
verses.textLatin: quomodo descenderint patres nostri in Ægyptum, et habitaverimus ibi multo tempore, afflixerintque nos Ægyptii, et patres nostros:

verses.text: And how we cried to the Lord, and he heard us, and sent an angel, who hath brought us out of Egypt. Lo, we are now in the city of Cades, which is in the uttermost of thy borders,
verses.textLatin: et quomodo clamaverimus ad Dominum, et exaudierit nos, miseritque angelum, qui eduxerit nos de Ægypto. Ecce in urbe Cades, quæ est in extremis finibus tuis, positi,

verses.text: And we beseech thee that we may have leave to pass through thy country. We will not go through the fields, nor through the vineyards, we will not drink the waters of thy wells, but we will go by the common highway, neither turning aside to the right hand, nor to the left, till we are past thy borders.
verses.textLatin: obsecramus ut nobis transire liceat per terram tuam. Non ibimus per agros, nec per vineas; non bibemus aquas de puteis tuis: sed gradiemur via publica, nec ad dexteram nec ad sinistram declinantes, donec transeamus terminos tuos.

verses.text: And Edom answered them: Thou shalt not pass by me: if thou dost I will come out armed against thee.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Edom: Non transibis per me, alioquin armatus occurram tibi.

verses.text: And the children of Israel said: We will go by the beaten way: and if we and our cattle drink of thy waters, we will give thee what is just: there shall be no difficulty in the price, only let us pass speedily.
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque filii Israël: Per tritam gradiemur viam: et si biberimus aquas tuas, nos et pecora nostra, dabimus quod justum est: nulla erit in pretio difficultas, tantum velociter transeamus.

verses.text: But he answered: Thou shalt not pass. And immediately he came forth to meet them with an infinite multitude, and a strong hand,
verses.textLatin: At ille respondit: Non transibis. Statimque egressus est obvius, cum infinita multitudo, et manu forti,

verses.text: Neither would he condescend to their desire to grant them passage through his borders. Wherefore Israel turned another way from him.
verses.textLatin: nec voluit acquiescere deprecanti, ut concederet transitum per fines suos. Quam ob rem divertit ab eo Israël.

verses.text: And when they had removed the camp from Cades, they came to mount Hor, which is in the borders of the land of Edom:
verses.textLatin: Cumque castra movissent de Cades, venerunt in montem Hor, qui est in finibus terræ Edom:

verses.text: Where the Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.textLatin: ubi locutus est Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Let Aaron, saith he, go to his people: for he shall not go into the land which I have given the children of Israel, because he was incredulous to my words, at the waters of contradiction.
verses.textLatin: Pergat, inquit, Aaron ad populos suos: non enim intrabit terram, quam dedi filiis Israël, eo quod incredulus fuerit ori meo, ad aquas contradictionis.

verses.text: Take Aaron and his son with him, and bring them up into mount Hor:
verses.textLatin: Tolle Aaron et filium ejus cum eo, et duces eos in montem Hor.

verses.text: And when thou hast stripped the father of his vesture, thou shalt vest therewith Eleazar his son: Aaron shall be gathered to his people, and die there.
verses.textLatin: Cumque nudaveris patrem veste sua, indues ea Eleazarum filium ejus: Aaron colligetur, et morietur ibi.

verses.text: Moses did as the Lord had commanded: and they went up into mount Hor before all the multitude.
verses.textLatin: Fecit Moyses ut præceperat Dominus: et ascenderunt in montem Hor coram omni multitudine.

verses.text: And when he had stripped Aaron of his vestments, he vested Eleazar his son with them.
verses.textLatin: Cumque Aaron spoliasset vestibus suis, induit eis Eleazarum filium ejus.

verses.text: And Aaron being dead in the top of the mountain, he came down with Eleazar.
verses.textLatin: Illo mortuo in montis supercilio, descendit cum Eleazaro.

verses.text: And all the multitude seeing that Aaron was dead, mourned for him thirty days throughout all their families.
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem multitudo videns occubuisse Aaron, flevit super eo triginta diebus per cunctas familias suas.

verses.text: And  when king Arad the Chanaanite, who dwelt towards the south, had heard this, to wit, that Israel was come by the way of the spies, he fought against them, and overcoming them carried off their spoils.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Chananæus rex Arad, qui habitabat ad meridiem, venisse scilicet Israël per exploratorum viam, pugnavit contra illum, et victor existens, duxit ex eo prædam.

verses.text: But Israel binding himself by vow to the Lord, said: If thou wilt deliver this people into my hand, I will utterly destroy their cities.
verses.textLatin: At Israël voto se Domino obligans, ait: Si tradideris populum istum in manu mea, delebo urbes ejus.

verses.text: And the Lord heard the prayers of Israel, and delivered up the Chanaanite, and they cut them off and destroyed their cities: and they called the name of that place Horma, that is to say, Anathema.
verses.textLatin: Exaudivitque Dominus preces Israël, et tradidit Chananæum, quem ille interfecit subversis urbibus ejus: et vocavit nomen loci illius Horma, id est, anathema.

verses.text: And they marched from mount Hor, by the way that leadeth to the Red Sea, to compass the land of Edom. And the people began to be weary of their journey and labour:
verses.textLatin: Profecti sunt autem et de monte Hor, per viam quæ ducit ad mare Rubrum, ut circumirent terram Edom. Et tædere cœpit populum itineris ac laboris:

verses.text: And speaking against God and Moses, they said: Why didst thou bring us out of Egypt, to die in the wilderness? There is no bread, nor have we any waters: our soul now loatheth this very light food.
verses.textLatin: locutusque contra Deum et Moysen, ait: Cur eduxisti nos de Ægypto, ut moreremur in solitudine? deest panis, non sunt aquæ: anima nostra jam nauseat super cibo isto levissimo.

verses.text: Wherefore the Lord sent among the people fiery serpents, which bit them and killed many of them.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem misit Dominus in populum ignitos serpentes, ad quorum plagas et mortes plurimorum,

verses.text: Upon which they came to Moses, and said: We have sinned, because we have spoken against the Lord and thee: pray that he may take away these serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.
verses.textLatin: venerunt ad Moysen, atque dixerunt: Peccavimus, quia locuti sumus contra Dominum et te: ora ut tollat a nobis serpentes. Oravitque Moyses pro populo,

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Make a brazen serpent, and set it up for a sign: whosoever being struck shall look on it, shall live.
verses.textLatin: et locutus est Dominus ad eum: Fac serpentem æneum, et pone eum pro signo: qui percussus aspexerit eum, vivet.

verses.text: Moses therefore made a brazen serpent, and set it up for a sign: which when they that were bitten looked upon, they were healed.
verses.textLatin: Fecit ergo Moyses serpentem æneum, et posuit eum pro signo: quem cum percussi aspicerent, sanabantur.

verses.text: And the children of Israel setting forwards camped in Oboth.
verses.textLatin: Profectique filii Israël castrametati sunt in Oboth.

verses.text: And departing thence they pitched their tents in Jeabarim, in the wilderness, that faceth Moab toward the east.
verses.textLatin: Unde egressi fixere tentoria in Jeabarim, in solitudine quæ respicit Moab contra orientalem plagam.

verses.text: And removing from thence, they came to the torrent Zared:
verses.textLatin: Et inde moventes, venerunt ad torrentem Zared.

verses.text: Which they left and encamped over against Arnon, which is in the desert and standeth out on the borders of the Amorrhite. For Arnon is the border of Moab, dividing the Moabites and the Amorrhites.
verses.textLatin: Quem relinquentes castrametati sunt contra Arnon, quæ est in deserto, et prominet in finibus Amorrhæi. Siquidem Arnon terminus est Moab, dividens Moabitas et Amorrhæos.

verses.text: Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord: As he did in the Red Sea, so will he do in the streams of Arnon.
verses.textLatin: Unde dicitur in libro bellorum Domini: Sicut fecit in mari Rubro, sic faciet in torrentibus Arnon.

verses.text: The rocks of the torrents were bowed down that they might rest in Ar, and lie down in the borders of the Moabites.
verses.textLatin: Scopuli torrentium inclinati sunt, ut requiescerent in Ar, et recumberent in finibus Moabitarum.

verses.text: When they went from that place, the well appeared whereof the Lord said to Moses: Gather the people together, and I will give them water.
verses.textLatin: Ex eo loco apparuit puteus, super quo locutus est Dominus ad Moysen: Congrega populum, et dabo ei aquam.

verses.text: Then Israel sung this song: Let the well spring up. They sung thereto:
verses.textLatin: Tunc cecinit Israël carmen istud: Ascendat puteus. Concinebant:

verses.text: The well, which the princes dug, and the chiefs of the people prepared by the direction of the lawgiver, and with their staves. And they marched from the wilderness to Mathana.
verses.textLatin: Puteus, quem foderunt principes et paraverunt duces multitudinis in datore legis, et in baculis suis. De solitudine, Matthana.

verses.text: From Mathana unto Nahaliel: from Nahaliel unto Bamoth.
verses.textLatin: De Matthana in Nahaliel: de Nahaliel in Bamoth.

verses.text: From Bamoth, is a valley in the country of Moab, to the top of Phasga, which looked towards the desert.
verses.textLatin: De Bamoth, vallis est in regione Moab, in vertice Phasga, quod respicit contra desertum.

verses.text: And Israel sent messengers to Sehon king of the Amorrhites, saying:
verses.textLatin: Misit autem Israël nuntios ad Sehon regem Amorrhæorum, dicens:

verses.text: I beseech thee that I may have leave to pass through thy land: we will not go aside into the fields or the vineyards, we will not drink waters of the wells, we will go the king’s highway, till we be past thy borders.
verses.textLatin: Obsecro ut transire mihi liceat per terram tuam: non declinabimus in agros et vineas; non bibemus aquas ex puteis: via regia gradiemur, donec transeamus terminos tuos.

verses.text: And he would not grant that Israel should pass by his borders: but rather gathering an army, went forth to meet them in the desert, and came to Jasa, and fought against them.
verses.textLatin: Qui concedere noluit ut transiret Israël per fines suos: quin potius exercitu congregato, egressus est obviam in desertum, et venit in Jasa, pugnavitque contra eum.

verses.text: And he was slain by them with the edge of the sword, and they possessed his land from the Arnon unto the Jeboc, and to the confines of the children of Ammon: for the borders of the Ammonites, were kept with a strong garrison.
verses.textLatin: A quo percussus est in ore gladii, et possessa est terra ejus ab Arnon usque Jeboc, et filios Ammon: quia forti præsidio tenebantur termini Ammonitarum.

verses.text: So Israel took all his cities, and dwelt in the cities of the Amorrhite, to wit, in Hesebon, and in the villages thereof.
verses.textLatin: Tulit ergo Israël omnes civitates ejus, et habitavit in urbibus Amorrhæi, in Hesebon scilicet, et viculis ejus.

verses.text: Hesebon was the city of Sehon the king of the Amorrhites, who fought against the king of Moab: and took all the land, that had been of his dominions, as far as the Arnon.
verses.textLatin: Urbs Hesebon fuit Sehon regis Amorrhæi, qui pugnavit contra regem Moab: et tulit omnem terram, quæ ditionis illius fuerat usque Arnon.

verses.text: Therefore it is said in the proverb: Come into Hesebon, let the city of Sehon be built and set up:
verses.textLatin: Idcirco dicitur in proverbio: Venite in Hesebon: ædificetur, et construatur civitas Sehon:

verses.text: A fire is gone out of Hesebon, a flame from the city of Sehon, and hath consumed Ar of the Moabites, and the inhabitants of the high places of the Arnon.
verses.textLatin: ignis egressus est de Hesebon, flamma de oppido Sehon, et devoravit Ar Moabitarum, et habitatores excelsorum Arnon.

verses.text: Woe to thee Moab: thou art undone, O people of Chamos. He hath given his sons to flight, and his daughters into captivity to Sehon the king of the Amorrhites.
verses.textLatin: Væ tibi Moab; peristi popule Chamos. Dedit filios ejus in fugam, et filias in captivitatem regi Amorrhæorum Sehon.

verses.text: Their yoke is perished from Hesebon unto Dibon, they came weary to Nophe, and unto Medaba.
verses.textLatin: Jugum ipsorum disperiit ad Hesebon usque Dibon: lassi pervenerunt in Nophe, et usque Medaba.

verses.text: So Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorrhite.
verses.textLatin: Habitavit itaque Israël in terra Amorrhæi.

verses.text: And Moses sent some to take a view of Jazer: and they took the villages of it, and conquered the inhabitants.
verses.textLatin: Misitque Moyses qui explorarent Jazer: cujus ceperunt viculos, et possederunt habitatores.

verses.text: And they turned themselves, and went up by the way of Basan, and Og the king of Basan came against them with all his people, to fight in Edrai.
verses.textLatin: Verteruntque se, et ascenderunt per viam Basan, et occurrit eis Og, rex Basan, cum omni populo suo, pugnaturus in Edrai.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Fear him not, for I have delivered him and all his people, and his country into thy hand: and thou shalt do to him as thou didst to Sehon the king of the Amorrhites, the inhabitant of Hesebon.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen: Ne timeas eum, quia in manu tua tradidi illum, et omnem populum ac terram ejus: faciesque illi sicut fecisti Sehon, regi Amorrhæorum habitatori Hesebon.

verses.text: So they slew him also with his sons, and all his people, not letting any one escape, and they possessed his land.
verses.textLatin: Percusserunt igitur et hunc cum filiis suis, universumque populum ejus usque ad internecionem, et possederunt terram illius.

verses.text: And  they went forward and encamped in the plains of Moab, over against where Jericho is situate beyond the Jordan.
verses.textLatin: Profectique castrametati sunt in campestribus Moab, ubi trans Jordanem Jericho sita est.

verses.text: And Balac the son of Sephor, seeing all that Israel had done to the Amorrhite,
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Balac filius Sephor omnia quæ fecerat Israël Amorrhæo,

verses.text: And that the Moabites were in great fear of him, and were not able to sustain his assault,
verses.textLatin: et quod pertimuissent eum Moabitæ, et impetum ejus ferre non possent,

verses.text: He said to the elders of Madian: So will this people destroy all that dwell in our borders, as the ox is wont to eat the grass to the very roots. Now he was at that time king in Moab.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad majores natu Madian: Ita delebit hic populus omnes, qui in nostris finibus commorantur, quomodo solet bos herbas usque ad radices carpere. Ipse erat eo tempore rex in Moab.

verses.text: He sent therefore messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, a soothsayer, who dwelt by the river of the land of the children of Ammon, to call him, and to say: Behold a people is come out of Egypt, that hath covered the face of the earth, sitting over against me.
verses.textLatin: Misit ergo nuntios ad Balaam filium Beor ariolum, qui habitabat super flumen terræ filiorum Ammon, ut vocarent eum, et dicerent: Ecce egressus est populus ex Ægypto, qui operuit superficiem terræ, sedens contra me.

verses.text: Come therefore, and curse this people, because it is mightier than I: if by any means I may beat them and drive them out of my land: for I know that he whom thou shalt bless is blessed, and he whom thou shalt curse is cursed.
verses.textLatin: Veni igitur, et maledic populo huic, quia fortior me est: si quomodo possim percutere et ejicere eum de terra mea. Novi enim quod benedictus sit cui benedixeris, et maledictus in quem maledicta congesseris.

verses.text: And the ancients of Moab, and the elders of Madian, went with the price of divination in their hands. And when they were come to Balaam, and had told him all the words of Balac:
verses.textLatin: Perrexeruntque seniores Moab, et majores natu Madian, habentes divinationis pretium in manibus. Cumque venissent ad Balaam, et narrassent ei omnia verba Balac,

verses.text: He answered: Tarry here this night, and I will answer whatsoever the Lord shall say to me. And while they stayed with Balaam, God came and said to him:
verses.textLatin: ille respondit: Manete hic nocte, et respondebo quidquid mihi dixerit Dominus. Manentibus illis apud Balaam, venit Deus, et ait ad eum:

verses.text: What mean these men that are with thee?
verses.textLatin: Quid sibi volunt homines isti apud te?

verses.text: He answered: Balac the son of Sephor king of the Moabites hath sent to me,
verses.textLatin: Respondit: Balac filius Sephor rex Moabitarum misit ad me,

verses.text: Saying: Behold a people that is come out of Egypt, hath covered the face of the land: come and curse them, if by any means I may fight with them and drive them away.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Ecce populus qui egressus est de Ægypto, operuit superficiem terræ: veni, et maledic ei, si quomodo possim pugnans abigere eum.

verses.text: And God said to Balaam: Thou shalt not go with them, nor shalt thou curse the people: because it is blessed.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Deus ad Balaam: Noli ire cum eis, neque maledicas populo: quia benedictus est.

verses.text: And he rose in the morning and said to the princes: Go into your country, because the Lord hath forbid me to come with you.
verses.textLatin: Qui mane consurgens dixit ad principes: Ite in terram vestram, quia prohibuit me Dominus venire vobiscum.

verses.text: The princes returning, said to Balac: Balaam would not come with us.
verses.textLatin: Reversi principes dixerunt ad Balac: Noluit Balaam venire nobiscum.

verses.text: Then he sent many more and more noble than he had sent before:
verses.textLatin: Rursum ille multo plures et nobiliores quam ante miserat, misit.

verses.text: Who, when they were come to Balaam, said: Thus saith Balac the son of Sephor, Delay not to come to me:
verses.textLatin: Qui cum venissent ad Balaam, dixerunt: Sic dicit Balac filius Sephor: Ne cuncteris venire ad me:

verses.text: For I am ready to honour thee, and will give thee whatsoever thou wilt: come and curse this people.
verses.textLatin: paratus sum honorare te, et quidquid volueris, dabo tibi: veni, et maledic populo isti.

verses.text: Balaam answered: If Balac would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot alter the word of the Lord my God, to speak either more or less.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Balaam: Si dederit mihi Balac plenam domum suam argenti et auri, non potero immutare verbum Domini Dei mei, ut vel plus, vel minus loquar.

verses.text: I pray you to stay here this night also, that I may know what the Lord will answer me once more.
verses.textLatin: Obsecro ut hic maneatis etiam hac nocte, et scire queam quid mihi rursum respondeat Dominus.

verses.text: God therefore came to Balaam in the night, and said to him: If these men be come to call thee, arise and go with them: yet so, that thou do what I shall command thee.
verses.textLatin: Venit ergo Deus ad Balaam nocte, et ait ei: Si vocare te venerunt homines isti, surge, et vade cum eis: ita dumtaxat, ut quod tibi præcepero, facias.

verses.text: Balaam arose in the morning, and saddling his ass went with them.
verses.textLatin: Surrexit Balaam mane, et strata asina sua profectus est cum eis.

verses.text: And God was angry. And an angel of the Lord stood in the way against Balaam, who sat on the ass, and had two servants with him.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus est Deus. Stetitque angelus Domini in via contra Balaam, qui insidebat asinæ, et duos pueros habebat secum.

verses.text: The ass seeing the angel standing in the way, with a drawn sword, turned herself out of the way, and went into the field. And when Balaam beat her, and had a mind to bring her again to the way,
verses.textLatin: Cernens asina angelum stantem in via, evaginato gladio, avertit se de itinere, et ibat per agrum. Quam cum verberaret Balaam, et vellet ad semitam reducere,

verses.text: The angel stood in a narrow place between two walls, wherewith the vineyards were enclosed.
verses.textLatin: stetit angelus in angustiis duarum maceriarum, quibus vineæ cingebantur.

verses.text: And the ass seeing him, thrust herself close to the wall, and bruised the foot of the rider. But he beat her again:
verses.textLatin: Quem videns asina, junxit se parieti, et attrivit sedentis pedem. At ille iterum verberabat eam:

verses.text: And nevertheless the angel going on to a narrow place, where there was no way to turn aside either to the right hand or to the left, stood to meet him.
verses.textLatin: et nihilominus angelus ad locum angustum transiens, ubi nec ad dexteram, nec ad sinistram poterat deviare, obvius stetit.

verses.text: And when the ass saw the angel standing, she fell under the feet of the rider: who being angry beat her sides more vehemently with a staff.
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset asina stantem angelum, concidit sub pedibus sedentis: qui iratus, vehementius cædebat fuste latera ejus.

verses.text: And the Lord opened the mouth of the ass, and she said: What have I done to thee? Why strikest thou me, lo, now this third time?
verses.textLatin: Aperuitque Dominus os asinæ, et locuta est: Quid feci tibi? cur percutis me ecce jam tertio?

verses.text: Balaam answered: Because thou hast deserved it, and hast served me ill: I would I had a sword that I might kill thee.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Balaam: Quia commeruisti, et illusisti mihi: utinam haberem gladium, ut te percuterem!

verses.text: The ass said: Am not I thy beast, on which thou hast been always accustomed to ride until this present day? tell me if I ever did the like thing to thee. But he said: Never.
verses.textLatin: Dixit asina: Nonne animal tuum sum, cui semper sedere consuevisti usque in præsentem diem? dic quid simile umquam fecerim tibi. At ille ait: Numquam.

verses.text: Forthwith the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel standing in the way with a drawn sword, and he worshipped him falling flat on the ground.
verses.textLatin: Protinus aperuit Dominus oculos Balaam, et vidit angelum stantem in via, evaginato gladio, adoravitque eum pronus in terram.

verses.text: And the angel said to him: Why beatest thou thy ass these three times? I am come to withstand thee, because thy way is perverse, and contrary to me:
verses.textLatin: Cui angelus: Cur, inquit, tertio verberas asinam tuam? ego veni ut adversarer tibi, quia perversa est via tua, mihique contraria:

verses.text: And unless the ass had turned out of the way, giving place to me who stood against thee, I had slain thee, and she should have lived.
verses.textLatin: et nisi asina declinasset de via, dans locum resistenti, te occidissem, et illa viveret.

verses.text: Balaam said: I have sinned, not knowing that thou didst stand against me: and now if it displease thee that I go, I will return.
verses.textLatin: Dixit Balaam: Peccavi, nesciens quod tu stares contra me: et nunc si displicet tibi ut vadam, revertar.

verses.text: The angel said: Go with these men, and see thou speak no other thing than what I shall command thee. He went therefore with the princes.
verses.textLatin: Ait angelus: Vade cum istis, et cave ne aliud quam præcepero tibi loquaris. Ivit igitur cum principibus.

verses.text: And when Balac heard it he came forth to meet him in a town of the Moabites, that is situate in the uttermost borders of Arnon.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Balac, egressus est in occursum ejus in oppido Moabitarum, quod situm est in extremis finibus Arnon.

verses.text: And he said to Balaam: I sent messengers to call thee, why didst thou not come immediately to me? was it because I am not able to reward thy coming?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad Balaam: Misi nuntios ut vocarent te: cur non statim venisti ad me? an quia mercedem adventui tuo reddere nequeo?

verses.text: He answered him: Lo, here I am: shall I have power to speak any other thing but that which God shall put in my mouth?
verses.textLatin: Cui ille respondit: Ecce adsum: numquid loqui potero aliud, nisi quod Deus posuerit in ore meo?

verses.text: So they went on together, and came into a city, that was in the uttermost borders of his kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Perrexerunt ergo simul, et venerunt in urbem, quæ in extremis regni ejus finibus erat.

verses.text: And when Balac had killed oxen and sheep, he sent presents to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.
verses.textLatin: Cumque occidisset Balac boves et oves, misit ad Balaam, et principes qui cum eo erant, munera.

verses.text: And when morning was come, he brought him to the high places of Baal, and he beheld the uttermost part of the people.
verses.textLatin: Mane autem facto, duxit eum ad excelsa Baal, et intuitus est extremam partem populi.

verses.text: And  Balaam said to Balac: Build me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and the same number of rams.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Balaam ad Balac: Ædifica mihi hic septem aras, et para totidem vitulos, ejusdemque numeri arietes.

verses.text: And when he had done according to the word of Balaam, they laid together a calf and a ram upon every altar.
verses.textLatin: Cumque fecisset juxta sermonem Balaam, imposuerunt simul vitulum et arietem super aram.

verses.text: And Balaam said to Balac: Stand a while by thy burnt offering, until I go, to see if perhaps the Lord will meet me, and whatsoever he shall command, I will speak to thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Balaam ad Balac: Sta paulisper juxta holocaustum tuum, donec vadam, si forte occurrat mihi Dominus, et quodcumque imperaverit, loquar tibi.

verses.text: And when he was gone with speed, God met him. And Balaam speaking to him, said: I have erected seven altars, and have laid on every one a calf and a ram.
verses.textLatin: Cumque abiisset velociter, occurrit illi Deus. Locutusque ad eum Balaam: Septem, inquit, aras erexi, et imposui vitulum et arietem desuper.

verses.text: And the Lord put the word in his mouth, and said: Return to Balac, and thus shalt thou speak.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem posuit verbum in ore ejus, et ait: Revertere ad Balac, et hæc loqueris.

verses.text: Returning he found Balac standing by his burnt offering, with all the princes of the Moabites:
verses.textLatin: Reversus invenit stantem Balac juxta holocaustum suum, et omnes principes Moabitarum:

verses.text: And taking up his parable, he said: Balac king of the Moabites hath brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east: Come, said he, and curse Jacob: make haste and detest Israel.
verses.textLatin: assumptaque parabola sua, dixit: De Aram adduxit me Balac rex Moabitarum, de montibus orientis: Veni, inquit, et maledic Jacob; propera, et detestare Israël.

verses.text: How shall I curse him, whom God hath not cursed? By what means should I detest him, whom the Lord detesteth not?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo maledicam, cui non maledixit Deus? qua ratione detester, quem Dominus non detestatur?

verses.text: I shall see him from the tops of the rocks, and shall consider him from the hills. This people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.
verses.textLatin: De summis silicibus videbo eum, et de collibus considerabo illum. Populus solus habitabit, et inter gentes non reputabitur.

verses.text: Who can count the dust of Jacob, and know the number of the stock of Israel? Let my soul die the death of the just, and my last end be like to them.
verses.textLatin: Quis dinumerare possit pulverem Jacob, et nosse numerum stirpis Israël? Moriatur anima mea morte justorum, et fiant novissima mea horum similia.

verses.text: And Balac said to Balaam: What is this that thou dost? I sent for thee to curse my enemies: and thou contrariwise blessest them.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Balac ad Balaam: Quid est hoc quod agis? ut malediceres inimicis meis vocavi te, et tu e contrario benedicis eis.

verses.text: He answered him: Can I speak any thing else but what the Lord commandeth?
verses.textLatin: Cui ille respondit: Num aliud possum loqui, nisi quod jusserit Dominus?

verses.text: Balac therefore said: Come with me to another place from whence thou mayest see part of Israel, and canst not see them all: curse them from thence.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Balac: Veni mecum in alterum locum unde partem Israël videas, et totum videre non possis: inde maledicito ei.

verses.text: And when he had brought him to a high place, upon the top of mount Phasga, Balaam built seven altars, and laying on every one a calf and a ram,
verses.textLatin: Cumque duxisset eum in locum sublimem, super verticem montis Phasga, ædificavit Balaam septem aras, et impositis supra vitulo atque ariete,

verses.text: He said to Balac: Stand here by thy burnt offering while I go to meet him.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad Balac: Sta hic juxta holocaustum tuum, donec ego obvius pergam.

verses.text: And when the Lord had met him, and had put the word in his mouth, he said: Return to Balac, and thus shalt thou say to him.
verses.textLatin: Cui cum Dominus occurrisset, posuissetque verbum in ore ejus, ait: Revertere ad Balac, et hæc loqueris ei.

verses.text: Returning he found him standing by his burnt sacrifice, and the princes of the Moabites with him. And Balac said to him: What hath the Lord spoken?
verses.textLatin: Reversus invenit eum stantem juxta holocaustum suum, et principes Moabitarum cum eo. Ad quem Balac: Quid, inquit, locutus est Dominus?

verses.text: But he taking up his parable, said: Stand, O Balac, and give ear: hear, thou son of Sephor:
verses.textLatin: At ille, assumpta parabola sua, ait: Sta, Balac, et ausculta; audi, fili Sephor:

verses.text: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor as the son of man, that he should be changed. Hath he said then, and will he not do? hath he spoken, and will he not fulfil?
verses.textLatin: non est Deus quasi homo, ut mentiatur, nec ut filius hominis, ut mutetur. Dixit ergo, et non faciet? locutus est, et non implebit?

verses.text: I was brought to bless, the blessing I am not able to hinder.
verses.textLatin: Ad benedicendum adductus sum: benedictionem prohibere non valeo.

verses.text: There is no idol in Jacob, neither is there an image god to be seen in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him.
verses.textLatin: Non est idolum in Jacob, nec videtur simulacrum in Israël. Dominus Deus ejus cum eo est, et clangor victoriæ regis in illo.

verses.text: God hath brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros.
verses.textLatin: Deus eduxit illum de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo similis est rhinocerotis.

verses.text: There is no soothsaying in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. In their times it shall be told to Jacob and to Israel what God hath wrought.
verses.textLatin: Non est augurium in Jacob, nec divinatio in Israël: temporibus suis dicetur Jacob et Israëli quid operatus sit Deus.

verses.text: Behold the people shall rise up as a lioness, and shall lift itself up as a lion: it shall not lie down till it devour the prey, and drink the blood of the slain.
verses.textLatin: Ecce populus ut leæna consurget, et quasi leo erigetur: non accubabit donec devoret prædam, et occisorum sanguinem bibat.

verses.text: And Balac said to Balaam: Neither curse, nor bless him.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Balac ad Balaam: Nec maledicas ei, nec benedicas.

verses.text: And he said: Did I not tell thee, that whatsoever God should command me, that I would do?
verses.textLatin: Et ille ait: Nonne dixi tibi quod quidquid mihi Deus imperaret, hoc facerem?

verses.text: And Balac said to him: Come and I will bring thee to another place; if peradventure it please God that thou mayest curse them from thence.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Balac ad eum: Veni, et ducam te ad alium locum: si forte placeat Deo ut inde maledicas eis.

verses.text: And when he had brought him upon the top of mount Phogor, which looketh towards the wilderness,
verses.textLatin: Cumque duxisset eum super verticem montis Phogor, qui respicit solitudinem,

verses.text: Balaam said to him: Build me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and the same number of rams.
verses.textLatin: dixit ei Balaam: Ædifica mihi hic septem aras, et para totidem vitulos, ejusdemque numeri arietes.

verses.text: Balac did as Balaam had said: and he laid on every altar, a calf and a ram.
verses.textLatin: Fecit Balac ut Balaam dixerat: imposuitque vitulos et arietes per singulas aras.

verses.text: And  when Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord that he should bless Israel. he went not as he had gone before, to seek divination: but setting his face towards the desert,
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset Balaam quod placeret Domino ut benediceret Israëli, nequaquam abiit ut ante perrexerat, ut augurium quæreret: sed dirigens contra desertum vultum suum,

verses.text: And lifting up his eyes, he saw Israel abiding in their tents by their tribes: and the spirit of God rushing upon him,
verses.textLatin: et elevans oculos, vidit Israël in tentoriis commorantem per tribus suas: et irruente in se spiritu Dei,

verses.text: He took up his parable and said: Balaam the son of Beor hath said: The man hath said, whose eye is stopped up:
verses.textLatin: assumpta parabola, ait: Dixit Balaam filius Beor: dixit homo, cujus obturatus est oculus:

verses.text: The hearer of the words of God hath said, he that hath beheld the vision of the Almighty, he that falleth, and so his eyes are opened:
verses.textLatin: dixit auditor sermonum Dei, qui visionem Omnipotentis intuitus est, qui cadit, et sic aperiuntur oculi ejus:

verses.text: How beautiful are thy tabernacles, O Jacob, and thy tents, O Israel!
verses.textLatin: Quam pulchra tabernacula tua, Jacob, et tentoria tua, Israël!

verses.text: As woody valleys, as watered gardens near the rivers, as tabernacles which the Lord hath pitched, as cedars by the waterside.
verses.textLatin: ut valles nemorosæ, ut horti juxta fluvios irrigui, ut tabernacula quæ fixit Dominus, quasi cedri prope aquas.

verses.text: Water shall flow out of his bucket, and his seed shall be in many waters. For Agag his king shall be removed, and his kingdom shall be taken away.
verses.textLatin: Fluet aqua de situla ejus, et semen illius erit in aquas multas. Tolletur propter Agag, rex ejus, et auferetur regnum illius.

verses.text: God hath brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros. They shall devour the nations that are his enemies, and break their bones, and pierce them with arrows.
verses.textLatin: Deus eduxit illum de Ægypto, cujus fortitudo similis est rhinocerotis. Devorabunt gentes hostes illius, ossaque eorum confringent, et perforabunt sagittis.

verses.text: Lying down he hath slept as a lion, and as a lioness, whom none shall dare to rouse. He that blesseth thee, shall also himself be blessed: he that curseth thee shall be reckoned accursed.
verses.textLatin: Accubans dormivit ut leo, et quasi leæna, quam suscitare nullus audebit. Qui benedixerit tibi, erit et ipse benedictus: qui maledixerit, in maledictione reputabitur.

verses.text: And Balac being angry against Balaam, clapped his hands together and said: I called thee to curse my enemies, and thou on the contrary hast blessed them three times.
verses.textLatin: Iratusque Balac contra Balaam, complosis manibus ait: Ad maledicendum inimicis meis vocavi te, quibus e contrario tertio benedixisti:

verses.text: Return to thy place. I had determined indeed greatly to honour thee, but the Lord hath deprived thee of the honour designed for thee.
verses.textLatin: revertere ad locum tuum. Decreveram quidem magnifice honorare te, sed Dominus privavit te honore disposito.

verses.text: Balaam made answer to Balac: Did I not say to thy messengers, whom thou sentest to me:
verses.textLatin: Respondit Balaam ad Balac: Nonne nuntiis tuis, quos misisti ad me, dixi:

verses.text: If Balac would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord my God, to utter any thing of my own head either good or evil: but whatsoever the Lord shall say, that I will speak?
verses.textLatin: Si dederit mihi Balac plenam domum suam argenti et auri, non potero præterire sermonem Domini Dei mei, ut vel boni quid vel mali proferam ex corde meo: sed quidquid Dominus dixerit, hoc loquar?

verses.text: But yet going to my people, I will give thee counsel, what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.
verses.textLatin: verumtamen pergens ad populum meum, dabo consilium, quid populus tuus populo huic faciat extremo tempore.

verses.text: Therefore taking up his parable, again he said: Balaam the son of Beor hath said: The man whose eye is stopped up, hath said:
verses.textLatin: Sumpta igitur parabola, rursum ait: Dixit Balaam filius Beor: dixit homo, cujus obturatus est oculus:

verses.text: The hearer of the words of God hath said, who knoweth the doctrine of the Highest, and seeth the visions of the Almighty, who falling hath his eyes opened:
verses.textLatin: dixit auditor sermonum Dei, qui novit doctrinam Altissimi, et visiones Omnipotentis videt, qui cadens apertos habet oculos:

verses.text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not near. A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel: and shall strike the chiefs of Moab, and shall waste all the children of Seth.
verses.textLatin: Videbo eum, sed non modo: intuebor illum, sed non prope. Orietur stella ex Jacob, et consurget virga de Israël: et percutiet duces Moab, vastabitque omnes filios Seth.

verses.text: And he shall possess Idumea: the inheritance of Seir shall come to their enemies, but Israel shall do manfully
verses.textLatin: Et erit Idumæa possessio ejus: hæreditas Seir cedet inimicis suis: Israël vero fortiter aget.

verses.text: Out of Jacob shall he come that shall rule, and shall destroy the remains of the city.
verses.textLatin: De Jacob erit qui dominetur, et perdat reliquias civitatis.

verses.text: And when he saw Amalec, he took up his parable, and said: Amalec the beginning of nations, whose latter ends shall be destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Cumque vidisset Amalec, assumens parabolam, ait: Principium gentium Amalec, cujus extrema perdentur.

verses.text: He saw also the Cinite: and took up his parable, and said: Thy habitation indeed is strong: but though thou build thy nest in a rock,
verses.textLatin: Vidit quoque Cinæum: et assumpta parabola, ait: Robustum quidem est habitaculum tuum: sed si in petra posueris nidum tuum,

verses.text: And thou be chosen of the stock of Cin, how long shalt thou be able to continue? For Assur shall take thee captive.
verses.textLatin: et fueris electus de stirpe Cin, quamdiu poteris permanere? Assur enim capiet te.

verses.text: And taking up his parable, again he said: Alas, who shall live when God shall do these things?
verses.textLatin: Assumptaque parabola iterum locutus est: Heu! quis victurus est, quando ista faciet Deus?

verses.text: They shall come in galleys from Italy, they shall overcome the Assyrians, and shall waste the Hebrews, and at the last they themselves also shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Venient in trieribus de Italia: superabunt Assyrios, vastabuntque Hebræos, et ad extremum etiam ipsi peribunt.

verses.text: And Balaam rose, and returned to his place: Balac also returned the way that he came.
verses.textLatin: Surrexitque Balaam, et reversus est in locum suum: Balac quoque via, qua venerat, rediit.

verses.text: And  Israel at that time abode in Settim, and the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab,
verses.textLatin: Morabatur autem eo tempore Israël in Settim, et fornicatus est populus cum filiabus Moab,

verses.text: Who called them to their sacrifices. And they ate of them, and adored their gods.
verses.textLatin: quæ vocaverunt eos ad sacrificia sua. At ille comederunt et adoraverunt deos earum.

verses.text: And Israel was initiated to Beelphegor: upon which the Lord being angry,
verses.textLatin: Initiatusque est Israël Beelphegor: et iratus Dominus,

verses.text: Said to Moses: Take all the princes of the people, and hang them up on gibbets against the sun: that my fury may be turned away from Israel.
verses.textLatin: ait ad Moysen: Tolle cunctos principes populi, et suspende eos contra solem in patibulis, ut avertatur furor meus ab Israël.

verses.text: And Moses said to the judges of Israel: Let every man kill his neighbours, that have been initiated to Beelphegor.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Moyses ad judices Israël: Occidat unusquisque proximos suos, qui initiati sunt Beelphegor.

verses.text: And behold one of the children of Israel went in before his brethren to a harlot of Madian, in the sight of Moses, and of all the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce unus de filiis Israël intravit coram fratribus suis ad scortum Madianitidem, vidente Moyse, et omni turba filiorum Israël, qui flebant ante fores tabernaculi.

verses.text: And when Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest saw it, he rose up from the midst of the multitude, and taking a dagger,
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidisset Phinees filius Eleazari filii Aaron sacerdotis, surrexit de medio multitudinis, et arrepto pugione,

verses.text: Went in after the Israelite into the brothel house, and thrust both of them through together, to wit, the man and the woman in the genital parts. And the scourge ceased from the children of Israel:
verses.textLatin: ingressus est post virum Israëlitem in lupanar, et perfodit ambos simul, virum scilicet et mulierem in locis genitalibus. Cessavitque plaga a filiis Israël:

verses.text: And there were slain four and twenty thousand men.
verses.textLatin: et occisi sunt viginti quatuor millia hominum.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned away my wrath from the children of Israel: because he was moved with my zeal against them, that I myself might not destroy the children of Israel in my zeal.
verses.textLatin: Phinees filius Eleazari filii Aaron sacerdotis avertit iram meam a filiis Israël: quia zelo meo commotus est contra eos, ut non ipse delerem filios Israël in zelo meo.

verses.text: Therefore say to him: Behold I give him the peace of my covenant,
verses.textLatin: Idcirco loquere ad eum: Ecce do ei pacem fœderis mei,

verses.text: And the covenant of the priesthood for ever shall be both to him and his seed, because he hath been zealous for his God, and hath made atonement for the wickedness of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et erit tam ipsi quam semini ejus pactum sacerdotii sempiternum: quia zelatus est pro Deo suo, et expiavit scelus filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And the name of the Israelite, that was slain with the woman of Madian, was Zambri the son of Salu, a prince of the kindred and tribe of Simeon.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem nomen viri Israëlitæ, qui occisus est cum Madianitide, Zambri filius Salu, dux de cognatione et tribu Simeonis.

verses.text: And the Madianite woman, that was slain with him, was called Cozbi the daughter of Sur, a most noble prince among the Madianites.
verses.textLatin: Porro mulier Madianitis, quæ pariter interfecta est, vocabatur Cozbi filia Sur principis nobilissimi Madianitarum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad Moysen, dicens:

verses.text: Let the Madianites find you their enemies, and slay you them:
verses.textLatin: Hostes vos sentiant Madianitæ, et percutite eos:

verses.text: Because they also have acted like enemies against you, and have guilefully deceived you by the idol Phogor, and Cozbi their sister, a daughter of a prince of Madian, who was slain in the day of the plague for the sacrilege of Phogor.
verses.textLatin: quia et ipsi hostiliter egerunt contra vos, et decepere insidiis per idolum Phogor, et Cozbi filiam ducis Madian sororem suam, quæ percussa est in die plagæ pro sacrilegio Phogor.

verses.text: After  the blood of the guilty was shed, the Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron, the priest:
verses.textLatin: Postquam noxiorum sanguis effusus est, dixit Dominus ad Moysen et Eleazarum filium Aaron sacerdotem:

verses.text: Number the whole sum of the children of Israel from twenty years old and upward, by their houses and kindreds, all that are able to go forth to war.
verses.textLatin: Numerate omnem summam filiorum Israël a viginti annis et supra, per domos et cognationes suas, cunctos qui possunt ad bella procedere.

verses.text: Moses therefore and Eleazar the priest, being in the plains of Moab upon the Jordan over against Jericho, spoke to them that were
verses.textLatin: Locuti sunt itaque Moyses et Eleazar sacerdos, in campestribus Moab super Jordanem contra Jericho, ad eos qui erant

verses.text: From twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded: and this is the number of them:
verses.textLatin: a viginti annis et supra, sicut Dominus imperaverat, quorum iste est numerus.

verses.text: Ruben the firstborn of Israel. His sons were Henoch, of whom is the family of the Henochites: and Phallu, of whom is the family of the Phalluites:
