verses.text: And from Sephama the bounds shall go down to Rebla over against the fountain of Daphnis: from thence they shall come eastward to the sea of Cenereth,
verses.textLatin: et de Sephama descendent termini in Rebla contra fontem Daphnim: inde pervenient contra orientem ad mare Cenereth,

verses.text: And shall reach as far as the Jordan, and at the last shall be closed in by the most salt sea. This shall be your land with its borders round about.
verses.textLatin: et tendent usque ad Jordanem, et ad ultimum salsissimo claudentur mari. Hanc habebitis terram per fines suos in circuitu.

verses.text: And Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: This shall be the land which you shall possess by lot, and which the Lord hath commanded to be given to the nine tribes, and to the half tribe.
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque Moyses filiis Israël, dicens: Hæc erit terra, quam possidebitis sorte, et quam jussit Dominus dari novem tribubus, et dimidiæ tribui.

verses.text: For the tribe of the children of Ruben by their families, and the tribe of the children of Gad according to the number of their kindreds, and half of the tribe of Manasses,
verses.textLatin: Tribus enim filiorum Ruben per familias suas, et tribus filiorum Gad juxta cognationum numerum, media quoque tribus Manasse,

verses.text: That is, two tribes and a half, have received their portion beyond the Jordan over against Jericho at the east side.
verses.textLatin: id est, duæ semis tribus, acceperunt partem suam trans Jordanem contra Jericho ad orientalem plagam.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: These are the names of the men, that shall divide the land unto you: Eleazar the priest, and Josue the son of Nun,
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt nomina virorum qui terram vobis divident, Eleazar sacerdos, et Josue filius Nun,

verses.text: And one prince of every tribe,
verses.textLatin: et singuli principes de tribubus singulis,

verses.text: Whose names are these: Of the tribe of Juda, Caleb the son of Jephone.
verses.textLatin: quorum ista sunt vocabula. De tribu Juda, Caleb filius Jephone.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Simeon, Samuel the son of Ammiud.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Simeon, Samuel filius Ammiud.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chaselon.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Benjamin, Elidad filius Chaselon.

verses.text: Of the tribe of the children of Dan, Bocci the son of Jogli.
verses.textLatin: De tribu filiorum Dan, Bocci filius Jogli.

verses.text: Of the children of Joseph of the tribe of Manasses, Hanniel the son of Ephod.
verses.textLatin: Filiorum Joseph de tribu Manasse, Hanniel filius Ephod.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Camuel the son of Sephtan.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Ephraim, Camuel filius Sephthan.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Zabulon, Elisaphan the son of Pharnach.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Zabulon, Elisaphan filius Pharnach.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Issachar, Phaltiel the prince, the son of Ozan.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Issachar, dux Phaltiel filius Ozan.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Aser, Ahiud the son of Salomi.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Aser, Ahiud filius Salomi.

verses.text: Of the tribe of Nephtali: Phedael the son of Ammiud.
verses.textLatin: De tribu Nephthali, Phedaël filius Ammiud.

verses.text: These are they Whom the Lord hath commanded to divide the land of Chanaan to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Hi sunt, quibus præcepit Dominus ut dividerent filiis Israël terram Chanaan.

verses.text: And  the Lord spoke these things also to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, over against Jericho:
verses.textLatin: Hæc quoque locutus est Dominus ad Moysen in campestribus Moab supra Jordanem, contra Jericho:

verses.text: Command the children of Israel that they give to the Levites out of their possessions,
verses.textLatin: Præcipe filiis Israël ut dent Levitis de possessionibus suis

verses.text: Cities to dwell in, and their suburbs round about: that they may abide in the towns, and the suburbs may be for their cattle and beasts:
verses.textLatin: urbes ad habitandum, et suburbana earum per circuitum: ut ipsi in oppidis maneant, et suburbana sint pecoribus ac jumentis:

verses.text: Which suburbs shall reach from the walls of the cities outward, a thousand paces on every side:
verses.textLatin: quæ a muris civitatum forinsecus, per circuitum, mille passuum spatio tendentur.

verses.text: Toward the east shall be two thousand cubits: and toward the south in like manner shall be two thousand cubits: toward the sea also, which looketh to the west, shall be the same extent: and the north side shall be bounded with the like limits. And the cities shall be in the midst, and the suburbs without.
verses.textLatin: Contra orientem duo millia erunt cubiti, et contra meridiem similiter erunt duo millia: ad mare quoque, quod respicit ad occidentem, eadem mensura erit, et septentrionalis plaga æquali termino finietur, eruntque urbes in medio, et foris suburbana.

verses.text: And among the cities, which you shall give to the Levites, six shall be separated for refuge to fugitives, that he who hath shed blood may flee to them: and besides these there shall be other forty-two cities,
verses.textLatin: De ipsis autem oppidis, quæ Levitis dabitis, sex erunt in fugitivorum auxilia separata, ut fugiat ad ea qui fuderit sanguinem: et exceptis his, alia quadraginta duo oppida,

verses.text: That is, in all forty-eight with their suburbs.
verses.textLatin: id est, simul quadraginta octo cum suburbanis suis.

verses.text: And of these cities which shall be given out of the possessions of the children of Israel, from them that have more, more shall be taken: and from them that have less, fewer. Each shall give towns to the Levites according to the extent of their inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Ipsæque urbes, quæ dabuntur de possessionibus filiorum Israël, ab his qui plus habent, plures auferentur: et qui minus, pauciores: singuli juxta mensuram hæreditatis suæ dabunt oppida Levitis.

verses.text: The Lord said to Moses:
verses.textLatin: Ait Dominus ad Moysen:

verses.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have passed over the Jordan into the land of Chanaan,
verses.textLatin: Loquere filiis Israël, et dices ad eos: Quando transgressi fueritis Jordanem in terram Chanaan,

verses.text: Determine what cities shall be for the refuge of fugitives, who have shed blood against their will.
verses.textLatin: decernite quæ urbes esse debeant in præsidia fugitivorum, qui nolentes sanguinem fuderint:

verses.text: And when the fugitive shall be in them, the kinsman of him that is slain may not have power to kill him, until he stand before the multitude, and his cause be judged.
verses.textLatin: in quibus cum fuerit profugus, cognatus occisi non poterit eum occidere, donec stet in conspectu multitudinis, et causa illius judicetur.

verses.text: And of those cities, that are separated for the refuge of fugitives,
verses.textLatin: De ipsis autem urbibus, quæ ad fugitivorum subsidia separantur,

verses.text: Three shall be beyond the Jordan, and three in the land of Chanaan,
verses.textLatin: tres erunt trans Jordanem, et tres in terra Chanaan,

verses.text: As well for the children of Israel as for strangers and sojourners, that he may flee to them, who hath shed blood against his will.
verses.textLatin: tam filiis Israël quam advenis atque peregrinis, ut confugiat ad eas qui nolens sanguinem fuderit.

verses.text: If any man strike with iron, and he die that was struck: he shall be guilty of murder, and he himself shall die.
verses.textLatin: Si quis ferro percusserit, et mortuus fuerit qui percussus est, reus erit homicidii, et ipse morietur.

verses.text: If he throw a stone, and he that is struck die: he shall be punished in the same manner.
verses.textLatin: Si lapidem jecerit, et ictus occubuerit, similiter punietur.

verses.text: If he that is struck with wood die: he shall be revenged by the blood of him that struck him.
verses.textLatin: Si ligno percussus interierit, percussoris sanguine vindicabitur.

verses.text: The kinsman of him that was slain, shall kill the murderer: as soon as he apprehendeth him, he shall kill him.
verses.textLatin: Propinquus occisi, homicidam interficiet: statim ut apprehenderit eum, interficiet.

verses.text: If through hatred any one push a man, or fling any thing at him with ill design:
verses.textLatin: Si per odium quis hominem impulerit, vel jecerit quippiam in eum per insidias:

verses.text: Or being his enemy, strike him with his hand, and he die: the striker shall be guilty of murder: the kinsman of him that was slain as soon as he findeth him, shall kill him.
verses.textLatin: aut cum esset inimicus, manu percusserit, et ille mortuus fuerit: percussor homicidii reus erit: cognatus occisi statim ut invenerit eum, jugulabit.

verses.text: But if by chance medley, and without hatred,
verses.textLatin: Quod si fortuitu, et absque odio

verses.text: And enmity, he do any of these things,
verses.textLatin: et inimicitiis quidquam horum fecerit,

verses.text: And this be proved in the hearing of the people, and the cause be debated between him that struck, and the next of kin:
verses.textLatin: et hoc audiente populo fuerit comprobatum, atque inter percussorem et propinquum sanguinis quæstio ventilata:

verses.text: The innocent shall be delivered from the hand of the revenger, and shall be brought back by sentence into the city, to which he had fled, and he shall abide there until the death of the high priest, that is anointed with the holy oil.
verses.textLatin: liberabitur innocens de ultoris manu, et reducetur per sententiam in urbem, ad quam confugerat, manebitque ibi, donec sacerdos magnus, qui oleo sancto unctus est, moriatur.

verses.text: If the murderer be found without the limits of the cities that are appointed for the banished,
verses.textLatin: Si interfector extra fines urbium, quæ exulibus deputatæ sunt,

verses.text: And be struck by him that is the avenger of blood: he shall not be guilty that killed him.
verses.textLatin: fuerit inventus, et percussus ab eo qui ultor est sanguinis: absque noxa erit qui eum occiderit.

verses.text: For the fugitive ought to have stayed in the city until the death of the high priest: and after he is dead, then shall the manslayer return to his own country.
verses.textLatin: Debuerat enim profugus usque ad mortem pontificis in urbe residere. Postquam autem ille obierit, homicida revertetur in terram suam.

verses.text: These things shall be perpetual, and for an ordinance in all your dwellings.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sempiterna erunt, et legitima in cunctis habitationibus vestris.

verses.text: The murderer shall be punished by witnesses: none shall be condemned upon the evidence of one man.
verses.textLatin: Homicida sub testibus punietur: ad unius testimonium nullus condemnabitur.

verses.text: You shall not take money of him that is guilty of blood, but he shall die forthwith.
verses.textLatin: Non accipietis pretium ab eo qui reus est sanguinis, statim et ipse morietur.

verses.text: The banished and fugitives before the death of the high priest may by no means return into their own cities.
verses.textLatin: Exules et profugi ante mortem pontificis nullo modo in urbes suas reverti poterunt,

verses.text: Defile not the land of your habitation, which is stained with the blood of the innocent: neither can it otherwise be expiated, but by his blood that hath shed the blood of another.
verses.textLatin: ne polluatis terram habitationis vestræ, quæ insontium cruore maculatur: nec aliter expiari potest, nisi per ejus sanguinem, qui alterius sanguinem fuderit.

verses.text: And thus shall your possession be cleansed, myself abiding with you. For I am the Lord that dwell among the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Atque ita emundabitur vestra possessio me commorante vobiscum. Ego enim sum Dominus qui habito inter filios Israël.

verses.text: And  the princes of the families of Galaad, the son of Machir, the son of Manasses, of the stock of the children of Joseph, came and spoke to Moses before the princes of Israel, and said:
verses.textLatin: Accesserunt autem et principes familiarum Galaad filii Machir filii Manasse, de stirpe filiorum Joseph: locutique sunt Moysi coram principibus Israël, atque dixerunt:

verses.text: The Lord hath commanded thee, my lord, that thou shouldst divide the land by lot to the children of Israel, and that thou shouldst give to the daughters of Salphaad our brother the possession due to their father:
verses.textLatin: Tibi domino nostro præcepit Dominus ut terram sorte divideres filiis Israël, et ut filiabus Salphaad fratris nostri dares possessionem debitam patri:

verses.text: Now if men of another tribe take them to wives, their possession will follow them, and being transferred to another tribe, will be a diminishing of our inheritance.
verses.textLatin: quas si alterius tribus homines uxores acceperint, sequetur possessio sua, et translata ad aliam tribum, de nostra hæreditate minuetur.

verses.text: And so it shall come to pass, that when the jubilee, that is, the fiftieth year of remission, is come, the distribution made by the lots shall be confounded, and the possession of the one shall pass to the others.
verses.textLatin: Atque ita fiet, ut cum jubilæus, id est, quinquagesimus annus remissionis advenerit, confundatur sortium distributio, et aliorum possessio ad alios transeat.

verses.text: Moses answered the children of Israel, and said by the command of the Lord: The tribe of the children of Joseph hath spoken rightly.
verses.textLatin: Respondit Moyses filiis Israël, et Domino præcipiente ait: Recte tribus filiorum Joseph locuta est.

verses.text: And this is the law promulgated by the Lord touching the daughters of Salphaad: Let them marry to whom they will, only so that it be to men of their own tribe.
verses.textLatin: Et hæc lex super filiabus Salphaad a Domino promulgata est: nubant quibus volunt, tantum ut suæ tribus hominibus:

verses.text: Lest the possession of the children of Israel be mingled from tribe to tribe. For all men shall marry wives of their own tribe and kindred:
verses.textLatin: ne commisceatur possessio filiorum Israël de tribu in tribum. Omnes enim viri ducent uxores de tribu et cognatione sua:

verses.text: And all women shall take husbands of the same tribe: that the inheritance may remain in the families,
verses.textLatin: et cunctæ feminæ de eadem tribu maritos accipient: ut hæreditas permaneat in familiis,

verses.text: And that the tribes be not mingled one with another, but remain so
verses.textLatin: nec sibi misceantur tribus, sed ita maneant

verses.text: As they were separated by the Lord. And the daughters of Salphaad did as was commanded:
verses.textLatin: ut a Domino separatæ sunt. Feceruntque filiæ Salphaad ut fuerat imperatum:

verses.text: And Maala, and Thersa, and Hegla, and Melcha, and Noa were married to the sons of their uncle by their father
verses.textLatin: et nupserunt Maala, et Thersa, et Hegla, et Melcha, et Noa, filiis patrui sui

verses.text: Of the family of Manasses, who was the son of Joseph: and the possession that had been allotted to them, remained in the tribe and family of their father.
verses.textLatin: de familia Manasse, qui fuit filius Joseph: et possessio, quæ illis fuerat attributa, mansit in tribu et familia patris earum.

verses.text: These are the commandments and judgments, which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to the children of Israel, in the plains of Moab upon the Jordan over against Jericho.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt mandata atque judicia, quæ mandavit Dominus per manum Moysi ad filios Israël, in campestribus Moab supra Jordanem contra Jericho.

verses.text: These  are the words, which Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the plain wilderness, over against the Red Sea, between Pharan and Thophel and Laban and Haseroth, where there is very much gold:
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt verba quæ locutus est Moyses ad omnem Israël trans Jordanem in solitudine campestri, contra mare Rubrum, inter Pharan et Tophel et Laban et Haseroth, ubi auri est plurimum:

verses.text: Eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of mount Seir to Cadesbarne.
verses.textLatin: undecim diebus de Horeb per viam montis Seir usque ad Cadesbarne.

verses.text: In the fortieth year, the eleventh month, the first day of the month, Moses spoke to the children of Israel all that the Lord had commanded him to say to them:
verses.textLatin: Quadragesimo anno, undecimo mense, prima die mensis, locutus est Moyses ad filios Israël omnia quæ præceperat illi Dominus, ut diceret eis,

verses.text: After that he had slain Sehon king of the Amorrhites, who dwelt in Hesebon: and Og king of Basan who abode in Astaroth, and in Edrai,
verses.textLatin: postquam percussit Sehon regem Amorrhæorum, qui habitabat in Hesebon, et Og regem Basan, qui mansit in Astaroth, et in Edrai,

verses.text: Beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab. And Moses began to expound the law, and to say:
verses.textLatin: trans Jordanem in terra Moab. Cœpitque Moyses explanare legem, et dicere:

verses.text: The Lord our God spoke to us in Horeb, saying: You have stayed long enough in this mountain:
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus noster locutus est ad nos in Horeb, dicens: Sufficit vobis quod in hoc monte mansistis:

verses.text: Turn you, and come to the mountain of the Amorrhites, and to the other places that are next to it, the plains and the hills and the vales towards the south, and by the sea shore, the land of the Chanaanites, and of Libanus, as far as the great river Euphrates.
verses.textLatin: revertimini, et venite ad montem Amorrhæorum, et ad cetera quæ ei proxima sunt campestria atque montana et humiliora loca contra meridiem, et juxta littus maris, terram Chananæorum, et Libani usque ad flumen magnum Euphraten.

verses.text: Behold, said he, I have delivered it to you: go in and possess it, concerning which the Lord swore to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that he would give it to them, and to their seed after them.
verses.textLatin: En, inquit, tradidi vobis: ingredimini et possidete eam, super qua juravit Dominus patribus vestris Abraham, Isaac, et Jacob, ut daret illam eis, et semini eorum post eos.

verses.text: And I said to you at that time:
verses.textLatin: Dixique vobis illo in tempore:

verses.text: I alone am not able to bear you: for the Lord your God hath multiplied you, and you are this day as the stars of heaven, for multitude.
verses.textLatin: Non possum solus sustinere vos: quia Dominus Deus vester multiplicavit vos, et estis hodie sicut stellæ cæli, plurimi.

verses.text: (The Lord God of your fathers add to this number many thousands, and bless you as he hath spoken.)
verses.textLatin: (Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum addat ad hunc numerum multa millia, et benedicat vobis sicut locutus est.)

verses.text: I alone am not able to bear your business, and the charge of you and your differences.
verses.textLatin: Non valeo solus negotia vestra sustinere, et pondus ac jurgia.

verses.text: Let me have from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers.
verses.textLatin: Date ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, et quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, ut ponam eos vobis principes.

verses.text: Then you answered me: The thing is good which thou meanest to do.
verses.textLatin: Tunc respondistis mihi: Bona res est, quam vis facere.

verses.text: And I took out of your tribes men wise and honourable, and appointed them rulers, tribunes, and centurions, and officers over fifties, and over tens, who might teach you all things.
verses.textLatin: Tulique de tribubus vestris viros sapientes et nobiles, et constitui eos principes, tribunos, et centuriones, et quinquagenarios ac decanos, qui docerent vos singula.

verses.text: And I commanded them, saying: Hear them, and judge that which is just: whether he be one of your country, or a stranger.
verses.textLatin: Præcepique eis, dicens: Audite illos, et quod justum est judicate: sive civis sit ille, sive peregrinus.

verses.text: There shall be no difference of persons, you shall hear the little as well as the great: neither shall you respect any man’s person, because it is the judgment of God. And if any thing seem hard to you, refer it to me, and I will hear it.
verses.textLatin: Nulla erit distantia personarum: ita parvum audietis ut magnum, nec accipietis cujusquam personam, quia Dei judicium est. Quod si difficile vobis visum aliquid fuerit, referte ad me, et ego audiam.

verses.text: And I commanded you all things that you were to do.
verses.textLatin: Præcepique omnia quæ facere deberetis.

verses.text: And departing from Horeb, we passed through the terrible and vast wilderness, which you saw, by the way of the mountain of the Amorrhite, as the Lord our God had commanded us. And when we were come into Cadesbarne,
verses.textLatin: Profecti autem de Horeb, transivimus per eremum terribilem et maximam, quam vidistis, per viam montis Amorrhæi, sicut præceperat Dominus Deus noster nobis. Cumque venissemus in Cadesbarne,

verses.text: I said to you: You are come to the mountain of the Amorrhite, which the Lord our God will give to us.
verses.textLatin: dixi vobis: Venistis ad montem Amorrhæi, quem Dominus Deus noster daturus est nobis:

verses.text: See the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee: go up and possess it, as the Lord our God hath spoken to thy fathers: fear not, nor be any way discouraged.
verses.textLatin: vide terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dat tibi: ascende et posside eam, sicut locutus est Dominus Deus noster patribus tuis: noli timere, nec quidquam paveas.

verses.text: And you came all to me, and said: Let us send men who may view the land, and bring us word what way we shall go up, and to what cities we shall go.
verses.textLatin: Et accessistis ad me omnes, atque dixistis: Mittamus viros qui considerent terram: et renuntient per quod iter debeamus ascendere, et ad quas pergere civitates.

verses.text: And because the saying pleased me, I sent of you twelve men, one of every tribe:
verses.textLatin: Cumque mihi sermo placuisset, misi ex vobis duodecim viros, singulos de tribubus suis.

verses.text: Who, when they had set forward and had gone up to the mountains, came as far as the valley of the cluster: and having viewed the land,
verses.textLatin: Qui cum perrexissent, et ascendissent in montana, venerunt usque ad Vallem botri: et considerata terra,

verses.text: Taking of the fruits thereof, to shew its fertility, they brought them to us, and said: The land is good, which the Lord our God will give us.
verses.textLatin: sumentes de fructibus ejus, ut ostenderent ubertatem, attulerunt ad nos, atque dixerunt: Bona est terra, quam Dominus Deus noster daturus est nobis.

verses.text: And you would not go up, but being incredulous to the word of the Lord our God,
verses.textLatin: Et noluistis ascendere, sed increduli ad sermonem Domini Dei nostri,

verses.text: You murmured in your tents, and said: The Lord hateth us, and therefore he hath brought us out of the land of Egypt, that he might deliver us into the hand of the Amorrhite, and destroy us.
verses.textLatin: murmurastis in tabernaculis vestris, atque dixistis: Odit nos Dominus, et idcirco eduxit nos de terra Ægypti, ut traderet nos in manu Amorrhæi, atque deleret.

verses.text: Whither shall we go up? the messengers have terrified our hearts, saying: The multitude is very great, and taller than we: the cities are great, and walled up to the sky, we have seen the sons of the Enacims there.
verses.textLatin: Quo ascendemus? nuntii terruerunt cor nostrum, dicentes: Maxima multitudo est, et nobis statura procerior; urbes magnæ, et ad cælum usque munitæ: filios Enacim vidimus ibi.

verses.text: And I said to you: Fear not, neither be ye afraid of them:
verses.textLatin: Et dixi vobis: Nolite metuere, nec timeatis eos:

verses.text: The Lord God, who is your leader, himself will fight for you, as he did in Egypt in the sight of all.
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus, qui ductor est vester, pro vobis ipse pugnabit, sicut fecit in Ægypto cunctis videntibus.

verses.text: And in the wilderness (as thou hast seen) the Lord thy God hath carried thee, as a man is wont to carry his little son, all the way that you have come, until you came to this place.
verses.textLatin: Et in solitudine (ipse vidisti) portavit te Dominus Deus tuus, ut solet homo gestare parvulum filium suum, in omni via per quam ambulastis, donec veniretis ad locum istum.

verses.text: And yet for all this you did not believe the Lord your God,
verses.textLatin: Et nec sic quidem credidistis Domino Deo vestro,

verses.text: Who went before you in the way, and marked out the place, wherein you should pitch your tents, in the night shewing you the way by fire, and in the day by the pillar of a cloud.
verses.textLatin: qui præcessit vos in via, et metatus est locum in quo tentoria figere deberetis, nocte ostendens vobis iter per ignem, et die per columnam nubis.

verses.text: And when the Lord had heard the voice of your words, he was angry and swore, and said:
verses.textLatin: Cumque audisset Dominus vocem sermonum vestrorum, iratus juravit, et ait:

verses.text: Not one of the men of this wicked generation shall see the good land, which I promised with an oath to your fathers:
verses.textLatin: Non videbit quispiam de hominibus generationis hujus pessimæ terram bonam, quam sub juramento pollicitus sum patribus vestris,

verses.text: Except Caleb the son of Jephone: for he shall see it, and to him I will give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath followed the Lord.
verses.textLatin: præter Caleb filium Jephone: ipse enim videbit eam, et ipsi dabo terram, quam calcavit, et filiis ejus, quia secutus est Dominum.

verses.text: Neither is his indignation against the people to be wondered at, since the Lord was angry with me also on your account, and said: Neither shalt thou go in thither.
verses.textLatin: Nec miranda indignatio in populum, cum mihi quoque iratus Dominus propter vos dixerit: Nec tu ingredieris illuc:

verses.text: But Josue the son of Nun, thy minister, he shall go in for thee: exhort and encourage him, and he shall divide the land by lot to Israel.
verses.textLatin: sed Josue filius Nun minister tuus, ipse intrabit pro te. Hunc exhortare et robora, et ipse sorte terram dividet Israëli.

verses.text: Your children, of whom you said that they should be led away captives, and your sons who know not this day the difference of good and evil, they shall go in: and to them I will give the land, and they shall possess it.
verses.textLatin: Parvuli vestri, de quibus dixistis quod captivi ducerentur, et filii qui hodie boni ac mali ignorant distantiam, ipsi ingredientur: et ipsis dabo terram, et possidebunt eam.

verses.text: But return you and go into the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem revertimini, et abite in solitudinem per viam maris Rubri.

verses.text: And you answered me: We have sinned against the Lord: we will go up and fight, as the Lord our God hath commanded. And when you went ready armed unto the mountain,
verses.textLatin: Et respondistis mihi: Peccavimus Domino: ascendemus et pugnabimus, sicut præcepit Dominus Deus noster. Cumque instructi armis pergeretis in montem,

verses.text: The Lord said to me: Say to them: Go not up, and fight not, for I am not with you: lest you fall before your enemies.
verses.textLatin: ait mihi Dominus: Dic ad eos: Nolite ascendere, neque pugnetis: non enim sum vobiscum: ne cadatis coram inimicis vestris.

verses.text: I spoke, and you hearkened not: but resisting the commandment of the Lord, and swelling with pride, you went up into the mountain.
verses.textLatin: Locutus sum, et non audistis: sed adversantes imperio Domini, et tumentes superbia, ascendistis in montem.

verses.text: And the Amorrhite that dwelt in the mountains coming out, and meeting you, chased you, as bees do: and made slaughter of you from Seir as far as Horma.
verses.textLatin: Itaque egressus Amorrhæus, qui habitabat in montibus, et obviam veniens, persecutus est vos, sicut solent apes persequi: et cecidit de Seir usque Horma.

verses.text: And when you returned and wept before the Lord, he heard you not, neither would he yield to your voice.
verses.textLatin: Cumque reversi ploraretis coram Domino, non audivit vos, nec voci vestræ voluit acquiescere.

verses.text: So you abode in Cadesbarne a long time.
verses.textLatin: Sedistis ergo in Cadesbarne multo tempore.

verses.text: And  departing from thence we came into the wilderness that leadeth to the Red Sea, as the Lord had spoken to me: and we compassed mount Seir a long time.
verses.textLatin: Profectique inde, venimus in solitudinem, quæ ducit ad mare Rubrum, sicut mihi dixerat Dominus: et circuivimus montem Seir longo tempore.

verses.text: And the Lord said to me:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad me:

verses.text: You have compassed this mountain long enough: go toward the north:
verses.textLatin: Sufficit vobis circuire montem istum: ite contra aquilonem:

verses.text: And command thou the people, saying: You shall pass by the borders of your brethren the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir, and they will be afraid of you.
verses.textLatin: et populo præcipe, dicens: Transibitis per terminos fratrum vestrorum filiorum Esau, qui habitant in Seir, et timebunt vos.

verses.text: Take ye then good heed that you stir not against them. For I will not give you of their land so much as the step of one foot can tread upon, because I have given mount Seir to Esau, for a possession.
verses.textLatin: Videte ergo diligenter ne moveamini contra eos. Neque enim dabo vobis de terra eorum quantum potest unius pedis calcare vestigium, quia in possessionem Esau dedi montem Seir.

verses.text: You shall buy meats of them for money and shall eat: you shall draw waters for money, and shall drink.
verses.textLatin: Cibos emetis ab eis pecunia, et comedetis: aquam emptam haurietis, et bibetis.

verses.text: The Lord thy God hath blessed thee in every work of thy hands: the Lord thy God dwelling with thee, knoweth thy journey, how thou hast passed through this great wilderness, for forty years, and thou hast wanted nothing.
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus tuus benedixit tibi in omni opere manuum tuarum: novit iter tuum, quomodo transieris solitudinem hanc magnam, per quadraginta annos habitans tecum Dominus Deus tuus, et nihil tibi defuit.

verses.text: And when we had passed by our brethren the children of Esau, that dwelt in Seir, by the way of the plain from Elath and from Asiongaber, we came to the way that leadeth to the desert of Moab.
verses.textLatin: Cumque transissemus fratres nostros filios Esau, qui habitabant in Seir, per viam campestrem de Elath, et de Asiongaber, venimus ad iter quod ducit in desertum Moab.

verses.text: And the Lord said to me: Fight not against the Moabites, neither go to battle against them: for I will not give thee any of their land, because I have given Ar to the children of Lot in possession.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad me: Non pugnes contra Moabitas, nec ineas adversus eos prælium: non enim dabo tibi quidquam de terra eorum, quia filiis Loth tradidi Ar in possessionem.

verses.text: The Emims first were the inhabitants thereof, a people great, and strong, and so tall, that like the race of the Enacims,
verses.textLatin: Emim primi fuerunt habitatores ejus, populus magnus, et validus, et tam excelsus ut de Enacim stirpe,

verses.text: They were esteemed as giants, and were like the sons of the Enacims. But the Moabites call them Emims.
verses.textLatin: quasi gigantes crederentur, et essent similes filiorum Enacim. Denique Moabitæ appellant eos Emim.

verses.text: The Horrhites also formerly dwelt in Seir: who being driven out and destroyed, the children of Esau dwelt there, as Israel did in the land of his possession, which the Lord gave him.
verses.textLatin: In Seir autem prius habitaverunt Horrhæi: quibus expulsis atque deletis, habitaverunt filii Esau, sicut fecit Israël in terra possessionis suæ, quam dedit illi Dominus.

verses.text: Then rising up to pass the torrent Zared, we came to it.
verses.textLatin: Surgentes ergo ut transiremus torrentem Zared, venimus ad eum.

verses.text: And the time that we journeyed from Cadesbarne till we passed over the torrent Zared, was thirty-eight years: until all the generation of the men that were fit for war was consumed out of the camp, as the Lord had sworn:
verses.textLatin: Tempus autem, quo ambulavimus de Cadesbarne usque ad transitum torrentis Zared, triginta et octo annorum fuit: donec consumeretur omnis generatio hominum bellatorum de castris, sicut juraverat Dominus:

verses.text: For his hand was against them, that they should perish from the midst of the camp.
verses.textLatin: cujus manus fuit adversum eos, ut interirent de castrorum medio.

verses.text: And after all the fighting men were dead,
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem universi ceciderunt pugnatores,

verses.text: The Lord spoke to me, saying:
verses.textLatin: locutus est Dominus ad me, dicens:

verses.text: Thou shalt pass this day the borders of Moab, the city named Ar:
verses.textLatin: Tu transibis hodie terminos Moab, urbem nomine Ar:

verses.text: And when thou comest nigh the frontiers of the children of Ammon, take heed thou fight not against them, nor once move to battle: for I will not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon, because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.
verses.textLatin: et accedens in vicina filiorum Ammon, cave ne pugnes contra eos, nec movearis ad prælium: non enim dabo tibi de terra filiorum Ammon, quia filiis Loth dedi eam in possessionem.

verses.text: It was accounted a land of giants: and giants formerly dwelt in it, whom the Ammonites call Zomzommims,
verses.textLatin: Terra gigantum reputata est: et in ipsa olim habitaverunt gigantes, quos Ammonitæ vocant Zomzommim,

verses.text: A people great and many, and of tall stature, like the Enacims whom the Lord destroyed before their face: and he made them to dwell in their stead,
verses.textLatin: populus magnus, et multus, et proceræ longitudinis, sicut Enacim, quos delevit Dominus a facie eorum: et fecit illos habitare pro eis,

verses.text: As he had done in favour of the children of Esau, that dwell in Seir, destroying the Horrhites, and delivering their land to them, which they possess to this day.
verses.textLatin: sicut fecerat filiis Esau, qui habitant in Seir, delens Horrhæos, et terram eorum illis tradens, quam possident usque in præsens.

verses.text: The Hevites also, that dwelt in Haserim as far as Gaza, were expelled by the Cappadocians: who came out of Cappadocia, and destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.
verses.textLatin: Hevæos quoque, qui habitabant in Haserim usque Gazan, Cappadoces expulerunt: qui egressi de Cappadocia deleverunt eos, et habitaverunt pro illis.

verses.text: Arise ye, and pass the torrent Arnon: Behold I have delivered into thy hand Sehon king of Hesebon the Amorrhite, and begin thou to possess his land and make war against him.
verses.textLatin: Surgite, et transite torrentem Arnon: ecce tradidi in manu tua Sehon regem Hesebon Amorrhæum, et terram ejus incipe possidere, et committe adversus eum prælium.

verses.text: This day will I begin to send the dread and fear of thee upon the nations that dwell under the whole heaven: that when they hear thy name they may fear and tremble, and be in pain like women in travail.
verses.textLatin: Hodie incipiam mittere terrorem atque formidinem tuam in populos, qui habitant sub omni cælo: ut audito nomine tuo paveant, et in morem parturientium contremiscant, et dolore teneantur.

verses.text: So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Cademoth to Sehon the king of Hesebon with peaceable words, saying:
verses.textLatin: Misi ergo nuntios de solitudine Cademoth ad Sehon regem Hesebon verbis pacificis, dicens:

verses.text: We will pass through thy land, we will go along by the highway: we will not turn aside neither to the right hand nor to the left.
verses.textLatin: Transibimus per terram tuam: publica gradiemur via; non declinabimus neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram.

verses.text: Sell us meat for money, that we may eat: give us water for money and so we will drink. We only ask that thou wilt let us pass through,
verses.textLatin: Alimenta pretio vende nobis, ut vescamur: aquam pecunia tribue, et sic bibemus. Tantum est ut nobis concedas transitum,

verses.text: As the children of Esau have done, that dwell in Seir, and the Moabites, that abide in Ar: until we come to the Jordan, and pass to the land which the Lord our God will give us.
verses.textLatin: sicut fecerunt filii Esau, qui habitant in Seir, et Moabitæ, qui morantur in Ar: donec veniamus ad Jordanem, et transeamus ad terram, quam Dominus Deus noster daturus est nobis.

verses.text: And Sehon the king of Hesebon would not let us pass: because the Lord thy God had hardened his spirit, and fixed his heart, that he might be delivered into thy hands, as now thou seest.
verses.textLatin: Noluitque Sehon rex Hesebon dare nobis transitum: quia induraverat Dominus Deus tuus spiritum ejus, et obfirmaverat cor illius, ut traderetur in manus tuas, sicut nunc vides.

verses.text: And the Lord said to me: Behold I have begun to deliver unto thee Sehon and his land, begin to possess it.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad me: Ecce cœpi tibi tradere Sehon, et terram ejus: incipe possidere eam.

verses.text: And Sehon came out to meet us with all his people to fight at Jasa.
verses.textLatin: Egressusque est Sehon obviam nobis cum omni populo suo ad prælium in Jasa.

verses.text: And the Lord our God delivered him to us: and we slew him with his sons and all his people.
verses.textLatin: Et tradidit eum Dominus Deus noster nobis: percussimusque eum cum filiis suis et omni populo suo.

verses.text: And we took all his cities at that time, killing the inhabitants of them, men and women and children. We left nothing of them:
verses.textLatin: Cunctasque urbes in tempore illo cepimus, interfectis habitatoribus earum, viris ac mulieribus et parvulis: non reliquimus in eis quidquam,

verses.text: Except the cattle which came to the share of them that took them: and the spoils of the cities, which we took:
verses.textLatin: absque jumentis, quæ in partem venere prædantium: et spoliis urbium, quas cepimus

verses.text: From Aroer, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, a town that is situate in a valley, as far as Galaad. There was not a village or city, that escaped our hands: the Lord our God delivered all unto us:
verses.textLatin: ab Aroër, quæ est super ripam torrentis Arnon, oppido quod in valle situm est, usque Galaad. Non fuit vicus et civitas, quæ nostras effugeret manus: omnes tradidit Dominus Deus noster nobis,

verses.text: Except the land of the children of Ammon, to which we approached not: and all that border upon the torrent Jeboc, and the cities in the mountains, and all the places which the Lord our God forbade us.
verses.textLatin: absque terra filiorum Ammon, ad quam non accessimus: et cunctis quæ adjacent torrenti Jeboc, et urbibus montanis, universisque locis, a quibus nos prohibuit Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: Then  we turned and went by the way of Basan: and Og the king of Basan came out to meet us with his people to fight in Edrai.
verses.textLatin: Itaque conversi ascendimus per iter Basan: egressusque est Og rex Basan in occursum nobis cum populo suo ad bellandum in Edrai.

verses.text: And the Lord said to me: Fear him not: because he is delivered into thy hand, with all his people and his land: and thou shalt do to him as thou hast done to Sehon king of the Amorrhites, that dwelt in Hesebon.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad me: Ne timeas eum: quia in manu tua traditus est cum omni populo ac terra sua: faciesque ei sicut fecisti Sehon regi Amorrhæorum, qui habitavit in Hesebon.

verses.text: So the Lord our God delivered into our hands, Og also the king of Basan, and all his people: and we utterly destroyed them,
verses.textLatin: Tradidit ergo Dominus Deus noster in manibus nostris etiam Og regem Basan, et universum populum ejus: percussimusque eos usque ad internecionem,

verses.text: Wasting all his cities at one time, there was not a town that escaped us: sixty cities, all the country of Argob the kingdom of Og in Basan.
verses.textLatin: vastantes cunctas civitates illius uno tempore. Non fuit oppidum, quod nos effugeret: sexaginta urbes, omnem regionem Argob regni Og in Basan.

verses.text: All the cities were fenced with very high walls, and with gates and bars, besides innumerable towns that had no walls.
verses.textLatin: Cunctæ urbes erant munitæ muris altissimis, portisque et vectibus, absque oppidis innumeris, quæ non habebant muros.

verses.text: And we utterly destroyed them, as we had done to Sehon the king of Hesebon, destroying every city, men and women and children:
verses.textLatin: Et delevimus eos, sicut feceramus Sehon regi Hesebon, disperdentes omnem civitatem, virosque ac mulieres et parvulos:

verses.text: But the cattle and the spoils of the cities we took for our prey.
verses.textLatin: jumenta autem et spolia urbium diripuimus.

verses.text: And we took at that time the land out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorrhites, that were beyond the Jordan: from the torrent Arnon unto the mount Hermon,
verses.textLatin: Tulimusque illo in tempore terram de manu duorum regum Amorrhæorum, qui erant trans Jordanem: a torrente Arnon usque ad montem Hermon,

verses.text: Which the Sidonians call Sarion, and the Amorrhites Sanir:
verses.textLatin: quem Sidonii Sarion vocant, et Amorrhæi Sanir:

verses.text: All the cities that are situate in the plain, and all the land of Galaad and Basan as far as Selcha and Edrai, cities of the kingdom of Og in Basan.
verses.textLatin: omnes civitates, quæ sitæ sunt in planitie, et universam terram Galaad et Basan usque ad Selcha, et Edrai civitates regni Og in Basan.

verses.text: For only Og king of Basan remained of the race of the giants. His bed of iron is shewn, which is in Rabbath of the children of Ammon, being nine cubits long, and four broad after the measure of the cubit of a man’s hand.
verses.textLatin: Solus quippe Og rex Basan restiterat de stirpe gigantum. Monstratur lectus ejus ferreus, qui est in Rabbath filiorum Ammon, novem cubitos habens longitudinis, et quatuor latitudinis ad mensuram cubiti virilis manus.

verses.text: And we possessed the land at that time from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, unto the half of mount Galaad: and I gave the cities thereof to Ruben and Gad.
verses.textLatin: Terramque possedimus tempore illo ab Aroër, quæ est super ripam torrentis Arnon, usque ad mediam partem montis Galaad: et civitates illius dedi Ruben et Gad.

verses.text: And I delivered the other part of Galaad, and all Basan the kingdom of Og to the half tribe of Manasses, all the country of Argob: and all Basan is called the Land of giants.
verses.textLatin: Reliquam autem partem Galaad, et omnem Basan regni Og, tradidi mediæ tribui Manasse, omnem regionem Argob: cunctaque Basan vocatur Terra gigantum.

verses.text: Jair the son of Manasses possessed all the country of Argob unto the borders of Gessuri, and Machati. And he called Basan by his own name, Havoth Jair, that is to say, the towns of Jair, until this present day.
verses.textLatin: Jair filius Manasse possedit omnem regionem Argob usque ad terminos Gessuri et Machati. Vocavitque ex nomine suo Basan, Havoth Jair, id est, Villas Jair, usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: To Machir also I gave Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Machir quoque dedi Galaad.

verses.text: And to the tribes of Ruben and Gad I gave of the land of Galaad as far as the torrent Arnon, half the torrent, and the confines even unto the torrent Jeboc, which is the border of the children of Ammon:
verses.textLatin: Et tribubus Ruben et Gad dedi de terra Galaad usque ad torrentem Arnon medium torrentis, et confinium usque ad torrentem Jeboc, qui est terminus filiorum Ammon:

verses.text: And the plain of the wilderness, and the Jordan, and the borders of Cenereth unto the sea of the desert, which is the most salt sea, to the foot of mount Phasga eastward.
verses.textLatin: et planitiem solitudinis, atque Jordanem, et terminos Cenereth usque ad mare deserti, quod est salsissimum, ad radices montis Phasga contra orientem.

verses.text: And I commanded you at that time, saying: The Lord your God giveth you this land for an inheritance, go ye well appointed before your brethren the children of Israel, all the strong men of you,
verses.textLatin: Præcepique vobis in tempore illo, dicens: Dominus Deus vester dat vobis terram hanc in hæreditatem: expediti præcedite fratres vestros filios Israël omnes viri robusti,

verses.text: Leaving your wives and children and cattle. For I know you have much cattle, and they must remain in the cities, which I have delivered to you.
verses.textLatin: absque uxoribus, et parvulis, atque jumentis. Novi enim quod plura habeatis pecora, et in urbibus remanere debebunt, quas tradidi vobis,

verses.text: Until the Lord give rest to your brethren, as he hath given to you: and they also possess the land, which he will give them beyond the Jordan: then shall every man return to his possession, which I have given you.
verses.textLatin: donec requiem tribuat Dominus fratribus vestris, sicut vobis tribuit: et possideant ipsi etiam terram, quam daturus est eis trans Jordanem: tunc revertetur unusquisque in possessionem suam, quam dedi vobis.

verses.text: I commanded Josue also at that time, saying: Thy eyes have seen what the Lord your God hath done to these two kings: so will he do to all the kingdoms to which thou shalt pass.
verses.textLatin: Josue quoque in tempore illo præcepi, dicens: Oculi tui viderunt quæ fecit Dominus Deus vester duobus his regibus: sic faciet omnibus regnis, ad quæ transiturus es.

verses.text: Fear them not: for the Lord your God will fight for you.
verses.textLatin: Ne timeas eos: Dominus enim Deus vester pugnabit pro vobis.

verses.text: And I besought the Lord at that time, saying:
verses.textLatin: Precatusque sum Dominum in tempore illo, dicens:

verses.text: Lord God, thou hast begun to shew unto thy servant thy greatness, and most mighty hand, for there is no other God either in heaven or earth, that is able to do thy works, or to be compared to thy strength.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus, tu cœpisti ostendere servo tuo magnitudinem tuam, manumque fortissimam: neque enim est alius deus vel in cælo, vel in terra, qui possit facere opera tua, et comparari fortitudini tuæ.

verses.text: I will pass over therefore, and will see this excellent land beyond the Jordan, and this goodly mountain, and Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Transibo igitur, et videbo terram hanc optimam trans Jordanem, et montem istum egregium, et Libanum.

verses.text: And the Lord was angry with me on your account and heard me not, but said to me: It is enough: speak no more to me of this matter.
verses.textLatin: Iratusque est Dominus mihi propter vos, nec exaudivit me, sed dixit mihi: Sufficit tibi: nequaquam ultra loquaris de hac re ad me.

verses.text: Go up to the top of Phasga, and cast thy eyes round about to the west, and to the north, and to the south, and to the east, and behold it, for thou shalt not pass this Jordan.
verses.textLatin: Ascende cacumen Phasgæ, et oculos tuos circumfer ad occidentem, et ad aquilonem, austrumque et orientem, et aspice; nec enim transibis Jordanem istum.

verses.text: Command Josue, and encourage and strengthen him: for he shall go before this people, and shall divide unto them the land which thou shalt see.
verses.textLatin: Præcipe Josue, et corrobora eum atque conforta: quia ipse præcedet populum istum, et dividet eis terram quam visurus es.

verses.text: And we abode in the valley over against the temple of Phogor
verses.textLatin: Mansimusque in valle contra fanum Phogor.

verses.text: And  now, O Israel, hear the commandments and judgments which I teach thee: that doing them, thou mayst live, and entering in mayst possess the land which the Lord the God of your fathers will give you.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc, Israël, audi præcepta et judicia, quæ ego doceo te: ut faciens ea, vivas, et ingrediens possideas terram, quam Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum daturus est vobis.

verses.text: You shall not add to the word that I speak to you, neither shall you take away from it: keep the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you.
verses.textLatin: Non addetis ad verbum, quod vobis loquor, nec auferetis ex eo: custodite mandata Domini Dei vestri, quæ ego præcipio vobis.

verses.text: Your eyes have seen all that the Lord hath done against Beelphegor, how he hath destroyed all his worshippers from among you.
verses.textLatin: Oculi vestri viderunt omnia quæ fecit Dominus contra Beelphegor, quomodo contriverit omnes cultores ejus de medio vestri.

verses.text: But you that adhere to the Lord your God, are all alive until this present day.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem qui adhæretis Domino Deo vestro, vivitis universi usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: You know that I have taught you statutes and justices, as the Lord my God hath commanded me: so shall you do them in the land which you shall possess:
verses.textLatin: Scitis quod docuerim vos præcepta atque justitias, sicut mandavit mihi Dominus Deus meus: sic facietis ea in terra, quam possessuri estis:

verses.text: And you shall observe, and fulfil them in practice. For this is your wisdom, and understanding in the sight of nations, that hearing all these precepts, they may say: Behold a wise and understanding people, a great nation.
verses.textLatin: et observabitis et implebitis opere. Hæc est enim vestra sapientia, et intellectus coram populis, ut audientes universa præcepta hæc, dicant: En populus sapiens et intelligens, gens magna.

verses.text: Neither is there any other nation so great, that hath gods so nigh them, as our God is present to all our petitions.
verses.textLatin: Nec est alia natio tam grandis, quæ habeat deos appropinquantes sibi, sicut Deus noster adest cunctis obsecrationibus nostris.

verses.text: For what other nation is there so renowned that hath ceremonies, and just judgments, and all the law, which I will set forth this day before your eyes?
verses.textLatin: Quæ est enim alia gens sic inclyta, ut habeat cæremonias, justaque judicia, et universam legem, quam ego proponam hodie ante oculos vestros?

verses.text: Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully. Forget not the words that thy eyes have seen, and let them not go out of thy heart all the days of thy life. Thou shalt teach them to thy sons and to thy grandsons,
verses.textLatin: Custodi igitur temetipsum, et animam tuam sollicite. Ne obliviscaris verborum, quæ viderunt oculi tui, et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ. Docebis ea filios ac nepotes tuos,

verses.text: From the day in which thou didst stand before the Lord thy God in Horeb, when the Lord spoke to me, saying: Call together the people unto me, that they may hear my words, and may learn to fear me all the time that they live on the earth, and may teach their children.
verses.textLatin: a die in quo stetisti coram Domino Deo tuo in Horeb, quando Dominus locutus est mihi, dicens: Congrega ad me populum, ut audiant sermones meos, et discant timere me omni tempore quo vivunt in terra, doceantque filios suos.

verses.text: And you came to the foot of the mount, which burned even unto heaven: and there was darkness, and a cloud and obscurity in it.
verses.textLatin: Et accessistis ad radices montis, qui ardebat usque ad cælum: erantque in eo tenebræ, et nubes, et caligo.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the voice of his words, but you saw not any form at all.
verses.textLatin: Locutusque est Dominus ad vos de medio ignis. Vocem verborum ejus audistis, et formam penitus non vidistis.

verses.text: And he shewed you his covenant, which he commanded you to do, and the ten words that he wrote in two tables of stone.
verses.textLatin: Et ostendit vobis pactum suum, quod præcepit ut faceretis, et decem verba, quæ scripsit in duabus tabulis lapideis.

verses.text: And he commanded me at that time that I should teach you the ceremonies and judgments which you shall do in the land, that you shall possess.
verses.textLatin: Mihique mandavit in illo tempore ut docerem vos cæremonias et judicia, quæ facere deberetis in terra, quam possessuri estis.

verses.text: Keep therefore your souls carefully. You saw not any similitude in the day that the Lord God spoke to you in Horeb from the midst of the fire:
verses.textLatin: Custodite igitur sollicite animas vestras. Non vidistis aliquam similitudinem in die, qua locutus est vobis Dominus in Horeb de medio ignis:

verses.text: Lest perhaps being deceived you might make you a graven similitude, or image of male or female,
verses.textLatin: ne forte decepti faciatis vobis sculptam similitudinem, aut imaginem masculi vel feminæ:

verses.text: The similitude of any beasts, that are upon the earth, or of birds, that fly under heaven,
verses.textLatin: similitudinem omnium jumentorum, quæ sunt super terram, vel avium sub cælo volantium,

verses.text: Or of creeping things, that move on the earth, or of fishes, that abide in the waters under the earth:
verses.textLatin: atque reptilium, quæ moventur in terra, sive piscium qui sub terra morantur in aquis:

verses.text: Lest perhaps lifting up thy eyes to heaven, thou see the sun and the moon, and all the stars of heaven, and being deceived by error thou adore and serve them, which the Lord thy God created for the service of all the nations, that are under heaven.
verses.textLatin: ne forte elevatis oculis ad cælum, videas solem et lunam, et omnia astra cæli, et errore deceptus adores ea, et colas quæ creavit Dominus Deus tuus in ministerium cunctis gentibus, quæ sub cælo sunt.

verses.text: But the Lord hath taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace of Egypt, to make you his people of inheritance, as it is this present day.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem tulit Dominus, et eduxit de fornace ferrea Ægypti, ut haberet populum hæreditarium, sicut est in præsenti die.

verses.text: And the Lord was angry with me for your words, and he swore that I should not pass over the Jordan, nor enter into the excellent land, which he will give you.
verses.textLatin: Iratusque est Dominus contra me propter sermones vestros, et juravit ut non transirem Jordanem, nec ingrederer terram optimam, quam daturus est vobis.

verses.text: Behold I die in this land, I shall not pass over the Jordan: you shall pass, and possess the goodly land.
verses.textLatin: Ecce morior in hac humo; non transibo Jordanem: vos transibitis, et possidebitis terram egregiam.

verses.text: Beware lest thou ever forget the covenant of the Lord thy God, which he hath made with thee: and make to thyself a graven likeness of those things which the Lord hath forbid to be made:
verses.textLatin: Cave nequando obliviscaris pacti Domini Dei tui, quod pepigit tecum, et facias tibi sculptam similitudinem eorum, quæ fieri Dominus prohibuit:

verses.text: Because the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
verses.textLatin: quia Dominus Deus tuus ignis consumens est, Deus æmulator.

verses.text: If you shall beget sons and grandsons, and abide in the land, and being deceived, make to yourselves any similitude, committing evil before the Lord your God, to provoke him to wrath:
verses.textLatin: Si genueritis filios ac nepotes, et morati fueritis in terra, deceptique feceritis vobis aliquam similitudinem, patrantes malum coram Domino Deo vestro, ut eum ad iracundiam provocetis:

verses.text: I call this day heaven and earth to witness, that you shall quickly perish out of the land, which, when you have passed over the Jordan, you shall possess. You shall not dwell therein long, but the Lord will destroy you,
verses.textLatin: testes invoco hodie cælum et terram, cito perituros vos esse de terra, quam transito Jordane possessuri estis: non habitabitis in ea longo tempore, sed delebit vos Dominus,

verses.text: And scatter you among all nations, and you shall remain a few among the nations, to which the Lord shall lead you.
verses.textLatin: atque disperget in omnes gentes, et remanebitis pauci in nationibus, ad quas vos ducturus est Dominus.

verses.text: And there you shall serve gods, that were framed with men’s hands: wood and stone, that neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
verses.textLatin: Ibique servietis diis, qui hominum manu fabricati sunt, ligno et lapidi qui non vident, nec audiunt, nec comedunt, nec odorantur.

verses.text: And when thou shalt seek there the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him: yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, and all the affliction of thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Cumque quæsieris ibi Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum: si tamen toto corde quæsieris, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ.

verses.text: After all the things aforesaid shall find thee, in the latter time thou shalt return to the Lord thy God, and shalt hear his voice.
verses.textLatin: Postquam te invenerint omnia quæ prædicta sunt, novissimo tempore reverteris ad Dominum Deum tuum, et audies vocem ejus.

verses.text: Because the Lord thy God is a merciful God: he will not leave thee, nor altogether destroy thee, nor forget the covenant, by which he swore to thy fathers.
verses.textLatin: Quia Deus misericors Dominus Deus tuus est: non dimittet te, nec omnino delebit, neque obliviscetur pacti, in quo juravit patribus tuis.

verses.text: Ask of the days of old, that have been before thy time from the day that God created man upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other end thereof, if ever there was done the like thing, or it hath been known at any time,
verses.textLatin: Interroga de diebus antiquis, qui fuerunt ante te ex die quo creavit Deus hominem super terram, a summo cælo usque ad summum ejus, si facta est aliquando hujuscemodi res, aut umquam cognitum est,

verses.text: That a people should hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of fire, as thou hast heard, and lived:
verses.textLatin: ut audiret populus vocem Dei loquentis de medio ignis, sicut tu audisti, et vixisti:

verses.text: If God ever did so as to go, and take to himself a nation out of the midst of nations by temptations, signs, and wonders, by fight, and a strong hand, and stretched out arm, and horrible visions according to all the things that the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before thy eyes.
verses.textLatin: si fecit Deus ut ingrederetur, et tolleret sibi gentem de medio nationum, per tentationes, signa atque portenta, per pugnam et robustam manum, extentumque brachium, et horribiles visiones juxta omnia quæ fecit pro vobis Dominus Deus vester in Ægypto, videntibus oculis tuis:

verses.text: That thou mightest know that the Lord he is God, and there is no other besides him.
verses.textLatin: ut scires quoniam Dominus ipse est Deus, et non est alius præter eum.

verses.text: From heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might teach thee. And upon earth he shewed thee his exceeding great fire, and thou didst hear his words out of the midst of the fire,
verses.textLatin: De cælo te fecit audire vocem suam, ut doceret te, et in terra ostendit tibi ignem suum maximum, et audisti verba illius de medio ignis:

verses.text: Because he loved thy fathers, and chose their seed after them. And he brought thee out of Egypt, going before thee with his great power,
verses.textLatin: quia dilexit patres tuos, et elegit semen eorum post eos. Eduxitque te præcedens in virtute sua magna ex Ægypto,

verses.text: To destroy at thy coming very great nations, and stronger than thou art, and to bring thee in, and give thee their land for a possession, as thou seest at this present day.
verses.textLatin: ut deleret nationes maximas et fortiores te in introitu tuo: et introduceret te, daretque tibi terram earum in possessionem, sicut cernis in præsenti die.

verses.text: Know therefore this day, and think in thy heart that the Lord he is God in heaven above, and in the earth beneath, and there is no other.
verses.textLatin: Scito ergo hodie, et cogitato in corde tuo quod Dominus ipse sit Deus in cælo sursum, et in terra deorsum, et non sit alius.

verses.text: Keep his precepts and commandments, which I command thee: that it may be well with thee, and thy children after thee, and thou mayst remain a long time upon the land, which the Lord thy God will give thee.
verses.textLatin: Custodi præcepta ejus atque mandata, quæ ego præcipio tibi: ut bene sit tibi, et filiis tuis post te, et permaneas multo tempore super terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus daturus est tibi.

verses.text: Then Moses set aside three cities beyond the Jordan at the east side,
verses.textLatin: Tunc separavit Moyses tres civitates trans Jordanem ad orientalem plagam,

verses.text: That any one might flee to them who should kill his neighbour unwillingly, and was not his enemy a day or two before, and that he might escape to some one of these cities:
verses.textLatin: ut confugiat ad eas qui occiderit nolens proximum suum, nec sibi fuerit inimicus ante unum et alterum diem, et ad harum aliquam urbium possit evadere:

verses.text: Bosor in the wilderness, which is situate in the plains of the tribe of Ruben: and Ramoth in Galaad, which is in the tribe of Gad: and Golan in Basan, which is in the tribe of Manasses.
verses.textLatin: Bosor in solitudine, quæ sita est in terra campestri de tribu Ruben: et Ramoth in Galaad, quæ est in tribu Gad: et Golan in Basan, quæ est in tribu Manasse.

verses.text: This is the law, that Moses set before the children of Israel,
verses.textLatin: Ista est lex, quam proposuit Moyses coram filiis Israël:

verses.text: And these are the testimonies and ceremonies and judgments, which he spoke to the children of Israel, when they came out of Egypt,
verses.textLatin: et hæc testimonia et cæremoniæ atque judicia, quæ locutus est ad filios Israël, quando egressi sunt de Ægypto,

verses.text: Beyond the Jordan in the valley over against the temple of Phogor, in the land of Sehon king of the Amorrhites, that dwelt in Hesebon, whom Moses slew. And the children of Israel coming out of Egypt,
verses.textLatin: trans Jordanem in valle contra fanum Phogor in terra Sehon regis Amorrhæi, qui habitavit in Hesebon, quem percussit Moyses. Filii quoque Israël egressi ex Ægypto

verses.text: Possessed his land, and the land of Og king of Basan, of the two kings of the Amorrhites, who were beyond the Jordan towards the rising of the sun:
verses.textLatin: possederunt terram ejus, et terram Og regis Basan, duorum regum Amorrhæorum, qui erant trans Jordanem ad solis ortum:

verses.text: From Aroer, which is situate upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, unto mount Sion, which is also called Hermon,
verses.textLatin: ab Aroër, quæ sita est super ripam torrentis Arnon, usque ad montem Sion, qui est et Hermon,

verses.text: All the plain beyond the Jordan at the east side, unto the sea of the wilderness, and unto the foot of mount Phasga.
verses.textLatin: omnem planitiem trans Jordanem ad orientalem plagam, usque ad mare solitudinis, et usque ad radices montis Phasga.

verses.text: And  Moses called all Israel, and said to them: Hear, O Israel, the ceremonies and judgments, which I speak in your ears this day: learn them, and fulfil them in work.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Moyses omnem Israëlem, et dixit ad eum: Audi, Israël, cæremonias atque judicia, quæ ego loquor in auribus vestris hodie: discite ea, et opere complete.

verses.text: The Lord our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus noster pepigit nobiscum fœdus in Horeb.

verses.text: He made not the covenant with our fathers, but with us, who are now present and living.
verses.textLatin: Non cum patribus nostris iniit pactum, sed nobiscum qui in præsentiarum sumus, et vivimus.

verses.text: He spoke to us face to face in the mount out of the midst of fire.
verses.textLatin: Facie ad faciem locutus est nobis in monte de medio ignis.

verses.text: I was the mediator and stood between the Lord and you at that time, to shew you his words, for you feared the fire, and went not up into the mountain, and he said:
verses.textLatin: Ego sequester et medius fui inter Dominum et vos in tempore illo, ut annuntiarem vobis verba ejus: timuistis enim ignem, et non ascendistis in montem. Et ait:

verses.text: I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti, de domo servitutis.

verses.text: Thou shalt not have strange gods in my sight.
verses.textLatin: Non habebis deos alienos in conspectu meo.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make to thyself a graven thing, nor the likeness of any things, that are in heaven above, or that are in the earth beneath, or that abide in the waters under the earth.
verses.textLatin: Non facies tibi sculptile, nec similitudinem omnium, quæ in cælo sunt desuper, et quæ in terra deorsum, et quæ versantur in aquis sub terra.

verses.text: Thou shalt not adore them, and thou shalt not serve them. For I am the Lord thy God, a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon their children unto the third and fourth generation, to them that hate me,
verses.textLatin: Non adorabis ea, et non coles. Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus: Deus æmulator, reddens iniquitatem patrum super filios in tertiam et quartam generationem his qui oderunt me:

verses.text: And shewing mercy unto many thousands, to them that love me, and keep my commandments.
verses.textLatin: et faciens misericordiam in multa millia diligentibus me, et custodientibus præcepta mea.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for he shall not be unpunished that taketh his name upon a vain thing.
verses.textLatin: Non usurpabis nomen Domini Dei tui frustra: quia non erit impunitus qui super re vana nomen ejus assumpserit.

verses.text: Observe the day of the sabbath, to sanctify it, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee.
verses.textLatin: Observa diem sabbati, ut sanctifices eum, sicut præcepit tibi Dominus Deus tuus.

verses.text: Six days shalt thou labour, and shalt do all thy works.
verses.textLatin: Sex diebus operaberis, et facies omnia opera tua.

verses.text: The seventh is the day of the sab©bath, that is, the rest of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not do any work therein, thou nor thy son nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant nor thy maidservant, nor thy ox, nor thy ass, nor any of thy beasts, nor the stranger that is within thy gates: that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest, even as thyself.
verses.textLatin: Septimus dies sabbati est, id est, requies Domini Dei tui. Non facies in eo quidquam operis tu, et filius tuus, et filia, servus et ancilla, et bos, et asinus, et omne jumentum tuum, et peregrinus qui est intra portas tuas: ut requiescat servus tuus, et ancilla tua, sicut et tu.

verses.text: Remember that thou also didst serve in Egypt, and the Lord thy God brought thee out from thence with a strong hand, and a stretched out arm. Therefore hath he commanded thee that thou shouldst observe the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Memento quod et ipse servieris in Ægypto, et eduxerit te inde Dominus Deus tuus in manu forti, et brachio extento. Idcirco præcepit tibi ut observares diem sabbati.

verses.text: Honour thy father and mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee, that thou mayst live a long time, and it may be well with thee in the land, which the Lord thy God will give thee.
verses.textLatin: Honora patrem tuum et matrem, sicut præcepit tibi Dominus Deus tuus, ut longo vivas tempore, et bene sit tibi in terra, quam Dominus Deus tuus daturus est tibi.

verses.text: Thou shalt not kill.
verses.textLatin: Non occides,

verses.text: Neither shalt thou commit adultery.
verses.textLatin: neque mœchaberis,

verses.text: And thou shalt not steal.
verses.textLatin: furtumque non facies:

verses.text: Neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour.
verses.textLatin: nec loqueris contra proximum tuum falsum testimonium.

verses.text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife: nor his house, nor his field, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is his.
verses.textLatin: Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui: non domum, non agrum, non servum, non ancillam, non bovem, non asinum, et universa quæ illius sunt.

verses.text: These words the Lord spoke to all the multitude of you in the mountain, out of the midst of the fire and the cloud, and the darkness, with a loud voice, adding nothing more: and he wrote them in two tables of stone, which he delivered unto me.
verses.textLatin: Hæc verba locutus est Dominus ad omnem multitudinem vestram in monte de medio ignis et nubis, et caliginis, voce magna, nihil addens amplius: et scripsit ea in duabus tabulis lapideis, quas tradidit mihi.

verses.text: But you, after you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, and saw the mountain burn, came to me, all the princes of the tribes and the elders, and you said:
verses.textLatin: Vos autem postquam audistis vocem de medio tenebrarum, et montem ardere vidistis, accessistis ad me omnes principes tribuum et majores natu, atque dixistis:

verses.text: Behold the Lord our God hath shewn us his majesty and his greatness, we have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire, and have proved this day that God speaking with man, man hath lived.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ostendit nobis Dominus Deus noster majestatem et magnitudinem suam: vocem ejus audivimus de medio ignis, et probavimus hodie, quod loquente Deo cum homine, vixerit homo.

verses.text: Why shall we die therefore, and why shall this exceeding great fire consume us: for if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, we shall die.
verses.textLatin: Cur ergo moriemur, et devorabit nos ignis hic maximus? si enim audierimus ultra vocem Domini Dei nostri, moriemur.

verses.text: What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God, who speaketh out of the midst of the fire, as we have heard, and be able to live?
verses.textLatin: Quid est omnis caro, ut audiat vocem Dei viventis, qui de medio ignis loquitur sicut nos audivimus, et possit vivere?

verses.text: Approach thou rather: and hear all things that the Lord our God shall say to thee, and thou shalt speak to us, and we will hear and will do them.
verses.textLatin: Tu magis accede: et audi cuncta quæ dixerit Dominus Deus noster tibi: loquerisque ad nos, et nos audientes faciemus ea.

verses.text: And when the Lord had heard this, he said to me: I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they spoke to thee: they have spoken all things well.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audisset Dominus, ait ad me: Audivi vocem verborum populi hujus quæ locuti sunt tibi: bene omnia sunt locuti.

verses.text: Who shall give them to have such a mind, to fear me, and to keep all my commandments at all times, that it may be well with them and with their children for ever?
verses.textLatin: Quis det talem eos habere mentem, ut timeant me, et custodiant universa mandata mea in omni tempore, ut bene sit eis et filiis eorum in sempiternum?

verses.text: Go and say to them: Return into your tents.
verses.textLatin: Vade et dic eis: Revertimini in tentoria vestra.

verses.text: But stand thou here with me, and I will speak to thee all my commandments, and ceremonies and judgments: which thou shalt teach them, that they may do them in the land, which I will give them for a possession.
verses.textLatin: Tu vero hic sta mecum, et loquar tibi omnia mandata mea, et cæremonias atque judicia: quæ docebis eos, ut faciant ea in terra, quam dabo illis in possessionem.

verses.text: Keep therefore and do the things which the Lord God hath commanded you: you shall not go aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left.
verses.textLatin: Custodite igitur et facite quæ præcepit Dominus Deus vobis: non declinabitis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram:

verses.text: But you shall walk in the way that the Lord your God hath commanded, that you may live, and it may be well with you, and your days may be long in the land of your possession.
verses.textLatin: sed per viam, quam præcepit Dominus Deus vester, ambulabitis, ut vivatis, et bene sit vobis, et protelentur dies in terra possessionis vestræ.

verses.text: These  are the precepts, and ceremo- nies, and judgments, which the Lord your God commanded that I should teach you, and that you should do them in the land into which you pass over to possess it:
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt præcepta, et cæremoniæ, atque judicia, quæ mandavit Dominus Deus vester ut docerem vos, et faciatis ea in terra, ad quam transgredimini possidendam:

verses.text: That thou mayst fear the Lord thy God, and keep all his commandments and precepts, which I command thee, and thy sons, and thy grandsons, all the days of thy life, that thy days may be prolonged.
verses.textLatin: ut timeas Dominum Deum tuum, et custodias omnia mandata et præcepta ejus, quæ ego præcipio tibi, et filiis, ac nepotibus tuis, cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ, ut prolongentur dies tui.

verses.text: Hear, O Israel, and observe to do the things which the Lord hath commanded thee, that it may be well with thee, and thou mayst be greatly multiplied, as the Lord the God of thy fathers hath promised thee a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: Audi, Israël, et observa ut facias quæ præcepit tibi Dominus, et bene sit tibi, et multipliceris amplius, sicut pollicitus est Dominus Deus patrum tuorum tibi terram lacte et melle manantem.

verses.text: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord.
verses.textLatin: Audi, Israël: Dominus Deus noster, Dominus unus est.

verses.text: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, and with thy whole soul, and with thy whole strength.
verses.textLatin: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua, et ex tota fortitudine tua.

verses.text: And these words which I command thee this day, shall be in thy heart:
verses.textLatin: Eruntque verba hæc, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, in corde tuo:

verses.text: And thou shalt tell them to thy children, and thou shalt meditate upon them sitting in thy house, and walking on thy journey, sleeping and rising.
verses.textLatin: et narrabis ea filiis tuis, et meditaberis in eis sedens in domo tua, et ambulans in itinere, dormiens atque consurgens.

verses.text: And thou shalt bind them as a sign on thy hand, and they shall be and shall move between thy eyes.
verses.textLatin: Et ligabis ea quasi signum in manu tua, eruntque et movebuntur inter oculos tuos,

verses.text: And thou shalt write them in the entry, and on the doors of thy house.
verses.textLatin: scribesque ea in limine, et ostiis domus tuæ.

verses.text: And when the Lord thy God shall have brought thee into the land, for which he swore to thy fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: and shall have given thee great and goodly cities, which thou didst not build,
verses.textLatin: Cumque introduxerit te Dominus Deus tuus in terram, pro qua juravit patribus tuis Abraham, Isaac, et Jacob, et dederit tibi civitates magnas et optimas, quas non ædificasti,

verses.text: Houses full of riches, which thou didst not set up, cisterns which thou didst not dig, vineyards and oliveyards, which thou didst not plant,
verses.textLatin: domos plenas cunctarum opum, quas non exstruxisti, cisternas, quas non fodisti, vineta et oliveta, quæ non plantasti,

verses.text: And thou shalt have eaten and be full:
verses.textLatin: et comederis, et saturatus fueris:

verses.text: Take heed diligently lest thou forget the Lord, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and shalt serve him only, and thou shalt swear by his name.
verses.textLatin: cave diligenter ne obliviscaris Domini, qui eduxit te de terra Ægypti, de domo servitutis. Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et illi soli servies, ac per nomen illius jurabis.

verses.text: You shall not go after the strange gods of all the nations, that are round about you:
verses.textLatin: Non ibitis post deos alienos cunctarum gentium, quæ in circuitu vestro sunt:

verses.text: Because the Lord thy God is a jealous God in the midst of thee: lest at any time the wrath of the Lord thy God be kindled against thee, and take thee away from the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: quoniam Deus æmulator Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui: nequando irascatur furor Domini Dei tui contra te, et auferat te de superficie terræ.

verses.text: Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God, as thou temptedst him in the place of temptation.
verses.textLatin: Non tentabis Dominum Deum tuum, sicut tentasti in loco tentationis.

verses.text: Keep the precepts of the Lord thy God, and the testimonies and ceremonies which he hath commanded thee.
verses.textLatin: Custodi præcepta Domini Dei tui, ac testimonia et cæremonias, quas præcepit tibi:

verses.text: And do that which is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, that it may be well with thee: and going in thou mayst possess the goodly land, concerning which the Lord swore to thy fathers,
verses.textLatin: et fac quod placitum est et bonum in conspectu Domini, ut bene sit tibi: et ingressus possideas terram optimam, de qua juravit Dominus patribus tuis,

verses.text: That he would destroy all thy enemies before thee, as he hath spoken.
verses.textLatin: ut deleret omnes inimicos tuos coram te, sicut locutus est.

verses.text: And when thy son shall ask thee to morrow, saying: What mean these testimonies, and ceremonies and judgments, which the Lord our God hath commanded us?
verses.textLatin: Cumque interrogaverit te filius tuus cras, dicens: Quid sibi volunt testimonia hæc, et cæremoniæ, atque judicia, quæ præcepit Dominus Deus noster nobis?

verses.text: Thou shalt say to him: We were bondmen of Pharao in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.textLatin: dices ei: Servi eramus Pharaonis in Ægypto, et eduxit nos Dominus de Ægypto in manu forti:

verses.text: And he wrought signs and wonders great and very grievous in Egypt against Pharao, and all his house, in our sight,
verses.textLatin: fecitque signa atque prodigia magna et pessima in Ægypto contra Pharaonem, et omnem domum illius in conspectu nostro,

verses.text: And he brought us out from thence, that he might bring us in and give us the land, concerning which he swore to our fathers.
verses.textLatin: et eduxit nos inde, ut introductis daret terram, super qua juravit patribus nostris.

verses.text: And the Lord commanded that we should do all these ordinances, and should fear the Lord our God, that it might be well with us all the days of our life, as it is at this day.
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque nobis Dominus ut faciamus omnia legitima hæc, et timeamus Dominum Deum nostrum, ut bene sit nobis cunctis diebus vitæ nostræ, sicut est hodie.

verses.text: And he will be merciful to us, if we keep and do all his precepts before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.
