verses.textLatin: et hoc tibi fuerit nuntiatum, audiensque inquisieris diligenter et verum esse repereris, et abominatio facta est in Israël:

verses.text: Thou shalt bring forth the man or the woman, who have committed that most wicked thing, to the gates of thy city, and they shall be stoned.
verses.textLatin: educes virum ac mulierem, qui rem sceleratissimam perpetrarunt, ad portas civitatis tuæ, et lapidibus obruentur.

verses.text: By the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he die that is to be slain. Let no man be put to death, when only one beareth witness against him.
verses.textLatin: In ore duorum aut trium testium peribit qui interficietur. Nemo occidatur, uno contra se dicente testimonium.

verses.text: The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to kill him, and afterwards the hands of the rest of the people: that thou mayst take away the evil out of the midst of thee.
verses.textLatin: Manus testium prima interficiet eum, et manus reliqui populi extrema mittetur: ut auferas malum de medio tui.

verses.text: If thou perceive that there be among you a hard and doubtful matter in judgment between blood and blood, cause and cause, leprosy and leprosy: and thou see that the words of the judges within thy gates do vary: arise, and go up to the place, which the Lord thy God shall choose.
verses.textLatin: Si difficile et ambiguum apud te judicium esse perspexeris inter sanguinem et sanguinem, causam et causam, lepram et lepram: et judicum intra portas tuas videris verba variari: surge, et ascende ad locum, quem elegerit Dominus Deus tuus.

verses.text: And thou shalt come to the priests of the Levitical race, and to the judge, that shall be at that time: and thou shalt ask of them, and they shall shew thee the truth of the judgment.
verses.textLatin: Veniesque ad sacerdotes Levitici generis, et ad judicem qui fuerit illo tempore: quæresque ab eis, qui indicabunt tibi judicii veritatem.

verses.text: And thou shalt do whatsoever they shall say, that preside in the place, which the Lord shall choose, and what they shall teach thee,
verses.textLatin: Et facies quodcumque dixerint qui præsunt loco quem elegerit Dominus, et docuerint te

verses.text: According to his law; and thou shalt follow their sentence: neither shalt thou decline to the right hand nor to the left hand.
verses.textLatin: juxta legem ejus, sequerisque sententiam eorum, nec declinabis ad dexteram neque ad sinistram.

verses.text: But he that will be proud, and refuse to obey the commandment of the priest, who ministereth at that time to the Lord thy God, and the decree of the judge, that man shall die, and thou shalt take away the evil from Israel:
verses.textLatin: Qui autem superbierit, nolens obedire sacerdotis imperio, qui eo tempore ministrat Domino Deo tuo, et decreto judicis, morietur homo ille, et auferes malum de Israël:

verses.text: And all the people hearing it shall fear, that no one afterwards swell with pride.
verses.textLatin: cunctusque populus audiens timebit, ut nullus deinceps intumescat superbia.

verses.text: When thou art come into the land, which the Lord thy God will give thee, and possessest it, and shalt say: I will set a king over me, as all nations have that are round about:
verses.textLatin: Cum ingressus fueris terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi, et possederis eam, habitaverisque in illa, et dixeris: Constituam super me regem, sicut habent omnes per circuitum nationes:

verses.text: Thou shalt set him whom the Lord thy God shall choose out of the number of thy brethren. Thou mayst not make a man of another nation king, that is not thy brother.
verses.textLatin: eum constitues, quem Dominus Deus tuus elegerit de numero fratrum tuorum. Non poteris alterius gentis hominem regem facere, qui non sit frater tuus.

verses.text: And when he is made king, he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor lead back the people into Egypt, being lifted up with the number of his horsemen, especially since the Lord hath commanded you to return no more the same way.
verses.textLatin: Cumque fuerit constitutus, non multiplicabit sibi equos, nec reducet populum in Ægyptum, equitatus numero sublevatus, præsertim cum Dominus præceperit vobis ut nequaquam amplius per eamdem viam revertamini.

verses.text: He shall not have many wives, that may allure his mind, nor immense sums of silver and gold.
verses.textLatin: Non habebit uxores plurimas, quæ alliciant animum ejus, neque argenti et auri immensa pondera.

verses.text: But after he is raised to the throne of his kingdom, he shall copy out to himself the Deuteronomy of this law in a volume, taking the copy of the priests of the Levitical tribe,
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem sederit in solio regni sui, describet sibi Deuteronomium legis hujus in volumine, accipiens exemplar a sacerdotibus Leviticæ tribus,

verses.text: And he shall have it with him, and shall read it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, and keep his words and ceremonies, that are commanded in the law;
verses.textLatin: et habebit secum, legetque illud omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, ut discat timere Dominum Deum suum, et custodire verba et cæremonias ejus, quæ in lege præcepta sunt.

verses.text: And that his heart be not lifted up with pride over his brethren, nor decline to the right or to the left, that he and his sons may reign a long time over Israel.
verses.textLatin: Nec elevetur cor ejus in superbiam super fratres suos, neque declinet in partem dexteram vel sinistram, ut longo tempore regnet ipse et filii ejus super Israël.

verses.text: The  priests and Levites, and all that are of the same tribe, shall have no part nor inheritance with the rest of Israel, because they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord, and his oblations,
verses.textLatin: Non habebunt sacerdotes et Levitæ, et omnes qui de eadem tribu sunt, partem et hæreditatem cum reliquo Israël, quia sacrificia Domini, et oblationes ejus comedent,

verses.text: And they shall receive nothing else of the possession of their brethren: for the Lord himself is their inheritance, as he hath said to them.
verses.textLatin: et nihil aliud accipient de possessione fratrum suorum: Dominus enim ipse est hæreditas eorum, sicut locutus est illis.

verses.text: This shall be the priest’s due from the people, and from them that offer victims: whether they sacrifice an ox, or a sheep, they shall give to the priest the shoulder and the breast:
verses.textLatin: Hoc erit judicium sacerdotum a populo, et ab his qui offerunt victimas: sive bovem, sive ovem immolaverint, dabunt sacerdoti armum ac ventriculum:

verses.text: The firstfruits also of corn, of wine, and of oil, and a part of the wool from the shearing of their sheep.
verses.textLatin: primitias frumenti, vini, et olei, et lanarum partem ex ovium tonsione.

verses.text: For the Lord thy God hath chosen him of all thy tribes, to stand and to minister to the name of the Lord, him and his sons for ever.
verses.textLatin: Ipsum enim elegit Dominus Deus tuus de cunctis tribubus tuis, ut stet, et ministret nomini Domini, ipse, et filii ejus in sempiternum.

verses.text: If a Levite go out of any one of the cities throughout all Israel, in which he dwelleth, and have a longing mind to come to the place which the Lord shall choose,
verses.textLatin: Si exierit Levites ex una urbium tuarum ex omni Israël in qua habitat, et voluerit venire, desiderans locum quem elegerit Dominus,

verses.text: He shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, as all his brethren the Levites do, that shall stand at that time before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ministrabit in nomine Domini Dei sui, sicut omnes fratres ejus Levitæ, qui stabunt eo tempore coram Domino.

verses.text: He shall receive the same portion of food that the rest do: besides that which is due to him in his own city, by succession from his fathers.
verses.textLatin: Partem ciborum eamdem accipiet, quam et ceteri: excepto eo, quod in urbe sua ex paterna ei successione debetur.

verses.text: When thou art come into the land which the Lord thy God shall give thee, beware lest thou have a mind to imitate the abominations of those nations.
verses.textLatin: Quando ingressus fueris terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi, cave ne imitari velis abominationes illarum gentium.

verses.text: Neither let there be found among you any one that shall expiate his son or daughter, making them to pass through the fire: or that consulteth soothsayers, or observeth dreams and omens, neither let there be any wizard,
verses.textLatin: Nec inveniatur in te qui lustret filium suum, aut filiam, ducens per ignem: aut qui ariolos sciscitetur, et observet somnia atque auguria, nec sit maleficus,

verses.text: Nor charmer, nor any one that consulteth pythonic spirits, or fortune tellers, or that seeketh the truth from the dead.
verses.textLatin: nec incantator, nec qui pythones consulat, nec divinos, aut quærat a mortuis veritatem.

verses.text: For the Lord abhorreth all these things, and for these abominations he will destroy them at thy coming.
verses.textLatin: Omnia enim hæc abominatur Dominus, et propter istiusmodi scelera delebit eos in introitu tuo.

verses.text: Thou shalt be perfect, and without spot before the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Perfectus eris, et absque macula cum Domino Deo tuo.

verses.text: These nations, whose land thou shalt possess, hearken to soothsayers and diviners: but thou art otherwise instructed by the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Gentes istæ, quarum possidebis terram, augures et divinos audiunt: tu autem a Domino Deo tuo aliter institutus es.

verses.text: The Lord thy God will raise up to thee a PROPHET of thy nation and of thy brethren like unto me: him thou shalt hear:
verses.textLatin: Prophetam de gente tua et de fratribus tuis, sicut me, suscitabit tibi Dominus Deus tuus: ipsum audies,

verses.text: As thou desiredst of the Lord thy God in Horeb, when the assembly was gathered together, and saidst: Let me not hear any more the voice of the Lord my God, neither let me see any more this exceeding great fire, lest I die.
verses.textLatin: ut petisti a Domino Deo tuo in Horeb, quando concio congregata est, atque dixisti: Ultra non audiam vocem Domini Dei mei, et ignem hunc maximum amplius non videbo, ne moriar.

verses.text: And the Lord said to me: They have spoken all things well.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Dominus mihi: Bene omnia sunt locuti.

verses.text: I will raise them up a prophet out of the midst of their brethren like to thee: and I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all that I shall command him.
verses.textLatin: Prophetam suscitabo eis de medio fratrum suorum similem tui: et ponam verba mea in ore ejus, loqueturque ad eos omnia quæ præcepero illi.

verses.text: And he that will not hear his words, which he shall speak in my name, I will be the revenger.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem verba ejus, quæ loquetur in nomine meo, audire noluerit, ego ultor existam.

verses.text: But the prophet, who being corrupted with pride, shall speak in my name things that I did not command him to say, or in the name of strange gods, shall be slain.
verses.textLatin: Propheta autem qui arrogantia depravatus voluerit loqui in nomine meo, quæ ego non præcepi illi ut diceret, aut ex nomine alienorum deorum, interficietur.

verses.text: And if in silent thought thou answer: How shall I know the word that the Lord hath not spoken?
verses.textLatin: Quod si tacita cogitatione responderis: Quomodo possum intelligere verbum, quod Dominus non est locutus?

verses.text: Thou shalt have this sign: Whatsoever that same prophet foretelleth in the name of the Lord, and it cometh not to pass: that thing the Lord hath not spoken, but the prophet hath forged it by the pride of his mind: and therefore thou shalt not fear him.
verses.textLatin: hoc habebis signum: quod in nomine Domini propheta ille prædixerit, et non evenerit: hoc Dominus non est locutus, sed per tumorem animi sui propheta confinxit: et idcirco non timebis eum.

verses.text: When  the Lord thy God hath de stroyed the nations, whose land he will deliver to thee, and thou shalt possess it, and shalt dwell in the cities and houses thereof:
verses.textLatin: Cum disperdiderit Dominus Deus tuus gentes, quarum tibi traditurus est terram, et possederis eam, habitaverisque in urbibus ejus et in ædibus:

verses.text: Thou shalt separate to thee three cities in the midst of the land, which the Lord will give thee in possession,
verses.textLatin: tres civitates separabis tibi in medio terræ, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi in possessionem,

verses.text: Paving diligently the way: and thou shalt divide the whole province of thy land equally into three parts: that he who is forced to flee for manslaughter, may have near at hand whither to escape.
verses.textLatin: sternens diligenter viam: et in tres æqualiter partes totam terræ tuæ provinciam divides: ut habeat e vicino qui propter homicidium profugus est, quo possit evadere.

verses.text: This shall be the law of the slayer that fleeth, whose life is to be saved: He that killeth his neighbor ignorantly, and who is proved to have had no hatred against him yesterday and the day before:
verses.textLatin: Hæc erit lex homicidæ fugientis, cujus vita servanda est: qui percusserit proximum suum nesciens, et qui heri et nudiustertius nullum contra eum odium habuisse comprobatur:

verses.text: But to have gone with him to the wood to hew wood, and in cutting down the tree the axe slipped out of his hand, and the iron slipping from the handle struck his friend, and killed him: he shall flee to one of the cities aforesaid, and live:
verses.textLatin: sed abiisse cum eo simpliciter in silvam ad ligna cædenda, et in succisione lignorum securis fugerit manu, ferrumque lapsum de manubrio amicum ejus percusserit, et occiderit: hic ad unam supradictarum urbium confugiet, et vivet:

verses.text: Lest perhaps the next kinsman of him whose blood was shed, pushed on by his grief should pursue, and apprehend him, if the way be too long, and take away the life of him who is not guilty of death, because he is proved to have had no hatred before against him that was slain.
verses.textLatin: ne forsitan proximus ejus, cujus effusus est sanguis, dolore stimulatus, persequatur, et apprehendat eum si longior via fuerit, et percutiat animam ejus, qui non est reus mortis: quia nullum contra eum, qui occisus est, odium prius habuisse monstratur.

verses.text: Therefore I command thee, that thou separate three cities at equal distance one from another.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco præcipio tibi, ut tres civitates æqualis inter se spatii dividas.

verses.text: And when the Lord thy God shall have enlarged thy borders, as he swore to the fathers, and shall give thee all the land that he promised them,
verses.textLatin: Cum autem dilataverit Dominus Deus tuus terminos tuos, sicut juravit patribus tuis, et dederit tibi cunctam terram, quam eis pollicitus est

verses.text: (Yet so, if thou keep his commandments, and do the things which I command thee this day, that thou love the Lord thy God, and walk in his ways at all times) thou shalt add to thee other three cities, and shalt double the number of the three cities aforesaid:
verses.textLatin: (si tamen custodieris mandata ejus, et feceris, quæ hodie præcipio tibi, ut diligas Dominum Deum tuum, et ambules in viis ejus omni tempore), addes tibi tres alias civitates, et supradictarum trium urbium numerum duplicabis:

verses.text: That innocent blood may not be shed in the midst of the land which the Lord thy God will give thee to possess, lest thou be guilty of blood.
verses.textLatin: ut non effundatur sanguis innoxius in medio terræ, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi possidendam, ne sis sanguinis reus.

verses.text: But if any man hating his neighbour, lie in wait for his life, and rise and strike him, and he die, and he flee to one of the cities aforesaid,
verses.textLatin: Si quis autem, odio habens proximum suum, insidiatus fuerit vitæ ejus, surgensque percusserit illum, et mortuus fuerit, fugeritque ad unam de supradictis urbibus,

verses.text: The ancients of his city shall send, and take him out of the place of refuge, and shall deliver him into the hand of the kinsman of him whose blood was shed, and he shall die.
verses.textLatin: mittent seniores civitatis illius, et arripient eum de loco effugii, tradentque in manu proximi, cujus sanguis effusus est, et morietur.

verses.text: Thou shalt not pity him, and thou shalt take away the guilt of innocent blood out of Israel, that it may be well with thee.
verses.textLatin: Non miseraberis ejus, et auferes innoxium sanguinem de Israël, ut bene sit tibi.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take nor remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which thy predecessors have set in thy possession, which the Lord thy God will give thee in the land that thou shalt receive to possess.
verses.textLatin: Non assumes, et transferes terminos proximi tui, quos fixerunt priores in possessione tua, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi in terra quam acceperis possidendam.

verses.text: One witness shall not rise up against any man, whatsoever the sin or wickedness be: but in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall stand.
verses.textLatin: Non stabit testis unus contra aliquem, quidquid illud peccati, et facinoris fuerit: sed in ore duorum aut trium testium stabit omne verbum.

verses.text: If a lying witness stand against a man, accusing him of transgression,
verses.textLatin: Si steterit testis mendax contra hominem, accusans eum prævaricationis,

verses.text: Both of them, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord in the sight of the priests and the judges that shall be in those days.
verses.textLatin: stabunt ambo, quorum causa est, ante Dominum in conspectu sacerdotum et judicum qui fuerint in diebus illis.

verses.text: And when after most diligent inquisition, they shall find that the false witness hath told a lie against his brother:
verses.textLatin: Cumque diligentissime perscrutantes, invenerint falsum testem dixisse contra fratrem suum mendacium,

verses.text: They shall render to him as he meant to do to his brother, and thou shalt take away the evil out of the midst of thee:
verses.textLatin: reddent ei sicut fratri suo facere cogitavit, et auferes malum de medio tui:

verses.text: That others hearing may fear, and may not dare to do such things.
verses.textLatin: ut audientes ceteri timorem habeant, et nequaquam talia audeant facere.

verses.text: Thou shalt not pity him, but shalt require life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
verses.textLatin: Non misereberis ejus, sed animam pro anima, oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente, manum pro manu, pedem pro pede exiges.

verses.text: If  thou go out to war against thy enemies, and see horsemen and chariots, and the numbers of the enemy’s army greater than thine, thou shalt not fear them: because the Lord thy God is with thee, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Si exieris ad bellum contra hostes tuos, et videris equitatus et currus, et majorem quam tu habeas adversarii exercitus multitudinem, non timebis eos: quia Dominus Deus tuus tecum est, qui eduxit te de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And when the battle is now at hand, the priest shall stand before the army, and shall speak to the people in this manner:
verses.textLatin: Appropinquante autem jam prælio, stabit sacerdos ante aciem, et sic loquetur ad populum:

verses.text: Hear, O Israel, you join battle this day against your enemies, let not your heart be dismayed, be not afraid, do not give back, fear ye them not:
verses.textLatin: Audi, Israël: vos hodie contra inimicos vestros pugnam committitis: non pertimescat cor vestrum, nolite metuere, nolite cedere, nec formidetis eos:

verses.text: Because the Lord your God is in the midst of you, and will fight for you against your enemies, to deliver you from danger.
verses.textLatin: quia Dominus Deus vester in medio vestri est, et pro vobis contra adversarios dimicabit, ut eruat vos de periculo.

verses.text: And the captains shall proclaim through every band in the hearing of the army: What man is there, that hath built a new house, and hath not dedicated it? let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man dedicate it.
verses.textLatin: Duces quoque per singulas turmas audiente exercitu proclamabunt: Quis est homo qui ædificavit domum novam, et non dedicavit eam? vadat, et revertatur in domum suam, ne forte moriatur in bello, et alius dedicet eam.

verses.text: What man is there, that hath planted a vineyard, and hath not as yet made it to be common, whereof all men may eat? let him go, and return to his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man execute his office.
verses.textLatin: Quis est homo qui plantavit vineam, et necdum fecit eam esse communem, de qua vesci omnibus liceat? vadat, et revertatur in domum suam, ne forte moriatur in bello, et alius homo ejus fungatur officio.

verses.text: What man is there, that hath espoused a wife, and not taken her? let him go, and return to his house, lest he die in the war, and another man take her.
verses.textLatin: Quis est homo, qui despondit uxorem, et non accepit eam? vadat, et revertatur in domum suam, ne forte moriatur in bello, et alius homo accipiat eam.

verses.text: After these things are declared they shall add the rest, and shall speak to the people: What man is there that is fearful, and faint hearted? let him go, and return to his house, lest he make the hearts of his brethren to fear, as he himself is possessed with fear.
verses.textLatin: His dictis addent reliqua, et loquentur ad populum: Quis est homo formidolosus, et corde pavido? vadat, et revertatur in domum suam, ne pavere faciat corda fratrum suorum, sicut ipse timore perterritus est.

verses.text: And when the captains of the army shall hold their peace, and have made an end of speaking, every man shall prepare their bands to fight.
verses.textLatin: Cumque siluerint duces exercitus, et finem loquendi fecerint, unusquisque suos ad bellandum cuneos præparabit.

verses.text: If at any time thou come to fight against a city, thou shalt first offer it peace.
verses.textLatin: Siquando accesseris ad expugnandam civitatem, offeres ei primum pacem.

verses.text: If they receive it, and open the gates to thee, all the people that are therein, shall be saved, and shall serve thee paying tribute.
verses.textLatin: Si receperit, et aperuerit tibi portas, cunctus populus, qui in ea est, salvabitur, et serviet tibi sub tributo.

verses.text: But if they will not make peace, and shall begin war against thee, thou shalt besiege it.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem fœdus inire noluerit, et cœperit contra te bellum, oppugnabis eam.

verses.text: And when the Lord thy God shall deliver it into thy hands, thou shalt slay all that are therein of the male sex, with the edge of the sword,
verses.textLatin: Cumque tradiderit Dominus Deus tuus illam in manu tua, percuties omne quod in ea generis masculini est, in ore gladii,

verses.text: Excepting women and children, cattle and other things, that are in the city. And thou shalt divide all the prey to the army, and thou shalt eat the spoils of thy enemies, which the Lord thy God shall give thee.
verses.textLatin: absque mulieribus et infantibus, jumentis et ceteris quæ in civitate sunt. Omnem prædam exercitui divides, et comedes de spoliis hostium tuorum, quæ Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi.

verses.text: So shalt thou do to all cities that are at a great distance from thee, and are not of these cities which thou shalt receive in possession.
verses.textLatin: Sic facies cunctis civitatibus, quæ a te procul valde sunt, et non sunt de his urbibus, quas in possessionem accepturus es.

verses.text: But of those cities that shall be given thee, thou shalt suffer none at all to live:
verses.textLatin: De his autem civitatibus, quæ dabuntur tibi, nullum omnino permittes vivere:

verses.text: But shalt kill them with the edge of the sword, to wit, the Hethite, and the Amorrhite, and the Chanaanite, the Pherezite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee:
verses.textLatin: sed interficies in ore gladii, Hethæum videlicet, et Amorrhæum, et Chananæum, Pherezæum, et Hevæum, et Jebusæum, sicut præcepit tibi Dominus Deus tuus:

verses.text: Lest they teach you to do all the abominations which they have done to their gods: and you should sin against the Lord your God.
verses.textLatin: ne forte doceant vos facere cunctas abominationes, quas ipsi operati sunt diis suis, et peccetis in Dominum Deum vestrum.

verses.text: When thou hast besieged a city a long time, and hath compassed it with bulwarks to take it, thou shalt not cut down the trees that may be eaten of, neither shalt thou spoil the country round about with axes: for it is a tree, and not a man, neither can it increase the number of them that fight against thee.
verses.textLatin: Quando obsederis civitatem multo tempore, et munitionibus circumdederis ut expugnes eam, non succides arbores, de quibus vesci potest, nec securibus per circuitum debes vastare regionem: quoniam lignum est, et non homo, nec potest bellantium contra te augere numerum.

verses.text: But if there be any trees that are not fruitful, but wild, and fit for other uses, cut them down, and make engines, until thou take the city, which fighteth against thee.
verses.textLatin: Si qua autem ligna non sunt pomifera, sed agrestia, et in ceteros apta usus, succide, et instrue machinas, donec capias civitatem, quæ contra te dimicat.

verses.text: When  there shall be found in the land, which the Lord thy God will give thee, the corpse of a man slain, and it is not known who is guilty of the murder,
verses.textLatin: Quando inventum fuerit in terra, quam Dominus Deus tuus daturus est tibi, hominis cadaver occisi, et ignorabitur cædis reus,

verses.text: Thy ancients and judges shall go out, and shall measure from the place where the body lieth the distance of every city round about:
verses.textLatin: egredientur majores natu, et judices tui, et metientur a loco cadaveris singularum per circuitum spatia civitatum:

verses.text: And the ancients of that city which they shall perceive to be nearer than the rest, shall take a heifer of the herd, that hath not drawn in the yoke, nor ploughed the ground,
verses.textLatin: et quam viciniorem ceteris esse perspexerint, seniores civitatis illius tollent vitulam de armento, quæ non traxit jugum, nec terram scidit vomere,

verses.text: And they shall bring her into a rough and stony valley, that never was ploughed, nor sown: and there they shall strike off the head of the heifer:
verses.textLatin: et ducent eam ad vallem asperam atque saxosam, quæ numquam arata est, nec sementem recepit: et cædent in ea cervices vitulæ:

verses.text: And the priests the sons of Levi shall come, whom the Lord thy God hath chosen to minister to him, and to bless in his name, and that by their word every matter should be decided, and whatsoever is clean or unclean should be judged.
verses.textLatin: accedentque sacerdotes filii Levi, quos elegerit Dominus Deus tuus ut ministrent ei, et benedicant in nomine ejus, et ad verbum eorum omne negotium, et quidquid mundum, vel immundum est, judicetur.

verses.text: And the ancients of that city shall come to the person slain, and shall wash their hands over the heifer that was killed in the valley,
verses.textLatin: Et venient majores natu civitatis illius ad interfectum, lavabuntque manus suas super vitulam, quæ in valle percussa est,

verses.text: And shall say: Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it.
verses.textLatin: et dicent: Manus nostræ non effuderunt sanguinem hunc, nec oculi viderunt:

verses.text: Be merciful to thy people Israel, whom thou hast redeemed, O Lord, and lay not innocent blood to their charge, in the midst of thy people Israel. And the guilt of blood shall be taken from them:
verses.textLatin: propitius esto populo tuo Israël, quem redemisti, Domine, et ne reputes sanguinem innocentem in medio populi tui Israël. Et auferetur ab eis reatus sanguinis:

verses.text: And thou shalt be free from the innocent’s blood, that was shed, when thou shalt have done what the Lord hath commanded thee.
verses.textLatin: tu autem alienus eris ab innocentis cruore, qui fusus est, cum feceris quod præcepit Dominus.

verses.text: If thou go out to fight against thy enemies, and the Lord thy God deliver them into thy hand, and thou lead them away captives,
verses.textLatin: Si egressus fueris ad pugnam contra inimicos tuos, et tradiderit eos Dominus Deus tuus in manu tua, captivosque duxeris,

verses.text: And seest in the number of the captives a beautiful woman, and lovest her, and wilt have her to wife,
verses.textLatin: et videris in numero captivorum mulierem pulchram, et adamaveris eam, voluerisque habere uxorem,

verses.text: Thou shalt bring her into thy house: and she shall shave her hair, and pare her nails,
verses.textLatin: introduces eam in domum tuam: quæ radet cæsariem, et circumcidet ungues,

verses.text: And shall put off the raiment, wherein she was taken: and shall remain in thy house, and mourn for her father and mother one month: and after that thou shalt go in unto her, and shalt sleep with her, and she shall be thy wife.
verses.textLatin: et deponet vestem, in qua capta est: sedensque in domo tua, flebit patrem et matrem suam uno mense: et postea intrabis ad eam, dormiesque cum illa, et erit uxor tua.

verses.text: But if afterwards she please thee not, thou shalt let her go free, but thou mayst not sell her for money nor oppress her by might because thou hast humbled her.
verses.textLatin: Si autem postea non sederit animo tuo, dimittes eam liberam, nec vendere poteris pecunia, nec opprimere per potentiam: quia humiliasti eam.

verses.text: If a man have two wives, one beloved, and the other hated, and they have had children by him, and the son of the hated be the firstborn,
verses.textLatin: Si habuerit homo uxores duas, unam dilectam, et alteram odiosam, genuerintque ex eo liberos, et fuerit filius odiosæ primogenitus,

verses.text: And he meaneth to divide his substance among his sons: he may not make the son of the beloved the firstborn, and prefer him before the son of the hated.
verses.textLatin: volueritque substantiam inter filios suos dividere, non poterit filium dilectæ facere primogenitum, et præferre filio odiosæ:

verses.text: But he shall acknowledge the son of the hated for the firstborn, and shall give him a double portion of all he hath: for this is the first of his children, and to him are due the first birthrights.
verses.textLatin: sed filium odiosæ agnoscet primogenitum, dabitque ei de his quæ habuerit cuncta duplicia: iste est enim principium liberorum ejus, et huic debentur primogenita.

verses.text: If a man have a stubborn and unruly son, who will not hear the commandments of his father or mother, and being corrected, slighteth obedience:
verses.textLatin: Si genuerit homo filium contumacem et protervum, qui non audiat patris aut matris imperium, et coërcitus obedire contempserit:

verses.text: They shall take him and bring him to the ancients of the city, and to the gate of judgment,
verses.textLatin: apprehendent eum, et ducent ad seniores civitatis illius, et ad portam judicii,

verses.text: And shall say to them: This our son is rebellious and stubborn, he slighteth hearing our admonitions, he giveth himself to revelling, and to debauchery and banquetings:
verses.textLatin: dicentque ad eos: Filius noster iste protervus et contumax est: monita nostra audire contemnit, comessationibus vacat, et luxuriæ atque conviviis:

verses.text: The people of the city shall stone him: and he shall die, that you may take away the evil out of the midst of you, and all Israel hearing it may be afraid.
verses.textLatin: lapidibus eum obruet populus civitatis, et morietur, ut auferatis malum de medio vestri, et universus Israël audiens pertimescat.

verses.text: When a man hath committed a crime for which he is to be punished with death, and being condemned to die is hanged on a gibbet:
verses.textLatin: Quando peccaverit homo quod morte plectendum est, et adjudicatus morti appensus fuerit in patibulo:

verses.text: His body shall not remain upon the tree, but shall be buried the same day: for he is accursed of God that hangeth on a tree: and thou shalt not defile thy land, which the Lord thy God shall give thee in possession.
verses.textLatin: non permanebit cadaver ejus in ligno, sed in eadem die sepelietur: quia maledictus a Deo est qui pendet in ligno: et nequaquam contaminabis terram tuam, quam Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi in possessionem.

verses.text: Thou  shalt not pass by if thou seest thy brother’s ox, or his sheep go astray: but thou shalt bring them back to thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Non videbis bovem fratris tui, aut ovem errantem, et præteribis: sed reduces fratri tuo,

verses.text: And if thy brother be not nigh, or thou know him not: thou shalt bring them to thy house, and they shall be with thee until thy brother seek them, and receive them.
verses.textLatin: etiamsi non est propinquus frater tuus, nec nosti eum: duces in domum tuam, et erunt apud te quamdiu quærat ea frater tuus, et recipiat.

verses.text: Thou shalt do in like manner with his ass, and with his raiment, and with every thing that is thy brother’s, which is lost: if thou find it, neglect it not as pertaining to another.
verses.textLatin: Similiter facies de asino, et de vestimento, et de omni re fratris tui, quæ perierit: si inveneris eam, ne negligas quasi alienam.

verses.text: If thou see thy brother’s ass or his ox to be fallen down in the way, thou shalt not slight it, but shalt lift it up with him.
verses.textLatin: Si videris asinum fratris tui aut bovem cecidisse in via, non despicies, sed sublevabis cum eo.

verses.text: A woman shall not be clothed with man’s apparel, neither shall a man use woman’s apparel: for he that doeth these things is abominable before God.
verses.textLatin: Non induetur mulier veste virili, nec vir utetur veste feminea: abominabilis enim apud Deum est qui facit hæc.

verses.text: If thou find as thou walkest by the way, a bird’s nest in a tree, or on the ground, and the dam sitting upon the young or upon the eggs: thou shalt not take her with her young:
verses.textLatin: Si ambulans per viam, in arbore vel in terra nidum avis inveneris, et matrem pullis vel ovis desuper incubantem: non tenebis eam cum filiis,

verses.text: But shalt let her go, keeping the young which thou hast caught: that it may be well with thee, and thou mayst live a long time.
verses.textLatin: sed abire patieris, captos tenens filios: ut bene sit tibi, et longo vivas tempore.

verses.text: When thou buildest a new house, thou shalt make a battlement to the roof round about: lest blood be shed in thy house, and thou be guilty, if any one slip, and fall down headlong.
verses.textLatin: Cum ædificaveris domum novam, facies murum tecti per circuitum: ne effundatur sanguis in domo tua, et sis reus labente alio, et in præceps ruente.

verses.text: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest both the seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of the vineyard, be sanctified together.
verses.textLatin: Non seres vineam tuam altero semine: ne et sementis quam sevisti, et quæ nascuntur ex vinea, pariter sanctificentur.

verses.text: Thou shalt not plough with an ox and an ass together.
verses.textLatin: Non arabis in bove simul et asino.

verses.text: Thou shalt not wear a garment that is woven of woollen and linen together.
verses.textLatin: Non indueris vestimento, quod ex lana linoque contextum est.

verses.text: Thou shalt make strings in the hem at the four corners of thy cloak, wherewith thou shalt be covered.
verses.textLatin: Funiculos in fimbriis facies per quatuor angulos pallii tui, quo operieris.

verses.text: If a man marry a wife, and afterwards hate her,
verses.textLatin: Si duxerit vir uxorem, et postea odio habuerit eam,

verses.text: And seek occasions to put her away, laying to her charge a very ill name, and say: I took this woman to wife, and going in to her, I found her not a virgin:
verses.textLatin: quæsieritque occasiones quibus dimittat eam, objiciens ei nomen pessimum, et dixerit: Uxorem hanc accepi, et ingressus ad eam non inveni virginem:

verses.text: Her father and mother shall take her, and shall bring with them the tokens of her virginity to the ancients of the city that are in the gate:
verses.textLatin: tollent eam pater et mater ejus, et ferent secum signa virginitatis ejus ad seniores urbis qui in porta sunt:

verses.text: And the father shall say: I gave my daughter unto this man to wife: and because he hateth her,
verses.textLatin: et dicet pater: Filiam meam dedi huic uxorem: quam quia odit,

verses.text: He layeth to her charge a very ill name, so as to say: I found not thy daughter a virgin: and behold these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall spread the cloth before the ancients of the city:
verses.textLatin: imponit ei nomen pessimum, ut dicat: Non inveni filiam tuam virginem: et ecce hæc sunt signa virginitatis filiæ meæ. Expandent vestimentum coram senioribus civitatis:

verses.text: And the ancients of that city shall take that man, and beat him,
verses.textLatin: apprehendentque senes urbis illius virum, et verberabunt illum,

verses.text: Condemning him besides in a hundred sicles of silver, which he shall give to the damsel’s father, because he hath defamed by a very ill name a virgin of Israel: and he shall have her to wife, and may not put her away all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: condemnantes insuper centum siclis argenti, quos dabit patri puellæ, quoniam diffamavit nomen pessimum super virginem Israël: habebitque eam uxorem, et non poterit dimittere eam omnibus diebus vitæ suæ.

verses.text: But if what he charged her with be true, and virginity be not found in the damsel:
verses.textLatin: Quod si verum est quod objicit, et non est in puella inventa virginitas,

verses.text: They shall cast her out of the doors of her father’s house, and the men of the city shall stone her to death, and she shall die: because she hath done a wicked thing in Israel, to play the whore in her father’s house: and thou shalt take away the evil out of the midst of thee.
verses.textLatin: ejicient eam extra fores domus patris sui, et lapidibus obruent viri civitatis illius, et morietur: quoniam fecit nefas in Israël, ut fornicaretur in domo patris sui: et auferes malum de medio tui.

verses.text: If a man lie with another man’s wife, they shall both die, that is to say, the adulterer and the adulteress: and thou shalt take away the evil out of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Si dormierit vir cum uxore alterius, uterque morietur, id est, adulter et adultera: et auferes malum de Israël.

verses.text: If a man have espoused a damsel that is a virgin, and some one find her in the city, and lie with her,
verses.textLatin: Si puellam virginem desponderit vir, et invenerit eam aliquis in civitate, et concubuerit cum ea,

verses.text: Thou shalt bring them both out to the gate of that city, and they shall be stoned: the damsel, because she cried not out, being in the city: the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour’s wife. And thou shalt take away the evil from the midst of thee.
verses.textLatin: educes utrumque ad portam civitatis illius, et lapidibus obruentur: puella, quia non clamavit, cum esset in civitate: vir, quia humiliavit uxorem proximi sui: et auferes malum de medio tui.

verses.text: But if a man find a damsel that is betrothed, in the field, and taking hold of her, lie with her, he alone shall die:
verses.textLatin: Sin autem in agro repererit vir puellam, quæ desponsata est, et apprehendens concubuerit cum ea, ipse morietur solus:

verses.text: The damsel shall suffer nothing, neither is she guilty of death: for as a robber riseth against his brother, and taketh away his life, so also did the damsel suffer:
verses.textLatin: puella nihil patietur, nec est rea mortis: quoniam sicut latro consurgit contra fratrem suum, et occidit animam ejus, ita et puella perpessa est.

verses.text: She was alone in the field: she cried, and there was no man to help her.
verses.textLatin: Sola erat in agro: clamavit, et nullus affuit qui liberaret eam.

verses.text: If a man find a damsel that is a virgin, who is not espoused, and taking her, lie with her, and the matter come to judgment:
verses.textLatin: Si invenerit vir puellam virginem, quæ non habet sponsum, et apprehendens concubuerit cum illa, et res ad judicium venerit:

verses.text: He that lay with her shall give to the father of the maid fifty sicles of silver, and shall have her to wife, because he hath humbled her: he may not put her away all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: dabit qui dormivit cum ea, patri puellæ quinquaginta siclos argenti, et habebit eam uxorem, quia humiliavit illam: non poterit dimittere eam cunctis diebus vitæ suæ.

verses.text: No man shall take his father’s wife, nor remove his covering.
verses.textLatin: Non accipiet homo uxorem patris sui, nec revelabit operimentum ejus.

verses.text: An  eunuch, whose testicles are broken or cut away, or yard cut off, shall not enter into the church of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non intravit eunuchus, attritis vel amputatis testiculis et abscisso veretro, ecclesiam Domini.

verses.text: A mamzer, that is to say, one born of a prostitute, shall not enter into the church of the Lord, until the tenth generation.
verses.textLatin: Non ingredietur mamzer, hoc est, de scorto natus, in ecclesiam Domini, usque ad decimam generationem.

verses.text: The Ammonite and the Moabite, even after the tenth generation shall not enter into the church of the Lord for ever:
verses.textLatin: Ammonites et Moabites etiam post decimam generationem non intrabunt ecclesiam Domini in æternum:

verses.text: Because they would not meet you with bread and water in the way, when you came out of Egypt: and because they hired against thee Balaam, the son of Beor, from Mesopotamia in Syria, to curse thee.
verses.textLatin: quia noluerunt vobis occurrere cum pane et aqua in via quando egressi estis de Ægypto: et quia conduxerunt contra te Balaam filium Beor de Mesopotamia Syriæ, ut malediceret tibi:

verses.text: And the Lord thy God would not hear Balaam, and he turned his cursing into thy blessing, because he loved thee.
verses.textLatin: et noluit Dominus Deus tuus audire Balaam, vertitque maledictionem ejus in benedictionem tuam, eo quod diligeret te.

verses.text: Thou shalt not make peace with them, neither shalt thou seek their prosperity all the days of thy life for ever.
verses.textLatin: Non facies cum eis pacem, nec quæras eis bona cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ in sempiternum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not abhor the Edomite, because he is thy brother: nor the Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land.
verses.textLatin: Non abominaberis Idumæum, quia frater tuus est: nec Ægyptium, quia advena fuisti in terra ejus.

verses.text: They that are born of them, in the third generation shall enter into the church of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui nati fuerint ex eis, tertia generatione intrabunt in ecclesiam Domini.

verses.text: When thou goest out to war against thy enemies, thou shalt keep thyself from every evil thing.
verses.textLatin: Quando egressus fueris adversus hostes tuos in pugnam, custodies te ab omni re mala.

verses.text: If there be among you any man, that is defiled in a dream by night, he shall go forth out of the camp.
verses.textLatin: Si fuerit inter vos homo, qui nocturno pollutus sit somnio, egredietur extra castra,

verses.text: And shall not return, before he be washed with water in the evening: and after sunset he shall return into the camp.
verses.textLatin: et non revertetur, priusquam ad vesperam lavetur aqua: et post solis occasum regredietur in castra.

verses.text: Thou shalt have a place without the camp, to which thou mayst go for the necessities of nature,
verses.textLatin: Habebis locum extra castra, ad quem egrediaris ad requisita naturæ,

verses.text: Carrying a paddle at thy girdle. And when thou sittest down, thou shalt dig round about, and with the earth that is dug up thou shalt cover
verses.textLatin: gerens paxillum in balteo: cumque sederis, fodies per circuitum, et egesta humo operies

verses.text: That which thou art eased of: (for the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee, and to give up thy enemies to thee:) and let thy camp be holy, and let no uncleanness appear therein, lest he go away from thee.
verses.textLatin: quo revelatus es: Dominus enim Deus tuus ambulat in medio castrorum, ut eruat te, et tradat tibi inimicos tuos: et sint castra tua sancta, et nihil in eis appareat fœditatis, ne derelinquat te.

verses.text: Thou shalt not deliver to his master the servant that is fled to thee.
verses.textLatin: Non trades servum domino suo, qui ad te confugerit.

verses.text: He shall dwell with thee in the place that shall please him, and shall rest in one of thy cities: give him no trouble.
verses.textLatin: Habitabit tecum in loco, qui ei placuerit, et in una urbium tuarum requiescet: ne contristes eum.

verses.text: There shall be no whore among the daughters of Israel, nor whoremonger among the sons of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Non erit meretrix de filiabus Israël, nec scortator de filiis Israël.

verses.text: Thou shalt not offer the hire of a strumpet, nor the price of a dog, in the house of the Lord thy God, whatsoever it be that thou hast vowed: because both these are an abomination to the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Non offeres mercedem prostibuli, nec pretium canis in domo Domini Dei tui, quidquid illud est quod voveris: quia abominatio est utrumque apud Dominum Deum tuum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not lend to thy brother money to usury, nor corn, nor any other thing:
verses.textLatin: Non fœnerabis fratri tuo ad usuram pecuniam, nec fruges, nec quamlibet aliam rem:

verses.text: But to the stranger. To thy brother thou shalt lend that which he wanteth, without usury: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all thy works in the land, which thou shalt go in to possess.
verses.textLatin: sed alieno. Fratri autem tuo absque usura id quo indiget, commodabis: ut benedicat tibi Dominus Deus tuus in omni opere tuo in terra, ad quam ingredieris possidendam.

verses.text: When thou hast made a vow to the Lord thy God, thou shalt not delay to pay it: because the Lord thy God will require it. And if thou delay, it shall be imputed to thee for a sin.
verses.textLatin: Cum votum voveris Domino Deo tuo, non tardabis reddere: quia requiret illud Dominus Deus tuus, et si moratus fueris, reputabitur tibi in peccatum.

verses.text: If thou wilt not promise, thou shalt be without sin.
verses.textLatin: Si nolueris polliceri, absque peccato eris.

verses.text: But that which is once gone out of thy lips, thou shalt observe, and shalt do as thou hast promised to the Lord thy God, and hast spoken with thy own will and with thy own mouth.
verses.textLatin: Quod autem semel egressum est de labiis tuis, observabis, et facies sicut promisisti Domino Deo tuo, et propria voluntate et ore tuo locutus es.

verses.text: Going into thy neighbour’s vineyard, thou mayst eat as many grapes as thou pleasest: but must carry none out with thee:
verses.textLatin: Ingressus vineam proximi tui, comede uvas, quantum tibi placuerit: foras autem ne efferas tecum.

verses.text: If thou go into thy friend’s corn, thou mayst break the ears, and rub them in thy hand: but not reap them with a sickle.
verses.textLatin: Si intraveris in segetem amici tui, franges spicas, et manu conteres: falce autem non metes.

verses.text: If  a man take a wife, and have her, and she find not favour in his eyes, for some uncleanness: he shall write a bill of divorce, and shall give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
verses.textLatin: Si acceperit homo uxorem, et habuerit eam, et non invenerit gratiam ante oculos ejus propter aliquam fœditatem: scribet libellum repudii, et dabit in manu illius, et dimittet eam de domo sua.

verses.text: And when she is departed, and marrieth another husband,
verses.textLatin: Cumque egressa alterum maritum duxerit,

verses.text: And he also hateth her, and hath given her a bill of divorce, and hath sent her out of his house or is dead:
verses.textLatin: et ille quoque oderit eam, dederitque ei libellum repudii, et dimiserit de domo sua, vel certe mortuus fuerit:

verses.text: The former husband cannot take her again to wife: because she is defiled, and is become abominable before the Lord: lest thou cause thy land to sin, which the Lord thy God shall give thee to possess.
verses.textLatin: non poterit prior maritus recipere eam in uxorem: quia polluta est, et abominabilis facta est coram Domino: ne peccare facias terram tuam, quam Dominus Deus tuus tradiderit tibi possidendam.

verses.text: When a man hath lately taken a wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall any public business be enjoined him, but he shall be free at home without fault, that for one year he may rejoice with his wife.
verses.textLatin: Cum acceperit homo nuper uxorem, non procedet ad bellum, nec ei quippiam necessitatis injungetur publicæ, sed vacabit absque culpa domi suæ, ut uno anno lætetur cum uxore sua.

verses.text: Thou shalt not take the nether, nor the upper millstone to pledge: for he hath pledged his life to thee.
verses.textLatin: Non accipies loco pignoris inferiorem, et superiorem molam: quia animam suam opposuit tibi.

verses.text: If any man be found soliciting his brother of the children of Israel, and selling him shall take a price, he shall be put to death, and thou shalt take away the evil from the midst of thee.
verses.textLatin: Si deprehensus fuerit homo sollicitans fratrem suum de filiis Israël, et vendito eo acceperit pretium, interficietur, et auferes malum de medio tui.

verses.text: Observe diligently that thou incur not the stroke of the leprosy, but thou shalt do whatsoever the priests of the Levitical race shall teach thee, according to what I have commanded them, and fulfil thou it carefully.
verses.textLatin: Observa diligenter ne incurras plagam lepræ, sed facies quæcumque docuerint te sacerdotes Levitici generis, juxta id quod præcepi eis, et imple sollicite.

verses.text: Remember what the Lord your God did to Mary, in the way when you came out of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Mementote quæ fecerit Dominus Deus vester Mariæ in via cum egrederemini de Ægypto.

verses.text: When thou shalt demand of thy neighbour any thing that he oweth thee, thou shalt not go into his house to take away a pledge:
verses.textLatin: Cum repetes a proximo tuo rem aliquam, quam debet tibi, non ingredieris domum ejus ut pignus auferas:

verses.text: But thou shalt stand without, and he shall bring out to thee what he hath.
verses.textLatin: sed stabis foris, et ille tibi proferet quod habuerit.

verses.text: But if he be poor, the pledge shall not lodge with thee that night,
verses.textLatin: Sin autem pauper est, non pernoctabit apud te pignus,

verses.text: But thou shalt restore it to him presently before the going down of the sun: that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and thou mayst have justice before the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: sed statim reddes ei ante solis occasum: ut dormiens in vestimento suo, benedicat tibi, et habeas justitiam coram Domino Deo tuo.

verses.text: Thou shalt not refuse the hire of the needy, and the poor, whether he be thy brother, or a stranger that dwelleth with thee in the land, and is within thy gates:
verses.textLatin: Non negabis mercedem indigentis, et pauperis fratris tui, sive advenæ, qui tecum moratur in terra, et intra portas tuas est:

verses.text: But thou shalt pay him the price of his labour the same day, before the going down of the sun, because he is poor, and with it maintaineth his life: lest he cry against thee to the Lord, and it be reputed to thee for a sin.
verses.textLatin: sed eadem die reddes ei pretium laboris sui ante solis occasum, quia pauper est, et ex eo sustentat animam suam: ne clamet contra te ad Dominum, et reputetur tibi in peccatum.

verses.text: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children for the fathers, but every one shall die for his own sin.
verses.textLatin: Non occidentur patres pro filiis, nec filii pro patribus, sed unusquisque pro peccato suo morietur.

verses.text: Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger nor of the fatherless, neither shalt thou take away the widow’s raiment for a pledge.
verses.textLatin: Non pervertes judicium advenæ et pupilli, nec auferes pignoris loco viduæ vestimentum.

verses.text: Remember that thou wast a slave in Egypt, and the Lord thy God delivered thee from thence. Therefore I command thee to do this thing.
verses.textLatin: Memento quod servieris in Ægypto, et eruerit te Dominus Deus tuus inde. Idcirco præcipio tibi ut facias hanc rem.

verses.text: When thou hast reaped the corn in thy field, and hast forgot and left a sheaf, thou shalt not return to take it away: but thou shalt suffer the stranger, and the fatherless and the widow to take it away: that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the works of thy hands.
verses.textLatin: Quando messueris segetem in agro tuo, et oblitus manipulum reliqueris, non reverteris, ut tollas illum: sed advenam, et pupillum, et viduam auferre patieris, ut benedicat tibi Dominus Deus tuus in omni opere manuum tuarum.

verses.text: If thou have gathered the fruit of thy olive trees, thou shalt not return to gather whatsoever remaineth on the trees: but shalt leave it for the stranger, for the fatherless, and the widow.
verses.textLatin: Si fruges collegeris olivarum, quidquid remanserit in arboribus, non reverteris ut colligas: sed relinques advenæ, pupillo, ac viduæ.

verses.text: If thou make the vintage of thy vineyard, thou shalt not gather the clusters that remain, but they shall be for the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.
verses.textLatin: Si vindemiaveris vineam tuam, non colliges remanentes racemos: sed cedent in usus advenæ, pupilli, ac viduæ.

verses.text: Remember that thou also wast a bondman in Egypt, and therefore I command thee to do this thing.
verses.textLatin: Memento quod et tu servieris in Ægypto, et idcirco præcipio tibi ut facias hanc rem.

verses.text: If  there be a controversy between men, and they call upon the judges: they shall give the prize of justice to him whom they perceive to be just: and him whom they find to be wicked, they shall condemn of wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Si fuerit causa inter aliquos, et interpellaverint judices: quem justum esse perspexerint, illi justitiæ palmam dabunt: quem impium, condemnabunt impietatis.

verses.text: And if they see that the offender be worthy of stripes: they shall lay him down, and shall cause him to be beaten before them. According to the measure of the sin shall the measure also of the stripes be:
verses.textLatin: Sin autem eum, qui peccavit, dignum viderint plagis: prosternent, et coram se facient verberari. Pro mensura peccati erit et plagarum modus:

verses.text: Yet so, that they exceed not the number of forty: lest thy brother depart shamefully torn before thy eyes.
verses.textLatin: ita dumtaxat, ut quadragenarium numerum non excedant: ne fœde laceratus ante oculos tuos abeat frater tuus.

verses.text: Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out thy corn on the floor.
verses.textLatin: Non ligabis os bovis terentis in area fruges tuas.

verses.text: When brethren dwell together, and one of them dieth without children, the wife of the deceased shall not marry to another: but his brother shall take her, and raise up seed for his brother:
verses.textLatin: Quando habitaverint fratres simul, et unus ex eis absque liberis mortuus fuerit, uxor defuncti non nubet alteri: sed accipiet eam frater ejus, et suscitabit semen fratris sui:

verses.text: And the first son he shall have of her he shall call by his name, that his name be not abolished out of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et primogenitum ex ea filium nomine illius appellabit, ut non deleatur nomen ejus ex Israël.

verses.text: But if he will not take his brother’s wife, who by law belongeth to him, the woman shall go to the gate of the city, and call upon the ancients, and say: My husband’s brother refuseth to raise up his brother’s name in Israel: and will not take me to wife.
verses.textLatin: Sin autem noluerit accipere uxorem fratris sui, quæ ei lege debetur, perget mulier ad portam civitatis, et interpellabit majores natu, dicetque: Non vult frater viri mei suscitare nomen fratris sui in Israël, nec me in conjugem sumere.

verses.text: And they shall cause him to be sent for forthwith, and shall ask him. If he answer: I will not take her to wife:
verses.textLatin: Statimque accersiri eum facient, et interrogabunt. Si responderit: Nolo eam uxorem accipere:

verses.text: The woman shall come to him before the ancients, and shall take off his shoe from his foot, and spit in his face, and say: So shall it be done to the man that will not build up his brother’s house:
verses.textLatin: accedet mulier ad eum coram senioribus, et tollet calceamentum de pede ejus, spuetque in faciem illius, et dicet: Sic fiet homini, qui non ædificat domum fratris sui.

verses.text: And his name shall be called in Israel, the house of the unshod.
verses.textLatin: Et vocabitur nomen illius in Israël, Domus discalceati.

verses.text: If two men have words together, and one begin to fight against the other, and the other’s wife willing to deliver her husband out of the hand of the stronger, shall put forth her hand, and take him by the secrets,
verses.textLatin: Si habuerint inter se jurgium viri duo, et unus contra alterum rixari cœperit, volensque uxor alterius eruere virum suum de manu fortioris, miseritque manum, et apprehenderit verenda ejus:

verses.text: Thou shalt cut off her hand, neither shalt thou be moved with any pity in her regard.
verses.textLatin: abscides manum illius, nec flecteris super eam ulla misericordia.

verses.text: Thou shalt not have divers weights in thy bag, a greater and a less:
verses.textLatin: Non habebis in sacculo diversa pondera, majus et minus:

verses.text: Neither shall there be in thy house a greater bushel and a less.
verses.textLatin: nec erit in domo tua modius major, et minor.

verses.text: Thou shalt have a just and a true weight, and thy bushel shall be equal and true: that thou mayest live a long time upon the land which the Lord thy God shall give thee.
verses.textLatin: Pondus habebis justum et verum, et modius æqualis et verus erit tibi: ut multo vivas tempore super terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi.

verses.text: For the Lord thy God abhorreth him that doth these things, and he hateth all injustice.
verses.textLatin: Abominatur enim Dominus tuus eum qui facit hæc, et aversatur omnem injustitiam.

verses.text: Remember what Amalec did to thee in the way when thou camest out of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Memento quæ fecerit tibi Amalec in via quando egrediebaris ex Ægypto:

verses.text: How he met thee: and slew the hindmost of the army, who sat down, being weary, when thou wast spent with hunger and labour, and he feared not God.
verses.textLatin: quomodo occurrerit tibi, et extremos agminis tui, qui lassi residebant, ceciderit, quando tu eras fame et labore confectus: et non timuerit Deum.

verses.text: Therefore when the Lord thy God shall give thee rest, and shall have subdued all the nations round about in the land which he hath promised thee: thou shalt blot out his name from under heaven. See thou forget it not.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi requiem, et subjecerit cunctas per circuitum nationes in terra, quam tibi pollicitus est: delebis nomen ejus sub cælo. Cave ne obliviscaris.

verses.text: And  when thou art come into the land which the Lord thy God will give thee to possess, and hast conquered it, and dwellest in it:
verses.textLatin: Cumque intraveris terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus tibi daturus est possidendam, et obtinueris eam, atque habitaveris in ea:

verses.text: Thou shalt take the first of all thy fruits, and put them in a basket, and shalt go to the place which the Lord thy God shall choose, that his name may be invocated there:
verses.textLatin: tolles de cunctis frugibus tuis primitias, et pones in cartallo, pergesque ad locum quem Dominus Deus tuus elegerit, ut ibi invocetur nomen ejus:

verses.text: And thou shalt go to the priest that shall be in those days, and say to him: I profess this day before the Lord thy God, that I am come into the land, for which he swore to our fathers, that he would give it us.
verses.textLatin: accedesque ad sacerdotem, qui fuerit in diebus illis, et dices ad eum: Profiteor hodie coram Domino Deo tuo, quod ingressus sum in terram, pro qua juravit patribus nostris, ut daret eam nobis.

verses.text: And the priest taking the basket at thy hand, shall set it before the altar of the Lord thy God:
verses.textLatin: Suscipiensque sacerdos cartallum de manu tua, ponet ante altare Domini Dei tui:

verses.text: And thou shalt speak thus in the sight of the Lord thy God: The Syrian pursued my father, who went down into Egypt, and sojourned there in a very small number, and grew into a nation great and strong and of an infinite multitude.
verses.textLatin: et loqueris in conspectu Domini Dei tui: Syrus persequebatur patrem meum, qui descendit in Ægyptum, et ibi peregrinatus est in paucissimo numero: crevitque in gentem magnam ac robustam et infinitæ multitudinis.

verses.text: And the Egyptians afflicted us, and persecuted us, laying on us most grievous burdens:
verses.textLatin: Afflixeruntque nos Ægyptii, et persecuti sunt, imponentes onera gravissima:

verses.text: And we cried to the Lord God of our fathers: who heard us, and looked down upon our affliction, and labour, and distress:
verses.textLatin: et clamavimus ad Dominum Deum patrum nostrorum: qui exaudivit nos, et respexit humilitatem nostram, et laborem, atque angustiam:

verses.text: And brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand, and a stretched out arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders:
verses.textLatin: et eduxit nos de Ægypto in manu forti, et brachio extento, in ingenti pavore, in signis atque portentis:

verses.text: And brought us into this place, and gave us this land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: et introduxit ad locum istum, et tradidit nobis terram lacte et melle manantem.

verses.text: And therefore now I offer the firstfruits of the land which the Lord hath given me. And thou shalt leave them in the sight of the Lord thy God, adoring the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Et idcirco nunc offero primitias frugum terræ, quam Dominus dedit mihi. Et dimittes eas in conspectu Domini Dei tui, et adorato Domino Deo tuo.

verses.text: And thou shalt feast in all the good things which the Lord thy God hath given thee, and thy house, thou and the Levite, and the stranger that is with thee.
verses.textLatin: Et epulaberis in omnibus bonis, quæ Dominus Deus tuus dederit tibi et domui tuæ, tu et Levites, et advena qui tecum est.

verses.text: When thou hast made an end of tithing all thy fruits, in the third year of tithes thou shalt give it to the Levite, and to the stranger, and to the fatherless, and to the widow, that they may eat within thy gates, and be filled:
verses.textLatin: Quando compleveris decimam cunctarum frugum tuarum, anno decimarum tertio, dabis Levitæ, et advenæ, et pupillo et viduæ, ut comedant intra portas tuas, et saturentur:

verses.text: And thou shalt speak thus in the sight of the Lord thy God: I have taken that which was sanctified out of my house, and I have given it to the Levite, and to the stranger, and to the fatherless, and to the widow, as thou hast commanded me: I have not transgressed thy commandments nor forgotten thy precepts.
verses.textLatin: loquerisque in conspectu Domini Deo tui: Abstuli quod sanctificatum est de domo mea, et dedi illud Levitæ et advenæ, et pupillo ac viduæ, sicut jussisti mihi: non præterivi mandata tua, nec sum oblitus imperii tui.

verses.text: I have not eaten of them in my mourning, nor separated them for any uncleanness, nor spent any thing of them in funerals. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all things as thou hast commanded me.
verses.textLatin: Non comedi ex eis in luctu meo, nec separavi ea in qualibet immunditia, nec expendi ex his quidquam in re funebri. Obedivi voci Domini Dei mei, et feci omnia sicut præcepisti mihi.

verses.text: Look from thy sanctuary, and thy high habitation of heaven, and bless thy people Israel, and the land which thou hast given us, as thou didst swear to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: Respice de sanctuario tuo, et de excelso cælorum habitaculo, et benedic populo tuo Israël, et terræ, quam dedisti nobis, sicut jurasti patribus nostris, terræ lacte et melle mananti.

verses.text: This day the Lord thy God hath commanded thee to do these commandments and judgments: and to keep and fulfil them with all thy heart, and with all thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Hodie Dominus Deus tuus præcepit tibi ut facias mandata hæc atque judicia: et custodias et impleas ex toto corde tuo, et ex tota anima tua.

verses.text: Thou hast chosen the Lord this day to be thy God, and to walk in his ways and keep his ceremonies, and precepts, and judgments, and obey his command.
verses.textLatin: Dominum elegisti hodie, ut sit tibi Deus, et ambules in viis ejus, et custodias cæremonias illius, et mandata atque judicia, et obedias ejus imperio.

verses.text: And the Lord hath chosen thee this day, to be his peculiar people, as he hath spoken to thee, and to keep all his commandments:
verses.textLatin: Et Dominus elegit te hodie ut sis ei populus peculiaris, sicut locutus est tibi, et custodias omnia præcepta illius:

verses.text: And to make thee higher than all nations which he hath created, to his own praise, and name, and glory: that thou mayst be a holy people of the Lord thy God, as he hath spoken.
verses.textLatin: et faciat te excelsiorem cunctis gentibus quas creavit, in laudem, et nomen, et gloriam suam: ut sis populus sanctus Domini Dei tui, sicut locutus est.

verses.text: And  Moses with the ancients of Israel commanded the people, saying: Keep every commandment that I command you this day.
verses.textLatin: Præcepit autem Moyses et seniores Israël populo, dicentes: Custodite omne mandatum quod præcipio vobis hodie.

verses.text: And when you are passed over the Jordan into the land which the Lord thy God will give thee, thou shalt set up great stones, and shalt plaster them over with plaster,
verses.textLatin: Cumque transieritis Jordanem in terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi, eriges ingentes lapides, et calce lævigabis eos,

verses.text: That thou mayst write on them all the words of this law, when thou art passed over the Jordan: that thou mayst enter into the land which the Lord thy God will give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, as he swore to thy fathers.
verses.textLatin: ut possis in eis scribere omnia verba legis hujus, Jordane transmisso: ut introëas terram, quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi, terram lacte et melle manantem, sicut juravit patribus tuis.

verses.text: Therefore when you are passed over the Jordan, set up the stones which I command you this day, in mount Hebal, and thou shalt plaster them with plaster:
verses.textLatin: Quando ergo transieritis Jordanem, erigite lapides, quos ego hodie præcipio vobis in monte Hebal, et lævigabis eos calce:

verses.text: And thou shalt build there an altar to the Lord thy God, of stones which iron hath not touched,
verses.textLatin: et ædificabis ibi altare Domino Deo tuo de lapidibus, quos ferrum non tetigit,

verses.text: And of stones not fashioned nor polished: and thou shalt offer upon it holocausts to the Lord thy God:
verses.textLatin: et de saxis informibus et impolitis: et offeres super eo holocausta Domino Deo tuo,

verses.text: And shalt immolate peace victims, and eat there, and feast before the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: et immolabis hostias pacificas, comedesque ibi, et epulaberis coram Domino Deo tuo.

verses.text: And thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law plainly and clearly.
verses.textLatin: Et scribes super lapides omnia verba legis hujus plane et lucide.

verses.text: And Moses and the priests of the race of Levi said to all Israel: Attend, and hear, O Israel: This day thou art made the people of the Lord thy God.
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque Moyses et sacerdotes Levitici generis ad omnem Israëlem: Attende, et audi, Israël: hodie factus es populus Domini Dei tui:

verses.text: Thou shalt hear his voice, and do the commandments and justices which I command thee.
verses.textLatin: audies vocem ejus, et facies mandata atque justitias, quas ego præcipio tibi.

verses.text: And Moses commanded the people in that day, saying:
verses.textLatin: Præcepitque Moyses populo in die illo, dicens:

verses.text: These shall stand upon mount Garizim to bless the people, when you are passed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Juda, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
verses.textLatin: Hi stabunt ad benedicendum populo super montem Garizim, Jordane transmisso: Simeon, Levi, Judas, Issachar, Joseph, et Benjamin.

verses.text: And over against them shall stand on mount Hebal to curse: Ruben, Gad, and Aser, and Zabulon, Dan, and Nephtali.
verses.textLatin: Et e regione isti stabunt ad maledicendum in monte Hebal: Ruben, Gad, et Aser, et Zabulon, Dan, et Nephthali.

verses.text: And the Levites shall pronounce, and say to all the men of Israel with a loud voice:
verses.textLatin: Et pronuntiabunt Levitæ, dicentque ad omnes viros Israël excelsa voce:

verses.text: Cursed be the man that maketh a graven and molten thing, the abomination of the Lord, the work of the hands of artificers, and shall put it in a secret place: and all the people shall answer and say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus homo qui facit sculptile et conflatile, abominationem Domini, opus manuum artificum, ponetque illud in abscondito: et respondebit omnis populus, et dicet: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that honoureth not his father and mother: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui non honorat patrem suum, et matrem: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmarks: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui transfert terminos proximi sui: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that maketh the blind to wander out of his way: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui errare facit cæcum in itinere: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that perverteth the judgment of the stranger, of the fatherless and the widow: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui pervertit judicium advenæ, pupilli et viduæ: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife, and uncovereth his bed: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui dormit cum uxore patris sui, et revelat operimentum lectuli ejus: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that lieth with any beast: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui dormit cum omni jumento: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or of his mother: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui dormit cum sorore sua, filia patris sui, vel matris suæ: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that lieth with his mother in law: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui dormit cum socru sua: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that secretly killeth his neighbour: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui clam percusserit proximum suum: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that taketh gifts, to slay an innocent person: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui accipit munera, ut percutiat animam sanguinis innocentis: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Cursed be he that abideth not in the words of this law, and fulfilleth them not in work: and all the people shall say: Amen.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus qui non permanet in sermonibus legis hujus, nec eos opere perficit: et dicet omnis populus: Amen.

verses.text: Now  if thou wilt hear the voice of the Lord thy God, to do and keep all his commandments, which I command thee this day, the Lord thy God will make thee higher than all the nations that are on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Si autem audieris vocem Domini Dei tui, ut facias atque custodias omnia mandata ejus, quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, faciet te Dominus Deus tuus excelsiorem cunctis gentibus, quæ versantur in terra.

verses.text: And all these blessings shall come upon thee and overtake thee: yet so if thou hear his precepts,
verses.textLatin: Venientque super te universæ benedictiones istæ, et apprehendent te: si tamen præcepta ejus audieris.

verses.text: Blessed shalt thou be in the city, and blessed in the field.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus tu in civitate, et benedictus in agro.

verses.text: Blessed shall be the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle, the droves of thy herds, and the folds of thy sheep.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus fructus ventris tui, et fructus terræ tuæ, fructusque jumentorum tuorum, greges armentorum tuorum, et caulæ ovium tuarum.

verses.text: Blessed shall be thy barns and blessed thy stores.
verses.textLatin: Benedicta horrea tua, et benedictæ reliquiæ tuæ.

verses.text: Blessed shalt thou be coming in and going out.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus eris tu ingrediens et egrediens.

verses.text: The Lord shall cause thy enemies, that rise up against thee, to fall down before thy face: one way shall they come out against thee, and seven ways shall they flee before thee.
verses.textLatin: Dabit Dominus inimicos tuos, qui consurgunt adversum te, corruentes in conspectu tuo: per unam viam venient contra te, et per septem fugient a facie tua.

verses.text: The Lord will send forth a blessing upon thy storehouses, and upon all the works of thy hands: and will bless thee in the land that thou shalt receive.
verses.textLatin: Emittet Dominus benedictionem super cellaria tua, et super omnia opera manuum tuarum: benedicetque tibi in terra, quam acceperis.

verses.text: The Lord will raise thee up to be a holy people to himself, as he swore to thee: if thou keep the commandments of the Lord thy God, and walk in his ways.
verses.textLatin: Suscitabit te Dominus sibi in populum sanctum, sicut juravit tibi: si custodieris mandata Domini Dei tui, et ambulaveris in viis ejus.

verses.text: And all the people of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is invocated upon thee, and they shall fear thee.
verses.textLatin: Videbuntque omnes terrarum populi quod nomen Domini invocatum sit super te, et timebunt te.

verses.text: The Lord will make thee abound with all goods, with the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy cattle, with the fruit of thy land, which the Lord swore to thy fathers that he would give thee.
verses.textLatin: Abundare te faciet Dominus omnibus bonis, fructu uteri tui, et fructu jumentorum tuorum, fructu terræ tuæ, quam juravit Dominus patribus tuis ut daret tibi.

verses.text: The Lord will open his excellent treasure, the heaven, that it may give rain in due season: and he will bless all the works of thy hands. And thou shalt lend to many nations, and shalt not borrow of any one.
verses.textLatin: Aperiet Dominus thesaurum suum optimum, cælum, ut tribuat pluviam terræ tuæ in tempore suo: benedicetque cunctis operibus manuum tuarum. Et fœnerabis gentibus multis, et ipse a nullo fœnus accipies.

verses.text: And the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail: and thou shalt be always above, and not beneath: yet so if thou wilt hear the commandments of the Lord thy God which I command thee this day, and keep and do them,
verses.textLatin: Constituet te Dominus in caput, et non in caudam: et eris semper supra, et non subter: si tamen audieris mandata Domini Dei tui quæ ego præcipio tibi hodie, et custodieris et feceris,

verses.text: And turn not away from them neither to the right hand, nor to the left, nor follow strange gods, nor worship them.
verses.textLatin: ac non declinaveris ab eis nec ad dexteram, nec ad sinistram, nec secutus fueris deos alienos, neque colueris eos.

verses.text: But if thou wilt not hear the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep and to do all his commandments and ceremonies, which I command thee this day, all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.
verses.textLatin: Quod si audire nolueris vocem Domini Dei tui, ut custodias, et facias omnia mandata ejus et cæremonias, quas ego præcipio tibi hodie, venient super te omnes maledictiones istæ, et apprehendent te.

verses.text: Cursed shalt thou be in the city, cursed in the field.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus eris in civitate, maledictus in agro.

verses.text: Cursed shall be thy barn, and cursed thy stores.
verses.textLatin: Maledictum horreum tuum, et maledictæ reliquiæ tuæ.

verses.text: Cursed shall be the fruit of thy womb, and the fruit of thy ground, the herds of thy oxen, and the flocks of thy sheep.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus fructus ventris tui, et fructus terræ tuæ, armenta boum tuorum, et greges ovium tuarum.

verses.text: Cursed shalt thou be coming in, and cursed going out.
verses.textLatin: Maledictus eris ingrediens, et maledictus egrediens.

verses.text: The Lord shall send upon thee famine and hunger, and a rebuke upon all the works which thou shalt do: until he consume and destroy thee quickly, for thy most wicked inventions, by which thou hast forsaken me.
verses.textLatin: Mittet Dominus super te famem et esuriem, et increpationem in omnia opera tua, quæ tu facies: donec conterat te, et perdat velociter, propter adinventiones tuas pessimas in quibus reliquisti me.

verses.text: May the Lord set the pestilence upon thee, until he consume thee out of the land, which thou shalt go in to possess.
verses.textLatin: Adjungat tibi Dominus pestilentiam, donec consumat te de terra ad quam ingredieris possidendam.

verses.text: May the Lord afflict thee with miserable want, with the fever and with cold, with burning and with heat, and with corrupted air and with blasting, and pursue thee till thou perish.
verses.textLatin: Percutiat te Dominus egestate, febri et frigore, ardore et æstu, et aëre corrupto ac rubigine, et persequatur donec pereas.

verses.text: Be the heaven, that is over thee, of brass: and the ground thou treadest on, of iron.
verses.textLatin: Sit cælum, quod supra te est, æneum: et terra, quam calcas, ferrea.

verses.text: The Lord give thee dust for rain upon thy land, and let ashes come down from heaven upon thee, till thou be consumed.
verses.textLatin: Det Dominus imbrem terræ tuæ pulverem, et de cælo descendat super te cinis, donec conteraris.

verses.text: The Lord make thee to fall down before thy enemies, one way mayst thou go out against them, and flee seven ways, and be scattered throughout all the kingdoms of the earth.
