verses.text: The Lord shall thunder from heaven: and the most high shall give forth his voice.
verses.textLatin: Tonabit de cælo Dominus, et excelsus dabit vocem suam.

verses.text: He shot arrows and scattered them: lightning, and consumed them.
verses.textLatin: Misit sagittas et dissipavit eos; fulgur, et consumpsit eos.

verses.text: And the overflowings of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid open at the rebuke of the Lord, at the blast of the spirit of his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Et apparuerunt effusiones maris, et revelata sunt fundamenta orbis ab increpatione Domini, ab inspiratione spiritus furoris ejus.

verses.text: He sent from on high, and took me, and drew me out of many waters.
verses.textLatin: Misit de excelso, et assumpsit me, et extraxit me de aquis multis.

verses.text: He delivered me from my most mighty enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
verses.textLatin: Liberavit me ab inimico meo potentissimo, et ab his qui oderant me: quoniam robustiores me erant.

verses.text: He prevented me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my stay.
verses.textLatin: Prævenit me in die afflictionis meæ, et factus est Dominus firmamentum meum.

verses.text: And he brought me forth into a large place, he delivered me, because I pleased him.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit me in latitudinem: liberavit me, quia complacui ei.

verses.text: The Lord will reward me according to my justice: and according to the cleanness of my hands he will render to me.
verses.textLatin: Retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam: et secundum munditiam manuum mearum reddet mihi.

verses.text: Because I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
verses.textLatin: Quia custodivi vias Domini, et non egi impie a Deo meo.

verses.text: For all his judgments are in my sight: and his precepts I have not removed from me.
verses.textLatin: Omnia enim judicia ejus in conspectu meo, et præcepta ejus non amovi a me.

verses.text: And I shall be perfect with him: and shall keep myself from my iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Et ero perfectus cum eo, et custodiam me ab iniquitate mea.

verses.text: And the Lord will recompense me according to my justice: and according to the cleanness of my hands in the sight of his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Et restituet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam, et secundum munditiam manuum mearum in conspectu oculorum suorum.

verses.text: With the holy one thou wilt be holy: and with the valiant perfect.
verses.textLatin: Cum sancto sanctus eris, et cum robusto perfectus.

verses.text: With the elect thou wilt be elect: and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.
verses.textLatin: Cum electo electus eris, et cum perverso perverteris.

verses.text: And the poor people thou wilt save: and with thy eyes thou wilt humble the haughty.
verses.textLatin: Et populum pauperem salvum facies: oculisque tuis excelsos humiliabis.

verses.text: For thou art my lamp, O Lord: and thou, O Lord, wilt enlighten my darkness.
verses.textLatin: Quia tu lucerna mea, Domine, et tu, Domine, illuminabis tenebras meas.

verses.text: For in thee I will run girded: in my God I will leap over the wall.
verses.textLatin: In te enim curram accinctus: in Deo meo transiliam murum.

verses.text: God, his way is immaculate, the word of the Lord is tried by fire: he is the shield of all that trust in him.
verses.textLatin: Deus, immaculata via ejus; eloquium Domini igne examinatum: scutum est omnium sperantium in se.

verses.text: Who is God but the Lord: and who is strong but our God?
verses.textLatin: Quis est Deus præter Dominum, et quis fortis præter Deum nostrum?

verses.text: God who hath girded me with strength, and made my way perfect.
verses.textLatin: Deus qui accinxit me fortitudine, et complanavit perfectam viam meam.

verses.text: Making my feet like the feet of harts, and setting me upon my high places.
verses.textLatin: Coæquans pedes meos cervis, et super excelsa mea statuens me;

verses.text: He teacheth my hands to war: and maketh my arms like a bow of brass.
verses.textLatin: docens manus meas ad prælium, et componens quasi arcum æreum brachia mea.

verses.text: Thou hast given me the shield of my salvation: and thy mildness hath multiplied me.
verses.textLatin: Dedisti mihi clypeum salutis tuæ, et mansuetudo tua multiplicavit me.

verses.text: Thou shalt enlarge my steps under me: and my ankles shall not fail.
verses.textLatin: Dilatabis gressus meos subtus me, et non deficient tali mei.

verses.text: I will pursue after my enemies, and crush them: and will not return again till I consume them.
verses.textLatin: Persequar inimicos meos, et conteram, et non convertar donec consumam eos.

verses.text: I will consume them and break them in pieces, so that they shall not rise: they shall fall under my feet.
verses.textLatin: Consumam eos et confringam, ut non consurgant: cadent sub pedibus meis.

verses.text: Thou hast girded me with strength to battle: thou hast made them that resisted me to bow under me.
verses.textLatin: Accinxisti me fortitudine ad prælium: incurvasti resistentes mihi subtus me.

verses.text: My enemies thou hast made to turn their back to me: them that hated me, and I shall destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Inimicos meos dedisti mihi dorsum; odientes me, et disperdam eos.

verses.text: They shall cry, and there shall be none to save: to the Lord, and he shall not hear them.
verses.textLatin: Clamabunt, et non erit qui salvet; ad Dominum, et non exaudiet eos.

verses.text: I shall beat them as small as the dust of the earth: I shall crush them and spread them abroad like the mire of the streets.
verses.textLatin: Delebo eos ut pulverem terræ; quasi lutum platearum comminuam eos atque confringam.

verses.text: Thou wilt save me from the contradictions of my people: thou wilt keep me to be the head of the Gentiles: the people which I know not, shall serve me,
verses.textLatin: Salvabis me a contradictionibus populi mei; custodies me in caput gentium: populus quem ignoro serviet mihi.

verses.text: The sons of the stranger will resist me, at the hearing of the ear they will obey me.
verses.textLatin: Filii alieni resistent mihi; auditu auris obedient mihi.

verses.text: The strangers are melted away, and shall be straitened in their distresses.
verses.textLatin: Filii alieni defluxerunt, et contrahentur in angustiis suis.

verses.text: The Lord liveth, and my God is blessed: and the strong God of my salvation shall be exalted:
verses.textLatin: Vivit Dominus, et benedictus Deus meus, et exaltabitur Deus fortis salutis meæ.

verses.text: God who giveth me revenge, and bringest down people under me,
verses.textLatin: Deus qui das vindictas mihi, et dejicis populos sub me.

verses.text: Who bringest me forth from my enemies, and liftest me up from them that resist me: from the wicked man thou shalt deliver me.
verses.textLatin: Qui educis me ab inimicis meis, et a resistentibus mihi elevas me: a viro iniquo liberabis me.

verses.text: Therefore will I give thanks to thee, O Lord, among the Gentiles, and will sing to thy name.
verses.textLatin: Propterea confitebor tibi, Domine, in gentibus, et nomini tuo cantabo:

verses.text: Giving great salvation to his king, and shewing mercy to David his anointed, and to his seed for ever.
verses.textLatin: magnificans salutes regis sui, et faciens misericordiam christo suo David, et semini ejus in sempiternum.

verses.text: Now  these are David’s last words. David the son of Isai said: The man to whom it was appointed concerning the Christ of the God of Jacob, the excellent psalmist of Israel said:
verses.textLatin: Hæc autem sunt verba David novissima. Dixit David filius Isai: Dixit vir, cui constitutum est de christo Dei Jacob, egregius psaltes Israël:

verses.text: The spirit of the Lord hath spoken by me and his word by my tongue.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus Domini locutus est per me, et sermo ejus per linguam meam.

verses.text: The God of Israel said to me, the strong one of Israel spoke, the ruler of men, the just ruler in the fear of God.
verses.textLatin: Dixit Deus Israël mihi, locutus est fortis Israël: Dominator hominum, justus dominator in timore Dei,

verses.text: As the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, shineth in the morning without clouds, and as the grass springeth out of the earth by rain.
verses.textLatin: sicut lux auroræ, oriente sole, mane absque nubibus rutilat: et sicut pluviis germinat herba de terra.

verses.text: Neither is my house so great with God, that he should make with me an eternal covenant, firm in all things and assured. For he is all my salvation, and all my will: neither is there ought thereof that springeth not up.
verses.textLatin: Nec tanta est domus mea apud Deum, ut pactum æternum iniret mecum, firmum in omnibus atque munitum. Cuncta enim salus mea, et omnis voluntas, nec est quidquam ex ea quod non germinet.

verses.text: But transgressors shall all of them be plucked up as thorns: which are not taken away with hands.
verses.textLatin: Prævaricatores autem quasi spinæ evellentur universi, quæ non tolluntur manibus.

verses.text: And if a man will touch them, he must be armed with iron and with the staff of a lance: but they shall be set on fire and burnt to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Et si quis tangere voluerit eas, armabitur ferro et ligno lanceato, igneque succensæ comburentur usque ad nihilum.

verses.text: These are the names of the valiant men of David: Jesbaham sitting in the chair was the wisest chief among the three, he was like the most tender little worm of the wood, who killed eight hundred men at one onset.
verses.textLatin: Hæc nomina fortium David. Sedens in cathedra sapientissimus princeps inter tres, ipse est quasi tenerrimus ligni vermiculus, qui octingentos interfecit impetu uno.

verses.text: After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three valiant men that were with David when they defied the Philistines, and they were there gathered together to battle.
verses.textLatin: Post hunc, Eleazar filius patrui ejus Ahohites inter tres fortes, qui erant cum David quando exprobraverunt Philisthiim, et congregati sunt illuc in prælium.

verses.text: And when the men of Israel were gone away, he stood and smote the Philistines till his hand was weary, and grew stiff with the sword: and the Lord wrought a great victory that day: and the people that were fled away, returned to take spoils of them that were slain.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ascendissent viri Israël, ipse stetit et percussit Philisthæos donec deficeret manus ejus, et obrigesceret cum gladio: fecitque Dominus salutem magnam in die illa: et populus qui fugerat, reversus est ad cæsorum spolia detrahenda.

verses.text: And after him was Semma the son of Age of Arari. And the Philistines were gathered together in a troop: for there was a field full of lentils. And when the people were fled from the face of the Philistines,
verses.textLatin: Et post hunc, Semma filius Age de Arari. Et congregati sunt Philisthiim in statione: erat quippe ibi ager lente plenus. Cumque fugisset populus a facie Philisthiim,

verses.text: He stood in the midst of the field, and defended it, and defeated the Philistines: and the Lord gave a great victory.
verses.textLatin: stetit ille in medio agri, et tuitus est eum, percussitque Philisthæos: et fecit Dominus salutem magnam.

verses.text: Moreover also before this the three who were princes among the thirty, went down and came to David in the harvest time into the cave of Odollam: and the camp of the Philistines was in the valley of the giants.
verses.textLatin: Necnon et ante descenderant tres qui erant principes inter triginta, et venerant tempore messis ad David in speluncam Odollam: castra autem Philisthinorum erant posita in Valle gigantum.

verses.text: And David was then in a hold: and there was a garrison of the Philistines then in Bethlehem.
verses.textLatin: Et David erat in præsidio: porro statio Philisthinorum tunc erat in Bethlehem.

verses.text: And David longed, and said: O that some man would get me a drink of the water out of the cistern, that is in Bethlehem, by the gate.
verses.textLatin: Desideravit ergo David, et ait: O si quis mihi daret potum aquæ de cisterna quæ est in Bethlehem juxta portam!

verses.text: And the three valiant men broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water out of the cistern of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and brought it to David: but he would not drink, but offered it to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Irruperunt ergo tres fortes castra Philisthinorum, et hauserunt aquam de cisterna Bethlehem, quæ erat juxta portam, et attulerunt ad David: at ille noluit bibere, sed libavit eam Domino,

verses.text: Saying: The Lord be merciful to me, that I may not do this: shall I drink the blood of these men that went, and the peril of their lives? therefore he would not drink. These things did these three mighty men.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Propitius sit mihi Dominus, ne faciam hoc: num sanguinem hominum istorum qui profecti sunt, et animarum periculum bibam? Noluit ergo bibere. Hæc fecerunt tres robustissimi.

verses.text: Abisai also the brother of Joab, the son of Sarvia, was chief among three: and he lifted up his spear against three hundred whom he slew, and he was renowned among the three,
verses.textLatin: Abisai quoque frater Joab filius Sarviæ, princeps erat de tribus: ipse est qui levavit hastam suam contra trecentos, quos interfecit: nominatus in tribus,

verses.text: And the noblest of three, and was their chief, but to the three first he attained not.
verses.textLatin: et inter tres nobilior, eratque eorum princeps, sed usque ad tres primos non pervenerat.

verses.text: And Banaias the son of Joiada a most valiant man, of great deeds, of Cabseel: he slew the two lions of Moab, and he went down, and slew a lion in the midst of a pit, in the time of snow.
verses.textLatin: Et Banaias filius Jojadæ viri fortissimi, magnorum operum, de Cabseel. Ipse percussit duos leones Moab, et ipse descendit, et percussit leonem in media cisterna in diebus nivis.

verses.text: He also slew an Egyptian, a man worthy to be a sight, having a spear in his hand: but he went down to him with a rod, and forced the spear out of the hand of the Egyptian, and slew him with his own spear.
verses.textLatin: Ipse quoque interfecit virum ægyptium, virum dignum spectaculo, habentem in manu hastam: itaque cum descendisset ad eum in virga, vi extorsit hastam de manu Ægyptii, et interfecit eum hasta sua.

verses.text: These things did Banaias the son of Joiada.
verses.textLatin: Hæc fecit Banaias filius Jojadæ.

verses.text: And he was renowned among the three valiant men, who were the most honourable among the thirty: but he attained not to the first three: and David made him of his privy council.
verses.textLatin: Et ipse nominatus inter tres robustos, qui erant inter triginta nobiliores: verumtamen usque ad tres non pervenerat: fecitque eum sibi David auricularium, a secreto.

verses.text: Asael the brother of Joab was one of the thirty, Elehanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem.
verses.textLatin: Asaël frater Joab inter triginta, Elehanan filius patrui ejus de Bethlehem,

verses.text: Semma of Harodi, Elica of Harodi,
verses.textLatin: Semma de Harodi, Elica de Harodi,

verses.text: Heles of Phalti, Hira the son of Acces of Thecua,
verses.textLatin: Heles de Phalti, Hira filius Acces de Thecua,

verses.text: Abiezer of Anathoth, Mobonnai of Husati,
verses.textLatin: Abiezer de Anathoth, Mobonnai de Husati,

verses.text: Selmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
verses.textLatin: Selmon Ahohites, Maharai Netophathites,

verses.text: Heled the son of Baana, also a Netophathite, Ithai the son of Ribai of Gabaath of the children of Benjamin,
verses.textLatin: Heled filius Baana, et ipse Netophathites, Ithai filius Ribai de Gabaath filiorum Benjamin,

verses.text: Banaia the Pharathonite, Heddai of the torrent Gaas,
verses.textLatin: Banaia Pharathonites, Heddai de torrente Gaas,

verses.text: Abialbon the Arbathite, Azmaveth of Beromi,
verses.textLatin: Abialbon Arbathites, Azmaveth de Beromi,

verses.text: Eliaba of Salaboni. The sons of Jassen, Jonathan,
verses.textLatin: Eliaba de Salaboni. Filii Jassen, Jonathan,

verses.text: Semma of Orori, Aliam the son of Sarar the Arorite,
verses.textLatin: Semma de Orori, Ajam filius Sarar Arorites,

verses.text: Eliphelet the son of Aasbai the son of Machati, Eliam the son of Achitophel the Gelonite,
verses.textLatin: Eliphelet filius Aasbai filii Machati, Eliam filius Achitophel Gelonites,

verses.text: Hesrai of Carmel, Pharai of Arbi,
verses.textLatin: Hesrai de Carmelo, Pharai de Arbi,

verses.text: Igaal the son of Nathan of Soba, Bonni of Gadi,
verses.textLatin: Igaal filius Nathan de Soba, Bonni de Gadi,

verses.text: Selec of Ammoni, Naharai the Berothite, armourbearer of Joab the son of Sarvia,
verses.textLatin: Selec de Ammoni, Naharai Berothites armiger Joab filii Sarviæ,

verses.text: Ira the Jethrite, Gareb also a Jethrite;
verses.textLatin: Ira Jethrites, Gareb et ipse Jethrites,

verses.text: Urias the Hethite, thirty and seven in all.
verses.textLatin: Urias Hethæus: omnes triginta septem.

verses.text: And  the anger of the Lord was again kindled against Israel, and stirred up David among them, saying: Go, number Israel and Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et addidit furor Domini irasci contra Israël, commovitque David in eis dicentem: Vade, numera Israël et Judam.

verses.text: And the king said to Joab the general of his army: Go through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Bersabee, and number ye the people that I may know the number of them.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque rex ad Joab principem exercitus sui: Perambula omnes tribus Israël a Dan usque Bersabee, et numerate populum, ut sciam numerum ejus.

verses.text: And Joab said to the king: The Lord thy God increase thy people, and make them as many more as they are now, and again multiply them a hundredfold in the sight of my lord the king: but what meaneth my lord the king by this kind of thing?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Joab regi: Adaugeat Dominus Deus tuus ad populum tuum, quantus nunc est, iterumque centuplicet in conspectu domini mei regis: sed quid sibi dominus meus rex vult in re hujuscemodi?

verses.text: But the king’s words prevailed over the words of Joab, and of the captains of the army: and Joab, and the captains of the soldiers went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Obtinuit autem sermo regis verba Joab et principum exercitus: egressusque est Joab et princeps militum a facie regis, ut numerarent populum Israël.

verses.text: And when they had passed the Jordan, they came to Aroer to the right side of the city, which is in the vale of Gad.
verses.textLatin: Cumque pertransissent Jordanem, venerunt in Aroër ad dexteram urbis, quæ est in valle Gad:

verses.text: And by Jazer they passed into Galaad, and to the lower land of Hodsi, and they came into the woodlands of Dan. And going about by Sidon,
verses.textLatin: et per Jazer transierunt in Galaad, et in terram inferiorem Hodsi, et venerunt in Dan silvestria. Circumeuntesque juxta Sidonem,

verses.text: They passed near the walls of Tyre, and all the land of the Hevite, and the Chanaanite, and they came to the south of Juda into Bersabee:
verses.textLatin: transierunt prope mœnia Tyri, et omnem terram Hevæi et Chananæi, veneruntque ad meridiem Juda in Bersabee:

verses.text: And having gone through the whole land, after nine months and twenty days, they came to Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et lustrata universa terra, affuerunt post novem menses et viginti dies in Jerusalem.

verses.text: And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people to the king, and there were found of Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword: and of Juda five hundred thousand fighting men.
verses.textLatin: Dedit ergo Joab numerum descriptionis populi regi, et inventa sunt de Israël octingenta millia virorum fortium qui educerent gladium, et de Juda quingenta millia pugnatorum.

verses.text: But David’s heart struck him, after the people were numbered: and David said to the Lord: I have sinned very much in what I have done: but I pray thee, O Lord, to take away the iniquity of thy servant, because I have done exceeding foolishly.
verses.textLatin: Percussit autem cor David eum, postquam numeratus est populus: et dixit David ad Dominum: Peccavi valde in hoc facto: sed precor, Domine, ut transferas iniquitatem servi tui, quia stulte egi nimis.

verses.text: And David arose in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet and the seer of David, saying:
verses.textLatin: Surrexit itaque David mane, et sermo Domini factus est ad Gad prophetam et videntem David, dicens:

verses.text: Go, and say to David: Thus saith the Lord: I give thee thy choice of three things, choose one of them which thou wilt, that I may do it to thee.
verses.textLatin: Vade, et loquere ad David: Hæc dicit Dominus: Trium tibi datur optio: elige unum quod volueris ex his, ut faciam tibi.

verses.text: And when Gad was come to David, he told him, saying: Either seven years of famine shall come to thee in thy land: or thou shalt flee three months before thy adversaries, and they shall pursue thee: or for three days there shall be a pestilence in thy land. Now therefore deliberate, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
verses.textLatin: Cumque venisset Gad ad David, nuntiavit ei, dicens: Aut septem annis veniet tibi fames in terra tua: aut tribus mensibus fugies adversarios tuos, et ille te persequentur: aut certe tribus diebus erit pestilentia in terra tua. Nunc ergo delibera, et vide quem respondeam ei qui me misit sermonem.

verses.text: And David said to Gad: I am in a great strait: but it is better that I should fall into the hands of the Lord (for his mercies are many) than into the hands of men.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem David ad Gad: Coarctor nimis: sed melius est ut incidam in manus Domini (multæ enim misericordiæ ejus sunt) quam in manus hominum.

verses.text: And the Lord sent a pestilence upon Israel, from the morning unto the time appointed, and there died of the people from Dan to Bersabee seventy thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Immisitque Dominus pestilentiam in Israël, de mane usque ad tempus constitutum, et mortui sunt ex populo a Dan usque ad Bersabee septuaginta millia virorum.

verses.text: And when the angel of the Lord had stretched out his hand over Jerusalem to destroy it, the Lord had pity on the affliction, and said to the angel that slew the people: It is enough: now hold thy hand. And the angel of the Lord was by the thrashingfloor of Areuna the Jebusite.
verses.textLatin: Cumque extendisset manum suam angelus Domini super Jerusalem ut disperderet eam, misertus est Dominus super afflictione, et ait angelo percutienti populum: Sufficit: nunc contine manum tuam. Erat autem angelus Domini juxta aream Areuna Jebusæi.

verses.text: And David said to the Lord, when he saw the angel striking the people: It is I; I am he that have sinned, I have done wickedly: these that are the sheep, what have they done? let thy hand, I beseech thee, be turned against me, and against my father’s house.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque David ad Dominum cum vidisset angelum cædentem populum: Ego sum qui peccavi, ego inique egi: isti qui oves sunt, quid fecerunt? vertatur, obsecro, manus tua contra me, et contra domum patris mei.

verses.text: And Gad came to David that day, and said: Go up, and build an altar to the Lord in the thrashingfloor of Areuna the Jebusite.
verses.textLatin: Venit autem Gad ad David in die illa, et dixit ei: Ascende, et constitue altare Domino in area Areuna Jebusæi.

verses.text: And David went up according to the word of Gad which the Lord had commanded him.
verses.textLatin: Et ascendit David juxta sermonem Gad, quem præceperat ei Dominus.

verses.text: And Areuna looked, and saw the king and his servants coming towards him:
verses.textLatin: Conspiciensque Areuna, animadvertit regem et servos ejus transire ad se:

verses.text: And going out he worshipped the king, bowing with his face to the earth, and said: Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said to him: To buy the thrashingfloor of thee, and build an altar to the Lord, that the plague, which rageth among the people, may cease.
verses.textLatin: et egressus adoravit regem prono vultu in terram, et ait: Quid causæ est ut veniat dominus meus rex ad servum suum? Cui David ait: Ut emam a te aream, et ædificem altare Domino, et cesset interfectio quæ grassatur in populo.

verses.text: And Areuna said to David: Let my lord the king take, and offer, as it seemeth good to him: thou hast here oxen for a holocaust, and the wain, and the yokes of the oxen for wood.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Areuna ad David: Accipiat, et offerat dominus meus rex sicut placet ei: habes boves in holocaustum, et plaustrum, et juga boum in usum lignorum.

verses.text: All these things Areuna as a king gave to the king: and Areuna said to the king: The Lord thy God receive thy vow.
verses.textLatin: Omnia dedit Areuna rex regi: dixitque Areuna ad regem: Dominus Deus tuus suscipiat votum tuum.

verses.text: And the king answered him, and said: Nay, but I will buy it of thee at a price, and I will not offer to the Lord my God holocausts free cost. So David bought the floor, and the oxen, for fifty sicles of silver:
verses.textLatin: Cui respondens rex, ait: Nequaquam ut vis, sed emam pretio a te, et non offeram Domino Deo meo holocausta gratuita. Emit ergo David aream, et boves, argenti siclis quinquaginta:

verses.text: And David built there an altar to the Lord, and offered holocausts and peace offerings: and the Lord became merciful to the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
verses.textLatin: et ædificavit ibi David altare Domino, et obtulit holocausta et pacifica: et propitiatus est Dominus terræ, et cohibita est plaga ab Israël.

verses.text: Now  king David was old, and advanced in years: and when he was covered with clothes, he was not warm.
verses.textLatin: Et rex David senuerat, habebatque ætatis plurimos dies: cumque operiretur vestibus, non calefiebat.

verses.text: His servants therefore said to him: Let us seek for our lord the king, a young virgin, and let her stand before the king, and cherish him, and sleep in his bosom, and warm our lord the king.
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt ergo ei servi sui: Quæramus domino nostro regi adolescentulam virginem, et stet coram rege, et foveat eum, dormiatque in sinu suo, et calefaciat dominum nostrum regem.

verses.text: So they sought a beautiful young woman in all the coasts of Israel, and they found Abisag a Sunamitess, and brought her to the king.
verses.textLatin: Quæsierunt igitur adolescentulam speciosam in omnibus finibus Israël, et invenerunt Abisag Sunamitidem, et adduxerunt eam ad regem.

verses.text: And the damsel was exceeding beautiful, and she slept with the king: and served him, but the king did not know her.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem puella pulchra nimis, dormiebatque cum rege, et ministrabat ei: rex vero non cognovit eam.

verses.text: And Adonias the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying: I will be king. And he made himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
verses.textLatin: Adonias autem filius Haggith elevabatur, dicens: Ego regnabo. Fecitque sibi currus et equites, et quinquaginta viros qui currerent ante eum.

verses.text: Neither did his father rebuke him at any time, saying: Why hast thou done this? And he also was very beautiful, the next in birth after Absalom.
verses.textLatin: Nec corripuit eum pater suus aliquando, dicens: Quare hoc fecisti? Erat autem et ipse pulcher valde, secundus natu post Absalom.

verses.text: And he conferred with Joab the son of Sarvia, and with Abiathar the priest, who furthered Adonias’s side.
verses.textLatin: Et sermo ei cum Joab filio Sarviæ, et cum Abiathar sacerdote, qui adjuvabant partes Adoniæ.

verses.text: But Sadoc the priest, and Banaias the son of Joiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Semei, and Rei, and the strength of David’s army was not with Adonias.
verses.textLatin: Sadoc vero sacerdos, et Banaias filius Jojadæ, et Nathan propheta, et Semei et Rei, et robur exercitus David, non erat cum Adonia.

verses.text: And Adonias having slain rams and calves, and all fat cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which was near the fountain Rogel, invited all his brethren the king’s sons, and all the men of Juda, the king’s servants:
verses.textLatin: Immolatis ergo Adonias arietibus et vitulis, et universis pinguibus, juxta lapidem Zoheleth, qui erat vicinus fonti Rogel, vocavit universos fratres suos filios regis, et omnes viros Juda servos regis.

verses.text: But Nathan the prophet, and Banaias, and all the valiant men, and Solomon his brother, he invited not.
verses.textLatin: Nathan autem prophetam, et Banaiam, et robustos quosque, et Salomonem fratrem suum non vocavit.

verses.text: And Nathan said to Bethsabee the mother of Solomon: Hast thou not heard that Adonias the son of Haggith reigneth, and our lord David knoweth it not?
verses.textLatin: Dixit itaque Nathan ad Bethsabee matrem Salomonis: Num audisti quod regnaverit Adonias filius Haggith, et dominus noster David hoc ignorat?

verses.text: Now then come, take my counsel and save thy life, and the life of thy son Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo veni, accipe consilium a me, et salva animam tuam, filiique tui Salomonis.

verses.text: Go, and get thee in to king David, and say to him: Didst not thou, my lord O king, swear to me thy handmaid, saying: Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne? why then doth Adonias reign?
verses.textLatin: Vade, et ingredere ad regem David, et dic ei: Nonne tu, domine mi rex, jurasti mihi ancillæ tuæ, dicens: Salomon filius tuus regnabit post me, et ipse sedebit in solio meo? quare ergo regnat Adonias?

verses.text: And while thou art yet speaking there with the king, I will come in after thee, and will fill up thy words.
verses.textLatin: Et adhuc ibi te loquente cum rege, ego veniam post te, et complebo sermones tuos.

verses.text: So Bethsabee went in to the king into the chamber: now the king was very old, and Abisag the Sunamitess ministered to him.
verses.textLatin: Ingressa est itaque Bethsabee ad regem in cubiculum: rex autem senuerat nimis, et Abisag Sunamitis ministrabat ei.

verses.text: Bethsabee bowed herself, and worshipped the king. And the king said to her: What is thy will?
verses.textLatin: Inclinavit se Bethsabee, et adoravit regem. Ad quam rex: Quid tibi, inquit, vis?

verses.text: She answered and said: My lord, thou didst swear to thy handmaid by the Lord thy God, saying: Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.
verses.textLatin: Quæ respondens, ait: Domine mi, tu jurasti per Dominum Deum tuum ancillæ tuæ: Salomon filius tuus regnabit post me, et ipse sedebit in solio meo.

verses.text: And behold now Adonias reigneth, and thou, my lord the king, knowest nothing of it.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce nunc Adonias regnat, te, domine mi rex, ignorante.

verses.text: He hath killed oxen, and all fat cattle, and many rams, and invited all the king’s sons, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the general of the army: but Solomon thy servant he invited not.
verses.textLatin: Mactavit boves, et pinguia quæque, et arietes plurimos, et vocavit omnes filios regis, Abiathar quoque sacerdotem, et Joab principem militiæ: Salomonem autem servum tuum non vocavit.

verses.text: And now, my lord O king, the eyes of all Israel are upon thee, that thou shouldst tell them, who shall sit on thy throne, my lord the king, after thee.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen, domine mi rex, in te oculi respiciunt totius Israël, ut indices eis quis sedere debeat in solio tuo, domine mi rex, post te.

verses.text: Otherwise it shall come to pass, when my lord the king sleepeth with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders.
verses.textLatin: Eritque, cum dormierit dominus meus rex cum patribus suis, erimus ego et filius meus Salomon peccatores.

verses.text: As she was yet speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc illa loquente cum rege, Nathan propheta venit.

verses.text: And they told the king, saying: Nathan the prophet is here. And when he was come in before the king, and had worshipped, bowing down to the ground,
verses.textLatin: Et nuntiaverunt regi, dicentes: Adest Nathan propheta. Cumque introisset in conspectu regis, et adorasset eum pronus in terram,

verses.text: Nathan said: My lord O king, hast thou said: Let Adonias reign after me, and let him sit upon my throne?
verses.textLatin: dixit Nathan: Domine mi rex, tu dixisti: Adonias regnet post me, et ipse sedeat super thronum meum?

verses.text: Because he is gone down to day, and hath killed oxen, and fatlings, and many rams, and invited all the king’s sons, and the captains of the army, and Abiathar the priest: and they are eating and drinking before him, and saying: God save king Adonias:
verses.textLatin: Quia descendit hodie, et immolavit boves, et pinguia, et arietes plurimos, et vocavit universos filios regis et principes exercitus, Abiathar quoque sacerdotem, illisque vescentibus et bibentibus coram eo, et dicentibus: Vivat rex Adonias:

verses.text: But me thy servant, and Sadoc the priest, and Banaias the son of Joiada, and Solomon thy servant he hath not invited.
verses.textLatin: me servum tuum, et Sadoc sacerdotem, et Banaiam filium Jojadæ, et Salomonem famulum tuum non vocavit.

verses.text: Is this word come out from my lord the king, and hast thou not told me thy servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?
verses.textLatin: Numquid a domino meo rege exivit hoc verbum, et mihi non indicasti servo tuo quis sessurus esset super thronum domini mei regis post eum?

verses.text: And king David answered and said: Call to me Bethsabee. And when she was come in to the king, and stood before him,
verses.textLatin: Et respondit rex David, dicens: Vocate ad me Bethsabee. Quæ cum fuisset ingressa coram rege, et stetisset ante eum,

verses.text: The king swore and said: As the Lord liveth, who hath delivered my soul out of all distress,
verses.textLatin: juravit rex, et ait: Vivit Dominus, qui eruit animam meam de omni angustia,

verses.text: Even as I swore to thee by the Lord the God of Israel, saying: Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead, so will I do this day.
verses.textLatin: quia sicut juravi tibi per Dominum Deum Israël, dicens: Salomon filius tuus regnabit post me, et ipse sedebit super solium meum pro me: sic faciam hodie.

verses.text: And Bethsabee bowing with her face to the earth worshipped the king, saying: May my lord David live for ever.
verses.textLatin: Summissoque Bethsabee in terram vultu, adoravit regem, dicens: Vivat dominus meus David in æternum.

verses.text: King David also said: Call me Sadoc the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Banaias the son of Joiada. And when they were come in before the king,
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque rex David: Vocate mihi Sadoc sacerdotem, et Nathan prophetam, et Banaiam filium Jojadæ. Qui cum ingressi fuissent coram rege,

verses.text: He said to them: Take with you the servants of your lord, and set my son Solomon upon my mule: and bring him to Gihon.
verses.textLatin: dixit ad eos: Tollite vobiscum servos domini vestri, et imponite Salomonem filium meum super mulam meam, et ducite eum in Gihon.

verses.text: And let Sadoc the priest, and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel: and you shall sound the trumpet, and shall say: God save king Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Et ungat eum ibi Sadoc sacerdos et Nathan propheta in regem super Israël: et canetis buccina, atque dicetis: Vivat rex Salomon.

verses.text: And you shall come up after him, and he shall come, and shall sit upon my throne, and he shall reign in my stead: and I will appoint him to be ruler over Israel, and over Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et ascendetis post eum, et veniet, et sedebit super solium meum, et ipse regnabit pro me: illique præcipiam ut sit dux super Israël et super Judam.

verses.text: And Banaias the son of Joiada answered the king, saying: Amen: so say the Lord the God of my lord the king.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Banaias filius Jojadæ regi, dicens: Amen: sic loquatur Dominus Deus domini mei regis.

verses.text: As the Lord hath been with my lord the king, so be he with Solomon, and make his throne higher than the throne of my lord king David.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo fuit Dominus cum domino meo rege, sic sit cum Salomone, et sublimius faciat solium ejus a solio domini mei regis David.

verses.text: So Sadoc the priest, and Nathan the prophet went down, and Banaias the son of Joiada, and the Cerethi, and Phelethi: and they set Solomon upon the mule of king David, and brought him to Gihon.
verses.textLatin: Descendit ergo Sadoc sacerdos, et Nathan propheta, et Banaias filius Jojadæ, et Cerethi, et Phelethi: et imposuerunt Salomonem super mulam regis David, et adduxerunt eum in Gihon.

verses.text: And Sadoc the priest took a horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon: and they sounded the trumpet, and all the people said: God save king Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Sumpsitque Sadoc sacerdos cornu olei de tabernaculo, et unxit Salomonem: et cecinerunt buccina, et dixit omnis populus: Vivat rex Salomon.

verses.text: And all the multitude went up after him, and the people played with pipes, and rejoiced with a great joy, and the earth rang with the noise of their cry.
verses.textLatin: Et ascendit universa multitudo post eum, et populus canentium tibiis, et lætantium gaudio magno: et insonuit terra a clamore eorum.

verses.text: And Adonias, and all that were invited by him, heard it, and now the feast was at an end: Joab also hearing the sound of the trumpet, said: What meaneth this noise of the city in an uproar?
verses.textLatin: Audivit autem Adonias, et omnes qui invitati fuerant ab eo: jamque convivium finitum erat: sed et Joab, audita voce tubæ, ait: Quid sibi vult clamor civitatis tumultuantis?

verses.text: While he yet spoke, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came: and Adonias said to him: Come in, because thou art a valiant man, and bringest good news.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc illo loquente, Jonathas filius Abiathar sacerdotis venit: cui dixit Adonias: Ingredere, quia vir fortis es, et bona nuntians.

verses.text: And Jonathan answered Adonias: Not so: for our lord king David hath appointed Solomon king.
verses.textLatin: Responditque Jonathas Adoniæ: Nequaquam: dominus enim noster rex David regem constituit Salomonem:

verses.text: And hath sent with him Sadoc the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Banaias the son of Joiada, and the Cerethi, and the Phelethi, and they have set him upon the king’s mule.
verses.textLatin: misitque cum eo Sadoc sacerdotem, et Nathan prophetam, et Banaiam filium Jojadæ, et Cerethi, et Phelethi, et imposuerunt eum super mulam regis.

verses.text: And Sadoc the priest, and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon: and they are gone up from thence rejoicing, so that the city rang again: this is the noise that you have heard.
verses.textLatin: Unxeruntque eum Sadoc sacerdos et Nathan propheta regem in Gihon: et ascenderunt inde lætantes, et insonuit civitas: hæc est vox quam audistis.

verses.text: Moreover Solomon sitteth upon the throne of the kingdom,
verses.textLatin: Sed et Salomon sedet super solium regni.

verses.text: And the king’s servants going in have blessed our lord king David, saying: May God make the name of Solomon greater than thy name, and make his throne greater than thy throne. And the king adored in his bed:
verses.textLatin: Et ingressi servi regis benedixerunt domino nostro regi David, dicentes: Amplificet Deus nomen Salomonis super nomen tuum, et magnificet thronus ejus super thronum tuum. Et adoravit rex in lectulo suo:

verses.text: And he said: Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, who hath given this day one to sit on my throne, my eyes seeing it.
verses.textLatin: et locutus est: Benedictus Dominus Deus Israël, qui dedit hodie sedentem in solio meo, videntibus oculis meis.

verses.text: Then all the guests of Adonias were afraid, and they all arose and every man went his way.
verses.textLatin: Territi sunt ergo, et surrexerunt omnes qui invitati fuerant ab Adonia, et ivit unusquisque in viam suam.

verses.text: And Adonias fearing Solomon, arose, and went, and took hold on the horn of the altar.
verses.textLatin: Adonias autem timens Salomonem, surrexit, et abiit, tenuitque cornu altaris.

verses.text: And they told Solomon, saying: Behold Adonias, fearing king Solomon, hath taken hold of the horn of the altar, saying: Let king Solomon swear to me this day, that he will not kill his servant with the sword.
verses.textLatin: Et nuntiaverunt Salomoni, dicentes: Ecce Adonias timens regem Salomonem, tenuit cornu altaris, dicens: Juret mihi rex Salomon hodie, quod non interficiat servum suum gladio.

verses.text: And Solomon said: If he be a good man, there shall not so much as one hair of his head fall to the ground: but if evil be found in him, he shall die.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Salomon: Si fuerit vir bonus, non cadet ne unus quidem capillus ejus in terram: sin autem malum inventum fuerit in eo, morietur.

verses.text: Then king Solomon sent, and brought him out from the altar: and going in he worshipped king Solomon: and Solomon said to him: Go to thy house.
verses.textLatin: Misit ergo rex Salomon, et eduxit eum ab altari: et ingressus adoravit regem Salomonem: dixitque ei Salomon: Vade in domum tuam.

verses.text: And  the days of David drew nigh that he should die, and he charged his son Solomon, saying:
verses.textLatin: Appropinquaverunt autem dies David ut moreretur: præcepitque Salomoni filio suo, dicens:

verses.text: I am going the way of all flesh: take thou courage, and shew thyself a man.
verses.textLatin: Ego ingredior viam universæ terræ: confortare, et esto vir.

verses.text: And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and observe his ceremonies, and his precepts, and judgments, and testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses: that thou mayest understand all thou dost, and whithersoever thou shalt turn thyself:
verses.textLatin: Et observa custodias Domini Dei tui, ut ambules in viis ejus: ut custodias cæremonias ejus, et præcepta ejus, et judicia, et testimonia, sicut scriptum est in lege Moysi: ut intelligas universa quæ facis, et quocumque te verteris:

verses.text: That the Lord may confirm his words, which he hath spoken of me, saying: If thy children shall take heed to their ways, and shall walk before me in truth, with all their heart, and with all their soul, there shall not be taken away from thee a man on the throne of Israel.
verses.textLatin: ut confirmet Dominus sermones suos quos locutus est de me, dicens: Si custodierint filii tui vias suas, et ambulaverint coram me in veritate, in omni corde suo et in omni anima sua, non auferetur tibi vir de solio Israël.

verses.text: Thou knowest also what Joab the son of Sarvia hath done to me, what he did to the two captains of the army of Israel, to Abner the son of Ner, and to Amasa the son of Jether: whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace, and put the blood of war on his girdle that was about his loins, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
verses.textLatin: Tu quoque nosti quæ fecerit mihi Joab filius Sarviæ, quæ fecerit duobus principibus exercitus Israël, Abner filio Ner, et Amasæ filio Jether: quos occidit, et effudit sanguinem belli in pace, et posuit cruorem prælii in balteo suo qui erat circa lumbos ejus, et in calceamento suo quod erat in pedibus ejus.

verses.text: Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoary head go down to hell in peace.
verses.textLatin: Facies ergo juxta sapientiam tuam, et non deduces canitiem ejus pacifice ad inferos.

verses.text: But shew kindness to the sons of Berzellai the Galaadite, and let them eat at thy table: for they met me when I fled from the face of Absalom thy brother.
verses.textLatin: Sed et filiis Berzellai Galaaditis reddes gratiam, eruntque comedentes in mensa tua: occurrerunt enim mihi quando fugiebam a facie Absalom fratris tui.

verses.text: Thou hast also with thee Semei the son of Gera the son of Jemini of Bahurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse, when I went to the camp: but because he came down to meet me when I passed over the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying: I will not kill thee with a sword:
verses.textLatin: Habes quoque apud te Semei filium Gera filii Jemini de Bahurim, qui maledixit mihi maledictione pessima quando ibam ad castra: sed quia descendit mihi in occursum cum transirem Jordanem, et juravi ei per Dominum, dicens: Non te interficiam gladio:

verses.text: Do not thou hold him guiltless. But thou art a wise man, and knowest what to do with him, and thou shalt bring down his grey hairs with blood to hell.
verses.textLatin: tu noli pati eum esse innoxium. Vir autem sapiens es, ut scias quæ facies ei: deducesque canos ejus cum sanguine ad inferos.

verses.text: So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David.
verses.textLatin: Dormivit igitur David cum patribus suis, et sepultus est in civitate David.

verses.text: And the days that David reigned in Israel, were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, in Jerusalem thirty-three.
verses.textLatin: Dies autem quibus regnavit David super Israël, quadraginta anni sunt: in Hebron regnavit septem annis; in Jerusalem, triginta tribus.

verses.text: And Solomon sat upon the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was strengthened exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Salomon autem sedit super thronum David patris sui, et firmatum est regnum ejus nimis.

verses.text: And Adonias the son of Haggith came to Bethsabee the mother of Solomon. And she said to him: Is thy coming peaceable? he answered: Peaceable.
verses.textLatin: Et ingressus est Adonias filius Haggith ad Bethsabee matrem Salomonis. Quæ dixit ei: Pacificusne est ingressus tuus? Qui respondit: Pacificus.

verses.text: And he added: I have a word to speak with thee. She said to him: Speak. And he said:
verses.textLatin: Addiditque: Sermo mihi est ad te. Cui ait: Loquere. Et ille:

verses.text: Thou knowest that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel had preferred me to be their king: but the kingdom is transferred, and is become my brother’s: for it was appointed him by the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Tu, inquit, nosti, quia meum erat regnum, et me præposuerat omnis Israël sibi in regem: sed translatum est regnum, et factum est fratris mei: a Domino enim constitutum est ei.

verses.text: Now therefore I ask one petition of thee: turn not away my face. And she said to him: Say on.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo petitionem unam precor a te: ne confundas faciem meam. Quæ dixit ad eum: Loquere.

verses.text: And he said: I pray thee speak to king Solomon (for he cannot deny thee any thing) to give me Abisag the Sunamitess to wife.
verses.textLatin: Et ille ait: Precor ut dicas Salomoni regi (neque enim negare tibi quidquam potest) ut det mihi Abisag Sunamitidem uxorem.

verses.text: And Bethsabee said: Well, I will speak for thee to the king.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Bethsabee: Bene: ego loquar pro te regi.

verses.text: Then Bethsabee came to king Solomon, to speak to him for Adonias: and the king arose to meet her, and bowed to her, and sat down upon his throne: and a throne was set for the king’s mother, and she sat on his right hand.
verses.textLatin: Venit ergo Bethsabee ad regem Salomonem ut loqueretur ei pro Adonia: et surrexit rex in occursum ejus, adoravitque eam, et sedit super thronum suum: positusque est thronus matri regis, quæ sedit ad dexteram ejus.

verses.text: And she said to him: I desire one small petition of thee, do not put me to confusion. And the king said to her: My mother, ask: for I must not turn away thy face.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei: Petitionem unam parvulam ego deprecor a te: ne confundas faciem meam. Et dixit ei rex: Pete, mater mea: neque enim fas est ut avertam faciem tuam.

verses.text: And she said: Let Abisag the Sunamitess be given to Adonias thy brother to wife.
verses.textLatin: Quæ ait: Detur Abisag Sunamitis Adoniæ fratri tuo uxor.

verses.text: And king Solomon answered, and said to his mother: Why dost thou ask Abisag the Sunamitess for Adonias? ask for him also the kingdom: for he is my elder brother, and hath Abiathar the priest, and Joab the son of Sarvia.
verses.textLatin: Responditque rex Salomon, et dixit matri suæ: Quare postulas Abisag Sunamitidem Adoniæ? postula ei et regnum: ipse est enim frater meus major me, et habet Abiathar sacerdotem, et Joab filium Sarviæ.

verses.text: Then king Solomon swore by the Lord, saying: So and so may God do to me, and add more, if Adonias hath not spoken this word against his own life.
verses.textLatin: Juravit itaque rex Salomon per Dominum, dicens: Hæc faciat mihi Deus, et hæc addat, quia contra animam suam locutus est Adonias verbum hoc.

verses.text: And now as the Lord liveth, who hath established me, and placed me upon the throne of David my father, and who hath made me a house, as he promised, Adonias shall be put to death this day.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc vivit Dominus, qui firmavit me, et collocavit me super solium David patris mei, et qui fecit mihi domum, sicut locutus est, quia hodie occidetur Adonias.

verses.text: And king Solomon sent by the hand of Banaias the son of Joiada, who slew him, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Misitque rex Salomon per manum Banaiæ filii Jojadæ, qui interfecit eum, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And the king said also to Abiathar the priest: Go to Anathoth to thy lands, for indeed thou art worthy of death: but I will not at this time put thee to death, because thou didst carry the ark of the Lord God before David my father, and hast endured trouble in all the troubles my father endured.
verses.textLatin: Abiathar quoque sacerdoti dixit rex: Vade in Anathoth ad agrum tuum: equidem vir mortis es: sed hodie te non interficiam, quia portasti arcam Domini Dei coram David patre meo, et sustinuisti laborem in omnibus in quibus laboravit pater meus.

verses.text: So Solomon cast out Abiathar, from being the priest of the Lord, that the word of the Lord might be fulfilled, which he spoke concerning the house of Heli in Silo.
verses.textLatin: Ejecit ergo Salomon Abiathar ut non esset sacerdos Domini, ut impleretur sermo Domini quem locutus est super domum Heli in Silo.

verses.text: And the news came to Joab, because Joab had turned after Adonias, and had not turned after Solomon: and Joab fled into the tabernacle of the Lord and laid hold on the horn of the altar.
verses.textLatin: Venit autem nuntius ad Joab, quod Joab declinasset post Adoniam, et post Salomonem non declinasset: fugit ergo Joab in tabernaculum Domini, et apprehendit cornu altaris.

verses.text: And it was told king Solomon, that Joab was fled into the tabernacle of the Lord, and was by the altar: and Solomon sent Banaias the son of Joiada, saying: Go, kill him.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiatumque est regi Salomoni quod fugisset Joab in tabernaculum Domini, et esset juxta altare: misitque Salomon Banaiam filium Jojadæ, dicens: Vade, interfice eum.

verses.text: And Banaias came to the tabernacle of the Lord, and said to him: Thus saith the king: Come forth. And he said: I will not come forth, but here I will die. Banaias brought word back to the king, saying: Thus saith Joab, and thus he answered me.
verses.textLatin: Et venit Banaias ad tabernaculum Domini, et dixit ei: Hæc dicit rex: Egredere. Qui ait: Non egrediar, sed hic moriar. Renuntiavit Banaias regi sermonem, dicens: Hæc locutus est Joab, et hæc respondit mihi.

verses.text: And the king said to him: Do as he hath said: and kill him, and bury him, and thou shalt remove the innocent blood which hath been shed by Joab, from me, and from the house of my father.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei rex: Fac sicut locutus est, et interfice eum, et sepeli: et amovebis sanguinem innocentem qui effusus est a Joab, a me, et a domo patris mei.

verses.text: And the Lord shall return his blood upon his own head, because he murdered two men, just and better than himself: and slew them with the sword, my father David not knowing it, Abner the son of Ner, general of the army of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, general of the army of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et reddet Dominus sanguinem ejus super caput ejus, quia interfecit duos viros justos, melioresque se: et occidit eos gladio, patre meo David ignorante, Abner filium Ner principem militiæ Israël, et Amasam filium Jether principem exercitus Juda:

verses.text: And their blood shall return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever. But to David and his seed and his house, and to his throne be peace for ever from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et revertetur sanguis illorum in caput Joab, et in caput seminis ejus in sempiternum. David autem et semini ejus, et domui, et throno illius, sit pax usque in æternum a Domino.

verses.text: So Banaias the son of Joiada went up, and setting upon him slew him, and he was buried in his house in the desert.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit itaque Banaias filius Jojadæ, et aggressus eum interfecit: sepultusque est in domo sua in deserto.

verses.text: And the king appointed Banaias the son of Joiada in his room over the army, and Sadoc the priest he put in the place of Abiathar.
verses.textLatin: Et constituit rex Banaiam filium Jojadæ pro eo super exercitum, et Sadoc sacerdotem posuit pro Abiathar.

verses.text: The king also sent, and called for Semei, and said to him: Build thee a house in Jerusalem, and dwell there: and go not out from thence any whither.
verses.textLatin: Misit quoque rex, et vocavit Semei: dixitque ei: Ædifica tibi domum in Jerusalem, et habita ibi: et non egredieris inde huc atque illuc.

verses.text: For on what day soever thou shalt go out, and shalt pass over the brook Cedron, know that thou shalt be put to death: thy blood shall be upon thy own head:
verses.textLatin: Quacumque autem die egressus fueris, et transieris torrentem Cedron, scito te interficiendum: sanguis tuus erit super caput tuum.

verses.text: And Semei said to the king: The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so will thy servant do. And Semei dwelt in Jerusalem, many days.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Semei regi: Bonus sermo: sicut locutus est dominus meus rex, sic faciet servus tuus. Habitavit itaque Semei in Jerusalem diebus multis.

verses.text: And it came to pass after three years, that the servants of Semei ran away to Achis the son of Maacha the king of Geth: and it was told Semei that his servants were gone to Geth.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem post annos tres ut fugerent servi Semei ad Achis filium Maacha regem Geth: nuntiatumque est Semei quod servi ejus issent in Geth.

verses.text: And Semei arose, and saddled his ass, and went to Achis to Geth to seek his servants, and he brought them out of Geth.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit Semei, et stravit asinum suum, ivitque ad Achis in Geth ad requirendum servos suos, et adduxit eos de Geth.

verses.text: And it was told Solomon that Semei had gone from Jerusalem to Geth, and was come back.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiatum est autem Salomoni quod isset Semei in Geth de Jerusalem, et rediisset.

verses.text: And sending he called for him, and said to him: Did I not protest to thee by the Lord, and tell thee before: On what day soever thou shalt go out and walk abroad any whither, know that thou shalt die? And thou answeredst me: The word that I have heard is good.
verses.textLatin: Et mittens vocavit eum, dixitque illi: Nonne testificatus sum tibi per Dominum, et prædixi tibi: Quacumque die egressus ieris huc et illuc, scito te esse moriturum: et respondisti mihi: Bonus sermo, quem audivi?

verses.text: Why then hast thou not kept the oath of the Lord, and the commandment that I laid upon thee?
verses.textLatin: quare ergo non custodisti jusjurandum Domini, et præceptum quod præceperam tibi?

verses.text: And the king said to Semei: Thou knowest all the evil, of which thy heart is conscious, which thou didst to David my father: the Lord hath returned thy wickedness upon thy own head:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque rex ad Semei: Tu nosti omne malum cujus tibi conscium est cor tuum, quod fecisti David patri meo: reddidit Dominus malitiam tuam in caput tuum:

verses.text: And king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before the Lord for ever.
verses.textLatin: et rex Salomon benedictus, et thronus David erit stabilis coram Domino usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: So the king commanded Banaias the son of Joiada: and he went out and struck him, and he died.
verses.textLatin: Jussit itaque rex Banaiæ filio Jojadæ, qui egressus, percussit eum, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And  the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon, and he made affinity with Pharao the king of Egypt: for he took his daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the Lord, and the wall of Jerusalem round about.
verses.textLatin: Confirmatum est igitur regnum in manu Salomonis, et affinitate conjunctus est Pharaoni regi Ægypti: accepit namque filiam ejus, et adduxit in civitatem David, donec compleret ædificans domum suam, et domum Domini, et murum Jerusalem per circuitum.

verses.text: But yet the people sacrificed in the high places: for there was no temple built to the name of the Lord until that day.
verses.textLatin: Attamen populus immolabat in excelsis: non enim ædificatum erat templum nomini Domini usque in diem illum.

verses.text: And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the precepts of David his father, only he sacrificed in the high places: and burnt incense.
verses.textLatin: Dilexit autem Salomon Dominum, ambulans in præceptis David patris sui, excepto quod in excelsis immolabat, et accendebat thymiama.

verses.text: He went therefore to Gabaon, to sacrifice there: for that was the great high place: a thousand victims for holocausts did Solomon offer upon that altar in Gabaon.
verses.textLatin: Abiit itaque in Gabaon, ut immolaret ibi: illud quippe erat excelsum maximum: mille hostias in holocaustum obtulit Salomon super altare illud in Gabaon.

verses.text: And the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, saying: Ask what thou wilt that I should give thee.
verses.textLatin: Apparuit autem Dominus Salomoni per somnium nocte, dicens: Postula quod vis ut dem tibi.

verses.text: And Solomon said: Thou hast shewn great mercy to thy servant David my father, even as he walked before thee in truth, and justice, and an upright heart with thee: and thou hast kept thy great mercy for him, and hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Salomon: Tu fecisti cum servo tuo David patre meo misericordiam magnam, sicut ambulavit in conspectu tuo in veritate et justitia, et recto corde tecum: custodisti ei misericordiam tuam grandem, et dedisti ei filium sedentem super thronum ejus, sicut est hodie.

verses.text: And now, O Lord God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a child, and know not how to go out and come in.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc Domine Deus, tu regnare fecisti servum tuum pro David patre meo: ego autem sum puer parvulus, et ignorans egressum et introitum meum.

verses.text: And thy servant is in the midst of the people which thou hast chosen, an immense people, which cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
verses.textLatin: Et servus tuus in medio est populi quem elegisti, populi infiniti, qui numerari et supputari non potest præ multitudine.

verses.text: Give therefore to thy servant an understanding heart, to judge thy people, and discern between good and evil. For who shall be able to judge this people, thy people which is so numerous?
verses.textLatin: Dabis ergo servo tuo cor docile, ut populum tuum judicare possit, et discernere inter bonum et malum. Quis enim poterit judicare populum istum, populum tuum hunc multum?

verses.text: And the word was pleasing to the Lord that Solomon had asked such a thing.
verses.textLatin: Placuit ergo sermo coram Domino, quod Salomon postulasset hujuscemodi rem.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Solomon: Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life or riches, nor the lives of thy enemies, but hast asked for thyself wisdom to discern judgment,
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus Salomoni: Quia postulasti verbum hoc, et non petisti tibi dies multos, nec divitias, aut animas inimicorum tuorum, sed postulasti tibi sapientiam ad discernendum judicium:

verses.text: Behold I have done for thee according to thy words, and have given thee a wise and understanding heart, insomuch that there hath been no one like thee before thee, nor shall arise after thee.
verses.textLatin: ecce feci tibi secundum sermones tuos, et dedi tibi cor sapiens et intelligens, in tantum ut nullus ante te similis tui fuerit, nec post te surrecturus sit.

verses.text: Yea and the things also which thou didst not ask, I have given thee: to wit, riches and glory, so that no one hath been like thee among the kings in all days heretofore.
verses.textLatin: Sed et hæc quæ non postulasti, dedi tibi: divitias scilicet, et gloriam, ut nemo fuerit similis tui in regibus cunctis retro diebus.

verses.text: And if thou wilt walk in my ways, and keep my precepts, and my commandments, as thy father walked, I will lengthen thy days.
verses.textLatin: Si autem ambulaveris in viis meis, et custodieris præcepta mea et mandata mea, sicut ambulavit pater tuus, longos faciam dies tuos.

verses.text: And Solomon awaked, and perceived that it was a dream: and when he was come to Jerusalem, he stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered holocausts, and sacrificed victims of peace offerings, and made a great feast for all his servants.
verses.textLatin: Igitur evigilavit Salomon, et intellexit quod esset somnium: cumque venisset Jerusalem, stetit coram arca fœderis Domini, et obtulit holocausta, et fecit victimas pacificas, et grande convivium universis famulis suis.

verses.text: Then there came two women that were harlots, to the king, and stood before him:
verses.textLatin: Tunc venerunt duæ mulieres meretrices ad regem, steteruntque coram eo:

verses.text: And one of them said: I beseech thee, my lord, I and this woman dwelt in one house, and I was delivered of a child with her in the chamber.
verses.textLatin: quarum una ait: Obsecro, mi domine: ego et mulier hæc habitabamus in domo una, et peperi apud eam in cubiculo.

verses.text: And the third day, after that I was delivered, she also was delivered, and we were together, and no other person with us in the house, only we two.
verses.textLatin: Tertia autem die postquam ego peperi, peperit et hæc: et eramus simul, nullusque alius nobiscum in domo, exceptis nobis duabus.

verses.text: And this woman’s child died in the night: for in her sleep she overlaid him.
verses.textLatin: Mortuus est autem filius mulieris hujus nocte: dormiens quippe oppressit eum.

verses.text: And rising in the dead time of the night, she took my child from my side, while I thy handmaid was asleep, and laid it in her bosom: and laid her dead child in my bosom.
verses.textLatin: Et consurgens intempestæ noctis silentio, tulit filium meum de latere meo, ancillæ tuæ dormientis, et collocavit in sinu suo: suum autem filium, qui erat mortuus, posuit in sinu meo.

verses.text: And when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold it was dead: but considering him more diligently when it was clear day, I found that it was not mine which I bore.
verses.textLatin: Cumque surrexissem mane ut darem lac filio meo, apparuit mortuus: quem diligentius intuens clara luce, deprehendi non esse meum quem genueram.

verses.text: And the other woman answered: It is not so as thou sayest, but thy child is dead, and mine is alive. On the contrary she said: Thou liest: for my child liveth, and thy child is dead. And in this manner they strove before the king.
verses.textLatin: Responditque altera mulier: Non est ita ut dicis, sed filius tuus mortuus est, meus autem vivit. E contrario illa dicebat: Mentiris: filius quippe meus vivit, et filius tuus mortuus est. Atque in hunc modum contendebant coram rege.

verses.text: Then said the king: The one saith, My child is alive, and thy child is dead. And the other answereth: Nay, but thy child is dead, and mine liveth.
verses.textLatin: Tunc rex ait: Hæc dicit: Filius meus vivit, et filius tuus mortuus est: et ista respondit: Non, sed filius tuus mortuus est, meus autem vivit.

verses.text: The king therefore said: Bring me a sword. And when they had brought a sword before the king,
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo rex: Afferte mihi gladium. Cumque attulissent gladium coram rege,

verses.text: Divide, said he, the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.
verses.textLatin: Dividite, inquit, infantem vivum in duas partes, et date dimidiam partem uni, et dimidiam partem alteri.

verses.text: But the woman whose child was alive, said to the king, (for her bowels were moved upon her child,) I beseech thee, my lord, give her the child alive, and do not kill it. But the other said: Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem mulier, cujus filius erat vivus, ad regem (commota sunt quippe viscera ejus super filio suo): Obsecro, domine, date illi infantem vivum, et nolite interficere eum. E contrario illa dicebat: Nec mihi nec tibi sit, sed dividatur.

verses.text: The king answered, and said: Give the living child to this woman, and let it not be killed, for she is the mother thereof.
verses.textLatin: Respondit rex, et ait: Date huic infantem vivum, et non occidatur: hæc est enim mater ejus.

verses.text: And all Israel heard the judgment which the king had judged, and they feared the king, seeing that the wisdom of God was in him to do judgment.
verses.textLatin: Audivit itaque omnis Israël judicium quod judicasset rex, et timuerunt regem, videntes sapientiam Dei esse in eo ad faciendum judicium.

verses.text: And  king Solomon reigned over all Israel:
verses.textLatin: Erat autem rex Salomon regnans super omnem Israël:

verses.text: And these were the princes which he had: Azarias the son of Sadoc the priest:
verses.textLatin: et hi principes quos habebat: Azarias filius Sadoc sacerdotis:

verses.text: Elihoreph, and Ahia, the sons of Sisa, scribes: Josaphat the son of Ahilud, recorder:
verses.textLatin: Elihoreph et Ahia filii Sisa scribæ: Josaphat filius Ahilud a commentariis:

verses.text: Banaias the son of Joiada, over the army: and Sadoc and Abiathar priests.
verses.textLatin: Banaias filius Jojadæ super exercitum: Sadoc autem et Abiathar sacerdotes:

verses.text: Azarias the son of Nathan, over them that were about the king: Zabud, the son of Nathan the priest, the king’s friend:
verses.textLatin: Azarias filius Nathan super eos qui assistebant regi: Zabud filius Nathan sacerdos, amicus regis:

verses.text: And Ahisar governor of the house: and Adoniram the son of Abda over the tribute.
verses.textLatin: et Ahisar præpositus domus: et Adoniram filius Abda super tributa.

verses.text: And Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, who provided victuals for the king and for his household: for every one provided necessaries, each man his month in the year.
verses.textLatin: Habebat autem Salomon duodecim præfectos super omnem Israël, qui præbebant annonam regi et domui ejus: per singulos enim menses in anno, singuli necessaria ministrabant.

verses.text: And these are their names: Benhur, in mount Ephraim,
verses.textLatin: Et hæc nomina eorum: Benhur in monte Ephraim.

verses.text: Bendecar, in Macces, and in Salebim, and in Bethsames, and in Elon, and in Bethanan.
verses.textLatin: Bendecar in Macces, et in Salebim, et in Bethsames, et in Elon, et in Bethanan.

verses.text: Benhesed in Aruboth: his was Socho, and all the land of Epher.
verses.textLatin: Benhesed in Aruboth: ipsius erat Socho, et omnis terra Epher.

verses.text: Benabinadab, to whom belonged all Nephath-Dor, he had Tapheth the daughter of Solomon to wife.
verses.textLatin: Benabinadab, cujus omnis Nephath Dor: Tapheth filiam Salomonis habebat uxorem.

verses.text: Bana the son of Ahilud, who governed Thanac and Mageddo, and all Bethsan, which is by Sarthana beneath Jezrael, from Bethsan unto Abelmehula over against Jecmaan.
verses.textLatin: Bana filius Ahilud regebat Thanac et Mageddo, et universam Bethsan, quæ est juxta Sarthana subter Jezrahel, a Bethsan usque Abelmehula e regione Jecmaan.

verses.text: Bengaber in Ramoth Galaad: he had the towns of Jair the son of Manasses in Galaad, he was chief in all the country of Argob, which is in Basan, threescore great cities with walls, and brazen bolts.
verses.textLatin: Bengaber in Ramoth Galaad: habebat Avothjair filii Manasse in Galaad: ipse præerat in omni regione Argob, quæ est in Basan, sexaginta civitatibus magnis atque muratis quæ habebant seras æreas.

verses.text: Abinadab the son of Addo was chief in Manaim.
verses.textLatin: Ahinadab filius Addo præerat in Manaim.

verses.text: Achimaas in Nephthali: he also had Basemath the daughter of Solomon to wife.
verses.textLatin: Achimaas in Nephthali: sed et ipse habebat Basemath filiam Salomonis in conjugio.

verses.text: Baana the son of Husi, in Aser and in Baloth.
verses.textLatin: Baana filius Husi in Aser, et in Baloth.

verses.text: Josaphat the son of Pharue, in Issachar.
verses.textLatin: Josaphat filius Pharue in Issachar.

verses.text: Semei the son of Ela in Benjamin.
verses.textLatin: Semei filius Ela in Benjamin.

verses.text: Gaber the son of Uri, in the land of Galaad, in the land of Sehon the king of the Amorrhites and of Og the king of Basan, over all that were in that land.
verses.textLatin: Gaber filius Uri in terra Galaad, in terra Sehon regis Amorrhæi et Og regis Basan, super omnia quæ erant in illa terra.

verses.text: Juda and Israel were innumerable, as the sand of the sea in multitude: eating and drinking, and rejoicing.
verses.textLatin: Juda et Israël innumerabiles, sicut arena maris in multitudine: comedentes, et bibentes, atque lætantes.

verses.text: And Solomon had under him all the kingdoms from the river to the land of the Philistines, even to the border of Egypt: and they brought him presents, and served him, all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: Salomon autem erat in ditione sua, habens omnia regna a flumine terræ Philisthiim usque ad terminum Ægypti: offerentium sibi munera, et servientium ei cunctis diebus vitæ ejus.

verses.text: And the provision of Solomon for each day, was thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal,
verses.textLatin: Erat autem cibus Salomonis per dies singulos triginta cori similæ, et sexaginta cori farinæ,

verses.text: Ten fat oxen and twenty out of the pastures, and a hundred rams, besides venison of harts, roes, and buffles, and fatted fowls.
verses.textLatin: decem boves pingues, et viginti boves pascuales, et centum arietes, excepta venatione cervorum, caprearum, atque bubalorum, et avium altilium.

verses.text: For he had all the country which was beyond the river, from Thaphsa to Gazan, and all the kings of those countries: and he had peace on every side round about.
verses.textLatin: Ipse enim obtinebat omnem regionem quæ erat trans flumen, a Thaphsa usque ad Gazan, et cunctos reges illarum regionum: et habebat pacem ex omni parte in circuitu.

verses.text: And Juda and Israel dwelt without any fear, every one under his vine, and under his fig tree, from Dan to Bersabee, all the days of Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Habitabatque Juda et Israël absque timore ullo, unusquisque sub vite sua et sub ficu sua, a Dan usque Bersabee, cunctis diebus Salomonis.

verses.text: And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of chariot horses, and twelve thousand for the saddle.
verses.textLatin: Et habebat Salomon quadraginta millia præsepia equorum currilium, et duodecim millia equestrium.

verses.text: And the foresaid governors of the king fed them: and they furnished the necessaries also for king Solomon’s table, with great care in their time.
verses.textLatin: Nutriebantque eos supradicti regis præfecti: sed et necessaria mensæ regis Salomonis cum ingenti cura præbebant in tempore suo.

verses.text: They brought barley also and straw for the horses, and beasts, to the place where the king was, according as it was appointed them.
verses.textLatin: Hordeum quoque, et paleas equorum et jumentorum, deferebant in locum ubi erat rex, juxta constitutum sibi.

verses.text: And God gave to Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart as the sand that is on the sea shore.
verses.textLatin: Dedit quoque Deus sapientiam Salomoni, et prudentiam multam nimis, et latitudinem cordis quasi arenam quæ est in littore maris.

verses.text: And the wisdom of Solomon surpassed the wisdom of all the Orientals, and of the Egyptians,
verses.textLatin: Et præcedebat sapientia Salomonis sapientiam omnium Orientalium et Ægyptiorum,

verses.text: And he was wiser than all men: wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Dorda the sons of Mahol, and he was renowned in all nations round about.
verses.textLatin: et erat sapientior cunctis hominibus: sapientior Ethan Ezrahita, et Heman, et Chalcol, et Dorda filiis Mahol: et erat nominatus in universis gentibus per circuitum.

verses.text: Solomon also spoke three thousand parables: and his poems were a thousand and five.
verses.textLatin: Locutus est quoque Salomon tria millia parabolas: et fuerunt carmina ejus quinque et mille.

verses.text: And he treated about trees from the cedar that is in Libanus, unto the hyssop that cometh out of the wall: and he discoursed of beasts, and of fowls, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
verses.textLatin: Et disputavit super lignis a cedro quæ est in Libano, usque ad hyssopum quæ egreditur de pariete: et disseruit de jumentis, et volucribus, et reptilibus, et piscibus.

verses.text: And they came from all nations to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and from all the kings of the earth, who heard of his wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Et veniebant de cunctis populis ad audiendam sapientiam Salomonis, et ab universis regibus terræ qui audiebant sapientiam ejus.

verses.text: And  Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon: for he heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram had always been David’s friend.
verses.textLatin: Misit quoque Hiram rex Tyri servos suos ad Salomonem: audivit enim quod ipsum unxissent regem pro patre ejus: quia amicus fuerat Hiram David omni tempore.

verses.text: And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying:
verses.textLatin: Misit autem Salomon ad Hiram, dicens:

verses.text: Thou knowest the will of David my father, and that he could not build a house to the name of the Lord his God, because of the wars that were round about him, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet.
verses.textLatin: Tu scis voluntatem David patris mei, et quia non potuerit ædificare domum nomini Domini Dei sui propter bella imminentia per circuitum, donec daret Dominus eos sub vestigio pedum ejus.

verses.text: But now the Lord my God hath given me rest round about: and there is no adversary nor evil occurrence.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem requiem dedit Dominus Deus meus mihi per circuitum, et non est satan, neque occursus malus.

verses.text: Wherefore I purpose to build a temple to the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord spoke to David my father, saying: Thy son, whom I will set upon the throne in thy place, he shall build a house to my name.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem cogito ædificare templum nomini Domini Dei mei, sicut locutus est Dominus David patri meo, dicens: Filius tuus, quem dabo pro te super solium tuum, ipse ædificabit domum nomini meo.

verses.text: Give orders therefore that thy servants cut me down cedar trees out of Libanus, and let my servants be with thy servants: and I will give thee the hire of thy servants whatsoever thou wilt ask, for thou knowest how there is not among my people a man that has skill to hew wood like to the Sidonians.
verses.textLatin: Præcipe igitur ut præcidant mihi servi tui cedros de Libano, et servi mei sint cum servis tuis: mercedem autem servorum tuorum dabo tibi quamcumque petieris: scis enim quomodo non est in populo meo vir qui noverit ligna cædere sicut Sidonii.

verses.text: Now when Hiram had heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced exceedingly, and said: Blessed be the Lord God this day, who hath given to David a very wise son over this numerous people.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo audisset Hiram verba Salomonis, lætatus est valde, et ait: Benedictus Dominus Deus hodie, qui dedit David filium sapientissimum super populum hunc plurimum.

verses.text: And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying: I have heard all thou hast desired of me: and I will do all thy desire concerning cedar trees, and fir trees.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Hiram ad Salomonem, dicens: Audivi quæcumque mandasti mihi: ego faciam omnem voluntatem tuam in lignis cedrinis et abiegnis.

verses.text: My servants shall bring them down from Libanus to the sea: and I will put them together in floats in the sea, and convey them to the place, which thou shalt signify to me; and will land them there, and thou shalt receive them: and thou shalt allow me necessaries, to furnish food for my household.
verses.textLatin: Servi mei deponent ea de Libano ad mare, et ego componam ea in ratibus in mari usque ad locum quem significaveris mihi: et applicabo ea ibi, et tu tolles ea: præbebisque necessaria mihi, ut detur cibus domui meæ.

verses.text: So Hiram gave Solomon cedar trees, and fir trees, according to all his desire.
verses.textLatin: Itaque Hiram dabat Salomoni ligna cedrina, et ligna abiegna, juxta omnem voluntatem ejus.

verses.text: And Solomon allowed Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat, for provision for his house, and twenty measures of the purest oil: thus gave Solomon to Hiram every year.
verses.textLatin: Salomon autem præbebat Hiram coros tritici viginti millia in cibum domui ejus, et viginti coros purissimi olei: hæc tribuebat Salomon Hiram per singulos annos.

verses.text: And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon, as he promised him: and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they two made a league together.
verses.textLatin: Dedit quoque Dominus sapientiam Salomoni, sicut locutus est ei: et erat pax inter Hiram et Salomonem, et percusserunt ambo fœdus.

verses.text: And king Solomon chose workmen out of all Israel, and the levy was of thirty thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Elegitque rex Salomon operarios de omni Israël, et erat indictio triginta millia virorum.

verses.text: And he sent them to Libanus, ten thousand every month by turns, so that two months they were at home: and Adoniram was over this levy.
verses.textLatin: Mittebatque eos in Libanum, decem millia per menses singulos vicissim, ita ut duobus mensibus essent in domibus suis: et Adoniram erat super hujuscemodi indictione.

verses.text: And Solomon had seventy thousand to carry burdens, and eighty thousand to hew stones in the mountain:
