verses.textLatin: Tunc ingressus Tobias, indicavit universa hæc patri suo. Super quæ admiratus pater, rogavit ut introiret ad eum.

verses.text: And Tobias said: What manner of joy shall be to me, who sit in darkness, and see not the light of heaven?
verses.textLatin: Ingressus itaque salutavit eum, et dixit: Gaudium tibi sit semper.

verses.text: And the young man said to him: Be of good courage, thy cure from God is at hand.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Tobias: Quale gaudium mihi erit, qui in tenebris sedeo, et lumen cæli non video?

verses.text: And Tobias said to him: Canst thou conduct my son to Gabelus at Rages, a city of the Medes? and when thou shalt return, I will pay thee thy hire.
verses.textLatin: Cui ait juvenis: Forti animo esto: in proximo est ut a Deo cureris.

verses.text: And the angel said to him: I will conduct him thither, and bring him back to thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixit itaque illi Tobias: Numquid poteris perducere filium meum ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum? et cum redieris, restituam tibi mercedem tuam.

verses.text: And Tobias said to him: I pray thee, tell me, of what family, or what tribe art thou?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ei angelus: Ego ducam, et reducam eum ad te.

verses.text: And Raphael the angel answered: Dost thou seek the family of him thou hirest, or the hired servant himself to go with thy son?
verses.textLatin: Cui Tobias respondit: Rogo te, indica mihi de qua domo aut de qua tribu es tu.

verses.text: But lest I should make thee uneasy, I am Azarias the son of the great Ananias.
verses.textLatin: Cui Raphaël angelus dixit: Genus quæris mercenarii, an ipsum mercenarium qui cum filio tuo eat?

verses.text: And Tobias answered: Thou art of a great family. But I pray thee be not angry that I desired to know thy family.
verses.textLatin: sed ne forte sollicitum te reddam, ego sum Azarias Ananiæ magni filius.

verses.text: And the angel said to him: I will lead thy son safe, and bring him to thee again safe.
verses.textLatin: Et Tobias respondit: Ex magno genere es tu. Sed peto ne irascaris quod voluerim cognoscere genus tuum.

verses.text: And Tobias answering, said: May you have a good journey, and God be with you in your way, and his angel accompany you.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem illi angelus: Ego sanum ducam, et sanum tibi reducam filium tuum.

verses.text: Then all things being ready, that were to be carried in their journey, Tobias bade his father and his mother farewell, and they set out both together.
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Tobias, ait: Bene ambuletis, et sit Deus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum.

verses.text: And when they were departed, his mother began to weep, and to say: Thou hast taken the staff of our old age, and sent him away from us.
verses.textLatin: Tunc paratis omnibus quæ erant in via portanda, fecit Tobias vale patri suo et matri suæ, et ambulaverunt ambo simul.

verses.text: I wish the money for which thou hast sent him, had never been.
verses.textLatin: Cumque profecti essent, cœpit mater ejus flere, et dicere: Baculum senectutis nostræ tulisti, et transmisisti a nobis.

verses.text: For our poverty was sufficient for us, that we might account it as riches, that we saw our son.
verses.textLatin: Numquam fuisset ipsa pecunia, pro qua misisti eum:

verses.text: And Tobias said to her: Weep not, our son will arrive thither safe, and will return safe to us, and thy eyes shall see him.
verses.textLatin: sufficiebat enim nobis paupertas nostra, ut divitias computaremus hoc, quod videbamus filium nostrum.

verses.text: For I believe that the good angel of God doth accompany him, and doth order all things well that are done about him, so that he shall return to us with joy.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei Tobias: Noli flere: salvus perveniet filius noster, et salvus revertetur ad nos, et oculi tui videbunt illum.

verses.text: At these words his mother ceased weeping, and held her peace.
verses.textLatin: Credo enim quod angelus Dei bonus comitetur ei, et bene disponat omnia quæ circa eum geruntur, ita ut cum gaudio revertatur ad nos.

verses.text: And  Tobias went forward, and the dog followed him, and he lodged the first night by the river of Tigris.
verses.textLatin: Ad hanc vocem cessavit mater ejus flere, et tacuit.

verses.text: And he went out to wash his feet, and behold a monstrous fish came up to devour him.
verses.textLatin: Profectus est autem Tobias, et canis secutus est eum, et mansit prima mansione juxta fluvium Tigris.

verses.text: And Tobias being afraid of him, cried out with a loud voice, saying: Sir, he cometh upon me.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit ut lavaret pedes suos, et ecce piscis immanis exivit ad devorandum eum.

verses.text: And the angel said to him: Take him by the gill, and draw him to thee. And when he had done so, he drew him out upon the land, and he began to pant before his feet.
verses.textLatin: Quem expavescens Tobias clamavit voce magna, dicens: Domine, invadit me.

verses.text: Then the angel said to him: Take out the entrails of this fish, and lay up his heart, and his gall, and his liver for thee: for these are necessary for useful medicines.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ei angelus: Apprehende branchiam ejus, et trahe eum ad te. Quod cum fecisset, attraxit eum in siccum, et palpitare cœpit ante pedes ejus.

verses.text: And when he had done so, he roasted the flesh thereof, and they took it with them in the way: the rest they salted as much as might serve them, till they came to Rages the city of the Medes.
verses.textLatin: Tunc dixit ei angelus: Exentera hunc piscem, et cor ejus, et fel, et jecur repone tibi: sunt enim hæc necessaria ad medicamenta utiliter.

verses.text: Then Tobias asked the angel, and said to him: I beseech thee, brother Azarias, tell me what remedies are these things good for, which thou hast bid me keep of the fish?
verses.textLatin: Quod cum fecisset, assavit carnes ejus, et secum tulerunt in via: cetera salierunt, quæ sufficerent eis, quousque pervenirent in Rages civitatem Medorum.

verses.text: And the angel, answering, said to him: If thou put a little piece of its heart upon coals, the smoke thereof driveth away all kind of devils, either from man or from woman, so that they come no more to them.
verses.textLatin: Tunc interrogavit Tobias angelum, et dixit ei: Obsecro te, Azaria frater, ut dicas mihi quod remedium habebunt ista, quæ de pisce servare jussisti?

verses.text: And the gall is good for anointing the eyes, in which there is a white speck, and they shall be cured.
verses.textLatin: Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Cordis ejus particulam si super carbones ponas, fumus ejus extricat omne genus dæmoniorum sive a viro, sive a muliere, ita ut ultra non accedat ad eos.

verses.text: And Tobias said to him: Where wilt thou that we lodge?
verses.textLatin: Et fel valet ad ungendos oculos in quibus fuerit albugo, et sanabuntur.

verses.text: And the angel answering, said: Here is one whose name is Raguel, a near kinsman of thy tribe, and he hath a daughter named Sara, but he hath no son nor any other daughter beside her.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ei Tobias: Ubi vis ut maneamus?

verses.text: All his substance is due to thee, and thou must take her to wife.
verses.textLatin: Respondensque angelus, ait: Est hic Raguel nomine, vir propinquus de tribu tua, et hic habet filiam nomine Saram, sed neque masculum neque feminam ullam habet aliam præter eam.

verses.text: Ask her therefore of her father, and he will give her thee to wife.
verses.textLatin: Tibi debetur omnis substantia ejus, et oportet eam te accipere conjugem.

verses.text: Then Tobias answered, and said: I hear that she hath been given to seven husbands, and they all died: moreover I have heard, that a devil killed them.
verses.textLatin: Pete ergo eam a patre ejus, et dabit tibi eam in uxorem.

verses.text: Now I am afraid, lest the same thing should happen to me also: and whereas I am the only child of my parents, I should bring down their old age with sorrow to hell.
verses.textLatin: Tunc respondit Tobias, et dixit: Audio quia tradita est septem viris, et mortui sunt: sed et hoc audivi, quia dæmonium occidit illos.

verses.text: Then the angel Raphael said to him: Hear me, and I will shew thee who they are, over whom the devil can prevail.
verses.textLatin: Timeo ergo, ne forte et mihi hæc eveniant: et cum sim unicus parentibus meis, deponam senectutem illorum cum tristitia ad inferos.

verses.text: For they who in such manner receive matrimony, as to shut out God from themselves, and from their mind, and to give themselves to their lust, as the horse and mule, which have not understanding, over them the devil hath power.
verses.textLatin: Tunc angelus Raphaël dixit ei: Audi me, et ostendam tibi qui sunt, quibus prævalere potest dæmonium.

verses.text: But thou when thou shalt take her, go into the chamber, and for three days keep thyself continent from her, and give thyself to nothing else but to prayers with her.
verses.textLatin: Hi namque qui conjugium ita suscipiunt, ut Deum a se et a sua mente excludant, et suæ libidini ita vacent sicut equus et mulus quibus non est intellectus: habet potestatem dæmonium super eos.

verses.text: And on that night lay the liver of the fish on the fire, and the devil shall be driven away.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem cum acceperis eam, ingressus cubiculum, per tres dies continens esto ab ea, et nihil aliud nisi orationibus vacabis cum ea.

verses.text: But the second night thou shalt be admitted into the society of the holy Patriarchs.
verses.textLatin: Ipsa autem nocte, incenso jecore piscis, fugabitur dæmonium.

verses.text: And the third night thou shalt obtain a blessing that sound children may be born of you.
verses.textLatin: Secunda vero nocte in copulatione sanctorum patriarcharum admitteris.

verses.text: And when the third night is past, thou shalt take the virgin with the fear of the Lord, moved rather for love of children than for lust, that in the seed of Abraham thou mayst obtain a blessing in children.
verses.textLatin: Tertia autem nocte, benedictionem consequeris, ut filii ex vobis procreentur incolumes.

verses.text: And  they went in to Raguel, and Raguel received them with joy.
verses.textLatin: Transacta autem tertia nocte, accipies virginem cum timore Domini, amore filiorum magis quam libidine ductus, ut in semine Abrahæ benedictionem in filiis consequaris.

verses.text: And Raguel looking upon Tobias, said to Anna his wife: How like is this young man to my cousin?
verses.textLatin: Ingressi sunt autem ad Raguelem, et suscepit eos Raguel cum gaudio.

verses.text: And when he had spoken these words, he said: Whence are ye young men our brethren?
verses.textLatin: Intuensque Tobiam Raguel, dixit Annæ uxori suæ: Quam similis est juvenis iste consobrino meo!

verses.text: But they said: We are of the tribe of Nephtali, of the captivity of Ninive.
verses.textLatin: Et cum hæc dixisset, ait: Unde estis juvenes fratres nostri? At illi dixerunt: Ex tribu Nephthali sumus, ex captivitate Ninive.

verses.text: And Raguel said to them: Do you know Tobias my brother? And they said: We know him.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque illis Raguel: Nostis Tobiam fratrem meum? Qui dixerunt: Novimus.

verses.text: And when he was speaking many good things of him, the angel said to Raguel: Tobias concerning whom thou inquirest is this young man’s father.
verses.textLatin: Cumque multa bona loqueretur de eo, dixit angelus ad Raguelem: Tobias, de quo interrogas, pater istius est.

verses.text: And Raguel went to him, and kissed him with tears, and weeping upon his neck, said: A blessing be upon thee, my son, because thou art the son of a good and most virtuous man.
verses.textLatin: Et misit se Raguel, et cum lacrimis osculatus est eum, et plorans supra collum ejus

verses.text: And Anna his wife, and Sara their daughter wept.
verses.textLatin: dixit: Benedictio sit tibi, fili mi, quia boni et optimi viri filius es.

verses.text: And after they had spoken, Raguel commanded a sheep to be killed, and a feast to be prepared. And when he desired them to sit down to dinner,
verses.textLatin: Et Anna uxor ejus, et Sara ipsorum filia, lacrimatæ sunt.

verses.text: Tobias said: I will not eat nor drink here this day, unless thou first grant me my petition, and promise to give me Sara thy daughter.
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem locuti sunt, præcepit Raguel occidi arietem, et parari convivium. Cumque hortaretur eos discumbere ad prandium,

verses.text: Now when Raguel heard this he was afraid, knowing what had happened to those seven husbands, that went in unto her: and he began to fear lest it might happen to him also in like manner: and as he was in suspense, and gave no answer to his petition,
verses.textLatin: Tobias dixit: Hic ego hodie non manducabo neque bibam, nisi prius petitionem meam confirmes, et promittas mihi dare Saram filiam tuam.

verses.text: The angel said to him: Be not afraid to give her to this man, for to him who feareth God is thy daughter due to be his wife: therefore another could not have her.
verses.textLatin: Quo audito verbo Raguel expavit, sciens quid evenerit illis septem viris qui ingressi sunt ad eam: et timere cœpit ne forte et hunc similiter contingeret. Et cum nutaret, et non daret petenti ullum responsum,

verses.text: Then Raguel said: I doubt not but God hath regarded my prayers and tears in his sight.
verses.textLatin: dixit ei angelus: Noli timere dare eam isti, quoniam huic timenti Deum debetur conjux filia tua: propterea alius non potuit habere illam.

verses.text: And I believe he hath therefore made you come to me, that this maid might be married to one of her own kindred, according to the law of Moses: and now doubt not but I will give her to thee.
verses.textLatin: Tunc dixit Raguel: Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas in conspectu suo admiserit.

verses.text: And taking the right hand of his daughter, he gave it into the right hand of Tobias, saying: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you, and may he join you together, and fulfil his blessing in you.
verses.textLatin: Et credo quoniam ideo fecit vos venire ad me, ut ista conjungeretur cognationi suæ secundum legem Moysi: et nunc noli dubium gerere quod tibi eam tradam.

verses.text: And taking paper they made a writing of the marriage.
verses.textLatin: Et apprehendens dexteram filiæ suæ, dexteræ Tobiæ tradidit, dicens: Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob vobiscum sit, et ipse conjungat vos, impleatque benedictionem suam in vobis.

verses.text: And afterwards they made merry, blessing God.
verses.textLatin: Et accepta carta, fecerunt conscriptionem conjugii.

verses.text: And Raguel called to him Anna his wife, and bade her prepare another chamber.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc epulati sunt, benedicentes Deum.

verses.text: And she brought Sara her daughter in thither, and she wept.
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque Raguel ad se Annam uxorem suam, et præcepit ei ut præpararet alterum cubiculum.

verses.text: And she said to her: Be of good cheer, my daughter: the Lord of heaven give thee joy for the trouble thou hast undergone.
verses.textLatin: Et introduxit illuc Saram filiam suam, et lacrimata est.

verses.text: And  after they had supped, they brought in the young man to her.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ei: Forti animo esto, filia mea: Dominus cæli det tibi gaudium pro tædio quod perpessa es.

verses.text: And Tobias remembering the angel’s word, took out of his bag part of the liver, and laid it upon burning coals.
verses.textLatin: Postquam vero cœnaverunt, introduxerunt juvenem ad eam.

verses.text: Then the angel Raphael took the devil, and bound him in the desert of upper Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Recordatus itaque Tobias sermonum angeli, protulit de cassidili suo partem jecoris, posuitque eam super carbones vivos.

verses.text: Then Tobias exhorted the virgin, and said to her: Sara, arise, and let us pray to God to day, and to morrow, and the next day: because for these three nights we are joined to God: and when the third night is over, we will be in our own wedlock.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Raphaël angelus apprehendit dæmonium, et religavit illud in deserto superioris Ægypti.

verses.text: For we are the children of saints, and we must not be joined together like heathens that know not God.
verses.textLatin: Tunc hortatus est virginem Tobias, dixitque ei: Sara, exsurge, et deprecemur Deum hodie, et cras, et secundum cras: quia his tribus noctibus Deo jungimur; tertia autem transacta nocte, in nostro erimus conjugio.

verses.text: So they both arose, and prayed earnestly both together that health might be given them,
verses.textLatin: Filii quippe sanctorum sumus, et non possumus ita conjungi sicut gentes quæ ignorant Deum.

verses.text: And Tobias said: Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens and the earth, and the sea, and the fountains, and the rivers, and all thy creatures that are in them, bless thee.
verses.textLatin: Surgentes autem pariter, instanter orabant ambo simul, ut sanitas daretur eis.

verses.text: Thou madest Adam of the slime of the earth, and gavest him Eve for a helper.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Tobias: Domine Deus patrum nostrorum, benedicant te cæli et terræ, mareque et fontes, et flumina, et omnes creaturæ tuæ quæ in eis sunt.

verses.text: And now, Lord, thou knowest, that not for fleshly lust do I take my sister to wife, but only for the love of posterity, in which thy name may be blessed for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Tu fecisti Adam de limo terræ, dedistique ei adjutorium Hevam.

verses.text: Sara also said: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us, and let us grow old both together in health.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc Domine, tu scis quia non luxuriæ causa accipio sororem meam conjugem, sed sola posteritatis dilectione, in qua benedicatur nomen tuum in sæcula sæculorum.

verses.text: And it came to pass about the cockcrowing, Raguel ordered his servants to be called for, and they went with him together to dig a grave.
verses.textLatin: Dixit quoque Sara: Miserere nobis Domine, miserere nobis, et consenescamus ambo pariter sani.

verses.text: For he said: Lest perhaps it may have happened to him, in like manner as it did to the other seven husbands, that went in unto her.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est circa pullorum cantum, accersiri jussit Raguel servos suos, et abierunt cum eo pariter ut foderent sepulchrum.

verses.text: And when they had prepared the pit, Raguel went back to his wife, and said to her:
verses.textLatin: Dicebat enim: Ne forte simili modo evenerit ei, quo et ceteris illis septem viris qui sunt ingressi ad eam.

verses.text: Send one of thy maids, and let her see if he be dead, that I may bury him before it be day.
verses.textLatin: Cumque parassent fossam, reversus Raguel ad uxorem suam, dixit ei:

verses.text: So she sent one of her maidservants, who went into the chamber, and found them safe and sound, sleeping both together.
verses.textLatin: Mitte unam de ancillis tuis, et videat si mortuus est, ut sepeliam eum antequam illucescat dies.

verses.text: And returning she brought the good news: and Raguel and Anna his wife blessed the Lord,
verses.textLatin: At illa misit unam ex ancillis suis. Quæ ingressa cubiculum, reperit eos salvos et incolumes, secum pariter dormientes.

verses.text: And said: We bless thee, O Lord God of Israel, because it hath not happened as we suspected.
verses.textLatin: Et reversa nuntiavit bonum nuntium: et benedixerunt Dominum, Raguel videlicet et Anna uxor ejus,

verses.text: For thou hast shewn thy mercy to us, and hast shut out from us the enemy that persecuted us.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt: Benedicimus te, Domine Deus Israël, quia non contigit quemadmodum putabamus.

verses.text: And thou hast taken pity upon two only children. Make them, O Lord, bless thee more fully: and to offer up to thee a sacrifice of thy praise, and of their health, that all nations may know, that thou alone art God in all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Fecisti enim nobiscum misericordiam tuam, et exclusisti a nobis inimicum persequentem nos.

verses.text: And immediately Raguel commanded his servants, to fill up the pit they had made, before it was day.
verses.textLatin: Misertus es autem duobus unicis. Fac eos, Domine, plenius benedicere te, et sacrificium tibi laudis tuæ et suæ sanitatis offerre, ut cognoscat universitas gentium quia tu es Deus solus in universa terra.

verses.text: And he spoke to his wife to make ready a feast, and prepare all kind of provisions that are necessary for such as go a journey.
verses.textLatin: Statimque præcepit servis suis Raguel ut replerent fossam quam fecerant priusquam elucesceret.

verses.text: He caused also two fat kine, and four wethers to be killed, and a banquet to be prepared for all his neighbours, and all his friends.
verses.textLatin: Uxori autem suæ dixit ut instrueret convivium, et præpararet omnia quæ in cibos erant iter agentibus necessaria.

verses.text: And Raguel adjured Tobias, to abide with him two weeks.
verses.textLatin: Duas quoque pingues vaccas, et quatuor arietes, occidi fecit, et parari epulas omnibus vicinis suis, cunctisque amicis.

verses.text: And of all things which Raguel possessed, he gave one half to Tobias, and made a writing, that the half that remained should after their decease come also to Tobias.
verses.textLatin: Et adjuravit Raguel Tobiam ut duas hebdomadas moraretur apud se.

verses.text: Then  Tobias called the angel to him, whom he took to be a man, and said to him: Brother Azarias, I pray thee hearken to my words:
verses.textLatin: De omnibus autem quæ possidebat Raguel, dimidiam partem dedit Tobiæ, et fecit scripturam, ut pars dimidia quæ supererat, post obitum eorum Tobiæ dominio deveniret.

verses.text: If I should give myself to be thy servant I should not make a worthy return for thy care.
verses.textLatin: Tunc vocavit Tobias angelum ad se, quem quidem hominem existimabat, dixitque ei: Azaria frater, peto ut auscultes verba mea.

verses.text: However, I beseech thee, to take with thee beasts and servants, and to go to Gabelus to Rages the city of the Medes: and to restore to him his note of hand, and receive of him the money, and desire him to come to my wedding.
verses.textLatin: Si meipsum tradam tibi servum, non ero condignus providentiæ tuæ:

verses.text: For thou knowest that my father numbereth the days: and if I stay one day more, his soul will be afflicted.
verses.textLatin: tamen obsecro te ut assumas tibi animalia sive servitia, et vadas ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum, reddasque ei chirographum suum, et recipias ab eo pecuniam, et roges eum venire ad nuptias meas.

verses.text: And indeed thou seest how Raguel hath adjured me, whose adjuring I cannot despise.
verses.textLatin: Scis enim ipse quoniam numerat pater meus dies, et si tardavero una die plus, contristatur anima ejus.

verses.text: Then Raphael took four of Raguel’s servants, and two camels, and went to Rages the city of the Medes: and finding Gabelus, gave him his note of hand, and received of him all the money.
verses.textLatin: Et certe vides quomodo adjuravit me Raguel, cujus adjuramentum spernere non possum.

verses.text: And he told him concerning Tobias the son of Tobias, all that had been done: and made him come with him to the wedding.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Raphaël assumens quatuor ex servis Raguelis, et duos camelos, in Rages civitatem Medorum perrexit: et inveniens Gabelum, reddidit ei chirographum suum, et recepit ab eo omnem pecuniam.

verses.text: And when he was come into Raguel’s house he found Tobias sitting at the table: and he leaped up, and they kissed each other: and Gabelus wept, and blessed God,
verses.textLatin: Indicavitque ei de Tobia filio Tobiæ omnia quæ gesta sunt, fecitque eum secum venire ad nuptias.

verses.text: And said: The God of Israel bless thee, because thou art the son of a very good and just man, and that feareth God, and doth almsdeeds:
verses.textLatin: Cumque ingressus esset domum Raguelis, invenit Tobiam discumbentem: et exiliens, osculati sunt se invicem: et flevit Gabelus, benedixitque Deum,

verses.text: And may a blessing come upon thy wife and upon your parents.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Benedicat te Deus Israël, quia filius es optimi viri et justi, et timentis Deum, et eleemosynas facientis:

verses.text: And may you see your children, and your children’s children, unto the third and fourth generation: and may your seed be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigneth for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: et dicatur benedictio super uxorem tuam, et super parentes vestros,

verses.text: And when all had said, Amen, they went to the feast: but the marriage feast they celebrated also with the fear of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et videatis filios vestros, et filios filiorum vestrorum, usque in tertiam et quartam generationem: et sit semen vestrum benedictum a Deo Israël, qui regnat in sæcula sæculorum.

verses.text: But  as Tobias made longer stay upon occasion of the marriage, Tobias his father was solicitous, saying: Why thinkest thou doth my son tarry, or why is he detained there?
verses.textLatin: Cumque omnes dixissent: Amen: accesserunt ad convivium: sed et cum timore Domini nuptiarum convivium exercebant.

verses.text: Is Gabelus dead, thinkest thou, and no man will pay him the money?
verses.textLatin: Cum vero moras faceret Tobias, causa nuptiarum, sollicitus erat pater ejus Tobias, dicens: Putas quare moratur filius meus, aut quare detentus est ibi?

verses.text: And he began to be exceeding sad, both he and Anna his wife with him: and they began both to weep together: because their son did not return to them on the day appointed.
verses.textLatin: Putasne Gabelus mortuus est, et nemo reddet illi pecuniam?

verses.text: But his mother wept and was quite disconsolate, and said: Woe, woe is me, my son; why did we send thee to go to a strange country, the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life, the hope of our posterity?
verses.textLatin: Cœpit autem contristari nimis ipse, et Anna uxor ejus cum eo: et cœperunt ambo simul flere, eo quod die statuto minime reverteretur filius eorum ad eos.

verses.text: We having all things together in thee alone, ought not to have let thee go from us.
verses.textLatin: Flebat igitur mater ejus irremediabilibus lacrimis, atque dicebat: Heu, heu me, fili mi! ut quid te misimus peregrinari, lumen oculorum nostrorum, baculum senectutis nostræ, solatium vitæ nostræ, spem posteritatis nostræ?

verses.text: And Tobias said to her: Hold thy peace, and be not troubled, our son is safe: that man with whom we sent him is very trusty.
verses.textLatin: omnia simul in te uno habentes, te non debuimus dimittere a nobis.

verses.text: But she could by no means be comforted, but daily running out looked round about, and went into all the ways by which there seemed any hope he might return, that she might if possible see him coming afar off.
verses.textLatin: Cui dicebat Tobias: Tace, et noli turbari: sanus est filius noster: satis fidelis est vir ille, cum quo misimus eum.

verses.text: But Raguel said to his son in law: Stay here, and I will send a messenger to Tobias thy father, that thou art in health.
verses.textLatin: Illa autem nullo modo consolari poterat, sed quotidie exiliens circumspiciebat, et circuibat vias omnes per quas spes remeandi videbatur, ut procul videret eum, si fieri posset, venientem.

verses.text: And Tobias said to him: I know that my father and mother now count the days, and their spirit is grievously afflicted within them.
verses.textLatin: At vero Raguel dicebat ad generum suum: Mane hic, et ego mittam nuntium salutis de te ad Tobiam patrem tuum.

verses.text: And when Raguel had pressed Tobias with many words, and he by no means would hearken to him, he delivered Sara unto him, and half of all his substance in menservants, and womenservants, in cattle, in camels, and in kine, and in much money, and sent him away safe and joyful from him,
verses.textLatin: Cui Tobias ait: Ego novi quia pater meus et mater mea modo dies computant, et cruciatur spiritus eorum in ipsis.

verses.text: Saying: The holy angel of the Lord be with you in your journey, and bring you through safe, and that you may find all things well about your parents, and my eyes may see your children before I die.
verses.textLatin: Cumque verbis multis rogaret Raguel Tobiam, et ille eum nulla ratione vellet audire, tradidit ei Saram, et dimidiam partem omnis substantiæ suæ in pueris, in puellis, in pecudibus, in camelis, et in vaccis, et in pecunia multa: et salvum atque gaudentem dimisit eum a se,

verses.text: And the parents taking their daughter kissed her, and let her go:
verses.textLatin: dicens: Angelus Domini sanctus sit in itinere vestro, perducatque vos incolumes, et inveniatis omnia recte circa parentes vestros, et videant oculi mei filios vestros priusquam moriar.

verses.text: Admonishing her to honour her father and mother in law, to love her husband, to take care of the family, to govern the house, and to behave herself irreprehensibly.
verses.textLatin: Et apprehendentes parentes filiam suam, osculati sunt eam: et dimiserunt ire,

verses.text: And  as they were returning they came to Charan, which is in the midway to Ninive, the eleventh day.
verses.textLatin: monentes eam honorare soceros, diligere maritum, regere familiam, gubernare domum, et seipsam irreprehensibilem exhibere.

verses.text: And the angel said: Brother Tobias, thou knowest how thou didst leave thy father.
verses.textLatin: Cumque reverterentur, pervenerunt ad Charan, quæ est in medio itinere contra Niniven, undecimo die.

verses.text: If it please thee therefore, let us go before, and let the family follow softly after us, together with thy wife, and with the beasts.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque angelus: Tobia frater, scis quemadmodum reliquisti patrem tuum.

verses.text: And as this their going pleased him, Raphael said to Tobias: Take with thee of the gall of the fish, for it will be necessary. So Tobias took some of that gall and departed.
verses.textLatin: Si placet itaque tibi, præcedamus, et lento gradu sequantur iter nostrum familiæ, simul cum conjuge tua, et cum animalibus.

verses.text: But Anna sat beside the way daily, on the top of a hill, from whence she might see afar off.
verses.textLatin: Cumque hoc placuisset ut irent, dixit Raphaël ad Tobiam: Tolle tecum ex felle piscis: erit enim necessarium. Tulit itaque Tobias ex felle illo, et abierunt.

verses.text: And while she watched his coming from that place, she saw him afar off, and presently perceived it was her son coming: and returning she told her husband, saying: Behold thy son cometh.
verses.textLatin: Anna autem sedebat secus viam quotidie in supercilio montis, unde respicere poterat de longinquo.

verses.text: And Raphael said to Tobias: As soon as thou shalt come into thy house, forthwith adore the Lord thy God: and giving thanks to him, go to thy father, and kiss him.
verses.textLatin: Et dum ex eodem loco specularetur adventum ejus, vidit a longe, et illico agnovit venientem filium suum: currensque nuntiavit viro suo, dicens: Ecce venit filius tuus.

verses.text: And immediately anoint his eyes with this gall of the fish, which thou carriest with thee. For be assured that his eyes shall be presently opened, and thy father shall see the light of heaven, and shall rejoice in the sight of thee.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Raphaël ad Tobiam: At ubi introieris domum tuam, statim adora Dominum Deum tuum: et gratias agens ei, accede ad patrem tuum, et osculare eum.

verses.text: Then the dog, which had been with them in the way, ran before, and coming as if he had brought the news, shewed his joy by his fawning and wagging his tail.
verses.textLatin: Statimque lini super oculos ejus ex felle isto piscis, quod portas tecum: scias enim quoniam mox aperientur oculi ejus, et videbit pater tuus lumen cæli, et in aspectu tuo gaudebit.

verses.text: And his father that was blind, rising up, began to run stumbling with his feet: and giving a servant his hand, went to meet his son.
verses.textLatin: Tunc præcucurrit canis, qui simul fuerat in via: et quasi nuntius adveniens, blandimento suæ caudæ gaudebat.

verses.text: And receiving him kissed him, as did also his wife, and they began to weep for joy.
verses.textLatin: Et consurgens cæcus pater ejus, cœpit offendens pedibus currere: et data manu puero, occurrit obviam filio suo.

verses.text: And when they had adored God, and given him thanks, they sat down together.
verses.textLatin: Et suscipiens osculatus est eum cum uxore sua, et cœperunt ambo flere præ gaudio.

verses.text: Then Tobias taking of the gall of the fish, anointed his father’s eyes.
verses.textLatin: Cumque adorassent Deum, et gratias egissent, consederunt.

verses.text: And he stayed about half an hour: and a white skin began to come out of his eyes, like the skin of an egg.
verses.textLatin: Tunc sumens Tobias de felle piscis, linivit oculos patris sui.

verses.text: And Tobias took hold of it, and drew it from his eyes, and immediately he recovered his sight.
verses.textLatin: Et sustinuit quasi dimidiam fere horam: et cœpit albugo ex oculis ejus, quasi membrana ovi, egredi.

verses.text: And they glorified God, both he and his wife and all that knew him.
verses.textLatin: Quam apprehendens Tobias, traxit ab oculis ejus: statimque visum recepit.

verses.text: And Tobias said: I bless thee, O Lord God of Israel, because thou hast chastised me, and thou hast saved me: and behold I see Tobias my son.
verses.textLatin: Et glorificabant Deum, ipse videlicet et uxor ejus, et omnes qui sciebant eum.

verses.text: And after seven days Sara his son’s wife, and all the family arrived safe, and the cattle, and the camels, and an abundance of money of his wife’s: and that money also which he had received of Gabelus:
verses.textLatin: Dicebatque Tobias: Benedico te, Domine Deus Israël, quia tu castigasti me, et tu salvasti me: et ecce ego video Tobiam filium meum.

verses.text: And he told his parents all the benefits of God, which he had done to him by the man that conducted him.
verses.textLatin: Ingressa est etiam post septem dies Sara uxor filii ejus et omnis familia sana, et pecora, et cameli, et pecunia multa uxoris; sed et illa pecunia, quam receperat a Gabelo.

verses.text: And Achior and Nabath the kinsmen of Tobias came, rejoicing for Tobias, and congratulating with him for all the good things that God had done for him.
verses.textLatin: Et narravit parentibus suis omnia beneficia Dei, quæ fecisset circa eum per hominem qui eum duxerat.

verses.text: And for seven days they feasted and rejoiced all with great joy.
verses.textLatin: Veneruntque Achior et Nabath consobrini Tobiæ gaudentes ad Tobiam, et congratulantes ei de omnibus bonis quæ circa illum ostenderat Deus.

verses.text: Then  Tobias called to him his son, and said to him: What can we give to this holy man, that is come with thee?
verses.textLatin: Et per septem dies epulantes, omnes cum gaudio magno gavisi sunt.

verses.text: Tobias answering, said to his father: Father, what wages shall we give him? or what can be worthy of his benefits?
verses.textLatin: Tunc vocavit ad se Tobias filium suum, dixitque ei: Quid possumus dare viro isti sancto, qui venit tecum?

verses.text: He conducted me and brought me safe again, he received the money of Gabelus, he caused me to have my wife, and he chased from her the evil spirit, he gave joy to her parents, myself he delivered from being devoured by the fish, thee also he hath made to see the light of heaven, and we are filled with all good things through him. What can we give him sufficient for these things?
verses.textLatin: Respondens Tobias, dixit patri suo: Pater, quam mercedem dabimus ei? aut quid dignum poterit esse beneficiis ejus?

verses.text: But I beseech thee, my father, to desire him, that he would vouchsafe to accept of one half of all things that have been brought.
verses.textLatin: Me duxit et reduxit sanum, pecuniam a Gabelo ipse recepit, uxorem ipse me habere fecit, et dæmonium ab ea ipse compescuit: gaudium parentibus ejus fecit, meipsum a devoratione piscis eripuit, te quoque videre fecit lumen cæli, et bonis omnibus per eum repleti sumus. Quid illi ad hæc poterimus dignum dare?

verses.text: So the father and the son calling him, took him aside: and began to desire him that he would vouchsafe to accept of half of all things that they had brought.
verses.textLatin: Sed peto te, pater mi, ut roges eum, si forte dignabitur medietatem de omnibus quæ allata sunt, sibi assumere.

verses.text: Then he said to them secretly: Bless ye the God of heaven, give glory to him in the sight of all that live, because he hath shewn his mercy to you.
verses.textLatin: Et vocantes eum, pater scilicet et filius, tulerunt eum in partem: et rogare cœperunt ut dignaretur dimidiam partem omnium quæ attulerant acceptam habere.

verses.text: For it is good to hide the secret of a king: but honourable to reveal and confess the works of God.
verses.textLatin: Tunc dixit eis occulte: Benedicite Deum cæli, et coram omnibus viventibus confitemini ei, quia fecit vobiscum misericordiam suam.

verses.text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms more than to lay up treasures of gold:
verses.textLatin: Etenim sacramentum regis abscondere bonum est: opera autem Dei revelare et confiteri honorificum est.

verses.text: For alms delivereth from death, and the same is that which purgeth away sins, and maketh to find mercy and life everlasting.
verses.textLatin: Bona est oratio cum jejunio, et eleemosyna magis quam thesauros auri recondere:

verses.text: But they that commit sin and iniquity, are enemies to their own soul.
verses.textLatin: quoniam eleemosyna a morte liberat, et ipsa est quæ purgat peccata, et facit invenire misericordiam et viam æternam.

verses.text: I discover then the truth unto you, and I will not hide the secret from you.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem faciunt peccatum et iniquitatem, hostes sunt animæ suæ.

verses.text: When thou didst pray with tears, and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner, and hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Manifesto ergo vobis veritatem, et non abscondam a vobis occultum sermonem.

verses.text: And because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee.
verses.textLatin: Quando orabas cum lacrimis, et sepeliebas mortuos, et derelinquebas prandium tuum, et mortuos abscondebas per diem in domo tua, et nocte sepeliebas eos, ego obtuli orationem tuam Domino.

verses.text: And now the Lord hath sent me to heal thee, and to deliver Sara thy son’s wife from the devil.
verses.textLatin: Et quia acceptus eras Deo, necesse fuit ut tentatio probaret te.

verses.text: For I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc misit me Dominus ut curarem te, et Saram uxorem filii tui a dæmonio liberarem.

verses.text: And when they had heard these things, they were troubled, and being seized with fear they fell upon the ground on their face.
verses.textLatin: Ego enim sum Raphaël angelus, unus ex septem qui adstamus ante Dominum.

verses.text: And the angel said to them: Peace be to you, fear not.
verses.textLatin: Cumque hæc audissent, turbati sunt, et trementes ceciderunt super terram in faciem suam.

verses.text: For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God: bless ye him, and sing praises to him.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque eis angelus: Pax vobis: nolite timere.

verses.text: I seemed indeed to eat and to drink with you: but I use an invisible meat and drink, which cannot be seen by men.
verses.textLatin: Etenim cum essem vobiscum, per voluntatem Dei eram: ipsum benedicite, et cantate illi.

verses.text: It is time therefore that I return to him that sent me: but bless ye God, and publish all his wonderful works.
verses.textLatin: Videbar quidem vobiscum manducare et bibere: sed ego cibo invisibili, et potu qui ab hominibus videri non potest, utor.

verses.text: And when he had said these things, he was taken from their sight, and they could see him no more.
verses.textLatin: Tempus est ergo ut revertar ad eum qui me misit: vos autem benedicite Deum, et narrate omnia mirabilia ejus.

verses.text: Then they lying prostrate for three hours upon their face, blessed God: and rising up, they told all his wonderful works.
verses.textLatin: Et cum hæc dixisset, ab aspectu eorum ablatus est, et ultra eum videre non potuerunt.

verses.text: And  Tobias the elder opening his mouth, blessed the Lord, and said: Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, and thy kingdom is unto all ages:
verses.textLatin: Tunc prostrati per horas tres in faciem, benedixerunt Deum: et exsurgentes narraverunt omnia mirabilia ejus.

verses.text: For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: and there is none that can escape thy hand.
verses.textLatin: Aperiens autem Tobias senior os suum, benedixit Dominum, et dixit: Magnus es, Domine, in æternum, et in omnia sæcula regnum tuum:

verses.text: Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:
verses.textLatin: quoniam tu flagellas, et salvas; deducis ad inferos, et reducis: et non est qui effugiat manum tuam.

verses.text: Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, that you may declare his wonderful works, and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino, filii Israël, et in conspectu gentium laudate eum:

verses.text: He hath chastised us for our iniquities: and he will save us for his own mercy.
verses.textLatin: quoniam ideo dispersit vos inter gentes quæ ignorant eum, ut vos enarretis mirabilia ejus, et faciatis scire eos quia non est alius deus omnipotens præter eum.

verses.text: See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.
verses.textLatin: Ipse castigavit nos propter iniquitates nostras, et ipse salvabit nos propter misericordiam suam.

verses.text: As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation.
verses.textLatin: Aspicite ergo quæ fecit nobiscum, et cum timore et tremore confitemini illi: regemque sæculorum exaltate in operibus vestris.

verses.text: Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, believing that he will shew his mercy to you.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in terra captivitatis meæ confitebor illi: quoniam ostendit majestatem suam in gentem peccatricem.

verses.text: And I and my soul will rejoice in him.
verses.textLatin: Convertimini itaque peccatores, et facite justitiam coram Deo, credentes quod faciat vobiscum misericordiam suam.

verses.text: Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, keep days of joy, and give glory to him.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem et anima mea in eo lætabimur.

verses.text: Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord hath chastised thee for the works of thy hands.
verses.textLatin: Benedicite Dominum omnes electi ejus: agite dies lætitiæ, et confitemini illi.

verses.text: Give glory to the Lord for thy good things, and bless the God eternal, that he may rebuild his tabernacle in thee, and may call back all the captives to thee, and thou mayst rejoice for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Jerusalem civitas Dei, castigavit te Dominus in operibus manuum tuarum.

verses.text: Thou shalt shine with a glorious light: and all the ends of the earth shall worship thee.
verses.textLatin: Confitere Domino in bonis tuis, et benedic Deum sæculorum: ut reædificet in te tabernaculum suum, et revocet ad te omnes captivos, et gaudeas in omnia sæcula sæculorum.

verses.text: Nations from afar shall come to thee: and shall bring gifts, and shall adore the Lord in thee, and shall esteem thy land as holy.
verses.textLatin: Luce splendida fulgebis, et omnes fines terræ adorabunt te.

verses.text: For they shall call upon the great name in thee.
verses.textLatin: Nationes ex longinquo ad te venient, et munera deferentes adorabunt in te Dominum, et terram tuam in sanctificationem habebunt:

verses.text: They shall be cursed that shall despise thee: and they shall be condemned that shall blaspheme thee: and blessed shall they be that shall build thee up.
verses.textLatin: nomen enim magnum invocabunt in te.

verses.text: But thou shalt rejoice in thy children, because they shall all be blessed, and shall be gathered together to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Maledicti erunt qui contempserint te, et condemnati erunt omnes qui blasphemaverint te: benedictique erunt qui ædificaverint te.

verses.text: Blessed are all they that love thee, and that rejoice in thy peace.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem lætaberis in filiis tuis, quoniam omnes benedicentur, et congregabuntur ad Dominum.

verses.text: My soul, bless thou the Lord, because the Lord our God hath delivered Jerusalem his city from all her troubles.
verses.textLatin: Beati omnes qui diligunt te, et qui gaudent super pace tua.

verses.text: Happy shall I be if there shall remain of my seed, to see the glory of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Anima mea, benedic Dominum, quoniam liberavit Jerusalem civitatem suam a cunctis tribulationibus ejus Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: The gates of Jerusalem shall be built of sapphire, and of emerald, and all the walls thereof round about of precious stones.
verses.textLatin: Beatus ero si fuerint reliquiæ seminis mei ad videndam claritatem Jerusalem.

verses.text: All its streets shall be paved with white and clean stones: and Alleluia shall be sung in its streets.
verses.textLatin: Portæ Jerusalem ex sapphiro et smaragdo ædificabuntur, et ex lapide pretioso omnis circuitus murorum ejus.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord, who hath exalted it, and may he reign over it for ever and ever, Amen.
verses.textLatin: Ex lapide candido et mundo omnes plateæ ejus sternentur, et per vicos ejus alleluja cantabitur.

verses.text: And  the words of Tobias were ended. And after Tobias was restored to his sight, he lived two and forty years, and saw the children of his grandchildren.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus, qui exaltavit eam, et sit regnum ejus in sæcula sæculorum super eam. Amen.

verses.text: And after he had lived a hundred and two years, he was buried honourably in Ninive.
verses.textLatin: Et consummati sunt sermones Tobiæ. Et postquam illuminatus est Tobias, vixit annis quadraginta duobus, et vidit filios nepotum suorum.

verses.text: For he was six and fifty years old when he lost the sight of his eyes, and sixty when he recovered it again.
verses.textLatin: Completis itaque annis centum duobus, sepultus est honorifice in Ninive.

verses.text: And the rest of his life was in joy, and with great increase of the fear of God he departed in peace.
verses.textLatin: Quinquaginta namque et sex annorum lumen oculorum amisit, sexagenarius vero recepit.

verses.text: And at the hour of his death he called unto him his son Tobias and his children, seven young men, his grandsons, and said to them:
verses.textLatin: Reliquum vero vitæ suæ in gaudio fuit, et cum bono profectu timoris Dei perrexit in pace.

verses.text: The destruction of Ninive is at hand: for the word of the Lord must be fulfilled: and our brethren, that are scattered abroad from the land of Israel, shall return to it.
verses.textLatin: In hora autem mortis suæ vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum, et septem juvenes filios ejus nepotes suos, dixitque eis:

verses.text: And all the land thereof that is desert shall be filled with people, and the house of God which is burnt in it, shall again be rebuilt: and all that fear God shall return thither.
verses.textLatin: Prope erit interitus Ninive: non enim excidit verbum Domini: et fratres nostri, qui dispersi sunt a terra Israël, revertentur ad eam.

verses.text: And the Gentiles shall leave their idols, and shall come into Jerusalem, and shall dwell in it.
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem deserta terra ejus replebitur, et domus Dei, quæ in ea incensa est, iterum reædificabitur: ibique revertentur omnes timentes Deum,

verses.text: And all the kings of the earth shall rejoice in it, adoring the King of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et relinquent gentes idola sua, et venient in Jerusalem, et inhabitabunt in ea:

verses.text: Hearken therefore, my children, to your father: serve the Lord in truth, and seek to do the things that please him:
verses.textLatin: et gaudebunt in ea omnes reges terræ, adorantes regem Israël.

verses.text: And command your children that they do justice and almsdeeds, and that they be mindful of God, and bless him at all times in truth, and with all their power.
verses.textLatin: Audite ergo, filii mei, patrem vestrum: servite Domino in veritate, et inquirite ut faciatis quæ placita sunt illi:

verses.text: And now, children, hear me, and do not stay here: but as soon as you shall bury your mother by me in one sepulchre, without delay direct your steps to depart hence:
verses.textLatin: et filiis vestris mandate ut faciant justitias et eleemosynas, ut sint memores Dei, et benedicant eum in omni tempore in veritate, et in tota virtute sua.

verses.text: For I see that its iniquity will bring it to destruction.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo filii, audite me, et nolite manere hic: sed quacumque die sepelieritis matrem vestram circa me in uno sepulchro, ex eo dirigite gressus vestros ut exeatis hinc:

verses.text: And it came to pass that after the death of his mother Tobias departed out of Ninive with his wife, and children, and children’s children, and returned to his father and mother in law.
verses.textLatin: video enim quia iniquitas ejus finem dabit ei.

verses.text: And he found them in health in a good old age: and he took care of them, and he closed their eyes: and all the inheritance of Raguel’s house came to him: and he saw his children’s children to the fifth generation.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem post obitum matris suæ, Tobias abscessit ex Ninive cum uxore sua, et filiis, et filiorum filiis, et reversus est ad soceros suos:

verses.text: And after he had lived ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, with joy they buried him.
verses.textLatin: invenitque eos incolumes in senectute bona: et curam eorum gessit, et ipse clausit oculos eorum: et omnem hæreditatem domus Raguelis ipse percepit: viditque quintam generationem, filios filiorum suorum.

verses.text: And all his kindred, and all his generation continued in good life, and in holy conversation, so that they were acceptable both to God, and to men, and to all that dwelt in the land.
verses.textLatin: Et completis annis nonaginta novem in timore Domini, cum gaudio sepelierunt eum.

verses.text: Now  Arphaxad king of the Medes had brought many nations under his dominions, and he built a very strong city, which he called Ecbatana,
verses.textLatin: Arphaxad itaque, rex Medorum, subjugaverat multas gentes imperio suo, et ipse ædificavit civitatem potentissimam, quam appellavit Ecbatanis,

verses.text: Of stones squared and hewed: he made the walls thereof seventy cubits broad, and thirty cubits high, and the towers thereof he made a hundred cubits high. But on the square of them, each side was extended the space of twenty feet.
verses.textLatin: ex lapidibus quadratis et sectis: fecit muros ejus in altitudinem cubitorum septuaginta, et in latitudinem cubitorum triginta: turres vero ejus posuit in altitudinem cubitorum centum.

verses.text: And he made the gates thereof according to the height of the towers:
verses.textLatin: Per quadrum vero earum latus utrumque vicenorum pedum spatio tendebatur, posuitque portas ejus in altitudinem turrium:

verses.text: And he gloried as a mighty one in the force of his army and in the glory of his chariots.
verses.textLatin: et gloriabatur quasi potens in potentia exercitus sui, et in gloria quadrigarum suarum.

verses.text: Now in the twelfth year of his reign, Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians, who reigned in Ninive the great city, fought against Arphaxad and overcame him,
verses.textLatin: Anno igitur duodecimo regni sui, Nabuchodonosor rex Assyriorum, qui regnabat in Ninive civitate magna, pugnavit contra Arphaxad, et obtinuit eum

verses.text: In the great plain which is called Ragua, about the Euphrates, and the Tigris, and the Jadason, in the plain of Erioch the king of the Elicians.
verses.textLatin: in campo magno qui appellatur Ragau, circa Euphraten, et Tigrin, et Jadason, in campo Erioch regis Elicorum.

verses.text: Then was the kingdom of Nabuchodonosor exalted, and his heart was elevated: and he sent to all that dwelt in Cilicia and Damascus, and Libanus,
verses.textLatin: Tunc exaltatum est regnum Nabuchodonosor, et cor ejus elevatum est: et misit ad omnes qui habitabant in Cilicia, et Damasco, et Libano,

verses.text: And to the nations that are in Carmelus, and Cedar, and to the inhabitants of Galilee in the great plain of Asdrelon,
verses.textLatin: et ad gentes quæ sunt in Carmelo et Cedar, et inhabitantes Galilæam in campo magno Esdrelon,

verses.text: And to all that were in Samaria, and beyond the river Jordan even to Jerusalem, and all the land of Jesse till you come to the borders of Ethiopia.
verses.textLatin: et ad omnes qui erant in Samaria, et trans flumen Jordanem usque ad Jerusalem, et omnem terram Jesse quousque perveniatur ad terminos Æthiopiæ.

verses.text: To all these Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians, sent messengers:
verses.textLatin: Ad hos omnes misit nuntios Nabuchodonosor rex Assyriorum:

verses.text: But they all with one mind refused, and sent them back empty, and rejected them without honour.
verses.textLatin: qui omnes uno animo contradixerunt, et remiserunt eos vacuos, et sine honore abjecerunt.

verses.text: Then king Nabuchodonosor being angry against all that land, swore by his throne and kingdom that he would revenge himself of all those countries.
verses.textLatin: Tunc indignatus Nabuchodonosor rex adversus omnem terram illam, juravit per thronum et regnum suum quod defenderet se de omnibus regionibus his.

verses.text: In  the thirteenth year of the reign of Nabuchodonosor, the two and twentieth day of the first month, the word was given out in the house of Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians, that he would revenge himself.
verses.textLatin: Anno tertiodecimo Nabuchodonosor regis, vigesima et secunda die mensis primi, factum est verbum in domo Nabuchodonosor regis Assyriorum ut defenderet se.

verses.text: And he called all the ancients, and all the governors, and his officers of war, and communicated to them the secret of his counsel:
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque omnes majores natu, omnesque duces et bellatores suos, et habuit cum eis mysterium consilii sui:

verses.text: And he said that his thoughts were to bring all the earth under his empire.
verses.textLatin: dixitque cogitationem suam in eo esse, ut omnem terram suo subjugaret imperio.

verses.text: And when this saying pleased them all, Nabuchodonosor, the king, called Holofernes the general of his armies,
verses.textLatin: Quod dictum cum placuisset omnibus, vocavit Nabuchodonosor rex Holofernem principem militiæ suæ,

verses.text: And said to him: Go out against all the kingdoms of the west, and against them especially that despised my commandment.
verses.textLatin: et dixit ei: Egredere adversus omne regnum occidentis, et contra eos præcipue, qui contempserunt imperium meum.

verses.text: Thy eye shall not spare any kingdom, and all the strong cities thou shalt bring under my yoke.
verses.textLatin: Non parcet oculus tuus ulli regno, omnemque urbem munitam subjugabis mihi.

verses.text: Then Holofernes called the captains, and officers of the power of the Assyrians: and he mustered men for the expedition, as the king commanded him, a hundred and twenty thousand fighting men on foot, and twelve thousand archers, horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Holofernes vocavit duces et magistratus virtutis Assyriorum, et dinumeravit viros in expeditionem sicut præcepit ei rex, centum viginti millia peditum pugnatorum, et equitum sagittariorum duodecim millia.

verses.text: And he made all his warlike preparations to go before with a multitude of innumerable camels, with all provisions sufficient for the armies in abundance, and herds of oxen, and flocks of sheep, without number.
verses.textLatin: Omnemque expeditionem suam fecit præire in multitudine innumerabilium camelorum, cum his quæ exercitibus sufficerent copiose, boum quoque armenta, gregesque ovium, quorum non erat numerus.

verses.text: He appointed corn to be prepared out of all Syria in his passage.
verses.textLatin: Frumentum ex omni Syria in transitu suo parari constituit.

verses.text: But gold and silver he took out of the king’s house in great abundance.
verses.textLatin: Aurum vero et argentum de domo regis assumpsit multum nimis.

verses.text: And he went forth he and all the army, with the chariots, and horsemen, and archers, who covered the face of the earth, like locusts.
verses.textLatin: Et profectus est ipse, et omnis exercitus cum quadrigis, et equitibus, et sagittariis: qui cooperuerunt faciem terræ sicut locustæ.

verses.text: And when he had passed through the borders of the Assyrians, he came to the great mountains of Ange, which are on the left of Cilicia: and he went up to all their castles, and took all the strong places.
verses.textLatin: Cumque pertransisset fines Assyriorum, venit ad magnos montes Ange, qui sunt a sinistro Ciliciæ: ascenditque omnia castella eorum, et obtinuit omnem munitionem.

verses.text: And he took by assault the renowned city of Melothus, and pillaged all the children of Tharsis, and the children of Ismahel, who were over against the face of the desert, and on the south of the land of Cellon.
verses.textLatin: Effregit autem civitatem opinatissimam Melothi, prædavitque omnes filios Tharsis et filios Ismaël qui erant contra faciem deserti, et ad austrum terræ Cellon.

verses.text: And he passed over the Euphrates, and came into Mesopotamia: and he forced all the stately cities that were there, from the torrent of Mambre, till one comes to the sea:
verses.textLatin: Et transivit Euphraten, et venit in Mesopotamiam: et fregit omnes civitates excelsas quæ erant ibi, a torrente Mambre usquequo perveniatur ad mare:

verses.text: And he took the borders thereof, from Cilicia to the coasts of Japheth, which are towards the south.
verses.textLatin: et occupavit terminos ejus, a Cilicia usque ad fines Japheth qui sunt ad austrum.

verses.text: And he carried away all the children of Madian, and stripped them of all their riches, and all that resisted him he slew with the edge of the sword.
verses.textLatin: Abduxitque omnes filios Madian, et prædavit omnem locupletationem eorum, omnesque resistentes sibi occidit in ore gladii.

verses.text: And after these things he went down into the plains of Damascus in the days of the harvest, and he set all the corn on fire, and he caused all the trees and vineyards to be cut down.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc descendit in campos Damasci in diebus messis, et succendit omnia sata, omnesque arbores, et vineas fecit incidi:

verses.text: And the fear of them fell upon all the inhabitants of the land.
verses.textLatin: et cecidit timor illius super omnes inhabitantes terram.

verses.text: Then  the kings and the princes of all the cities and provinces, of Syria, Mesopotamia, and Syria Sobal, and Libya, and Cilicia sent their ambassadors, who coming to Holofernes, said:
verses.textLatin: Tunc miserunt legatos suos universarum urbium ac provinciarum reges ac principes, Syriæ scilicet Mesopotamiæ, et Syriæ Sobal, et Libyæ, atque Ciliciæ: qui venientes ad Holofernem, dixerunt:

verses.text: Let thy indignation towards us cease: for it is better for us to live and serve Nabuchodonosor the great king, and be subject to thee, than to die and to perish, or suffer the miseries of slavery.
verses.textLatin: Desinat indignatio tua circa nos: melius est enim ut viventes serviamus Nabuchodonosor regi magno, et subditi simus tibi, quam morientes cum interitu nostro ipsi servitutis nostræ damna patiamur.

verses.text: All our cities and our possessions, all mountains and hills, and fields, and herds of oxen, and flocks of sheep, and goats, and horses, and camels, and all our goods, and families are in thy sight:
verses.textLatin: Omnis civitas nostra, omnisque possessio, omnes montes, et colles, et campi, et armenta boum, gregesque ovium, et caprarum, equorumque et camelorum, et universæ facultates nostræ atque familiæ, in conspectu tuo sunt:

verses.text: Let all we have be subject to thy law.
verses.textLatin: sint omnia nostra sub lege tua.

verses.text: Both we and our children are thy servants.
verses.textLatin: Nos, et filii nostri, servi tui sumus.

verses.text: Come to us a peaceable lord, and use our service as it shall please thee.
verses.textLatin: Veni nobis pacificus dominus, et utere servitio nostro, sicut placuerit tibi.

verses.text: Then he came down from the mountains with horsemen, in great power, and made himself master of every city, and all the inhabitants of the land.
verses.textLatin: Tunc descendit de montibus cum equitibus in virtute magna, et obtinuit omnem civitatem, et omnem inhabitantem terram.

verses.text: And from all the cities he took auxiliaries valiant men, and chosen for war.
verses.textLatin: De universis autem urbibus assumpsit sibi auxiliarios viros fortes, et electos ad bellum.

verses.text: And so great a fear lay upon all those provinces, that the inhabitants of all the cities, both princes and nobles, as well as the people, went out to meet him at his coming.
verses.textLatin: Tantusque metus provinciis illis incubuit, ut universarum urbium habitatores principes et honorati simul cum populis exirent obviam venienti,

verses.text: And received him with garlands, and lights, and dances, and timbrels, and flutes.
verses.textLatin: excipientes eum cum coronis et lampadibus, ducentes choros in tympanis et tibiis.

verses.text: And though they did these things, they could not for all that mitigate the fierceness of his heart:
verses.textLatin: Nec ista tamen facientes, ferocitatem ejus pectoris mitigare potuerunt:

verses.text: For he both destroyed their cities, and cut down their groves.
verses.textLatin: nam et civitates eorum destruxit, et lucos eorum excidit.

verses.text: For Nabuchodonosor the king had commanded him to destroy all the gods of the earth, that he only might be called God by those nations which could be brought under him by the power of Holofernes.
verses.textLatin: Præceperat enim illi Nabuchodonosor rex, ut omnes deos terræ exterminaret, videlicet ut ipse solus diceretur deus ab his nationibus quæ potuissent Holofernis potentia subjugari.

verses.text: And when he had passed through all Syria Sobal, and all Apamea, and all Mesopotamia, he came to the Idumeans into the land of Gabaa,
verses.textLatin: Pertransiens autem Syriam Sobal, et omnem Apameam, omnemque Mesopotamiam, venit ad Idumæos in terram Gabaa,

verses.text: And he took possession of their cities, and stayed there for thirty days, in which days he commanded all the troops of his army to be united.
verses.textLatin: accepitque civitates eorum, et sedit ibi per triginta dies, in quibus diebus adunari præcepit universum exercitum virtutis suæ.

verses.text: Then  the children of Israel who dwelt in the land of Juda, hearing these things, were exceedingly afraid of him.
verses.textLatin: Tunc audientes hæc filii Israël qui habitabant in terra Juda, timuerunt valde a facie ejus.

verses.text: Dread and horror seized upon their minds, lest he should do the same to Jerusalem and to the temple of the Lord, that he had done to other cities and their temples.
verses.textLatin: Tremor et horror invasit sensus eorum, ne hoc faceret Jerusalem et templo Domini, quod fecerat ceteris civitatibus et templis earum.

verses.text: And they sent into all Samaria round about, as far as Jericho, and seized upon all the tops of the mountains:
verses.textLatin: Et miserunt in omnem Samariam per circuitum usque Jericho, et præoccupaverunt omnes vertices montium:

verses.text: And they compassed their towns with walls, and gathered together corn for provision for war.
verses.textLatin: et muris circumdederunt vicos suos, et congregaverunt frumenta in præparationem pugnæ.

verses.text: And Eliachim the priest wrote to all that were over against Esdrelon, which faceth the great plain near Dothain, and to all by whom there might be a passage of way, that they should take possession of the ascents of the mountains, by which there might be any way to Jerusalem, and should keep watch where the way was narrow between the mountains.
verses.textLatin: Sacerdos etiam Eliachim scripsit ad universos qui erant contra Esdrelon, quæ est contra faciem campi magni juxta Dothain, et universos per quos viæ transitus esse poterat,
ut obtinerent ascensus montium, per quos via esse poterat ad Jerusalem, et illic custodirent ubi angustum iter esse poterat inter montes.

verses.text: And the children of Israel did as the priests of the Lord Eliachim had appointed them.
verses.textLatin: Et fecerunt filii Israël secundum quod constituerat eis sacerdos Domini Eliachim.

verses.text: And all the people cried to the Lord with great earnestness, and they humbled their souls in fastings, and prayers, both they and their wives.
verses.textLatin: Et clamavit omnis populus ad Dominum instantia magna, et humiliaverunt animas suas in jejuniis et orationibus, ipsi et mulieres eorum.

verses.text: And the priests put on haircloths, and they caused the little children to lie prostrate before the temple of the Lord, and the altar of the Lord they covered with haircloth.
verses.textLatin: Et induerunt se sacerdotes ciliciis, et infantes prostraverunt contra faciem templi Domini, et altare Domini operuerunt cilicio:

verses.text: And they cried to the Lord the God of Israel with one accord, that their children might not be made a prey, and their wives carried off, and their cities destroyed, and their holy things profaned, and that they might not be made a reproach to the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: et clamaverunt ad Dominum Deum Israël unanimiter ne darentur in prædam infantes eorum, et uxores eorum in divisionem, et civitates eorum in exterminium, et sancta eorum in pollutionem, et fierent opprobrium gentibus.

verses.text: Then Eliachim the high priest of the Lord went about all Israel and spoke to them,
verses.textLatin: Tunc Eliachim sacerdos Domini magnus circuivit omnem Israël, allocutusque est eos,

verses.text: Saying: Know ye that the Lord will hear your prayers, if you continue with perseverance in fastings and prayers in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Scitote quoniam exaudiet Dominus preces vestras, si manentes permanseritis in jejuniis et orationibus in conspectu Domini.

verses.text: Remember Moses the servant of the Lord, who overcame Amalec that trusted in his own strength, and in his power, and in his army, and in his shields, and in his chariots, and in his horsemen, not by fighting with the sword, but by holy prayers:
verses.textLatin: Memores estote Moysi servi Domini, qui Amalec confidentem in virtute sua, et in potentia sua, et in exercitu suo, et in clypeis suis, et in curribus suis, et in equitibus suis, non ferro pugnando, sed precibus sanctis orando dejecit:

verses.text: So shall all the enemies of Israel be, if you persevere in this work which you have begun.
verses.textLatin: sic erunt universi hostes Israël, si perseveraveritis in hoc opere quod cœpistis.

verses.text: So they being moved by this exhortation of his, prayed to the Lord, and continued in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ad hanc igitur exhortationem ejus deprecantes Dominum, permanebant in conspectu Domini,

verses.text: So that even they who offered the holocausts to the Lord, offered the sacrifices to the Lord girded with haircloths, and with ashes upon their head.
verses.textLatin: ita ut etiam hi qui offerebant Domino holocausta, præcincti ciliciis offerrent sacrificia Domino, et erat cinis super capita eorum.

verses.text: And they all begged of God with all their heart, that he would visit his people Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et ex toto corde suo omnes orabant Deum, ut visitaret populum suum Israël.

verses.text: And  it was told Holofernes the general of the army of the Assyrians, that the children of Israel prepared themselves to resist, and had shut up the ways of the mountains.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiatumque est Holoferni principi militiæ Assyriorum, quod filii Israël præpararent se ad resistendum, ac montium itinera conclusissent:

verses.text: And he was transported with exceeding great fury and indignation, and he called all the princes of Moab and the leaders of Ammon.
verses.textLatin: et furore nimio exarsit in iracundia magna, vocavitque omnes principes Moab et duces Ammon,

verses.text: And he said to them: Tell me what is this people that besetteth the mountains: or what are their cities, and of what sort, and how great: also what is their power, or what is their multitude: or who is the king over their warfare:
verses.textLatin: et dixit eis: Dicite mihi quis sit populus iste, qui montana obsidet: aut quæ, et quales, et quantæ sint civitates eorum: quæ etiam sit virtus eorum, aut quæ sit multitudo eorum, vel quis rex militiæ illorum:

verses.text: And why they above all that dwell in the east, have despised us, and have not come out to meet us, that they might receive us with peace?
verses.textLatin: et quare præ omnibus qui habitant in oriente, isti contempserunt nos, et non exierunt obviam nobis ut susciperent nos cum pace?

verses.text: Then Achior captain of all the children of Ammon answering, said: If thou vouchsafe, my lord, to hear, I will tell the truth in thy sight concerning this people, that dwelleth in the mountains, and there shall not a false word come out of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Achior dux omnium filiorum Ammon respondens, ait: Si digneris audire, domine mi, dicam veritatem in conspectu tuo de populo isto qui in montanis habitat, et non egredietur verbum falsum ex ore meo.

verses.text: This people is of the offspring of the Chaldeans.
verses.textLatin: Populus iste ex progenie Chaldæorum est.

verses.text: They dwelt first in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods of their fathers, who were in the land of the Chaldeans.
verses.textLatin: Hic primum in Mesopotamia habitavit, quoniam noluerunt sequi deos patrum suorum, qui erant in terra Chaldæorum.

verses.text: Wherefore forsaking the ceremonies of their fathers, which consisted in the worship of many gods,
verses.textLatin: Deserentes itaque cæremonias patrum suorum, quæ in multitudine deorum erant,

verses.text: They worshipped one God of heaven, who also commanded them to depart from thence, and to dwell in Charan. And when there was a famine over all the land, they went down into Egypt, and there for four hundred years were so multiplied, that the army of them could not be numbered.
verses.textLatin: unum Deum cæli coluerunt, qui et præcepit eis ut exirent inde et habitarent in Charan. Cumque operuisset omnem terram fames, descenderunt in Ægyptum, illicque per quadringentos annos sic multiplicati sunt, ut dinumerari eorum non posset exercitus.

verses.text: And when the king of Egypt oppressed them, and made slaves of them to labour in clay and brick, in the building of his cities, they cried to their Lord, and he struck the whole land of Egypt with divers plagues.
verses.textLatin: Cumque gravaret eos rex Ægypti, atque in ædificationibus urbium suarum in luto et latere subjugasset eos, clamaverunt ad Dominum suum, et percussit totam terram Ægypti plagis variis.

verses.text: And when the Egyptians had cast them out from them, and the plague had ceased from them, and they had a mind to take them again, and bring them back to their service,
verses.textLatin: Cumque ejecissent eos Ægyptii a se, et cessasset plaga ab eis, et iterum eos vellent capere, et ad suum servitium revocare,

verses.text: The God of heaven opened the sea to them in their flight, so that the waters were made to stand firm as a wall on either side, and they walked through the bottom of the sea and passed it dry foot.
verses.textLatin: fugientibus his, Deus cæli mare aperuit, ita ut hinc inde aquæ quasi murus solidarentur, et isti pede sicco fundum maris perambulando transirent.

verses.text: And when an innumerable army of the Egyptians pursued after them in that place, they were so overwhelmed with the waters, that there was not one left, to tell what had happened to posterity.
verses.textLatin: In quo loco dum innumerabilis exercitus Ægyptiorum eos persequeretur, ita aquis coopertus est, ut non remaneret vel unus, qui factum posteris nuntiaret.

verses.text: And after they came out of the Red Sea, they abode in the deserts of mount Sina, in which never man could dwell, or son of man rested.
verses.textLatin: Egressi vero mare Rubrum, deserta Sina montis occupaverunt, in quibus numquam homo habitare potuit, vel filius hominis requievit.

verses.text: There bitter fountains were made sweet for them to drink, and for forty years they received food from heaven.
verses.textLatin: Illic fontes amari obdulcati sunt eis ad bibendum, et per annos quadraginta annonam de cælo consecuti sunt.

verses.text: Wheresoever they went in without bow and arrow, and without shield and sword, their God fought for them and overcame.
verses.textLatin: Ubicumque ingressi sunt sine arcu et sagitta, et absque scuto et gladio, Deus eorum pugnavit pro eis, et vicit.

verses.text: And there was no one that triumphed over this people, but when they departed from the worship of the Lord their God.
verses.textLatin: Et non fuit qui insultaret populo isti, nisi quando recessit a cultu Domini Dei sui.

verses.text: But as often as beside their own God, they worshipped any other, they were given to spoil, and to the sword, and to reproach.
verses.textLatin: Quotiescumque autem præter ipsum Deum suum, alterum coluerunt, dati sunt in prædam, et in gladium, et in opprobrium.

verses.text: And as often as they were penitent for having revolted from the worship of their God, the God of heaven gave them power to resist.
verses.textLatin: Quotiescumque autem pœnituerunt se recessisse a cultura Dei sui, dedit eis Deus cæli virtutem resistendi.

verses.text: So they overthrew the king of the Chanaanites, and of the Jebusites, and of the Pherezites, and of the Hethites, and of the Hevites, and of the Amorrhites, and all the mighty ones in Hesebon, and they possessed their lands, and their cities:
verses.textLatin: Denique Chananæum regem, et Jebusæum, et Pherezæum, et Hethæum, et Hevæum, et Amorrhæum, et omnes potentes in Hesebon prostraverunt, et terras eorum et civitates eorum ipsi possederunt:

verses.text: And as long as they sinned not in the sight of their God, it was well with them: for their God hateth iniquity.
verses.textLatin: et usque dum non peccarent in conspectu Dei sui, erant cum illis bona: Deus enim illorum odit iniquitatem.

verses.text: And even some years ago when they had revolted from the way which God had given them to walk therein, they were destroyed in battles by many nations, and very many of them were led away captive into a strange land.
verses.textLatin: Nam et ante hos annos cum recessissent a via quam dederat illis Deus ut ambularent in ea, exterminati sunt præliis a multis nationibus, et plurimi eorum captivi abducti sunt in terram non suam.

verses.text: But of late returning to the Lord their God, from the different places wherein they were scattered, they are come together and are gone up into all these mountains, and possess Jerusalem again, where their holies are.
verses.textLatin: Nuper autem reversi ad Dominum Deum suum, ex dispersione qua dispersi fuerant, adunati sunt, et ascenderunt montana hæc omnia, et iterum possident Jerusalem, ubi sunt sancta eorum.

verses.text: Now therefore, my lord, search if there be any iniquity of theirs in the sight of their God: let us go up to them, because their God will surely deliver them to thee, and they shall be brought under the yoke of thy power:
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo mi domine, perquire si est aliqua iniquitas eorum in conspectu Dei eorum: ascendamus ad illos, quoniam tradens tradet illos Deus eorum tibi, et subjugati erunt sub jugo potentiæ tuæ.

verses.text: But if there be no offence of this people in the sight of their God, we cannot resist them, because their God will defend them: and we shall be a reproach to the whole earth.
verses.textLatin: Si vero non est offensio populi hujus coram Deo suo, non poterimus resistere illis, quoniam Deus eorum defendet illos: et erimus in opprobrium universæ terræ.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when Achior had ceased to speak these words, all the great men of Holofernes were angry, and they had a mind to kill him, saying to each other:
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, cum cessasset loqui Achior verba hæc, irati sunt omnes magnates Holofernis, et cogitabant interficere eum, dicentes ad alterutrum:

verses.text: Who is this, that saith the children of Israel can resist king Nabuchodonosor, and his armies, men unarmed, and without force, and without skill in the art of war?
verses.textLatin: Quis est iste, qui filios Israël posse dicat resistere regi Nabuchodonosor et exercitibus ejus, homines inermes, et sine virtute, et sine peritia artis pugnæ?

verses.text: That Achior therefore may know that he deceiveth us, let us go up into the mountains: and when the bravest of them shall be taken, then shall he with them be stabbed with the sword:
verses.textLatin: Ut ergo agnoscat Achior quoniam fallit nos, ascendamus in montana: et cum capti fuerint potentes eorum, tunc cum eisdem gladio transverberabitur:

verses.text: That every nation may know that Nabuchodonosor is god of the earth, and besides him there is no other.
verses.textLatin: ut sciat omnis gens quoniam Nabuchodonosor deus terræ est, et præter ipsum alius non est.

verses.text: And  it came to pass when they had left off speaking, that Holofernes being in a violent passion, said to Achior:
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem cum cessassent loqui, indignatus Holofernes vehementer, dixit ad Achior:

verses.text: Because thou hast prophesied unto us, saying: That the nation of Israel is defended by their God, to shew thee that there is no God, but Nabuchodonosor:
verses.textLatin: Quoniam prophetasti nobis, dicens quod gens Israël defendatur a Deo suo, ut ostendam tibi quoniam non est deus nisi Nabuchodonosor,

verses.text: When we shall slay them all as one man, then thou also shalt die with them by the sword of the Assyrians, and all Israel shall perish with thee:
verses.textLatin: cum percusserimus eos omnes, sicut hominem unum, tunc et ipse cum illis Assyriorum gladio interibis, et omnis Israël tecum perditione disperiet:

verses.text: And thou shalt find that Nabuchodonosor is lord of the whole earth: and then the sword of my soldiers shall pass through thy sides, and thou shalt be stabbed and fall among the wounded of Israel, and thou shalt breathe no more till thou be destroyed with them.
verses.textLatin: et probabis quoniam Nabuchodonosor dominus sit universæ terræ: tuncque gladius militiæ meæ transiet per latera tua, et confixus cades inter vulneratos Israël, et non respirabis ultra, donec extermineris cum illis.
