verses.text: But if thou think thy prophecy true, let not thy countenance sink, and let the paleness that is in thy face, depart from thee, if thou imaginest these my words cannot be accomplished.
verses.textLatin: Porro autem si prophetiam tuam veram existimas, non concidat vultus tuus: et pallor qui faciem tuam obtinet abscedat a te, si verba mea hæc putas impleri non posse.

verses.text: And that thou mayst know that thou shalt experience these things together with them, behold from this hour thou shalt be associated to their people, that when they shall receive the punishment they deserve from my sword, thou mayst fall under the same vengeance.
verses.textLatin: Ut autem noveris quia simul cum illis hæc experieris, ecce ex hac hora illorum populo sociaberis, ut, dum dignas mei gladii pœnas exceperint, ipse simul ultioni subjaceas.

verses.text: Then Holofernes commanded his servants to take Achior, and to lead him to Bethulia, and to deliver him into the hands of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Holofernes præcepit servis suis ut comprehenderent Achior, et perducerent eum in Bethuliam, et traderent eum in manus filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And the servants of Holofernes taking him, went through the plains: but when they came near the mountains, the slingers came out against them.
verses.textLatin: Et accipientes eum servi Holofernis, profecti sunt per campestria: sed cum appropinquassent ad montana, exierunt contra eos fundibularii.

verses.text: Then turning out of the way by the side of the mountain, they tied Achior to a tree hand and foot, and so left him bound with ropes, and returned to their master.
verses.textLatin: Illi autem divertentes a latere montis, ligaverunt Achior ad arborem manibus et pedibus, et sic vinctum restibus dimiserunt eum, et reversi sunt ad dominum suum.

verses.text: And the children of Israel coming down from Bethulia, came to him, and loosing him they brought him to Bethulia, and setting him in the midst of the people, asked him what was the matter, that the Assyrians had left him bound.
verses.textLatin: Porro filii Israël descendentes de Bethulia, venerunt ad eum: quem solventes, duxerunt ad Bethuliam, atque in medium populi illum statuentes, percunctati sunt quid rerum esset quod illum vinctum Assyrii reliquissent.

verses.text: In those days the rulers there, were Ozias the son of Micha of the tribe of Simeon, and Charmi, called also Gothoniel.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis erant illic principes Ozias filius Micha de tribu Simeon, et Charmi, qui et Gothoniel.

verses.text: And Achior related in the midst of the ancients, and in the presence of all the people, all that he had said being asked by Holofernes: and how the people of Holofernes would have killed him for this word,
verses.textLatin: In medio itaque seniorum, et in conspectu omnium, Achior dixit omnia quæ locutus ipse fuerat ab Holoferne interrogatus: et qualiter populus Holofernis voluisset propter hoc verbum interficere eum,

verses.text: And how Holofernes himself being angry had commanded him to be delivered for this cause to the Israelites: that when he should overcome the children of Israel, then he might command Achior also himself to be put to death by diverse torments, for having said: The God of heaven is their defender.
verses.textLatin: et quemadmodum ipse Holofernes iratus jusserit eum Israëlitis hac de causa tradi, ut dum vicerit filios Israël, tunc et ipsum Achior diversis jubeat interire suppliciis, propter hoc quod dixisset: Deus cæli defensor eorum est.

verses.text: And when Achior had declared all these things, all the people fell upon their faces, adoring the Lord, and all of them together mourning and weeping poured out their prayers with one accord to the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Cumque Achior universa hæc exposuisset, omnis populus cecidit in faciem, adorantes Dominum, et communi lamentatione et fletu unanimes preces suas Domino effuderunt,

verses.text: Saying: O Lord God of heaven and earth, behold their pride, and look on our low condition, and have regard to the face of thy saints, and shew that thou forsakest not them that trust on thee, and that thou humblest them that presume of themselves, and glory in their own strength.
verses.textLatin: dicentes: Domine Deus cæli et terræ, intuere superbiam eorum, et respice ad nostram humilitatem, et faciem sanctorum tuorum attende, et ostende quoniam non derelinquis præsumentes de te: et præsumentes de se, et de sua virtute gloriantes, humilias.

verses.text: So when their weeping was ended, and the people’s prayer, in which they continued all the day, was concluded, they comforted Achior,
verses.textLatin: Finito itaque fletu, et per totam diem oratione populorum completa, consolati sunt Achior,

verses.text: Saying: The God of our fathers, whose power thou hast set forth, will make this return to thee, that thou rather shalt see their destruction.
verses.textLatin: dicentes: Deus patrum nostrorum, cujus tu virtutem prædicasti, ipse tibi hanc dabit vicissitudinem, ut eorum magis tu interitum videas.

verses.text: And when the Lord our God shall give this liberty to his servants, let God be with thee also in the midst of us: that as it shall please thee, so thou with all thine mayst converse with us.
verses.textLatin: Cum vero Dominus Deus noster dederit hanc libertatem servis suis, sit et tecum Deus in medio nostri: ut sicut placuerit tibi, ita cum tuis omnibus converseris nobiscum.

verses.text: Then Ozias, after the assembly was broken up, received him into his house, and made him a great supper.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Ozias, finito consilio, suscepit eum in domum suam, et fecit ei cœnam magnam.

verses.text: And all the ancients were invited, and they refreshed themselves together after their fast was over.
verses.textLatin: Et vocatis omnibus presbyteris, simul expleto jejunio refecerunt.

verses.text: And afterwards all the people were called together, and they prayed all the night long within the church, desiring help of the God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Postea vero convocatus est omnis populus, et per totam noctem intra ecclesiam oraverunt, petentes auxilium a Deo Israël.

verses.text: But  Holofernes on the next day gave orders to his army, to go up against Bethulia.
verses.textLatin: Holofernes autem altera die præcepit exercitibus suis ut ascenderent contra Bethuliam.

verses.text: Now there were in his troops a hundred and twenty thousand footmen, and two and twenty thousand horsemen, besides the preparations of those men who had been taken, and who had been brought away out of the provinces and cities of all the youth.
verses.textLatin: Erant autem pedites bellatorum centum viginti millia, et equites viginti duo millia, præter præparationes virorum illorum quos occupaverat captivitas, et abducti fuerant de provinciis et urbibus universæ juventutis.

verses.text: All these prepared themselves together to fight against the children of Israel, and they came by the hillside to the top, which looketh toward Dothain, from the place which is called Belma, unto Chelmon, which is over against Esdrelon.
verses.textLatin: Omnes paraverunt se pariter ad pugnam contra filios Israël, et venerunt per crepidinem montis usque ad apicem, qui respicit super Dothain, a loco qui dicitur Belma usque ad Chelmon, qui est contra Esdrelon.

verses.text: But the children of Israel, when they saw the multitude of them, prostrated themselves upon the ground, putting ashes upon their heads, praying with one accord, that the God of Israel would shew his mercy upon his people.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem Israël, ut viderunt multitudinem illorum, prostraverunt se super terram, mittentes cinerem super capita sua, unanimes orantes ut Deus Israël misericordiam suam ostenderet super populum suum.

verses.text: And taking their arms of war, they posted themselves at the places, which by a narrow pathway lead directly between the mountains, and they guarded them all day and night.
verses.textLatin: Et assumentes arma sua bellica, sederunt per loca quæ ad angusti itineris tramitem dirigunt inter montosa, et erant custodientes ea tota die et nocte.

verses.text: Now Holofernes, in going round about, found that the fountain which supplied them with water, ran through an aqueduct without the city on the south side: and he commanded their aqueduct to be cut off.
verses.textLatin: Porro Holofernes, dum circuit per gyrum, reperit quod fons qui influebat, aquæductum illorum a parte australi extra civitatem dirigeret: et incidi præcepit aquæductum illorum.

verses.text: Nevertheless there were springs not far from the walls, out of which they were seen secretly to draw water, to refresh themselves a little rather than to drink their fill.
verses.textLatin: Erant tamen non longe a muris fontes, ex quibus furtim videbantur haurire aquam ad refocillandum potius quam ad potandum.

verses.text: But the children of Ammon and Moab came to Holofernes, saying: The children of Israel trust not in their spears, nor in their arrows, but the mountains are their defence, and the steep hills and precipices guard them.
verses.textLatin: Sed filii Ammon et Moab accesserunt ad Holofernem, dicentes: Filii Israël non in lancea nec in sagitta confidunt, sed montes defendunt illos, et muniunt illos colles in præcipitio constituti.

verses.text: Wherefore that thou mayst overcome them without joining battle, set guards at the springs that they may not draw water out of them, and thou shalt destroy them without sword, or at least being wearied out they will yield up their city, which they suppose, because it is situate in the mountains, to be impregnable.
verses.textLatin: Ut ergo sine congressione pugnæ possis superare eos, pone custodes fontium, ut non hauriant aquam ex eis, et sine gladio interficies eos, vel certe fatigati tradent civitatem suam, quam putant in montibus positam superari non posse.

verses.text: And these words pleased Holofernes, and his officers, and he placed all round about a hundred men at every spring.
verses.textLatin: Et placuerunt verba hæc coram Holoferne et coram satellitibus ejus, et constituit per gyrum centenarios per singulos fontes.

verses.text: And when they had kept this watch for full twenty days, the cisterns, and the reserve of waters failed among all the inhabitants of Bethulia, so that there was not within the city, enough to satisfy them, no not for one day, for water was daily given out to the people by measure.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ista custodia per dies viginti fuisset expleta, defecerunt cisternæ et collectiones aquarum omnibus habitantibus Bethuliam, ita ut non esset intra civitatem unde satiarentur vel una die, quoniam ad mensuram dabatur populis aqua quotidie.

verses.text: Then all the men and women, young men, and children, gathering themselves together to Ozias, all together with one voice,
verses.textLatin: Tunc ad Oziam congregati omnes viri feminæque, juvenes et parvuli, omnes simul una voce

verses.text: Said: God be judge between us and thee, for thou hast done evil against us, in that thou wouldst not speak peaceably with the Assyrians, and for this cause God hath sold us into their hands.
verses.textLatin: dixerunt: Judicet Deus inter nos et te, quoniam fecisti in nos mala, nolens loqui pacifice cum Assyriis, et propter hoc vendidit nos Deus in manibus eorum.

verses.text: And therefore there is no one to help us, while we are cast down before their eyes in thirst, and sad destruction.
verses.textLatin: Et ideo non est qui adjuvet, cum prosternamur ante oculos eorum in siti, et perditione magna.

verses.text: And now assemble ye all that are in the city, that we may of our own accord yield ourselves all up to the people of Holofernes.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc congregate universos qui in civitate sunt, ut sponte tradamus nos omnes populo Holofernis.

verses.text: For it is better, that being captives we should live and bless the Lord, than that we should die, and be a reproach to all flesh, after we have seen our wives and our infants die before our eyes.
verses.textLatin: Melius est enim ut captivi benedicamus Dominum viventes, quam moriamur, et simus opprobrium omni carni, cum viderimus uxores nostras et infantes nostros mori ante oculos nostros.

verses.text: We call to witness this day heaven and earth, and the God of our fathers, who taketh vengeance upon us according to our sins, conjuring you to deliver now the city into the hand of the army of Holofernes, that our end may be short by the edge of the sword, which is made longer by the drought of thirst.
verses.textLatin: Contestamur hodie cælum et terram, et Deum patrum nostrorum, qui ulciscitur nos secundum peccata nostra, ut jam tradatis civitatem in manu militiæ Holofernis, et sit finis noster brevis in ore gladii, qui longior efficitur in ariditate sitis.

verses.text: And when they had said these things, there was great weeping and lamentation of all in the assembly, and for many hours with one voice they cried to God, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et cum hæc dixissent, factus est fletus et ululatus magnus in ecclesia ab omnibus, et per multas horas una voce clamaverunt ad Deum, dicentes:

verses.text: We have sinned with our fathers, we have done unjustly, we have committed iniquity:
verses.textLatin: Peccavimus cum patribus nostris: injuste egimus, iniquitatem fecimus.

verses.text: Have thou mercy on us, because thou art good, or punish our iniquities by chastising us thyself, and deliver not them that trust in thee to a people that knoweth not thee,
verses.textLatin: Tu, quia pius es, miserere nostri, aut in tuo flagello vindica iniquitates nostras, et noli tradere confitentes te populo qui ignorat te,

verses.text: That they may not say among the Gentiles: Where is their God?
verses.textLatin: ut non dicant inter gentes: Ubi est Deus eorum?

verses.text: And when being wearied with these cries, and tired with these weepings, they held their peace,
verses.textLatin: Et cum fatigati ex his clamoribus et his fletibus lassati siluissent,

verses.text: Ozias rising up all in tears, said: Be of good courage, my brethren, and let us wait these five days for mercy from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: exsurgens Ozias infusus lacrimis, dixit: Æquo animo estote, fratres, et hos quinque dies expectemus a Domino misericordiam.

verses.text: For perhaps he will put a stop to his indignation, and will give glory to his own name.
verses.textLatin: Forsitan enim indignationem suam abscindet, et dabit gloriam nomini suo.

verses.text: But if after five days be past there come no aid, we will do the things which you have spoken.
verses.textLatin: Si autem transactis quinque diebus non venerit adjutorium, faciemus hæc verba quæ locuti estis.

verses.text: Now  it came to pass, when Judith a widow had heard these words, who was the daughter of Merari, the son of Idox, the son of Joseph, the son of Ozias, the son of Elai, the son of Jamnor, the son of Gedeon, the son of Raphaim, the son of Achitob, the son of Melchias, the son of Enan, the son of Nathanias, the son of Salathiel, the son of Simeon, the son of Ruben:
verses.textLatin: Et factum est cum audisset hæc verba Judith vidua, quæ erat filia Merari filii Idox filii Joseph filii Oziæ filii Elai filii Jamnor filii Gedeon filii Raphaim filii Achitob filii Melchiæ filii Enan filii Nathaniæ filii Salathiel filii Simeon filii Ruben,

verses.text: And her husband was Manasses, who died in the time of the barley harvest:
verses.textLatin: et vir ejus fuit Manasses, qui mortuus est in diebus messis hordeaceæ:

verses.text: For he was standing over them that bound sheaves in the field; and the heat came upon his head, and he died in Bethulia his own city, and was buried there with his fathers.
verses.textLatin: instabat enim super alligantes manipulos in campo, et venit æstus super caput ejus, et mortuus est in Bethulia civitate sua, et sepultus est illic cum patribus suis.

verses.text: And Judith his relict was a widow now three years and six months.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Judith relicta ejus vidua jam annis tribus et mensibus sex.

verses.text: And she made herself a private chamber in the upper part of her house, in which she abode shut up with her maids.
verses.textLatin: Et in superioribus domus suæ fecit sibi secretum cubiculum, in quo cum puellis suis clausa morabatur,

verses.text: And she wore haircloth upon her loins, and fasted all the days of her life, except the sabbaths, and new moons, and the feasts of the house of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et habens super lumbos suos cilicium, jejunabat omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, præter sabbata et neomenias et festa domus Israël.

verses.text: And she was exceedingly beautiful, and her husband left her great riches, and very many servants, and large possessions of herds of oxen, and flocks of sheep.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem eleganti aspectu nimis, cui vir suus reliquerat divitias multas, et familiam copiosam, ac possessiones armentis boum, et gregibus ovium plenas.

verses.text: And she was greatly renowned among all, because she feared the Lord very much, neither was there any one that spoke an ill word of her.
verses.textLatin: Et erat hæc in omnibus famosissima, quoniam timebat Dominum valde, nec erat qui loqueretur de illa verbum malum.

verses.text: When therefore she had heard that Ozias had promised that he would deliver up the city after the fifth day, she sent to the ancients Chabri and Charmi.
verses.textLatin: Hæc itaque cum audisset quoniam Ozias promisisset quod transacto quinto die traderet civitatem, misit ad presbyteros Chabri et Charmi.

verses.text: And they came to her, and she said to them: What is this word, by which Ozias hath consented to give up the city to the Assyrians, if within five days there come no aid to us?
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt ad illam, et dixit illis: Quod est hoc verbum, in quo consensit Ozias, ut tradat civitatem Assyriis si intra quinque dies non venerit vobis adjutorium?

verses.text: And who are you that tempt the Lord?
verses.textLatin: et qui estis vos, qui tentatis Dominum?

verses.text: This is not a word that may draw down mercy, but rather that may stir up wrath, and enkindle indignation.
verses.textLatin: non est iste sermo qui misericordiam provocet, sed potius qui iram excitet, et furorem accendat.

verses.text: You have set a time for the mercy of the Lord, and you have appointed him a day, according to your pleasure.
verses.textLatin: Posuistis vos tempus miserationis Domini, et in arbitrium vestrum, diem constituistis ei.

verses.text: But forasmuch as the Lord is patient, let us be penitent for this same thing, and with many tears let us beg his pardon:
verses.textLatin: Sed quia patiens Dominus est, in hoc ipso pœniteamus, et indulgentiam ejus fusis lacrimis postulemus:

verses.text: For God will not threaten like man, nor be inflamed to anger like the son of man.
verses.textLatin: non enim quasi homo sic Deus comminabitur, neque sicut filius hominis ad iracundiam inflammabitur.

verses.text: And therefore let us humble our souls before him, and continuing in an humble spirit, in his service:
verses.textLatin: Et ideo humiliemus illi animas nostras, et in spiritu constituti humiliato, servientes illi

verses.text: Let us ask the Lord with tears, that according to his will so he would shew his mercy to us: that as our heart is troubled by their pride, so also we may glorify in our humility.
verses.textLatin: dicamus flentes Domino, ut secundum voluntatem suam sic faciat nobiscum misericordiam suam: ut sicut conturbatum est cor nostrum in superbia eorum, ita etiam de nostra humilitate gloriemur:

verses.text: For we have not followed the sins of our fathers, who forsook their God, and worshipped strange gods.
verses.textLatin: quoniam non sumus secuti peccata patrum nostrorum, qui dereliquerunt Deum suum, et adoraverunt deos alienos,

verses.text: For which crime they were given up to their enemies, to the sword, and to pillage, and to confusion: but we know no other God but him.
verses.textLatin: pro quo scelere dati sunt in gladium, et in rapinam, et in confusionem inimicis suis: nos autem alterum deum nescimus præter ipsum.

verses.text: Let us humbly wait for his consolation, and the Lord our God will require our blood of the afflictions of our enemies, and he will humble all the nations that shall rise up against us, and bring them to disgrace.
verses.textLatin: Expectemus humiles consolationem ejus, et exquiret sanguinem nostrum de afflictionibus inimicorum nostrorum, et humiliabit omnes gentes, quæcumque insurgunt contra nos, et faciet illas sine honore Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: And now, brethren, as you are the ancients among the people of God, and their very soul resteth upon you: comfort their hearts by your speech, that they may be mindful how our fathers were tempted that they might be proved, whether they worshipped their God truly.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc fratres, quoniam vos estis presbyteri in populo Dei, et ex vobis pendet anima illorum, ad eloquium vestrum corda eorum erigite, ut memores sint quia tentati sunt patres nostri, ut probarentur si vere colerent Deum suum.

verses.text: They must remember how our father Abraham was tempted, and being proved by many tribulations, was made the friend of God.
verses.textLatin: Memores esse debent quomodo pater noster Abraham tentatus est, et per multas tribulationes probatus, Dei amicus effectus est.

verses.text: So Isaac, so Jacob, so Moses, and all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful.
verses.textLatin: Sic Isaac, sic Jacob, sic Moyses, et omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles.

verses.text: But they that did not receive the trials with the fear of the Lord, but uttered their impatience and the reproach of their murmuring against the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Illi autem qui tentationes non susceperunt cum timore Domini, et impatientiam suam et improperium murmurationis suæ contra Dominum protulerunt,

verses.text: Were destroyed by the destroyer, and perished by serpents.
verses.textLatin: exterminati sunt ab exterminatore, et a serpentibus perierunt.

verses.text: As for us therefore let us not revenge ourselves for these things which we suffer.
verses.textLatin: Et nos ergo non ulciscamur nos pro his quæ patimur,

verses.text: But esteeming these very punishments to be less than our sins deserve, let us believe that these scourges of the Lord, with which like servants we are chastised, have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction.
verses.textLatin: sed reputantes peccatis nostris hæc ipsa supplicia minora esse flagella Domini, quibus quasi servi corripimur ad emendationem, et non ad perditionem nostram evenisse credamus.

verses.text: And Ozias and the ancients said to her: All things which thou hast spoken are true, and there is nothing to be reprehended in thy words.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt illi Ozias et presbyteri: Omnia quæ locuta es, vera sunt, et non est in sermonibus tuis ulla reprehensio.

verses.text: Now therefore pray for us, for thou art a holy woman, and one fearing God.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo ora pro nobis, quoniam mulier sancta es, et timens Deum.

verses.text: And Judith said to them: As you know that what I have been able to say is of God:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit illis Judith: Sicut quod potui loqui, Dei esse cognoscitis,

verses.text: So that which I intend to do prove ye if it be of God, and pray that God may strengthen my design.
verses.textLatin: ita quod facere disposui, probate si ex Deo est, et orate ut firmum faciat Deus consilium meum.

verses.text: You shall stand at the gate this night, and I will go out with my maidservant: and pray ye, that as you have said, in five days the Lord may look down upon his people Israel.
verses.textLatin: Stabitis vos ad portam nocte ista, et ego exeam cum abra mea: et orate, ut sicut dixistis, in diebus quinque respiciat Dominus populum suum Israël.

verses.text: But I desire that you search not into what I am doing, and till I bring you word let nothing else be done but to pray for me to the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem nolo ut scrutemini actum meum, et usque dum renuntiem vobis, nihil aliud fiat, nisi oratio pro me ad Dominum Deum nostrum.

verses.text: And Ozias the prince of Juda said to her: Go in peace, and the Lord be with thee to take revenge of our enemies. So returning they departed.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad eam Ozias princeps Juda: Vade in pace, et Dominus sit tecum in ultionem inimicorum nostrorum. Et revertentes abierunt.

verses.text: And  when they were gone, Judith went into her oratory: and putting on haircloth, laid ashes on her head: and falling down prostrate before the Lord, she cried to the Lord, saying:
verses.textLatin: Quibus ascendentibus, Judith ingressa est oratorium suum: et induens se cilicio, posuit cinerem super caput suum: et prosternens se Domino, clamabat ad Dominum, dicens:

verses.text: O Lord God of my father Simeon, who gavest him a sword to execute vengeance against strangers, who had defiled by their uncleanness, and uncovered the virgin unto confusion:
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus patris mei Simeon, qui dedisti illi gladium in defensionem alienigenarum, qui violatores extiterunt in coinquinatione sua, et denudaverunt femur virginis in confusionem:

verses.text: And who gavest their wives to be made a prey, and their daughters into captivity: and all their spoils to be divided to thy servants, who were zealous with thy zeal: assist, I beseech thee, O Lord God, me a widow.
verses.textLatin: et dedisti mulieres illorum in prædam, et filias illorum in captivitatem: et omnem prædam in divisionem servis tuis, qui zelaverunt zelum tuum: subveni, quæso te, Domine Deus meus, mihi viduæ.

verses.text: For thou hast done the things of old, and hast devised one thing after another: and what thou hast designed hath been done.
verses.textLatin: Tu enim fecisti priora, et illa post illa cogitasti: et hoc factum est quod ipse voluisti.

verses.text: For all thy ways are prepared, and in thy providence thou hast placed thy judgments.
verses.textLatin: Omnes enim viæ tuæ paratæ sunt, et tua judicia in tua providentia posuisti.

verses.text: Look upon the camp of the Assyrians now, as thou wast pleased to look upon the camp of the Egyptians, when they pursued armed after thy servants, trusting in their chariots, and in their horsemen, and in a multitude of warriors.
verses.textLatin: Respice castra Assyriorum nunc, sicut tunc castra Ægyptiorum videre dignatus es, quando post servos tuos armati currebant, confidentes in quadrigis, et in equitatu suo, et in multitudine bellatorum.

verses.text: But thou lookedst over their camp, and darkness wearied them.
verses.textLatin: Sed aspexisti super castra eorum, et tenebræ fatigaverunt eos.

verses.text: The deep held their feet, and the waters overwhelmed them.
verses.textLatin: Tenuit pedes eorum abyssus, et aquæ operuerunt eos.

verses.text: So may it be with these also, O Lord, who trust in their multitude, and in their chariots, and in their pikes, and in their shields, and in their arrows, and glory in their spears,
verses.textLatin: Sic fiant et isti, Domine, qui confidunt in multitudine sua, et in curribus suis, et in contis, et in scutis, et in sagittis suis, et in lanceis gloriantur,

verses.text: And know not that thou art our God, who destroyest wars from the beginning, and the Lord is thy name.
verses.textLatin: et nesciunt quia tu ipse es Deus noster, qui conteris bella ab initio, et Dominus nomen est tibi.

verses.text: Lift up thy arm as from the beginning, and crush their power with thy power: let their power fall in their wrath, who promise themselves to violate thy sanctuary, and defile the dwelling place of thy name, and to beat down with their sword the horn of thy altar.
verses.textLatin: Erige brachium tuum sicut ab initio, et allide virtutem illorum in virtute tua: cadat virtus eorum in iracundia tua, qui promittunt se violare sancta tua, et polluere tabernaculum nominis tui, et dejicere gladio suo cornu altaris tui.

verses.text: Bring to pass, O Lord, that his pride may be cut off with his own sword.
verses.textLatin: Fac, Domine, ut gladio proprio ejus superbia amputetur:

verses.text: Let him be caught in the net of his own eyes in my regard, and do thou strike him by the graces of the words of my lips.
verses.textLatin: capiatur laqueo oculorum suorum in me, et percuties eum ex labiis caritatis meæ.

verses.text: Give me constancy in my mind, that I may despise him: and fortitude that I may overthrow him.
verses.textLatin: Da mihi in animo constantiam ut contemnam illum, et virtutem, ut evertam illum.

verses.text: For this will be a glorious monument for thy name, when he shall fall by the hand of a woman.
verses.textLatin: Erit enim hoc memoriale nominis tui, cum manus feminæ dejecerit eum.

verses.text: For thy power, O Lord, is not in a multitude, nor is thy pleasure in the strength of horses, nor from the beginning have the proud been acceptable to thee: but the prayer of the humble and the meek hath always pleased thee.
verses.textLatin: Non enim in multitudine est virtus tua, Domine, neque in equorum viribus voluntas tua est, nec superbi ab initio placuerunt tibi: sed humilium et mansuetorum semper tibi placuit deprecatio.

verses.text: O God of the heavens, creator of the waters, and Lord of the whole creation, hear me a poor wretch, making supplication to thee, and presuming of thy mercy.
verses.textLatin: Deus cælorum, creator aquarum, et Dominus totius creaturæ, exaudi me miseram deprecantem, et de tua misericordia præsumentem.

verses.text: Remember, O Lord, thy covenant, and put thou words in my mouth, and strengthen the resolution in my heart, that thy house may continue in thy holiness:
verses.textLatin: Memento, Domine, testamenti tui, et da verbum in ore meo, et in corde meo consilium corrobora, ut domus tua in sanctificatione tua permaneat:

verses.text: And all nations may acknowledge that thou art God, and there is no other besides thee.
verses.textLatin: et omnes gentes agnoscant quia tu es Deus, et non est alius præter te.

verses.text: And  it came to pass, when she had ceased to cry to the Lord, that she rose from the place wherein she lay prostrate before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem, cum cessasset clamare ad Dominum, surrexit de loco in quo jacuerat prostrata ad Dominum.

verses.text: And she called her maid, and going down into her house she took off her haircloth, and put away the garments of her widowhood,
verses.textLatin: Vocavitque abram suam, et descendens in domum suam, abstulit a se cilicium, et exuit se vestimentis viduitatis suæ,

verses.text: And she washed her body, and anointed herself with the best ointment, and plaited the hair of her head, and put a bonnet upon her head, and clothed herself with the garments of her gladness, and put sandals on her feet, and took her bracelets, and lilies, and earlets, and rings, and adorned herself with all her ornaments.
verses.textLatin: et lavit corpus suum, et unxit se myro optimo, et discriminavit crinem capitis sui, et imposuit mitram super caput suum, et induit se vestimentis jucunditatis suæ, induitque sandalia pedibus suis, assumpsitque dextraliola, et lilia, et inaures, et annulos, et omnibus ornamentis suis ornavit se.

verses.text: And the Lord also gave her more beauty: because all this dressing up did not proceed from sensuality, but from virtue: and therefore the Lord increased this her beauty, so that she appeared to all men’s eyes incomparably lovely.
verses.textLatin: Cui etiam Dominus contulit splendorem: quoniam omnis ista compositio non ex libidine, sed ex virtute pendebat: et ideo Dominus hanc in illam pulchritudinem ampliavit, ut incomparabili decore omnium oculis appareret.

verses.text: And she gave to her maid a bottle of wine to carry, and a vessel of oil, and parched corn, and dry figs, and bread and cheese, and went out.
verses.textLatin: Imposuit itaque abræ suæ ascoperam vini, et vas olei, et polentam, et palathas, et panes, et caseum, et profecta est.

verses.text: And when they came to the gate of the city, they found Ozias, and the ancients of the city waiting.
verses.textLatin: Cumque venissent ad portam civitatis, invenerunt expectantem Oziam et presbyteros civitatis.

verses.text: And when they saw her they were astonished, and admired her beauty exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum vidissent eam, stupentes mirati sunt nimis pulchritudinem ejus.

verses.text: But they asked her no question, only they let her pass, saying: The God of our fathers give thee grace, and may he strengthen all the counsel of thy heart with his power, that Jerusalem may glory in thee, and thy name may be in the number of the holy and just.
verses.textLatin: Nihil tamen interrogantes eam, dimiserunt transire, dicentes: Deus patrum nostrorum det tibi gratiam, et omne consilium tui cordis sua virtute corroboret, ut glorietur super te Jerusalem, et sit nomen tuum in numero sanctorum et justorum.

verses.text: And they that were there said, all with one voice: So be it, so be it.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt hi qui illic erant omnes una voce: Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: But Judith praying to the Lord, passed through the gates, she and her maid.
verses.textLatin: Judith vero orans Dominum, transivit per portas, ipsa et abra ejus.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when she went down the hill, about break of day, that the watchmen of the Assyrians met her, and stopped her, saying: Whence comest thou? or whither goest thou?
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem cum descenderet montem, circa ortum diei, occurrerunt ei exploratores Assyriorum, et tenuerunt eam, dicentes: Unde venis? aut quo vadis?

verses.text: And she answered: I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I am fled from them, because I knew they would be made a prey to you, because they despised you, and would not of their own accord yield themselves, that they might find mercy in your sight.
verses.textLatin: Quæ respondit: Filia sum Hebræorum, ideo ego fugi a facie eorum, quoniam futurum agnovi quod dentur vobis in deprædationem, pro eo quod contemnentes vos, noluerunt ultro tradere seipsos ut invenirent misericordiam in conspectu vestro.

verses.text: For this reason I thought with myself, saying: I will go to the presence of the prince Holofernes, that I may tell him their secrets, and shew him by what way he may take them, without the loss of one man of his army.
verses.textLatin: Hac de causa cogitavi mecum, dicens: Vadam ad faciem principis Holofernis, ut indicem illi secreta illorum, et ostendam illi quo aditu possit obtinere eos, ita ut non cadat vir unus de exercitu ejus.

verses.text: And when the men had heard her words, they beheld her face, and their eyes were amazed, for they wondered exceedingly at her beauty.
verses.textLatin: Et cum audissent viri illi verba ejus, considerabant faciem ejus, et erat in oculis eorum stupor, quoniam pulchritudinem ejus mirabantur nimis.

verses.text: And they said to her: Thou hast saved thy life by taking this resolution, to come down to our lord.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt ad eam: Conservasti animam tuam, eo quod tale reperisti consilium, ut descenderes ad dominum nostrum.

verses.text: And be assured of this, that when thou shalt stand before him, he will treat thee well, and thou wilt be most acceptable to his heart. And they brought her to the tent of Holofernes, telling him of her.
verses.textLatin: Hoc autem scias, quoniam cum steteris in conspectu ejus, bene tibi faciet, et eris gratissima in corde ejus. Duxeruntque illam ad tabernaculum Holofernis, annuntiantes eam.

verses.text: And when she was come into his presence, forthwith Holofernes was caught by his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Cumque intrasset ante faciem ejus, statim captus est in suis oculis Holofernes.

verses.text: And his officers said to him: Who can despise the people of the Hebrews, who have such beautiful women, that we should not think it worth our while for their sakes to fight against them?
verses.textLatin: Dixeruntque ad eum satellites ejus: Quis contemnat populum Hebræorum, qui tam decoras mulieres habent, ut non pro his merito pugnare contra eos debeamus?

verses.text: And Judith seeing Holofernes sitting under a canopy, which was woven of purple and gold, with emeralds and precious stones:
verses.textLatin: Videns itaque Judith Holofernem sedentem in conopeo, quod erat ex purpura, et auro, et smaragdo, et lapidibus pretiosis intextum,

verses.text: After she had looked on his face, bowed down to him, prostrating herself to the ground. And the servants of Holofernes lifted her up, by the command of their master.
verses.textLatin: et cum in faciem ejus intendisset, adoravit eum, prosternens se super terram. Et elevaverunt eam servi Holofernis, jubente domino suo.

verses.text: Then  Holofernes said to her: Be of good comfort, and fear not in thy heart: for I have never hurt a man that was willing to serve Nabuchodonosor the king.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Holofernes dixit ei: Æquo animo esto, et noli pavere in corde tuo: quoniam ego numquam nocui viro qui voluit servire Nabuchodonosor regi:

verses.text: And if thy people had not despised me, I would never have lifted up my spear against them.
verses.textLatin: populus autem tuus, si non contempsisset me, non levassem lanceam meam super eum.

verses.text: But now tell me, for what cause hast thou left them, and why it hath pleased thee to come to us?
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem dic mihi, qua ex causa recessisti ab illis, et placuit tibi ut venires ad nos?

verses.text: And Judith said to him: Receive the words of thy handmaid, for if thou wilt follow the words of thy handmaid, the Lord will do with thee a perfect thing.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit illi Judith: Sume verba ancillæ tuæ, quoniam si secutus fueris verba ancillæ tuæ, perfectam rem faciet Dominus tecum.

verses.text: For as Nabuchodonosor the king of the earth liveth, and his power liveth which is in thee for chastising of all straying souls: not only men serve him through thee, but also the beasts of the field obey him.
verses.textLatin: Vivit enim Nabuchodonosor rex terræ, et vivit virtus ejus, quæ est in te ad correptionem omnium animarum errantium: quoniam non solum homines serviunt illi per te, sed et bestiæ agri obtemperant illi.

verses.text: For the industry of thy mind is spoken of among all nations, and it is told through the whole world, that thou only art excellent, and mighty in all his kingdom, and thy discipline is cried up in all provinces.
verses.textLatin: Nuntiatur enim animi tui industria universis gentibus, et indicatum est omni sæculo quoniam tu solus bonus et potens es in omni regno ejus: et disciplina tua omnibus provinciis prædicatur.

verses.text: It is known also what Achior said, nor are we ignorant of what thou hast commanded to be done to him.
verses.textLatin: Nec hoc latet, quod locutus est Achior, nec illud ignoratur, quod ei jusseris evenire.

verses.text: For it is certain that our God is so offended with sins, that he hath sent word by his prophets to the people, that he will deliver them up for their sins.
verses.textLatin: Constat enim Deum nostrum sic peccatis offensum, ut mandaverit per prophetas suos ad populum quod tradat eum pro peccatis suis.

verses.text: And because the children of Israel know they have offended their God, thy dread is upon them.
verses.textLatin: Et quoniam sciunt se offendisse Deum suum filii Israël, tremor tuus super ipsos est.

verses.text: Moreover also a famine hath come upon them, and for drought of water they are already to be counted among the dead.
verses.textLatin: Insuper etiam fames invasit eos, et ab ariditate aquæ jam inter mortuos computantur.

verses.text: And they have a design even to kill their cattle, and to drink the blood of them.
verses.textLatin: Denique hoc ordinant, ut interficient pecora sua, et bibant sanguinem eorum:

verses.text: And the consecrated things of the Lord their God which God forbade them to touch, in corn, wine, and oil, these have they purposed to make use of, and they design to consume the things which they ought not to touch with their hands: therefore because they do these things, it is certain they will be given up to destruction.
verses.textLatin: et sancta Domini Dei sui, quæ præcepit Deus non contingi, in frumento, vino, et oleo, hæc cogitaverunt impendere, et volunt consumere quæ nec manibus deberent contingere: ergo quoniam hæc faciunt, certum est quod in perditionem dabuntur.

verses.text: And I thy handmaid knowing this, am fled from them, and the Lord hath sent me to tell thee these very things.
verses.textLatin: Quod ego ancilla tua cognoscens, fugi ab illis, et misit me Dominus hæc ipsa nuntiare tibi.

verses.text: For I thy handmaid worship God even now that I am with thee, and thy handmaid will go out, and I will pray to God,
verses.textLatin: Ego enim ancilla tua Deum colo, etiam nunc apud te: et exiet ancilla tua, et orabo Deum,

verses.text: And he will tell me when he will repay them for their sins, and I will come and tell thee, so that I may bring thee through the midst of Jerusalem, and thou shalt have all the people of Israel, as sheep that have no shepherd, and there shall not so much as one dog bark against thee:
verses.textLatin: et dicet mihi quando eis reddat peccatum suum, et veniens nuntiabo tibi, ita ut ego adducam te per mediam Jerusalem, et habebis omnem populum Israël, sicut oves quibus non est pastor, et non latrabit vel unus canis contra te:

verses.text: Because these things are told me by the providence of God.
verses.textLatin: quoniam hæc mihi dicta sunt per providentiam Dei,

verses.text: And because God is angry with them, I am sent to tell these very things to thee.
verses.textLatin: et quoniam iratus est illis Deus, hæc ipsa missa sum nuntiare tibi.

verses.text: And all these words pleased Holofernes, and his servants, and they admired her wisdom, and they said one to another:
verses.textLatin: Placuerunt autem omnia verba hæc coram Holoferne, et coram pueris ejus, et mirabantur sapientiam ejus, et dicebant alter ad alterum:

verses.text: There is not such another woman upon earth in look, in beauty, and in sense of words.
verses.textLatin: Non est talis mulier super terram in aspectu, in pulchritudine, et in sensu verborum.

verses.text: And Holofernes said to her: God hath done well who sent thee before the people, that thou mightest give them into our hands:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad illam Holofernes: Benefecit Deus, qui misit te ante populum, ut des illum tu in manibus nostris:

verses.text: And because thy promise is good, if thy God shall do this for me, he shall also be my God, and thou shalt be great in the house of Nabuchodonosor, and thy name shall be renowned through all the earth.
verses.textLatin: et quoniam bona est promissio tua, si fecerit mihi hoc Deus tuus, erit et Deus meus, et tu in domo Nabuchodonosor magna eris, et nomen tuum nominabitur in universa terra.

verses.text: Then  he ordered that she should go in where his treasures were laid up, and bade her tarry there, and he appointed what should be given her from his own table.
verses.textLatin: Tunc jussit eam introire ubi repositi erant thesauri ejus, et jussit illic manere eam, et constituit quid daretur illi de convivio suo.

verses.text: And Judith answered him and said: Now I cannot eat of these things which thou commandest to be given me, lest sin come upon me: but I will eat of the things which I have brought.
verses.textLatin: Cui respondit Judith, et dixit: Nunc non potero manducare ex his quæ mihi præcipis tribui, ne veniat super me offensio: ex his autem quæ mihi detuli, manducabo.

verses.text: And Holofernes said to her: If these things which thou hast brought with thee fail thee, what shall we do for thee?
verses.textLatin: Cui Holofernes ait: Si defecerint tibi ista, quæ tecum detulisti, quid faciemus tibi?

verses.text: And Judith said: As thy soul liveth, my lord, thy handmaid shall not spend all these things till God do by my hand that which I have purposed. And his servants brought her into the tent which he had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Judith: Vivit anima tua, domine meus, quoniam non expendet omnia hæc ancilla tua, donec faciat Deus in manu mea hæc quæ cogitavi. Et induxerunt illam servi ejus in tabernaculum quod præceperat.

verses.text: And when she was going in, she desired that she might have liberty to go out at night and before day to prayer, and to beseech the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et petiit dum introiret, ut daretur ei copia nocte et ante lucem egrediendi foras ad orationem, et deprecandi Dominum.

verses.text: And he commanded his chamberlains, that she might go out and in, to adore her God as she pleased, for three days.
verses.textLatin: Et præcepit cubiculariis suis ut sicut placeret illi, exiret et introiret ad adorandum Deum suum per triduum:

verses.text: And she went out in the nights into the valley of Bethulia, and washed herself in a fountain of water.
verses.textLatin: et exibat noctibus in vallem Bethuliæ, et baptizabat se in fonte aquæ.

verses.text: And as she came up, she prayed to the Lord the God of Israel, that he would direct her way to the deliverance of his people.
verses.textLatin: Et ut ascendebat, orabat Dominum Deum Israël ut dirigeret viam ejus ad liberationem populi sui.

verses.text: And going in, she remained pure in the tent, until she took her own meat in the evening.
verses.textLatin: Et introiens, munda manebat in tabernaculo usque dum acciperet escam suam in vespere.

verses.text: And it came to pass on the fourth day, that Holofernes made a supper for his servants, and said to Vagao his eunuch: Go, and persuade that Hebrew woman, to consent of her own accord to dwell with me.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, in quarto die Holofernes fecit cœnam servis suis, et dixit ad Vagao eunuchum suum: Vade, et suade Hebræam illam ut sponte consentiat habitare mecum.

verses.text: For it is looked upon as shameful among the Assyrians, if a woman mock a man, by doing so as to pass free from him.
verses.textLatin: Fœdum est enim apud Assyrios, si femina irrideat virum agendo ut immunis ab eo transeat.

verses.text: Then Vagao went in to Judith, and said: Let not my good maid be afraid to go in to my lord, that she may be honoured before his face, that she may eat with him and drink wine and be merry.
verses.textLatin: Tunc introivit Vagao ad Judith, et dixit: Non vereatur bona puella introire ad dominum meum, ut honorificetur ante faciem ejus, ut manducet cum eo, et bibat vinum in jucunditate.

verses.text: And Judith answered him: Who am I, that I should gainsay my lord?
verses.textLatin: Cui Judith respondit: Quæ ego sum, ut contradicam domino meo?

verses.text: All that shall be good and best before his eyes, I will do. And whatsoever shall please him, that shall be best to me all the days of my life.
verses.textLatin: omne quod erit ante oculos ejus bonum et optimum, faciam. Quidquid autem illi placuerit, hoc mihi erit optimum omnibus diebus vitæ meæ.

verses.text: And she arose and dressed herself out with her garments, and going in she stood before his face.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit, et ornavit se vestimento suo, et ingressa stetit ante faciem ejus.

verses.text: And the heart of Holofernes was smitten, for he was burning with the desire of her.
verses.textLatin: Cor autem Holofernes concussum est: erat enim ardens in concupiscentia ejus.

verses.text: And Holofernes said to her: Drink now, and sit down and be merry; for thou hast found favour before me.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad eam Holofernes: Bibe nunc, et accumbe in jucunditate, quoniam invenisti gratiam coram me.

verses.text: And Judith said: I will drink my lord, because my life is magnified this day above all my days.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Judith: Bibam, domine, quoniam magnificata est anima mea hodie præ omnibus diebus meis.

verses.text: And she took and ate and drank before him what her maid had prepared for her.
verses.textLatin: Et accepit, et manducavit et bibit coram ipso ea quæ paraverat illi ancilla ejus.

verses.text: And Holofernes was made merry on her occasion, and drank exceeding much wine, so much as he had never drunk in his life.
verses.textLatin: Et jucundus factus est Holofernes ad eam, bibitque vinum multum nimis, quantum numquam biberat in vita sua.

verses.text: And  when it was grown late, his servants made haste to their lodgings, and Vagao shut the chamber doors, and went his way.
verses.textLatin: Ut autem sero factum est, festinaverunt servi illius ad hospitia sua, et conclusit Vagao ostia cubiculi, et abiit.

verses.text: And they were all overcharged with wine.
verses.textLatin: Erant autem omnes fatigati a vino,

verses.text: And Judith was alone in the chamber.
verses.textLatin: eratque Judith sola in cubiculo.

verses.text: But Holofernes lay on his bed, fast asleep, being exceedingly drunk.
verses.textLatin: Porro Holofernes jacebat in lecto, nimia ebrietate sopitus.

verses.text: And Judith spoke to her maid to stand without before the chamber, and to watch:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Judith puellæ suæ ut staret foris ante cubiculum, et observaret.

verses.text: And Judith stood before the bed praying with tears, and the motion of her lips in silence,
verses.textLatin: Stetitque Judith ante lectum, orans cum lacrimis, et labiorum motu in silentio,

verses.text: Saying: Strengthen me, O Lord God of Israel, and in this hour look on the works of my hands, that as thou hast promised, thou mayst raise up Jerusalem thy city: and that I may bring to pass that which I have purposed, having a belief that it might be done by thee.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Confirma me, Domine Deus Israël, et respice in hac hora ad opera manuum mearum, ut, sicut promisisti, Jerusalem civitatem tuam erigas: et hoc quod credens per te posse fieri cogitavi, perficiam.

verses.text: And when she had said this, she went to the pillar that was at his bed’s head, and loosed his sword that hung tied upon it.
verses.textLatin: Et cum hæc dixisset, accessit ad columnam quæ erat ad caput lectuli ejus, et pugionem ejus, qui in ea ligatus pendebat, exsolvit.

verses.text: And when she had drawn it out, she took him by the hair of his head, and said: Strengthen me, O Lord God, at this hour.
verses.textLatin: Cumque evaginasset illum, apprehendit comam capitis ejus, et ait: Confirma me, Domine Deus, in hac hora.

verses.text: And she struck twice upon his neck, and cut off his head, and took off his canopy from the pillars, and rolled away his headless body.
verses.textLatin: Et percussit bis in cervicem ejus, et abscidit caput ejus, et abstulit conopeum ejus a columnis, et evolvit corpus ejus truncum.

verses.text: And after a while she went out, and delivered the head of Holofernes to her maid, and bade her put it into her wallet.
verses.textLatin: Et post pusillum exivit, et tradidit caput Holofernis ancillæ suæ, et jussit ut mitteret illud in peram suam.

verses.text: And they two went out according to their custom, as it were to prayer, and they passed the camp, and having compassed the valley, they came to the gate of the city.
verses.textLatin: Et exierunt duæ, secundum consuetudinem suam, quasi ad orationem, et transierunt castra, et gyrantes vallem, venerunt ad portam civitatis.

verses.text: And Judith from afar off cried to the watchmen upon the walls: Open the gates for God is with us, who hath shewn his power in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Judith a longe custodibus murorum: Aperite portas, quoniam nobiscum est Deus, qui fecit virtutem in Israël.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when the men had heard her voice, that they called the ancients of the city.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est cum audissent viri vocem ejus, vocaverunt presbyteros civitatis.

verses.text: And all ran to meet her from the least to the greatest: for they now had no hopes that she would come.
verses.textLatin: Et concurrerunt ad eam omnes, a minimo usque ad maximum: quoniam sperabant eam jam non esse venturam.

verses.text: And lighting up lights they all gathered round about her: and she went up to a higher place, and commanded silence to be made. And when all had held their peace,
verses.textLatin: Et accendentes luminaria, congyraverunt circa eam universi: illa autem ascendens in eminentiorem locum, jussit fieri silentium. Cumque omnes tacuissent,

verses.text: Judith said: Praise ye the Lord our God, who hath not forsaken them that hope in him.
verses.textLatin: dixit Judith: Laudate Dominum Deum nostrum, qui non deseruit sperantes in se,

verses.text: And by me his handmaid he hath fulfilled his mercy, which he promised to the house of Israel: and he hath killed the enemy of his people by my hand this night.
verses.textLatin: et in me ancilla sua adimplevit misericordiam suam, quam promisit domui Israël: et interfecit in manu mea hostem populi sui hac nocte.

verses.text: Then she brought forth the head of Holofernes out of the wallet, and shewed it them, saying: Behold the head of Holofernes the general of the army of the Assyrians, and behold his canopy, wherein he lay in his drunkenness, where the Lord our God slew him by the hand of a woman.
verses.textLatin: Et proferens de pera caput Holofernis, ostendit illis, dicens: Ecce caput Holofernis principis militiæ Assyriorum, et ecce conopeum illius, in quo recumbebat in ebrietate sua, ubi per manum feminæ percussit illum Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: But as the same Lord liveth, his angel hath been my keeper both going hence, and abiding there, and returning from thence hither: and the Lord hath not suffered me his handmaid to be defiled, but hath brought me back to you without pollution of sin, rejoicing for his victory, for my escape, and for your deliverance.
verses.textLatin: Vivit autem ipse Dominus, quoniam custodivit me angelus ejus et hinc euntem, et ibi commorantem, et inde huc revertentem, et non permisit me Dominus ancillam suam coinquinari, sed sine pollutione peccati revocavit me vobis gaudentem in victoria sua, in evasione mea, et in liberatione vestra.

verses.text: Give all of you glory to him, because he is good, because his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini illi omnes, quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: And they all adored the Lord, and said to her: The Lord hath blessed thee by his power, because by thee he hath brought our enemies to nought.
verses.textLatin: Universi autem adorantes Dominum, dixerunt ad eam: Benedixit te Dominus in virtute sua, quia per te ad nihilum redegit inimicos nostros.

verses.text: And Ozias the prince of the people of Israel, said to her: Blessed art thou, O daughter, by the Lord the most high God, above all women upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Porro Ozias princeps populi Israël dixit ad eam: Benedicta es tu, filia, a Domino Deo excelso præ omnibus mulieribus super terram.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord who made heaven and earth, who hath directed thee to the cutting off the head of the prince of our enemies.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus, qui creavit cælum et terram, qui te direxit in vulnera capitis principis inimicorum nostrorum:

verses.text: Because he hath so magnified thy name this day, that thy praise shall not depart out of the mouth of men who shall be mindful of the power of the Lord for ever, for that thou hast not spared thy life, by reason of the distress and tribulation of thy people, but hast prevented our ruin in the presence of our God.
verses.textLatin: quia hodie nomen tuum ita magnificavit, ut non recedat laus tua de ore hominum qui memores fuerint virtutis Domini in æternum, pro quibus non pepercisti animæ tuæ propter angustias et tribulationem generis tui, sed subvenisti ruinæ ante conspectum Dei nostri.

verses.text: And all the people said: So be it, so be it.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit omnis populus: Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: And Achior being called for came, and Judith said to him: The God of Israel, to whom thou gavest testimony, that he revengeth himself of his enemies, he hath cut off the head of all the unbelievers this night by my hand.
verses.textLatin: Porro Achior vocatus venit, et dixit ei Judith: Deus Israël, cui tu testimonium dedisti quod ulciscatur se de inimicis suis, ipse caput omnium incredulorum incidit hac nocte in manu mea.

verses.text: And that thou mayst find that it is so, behold the head of Holofernes, who in the contempt of his pride despised the God of Israel: and threatened thee with death, saying: When the people of Israel shall be taken, I will command thy sides to be pierced with a sword.
verses.textLatin: Et ut probes quia ita est, ecce caput Holofernis, qui in contemptu superbiæ suæ Deum Israël contempsit, et tibi interitum minabatur, dicens: Cum captus fuerit populus Israël, gladio perforari præcipiam latera tua.

verses.text: Then Achior seeing the head of Holofernes, being seized with a great fear he fell on his face upon the earth, and his soul swooned away.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Achior caput Holofernis, angustiatus præ pavore cecidit in faciem suam super terram, et æstuavit anima ejus.

verses.text: But after he had recovered his spirits he fell down at her feet, and reverenced her, and said:
verses.textLatin: Postea vero quam resumpto spiritu recreatus est, procidit ad pedes ejus, et adoravit eam, et dixit:

verses.text: Blessed art thou by thy God in every tabernacle of Jacob, for in every nation which shall hear thy name, the God of Israel shall be magnified on occasion of thee.
verses.textLatin: Benedicta tu a Deo tuo in omni tabernaculo Jacob, quoniam in omni gente quæ audierit nomen tuum, magnificabitur super te Deus Israël.

verses.text: And  Judith said to all the people: Hear me, my brethren, hang ye up this head upon our walls.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Judith ad omnem populum: Audite me, fratres: suspendite caput hoc super muros nostros:

verses.text: And as soon as the sun shall rise, let every man take his arms, and rush ye out, not as going down beneath, but as making an assault.
verses.textLatin: et erit, cum exierit sol, accipiat unusquisque arma sua, et exite cum impetu, non ut descendatis deorsum, sed quasi impetum facientes.

verses.text: Then the watchmen must needs run to awake their prince for the battle.
verses.textLatin: Tunc exploratores necesse erit ut fugiant ad principem suum excitandum ad pugnam.

verses.text: And when the captains of them shall run to the tent of Holofernes, and shall find him without his head wallowing in his blood, fear shall fall upon them.
verses.textLatin: Cumque duces eorum cucurrerint ad tabernaculum Holofernis, et invenerint eum truncum in suo sanguine volutatum, decidet super eos timor.

verses.text: And when you shall know that they are fleeing, go after them securely, for the Lord will destroy them under your feet.
verses.textLatin: Cumque cognoveritis fugere eos, ite post illos securi, quoniam Dominus conteret eos sub pedibus vestris.

verses.text: Then Achior seeing the power that the God of Israel had wrought, leaving the religion of the Gentiles, he believed God, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the people of Israel, with all the succession of his kindred until this present day.
verses.textLatin: Tunc Achior, videns virtutem quam fecit Deus Israël, relicto gentilitatis ritu, credidit Deo, et circumcidit carnem præputii sui, et appositus est ad populum Israël, et omnis successio generis ejus usque in hodiernum diem.

verses.text: And immediately at break of day, they hung up the head of Holofernes upon the walls, and every man took his arms, and they went out with a great noise and shouting.
verses.textLatin: Mox autem ut ortus est dies, suspenderunt super muros caput Holofernis, accepitque unusquisque vir arma sua, et egressi sunt cum grandi strepitu et ululatu.

verses.text: And the watchmen seeing this, ran to the tent of Holofernes.
verses.textLatin: Quod videntes exploratores, ad tabernaculum Holofernis cucurrerunt.

verses.text: And they that were in the tent came, and made a noise before the door of the chamber to awake him, endeavouring by art to break his rest, that Holofernes might awake, not by their calling him, but by their noise.
verses.textLatin: Porro hi qui in tabernaculo erant, venientes, et ante ingressum cubiculi perstrepentes, excitandi gratia, inquietudinem arte moliebantur, ut non ab excitantibus, sed a sonantibus Holofernes evigilaret.

verses.text: For no man durst knock, or open and go into the chamber of the general of the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: Nullus enim audebat cubiculum virtutis Assyriorum pulsando aut intrando aperire.

verses.text: But when his captains and tribunes were come, and all the chiefs of the army of the king of the Assyrians, they said to the chamberlains:
verses.textLatin: Sed cum venissent ejus duces ac tribuni, et universi majores exercitus regis Assyriorum, dixerunt cubiculariis:

verses.text: Go in, and awake him, for the mice, coming out of their holes, have presumed to challenge us to fight.
verses.textLatin: Intrate, et excitate illum, quoniam egressi mures de cavernis suis, ausi sunt provocare nos ad prælium.

verses.text: Then Vagao going into his chamber, stood before the curtain, and made a clapping with his hands: for he thought that he was sleeping with Judith.
verses.textLatin: Tunc ingressus Vagao cubiculum ejus, stetit ante cortinam, et plausum fecit manibus suis: suspicabatur enim illum cum Judith dormire.

verses.text: But when with hearkening, he perceived no motion of one lying, he came near to the curtain, and lifting it up, and seeing the body of Holofernes, lying upon the ground, without the head, weltering in his blood, he cried out with a loud voice, with weeping, and rent his garments.
verses.textLatin: Sed cum nullum motum jacentis sensu aurium caperet, accessit proximans ad cortinam, et elevans eam, vidensque cadaver absque capite Holofernis in suo sanguine tabefactum jacere super terram, exclamavit voce magna cum fletu, et scidit vestimenta sua.

verses.text: And he went into the tent of Judith, and not finding her, he ran out to the people,
verses.textLatin: Et ingressus tabernaculum Judith, non invenit eam, et exiliit foras ad populum,

verses.text: And said: One Hebrew woman hath made confusion in the house of king Nabuchodonosor: for behold Holofernes lieth upon the ground, and his head is not upon him.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Una mulier hebræa fecit confusionem in domo regis Nabuchodonosor: ecce enim Holofernes jacet in terra, et caput ejus non est in illo.

verses.text: Now when the chiefs of the army of the Assyrians had heard this, they all rent their garments, and an intolerable fear and dread fell upon them, and their minds were troubled exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audissent principes virtutis Assyriorum, sciderunt omnes vestimenta sua, et intolerabilis timor et tremor cecidit super eos, et turbati sunt animi eorum valde.

verses.text: And there was a very great cry in the midst of their camp.
verses.textLatin: Et factus est clamor incomparabilis in medio castrorum eorum.

verses.text: And  when all the army heard that Holofernes was beheaded, courage and counsel fled from them, and being seized with trembling and fear they thought only to save themselves by flight:
verses.textLatin: Cumque omnis exercitus decollatum Holofernem audisset, fugit mens et consilium ab eis, et solo tremore et metu agitati, fugæ præsidium sumunt,

verses.text: So that no one spoke to his neighbour, but hanging down the head, leaving all things behind, they made haste to escape from the Hebrews, who, as they heard, were coming armed upon them, and fled by the ways of the fields, and the paths of the hills.
verses.textLatin: ita ut nullus loqueretur cum proximo suo, sed inclinato capite, relictis omnibus, evadere festinabant Hebræos, quos armatos super se venire audiebant, fugientes per vias camporum et semitas collium.

verses.text: So the children of Israel seeing them fleeing, followed after them. And they went down sounding with trumpets and shouting after them.
verses.textLatin: Videntes itaque filii Israël fugientes, secuti sunt illos. Descenderuntque clangentes tubis, et ululantes post ipsos.

verses.text: And because the Assyrians were not united together, they went without order in their flight; but the children of Israel pursuing in one body, defeated all that they could find.
verses.textLatin: Et quoniam Assyrii non adunati, in fugam ibant præcipites: filii autem Israël uno agmine persequentes debilitabant omnes quos invenire potuissent.

verses.text: And Ozias sent messengers through all the cities and countries of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Misit itaque Ozias nuntios per omnes civitates et regiones Israël.

verses.text: And every country, and every city, sent their chosen young men armed after them, and they pursued them with the edge of the sword until they came to the extremities of their confines.
verses.textLatin: Omnis itaque regio, omnisque urbs electam juventutem armatam misit post eos, et persecuti sunt eos in ore gladii, quousque pervenirent ad extremitatem finium suorum.

verses.text: And the rest that were in Bethulia went into the camp of the Assyrians, and took away the spoils, which the Assyrians in their flight had left behind them, and they were laden exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Reliqui autem qui erant in Bethulia, ingressi sunt castra Assyriorum, et prædam quam fugientes Assyrii reliquerant, abstulerunt, et onustati sunt valde.

verses.text: But they that returned conquerors to Bethulia, brought with them all things that were theirs, so that there was no numbering of their cattle, and beasts, and all their moveables, insomuch that from the least to the greatest all were made rich by their spoils.
verses.textLatin: Hi vero qui victores reversi sunt ad Bethuliam, omnia quæ erant illorum attulerunt secum, ita ut non esset numerus in pecoribus et jumentis et universis mobilibus eorum, ut a minimo usque ad maximum omnes divites fierent de prædationibus eorum.

verses.text: And Joachim the high priest came from Jerusalem to Bethulia with all his ancients to see Judith.
verses.textLatin: Joacim autem summus pontifex de Jerusalem venit in Bethuliam cum universis presbyteris suis ut videret Judith.

verses.text: And when she was come out to him, they all blessed her with one voice, saying: Thou art the glory of Jerusalem, thou art the joy of Israel, thou art the honour of our people:
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum exisset ad illum, benedixerunt eam omnes una voce, dicentes: Tu gloria Jerusalem; tu lætitia Israël; tu honorificentia populi nostri:

verses.text: For thou hast done manfully, and thy heart has been strengthened, because thou hast loved chastity, and after thy husband hast not known any other: therefore also the hand of the Lord hath strengthened thee, and therefore thou shalt be blessed for ever.
verses.textLatin: quia fecisti viriliter, et confortatum est cor tuum, eo quod castitatem amaveris, et post virum tuum, alterum nescieris: ideo et manus Domini confortavit te, et ideo eris benedicta in æternum.

verses.text: And all the people said: So be it, so be it.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit omnis populus: Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: And thirty days were scarce sufficient for the people of Israel to gather up the spoils of the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: Per dies autem triginta, vix collecta sunt spolia Assyriorum a populo Israël.

verses.text: But all those things that were proved to be the peculiar goods of Holofernes, they gave to Judith in gold, and silver, and garments and precious stones, and all household stuff, and they all were delivered to her by the people.
verses.textLatin: Porro autem universa quæ Holofernis peculiaria fuisse probata sunt, dederunt Judith in auro, et argento, et vestibus, et gemmis, et omni supellectili: et tradita sunt omnia illi a populo.

verses.text: And all the people rejoiced, with the women, and virgins, and young men, playing on instruments and harps.
verses.textLatin: Et omnes populi gaudebant cum mulieribus, et virginibus, et juvenibus, in organis et citharis.

verses.text: Then  Judith sung this canticle to the Lord, saying:
verses.textLatin: Tunc cantavit canticum hoc Domino Judith, dicens:

verses.text: Begin ye to the Lord with timbrels, sing ye to the Lord with cymbals, tune unto him a new psalm, extol and call upon his name.
verses.textLatin: Incipite Domino in tympanis; cantate Domino in cymbalis; modulamini illi psalmum novum: exaltate, et invocate nomen ejus.

verses.text: The Lord putteth an end to wars, the Lord is his name.
verses.textLatin: Dominus conterens bella, Dominus nomen est illi.

verses.text: He hath set his camp in the midst of his people, to deliver us from the hand of all our enemies.
verses.textLatin: Qui posuit castra sua in medio populi sui, ut eriperet nos de manu omnium inimicorum nostrorum.

verses.text: The Assyrian came out of the mountains from the north in the multitude of his strength: his multitude stopped up the torrents, and their horses covered the valleys.
verses.textLatin: Venit Assur ex montibus ab aquilone in multitudine fortitudinis suæ: cujus multitudo obturavit torrentes, et equi eorum cooperuerunt valles.

verses.text: He bragged that he would set my borders on fire, and kill my young men with the sword, to make my infants a prey, and my virgins captives.
verses.textLatin: Dixit se incensurum fines meos, et juvenes meos occisurum gladio; infantes meos dare in prædam, et virgines in captivitatem.

verses.text: But the almighty Lord hath struck him, and hath delivered him into the hands of a woman, and hath slain him.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem omnipotens nocuit eum, et tradidit eum in manus feminæ, et confodit eum.

verses.text: For their mighty one did not fall by young men, neither did the sons of Titan strike him, nor tall giants oppose themselves to him, but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her face.
verses.textLatin: Non enim cecidit potens eorum a juvenibus, nec filii Titan percusserunt eum, nec excelsi gigantes opposuerunt se illi: sed Judith filia Merari in specie faciei suæ dissolvit eum.

verses.text: For she put off her the garments of widowhood, and put on her the garments of joy, to give joy to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Exuit enim se vestimento viduitatis, et induit se vestimento lætitiæ in exultatione filiorum Israël.

verses.text: She anointed her face with ointment, and bound up her locks with a crown, she took a new robe to deceive him.
verses.textLatin: Unxit faciem suam unguento, et colligavit cincinnos suos mitra; accepit stolam novam ad decipiendum illum.

verses.text: Her sandals ravished his eyes, her beauty made his soul her captive, with a sword she cut off his head.
verses.textLatin: Sandalia ejus rapuerunt oculos ejus; pulchritudo ejus captivam fecit animam ejus: amputavit pugione cervicem ejus.

verses.text: The Persians quaked at her constancy, and the Medes at her boldness.
verses.textLatin: Horruerunt Persæ constantiam ejus, et Medi audaciam ejus.

verses.text: Then the camp of the Assyrians howled, when my lowly ones appeared, parched with thirst.
verses.textLatin: Tunc ululaverunt castra Assyriorum, quando apparuerunt humiles mei, arescentes in siti.

verses.text: The sons of the damsels have pierced them through, and they have killed them like children fleeing away: they perished in battle before the face of the Lord my God.
verses.textLatin: Filii puellarum compunxerunt eos, et sicut pueros fugientes occiderunt eos: perierunt in prælio a facie Domini Dei mei.

verses.text: Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, let us sing a new hymn to our God.
verses.textLatin: Hymnum cantemus Domino; hymnum novum cantemus Deo nostro.

verses.text: O Adonai, Lord, great art thou, and glorious in thy power, and no one can overcome thee.
verses.textLatin: Adonai Domine, magnus es tu, et præclarus in virtute tua: et quem superare nemo potest.

verses.text: Let all thy creatures serve thee: because thou hast spoken, and they were made: thou didst send forth thy spirit, and they were created, and there is no one that can resist thy voice.
verses.textLatin: Tibi serviat omnis creatura tua, quia dixisti, et facta sunt; misisti spiritum tuum, et creata sunt: et non est qui resistat voci tuæ.

verses.text: The mountains shall be moved from the foundations with the waters: the rocks shall melt as wax before thy face.
verses.textLatin: Montes a fundamentis movebuntur cum aquis; petræ, sicut cera, liquescent ante faciem tuam.

verses.text: But they that fear thee, shall be great with thee in all things.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem timent te, magni erunt apud te per omnia.

verses.text: Woe be to the nation that riseth up against my people: for the Lord almighty will take revenge on them, in the day of judgment he will visit them.
verses.textLatin: Væ genti insurgenti super genus meum: Dominus enim omnipotens vindicabit in eis; in die judicii visitabit illos.

verses.text: For he will give fire, and worms into their flesh, that they may burn, and may feel for ever.
verses.textLatin: Dabit enim ignem et vermes in carnes eorum, ut urantur et sentiant usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: And it came to pass after these things, that all the people, after the victory, came to Jerusalem to adore the Lord: and as soon as they were purified, they all offered holocausts, and vows, and their promises.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est post hæc, omnis populus post victoriam venit in Jerusalem adorare Dominum: et mox ut purificati sunt, obtulerunt omnes holocausta, et vota, et repromissiones suas.

verses.text: And Judith offered for an anathema of oblivion all the arms of Holofernes, which the people gave her, and the canopy that she had taken away out of his chamber.
verses.textLatin: Porro Judith universa vasa bellica Holofernis, quæ dedit illi populus, et conopeum quod ipsa sustulerat de cubili ipsius, obtulit in anathema oblivionis.

verses.text: And the people were joyful in the sight of the sanctuary, and for three months the joy of this victory was celebrated with Judith.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem populus jucundus secundum faciem sanctorum: et per tres menses gaudium hujus victoriæ celebratum est cum Judith.

verses.text: And after those days every man returned to his house, and Judith was made great in Bethulia, and she was most renowned in all the land of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Post dies autem illos, unusquisque rediit in domum suam: et Judith magna facta est in Bethulia, et præclarior erat universæ terræ Israël.

verses.text: And chastity was joined to her virtue, so that she knew no man all the days of her life, after the death of Manasses her husband.
verses.textLatin: Erat enim virtuti castitas adjuncta, ita ut non cognosceret virum omnibus diebus vitæ suæ, ex quo defunctus est Manasses vir ejus.

verses.text: And on festival days she came forth with great glory.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem, diebus festis, procedens cum magna gloria.

verses.text: And she abode in her husband’s house a hundred and five years, and made her handmaid free, and she died, and was buried with her husband in Bethulia.
verses.textLatin: Mansit autem in domo viri sui annos centum quinque, et dimisit abram suam liberam: et defuncta est ac sepulta cum viro suo in Bethulia.

verses.text: And all the people mourned for seven days.
verses.textLatin: Luxitque illam omnis populus diebus septem.

verses.text: And all the time of her life there was none that troubled Israel, nor many years after her death.
verses.textLatin: In omni autem spatio vitæ ejus non fuit qui perturbaret Israël, et post mortem ejus annis multis.

verses.text: But the day of the festivity of this victory is received by the Hebrews in the number of holy days, and is religiously observed by the Jews from that time until this day.
verses.textLatin: Dies autem victoriæ hujus festivitatis ab Hebræis in numero sanctorum dierum accipitur, et colitur a Judæis ex illo tempore usque in præsentem diem.

verses.text: In  the days of Assuerus, who reigned from India to Ethiopia over a hundred and twenty seven provinces:
verses.textLatin: In diebus Assueri, qui regnavit ab India usque Æthiopiam super centum viginti septem provincias,

verses.text: When he sat on the throne of his kingdom, the city Susan was the capital of his kingdom.
verses.textLatin: quando sedit in solio regni sui, Susan civitas regni ejus exordium fuit.

verses.text: Now in the third year of his reign he made a great feast for all the princes, and for his servants, for the most mighty of the Persians, and the nobles of the Medes, and the governors of the provinces in his sight,
verses.textLatin: Tertio igitur anno imperii sui fecit grande convivium cunctis principibus et pueris suis, fortissimis Persarum, et Medorum inclytis, et præfectis provinciarum coram se,

verses.text: That he might shew the riches of the glory of his kingdom, and the greatness, and boasting of his power, for a long time, to wit, for a hundred and fourscore days.
verses.textLatin: ut ostenderet divitias gloriæ regni sui, ac magnitudinem atque jactantiam potentiæ suæ, multo tempore, centum videlicet et octoginta diebus.

verses.text: And when the days of the feast were expired, he invited all the people that were found in Susan, from the greatest to the least: and commanded a feast to be made seven days in the court of the garden, and of the wood, which was planted by the care and the hand of the king.
verses.textLatin: Cumque implerentur dies convivii, invitavit omnem populum, qui inventus est in Susan, a maximo usque ad minimum: et jussit septem diebus convivium præparari in vestibulo horti, et nemoris quod regio cultu et manu consitum erat.

verses.text: And there were hung up on every side sky coloured, and green, and violet hangings, fastened with cords of silk, and of purple, which were put into rings of ivory, and were held up with marble pillars. The beds also were of gold and silver, placed in order upon a floor paved with porphyry and white marble: which was embellished with painting of wonderful variety.
verses.textLatin: Et pendebant ex omni parte tentoria ærii coloris et carbasini ac hyacinthini, sustentata funibus byssinis atque purpureis, qui eburneis circulis inserti erant, et columnis marmoreis fulciebantur. Lectuli quoque aurei et argentei, super pavimentum smaragdino et pario stratum lapide, dispositi erant: quod mira varietate pictura decorabat.

verses.text: And they that were invited, drank in golden cups, and the meats were brought in divers vessels one after another. Wine also in abundance and of the best was presented, as was worthy of a king’s magnificence.
verses.textLatin: Bibebant autem qui invitati erant aureis poculis, et aliis atque aliis vasis cibi inferebantur. Vinum quoque, ut magnificentia regia dignum erat, abundans, et præcipuum ponebatur.

verses.text: Neither was there any one to compel them to drink that were not willing, but as the king had appointed, who set over every table one of his nobles, that every man might take what he would.
verses.textLatin: Nec erat qui nolentes cogeret ad bibendum, sed sicut rex statuerat, præponens mensis singulos de principibus suis ut sumeret unusquisque quod vellet.

verses.text: Also Vasthi the queen made a feast for the women in the palace, where king Assuerus was used to dwell.
verses.textLatin: Vasthi quoque regina fecit convivium feminarum in palatio, ubi rex Assuerus manere consueverat.
