verses.textLatin: Et mandavit ei (haud dubium quin esset Mardochæus) ut ingrederetur ad regem, et rogaret pro populo suo et pro patria sua.

verses.text: Remember, (said he,) the days of thy low estate, how thou wast brought up by my hand, because Aman the second after the king hath spoken against us unto death.
verses.textLatin: Memorare, inquit, dierum humilitatis tuæ, quomodo nutrita sis in manu mea, quia Aman secundus a rege locutus est contra nos in mortem:

verses.text: And do thou call upon the Lord, and speak to the king for us, and deliver us from death.
verses.textLatin: et tu invoca Dominum, et loquere regi pro nobis, et libera nos de morte.

verses.text: And on the third day she laid away the garments she wore, and put on her glorious apparel.
verses.textLatin: Die autem tertio deposuit vestimenta ornatus sui, et circumdata est gloria sua.

verses.text: And glittering in royal robes, after she had called upon God the ruler and Saviour of all, she took two maids with her,
verses.textLatin: Cumque regio fulgeret habitu, et invocasset omnium rectorem et salvatorem Deum, assumpsit duas famulas,

verses.text: And upon one of them she leaned, as if for delicateness and overmuch tenderness she were not able to bear up her own body.
verses.textLatin: et super unam quidem innitebatur, quasi præ deliciis et nimia teneritudine corpus suum ferre non sustinens:

verses.text: And the other maid followed her lady, bearing up her train flowing on the ground.
verses.textLatin: altera autem famularum sequebatur dominam, defluentia in humum indumenta sustentans.

verses.text: But she with a rosy colour in her face, and with gracious and bright eyes, hid a mind full of anguish, and exceeding great fear.
verses.textLatin: Ipsa autem roseo colore vultum perfusa, et gratis ac nitentibus oculis, tristem celabat animum, et nimio timore contractum.

verses.text: So going in she passed through all the doors in order, and stood before the king, where he sat upon his royal throne, clothed with his royal robes, and glittering with gold, and precious stones, and he was terrible to behold.
verses.textLatin: Ingressa igitur cuncta per ordinem ostia, stetit contra regem, ubi ille residebat super solium regni sui, indutus vestibus regiis, auroque fulgens, et pretiosis lapidibus: eratque terribilis aspectu.

verses.text: And when he had lifted up his countenance, and with burning eyes had shewn the wrath of his heart, the queen sunk down, and her colour turned pale, and she rested her weary head upon her handmaid.
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevasset faciem, et ardentibus oculis furorem pectoris indicasset, regina corruit, et in pallorem colore mutato, lassum super ancillulam reclinavit caput.

verses.text: And God changed the king’s spirit into mildness, and all in haste and in fear he leaped from his throne, and holding her up in his arms, till she came to herself, caressed her with these words:
verses.textLatin: Convertitque Deus spiritum regis in mansuetudinem, et festinus ac metuens exilivit de solio, et sustentans eam ulnis suis donec rediret ad se, his verbis blandiebatur:

verses.text: What is the matter, Esther? I am thy brother, fear not.
verses.textLatin: Quid habes, Esther? ego sum frater tuus: noli metuere.

verses.text: Thou shalt not die: for this law is not made for thee, but for all others.
verses.textLatin: Non morieris: non enim pro te, sed pro omnibus hæc lex constituta est.

verses.text: Come near then, and touch the sceptre.
verses.textLatin: Accede igitur, et tange sceptrum.

verses.text: And as she held her peace, he took the golden sceptre, and laid it upon her neck, and kissed her, and said: Why dost thou not speak to me?
verses.textLatin: Cumque illa reticeret, tulit auream virgam, et posuit super collum ejus, et osculatus est eam, et ait: Cur mihi non loqueris?

verses.text: She answered: I saw thee, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled for fear of thy majesty.
verses.textLatin: Quæ respondit: Vidi te, domine, quasi angelum Dei, et conturbatum est cor meum præ timore gloriæ tuæ.

verses.text: For thou, my lord, art very admirable, and thy face is full of graces.
verses.textLatin: Valde enim mirabilis es, domine, et facies tua plena est gratiarum.

verses.text: And while she was speaking, she fell down again, and was almost in a swoon.
verses.textLatin: Cumque loqueretur, rursus corruit, et pene exanimata est.

verses.text: But the king was troubled, and all his servants comforted her.
verses.textLatin: Rex autem turbabatur, et omnes ministri ejus consolabantur eam.

verses.text: The  great king Artaxerxes, from India to Ethiopia, to the governors and princes of a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, which obey our command, sendeth greeting.
verses.textLatin: Rex magnus Artaxerxes ab India usque Æthiopiam, centum viginti septem provinciarum ducibus ac principibus qui nostræ jussioni obediunt, salutem dicit.

verses.text: Many have abused unto pride the goodness of princes, and the honour that hath been bestowed upon them:
verses.textLatin: Multi bonitate principum et honore, qui in eos collatus est, abusi sunt in superbiam:

verses.text: And not only endeavour to oppress the king’s subjects, but not bearing the glory that is given them, take in hand to practise also against them that gave it.
verses.textLatin: et non solum subjectos regibus nituntur opprimere, sed datam sibi gloriam non ferentes, in ipsos qui dederunt, moliuntur insidias.

verses.text: Neither are they content not to return thanks for benefits received, and to violate in themselves the laws of humanity, but they think they can also escape the justice of God who seeth all things.
verses.textLatin: Nec contenti sunt gratias non agere beneficiis, et humanitatis in se jura violare, sed Dei quoque cuncta cernentis arbitrantur se posse fugere sententiam.

verses.text: And they break out into so great madness, as to endeavour to undermine by lies such as observe diligently the offices committed to them, and do all things in such manner as to be worthy of all men’s praise,
verses.textLatin: Et in tantum vesaniæ proruperunt, ut eos qui credita sibi officia diligenter observant, et ita cuncta agunt ut omnium laude digni sint, mendaciorum cuniculis conentur subvertere,

verses.text: While with crafty fraud they deceive the ears of princes that are well meaning, and judge of others by their own nature.
verses.textLatin: dum aures principum simplices, et ex sua natura alios æstimantes, callida fraude decipiunt.

verses.text: Now this is proved both from ancient histories, and by the things which are done daily, how the good designs of kings are depraved by the evil suggestions of certain men.
verses.textLatin: Quæ res et ex veteribus probatur historiis, et ex his quæ geruntur quotidie, quomodo malis quorumdam suggestionibus regum studia depraventur.

verses.text: Wherefore we must provide for the peace of all provinces.
verses.textLatin: Unde providendum est paci omnium provinciarum.

verses.text: Neither must you think, if we command different things, that it cometh of the levity of our mind, but that we give sentence according to the quality and necessity of times, as the profit of the commonwealth requireth.
verses.textLatin: Nec putare debetis, si diversa jubeamus, ex animi nostri venire levitate, sed pro qualitate et necessitate temporum, ut reipublicæ poscit utilitas, ferre sententiam.

verses.text: Now that you may more plainly understand what we say, Aman the son of Amadathi, a Macedonian both in mind and country, and having nothing of the Persian blood, but with his cruelty staining our goodness, was received being a stranger by us:
verses.textLatin: Et ut manifestius quod dicimus intelligatis, Aman filius Amadathi, et animo et gente Macedo, alienusque a Persarum sanguine, et pietatem nostram sua crudelitate commaculans, peregrinus a nobis susceptus est:

verses.text: And found our humanity so great towards him, that he was called our father, and was worshipped by all as the next man after the king:
verses.textLatin: et tantam in se expertus humanitatem, ut pater noster vocaretur, et adoraretur ab omnibus post regem secundus:

verses.text: But he was so far puffed up with arrogancy, as to go about to deprive us of our kingdom and life.
verses.textLatin: qui in tantum arrogantiæ tumorem sublatus est, ut regno privare nos niteretur et spiritu.

verses.text: For with certain new and unheard of devices he hath sought the destruction of Mardochai, by whose fidelity and good services our life was saved, and of Esther the partner of our kingdom, with all their nation:
verses.textLatin: Nam Mardochæum, cujus fide et beneficiis vivimus, et consortem regni nostri Esther cum omni gente sua, novis quibusdam atque inauditis machinis expetivit in mortem:

verses.text: Thinking that after they were slain, he might work treason against us left alone without friends, and might transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.
verses.textLatin: hoc cogitans ut illis interfectis, insidiaretur nostræ solitudini, et regnum Persarum transferret in Macedonas.

verses.text: But we have found that the Jews, who were by that most wicked man appointed to be slain, are in no fault at all, but contrariwise, use just laws,
verses.textLatin: Nos autem a pessimo mortalium Judæos neci destinatos, in nulla penitus culpa reperimus, sed e contrario justis utentes legibus,

verses.text: And are the children of the highest and the greatest, and the ever living God, by whose benefit the kingdom was given both to our fathers and to us, and is kept unto this day.
verses.textLatin: et filios altissimi et maximi semperque viventis Dei, cujus beneficio et patribus nostris et nobis regnum est traditum, et usque hodie custoditur.

verses.text: Wherefore know ye that those letters which he sent in our name, are void and of no effect.
verses.textLatin: Unde eas litteras, quas sub nomine nostro ille direxerat, sciatis esse irritas.

verses.text: For which crime both he himself that devised it, and all his kindred hang on gibbets, before the gates of this city Susan: not we, but God repaying him as he deserved.
verses.textLatin: Pro quo scelere ante portas hujus urbis, id est, Susan, et ipse qui machinatus est, et omnis cognatio ejus pendet in patibulis: non nobis, sed Deo reddente ei quod meruit.

verses.text: But this edict, which we now send, shall be published in all cities, that the Jews may freely follow their own laws.
verses.textLatin: Hoc autem edictum, quod nunc mittimus, in cunctis urbibus proponatur, ut liceat Judæis uti legibus suis.

verses.text: And you shall aid them that they may kill those who had prepared themselves to kill them, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is called Adar.
verses.textLatin: Quibus debetis esse adminiculo, ut eos qui se ad necem eorum paraverant, possint interficere tertiadecima die mensis duodecimi, qui vocatur Adar.

verses.text: For the almighty God hath turned this day of sadness and mourning into joy to them.
verses.textLatin: Hanc enim diem, Deus omnipotens, mœroris et luctus, eis vertit in gaudium.

verses.text: Wherefore you shall also count this day among other festival days, and celebrate it with all joy, that it may be known also in times to come,
verses.textLatin: Unde et vos inter ceteros festos dies, hanc habetote diem, et celebrate eam cum omni lætitia, ut et in posterum cognoscatur,

verses.text: That all they who faithfully obey the Persians, receive a worthy reward for their fidelity: but they that are traitors to their kingdom, are destroyed for their wickedness.
verses.textLatin: omnes qui fideliter Persis obediunt, dignam pro fide recipere mercedem; qui autem insidiantur regno eorum, perire pro scelere.

verses.text: And let every province and city, that will not be partaker of this solemnity, perish by the sword and by fire, and be destroyed in such manner as to be made unpassable, both to men and beasts, for an example of contempt, and disobedience.
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem provincia et civitas quæ noluerit solemnitatis hujus esse particeps, gladio et igne pereat, et sic deleatur, ut non solum hominibus, sed etiam bestiis invia sit in sempiternum, pro exemplo contemptus et inobedientiæ.

verses.text: There  was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job, and that man was simple and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil.
verses.textLatin: Vir erat in terra Hus, nomine Job: et erat vir ille simplex, et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo.

verses.text: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.
verses.textLatin: Natique sunt ei septem filii, et tres filiæ.

verses.text: And his possession was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a family exceeding great: and this man was great among all the people of the east.
verses.textLatin: Et fuit possessio ejus septem millia ovium, et tria millia camelorum, quingenta quoque juga boum, et quingentæ asinæ, ac familia multa nimis: eratque vir ille magnus inter omnes orientales.

verses.text: And his sons went, and made a feast by houses every one in his day. And sending they called their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
verses.textLatin: Et ibant filii ejus, et faciebant convivium per domos, unusquisque in die suo. Et mittentes vocabant tres sorores suas, ut comederent et biberent cum eis.

verses.text: And when the days of their feasting were gone about, Job sent to them, and sanctified them: and rising up early offered holocausts for every one of them. For he said: Lest perhaps my sons have sinned, and have blessed God in their hearts. So did Job all days.
verses.textLatin: Cumque in orbem transissent dies convivii, mittebat ad eos Job, et sanctificabat illos: consurgensque diluculo, offerebat holocausta pro singulis. Dicebat enim: Ne forte peccaverint filii mei, et benedixerint Deo in cordibus suis. Sic faciebat Job cunctis diebus.

verses.text: Now on a certain day when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, Satan also was present among them.
verses.textLatin: Quadam autem die, cum venissent filii Dei ut assisterent coram Domino, affuit inter eos etiam Satan.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Whence comest thou? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit Dominus: Unde venis? Qui respondens, ait: Circuivi terram, et perambulavi eam.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a simple and upright man, and fearing God, and avoiding evil?
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Dominus ad eum: Numquid considerasti servum meum Job, quod non sit ei similis in terra, homo simplex et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo?

verses.text: And Satan answering, said: Doth Job fear God in vain?
verses.textLatin: Cui respondens Satan, ait: Numquid Job frustra timet Deum?

verses.text: Hast not thou made a fence for him, and his house, and all his substance round about, blessed the works of his hands, and his possession hath increased on the earth?
verses.textLatin: nonne tu vallasti eum, ac domum ejus, universamque substantiam per circuitum; operibus manuum ejus benedixisti, et possessio ejus crevit in terra?

verses.text: But stretch forth thy hand a little, and touch all that he hath, and see if he blesseth thee not to thy face.
verses.textLatin: sed extende paululum manum tuam et tange cuncta quæ possidet, nisi in faciem benedixerit tibi.

verses.text: Then the Lord said to Satan: Behold, all that he hath is in thy hand: only put not forth thy hand upon his person. And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Dominus ad Satan: Ecce universa quæ habet in manu tua sunt: tantum in eum ne extendas manum tuam. Egressusque est Satan a facie Domini.

verses.text: Now upon a certain day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,
verses.textLatin: Cum autem quadam die filii et filiæ ejus comederent et biberent vinum in domo fratris sui primogeniti,

verses.text: There came a messenger to Job, and said: The oxen were ploughing, and the asses feeding beside them,
verses.textLatin: nuntius venit ad Job, qui diceret: Boves arabant, et asinæ pascebantur juxta eos:

verses.text: And the Sabeans rushed in, and took all away, and slew the servants with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.
verses.textLatin: et irruerunt Sabæi, tuleruntque omnia, et pueros percusserunt gladio: et evasi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.

verses.text: And while he was yet speaking, another came, and said: The fire of God fell from heaven, and striking the sheep and the servants, hath consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.
verses.textLatin: Cumque adhuc ille loqueretur, venit alter, et dixit: Ignis Dei cecidit e cælo, et tactas oves puerosque consumpsit: et effugi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.

verses.text: And while he also was yet speaking, there came another, and said: The Chaldeans made three troops, and have fallen upon the camels, and taken them, moreover they have slain the servants with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.
verses.textLatin: Sed et illo adhuc loquente, venit alius, et dixit: Chaldæi fecerunt tres turmas, et invaserunt camelos, et tulerunt eos, necnon et pueros percusserunt gladio: et ego fugi solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.

verses.text: He was yet speaking, and behold another came in, and said: Thy sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their elder brother:
verses.textLatin: Adhuc loquebatur ille, et ecce alius intravit, et dixit: Filiis tuis et filiabus vescentibus et bibentibus vinum in domo fratris sui primogeniti,

verses.text: A violent wind came on a sudden from the side of the desert, and shook the four corners of the house, and it fell upon thy children and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.
verses.textLatin: repente ventus vehemens irruit a regione deserti, et concussit quatuor angulos domus: quæ corruens oppressit liberos tuos, et mortui sunt: et effugi ego solus, ut nuntiarem tibi.

verses.text: Then Job rose up, and rent his garments, and having shaven his head fell down upon the ground and worshipped,
verses.textLatin: Tunc surrexit Job, et scidit vestimenta sua: et tonso capite corruens in terram, adoravit,

verses.text: And said: Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Nudus egressus sum de utero matris meæ, et nudus revertar illuc. Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est. Sit nomen Domini benedictum.

verses.text: In all these things Job sinned not by his lips, nor spoke he any foolish thing against God.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus his non peccavit Job labiis suis, neque stultum quid contra Deum locutus est.

verses.text: And  it came to pass, when on a certain day the sons of God came, and stood before the Lord, and Satan came among them, and stood in his sight,
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem, cum quadam die venissent filii Dei, et starent coram Domino, venisset quoque Satan inter eos, et staret in conspectu ejus,

verses.text: That the Lord said to Satan: Whence comest thou? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.
verses.textLatin: ut diceret Dominus ad Satan: Unde venis? Qui respondens ait: Circuivi terram, et perambulavi eam.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Satan: Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a man simple, and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil, and still keeping his innocence? But thou hast moved me against him, that I should afflict him without cause.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Satan: Numquid considerasti servum meum Job, quod non sit ei similis in terra, vir simplex et rectus, ac timens Deum, et recedens a malo, et adhuc retinens innocentiam? tu autem commovisti me adversus eum, ut affligerem eum frustra.

verses.text: And Satan answered, and said: Skin for skin, and all that a man hath he will give for his life:
verses.textLatin: Cui respondens Satan, ait: Pellem pro pelle, et cuncta quæ habet homo dabit pro anima sua;

verses.text: But put forth thy hand, and touch his bone and his flesh, and then thou shalt see that he will bless thee to thy face.
verses.textLatin: alioquin mitte manum tuam, et tange os ejus et carnem, et tunc videbis quod in faciem benedicat tibi.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Satan: Behold he is in thy hand, but yet save his life.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo Dominus ad Satan: Ecce in manu tua est: verumtamen animam illius serva.

verses.text: So Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord, and struck Job with a very grievous ulcer, from the sole of the foot even to the top of his head:
verses.textLatin: Egressus igitur Satan a facie Domini, percussit Job ulcere pessimo, a planta pedis usque ad verticem ejus;

verses.text: And he took a potsherd and scraped the corrupt matter, sitting on a dunghill.
verses.textLatin: qui testa saniem radebat, sedens in sterquilinio.

verses.text: And his wife said to him: Dost thou still continue in thy simplicity? bless God, and die.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem illi uxor sua: Adhuc tu permanes in simplicitate tua? Benedic Deo, et morere.

verses.text: And he said to her: Thou hast spoken like one of the foolish women: if we have received good things at the hand of God, why should we not receive evil? In all these things Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.textLatin: Qui ait ad illam: Quasi una de stultis mulieribus locuta es: si bona suscepimus de manu Dei, mala quare non suscipiamus? In omnibus his non peccavit Job labiis suis.

verses.text: Now when Job’s three friends heard all the evil that had befallen him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite. For they had made an appointment to come together and visit him, and comfort him.
verses.textLatin: Igitur audientes tres amici Job omne malum quod accidisset ei, venerunt singuli de loco suo, Eliphaz Themanites, et Baldad Suhites, et Sophar Naamathites. Condixerant enim ut pariter venientes visitarent eum, et consolarentur.

verses.text: And when they had lifted up their eyes afar off, they knew him not, and crying out they wept, and rending their garments they sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
verses.textLatin: Cumque elevassent procul oculos suos, non cognoverunt eum, et exclamantes ploraverunt, scissisque vestibus sparserunt pulverem super caput suum in cælum.

verses.text: And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no man spoke to him a word: for they saw that his grief was very great.
verses.textLatin: Et sederunt cum eo in terra septem diebus et septem noctibus: et nemo loquebatur ei verbum: videbant enim dolorem esse vehementem.

verses.text: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day,
verses.textLatin: Post hæc aperuit Job os suum, et maledixit diei suo,

verses.text: And he said:
verses.textLatin: et locutus est:

verses.text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said: A man child is conceived.
verses.textLatin: Pereat dies in qua natus sum, et nox in qua dictum est: Conceptus est homo.

verses.text: Let that day be turned into darkness, let not God regard it from above, and let not the light shine upon it.
verses.textLatin: Dies ille vertatur in tenebras: non requirat eum Deus desuper, et non illustretur lumine.

verses.text: Let darkness, and the shadow of death cover it, let a mist overspread it, and let it be wrapped up in bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Obscurent eum tenebræ et umbra mortis; occupet eum caligo, et involvatur amaritudine.

verses.text: Let a darksome whirlwind seize upon that night, let it not be counted in the days of the year, nor numbered in the months.
verses.textLatin: Noctem illam tenebrosus turbo possideat; non computetur in diebus anni, nec numeretur in mensibus.

verses.text: Let that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise.
verses.textLatin: Sit nox illa solitaria, nec laude digna.

verses.text: Let them curse it who curse the day, who are ready to raise up a leviathan:
verses.textLatin: Maledicant ei qui maledicunt diei, qui parati sunt suscitare Leviathan.

verses.text: Let the stars be darkened with the mist thereof: let it expect light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawning of the day:
verses.textLatin: Obtenebrentur stellæ caligine ejus; expectet lucem, et non videat, nec ortum surgentis auroræ.

verses.text: Because it shut not up the doors of the womb that bore me, nor took away evils from my eyes.
verses.textLatin: Quia non conclusit ostia ventris qui portavit me, nec abstulit mala ab oculis meis.

verses.text: Why did I not die in the womb, why did I not perish when I came out of the belly?
verses.textLatin: Quare non in vulva mortuus sum? egressus ex utero non statim perii?

verses.text: Why received upon the knees? why suckled at the breasts?
verses.textLatin: Quare exceptus genibus? cur lactatus uberibus?

verses.text: For now I should have been asleep and still, and should have rest in my sleep.
verses.textLatin: Nunc enim dormiens silerem, et somno meo requiescerem

verses.text: With kings and consuls of the earth, who build themselves solitudes:
verses.textLatin: cum regibus et consulibus terræ, qui ædificant sibi solitudines;

verses.text: Or with princes, that possess gold, and fill their houses with silver:
verses.textLatin: aut cum principibus qui possident aurum, et replent domos suas argento;

verses.text: Or as a hidden untimely birth I should not be, or as they that being conceived have not seen the light.
verses.textLatin: aut sicut abortivum absconditum non subsisterem, vel qui concepti non viderunt lucem.

verses.text: There the wicked cease from tumult, and there the wearied in strength are at rest.
verses.textLatin: Ibi impii cessaverunt a tumultu, et ibi requieverunt fessi robore.

verses.text: And they sometime bound together without disquiet, have not heard the voice of the oppressor.
verses.textLatin: Et quondam vincti pariter sine molestia, non audierunt vocem exactoris.

verses.text: The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
verses.textLatin: Parvus et magnus ibi sunt, et servus liber a domino suo.

verses.text: Why is light given to him that is in misery, and life to them that are in bitterness of soul?
verses.textLatin: Quare misero data est lux, et vita his qui in amaritudine animæ sunt:

verses.text: That look for death, and it cometh not, as they that dig for a treasure:
verses.textLatin: qui expectant mortem, et non venit, quasi effodientes thesaurum;

verses.text: And they rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave.
verses.textLatin: gaudentque vehementer cum invenerint sepulchrum?

verses.text: To a man whose way is hidden, and God hath surrounded him with darkness?
verses.textLatin: viro cujus abscondita est via et circumdedit eum Deus tenebris?

verses.text: Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring:
verses.textLatin: Antequam comedam, suspiro; et tamquam inundantes aquæ, sic rugitus meus:

verses.text: For the fear which I feared, hath come upon me: and that which I was afraid of, hath befallen me.
verses.textLatin: quia timor quem timebam evenit mihi, et quod verebar accidit.

verses.text: Have I not dissembled? have I not kept silence? have I not been quiet? and indignation is come upon me.
verses.textLatin: Nonne dissimulavi? nonne silui? nonne quievi? et venit super me indignatio.

verses.text: Then  Eliphaz the Themanite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:

verses.text: If we begin to speak to thee, perhaps thou wilt take it ill, but who can withhold the words he hath conceived?
verses.textLatin: Si cœperimus loqui tibi, forsitan moleste accipies; sed conceptum sermonem tenere quis poterit?

verses.text: Behold thou hast taught many, and thou hast strengthened the weary hands:
verses.textLatin: Ecce docuisti multos, et manus lassas roborasti;

verses.text: Thy words have confirmed them that were staggering, and thou hast strengthened the trembling knees:
verses.textLatin: vacillantes confirmaverunt sermones tui, et genua trementia confortasti.

verses.text: But now the scourge is come upon thee, and thou faintest: it hath touched thee, and thou art troubled.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem venit super te plaga, et defecisti; tetigit te, et conturbatus es.

verses.text: Where is thy fear, thy fortitude, thy patience, and the perfection of thy ways?
verses.textLatin: Ubi est timor tuus, fortitudo tua, patientia tua, et perfectio viarum tuarum?

verses.text: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished being innocent? or when were the just destroyed?
verses.textLatin: Recordare, obsecro te, quis umquam innocens periit? aut quando recti deleti sunt?

verses.text: On the contrary I have seen those who work iniquity, and sow sorrows, and reap them,
verses.textLatin: Quin potius vidi eos qui operantur iniquitatem, et seminant dolores, et metunt eos,

verses.text: Perishing by the blast of God, and consumed by the spirit of his wrath.
verses.textLatin: flante Deo perisse, et spiritu iræ ejus esse consumptos.

verses.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the teeth of the whelps of lions are broken:
verses.textLatin: Rugitus leonis, et vox leænæ, et dentes catulorum leonum contriti sunt.

verses.text: The tiger hath perished for want of prey, and the young lions are scattered abroad.
verses.textLatin: Tigris periit, eo quod non haberet prædam, et catuli leonis dissipati sunt.

verses.text: Now there was a word spoken to me in private, and my ears by stealth as it were received the veins of its whisper.
verses.textLatin: Porro ad me dictum est verbum absconditum, et quasi furtive suscepit auris mea venas susurri ejus.

verses.text: In the horror of a vision by night, when deep sleep is wont to hold men,
verses.textLatin: In horrore visionis nocturnæ, quando solet sopor occupare homines,

verses.text: Fear seized upon me, and trembling, and all my bones were affrighted:
verses.textLatin: pavor tenuit me, et tremor, et omnia ossa mea perterrita sunt;

verses.text: And when a spirit passed before me, the hair of my flesh stood up.
verses.textLatin: et cum spiritus, me præsente, transiret, inhorruerunt pili carnis meæ.

verses.text: There stood one whose countenance I knew not, an image before my eyes, and I heard the voice as it were of a gentle wind:
verses.textLatin: Stetit quidam, cujus non agnoscebam vultum, imago coram oculis meis, et vocem quasi auræ lenis audivi.

verses.text: Shall man be justified in comparison of God, or shall a man be more pure than his maker?
verses.textLatin: Numquid homo, Dei comparatione, justificabitur? aut factore suo purior erit vir?

verses.text: Behold they that serve him are not steadfast, and in his angels he found wickedness:
verses.textLatin: Ecce qui serviunt ei, non sunt stabiles, et in angelis suis reperit pravitatem;

verses.text: How much more shall they that dwell in houses of clay, who have an earthly foundation, be consumed as with the moth?
verses.textLatin: quanto magis hi qui habitant domos luteas, qui terrenum habent fundamentum, consumentur velut a tinea?

verses.text: From morning till evening they shall be cut down: and because no one understandeth, they shall perish for ever.
verses.textLatin: De mane usque ad vesperam succidentur; et quia nullus intelligit, in æternum peribunt.

verses.text: And they that shall be left, shall be taken away from them: they shall die, and not in wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem reliqui fuerint, auferentur ex eis; morientur, et non in sapientia.

verses.text: Call  now if there be any that will answer thee, and turn to some of the saints.
verses.textLatin: Voca ergo, si est qui tibi respondeat, et ad aliquem sanctorum convertere.

verses.text: Anger indeed killeth the foolish, and envy slayeth the little one.
verses.textLatin: Vere stultum interficit iracundia, et parvulum occidit invidia.

verses.text: I have seen a fool with a strong root, and I cursed his beauty immediately.
verses.textLatin: Ego vidi stultum firma radice, et maledixi pulchritudini ejus statim.

verses.text: His children shall be far from safety, and shall be destroyed in the gate, and there shall be none to deliver them.
verses.textLatin: Longe fient filii ejus a salute, et conterentur in porta, et non erit qui eruat.

verses.text: Whose harvest the hungry shall eat, and the armed man shall take him by violence, and the thirsty shall drink up his riches.
verses.textLatin: Cujus messem famelicus comedet, et ipsum rapiet armatus, et bibent sitientes divitias ejus.

verses.text: Nothing upon earth is done without a cause, and sorrow doth not spring out of the ground.
verses.textLatin: Nihil in terra sine causa fit, et de humo non oritur dolor.

verses.text: Man is born to labour and the bird to fly.
verses.textLatin: Homo nascitur ad laborem, et avis ad volatum.

verses.text: Wherefore I will pray to the Lord, and address my speech to God:
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem ego deprecabor Dominum, et ad Deum ponam eloquium meum:

verses.text: Who doth great things and unsearchable and wonderful things without number:
verses.textLatin: qui facit magna et inscrutabilia, et mirabilia absque numero;

verses.text: Who giveth rain upon the face of the earth, and watereth all things with waters:
verses.textLatin: qui dat pluviam super faciem terræ, et irrigat aquis universa;

verses.text: Who setteth up the humble on high, and comforteth with health those that mourn.
verses.textLatin: qui ponit humiles in sublime, et mœrentes erigit sospitate;

verses.text: Who bringeth to nought the designs of the malignant, so that their hands cannot accomplish what they had begun:
verses.textLatin: qui dissipat cogitationes malignorum, ne possint implere manus eorum quod cœperant;

verses.text: Who catcheth the wise in their craftiness, and disappointeth the counsel of the wicked:
verses.textLatin: qui apprehendit sapientes in astutia eorum, et consilium pravorum dissipat.

verses.text: They shall meet with darkness in the day, and grope at noonday as in the night.
verses.textLatin: Per diem incurrent tenebras, et quasi in nocte, sic palpabunt in meridie.

verses.text: But he shall save the needy from the sword of their mouth, and the poor from the hand of the violent.
verses.textLatin: Porro salvum faciet egenum a gladio oris eorum, et de manu violenti pauperem.

verses.text: And to the needy there shall be hope, but iniquity shall draw in her mouth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit egeno spes; iniquitas autem contrahet os suum.

verses.text: Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not therefore the chastising of the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Beatus homo qui corripitur a Deo: increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes:

verses.text: For he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal.
verses.textLatin: quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt.

verses.text: In six troubles he shall deliver thee, and in the seventh, evil shall not touch thee.
verses.textLatin: In sex tribulationibus liberabit te, et in septima non tanget te malum.

verses.text: In famine he shall deliver thee from death: and in battle, from the hand of the sword.
verses.textLatin: In fame eruet te de morte, et in bello de manu gladii.

verses.text: Thou shalt be hidden from the scourge of the tongue: and thou shalt not fear calamity when it cometh.
verses.textLatin: A flagello linguæ absconderis, et non timebis calamitatem cum venerit.

verses.text: In destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: and thou shalt not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
verses.textLatin: In vastitate et fame ridebis, et bestias terræ non formidabis.

verses.text: But thou shalt have a covenant with the stones of the lands, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with thee.
verses.textLatin: Sed cum lapidibus regionum pactum tuum, et bestiæ terræ pacificæ erunt tibi.

verses.text: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle is in peace, and visiting thy beauty thou shalt not sin.
verses.textLatin: Et scies quod pacem habeat tabernaculum tuum; et visitans speciem tuam, non peccabis.

verses.text: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be multiplied, and thy offspring like the grass of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Scies quoque quoniam multiplex erit semen tuum, et progenies tua quasi herba terræ.

verses.text: Thou shalt enter into the grave in abundance, as a heap of wheat is brought in its season.
verses.textLatin: Ingredieris in abundantia sepulchrum, sicut infertur acervus tritici in tempore suo.

verses.text: Behold, this is even so, as we have searched out: which thou having heard, consider it thoroughly in thy mind.
verses.textLatin: Ecce hoc, ut investigavimus, ita est: quod auditum, mente pertracta.

verses.text: But  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, dixit:

verses.text: O that my sins, whereby I have de-served wrath, and the calamity that I suffer, were weighed in a balance.
verses.textLatin: Utinam appenderentur peccata mea quibus iram merui, et calamitas quam patior, in statera!

verses.text: As the sand of the sea this would appear heavier: therefore my words are full of sorrow:
verses.textLatin: Quasi arena maris hæc gravior appareret; unde et verba mea dolore sunt plena:

verses.text: For the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me.
verses.textLatin: quia sagittæ Domini in me sunt, quarum indignatio ebibit spiritum meum; et terrores Domini militant contra me.

verses.text: Will the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or will the ox low when he standeth before a full manger?
verses.textLatin: Numquid rugiet onager cum habuerit herbam? aut mugiet bos cum ante præsepe plenum steterit?

verses.text: Or can an unsavoury thing be eaten, that is not seasoned with salt? or can a man taste that which when tasted bringeth death?
verses.textLatin: aut poterit comedi insulsum, quod non est sale conditum? aut potest aliquis gustare quod gustatum affert mortem?

verses.text: The things which before my soul would not touch, now, through anguish are my meats.
verses.textLatin: Quæ prius nolebat tangere anima mea, nunc, præ angustia, cibi mei sunt.

verses.text: Who will grant that my request may come: and that God may give me what I look for?
verses.textLatin: Quis det ut veniat petitio mea, et quod expecto tribuat mihi Deus?

verses.text: And that he that hath begun may destroy me, that he may let loose his hand, and cut me off?
verses.textLatin: et qui cœpit, ipse me conterat; solvat manum suam, et succidat me?

verses.text: And that this may be my comfort, that afflicting me with sorrow, he spare not, nor I contradict the words of the Holy One.
verses.textLatin: Et hæc mihi sit consolatio, ut affligens me dolore, non parcat, nec contradicam sermonibus Sancti.

verses.text: For what is my strength, that I can hold out? or what is my end that I should keep patience?
verses.textLatin: Quæ est enim fortitudo mea, ut sustineam? aut quis finis meus, ut patienter agam?

verses.text: My strength is not the strength of stones, nor is my flesh of brass.
verses.textLatin: Nec fortitudo lapidum fortitudo mea, nec caro mea ænea est.

verses.text: Behold there is no help for me in myself, and my familiar friends also are departed from me.
verses.textLatin: Ecce non est auxilium mihi in me, et necessarii quoque mei recesserunt a me.

verses.text: He that taketh away mercy from his friend, forsaketh the fear of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui tollit ab amico suo misericordiam, timorem Domini derelinquit.

verses.text: My brethren have passed by me, as the torrent that passeth swiftly in the valleys.
verses.textLatin: Fratres mei præterierunt me, sicut torrens qui raptim transit in convallibus.

verses.text: They that fear the hoary frost, the snow shall fall upon them.
verses.textLatin: Qui timent pruinam, irruet super eos nix.

verses.text: At the time when they shall be scattered they shall perish: and after it groweth hot they shall be melted out of their place.
verses.textLatin: Tempore quo fuerint dissipati, peribunt; et ut incaluerit, solventur de loco suo.

verses.text: The paths of their steps are entangled: they shall walk in vain, and shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Involutæ sunt semitæ gressuum eorum; ambulabunt in vacuum, et peribunt.

verses.text: Consider the paths of Thema, the ways of Saba, and wait a little while.
verses.textLatin: Considerate semitas Thema, itinera Saba, et expectate paulisper.

verses.text: They are confounded, because I have hoped: they are come also even unto me, and are covered with shame.
verses.textLatin: Confusi sunt, quia speravi: venerunt quoque usque ad me, et pudore cooperti sunt.

verses.text: Now you are come: and now seeing my affliction you are afraid.
verses.textLatin: Nunc venistis; et modo videntes plagam meam, timetis.

verses.text: Did I say: Bring to me, and give me of your substance?
verses.textLatin: Numquid dixi: Afferte mihi, et de substantia vestra donate mihi?

verses.text: Or deliver me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me out of the hand of the mighty?
verses.textLatin: vel: Liberate me de manu hostis, et de manu robustorum eruite me?

verses.text: Teach me, and I will hold my peace: and if I have been ignorant in any thing, instruct me.
verses.textLatin: Docete me, et ego tacebo: et si quid forte ignoravi, instruite me.

verses.text: Why have you detracted the words of truth, whereas there is none of you that can reprove me?
verses.textLatin: Quare detraxistis sermonibus veritatis, cum e vobis nullus sit qui possit arguere me?

verses.text: You dress up speeches only to rebuke, and you utter words to the wind.
verses.textLatin: Ad increpandum tantum eloquia concinnatis, et in ventum verba profertis.

verses.text: You rush in upon the fatherless, and you endeavour to overthrow your friend.
verses.textLatin: Super pupillum irruitis, et subvertere nitimini amicum vestrum.

verses.text: However finish what you have begun, give ear, and see whether I lie.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen quod cœpistis explete: præbete aurem, et videte an mentiar.

verses.text: Answer, I beseech you, without contention: and speaking that which is just, judge ye.
verses.textLatin: Respondete, obsecro, absque contentione; et loquentes id quod justum est, judicate.

verses.text: And you shall not find iniquity in my tongue, neither shall folly sound in my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Et non invenietis in lingua mea iniquitatem, nec in faucibus meis stultitia personabit.

verses.text: The  life of man upon earth is a warfare, and his days are like the days of a hireling.
verses.textLatin: Militia est vita hominis super terram, et sicut dies mercenarii dies ejus.

verses.text: As a servant longeth for the shade, as the hireling looketh for the end of his work;
verses.textLatin: Sicut servus desiderat umbram, et sicut mercenarius præstolatur finem operis sui,

verses.text: So I also have had empty months, and have numbered to myself wearisome nights.
verses.textLatin: sic et ego habui menses vacuos, et noctes laboriosas enumeravi mihi.

verses.text: If I lie down to sleep, I shall say: When shall I arise? and again I shall look for the evening, and shall be filled with sorrows even till darkness.
verses.textLatin: Si dormiero, dicam: Quando consurgam? et rursum expectabo vesperam, et replebor doloribus usque ad tenebras.

verses.text: My flesh is clothed with rottenness and the filth of dust, my skin is withered and drawn together.
verses.textLatin: Induta est caro mea putredine, et sordibus pulveris cutis mea aruit et contracta est.

verses.text: My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver, and are consumed without any hope.
verses.textLatin: Dies mei velocius transierunt quam a texente tela succiditur, et consumpti sunt absque ulla spe.

verses.text: Remember that my life is but wind, and my eye shall not return to see good things.
verses.textLatin: Memento quia ventus est vita mea, et non revertetur oculus meus ut videat bona.

verses.text: Nor shall the sight of man behold me: thy eyes are upon me, and I shall be no more.
verses.textLatin: Nec aspiciet me visus hominis; oculi tui in me, et non subsistam.

verses.text: As a cloud is consumed, and passeth away: so he that shall go down to hell shall not come up.
verses.textLatin: Sicut consumitur nubes, et pertransit, sic qui descenderit ad inferos, non ascendet.

verses.text: Nor shall he return any more into his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.textLatin: Nec revertetur ultra in domum suam, neque cognoscet eum amplius locus ejus.

verses.text: Wherefore I will not spare my mouth, I will speak in the affliction of my spirit: I will talk with the bitterness of my soul.
verses.textLatin: Quapropter et ego non parcam ori meo: loquar in tribulatione spiritus mei; confabulabor cum amaritudine animæ meæ.

verses.text: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou hast enclosed me in a prison?
verses.textLatin: Numquid mare ego sum, aut cetus, quia circumdedisti me carcere?

verses.text: If I say: My bed shall comfort me, and I shall be relieved speaking with myself on my couch:
verses.textLatin: Si dixero: Consolabitur me lectulus meus, et relevabor loquens mecum in strato meo:

verses.text: Thou wilt frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
verses.textLatin: terrebis me per somnia, et per visiones horrore concuties.

verses.text: So that my soul rather chooseth hanging, and my bones death.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem elegit suspendium anima mea, et mortem ossa mea.

verses.text: I have done with hope, I shall now live no longer: spare me, for my days are nothing.
verses.textLatin: Desperavi: nequaquam ultra jam vivam: parce mihi, nihil enim sunt dies mei.

verses.text: What is a man that thou shouldst magnify him? or why dost thou set thy heart upon him?
verses.textLatin: Quid est homo, quia magnificas eum? aut quid apponis erga eum cor tuum?

verses.text: Thou visitest him early in the morning, and thou provest him suddenly.
verses.textLatin: Visitas eum diluculo, et subito probas illum.

verses.text: How long wilt thou not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo non parcis mihi, nec dimittis me ut glutiam salivam meam?

verses.text: I have sinned: what shall I do to thee, O keeper of men? why hast thou set me opposite to thee, and I am become burdensome to myself?
verses.textLatin: Peccavi; quid faciam tibi, o custos hominum? quare posuisti me contrarium tibi, et factus sum mihimetipsi gravis?

verses.text: Why dost thou not remove my sin, and why dost thou not take away my iniquity? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if thou seek me in the morning, I shall not be.
verses.textLatin: Cur non tollis peccatum meum, et quare non aufers iniquitatem meam? ecce nunc in pulvere dormiam, et si mane me quæsieris, non subsistam.

verses.text: Then  Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:

verses.text: How long wilt thou speak these things, and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo loqueris talia, et spiritus multiplex sermones oris tui?

verses.text: Doth God pervert judgment, or doth the Almighty overthrow that which is just?
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deus supplantat judicium? aut Omnipotens subvertit quod justum est?

verses.text: Although thy children have sinned against him, and he hath left them in the hand of their iniquity:
verses.textLatin: Etiam si filii tui peccaverunt ei, et dimisit eos in manu iniquitatis suæ:

verses.text: Yet if thou wilt arise early to God, and wilt beseech the Almighty:
verses.textLatin: tu tamen si diluculo consurrexeris ad Deum, et Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus;

verses.text: If thou wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee, and will make the dwelling of thy justice peaceable:
verses.textLatin: si mundus et rectus incesseris: statim evigilabit ad te, et pacatum reddet habitaculum justitiæ tuæ,

verses.text: Insomuch, that if thy former things were small, thy latter things would be multiplied exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: in tantum ut si priora tua fuerint parva, et novissima tua multiplicentur nimis.

verses.text: For inquire of the former generation, and search diligently into the memory of the fathers:
verses.textLatin: Interroga enim generationem pristinam, et diligenter investiga patrum memoriam

verses.text: (For we are but of yesterday, and are ignorant that our days upon earth are but a shadow:)
verses.textLatin: (hesterni quippe sumus, et ignoramus, quoniam sicut umbra dies nostri sunt super terram),

verses.text: And they shall teach thee: they shall speak to thee, and utter words out of their hearts.
verses.textLatin: et ipsi docebunt te, loquentur tibi, et de corde suo proferent eloquia.

verses.text: Can the rush be green without moisture? or a sedge-bush grow without water?
verses.textLatin: Numquid vivere potest scirpus absque humore? aut crescere carectum sine aqua?

verses.text: When it is yet in flower, and is not plucked up with the hand, it withereth before all herbs.
verses.textLatin: Cum adhuc sit in flore, nec carpatur manu, ante omnes herbas arescit.

verses.text: Even so are the ways of all that forget God, and the hope of the hypocrite shall perish:
verses.textLatin: Sic viæ omnium qui obliviscuntur Deum, et spes hypocritæ peribit.

verses.text: His folly shall not please him, and his trust shall be like the spider’s web.
verses.textLatin: Non ei placebit vecordia sua, et sicut tela aranearum fiducia ejus.

verses.text: He shall lean upon his house, and it shall not stand: he shall prop it up, and it shall not rise:
verses.textLatin: Innitetur super domum suam, et non stabit; fulciet eam, et non consurget.

verses.text: He seemeth to have moisture before the sun cometh, and at his rising, his blossom shall shoot forth.
verses.textLatin: Humectus videtur antequam veniat sol, et in ortu suo germen ejus egredietur.

verses.text: His roots shall be thick upon a heap of stones, and among the stones he shall abide.
verses.textLatin: Super acervum petrarum radices ejus densabuntur, et inter lapides commorabitur.

verses.text: If one swallow him up out of his place, he shall deny him, and shall say: I know thee not.
verses.textLatin: Si absorbuerit eum de loco suo, negabit eum, et dicet: Non novi te.

verses.text: For this is the joy of his way, that others may spring again out of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est enim lætitia viæ ejus, ut rursum de terra alii germinentur.

verses.text: God will not cast away the simple, nor reach out his hand to the evildoer:
verses.textLatin: Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis,

verses.text: Until thy mouth be filled with laughter, and thy lips with rejoicing.
verses.textLatin: donec impleatur risu os tuum, et labia tua jubilo.

verses.text: They that hate thee, shall be clothed with confusion: and the dwelling of the wicked shall not stand.
verses.textLatin: Qui oderunt te induentur confusione, et tabernaculum impiorum non subsistet.

verses.text: And  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Et respondens Job, ait:

verses.text: Indeed I know it is so, and thatman cannot be justified compared with God.
verses.textLatin: Vere scio quod ita sit, et quod non justificetur homo compositus Deo.

verses.text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand.
verses.textLatin: Si voluerit contendere cum eo, non poterit ei respondere unum pro mille.

verses.text: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath resisted him, and hath had peace?
verses.textLatin: Sapiens corde est, et fortis robore: quis restitit ei, et pacem habuit?

verses.text: Who hath removed mountains, and they whom he overthrew in his wrath, knew it not.
verses.textLatin: Qui transtulit montes, et nescierunt hi quos subvertit in furore suo.

verses.text: Who shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
verses.textLatin: Qui commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutiuntur.

verses.text: Who commandeth the sun and it riseth not: and shutteth up the stars as it were under a seal:
verses.textLatin: Qui præcipit soli, et non oritur, et stellas claudit quasi sub signaculo.

verses.text: Who alone spreadeth out the heavens, and walketh upon the waves of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Qui extendit cælos solus, et graditur super fluctus maris.

verses.text: Who maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and Hyades, and the inner parts of the south.
verses.textLatin: Qui facit Arcturum et Oriona, et Hyadas et interiora austri.

verses.text: Who doth things great and incomprehensible, and wonderful, of which there is no number.
verses.textLatin: Qui facit magna, et incomprehensibilia, et mirabilia, quorum non est numerus.

verses.text: If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart I shall not understand.
verses.textLatin: Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum; si abierit, non intelligam.

verses.text: If he examine on a sudden, who shall answer him? or who can say: Why dost thou so?
verses.textLatin: Si repente interroget, quis respondebit ei? vel quis dicere potest: Cur ita facis?

verses.text: God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world.
verses.textLatin: Deus, cujus iræ nemo resistere potest, et sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem.

verses.text: What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?
verses.textLatin: Quantus ergo sum ego, ut respondeam ei, et loquar verbis meis cum eo?

verses.text: I, who although I should have any just thing, would not answer, but would make supplication to my judge.
verses.textLatin: qui etiam si habuero quippiam justum, non respondebo: sed meum judicem deprecabor.

verses.text: And if he should hear me when I call, I should not believe that he had heard my voice.
verses.textLatin: Et cum invocantem exaudierit me, non credo quod audierit vocem meam.

verses.text: For he shall crush me in a whirlwind, and multiply my wounds even without cause.
verses.textLatin: In turbine enim conteret me, et multiplicabit vulnera mea, etiam sine causa.

verses.text: He alloweth not my spirit to rest, and he filleth me with bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Non concedit requiescere spiritum meum, et implet me amaritudinibus.

verses.text: If strength be demanded, he is most strong: if equity of judgment, no man dare bear witness for me.
verses.textLatin: Si fortitudo quæritur, robustissimus est; si æquitas judicii, nemo audet pro me testimonium dicere.

verses.text: If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me: if I would shew myself innocent, he shall prove me wicked.
verses.textLatin: Si justificare me voluero, os meum condemnabit me; si innocentem ostendero, pravum me comprobabit.

verses.text: Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of, and I shall be weary of my life.
verses.textLatin: Etiam si simplex fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea, et tædebit me vitæ meæ.

verses.text: One thing there is that I have spoken, both the innocent and the wicked he consumeth.
verses.textLatin: Unum est quod locutus sum: et innocentem et impium ipse consumit.

verses.text: If he scourge, let him kill at once, and not laugh at the pains of the innocent.
verses.textLatin: Si flagellat, occidat semel, et non de pœnis innocentum rideat.

verses.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, he covereth the face of the judges thereof: and if it be not he, who is it then?
verses.textLatin: Terra data est in manus impii; vultum judicum ejus operit. Quod si non ille est, quis ergo est?

verses.text: My days have been swifter than a post: they have fled away and have not seen good.
verses.textLatin: Dies mei velociores fuerunt cursore; fugerunt, et non viderunt bonum.

verses.text: They have passed by as ships carrying fruits, as an eagle flying to the prey.
verses.textLatin: Pertransierunt quasi naves poma portantes; sicut aquila volans ad escam.

verses.text: If I say: I will not speak so: I change my face, and am tormented with sorrow.
verses.textLatin: Cum dixero: Nequaquam ita loquar: commuto faciem meam, et dolore torqueor.

verses.text: I feared all my works, knowing that thou didst not spare the offender.
verses.textLatin: Verebar omnia opera mea, sciens quod non parceres delinquenti.

verses.text: But if so also I am wicked, why have I laboured in vain?
verses.textLatin: Si autem et sic impius sum, quare frustra laboravi?

verses.text: If I be washed as it were with snow waters, and my hands shall shine ever so clean:
verses.textLatin: Si lotus fuero quasi aquis nivis, et fulserint velut mundissimæ manus meæ,

verses.text: Yet thou shalt plunge me in filth, and my garments shall abhor me,
verses.textLatin: tamen sordibus intinges me, et abominabuntur me vestimenta mea.

verses.text: For I shall not answer a man that is like myself: nor one that may be heard with me equally in judgment.
verses.textLatin: Neque enim viro qui similis mei est, respondebo; nec qui mecum in judicio ex æquo possit audiri.

verses.text: There is none that may be able to reprove both, and to put his hand between both.
verses.textLatin: Non est qui utrumque valeat arguere, et ponere manum suam in ambobus.

verses.text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me.
verses.textLatin: Auferat a me virgam suam, et pavor ejus non me terreat.

verses.text: I will speak, and will not fear him: for I cannot answer while I am in fear.
verses.textLatin: Loquar, et non timebo eum; neque enim possum metuens respondere.

verses.text: My  soul is weary of my life, I will let go my speech against myself, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.textLatin: Tædet animam meam vitæ meæ; dimittam adversum me eloquium meum: loquar in amaritudine animæ meæ.

verses.text: I will say to God: Do not condemn me: tell me why thou judgest me so.
verses.textLatin: Dicam Deo: Noli me condemnare; indica mihi cur me ita judices.

verses.text: Doth it seem good to thee that thou shouldst calumniate me, and oppress me, the work of thy own hands, and help the counsel of the wicked?
verses.textLatin: Numquid bonum tibi videtur, si calumnieris me, et opprimas me opus manuum tuarum, et consilium impiorum adjuves?

verses.text: Hast thou eyes of flesh: or, shalt thou see as man seeth?
verses.textLatin: Numquid oculi carnei tibi sunt? aut sicut videt homo, et tu videbis?

verses.text: Are thy days as the days of man, and are thy years as the times of men:
verses.textLatin: Numquid sicut dies hominis dies tui, et anni tui sicut humana sunt tempora,

verses.text: That thou shouldst inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?
verses.textLatin: ut quæras iniquitatem meam, et peccatum meum scruteris,

verses.text: And shouldst know that I have done no wicked thing, whereas there is no man that can deliver out of thy hand.
verses.textLatin: et scias quia nihil impium fecerim, cum sit nemo qui de manu tua possit eruere?

verses.text: Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about, and dost thou thus cast me down headlong on a sudden?
verses.textLatin: Manus tuæ fecerunt me, et plasmaverunt me totum in circuitu: et sic repente præcipitas me?

verses.text: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay, and thou wilt bring me into dust again.
verses.textLatin: Memento, quæso, quod sicut lutum feceris me, et in pulverem reduces me.

verses.text: Hast thou not milked me as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
verses.textLatin: Nonne sicut lac mulsisti me, et sicut caseum me coagulasti?

verses.text: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh: thou hast put me together with bones and sinews:
verses.textLatin: Pelle et carnibus vestisti me; ossibus et nervis compegisti me.

verses.text: Thou hast granted me life and mercy, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
verses.textLatin: Vitam et misericordiam tribuisti mihi, et visitatio tua custodivit spiritum meum.

verses.text: Although thou conceal these things in thy heart, yet I know that thou rememberest all things.
verses.textLatin: Licet hæc celes in corde tuo, tamen scio quia universorum memineris.

verses.text: If I have sinned and thou hast spared me for an hour: why dost thou not suffer me to be clean from my iniquity?
verses.textLatin: Si peccavi, et ad horam pepercisti mihi, cur ab iniquitate mea mundum me esse non pateris?

verses.text: And if I be wicked, woe unto me: and if just, I shall not lift up my head, being filled with affliction and misery.
verses.textLatin: Et si impius fuero, væ mihi est; et si justus, non levabo caput, saturatus afflictione et miseria.

verses.text: And for pride thou wilt take me as a lioness, and returning thou tormentest me wonderfully.
verses.textLatin: Et propter superbiam quasi leænam capies me, reversusque mirabiliter me crucias.

verses.text: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and multipliest thy wrath upon me, and pains war against me.
verses.textLatin: Instauras testes tuos contra me, et multiplicas iram tuam adversum me, et pœnæ militant in me.

verses.text: Why didst thou bring me forth out of the womb: O that I had been consumed that eye might not see me!
verses.textLatin: Quare de vulva eduxisti me? qui utinam consumptus essem, ne oculus me videret.

verses.text: I should have been as if I had not been, carried from the womb to the grave.
verses.textLatin: Fuissem quasi non essem, de utero translatus ad tumulum.

verses.text: Shall not the fewness of my days be ended shortly? suffer me, therefore, that I may lament my sorrow a little:
verses.textLatin: Numquid non paucitas dierum meorum finietur brevi? dimitte ergo me, ut plangam paululum dolorem meum,

verses.text: Before I go, and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death:
verses.textLatin: antequam vadam, et non revertar, ad terram tenebrosam, et opertam mortis caligine:

verses.text: A land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth.
verses.textLatin: terram miseriæ et tenebrarum, ubi umbra mortis et nullus ordo, sed sempiternus horror inhabitat.

verses.text: Then  Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit:

verses.text: Shall not he that speaketh much, hear also? or shall a man full of talk be justified?
verses.textLatin: Numquid qui multa loquitur, non et audiet? aut vir verbosus justificabitur?

verses.text: Shall men hold their peace to thee only? and when thou hast mocked others, shall no man confute thee?
verses.textLatin: Tibi soli tacebunt homines? et cum ceteros irriseris, a nullo confutaberis?

verses.text: For thou hast said: My word is pure, and I am clean in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: Dixisti enim: Purus est sermo meus, et mundus sum in conspectu tuo.

verses.text: And I wish that God would speak with thee, and would open his lips to thee,
verses.textLatin: Atque utinam Deus loqueretur tecum, et aperiret labia sua tibi,

verses.text: That he might shew thee the secrets of wisdom, and that his law is manifold, and thou mightest understand that he exacteth much less of thee, than thy iniquity deserveth.
verses.textLatin: ut ostenderet tibi secreta sapientiæ, et quod multiplex esset lex ejus: et intelligeres quod multo minora exigaris ab eo quam meretur iniquitas tua!

verses.text: Peradventure thou wilt comprehend the steps of God, and wilt find out the Almighty perfectly?
verses.textLatin: Forsitan vestigia Dei comprehendes, et usque ad perfectum Omnipotentem reperies?

verses.text: He is higher than heaven, and what wilt thou do? he is deeper than hell, and how wilt thou know?
verses.textLatin: Excelsior cælo est, et quid facies? profundior inferno, et unde cognosces?

verses.text: The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
verses.textLatin: Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari.

verses.text: If he shall overturn all things, or shall press them together, who shall contradict him?
verses.textLatin: Si subverterit omnia, vel in unum coarctaverit, quis contradicet ei?

verses.text: For he knoweth the vanity of men, and when he seeth iniquity, doth he not consider it?
verses.textLatin: Ipse enim novit hominum vanitatem; et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat?

verses.text: A vain man is lifted up into pride, and thinketh himself born free like a wild ass’s colt.
verses.textLatin: Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tamquam pullum onagri se liberum natum putat.

verses.text: But thou hast hardened thy heart, and hast spread thy hands to him.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem firmasti cor tuum, et expandisti ad eum manus tuas.

verses.text: If thou wilt put away from thee the iniquity that is in thy hand, and let not injustice remain in thy tabernacle:
verses.textLatin: Si iniquitatem quæ est in manu tua abstuleris a te, et non manserit in tabernaculo tuo injustitia,

verses.text: Then mayst thou lift up thy face without spot, and thou shalt be steadfast, and shalt not fear.
verses.textLatin: tunc levare poteris faciem tuam absque macula; et eris stabilis, et non timebis.

verses.text: Thou shalt also forget misery, and remember it only as waters that are passed away.
verses.textLatin: Miseriæ quoque oblivisceris, et quasi aquarum quæ præterierunt recordaberis.

verses.text: And brightness like that of the noonday, shall arise to thee at evening: and when thou shalt think thyself consumed, thou shalt rise as the day star.
verses.textLatin: Et quasi meridianus fulgor consurget tibi ad vesperam; et cum te consumptum putaveris, orieris ut lucifer.

verses.text: And thou shalt have confidence, hope being set before thee, and being buried thou shalt sleep secure.
verses.textLatin: Et habebis fiduciam, proposita tibi spe: et defossus securus dormies.

verses.text: Thou shalt rest, and there shall be none to make thee afraid: and many shall entreat thy face.
verses.textLatin: Requiesces, et non erit qui te exterreat; et deprecabuntur faciem tuam plurimi.

verses.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall decay, and the way to escape shall fail them, and their hope the abomination of the soul.
verses.textLatin: Oculi autem impiorum deficient, et effugium peribit ab eis: et spes illorum abominatio animæ.

verses.text: THEN Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, dixit:

verses.text: Are you then men alone, and shall wisdom die with you?
verses.textLatin: Ergo vos estis soli homines, et vobiscum morietur sapientia?

verses.text: I also have a heart as well as you: for who is ignorant of these things, which you know?
verses.textLatin: Et mihi est cor sicut et vobis, nec inferior vestri sum; quis enim hæc quæ nostis ignorat?

verses.text: He that is mocked by his friends as I, shall call upon God and he will hear him: for the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn.
verses.textLatin: Qui deridetur ab amico suo, sicut ego, invocabit Deum, et exaudiet eum: deridetur enim justi simplicitas.

verses.text: The lamp despised in the thoughts of the rich, is ready for the time appointed.
verses.textLatin: Lampas contempta apud cogitationes divitum parata ad tempus statutum.

verses.text: The tabernacles of robbers abound, and they provoke God boldly; whereas it is he that hath given all into their hands:
verses.textLatin: Abundant tabernacula prædonum, et audacter provocant Deum, cum ipse dederit omnia in manus eorum.

verses.text: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee: and the birds of the air, and they shall tell thee.
verses.textLatin: Nimirum interroga jumenta, et docebunt te; et volatilia cæli, et indicabunt tibi.

verses.text: Speak to the earth, and it shall answer thee: and the fishes of the sea shall tell.
verses.textLatin: Loquere terræ, et respondebit tibi, et narrabunt pisces maris.

verses.text: Who is ignorant that the hand of the Lord hath made all these things?
verses.textLatin: Quis ignorat quod omnia hæc manus Domini fecerit?

verses.text: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all flesh of man.
verses.textLatin: In cujus manu anima omnis viventis, et spiritus universæ carnis hominis.

verses.text: Doth not the ear discern words, and the palate of him that eateth, the taste?
verses.textLatin: Nonne auris verba dijudicat? et fauces comedentis, saporem?

verses.text: In the ancient is wisdom, and in length of days prudence.
verses.textLatin: In antiquis est sapientia, et in multo tempore prudentia.

verses.text: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.
verses.textLatin: Apud ipsum est sapientia et fortitudo; ipse habet consilium et intelligentiam.

verses.text: If he pull down, there is no man that can build up: if he shut up a man, there is none that can open.
verses.textLatin: Si destruxerit, nemo est qui ædificet; si incluserit hominem, nullus est qui aperiat.

verses.text: If he withhold the waters, all things shall be dried up: and if he send them out, they shall overturn the earth.
verses.textLatin: Si continuerit aquas, omnia siccabuntur; et si emiserit eas, subvertent terram.

verses.text: With him is strength and wisdom: he knoweth both the deceiver, and him that is deceived.
verses.textLatin: Apud ipsum est fortitudo et sapientia; ipse novit et decipientem, et eum qui decipitur.

verses.text: He bringeth counsellors to a foolish end, and judges to insensibility.
verses.textLatin: Adducit consiliarios in stultum finem, et judices in stuporem.

verses.text: He looseth the belt of kings, and girdeth their loins with a cord.
verses.textLatin: Balteum regum dissolvit, et præcingit fune renes eorum.

verses.text: He leadeth away priests without glory, and overthroweth nobles.
verses.textLatin: Ducit sacerdotes inglorios, et optimates supplantat:

verses.text: He changeth the speech of the true speakers, and taketh away the doctrine of the aged.
verses.textLatin: commutans labium veracium, et doctrinam senum auferens.

verses.text: He poureth contempt upon princes, and relieveth them that were oppressed.
verses.textLatin: Effundit despectionem super principes, eos qui oppressi fuerant relevans.

verses.text: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth up to light the shadow of death.
verses.textLatin: Qui revelat profunda de tenebris, et producit in lucem umbram mortis.

verses.text: He multiplieth nations, and destroyeth them, and restoreth them again after they were overthrown.
verses.textLatin: Qui multiplicat gentes, et perdit eas, et subversas in integrum restituit.

verses.text: He changeth the heart of the princes of the people of the earth, and deceiveth them that they walk in vain where there is no way.
verses.textLatin: Qui immutat cor principum populi terræ, et decipit eos ut frustra incedant per invium:

verses.text: They shall grope as in the dark, and not in the light, and he shall make them stagger like men that are drunk.
verses.textLatin: palpabunt quasi in tenebris, et non in luce, et errare eos faciet quasi ebrios.

verses.text: Behold  my eye hath seen all these things, and my ear hath heard them, and I have understood them all.
verses.textLatin: Ecce omnia hæc vidit oculus meus, et audivit auris mea, et intellexi singula.

verses.text: According to your knowledge I also know: neither am I inferior to you.
verses.textLatin: Secundum scientiam vestram et ego novi: nec inferior vestri sum.

verses.text: But yet I will speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.
verses.textLatin: Sed tamen ad Omnipotentem loquar, et disputare cum Deo cupio:

verses.text: Having first shewn that you are forgers of lies, and maintainers of perverse opinions.
verses.textLatin: prius vos ostendens fabricatores mendacii, et cultores perversorum dogmatum.

verses.text: And I wish you would hold your peace, that you might be thought to be wise men.
verses.textLatin: Atque utinam taceretis, ut putaremini esse sapientes.

verses.text: Hear ye therefore my reproof, and attend to the judgment of my lips.
verses.textLatin: Audite ergo correptionem meam, et judicium labiorum meorum attendite.

verses.text: Hath God any need of your lie, that you should speak deceitfully for him?
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deus indiget vestro mendacio, ut pro illo loquamini dolos?

verses.text: Do you accept his person, and do you endeavour to judge for God?
verses.textLatin: numquid faciem ejus accipitis, et pro Deo judicare nitimini?

verses.text: Or shall it please him, from whom nothing can be concealed? or shall he be deceived as a man, with your deceitful dealings?
verses.textLatin: aut placebit ei quem celare nihil potest? aut decipietur, ut homo, vestris fraudulentiis?

verses.text: He shall reprove you, because in secret you accept his person.
verses.textLatin: Ipse vos arguet, quoniam in abscondito faciem ejus accipitis.

verses.text: As soon as he shall move himself, he shall trouble you: and his dread shall fall upon you.
verses.textLatin: Statim ut se commoverit, turbabit vos, et terror ejus irruet super vos.

verses.text: Your remembrance shall be compared to ashes, and your necks shall be brought to clay.
verses.textLatin: Memoria vestra comparabitur cineri, et redigentur in lutum cervices vestræ.

verses.text: Hold your peace a little while, that I may speak whatsoever my mind shall suggest to me.
verses.textLatin: Tacete paulisper, ut loquar quodcumque mihi mens suggesserit.

verses.text: Why do I tear my flesh with my teeth, and carry my soul in my hands?
verses.textLatin: Quare lacero carnes meas dentibus meis, et animam meam porto in manibus meis?

verses.text: Although he should kill me, I will trust in him: but yet I will reprove my ways in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Etiam si occiderit me, in ipso sperabo: verumtamen vias meas in conspectu ejus arguam.

verses.text: And he shall be my saviour: for no hypocrite shall come before his presence.
verses.textLatin: Et ipse erit salvator meus: non enim veniet in conspectu ejus omnis hypocrita.

verses.text: Hear ye my speech, and receive with your ears hidden truths.
verses.textLatin: Audite sermonem meum, et ænigmata percipite auribus vestris.

verses.text: If I shall be judged, I know that I shall be found just.
verses.textLatin: Si fuero judicatus, scio quod justus inveniar.

verses.text: Who is he that will plead against me? let him come: why am I consumed holding my peace?
verses.textLatin: Quis est qui judicetur mecum? veniat: quare tacens consumor?

verses.text: Two things only do not to me, and then from thy face I shall not be hid:
verses.textLatin: Duo tantum ne facias mihi, et tunc a facie tua non abscondar:

verses.text: Withdraw thy hand far from me, and let not thy dread terrify me.
verses.textLatin: manum tuam longe fac a me, et formido tua non me terreat.

verses.text: Call me, and I will answer thee: or else I will speak, and do thou answer me.
verses.textLatin: Voca me, et ego respondebo tibi: aut certe loquar, et tu responde mihi.

verses.text: How many are my iniquities and sins? make me know my crimes and offences.
verses.textLatin: Quantas habeo iniquitates et peccata? scelera mea et delicta ostende mihi.

verses.text: Why hidest thou thy face, and thinkest me thy enemy?
verses.textLatin: Cur faciem tuam abscondis, et arbitraris me inimicum tuum?

verses.text: Against a leaf, that is carried away with the wind, thou shewest thy power, and thou pursuest a dry straw.
verses.textLatin: Contra folium, quod vento rapitur, ostendis potentiam tuam, et stipulam siccam persequeris:

verses.text: For thou writest bitter things against me, and wilt consume me for the sins of my youth.
verses.textLatin: scribis enim contra me amaritudines, et consumere me vis peccatis adolescentiæ meæ.

verses.text: Thou hast put my feet in the stocks, and hast observed all my paths, and hast considered the steps of my feet:
verses.textLatin: Posuisti in nervo pedem meum, et observasti omnes semitas meas, et vestigia pedum meorum considerasti:

verses.text: Who am to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is moth-eaten.
verses.textLatin: qui quasi putredo consumendus sum, et quasi vestimentum quod comeditur a tinea.

verses.text: Man  born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.
verses.textLatin: Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis.

verses.text: Who cometh forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and fleeth as a shadow, and never continueth in the same state.
verses.textLatin: Qui quasi flos egreditur et conteritur, et fugit velut umbra, et numquam in eodem statu permanet.

verses.text: And dost thou think it meet to open thy eyes upon such an one, and to bring him into judgment with thee?
verses.textLatin: Et dignum ducis super hujuscemodi aperire oculos tuos, et adducere eum tecum in judicium?

verses.text: Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed? is it not thou who only art?
verses.textLatin: Quis potest facere mundum de immundo conceptum semine? nonne tu qui solus es?

verses.text: The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee: thou hast appointed his bounds which cannot be passed.
verses.textLatin: Breves dies hominis sunt: numerus mensium ejus apud te est: constituisti terminos ejus, qui præteriri non poterunt.

verses.text: Depart a little from him, that he may rest, until his wished for day come, as that of the hireling.
verses.textLatin: Recede paululum ab eo, ut quiescat, donec optata veniat, sicut mercenarii, dies ejus.

verses.text: A tree hath hope: if it be cut, it groweth green again, and the boughs thereof sprout.
verses.textLatin: Lignum habet spem: si præcisum fuerit, rursum virescit, et rami ejus pullulant.

verses.text: If its root be old in the earth, and its stock be dead in the dust:
verses.textLatin: Si senuerit in terra radix ejus, et in pulvere emortuus fuerit truncus illius,

verses.text: At the scent of water, it shall spring, and bring forth leaves, as when it was first planted.
verses.textLatin: ad odorem aquæ germinabit, et faciet comam, quasi cum primum plantatum est.

verses.text: But man when he shall be dead, and stripped and consumed, I pray you where is he?
verses.textLatin: Homo vero cum mortuus fuerit, et nudatus, atque consumptus, ubi, quæso, est?

verses.text: As if the waters should depart out of the sea, and an emptied river should be dried up:
verses.textLatin: Quomodo si recedant aquæ de mari, et fluvius vacuefactus arescat:

verses.text: So man when he is fallen asleep shall not rise again; till the heavens be broken. he shall not awake, nor rise up out of his sleep.
verses.textLatin: sic homo, cum dormierit, non resurget: donec atteratur cælum, non evigilabit, nec consurget de somno suo.

verses.text: Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass, and appoint me a time when thou wilt remember me?
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi hoc tribuat, ut in inferno protegas me, et abscondas me donec pertranseat furor tuus, et constituas mihi tempus in quo recorderis mei?

verses.text: Shall man that is dead, thinkest thou, live again? all the days in which I am now in warfare, I expect until my change come.
verses.textLatin: Putasne mortuus homo rursum vivat? cunctis diebus quibus nunc milito, expecto donec veniat immutatio mea.

verses.text: Thou shalt call me, and I will answer thee: to the work of thy hands thou shalt reach out thy right hand.
