verses.textLatin: Vocabis me, et ego respondebo tibi: operi manuum tuarum porriges dexteram.

verses.text: Thou indeed hast numbered my steps, but spare my sins.
verses.textLatin: Tu quidem gressus meos dinumerasti: sed parce peccatis meis.

verses.text: Thou hast sealed up my offences as it were in a bag, but hast cured my iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Signasti quasi in sacculo delicta mea, sed curasti iniquitatem meam.

verses.text: A mountain falling cometh to nought, and a rock is removed out of its place.
verses.textLatin: Mons cadens defluit, et saxum transfertur de loco suo:

verses.text: Waters wear away the stones, and with inundation the ground by little and little is washed away: so in like manner thou shalt destroy man.
verses.textLatin: lapides excavant aquæ, et alluvione paulatim terra consumitur: et hominem ergo similiter perdes.

verses.text: Thou hast strengthened him for a little while, that he may pass away for ever: thou shalt change his face, and shalt send him away.
verses.textLatin: Roborasti eum paululum, ut in perpetuum transiret: immutabis faciem ejus, et emittes eum.

verses.text: Whether his children come to honour or dishonour, he shall not understand.
verses.textLatin: Sive nobiles fuerint filii ejus, sive ignobiles, non intelliget.

verses.text: But yet his flesh, while he shall live, shall have pain, and his soul shall mourn over him.
verses.textLatin: Attamen caro ejus, dum vivet, dolebit, et anima illius super semetipso lugebit.

verses.text: And  Eliphaz the Themanite, answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:

verses.text: Will a wise man answer as if he were speaking in the wind, and fill his stomach with burning heat?
verses.textLatin: Numquid sapiens respondebit quasi in ventum loquens, et implebit ardore stomachum suum?

verses.text: Thou reprovest him by words, who is not equal to thee, and thou speakest that which is not good for thee.
verses.textLatin: Arguis verbis eum qui non est æqualis tibi, et loqueris quod tibi non expedit.

verses.text: As much as is in thee, thou hast made void fear, and hast taken away prayers from before God.
verses.textLatin: Quantum in te est, evacuasti timorem, et tulisti preces coram Deo.

verses.text: For thy iniquity hath taught thy mouth, and thou imitatest the tongue of blasphemers.
verses.textLatin: Docuit enim iniquitas tua os tuum, et imitaris linguam blasphemantium.

verses.text: Thy own mouth shall condemn thee, and not I: and thy own lips shall answer thee.
verses.textLatin: Condemnabit te os tuum, et non ego: et labia tua respondebunt tibi.

verses.text: Art thou the first man that was born, or wast thou made before the hills?
verses.textLatin: Numquid primus homo tu natus es, et ante colles formatus?

verses.text: Hast thou heard God’s counsel, and shall his wisdom be inferior to thee?
verses.textLatin: numquid consilium Dei audisti, et inferior te erit ejus sapientia?

verses.text: What knowest thou that we are ignorant of? what dost thou understand that we know not?
verses.textLatin: Quid nosti quod ignoremus? quid intelligis quod nesciamus?

verses.text: There are with us also aged and ancient men, much elder than thy fathers.
verses.textLatin: Et senes et antiqui sunt in nobis, multo vetustiores quam patres tui.

verses.text: Is it a great matter that God should comfort thee? but thy wicked words hinder this.
verses.textLatin: Numquid grande est ut consoletur te Deus? sed verba tua prava hoc prohibent.

verses.text: Why doth thy heart elevate thee, and why dost thou stare with thy eyes, as if they were thinking great things?
verses.textLatin: Quid te elevat cor tuum, et quasi magna cogitans attonitos habes oculos?

verses.text: Why doth thy spirit swell against God, to utter such words out of thy mouth?
verses.textLatin: Quid tumet contra Deum spiritus tuus, ut proferas de ore tuo hujuscemodi sermones?

verses.text: What is man that he should be without spot, and he that is born of a woman that he should appear just?
verses.textLatin: Quid est homo ut immaculatus sit, et ut justus appareat natus de muliere?

verses.text: Behold among his saints none is unchangeable, and the heavens are not pure in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Ecce inter sanctos ejus nemo immutabilis, et cæli non sunt mundi in conspectu ejus.

verses.text: How much more is man abominable, and unprofitable, who drinketh iniquity like water?
verses.textLatin: Quanto magis abominabilis et inutilis homo, qui bibit quasi aquam iniquitatem?

verses.text: I will shew thee, hear me: and I will tell thee what I have seen.
verses.textLatin: Ostendam tibi: audi me: quod vidi, narrabo tibi.

verses.text: Wise men confess and hide not their fathers.
verses.textLatin: Sapientes confitentur, et non abscondunt patres suos:

verses.text: To whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger hath passed among them.
verses.textLatin: quibus solis data est terra, et non transivit alienus per eos.

verses.text: The wicked man is proud all his days, and the number of the years of his tyranny is uncertain.
verses.textLatin: Cunctis diebus suis impius superbit, et numerus annorum incertus est tyrannidis ejus.

verses.text: The sound of dread is always in his ears: and when there is peace, he always suspecteth treason.
verses.textLatin: Sonitus terroris semper in auribus illius: et cum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur.

verses.text: He believeth not that he may return from darkness to light, looking round about for the sword on every side.
verses.textLatin: Non credit quod reverti possit de tenebris ad lucem, circumspectans undique gladium.

verses.text: When he moveth himself to seek bread, he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.textLatin: Cum se moverit ad quærendum panem, novit quod paratus sit in manu ejus tenebrarum dies.

verses.text: Tribulation shall terrify him, and distress shall surround him, as a king that is prepared for the battle.
verses.textLatin: Terrebit eum tribulatio, et angustia vallabit eum, sicut regem qui præparatur ad prælium.

verses.text: For he hath stretched out his hand against God, and hath strengthened himself against the Almighty.
verses.textLatin: Tetendit enim adversus Deum manum suam, et contra Omnipotentem roboratus est.

verses.text: He hath run against him with his neck raised up, and is armed with a fat neck.
verses.textLatin: Cucurrit adversus eum erecto collo, et pingui cervice armatus est.

verses.text: Fatness hath covered his face, and the fat hangeth down on his sides.
verses.textLatin: Operuit faciem ejus crassitudo, et de lateribus ejus arvina dependet.

verses.text: He hath dwelt in desolate cities, and in desert houses that are reduced into heaps.
verses.textLatin: Habitavit in civitatibus desolatis, et in domibus desertis, quæ in tumulos sunt redactæ.

verses.text: He shall not be enriched, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he push his root in the earth.
verses.textLatin: Non ditabitur, nec perseverabit substantia ejus, nec mittet in terra radicem suam.

verses.text: He shall not depart out of darkness: the flame shall dry up his branches, and he shall be taken away by the breath of his own mouth.
verses.textLatin: Non recedet de tenebris: ramos ejus arefaciet flamma, et auferetur spiritu oris sui.

verses.text: He shall not believe, being vainly deceived by error, that he may be redeemed with any price.
verses.textLatin: Non credet, frustra errore deceptus, quod aliquo pretio redimendus sit.

verses.text: Before his days be full he shall perish: and his hands shall wither away.
verses.textLatin: Antequam dies ejus impleantur peribit, et manus ejus arescent.

verses.text: He shall be blasted as a vine when its grapes are in the first flower, and as an olive tree that casteth its flower.
verses.textLatin: Lædetur quasi vinea in primo flore botrus ejus, et quasi oliva projiciens florem suum.

verses.text: For the congregation of the hypocrite is barren, and fire shall devour their tabernacles, who love to take bribes.
verses.textLatin: Congregatio enim hypocritæ sterilis, et ignis devorabit tabernacula eorum qui munera libenter accipiunt.

verses.text: He hath conceived sorrow, and hath brought forth iniquity, and his womb prepareth deceits.
verses.textLatin: Concepit dolorem, et peperit iniquitatem, et uterus ejus præparat dolos.

verses.text: Then  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, dixit:

verses.text: I have often heard such things as these: you are all troublesome comforters.
verses.textLatin: Audivi frequenter talia: consolatores onerosi omnes vos estis.

verses.text: Shall windy words have no end? or is it any trouble to thee to speak?
verses.textLatin: Numquid habebunt finem verba ventosa? aut aliquid tibi molestum est, si loquaris?

verses.text: I also could speak like you: and would God your soul were for my soul.
verses.textLatin: Poteram et ego similia vestri loqui, atque utinam esset anima vestra pro anima mea:

verses.text: I would comfort you also with words, and would wag my head over you.
verses.textLatin: consolarer et ego vos sermonibus, et moverem caput meum super vos;

verses.text: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and would move my lips, as sparing you.
verses.textLatin: roborarem vos ore meo, et moverem labia mea, quasi parcens vobis.

verses.text: But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain will not rest: and if I hold my peace, it will not depart from me.
verses.textLatin: Sed quid agam? Si locutus fuero, non quiescet dolor meus, et si tacuero, non recedet a me.

verses.text: But now my sorrow hath oppressed me, and all my limbs are brought to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem oppressit me dolor meus, et in nihilum redacti sunt omnes artus mei.

verses.text: My wrinkles bear witness against me, and a false speaker riseth up against my face, contradicting me.
verses.textLatin: Rugæ meæ testimonium dicunt contra me, et suscitatur falsiloquus adversus faciem meam, contradicens mihi.

verses.text: He hath gathered together his fury against me, and threatening me he hath gnashed with his teeth upon me: my enemy hath beheld me with terrible eyes.
verses.textLatin: Collegit furorem suum in me, et comminans mihi, infremuit contra me dentibus suis: hostis meus terribilibus oculis me intuitus est.

verses.text: They have opened their mouths upon me, and reproaching me they have struck me on the cheek, they are filled with my pains.
verses.textLatin: Aperuerunt super me ora sua, et exprobrantes percusserunt maxillam meam: satiati sunt pœnis meis.

verses.text: God hath shut me up with the unjust man, and hath delivered me into the hands of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Conclusit me Deus apud iniquum, et manibus impiorum me tradidit.

verses.text: I that was formerly so wealthy, am all on a sudden broken to pieces: he hath taken me by my neck, he hath broken me, and hath set me up to be his mark.
verses.textLatin: Ego ille quondam opulentus, repente contritus sum: tenuit cervicem meam, confregit me, et posuit me sibi quasi in signum.

verses.text: He hath compassed me round about with his lances, he hath wounded my loins, he hath not spared, and hath poured out my bowels on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Circumdedit me lanceis suis; convulneravit lumbos meos: non pepercit, et effudit in terra viscera mea.

verses.text: He hath torn me with wound upon wound, he hath rushed in upon me like a giant.
verses.textLatin: Concidit me vulnere super vulnus: irruit in me quasi gigas.

verses.text: I have sowed sackcloth upon my skin, and have covered my flesh with ashes.
verses.textLatin: Saccum consui super cutem meam, et operui cinere carnem meam.

verses.text: My face is swollen with weeping, and my eyelids are dim.
verses.textLatin: Facies mea intumuit a fletu, et palpebræ meæ caligaverunt.

verses.text: These things have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God.
verses.textLatin: Hæc passus sum absque iniquitate manus meæ, cum haberem mundas ad Deum preces.

verses.text: O earth, cover not thou my blood, neither let my cry find a hiding place in thee.
verses.textLatin: Terra, ne operias sanguinem meum, neque inveniat in te locum latendi clamor meus:

verses.text: For behold my witness is in heaven, and he that knoweth my conscience is on high.
verses.textLatin: ecce enim in cælo testis meus, et conscius meus in excelsis.

verses.text: My friends are full of words: my eye poureth out tears to God.
verses.textLatin: Verbosi amici mei: ad Deum stillat oculus meus:

verses.text: And O that a man might so be judged with God, as the son of man is judged with his companion!
verses.textLatin: atque utinam sic judicaretur vir cum Deo, quomodo judicatur filius hominis cum collega suo.

verses.text: For behold short years pass away, and I am walking in a path by which I shall not return.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim breves anni transeunt, et semitam per quam non revertar ambulo.

verses.text: My  spirit shall be wasted, my days shall be shortened, and only the grave remaineth for me.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus meus attenuabitur; dies mei breviabuntur: et solum mihi superest sepulchrum.

verses.text: I have not sinned, and my eye abideth in bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Non peccavi, et in amaritudinibus moratur oculus meus.

verses.text: Deliver me, O Lord, and set me beside thee, and let any man’s hand fight against me.
verses.textLatin: Libera me, Domine, et pone me juxta te, et cujusvis manus pugnet contra me.

verses.text: Thou hast set their heart far from understanding, therefore they shall not be exalted.
verses.textLatin: Cor eorum longe fecisti a disciplina: propterea non exaltabuntur.

verses.text: He promiseth a prey to his companions, and the eyes of his children shall fail.
verses.textLatin: Prædam pollicetur sociis, et oculi filiorum ejus deficient.

verses.text: He hath made me as it were a byword of the people, and I am an example before them.
verses.textLatin: Posuit me quasi in proverbium vulgi, et exemplum sum coram eis.

verses.text: My eye is dim through indignation, and my limbs are brought as it were to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Caligavit ab indignatione oculus meus, et membra mea quasi in nihilum redacta sunt.

verses.text: The just shall be astonished at this, and the innocent shall be raised up against the hypocrite.
verses.textLatin: Stupebunt justi super hoc, et innocens contra hypocritam suscitabitur.

verses.text: And the just man shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.
verses.textLatin: Et tenebit justus viam suam, et mundis manibus addet fortitudinem.

verses.text: Wherefore be you all converted, and come, and I shall not find among you any wise man.
verses.textLatin: Igitur omnes vos convertimini, et venite, et non inveniam in vobis ullum sapientem.

verses.text: My days have passed away, my thoughts are dissipated, tormenting my heart.
verses.textLatin: Dies mei transierunt; cogitationes meæ dissipatæ sunt, torquentes cor meum.

verses.text: They have turned night into day, and after darkness I hope for light again.
verses.textLatin: Noctem verterunt in diem, et rursum post tenebras spero lucem.

verses.text: If I wait hell is my house, and I have made my bed in darkness.
verses.textLatin: Si sustinuero, infernus domus mea est, et in tenebris stravi lectulum meum.

verses.text: I have said to rottenness: Thou art my father; to worms, my mother and my sister.
verses.textLatin: Putredini dixi: Pater meus es; Mater mea, et soror mea, vermibus.

verses.text: Where is now then my expectation, and who considereth my patience?
verses.textLatin: Ubi est ergo nunc præstolatio mea? et patientiam meam quis considerat?

verses.text: All that I have shall go down into the deepest pit: thinkest thou that there at least I shall have rest?
verses.textLatin: In profundissimum infernum descendent omnia mea: putasne saltem ibi erit requies mihi?

verses.text: Then  Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:

verses.text: How long will you throw out words? understand first, and so let us speak.
verses.textLatin: Usque ad quem finem verba jactabitis? intelligite prius, et sic loquamur.

verses.text: Why are we reputed as beasts, and counted vile before you?
verses.textLatin: Quare reputati sumus ut jumenta, et sorduimus coram vobis?

verses.text: Thou that destroyest thy soul in thy fury, shall the earth be forsaken for thee, and shall rocks be removed out of their place?
verses.textLatin: Qui perdis animam tuam in furore tuo, numquid propter te derelinquetur terra, et transferentur rupes de loco suo?

verses.text: Shall not the light of the wicked be extinguished, and the flame of his fire not shine?
verses.textLatin: Nonne lux impii extinguetur, nec splendebit flamma ignis ejus?

verses.text: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and the lamp that is over him, shall be put out.
verses.textLatin: Lux obtenebrescet in tabernaculo illius, et lucerna quæ super eum est extinguetur.

verses.text: The step of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down headlong.
verses.textLatin: Arctabuntur gressus virtutis ejus, et præcipitabit eum consilium suum.

verses.text: For he hath thrust his feet into a net, and walketh in its meshes.
verses.textLatin: Immisit enim in rete pedes suos, et in maculis ejus ambulat.

verses.text: The sole of his foot shall be held in a snare, and thirst shall burn against him.
verses.textLatin: Tenebitur planta illius laqueo, et exardescet contra eum sitis.

verses.text: A gin is hidden for him in the earth, and his trap upon the path.
verses.textLatin: Abscondita est in terra pedica ejus, et decipula illius super semitam.

verses.text: Fears shall terrify him on every side, and shall entangle his feet.
verses.textLatin: Undique terrebunt eum formidines, et involvent pedes ejus.

verses.text: Let his strength be wasted with famine, and let hunger invade his ribs.
verses.textLatin: Attenuetur fame robur ejus, et inedia invadat costas illius.

verses.text: Let it devour the beauty of his skin, let the firstborn death consume his arms.
verses.textLatin: Devoret pulchritudinem cutis ejus; consumat brachia illius primogenita mors.

verses.text: Let his confidence be rooted out of his tabernacle, and let destruction tread upon him like a king.
verses.textLatin: Avellatur de tabernaculo suo fiducia ejus, et calcet super eum, quasi rex, interitus.

verses.text: Let the companions of him that is not, dwell in his tabernacle, let brimstone be sprinkled in his tent.
verses.textLatin: Habitent in tabernaculo illius socii ejus qui non est; aspergatur in tabernaculo ejus sulphur.

verses.text: Let his roots be dried up beneath, and his harvest destroyed above.
verses.textLatin: Deorsum radices ejus siccentur: sursum autem atteratur messis ejus.

verses.text: Let the memory of him perish from the earth, and let not his name be renowned in the streets.
verses.textLatin: Memoria illius pereat de terra, et non celebretur nomen ejus in plateis.

verses.text: He shall drive him out of light into darkness, and shall remove him out of the world.
verses.textLatin: Expellet eum de luce in tenebras, et de orbe transferet eum.

verses.text: His seed shall not subsist, nor his offspring among his people, nor any remnants in his country.
verses.textLatin: Non erit semen ejus, neque progenies in populo suo, nec ullæ reliquiæ in regionibus ejus.

verses.text: They that come after him shall be astonished at his day, and horror shall fall upon them that went before.
verses.textLatin: In die ejus stupebunt novissimi, et primos invadet horror.

verses.text: These then are the tabernacles of the wicked, and this the place of him that knoweth not God.
verses.textLatin: Hæc sunt ergo tabernacula iniqui, et iste locus ejus qui ignorat Deum.

verses.text: Then  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, dixit:

verses.text: How long do you afflict my soul,and break me in pieces with words?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo affligitis animam meam, et atteritis me sermonibus?

verses.text: Behold, these ten times you confound me, and are not ashamed to oppress me.
verses.textLatin: En decies confunditis me, et non erubescitis opprimentes me.

verses.text: For if I have been ignorant, my ignorance shall be with me.
verses.textLatin: Nempe etsi ignoravi, mecum erit ignorantia mea.

verses.text: But you set yourselves up against me, and reprove me with my reproaches.
verses.textLatin: At vos contra me erigimini, et arguitis me opprobriis meis.

verses.text: At least now understand, that God hath not afflicted me with an equal judgment, and compassed me with his scourges.
verses.textLatin: Saltem nunc intelligite quia Deus non æquo judicio afflixerit me, et flagellis suis me cinxerit.

verses.text: Behold I shall cry suffering violence, and no one will hear: I shall cry aloud, and there is none to judge.
verses.textLatin: Ecce clamabo, vim patiens, et nemo audiet; vociferabor, et non est qui judicet.

verses.text: He hath hedged in my path round about, and I cannot pass, and in my way he hath set darkness.
verses.textLatin: Semitam meam circumsepsit, et transire non possum: et in calle meo tenebras posuit.

verses.text: He hath stripped me of my glory, and hath taken the crown from my head.
verses.textLatin: Spoliavit me gloria mea, et abstulit coronam de capite meo.

verses.text: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am lost, and he hath taken away my hope, as from a tree that is plucked up.
verses.textLatin: Destruxit me undique, et pereo: et quasi evulsæ arbori abstulit spem meam.

verses.text: His wrath is kindled against me, and he hath counted me as his enemy.
verses.textLatin: Iratus est contra me furor ejus, et sic me habuit quasi hostem suum.

verses.text: His troops have come together, and have made themselves a way by me, and have besieged my tabernacle round about.
verses.textLatin: Simul venerunt latrones ejus, et fecerunt sibi viam per me, et obsederunt in gyro tabernaculum meum.

verses.text: He hath put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me.
verses.textLatin: Fratres meos longe fecit a me, et noti mei quasi alieni recesserunt a me.

verses.text: My kinsmen have forsaken me, and they that knew me, have forgotten me.
verses.textLatin: Dereliquerunt me propinqui mei, et qui me noverant obliti sunt mei.

verses.text: They that dwell in my house, and my maidservants have counted me as a stranger, and I have been like an alien in their eyes.
verses.textLatin: Inquilini domus meæ et ancillæ meæ sicut alienum habuerunt me, et quasi peregrinus fui in oculis eorum.

verses.text: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer, I entreated him with my own mouth.
verses.textLatin: Servum meum vocavi, et non respondit: ore proprio deprecabar illum.

verses.text: My wife hath abhorred my breath, and I entreated the children of my womb.
verses.textLatin: Halitum meum exhorruit uxor mea, et orabam filios uteri mei.

verses.text: Even fools despised me, and when I was gone from them, they spoke against me.
verses.textLatin: Stulti quoque despiciebant me: et cum ab eis recessissem, detrahebant mihi.

verses.text: They that were sometime my counsellors, have abhorred me: and he whom I loved most is turned against me.
verses.textLatin: Abominati sunt me quondam consiliarii mei, et quem maxime diligebam, aversatus est me.

verses.text: The flesh being consumed, my bone hath cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth.
verses.textLatin: Pelli meæ, consumptis carnibus, adhæsit os meum, et derelicta sunt tantummodo labia circa dentes meos.

verses.text: Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord hath touched me.
verses.textLatin: Miseremini mei, miseremini mei saltem vos, amici mei, quia manus Domini tetigit me.

verses.text: Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh?
verses.textLatin: Quare persequimini me sicut Deus, et carnibus meis saturamini?

verses.text: Who will grant me that my words may be written? who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi tribuat ut scribantur sermones mei? quis mihi det ut exarentur in libro

verses.text: With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone?
verses.textLatin: stylo ferreo et plumbi lamina, vel celte sculpantur in silice?

verses.text: For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Scio enim quod redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum:

verses.text: And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see my God.
verses.textLatin: et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea videbo Deum meum:

verses.text: Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.
verses.textLatin: quem visurus sum ego ipse, et oculi mei conspecturi sunt, et non alius: reposita est hæc spes mea in sinu meo.

verses.text: Why then do you say now: Let us persecute him, and let us find occasion of word against him?
verses.textLatin: Quare ergo nunc dicitis: Persequamur eum, et radicem verbi inveniamus contra eum?

verses.text: Flee then from the face of the sword, for the sword is the revenger of iniquities: and know ye that there is a judgment.
verses.textLatin: Fugite ergo a facie gladii, quoniam ultor iniquitatum gladius est: et scitote esse judicium.

verses.text: Then  Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Sophar Naamathites, dixit:

verses.text: Therefore various thoughts succeed one another in me, and my mind is hurried away to different things.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, et mens in diversa rapitur.

verses.text: The doctrine with which thou reprovest me, I will hear, and the spirit of my understanding shall answer for me.
verses.textLatin: Doctrinam qua me arguis audiam, et spiritus intelligentiæ meæ respondebit mihi.

verses.text: This I know from the beginning, since man was placed upon the earth,
verses.textLatin: Hoc scio a principio, ex quo positus est homo super terram,

verses.text: That the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment.
verses.textLatin: quod laus impiorum brevis sit, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti.

verses.text: If his pride mount up even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds:
verses.textLatin: Si ascenderit usque ad cælum superbia ejus, et caput ejus nubes tetigerit,

verses.text: In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill, and they that had seen him, shall say: Where is he?
verses.textLatin: quasi sterquilinium in fine perdetur, et qui eum viderant, dicent: Ubi est?

verses.text: As a dream that fleeth away he shall not be found, he shall pass as a vision of the night:
verses.textLatin: Velut somnium avolans non invenietur: transiet sicut visio nocturna.

verses.text: The eyes that had seen him, shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more behold him.
verses.textLatin: Oculus qui eum viderat non videbit, neque ultra intuebitur eum locus suus.

verses.text: His children shall be oppressed with want, and his hands shall render to him his sorrow.
verses.textLatin: Filii ejus atterentur egestate, et manus illius reddent ei dolorem suum.

verses.text: His bones shall be filled with the vices of his youth, and they shall sleep with him in the dust.
verses.textLatin: Ossa ejus implebuntur vitiis adolescentiæ ejus, et cum eo in pulvere dormient.

verses.text: For when evil shall be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
verses.textLatin: Cum enim dulce fuerit in ore ejus malum, abscondet illud sub lingua sua.

verses.text: He will spare it, and not leave it, and will hide it in his throat.
verses.textLatin: Parcet illi, et non derelinquet illud, et celabit in gutture suo.

verses.text: His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of asps within him.
verses.textLatin: Panis ejus in utero illius vertetur in fel aspidum intrinsecus.

verses.text: The riches which he hath swallowed, he shall vomit up, and God shall draw them out of his belly.
verses.textLatin: Divitias quas devoravit evomet, et de ventre illius extrahet eas Deus.

verses.text: He shall suck the head of asps, and the viper’s tongue shall kill him.
verses.textLatin: Caput aspidum suget, et occidet eum lingua viperæ.

verses.text: (Let him not see the streams of the river, the brooks of honey and of butter.)
verses.textLatin: (Non videat rivulos fluminis, torrentes mellis et butyri.)

verses.text: He shall be punished for all that he did, and yet shall not be consumed: according to the multitude of his devices so also shall he suffer.
verses.textLatin: Luet quæ fecit omnia, nec tamen consumetur: juxta multitudinem adinventionum suarum, sic et sustinebit.

verses.text: Because he broke in and stripped the poor: he hath violently taken away a house which he did not build.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam confringens nudavit pauperes: domum rapuit, et non ædificavit eam.

verses.text: And yet his belly was not filled: and when he hath the things he coveted, he shall not be able to possess them.
verses.textLatin: Nec est satiatus venter ejus: et cum habuerit quæ concupierat, possidere non poterit.

verses.text: There was nothing left of his meat, and therefore nothing shall continue of his goods:
verses.textLatin: Non remansit de cibo ejus, et propterea nihil permanebit de bonis ejus.

verses.text: When he shall be filled, he shall be straitened, he shall burn, and every sorrow shall fall upon him.
verses.textLatin: Cum satiatus fuerit, arctabitur: æstuabit, et omnis dolor irruet super eum.

verses.text: May his belly be filled, that God may send forth the wrath of his indignation upon him, and rain down his war upon him.
verses.textLatin: Utinam impleatur venter ejus, ut emittat in eum iram furoris sui, et pluat super illum bellum suum.

verses.text: He shall flee from weapons of iron, and shall fall upon a bow of brass.
verses.textLatin: Fugiet arma ferrea, et irruet in arcum æreum.

verses.text: The sword is drawn out, and cometh forth from its scabbard, and glittereth in his bitterness: the terrible ones shall go and come upon him.
verses.textLatin: Eductus, et egrediens de vagina sua, et fulgurans in amaritudine sua: vadent et venient super eum horribiles.

verses.text: All darkness is hid in his secret places: a fire that is not kindled shall devour him, he shall be afflicted when left in his tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Omnes tenebræ absconditæ sunt in occultis ejus; devorabit eum ignis qui non succenditur: affligetur relictus in tabernaculo suo.

verses.text: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him.
verses.textLatin: Revelabunt cæli iniquitatem ejus, et terra consurget adversus eum.

verses.text: The offspring of his house shall be exposed, he shall be pulled down in the day of God’s wrath.
verses.textLatin: Apertum erit germen domus illius: detrahetur in die furoris Dei.

verses.text: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance of his doings from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est pars hominis impii a Deo, et hæreditas verborum ejus a Domino.

verses.text: Then  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, dixit:

verses.text: Hear, I beseech you, my words, and do penance.
verses.textLatin: Audite, quæso, sermones meos, et agite pœnitentiam.

verses.text: Suffer me, and I will speak, and after, if you please, laugh at my words.
verses.textLatin: Sustinete me, et ego loquar: et post mea, si videbitur, verba, ridete.

verses.text: Is my debate against man, that I should not have just reason to be troubled?
verses.textLatin: Numquid contra hominem disputatio mea est, ut merito non debeam contristari?

verses.text: Hearken to me and be astonished, and lay your finger on your mouth.
verses.textLatin: Attendite me et obstupescite, et superponite digitum ori vestro.

verses.text: As for me, when I remember, I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.
verses.textLatin: Et ego, quando recordatus fuero, pertimesco, et concutit carnem meam tremor.

verses.text: Why then do the wicked live, are they advanced, and strengthened with riches?
verses.textLatin: Quare ergo impii vivunt, sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis?

verses.text: Their seed continueth before them, a multitude of kinsmen, and of children’s children in their sight.
verses.textLatin: Semen eorum permanet coram eis: propinquorum turba et nepotum in conspectu eorum.

verses.text: Their houses are secure and peaceable, and the rod of God is not upon them.
verses.textLatin: Domus eorum securæ sunt et pacatæ, et non est virga Dei super illos.

verses.text: Their cattle have conceived, and failed not: their cow has calved, and is not deprived of her fruit.
verses.textLatin: Bos eorum concepit, et non abortivit: vacca peperit, et non est privata fœtu suo.

verses.text: Their little ones go out like a flock, and their children dance and play.
verses.textLatin: Egrediuntur quasi greges parvuli eorum, et infantes eorum exultant lusibus.

verses.text: They take the timbrel, and the harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
verses.textLatin: Tenent tympanum et citharam, et gaudent ad sonitum organi.

verses.text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell.
verses.textLatin: Ducunt in bonis dies suos, et in puncto ad inferna descendunt.

verses.text: Who have said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
verses.textLatin: Qui dixerunt Deo: Recede a nobis, et scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus.

verses.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what doth it profit us if we pray to him?
verses.textLatin: Quis est Omnipotens, ut serviamus ei? et quid nobis prodest si oraverimus illum?

verses.text: Yet because their good things are not in their hand, may the counsel of the wicked be far from me.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen quia non sunt in manu eorum bona sua, consilium impiorum longe sit a me.

verses.text: How often shall the lamp of the wicked be put out, and a deluge come upon them, and he shall distribute the sorrows of his wrath?
verses.textLatin: Quoties lucerna impiorum extinguetur, et superveniet eis inundatio, et dolores dividet furoris sui?

verses.text: They shall be as chaff before the face of the wind, and as ashes which the whirlwind scattereth.
verses.textLatin: Erunt sicut paleæ ante faciem venti, et sicut favilla quam turbo dispergit.

verses.text: God shall lay up the sorrow of the father for his children: and when he shall repay, then shall he know.
verses.textLatin: Deus servabit filiis illius dolorem patris, et cum reddiderit, tunc sciet.

verses.text: His eyes shall see his own destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt oculi ejus interfectionem suam, et de furore Omnipotentis bibet.

verses.text: For what is it to him what befalleth his house after him: and if the number of his months be diminished by one half?
verses.textLatin: Quid enim ad eum pertinet de domo sua post se, et si numerus mensium ejus dimidietur?

verses.text: Shall any one teach God knowledge, who judgeth those that are high?
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deus docebit quispiam scientiam, qui excelsos judicat?

verses.text: One man dieth strong, and hale, rich and happy.
verses.textLatin: Iste moritur robustus et sanus, dives et felix:

verses.text: His bowels are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
verses.textLatin: viscera ejus plena sunt adipe, et medullis ossa illius irrigantur:

verses.text: But another dieth in bitterness of soul without any riches:
verses.textLatin: alius vero moritur in amaritudine animæ absque ullis opibus:

verses.text: And yet they shall sleep together in the dust, and worms shall cover them.
verses.textLatin: et tamen simul in pulvere dormient, et vermes operient eos.

verses.text: Surely I know your thoughts, and your unjust judgments against me.
verses.textLatin: Certe novi cogitationes vestras, et sententias contra me iniquas.

verses.text: For you say: Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?
verses.textLatin: Dicitis enim: Ubi est domus principis? et ubi tabernacula impiorum?

verses.text: Ask any one of them that go by the way, and you shall perceive that he knoweth these same things.
verses.textLatin: Interrogate quemlibet de viatoribus, et hæc eadem illum intelligere cognoscetis:

verses.text: Because the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath.
verses.textLatin: quia in diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur.

verses.text: Who shall reprove his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?
verses.textLatin: Quis arguet coram eo viam ejus? et quæ fecit, quis reddet illi?

verses.text: He shall be brought to the graves, and shall watch in the heap of the dead.
verses.textLatin: Ipse ad sepulchra ducetur, et in congerie mortuorum vigilabit.

verses.text: He hath been acceptable to the gravel of Cocytus, and he shall draw every man after him, and there are innumerable before him.
verses.textLatin: Dulcis fuit glareis Cocyti, et post se omnem hominem trahet, et ante se innumerabiles.

verses.text: How then do ye comfort me in vain, whereas your answer is shewn to be repugnant to truth?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo igitur consolamini me frustra, cum responsio vestra repugnare ostensa sit veritati?

verses.text: Then  Eliphaz the Themanite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Eliphaz Themanites, dixit:

verses.text: Can man be compared with God, even though he were of perfect knowledge?
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deo potest comparari homo, etiam cum perfectæ fuerit scientiæ?

verses.text: What doth it profit God if thou be just? or what dost thou give him if thy way be unspotted?
verses.textLatin: Quid prodest Deo, si justus fueris? aut quid ei confers, si immaculata fuerit via tua?

verses.text: Shall he reprove thee for fear, and come with thee into judgment:
verses.textLatin: Numquid timens arguet te, et veniet tecum in judicium,

verses.text: And not for thy manifold wickedness, and thy infinite iniquities?
verses.textLatin: et non propter malitiam tuam plurimam, et infinitas iniquitates tuas?

verses.text: For thou hast taken away the pledge of thy brethren without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
verses.textLatin: Abstulisti enim pignus fratrum tuorum sine causa, et nudos spoliasti vestibus.

verses.text: Thou hast not given water to the weary, thou hast withdrawn bread from the hungry.
verses.textLatin: Aquam lasso non dedisti, et esurienti subtraxisti panem.

verses.text: In the strength of thy arm thou didst possess the land, and being the most mighty thou holdest it.
verses.textLatin: In fortitudine brachii tui possidebas terram, et potentissimus obtinebas eam.

verses.text: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless thou hast broken in pieces.
verses.textLatin: Viduas dimisisti vacuas, et lacertos pupillorum comminuisti.

verses.text: Therefore art thou surrounded with snares, and sudden fear troubleth thee.
verses.textLatin: Propterea circumdatus es laqueis, et conturbat te formido subita.

verses.text: And didst thou think that thou shouldst not see darkness, and that thou shouldst not be covered with the violence of overflowing waters?
verses.textLatin: Et putabas te tenebras non visurum, et impetu aquarum inundantium non oppressum iri?

verses.text: Dost not thou think that God is higher than heaven, and is elevated above the height of the stars?
verses.textLatin: an non cogitas quod Deus excelsior cælo sit, et super stellarum verticem sublimetur?

verses.text: And thou sayst: What doth God know? and he judgeth as it were through a mist.
verses.textLatin: Et dicis: Quid enim novit Deus? et quasi per caliginem judicat.

verses.text: The clouds are his covert, and he doth not consider our things, and he walketh about the poles of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Nubes latibulum ejus, nec nostra considerat, et circa cardines cæli perambulat.

verses.text: Dost thou desire to keep the path of ages, which wicked men have trodden?
verses.textLatin: Numquid semitam sæculorum custodire cupis, quam calcaverunt viri iniqui,

verses.text: Who were taken away before their time, and a flood hath overthrown their foundation.
verses.textLatin: qui sublati sunt ante tempus suum, et fluvius subvertit fundamentum eorum?

verses.text: Who said to God: Depart from us: and looked upon the Almighty as if he could do nothing:
verses.textLatin: Qui dicebant Deo: Recede a nobis: et quasi nihil posset facere Omnipotens, æstimabant eum,

verses.text: Whereas he had filled their houses with good things: whose way of thinking be far from me.
verses.textLatin: cum ille implesset domos eorum bonis: quorum sententia procul sit a me.

verses.text: The just shall see, and shall rejoice, and the innocent shall laugh them to scorn.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt justi, et lætabuntur, et innocens subsannabit eos:

verses.text: Is not their exaltation cut down, and hath not fire devoured the remnants of them?
verses.textLatin: nonne succisa est erectio eorum? et reliquias eorum devoravit ignis?

verses.text: Submit thyself then to him, and be at peace: and thereby thou shalt have the best fruits.
verses.textLatin: Acquiesce igitur ei, et habeto pacem, et per hæc habebis fructus optimos.

verses.text: Receive the law of his mouth, and lay up his words in thy heart.
verses.textLatin: Suscipe ex ore illius legem, et pone sermones ejus in corde tuo.

verses.text: If thou wilt return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, and shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Si reversus fueris ad Omnipotentem, ædificaberis, et longe facies iniquitatem a tabernaculo tuo.

verses.text: He shall give for earth flint, and for flint torrents of gold.
verses.textLatin: Dabit pro terra silicem, et pro silice torrentes aureos.

verses.text: And the Almighty shall be against thy enemies, and silver shall be heaped together for thee.
verses.textLatin: Eritque Omnipotens contra hostes tuos, et argentum coacervabitur tibi.

verses.text: Then shalt thou abound in delights in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face to God.
verses.textLatin: Tunc super Omnipotentem deliciis afflues, et elevabis ad Deum faciem tuam.

verses.text: Thou shalt pray to him, and he will hear thee, and thou shalt pay vows.
verses.textLatin: Rogabis eum, et exaudiet te, et vota tua reddes.

verses.text: Thou shalt decree a thing, and it shall come to thee, and light shall shine in thy ways.
verses.textLatin: Decernes rem, et veniet tibi, et in viis tuis splendebit lumen.

verses.text: For he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory: and he that shall bow down his eyes, he shall be saved.
verses.textLatin: Qui enim humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria, et qui inclinaverit oculos, ipse salvabitur.

verses.text: The innocent shall be saved, and he shall be saved by the cleanness of his hands.
verses.textLatin: Salvabitur innocens: salvabitur autem in munditia manuum suarum.

verses.text: Then  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job, ait:

verses.text: Now also my words are in bitterness, and the hand of my scourge is more grievous than my mourning.
verses.textLatin: Nunc quoque in amaritudine est sermo meus, et manus plagæ meæ aggravata est super gemitum meum.

verses.text: Who will grant me that I might know and find him, and come even to his throne?
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi tribuat ut cognoscam et inveniam illum, et veniam usque ad solium ejus?

verses.text: I would set judgment before him, and would fill my mouth with complaints.
verses.textLatin: Ponam coram eo judicium, et os meum replebo increpationibus:

verses.text: That I might know the words that he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.
verses.textLatin: ut sciam verba quæ mihi respondeat, et intelligam quid loquatur mihi.

verses.text: I would not that he should contend with me with much strength, nor overwhelm me with the weight of his greatness.
verses.textLatin: Nolo multa fortitudine contendat mecum, nec magnitudinis suæ mole me premat.

verses.text: Let him propose equity against me, and let my judgment come to victory.
verses.textLatin: Proponat æquitatem contra me, et perveniat ad victoriam judicium meum.

verses.text: But if I go to the east, he appeareth not; if to the west, I shall not understand him.
verses.textLatin: Si ad orientem iero, non apparet; si ad occidentem, non intelligam eum.

verses.text: If to the left hand, what shall I do? I shall not take hold on him: if I turn myself to the right hand, I shall not see him.
verses.textLatin: Si ad sinistram, quid agam? non apprehendam eum; si me vertam ad dexteram, non videbo illum.

verses.text: But he knoweth my way, and has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire:
verses.textLatin: Ipse vero scit viam meam, et probavit me quasi aurum quod per ignem transit.

verses.text: My foot hath followed his steps, I have kept his way, and have not declined from it.
verses.textLatin: Vestigia ejus secutus est pes meus: viam ejus custodivi, et non declinavi ex ea.

verses.text: I have not departed from the commandments of his lips, and the words of his mouth I have hid in my bosom.
verses.textLatin: A mandatis labiorum ejus non recessi, et in sinu meo abscondi verba oris ejus.

verses.text: For he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought: and whatsoever his soul hath desired, that hath he done.
verses.textLatin: Ipse enim solus est, et nemo avertere potest cogitationem ejus: et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, hoc fecit.

verses.text: And when he shall have fulfilled his will in me, many other like things are also at hand with him.
verses.textLatin: Cum expleverit in me voluntatem suam, et alia multa similia præsto sunt ei.

verses.text: And therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him I am made pensive with fear.
verses.textLatin: Et idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum, et considerans eum, timore sollicitor.

verses.text: God hath softened my heart, and the Almighty hath troubled me.
verses.textLatin: Deus mollivit cor meum, et Omnipotens conturbavit me.

verses.text: For I have not perished because of the darkness that hangs over me, neither hath the mist covered my face.
verses.textLatin: Non enim perii propter imminentes tenebras, nec faciem meam operuit caligo.

verses.text: Times  are not hid from the Almighty: but they that know him, know not his days.
verses.textLatin: Ab Omnipotente non sunt abscondita tempora: qui autem noverunt eum, ignorant dies illius.

verses.text: Some have removed landmarks, have taken away flocks by force, and fed them.
verses.textLatin: Alii terminos transtulerunt; diripuerunt greges, et paverunt eos.

verses.text: They have driven away the ass of the fatherless, and have taken away the widow’s ox for a pledge.
verses.textLatin: Asinum pupillorum abegerunt, et abstulerunt pro pignore bovem viduæ.

verses.text: They have overturned the way of the poor, and have oppressed together the meek of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Subverterunt pauperum viam, et oppresserunt pariter mansuetos terræ.

verses.text: Others like wild asses in the desert go forth to their work: by watching for a prey they get bread for their children.
verses.textLatin: Alii quasi onagri in deserto egrediuntur ad opus suum: vigilantes ad prædam, præparant panem liberis.

verses.text: They reap the field that is not their own, and gather the vintage of his vineyard whom by violence they have oppressed.
verses.textLatin: Agrum non suum demetunt, et vineam ejus, quem vi oppresserint, vindemiant.

verses.text: They send men away naked, taking away their clothes who have no covering in the cold:
verses.textLatin: Nudos dimittunt homines, indumenta tollentes, quibus non est operimentum in frigore:

verses.text: Who are wet, with the showers of the mountains, and having no covering embrace the stones.
verses.textLatin: quos imbres montium rigant, et non habentes velamen, amplexantur lapides.

verses.text: They have violently robbed the fatherless, and stripped the poor common people.
verses.textLatin: Vim fecerunt deprædantes pupillos, et vulgum pauperem spoliaverunt.

verses.text: From the naked and them that go without clothing, and from the hungry they have taken away the ears of corn.
verses.textLatin: Nudis et incedentibus absque vestitu, et esurientibus tulerunt spicas.

verses.text: They have taken their rest at noon among the stores of them, who after having trodden the winepresses suffer thirst.
verses.textLatin: Inter acervos eorum meridiati sunt, qui calcatis torcularibus sitiunt.

verses.text: Out of the cities they have made men to groan, and the soul of the wounded hath cried out, and God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged.
verses.textLatin: De civitatibus fecerunt viros gemere, et anima vulneratorum clamavit: et Deus inultum abire non patitur.

verses.text: They have been rebellious to the light, they have not known his ways, neither have they returned by his paths.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini: nescierunt vias ejus, nec reversi sunt per semitas ejus.

verses.text: The murderer riseth at the very break of day, he killeth the needy, and the poor man: but in the night he will be as a thief.
verses.textLatin: Mane primo consurgit homicida; interficit egenum et pauperem: per noctem vero erit quasi fur.

verses.text: The eye of the adulterer observeth darkness, saying: No eye shall see me: and he will cover his face.
verses.textLatin: Oculus adulteri observat caliginem, dicens: Non me videbit oculus: et operiet vultum suum.

verses.text: He diggeth through houses in the dark, as in the day they had appointed for themselves, and they have not known the light.
verses.textLatin: Perfodit in tenebris domos, sicut in die condixerant sibi, et ignoraverunt lucem.

verses.text: If the morning suddenly appear, it is to them the shadow of death: and they walk in darkness as if it were in light.
verses.textLatin: Si subito apparuerit aurora, arbitrantur umbram mortis: et sic in tenebris quasi in luce ambulant.

verses.text: He is light upon the face of the water: cursed be his portion on the earth, let him not walk by the way of the vineyards.
verses.textLatin: Levis est super faciem aquæ: maledicta sit pars ejus in terra, nec ambulet per viam vinearum.

verses.text: Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat, and his sin even to hell.
verses.textLatin: Ad nimium calorem transeat ab aquis nivium, et usque ad inferos peccatum illius.

verses.text: Let mercy forget him: may worms be his sweetness: let him be remembered no more, but be broken in pieces as an unfruitful tree.
verses.textLatin: Obliviscatur ejus misericordia; dulcedo illius vermes: non sit in recordatione, sed conteratur quasi lignum infructuosum.

verses.text: For he hath fed the barren that beareth not, and to the widow he hath done no good.
verses.textLatin: Pavit enim sterilem quæ non parit, et viduæ bene non fecit.

verses.text: He hath pulled down the strong by his might: and when he standeth up, he shall not trust to his life.
verses.textLatin: Detraxit fortes in fortitudine sua, et cum steterit, non credet vitæ suæ.

verses.text: God hath given him place for penance, and he abuseth it unto pride: but his eyes are upon his ways.
verses.textLatin: Dedit ei Deus locum pœnitentiæ, et ille abutitur eo in superbiam: oculi autem ejus sunt in viis illius.

verses.text: They are lifted up for a little while and shall not stand, and shall be brought down as all things, and shall be taken away, and as the tops of the ears of corn they shall be broken.
verses.textLatin: Elevati sunt ad modicum, et non subsistent: et humiliabuntur sicut omnia, et auferentur, et sicut summitates spicarum conterentur.

verses.text: And if it be not so, who can convince me that I have lied, and set my words before God?
verses.textLatin: Quod si non est ita, quis me potest arguere esse mentitum, et ponere ante Deum verba mea?

verses.text: Then  Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Baldad Suhites, dixit:

verses.text: Power and terror are with him, who maketh peace in his high places.
verses.textLatin: Potestas et terror apud eum est, qui facit concordiam in sublimibus suis.

verses.text: Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?
verses.textLatin: Numquid est numerus militum ejus? et super quem non surget lumen illius?

verses.text: Can men be justified compared with God, or he that is born of a women appear clean?
verses.textLatin: Numquid justificari potest homo comparatus Deo? aut apparere mundus natus de muliere?

verses.text: Behold even the moon doth not shine, and the stars are not pure in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Ecce luna etiam non splendet, et stellæ non sunt mundæ in conspectu ejus:

verses.text: How much less man that is rottenness and the son of man who is a worm?
verses.textLatin: quanto magis homo putredo, et filius hominis vermis?

verses.text: Then  Job answered, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job dixit:

verses.text: Whose helper art thou? is it of him that is weak? and dost thou hold up the arm of him that has no strength?
verses.textLatin: Cujus adjutor es? numquid imbecillis? et sustentas brachium ejus qui non est fortis?

verses.text: To whom hast thou given counsel? perhaps to him that hath no wisdom, and thou hast shewn thy very great prudence.
verses.textLatin: Cui dedisti consilium? forsitan illi qui non habet sapientiam: et prudentiam tuam ostendisti plurimam.

verses.text: Whom hast thou desired to teach? was it not him that made life?
verses.textLatin: Quem docere voluisti? nonne eum qui fecit spiramentum?

verses.text: Behold the giants groan under the waters, and they that dwell with them.
verses.textLatin: Ecce gigantes gemunt sub aquis, et qui habitant cum eis.

verses.text: Hell is naked before him, and there is no covering for destruction.
verses.textLatin: Nudus est infernus coram illo, et nullum est operimentum perditioni.

verses.text: He stretched out the north over the empty space, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.
verses.textLatin: Qui extendit aquilonem super vacuum, et appendit terram super nihilum.

verses.text: He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together.
verses.textLatin: Qui ligat aquas in nubibus suis, ut non erumpant pariter deorsum.

verses.text: He withholdeth the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud over it.
verses.textLatin: Qui tenet vultum solii sui, et expandit super illud nebulam suam.

verses.text: He hath set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end.
verses.textLatin: Terminum circumdedit aquis, usque dum finiantur lux et tenebræ.

verses.text: The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck.
verses.textLatin: Columnæ cæli contremiscunt, et pavent ad nutum ejus.

verses.text: By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together, and his wisdom has struck the proud one.
verses.textLatin: In fortitudine illius repente maria congregata sunt, et prudentia ejus percussit superbum.

verses.text: His spirit hath adorned the heavens, and his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus ejus ornavit cælos, et obstetricante manu ejus, eductus est coluber tortuosus.

verses.text: Lo, these things are said in part of his ways: and seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?
verses.textLatin: Ecce hæc ex parte dicta sunt viarum ejus: et cum vix parvam stillam sermonis ejus audierimus, quis poterit tonitruum magnitudinis illius intueri?

verses.text: Job  also added, taking up his parable, and said:
verses.textLatin: Addidit quoque Job, assumens parabolam suam, et dixit:

verses.text: As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment, and the Almighty, who hath brought my soul to bitterness,
verses.textLatin: Vivit Deus, qui abstulit judicium meum, et Omnipotens, qui ad amaritudinem adduxit animam meam.

verses.text: As long as breath remaineth in me, and the spirit of God in my nostrils,
verses.textLatin: Quia donec superest halitus in me, et spiritus Dei in naribus meis,

verses.text: My lips shall not speak iniquity, neither shall my tongue contrive lying.
verses.textLatin: non loquentur labia mea iniquitatem, nec lingua mea meditabitur mendacium.

verses.text: God forbid that I should judge you to be just: till I die I will not depart from my innocence.
verses.textLatin: Absit a me ut justos vos esse judicem: donec deficiam, non recedam ab innocentia mea.

verses.text: My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake: for my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life.
verses.textLatin: Justificationem meam, quam cœpi tenere, non deseram: neque enim reprehendit me cor meum in omni vita mea.

verses.text: Let my enemy be as the ungodly, and my adversary as the wicked one.
verses.textLatin: Sit ut impius, inimicus meus, et adversarius meus quasi iniquus.

verses.text: For what is the hope of the hypocrite if through covetousness he take by violence, and God deliver not his soul?
verses.textLatin: Quæ est enim spes hypocritæ, si avare rapiat, et non liberet Deus animam ejus?

verses.text: Will God hear his cry, when distress shall come upon him?
verses.textLatin: Numquid Deus audiet clamorem ejus, cum venerit super eum angustia?

verses.text: Or can he delight himself in the Almighty, and call upon God at all times?
verses.textLatin: aut poterit in Omnipotente delectari, et invocare Deum omni tempore?

verses.text: I will teach you by the hand of God, what the Almighty hath, and I will not conceal it.
verses.textLatin: Docebo vos per manum Dei quæ Omnipotens habeat, nec abscondam.

verses.text: Behold you all know it, and why do you speak vain things without cause?
verses.textLatin: Ecce vos omnes nostis: et quid sine causa vana loquimini?

verses.text: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they shall receive of the Almighty.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est pars hominis impii apud Deum, et hæreditas violentorum, quam ob Omnipotente suscipient.

verses.text: If his sons be multiplied, they shall be for the sword, and his grandsons shall not be filled with bread.
verses.textLatin: Si multiplicati fuerint filii ejus, in gladio erunt, et nepotes ejus non saturabuntur pane:

verses.text: They that shall remain of him, shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not weep.
verses.textLatin: qui reliqui fuerint ex eo sepelientur in interitu, et viduæ illius non plorabunt.

verses.text: If he shall heap together silver as earth, and prepare raiment as clay,
verses.textLatin: Si comportaverit quasi terram argentum, et sicut lutum præparaverit vestimenta:

verses.text: He shall prepare indeed, but the just man shall be clothed with it: and the innocent shall divide the silver.
verses.textLatin: præparabit quidem, sed justus vestietur illis, et argentum innocens dividet.

verses.text: He hath built his house as a moth, and as a keeper he hath made a booth.
verses.textLatin: Ædificavit sicut tinea domum suam, et sicut custos fecit umbraculum.

verses.text: The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him: he shall open his eyes and find nothing.
verses.textLatin: Dives, cum dormierit, nihil secum auferet: aperiet oculos suos, et nihil inveniet.

verses.text: Poverty like water shall take hold on him, a tempest shall oppress him in the night:
verses.textLatin: Apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia: nocte opprimet eum tempestas.

verses.text: A burning wind shall take him up, and carry him away, and as a whirlwind shall snatch him from his place.
verses.textLatin: Tollet eum ventus urens, et auferet, et velut turbo rapiet eum de loco suo.

verses.text: And he shall cast upon him, and shall not spare: out of his hand he would willingly flee.
verses.textLatin: Et mittet super eum, et non parcet: de manu ejus fugiens fugiet.

verses.text: He shall clasp his hands upon him, and shall hiss at him, beholding his place.
verses.textLatin: Stringet super eum manus suas, et sibilabit super illum, intuens locum ejus.

verses.text: Silver  hath beginnings of its veins, and gold hath a place wherein it is melted.
verses.textLatin: Habet argentum venarum suarum principia, et auro locus est in quo conflatur.

verses.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and stone melted with heat is turned into brass.
verses.textLatin: Ferrum de terra tollitur, et lapis solutus calore in æs vertitur.

verses.text: He hath set a time for darkness, and the end of all things he considereth, the stone also that is in the dark and the shadow of death.
verses.textLatin: Tempus posuit tenebris, et universorum finem ipse considerat: lapidem quoque caliginis et umbram mortis.

verses.text: The flood divideth from the people that are on their journey, those whom the food of the needy man hath forgotten, and who cannot be come at.
verses.textLatin: Dividit torrens a populo peregrinante eos quos oblitus est pes egentis hominis, et invios.

verses.text: The land, out of which bread grew in its place, hath been overturned with fire.
verses.textLatin: Terra de qua oriebatur panis, in loco suo igni subversa est.

verses.text: The stones of it are the place of sapphires, and the clods of it are gold.
verses.textLatin: Locus sapphiri lapides ejus, et glebæ illius aurum.

verses.text: The bird hath not known the path, neither hath the eye of the vulture beheld it.
verses.textLatin: Semitam ignoravit avis, nec intuitus est eam oculus vulturis.

verses.text: The children of the merchants have not trodden it, neither hath the lioness passed by it.
verses.textLatin: Non calcaverunt eam filii institorum, nec pertransivit per eam leæna.

verses.text: He hath stretched forth his hand to the flint, he hath overturned mountains from the roots.
verses.textLatin: Ad silicem extendit manum suam: subvertit a radicibus montes.

verses.text: In the rocks he hath cut out rivers, and his eye hath seen every precious thing.
verses.textLatin: In petris rivos excidit, et omne pretiosum vidit oculus ejus.

verses.text: The depths also of rivers he hath searched, and hidden things he hath brought forth to light.
verses.textLatin: Profunda quoque fluviorum scrutatus est, et abscondita in lucem produxit.

verses.text: But where is wisdom to be found, and where is the place of understanding?
verses.textLatin: Sapientia vero ubi invenitur? et quis est locus intelligentiæ?

verses.text: Man knoweth not the price thereof, neither is it found in the land of them that live in delights.
verses.textLatin: Nescit homo pretium ejus, nec invenitur in terra suaviter viventium.

verses.text: The depth saith: It is not in me: and the sea saith: It is not with me.
verses.textLatin: Abyssus dicit: Non est in me, et mare loquitur: Non est mecum.

verses.text: The finest gold shall not purchase it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it.
verses.textLatin: Non dabitur aurum obrizum pro ea, nec appendetur argentum in commutatione ejus.

verses.text: It shall not be compared with the dyed colours of India, or with the most precious stone sardonyx, or the sapphire.
verses.textLatin: Non conferetur tinctis Indiæ coloribus, nec lapidi sardonycho pretiosissimo vel sapphiro.

verses.text: Gold or crystal cannot equal it, neither shall any vessels of gold be changed for it.
verses.textLatin: Non adæquabitur ei aurum vel vitrum, nec commutabuntur pro ea vasa auri.

verses.text: High and eminent things shall not be mentioned in comparison of it: but wisdom is drawn out of secret places.
verses.textLatin: Excelsa et eminentia non memorabuntur comparatione ejus: trahitur autem sapientia de occultis.

verses.text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equal to it, neither shall it be compared to the cleanest dyeing.
verses.textLatin: Non adæquabitur ei topazius de Æthiopia, nec tincturæ mundissimæ componetur.

verses.text: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?
verses.textLatin: Unde ergo sapientia venit? et quis est locus intelligentiæ?

verses.text: It is hid from the eyes of all living, and the fowls of the air know it not.
verses.textLatin: Abscondita est ab oculis omnium viventium: volucres quoque cæli latet.

verses.text: Destruction and death have said: With our ears we have heard the fame thereof.
verses.textLatin: Perditio et mors dixerunt: Auribus nostris audivimus famam ejus.

verses.text: God understandeth the way of it, and he knoweth the place thereof.
verses.textLatin: Deus intelligit viam ejus, et ipse novit locum illius.

verses.text: For he beholdeth the ends of the world: and looketh on all things that are under heaven.
verses.textLatin: Ipse enim fines mundi intuetur, et omnia quæ sub cælo sunt respicit.

verses.text: Who made a weight for the winds, and weighed the waters by measure.
verses.textLatin: Qui fecit ventis pondus, et aquas appendit in mensura.

verses.text: When he gave a law for the rain, and a way for the sounding storms.
verses.textLatin: Quando ponebat pluviis legem, et viam procellis sonantibus:

verses.text: Then he saw it, and declared, and prepared, and searched it.
verses.textLatin: tunc vidit illam et enarravit, et præparavit, et investigavit.

verses.text: And he said to man: Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom: and to depart from evil, is understanding.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit homini: Ecce timor Domini, ipsa est sapientia; et recedere a malo, intelligentia.

verses.text: Job  also added, taking up his parable, and said:
verses.textLatin: Addidit quoque Job, assumens parabolam suam, et dixit:

verses.text: Who will grant me, that I might be according to the months past, according to the days in which God kept me?
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi tribuat ut sim juxta menses pristinos, secundum dies quibus Deus custodiebat me?

verses.text: When his lamp shined over my head, and I walked by his light in darkness?
verses.textLatin: Quando splendebat lucerna ejus super caput meum, et ad lumen ejus ambulabam in tenebris:

verses.text: As I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly in my tabernacle?
verses.textLatin: sicut fui in diebus adolescentiæ meæ, quando secreto Deus erat in tabernaculo meo:

verses.text: When the Almighty was with me: and my servants round about me?
verses.textLatin: quando erat Omnipotens mecum, et in circuitu meo pueri mei:

verses.text: When I washed my feet with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil?
verses.textLatin: quando lavabam pedes meos butyro, et petra fundebat mihi rivos olei:

verses.text: When I went out to the gate of the city, and in the street they prepared me a chair?
verses.textLatin: quando procedebam ad portam civitatis, et in platea parabant cathedram mihi.

verses.text: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the old men rose up and stood.
verses.textLatin: Videbant me juvenes, et abscondebantur: et senes assurgentes stabant.

verses.text: The princes ceased to speak, and laid the finger on their mouth.
verses.textLatin: Principes cessabant loqui, et digitum superponebant ori suo.

verses.text: The rulers held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to their throat.
verses.textLatin: Vocem suam cohibebant duces, et lingua eorum gutturi suo adhærebat.

verses.text: The ear that heard me blessed me, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me:
verses.textLatin: Auris audiens beatificabat me, et oculus videns testimonium reddebat mihi:

verses.text: Because I had delivered the poor man that cried out; and the fatherless, that had no helper.
verses.textLatin: eo quod liberassem pauperem vociferantem, et pupillum cui non esset adjutor.

verses.text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio perituri super me veniebat, et cor viduæ consolatus sum.

verses.text: I was clad with justice: and I clothed myself with my judgment, as with a robe and a diadem.
verses.textLatin: Justitia indutus sum, et vestivi me, sicut vestimento et diademate, judicio meo.

verses.text: I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame.
verses.textLatin: Oculus fui cæco, et pes claudo.

verses.text: I was the father of the poor: and the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently.
verses.textLatin: Pater eram pauperum, et causam quam nesciebam diligentissime investigabam.

verses.text: I broke the jaws of the wicked man, and out of his teeth I took away the prey.
verses.textLatin: Conterebam molas iniqui, et de dentibus illius auferebam prædam.

verses.text: And I said: I shall die in my nest, and as a palm tree shall multiply my days.
verses.textLatin: Dicebamque: In nidulo meo moriar, et sicut palma multiplicabo dies.

verses.text: My root is opened beside the waters, and dew shall continue in my harvest.
verses.textLatin: Radix mea aperta est secus aquas, et ros morabitur in messione mea.

verses.text: My glory shall always be renewed, and my bow in my hand shall be repaired.
verses.textLatin: Gloria mea semper innovabitur, et arcus meus in manu mea instaurabitur.

verses.text: They that heard me, waited for my sentence, and being attentive held their peace at my counsel.
verses.textLatin: Qui me audiebant, expectabant sententiam, et intenti tacebant ad consilium meum.

verses.text: To my words they durst add nothing, and my speech dropped upon them.
verses.textLatin: Verbis meis addere nihil audebant, et super illos stillabat eloquium meum.

verses.text: They waited for me as for rain, and they opened their mouth as for a latter shower.
verses.textLatin: Expectabant me sicut pluviam, et os suum aperiebant quasi ad imbrem serotinum.

verses.text: If at any time I laughed on them, they believed not, and the light of my countenance fell not on earth.
verses.textLatin: Siquando ridebam ad eos, non credebant: et lux vultus mei non cadebat in terram.

verses.text: If I had a mind to go to them, I sat first, and when I sat as a king, with his army standing about him, yet I was a comforter of them that mourned.
verses.textLatin: Si voluissem ire ad eos, sedebam primus: cumque sederem quasi rex, circumstante exercitu, eram tamen mœrentium consolator.

verses.text: But now the younger in time scorn me, whose fathers I would not have set with the dogs of my flock:
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem derident me juniores tempore, quorum non dignabar patres ponere cum canibus gregis mei:

verses.text: The strength of whose hands was to me as nothing, and they were thought unworthy of life itself.
verses.textLatin: quorum virtus manuum mihi erat pro nihilo, et vita ipsa putabantur indigni:

verses.text: Barren with want and hunger, who gnawed in the wilderness, disfigured with calamity and misery.
verses.textLatin: egestate et fame steriles, qui rodebant in solitudine, squallentes calamitate et miseria.

verses.text: And they ate grass, and barks of trees, and the root of junipers was their food.
verses.textLatin: Et mandebant herbas, et arborum cortices, et radix juniperorum erat cibus eorum:

verses.text: Who snatched up these things out of the valleys, and when they had found any of them, they ran to them with a cry.
verses.textLatin: qui de convallibus ista rapientes, cum singula reperissent, ad ea cum clamore currebant.

verses.text: They dwelt in the desert places of torrents, and in caves of earth, or upon the gravel.
verses.textLatin: In desertis habitabant torrentium, et in cavernis terræ, vel super glaream:

verses.text: They pleased themselves among these kind of things, and counted it delightful to be under the briers.
verses.textLatin: qui inter hujuscemodi lætabantur, et esse sub sentibus delicias computabant:

verses.text: The children of foolish and base men, and not appearing at all upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: filii stultorum et ignobilium, et in terra penitus non parentes.

verses.text: Now I am turned into their song, and am become their byword.
verses.textLatin: Nunc in eorum canticum versus sum, et factus sum eis in proverbium.

verses.text: They abhor me, and flee far from me, and are not afraid to spit in my face.
verses.textLatin: Abominantur me, et longe fugiunt a me, et faciem meam conspuere non verentur.

verses.text: For he hath opened his quiver, and hath afflicted me, and hath put a bridle into my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Pharetram enim suam aperuit, et afflixit me, et frenum posuit in os meum.

verses.text: At the right hand of my rising, my calamities forthwith arose: they have overthrown my feet, and have overwhelmed me with their paths as with waves.
verses.textLatin: Ad dexteram orientis calamitates meæ illico surrexerunt: pedes meos subverterunt, et oppresserunt quasi fluctibus semitis suis.

verses.text: They have destroyed my ways, they have lain in wait against me, and they have prevailed, and there was none to help.
verses.textLatin: Dissipaverunt itinera mea; insidiati sunt mihi, et prævaluerunt: et non fuit qui ferret auxilium.

verses.text: They have rushed in upon me, as when a wall is broken, and a gate opened, and have rolled themselves down to my miseries.
verses.textLatin: Quasi rupto muro, et aperta janua, irruerunt super me, et ad meas miserias devoluti sunt.

verses.text: I am brought to nothing: as a wind thou hast taken away my desire: and my prosperity hath passed away like a cloud.
verses.textLatin: Redactus sum in nihilum: abstulisti quasi ventus desiderium meum, et velut nubes pertransiit salus mea.

verses.text: And now my soul fadeth within myself, and the days of affliction possess me.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem in memetipso marcescit anima mea, et possident me dies afflictionis.

verses.text: In the night my bone is pierced with sorrows: and they that feed upon me, do not sleep.
verses.textLatin: Nocte os meum perforatur doloribus, et qui me comedunt, non dormiunt.

verses.text: With the multitude of them my garment is consumed, and they have girded me about, as with the collar of my coat.
verses.textLatin: In multitudine eorum consumitur vestimentum meum, et quasi capitio tunicæ succinxerunt me.

verses.text: I am compared to dirt, and am likened to embers and ashes.
verses.textLatin: Comparatus sum luto, et assimilatus sum favillæ et cineri.

verses.text: I cry to thee, and thou hearest me not: I stand up, and thou dost not regard me.
verses.textLatin: Clamo ad te, et non exaudis me: sto, et non respicis me.

verses.text: Thou art changed to be cruel toward me, and in the hardness of thy hand thou art against me.
verses.textLatin: Mutatus es mihi in crudelem, et in duritia manus tuæ adversaris mihi.

verses.text: Thou hast lifted me up, and set me as it were upon the wind, and thou hast mightily dashed me.
verses.textLatin: Elevasti me, et quasi super ventum ponens; elisisti me valide.

verses.text: I know that thou wilt deliver me to death, where a house is appointed for every one that liveth.
verses.textLatin: Scio quia morti trades me, ubi constituta est domus omni viventi.

verses.text: But yet thou stretchest not forth thy hand to their consumption: and if they shall fall down thou wilt save.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen non ad consumptionem eorum emittis manum tuam: et si corruerint, ipse salvabis.

verses.text: I wept heretofore for him that was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor.
verses.textLatin: Flebam quondam super eo qui afflictus erat, et compatiebatur anima mea pauperi.

verses.text: I expected good things, and evils are come upon me: I waited for light, and darkness broke out.
verses.textLatin: Expectabam bona, et venerunt mihi mala: præstolabar lucem, et eruperunt tenebræ.

verses.text: My inner parts have boiled without any rest, the days of affliction have prevented me.
verses.textLatin: Interiora mea efferbuerunt absque ulla requie: prævenerunt me dies afflictionis.

verses.text: I went mourning without indignation; I rose up, and cried in the crowd.
verses.textLatin: Mœrens incedebam sine furore; consurgens, in turba clamabam.

verses.text: I was the brother of dragons, and companion of ostriches.
verses.textLatin: Frater fui draconum, et socius struthionum.

verses.text: My skin is become black upon me, and my bones are dried up with heat.
verses.textLatin: Cutis mea denigrata est super me, et ossa mea aruerunt præ caumate.

verses.text: My harp is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of those that weep.
verses.textLatin: Versa est in luctum cithara mea, et organum meum in vocem flentium.

verses.text: I  MADE a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin.
verses.textLatin: Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine.

verses.text: For what part should God from above have in me, and what inheritance the Almighty from on high?
verses.textLatin: Quam enim partem haberet in me Deus desuper, et hæreditatem Omnipotens de excelsis?

verses.text: Is not destruction to the wicked, and aversion to them that work iniquity?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non perditio est iniquo, et alienatio operantibus injustitiam?

verses.text: Doth not he consider my ways, and number all my steps?
verses.textLatin: Nonne ipse considerat vias meas, et cunctos gressus meos dinumerat?

verses.text: If I have walked in vanity, and my foot hath made haste to deceit:
verses.textLatin: Si ambulavi in vanitate, et festinavit in dolo pes meus,

verses.text: Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my simplicity.
verses.textLatin: appendat me in statera justa, et sciat Deus simplicitatem meam.

verses.text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and if my heart hath followed my eyes, and if a spot hath cleaved to my hands:
verses.textLatin: Si declinavit gressus meus de via, et si secutum est oculos meos cor meum, et si manibus meis adhæsit macula,

verses.text: Then let me sow and let another eat: and let my offspring be rooted out.
verses.textLatin: seram, et alius comedat, et progenies mea eradicetur.

verses.text: If my heart hath been deceived upon a woman, and if I have laid wait at my friend’s door:
verses.textLatin: Si deceptum est cor meum super muliere, et si ad ostium amici mei insidiatus sum,

verses.text: Let my wife be the harlot of another, and let other men lie with her.
verses.textLatin: scortum alterius sit uxor mea, et super illam incurventur alii.

verses.text: For this is a heinous crime, and a most grievous iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Hoc enim nefas est, et iniquitas maxima.

verses.text: It is a fire that devoureth even to destruction, and rooteth up all things that spring.
verses.textLatin: Ignis est usque ad perditionem devorans, et omnia eradicans genimina.

verses.text: If I have despised to abide judgment with my manservant, or my maidservant, when they had any controversy against me:
verses.textLatin: Si contempsi subire judicium cum servo meo et ancilla mea, cum disceptarent adversum me:

verses.text: For what shall I do when God shall rise to judge? and when he shall examine, what shall I answer him?
verses.textLatin: quid enim faciam cum surrexerit ad judicandum Deus? et cum quæsierit, quid respondebo illi?

verses.text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him also: and did not one and the same form me in the womb?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non in utero fecit me, qui et illum operatus est, et formavit me in vulva unus?

verses.text: If I have denied to the poor what they desired, and have made the eyes of the widow wait:
verses.textLatin: Si negavi quod volebant pauperibus, et oculos viduæ expectare feci;
