verses.text: If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof:
verses.textLatin: si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea

verses.text: (For from my infancy mercy grew up with me: and it came out with me from my mother’s womb:)
verses.textLatin: (quia ab infantia mea crevit mecum miseratio, et de utero matris meæ egressa est mecum);

verses.text: If I have despised him that was perishing for want of clothing, and the poor man that had no covering:
verses.textLatin: si despexi pereuntem, eo quod non habuerit indumentum, et absque operimento pauperem;

verses.text: If his sides have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep:
verses.textLatin: si non benedixerunt mihi latera ejus, et de velleribus ovium mearum calefactus est;

verses.text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, even when I saw myself superior in the gate:
verses.textLatin: si levavi super pupillum manum meam, etiam cum viderem me in porta superiorem:

verses.text: Let my shoulder fall from its joint, and let my arm with its bones be broken.
verses.textLatin: humerus meus a junctura sua cadat, et brachium meum cum suis ossibus confringatur.

verses.text: For I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was not able to bear.
verses.textLatin: Semper enim quasi tumentes super me fluctus timui Deum, et pondus ejus ferre non potui.

verses.text: If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence:
verses.textLatin: Si putavi aurum robur meum, et obrizo dixi: Fiducia mea;

verses.text: If I have rejoiced over my great riches, and because my hand had gotten much.
verses.textLatin: si lætatus sum super multis divitiis meis, et quia plurima reperit manus mea;

verses.text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, and the moon going in brightness:
verses.textLatin: si vidi solem cum fulgeret, et lunam incedentem clare,

verses.text: And my heart in secret hath rejoiced, and I have kissed my hand with my mouth:
verses.textLatin: et lætatum est in abscondito cor meum, et osculatus sum manum meam ore meo:

verses.text: Which is a very great iniquity, and a denial against the most high God.
verses.textLatin: quæ est iniquitas maxima, et negatio contra Deum altissimum.

verses.text: If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him.
verses.textLatin: Si gavisus sum ad ruinam ejus qui me oderat, et exsultavi quod invenisset eum malum:

verses.text: For I have not given my mouth to sin, by wishing a curse to his soul.
verses.textLatin: non enim dedi ad peccandum guttur meum, ut expeterem maledicens animam ejus.

verses.text: If the men of my tabernacle have not said: Who will give us of his flesh that we may be filled?
verses.textLatin: Si non dixerunt viri tabernaculi mei: Quis det de carnibus ejus, ut saturemur?

verses.text: The stranger did not stay without, my door was open to the traveller.
verses.textLatin: foris non mansit peregrinus: ostium meum viatori patuit.

verses.text: If as a man I have hid my sin, and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom.
verses.textLatin: Si abscondi quasi homo peccatum meum, et celavi in sinu meo iniquitatem meam;

verses.text: If I have been afraid at a very great multitude, and the contempt of kinsmen hath terrified me: and I have not rather held my peace, and not gone out of the door.
verses.textLatin: si expavi ad multitudinem nimiam, et despectio propinquorum terruit me: et non magis tacui, nec egressus sum ostium.

verses.text: Who would grant me a hearer, that the Almighty may hear my desire; and that he himself that judgeth would write a book,
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi tribuat auditorem, ut desiderium meum audiat Omnipotens, et librum scribat ipse qui judicat,

verses.text: That I may carry it on my shoulder, and put it about me as a crown?
verses.textLatin: ut in humero meo portem illum, et circumdem illum quasi coronam mihi?

verses.text: At every step of mine I would pronounce it, and offer it as to a prince.
verses.textLatin: Per singulos gradus meos pronuntiabo illum, et quasi principi offeram eum.

verses.text: If my land cry against me, and with it the furrows thereof mourn:
verses.textLatin: Si adversum me terra mea clamat, et cum ipsa sulci ejus deflent:

verses.text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, and have afflicted the soul of the tillers thereof:
verses.textLatin: si fructus ejus comedi absque pecunia, et animam agricolarum ejus afflixi:

verses.text: Let thistles grow up to me instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley.
verses.textLatin: pro frumento oriatur mihi tribulus, et pro hordeo spina. Finita sunt verba Job.

verses.text: So  these three men ceased to answer Job, because he seemed just to himself.
verses.textLatin: Omiserunt autem tres viri isti respondere Job, eo quod justus sibi videretur.

verses.text: And Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was angry and was moved to indignation: now he was angry against Job, because he said he was just before God.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus indignatusque est Eliu filius Barachel Buzites, de cognatione Ram: iratus est autem adversum Job, eo quod justum se esse diceret coram Deo.

verses.text: And he was angry with his friends, because they had not found a reasonable answer, but only had condemned Job.
verses.textLatin: Porro adversum amicos ejus indignatus est, eo quod non invenissent responsionem rationabilem, sed tantummodo condemnassent Job.

verses.text: So Eliu waited while Job was speaking, because they were his elders that were speaking.
verses.textLatin: Igitur Eliu expectavit Job loquentem, eo quod seniores essent qui loquebantur.

verses.text: But when he saw that the three were not able to answer, he was exceedingly angry.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem vidisset quod tres respondere non potuissent, iratus est vehementer.

verses.text: Then Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, and said: I am younger in days, and you are more ancient; therefore hanging down my head, I was afraid to shew you my opinion.
verses.textLatin: Respondensque Eliu filius Barachel Buzites, dixit: Junior sum tempore, vos autem antiquiores: idcirco, demisso capite, veritus sum vobis indicare meam sententiam.

verses.text: For I hoped that greater age would speak, and that a multitude of years would teach wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Sperabam enim quod ætas prolixior loqueretur, et annorum multitudo doceret sapientiam.

verses.text: But, as I see, there is a spirit in men, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding.
verses.textLatin: Sed, ut video, spiritus est in hominibus, et inspiratio Omnipotentis dat intelligentiam.

verses.text: They that are aged are not the wise men, neither do the ancients understand judgment.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt longævi sapientes, nec senes intelligunt judicium.

verses.text: Therefore I will speak: Hearken to me, I also will shew you my wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Ideo dicam: Audite me: ostendam vobis etiam ego meam sapientiam.

verses.text: For I have waited for your words, I have given ear to your wisdom, as long as you were disputing in words.
verses.textLatin: Expectavi enim sermones vestros; audivi prudentiam vestram, donec disceptaremini sermonibus;

verses.text: And as long as I thought you said some thing, I considered: but, as I see, there is none of you that can convince Job, and answer his words.
verses.textLatin: et donec putabam vos aliquid dicere, considerabam: sed, ut video, non est qui possit arguere Job, et respondere ex vobis sermonibus ejus.

verses.text: Lest you should say: We have found wisdom, God hath cast him down, not man.
verses.textLatin: Ne forte dicatis: Invenimus sapientiam: Deus projecit eum, non homo.

verses.text: He hath spoken nothing to me, and I will not answer him according to your words.
verses.textLatin: Nihil locutus est mihi: et ego non secundum sermones vestros respondebo illi.

verses.text: They were afraid, and answered no more, and they left off speaking.
verses.textLatin: Extimuerunt, nec responderunt ultra, abstuleruntque a se eloquia.

verses.text: Therefore because I have waited, and they have not spoken: they stood, and answered no more:
verses.textLatin: Quoniam igitur expectavi, et non sunt locuti: steterunt, nec ultra responderunt:

verses.text: I also will answer my part, and will shew my knowledge.
verses.textLatin: respondebo et ego partem meam, et ostendam scientiam meam.

verses.text: For I am full of matter to speak of, and the spirit of my bowels straiteneth me.
verses.textLatin: Plenus sum enim sermonibus, et coarctat me spiritus uteri mei.

verses.text: Behold, my belly is as new wine which wanteth vent, which bursteth the new vessels.
verses.textLatin: En venter meus quasi mustum absque spiraculo, quod lagunculas novas disrumpit.

verses.text: I will speak and take breath a little: I will open my lips, and will answer.
verses.textLatin: Loquar, et respirabo paululum: aperiam labia mea, et respondebo.

verses.text: I will not accept the person of man, and I will not level God with man.
verses.textLatin: Non accipiam personam viri, et Deum homini non æquabo.

verses.text: For I know not how long I shall continue, and whether after a while my Maker may take me away.
verses.textLatin: Nescio enim quamdiu subsistam, et si post modicum tollat me factor meus.

verses.text: Hear  therefore, O Job, my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
verses.textLatin: Audi igitur, Job, eloquia mea, et omnes sermones meos ausculta.

verses.text: Behold now I have opened my mouth, let my tongue speak within my jaws.
verses.textLatin: Ecce aperui os meum: loquatur lingua mea in faucibus meis.

verses.text: My words are from my upright heart, and my lips shall speak a pure sentence.
verses.textLatin: Simplici corde meo sermones mei, et sententiam puram labia mea loquentur.

verses.text: The spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus Dei fecit me, et spiraculum Omnipotentis vivificavit me.

verses.text: If thou canst, answer me, and stand up against my face.
verses.textLatin: Si potes, responde mihi, et adversus faciem meam consiste.

verses.text: Behold God hath made me as well as thee, and of the same clay I also was formed.
verses.textLatin: Ecce, et me sicut et te fecit Deus, et de eodem luto ego quoque formatus sum.

verses.text: But yet let not my wonder terrify thee, and let not my eloquence be burdensome to thee.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen miraculum meum non te terreat, et eloquentia mea non sit tibi gravis.

verses.text: Now thou hast said in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words:
verses.textLatin: Dixisti ergo in auribus meis, et vocem verborum tuorum audivi:

verses.text: I am clean, and without sin: I am unspotted, and there is no iniquity in me.
verses.textLatin: Mundus sum ego, et absque delicto: immaculatus, et non est iniquitas in me.

verses.text: Because he hath found complaints against me, therefore he hath counted me for his enemy.
verses.textLatin: Quia querelas in me reperit, ideo arbitratus est me inimicum sibi.

verses.text: He hath put my feet in the stocks, he hath observed all my paths.
verses.textLatin: Posuit in nervo pedes meos; custodivit omnes semitas meas.

verses.text: Now this is the thing in which thou art not justified: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
verses.textLatin: Hoc est ergo in quo non es justificatus: respondebo tibi, quia major sit Deus homine.

verses.text: Dost thou strive against him, because he hath not answered thee to all words?
verses.textLatin: Adversus eum contendis, quod non ad omnia verba responderit tibi?

verses.text: God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time.
verses.textLatin: Semel loquitur Deus, et secundo idipsum non repetit.

verses.text: By a dream in a vision by night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, and they are sleeping in their beds:
verses.textLatin: Per somnium, in visione nocturna, quando irruit sopor super homines, et dormiunt in lectulo,

verses.text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and teaching instructeth them in what they are to learn.
verses.textLatin: tunc aperit aures virorum, et erudiens eos instruit disciplina,

verses.text: That he may withdraw a man from the things he is doing, and may deliver him from pride.
verses.textLatin: ut avertat hominem ab his quæ facit, et liberet eum de superbia,

verses.text: Rescuing his soul from corruption: and his life from passing to the sword.
verses.textLatin: eruens animam ejus a corruptione, et vitam illius ut non transeat in gladium.

verses.text: He rebuketh also by sorrow in the bed, and he maketh all his bones to wither.
verses.textLatin: Increpat quoque per dolorem in lectulo, et omnia ossa ejus marcescere facit.

verses.text: Bread becometh abominable to him in his life, and to his soul the meat which before he desired.
verses.textLatin: Abominabilis ei fit in vita sua panis, et animæ illius cibus ante desiderabilis.

verses.text: His flesh shall be consumed away, and his bones that were covered shall be made bare.
verses.textLatin: Tabescet caro ejus, et ossa, quæ tecta fuerant, nudabuntur.

verses.text: His soul hath drawn near to corruption, and his life to the destroyers.
verses.textLatin: Appropinquavit corruptioni anima ejus, et vita illius mortiferis.

verses.text: If there shall be an angel speaking for him, one among thousands, to declare man’s uprightness,
verses.textLatin: Si fuerit pro eo angelus loquens, unus de millibus, ut annuntiet hominis æquitatem,

verses.text: He shall have mercy on him, and shall say: Deliver him, that he may not go down to corruption: I have found wherein I may be merciful to him.
verses.textLatin: miserebitur ejus, et dicet: Libera eum, ut non descendat in corruptionem: inveni in quo ei propitier.

verses.text: His flesh is consumed with punishments, let him return to the days of his youth.
verses.textLatin: Consumpta est caro ejus a suppliciis: revertatur ad dies adolescentiæ suæ.

verses.text: He shall pray to God, and he will be gracious to him: and he shall see his face with joy, and he will render to man his justice.
verses.textLatin: Deprecabitur Deum, et placabilis ei erit: et videbit faciem ejus in jubilo, et reddet homini justitiam suam.

verses.text: He shall look upon men, and shall say: I have sinned, and indeed I have offended, and I have not received what I have deserved.
verses.textLatin: Respiciet homines, et dicet: Peccavi, et vere deliqui, et ut eram dignus, non recepi.

verses.text: He hath delivered his soul from going into destruction, that it may live and see the light.
verses.textLatin: Liberavit animam suam, ne pergeret in interitum, sed vivens lucem videret.

verses.text: Behold, all these things God worketh three times within every one.
verses.textLatin: Ecce hæc omnia operatur Deus tribus vicibus per singulos,

verses.text: That he may withdraw their souls from corruption, and enlighten them with the light of the living.
verses.textLatin: ut revocet animas eorum a corruptione, et illuminet luce viventium.

verses.text: Attend, Job, and hearken to me: and hold thy peace, whilst I speak.
verses.textLatin: Attende, Job, et audi me: et tace, dum ego loquor.

verses.text: But if thou hast any thing to say, answer me, speak: for I would have thee to appear just.
verses.textLatin: Si autem habes quod loquaris, responde mihi: loquere, volo enim te apparere justum.

verses.text: And if thou have not, hear me: hold thy peace, and I will teach thee wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non habes, audi me: tace, et docebo te sapientiam.

verses.text: And  Eliu continued his discourse, and said:
verses.textLatin: Pronuntians itaque Eliu, etiam hæc locutus est:

verses.text: Hear ye, wise men, my words, and ye learned, hearken to me:
verses.textLatin: Audite, sapientes, verba mea: et eruditi, auscultate me.

verses.text: For the ear trieth words, and the mouth discerneth meats by the taste.
verses.textLatin: Auris enim verba probat, et guttur escas gustu dijudicat.

verses.text: Let us choose to us judgment, and let us see among ourselves what is the best.
verses.textLatin: Judicium eligamus nobis, et inter nos videamus quid sit melius.

verses.text: For Job hath said: I am just, and God hath overthrown my judgment.
verses.textLatin: Quia dixit Job: Justus sum, et Deus subvertit judicium meum.

verses.text: For in judging me there is a lie: my arrow is violent without any sin.
verses.textLatin: In judicando enim me mendacium est: violenta sagitta mea absque ullo peccato.

verses.text: What man is there like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?
verses.textLatin: Quis est vir ut est Job, qui bibit subsannationem quasi aquam:

verses.text: Who goeth in company with them that work iniquity, and walketh with wicked men?
verses.textLatin: qui graditur cum operantibus iniquitatem, et ambulat cum viris impiis?

verses.text: For he hath said: Man shall not please God, although he run with him.
verses.textLatin: Dixit enim: Non placebit vir Deo, etiam si cucurrerit cum eo.

verses.text: Therefore, ye men of understanding, hear me: far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty.
verses.textLatin: Ideo, viri cordati, audite me: absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas.

verses.text: For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them.
verses.textLatin: Opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet eis.

verses.text: For in very deed God will not condemn without cause, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
verses.textLatin: Vere enim Deus non condemnabit frustra, nec Omnipotens subvertet judicium.

verses.text: What other hath he appointed over the earth? or whom hath he set over the world which he made?
verses.textLatin: Quem constituit alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est?

verses.text: If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself.
verses.textLatin: Si direxerit ad eum cor suum, spiritum illius et flatum ad se trahet.

verses.text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall return into ashes.
verses.textLatin: Deficiet omnis caro simul, et homo in cinerem revertetur.

verses.text: If then thou hast understanding, hear what is said, and hearken to the voice of my words.
verses.textLatin: Si habes ergo intellectum, audi quod dicitur, et ausculta vocem eloquii mei:

verses.text: Can he be healed that loveth not judgment? and how dost thou so far condemn him that is just?
verses.textLatin: numquid qui non amat judicium sanari potest? et quomodo tu eum qui justus est in tantum condemnas?

verses.text: Who saith to the king: Thou art an apostate: who calleth rulers ungodly:
verses.textLatin: Qui dicit regi: Apostata; qui vocat duces impios;

verses.text: Who accepteth not the persons of princes: nor hath regarded the tyrant, when he contended against the poor man: for all are the work of his hands.
verses.textLatin: qui non accipit personas principum, nec cognovit tyrannum cum disceptaret contra pauperem: opus enim manuum ejus sunt universi.

verses.text: They shall suddenly die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and they shall pass, and take away the violent without hand.
verses.textLatin: Subito morientur, et in media nocte turbabuntur populi: et pertransibunt, et auferent violentum absque manu.

verses.text: For his eyes are upon the ways of men, and he considereth all their steps.
verses.textLatin: Oculi enim ejus super vias hominum, et omnes gressus eorum considerat.

verses.text: There is no darkness, and there is no shadow of death, where they may be hid who work iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt tenebræ, et non est umbra mortis, ut abscondantur ibi qui operantur iniquitatem,

verses.text: For it is no longer in the power of man to enter into judgment with God.
verses.textLatin: neque enim ultra in hominis potestate est, ut veniat ad Deum in judicium.

verses.text: He shall break in pieces many and innumerable, and shall make others to stand in their stead.
verses.textLatin: Conteret multos, et innumerabiles, et stare faciet alios pro eis.

verses.text: For he knoweth their works: and therefore he shall bring night on them, and they shall be destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Novit enim opera eorum, et idcirco inducet noctem, et conterentur.

verses.text: He hath struck them, as being wicked, in open sight.
verses.textLatin: Quasi impios percussit eos in loco videntium:

verses.text: Who as it were on purpose have revolted from him, and would not understand all his ways:
verses.textLatin: qui quasi de industria recesserunt ab eo, et omnes vias ejus intelligere noluerunt:

verses.text: So that they caused the cry of the needy to come to him, and he heard the voice of the poor.
verses.textLatin: ut pervenire facerent ad eum clamorem egeni, et audiret vocem pauperum.

verses.text: For when he granteth peace, who is there that can condemn? When he hideth his countenance, who is there that can behold him, whether it regard nations, or all men?
verses.textLatin: Ipso enim concedente pacem, quis est qui condemnet? ex quo absconderit vultum, quis est qui contempletur eum, et super gentes, et super omnes homines?

verses.text: Who maketh a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people?
verses.textLatin: Qui regnare facit hominem hypocritam propter peccata populi.

verses.text: Seeing then I have spoken of God, I will not hinder thee in thy turn.
verses.textLatin: Quia ergo ego locutus sum ad Deum, te quoque non prohibebo.

verses.text: If I have erred, teach thou me: if I have spoken iniquity, I will add no more.
verses.textLatin: Si erravi, tu doce me; si iniquitatem locutus sum, ultra non addam.

verses.text: Doth God require it of thee, because it hath displeased thee? for thou begannest to speak, and not I: but if thou know any thing better, speak.
verses.textLatin: Numquid a te Deus expetit eam, quia displicuit tibi? tu enim cœpisti loqui, et non ego: quod si quid nosti melius, loquere.

verses.text: Let men of understanding speak to me, and let a wise man hearken to me.
verses.textLatin: Viri intelligentes loquantur mihi, et vir sapiens audiat me.

verses.text: But Job hath spoken foolishly, and his words sound not discipline.
verses.textLatin: Job autem stulte locutus est, et verba illius non sonant disciplinam.

verses.text: My father, let Job be tried even to the end: cease not from the man of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Pater mi, probetur Job usque ad finem: ne desinas ab homine iniquitatis:

verses.text: Because he addeth blasphemy upon his sins, let him be tied fast in the mean time amongst us: and then let him provoke God to judgment with his speeches.
verses.textLatin: quia addit super peccata sua blasphemiam, inter nos interim constringatur: et tunc ad judicium provocet sermonibus suis Deum.

verses.text: Moreover  Eliu spoke these words:
verses.textLatin: Igitur Eliu hæc rursum locutus est:

verses.text: Doth thy thought seem right to thee, that thou shouldst say: I am more just than God?
verses.textLatin: Numquid æqua tibi videtur tua cogitatio, ut diceres: Justior sum Deo?

verses.text: For thou saidst: That which is right doth not please thee: or what will it profit thee if I sin?
verses.textLatin: Dixisti enim: Non tibi placet quod rectum est: vel quid tibi proderit, si ego peccavero?

verses.text: Therefore I will answer thy words, and thy friends with thee.
verses.textLatin: Itaque ego respondebo sermonibus tuis, et amicis tuis tecum.

verses.text: Look up to heaven and see, and behold the sky, that it is higher than thee.
verses.textLatin: Suspice cælum, et intuere: et contemplare æthera quod altior te sit.

verses.text: If thou sin, what shalt thou hurt him? and if thy iniquities be multiplied, what shalt thou do against him?
verses.textLatin: Si peccaveris, quid ei nocebis? et si multiplicatæ fuerint iniquitates tuæ, quid facies contra eum?

verses.text: And if thou do justly, what shalt thou give him, or what shall he receive of thy hand?
verses.textLatin: Porro si juste egeris, quid donabis ei? aut quid de manu tua accipiet?

verses.text: Thy wickedness may hurt a man that is like thee: and thy justice may help the son of man.
verses.textLatin: Homini qui similis tui est, nocebit impietas tua: et filium hominis adjuvabit justitia tua.

verses.text: By reason of the multitude of oppressors they shall cry out: and shall wail for the violence of the arm of tyrants.
verses.textLatin: Propter multitudinem calumniatorum clamabunt, et ejulabunt propter vim brachii tyrannorum.

verses.text: And he hath not said: Where is God, who made me, who hath given songs in the night?
verses.textLatin: Et non dixit: Ubi est Deus qui fecit me, qui dedit carmina in nocte;

verses.text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and instructeth us more than the fowls of the air.
verses.textLatin: qui docet nos super jumenta terræ, et super volucres cæli erudit nos?

verses.text: There shall they cry, and he will not hear, because of the pride of evil men.
verses.textLatin: Ibi clamabunt, et non exaudiet, propter superbiam malorum.

verses.text: God therefore will not hear in vain, and the Almighty will look into the causes of every one.
verses.textLatin: Non ergo frustra audiet Deus, et Omnipotens causas singulorum intuebitur.

verses.text: Yea when thou shalt say: He considereth not: be judged before him, and expect him.
verses.textLatin: Etiam cum dixeris: Non considerat: judicare coram illo, et expecta eum.

verses.text: For he doth not now bring on his fury, neither doth he revenge wickedness exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Nunc enim non infert furorem suum, nec ulciscitur scelus valde.

verses.text: Therefore Job openeth his mouth in vain, and multiplieth words without knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Ergo Job frustra aperit os suum, et absque scientia verba multiplicat.

verses.text: Eliu  also proceeded, and said:
verses.textLatin: Addens quoque Eliu, hæc locutus est:

verses.text: Suffer me a little, and I will shewthee: for I have yet somewhat to speak in God’s behalf.
verses.textLatin: Sustine me paululum, et indicabo tibi: adhuc enim habeo quod pro Deo loquar.

verses.text: I will repeat my knowledge from the beginning, and I will prove my Maker just.
verses.textLatin: Repetam scientiam meam a principio, et operatorem meum probabo justum.

verses.text: For indeed my words are without a lie, and perfect knowledge shall be proved to thee.
verses.textLatin: Vere enim absque mendacio sermones mei, et perfecta scientia probabitur tibi.

verses.text: God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty.
verses.textLatin: Deus potentes non abjicit, cum et ipse sit potens:

verses.text: But he saveth not the wicked, and he giveth judgment to the poor.
verses.textLatin: sed non salvat impios, et judicium pauperibus tribuit.

verses.text: He will not take away his eyes from the just, and he placeth kings on the throne for ever, and they are exalted.
verses.textLatin: Non auferet a justo oculos suos: et reges in solio collocat in perpetuum, et illi eriguntur.

verses.text: And if they shall be in chains, and be bound with the cords of poverty:
verses.textLatin: Et si fuerint in catenis, et vinciantur funibus paupertatis,

verses.text: He shall shew them their works, and their wicked deeds, because they have been violent.
verses.textLatin: indicabit eis opera eorum, et scelera eorum, quia violenti fuerunt.

verses.text: He also shall open their ear, to correct them: and shall speak, that they may return from iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Revelabit quoque aurem eorum, ut corripiat: et loquetur, ut revertantur ab iniquitate.

verses.text: If they shall hear and observe, they shall accomplish their days in good, and their years in glory.
verses.textLatin: Si audierint et observaverint, complebunt dies suos in bono, et annos suos in gloria:

verses.text: But if they hear not, they shall pass by the sword, and shall be consumed in folly.
verses.textLatin: si autem non audierint, transibunt per gladium, et consumentur in stultitia.

verses.text: Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God, neither shall they cry when they are bound.
verses.textLatin: Simulatores et callidi provocant iram Dei, neque clamabunt cum vincti fuerint.

verses.text: Their soul shall die in a storm, and their life among the effeminate.
verses.textLatin: Morietur in tempestate anima eorum, et vita eorum inter effeminatos.

verses.text: He shall deliver the poor out of his distress, and shall open his ear in affliction.
verses.textLatin: Eripiet de angustia sua pauperem, et revelabit in tribulatione aurem ejus.

verses.text: Therefore he shall set thee at large out of the narrow mouth, and which hath no foundation under it: and the rest of thy table shall be full of fatness.
verses.textLatin: Igitur salvabit te de ore angusto latissime, et non habente fundamentum subter se: requies autem mensæ tuæ erit plena pinguedine.

verses.text: Thy cause hath been judged as that of the wicked, cause and judgment thou shalt recover.
verses.textLatin: Causa tua quasi impii judicata est: causam judiciumque recipies.

verses.text: Therefore let not anger overcome thee to oppress any man: neither let multitude of gifts turn thee aside.
verses.textLatin: Non te ergo superet ira ut aliquem opprimas: nec multitudo donorum inclinet te.

verses.text: Lay down thy greatness without tribulation, and all the mighty of strength.
verses.textLatin: Depone magnitudinem tuam absque tribulatione, et omnes robustos fortitudine.

verses.text: Prolong not the night that people may come up for them.
verses.textLatin: Ne protrahas noctem, ut ascendant populi pro eis.

verses.text: Beware thou turn not aside to iniquity: for this thou hast begun to follow after misery.
verses.textLatin: Cave ne declines ad iniquitatem: hanc enim cœpisti sequi post miseriam.

verses.text: Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Deus excelsus in fortitudine sua, et nullus ei similis in legislatoribus.

verses.text: Who can search out his ways? or who can say to him: Thou hast wrought iniquity?
verses.textLatin: Quis poterit scrutari vias ejus? aut quis potest ei dicere: Operatus es iniquitatem?

verses.text: Remember that thou knowest not his work, concerning which men have sung.
verses.textLatin: Memento quod ignores opus ejus, de quo cecinerunt viri.

verses.text: All men see him, every one beholdeth afar off.
verses.textLatin: Omnes homines vident eum: unusquisque intuetur procul.

verses.text: Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge: the number of his years is inestimable.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Deus magnus vincens scientiam nostram: numerus annorum ejus inæstimabilis.

verses.text: He lifteth up the drops of rain, and poureth out showers like floods:
verses.textLatin: Qui aufert stillas pluviæ, et effundit imbres ad instar gurgitum,

verses.text: Which flow from the clouds that cover all above.
verses.textLatin: qui de nubibus fluunt quæ prætexunt cuncta desuper.

verses.text: If he will spread out clouds as his tent,
verses.textLatin: Si voluerit extendere nubes quasi tentorium suum,

verses.text: And lighten with his light from above, he shall cover also the ends of the sea.
verses.textLatin: et fulgurare lumine suo desuper, cardines quoque maris operiet.

verses.text: For by these he judgeth people, and giveth food to many mortals.
verses.textLatin: Per hæc enim judicat populos, et dat escas multis mortalibus.

verses.text: In his hands he hideth the light, and commandeth it to come again.
verses.textLatin: In manibus abscondit lucem, et præcepit ei ut rursus adveniat.

verses.text: He sheweth his friend concerning it, that it is his possession, and that he may come up to it.
verses.textLatin: Annuntiat de ea amico suo, quod possessio ejus sit, et ad eam possit ascendere.

verses.text: At  this my heart trembleth, and is moved out of its place.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc expavit cor meum, et emotum est de loco suo.

verses.text: Hear ye attentively the terror of his voice, and the sound that cometh out of his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Audite auditionem in terrore vocis ejus, et sonum de ore illius procedentem.

verses.text: He beholdeth under all the heavens, and his light is upon the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Subter omnes cælos ipse considerat, et lumen illius super terminos terræ.

verses.text: After it a noise shall roar, he shall thunder with the voice of his majesty, and shall not be found out, when his voice shall be heard.
verses.textLatin: Post eum rugiet sonitus; tonabit voce magnitudinis suæ: et non investigabitur, cum audita fuerit vox ejus.

verses.text: God shall thunder wonderfully with his voice, he that doth great and unsearchable things.
verses.textLatin: Tonabit Deus in voce sua mirabiliter, qui facit magna et inscrutabilia;

verses.text: He commandeth the snow to go down upon the earth, and the winter rain, and the shower of his strength.
verses.textLatin: qui præcipit nivi ut descendat in terram, et hiemis pluviis, et imbri fortitudinis suæ;

verses.text: He sealeth up the hand of all men, that every one may know his works.
verses.textLatin: qui in manu omnium hominum signat, ut noverint singuli opera sua.

verses.text: Then the beast shall go into his covert, and shall abide in his den.
verses.textLatin: Ingredietur bestia latibulum, et in antro suo morabitur.

verses.text: Out of the inner parts shall a tempest come, and cold out of the north.
verses.textLatin: Ab interioribus egredietur tempestas, et ab Arcturo frigus.

verses.text: When God bloweth there cometh frost, and again the waters are poured out abundantly.
verses.textLatin: Flante Deo, concrescit gelu, et rursum latissimæ funduntur aquæ.

verses.text: Corn desireth clouds, and the clouds spread their light:
verses.textLatin: Frumentum desiderat nubes, et nubes spargunt lumen suum.

verses.text: Which go round about, whithersoever the will of him that governeth them shall lead them, to whatsoever he shall command them upon the face of the whole earth:
verses.textLatin: Quæ lustrant per circuitum, quocumque eas voluntas gubernantis duxerit, ad omne quod præceperit illis super faciem orbis terrarum:

verses.text: Whether in one tribe, or in his own land, or in what place soever of his mercy he shall command them to be found.
verses.textLatin: sive in una tribu, sive in terra sua, sive in quocumque loco misericordiæ suæ eas jusserit inveniri.

verses.text: Hearken to these things, Job: Stand, and consider the wondrous works of God.
verses.textLatin: Ausculta hæc, Job: sta, et considera mirabilia Dei.

verses.text: Dost thou know when God commanded the rains, to shew his light of his clouds?
verses.textLatin: Numquid scis quando præceperit Deus pluviis, ut ostenderent lucem nubium ejus?

verses.text: Knowest thou the great paths of the clouds, and the perfect knowledges?
verses.textLatin: Numquid nosti semitas nubium magnas, et perfectas scientias?

verses.text: Are not thy garments hot, when the south wind blows upon the earth?
verses.textLatin: Nonne vestimenta tua calida sunt, cum perflata fuerit terra austro?

verses.text: Thou perhaps hast made the heavens with him, which are most strong, as if they were of molten brass.
verses.textLatin: Tu forsitan cum eo fabricatus es cælos, qui solidissimi quasi ære fusi sunt.

verses.text: Shew us what we may say to him: for we are wrapped up in darkness.
verses.textLatin: Ostende nobis quid dicamus illi: nos quippe involvimur tenebris.

verses.text: Who shall tell him the things I speak? even if a man shall speak, he shall be swallowed up.
verses.textLatin: Quis narrabit ei quæ loquor? etiam si locutus fuerit homo, devorabitur.

verses.text: But now they see not the light: the air on a sudden shall be thickened into clouds, and the wind shall pass and drive them away.
verses.textLatin: At nunc non vident lucem: subito aër cogetur in nubes, et ventus transiens fugabit eas.

verses.text: Cold cometh out of the north, and to God praise with fear.
verses.textLatin: Ab aquilone aurum venit, et ad Deum formidolosa laudatio.

verses.text: We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable.
verses.textLatin: Digne eum invenire non possumus: magnus fortitudine, et judicio, et justitia: et enarrari non potest.

verses.text: Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him.
verses.textLatin: Ideo timebunt eum viri, et non audebunt contemplari omnes qui sibi videntur esse sapientes.

verses.text: Then  the Lord answered Job out of a whirlwind, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Dominus Job de turbine, dixit:

verses.text: Who is this that wrappeth up sentences in unskilful words?
verses.textLatin: Quis est iste involvens sententias sermonibus imperitis?

verses.text: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and answer thou me.
verses.textLatin: Accinge sicut vir lumbos tuos: interrogabo te, et responde mihi.

verses.text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? tell me if thou hast understanding.
verses.textLatin: Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ? indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam.

verses.text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
verses.textLatin: Quis posuit mensuras ejus, si nosti? vel quis tetendit super eam lineam?

verses.text: Upon what are its bases grounded? or who laid the corner stone thereof,
verses.textLatin: Super quo bases illius solidatæ sunt? aut quis demisit lapidem angularem ejus,

verses.text: When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?
verses.textLatin: cum me laudarent simul astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei?

verses.text: Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb:
verses.textLatin: Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens;

verses.text: When I made a cloud the garment thereof, and wrapped it in a mist as in swaddling bands?
verses.textLatin: cum ponerem nubem vestimentum ejus, et caligine illud quasi pannis infantiæ obvolverem?

verses.text: I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors:
verses.textLatin: Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectem et ostia,

verses.text: And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.
verses.textLatin: et dixi: Usque huc venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos.

verses.text: Didst thou since thy birth command the morning, and shew the dawning of the day its place?
verses.textLatin: Numquid post ortum tuum præcepisti diluculo, et ostendisti auroræ locum suum?

verses.text: And didst thou hold the extremities of the earth shaking them, and hast thou shaken the ungodly out of it?
verses.textLatin: Et tenuisti concutiens extrema terræ, et excussisti impios ex ea?

verses.text: The seal shall be restored as clay, and shall stand as a garment:
verses.textLatin: Restituetur ut lutum signaculum, et stabit sicut vestimentum:

verses.text: From the wicked their light shall be taken away, and the high arm shall be broken.
verses.textLatin: auferetur ab impiis lux sua, et brachium excelsum confringetur.

verses.text: Hast thou entered into the depths of the sea, and walked in the lowest parts of the deep?
verses.textLatin: Numquid ingressus es profunda maris, et in novissimis abyssi deambulasti?

verses.text: Have the gates of death been opened to thee, and hast thou seen the darksome doors?
verses.textLatin: Numquid apertæ sunt tibi portæ mortis, et ostia tenebrosa vidisti?

verses.text: Hast thou considered the breadth of the earth? tell me, if thou knowest all things?
verses.textLatin: Numquid considerasti latitudinem terræ? indica mihi, si nosti, omnia:

verses.text: Where is the way where light dwelleth, and where is the place of darkness:
verses.textLatin: in qua via lux habitet, et tenebrarum quis locus sit:

verses.text: That thou mayst bring every thing to its own bounds, and understand the paths of the house thereof.
verses.textLatin: ut ducas unumquodque ad terminos suos, et intelligas semitas domus ejus.

verses.text: Didst thou know then that thou shouldst be born? and didst thou know the number of thy days?
verses.textLatin: Sciebas tunc quod nasciturus esses, et numerum dierum tuorum noveras?

verses.text: Hast thou entered into the storehouses of the snow, or hast thou beheld the treasures of the hail:
verses.textLatin: Numquid ingressus es thesauros nivis, aut thesauros grandinis aspexisti,

verses.text: Which I have prepared for the time of the enemy, against the day of battle and war?
verses.textLatin: quæ præparavi in tempus hostis, in diem pugnæ et belli?

verses.text: By what way is the light spread, and heat divided upon the earth?
verses.textLatin: Per quam viam spargitur lux, dividitur æstus super terram?

verses.text: Who gave a course to violent showers, or a way for noisy thunder:
verses.textLatin: Quis dedit vehementissimo imbri cursum, et viam sonantis tonitrui,

verses.text: That it should rain on the earth without man in the wilderness, where no mortal dwelleth:
verses.textLatin: ut plueret super terram absque homine in deserto, ubi nullus mortalium commoratur;

verses.text: That it should fill the desert and desolate land, and should bring forth green grass?
verses.textLatin: ut impleret inviam et desolatam, et produceret herbas virentes?

verses.text: Who is the father of rain? or who begot the drops of dew?
verses.textLatin: Quis est pluviæ pater? vel quis genuit stillas roris?

verses.text: Out of whose womb came the ice; and the frost from heaven who hath gendered it?
verses.textLatin: De cujus utero egressa est glacies? et gelu de cælo quis genuit?

verses.text: The waters are hardened like a stone, and the surface of the deep is congealed.
verses.textLatin: In similitudinem lapidis aquæ durantur, et superficies abyssi constringitur.

verses.text: Shalt thou be able to join together the shining stars the Pleiades, or canst thou stop the turning about of Arcturus?
verses.textLatin: Numquid conjungere valebis micantes stellas Pleiadas, aut gyrum Arcturi poteris dissipare?

verses.text: Canst thou bring forth the day star in its time, and make the evening star to rise upon the children of the earth?
verses.textLatin: Numquid producis luciferum in tempore suo, et vesperum super filios terræ consurgere facis?

verses.text: Dost thou know the order of heaven, and canst thou set down the reason thereof on the earth?
verses.textLatin: Numquid nosti ordinem cæli, et pones rationem ejus in terra?

verses.text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that an abundance of waters may cover thee?
verses.textLatin: Numquid elevabis in nebula vocem tuam, et impetus aquarum operiet te?

verses.text: Canst thou send lightnings, and will they go, and will they return and say to thee: Here we are?
verses.textLatin: Numquid mittes fulgura, et ibunt, et revertentia dicent tibi: Adsumus?

verses.text: Who hath put wisdom in the heart of man? or who gave the cock understanding?
verses.textLatin: Quis posuit in visceribus hominis sapientiam? vel quis dedit gallo intelligentiam?

verses.text: Who can declare the order of the heavens, or who can make the harmony of heaven to sleep?
verses.textLatin: Quis enarrabit cælorum rationem? et concentum cæli quis dormire faciet?

verses.text: When was the dust poured on the earth, and the clods fastened together?
verses.textLatin: Quando fundebatur pulvis in terra, et glebæ compingebantur?

verses.text: Wilt thou take the prey for the lioness, and satisfy the appetite of her whelps,
verses.textLatin: Numquid capies leænæ prædam, et animam catulorum ejus implebis,

verses.text: When they couch in the dens and lie in wait in holes?
verses.textLatin: quando cubant in antris, et in specubus insidiantur?

verses.text: Who provideth food for the raven, when her young ones cry to God, wandering about, because they have no meat?
verses.textLatin: Quis præparat corvo escam suam, quando pulli ejus clamant ad Deum, vagantes, eo quod non habeant cibos?

verses.text: Knowest  thou the time when the wild goats bring forth among the rocks, or hast thou observed the hinds when they fawn?
verses.textLatin: Numquid nosti tempus partus ibicum in petris, vel parturientes cervas observasti?

verses.text: Hast thou numbered the months of their conceiving, or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
verses.textLatin: Dinumerasti menses conceptus earum, et scisti tempus partus earum?

verses.text: They bow themselves to bring forth young, and they cast them, and send forth roarings.
verses.textLatin: Incurvantur ad fœtum, et pariunt, et rugitus emittunt.

verses.text: Their young are weaned and go to feed: they go forth, and return not to them.
verses.textLatin: Separantur filii earum, et pergunt ad pastum: egrediuntur, et non revertuntur ad eas.

verses.text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free, and who hath loosed his bonds?
verses.textLatin: Quis dimisit onagrum liberum, et vincula ejus quis solvit?

verses.text: To whom I have given a house in the wilderness, and his dwellings in the barren land.
verses.textLatin: cui dedi in solitudine domum, et tabernacula ejus in terra salsuginis.

verses.text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, he heareth not the cry of the driver.
verses.textLatin: Contemnit multitudinem civitatis: clamorem exactoris non audit.

verses.text: He looketh round about the mountains of his pasture, and seeketh for every green thing.
verses.textLatin: Circumspicit montes pascuæ suæ, et virentia quæque perquirit.

verses.text: Shall the rhinoceros be willing to serve thee, or will he stay at thy crib?
verses.textLatin: Numquid volet rhinoceros servire tibi, aut morabitur ad præsepe tuum?

verses.text: Canst thou bind the rhinoceros with thy thong to plough, or will he break the clods of the valleys after thee?
verses.textLatin: Numquid alligabis rhinocerota ad arandum loro tuo, aut confringet glebas vallium post te?

verses.text: Wilt thou have confidence in his great strength, and leave thy labours to him?
verses.textLatin: Numquid fiduciam habebis in magna fortitudine ejus, et derelinques ei labores tuos?

verses.text: Wilt thou trust him that he will render thee the seed, and gather it into thy barnfloor?
verses.textLatin: Numquid credes illi quod sementem reddat tibi, et aream tuam congreget?

verses.text: The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron, and of the hawk.
verses.textLatin: Penna struthionis similis est pennis herodii et accipitris.

verses.text: When she leaveth her eggs on the earth, thou perhaps wilt warm them in the dust.
verses.textLatin: Quando derelinquit ova sua in terra, tu forsitan in pulvere calefacies ea?

verses.text: She forgetteth that the foot may tread upon them, or that the beasts of the field may break them.
verses.textLatin: Obliviscitur quod pes conculcet ea, aut bestia agri conterat.

verses.text: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers, she hath laboured in vain, no fear constraining her.
verses.textLatin: Duratur ad filios suos, quasi non sint sui: frustra laboravit, nullo timore cogente.

verses.text: For God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he given her understanding.
verses.textLatin: Privavit enim eam Deus sapientia, nec dedit illi intelligentiam.

verses.text: When time shall be, she setteth up her wings on high: she scorneth the horse and his rider.
verses.textLatin: Cum tempus fuerit, in altum alas erigit: deridet equum et ascensorem ejus.

verses.text: Wilt thou give strength to the horse, or clothe his neck with neighing?
verses.textLatin: Numquid præbebis equo fortitudinem, aut circumdabis collo ejus hinnitum?

verses.text: Wilt thou lift him up like the locusts? the glory of his nostrils is terror.
verses.textLatin: Numquid suscitabis eum quasi locustas? gloria narium ejus terror.

verses.text: He breaketh up the earth with his hoof, he pranceth boldly, he goeth forward to meet armed men.
verses.textLatin: Terram ungula fodit; exultat audacter: in occursum pergit armatis.

verses.text: He despiseth fear, he turneth not his back to the sword.
verses.textLatin: Contemnit pavorem, nec cedit gladio.

verses.text: Above him shall the quiver rattle, the spear and shield shall glitter.
verses.textLatin: Super ipsum sonabit pharetra; vibrabit hasta et clypeus:

verses.text: Chasing and raging he swalloweth the ground, neither doth he make account when the noise of the trumpet soundeth.
verses.textLatin: fervens et fremens sorbet terram, nec reputat tubæ sonare clangorem.

verses.text: When he heareth the trumpet he saith: Ha, ha: he smelleth the battle afar off, the encouraging of the captains, and the shouting of the army.
verses.textLatin: Ubi audierit buccinam, dicit: Vah! procul odoratur bellum: exhortationem ducum, et ululatum exercitus.

verses.text: Doth the hawk wax feathered by thy wisdom, spreading her wings to the south?
verses.textLatin: Numquid per sapientiam tuam plumescit accipiter, expandens alas suas ad austrum?

verses.text: Will the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest in high places?
verses.textLatin: Numquid ad præceptum tuum elevabitur aquila, et in arduis ponet nidum suum?

verses.text: She abideth among the rocks, and dwelleth among cragged flints, and stony hills, where there is no access.
verses.textLatin: In petris manet, et in præruptis silicibus commoratur, atque inaccessis rupibus.

verses.text: From thence she looketh for the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.
verses.textLatin: Inde contemplatur escam, et de longe oculi ejus prospiciunt.

verses.text: Her young ones shall suck up blood: and wheresoever the carcass shall be, she is immediately there.
verses.textLatin: Pulli ejus lambent sanguinem: et ubicumque cadaver fuerit, statim adest.

verses.text: And the Lord went on, and said to Job:
verses.textLatin: Et adjecit Dominus, et locutus est ad Job:

verses.text: Shall he that contendeth with God be so easily silenced? surely he that reproveth God, ought to answer him.
verses.textLatin: Numquid qui contendit cum Deo, tam facile conquiescit? utique qui arguit Deum, debet respondere ei.

verses.text: Then Job answered the Lord, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job Domino, dixit:

verses.text: What can I answer, who hath spoken inconsiderately? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Qui leviter locutus sum, respondere quid possum? manum meam ponam super os meum.

verses.text: One thing I have spoken, which I wish I had not said: and another, to which I will add no more.
verses.textLatin: Unum locutus sum, quod utinam non dixissem: et alterum, quibus ultra non addam.

verses.text: And  the Lord answering Job out of the whirlwind, said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Dominus Job de turbine, dixit:

verses.text: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.
verses.textLatin: Accinge sicut vir lumbos tuos: interrogabo te, et indica mihi.

verses.text: Wilt thou make void my judgment: and condemn me, that thou mayst be justified?
verses.textLatin: Numquid irritum facies judicium meum, et condemnabis me, ut tu justificeris?

verses.text: And hast thou an arm like God, and canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
verses.textLatin: Et si habes brachium sicut Deus? et si voce simili tonas?

verses.text: Clothe thyself with beauty, and set thyself up on high, and be glorious, and put on goodly garments.
verses.textLatin: Circumda tibi decorem, et in sublime erigere, et esto gloriosus, et speciosis induere vestibus.

verses.text: Scatter the proud in thy indignation, and behold every arrogant man, and humble him.
verses.textLatin: Disperge superbos in furore tuo, et respiciens omnem arrogantem humilia.

verses.text: Look on all that are proud, and confound them, and crush the wicked in their place.
verses.textLatin: Respice cunctos superbos, et confunde eos, et contere impios in loco suo.

verses.text: Hide them in the dust together, and plunge their faces into the pit.
verses.textLatin: Absconde eos in pulvere simul, et facies eorum demerge in foveam.

verses.text: Then I will confess that thy right hand is able to save thee.
verses.textLatin: Et ego confitebor quod salvare te possit dextera tua.

verses.text: Behold behemoth whom I made with thee, he eateth grass like an ox.
verses.textLatin: Ecce behemoth quem feci tecum, fœnum quasi bos comedet.

verses.text: His strength is in his loins, and his force in the navel of his belly.
verses.textLatin: Fortitudo ejus in lumbis ejus, et virtus illius in umbilico ventris ejus.

verses.text: He setteth up his tail like a cedar, the sinews of his testicles are wrapped together.
verses.textLatin: Stringit caudam suam quasi cedrum; nervi testiculorum ejus perplexi sunt.

verses.text: His bones are like pipes of brass, his gristle like plates of iron.
verses.textLatin: Ossa ejus velut fistulæ æris; cartilago illius quasi laminæ ferreæ.

verses.text: He is the beginning of the ways of God, who made him, he will apply his sword.
verses.textLatin: Ipse est principium viarum Dei: qui fecit eum applicabit gladium ejus.

verses.text: To him the mountains bring forth grass: there all the beasts of the field shall play.
verses.textLatin: Huic montes herbas ferunt: omnes bestiæ agri ludent ibi.

verses.text: He sleepeth under the shadow, in the covert of the reed, and in moist places.
verses.textLatin: Sub umbra dormit in secreto calami, et in locis humentibus.

verses.text: The shades cover his shadow, the willows of the brook shall compass him about.
verses.textLatin: Protegunt umbræ umbram ejus: circumdabunt eum salices torrentis.

verses.text: Behold, he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Ecce absorbebit fluvium, et non mirabitur, et habet fiduciam quod influat Jordanis in os ejus.

verses.text: In his eyes as with a hook he shall take him, and bore through his nostrils with stakes.
verses.textLatin: In oculis ejus quasi hamo capiet eum, et in sudibus perforabit nares ejus.

verses.text: Canst thou draw out the leviathan with a hook, or canst thou tie his tongue with a cord?
verses.textLatin: An extrahere poteris Leviathan hamo, et fune ligabis linguam ejus?

verses.text: Canst thou put a ring in his nose, or bore through his jaw with a buckle?
verses.textLatin: Numquid pones circulum in naribus ejus, aut armilla perforabis maxillam ejus?

verses.text: Will he make many supplications to thee, or speak soft words to thee?
verses.textLatin: Numquid multiplicabit ad te preces, aut loquetur tibi mollia?

verses.text: Will he make a covenant with thee, and wilt thou take him to be a servant for ever.
verses.textLatin: Numquid feriet tecum pactum, et accipies eum servum sempiternum?

verses.text: Shalt thou play with him as with a bird, or tie him up for thy handmaids?
verses.textLatin: Numquid illudes ei quasi avi, aut ligabis eum ancillis tuis?

verses.text: Shall friends cut him in pieces, shall merchants divide him?
verses.textLatin: Concident eum amici? divident illum negotiatores?

verses.text: Wilt thou fill nets with his skin, and the cabins of fishes with his head?
verses.textLatin: Numquid implebis sagenas pelle ejus, et gurgustium piscium capite illius?

verses.text: Lay thy hand upon him: remember the battle, and speak no more.
verses.textLatin: Pone super eum manum tuam: memento belli, nec ultra addas loqui.

verses.text: Behold his hope shall fail him, and in the sight of all he shall be cast down.
verses.textLatin: Ecce spes ejus frustrabitur eum, et videntibus cunctis præcipitabitur.

verses.text: I  WILL not stir him up, like one that is cruel: for who can resist my countenance?
verses.textLatin: Non quasi crudelis suscitabo eum: quis enim resistere potest vultui meo?

verses.text: Who hath given me before that I should repay him? All things that are under heaven are mine.
verses.textLatin: Quis ante dedit mihi, ut reddam ei? omnia quæ sub cælo sunt, mea sunt.

verses.text: I will not spare him, nor his mighty words, and framed to make supplication.
verses.textLatin: Non parcam ei, et verbis potentibus, et ad deprecandum compositis.

verses.text: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can go into the midst of his mouth?
verses.textLatin: Quis revelabit faciem indumenti ejus? et in medium oris ejus quis intrabit?

verses.text: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.
verses.textLatin: Portas vultus ejus quis aperiet? per gyrum dentium ejus formido.

verses.text: His body is like molten shields, shut close up with scales pressing upon one another.
verses.textLatin: Corpus illius quasi scuta fusilia, compactum squamis se prementibus.

verses.text: One is joined to another, and not so much as any air can come between them:
verses.textLatin: Una uni conjungitur, et ne spiraculum quidem incedit per eas.

verses.text: They stick one to another and they hold one another fast, and shall not be separated.
verses.textLatin: Una alteri adhærebit, et tenentes se nequaquam separabuntur.

verses.text: His sneezing is like the shining of fire, and his eyes like the eyelids of the morning.
verses.textLatin: Sternutatio ejus splendor ignis, et oculi ejus ut palpebræ diluculi.

verses.text: Out of his mouth go forth lamps, like torches of lighted fire.
verses.textLatin: De ore ejus lampades procedunt, sicut tædæ ignis accensæ.

verses.text: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, like that of a pot heated and boiling.
verses.textLatin: De naribus ejus procedit fumus, sicut ollæ succensæ atque ferventis.

verses.text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame cometh forth out of his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Halitus ejus prunas ardere facit, et flamma de ore ejus egreditur.

verses.text: In his neck strength shall dwell, and want goeth before his face.
verses.textLatin: In collo ejus morabitur fortitudo, et faciem ejus præcedit egestas.

verses.text: The members of his flesh cleave one to another: he shall send lightnings against him, and they shall not be carried to another place.
verses.textLatin: Membra carnium ejus cohærentia sibi: mittet contra eum fulmina, et ad locum alium non ferentur.

verses.text: His heart shall be as hard as a stone, and as firm as a smith’s anvil.
verses.textLatin: Cor ejus indurabitur tamquam lapis, et stringetur quasi malleatoris incus.

verses.text: When he shall raise him up, the angels shall fear, and being affrighted shall purify themselves.
verses.textLatin: Cum sublatus fuerit, timebunt angeli, et territi purgabuntur.

verses.text: When a sword shall lay at him, it shall not be able to hold, nor a spear, nor a breastplate.
verses.textLatin: Cum apprehenderit eum gladius, subsistere non poterit, neque hasta, neque thorax:

verses.text: For he shall esteem iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
verses.textLatin: reputabit enim quasi paleas ferrum, et quasi lignum putridum æs.

verses.text: The archer shall not put him to flight, the stones of the sling are to him like stubble.
verses.textLatin: Non fugabit eum vir sagittarius: in stipulam versi sunt ei lapides fundæ.

verses.text: As stubble will he esteem the hammer, and he will laugh him to scorn who shaketh the spear.
verses.textLatin: Quasi stipulam æstimabit malleum, et deridebit vibrantem hastam.

verses.text: The beams of the sun shall be under him, and he shall strew gold under him like mire.
verses.textLatin: Sub ipso erunt radii solis, et sternet sibi aurum quasi lutum.

verses.text: He shall make the deep sea to boil like a pot, and shall make it as when ointments boil.
verses.textLatin: Fervescere faciet quasi ollam profundum mare, et ponet quasi cum unguenta bulliunt.

verses.text: A path shall shine after him, he shall esteem the deep as growing old.
verses.textLatin: Post eum lucebit semita: æstimabit abyssum quasi senescentem.

verses.text: There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one.
verses.textLatin: Non est super terram potestas quæ comparetur ei, qui factus est ut nullum timeret.

verses.text: He beholdeth every high thing, he is king over all the children of pride.
verses.textLatin: Omne sublime videt: ipse est rex super universos filios superbiæ.

verses.text: Then  Job answered the Lord, and said:
verses.textLatin: Respondens autem Job Domino, dixit:

verses.text: I know that thou canst do all things, and no thought is hid from thee.
verses.textLatin: Scio quia omnia potes, et nulla te latet cogitatio.

verses.text: Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and things that above measure exceeded my knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Quis est iste qui celat consilium absque scientia? ideo insipienter locutus sum, et quæ ultra modum excederent scientiam meam.

verses.text: Hear, and I will speak: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.
verses.textLatin: Audi, et ego loquar: interrogabo te, et responde mihi.

verses.text: With the hearing of the ear, I have heard thee, but now my eye seeth thee.
verses.textLatin: Auditu auris audivi te: nunc autem oculus meus videt te.

verses.text: Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco ipse me reprehendo, et ago pœnitentiam in favilla et cinere.

verses.text: And after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Themanite: My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends, because you have not spoken the thing that is right before me, as my servant Job hath.
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem locutus est Dominus verba hæc ad Job, dixit ad Eliphaz Themanitem: Iratus est furor meus in te, et in duos amicos tuos, quoniam non estis locuti coram me rectum, sicut servus meus Job.

verses.text: Take unto you therefore seven oxen, and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer for yourselves a holocaust: and my servant Job shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you: for you have not spoken right things before me, as my servant Job hath.
verses.textLatin: Sumite ergo vobis septem tauros et septem arietes, et ite ad servum meum Job, et offerte holocaustum pro vobis: Job autem servus meus orabit pro vobis. Faciem ejus suscipiam, ut non vobis imputetur stultitia: neque enim locuti estis ad me recta, sicut servus meus Job.

verses.text: So Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went, and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job.
verses.textLatin: Abierunt ergo Eliphaz Themanites, et Baldad Suhites, et Sophar Naamathites, et fecerunt sicut locutus fuerat Dominus ad eos: et suscepit Dominus faciem Job.

verses.text: The Lord also was turned at the penance of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
verses.textLatin: Dominus quoque conversus est ad pœnitentiam Job, cum oraret ille pro amicis suis: et addidit Dominus omnia quæcumque fuerant Job, duplicia.

verses.text: And all his brethren came to him, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and they ate bread with him in his house: and bemoaned him, and comforted him upon all the evil that God had brought upon him. And every man gave him one ewe, and one earring of gold.
verses.textLatin: Venerunt autem ad eum omnes fratres sui, et universæ sorores suæ, et cuncti qui noverant eum prius, et comederunt cum eo panem in domo ejus: et moverunt super eum caput, et consolati sunt eum super omni malo quod intulerat Dominus super eum: et dederunt ei unusquisque ovem unam, et inaurem auream unam.

verses.text: And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem benedixit novissimis Job magis quam principio ejus: et facta sunt ei quatuordecim millia ovium, et sex millia camelorum, et mille juga boum, et mille asinæ.

verses.text: And he had seven sons, and three daughters.
verses.textLatin: Et fuerunt ei septem filii, et tres filiæ.

verses.text: And he called the name of one Dies, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornustibii.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit nomen unius Diem, et nomen secundæ Cassiam, et nomen tertiæ Cornustibii.

verses.text: And there were not found in all the earth women so beautiful as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt autem inventæ mulieres speciosæ sicut filiæ Job in universa terra: deditque eis pater suus hæreditatem inter fratres earum.

verses.text: And Job lived after these things, a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children, and his children’s children, unto the fourth generation, and he died an old man, and full of days.
verses.textLatin: Vixit autem Job post hæc centum quadraginta annis, et vidit filios suos, et filios filiorum suorum usque ad quartam generationem: et mortuus est senex, et plenus dierum.

verses.text: Blessed  is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, nor sat in the chair of pestilence:
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir qui non abiit in consilio impiorum, et in via peccatorum non stetit, et in cathedra pestilentiæ non sedit;

verses.text: But his will is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he shall meditate day and night.
verses.textLatin: sed in lege Domini voluntas ejus, et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte.

verses.text: And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season. And his leaf shall not fall off: and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.
verses.textLatin: Et erit tamquam lignum quod plantatum est secus decursus aquarum, quod fructum suum dabit in tempore suo: et folium ejus non defluet; et omnia quæcumque faciet prosperabuntur.

verses.text: Not so the wicked, not so: but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Non sic impii, non sic; sed tamquam pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ.

verses.text: Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: nor sinners in the council of the just.
verses.textLatin: Ideo non resurgent impii in judicio, neque peccatores in concilio justorum:

verses.text: For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: and the way of the wicked shall perish.
verses.textLatin: quoniam novit Dominus viam justorum, et iter impiorum peribit.

verses.text: Why  have the Gentiles raged, and the people devised vain things?
verses.textLatin: Quare fremuerunt gentes, et populi meditati sunt inania?

verses.text: The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, against the Lord, and against his Christ.
verses.textLatin: Astiterunt reges terræ, et principes convenerunt in unum adversus Dominum, et adversus christum ejus.

verses.text: Let us break their bonds asunder: and let us cast away their yoke from us.
verses.textLatin: Dirumpamus vincula eorum, et projiciamus a nobis jugum ipsorum.

verses.text: He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: and the Lord shall deride them.
verses.textLatin: Qui habitat in cælis irridebit eos, et Dominus subsannabit eos.

verses.text: Then shall he speak to them in his anger, and trouble them in his rage.
verses.textLatin: Tunc loquetur ad eos in ira sua, et in furore suo conturbabit eos.

verses.text: But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, preaching his commandment.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion, montem sanctum ejus, prædicans præceptum ejus.

verses.text: The Lord hath said to me: Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.
verses.textLatin: Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu; ego hodie genui te.

verses.text: Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.
verses.textLatin: Postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terræ.

verses.text: Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.
verses.textLatin: Reges eos in virga ferrea, et tamquam vas figuli confringes eos.

verses.text: And now, O ye kings, understand: receive instruction, you that judge the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc, reges, intelligite; erudimini, qui judicatis terram.

verses.text: Serve ye the Lord with fear: and rejoice unto him with trembling.
verses.textLatin: Servite Domino in timore, et exsultate ei cum tremore.

verses.text: Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, and you perish from the just way.
verses.textLatin: Apprehendite disciplinam, nequando irascatur Dominus, et pereatis de via justa.

verses.text: When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, blessed are all they that trust in him.
verses.textLatin: Cum exarserit in brevi ira ejus, beati omnes qui confidunt in eo.

verses.text: The psalm of David when he fled from the face of his son Absalom. (2 Kings 15).
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, cum fugeret a facie Absalom filii sui.

verses.text: Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? many are they who rise up against me.
verses.textLatin: Domine, quid multiplicati sunt qui tribulant me? Multi insurgunt adversum me;

verses.text: Many say to my soul: There is no salvation for him in his God.
verses.textLatin: multi dicunt animæ meæ: Non est salus ipsi in Deo ejus.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, art my protector, my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem Domine, susceptor meus es, gloria mea, et exaltans caput meum.

verses.text: I have cried to the Lord with my voice: and he hath heard me from his holy hill.
verses.textLatin: Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi; et exaudivit me de monte sancto suo.

verses.text: I have slept and have taken my rest: and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.
verses.textLatin: Ego dormivi, et soporatus sum; et exsurrexi, quia Dominus suscepit me.

verses.text: I will not fear thousands of the people surrounding me: arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.
verses.textLatin: Non timebo millia populi circumdantis me. Exsurge, Domine; salvum me fac, Deus meus.

verses.text: For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu percussisti omnes adversantes mihi sine causa; dentes peccatorum contrivisti.

verses.text: Salvation is of the Lord: and thy blessing is upon thy people.
verses.textLatin: Domini est salus; et super populum tuum benedictio tua.

verses.text: Unto the end, in verses. A psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in carminibus. Psalmus David.

verses.text: When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me. Have mercy on me: and hear my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Cum invocarem exaudivit me Deus justitiæ meæ, in tribulatione dilatasti mihi. Miserere mei, et exaudi orationem meam.

verses.text: O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?
verses.textLatin: Filii hominum, usquequo gravi corde? ut quid diligitis vanitatem, et quæritis mendacium?

verses.text: Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.
verses.textLatin: Et scitote quoniam mirificavit Dominus sanctum suum; Dominus exaudiet me cum clamavero ad eum.

verses.text: Be ye angry, and sin not: the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.
verses.textLatin: Irascimini, et nolite peccare; quæ dicitis in cordibus vestris, in cubilibus vestris compungimini.

verses.text: Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: many say, Who sheweth us good things?
verses.textLatin: Sacrificate sacrificium justitiæ, et sperate in Domino. Multi dicunt: Quis ostendit nobis bona?

verses.text: The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: thou hast given gladness in my heart.
verses.textLatin: Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine: dedisti lætitiam in corde meo.

verses.text: By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, they are multiplied:
verses.textLatin: A fructu frumenti, vini, et olei sui, multiplicati sunt.

verses.text: In peace in the self same I will sleep, and I will rest:
verses.textLatin: In pace in idipsum dormiam, et requiescam;

verses.text: For thou, O Lord, singularly hast settled me in hope.
verses.textLatin: quoniam tu, Domine, singulariter in spe constituisti me.

verses.text: Unto the end, for her that obtaineth the inheritance. A psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro ea quæ hæreditatem consequitur. Psalmus David.

verses.text: Give ear, O Lord, to my words, understand my cry.
verses.textLatin: Verba mea auribus percipe, Domine; intellige clamorem meum.

verses.text: Hearken to the voice of my prayer, O my King and my God.
verses.textLatin: Intende voci orationis meæ, rex meus et Deus meus.

verses.text: For to thee will I pray: O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ad te orabo, Domine: mane exaudies vocem meam.

verses.text: In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Mane astabo tibi, et videbo quoniam non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es.

verses.text: Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.
verses.textLatin: Neque habitabit juxta te malignus, neque permanebunt injusti ante oculos tuos.

verses.text: Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie. The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor.
verses.textLatin: Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem; perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium. Virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus.

verses.text: But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy, I will come into thy house; I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in multitudine misericordiæ tuæ introibo in domum tuam; adorabo ad templum sanctum tuum in timore tuo.

verses.text: Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: Domine, deduc me in justitia tua: propter inimicos meos dirige in conspectu tuo viam meam.

verses.text: For there is no truth in their mouth: their heart is vain.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam non est in ore eorum veritas; cor eorum vanum est.

verses.text: Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: judge them, O God. Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: for they have provoked thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sepulchrum patens est guttur eorum; linguis suis dolose agebant: judica illos, Deus. Decidant a cogitationibus suis; secundum multitudinem impietatum eorum expelle eos, quoniam irritaverunt te, Domine.

verses.text: But let all them be glad that hope in thee: they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them. And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee.
verses.textLatin: Et lætentur omnes qui sperant in te; in æternum exsultabunt, et habitabis in eis. Et gloriabuntur in te omnes qui diligunt nomen tuum,

verses.text: For thou wilt bless the just. O Lord, thou hast crowned us, as with a shield of thy good will.
verses.textLatin: quoniam tu benedices justo. Domine, ut scuto bonæ voluntatis tuæ coronasti nos.

verses.text: Unto the end, in verses, a psalm for David, for the octave.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in carminibus. Psalmus David. Pro octava.

verses.text: O Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, nor chastise me in thy wrath.
verses.textLatin: Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me, neque in ira tua corripias me.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Domine, quoniam infirmus sum; sana me, Domine, quoniam conturbata sunt ossa mea.

verses.text: And my soul is troubled exceedingly: but thou, O Lord, how long?
verses.textLatin: Et anima mea turbata est valde; sed tu, Domine, usquequo?

verses.text: Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: O save me for thy mercy’s sake.
verses.textLatin: Convertere, Domine, et eripe animam meam; salvum me fac propter misericordiam tuam.

verses.text: For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: and who shall confess to thee in hell?
verses.textLatin: Quoniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui; in inferno autem quis confitebitur tibi?

verses.text: I have laboured in my groanings, every night I will wash my bed: I will water my couch with my tears.
verses.textLatin: Laboravi in gemitu meo; lavabo per singulas noctes lectum meum: lacrimis meis stratum meum rigabo.

verses.text: My eye is troubled through indignation: I have grown old amongst all my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Turbatus est a furore oculus meus; inveteravi inter omnes inimicos meos.

verses.text: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
verses.textLatin: Discedite a me omnes qui operamini iniquitatem, quoniam exaudivit Dominus vocem fletus mei.

verses.text: The Lord hath heard my supplication: the Lord hath received my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Exaudivit Dominus deprecationem meam; Dominus orationem meam suscepit.

verses.text: Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.
verses.textLatin: Erubescant, et conturbentur vehementer, omnes inimici mei; convertantur, et erubescant valde velociter.

verses.text: The psalm of David, which he sung to the Lord, for the words of Chusi, the son of Jemini. (2 Kings 16.)
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, quem cantavit Domino pro verbis Chusi, filii Jemini.

verses.text: O Lord, my God, in thee have I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus meus, in te speravi; salvum me fac ex omnibus persequentibus me, et libera me:

verses.text: Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.
verses.textLatin: nequando rapiat ut leo animam meam, dum non est qui redimat, neque qui salvum faciat.

verses.text: O Lord, my God, if I have done this thing, if there be iniquity in my hands:
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus meus, si feci istud, si est iniquitas in manibus meis,

verses.text: If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.
verses.textLatin: si reddidi retribuentibus mihi mala, decidam merito ab inimicis meis inanis.

verses.text: Let the enemy pursue my soul, and take it, and tread down my life, on the earth, and bring down my glory to the dust.
verses.textLatin: Persequatur inimicus animam meam, et comprehendat; et conculcet in terra vitam meam, et gloriam meam in pulverem deducat.

verses.text: Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies. And arise, O Lord, my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded:
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Domine, in ira tua, et exaltare in finibus inimicorum meorum: et exsurge, Domine Deus meus, in præcepto quod mandasti,

verses.text: and a congregation of people shall surround thee. And for their sakes return thou on high.
verses.textLatin: et synagoga populorum circumdabit te: et propter hanc in altum regredere:

verses.text: The Lord judgeth the people. Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, and according to my innocence in me.
