verses.textLatin: Dominus judicat populos. Judica me, Domine, secundum justitiam meam, et secundum innocentiam meam super me.

verses.text: The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: the searcher of hearts and reins is God.
verses.textLatin: Consumetur nequitia peccatorum, et diriges justum, scrutans corda et renes, Deus.

verses.text: Just is my help from the Lord: who saveth the upright of heart.
verses.textLatin: Justum adjutorium meum a Domino, qui salvos facit rectos corde.

verses.text: God is a just judge, strong and patient: is he angry every day?
verses.textLatin: Deus judex justus, fortis, et patiens; numquid irascitur per singulos dies?

verses.text: Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
verses.textLatin: Nisi conversi fueritis, gladium suum vibrabit; arcum suum tetendit, et paravit illum.

verses.text: And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.
verses.textLatin: Et in eo paravit vasa mortis, sagittas suas ardentibus effecit.

verses.text: Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Ecce parturiit injustitiam; concepit dolorem, et peperit iniquitatem.

verses.text: He hath opened a pit and dug it: and he is fallen into the hole he made.
verses.textLatin: Lacum aperuit, et effodit eum; et incidit in foveam quam fecit.

verses.text: His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.
verses.textLatin: Convertetur dolor ejus in caput ejus, et in verticem ipsius iniquitas ejus descendet.

verses.text: I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: and will sing to the name of the Lord the most high.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor Domino secundum justitiam ejus, et psallam nomini Domini altissimi.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the presses: a psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro torcularibus. Psalmus David.

verses.text: O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is thy name in the whole earth! For thy magnificence is elevated above the heavens.
verses.textLatin: Domine, Dominus noster, quam admirabile est nomen tuum in universa terra! quoniam elevata est magnificentia tua super cælos.

verses.text: Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.
verses.textLatin: Ex ore infantium et lactentium perfecisti laudem propter inimicos tuos, ut destruas inimicum et ultorem.

verses.text: For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam videbo cælos tuos, opera digitorum tuorum, lunam et stellas quæ tu fundasti.

verses.text: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man that thou visitest him?
verses.textLatin: Quid est homo, quod memor es ejus? aut filius hominis, quoniam visitas eum?

verses.text: Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour:
verses.textLatin: Minuisti eum paulominus ab angelis; gloria et honore coronasti eum;

verses.text: and hast set him over the works of thy hands.
verses.textLatin: et constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum.

verses.text: Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.
verses.textLatin: Omnia subjecisti sub pedibus ejus, oves et boves universas, insuper et pecora campi,

verses.text: The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, that pass through the paths of the sea.
verses.textLatin: volucres cæli, et pisces maris qui perambulant semitas maris.

verses.text: O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is thy name in all the earth!
verses.textLatin: Domine, Dominus noster, quam admirabile est nomen tuum in universa terra!

verses.text: Unto the end, for the hidden things of the Son. A psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro occultis filii. Psalmus David.

verses.text: I will give praise to thee, O Lord, with my whole heart: I will relate all thy wonders.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo; narrabo omnia mirabilia tua.

verses.text: I will be glad, and rejoice in thee: I will sing to thy name, O thou most high.
verses.textLatin: Lætabor et exsultabo in te; psallam nomini tuo, Altissime.

verses.text: When my enemy shall be turned back: they shall be weakened, and perish before thy face.
verses.textLatin: In convertendo inimicum meum retrorsum; infirmabuntur, et peribunt a facie tua.

verses.text: For thou hast maintained my judgment and my cause: thou hast sat on the throne, who judgest justice.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam fecisti judicium meum et causam meam; sedisti super thronum, qui judicas justitiam.

verses.text: Thou hast rebuked the Gentiles, and the wicked one hath perished: thou hast blotted out their name for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Increpasti gentes, et periit impius: nomen eorum delesti in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: The swords of the enemy have failed unto the end: and their cities thou hast destroyed. Their memory hath perished with a noise:
verses.textLatin: Inimici defecerunt frameæ in finem, et civitates eorum destruxisti. Periit memoria eorum cum sonitu;

verses.text: but the Lord remaineth for ever. He hath prepared his throne in judgment:
verses.textLatin: et Dominus in æternum permanet. Paravit in judicio thronum suum,

verses.text: and he shall judge the world in equity, he shall judge the people in justice.
verses.textLatin: et ipse judicabit orbem terræ in æquitate: judicabit populos in justitia.

verses.text: And the Lord is become a refuge for the poor: a helper in due time in tribulation.
verses.textLatin: Et factus est Dominus refugium pauperi; adjutor in opportunitatibus, in tribulatione.

verses.text: And let them trust in thee who know thy name: for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et sperent in te qui noverunt nomen tuum, quoniam non dereliquisti quærentes te, Domine.

verses.text: Sing ye to the Lord, who dwelleth in Sion: declare his ways among the Gentiles:
verses.textLatin: Psallite Domino qui habitat in Sion; annuntiate inter gentes studia ejus:

verses.text: For requiring their blood, he hath remembered them: he hath not forgotten the cry of the poor.
verses.textLatin: quoniam requirens sanguinem eorum recordatus est; non est oblitus clamorem pauperum.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O Lord: see my humiliation which I suffer from my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Domine: vide humilitatem meam de inimicis meis,

verses.text: Thou that liftest me up from the gates of death, that I may declare all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.
verses.textLatin: qui exaltas me de portis mortis, ut annuntiem omnes laudationes tuas in portis filiæ Sion:

verses.text: I will rejoice in thy salvation: the Gentiles have stuck fast in the destruction which they prepared. Their foot hath been taken in the very snare which they hid.
verses.textLatin: exultabo in salutari tuo. Infixæ sunt gentes in interitu quem fecerunt; in laqueo isto quem absconderunt comprehensus est pes eorum.

verses.text: The Lord shall be known when he executeth judgments: the sinner hath been caught in the works of his own hands.
verses.textLatin: Cognoscetur Dominus judicia faciens; in operibus manuum suarum comprehensus est peccator.

verses.text: The wicked shall be turned into hell, all the nations that forget God.
verses.textLatin: Convertantur peccatores in infernum, omnes gentes quæ obliviscuntur Deum.

verses.text: For the poor man shall not be forgotten to the end: the patience of the poor shall not perish for ever.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam non in finem oblivio erit pauperis; patientia pauperum non peribit in finem.

verses.text: Arise, O Lord, let not man be strengthened: let the Gentiles be judged in thy sight.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Domine; non confortetur homo: judicentur gentes in conspectu tuo.

verses.text: Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them: that the Gentiles may know themselves to be but men.  PSALM 10 ACCORDING TO THE HEBREWS.
verses.textLatin: Constitue, Domine, legislatorem super eos, ut sciant gentes quoniam homines sunt. PSALMUS X. SECUNDUM HEBRÆOS

verses.text: Why, O Lord, hast thou retired afar off? why dost thou slight us in our wants, in the time of trouble?
verses.textLatin: Ut quid, Domine, recessisti longe; despicis in opportunitatibus, in tribulatione?

verses.text: Whilst the wicked man is proud, the poor is set on fire: they are caught in the counsels which they devise.
verses.textLatin: Dum superbit impius, incenditur pauper: comprehenduntur in consiliis quibus cogitant.

verses.text: For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul: and the unjust man is blessed.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam laudatur peccator in desideriis animæ suæ, et iniquus benedicitur.

verses.text: The sinner hath provoked the Lord, according to the multitude of his wrath he will not seek him:
verses.textLatin: Exacerbavit Dominum peccator: secundum multitudinem iræ suæ, non quæret.

verses.text: God is not before his eyes: his ways are filthy at all times. Thy judgments are removed from his sight: he shall rule over all his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Non est Deus in conspectu ejus; inquinatæ sunt viæ illius in omni tempore. Auferuntur judicia tua a facie ejus; omnium inimicorum suorum dominabitur.

verses.text: For he hath said in his heart: I shall not be moved from generation to generation, and shall be without evil.
verses.textLatin: Dixit enim in corde suo: Non movebor a generatione in generationem, sine malo.

verses.text: His mouth is full of cursing, and of bitterness, and of deceit: under his tongue are labour and sorrow.
verses.textLatin: Cujus maledictione os plenum est, et amaritudine, et dolo; sub lingua ejus labor et dolor.

verses.text: He sitteth in ambush with the rich in private places, that he may kill the innocent.
verses.textLatin: Sedet in insidiis cum divitibus in occultis, ut interficiat innocentem.

verses.text: His eyes are upon the poor man: he lieth in wait in secret like a lion in his den. He lieth in ambush that he may catch the poor man: to catch the poor, whilst he draweth him to him.
verses.textLatin: Oculi ejus in pauperem respiciunt; insidiatur in abscondito, quasi leo in spelunca sua. Insidiatur ut rapiat pauperem; rapere pauperem dum attrahit eum.

verses.text: In his net he will bring him down, he will crouch and fall, when he shall have power over the poor.
verses.textLatin: In laqueo suo humiliabit eum; inclinabit se, et cadet cum dominatus fuerit pauperum.

verses.text: For he hath said in his heart: God hath forgotten, he hath turned away his face, not to see to the end.
verses.textLatin: Dixit enim in corde suo: Oblitus est Deus; avertit faciem suam, ne videat in finem.

verses.text: Arise, O Lord God, let thy hand be exalted: forget not the poor.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Domine Deus, exaltetur manus tua; ne obliviscaris pauperum.

verses.text: Wherefore hath the wicked provoked God? for he hath said in his heart: He will not require it.
verses.textLatin: Propter quid irritavit impius Deum? dixit enim in corde suo: Non requiret.

verses.text: Thou seest it, for thou considerest labour and sorrow: that thou mayst deliver them into thy hands. To thee is the poor man left: thou wilt be a helper to the orphan.
verses.textLatin: Vides, quoniam tu laborem et dolorem consideras, ut tradas eos in manus tuas. Tibi derelictus est pauper; orphano tu eris adjutor.

verses.text: Break thou the arm of the sinner and of the malignant: his sin shall be sought, and shall not be found.
verses.textLatin: Contere brachium peccatoris et maligni; quæretur peccatum illius, et non invenietur.

verses.text: The Lord shall reign to eternity, yea, for ever and ever: ye Gentiles shall perish from his land.
verses.textLatin: Dominus regnabit in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi; peribitis, gentes, de terra illius.

verses.text: The Lord hath heard the desire of the poor: thy ear hath heard the preparation of their heart.
verses.textLatin: Desiderium pauperum exaudivit Dominus; præparationem cordis eorum audivit auris tua:

verses.text: To judge for the fatherless and for the humble, that man may no more presume to magnify himself upon earth.
verses.textLatin: judicare pupillo et humili, ut non apponat ultra magnificare se homo super terram.

verses.text: Unto the end. A psalm to David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: In the Lord I put my trust: how then do you say to my soul: Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow.
verses.textLatin: In Domino confido; quomodo dicitis animæ meæ: Transmigra in montem sicut passer?

verses.text: For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow; they have prepared their arrows in the quiver; to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ecce peccatores intenderunt arcum; paraverunt sagittas suas in pharetra, ut sagittent in obscuro rectos corde:

verses.text: For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: but what has the just man done?
verses.textLatin: quoniam quæ perfecisti destruxerunt; justus autem, quid fecit?

verses.text: The Lord is in his holy temple, the Lord’s throne is in heaven. His eyes look on the poor man: his eyelids examine the sons of men.
verses.textLatin: Dominus in templo sancto suo; Dominus in cælo sedes ejus. Oculi ejus in pauperem respiciunt; palpebræ ejus interrogant filios hominum.

verses.text: The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Dominus interrogat justum et impium; qui autem diligit iniquitatem, odit animam suam.

verses.text: He shall rain snares upon sinners: fire and brimstone and storms of winds shall be the portion of their cup.
verses.textLatin: Pluet super peccatores laqueos; ignis et sulphur, et spiritus procellarum, pars calicis eorum.

verses.text: For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: his countenance hath beheld righteousness.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam justus Dominus, et justitias dilexit: æquitatem vidit vultus ejus.

verses.text: Unto the end; for the octave, a psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro octava. Psalmus David.

verses.text: Save me, O Lord, for there is now no saint: truths are decayed from among the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Salvum me fac, Domine, quoniam defecit sanctus, quoniam diminutæ sunt veritates a filiis hominum.

verses.text: They have spoken vain things every one to his neighbour: with deceitful lips, and with a double heart have they spoken.
verses.textLatin: Vana locuti sunt unusquisque ad proximum suum; labia dolosa, in corde et corde locuti sunt.

verses.text: May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things.
verses.textLatin: Disperdat Dominus universa labia dolosa, et linguam magniloquam.

verses.text: Who have said: We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is Lord over us?
verses.textLatin: Qui dixerunt: Linguam nostram magnificabimus; labia nostra a nobis sunt. Quis noster dominus est?

verses.text: By reason of the misery of the needy, and the groans of the poor, now will I arise, saith the Lord. I will set him in safety; I will deal confidently in his regard.
verses.textLatin: Propter miseriam inopum, et gemitum pauperum, nunc exsurgam, dicit Dominus. Ponam in salutari; fiducialiter agam in eo.

verses.text: The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times.
verses.textLatin: Eloquia Domini, eloquia casta; argentum igne examinatum, probatum terræ, purgatum septuplum.

verses.text: Thou, O Lord, wilt preserve us: and keep us from this generation for ever.
verses.textLatin: Tu, Domine, servabis nos, et custodies nos a generatione hac in æternum.

verses.text: The wicked walk round about: according to thy highness, thou hast multiplied the children of men.
verses.textLatin: In circuitu impii ambulant: secundum altitudinem tuam multiplicasti filios hominum.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David.  How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end? how long dost thou turn away thy face from me?
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.  Usquequo, Domine, oblivisceris me in finem? usquequo avertis faciem tuam a me?

verses.text: How long shall I take counsels in my soul, sorrow in my heart all the day?
verses.textLatin: quamdiu ponam consilia in anima mea; dolorem in corde meo per diem?

verses.text: How long shall my enemy be exalted over me?
verses.textLatin: usquequo exaltabitur inimicus meus super me?

verses.text: Consider, and hear me, O Lord, my God. Enlighten my eyes, that I never sleep in death:
verses.textLatin: Respice, et exaudi me, Domine Deus meus. Illumina oculos meos, ne umquam obdormiam in morte;

verses.text: lest at any time my enemy say: I have prevailed against him. They that trouble me, will rejoice when I am moved:
verses.textLatin: nequando dicat inimicus meus: Prævalui adversus eum. Qui tribulant me exsultabunt si motus fuero;

verses.text: but I have trusted in thy mercy. My heart shall rejoice in thy salvation: I will sing to the Lord, who giveth me good things: yea I will sing to the name of the Lord the most high.
verses.textLatin: ego autem in misericordia tua speravi. Exsultabit cor meum in salutari tuo. Cantabo Domino qui bona tribuit mihi; et psallam nomini Domini altissimi.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David. THE fool hath said in his heart: There is no God. They are corrupt, and are become abominable in their ways: there is none that doth good, no not one.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David. Dixit insipiens in corde suo: Non est Deus. Corrupti sunt, et abominabiles facti sunt in studiis suis; non est qui faciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

verses.text: The Lord hath looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there be any that understand and seek God.
verses.textLatin: Dominus de cælo prospexit super filios hominum, ut videat si est intelligens, aut requirens Deum.

verses.text: They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together: there is none that doth good, no not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre: with their tongues they acted deceitfully; the poison of asps is under their lips. Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; their feet are swift to shed blood. Destruction and unhappiness in their ways: and the way of peace they have not known: there is no fear of God before their eyes.
verses.textLatin: Omnes declinaverunt, simul inutiles facti sunt. Non est qui faciat bonum, non est usque ad unum. Sepulchrum patens est guttur eorum; linguis suis dolose agebant. Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum, quorum os maledictione et amaritudine plenum est; veloces pedes eorum ad effundendum sanguinem. Contritio et infelicitas in viis eorum, et viam pacis non cognoverunt; non est timor Dei ante oculos eorum.

verses.text: Shall not all they know that work iniquity, who devour my people as they eat bread?
verses.textLatin: Nonne cognoscent omnes qui operantur iniquitatem, qui devorant plebem meam sicut escam panis?

verses.text: They have not called upon the Lord: there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.
verses.textLatin: Dominum non invocaverunt; illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non erat timor.

verses.text: For the Lord is in the just generation: you have confounded the counsel of the poor man, but the Lord is his hope.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam Dominus in generatione justa est: consilium inopis confudistis, quoniam Dominus spes ejus est.

verses.text: Who shall give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? when the Lord shall have turned away the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad.
verses.textLatin: Quis dabit ex Sion salutare Israël? Cum averterit Dominus captivitatem plebis suæ, exsultabit Jacob, et lætabitur Israël.

verses.text: A psalm for David. Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? or who shall rest in thy holy hill?
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David. Domine, quis habitabit in tabernaculo tuo? aut quis requiescet in monte sancto tuo?

verses.text: He that walketh without blemish, and worketh justice:
verses.textLatin: Qui ingreditur sine macula, et operatur justitiam;

verses.text: He that speaketh truth in his heart, who hath not used deceit in his tongue: Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.
verses.textLatin: qui loquitur veritatem in corde suo: qui non egit dolum in lingua sua, nec fecit proximo suo malum, et opprobrium non accepit adversus proximos suos.

verses.text: In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord. He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not;
verses.textLatin: Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus; timentes autem Dominum glorificat. Qui jurat proximo suo, et non decipit;

verses.text: he that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent: He that doth these things, shall not be moved for ever.
verses.textLatin: qui pecuniam suam non dedit ad usuram, et munera super innocentem non accepit: qui facit hæc non movebitur in æternum.

verses.text: The inscription of a title to David himself. Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee.
verses.textLatin: Tituli inscriptio, ipsi David. Conserva me, Domine, quoniam speravi in te.

verses.text: I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.
verses.textLatin: Dixi Domino: Deus meus es tu, quoniam bonorum meorum non eges.

verses.text: To the saints, who are in his land, he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.
verses.textLatin: Sanctis qui sunt in terra ejus, mirificavit omnes voluntates meas in eis.

verses.text: Their infirmities were multiplied: afterwards they made haste. I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.
verses.textLatin: Multiplicatæ sunt infirmitates eorum: postea acceleraverunt. Non congregabo conventicula eorum de sanguinibus, nec memor ero nominum eorum per labia mea.

verses.text: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.
verses.textLatin: Dominus pars hæreditatis meæ, et calicis mei: tu es qui restitues hæreditatem meam mihi.

verses.text: The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: for my inheritance is goodly to me.
verses.textLatin: Funes ceciderunt mihi in præclaris; etenim hæreditas mea præclara est mihi.

verses.text: I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: moreover, my reins also have corrected me even till night.
verses.textLatin: Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum; insuper et usque ad noctem increpuerunt me renes mei.

verses.text: I set the Lord always in my sight: for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.
verses.textLatin: Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper: quoniam a dextris est mihi, ne commovear.

verses.text: Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc lætatum est cor meum, et exsultavit lingua mea; insuper et caro mea requiescet in spe.

verses.text: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum videre corruptionem. Notas mihi fecisti vias vitæ; adimplebis me lætitia cum vultu tuo: delectationes in dextera tua usque in finem.

verses.text: The prayer of David. Hear, O Lord, my justice: attend to my supplication. Give ear unto my prayer, which proceedeth not from deceitful lips.
verses.textLatin: Oratio David. Exaudi, Domine, justitiam meam; intende deprecationem meam. Auribus percipe orationem meam, non in labiis dolosis.

verses.text: Let my judgment come forth from thy countenance: let thy eyes behold the things that are equitable.
verses.textLatin: De vultu tuo judicium meum prodeat; oculi tui videant æquitates.

verses.text: Thou hast proved my heart, and visited it by night, thou hast tried me by fire: and iniquity hath not been found in me.
verses.textLatin: Probasti cor meum, et visitasti nocte; igne me examinasti, et non est inventa in me iniquitas.

verses.text: That my mouth may not speak the works of men: for the sake of the words of thy lips, I have kept hard ways.
verses.textLatin: Ut non loquatur os meum opera hominum: propter verba labiorum tuorum, ego custodivi vias duras.

verses.text: Perfect thou my goings in thy paths: that my footsteps be not moved.
verses.textLatin: Perfice gressus meos in semitis tuis, ut non moveantur vestigia mea.

verses.text: I have cried to thee, for thou, O God, hast heard me: O incline thy ear unto me, and hear my words.
verses.textLatin: Ego clamavi, quoniam exaudisti me, Deus; inclina aurem tuam mihi, et exaudi verba mea.

verses.text: Shew forth thy wonderful mercies; thou who savest them that trust in thee.
verses.textLatin: Mirifica misericordias tuas, qui salvos facis sperantes in te.

verses.text: From them that resist thy right hand keep me, as the apple of thy eye. Protect me under the shadow of thy wings.
verses.textLatin: A resistentibus dexteræ tuæ custodi me ut pupillam oculi. Sub umbra alarum tuarum protege me

verses.text: From the face of the wicked who have afflicted me. My enemies have surrounded my soul:
verses.textLatin: a facie impiorum qui me afflixerunt. Inimici mei animam meam circumdederunt;

verses.text: they have shut up their fat: their mouth hath spoken proudly.
verses.textLatin: adipem suum concluserunt: os eorum locutum est superbiam.

verses.text: They have cast me forth and now they have surrounded me: they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth.
verses.textLatin: Projicientes me nunc circumdederunt me; oculos suos statuerunt declinare in terram.

verses.text: They have taken me, as a lion prepared for the prey; and as a young lion dwelling in secret places.
verses.textLatin: Susceperunt me sicut leo paratus ad prædam, et sicut catulus leonis habitans in abditis.

verses.text: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him and supplant him; deliver my soul from the wicked one: thy sword
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Domine: præveni eum, et supplanta eum: eripe animam meam ab impio; frameam tuam

verses.text: from the enemies of thy hand. O Lord, divide them from the few of the earth in their life: their belly is filled from thy hidden stores. They are full of children: and they have left to their little ones the rest of their substance.
verses.textLatin: ab inimicis manus tuæ. Domine, a paucis de terra divide eos in vita eorum; de absconditis tuis adimpletus est venter eorum. Saturati sunt filiis, et dimiserunt reliquias suas parvulis suis.

verses.text: But as for me, I will appear before thy sight in justice: I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in justitia apparebo conspectui tuo; satiabor cum apparuerit gloria tua.

verses.text: Unto the end, for David, the servant of the Lord, who spoke to the Lord the words of this canticle, in the day that the Lord delivered him from the hands of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul. (2 Kings 22.)
verses.textLatin: In finem. Puero Domini David, qui locutus est Domino verba cantici hujus, in die qua eripuit eum Dominus de manu omnium inimicorum ejus, et de manu Saul, et dixit: (II Regum 22)

verses.text: I will love thee, O Lord, my strength:
verses.textLatin: Diligam te, Domine, fortitudo mea.

verses.text: The Lord is my firmament, my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is my helper, and in him will I put my trust. My protector and the horn of my salvation, and my support.
verses.textLatin: Dominus firmamentum meum, et refugium meum, et liberator meus. Deus meus adjutor meus, et sperabo in eum; protector meus, et cornu salutis meæ, et susceptor meus.

verses.text: Praising I will call upon the Lord: and I shall be saved from my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero.

verses.text: The sorrows of death surrounded me: and the torrents of iniquity troubled me.
verses.textLatin: Circumdederunt me dolores mortis, et torrentes iniquitatis conturbaverunt me.

verses.text: The sorrows of hell encompassed me: and the snares of death prevented me.
verses.textLatin: Dolores inferni circumdederunt me; præoccupaverunt me laquei mortis.

verses.text: In my affliction I called upon the Lord, and I cried to my God: And he heard my voice from his holy temple: and my cry before him came into his ears.
verses.textLatin: In tribulatione mea invocavi Dominum, et ad Deum meum clamavi: et exaudivit de templo sancto suo vocem meam; et clamor meus in conspectu ejus introivit in aures ejus.

verses.text: The earth shook and trembled: the foundations of the mountains were troubled and were moved, because he was angry with them.
verses.textLatin: Commota est, et contremuit terra; fundamenta montium conturbata sunt, et commota sunt: quoniam iratus est eis.

verses.text: There went up a smoke in his wrath: and a fire flamed from his face: coals were kindled by it.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit fumus in ira ejus, et ignis a facie ejus exarsit; carbones succensi sunt ab eo.

verses.text: He bowed the heavens, and came down: and darkness was under his feet.
verses.textLatin: Inclinavit cælos, et descendit, et caligo sub pedibus ejus.

verses.text: And he ascended upon the cherubim, and he flew; he flew upon the wings of the winds.
verses.textLatin: Et ascendit super cherubim, et volavit; volavit super pennas ventorum.

verses.text: And he made darkness his covert, his pavilion round about him: dark waters in the clouds of the air.
verses.textLatin: Et posuit tenebras latibulum suum; in circuitu ejus tabernaculum ejus, tenebrosa aqua in nubibus aëris.

verses.text: At the brightness that was before him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire.
verses.textLatin: Præ fulgore in conspectu ejus nubes transierunt; grando et carbones ignis.

verses.text: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the highest gave his voice: hail and coals of fire.
verses.textLatin: Et intonuit de cælo Dominus, et Altissimus dedit vocem suam: grando et carbones ignis.

verses.text: And he sent forth his arrows, and he scattered them: he multiplied lightnings, and troubled them.
verses.textLatin: Et misit sagittas suas, et dissipavit eos; fulgura multiplicavit, et conturbavit eos.

verses.text: Then the fountains of waters appeared, and the foundations of the world were discovered: At thy rebuke, O Lord, at the blast of the spirit of thy wrath.
verses.textLatin: Et apparuerunt fontes aquarum, et revelata sunt fundamenta orbis terrarum, ab increpatione tua, Domine, ab inspiratione spiritus iræ tuæ.

verses.text: He sent from on high, and took me: and received me out of many waters.
verses.textLatin: Misit de summo, et accepit me; et assumpsit me de aquis multis.

verses.text: He delivered me from my strongest enemies, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
verses.textLatin: Eripuit me de inimicis meis fortissimis, et ab his qui oderunt me. Quoniam confortati sunt super me;

verses.text: They prevented me in the day of my affliction: and the Lord became my protector.
verses.textLatin: prævenerunt me in die afflictionis meæ: et factus est Dominus protector meus.

verses.text: And he brought me forth into a large place: he saved me, because he was well pleased with me.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit me in latitudinem; salvum me fecit, quoniam voluit me,

verses.text: And the Lord will reward me according to my justice; and will repay me according to the cleanness of my hands:
verses.textLatin: et retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam, et secundum puritatem manuum mearum retribuet mihi:

verses.text: Because I have kept the ways of the Lord; and have not done wickedly against my God.
verses.textLatin: quia custodivi vias Domini, nec impie gessi a Deo meo;

verses.text: For all his judgments are in my sight: and his justices I have not put away from me.
verses.textLatin: quoniam omnia judicia ejus in conspectu meo, et justitias ejus non repuli a me.

verses.text: And I shall be spotless with him: and shall keep myself from my iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Et ero immaculatus cum eo; et observabo me ab iniquitate mea.

verses.text: And the Lord will reward me according to my justice; and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Et retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam, et secundum puritatem manuum mearum in conspectu oculorum ejus.

verses.text: With the holy, thou wilt be holy; and with the innocent man thou wilt be innocent.
verses.textLatin: Cum sancto sanctus eris, et cum viro innocente innocens eris,

verses.text: And with the elect thou wilt be elect: and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.
verses.textLatin: et cum electo electus eris, et cum perverso perverteris.

verses.text: For thou wilt save the humble people; but wilt bring down the eyes of the proud.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu populum humilem salvum facies, et oculos superborum humiliabis.

verses.text: For thou lightest my lamp, O Lord: O my God enlighten my darkness.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu illuminas lucernam meam, Domine; Deus meus, illumina tenebras meas.

verses.text: For by thee I shall be delivered from temptation; and through my God I shall go over a wall.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam in te eripiar a tentatione; et in Deo meo transgrediar murum.

verses.text: As for my God, his way is undefiled: the words of the Lord are fire tried: he is the protector of all that trust in him.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus, impolluta via ejus; eloquia Domini igne examinata: protector est omnium sperantium in se.

verses.text: For who is God but the Lord? or who is God but our God?
verses.textLatin: Quoniam quis deus præter Dominum? aut quis deus præter Deum nostrum?

verses.text: God, who hath girt me with strength; and made my way blameless.
verses.textLatin: Deus qui præcinxit me virtute, et posuit immaculatam viam meam;

verses.text: Who hath made my feet like the feet of harts: and who setteth me upon high places.
verses.textLatin: qui perfecit pedes meos tamquam cervorum, et super excelsa statuens me;

verses.text: Who teacheth my hands to war: and thou hast made my arms like a brazen bow.
verses.textLatin: qui docet manus meas ad prælium. Et posuisti, ut arcum æreum, brachia mea,

verses.text: And thou hast given me the protection of thy salvation: and thy right hand hath held me up: And thy discipline hath corrected me unto the end: and thy discipline, the same shall teach me.
verses.textLatin: et dedisti mihi protectionem salutis tuæ: et dextera tua suscepit me, et disciplina tua correxit me in finem, et disciplina tua ipsa me docebit.

verses.text: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; and my feet are not weakened.
verses.textLatin: Dilatasti gressus meos subtus me, et non sunt infirmata vestigia mea.

verses.text: I will pursue after my enemies, and overtake them: and I will not turn again till they are consumed.
verses.textLatin: Persequar inimicos meos, et comprehendam illos; et non convertar donec deficiant.

verses.text: I will break them, and they shall not be able to stand: they shall fall under my feet.
verses.textLatin: Confringam illos, nec poterunt stare; cadent subtus pedes meos.

verses.text: And thou hast girded me with strength unto battle; and hast subdued under me them that rose up against me.
verses.textLatin: Et præcinxisti me virtute ad bellum, et supplantasti insurgentes in me subtus me.

verses.text: And thou hast made my enemies turn their back upon me, and hast destroyed them that hated me.
verses.textLatin: Et inimicos meos dedisti mihi dorsum, et odientes me disperdidisti.

verses.text: They cried, but there was none to save them, to the Lord: but he heard them not.
verses.textLatin: Clamaverunt, nec erat qui salvos faceret; ad Dominum, nec exaudivit eos.

verses.text: And I shall beat them as small as the dust before the wind; I shall bring them to nought, like the dirt in the streets.
verses.textLatin: Et comminuam eos ut pulverem ante faciem venti; ut lutum platearum delebo eos.

verses.text: Thou wilt deliver me from the contradictions of the people: thou wilt make me head of the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Eripies me de contradictionibus populi; constitues me in caput gentium.

verses.text: A people, which I knew not, hath served me: at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.
verses.textLatin: Populus quem non cognovi servivit mihi; in auditu auris obedivit mihi.

verses.text: The children that are strangers have lied to me, strange children have faded away, and have halted from their paths.
verses.textLatin: Filii alieni mentiti sunt mihi, filii alieni inveterati sunt, et claudicaverunt a semitis suis.

verses.text: The Lord liveth, and blessed be my God, and let the God of my salvation be exalted:
verses.textLatin: Vivit Dominus, et benedictus Deus meus, et exaltetur Deus salutis meæ.

verses.text: O God, who avengest me, and subduest the people under me, my deliverer from my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Deus qui das vindictas mihi, et subdis populos sub me; liberator meus de inimicis meis iracundis.

verses.text: And thou wilt lift me up above them that rise up against me: from the unjust man thou wilt deliver me.
verses.textLatin: Et ab insurgentibus in me exaltabis me; a viro iniquo eripies me.

verses.text: Therefore will I give glory to thee, O Lord, among the nations, and I will sing a psalm to thy name.
verses.textLatin: Propterea confitebor tibi in nationibus, Domine, et nomini tuo psalmum dicam;

verses.text: Giving great deliverance to his king, and shewing mercy to David his anointed: and to his seed for ever.
verses.textLatin: magnificans salutes regis ejus, et faciens misericordiam christo suo David, et semini ejus usque in sæculum.

verses.text: Unto the end. A Psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: The heavens shew forth the glory of God, and the firmament declareth the work of his hands.
verses.textLatin: Cæli enarrant gloriam Dei, et opera manuum ejus annuntiat firmamentum.

verses.text: Day to day uttereth speech, and night to night sheweth knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Dies diei eructat verbum, et nox nocti indicat scientiam.

verses.text: There are no speeches nor languages, where their voices are not heard.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt loquelæ, neque sermones, quorum non audiantur voces eorum.

verses.text: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.
verses.textLatin: In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum, et in fines orbis terræ verba eorum.

verses.text: He hath set his tabernacle in the sun: and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bride chamber, Hath rejoiced as a giant to run the way:
verses.textLatin: In sole posuit tabernaculum suum; et ipse tamquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo. Exsultavit ut gigas ad currendam viam;

verses.text: His going out is from the end of heaven, And his circuit even to the end thereof: and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.
verses.textLatin: a summo cælo egressio ejus. Et occursus ejus usque ad summum ejus; nec est qui se abscondat a calore ejus.

verses.text: The law of the Lord is unspotted, converting souls: the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.
verses.textLatin: Lex Domini immaculata, convertens animas; testimonium Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis.

verses.text: The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: the commandment of the Lord is lightsome, enlightening the eyes.
verses.textLatin: Justitiæ Domini rectæ, lætificantes corda; præceptum Domini lucidum, illuminans oculos.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini sanctus, permanens in sæculum sæculi; judicia Domini vera, justificata in semetipsa,

verses.text: More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
verses.textLatin: desiderabilia super aurum et lapidem pretiosum multum, et dulciora super mel et favum.

verses.text: For thy servant keepeth them, and in keeping them there is a great reward.
verses.textLatin: Etenim servus tuus custodit ea; in custodiendis illis retributio multa.

verses.text: Who can understand sins? from my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord:
verses.textLatin: Delicta quis intelligit? ab occultis meis munda me;

verses.text: and from those of others spare thy servant. If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be without spot: and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.
verses.textLatin: et ab alienis parce servo tuo. Si mei non fuerint dominati, tunc immaculatus ero, et emundabor a delicto maximo.

verses.text: And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: and the meditation of my heart always in thy sight. O Lord, my helper, and my redeemer.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt ut complaceant eloquia oris mei, et meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper. Domine, adjutor meus, et redemptor meus.

verses.text: Unto the end. A psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: May the Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation: may the name of the God of Jacob protect thee.
verses.textLatin: Exaudiat te Dominus in die tribulationis; protegat te nomen Dei Jacob.

verses.text: May he send thee help from the sanctuary: and defend thee out of Sion.
verses.textLatin: Mittat tibi auxilium de sancto, et de Sion tueatur te.

verses.text: May he be mindful of all thy sacrifices: and may thy whole burnt offering be made fat.
verses.textLatin: Memor sit omnis sacrificii tui, et holocaustum tuum pingue fiat.

verses.text: May he give thee according to thy own heart; and confirm all thy counsels.
verses.textLatin: Tribuat tibi secundum cor tuum, et omne consilium tuum confirmet.

verses.text: We will rejoice in thy salvation; and in the name of our God we shall be exalted.
verses.textLatin: Lætabimur in salutari tuo; et in nomine Dei nostri magnificabimur.

verses.text: The Lord fulfil all thy petitions: now have I known that the Lord hath saved his anointed. He will hear him from his holy heaven: the salvation of his right hand is in powers.
verses.textLatin: Impleat Dominus omnes petitiones tuas; nunc cognovi quoniam salvum fecit Dominus christum suum. Exaudiet illum de cælo sancto suo, in potentatibus salus dexteræ ejus.

verses.text: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Hi in curribus, et hi in equis; nos autem in nomine Domini Dei nostri invocabimus.

verses.text: They are bound, and have fallen; but we are risen, and are set upright. O Lord, save the king: and hear us in the day that we shall call upon thee.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi obligati sunt, et ceciderunt; nos autem surreximus, et erecti sumus.
Domine, salvum fac regem, et exaudi nos in die qua invocaverimus te.

verses.text: Unto the end. A psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: In thy strength, O Lord, the king shall joy; and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Domine, in virtute tua lætabitur rex, et super salutare tuum exsultabit vehementer.

verses.text: Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.
verses.textLatin: Desiderium cordis ejus tribuisti ei, et voluntate labiorum ejus non fraudasti eum.

verses.text: For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam prævenisti eum in benedictionibus dulcedinis; posuisti in capite ejus coronam de lapide pretioso.

verses.text: He asked life of thee: and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Vitam petiit a te, et tribuisti ei longitudinem dierum, in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: His glory is great in thy salvation: glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.
verses.textLatin: Magna est gloria ejus in salutari tuo; gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum.

verses.text: For thou shalt give him to be a blessing for ever and ever: thou shalt make him joyful in gladness with thy countenance.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam dabis eum in benedictionem in sæculum sæculi; lætificabis eum in gaudio cum vultu tuo.

verses.text: For the king hopeth in the Lord: and through the mercy of the most High he shall not be moved.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam rex sperat in Domino, et in misericordia Altissimi non commovebitur.

verses.text: Let thy hand be found by all thy enemies: let thy right hand find out all them that hate thee.
verses.textLatin: Inveniatur manus tua omnibus inimicis tuis; dextera tua inveniat omnes qui te oderunt.

verses.text: Thou shalt make them as an oven of fire, in the time of thy anger: the Lord shall trouble them in his wrath, and fire shall devour them.
verses.textLatin: Pones eos ut clibanum ignis in tempore vultus tui: Dominus in ira sua conturbabit eos, et devorabit eos ignis.

verses.text: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth: and their seed from among the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Fructum eorum de terra perdes, et semen eorum a filiis hominum,

verses.text: For they have intended evils against thee: they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish.
verses.textLatin: quoniam declinaverunt in te mala; cogitaverunt consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire.

verses.text: For thou shalt make them turn their back: in thy remnants thou shalt prepare their face.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam pones eos dorsum; in reliquiis tuis præparabis vultum eorum.

verses.text: Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy own strength: we will sing and praise thy power.
verses.textLatin: Exaltare, Domine, in virtute tua; cantabimus et psallemus virtutes tuas.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the morning protection, a psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro susceptione matutina. Psalmus David.

verses.text: O God my God, look upon me: why hast thou forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my sins.
verses.textLatin: Deus, Deus meus, respice in me: quare me dereliquisti? longe a salute mea verba delictorum meorum.

verses.text: O my God, I shall cry by day, and thou wilt not hear: and by night, and it shall not be reputed as folly in me.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus, clamabo per diem, et non exaudies; et nocte, et non ad insipientiam mihi.

verses.text: But thou dwellest in the holy place, the praise of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem in sancto habitas, laus Israël.

verses.text: In thee have our fathers hoped: they have hoped, and thou hast delivered them.
verses.textLatin: In te speraverunt patres nostri; speraverunt, et liberasti eos.

verses.text: They cried to thee, and they were saved: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.
verses.textLatin: Ad te clamaverunt, et salvi facti sunt; in te speraverunt, et non sunt confusi.

verses.text: But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo; opprobrium hominum, et abjectio plebis.

verses.text: All they that saw me have laughed me to scorn: they have spoken with the lips, and wagged the head.
verses.textLatin: Omnes videntes me deriserunt me; locuti sunt labiis, et moverunt caput.

verses.text: He hoped in the Lord, let him deliver him: let him save him, seeing he delighteth in him.
verses.textLatin: Speravit in Domino, eripiat eum: salvum faciat eum, quoniam vult eum.

verses.text: For thou art he that hast drawn me out of the womb: my hope from the breasts of my mother.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu es qui extraxisti me de ventre, spes mea ab uberibus matris meæ.

verses.text: I was cast upon thee from the womb. From my mother’s womb thou art my God,
verses.textLatin: In te projectus sum ex utero; de ventre matris meæ Deus meus es tu:

verses.text: depart not from me. For tribulation is very near: for there is none to help me.
verses.textLatin: ne discesseris a me, quoniam tribulatio proxima est, quoniam non est qui adjuvet.

verses.text: Many calves have surrounded me: fat bulls have besieged me.
verses.textLatin: Circumdederunt me vituli multi; tauri pingues obsederunt me.

verses.text: They have opened their mouths against me, as a lion ravening and roaring.
verses.textLatin: Aperuerunt super me os suum, sicut leo rapiens et rugiens.

verses.text: I am poured out like water; and all my bones are scattered. My heart is become like wax melting in the midst of my bowels.
verses.textLatin: Sicut aqua effusus sum, et dispersa sunt omnia ossa mea: factum est cor meum tamquam cera liquescens in medio ventris mei.

verses.text: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws: and thou hast brought me down into the dust of death.
verses.textLatin: Aruit tamquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhæsit faucibus meis: et in pulverem mortis deduxisti me.

verses.text: For many dogs have encompassed me: the council of the malignant hath besieged me. They have dug my hands and feet.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi; concilium malignantium obsedit me. Foderunt manus meas et pedes meos;

verses.text: They have numbered all my bones. And they have looked and stared upon me.
verses.textLatin: dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea. Ipsi vero consideraverunt et inspexerunt me.

verses.text: They parted my garments amongst them; and upon my vesture they cast lots.
verses.textLatin: Diviserunt sibi vestimenta mea, et super vestem meam miserunt sortem.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, remove not thy help to a distance from me; look towards my defence.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, Domine, ne elongaveris auxilium tuum a me; ad defensionem meam conspice.

verses.text: Deliver, O God, my soul from the sword: my only one from the hand of the dog.
verses.textLatin: Erue a framea, Deus, animam meam, et de manu canis unicam meam.

verses.text: Save me from the lion’s mouth; and my lowness from the horns of the unicorns.
verses.textLatin: Salva me ex ore leonis, et a cornibus unicornium humilitatem meam.

verses.text: I will declare thy name to my brethren: in the midst of the church will I praise thee.
verses.textLatin: Narrabo nomen tuum fratribus meis; in medio ecclesiæ laudabo te.

verses.text: Ye that fear the Lord, praise him: all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him.
verses.textLatin: Qui timetis Dominum, laudate eum; universum semen Jacob, glorificate eum.

verses.text: Let all the seed of Israel fear him: because he hath not slighted nor despised the supplication of the poor man. Neither hath he turned away his face from me: and when I cried to him he heard me.
verses.textLatin: Timeat eum omne semen Israël, quoniam non sprevit, neque despexit deprecationem pauperis, nec avertit faciem suam a me: et cum clamarem ad eum, exaudivit me.

verses.text: With thee is my praise in a great church: I will pay my vows in the sight of them that fear him.
verses.textLatin: Apud te laus mea in ecclesia magna; vota mea reddam in conspectu timentium eum.

verses.text: The poor shall eat and shall be filled: and they shall praise the Lord that seek him: their hearts shall live for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Edent pauperes, et saturabuntur, et laudabunt Dominum qui requirunt eum: vivent corda eorum in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: All the ends of the earth shall remember, and shall be converted to the Lord: And all the kindreds of the Gentiles shall adore in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Reminiscentur et convertentur ad Dominum universi fines terræ; et adorabunt in conspectu ejus universæ familiæ gentium:

verses.text: For the kingdom is the Lord’s; and he shall have dominion over the nations.
verses.textLatin: quoniam Domini est regnum, et ipse dominabitur gentium.

verses.text: All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and have adored: all they that go down to the earth shall fall before him.
verses.textLatin: Manducaverunt et adoraverunt omnes pingues terræ; in conspectu ejus cadent omnes qui descendunt in terram.

verses.text: And to him my soul shall live: and my seed shall serve him.
verses.textLatin: Et anima mea illi vivet; et semen meum serviet ipsi.

verses.text: There shall be declared to the Lord a generation to come: and the heavens shall shew forth his justice to a people that shall be born, which the Lord hath made.
verses.textLatin: Annuntiabitur Domino generatio ventura; et annuntiabunt cæli justitiam ejus populo qui nascetur, quem fecit Dominus.

verses.text: A psalm for David. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David. Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit:

verses.text: He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment:
verses.textLatin: in loco pascuæ, ibi me collocavit. Super aquam refectionis educavit me;

verses.text: he hath converted my soul. He hath led me on the paths of justice, for his own name’s sake.
verses.textLatin: animam meam convertit. Deduxit me super semitas justitiæ propter nomen suum.

verses.text: For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me.
verses.textLatin: Nam etsi ambulavero in medio umbræ mortis, non timebo mala, quoniam tu mecum es. Virga tua, et baculus tuus, ipsa me consolata sunt.

verses.text: Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil; and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!
verses.textLatin: Parasti in conspectu meo mensam adversus eos qui tribulant me; impinguasti in oleo caput meum: et calix meus inebrians, quam præclarus est!

verses.text: And thy mercy will follow me all the days of my life. And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days.
verses.textLatin: Et misericordia tua subsequetur me omnibus diebus vitæ meæ; et ut inhabitem in domo Domini in longitudinem dierum.

verses.text: On the first day of the week, a psalm for David. The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: the world, and all they that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Prima sabbati. Psalmus David. Domini est terra, et plenitudo ejus; orbis terrarum, et universi qui habitant in eo.

verses.text: For he hath founded it upon the seas; and hath prepared it upon the rivers.
verses.textLatin: Quia ipse super maria fundavit eum, et super flumina præparavit eum.

verses.text: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: or who shall stand in his holy place?
verses.textLatin: Quis ascendet in montem Domini? aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?

verses.text: The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Innocens manibus et mundo corde, qui non accepit in vano animam suam, nec juravit in dolo proximo suo:

verses.text: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and mercy from God his Saviour.
verses.textLatin: hic accipiet benedictionem a Domino, et misericordiam a Deo salutari suo.

verses.text: This is the generation of them that seek him, of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est generatio quærentium eum, quærentium faciem Dei Jacob.

verses.text: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory shall enter in.
verses.textLatin: Attollite portas, principes, vestras, et elevamini, portæ æternales, et introibit rex gloriæ.

verses.text: Who is this King of Glory? the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle.
verses.textLatin: Quis est iste rex gloriæ? Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio.

verses.text: Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: and the King of Glory shall enter in.
verses.textLatin: Attollite portas, principes, vestras, et elevamini, portæ æternales, et introibit rex gloriæ.

verses.text: Who is this King of Glory? the Lord of hosts, he is the King of Glory.
verses.textLatin: Quis est iste rex gloriæ? Dominus virtutum ipse est rex gloriæ.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David. To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David. Ad te, Domine, levavi animam meam:

verses.text: In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus, in te confido; non erubescam.

verses.text: Neither let my enemies laugh at me: for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Neque irrideant me inimici mei: etenim universi qui sustinent te, non confundentur.

verses.text: Let all them be confounded that act unjust things without cause. Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, and teach me thy paths.
verses.textLatin: Confundantur omnes iniqua agentes supervacue. Vias tuas, Domine, demonstra mihi, et semitas tuas edoce me.

verses.text: Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Dirige me in veritate tua, et doce me, quia tu es Deus salvator meus, et te sustinui tota die.

verses.text: Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.
verses.textLatin: Reminiscere miserationum tuarum, Domine, et misericordiarum tuarum quæ a sæculo sunt.

verses.text: The sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember. According to thy mercy remember thou me: for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Delicta juventutis meæ, et ignorantias meas, ne memineris. Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu, propter bonitatem tuam, Domine.

verses.text: The Lord is sweet and righteous: therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.
verses.textLatin: Dulcis et rectus Dominus; propter hoc legem dabit delinquentibus in via.

verses.text: He will guide the mild in judgment: he will teach the meek his ways.
verses.textLatin: Diriget mansuetos in judicio; docebit mites vias suas.

verses.text: All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.
verses.textLatin: Universæ viæ Domini, misericordia et veritas, requirentibus testamentum ejus et testimonia ejus.

verses.text: For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: for it is great.
verses.textLatin: Propter nomen tuum, Domine, propitiaberis peccato meo; multum est enim.

verses.text: Who is the man that feareth the Lord? He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.
verses.textLatin: Quis est homo qui timet Dominum? legem statuit ei in via quam elegit.

verses.text: His soul shall dwell in good things: and his seed shall inherit the land.
verses.textLatin: Anima ejus in bonis demorabitur, et semen ejus hæreditabit terram.

verses.text: The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.
verses.textLatin: Firmamentum est Dominus timentibus eum; et testamentum ipsius ut manifestetur illis.

verses.text: My eyes are ever towards the Lord: for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.
verses.textLatin: Oculi mei semper ad Dominum, quoniam ipse evellet de laqueo pedes meos.

verses.text: Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; for I am alone and poor.
verses.textLatin: Respice in me, et miserere mei, quia unicus et pauper sum ego.

verses.text: The troubles of my heart are multiplied: deliver me from my necessities.
verses.textLatin: Tribulationes cordis mei multiplicatæ sunt: de necessitatibus meis erue me.

verses.text: See my abjection and my labour; and forgive me all my sins.
verses.textLatin: Vide humilitatem meam et laborem meum, et dimitte universa delicta mea.

verses.text: Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, and have hated me with an unjust hatred.
verses.textLatin: Respice inimicos meos, quoniam multiplicati sunt, et odio iniquo oderunt me.

verses.text: Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.
verses.textLatin: Custodi animam meam, et erue me: non erubescam, quoniam speravi in te.

verses.text: The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: because I have waited on thee.
verses.textLatin: Innocentes et recti adhæserunt mihi, quia sustinui te.

verses.text: Deliver Israel, O God, from all his tribulations.
verses.textLatin: Libera, Deus, Israël ex omnibus tribulationibus suis.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David. Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David. Judica me, Domine, quoniam ego in innocentia mea ingressus sum, et in Domino sperans non infirmabor.

verses.text: Prove me, O Lord, and try me; burn my reins and my heart.
verses.textLatin: Proba me, Domine, et tenta me; ure renes meos et cor meum.

verses.text: For thy mercy is before my eyes; and I am well pleased with thy truth.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam misericordia tua ante oculos meos est, et complacui in veritate tua.

verses.text: I have not sat with the council of vanity: neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.
verses.textLatin: Non sedi cum concilio vanitatis, et cum iniqua gerentibus non introibo.

verses.text: I have hated the assembly of the malignant; and with the wicked I will not sit.
verses.textLatin: Odivi ecclesiam malignantium, et cum impiis non sedebo.

verses.text: I will wash my hands among the innocent; and will compass thy altar, O Lord:
verses.textLatin: Lavabo inter innocentes manus meas, et circumdabo altare tuum, Domine:

verses.text: That I may hear the voice of thy praise: and tell of all thy wondrous works.
verses.textLatin: ut audiam vocem laudis, et enarrem universa mirabilia tua.

verses.text: I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; and the place where thy glory dwelleth.
verses.textLatin: Domine, dilexi decorem domus tuæ, et locum habitationis gloriæ tuæ.

verses.text: Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: nor my life with bloody men:
verses.textLatin: Ne perdas cum impiis, Deus, animam meam, et cum viris sanguinum vitam meam:

verses.text: In whose hands are iniquities: their right hand is filled with gifts.
verses.textLatin: in quorum manibus iniquitates sunt; dextera eorum repleta est muneribus.

verses.text: But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: redeem me, and have mercy on me.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in innocentia mea ingressus sum; redime me, et miserere mei.

verses.text: My foot hath stood in the direct way: in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Pes meus stetit in directo; in ecclesiis benedicam te, Domine.

verses.text: The psalm of David before he was anointed. The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life: of whom shall I be afraid?
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, priusquam liniretur. Dominus illuminatio mea et salus mea: quem timebo? Dominus protector vitæ meæ: a quo trepidabo?

verses.text: Whilst the wicked draw near against me, to eat my flesh. My enemies that trouble me, have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.
verses.textLatin: Dum appropiant super me nocentes ut edant carnes meas, qui tribulant me inimici mei, ipsi infirmati sunt et ceciderunt.

verses.text: If armies in camp should stand together against me, my heart shall not fear. If a battle should rise up against me, in this will I be confident.
verses.textLatin: Si consistant adversum me castra, non timebit cor meum; si exsurgat adversum me prælium, in hoc ego sperabo.

verses.text: One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life. That I may see the delight of the Lord, and may visit his temple.
verses.textLatin: Unam petii a Domino, hanc requiram, ut inhabitem in domo Domini omnibus diebus vitæ meæ; ut videam voluptatem Domini, et visitem templum ejus.

verses.text: For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam abscondit me in tabernaculo suo; in die malorum protexit me in abscondito tabernaculi sui.

verses.text: He hath exalted me upon a rock: and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies. I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: In petra exaltavit me, et nunc exaltavit caput meum super inimicos meos. Circuivi, et immolavi in tabernaculo ejus hostiam vociferationis; cantabo, et psalmum dicam Domino.

verses.text: Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: have mercy on me and hear me.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Domine, vocem meam, qua clamavi ad te; miserere mei, et exaudi me.

verses.text: My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.
verses.textLatin: Tibi dixit cor meum: Exquisivit te facies mea; faciem tuam, Domine, requiram.

verses.text: Turn not away thy face from me; decline not in thy wrath from thy servant. Be thou my helper, forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.
verses.textLatin: Ne avertas faciem tuam a me; ne declines in ira a servo tuo. Adjutor meus esto; ne derelinquas me, neque despicias me, Deus salutaris meus.

verses.text: For my father and my mother have left me: but the Lord hath taken me up.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam pater meus et mater mea dereliquerunt me; Dominus autem assumpsit me.

verses.text: Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Legem pone mihi, Domine, in via tua, et dirige me in semitam rectam, propter inimicos meos.

verses.text: Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.
verses.textLatin: Ne tradideris me in animas tribulantium me, quoniam insurrexerunt in me testes iniqui, et mentita est iniquitas sibi.

verses.text: I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
verses.textLatin: Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium.

verses.text: Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Expecta Dominum, viriliter age: et confortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum.

verses.text: A psalm for David himself. Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: O my God, be not thou silent to me: lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus ipsi David.  Ad te, Domine, clamabo; Deus meus, ne sileas a me: nequando taceas a me, et assimilabor descendentibus in lacum.

verses.text: Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Domine, vocem deprecationis meæ dum oro ad te; dum extollo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.

verses.text: Draw me not away together with the wicked; and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not: Who speak peace with their neighbour, but evils are in their hearts.
verses.textLatin: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatoribus, et cum operantibus iniquitatem ne perdas me; qui loquuntur pacem cum proximo suo, mala autem in cordibus eorum.

verses.text: Give them according to their works, and according to the wickedness of their inventions. According to the works of their hands give thou to them: render to them their reward.
verses.textLatin: Da illis secundum opera eorum, et secundum nequitiam adinventionum ipsorum. Secundum opera manuum eorum tribue illis; redde retributionem eorum ipsis.

verses.text: Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam non intellexerunt opera Domini, et in opera manuum ejus destrues illos, et non ædificabis eos.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord, for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus, quoniam exaudivit vocem deprecationis meæ.

verses.text: The Lord is my helper and my protector: in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped. And my flesh hath flourished again, and with my will I will give praise to him.
verses.textLatin: Dominus adjutor meus et protector meus; in ipso speravit cor meum, et adjutus sum: et refloruit caro mea, et ex voluntate mea confitebor ei.

verses.text: The Lord is the strength of his people, and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.
verses.textLatin: Dominus fortitudo plebis suæ, et protector salvationum christi sui est.

verses.text: Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: and rule them and exalt them for ever.
verses.textLatin: Salvum fac populum tuum, Domine, et benedic hæreditati tuæ; et rege eos, et extolle illos usque in æternum.

verses.text: A psalm for David, at the finishing of the tabernacle. Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, in consummatione tabernaculi. Afferte Domino, filii Dei, afferte Domino filios arietum.

verses.text: Bring to the Lord glory and honour: bring to the Lord glory to his name: adore ye the Lord in his holy court.
verses.textLatin: Afferte Domino gloriam et honorem; afferte Domino gloriam nomini ejus; adorate Dominum in atrio sancto ejus.

verses.text: The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty hath thundered, The Lord is upon many waters.
verses.textLatin: Vox Domini super aquas; Deus majestatis intonuit: Dominus super aquas multas.

verses.text: The voice of the Lord is in power; the voice of the Lord in magnificence.
verses.textLatin: Vox Domini in virtute; vox Domini in magnificentia.

verses.text: The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars: yea, the Lord shall break the cedars of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Vox Domini confringentis cedros, et confringet Dominus cedros Libani:

verses.text: And shall reduce them to pieces, as a calf of Libanus, and as the beloved son of unicorns.
verses.textLatin: et comminuet eas, tamquam vitulum Libani, et dilectus quemadmodum filius unicornium.

verses.text: The voice of the Lord divideth the flame of fire:
verses.textLatin: Vox Domini intercidentis flammam ignis;

verses.text: The voice of the Lord shaketh the desert: and the Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.
verses.textLatin: vox Domini concutientis desertum: et commovebit Dominus desertum Cades.

verses.text: The voice of the Lord prepareth the stags: and he will discover the thick woods: and in his temple all shall speak his glory.
verses.textLatin: Vox Domini præparantis cervos: et revelabit condensa, et in templo ejus omnes dicent gloriam.

verses.text: The Lord maketh the flood to dwell: and the Lord shall sit king for ever. The Lord will give strength to his people: the Lord will bless his people with peace.
verses.textLatin: Dominus diluvium inhabitare facit, et sedebit Dominus rex in æternum.
Dominus virtutem populo suo dabit; Dominus benedicet populo suo in pace.

verses.text: A psalm of a canticle, at the dedication of David’s house.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus cantici, in dedicatione domus David.

verses.text: I will extol thee, O Lord, for thou hast upheld me: and hast not made my enemies to rejoice over me.
verses.textLatin: Exaltabo te, Domine, quoniam suscepisti me, nec delectasti inimicos meos super me.

verses.text: O Lord my God, I have cried to thee, and thou hast healed me.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus meus, clamavi ad te, et sanasti me.

verses.text: Thou hast brought forth, O Lord, my soul from hell: thou hast saved me from them that go down into the pit.
verses.textLatin: Domine, eduxisti ab inferno animam meam; salvasti me a descendentibus in lacum.

verses.text: Sing to the Lord, O ye his saints: and give praise to the memory of his holiness.
verses.textLatin: Psallite Domino, sancti ejus; et confitemini memoriæ sanctitatis ejus.

verses.text: For wrath is in his indignation; and life in his good will. In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ira in indignatione ejus, et vita in voluntate ejus: ad vesperum demorabitur fletus, et ad matutinum lætitia.

verses.text: And in my abundance I said: I shall never be moved.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem dixi in abundantia mea: Non movebor in æternum.

verses.text: O Lord, in thy favour, thou gavest strength to my beauty. Thou turnedst away thy face from me, and I became troubled.
verses.textLatin: Domine, in voluntate tua præstitisti decori meo virtutem; avertisti faciem tuam a me, et factus sum conturbatus.

verses.text: To thee, O Lord, will I cry: and I will make supplication to my God.
verses.textLatin: Ad te, Domine, clamabo, et ad Deum meum deprecabor.

verses.text: What profit is there in my blood, whilst I go down to corruption? Shall dust confess to thee, or declare thy truth?
verses.textLatin: Quæ utilitas in sanguine meo, dum descendo in corruptionem? numquid confitebitur tibi pulvis, aut annuntiabit veritatem tuam?

verses.text: The Lord hath heard, and hath had mercy on me: the Lord became my helper.
verses.textLatin: Audivit Dominus, et misertus est mei; Dominus factus est adjutor meus.

verses.text: Thou hast turned for me my mourning into joy: thou hast cut my sackcloth, and hast compassed me with gladness:
verses.textLatin: Convertisti planctum meum in gaudium mihi; conscidisti saccum meum, et circumdedisti me lætitia:

verses.text: To the end that my glory may sing to thee, and I may not regret: O Lord my God, I will give praise to thee for ever.
verses.textLatin: ut cantet tibi gloria mea, et non compungar. Domine Deus meus, in æternum confitebor tibi.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David, in an ecstasy.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David, pro extasi.

verses.text: In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: deliver me in thy justice.
verses.textLatin: In te, Domine, speravi; non confundar in æternum: in justitia tua libera me.

verses.text: Bow down thy ear to me: make haste to deliver me. Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, to save me.
verses.textLatin: Inclina ad me aurem tuam; accelera ut eruas me. Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, et in domum refugii, ut salvum me facias:

verses.text: For thou art my strength and my refuge; and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.
verses.textLatin: quoniam fortitudo mea et refugium meum es tu; et propter nomen tuum deduces me et enutries me.

verses.text: Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: for thou art my protector.
verses.textLatin: Educes me de laqueo hoc quem absconderunt mihi, quoniam tu es protector meus.

verses.text: Into thy hands I commend my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.
verses.textLatin: In manus tuas commendo spiritum meum; redemisti me, Domine Deus veritatis.

verses.text: Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, to no purpose. But I have hoped in the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Odisti observantes vanitates supervacue; ego autem in Domino speravi.

verses.text: I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy. For thou hast regarded my humility, thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.
verses.textLatin: Exsultabo, et lætabor in misericordia tua, quoniam respexisti humilitatem meam; salvasti de necessitatibus animam meam.

verses.text: And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.
verses.textLatin: Nec conclusisti me in manibus inimici: statuisti in loco spatioso pedes meos.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Domine, quoniam tribulor; conturbatus est in ira oculus meus, anima mea, et venter meus.

verses.text: For my life is wasted with grief: and my years in sighs. My strength is weakened through poverty and my bones are disturbed.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam defecit in dolore vita mea, et anni mei in gemitibus. Infirmata est in paupertate virtus mea, et ossa mea conturbata sunt.

verses.text: I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; and a fear to my acquaintance. They that saw me without fled from me.
verses.textLatin: Super omnes inimicos meos factus sum opprobrium, et vicinis meis valde, et timor notis meis; qui videbant me foras fugerunt a me.

verses.text: I am forgotten as one dead from the heart. I am become as a vessel that is destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Oblivioni datus sum, tamquam mortuus a corde; factus sum tamquam vas perditum:

verses.text: For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about. While they assembled together against me, they consulted to take away my life.
verses.textLatin: quoniam audivi vituperationem multorum commorantium in circuitu. In eo dum convenirent simul adversum me, accipere animam meam consiliati sunt.

verses.text: But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: I said: Thou art my God.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in te speravi, Domine; dixi: Deus meus es tu;

verses.text: My lots are in thy hands. Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; and from them that persecute me.
verses.textLatin: in manibus tuis sortes meæ: eripe me de manu inimicorum meorum, et a persequentibus me.

verses.text: Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy.
verses.textLatin: Illustra faciem tuam super servum tuum; salvum me fac in misericordia tua.

verses.text: Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee. Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell.
verses.textLatin: Domine, non confundar, quoniam invocavi te. Erubescant impii, et deducantur in infernum;

verses.text: Let deceitful lips be made dumb. Which speak iniquity against the just, with pride and abuse.
verses.textLatin: muta fiant labia dolosa, quæ loquuntur adversus justum iniquitatem, in superbia, et in abusione.

verses.text: O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee! Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, in the sight of the sons of men.
verses.textLatin: Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine, quam abscondisti timentibus te; perfecisti eis qui sperant in te in conspectu filiorum hominum!

verses.text: Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, from the disturbance of men. Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.
verses.textLatin: Abscondes eos in abscondito faciei tuæ a conturbatione hominum; proteges eos in tabernaculo tuo, a contradictione linguarum.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord, for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus, quoniam mirificavit misericordiam suam mihi in civitate munita.

verses.text: But I said in the excess of my mind: I am cast away from before thy eyes. Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, when I cried to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem dixi in excessu mentis meæ: Projectus sum a facie oculorum tuorum: ideo exaudisti vocem orationis meæ, dum clamarem ad te.

verses.text: O love the Lord, all ye his saints: for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.
verses.textLatin: Diligite Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam veritatem requiret Dominus, et retribuet abundanter facientibus superbiam.

verses.text: Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all ye that hope in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Viriliter agite, et confortetur cor vestrum, omnes qui speratis in Domino.
