verses.text: To David himself, understanding. Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi David intellectus. Beati quorum remissæ sunt iniquitates, et quorum tecta sunt peccata.

verses.text: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir cui non imputavit Dominus peccatum, nec est in spiritu ejus dolus.

verses.text: Because I was silent my bones grew old; whilst I cried out all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tacui, inveteraverunt ossa mea, dum clamarem tota die.

verses.text: For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam die ac nocte gravata est super me manus tua, conversus sum in ærumna mea, dum configitur spina.

verses.text: I have acknowledged my sin to thee, and my injustice I have not concealed. I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.
verses.textLatin: Delictum meum cognitum tibi feci, et injustitiam meam non abscondi. Dixi: Confitebor adversum me injustitiam meam Domino; et tu remisisti impietatem peccati mei.

verses.text: For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee in a seasonable time. And yet in a flood of many waters, they shall not come nigh unto him.
verses.textLatin: Pro hac orabit ad te omnis sanctus in tempore opportuno. Verumtamen in diluvio aquarum multarum, ad eum non approximabunt.

verses.text: Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.
verses.textLatin: Tu es refugium meum a tribulatione quæ circumdedit me; exsultatio mea, erue me a circumdantibus me.

verses.text: I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: I will fix my eyes upon thee.
verses.textLatin: Intellectum tibi dabo, et instruam te in via hac qua gradieris; firmabo super te oculos meos.

verses.text: Do not become like the horse and the mule, who have no understanding. With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, who come not near unto thee.
verses.textLatin: Nolite fieri sicut equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus. In camo et freno maxillas eorum constringe, qui non approximant ad te.

verses.text: Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Multa flagella peccatoris; sperantem autem in Domino misericordia circumdabit.

verses.text: Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, and glory, all ye right of heart.
verses.textLatin: Lætamini in Domino, et exsultate, justi; et gloriamini, omnes recti corde.

verses.text: A psalm for David. Rejoice in the Lord, O ye just: praise becometh the upright.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David. Exsultate, justi, in Domino; rectos decet collaudatio.

verses.text: Give praise to the Lord on the harp; sing to him with the psaltery, the instrument of ten strings.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino in cithara; in psalterio decem chordarum psallite illi.

verses.text: Sing to him a new canticle, sing well unto him with a loud noise.
verses.textLatin: Cantate ei canticum novum; bene psallite ei in vociferatione.

verses.text: For the word of the Lord is right, and all his works are done with faithfulness.
verses.textLatin: Quia rectum est verbum Domini, et omnia opera ejus in fide.

verses.text: He loveth mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Diligit misericordiam et judicium; misericordia Domini plena est terra.

verses.text: By the word of the Lord the heavens were established; and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth:
verses.textLatin: Verbo Domini cæli firmati sunt, et spiritu oris ejus omnis virtus eorum.

verses.text: Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; laying up the depths in storehouses.
verses.textLatin: Congregans sicut in utre aquas maris; ponens in thesauris abyssos.

verses.text: Let all the earth fear the Lord, and let all the inhabitants of the world be in awe of him.
verses.textLatin: Timeat Dominum omnis terra; ab eo autem commoveantur omnes inhabitantes orbem.

verses.text: For he spoke and they were made: he commanded and they were created.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ipse dixit, et facta sunt; ipse mandavit et creata sunt.

verses.text: The Lord bringeth to nought the counsels of nations; and he rejecteth the devices of people, and casteth away the counsels of princes.
verses.textLatin: Dominus dissipat consilia gentium; reprobat autem cogitationes populorum, et reprobat consilia principum.

verses.text: But the counsel of the Lord standeth for ever: the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
verses.textLatin: Consilium autem Domini in æternum manet; cogitationes cordis ejus in generatione et generationem.

verses.text: Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord: the people whom he hath chosen for his inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Beata gens cujus est Dominus Deus ejus; populus quem elegit in hæreditatem sibi.

verses.text: The Lord hath looked from heaven: he hath beheld all the sons of men.
verses.textLatin: De cælo respexit Dominus; vidit omnes filios hominum.

verses.text: From his habitation which he hath prepared, he hath looked upon all that dwell on the earth.
verses.textLatin: De præparato habitaculo suo respexit super omnes qui habitant terram:

verses.text: He who hath made the hearts of every one of them: who understandeth all their works.
verses.textLatin: qui finxit sigillatim corda eorum; qui intelligit omnia opera eorum.

verses.text: The king is not saved by a great army: nor shall the giant be saved by his own great strength.
verses.textLatin: Non salvatur rex per multam virtutem, et gigas non salvabitur in multitudine virtutis suæ.

verses.text: Vain is the horse for safety: neither shall he be saved by the abundance of his strength.
verses.textLatin: Fallax equus ad salutem; in abundantia autem virtutis suæ non salvabitur.

verses.text: Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them that fear him: and on them that hope in his mercy.
verses.textLatin: Ecce oculi Domini super metuentes eum, et in eis qui sperant super misericordia ejus:

verses.text: To deliver their souls from death; and feed them in famine.
verses.textLatin: ut eruat a morte animas eorum, et alat eos in fame.

verses.text: Our soul waiteth for the Lord: for he is our helper and protector.
verses.textLatin: Anima nostra sustinet Dominum, quoniam adjutor et protector noster est.

verses.text: For in him our heart shall rejoice: and in his holy name we have trusted.
verses.textLatin: Quia in eo lætabitur cor nostrum, et in nomine sancto ejus speravimus.

verses.text: Let thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, as we have hoped in thee.
verses.textLatin: Fiat misericordia tua, Domine, super nos, quemadmodum speravimus in te.

verses.text: For David, when he changed his countenance before Achimelech, who dismissed him, and he went his way. (1 Kings 21.)
verses.textLatin: Davidi, cum immutavit vultum suum coram Achimelech, et dimisit eum, et abiit.

verses.text: I will bless the Lord at all times, his praise shall be always in my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore; semper laus ejus in ore meo.

verses.text: In the Lord shall my soul be praised: let the meek hear and rejoice.
verses.textLatin: In Domino laudabitur anima mea: audiant mansueti, et lætentur.

verses.text: O magnify the Lord with me; and let us extol his name together.
verses.textLatin: Magnificate Dominum mecum, et exaltemus nomen ejus in idipsum.

verses.text: I sought the Lord, and he heard me; and he delivered me from all my troubles.
verses.textLatin: Exquisivi Dominum, et exaudivit me; et ex omnibus tribulationibus meis eripuit me.

verses.text: Come ye to him and be enlightened: and your faces shall not be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini; et facies vestræ non confundentur.

verses.text: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him: and saved him out of all his troubles.
verses.textLatin: Iste pauper clamavit, et Dominus exaudivit eum, et de omnibus tribulationibus ejus salvavit eum.

verses.text: The angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him: and shall deliver them.
verses.textLatin: Immittet angelus Domini in circuitu timentium eum, et eripiet eos.

verses.text: O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet: blessed is the man that hopeth in him.
verses.textLatin: Gustate et videte quoniam suavis est Dominus; beatus vir qui sperat in eo.

verses.text: Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.
verses.textLatin: Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam non est inopia timentibus eum.

verses.text: The rich have wanted, and have suffered hunger: but they that seek the Lord shall not be deprived of any good.
verses.textLatin: Divites eguerunt, et esurierunt; inquirentes autem Dominum non minuentur omni bono.

verses.text: Come, children, hearken to me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Venite, filii; audite me: timorem Domini docebo vos.

verses.text: Who is the man that desireth life: who loveth to see good days?
verses.textLatin: Quis est homo qui vult vitam; diligit dies videre bonos?

verses.text: Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
verses.textLatin: Prohibe linguam tuam a malo, et labia tua ne loquantur dolum.

verses.text: Turn away from evil and do good: seek after peace and pursue it.
verses.textLatin: Diverte a malo, et fac bonum; inquire pacem, et persequere eam.

verses.text: The eyes of the Lord are upon the just: and his ears unto their prayers.
verses.textLatin: Oculi Domini super justos, et aures ejus in preces eorum.

verses.text: But the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things: to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Vultus autem Domini super facientes mala, ut perdat de terra memoriam eorum.

verses.text: The just cried, and the Lord heard them: and delivered them out of all their troubles.
verses.textLatin: Clamaverunt justi, et Dominus exaudivit eos; et ex omnibus tribulationibus eorum liberavit eos.

verses.text: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: and he will save the humble of spirit.
verses.textLatin: Juxta est Dominus iis qui tribulato sunt corde, et humiles spiritu salvabit.

verses.text: Many are the afflictions of the just; but out of them all will the Lord deliver them.
verses.textLatin: Multæ tribulationes justorum; et de omnibus his liberabit eos Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord keepeth all their bones, not one of them shall be broken.
verses.textLatin: Custodit Dominus omnia ossa eorum: unum ex his non conteretur.

verses.text: The death of the wicked is very evil: and they that hate the just shall be guilty.
verses.textLatin: Mors peccatorum pessima; et qui oderunt justum delinquent.

verses.text: The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall offend.
verses.textLatin: Redimet Dominus animas servorum suorum, et non delinquent omnes qui sperant in eo.

verses.text: For David himself. Judge thou, O Lord, them that wrong me: overthrow them that fight against me.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi David. Judica, Domine, nocentes me; expugna impugnantes me.

verses.text: Take hold of arms and shield: and rise up to help me.
verses.textLatin: Apprehende arma et scutum, et exsurge in adjutorium mihi.

verses.text: Bring out the sword, and shut up the way against them that persecute me: say to my soul: I am thy salvation.
verses.textLatin: Effunde frameam, et conclude adversus eos qui persequuntur me; dic animæ meæ: Salus tua ego sum.

verses.text: Let them be confounded and ashamed that seek after my soul. Let them be turned back and be confounded that devise evil against me.
verses.textLatin: Confundantur et revereantur quærentes animam meam; avertantur retrorsum et confundantur cogitantes mihi mala.

verses.text: Let them become as dust before the wind: and let the angel of the Lord straiten them.
verses.textLatin: Fiant tamquam pulvis ante faciem venti, et angelus Domini coarctans eos.

verses.text: Let their way become dark and slippery; and let the angel of the Lord pursue them.
verses.textLatin: Fiat via illorum tenebræ et lubricum, et angelus Domini persequens eos.

verses.text: For without cause they have hidden their net for me unto destruction: without cause they have upbraided my soul.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam gratis absconderunt mihi interitum laquei sui; supervacue exprobraverunt animam meam.

verses.text: Let the snare which he knoweth not come upon him: and let the net which he hath hidden catch him: and into that very snare let them fall.
verses.textLatin: Veniat illi laqueus quem ignorat, et captio quam abscondit apprehendat eum, et in laqueum cadat in ipsum.

verses.text: But my soul shall rejoice in the Lord; and shall be delighted in his salvation.
verses.textLatin: Anima autem mea exsultabit in Domino, et delectabitur super salutari suo.

verses.text: All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like to thee? Who deliverest the poor from the hand of them that are stronger than he; the needy and the poor from them that strip him.
verses.textLatin: Omnia ossa mea dicent: Domine, quis similis tibi? eripiens inopem de manu fortiorum ejus; egenum et pauperem a diripientibus eum.

verses.text: Unjust witnesses rising up have asked me things I knew not.
verses.textLatin: Surgentes testes iniqui, quæ ignorabam interrogabant me.

verses.text: They repaid me evil for good: to the depriving me of my soul.
verses.textLatin: Retribuebant mihi mala pro bonis, sterilitatem animæ meæ.

verses.text: But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, I was clothed with haircloth. I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer shall be turned into my bosom.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem, cum mihi molesti essent, induebar cilicio; humiliabam in jejunio animam meam, et oratio mea in sinu meo convertetur.

verses.text: As a neighbour and as an own brother, so did I please: as one mourning and sorrowful so was I humbled.
verses.textLatin: Quasi proximum et quasi fratrem nostrum sic complacebam; quasi lugens et contristatus sic humiliabar.

verses.text: But they rejoiced against me, and came together: scourges were gathered together upon me, and I knew not.
verses.textLatin: Et adversum me lætati sunt, et convenerunt; congregata sunt super me flagella, et ignoravi.

verses.text: They were separated, and repented not: they tempted me, they scoffed at me with scorn: they gnashed upon me with their teeth.
verses.textLatin: Dissipati sunt, nec compuncti; tentaverunt me, subsannaverunt me subsannatione; frenduerunt super me dentibus suis.

verses.text: Lord, when wilt thou look upon me? rescue thou my soul from their malice: my only one from the lions.
verses.textLatin: Domine, quando respicies? Restitue animam meam a malignitate eorum; a leonibus unicam meam.

verses.text: I will give thanks to thee in a great church; I will praise thee in a strong people.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi in ecclesia magna; in populo gravi laudabo te.

verses.text: Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: who have hated me without cause, and wink with the eyes.
verses.textLatin: Non supergaudeant mihi qui adversantur mihi inique, qui oderunt me gratis, et annuunt oculis.

verses.text: For they spoke indeed peaceably to me; and speaking in the anger of the earth they devised guile.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam mihi quidem pacifice loquebantur; et in iracundia terræ loquentes, dolos cogitabant.

verses.text: And they opened their mouth wide against me; they said: Well done, well done, our eyes have seen it.
verses.textLatin: Et dilataverunt super me os suum; dixerunt: Euge, euge! viderunt oculi nostri.

verses.text: Thou hast seen, O Lord, be not thou silent: O Lord, depart not from me.
verses.textLatin: Vidisti, Domine: ne sileas; Domine, ne discedas a me.

verses.text: Arise, and be attentive to my judgment: to my cause, my God, and my Lord.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge et intende judicio meo, Deus meus; et Dominus meus, in causam meam.

verses.text: Judge me, O Lord my God according to thy justice, and let them not rejoice over me.
verses.textLatin: Judica me secundum justitiam tuam, Domine Deus meus, et non supergaudeant mihi.

verses.text: Let them not say in their hearts: It is well, it is well, to our mind: neither let them say: We have swallowed him up.
verses.textLatin: Non dicant in cordibus suis: Euge, euge, animæ nostræ; nec dicant: Devoravimus eum.

verses.text: Let them blush: and be ashamed together, who rejoice at my evils. Let them be clothed with confusion and shame, who speak great things against me.
verses.textLatin: Erubescant et revereantur simul qui gratulantur malis meis; induantur confusione et reverentia qui magna loquuntur super me.

verses.text: Let them rejoice and be glad, who are well pleased with my justice, and let them say always: The Lord be magnified, who delights in the peace of his servant.
verses.textLatin: Exsultent et lætentur qui volunt justitiam meam; et dicant semper: Magnificetur Dominus, qui volunt pacem servi ejus.

verses.text: And my tongue shall meditate thy justice, thy praise all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Et lingua mea meditabitur justitiam tuam; tota die laudem tuam.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the servant of God, David himself.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Servo Domini ipsi David.

verses.text: The unjust hath said within himself, that he would sin: there is no fear of God before his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Dixit injustus ut delinquat in semetipso: non est timor Dei ante oculos ejus.

verses.text: For in his sight he hath done deceitfully, that his iniquity may be found unto hatred.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam dolose egit in conspectu ejus, ut inveniatur iniquitas ejus ad odium.

verses.text: The words of his mouth are iniquity and guile: he would not understand that he might do well.
verses.textLatin: Verba oris ejus iniquitas, et dolus; noluit intelligere ut bene ageret.

verses.text: He hath devised iniquity on his bed, he hath set himself on every way that is not good: but evil he hath not hated.
verses.textLatin: Iniquitatem meditatus est in cubili suo; astitit omni viæ non bonæ: malitiam autem non odivit.

verses.text: O Lord, thy mercy is in heaven, and thy truth reacheth even to the clouds.
verses.textLatin: Domine, in cælo misericordia tua, et veritas tua usque ad nubes.

verses.text: Thy justice is as the mountains of God, thy judgments are a great deep. Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord:
verses.textLatin: Justitia tua sicut montes Dei; judicia tua abyssus multa. Homines et jumenta salvabis, Domine,

verses.text: O how hast thou multiplied thy mercy, O God! But the children of men shall put their trust under the covert of thy wings.
verses.textLatin: quemadmodum multiplicasti misericordiam tuam, Deus. Filii autem hominum in tegmine alarum tuarum sperabunt.

verses.text: They shall be inebriated with the plenty of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure.
verses.textLatin: Inebriabuntur ab ubertate domus tuæ, et torrente voluptatis tuæ potabis eos:

verses.text: For with thee is the fountain of life; and in thy light we shall see light.
verses.textLatin: quoniam apud te est fons vitæ, et in lumine tuo videbimus lumen.

verses.text: Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, and thy justice to them that are right in heart.
verses.textLatin: Prætende misericordiam tuam scientibus te, et justitiam tuam his qui recto sunt corde.

verses.text: Let not the foot of pride come to me, and let not the hand of the sinner move me.
verses.textLatin: Non veniat mihi pes superbiæ, et manus peccatoris non moveat me.

verses.text: There the workers of iniquity are fallen, they are cast out, and could not stand.
verses.textLatin: Ibi ceciderunt qui operantur iniquitatem; expulsi sunt, nec potuerunt stare.

verses.text: A psalm for David himself. Be not emulous of evildoers; nor envy them that work iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus ipsi David. Noli æmulari in malignantibus, neque zelaveris facientes iniquitatem:

verses.text: For they shall shortly wither away as grass, and as the green herbs shall quickly fall.
verses.textLatin: quoniam tamquam fœnum velociter arescent, et quemadmodum olera herbarum cito decident.

verses.text: Trust in the Lord, and do good, and dwell in the land, and thou shalt be fed with its riches.
verses.textLatin: Spera in Domino, et fac bonitatem; et inhabita terram, et pasceris in divitiis ejus.

verses.text: Delight in the Lord, and he will give thee the requests of thy heart.
verses.textLatin: Delectare in Domino, et dabit tibi petitiones cordis tui.

verses.text: Commit thy way to the Lord, and trust in him, and he will do it.
verses.textLatin: Revela Domino viam tuam, et spera in eo, et ipse faciet.

verses.text: And he will bring forth thy justice as the light, and thy judgment as the noonday.
verses.textLatin: Et educet quasi lumen justitiam tuam, et judicium tuum tamquam meridiem.

verses.text: Be subject to the Lord and pray to him. Envy not the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.
verses.textLatin: Subditus esto Domino, et ora eum. Noli æmulari in eo qui prosperatur in via sua; in homine faciente injustitias.

verses.text: Cease from anger, and leave rage; have no emulation to do evil.
verses.textLatin: Desine ab ira, et derelinque furorem; noli æmulari ut maligneris.

verses.text: For evildoers shall be cut off: but they that wait upon the Lord, they shall inherit the land.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam qui malignantur exterminabuntur; sustinentes autem Dominum, ipsi hæreditabunt terram.

verses.text: For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: and thou shalt seek his place, and shalt not find it.
verses.textLatin: Et adhuc pusillum, et non erit peccator; et quæres locum ejus, et non invenies.

verses.text: But the meek shall inherit the land, and shall delight in abundance of peace.
verses.textLatin: Mansueti autem hæreditabunt terram, et delectabuntur in multitudine pacis.

verses.text: The sinner shall watch the just man: and shall gnash upon him with his teeth.
verses.textLatin: Observabit peccator justum, et stridebit super eum dentibus suis.

verses.text: But the Lord shall laugh at him: for he foreseeth that his day shall come.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem irridebit eum, quoniam prospicit quod veniet dies ejus.

verses.text: The wicked have drawn out the sword: they have bent their bow. To cast down the poor and needy, to kill the upright of heart.
verses.textLatin: Gladium evaginaverunt peccatores; intenderunt arcum suum: ut dejiciant pauperem et inopem, ut trucident rectos corde.

verses.text: Let their sword enter into their own hearts, and let their bow be broken.
verses.textLatin: Gladius eorum intret in corda ipsorum, et arcus eorum confringatur.

verses.text: Better is a little to the just, than the great riches of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Melius est modicum justo, super divitias peccatorum multas:

verses.text: For the arms of the wicked shall be broken in pieces; but the Lord strengtheneth the just.
verses.textLatin: quoniam brachia peccatorum conterentur: confirmat autem justos Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord knoweth the days of the undefiled; and their inheritance shall be for ever.
verses.textLatin: Novit Dominus dies immaculatorum, et hæreditas eorum in æternum erit.

verses.text: They shall not be confounded in the evil time; and in the days of famine they shall be filled:
verses.textLatin: Non confundentur in tempore malo, et in diebus famis saturabuntur:

verses.text: because the wicked shall perish. And the enemies of the Lord, presently after they shall be honoured and exalted, shall come to nothing and vanish like smoke.
verses.textLatin: quia peccatores peribunt. Inimici vero Domini mox ut honorificati fuerint et exaltati, deficientes quemadmodum fumus deficient.

verses.text: The sinner shall borrow, and not pay again; but the just sheweth mercy and shall give.
verses.textLatin: Mutuabitur peccator, et non solvet; justus autem miseretur et tribuet:

verses.text: For such as bless him shall inherit the land: but such as curse him shall perish.
verses.textLatin: quia benedicentes ei hæreditabunt terram; maledicentes autem ei disperibunt.

verses.text: With the Lord shall the steps of a man be directed, and he shall like well his way.
verses.textLatin: Apud Dominum gressus hominis dirigentur, et viam ejus volet.

verses.text: When he shall fall he shall not be bruised, for the Lord putteth his hand under him.
verses.textLatin: Cum ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus supponit manum suam.

verses.text: I have been young, and now am old; and I have not seen the just forsaken, nor his seed seeking bread.
verses.textLatin: Junior fui, etenim senui; et non vidi justum derelictum, nec semen ejus quærens panem.

verses.text: He sheweth mercy, and lendeth all the day long; and his seed shall be in blessing.
verses.textLatin: Tota die miseretur et commodat; et semen illius in benedictione erit.

verses.text: Decline from evil and do good, and dwell for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Declina a malo, et fac bonum, et inhabita in sæculum sæculi:

verses.text: For the Lord loveth judgment, and will not forsake his saints: they shall be preserved for ever. The unjust shall be punished, and the seed of the wicked shall perish.
verses.textLatin: quia Dominus amat judicium, et non derelinquet sanctos suos: in æternum conservabuntur. Injusti punientur, et semen impiorum peribit.

verses.text: But the just shall inherit the land, and shall dwell therein for evermore.
verses.textLatin: Justi autem hæreditabunt terram, et inhabitabunt in sæculum sæculi super eam.

verses.text: The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: and his tongue shall speak judgment.
verses.textLatin: Os justi meditabitur sapientiam, et lingua ejus loquetur judicium.

verses.text: The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps shall not be supplanted.
verses.textLatin: Lex Dei ejus in corde ipsius, et non supplantabuntur gressus ejus.

verses.text: The wicked watcheth the just man, and seeketh to put him to death.
verses.textLatin: Considerat peccator justum, et quærit mortificare eum.

verses.text: But the Lord will not leave him in his hands; nor condemn him when he shall be judged.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem non derelinquet eum in manibus ejus, nec damnabit eum cum judicabitur illi.

verses.text: Expect the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land: when the sinners shall perish thou shalt see.
verses.textLatin: Exspecta Dominum, et custodi viam ejus, et exaltabit te ut hæreditate capias terram: cum perierint peccatores, videbis.

verses.text: I have seen the wicked highly exalted, and lifted up like the cedars of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Vidi impium superexaltatum, et elevatum sicut cedros Libani:

verses.text: And I passed by, and lo, he was not: and I sought him and his place was not found.
verses.textLatin: et transivi, et ecce non erat; et quæsivi eum, et non est inventus locus ejus.

verses.text: Keep innocence, and behold justice: for there are remnants for the peaceable man.
verses.textLatin: Custodi innocentiam, et vide æquitatem, quoniam sunt reliquiæ homini pacifico.

verses.text: But the unjust shall be destroyed together: the remnants of the wicked shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Injusti autem disperibunt simul; reliquiæ impiorum interibunt.

verses.text: But the salvation of the just is from the Lord, and he is their protector in the time of trouble.
verses.textLatin: Salus autem justorum a Domino; et protector eorum in tempore tribulationis.

verses.text: And the Lord will help them and deliver them: and he will rescue them from the wicked, and save them, because they have hoped in him.
verses.textLatin: Et adjuvabit eos Dominus, et liberabit eos; et eruet eos a peccatoribus, et salvabit eos, quia speraverunt in eo.

verses.text: A psalm for David, for a remembrance of the sabbath.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, in rememorationem de sabbato.

verses.text: Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; nor chastise me in thy wrath.
verses.textLatin: Domine, ne in furore tuo arguas me, neque in ira tua corripias me:

verses.text: For thy arrows are fastened in me: and thy hand hath been strong upon me.
verses.textLatin: quoniam sagittæ tuæ infixæ sunt mihi, et confirmasti super me manum tuam.

verses.text: There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.
verses.textLatin: Non est sanitas in carne mea, a facie iræ tuæ; non est pax ossibus meis, a facie peccatorum meorum:

verses.text: For my iniquities are gone over my head: and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.
verses.textLatin: quoniam iniquitates meæ supergressæ sunt caput meum, et sicut onus grave gravatæ sunt super me.

verses.text: My sores are putrified and corrupted, because of my foolishness.
verses.textLatin: Putruerunt et corruptæ sunt cicatrices meæ, a facie insipientiæ meæ.

verses.text: I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: I walked sorrowful all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Miser factus sum et curvatus sum usque in finem; tota die contristatus ingrediebar.

verses.text: For my loins are filled with illusions; and there is no health in my flesh.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam lumbi mei impleti sunt illusionibus, et non est sanitas in carne mea.

verses.text: I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: I roared with the groaning of my heart.
verses.textLatin: Afflictus sum, et humiliatus sum nimis; rugiebam a gemitu cordis mei.

verses.text: Lord, all my desire is before thee, and my groaning is not hidden from thee.
verses.textLatin: Domine, ante te omne desiderium meum, et gemitus meus a te non est absconditus.

verses.text: My heart is troubled, my strength hath left me, and the light of my eyes itself is not with me.
verses.textLatin: Cor meum conturbatum est; dereliquit me virtus mea, et lumen oculorum meorum, et ipsum non est mecum.

verses.text: My friends and my neighbours have drawn near, and stood against me. And they that were near me stood afar off:
verses.textLatin: Amici mei et proximi mei adversum me appropinquaverunt, et steterunt; et qui juxta me erant, de longe steterunt: et vim faciebant qui quærebant animam meam.

verses.text: And they that sought my soul used violence. And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, and studied deceits all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Et qui inquirebant mala mihi, locuti sunt vanitates, et dolos tota die meditabantur.

verses.text: But I, as a deaf man, heard not: and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem, tamquam surdus, non audiebam; et sicut mutus non aperiens os suum.

verses.text: And I became as a man that heareth not: and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Et factus sum sicut homo non audiens, et non habens in ore suo redargutiones.

verses.text: For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam in te, Domine, speravi; tu exaudies me, Domine Deus meus.

verses.text: For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.
verses.textLatin: Quia dixi: Nequando supergaudeant mihi inimici mei; et dum commoventur pedes mei, super me magna locuti sunt.

verses.text: For I am ready for scourges: and my sorrow is continually before me.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ego in flagella paratus sum, et dolor meus in conspectu meo semper.

verses.text: For I will declare my iniquity: and I will think for my sin.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam iniquitatem meam annuntiabo, et cogitabo pro peccato meo.

verses.text: But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
verses.textLatin: Inimici autem mei vivunt, et confirmati sunt super me: et multiplicati sunt qui oderunt me inique.

verses.text: They that render evil for good, have detracted me, because I followed goodness.
verses.textLatin: Qui retribuunt mala pro bonis detrahebant mihi, quoniam sequebar bonitatem.

verses.text: Forsake me not, O Lord my God: do not thou depart from me.
verses.textLatin: Ne derelinquas me, Domine Deus meus; ne discesseris a me.

verses.text: Attend unto my help, O Lord, the God of my salvation.
verses.textLatin: Intende in adjutorium meum, Domine Deus salutis meæ.

verses.text: Unto the end, for Idithun himself, a canticle of David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, ipsi Idithun. Canticum David.

verses.text: I said: I will take heed to my ways: that I sin not with my tongue. I have set a guard to my mouth, when the sinner stood against me.
verses.textLatin: Dixi: Custodiam vias meas: ut non delinquam in lingua mea. Posui ori meo custodiam, cum consisteret peccator adversum me.

verses.text: I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: and my sorrow was renewed.
verses.textLatin: Obmutui, et humiliatus sum, et silui a bonis; et dolor meus renovatus est.

verses.text: My heart grew hot within me: and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.
verses.textLatin: Concaluit cor meum intra me; et in meditatione mea exardescet ignis.

verses.text: I spoke with my tongue: O Lord, make me know my end. And what is the number of my days: that I may know what is wanting to me.
verses.textLatin: Locutus sum in lingua mea: Notum fac mihi, Domine, finem meum, et numerum dierum meorum quis est, ut sciam quid desit mihi.

verses.text: Behold thou hast made my days measurable: and my substance is as nothing before thee. And indeed all things are vanity: every man living.
verses.textLatin: Ecce mensurabiles posuisti dies meos, et substantia mea tamquam nihilum ante te. Verumtamen universa vanitas, omnis homo vivens.

verses.text: Surely man passeth as an image: yea, and he is disquieted in vain. He storeth up: and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen in imagine pertransit homo; sed et frustra conturbatur: thesaurizat, et ignorat cui congregabit ea.

verses.text: And now what is my hope? is it not the Lord? and my substance is with thee.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc quæ est exspectatio mea: nonne Dominus? et substantia mea apud te est.

verses.text: Deliver thou me from all my iniquities: thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.
verses.textLatin: Ab omnibus iniquitatibus meis erue me: opprobrium insipienti dedisti me.

verses.text: I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because thou hast done it.
verses.textLatin: Obmutui, et non aperui os meum, quoniam tu fecisti;

verses.text: Remove thy scourges from me. The strength of thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes:
verses.textLatin: amove a me plagas tuas.

verses.text: thou hast corrected man for iniquity. And thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: surely in vain is any man disquieted.
verses.textLatin: A fortitudine manus tuæ ego defeci in increpationibus: propter iniquitatem corripuisti hominem. Et tabescere fecisti sicut araneam animam ejus: verumtamen vane conturbatur omnis homo.

verses.text: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: give ear to my tears. Be not silent: for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi orationem meam, Domine, et deprecationem meam; auribus percipe lacrimas meas. Ne sileas, quoniam advena ego sum apud te, et peregrinus sicut omnes patres mei.

verses.text: O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, and be no more.
verses.textLatin: Remitte mihi, ut refrigerer priusquam abeam et amplius non ero.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David himself.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus ipsi David.

verses.text: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, and he was attentive to me.
verses.textLatin: Exspectans exspectavi Dominum, et intendit mihi.

verses.text: And he heard my prayers, and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs. And he set my feet upon a rock, and directed my steps.
verses.textLatin: Et exaudivit preces meas, et eduxit me de lacu miseriæ et de luto fæcis. Et statuit super petram pedes meos, et direxit gressus meos.

verses.text: And he put a new canticle into my mouth, a song to our God. Many shall see, and shall fear: and they shall hope in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et immisit in os meum canticum novum, carmen Deo nostro. Videbunt multi, et timebunt, et sperabunt in Domino.

verses.text: Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord; and who hath not had regard to vanities, and lying follies.
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir cujus est nomen Domini spes ejus, et non respexit in vanitates et insanias falsas.

verses.text: Thou hast multiplied thy wonderful works, O Lord my God: and in thy thoughts there is no one like to thee. I have declared and I have spoken they are multiplied above number.
verses.textLatin: Multa fecisti tu, Domine Deus meus, mirabilia tua; et cogitationibus tuis non est qui similis sit tibi. Annuntiavi et locutus sum: multiplicati sunt super numerum.

verses.text: Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire; but thou hast pierced ears for me. Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require:
verses.textLatin: Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti; aures autem perfecisti mihi. Holocaustum et pro peccato non postulasti;

verses.text: then said I, Behold I come. In the head of the book it is written of me
verses.textLatin: tunc dixi: Ecce venio. In capite libri scriptum est de me,

verses.text: that I should do thy will: O my God, I have desired it, and thy law in the midst of my heart.
verses.textLatin: ut facerem voluntatem tuam. Deus meus, volui, et legem tuam in medio cordis mei.

verses.text: I have declared thy justice in a great church, lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, thou knowest it.
verses.textLatin: Annuntiavi justitiam tuam in ecclesia magna; ecce labia mea non prohibebo: Domine, tu scisti.

verses.text: I have not hid thy justice within my heart: I have declared thy truth and thy salvation. I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth from a great council.
verses.textLatin: Justitiam tuam non abscondi in corde meo; veritatem tuam et salutare tuum dixi; non abscondi misericordiam tuam et veritatem tuam a concilio multo.

verses.text: Withhold not thou, O Lord, thy tender mercies from me: thy mercy and thy truth have always upheld me.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, Domine, ne longe facias miserationes tuas a me; misericordia tua et veritas tua semper susceperunt me.

verses.text: For evils without number have surrounded me; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see. They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: and my heart hath forsaken me.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam circumdederunt me mala quorum non est numerus; comprehenderunt me iniquitates meæ, et non potui ut viderem. Multiplicatæ sunt super capillos capitis mei, et cor meum dereliquit me.

verses.text: Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: look down, O Lord, to help me.
verses.textLatin: Complaceat tibi, Domine, ut eruas me; Domine, ad adjuvandum me respice.

verses.text: Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul to take it away. Let them be turned backward and be ashamed that desire evils to me.
verses.textLatin: Confundantur et revereantur simul, qui quærunt animam meam ut auferant eam; convertantur retrorsum et revereantur, qui volunt mihi mala.

verses.text: Let them immediately bear their confusion, that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.
verses.textLatin: Ferant confestim confusionem suam, qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge!

verses.text: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.
verses.textLatin: Exsultent et lætentur super te omnes quærentes te; et dicant semper: Magnificetur Dominus, qui diligunt salutare tuum.

verses.text: But I am a beggar and poor: the Lord is careful for me. Thou art my helper and my protector: O my God, be not slack.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem mendicus sum et pauper; Dominus sollicitus est mei. Adjutor meus et protector meus tu es; Deus meus, ne tardaveris.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David himself.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus ipsi David.

verses.text: Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem: in die mala liberabit eum Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Dominus conservet eum, et vivificet eum, et beatum faciat eum in terra, et non tradat eum in animam inimicorum ejus.

verses.text: The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.
verses.textLatin: Dominus opem ferat illi super lectum doloris ejus; universum stratum ejus versasti in infirmitate ejus.

verses.text: I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.
verses.textLatin: Ego dixi: Domine, miserere mei; sana animam meam, quia peccavi tibi.

verses.text: My enemies have spoken evils against me: when shall he die and his name perish?
verses.textLatin: Inimici mei dixerunt mala mihi: Quando morietur, et peribit nomen ejus?

verses.text: And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: his heart gathered together iniquity to itself. He went out and spoke to the same purpose.
verses.textLatin: Et si ingrediebatur ut videret, vana loquebatur; cor ejus congregavit iniquitatem sibi. Egrediebatur foras et loquebatur.

verses.text: All my enemies whispered together against me: they devised evils to me.
verses.textLatin: In idipsum adversum me susurrabant omnes inimici mei; adversum me cogitabant mala mihi.

verses.text: They determined against me an unjust word: shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?
verses.textLatin: Verbum iniquum constituerunt adversum me: Numquid qui dormit non adjiciet ut resurgat?

verses.text: For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.
verses.textLatin: Etenim homo pacis meæ in quo speravi, qui edebat panes meos, magnificavit super me supplantationem.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: and I will requite them.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, Domine, miserere mei, et resuscita me; et retribuam eis.

verses.text: By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.
verses.textLatin: In hoc cognovi quoniam voluisti me, quoniam non gaudebit inimicus meus super me.

verses.text: But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: and hast established me in thy sight for ever.
verses.textLatin: Me autem propter innocentiam suscepisti; et confirmasti me in conspectu tuo in æternum.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. So be it. So be it.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus Deus Israël a sæculo et usque in sæculum. Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: Unto the end, understanding for the sons of Core.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Intellectus filiis Core.

verses.text: As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; so my soul panteth after thee, O God.
verses.textLatin: Quemadmodum desiderat cervus ad fontes aquarum, ita desiderat anima mea ad te, Deus.

verses.text: My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; when shall I come and appear before the face of God?
verses.textLatin: Sitivit anima mea ad Deum fortem, vivum; quando veniam, et apparebo ante faciem Dei?

verses.text: My tears have been my bread day and night, whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?
verses.textLatin: Fuerunt mihi lacrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte, dum dicitur mihi quotidie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

verses.text: These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God: With the voice of joy and praise; the noise of one feasting.
verses.textLatin: Hæc recordatus sum, et effudi in me animam meam, quoniam transibo in locum tabernaculi admirabilis, usque ad domum Dei, in voce exsultationis et confessionis, sonus epulantis.

verses.text: Why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou trouble me? Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: the salvation of my countenance,
verses.textLatin: Quare tristis es, anima mea? et quare conturbas me? Spera in Deo, quoniam adhuc confitebor illi, salutare vultus mei,

verses.text: and my God. My soul is troubled within myself: therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.
verses.textLatin: et Deus meus. Ad meipsum anima mea conturbata est: propterea memor ero tui de terra Jordanis et Hermoniim a monte modico.

verses.text: Deep calleth on deep, at the noise of thy flood-gates. All thy heights and thy billows have passed over me.
verses.textLatin: Abyssus abyssum invocat, in voce cataractarum tuarum; omnia excelsa tua, et fluctus tui super me transierunt.

verses.text: In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; and a canticle to him in the night. With me is prayer to the God of my life.
verses.textLatin: In die mandavit Dominus misericordiam suam, et nocte canticum ejus; apud me oratio Deo vitæ meæ.

verses.text: I will say to God: Thou art my support. Why hast thou forgotten me? and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?
verses.textLatin: Dicam Deo: Susceptor meus es; quare oblitus es mei? et quare contristatus incedo, dum affligit me inimicus?

verses.text: Whilst my bones are broken, my enemies who trouble me have reproached me; Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God?
verses.textLatin: Dum confringuntur ossa mea, exprobraverunt mihi qui tribulant me inimici mei, dum dicunt mihi per singulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus?

verses.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me? Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: the salvation of my countenance, and my God.
verses.textLatin: Quare tristis es, anima mea? et quare conturbas me? Spera in Deo, quoniam adhuc confitebor illi, salutare vultus mei, et Deus meus.

verses.text: A psalm for David. Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David. Judica me, Deus, et discerne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab homine iniquo et doloso erue me.

verses.text: For thou art God my strength: why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?
verses.textLatin: Quia tu es, Deus, fortitudo mea: quare me repulisti? et quare tristis incedo, dum affligit me inimicus?

verses.text: Sent forth thy light and thy truth: they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: Emitte lucem tuam et veritatem tuam: ipsa me deduxerunt, et adduxerunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernacula tua.

verses.text: And I will go in to the altar of God: to God who giveth joy to my youth.
verses.textLatin: Et introibo ad altare Dei, ad Deum qui lætificat juventutem meam. Confitebor tibi in cithara, Deus, Deus meus.

verses.text: To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?
verses.textLatin: Quare tristis es, anima mea? et quare conturbas me? Spera in Deo, quoniam adhuc confitebor illi, salutare vultus mei, et Deus meus.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the sons of Core, to give understanding.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Filiis Core ad intellectum.

verses.text: We have heard, O God, with our ears: our fathers have declared to us, The work thou hast wrought in their days, and in the days of old.
verses.textLatin: Deus, auribus nostris audivimus, patres nostri annuntiaverunt nobis, opus quod operatus es in diebus eorum, et in diebus antiquis.

verses.text: Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and thou plantedst them: thou didst afflict the people and cast them out.
verses.textLatin: Manus tua gentes disperdidit, et plantasti eos; afflixisti populos, et expulisti eos.

verses.text: For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: neither did their own arm save them. But thy right hand and thy arm, and the light of thy countenance: because thou wast pleased with them.
verses.textLatin: Nec enim in gladio suo possederunt terram, et brachium eorum non salvavit eos: sed dextera tua et brachium tuum, et illuminatio vultus tui, quoniam complacuisti in eis.

verses.text: Thou art thyself my king and my God, who commandest the saving of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Tu es ipse rex meus et Deus meus, qui mandas salutes Jacob.

verses.text: Through thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: and through thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.
verses.textLatin: In te inimicos nostros ventilabimus cornu, et in nomine tuo spernemus insurgentes in nobis.

verses.text: For I will not trust in my bow: neither shall my sword save me.
verses.textLatin: Non enim in arcu meo sperabo, et gladius meus non salvabit me:

verses.text: But thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: and hast put them to shame that hate us.
verses.textLatin: salvasti enim nos de affligentibus nos, et odientes nos confudisti.

verses.text: In God shall we glory all the day long: and in thy name we will give praise for ever.
verses.textLatin: In Deo laudabimur tota die, et in nomine tuo confitebimur in sæculum.

verses.text: But now thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: and thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem repulisti et confudisti nos, et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris.

verses.text: Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: and they that hated us plundered for themselves.
verses.textLatin: Avertisti nos retrorsum post inimicos nostros, et qui oderunt nos diripiebant sibi.

verses.text: Thou hast given us up like sheep to be eaten: thou hast scattered us among the nations.
verses.textLatin: Dedisti nos tamquam oves escarum, et in gentibus dispersisti nos.

verses.text: Thou hast sold thy people for no price: and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.
verses.textLatin: Vendidisti populum tuum sine pretio, et non fuit multitudo in commutationibus eorum.

verses.text: Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.
verses.textLatin: Posuisti nos opprobrium vicinis nostris; subsannationem et derisum his qui sunt in circuitu nostro.

verses.text: Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: a shaking of the head among the people.
verses.textLatin: Posuisti nos in similitudinem gentibus; commotionem capitis in populis.

verses.text: All the day long my shame is before me: and the confusion of my face hath covered me,
verses.textLatin: Tota die verecundia mea contra me est, et confusio faciei meæ cooperuit me:

verses.text: At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: at the face of the enemy and persecutor.
verses.textLatin: a voce exprobrantis et obloquentis, a facie inimici et persequentis.

verses.text: All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten thee: and we have not done wickedly in thy covenant.
verses.textLatin: Hæc omnia venerunt super nos; nec obliti sumus te, et inique non egimus in testamento tuo.

verses.text: And our heart hath not turned back: neither hast thou turned aside our steps from thy way.
verses.textLatin: Et non recessit retro cor nostrum; et declinasti semitas nostras a via tua:

verses.text: For thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: and the shadow of death hath covered us.
verses.textLatin: quoniam humiliasti nos in loco afflictionis, et cooperuit nos umbra mortis.

verses.text: If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:
verses.textLatin: Si obliti sumus nomen Dei nostri, et si expandimus manus nostras ad deum alienum,

verses.text: Shall not God search out these things: for he knoweth the secrets of the heart. Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long: we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
verses.textLatin: nonne Deus requiret ista? ipse enim novit abscondita cordis. Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die; æstimati sumus sicut oves occisionis.

verses.text: Arise, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, and cast us not off to the end.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge; quare obdormis, Domine? exsurge, et ne repellas in finem.

verses.text: Why turnest thou thy face away? and forgettest our want and our trouble?
verses.textLatin: Quare faciem tuam avertis? oblivisceris inopiæ nostræ et tribulationis nostræ?

verses.text: For our soul is humbled down to the dust: our belly cleaveth to the earth.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam humiliata est in pulvere anima nostra; conglutinatus est in terra venter noster.

verses.text: Arise, O Lord, help us and redeem us for thy name’s sake.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Domine, adjuva nos, et redime nos propter nomen tuum.

verses.text: Unto the end, for them that shall be changed, for the sons of Core, for understanding. A canticle for the Beloved.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro iis qui commutabuntur. Filiis Core, ad intellectum. Canticum pro dilecto.

verses.text: My heart hath uttered a good word: I speak my works to the king: My tongue is the pen of a scrivener that writeth swiftly.
verses.textLatin: Eructavit cor meum verbum bonum: dico ego opera mea regi. Lingua mea calamus scribæ velociter scribentis.

verses.text: Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in thy lips; therefore hath God blessed thee for ever.
verses.textLatin: Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum, diffusa est gratia in labiis tuis: propterea benedixit te Deus in æternum.

verses.text: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh, O thou most mighty.
verses.textLatin: Accingere gladio tuo super femur tuum, potentissime.

verses.text: With thy comeliness and thy beauty set out, proceed prosperously, and reign. Because of truth and meekness and justice: and thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.
verses.textLatin: Specie tua et pulchritudine tua intende, prospere procede, et regna, propter veritatem, et mansuetudinem, et justitiam; et deducet te mirabiliter dextera tua.

verses.text: Thy arrows are sharp: under thee shall people fall, into the hearts of the king’s enemies.
verses.textLatin: Sagittæ tuæ acutæ: populi sub te cadent, in corda inimicorum regis.

verses.text: Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.
verses.textLatin: Sedes tua, Deus, in sæculum sæculi; virga directionis virga regni tui.

verses.text: Thou hast loved justice, and hated iniquity: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
verses.textLatin: Dilexisti justitiam, et odisti iniquitatem; propterea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ, præ consortibus tuis.

verses.text: Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume thy garments, from the ivory houses: out of which
verses.textLatin: Myrrha, et gutta, et casia a vestimentis tuis, a domibus eburneis; ex quibus delectaverunt te

verses.text: the daughters of kings have delighted thee in thy glory. The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; surrounded with variety.
verses.textLatin: filiæ regum in honore tuo. Astitit regina a dextris tuis in vestitu deaurato, circumdata varietate.

verses.text: Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: and forget thy people and thy father’s house.
verses.textLatin: Audi, filia, et vide, et inclina aurem tuam; et obliviscere populum tuum, et domum patris tui.

verses.text: And the king shall greatly desire thy beauty; for he is the Lord thy God, and him they shall adore.
verses.textLatin: Et concupiscet rex decorem tuum, quoniam ipse est Dominus Deus tuus, et adorabunt eum.

verses.text: And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.
verses.textLatin: Et filiæ Tyri in muneribus vultum tuum deprecabuntur; omnes divites plebis.

verses.text: All the glory of the king’s daughter is within in golden borders,
verses.textLatin: Omnis gloria ejus filiæ regis ab intus, in fimbriis aureis,

verses.text: clothed round about with varieties. After her shall virgins be brought to the king: her neighbours shall be brought to thee.
verses.textLatin: circumamicta varietatibus. Adducentur regi virgines post eam; proximæ ejus afferentur tibi.

verses.text: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: they shall be brought into the temple of the king.
verses.textLatin: Afferentur in lætitia et exsultatione; adducentur in templum regis.

verses.text: Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Pro patribus tuis nati sunt tibi filii; constitues eos principes super omnem terram.

verses.text: They shall remember thy name throughout all generations. Therefore shall people praise thee for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Memores erunt nominis tui in omni generatione et generationem: propterea populi confitebuntur tibi in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the sons of Core, for the hidden.
verses.textLatin: In finem, filiis Core, pro arcanis. Psalmus.

verses.text: Our God is our refuge and strength: a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Deus noster refugium et virtus; adjutor in tribulationibus quæ invenerunt nos nimis.

verses.text: Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Propterea non timebimus dum turbabitur terra, et transferentur montes in cor maris.

verses.text: Their waters roared and were troubled: the mountains were troubled with his strength.
verses.textLatin: Sonuerunt, et turbatæ sunt aquæ eorum; conturbati sunt montes in fortitudine ejus.

verses.text: The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: the most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle.
verses.textLatin: Fluminis impetus lætificat civitatem Dei: sanctificavit tabernaculum suum Altissimus.

verses.text: God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: God will help it in the morning early.
verses.textLatin: Deus in medio ejus, non commovebitur; adjuvabit eam Deus mane diluculo.

verses.text: Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: he uttered his voice, the earth trembled.
verses.textLatin: Conturbatæ sunt gentes, et inclinata sunt regna: dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.

verses.text: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.
verses.textLatin: Dominus virtutum nobiscum; susceptor noster Deus Jacob.

verses.text: Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth,
verses.textLatin: Venite, et videte opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram,

verses.text: making wars to cease even to the end of the earth. He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield he shall burn in the fire.
verses.textLatin: auferens bella usque ad finem terræ. Arcum conteret, et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni.

verses.text: Be still and see that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.
verses.textLatin: Vacate, et videte quoniam ego sum Deus; exaltabor in gentibus, et exaltabor in terra.

verses.text: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.
verses.textLatin: Dominus virtutum nobiscum; susceptor noster Deus Jacob.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the sons of Core.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro filiis Core. Psalmus.

verses.text: O clap your hands, all ye nations: shout unto God with the voice of joy,
verses.textLatin: Omnes gentes, plaudite manibus; jubilate Deo in voce exsultationis:

verses.text: For the Lord is high, terrible: a great king over all the earth.
verses.textLatin: quoniam Dominus excelsus, terribilis, rex magnus super omnem terram.

verses.text: He hath subdued the people under us; and the nations under our feet.
verses.textLatin: Subjecit populos nobis, et gentes sub pedibus nostris.

verses.text: He hath chosen for us his inheritance, the beauty of Jacob which he hath loved.
verses.textLatin: Elegit nobis hæreditatem suam; speciem Jacob quam dilexit.

verses.text: God is ascended with jubilee, and the Lord with the sound of trumpet.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit Deus in jubilo, et Dominus in voce tubæ.

verses.text: Sing praises to our God, sing ye: sing praises to our king, sing ye.
verses.textLatin: Psallite Deo nostro, psallite; psallite regi nostro, psallite:

verses.text: For God is the king of all the earth: sing ye wisely.
verses.textLatin: quoniam rex omnis terræ Deus, psallite sapienter.

verses.text: God shall reign over the nations: God sitteth on his holy throne.
verses.textLatin: Regnabit Deus super gentes; Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam.

verses.text: The princes of the people are gathered together, with the God of Abraham: for the strong gods of the earth are exceedingly exalted.
verses.textLatin: Principes populorum congregati sunt cum Deo Abraham, quoniam dii fortes terræ vehementer elevati sunt.

verses.text: A psalm of a canticle, for the sons of Core, on the second day of the week.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus cantici. Filiis Core, secunda sabbati.

verses.text: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.
verses.textLatin: Magnus Dominus et laudabilis nimis, in civitate Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.

verses.text: With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, on the sides of the north, the city of the great king.
verses.textLatin: Fundatur exsultatione universæ terræ mons Sion; latera aquilonis, civitas regis magni.

verses.text: In her houses shall God be known, when he shall protect her.
verses.textLatin: Deus in domibus ejus cognoscetur cum suscipiet eam.

verses.text: For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: they gathered together.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ecce reges terræ congregati sunt; convenerunt in unum.

verses.text: So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved:
verses.textLatin: Ipsi videntes, sic admirati sunt, conturbati sunt, commoti sunt.

verses.text: trembling took hold of them. There were pains as of a woman in labour.
verses.textLatin: Tremor apprehendit eos; ibi dolores ut parturientis:

verses.text: With a vehement wind thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.
verses.textLatin: in spiritu vehementi conteres naves Tharsis.

verses.text: As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God hath founded it for ever.
verses.textLatin: Sicut audivimus, sic vidimus, in civitate Domini virtutum, in civitate Dei nostri: Deus fundavit eam in æternum.

verses.text: We have received thy mercy, O God, in the midst of thy temple.
verses.textLatin: Suscepimus, Deus, misericordiam tuam in medio templi tui.

verses.text: According to thy name, O God, so also is thy praise unto the ends of the earth: thy right hand is full of justice.
verses.textLatin: Secundum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ; justitia plena est dextera tua.

verses.text: Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad; because of thy judgments, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Lætetur mons Sion, et exsultent filiæ Judæ, propter judicia tua, Domine.

verses.text: Surround Sion, and encompass her: tell ye in her towers.
verses.textLatin: Circumdate Sion, et complectimini eam; narrate in turribus ejus.

verses.text: Set your hearts on her strength; and distribute her houses, that ye may relate it in another generation.
verses.textLatin: Ponite corda vestra in virtute ejus, et distribuite domos ejus, ut enarretis in progenie altera.

verses.text: For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: he shall rule us for evermore.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi: ipse reget nos in sæcula.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for the sons of Core.
verses.textLatin: In finem, filiis Core. Psalmus.

verses.text: Hear these things, all ye nations: give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.
verses.textLatin: Audite hæc, omnes gentes; auribus percipite, omnes qui habitatis orbem:

verses.text: All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: both rich and poor together.
verses.textLatin: quique terrigenæ et filii hominum, simul in unum dives et pauper.

verses.text: My mouth shall speak wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.
verses.textLatin: Os meum loquetur sapientiam, et meditatio cordis mei prudentiam.

verses.text: I will incline my ear to a parable; I will open my proposition on the psaltery.
verses.textLatin: Inclinabo in parabolam aurem meam; aperiam in psalterio propositionem meam.

verses.text: Why shall I fear in the evil day? the iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.
verses.textLatin: Cur timebo in die mala? iniquitas calcanei mei circumdabit me.

verses.text: They that trust in their own strength, and glory in the multitude of their riches,
verses.textLatin: Qui confidunt in virtute sua, et in multitudine divitiarum suarum, gloriantur.

verses.text: No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: he shall not give to God his ransom,
verses.textLatin: Frater non redimit, redimet homo: non dabit Deo placationem suam,

verses.text: Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: and shall labour for ever,
verses.textLatin: et pretium redemptionis animæ suæ. Et laborabit in æternum;

verses.text: and shall still live unto the end.
verses.textLatin: et vivet adhuc in finem.

verses.text: He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: the senseless and the fool shall perish together: And they shall leave their riches to strangers:
verses.textLatin: Non videbit interitum, cum viderit sapientes morientes: simul insipiens et stultus peribunt. Et relinquent alienis divitias suas,

verses.text: and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever. Their dwelling places to all generations: they have called their lands by their names.
verses.textLatin: et sepulchra eorum domus illorum in æternum; tabernacula eorum in progenie et progenie: vocaverunt nomina sua in terris suis.

verses.text: And man when he was in honour did not understand; he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.
verses.textLatin: Et homo, cum in honore esset, non intellexit. Comparatus est jumentis insipientibus, et similis factus est illis.

verses.text: This way of theirs is a stumbling-block to them: and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.
verses.textLatin: Hæc via illorum scandalum ipsis; et postea in ore suo complacebunt.

verses.text: They are laid in hell like sheep: death shall feed upon them. And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning; and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.
verses.textLatin: Sicut oves in inferno positi sunt: mors depascet eos. Et dominabuntur eorum justi in matutino; et auxilium eorum veterascet in inferno a gloria eorum.

verses.text: But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, when he shall receive me.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen Deus redimet animam meam de manu inferi, cum acceperit me.

verses.text: Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich, and when the glory of his house shall be increased.
verses.textLatin: Ne timueris cum dives factus fuerit homo, et cum multiplicata fuerit gloria domus ejus:

verses.text: For when he shall die he shall take nothing away; nor shall his glory descend with him.
verses.textLatin: quoniam, cum interierit, non sumet omnia, neque descendet cum eo gloria ejus.

verses.text: For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: and he will praise thee when thou shalt do well to him.
verses.textLatin: Quia anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur; confitebitur tibi cum benefeceris ei.

verses.text: He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: and he shall never see light.
verses.textLatin: Introibit usque in progenies patrum suorum; et usque in æternum non videbit lumen.

verses.text: Man when he was in honour did not understand: he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.
verses.textLatin: Homo, cum in honore esset, non intellexit. Comparatus est jumentis insipientibus, et similis factus est illis.

verses.text: A psalm for Asaph. The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: and he hath called the earth. From the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof:
verses.textLatin: Psalmus Asaph. Deus deorum Dominus locutus est, et vocavit terram a solis ortu usque ad occasum.

verses.text: out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty.
verses.textLatin: Ex Sion species decoris ejus:

verses.text: God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, and shall not keep silence. A fire shall burn before him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about him.
verses.textLatin: Deus manifeste veniet; Deus noster, et non silebit. Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet; et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida.

verses.text: He shall call heaven from above, and the earth, to judge his people.
verses.textLatin: Advocabit cælum desursum, et terram, discernere populum suum.

verses.text: Gather ye together his saints to him: who set his covenant before sacrifices.
verses.textLatin: Congregate illi sanctos ejus, qui ordinant testamentum ejus super sacrificia.

verses.text: And the heavens shall declare his justice: for God is judge.
verses.textLatin: Et annuntiabunt cæli justitiam ejus, quoniam Deus judex est.

verses.text: Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: I am God, thy God.
verses.textLatin: Audi, populus meus, et loquar; Israël, et testificabor tibi: Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.

verses.text: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: and thy burnt offerings are always in my sight.
verses.textLatin: Non in sacrificiis tuis arguam te; holocausta autem tua in conspectu meo sunt semper.

verses.text: I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks.
verses.textLatin: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, neque de gregibus tuis hircos:

verses.text: For all the beasts of the woods are mine: the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.
verses.textLatin: quoniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvarum, jumenta in montibus, et boves.

verses.text: I know all the fowls of the air: and with me is the beauty of the field.
verses.textLatin: Cognovi omnia volatilia cæli, et pulchritudo agri mecum est.

verses.text: If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof.
verses.textLatin: Si esuriero, non dicam tibi: meus est enim orbis terræ et plenitudo ejus.

verses.text: Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? or shall I drink the blood of goats?
verses.textLatin: Numquid manducabo carnes taurorum? aut sanguinem hircorum potabo?

verses.text: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: and pay thy vows to the most High.
verses.textLatin: Immola Deo sacrificium laudis, et redde Altissimo vota tua.

verses.text: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
verses.textLatin: Et invoca me in die tribulationis: eruam te, et honorificabis me.

verses.text: But to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare my justices, and take my covenant in thy mouth?
verses.textLatin: Peccatori autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enarras justitias meas? et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum?

verses.text: Seeing thou hast hated discipline: and hast cast my words behind thee.
verses.textLatin: Tu vero odisti disciplinam, et projecisti sermones meos retrorsum.

verses.text: If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.
verses.textLatin: Si videbas furem, currebas cum eo; et cum adulteris portionem tuam ponebas.

verses.text: Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, and thy tongue framed deceits.
verses.textLatin: Os tuum abundavit malitia, et lingua tua concinnabat dolos.

verses.text: Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother’s son:
verses.textLatin: Sedens adversus fratrem tuum loquebaris, et adversus filium matris tuæ ponebas scandalum.

verses.text: these things hast thou done, and I was silent. Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.
verses.textLatin: Hæc fecisti, et tacui. Existimasti inique quod ero tui similis: arguam te, et statuam contra faciem tuam.

verses.text: Understand these things, you that forget God; lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.
verses.textLatin: Intelligite hæc, qui obliviscimini Deum, nequando rapiat, et non sit qui eripiat.

verses.text: The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: and there is the way by which I will shew him the salvation of God.
verses.textLatin: Sacrificium laudis honorificabit me, et illic iter quo ostendam illi salutare Dei.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm of David,
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David,

verses.text: When Nathan the prophet came to him, after he had sinned with Bethsabee. (2 Kings 12.)
verses.textLatin: cum venit ad eum Nathan propheta, quando intravit ad Bethsabee. (II Regum 12.)

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy. And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Deus, secundum magnam misericordiam tuam; et secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum, dele iniquitatem meam.

verses.text: Wash me yet more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
verses.textLatin: Amplius lava me ab iniquitate mea, et a peccato meo munda me.

verses.text: For I know my iniquity, and my sin is always before me.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam iniquitatem meam ego cognosco, et peccatum meum contra me est semper.

verses.text: To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.
verses.textLatin: Tibi soli peccavi, et malum coram te feci; ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis, et vincas cum judicaris.

verses.text: For behold I was conceived in iniquities; and in sins did my mother conceive me.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim in iniquitatibus conceptus sum, et in peccatis concepit me mater mea.

verses.text: For behold thou hast loved truth: the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim veritatem dilexisti; incerta et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi.

verses.text: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.
verses.textLatin: Asperges me hyssopo, et mundabor; lavabis me, et super nivem dealbabor.

verses.text: To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Auditui meo dabis gaudium et lætitiam, et exsultabunt ossa humiliata.

verses.text: Turn away thy face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Averte faciem tuam a peccatis meis, et omnes iniquitates meas dele.

verses.text: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels.
verses.textLatin: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis.

verses.text: Cast me not away from thy face; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
verses.textLatin: Ne projicias me a facie tua, et spiritum sanctum tuum ne auferas a me.

verses.text: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.
verses.textLatin: Redde mihi lætitiam salutaris tui, et spiritu principali confirma me.

verses.text: I will teach the unjust thy ways: and the wicked shall be converted to thee.
verses.textLatin: Docebo iniquos vias tuas, et impii ad te convertentur.

verses.text: Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol thy justice.
verses.textLatin: Libera me de sanguinibus, Deus, Deus salutis meæ, et exsultabit lingua mea justitiam tuam.

verses.text: O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
verses.textLatin: Domine, labia mea aperies, et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.

verses.text: For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium, dedissem utique; holocaustis non delectaberis.

verses.text: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
verses.textLatin: Sacrificium Deo spiritus contribulatus; cor contritum et humiliatum, Deus, non despicies.

verses.text: Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.
verses.textLatin: Benigne fac, Domine, in bona voluntate tua Sion, ut ædificentur muri Jerusalem.

verses.text: Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.
verses.textLatin: Tunc acceptabis sacrificium justitiæ, oblationes et holocausta; tunc imponent super altare tuum vitulos.

verses.text: Unto the end, understanding for David,
verses.textLatin: In finem. Intellectus David,

verses.text: when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul: David went to the house of Achimelech. (1 Kings 22.9.)
verses.textLatin: cum venit Doëg Idumæus, et nuntiavit Sauli: Venit David in domum Achimelech. (I Regum 22.9.)

verses.text: Why dost thou glory in malice, thou that art mighty in iniquity?
verses.textLatin: Quid gloriaris in malitia, qui potens es in iniquitate?

verses.text: All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.
verses.textLatin: Tota die injustitiam cogitavit lingua tua; sicut novacula acuta fecisti dolum.

verses.text: Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.
verses.textLatin: Dilexisti malitiam super benignitatem; iniquitatem magis quam loqui æquitatem.

verses.text: Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, O deceitful tongue.
verses.textLatin: Dilexisti omnia verba præcipitationis; lingua dolosa.

verses.text: Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.
verses.textLatin: Propterea Deus destruet te in finem; evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo, et radicem tuam de terra viventium.

verses.text: The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say:
verses.textLatin: Videbunt justi, et timebunt; et super eum ridebunt, et dicent:

verses.text: Behold the man that made not God his helper: But trusted in the abundance of his riches: and prevailed in his vanity.
verses.textLatin: Ecce homo qui non posuit Deum adjutorem suum; sed speravit in multitudine divitiarum suarum, et prævaluit in vanitate sua.

verses.text: But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem, sicut oliva fructifera in domo Dei; speravi in misericordia Dei, in æternum et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi in sæculum, quia fecisti; et exspectabo nomen tuum, quoniam bonum est in conspectu sanctorum tuorum.

verses.text: Unto the end, for Maeleth, understandings to David. The fool said in his heart: There is no God.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro Maëleth intelligentiæ David. Dixit insipiens in corde suo: Non est Deus.
