verses.text: They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: there is none that doth good.
verses.textLatin: Corrupti sunt, et abominabiles facti sunt in iniquitatibus; non est qui faciat bonum.

verses.text: God looked down from heaven on the children of men: to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.
verses.textLatin: Deus de cælo prospexit super filios hominum, ut videat si est intelligens, aut requirens Deum.

verses.text: All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, there is none that doth good, no not one.
verses.textLatin: Omnes declinaverunt; simul inutiles facti sunt: non est qui faciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

verses.text: Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, who eat up my people as they eat bread?
verses.textLatin: Nonne scient omnes qui operantur iniquitatem, qui devorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

verses.text: They have not called upon God: there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear. For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.
verses.textLatin: Deum non invocaverunt; illic trepidaverunt timore, ubi non erat timor. Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent: confusi sunt, quoniam Deus sprevit eos.

verses.text: Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
verses.textLatin: Quis dabit ex Sion salutare Israël? cum converterit Deus captivitatem plebis suæ, exsultabit Jacob, et lætabitur Israël.

verses.text: Unto the end, in verses, understanding for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in carminibus. Intellectus David,

verses.text: When the men of Ziph had come and said to Saul: Is not David hidden with us? (1 Kings 23.19.)
verses.textLatin: cum venissent Ziphæi, et dixissent ad Saul: Nonne David absconditus est apud nos? (I Regum 23.19.)

verses.text: Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.
verses.textLatin: Deus, in nomine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtute tua judica me.

verses.text: O God, hear my prayer: give ear to the words of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Deus, exaudi orationem meam; auribus percipe verba oris mei.

verses.text: For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: and they have not set God before their eyes.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam alieni insurrexerunt adversum me, et fortes quæsierunt animam meam, et non proposuerunt Deum ante conspectum suum.

verses.text: For behold God is my helper: and the Lord is the protector of my soul.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim Deus adjuvat me, et Dominus susceptor est animæ meæ.

verses.text: Turn back the evils upon my enemies; and cut them off in thy truth.
verses.textLatin: Averte mala inimicis meis; et in veritate tua disperde illos.

verses.text: I will freely sacrifice to thee, and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:
verses.textLatin: Voluntarie sacrificabo tibi, et confitebor nomini tuo, Domine, quoniam bonum est.

verses.text: For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me, et super inimicos meos despexit oculus meus.

verses.text: Unto the end, in verses, understanding for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in carminibus. Intellectus David.

verses.text: Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication:
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam, et ne despexeris deprecationem meam:

verses.text: be attentive to me and hear me. I am grieved in my exercise; and am troubled,
verses.textLatin: intende mihi, et exaudi me. Contristatus sum in exercitatione mea, et conturbatus sum

verses.text: at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner. For they have cast iniquities upon me: and in wrath they were troublesome to me.
verses.textLatin: a voce inimici, et a tribulatione peccatoris. Quoniam declinaverunt in me iniquitates, et in ira molesti erant mihi.

verses.text: My heart is troubled within me: and the fear of death is fallen upon me.
verses.textLatin: Cor meum conturbatum est in me, et formido mortis cecidit super me.

verses.text: Fear and trembling are come upon me: and darkness hath covered me.
verses.textLatin: Timor et tremor venerunt super me, et contexerunt me tenebræ.

verses.text: And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, and I will fly and be at rest?
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ, et volabo, et requiescam?

verses.text: Lo, I have gone far off flying away; and I abode in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Ecce elongavi fugiens, et mansi in solitudine.

verses.text: I waited for him that hath saved me from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.
verses.textLatin: Exspectabam eum qui salvum me fecit a pusillanimitate spiritus, et tempestate.

verses.text: Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.
verses.textLatin: Præcipita, Domine; divide linguas eorum: quoniam vidi iniquitatem et contradictionem in civitate.

verses.text: Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: and in the midst thereof are labour,
verses.textLatin: Die ac nocte circumdabit eam super muros ejus iniquitas; et labor in medio ejus,

verses.text: and injustice. And usury and deceit have not departed from its streets.
verses.textLatin: et injustitia: et non defecit de plateis ejus usura et dolus.

verses.text: For if my enemy had reviled me, I would verily have borne with it. And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, I would perhaps have hidden my self from him.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam si inimicus meus maledixisset mihi, sustinuissem utique. Et si is qui oderat me super me magna locutus fuisset, abscondissem me forsitan ab eo.

verses.text: But thou a man of one mind, my guide, and my familiar,
verses.textLatin: Tu vero homo unanimis, dux meus, et notus meus:

verses.text: Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: in the house of God we walked with consent.
verses.textLatin: qui simul mecum dulces capiebas cibos; in domo Dei ambulavimus cum consensu.

verses.text: Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into hell. For there is wickedness in their dwellings: in the midst of them.
verses.textLatin: Veniat mors super illos, et descendant in infernum viventes: quoniam nequitiæ in habitaculis eorum, in medio eorum.

verses.text: But I have cried to God: and the Lord will save me.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem ad Deum clamavi, et Dominus salvabit me.

verses.text: Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: and he shall hear my voice.
verses.textLatin: Vespere, et mane, et meridie, narrabo, et annuntiabo; et exaudiet vocem meam.

verses.text: He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: for among many they were with me.
verses.textLatin: Redimet in pace animam meam ab his qui appropinquant mihi: quoniam inter multos erant mecum.

verses.text: God shall hear, and the Eternal shall humble them. For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God:
verses.textLatin: Exaudiet Deus, et humiliabit illos, qui est ante sæcula. Non enim est illis commutatio, et non timuerunt Deum.

verses.text: he hath stretched forth his hand to repay. They have defiled his covenant,
verses.textLatin: Extendit manum suam in retribuendo; contaminaverunt testamentum ejus:

verses.text: they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, and his heart hath drawn near. His words are smoother than oil, and the same are darts.
verses.textLatin: divisi sunt ab ira vultus ejus, et appropinquavit cor illius. Molliti sunt sermones ejus super oleum; et ipsi sunt jacula.

verses.text: Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.
verses.textLatin: Jacta super Dominum curam tuam, et ipse te enutriet; non dabit in æternum fluctuationem justo.

verses.text: But thou, O God, shalt bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Tu vero, Deus, deduces eos in puteum interitus. Viri sanguinum et dolosi non dimidiabunt dies suos; ego autem sperabo in te, Domine.

verses.text: Unto the end, for a people that is removed at a distance from the sanctuary: for David, for an inscription of a title (or pillar) when the Philistines held him in Geth.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro populo qui a sanctis longe factus est. David in tituli inscriptionem, cum tenuerunt eum Allophyli in Geth.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Deus, quoniam conculcavit me homo; tota die impugnans, tribulavit me.

verses.text: My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; for they are many that make war against me.
verses.textLatin: Conculcaverunt me inimici mei tota die, quoniam multi bellantes adversum me.

verses.text: From the height of the day I shall fear: but I will trust in thee.
verses.textLatin: Ab altitudine diei timebo: ego vero in te sperabo.

verses.text: In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: I will not fear what flesh can do against me.
verses.textLatin: In Deo laudabo sermones meos; in Deo speravi: non timebo quid faciat mihi caro.

verses.text: All the day long they detested my words: all their thoughts were against me unto evil.
verses.textLatin: Tota die verba mea execrabantur; adversum me omnes cogitationes eorum in malum.

verses.text: They will dwell and hide themselves: they will watch my heel. As they have waited for my soul,
verses.textLatin: Inhabitabunt, et abscondent; ipsi calcaneum meum observabunt. Sicut sustinuerunt animam meam,

verses.text: for nothing shalt thou save them: in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces. O God,
verses.textLatin: pro nihilo salvos facies illos; in ira populos confringes.

verses.text: I have declared to thee my life: thou hast set my tears in thy sight, As also in thy promise.
verses.textLatin: Deus, vitam meam annuntiavi tibi; posuisti lacrimas meas in conspectu tuo, sicut et in promissione tua:

verses.text: Then shall my enemies be turned back. In what day soever I shall call upon thee, behold I know thou art my God.
verses.textLatin: tunc convertentur inimici mei retrorsum. In quacumque die invocavero te, ecce cognovi quoniam Deus meus es.

verses.text: In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.
verses.textLatin: In Deo laudabo verbum; in Domino laudabo sermonem. In Deo speravi: non timebo quid faciat mihi homo.

verses.text: In me, O God, are vows to thee, which I will pay, praises to thee:
verses.textLatin: In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, quæ reddam, laudationes tibi:

verses.text: Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.
verses.textLatin: quoniam eripuisti animam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu, ut placeam coram Deo in lumine viventium.

verses.text: Unto the end, destroy not, for David, for an inscription of a title, when he fled from Saul into the cave. (1 Kings 24.)
verses.textLatin: In finem, ne disperdas. David in tituli inscriptionem, cum fugeret a facie Saul in speluncam.(I Regum 24.)

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: for my soul trusteth in thee. And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, until iniquity pass away.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Deus, miserere mei, quoniam in te confidit anima mea. Et in umbra alarum tuarum sperabo, donec transeat iniquitas.

verses.text: I will cry to God the most High; to God who hath done good to me.
verses.textLatin: Clamabo ad Deum altissimum, Deum qui benefecit mihi.

verses.text: He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me. God hath sent his mercy and his truth,
verses.textLatin: Misit de cælo, et liberavit me; dedit in opprobrium conculcantes me. Misit Deus misericordiam suam et veritatem suam,

verses.text: and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled. The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
verses.textLatin: et eripuit animam meam de medio catulorum leonum. Dormivi conturbatus. Filii hominum dentes eorum arma et sagittæ, et lingua eorum gladius acutus.

verses.text: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory above all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Exaltare super cælos, Deus, et in omnem terram gloria tua.

verses.text: They prepared a snare for my feet; and they bowed down my soul. They dug a pit before my face, and they are fallen into it.
verses.textLatin: Laqueum paraverunt pedibus meis, et incurvaverunt animam meam. Foderunt ante faciem meam foveam, et inciderunt in eam.

verses.text: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.
verses.textLatin: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum; cantabo, et psalmum dicam.

verses.text: Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: I will arise early.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, gloria mea; exsurge, psalterium et cithara: exsurgam diluculo.

verses.text: I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine, et psalmum dicam tibi in gentibus:

verses.text: For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: and thy truth unto the clouds.
verses.textLatin: quoniam magnificata est usque ad cælos misericordia tua, et usque ad nubes veritas tua.

verses.text: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Exaltare super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua.

verses.text: Unto the end, destroy not, for David, for an inscription of a title.
verses.textLatin: In finem, ne disperdas. David in tituli inscriptionem.

verses.text: If in very deed you speak justice: judge right things, ye sons of men.
verses.textLatin: Si vere utique justitiam loquimini, recta judicate, filii hominum.

verses.text: For in your heart you work iniquity: your hands forge injustice in the earth.
verses.textLatin: Etenim in corde iniquitates operamini; in terra injustitias manus vestræ concinnant.

verses.text: The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: they have spoken false things.
verses.textLatin: Alienati sunt peccatores a vulva; erraverunt ab utero: locuti sunt falsa.

verses.text: Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:
verses.textLatin: Furor illis secundum similitudinem serpentis, sicut aspidis surdæ et obturantis aures suas,

verses.text: Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.
verses.textLatin: quæ non exaudiet vocem incantantium, et venefici incantantis sapienter.

verses.text: God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.
verses.textLatin: Deus conteret dentes eorum in ore ipsorum; molas leonum confringet Dominus.

verses.text: They shall come to nothing, like water running down; he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.
verses.textLatin: Ad nihilum devenient tamquam aqua decurrens; intendit arcum suum donec infirmentur.

verses.text: Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.
verses.textLatin: Sicut cera quæ fluit auferentur; supercecidit ignis, et non viderunt solem.

verses.text: Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, as alive, in his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Priusquam intelligerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum, sicut viventes sic in ira absorbet eos.

verses.text: The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.
verses.textLatin: Lætabitur justus cum viderit vindictam; manus suas lavabit in sanguine peccatoris.

verses.text: And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et dicet homo: Si utique est fructus justo, utique est Deus judicans eos in terra.

verses.text: Unto the end, destroy not, for David for an inscription of a title, when Saul sent and watched his house to kill him. (1 Kings 19.)
verses.textLatin: In finem, ne disperdas. David in tituli inscriptionem, quando misit Saul et custodivit domum ejus ut eum interficeret. (I Regum 19.)

verses.text: Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; and defend me from them that rise up against me.
verses.textLatin: Eripe me de inimicis meis, Deus meus, et ab insurgentibus in me libera me.

verses.text: Deliver me from them that work iniquity, and save me from bloody men.
verses.textLatin: Eripe me de operantibus iniquitatem, et de viris sanguinum salva me.

verses.text: For behold they have caught my soul: the mighty have rushed in upon me:
verses.textLatin: Quia ecce ceperunt animam meam; irruerunt in me fortes.

verses.text: Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.
verses.textLatin: Neque iniquitas mea, neque peccatum meum, Domine; sine iniquitate cucurri, et direxi.

verses.text: Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel. Attend to visit all the nations: have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge in occursum meum, et vide: et tu, Domine Deus virtutum, Deus Israël, intende ad visitandas omnes gentes: non miserearis omnibus qui operantur iniquitatem.

verses.text: They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: and shall go round about the city.
verses.textLatin: Convertentur ad vesperam, et famem patientur ut canes: et circuibunt civitatem.

verses.text: Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: for who, say they, hath heard us?
verses.textLatin: Ecce loquentur in ore suo, et gladius in labiis eorum: quoniam quis audivit?

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, Domine, deridebis eos; ad nihilum deduces omnes gentes.

verses.text: I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector:
verses.textLatin: Fortitudinem meam ad te custodiam, quia, Deus, susceptor meus es:

verses.text: My God, his mercy shall prevent me.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus misericordia ejus præveniet me.

verses.text: God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, lest at any time my people forget. Scatter them by thy power; and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:
verses.textLatin: Deus ostendet mihi super inimicos meos: ne occidas eos, nequando obliviscantur populi mei. Disperge illos in virtute tua, et depone eos, protector meus, Domine:

verses.text: For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: and let them be taken in their pride. And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of,
verses.textLatin: delictum oris eorum, sermonem labiorum ipsorum; et comprehendantur in superbia sua. Et de execratione et mendacio annuntiabuntur

verses.text: when they are consumed: when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more. And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, and all the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: in consummatione: in ira consummationis, et non erunt. Et scient quia Deus dominabitur Jacob, et finium terræ.

verses.text: They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: and shall go round about the city.
verses.textLatin: Convertentur ad vesperam, et famem patientur ut canes: et circuibunt civitatem.

verses.text: They shall be scattered abroad to eat, and shall murmur if they be not filled.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi dispergentur ad manducandum; si vero non fuerint saturati, et murmurabunt.

verses.text: But I will sing thy strength: and will extol thy mercy in the morning. For thou art become my support, and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem cantabo fortitudinem tuam, et exsultabo mane misericordiam tuam: quia factus es susceptor meus, et refugium meum in die tribulationis meæ.

verses.text: Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: my God my mercy.
verses.textLatin: Adjutor meus, tibi psallam, quia Deus susceptor meus es; Deus meus, misericordia mea.

verses.text: Unto the end, for them that shall be changed, for the inscription of a title, to David himself, for doctrine,
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro his qui immutabuntur, in tituli inscriptionem ipsi David, in doctrinam,

verses.text: when he set fire to Mesopotamia of Syria and Sobal: and Joab returned and slew of Edom, in the vale of the saltpits, twelve thousand men.
verses.textLatin: cum succendit Mesopotamiam Syriæ et Sobal, et convertit Joab, et percussit Idumæam in valle Salinarum duodecim millia.

verses.text: O God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.
verses.textLatin: Deus, repulisti nos, et destruxisti nos; iratus es, et misertus es nobis.

verses.text: Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.
verses.textLatin: Commovisti terram, et conturbasti eam; sana contritiones ejus, quia commota est.

verses.text: Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.
verses.textLatin: Ostendisti populo tuo dura; potasti nos vino compunctionis.

verses.text: Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: that they may flee from before the bow: That thy beloved may be delivered.
verses.textLatin: Dedisti metuentibus te significationem, ut fugiant a facie arcus; ut liberentur dilecti tui.

verses.text: Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.
verses.textLatin: Salvum fac dextera tua, et exaudi me.

verses.text: God hath spoken in his holy place: I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: Deus locutus est in sancto suo: lætabor, et partibor Sichimam; et convallem tabernaculorum metibor.

verses.text: Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: and Ephraim is the strength of my head. Juda is my king:
verses.textLatin: Meus est Galaad, et meus est Manasses; et Ephraim fortitudo capitis mei. Juda rex meus;

verses.text: Moab is the pot of my hope. Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: to me the foreigners are made subject.
verses.textLatin: Moab olla spei meæ. In Idumæam extendam calceamentum meum: mihi alienigenæ subditi sunt.

verses.text: Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?
verses.textLatin: Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam? quis deducet me usque in Idumæam?

verses.text: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?
verses.textLatin: nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos? et non egredieris, Deus, in virtutibus nostris?

verses.text: Give us help from trouble: for vain is the salvation of man.
verses.textLatin: Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione, quia vana salus hominis.

verses.text: Through God we shall do mightily: and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.
verses.textLatin: In Deo faciemus virtutem; et ipse ad nihilum deducet tribulantes nos.

verses.text: Unto the end, in hymns, for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. In hymnis David.

verses.text: Hear, O God, my supplication: be attentive to my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Deus, deprecationem meam; intende orationi meæ.

verses.text: To thee have I cried from the ends of the earth: when my heart was in anguish, thou hast exalted me on a rock. Thou hast conducted me;
verses.textLatin: A finibus terræ ad te clamavi, dum anxiaretur cor meum; in petra exaltasti me. Deduxisti me,

verses.text: for thou hast been my hope; a tower of strength against the face of the enemy.
verses.textLatin: quia factus es spes mea: turris fortitudinis a facie inimici.

verses.text: In thy tabernacle I shall dwell for ever: I shall be protected under the covert of thy wings.
verses.textLatin: Inhabitabo in tabernaculo tuo in sæcula; protegar in velamento alarum tuarum.

verses.text: For thou, my God, hast heard my prayer: thou hast given an inheritance to them that fear thy name.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu, Deus meus, exaudisti orationem meam; dedisti hæreditatem timentibus nomen tuum.

verses.text: Thou wilt add days to the days of the king: his years even to generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Dies super dies regis adjicies; annos ejus usque in diem generationis et generationis.

verses.text: He abideth for ever in the sight of God: his mercy and truth who shall search?
verses.textLatin: Permanet in æternum in conspectu Dei: misericordiam et veritatem ejus quis requiret?

verses.text: So will I sing a psalm to thy name for ever and ever: that I may pay my vows from day to day.
verses.textLatin: Sic psalmum dicam nomini tuo in sæculum sæculi, ut reddam vota mea de die in diem.

verses.text: Unto the end, for Idithun, a psalm of David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro Idithun. Psalmus David.

verses.text: Shall not my soul be subject to God? for from him is my salvation.
verses.textLatin: Nonne Deo subjecta erit anima mea? ab ipso enim salutare meum.

verses.text: For he is my God and my saviour: he is my protector, I shall be moved no more.
verses.textLatin: Nam et ipse Deus meus et salutaris meus; susceptor meus, non movebor amplius.

verses.text: How long do you rush in upon a man? you all kill, as if you were thrusting down a leaning wall, and a tottering fence.
verses.textLatin: Quousque irruitis in hominem? interficitis universi vos, tamquam parieti inclinato et maceriæ depulsæ.

verses.text: But they have thought to cast away my price; I ran in thirst: they blessed with their mouth, but cursed with their heart.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen pretium meum cogitaverunt repellere; cucurri in siti: ore suo benedicebant, et corde suo maledicebant.

verses.text: But be thou, O my soul, subject to God: for from him is my patience.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen Deo subjecta esto, anima mea, quoniam ab ipso patientia mea:

verses.text: For he is my God and my saviour: he is my helper, I shall not be moved.
verses.textLatin: quia ipse Deus meus et salvator meus, adjutor meus, non emigrabo.

verses.text: In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.
verses.textLatin: In Deo salutare meum et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.

verses.text: Trust in him, all ye congregation of people: pour out your hearts before him. God is our helper for ever.
verses.textLatin: Sperate in eo, omnis congregatio populi; effundite coram illo corda vestra: Deus adjutor noster in æternum.

verses.text: But vain are the sons of men, the sons of men are liars in the balances: that by vanity they may together deceive.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen vani filii hominum, mendaces filii hominum in stateris, ut decipiant ipsi de vanitate in idipsum.

verses.text: Trust not in iniquity, and cover not robberies: if riches abound, set not your heart upon them.
verses.textLatin: Nolite sperare in iniquitate, et rapinas nolite concupiscere; divitiæ si affluant, nolite cor apponere.

verses.text: God hath spoken once, these two things have I heard, that power belongeth to God,
verses.textLatin: Semel locutus est Deus; duo hæc audivi: quia potestas Dei est,

verses.text: and mercy to thee, O Lord; for thou wilt render to every man according to his works.
verses.textLatin: et tibi, Domine, misericordia: quia tu reddes unicuique juxta opera sua.

verses.text: A psalm of David while he was in the desert of Edom.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, cum esset in deserto Idumææ.

verses.text: O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day. For thee my soul hath thirsted; for thee my flesh, O how many ways!
verses.textLatin: Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vigilo. Sitivit in te anima mea; quam multipliciter tibi caro mea!

verses.text: In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.
verses.textLatin: In terra deserta, et invia, et inaquosa, sic in sancto apparui tibi, ut viderem virtutem tuam et gloriam tuam.

verses.text: For thy mercy is better than lives: thee my lips shall praise.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam melior est misericordia tua super vitas, labia mea laudabunt te.

verses.text: Thus will I bless thee all my life long: and in thy name I will lift up my hands.
verses.textLatin: Sic benedicam te in vita mea, et in nomine tuo levabo manus meas.

verses.text: Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.
verses.textLatin: Sicut adipe et pinguedine repleatur anima mea, et labiis exsultationis laudabit os meum.

verses.text: If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning:
verses.textLatin: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutinis meditabor in te.

verses.text: because thou hast been my helper. And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings:
verses.textLatin: Quia fuisti adjutor meus, et in velamento alarum tuarum exsultabo.

verses.text: my soul hath stuck close to thee: thy right hand hath received me.
verses.textLatin: Adhæsit anima mea post te; me suscepit dextera tua.

verses.text: But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth:
verses.textLatin: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsierunt animam meam: introibunt in inferiora terræ;

verses.text: They shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.
verses.textLatin: tradentur in manus gladii: partes vulpium erunt.

verses.text: But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.
verses.textLatin: Rex vero lætabitur in Deo; laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo: quia obstructum est os loquentium iniqua.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: Hear, O God, my prayer, when I make supplication to thee: deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Deus, orationem meam cum deprecor; a timore inimici eripe animam meam.

verses.text: Thou hast protected me from the assembly of the malignant; from the multitude of the workers of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Protexisti me a conventu malignantium, a multitudine operantium iniquitatem.

verses.text: For they have whetted their tongues like a sword; they have bent their bow, a bitter thing,
verses.textLatin: Quia exacuerunt ut gladium linguas suas; intenderunt arcum rem amaram,

verses.text: to shoot in secret the undefiled.
verses.textLatin: ut sagittent in occultis immaculatum.

verses.text: They will shoot at him on a sudden, and will not fear: they are resolute in wickedness. They have talked of hiding snares; they have said: Who shall see them?
verses.textLatin: Subito sagittabunt eum, et non timebunt; firmaverunt sibi sermonem nequam. Narraverunt ut absconderent laqueos; dixerunt: Quis videbit eos?

verses.text: They have searched after iniquities: they have failed in their search. Man shall come to a deep heart:
verses.textLatin: Scrutati sunt iniquitates; defecerunt scrutantes scrutinio. Accedet homo ad cor altum,

verses.text: and God shall be exalted. The arrows of children are their wounds:
verses.textLatin: et exaltabitur Deus. Sagittæ parvulorum factæ sunt plagæ eorum,

verses.text: and their tongues against them are made weak. All that saw them were troubled;
verses.textLatin: et infirmatæ sunt contra eos linguæ eorum. Conturbati sunt omnes qui videbant eos,

verses.text: and every man was afraid. And they declared the works of God: and understood his doings.
verses.textLatin: et timuit omnis homo. Et annuntiaverunt opera Dei, et facta ejus intellexerunt.

verses.text: The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him: and all the upright in heart shall be praised.
verses.textLatin: Lætabitur justus in Domino, et sperabit in eo, et laudabuntur omnes recti corde.

verses.text: To the end, a psalm of David. The canticle of Jeremias and Ezechiel to the people of the captivity, when they began to go out.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David, canticum Jeremiæ et Ezechielis populo transmigrationis, cum inciperent exire.

verses.text: A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion, et tibi reddetur votum in Jerusalem.

verses.text: O hear my prayer: all flesh shall come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi orationem meam; ad te omnis caro veniet.

verses.text: The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.
verses.textLatin: Verba iniquorum prævaluerunt super nos, et impietatibus nostris tu propitiaberis.

verses.text: Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: he shall dwell in thy courts. We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple,
verses.textLatin: Beatus quem elegisti et assumpsisti: inhabitabit in atriis tuis. Replebimur in bonis domus tuæ; sanctum est templum tuum,

verses.text: wonderful in justice. Hear us, O God our saviour, who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.
verses.textLatin: mirabile in æquitate. Exaudi nos, Deus, salutaris noster, spes omnium finium terræ, et in mari longe.

verses.text: Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power:
verses.textLatin: Præparans montes in virtute tua, accinctus potentia;

verses.text: who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves. The Gentiles shall be troubled,
verses.textLatin: qui conturbas profundum maris, sonum fluctuum ejus. Turbabuntur gentes,

verses.text: and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.
verses.textLatin: et timebunt qui habitant terminos a signis tuis; exitus matutini et vespere delectabis.

verses.text: Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; thou hast many ways enriched it. The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food: for so is its preparation.
verses.textLatin: Visitasti terram, et inebriasti eam; multiplicasti locupletare eam. Flumen Dei repletum est aquis; parasti cibum illorum: quoniam ita est præparatio ejus.

verses.text: Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.
verses.textLatin: Rivos ejus inebria; multiplica genimina ejus: in stillicidiis ejus lætabitur germinans.

verses.text: Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.
verses.textLatin: Benedices coronæ anni benignitatis tuæ, et campi tui replebuntur ubertate.

verses.text: The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: and the hills shall be girded about with joy,
verses.textLatin: Pinguescent speciosa deserti, et exsultatione colles accingentur.

verses.text: The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.
verses.textLatin: Induti sunt arietes ovium, et valles abundabunt frumento; clamabunt, etenim hymnum dicent.

verses.text: Unto the end, a canticle of a psalm of the resurrection.  Shout with joy to God, all the earth,
verses.textLatin: In finem. Canticum psalmi resurrectionis. Jubilate Deo, omnis terra;

verses.text: sing ye a psalm to his name; give glory to his praise.
verses.textLatin: psalmum dicite nomini ejus; date gloriam laudi ejus.

verses.text: Say unto God, How terrible are thy works, O Lord! in the multitude of thy strength thy enemies shall lie to thee.
verses.textLatin: Dicite Deo: Quam terribilia sunt opera tua, Domine! in multitudine virtutis tuæ mentientur tibi inimici tui.

verses.text: Let all the earth adore thee, and sing to thee: let it sing a psalm to thy name.
verses.textLatin: Omnis terra adoret te, et psallat tibi; psalmum dicat nomini tuo.

verses.text: Come and see the works of God; who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men.
verses.textLatin: Venite, et videte opera Dei: terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum.

verses.text: Who turneth the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass on foot: there shall we rejoice in him.
verses.textLatin: Qui convertit mare in aridam; in flumine pertransibunt pede: ibi lætabimur in ipso.

verses.text: Who by his power ruleth for ever: his eyes behold the nations; let not them that provoke him be exalted in themselves.
verses.textLatin: Qui dominatur in virtute sua in æternum; oculi ejus super gentes respiciunt: qui exasperant non exaltentur in semetipsis.

verses.text: O bless our God, ye Gentiles: and make the voice of his praise to be heard.
verses.textLatin: Benedicite, gentes, Deum nostrum, et auditam facite vocem laudis ejus:

verses.text: Who hath set my soul to live: and hath not suffered my feet to be moved:
verses.textLatin: qui posuit animam meam ad vitam, et non dedit in commotionem pedes meos.

verses.text: For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us by fire, as silver is tried.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam probasti nos, Deus; igne nos examinasti, sicut examinatur argentum.

verses.text: Thou hast brought us into a net, thou hast laid afflictions on our back:
verses.textLatin: Induxisti nos in laqueum; posuisti tribulationes in dorso nostro;

verses.text: thou hast set men over our heads. We have passed through fire and water, and thou hast brought us out into a refreshment.
verses.textLatin: imposuisti homines super capita nostra. Transivimus per ignem et aquam, et eduxisti nos in refrigerium.

verses.text: I will go into thy house with burnt offerings: I will pay thee my vows,
verses.textLatin: Introibo in domum tuam in holocaustis; reddam tibi vota mea

verses.text: which my lips have uttered, And my mouth hath spoken, when I was in trouble.
verses.textLatin: quæ distinxerunt labia mea: et locutum est os meum in tribulatione mea.

verses.text: I will offer up to thee holocausts full of marrow, with burnt offerings of rams: I will offer to thee bullocks with goats.
verses.textLatin: Holocausta medullata offeram tibi, cum incenso arietum; offeram tibi boves cum hircis.

verses.text: Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will tell you what great things he hath done for my soul.
verses.textLatin: Venite, audite, et narrabo, omnes qui timetis Deum, quanta fecit animæ meæ.

verses.text: I cried to him with my mouth: and I extolled him with my tongue.
verses.textLatin: Ad ipsum ore meo clamavi, et exaltavi sub lingua mea.

verses.text: If I have looked at iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.
verses.textLatin: Iniquitatem si aspexi in corde meo, non exaudiet Dominus.

verses.text: Therefore hath God heard me, and hath attended to the voice of my supplication.
verses.textLatin: Propterea exaudivit Deus, et attendit voci deprecationis meæ.

verses.text: Blessed be God, who hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Deus, qui non amovit orationem meam, et misericordiam suam a me.

verses.text: Unto the end, in hymns, a psalm of a canticle for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in hymnis. Psalmus cantici David.

verses.text: May God have mercy on us, and bless us: may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.
verses.textLatin: Deus misereatur nostri, et benedicat nobis; illuminet vultum suum super nos, et misereatur nostri:

verses.text: That we may know thy way upon earth: thy salvation in all nations.
verses.textLatin: ut cognoscamus in terra viam tuam, in omnibus gentibus salutare tuum.

verses.text: Let people confess to thee, O God: let all people give praise to thee.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus: confiteantur tibi populi omnes.

verses.text: Let the nations be glad and rejoice: for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.
verses.textLatin: Lætentur et exsultent gentes, quoniam judicas populos in æquitate, et gentes in terra dirigis.

verses.text: Let the people, O God, confess to thee: let all the people give praise to thee:
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur tibi populi, Deus: confiteantur tibi populi omnes.

verses.text: the earth hath yielded her fruit. May God, our God bless us,
verses.textLatin: Terra dedit fructum suum: benedicat nos Deus, Deus noster!

verses.text: may God bless us: and all the ends of the earth fear him.
verses.textLatin: Benedicat nos Deus, et metuant eum omnes fines terræ.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm of a canticle for David himself.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus cantici ipsi David.

verses.text: Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered: and let them that hate him flee from before his face.
verses.textLatin: Exsurgat Deus, et dissipentur inimici ejus; et fugiant qui oderunt eum a facie ejus.

verses.text: As smoke vanisheth, so let them vanish away: as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.
verses.textLatin: Sicut deficit fumus, deficiant; sicut fluit cera a facie ignis, sic pereant peccatores a facie Dei.

verses.text: And let the just feast, and rejoice before God: and be delighted with gladness.
verses.textLatin: Et justi epulentur, et exsultent in conspectu Dei, et delectentur in lætitia.

verses.text: Sing ye to God, sing a psalm to his name, make a way for him who ascendeth upon the west: the Lord is his name. Rejoice ye before him: but the wicked shall be troubled at his presence,
verses.textLatin: Cantate Deo; psalmum dicite nomini ejus: iter facite ei qui ascendit super occasum. Dominus nomen illi; exsultate in conspectu ejus. Turbabuntur a facie ejus,

verses.text: who is the father of orphans, and the judge of widows. God in his holy place:
verses.textLatin: patris orphanorum, et judicis viduarum; Deus in loco sancto suo.

verses.text: God who maketh men of one manner to dwell in a house: Who bringeth out them that were bound in strength; in like manner them that provoke, that dwell in sepulchres.
verses.textLatin: Deus qui inhabitare facit unius moris in domo; qui educit vinctos in fortitudine, similiter eos qui exasperant, qui habitant in sepulchris.

verses.text: O God, when thou didst go forth in the sight of thy people, when thou didst pass through the desert:
verses.textLatin: Deus, cum egredereris in conspectu populi tui, cum pertransires in deserto,

verses.text: The earth was moved, and the heavens dropped at the presence of the God of Sina, at the presence of the God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: terra mota est, etenim cæli distillaverunt, a facie Dei Sinai, a facie Dei Israël.

verses.text: Thou shalt set aside for thy inheritance a free rain, O God: and it was weakened, but thou hast made it perfect.
verses.textLatin: Pluviam voluntariam segregabis, Deus, hæreditati tuæ; et infirmata est, tu vero perfecisti eam.

verses.text: In it shall thy animals dwell; in thy sweetness, O God, thou hast provided for the poor.
verses.textLatin: Animalia tua habitabunt in ea; parasti in dulcedine tua pauperi, Deus.

verses.text: The Lord shall give the word to them that preach good tidings with great power.
verses.textLatin: Dominus dabit verbum evangelizantibus, virtute multa.

verses.text: The king of powers is of the beloved, of the beloved; and the beauty of the house shall divide spoils.
verses.textLatin: Rex virtutum dilecti, dilecti; et speciei domus dividere spolia.

verses.text: If you sleep among the midst of lots, you shall be as the wings of a dove covered with silver, and the hinder parts of her back with the paleness of gold.
verses.textLatin: Si dormiatis inter medios cleros, pennæ columbæ deargentatæ, et posteriora dorsi ejus in pallore auri.

verses.text: When he that is in heaven appointeth kings over her, they shall be whited with snow in Selmon.
verses.textLatin: Dum discernit cælestis reges super eam, nive dealbabuntur in Selmon.

verses.text: The mountain of God is a fat mountain. A curdled mountain, a fat mountain.
verses.textLatin: Mons Dei, mons pinguis: mons coagulatus, mons pinguis.

verses.text: Why suspect, ye curdled mountains? A mountain in which God is well pleased to dwell: for there the Lord shall dwell unto the end.
verses.textLatin: Ut quid suspicamini, montes coagulatos? mons in quo beneplacitum est Deo habitare in eo; etenim Dominus habitabit in finem.

verses.text: The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: the Lord is among them in Sina, in the holy place.
verses.textLatin: Currus Dei decem millibus multiplex, millia lætantium; Dominus in eis in Sina, in sancto.

verses.text: Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive; thou hast received gifts in men. Yea for those also that do not believe, the dwelling of the Lord God.
verses.textLatin: Ascendisti in altum, cepisti captivitatem, accepisti dona in hominibus; etenim non credentes inhabitare Dominum Deum.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord day by day: the God of our salvation will make our journey prosperous to us.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus die quotidie: prosperum iter faciet nobis Deus salutarium nostrorum.

verses.text: Our God is the God of salvation: and of the Lord, of the Lord are the issues from death.
verses.textLatin: Deus noster, Deus salvos faciendi; et Domini, Domini exitus mortis.

verses.text: But God shall break the heads of his enemies: the hairy crown of them that walk on in their sins.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen Deus confringet capita inimicorum suorum, verticem capilli perambulantium in delictis suis.

verses.text: The Lord said: I will turn them from Basan, I will turn them into the depth of the sea:
verses.textLatin: Dixit Dominus: Ex Basan convertam, convertam in profundum maris:

verses.text: That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thy enemies; the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same.
verses.textLatin: ut intingatur pes tuus in sanguine; lingua canum tuorum ex inimicis, ab ipso.

verses.text: They have seen thy goings, O God, the goings of my God: of my king who is in his sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus, ingressus Dei mei, regis mei, qui est in sancto.

verses.text: Princes went before joined with singers, in the midst of young damsels playing on timbrels.
verses.textLatin: Prævenerunt principes conjuncti psallentibus, in medio juvencularum tympanistriarum.

verses.text: In the churches bless ye God the Lord, from the fountains of Israel.
verses.textLatin: In ecclesiis benedicite Deo Domino de fontibus Israël.

verses.text: There is Benjamin a youth, in ecstasy of mind. The princes of Juda are their leaders: the princes of Zabulon, the princes of Nephthali.
verses.textLatin: Ibi Benjamin adolescentulus, in mentis excessu; principes Juda, duces eorum; principes Zabulon, principes Nephthali.

verses.text: Command thy strength, O God: confirm, O God, what thou hast wrought in us.
verses.textLatin: Manda, Deus, virtuti tuæ; confirma hoc, Deus, quod operatus es in nobis.

verses.text: From thy temple in Jerusalem, kings shall offer presents to thee.
verses.textLatin: A templo tuo in Jerusalem, tibi offerent reges munera.

verses.text: Rebuke the wild beasts of the reeds, the congregation of bulls with the kine of the people; who seek to exclude them who are tried with silver. Scatter thou the nations that delight in wars:
verses.textLatin: Increpa feras arundinis; congregatio taurorum in vaccis populorum: ut excludant eos qui probati sunt argento. Dissipa gentes quæ bella volunt.

verses.text: ambassadors shall come out of Egypt: Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands to God.
verses.textLatin: Venient legati ex Ægypto; Æthiopia præveniet manus ejus Deo.

verses.text: Sing to God, ye kingdoms of the earth: sing ye to the Lord: Sing ye to God,
verses.textLatin: Regna terræ, cantate Deo; psallite Domino; psallite Deo.

verses.text: who mounteth above the heaven of heavens, to the east. Behold he will give to his voice the voice of power:
verses.textLatin: Qui ascendit super cælum cæli, ad orientem: ecce dabit voci suæ vocem virtutis.

verses.text: give ye glory to God for Israel, his magnificence, and his power is in the clouds.
verses.textLatin: Date gloriam Deo super Israël; magnificentia ejus et virtus ejus in nubibus.

verses.text: God is wonderful in his saints: the God of Israel is he who will give power and strength to his people. Blessed be God.
verses.textLatin: Mirabilis Deus in sanctis suis; Deus Israël ipse dabit virtutem et fortitudinem plebi suæ. Benedictus Deus!

verses.text: Unto the end, for them that shall be changed; for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro iis qui commutabuntur. David.

verses.text: Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul.
verses.textLatin: Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam.

verses.text: I stick fast in the mire of the deep: and there is no sure standing. I am come into the depth of the sea: and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.
verses.textLatin: Infixus sum in limo profundi et non est substantia. Veni in altitudinem maris, et tempestas demersit me.

verses.text: I have laboured with crying; my jaws are become hoarse, my eyes have failed, whilst I hope in my God.
verses.textLatin: Laboravi clamans, raucæ factæ sunt fauces meæ; defecerunt oculi mei, dum spero in Deum meum.

verses.text: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head, who hate me without cause. My enemies are grown strong who have wrongfully persecuted me: then did I pay that which I took not away.
verses.textLatin: Multiplicati sunt super capillos capitis mei qui oderunt me gratis. Confortati sunt qui persecuti sunt me inimici mei injuste; quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam.

verses.text: O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee:
verses.textLatin: Deus, tu scis insipientiam meam; et delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita.

verses.text: Let not them be ashamed for me, who look for thee, O Lord, the Lord of hosts. Let them not be confounded on my account, who seek thee, O God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Non erubescant in me qui exspectant te, Domine, Domine virtutum; non confundantur super me qui quærunt te, Deus Israël.

verses.text: Because for thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam propter te sustinui opprobrium; operuit confusio faciem meam.

verses.text: I am become a stranger to my brethren, and an alien to the sons of my mother.
verses.textLatin: Extraneus factus sum fratribus meis, et peregrinus filiis matris meæ.

verses.text: For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up: and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam zelus domus tuæ comedit me, et opprobria exprobrantium tibi ceciderunt super me.

verses.text: And I covered my soul in fasting: and it was made a reproach to me.
verses.textLatin: Et operui in jejunio animam meam, et factum est in opprobrium mihi.

verses.text: And I made haircloth my garment: and I became a byword to them.
verses.textLatin: Et posui vestimentum meum cilicium; et factus sum illis in parabolam.

verses.text: They that sat in the gate spoke against me: and they that drank wine made me their song.
verses.textLatin: Adversum me loquebantur qui sedebant in porta, et in me psallebant qui bibebant vinum.

verses.text: But as for me, my prayer is to thee, O Lord; for the time of thy good pleasure, O God. In the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
verses.textLatin: Ego vero orationem meam ad te, Domine; tempus beneplaciti, Deus. In multitudine misericordiæ tuæ, exaudi me in veritate salutis tuæ.

verses.text: Draw me out of the mire, that I may not stick fast: deliver me from them that hate me, and out of the deep waters.
verses.textLatin: Eripe me de luto, ut non infigar; libera me ab iis qui oderunt me, et de profundis aquarum.

verses.text: Let not the tempest of water drown me, nor the deep swallow me up: and let not the pit shut her mouth upon me.
verses.textLatin: Non me demergat tempestas aquæ, neque absorbeat me profundum, neque urgeat super me puteus os suum.

verses.text: Hear me, O Lord, for thy mercy is kind; look upon me according to the multitude of thy tender mercies.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi me, Domine, quoniam benigna est misericordia tua; secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum respice in me.

verses.text: And turn not away thy face from thy servant: for I am in trouble, hear me speedily.
verses.textLatin: Et ne avertas faciem tuam a puero tuo; quoniam tribulor, velociter exaudi me.

verses.text: Attend to my soul, and deliver it: save me because of my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Intende animæ meæ, et libera eam; propter inimicos meos, eripe me.

verses.text: Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, and my shame.
verses.textLatin: Tu scis improperium meum, et confusionem meam, et reverentiam meam;

verses.text: In thy sight are all they that afflict me; my heart hath expected reproach and misery. And I looked for one that would grieve together with me, but there was none: and for one that would comfort me, and I found none.
verses.textLatin: in conspectu tuo sunt omnes qui tribulant me. Improperium exspectavit cor meum et miseriam: et sustinui qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit; et qui consolaretur, et non inveni.

verses.text: And they gave me gall for my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
verses.textLatin: Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto.

verses.text: Let their table become as a snare before them, and a recompense, and a stumbling-block.
verses.textLatin: Fiat mensa eorum coram ipsis in laqueum, et in retributiones, et in scandalum.

verses.text: Let their eyes be darkened that they see not; and their back bend thou down always.
verses.textLatin: Obscurentur oculi eorum, ne videant, et dorsum eorum semper incurva.

verses.text: Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.
verses.textLatin: Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos.

verses.text: Let their habitation be made desolate: and let there be none to dwell in their tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: Fiat habitatio eorum deserta, et in tabernaculis eorum non sit qui inhabitet.

verses.text: Because they have persecuted him whom thou hast smitten; and they have added to the grief of my wounds.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam quem tu percussisti persecuti sunt, et super dolorem vulnerum meorum addiderunt.

verses.text: Add thou iniquity upon their iniquity: and let them not come into thy justice.
verses.textLatin: Appone iniquitatem super iniquitatem eorum, et non intrent in justitiam tuam.

verses.text: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; and with the just let them not be written.
verses.textLatin: Deleantur de libro viventium, et cum justis non scribantur.

verses.text: But I am poor and sorrowful: thy salvation, O God, hath set me up.
verses.textLatin: Ego sum pauper et dolens; salus tua, Deus, suscepit me.

verses.text: I will praise the name of God with a canticle: and I will magnify him with praise.
verses.textLatin: Laudabo nomen Dei cum cantico, et magnificabo eum in laude:

verses.text: And it shall please God better than a young calf, that bringeth forth horns and hoofs.
verses.textLatin: et placebit Deo super vitulum novellum, cornua producentem et ungulas.

verses.text: Let the poor see and rejoice: seek ye God, and your soul shall live.
verses.textLatin: Videant pauperes, et lætentur; quærite Deum, et vivet anima vestra:

verses.text: For the Lord hath heard the poor: and hath not despised his prisoners.
verses.textLatin: quoniam exaudivit pauperes Dominus, et vinctos suos non despexit.

verses.text: Let the heavens and the earth praise him; the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein.
verses.textLatin: Laudent illum cæli et terra; mare, et omnia reptilia in eis.

verses.text: For God will save Sion, and the cities of Juda shall be built up. And they shall dwell there, and acquire it by inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam Deus salvam faciet Sion, et ædificabuntur civitates Juda, et inhabitabunt ibi, et hæreditate acquirent eam.

verses.text: And the seed of his servants shall possess it; and they that love his name shall dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Et semen servorum ejus possidebit eam; et qui diligunt nomen ejus habitabunt in ea.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David, to bring to remembrance that the Lord saved him.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David in rememorationem, quod salvum fecerit eum Dominus.

verses.text: O God, come to my assistance; O Lord, make haste to help me.
verses.textLatin: Deus, in adjutorium meum intende; Domine, ad adjuvandum me festina.

verses.text: Let them be confounded and ashamed that seek my soul:
verses.textLatin: Confundantur, et revereantur, qui quærunt animam meam.

verses.text: Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame that desire evils to me: Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.
verses.textLatin: Avertantur retrorsum, et erubescant, qui volunt mihi mala; avertantur statim erubescentes qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge!

verses.text: Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.
verses.textLatin: Exsultent et lætentur in te omnes qui quærunt te; et dicant semper: Magnificetur Dominus, qui diligunt salutare tuum.

verses.text: But I am needy and poor; O God, help me. Thou art my helper and my deliverer: O Lord, make no delay.
verses.textLatin: Ego vero egenus et pauper sum; Deus, adjuva me. Adjutor meus et liberator meus es tu; Domine, ne moreris.

verses.text: A psalm for David. Of the sons of Jonadab, and the former captives. In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion:
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David, filiorum Jonadab, et priorum captivorum. In te, Domine, speravi; non confundar in æternum.

verses.text: deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me. Incline thy ear unto me, and save me.
verses.textLatin: In justitia tua libera me, et eripe me: inclina ad me aurem tuam, et salva me.

verses.text: Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: that thou mayst make me safe. For thou art my firmament and my refuge.
verses.textLatin: Esto mihi in Deum protectorem, et in locum munitum, ut salvum me facias: quoniam firmamentum meum et refugium meum es tu.

verses.text: Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus, eripe me de manu peccatoris, et de manu contra legem agentis, et iniqui:

verses.text: For thou art my patience, O Lord: my hope, O Lord, from my youth.
verses.textLatin: quoniam tu es patientia mea, Domine; Domine, spes mea a juventute mea.

verses.text: By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: from my mother’s womb thou art my protector. Of thee I shall continually sing:
verses.textLatin: In te confirmatus sum ex utero; de ventre matris meæ tu es protector meus; in te cantatio mea semper.

verses.text: I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.
verses.textLatin: Tamquam prodigium factus sum multis; et tu adjutor fortis.

verses.text: Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; thy greatness all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Repleatur os meum laude, ut cantem gloriam tuam, tota die magnitudinem tuam.

verses.text: Cast me not off in the time of old age: when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.
verses.textLatin: Ne projicias me in tempore senectutis; cum defecerit virtus mea, ne derelinquas me.

verses.text: For my enemies have spoken against me; and they that watched my soul have consulted together,
verses.textLatin: Quia dixerunt inimici mei mihi, et qui custodiebant animam meam consilium fecerunt in unum,

verses.text: Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, for there is none to deliver him.
verses.textLatin: dicentes: Deus dereliquit eum: persequimini et comprehendite eum, quia non est qui eripiat.

verses.text: O God, be not thou far from me: O my God, make haste to my help.
verses.textLatin: Deus, ne elongeris a me; Deus meus, in auxilium meum respice.

verses.text: Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.
verses.textLatin: Confundantur et deficiant detrahentes animæ meæ; operiantur confusione et pudore qui quærunt mala mihi.

verses.text: But I will always hope; and will add to all thy praise.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem semper sperabo, et adjiciam super omnem laudem tuam.

verses.text: My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; thy salvation all the day long. Because I have not known learning,
verses.textLatin: Os meum annuntiabit justitiam tuam, tota die salutare tuum. Quoniam non cognovi litteraturam,

verses.text: I will enter into the powers of the Lord: O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.
verses.textLatin: introibo in potentias Domini; Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius.

verses.text: Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.
verses.textLatin: Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea; et usque nunc pronuntiabo mirabilia tua.

verses.text: And unto old age and grey hairs: O God, forsake me not, Until I shew forth thy arm to all the generation that is to come: Thy power,
verses.textLatin: Et usque in senectam et senium, Deus, ne derelinquas me, donec annuntiem brachium tuum generationi omni quæ ventura est, potentiam tuam,

verses.text: and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: O God, who is like to thee?
verses.textLatin: et justitiam tuam, Deus, usque in altissima; quæ fecisti magnalia, Deus: quis similis tibi?

verses.text: How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:
verses.textLatin: Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas! et conversus vivificasti me, et de abyssis terræ iterum reduxisti me.

verses.text: Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; and turning to me thou hast comforted me.
verses.textLatin: Multiplicasti magnificentiam tuam; et conversus consolatus es me.

verses.text: For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: O God, I will sing to thee with the harp, thou holy one of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Nam et ego confitebor tibi in vasis psalmi veritatem tuam, Deus; psallam tibi in cithara, sanctus Israël.

verses.text: My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; and my soul which thou hast redeemed.
verses.textLatin: Exsultabunt labia mea cum cantavero tibi; et anima mea quam redemisti.

verses.text: Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.
verses.textLatin: Sed et lingua mea tota die meditabitur justitiam tuam, cum confusi et reveriti fuerint qui quærunt mala mihi.

verses.text: A psalm on Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus, in Salomonem.

verses.text: Give to the king thy judgment, O God, and to the king’s son thy justice: To judge thy people with justice, and thy poor with judgment.
verses.textLatin: Deus, judicium tuum regi da, et justitiam tuam filio regis; judicare populum tuum in justitia, et pauperes tuos in judicio.

verses.text: Let the mountains receive peace for the people: and the hills justice.
verses.textLatin: Suscipiant montes pacem populo, et colles justitiam.

verses.text: He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: and he shall humble the oppressor.
verses.textLatin: Judicabit pauperes populi, et salvos faciet filios pauperum, et humiliabit calumniatorem.

verses.text: And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, throughout all generations.
verses.textLatin: Et permanebit cum sole, et ante lunam, in generatione et generationem.

verses.text: He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; and as showers falling gently upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Descendet sicut pluvia in vellus, et sicut stillicidia stillantia super terram.

verses.text: In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, till the moon be taken away.
verses.textLatin: Orietur in diebus ejus justitia, et abundantia pacis, donec auferatur luna.

verses.text: And he shall rule from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et dominabitur a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos orbis terrarum.

verses.text: Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: and his enemies shall lick the ground.
verses.textLatin: Coram illo procident Æthiopes, et inimici ejus terram lingent.

verses.text: The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:
verses.textLatin: Reges Tharsis et insulæ munera offerent; reges Arabum et Saba dona adducent:

verses.text: And all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him.
verses.textLatin: et adorabunt eum omnes reges terræ; omnes gentes servient ei.

verses.text: For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: and the needy that had no helper.
verses.textLatin: Quia liberabit pauperem a potente, et pauperem cui non erat adjutor.

verses.text: He shall spare the poor and needy: and he shall save the souls of the poor.
verses.textLatin: Parcet pauperi et inopi, et animas pauperum salvas faciet.

verses.text: He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: and their names shall be honourable in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Ex usuris et iniquitate redimet animas eorum, et honorabile nomen eorum coram illo.

verses.text: And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: they shall bless him all the day.
verses.textLatin: Et vivet, et dabitur ei de auro Arabiæ; et adorabunt de ipso semper, tota die benedicent ei.

verses.text: And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium; superextolletur super Libanum fructus ejus, et florebunt de civitate sicut fœnum terræ.

verses.text: Let his name be blessed for evermore: his name continueth before the sun. And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: all nations shall magnify him.
verses.textLatin: Sit nomen ejus benedictum in sæcula; ante solem permanet nomen ejus. Et benedicentur in ipso omnes tribus terræ; omnes gentes magnificabunt eum.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone doth wonderful things.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus Deus Israël, qui facit mirabilia solus.

verses.text: And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.
verses.textLatin: Et benedictum nomen majestatis ejus in æternum, et replebitur majestate ejus omnis terra. Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: The praises of David, the son of Jesse, are ended.
verses.textLatin: Defecerunt laudes David, filii Jesse.

verses.text: A psalm for Asaph. How good is God to Israel, to them that are of a right heart!
verses.textLatin: Psalmus Asaph. Quam bonus Israël Deus, his qui recto sunt corde!

verses.text: But my feet were almost moved; my steps had wellnigh slipped.
verses.textLatin: Mei autem pene moti sunt pedes, pene effusi sunt gressus mei:

verses.text: Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, seeing the prosperity of sinners.
verses.textLatin: quia zelavi super iniquos, pacem peccatorum videns.

verses.text: For there is no regard to their death, nor is there strength in their stripes.
verses.textLatin: Quia non est respectus morti eorum, et firmamentum in plaga eorum.

verses.text: They are not in the labour of men: neither shall they be scourged like other men.
verses.textLatin: In labore hominum non sunt, et cum hominibus non flagellabuntur.

verses.text: Therefore pride hath held them fast: they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Ideo tenuit eos superbia; operti sunt iniquitate et impietate sua.

verses.text: Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: they have passed into the affection of the heart.
verses.textLatin: Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum; transierunt in affectum cordis.

verses.text: They have thought and spoken wickedness: they have spoken iniquity on high.
verses.textLatin: Cogitaverunt et locuti sunt nequitiam; iniquitatem in excelso locuti sunt.

verses.text: They have set their mouth against heaven: and their tongue hath passed through the earth.
verses.textLatin: Posuerunt in cælum os suum, et lingua eorum transivit in terra.

verses.text: Therefore will my people return here and full days shall be found in them.
verses.textLatin: Ideo convertetur populus meus hic, et dies pleni invenientur in eis.

verses.text: And they said: How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt: Quomodo scit Deus, et si est scientia in excelso?

verses.text: Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world they have obtained riches.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ipsi peccatores, et abundantes in sæculo obtinuerunt divitias.

verses.text: And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, and washed my hands among the innocent.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Ergo sine causa justificavi cor meum, et lavi inter innocentes manus meas,

verses.text: And I have been scourged all the day; and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.
verses.textLatin: et fui flagellatus tota die, et castigatio mea in matutinis.

verses.text: If I said: I will speak thus; behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.
verses.textLatin: Si dicebam: Narrabo sic; ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobavi.

verses.text: I studied that I might know this thing, it is a labour in my sight:
verses.textLatin: Existimabam ut cognoscerem hoc; labor est ante me:

verses.text: Until I go into the sanctuary of God, and understand concerning their last ends.
verses.textLatin: donec intrem in sanctuarium Dei, et intelligam in novissimis eorum.

verses.text: But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: when they were lifted up thou hast cast them down.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen propter dolos posuisti eis; dejecisti eos dum allevarentur.

verses.text: How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? subito defecerunt: perierunt propter iniquitatem suam.

verses.text: As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Velut somnium surgentium, Domine, in civitate tua imaginem ipsorum ad nihilum rediges.

verses.text: For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed:
verses.textLatin: Quia inflammatum est cor meum, et renes mei commutati sunt;

verses.text: and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.
verses.textLatin: et ego ad nihilum redactus sum, et nescivi:

verses.text: I am become as a beast before thee: and I am always with thee.
verses.textLatin: ut jumentum factus sum apud te, et ego semper tecum.

verses.text: Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, and with thy glory thou hast received me.
verses.textLatin: Tenuisti manum dexteram meam, et in voluntate tua deduxisti me, et cum gloria suscepisti me.

verses.text: For what have I in heaven? and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?
verses.textLatin: Quid enim mihi est in cælo? et a te quid volui super terram?

verses.text: For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.
verses.textLatin: Defecit caro mea et cor meum; Deus cordis mei, et pars mea, Deus in æternum.

verses.text: For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.
verses.textLatin: Quia ecce qui elongant se a te peribunt; perdidisti omnes qui fornicantur abs te.

verses.text: But it is good for me to adhere to my God, to put my hope in the Lord God: That I may declare all thy praises, in the gates of the daughter of Sion.
verses.textLatin: Mihi autem adhærere Deo bonum est; ponere in Domino Deo spem meam: ut annuntiem omnes prædicationes tuas in portis filiæ Sion.

verses.text: Understanding for Asaph.  O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?
verses.textLatin: Intellectus Asaph. Ut quid, Deus, repulisti in finem, iratus est furor tuus super oves pascuæ tuæ?

verses.text: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast possessed from the beginning. The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.
verses.textLatin: Memor esto congregationis tuæ, quam possedisti ab initio. Redemisti virgam hæreditatis tuæ, mons Sion, in quo habitasti in eo.

verses.text: Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Leva manus tuas in superbias eorum in finem: quanta malignatus est inimicus in sancto!

verses.text: And they that hate thee have made their boasts, in the midst of thy solemnity. They have set up their ensigns for signs,
verses.textLatin: Et gloriati sunt qui oderunt te in medio solemnitatis tuæ; posuerunt signa sua, signa:

verses.text: and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top. As with axes in a wood of trees,
verses.textLatin: et non cognoverunt sicut in exitu super summum. Quasi in silva lignorum securibus

verses.text: they have cut down at once the gates thereof, with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.
verses.textLatin: exciderunt januas ejus in idipsum; in securi et ascia dejecerunt eam.

verses.text: They have set fire to thy sanctuary: they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Incenderunt igni sanctuarium tuum; in terra polluerunt tabernaculum nominis tui.

verses.text: They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt in corde suo cognatio eorum simul: Quiescere faciamus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.

verses.text: Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: and he will know us no more.
verses.textLatin: Signa nostra non vidimus; jam non est propheta; et nos non cognoscet amplius.

verses.text: How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, Deus, improperabit inimicus? irritat adversarius nomen tuum in finem?

verses.text: Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?
verses.textLatin: Ut quid avertis manum tuam, et dexteram tuam de medio sinu tuo in finem?

verses.text: But God is our king before ages: he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula: operatus est salutem in medio terræ.

verses.text: Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.
verses.textLatin: Tu confirmasti in virtute tua mare; contribulasti capita draconum in aquis.

verses.text: Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.
verses.textLatin: Tu confregisti capita draconis; dedisti eum escam populis Æthiopum.

verses.text: Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.
verses.textLatin: Tu dirupisti fontes et torrentes; tu siccasti fluvios Ethan.

verses.text: Thine is the day, and thine is the night: thou hast made the morning light and the sun.
verses.textLatin: Tuus est dies, et tua est nox; tu fabricatus es auroram et solem.

verses.text: Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: the summer and the spring were formed by thee.
verses.textLatin: Tu fecisti omnes terminos terræ; æstatem et ver tu plasmasti ea.

verses.text: Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.
verses.textLatin: Memor esto hujus: inimicus improperavit Domino, et populus insipiens incitavit nomen tuum.

verses.text: Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.
verses.textLatin: Ne tradas bestiis animas confitentes tibi, et animas pauperum tuorum ne obliviscaris in finem.

verses.text: Have regard to thy covenant: for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Respice in testamentum tuum, quia repleti sunt qui obscurati sunt terræ domibus iniquitatum.

verses.text: Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: the poor and needy shall praise thy name.
verses.textLatin: Ne avertatur humilis factus confusus; pauper et inops laudabunt nomen tuum.

verses.text: Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Deus, judica causam tuam; memor esto improperiorum tuorum, eorum quæ ab insipiente sunt tota die.

verses.text: Forget not the voices of thy enemies: the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.
verses.textLatin: Ne obliviscaris voces inimicorum tuorum: superbia eorum qui te oderunt ascendit semper.

verses.text: Unto the end, corrupt not, a psalm of a canticle for Asaph.
verses.textLatin: In finem, ne corrumpas. Psalmus cantici Asaph.

verses.text: We will praise thee, O God: we will praise, and we will call upon thy name. We will relate thy wondrous works:
verses.textLatin: Confitebimur tibi, Deus, confitebimur, et invocabimus nomen tuum; narrabimus mirabilia tua.

verses.text: when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.
verses.textLatin: Cum accepero tempus, ego justitias judicabo.

verses.text: The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: I have established the pillars thereof.
verses.textLatin: Liquefacta est terra et omnes qui habitant in ea: ego confirmavi columnas ejus.

verses.text: I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.
verses.textLatin: Dixi iniquis: Nolite inique agere: et delinquentibus: Nolite exaltare cornu:

verses.text: Lift not up your horn on high: speak not iniquity against God.
verses.textLatin: nolite extollere in altum cornu vestrum; nolite loqui adversus Deum iniquitatem.

verses.text: For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills:
verses.textLatin: Quia neque ab oriente, neque ab occidente, neque a desertis montibus:

verses.text: for God is the judge. One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up:
verses.textLatin: quoniam Deus judex est. Hunc humiliat, et hunc exaltat:

verses.text: for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture. And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: all the sinners of the earth shall drink.
verses.textLatin: quia calix in manu Domini vini meri, plenus misto. Et inclinavit ex hoc in hoc; verumtamen fæx ejus non est exinanita: bibent omnes peccatores terræ.

verses.text: But I will declare for ever: I will sing to the God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem annuntiabo in sæculum; cantabo Deo Jacob:
