verses.text: And I will break all the horns of sinners: but the horns of the just shall be exalted.
verses.textLatin: et omnia cornua peccatorum confringam, et exaltabuntur cornua justi.

verses.text: Unto the end, in praises, a psalm for Asaph: a canticle to the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: In finem, in laudibus. Psalmus Asaph, canticum ad Assyrios.

verses.text: In Judea God is known: his name is great in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Notus in Judæa Deus; in Israël magnum nomen ejus.

verses.text: And his place is in peace: and his abode in Sion:
verses.textLatin: Et factus est in pace locus ejus, et habitatio ejus in Sion.

verses.text: There hath he broken the powers of bows, the shield, the sword, and the battle.
verses.textLatin: Ibi confregit potentias arcuum, scutum, gladium, et bellum.

verses.text: Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills.
verses.textLatin: Illuminans tu mirabiliter a montibus æternis;

verses.text: All the foolish of heart were troubled. They have slept their sleep; and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.
verses.textLatin: turbati sunt omnes insipientes corde. Dormierunt somnum suum, et nihil invenerunt omnes viri divitiarum in manibus suis.

verses.text: At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.
verses.textLatin: Ab increpatione tua, Deus Jacob, dormitaverunt qui ascenderunt equos.

verses.text: Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? from that time thy wrath.
verses.textLatin: Tu terribilis es; et quis resistet tibi? ex tunc ira tua.

verses.text: Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: the earth trembled and was still,
verses.textLatin: De cælo auditum fecisti judicium: terra tremuit et quievit

verses.text: When God arose in judgment, to save all the meek of the earth.
verses.textLatin: cum exsurgeret in judicium Deus, ut salvos faceret omnes mansuetos terræ.

verses.text: For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam cogitatio hominis confitebitur tibi, et reliquiæ cogitationis diem festum agent tibi.

verses.text: Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: all you that are round about him bring presents. To him that is terrible,
verses.textLatin: Vovete et reddite Domino Deo vestro, omnes qui in circuitu ejus affertis munera: terribili,

verses.text: even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: to the terrible with the kings of the earth.
verses.textLatin: et ei qui aufert spiritum principum: terribili apud reges terræ.

verses.text: Unto the end, for Idithun, a psalm of Asaph.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro Idithun. Psalmus Asaph.

verses.text: I cried to the Lord with my voice; to God with my voice, and he gave ear to me.
verses.textLatin: Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi; voce mea ad Deum, et intendit mihi.

verses.text: In the days of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night, and I was not deceived. My soul refused to be comforted:
verses.textLatin: In die tribulationis meæ Deum exquisivi; manibus meis nocte contra eum, et non sum deceptus. Renuit consolari anima mea;

verses.text: I remembered God, and was delighted, and was exercised, and my spirit swooned away.
verses.textLatin: memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum, et exercitatus sum, et defecit spiritus meus.

verses.text: My eyes prevented the watches: I was troubled, and I spoke not.
verses.textLatin: Anticipaverunt vigilias oculi mei; turbatus sum, et non sum locutus.

verses.text: I thought upon the days of old: and I had in my mind the eternal years.
verses.textLatin: Cogitavi dies antiquos, et annos æternos in mente habui.

verses.text: And I meditated in the night with my own heart: and I was exercised and I swept my spirit.
verses.textLatin: Et meditatus sum nocte cum corde meo, et exercitabar, et scopebam spiritum meum.

verses.text: Will God then cast off for ever? or will he never be more favourable again?
verses.textLatin: Numquid in æternum projiciet Deus? aut non apponet ut complacitior sit adhuc?

verses.text: Or will he cut off his mercy for ever, from generation to generation?
verses.textLatin: aut in finem misericordiam suam abscindet, a generatione in generationem?

verses.text: Or will God forget to shew mercy? or will he in his anger shut up his mercies?
verses.textLatin: aut obliviscetur misereri Deus? aut continebit in ira sua misericordias suas?

verses.text: And I said, Now have I begun: this is the change of the right hand of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Nunc cœpi; hæc mutatio dexteræ Excelsi.

verses.text: I remembered the works of the Lord: for I will be mindful of thy wonders from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Memor fui operum Domini, quia memor ero ab initio mirabilium tuorum:

verses.text: And I will meditate on all thy works: and will be employed in thy inventions.
verses.textLatin: et meditabor in omnibus operibus tuis, et in adinventionibus tuis exercebor.

verses.text: Thy way, O God, is in the holy place: who is the great God like our God?
verses.textLatin: Deus, in sancto via tua: quis deus magnus sicut Deus noster?

verses.text: Thou art the God that dost wonders. Thou hast made thy power known among the nations:
verses.textLatin: Tu es Deus qui facis mirabilia: notam fecisti in populis virtutem tuam.

verses.text: with thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people the children of Jacob and of Joseph.
verses.textLatin: Redemisti in brachio tuo populum tuum, filios Jacob et Joseph.

verses.text: The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee: and they were afraid, and the depths were troubled.
verses.textLatin: Viderunt te aquæ, Deus; viderunt te aquæ, et timuerunt: et turbatæ sunt abyssi.

verses.text: Great was the noise of the waters: the clouds sent out a sound. For thy arrows pass:
verses.textLatin: Multitudo sonitus aquarum; vocem dederunt nubes. Etenim sagittæ tuæ transeunt;

verses.text: the voice of thy thunder in a wheel. Thy lightnings enlightened the world: the earth shook and trembled.
verses.textLatin: vox tonitrui tui in rota. Illuxerunt coruscationes tuæ orbi terræ; commota est, et contremuit terra.

verses.text: Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters: and thy footsteps shall not be known.
verses.textLatin: In mari via tua, et semitæ tuæ in aquis multis, et vestigia tua non cognoscentur.

verses.text: Thou hast conducted thy people like sheep, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Deduxisti sicut oves populum tuum, in manu Moysi et Aaron.

verses.text: Understanding for Asaph. Attend, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Intellectus Asaph. Attendite, popule meus, legem meam; inclinate aurem vestram in verba oris mei.

verses.text: I will open my mouth in parables: I will utter propositions from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Aperiam in parabolis os meum; loquar propositiones ab initio.

verses.text: How great things have we heard and known, and our fathers have told us.
verses.textLatin: Quanta audivimus, et cognovimus ea, et patres nostri narraverunt nobis.

verses.text: They have not been hidden from their children, in another generation. Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, and his wonders which he hath done.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt occultata a filiis eorum in generatione altera, narrantes laudes Domini et virtutes ejus, et mirabilia ejus quæ fecit.

verses.text: And he set up a testimony in Jacob: and made a law in Israel. How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children:
verses.textLatin: Et suscitavit testimonium in Jacob, et legem posuit in Israël, quanta mandavit patribus nostris nota facere ea filiis suis:

verses.text: that another generation might know them. The children that should be born and should rise up, and declare them to their children.
verses.textLatin: ut cognoscat generatio altera: filii qui nascentur et exsurgent, et narrabunt filiis suis,

verses.text: That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: and may seek his commandments.
verses.textLatin: ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscantur operum Dei, et mandata ejus exquirant:

verses.text: That they may not become like their fathers, a perverse and exasperating generation. A generation that set not their heart aright: and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
verses.textLatin: ne fiant, sicut patres eorum, generatio prava et exasperans; generatio quæ non direxit cor suum, et non est creditus cum Deo spiritus ejus.

verses.text: The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: they have turned back in the day of battle.
verses.textLatin: Filii Ephrem, intendentes et mittentes arcum, conversi sunt in die belli.

verses.text: They kept not the covenant of God: and in his law they would not walk.
verses.textLatin: Non custodierunt testamentum Dei, et in lege ejus noluerunt ambulare.

verses.text: And they forgot his benefits, and his wonders that he had shewn them.
verses.textLatin: Et obliti sunt benefactorum ejus, et mirabilium ejus quæ ostendit eis.

verses.text: Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Tanis.
verses.textLatin: Coram patribus eorum fecit mirabilia in terra Ægypti, in campo Taneos.

verses.text: He divided the sea and brought them through: and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.
verses.textLatin: Interrupit mare, et perduxit eos, et statuit aquas quasi in utre:

verses.text: And he conducted them with a cloud by day: and all the night with a light of fire.
verses.textLatin: et deduxit eos in nube diei, et tota nocte in illuminatione ignis.

verses.text: He struck the rock in the wilderness: and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.
verses.textLatin: Interrupit petram in eremo, et adaquavit eos velut in abysso multa.

verses.text: He brought forth water out of the rock: and made streams run down as rivers.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit aquam de petra, et deduxit tamquam flumina aquas.

verses.text: And they added yet more sin against him: they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.
verses.textLatin: Et apposuerunt adhuc peccare ei; in iram excitaverunt Excelsum in inaquoso.

verses.text: And they tempted God in their hearts, by asking meat for their desires.
verses.textLatin: Et tentaverunt Deum in cordibus suis, ut peterent escas animabus suis.

verses.text: And they spoke ill of God: they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?
verses.textLatin: Et male locuti sunt de Deo; dixerunt: Numquid poterit Deus parare mensam in deserto?

verses.text: Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, and the streams overflowed. Can he also give bread, or provide a table for his people?
verses.textLatin: quoniam percussit petram, et fluxerunt aquæ, et torrentes inundaverunt. Numquid et panem poterit dare, aut parare mensam populo suo?

verses.text: Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.
verses.textLatin: Ideo audivit Dominus et distulit; et ignis accensus est in Jacob, et ira ascendit in Israël:

verses.text: Because they believed not in God: and trusted not in his salvation.
verses.textLatin: quia non crediderunt in Deo, nec speraverunt in salutari ejus.

verses.text: And he had commanded the clouds from above, and had opened the doors of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Et mandavit nubibus desuper, et januas cæli aperuit.

verses.text: And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them the bread of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Et pluit illis manna ad manducandum, et panem cæli dedit eis.

verses.text: Man ate the bread of angels: he sent them provisions in abundance.
verses.textLatin: Panem angelorum manducavit homo; cibaria misit eis in abundantia.

verses.text: He removed the south wind from heaven: and by his power brought in the southwest wind.
verses.textLatin: Transtulit austrum de cælo, et induxit in virtute sua africum.

verses.text: And he rained upon them flesh as dust: and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Et pluit super eos sicut pulverem carnes, et sicut arenam maris volatilia pennata.

verses.text: And they fell in the midst of their camp, round about their pavilions.
verses.textLatin: Et ceciderunt in medio castrorum eorum, circa tabernacula eorum.

verses.text: So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire:
verses.textLatin: Et manducaverunt, et saturati sunt nimis, et desiderium eorum attulit eis:

verses.text: they were not defrauded of that which they craved. As yet their meat was in their mouth:
verses.textLatin: non sunt fraudati a desiderio suo. Adhuc escæ eorum erant in ore ipsorum,

verses.text: and the wrath of God came upon them. And he slew the fat ones amongst them, and brought down the chosen men of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et ira Dei ascendit super eos: et occidit pingues eorum, et electos Israël impedivit.

verses.text: In all these things they sinned still: and they believed not for his wondrous works.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus his peccaverunt adhuc, et non crediderunt in mirabilibus ejus.

verses.text: And their days were consumed in vanity, and their years in haste.
verses.textLatin: Et defecerunt in vanitate dies eorum, et anni eorum cum festinatione.

verses.text: When he slew them, then they sought him: and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.
verses.textLatin: Cum occideret eos, quærebant eum et revertebantur, et diluculo veniebant ad eum.

verses.text: And they remembered that God was their helper: and the most high God their redeemer.
verses.textLatin: Et rememorati sunt quia Deus adjutor est eorum, et Deus excelsus redemptor eorum est.

verses.text: And they loved him with their mouth: and with their tongue they lied unto him:
verses.textLatin: Et dilexerunt eum in ore suo, et lingua sua mentiti sunt ei;

verses.text: But their heart was not right with him: nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.
verses.textLatin: cor autem eorum non erat rectum cum eo, nec fideles habiti sunt in testamento ejus.

verses.text: But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: and will not destroy them. And many a time did he turn away his anger: and did not kindle all his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Ipse autem est misericors, et propitius fiet peccatis eorum, et non disperdet eos. Et abundavit ut averteret iram suam, et non accendit omnem iram suam.

verses.text: And he remembered that they are flesh: a wind that goeth and returneth not.
verses.textLatin: Et recordatus est quia caro sunt, spiritus vadens et non rediens.

verses.text: How often did they provoke him in the desert: and move him to wrath in the place without water?
verses.textLatin: Quoties exacerbaverunt eum in deserto; in iram concitaverunt eum in inaquoso?

verses.text: And they turned back and tempted God: and grieved the holy one of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et conversi sunt, et tentaverunt Deum, et sanctum Israël exacerbaverunt.

verses.text: They remembered not his hand, in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:
verses.textLatin: Non sunt recordati manus ejus, die qua redemit eos de manu tribulantis:

verses.text: How he wrought his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the field of Tanis.
verses.textLatin: sicut posuit in Ægypto signa sua, et prodigia sua in campo Taneos;

verses.text: And he turned their rivers into blood, and their showers that they might not drink.
verses.textLatin: et convertit in sanguinem flumina eorum, et imbres eorum, ne biberent.

verses.text: He sent amongst them divers sorts of flies, which devoured them: and frogs which destroyed them.
verses.textLatin: Misit in eos cœnomyiam, et comedit eos, et ranam, et disperdidit eos;

verses.text: And he gave up their fruits to the blast, and their labours to the locust.
verses.textLatin: et dedit ærugini fructus eorum, et labores eorum locustæ;

verses.text: And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.
verses.textLatin: et occidit in grandine vineas eorum, et moros eorum in pruina;

verses.text: And he gave up their cattle to the hail, and their stock to the fire.
verses.textLatin: et tradidit grandini jumenta eorum, et possessionem eorum igni;

verses.text: And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.
verses.textLatin: misit in eos iram indignationis suæ, indignationem, et iram, et tribulationem, immissiones per angelos malos.

verses.text: He made a way for a path to his anger: he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.
verses.textLatin: Viam fecit semitæ iræ suæ: non pepercit a morte animabus eorum, et jumenta eorum in morte conclusit:

verses.text: And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.
verses.textLatin: et percussit omne primogenitum in terra Ægypti; primitias omnis laboris eorum in tabernaculis Cham:

verses.text: And he took away his own people as sheep: and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
verses.textLatin: et abstulit sicut oves populum suum, et perduxit eos tamquam gregem in deserto:

verses.text: And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
verses.textLatin: et deduxit eos in spe, et non timuerunt, et inimicos eorum operuit mare.

verses.text: And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: the mountain which his right hand had purchased. And he cast out the Gentiles before them: and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.
verses.textLatin: Et induxit eos in montem sanctificationis suæ, montem quem acquisivit dextera ejus; et ejecit a facie eorum gentes, et sorte divisit eis terram in funiculo distributionis;

verses.text: And he made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: et habitare fecit in tabernaculis eorum tribus Israël.

verses.text: Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: and they kept not his testimonies.
verses.textLatin: Et tentaverunt, et exacerbaverunt Deum excelsum, et testimonia ejus non custodierunt.

verses.text: And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.
verses.textLatin: Et averterunt se, et non servaverunt pactum: quemadmodum patres eorum, conversi sunt in arcum pravum.

verses.text: They provoked him to anger on their hills: and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.
verses.textLatin: In iram concitaverunt eum in collibus suis, et in sculptilibus suis ad æmulationem eum provocaverunt.

verses.text: God heard, and despised them, and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.
verses.textLatin: Audivit Deus, et sprevit, et ad nihilum redegit valde Israël.

verses.text: And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.
verses.textLatin: Et repulit tabernaculum Silo, tabernaculum suum, ubi habitavit in hominibus.

verses.text: And he delivered their strength into captivity: and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Et tradidit in captivitatem virtutem eorum, et pulchritudinem eorum in manus inimici.

verses.text: And he shut up his people under the sword: and he despised his inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Et conclusit in gladio populum suum, et hæreditatem suam sprevit.

verses.text: Fire consumed their young men: and their maidens were not lamented.
verses.textLatin: Juvenes eorum comedit ignis, et virgines eorum non sunt lamentatæ.

verses.text: Their priests fell by the sword: and their widows did not mourn.
verses.textLatin: Sacerdotes eorum in gladio ceciderunt, et viduæ eorum non plorabantur.

verses.text: And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.
verses.textLatin: Et excitatus est tamquam dormiens Dominus, tamquam potens crapulatus a vino.

verses.text: And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: he put them to an everlasting reproach.
verses.textLatin: Et percussit inimicos suos in posteriora; opprobrium sempiternum dedit illis.

verses.text: And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:
verses.textLatin: Et repulit tabernaculum Joseph, et tribum Ephraim non elegit:

verses.text: But he chose the tribe of Juda, mount Sion which he loved.
verses.textLatin: sed elegit tribum Juda, montem Sion, quem dilexit.

verses.text: And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land which he founded for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et ædificavit sicut unicornium sanctificium suum, in terra quam fundavit in sæcula.

verses.text: And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: he brought him from following the ewes great with young,
verses.textLatin: Et elegit David, servum suum, et sustulit eum de gregibus ovium; de post fœtantes accepit eum:

verses.text: To feed Jacob his servant, and Israel his inheritance.
verses.textLatin: pascere Jacob servum suum, et Israël hæreditatem suam.

verses.text: And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.
verses.textLatin: Et pavit eos in innocentia cordis sui, et in intellectibus manuum suarum deduxit eos.

verses.text: A psalm for Asaph. O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus Asaph. Deus, venerunt gentes in hæreditatem tuam; polluerunt templum sanctum tuum; posuerunt Jerusalem in pomorum custodiam.

verses.text: They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Posuerunt morticina servorum tuorum escas volatilibus cæli; carnes sanctorum tuorum bestiis terræ.

verses.text: They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem and there was none to bury them.
verses.textLatin: Effuderunt sanguinem eorum tamquam aquam in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret.

verses.text: We are become a reproach to our neighbours: a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
verses.textLatin: Facti sumus opprobrium vicinis nostris; subsannatio et illusio his qui in circuitu nostro sunt.

verses.text: How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, Domine, irasceris in finem? accendetur velut ignis zelus tuus?

verses.text: Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.
verses.textLatin: Effunde iram tuam in gentes quæ te non noverunt, et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocaverunt:

verses.text: Because they have devoured Jacob; and have laid waste his place.
verses.textLatin: quia comederunt Jacob, et locum ejus desolaverunt.

verses.text: Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, for we are become exceeding poor.
verses.textLatin: Ne memineris iniquitatum nostrarum antiquarum; cito anticipent nos misericordiæ tuæ, quia pauperes facti sumus nimis.

verses.text: Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:
verses.textLatin: Adjuva nos, Deus salutaris noster, et propter gloriam nominis tui, Domine, libera nos: et propitius esto peccatis nostris, propter nomen tuum.

verses.text: Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes, By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed:
verses.textLatin: Ne forte dicant in gentibus: Ubi est Deus eorum? et innotescat in nationibus coram oculis nostris ultio sanguinis servorum tuorum qui effusus est.

verses.text: let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee. According to the greatness of thy arm, take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.
verses.textLatin: Introëat in conspectu tuo gemitus compeditorum; secundum magnitudinem brachii tui posside filios mortificatorum:

verses.text: And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: et redde vicinis nostris septuplum in sinu eorum; improperium ipsorum quod exprobraverunt tibi, Domine.

verses.text: But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, will give thanks to thee for ever. We will shew forth thy praise, unto generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Nos autem populus tuus, et oves pascuæ tuæ, confitebimur tibi in sæculum; in generationem et generationem annuntiabimus laudem tuam.

verses.text: Unto the end, for them that shall be changed, a testimony for Asaph, a psalm.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro iis qui commutabuntur. Testimonium Asaph, psalmus.

verses.text: Give ear, O thou that rulest Israel: thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep. Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, shine forth
verses.textLatin: Qui regis Israël, intende; qui deducis velut ovem Joseph. Qui sedes super cherubim, manifestare

verses.text: before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasses. Stir up thy might, and come to save us.
verses.textLatin: coram Ephraim, Benjamin, et Manasse. Excita potentiam tuam, et veni, ut salvos facias nos.

verses.text: Convert us, O God: and shew us thy face, and we shall be saved.
verses.textLatin: Deus, converte nos, et ostende faciem tuam, et salvi erimus.

verses.text: O Lord God of hosts, how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy servant?
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus virtutum, quousque irasceris super orationem servi tui?

verses.text: How long wilt thou feed us with the bread of tears: and give us for our drink tears in measure?
verses.textLatin: cibabis nos pane lacrimarum, et potum dabis nobis in lacrimis in mensura?

verses.text: Thou hast made us to be a contradiction to our neighbours: and our enemies have scoffed at us.
verses.textLatin: Posuisti nos in contradictionem vicinis nostris, et inimici nostri subsannaverunt nos.

verses.text: O God of hosts, convert us: and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
verses.textLatin: Deus virtutum, converte nos, et ostende faciem tuam, et salvi erimus.

verses.text: Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it.
verses.textLatin: Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti: ejecisti gentes, et plantasti eam.

verses.text: Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight: thou plantedst the roots thereof, and it filled the land.
verses.textLatin: Dux itineris fuisti in conspectu ejus; plantasti radices ejus, et implevit terram.

verses.text: The shadow of it covered the hills: and the branches thereof the cedars of God.
verses.textLatin: Operuit montes umbra ejus, et arbusta ejus cedros Dei.

verses.text: It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, and its boughs unto the river.
verses.textLatin: Extendit palmites suos usque ad mare, et usque ad flumen propagines ejus.

verses.text: Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it?
verses.textLatin: Ut quid destruxisti maceriam ejus, et vindemiant eam omnes qui prætergrediuntur viam?

verses.text: The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: and a singular wild beast hath devoured it.
verses.textLatin: Exterminavit eam aper de silva, et singularis ferus depastus est eam.

verses.text: Turn again, O God of hosts, look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:
verses.textLatin: Deus virtutum, convertere, respice de cælo, et vide, et visita vineam istam:

verses.text: And perfect the same which thy right hand hath planted: and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
verses.textLatin: et perfice eam quam plantavit dextera tua, et super filium hominis quem confirmasti tibi.

verses.text: Things set on fire and dug down shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
verses.textLatin: Incensa igni et suffossa, ab increpatione vultus tui peribunt.

verses.text: Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand: and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
verses.textLatin: Fiat manus tua super virum dexteræ tuæ, et super filium hominis quem confirmasti tibi.

verses.text: And we depart not from thee, thou shalt quicken us: and we will call upon thy name.
verses.textLatin: Et non discedimus a te: vivificabis nos, et nomen tuum invocabimus.

verses.text: O Lord God of hosts, convert us: and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus virtutum, converte nos, et ostende faciem tuam, et salvi erimus.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the winepresses, a psalm for Asaph himself.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro torcularibus. Psalmus ipsi Asaph.

verses.text: Rejoice to God our helper: sing aloud to the God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Exsultate Deo adjutori nostro; jubilate Deo Jacob.

verses.text: Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel: the pleasant psaltery with the harp.
verses.textLatin: Sumite psalmum, et date tympanum; psalterium jucundum cum cithara.

verses.text: Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, on the noted day of your solemnity.
verses.textLatin: Buccinate in neomenia tuba, in insigni die solemnitatis vestræ:

verses.text: For it is a commandment in Israel, and a judgment to the God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: quia præceptum in Israël est, et judicium Deo Jacob.

verses.text: He ordained it for a testimony in Joseph, when he came out of the land of Egypt: he heard a tongue which he knew not.
verses.textLatin: Testimonium in Joseph posuit illud, cum exiret de terra Ægypti; linguam quam non noverat, audivit.

verses.text: He removed his back from the burdens: his hands had served in baskets.
verses.textLatin: Divertit ab oneribus dorsum ejus; manus ejus in cophino servierunt.

verses.text: Thou calledst upon me in affliction, and I delivered thee: I heard thee in the secret place of tempest: I proved thee at the waters of contradiction.
verses.textLatin: In tribulatione invocasti me, et liberavi te. Exaudivi te in abscondito tempestatis; probavi te apud aquam contradictionis.

verses.text: Hear, O my people, and I will testify to thee: O Israel, if thou wilt hearken to me,
verses.textLatin: Audi, populus meus, et contestabor te. Israël, si audieris me,

verses.text: there shall be no new god in thee: neither shalt thou adore a strange god.
verses.textLatin: non erit in te deus recens, neque adorabis deum alienum.

verses.text: For I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.textLatin: Ego enim sum Dominus Deus tuus, qui eduxi te de terra Ægypti. Dilata os tuum, et implebo illud.

verses.text: But my people heard not my voice: and Israel hearkened not to me.
verses.textLatin: Et non audivit populus meus vocem meam, et Israël non intendit mihi.

verses.text: So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions.
verses.textLatin: Et dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum; ibunt in adinventionibus suis.

verses.text: If my people had heard me: if Israel had walked in my ways:
verses.textLatin: Si populus meus audisset me, Israël si in viis meis ambulasset,

verses.text: I should soon have humbled their enemies, and laid my hand on them that troubled them.
verses.textLatin: pro nihilo forsitan inimicos eorum humiliassem, et super tribulantes eos misissem manum meam.

verses.text: The enemies of the Lord have lied to him: and their time shall be for ever.
verses.textLatin: Inimici Domini mentiti sunt ei, et erit tempus eorum in sæcula.

verses.text: And he fed them with the fat of wheat, and filled them with honey out of the rock.
verses.textLatin: Et cibavit eos ex adipe frumenti, et de petra melle saturavit eos.

verses.text: A psalm for Asaph. God hath stood in the congregation of gods: and being in the midst of them he judgeth gods.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus Asaph. Deus stetit in synagoga deorum; in medio autem deos dijudicat.

verses.text: How long will you judge unjustly: and accept the persons of the wicked?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo judicatis iniquitatem, et facies peccatorum sumitis?

verses.text: Judge for the needy and fatherless: do justice to the humble and the poor.
verses.textLatin: Judicate egeno et pupillo; humilem et pauperem justificate.

verses.text: Rescue the poor; and deliver the needy out of the hand of the sinner.
verses.textLatin: Eripite pauperem, et egenum de manu peccatoris liberate.

verses.text: They have not known nor understood: they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth shall be moved.
verses.textLatin: Nescierunt, neque intellexerunt; in tenebris ambulant: movebuntur omnia fundamenta terræ.

verses.text: I have said: You are gods and all of you the sons of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Ego dixi: Dii estis, et filii Excelsi omnes.

verses.text: But you like men shall die: and shall fall like one of the princes.
verses.textLatin: Vos autem sicut homines moriemini, et sicut unus de principibus cadetis.

verses.text: Arise, O God, judge thou the earth: for thou shalt inherit among all the nations.
verses.textLatin: Surge, Deus, judica terram, quoniam tu hæreditabis in omnibus gentibus.

verses.text: A canticle of a psalm for Asaph.
verses.textLatin: Canticum Psalmi Asaph.

verses.text: O God, who shall be like to thee? hold not thy peace, neither be thou still, O God.
verses.textLatin: Deus, quis similis erit tibi? ne taceas, neque compescaris, Deus:

verses.text: For lo, thy enemies have made a noise: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.
verses.textLatin: quoniam ecce inimici tui sonuerunt, et qui oderunt te extulerunt caput.

verses.text: They have taken a malicious counsel against thy people, and have consulted against thy saints.
verses.textLatin: Super populum tuum malignaverunt consilium, et cogitaverunt adversus sanctos tuos.

verses.text: They have said: Come and let us destroy them, so that they be not a nation: and let the name of Israel be remembered no more.
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt: Venite, et disperdamus eos de gente, et non memoretur nomen Israël ultra.

verses.text: For they have contrived with one consent: they have made a covenant together against thee,
verses.textLatin: Quoniam cogitaverunt unanimiter; simul adversum te testamentum disposuerunt:

verses.text: the tabernacles of the Edomites, and the Ishmahelites: Moab, and the Agarens,
verses.textLatin: tabernacula Idumæorum et Ismahelitæ, Moab et Agareni,

verses.text: Gebal, and Ammon and Amalec: the Philistines, with the inhabitants of Tyre.
verses.textLatin: Gebal, et Ammon, et Amalec; alienigenæ cum habitantibus Tyrum.

verses.text: Yea, and the Assyrian also is joined with them: they are come to the aid of the sons of Lot.
verses.textLatin: Etenim Assur venit cum illis: facti sunt in adjutorium filiis Lot.

verses.text: Do to them as thou didst to Madian and to Sisara: as to Jabin at the brook of Cisson.
verses.textLatin: Fac illis sicut Madian et Sisaræ, sicut Jabin in torrente Cisson.

verses.text: Who perished at Endor: and became as dung for the earth.
verses.textLatin: Disperierunt in Endor; facti sunt ut stercus terræ.

verses.text: Make their princes like Oreb, and Zeb, and Zebee, and Salmana. All their princes,
verses.textLatin: Pone principes eorum sicut Oreb, et Zeb, et Zebee, et Salmana: omnes principes eorum,

verses.text: who have said: Let us possess the sanctuary of God for an inheritance.
verses.textLatin: qui dixerunt: Hæreditate possideamus sanctuarium Dei.

verses.text: O my God, make them like a wheel; and as stubble before the wind.
verses.textLatin: Deus meus, pone illos ut rotam, et sicut stipulam ante faciem venti.

verses.text: As fire which burneth the wood: and as a flame burning mountains:
verses.textLatin: Sicut ignis qui comburit silvam, et sicut flamma comburens montes,

verses.text: So shalt thou pursue them with thy tempest: and shalt trouble them in thy wrath.
verses.textLatin: ita persequeris illos in tempestate tua, et in ira tua turbabis eos.

verses.text: Fill their faces with shame; and they shall seek thy name, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Imple facies eorum ignominia, et quærent nomen tuum, Domine.

verses.text: Let them be ashamed and troubled for ever and ever: and let them be confounded and perish.
verses.textLatin: Erubescant, et conturbentur in sæculum sæculi, et confundantur, et pereant.

verses.text: And let them know that the Lord is thy name: thou alone art the most High over all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et cognoscant quia nomen tibi Dominus: tu solus Altissimus in omni terra.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the winepresses, a psalm for the sons of Core.
verses.textLatin: In finem, pro torcularibus filiis Core. Psalmus.

verses.text: How lovely are thy tabernacles, O Lord of hosts!
verses.textLatin: Quam dilecta tabernacula tua, Domine virtutum!

verses.text: my soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God.
verses.textLatin: Concupiscit, et deficit anima mea in atria Domini; cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum.

verses.text: For the sparrow hath found herself a house, and the turtle a nest for herself where she may lay her young ones: Thy altars, O Lord of hosts, my king and my God.
verses.textLatin: Etenim passer invenit sibi domum, et turtur nidum sibi, ubi ponat pullos suos: altaria tua, Domine virtutum, rex meus, et Deus meus.

verses.text: Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: they shall praise thee for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Beati qui habitant in domo tua, Domine; in sæcula sæculorum laudabunt te.

verses.text: Blessed is the man whose help is from thee: in his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps,
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir cujus est auxilium abs te: ascensiones in corde suo disposuit,

verses.text: in the vale of tears, in the place which he hath set.
verses.textLatin: in valle lacrimarum, in loco quem posuit.

verses.text: For the lawgiver shall give a blessing, they shall go from virtue to virtue: the God of gods shall be seen in Sion.
verses.textLatin: Etenim benedictionem dabit legislator; ibunt de virtute in virtutem: videbitur Deus deorum in Sion.

verses.text: O Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer: give ear, O God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus virtutum, exaudi orationem meam; auribus percipe, Deus Jacob.

verses.text: Behold, O God our protector: and look on the face of thy Christ.
verses.textLatin: Protector noster, aspice, Deus, et respice in faciem christi tui.

verses.text: For better is one day in thy courts above thousands. I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God, rather than to dwell in the tabernacles of sinners.
verses.textLatin: Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis super millia; elegi abjectus esse in domo Dei mei magis quam habitare in tabernaculis peccatorum.

verses.text: For God loveth mercy and truth: the Lord will give grace and glory.
verses.textLatin: Quia misericordiam et veritatem diligit Deus: gratiam et gloriam dabit Dominus.

verses.text: He will not deprive of good things them that walk in innocence: O Lord of hosts, blessed is the man that trusteth in thee.
verses.textLatin: Non privabit bonis eos qui ambulant in innocentia: Domine virtutum, beatus homo qui sperat in te.

verses.text: Unto the end, for the sons of Core, a psalm.
verses.textLatin: In finem, filiis Core. Psalmus.

verses.text: Lord, thou hast blessed thy land: thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Benedixisti, Domine, terram tuam; avertisti captivitatem Jacob.

verses.text: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people: thou hast covered all their sins.
verses.textLatin: Remisisti iniquitatem plebis tuæ; operuisti omnia peccata eorum.

verses.text: Thou hast mitigated all thy anger: thou hast turned away from the wrath of thy indignation.
verses.textLatin: Mitigasti omnem iram tuam; avertisti ab ira indignationis tuæ.

verses.text: Convert us, O God our saviour: and turn off thy anger from us.
verses.textLatin: Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster, et averte iram tuam a nobis.

verses.text: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever: or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation to generation?
verses.textLatin: Numquid in æternum irasceris nobis? aut extendes iram tuam a generatione in generationem?

verses.text: Thou wilt turn, O God, and bring us to life: and thy people shall rejoice in thee.
verses.textLatin: Deus, tu conversus vivificabis nos, et plebs tua lætabitur in te.

verses.text: Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy; and grant us thy salvation.
verses.textLatin: Ostende nobis, Domine, misericordiam tuam, et salutare tuum da nobis.

verses.text: I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me: for he will speak peace unto his people: And unto his saints: and unto them that are converted to the heart.
verses.textLatin: Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus, quoniam loquetur pacem in plebem suam, et super sanctos suos, et in eos qui convertuntur ad cor.

verses.text: Surely his salvation is near to them that fear him: that glory may dwell in our land.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen prope timentes eum salutare ipsius, ut inhabitet gloria in terra nostra.

verses.text: Mercy and truth have met each other: justice and peace have kissed.
verses.textLatin: Misericordia et veritas obviaverunt sibi; justitia et pax osculatæ sunt.

verses.text: Truth is sprung out of the earth: and justice hath looked down from heaven.
verses.textLatin: Veritas de terra orta est, et justitia de cælo prospexit.

verses.text: For the Lord will give goodness: and our earth shall yield her fruit.
verses.textLatin: Etenim Dominus dabit benignitatem, et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.

verses.text: Justice shall walk before him: and shall set his steps in the way.
verses.textLatin: Justitia ante eum ambulabit, et ponet in via gressus suos.

verses.text: A prayer for David himself. Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear me: for I am needy and poor.
verses.textLatin: Oratio ipsi David. Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam et exaudi me, quoniam inops et pauper sum ego.

verses.text: Preserve my soul, for I am holy: save thy servant, O my God, that trusteth in thee.
verses.textLatin: Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum; salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperantem in te.

verses.text: Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I have cried to thee all the day.
verses.textLatin: Miserere mei, Domine, quoniam ad te clamavi tota die;

verses.text: Give joy to the soul of thy servant, for to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
verses.textLatin: lætifica animam servi tui, quoniam ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi.

verses.text: For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild: and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu, Domine, suavis et mitis, et multæ misericordiæ omnibus invocantibus te.

verses.text: Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer: and attend to the voice of my petition.
verses.textLatin: Auribus percipe, Domine, orationem meam, et intende voci deprecationis meæ.

verses.text: I have called upon thee in the day of my trouble: because thou hast heard me.
verses.textLatin: In die tribulationis meæ clamavi ad te, quia exaudisti me.

verses.text: There is none among the gods like unto thee, O Lord: and there is none according to thy works.
verses.textLatin: Non est similis tui in diis, Domine, et non est secundum opera tua.

verses.text: All the nations thou hast made shall come and adore before thee, O Lord: and they shall glorify thy name.
verses.textLatin: Omnes gentes quascumque fecisti venient, et adorabunt coram te, Domine, et glorificabunt nomen tuum.

verses.text: For thou art great and dost wonderful things: thou art God alone.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam magnus es tu, et faciens mirabilia; tu es Deus solus.

verses.text: Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way, and I will walk in thy truth: let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name.
verses.textLatin: Deduc me, Domine, in via tua, et ingrediar in veritate tua; lætetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum.

verses.text: I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, and I will glorify thy name for ever:
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus, in toto corde meo, et glorificabo nomen tuum in æternum:

verses.text: For thy mercy is great towards me: and thou hast delivered my soul out of the lower hell.
verses.textLatin: quia misericordia tua magna est super me, et eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiori.

verses.text: O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the assembly of the mighty have sought my soul: and they have not set thee before their eyes.
verses.textLatin: Deus, iniqui insurrexerunt super me, et synagoga potentium quæsierunt animam meam: et non proposuerunt te in conspectu suo.

verses.text: And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion, and merciful, patient, and of much mercy, and true.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, Domine Deus, miserator et misericors; patiens, et multæ misericordiæ, et verax.

verses.text: O look upon me, and have mercy on me: give thy command to thy servant, and save the son of thy handmaid.
verses.textLatin: Respice in me, et miserere mei; da imperium tuum puero tuo, et salvum fac filium ancillæ tuæ.

verses.text: Shew me a token for good: that they who hate me may see, and be confounded, because thou, O Lord, hast helped me and hast comforted me.
verses.textLatin: Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut videant qui oderunt me, et confundantur: quoniam tu, Domine, adjuvisti me, et consolatus es me.

verses.text: For the sons of Core, a psalm of a canticle. The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains:
verses.textLatin: Filiis Core. Psalmus cantici. Fundamenta ejus in montibus sanctis;

verses.text: The Lord loveth the gates of Sion above all the tabernacles of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: diligit Dominus portas Sion super omnia tabernacula Jacob.

verses.text: Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God.
verses.textLatin: Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei!

verses.text: I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon knowing me. Behold the foreigners, and Tyre, and the people of the Ethiopians, these were there.
verses.textLatin: Memor ero Rahab et Babylonis, scientium me; ecce alienigenæ, et Tyrus, et populus Æthiopum, hi fuerunt illic.

verses.text: Shall not Sion say: This man and that man is born in her? and the Highest himself hath founded her.
verses.textLatin: Numquid Sion dicet: Homo et homo natus est in ea, et ipse fundavit eam Altissimus?

verses.text: The Lord shall tell in his writings of peoples and of princes, of them that have been in her.
verses.textLatin: Dominus narrabit in scripturis populorum et principum, horum qui fuerunt in ea.

verses.text: The dwelling in thee is as it were of all rejoicing.
verses.textLatin: Sicut lætantium omnium habitatio est in te.

verses.text: A canticle of a psalm for the sons of Core: unto the end, for Maheleth, to answer understanding of Eman the Ezrahite.
verses.textLatin: Canticum Psalmi, filiis Core, in finem, pro Maheleth ad respondendum. Intellectus Eman Ezrahitæ.

verses.text: O Lord, the God of my salvation: I have cried in the day, and in the night before thee.
verses.textLatin: Domine, Deus salutis meæ, in die clamavi et nocte coram te.

verses.text: Let my prayer come in before thee: incline thy ear to my petition.
verses.textLatin: Intret in conspectu tuo oratio mea, inclina aurem tuam ad precem meam.

verses.text: For my soul is filled with evils: and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.
verses.textLatin: Quia repleta est malis anima mea, et vita mea inferno appropinquavit.

verses.text: I am counted among them that go down to the pit: I am become as a man without help,
verses.textLatin: Æstimatus sum cum descendentibus in lacum, factus sum sicut homo sine adjutorio,

verses.text: free among the dead. Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: and they are cast off from thy hand.
verses.textLatin: inter mortuos liber; sicut vulnerati dormientes in sepulchris, quorum non es memor amplius, et ipsi de manu tua repulsi sunt.

verses.text: They have laid me in the lower pit: in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.
verses.textLatin: Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, in tenebrosis, et in umbra mortis.

verses.text: Thy wrath is strong over me: and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.
verses.textLatin: Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, et omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me.

verses.text: Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: they have set me an abomination to themselves. I was delivered up, and came not forth:
verses.textLatin: Longe fecisti notos meos a me; posuerunt me abominationem sibi. Traditus sum, et non egrediebar;

verses.text: my eyes languished through poverty. All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: I stretched out my hands to thee.
verses.textLatin: oculi mei languerunt præ inopia. Clamavi ad te, Domine, tota die; expandi ad te manus meas.

verses.text: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?
verses.textLatin: Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia? aut medici suscitabunt, et confitebuntur tibi?

verses.text: Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: and thy truth in destruction?
verses.textLatin: Numquid narrabit aliquis in sepulchro misericordiam tuam, et veritatem tuam in perditione?

verses.text: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?
verses.textLatin: Numquid cognoscentur in tenebris mirabilia tua? et justitia tua in terra oblivionis?

verses.text: But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.
verses.textLatin: Et ego ad te, Domine, clamavi, et mane oratio mea præveniet te.

verses.text: Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: why turnest thou away thy face from me?
verses.textLatin: Ut quid, Domine, repellis orationem meam; avertis faciem tuam a me?

verses.text: I am poor, and in labours from my youth: and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.
verses.textLatin: Pauper sum ego, et in laboribus a juventute mea; exaltatus autem, humiliatus sum et conturbatus.

verses.text: Thy wrath hath come upon me: and thy terrors have troubled me.
verses.textLatin: In me transierunt iræ tuæ, et terrores tui conturbaverunt me:

verses.text: They have come round about me like water all the day: they have compassed me about together.
verses.textLatin: circumdederunt me sicut aqua tota die; circumdederunt me simul.

verses.text: Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: and my acquaintance, because of misery.
verses.textLatin: Elongasti a me amicum et proximum, et notos meos a miseria.

verses.text: Of understanding, for Ethan the Ezrahite.
verses.textLatin: Intellectus Ethan Ezrahitæ.

verses.text: The mercies of the Lord I will sing for ever. I will shew forth thy truth with my mouth to generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Misericordias Domini in æternum cantabo; in generationem et generationem annuntiabo veritatem tuam in ore meo.

verses.text: For thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up for ever in the heavens: thy truth shall be prepared in them.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam dixisti: In æternum misericordia ædificabitur in cælis; præparabitur veritas tua in eis.

verses.text: I have made a covenant with my elect: I have sworn to David my servant:
verses.textLatin: Disposui testamentum electis meis; juravi David servo meo:

verses.text: Thy seed will I settle for ever. And I will build up thy throne unto generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Usque in æternum præparabo semen tuum, et ædificabo in generationem et generationem sedem tuam.

verses.text: The heavens shall confess thy wonders, O Lord: and thy truth in the church of the saints.
verses.textLatin: Confitebuntur cæli mirabilia tua, Domine; etenim veritatem tuam in ecclesia sanctorum.

verses.text: For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord: or who among the sons of God shall be like to God?
verses.textLatin: Quoniam quis in nubibus æquabitur Domino; similis erit Deo in filiis Dei?

verses.text: God, who is glorified in the assembly of the saints: great and terrible above all them that are about him.
verses.textLatin: Deus, qui glorificatur in consilio sanctorum, magnus et terribilis super omnes qui in circuitu ejus sunt.

verses.text: O Lord God of hosts, who is like to thee? thou art mighty, O Lord, and thy truth is round about thee.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus virtutum, quis similis tibi? potens es, Domine, et veritas tua in circuitu tuo.

verses.text: Thou rulest the power of the sea: and appeasest the motion of the waves thereof.
verses.textLatin: Tu dominaris potestati maris; motum autem fluctuum ejus tu mitigas.

verses.text: Thou hast humbled the proud one, as one that is slain: with the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thy enemies.
verses.textLatin: Tu humiliasti, sicut vulneratum, superbum; in brachio virtutis tuæ dispersisti inimicos tuos.

verses.text: Thine are the heavens, and thine is the earth: the world and the fulness thereof thou hast founded:
verses.textLatin: Tui sunt cæli, et tua est terra: orbem terræ, et plenitudinem ejus tu fundasti;

verses.text: the north and the sea thou hast created. Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name:
verses.textLatin: aquilonem et mare tu creasti. Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo exsultabunt:

verses.text: thy arm is with might. Let thy hand be strengthened, and thy right hand exalted:
verses.textLatin: tuum brachium cum potentia. Firmetur manus tua, et exaltetur dextera tua:

verses.text: justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne. Mercy and truth shall go before thy face:
verses.textLatin: justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ: misericordia et veritas præcedent faciem tuam.

verses.text: blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation. They shall walk, O Lord, in the light of thy countenance:
verses.textLatin: Beatus populus qui scit jubilationem: Domine, in lumine vultus tui ambulabunt,

verses.text: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, and in thy justice they shall be exalted.
verses.textLatin: et in nomine tuo exsultabunt tota die, et in justitia tua exaltabuntur.

verses.text: For thou art the glory of their strength: and in thy good pleasure shall our horn be exalted.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam gloria virtutis eorum tu es, et in beneplacito tuo exaltabitur cornu nostrum.

verses.text: For our protection is of the Lord, and of our king the holy one of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Quia Domini est assumptio nostra, et sancti Israël regis nostri.

verses.text: Then thou spokest in a vision to thy saints, and saidst: I have laid help upon one that is mighty, and have exalted one chosen out of my people.
verses.textLatin: Tunc locutus es in visione sanctis tuis, et dixisti: Posui adjutorium in potente, et exaltavi electum de plebe mea.

verses.text: I have found David my servant: with my holy oil I have anointed him.
verses.textLatin: Inveni David, servum meum; oleo sancto meo unxi eum.

verses.text: For my hand shall help him: and my arm shall strengthen him.
verses.textLatin: Manus enim mea auxiliabitur ei, et brachium meum confortabit eum.

verses.text: The enemy shall have no advantage over him: nor the son of iniquity have power to hurt him.
verses.textLatin: Nihil proficiet inimicus in eo, et filius iniquitatis non apponet nocere ei.

verses.text: And I will cut down his enemies before his face; and them that hate him I will put to flight.
verses.textLatin: Et concidam a facie ipsius inimicos ejus, et odientes eum in fugam convertam.

verses.text: And my truth and my mercy shall be with him: and in my name shall his horn be exalted.
verses.textLatin: Et veritas mea et misericordia mea cum ipso, et in nomine meo exaltabitur cornu ejus.

verses.text: And I will set his hand in the sea; and his right hand in the rivers.
verses.textLatin: Et ponam in mari manum ejus, et in fluminibus dexteram ejus.

verses.text: He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father: my God, and the support of my salvation.
verses.textLatin: Ipse invocabit me: Pater meus es tu, Deus meus, et susceptor salutis meæ.

verses.text: And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et ego primogenitum ponam illum, excelsum præ regibus terræ.

verses.text: I will keep my mercy for him for ever: and my covenant faithful to him.
verses.textLatin: In æternum servabo illi misericordiam meam, et testamentum meum fidele ipsi.

verses.text: And I will make his seed to endure for evermore: and his throne as the days of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Et ponam in sæculum sæculi semen ejus, et thronum ejus sicut dies cæli.

verses.text: And if his children forsake my law, and walk not in my judgments:
verses.textLatin: Si autem dereliquerint filii ejus legem meam, et in judiciis meis non ambulaverint;

verses.text: If they profane my justices: and keep not my commandments:
verses.textLatin: si justitias meas profanaverint, et mandata mea non custodierint:

verses.text: I will visit their iniquities with a rod : and their sins with stripes.
verses.textLatin: visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, et in verberibus peccata eorum;

verses.text: But my mercy I will not take away from him: nor will I suffer my truth to fail.
verses.textLatin: misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo, neque nocebo in veritate mea,

verses.text: Neither will I profane my covenant: and the words that proceed from my mouth I will not make void.
verses.textLatin: neque profanabo testamentum meum: et quæ procedunt de labiis meis non faciam irrita.

verses.text: Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David:
verses.textLatin: Semel juravi in sancto meo, si David mentiar:

verses.text: his seed shall endure for ever.
verses.textLatin: semen ejus in æternum manebit. Et thronus ejus sicut sol in conspectu meo,

verses.text: And his throne as the sun before me: and as the moon perfect for ever, and a faithful witness in heaven.
verses.textLatin: et sicut luna perfecta in æternum, et testis in cælo fidelis.

verses.text: But thou hast rejected and despised: thou hast been angry with thy anointed.
verses.textLatin: Tu vero repulisti et despexisti; distulisti christum tuum.

verses.text: Thou hast overthrown the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his sanctuary on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Evertisti testamentum servi tui; profanasti in terra sanctuarium ejus.

verses.text: Thou hast broken down all his hedges: thou hast made his strength fear.
verses.textLatin: Destruxisti omnes sepes ejus; posuisti firmamentum ejus formidinem.

verses.text: All that pass by the way have robbed him: he is become a reproach to his neighbours.
verses.textLatin: Diripuerunt eum omnes transeuntes viam; factus est opprobrium vicinis suis.

verses.text: Thou hast set up the right hand of them that oppress him: thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Exaltasti dexteram deprimentium eum; lætificasti omnes inimicos ejus.

verses.text: Thou hast turned away the help of his sword; and hast not assisted him in battle.
verses.textLatin: Avertisti adjutorium gladii ejus, et non es auxiliatus ei in bello.

verses.text: Thou hast made his purification to cease: and thou hast cast his throne down to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Destruxisti eum ab emundatione, et sedem ejus in terram collisisti.

verses.text: Thou hast shortened the days of his time: thou hast covered him with confusion.
verses.textLatin: Minorasti dies temporis ejus; perfudisti eum confusione.

verses.text: How long, O Lord, turnest thou away unto the end? shall thy anger burn like fire?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, Domine, avertis in finem? exardescet sicut ignis ira tua?

verses.text: Remember what my substance is: for hast thou made all the children of men in vain?
verses.textLatin: Memorare quæ mea substantia: numquid enim vane constituisti omnes filios hominum?

verses.text: Who is the man that shall live, and not see death: that shall deliver his soul from the hand of hell?
verses.textLatin: Quis est homo qui vivet et non videbit mortem? eruet animam suam de manu inferi?

verses.text: Lord, where are thy ancient mercies, according to what thou didst swear to David in thy truth?
verses.textLatin: Ubi sunt misericordiæ tuæ antiquæ, Domine, sicut jurasti David in veritate tua?

verses.text: Be mindful, O Lord, of the reproach of thy servants (which I have held in my bosom) of many nations:
verses.textLatin: Memor esto, Domine, opprobrii servorum tuorum, quod continui in sinu meo, multarum gentium:

verses.text: Wherewith thy enemies have reproached, O Lord; wherewith they have reproached the change of thy anointed.
verses.textLatin: quod exprobraverunt inimici tui, Domine; quod exprobraverunt commutationem christi tui.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord for evermore. So be it. So be it.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus in æternum. Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: A prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, thou hast been our refuge from generation to generation.
verses.textLatin: Oratio Moysi, hominis Dei. Domine, refugium factus es nobis a generatione in generationem.

verses.text: Before the mountains were made, or the earth and the world was formed; from eternity and to eternity thou art God.
verses.textLatin: Priusquam montes fierent, aut formaretur terra et orbis, a sæculo et usque in sæculum tu es, Deus.

verses.text: Turn not man away to be brought low: and thou hast said: Be converted, O ye sons of men.
verses.textLatin: Ne avertas hominem in humilitatem: et dixisti: Convertimini, filii hominum.

verses.text: For a thousand years in thy sight are as yesterday, which is past. And as a watch in the night,
verses.textLatin: Quoniam mille anni ante oculos tuos tamquam dies hesterna quæ præteriit: et custodia in nocte

verses.text: things that are counted nothing, shall their years be.
verses.textLatin: quæ pro nihilo habentur, eorum anni erunt.

verses.text: In the morning man shall grow up like grass; in the morning he shall flourish and pass away: in the evening he shall fall, grow dry, and wither.
verses.textLatin: Mane sicut herba transeat; mane floreat, et transeat; vespere decidat, induret, et arescat.

verses.text: For in thy wrath we have fainted away: and are troubled in thy indignation.
verses.textLatin: Quia defecimus in ira tua, et in furore tuo turbati sumus.

verses.text: Thou hast set our iniquities before thy eyes: our life in the light of thy countenance.
verses.textLatin: Posuisti iniquitates nostras in conspectu tuo; sæculum nostrum in illuminatione vultus tui.

verses.text: For all our days are spent; and in thy wrath we have fainted away. Our years shall be considered as a spider:
verses.textLatin: Quoniam omnes dies nostri defecerunt, et in ira tua defecimus. Anni nostri sicut aranea meditabuntur;

verses.text: the days of our years in them are threescore and ten years. But if in the strong they be fourscore years: and what is more of them is labour and sorrow. For mildness is come upon us: and we shall be corrected.
verses.textLatin: dies annorum nostrorum in ipsis septuaginta anni. Si autem in potentatibus octoginta anni, et amplius eorum labor et dolor; quoniam supervenit mansuetudo, et corripiemur.

verses.text: Who knoweth the power of thy anger, and for thy fear
verses.textLatin: Quis novit potestatem iræ tuæ, et præ timore tuo iram tuam

verses.text: can number thy wrath? So make thy right hand known: and men learned in heart, in wisdom.
verses.textLatin: dinumerare? Dexteram tuam sic notam fac, et eruditos corde in sapientia.

verses.text: Return, O Lord, how long? and be entreated in favour of thy servants.
verses.textLatin: Convertere, Domine; usquequo? et deprecabilis esto super servos tuos.

verses.text: We are filled in the morning with thy mercy: and we have rejoiced, and are delighted all our days.
verses.textLatin: Repleti sumus mane misericordia tua; et exsultavimus, et delectati sumus omnibus diebus nostris.

verses.text: We have rejoiced for the days in which thou hast humbled us: for the years in which we have seen evils.
verses.textLatin: Lætati sumus pro diebus quibus nos humiliasti; annis quibus vidimus mala.

verses.text: Look upon thy servants and upon their works: and direct their children.
verses.textLatin: Respice in servos tuos et in opera tua, et dirige filios eorum.

verses.text: And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us: and direct thou the works of our hands over us; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.
verses.textLatin: Et sit splendor Domini Dei nostri super nos, et opera manuum nostrarum dirige super nos, et opus manuum nostrarum dirige.

verses.text: The praise of a canticle for David. He that dwelleth in the aid of the most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Laus cantici David. Qui habitat in adjutorio Altissimi, in protectione Dei cæli commorabitur.

verses.text: He shall say to the Lord: Thou art my protector, and my refuge: my God, in him will I trust.
verses.textLatin: Dicet Domino: Susceptor meus es tu, et refugium meum; Deus meus, sperabo in eum.

verses.text: For he hath delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the sharp word.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ipse liberavit me de laqueo venantium, et a verbo aspero.

verses.text: He will overshadow thee with his shoulders: and under his wings thou shalt trust.
verses.textLatin: Scapulis suis obumbrabit tibi, et sub pennis ejus sperabis.

verses.text: His truth shall compass thee with a shield: thou shalt not be afraid of the terror of the night.
verses.textLatin: Scuto circumdabit te veritas ejus: non timebis a timore nocturno;

verses.text: Of the arrow that flieth in the day, of the business that walketh about in the dark: of invasion, or of the noonday devil.
verses.textLatin: a sagitta volante in die, a negotio perambulante in tenebris, ab incursu, et dæmonio meridiano.

verses.text: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand: but it shall not come nigh thee.
verses.textLatin: Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis; ad te autem non appropinquabit.

verses.text: But thou shalt consider with thy eyes: and shalt see the reward of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen oculis tuis considerabis, et retributionem peccatorum videbis.

verses.text: Because thou, O Lord, art my hope: thou hast made the most High thy refuge.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea; Altissimum posuisti refugium tuum.

verses.text: There shall no evil come to thee: nor shall the scourge come near thy dwelling.
verses.textLatin: Non accedet ad te malum, et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernaculo tuo.

verses.text: For he hath given his angels charge over thee; to keep thee in all thy ways.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in omnibus viis tuis.

verses.text: In their hands they shall bear thee up: lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.
verses.textLatin: In manibus portabunt te, ne forte offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum.

verses.text: Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.
verses.textLatin: Super aspidem et basiliscum ambulabis, et conculcabis leonem et draconem.

verses.text: Because he hoped in me I will deliver him: I will protect him because he hath known my name.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam in me speravit, liberabo eum; protegam eum, quoniam cognovit nomen meum.

verses.text: He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.
verses.textLatin: Clamabit ad me, et ego exaudiam eum; cum ipso sum in tribulatione: eripiam eum, et glorificabo eum.

verses.text: I will fill him with length of days; and I will shew him my salvation.
verses.textLatin: Longitudine dierum replebo eum, et ostendam illi salutare meum.

verses.text: A psalm of a canticle on the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus cantici, in die sabbati.

verses.text: It is good to give praise to the Lord: and to sing to thy name, O most High.
verses.textLatin: Bonum est confiteri Domino, et psallere nomini tuo, Altissime:

verses.text: To shew forth thy mercy in the morning, and thy truth in the night:
verses.textLatin: ad annuntiandum mane misericordiam tuam, et veritatem tuam per noctem,

verses.text: Upon an instrument of ten strings, upon the psaltery: with a canticle upon the harp.
verses.textLatin: in decachordo, psalterio; cum cantico, in cithara.

verses.text: For thou hast given me, O Lord, a delight in thy doings: and in the works of thy hands I shall rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Quia delectasti me, Domine, in factura tua; et in operibus manuum tuarum exsultabo.

verses.text: O Lord, how great are thy works! thy thoughts are exceeding deep.
verses.textLatin: Quam magnificata sunt opera tua, Domine! nimis profundæ factæ sunt cogitationes tuæ.

verses.text: The senseless man shall not know: nor will the fool understand these things.
verses.textLatin: Vir insipiens non cognoscet, et stultus non intelliget hæc.

verses.text: When the wicked shall spring up as grass: and all the workers of iniquity shall appear: That they may perish for ever and ever:
verses.textLatin: Cum exorti fuerint peccatores sicut fœnum, et apparuerint omnes qui operantur iniquitatem, ut intereant in sæculum sæculi:

verses.text: but thou, O Lord, art most high for evermore.
verses.textLatin: tu autem Altissimus in æternum, Domine.

verses.text: For behold thy enemies, O Lord, for behold thy enemies shall perish: and all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ecce inimici tui, Domine, quoniam ecce inimici tui peribunt; et dispergentur omnes qui operantur iniquitatem.

verses.text: But my horn shall be exalted like that of the unicorn: and my old age in plentiful mercy.
verses.textLatin: Et exaltabitur sicut unicornis cornu meum, et senectus mea in misericordia uberi.

verses.text: My eye also hath looked down upon my enemies: and my ear shall hear of the downfall of the malignant that rise up against me.
verses.textLatin: Et despexit oculus meus inimicos meos, et in insurgentibus in me malignantibus audiet auris mea.

verses.text: The just shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Justus ut palma florebit; sicut cedrus Libani multiplicabitur.

verses.text: They that are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
verses.textLatin: Plantati in domo Domini, in atriis domus Dei nostri florebunt.

verses.text: They shall still increase in a fruitful old age: and shall be well treated,
verses.textLatin: Adhuc multiplicabuntur in senecta uberi, et bene patientes erunt:

verses.text: that they may shew, That the Lord our God is righteous, and there is no iniquity in him.
verses.textLatin: ut annuntient quoniam rectus Dominus Deus noster, et non est iniquitas in eo.

verses.text: The  Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself. For he hath established the world which shall not be moved.
verses.textLatin: Dominus regnavit, decorem indutus est: indutus est Dominus fortitudinem, et præcinxit se. Etenim firmavit orbem terræ, qui non commovebitur.

verses.text: Thy throne is prepared from of old: thou art from everlasting.
verses.textLatin: Parata sedes tua ex tunc; a sæculo tu es.

verses.text: The floods have lifted up, O Lord: the floods have lifted up their voice. The floods have lifted up their waves,
verses.textLatin: Elevaverunt flumina, Domine, elevaverunt flumina vocem suam; elevaverunt flumina fluctus suos,

verses.text: with the noise of many waters. Wonderful are the surges of the sea: wonderful is the Lord on high.
verses.textLatin: a vocibus aquarum multarum. Mirabiles elationes maris; mirabilis in altis Dominus.

verses.text: Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.
verses.textLatin: Testimonia tua credibilia facta sunt nimis; domum tuam decet sanctitudo, Domine, in longitudinem dierum.

verses.text: The  Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: the God of revenge hath acted freely.
verses.textLatin: Deus ultionum Dominus; Deus ultionum libere egit.

verses.text: Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: render a reward to the proud.
verses.textLatin: Exaltare, qui judicas terram; redde retributionem superbis.

verses.text: How long shall sinners, O Lord: how long shall sinners glory?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo peccatores, Domine, usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur;

verses.text: Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: shall all speak who work injustice?
verses.textLatin: effabuntur et loquentur iniquitatem; loquentur omnes qui operantur injustitiam?

verses.text: Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: and they have afflicted thy inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Populum tuum, Domine, humiliaverunt, et hæreditatem tuam vexaverunt.

verses.text: They have slain the widow and the stranger: and they have murdered the fatherless.
verses.textLatin: Viduam et advenam interfecerunt, et pupillos occiderunt.

verses.text: And they have said: The Lord shall not see: neither shall the God of Jacob understand.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt: Non videbit Dominus, nec intelliget Deus Jacob.

verses.text: Understand, ye senseless among the people: and, you fools, be wise at last.
verses.textLatin: Intelligite, insipientes in populo; et stulti, aliquando sapite.

verses.text: He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?
verses.textLatin: Qui plantavit aurem non audiet? aut qui finxit oculum non considerat?

verses.text: He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: he that teacheth man knowledge?
verses.textLatin: Qui corripit gentes non arguet, qui docet hominem scientiam?

verses.text: The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, that they are vain.
verses.textLatin: Dominus scit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanæ sunt.

verses.text: Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: and shalt teach him out of thy law.
verses.textLatin: Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine, et de lege tua docueris eum:

verses.text: That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: till a pit be dug for the wicked.
verses.textLatin: ut mitiges ei a diebus malis, donec fodiatur peccatori fovea.

verses.text: For the Lord will not cast off his people: neither will he forsake his own inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Quia non repellet Dominus plebem suam, et hæreditatem suam non derelinquet,

verses.text: Until justice be turned into judgment: and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.
verses.textLatin: quoadusque justitia convertatur in judicium: et qui juxta illam, omnes qui recto sunt corde.

verses.text: Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?
verses.textLatin: Quis consurget mihi adversus malignantes? aut quis stabit mecum adversus operantes iniquitatem?

verses.text: Unless the Lord had been my helper, my soul had almost dwelt in hell.
verses.textLatin: Nisi quia Dominus adjuvit me, paulominus habitasset in inferno anima mea.

verses.text: If I said: My foot is moved: thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me.
verses.textLatin: Si dicebam: Motus est pes meus: misericordia tua, Domine, adjuvabat me.

verses.text: According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.
verses.textLatin: Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam.

verses.text: Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee, who framest labour in commandment?
verses.textLatin: Numquid adhæret tibi sedes iniquitatis, qui fingis laborem in præcepto?

verses.text: They will hunt after the soul of the just, and will condemn innocent blood.
verses.textLatin: Captabunt in animam justi, et sanguinem innocentem condemnabunt.

verses.text: But the Lord is my refuge: and my God the help of my hope.
verses.textLatin: Et factus est mihi Dominus in refugium, et Deus meus in adjutorium spei meæ.

verses.text: And he will render them their iniquity: and in their malice he will destroy them: the Lord our God will destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Et reddet illis iniquitatem ipsorum, et in malitia eorum disperdet eos: disperdet illos Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: Come  let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour.
verses.textLatin: Venite, exsultemus Domino; jubilemus Deo salutari nostro;

verses.text: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
verses.textLatin: præoccupemus faciem ejus in confessione, et in psalmis jubilemus ei:

verses.text: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
verses.textLatin: quoniam Deus magnus Dominus, et rex magnus super omnes deos.

verses.text: For in his hand are all the ends of the earth: and the heights of the mountains are his.
verses.textLatin: Quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitudines montium ipsius sunt;

verses.text: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.
verses.textLatin: quoniam ipsius est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et siccam manus ejus formaverunt.

verses.text: Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us.
verses.textLatin: Venite, adoremus, et procidamus, et ploremus ante Dominum qui fecit nos:

verses.text: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
verses.textLatin: quia ipse est Dominus Deus noster, et nos populus pascuæ ejus, et oves manus ejus.

verses.text: To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts:
verses.textLatin: Hodie si vocem ejus audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra

verses.text: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
verses.textLatin: sicut in irritatione, secundum diem tentationis in deserto, ubi tentaverunt me patres vestri: probaverunt me, et viderunt opera mea.

verses.text: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart.
verses.textLatin: Quadraginta annis offensus fui generationi illi, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde.

verses.text: And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
verses.textLatin: Et isti non cognoverunt vias meas: ut juravi in ira mea: Si introibunt in requiem meam.

verses.text: A canticle for David himself, when the house was built after the captivity. Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: sing to the Lord, all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Canticum ipsi David, quando domus ædificabatur post captivitatem. Cantate Domino canticum novum; cantate Domino omnis terra.

verses.text: Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: shew forth his salvation from day to day.
verses.textLatin: Cantate Domino, et benedicite nomini ejus; annuntiate de die in diem salutare ejus.

verses.text: Declare his glory among the Gentiles: his wonders among all people.
verses.textLatin: Annuntiate inter gentes gloriam ejus; in omnibus populis mirabilia ejus.

verses.text: For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam magnus Dominus, et laudabilis nimis: terribilis est super omnes deos.

verses.text: For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: but the Lord made the heavens.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam omnes dii gentium dæmonia; Dominus autem cælos fecit.

verses.text: Praise and beauty are before him: holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Confessio et pulchritudo in conspectu ejus; sanctimonia et magnificentia in sanctificatione ejus.
