verses.text: Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour:
verses.textLatin: Afferte Domino, patriæ gentium, afferte Domino gloriam et honorem;

verses.text: bring to the Lord glory unto his name. Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts:
verses.textLatin: afferte Domino gloriam nomini ejus. Tollite hostias, et introite in atria ejus;

verses.text: adore ye the Lord in his holy court. Let all the earth be moved at his presence.
verses.textLatin: adorate Dominum in atrio sancto ejus. Commoveatur a facie ejus universa terra;

verses.text: Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned. For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: he will judge the people with justice.
verses.textLatin: dicite in gentibus, quia Dominus regnavit. Etenim correxit orbem terræ, qui non commovebitur; judicabit populos in æquitate.

verses.text: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fulness thereof:
verses.textLatin: Lætentur cæli, et exsultet terra; commoveatur mare et plenitudo ejus;

verses.text: the fields and all things that are in them shall be joyful. Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice
verses.textLatin: gaudebunt campi, et omnia quæ in eis sunt. Tunc exsultabunt omnia ligna silvarum

verses.text: before the face of the Lord, because he cometh: because he cometh to judge the earth. He shall judge the world with justice, and the people with his truth.
verses.textLatin: a facie Domini, quia venit, quoniam venit judicare terram. Judicabit orbem terræ in æquitate, et populos in veritate sua.

verses.text: For the same David, when his land was restored again to him. The Lord hath reigned, let the earth rejoice: let many islands be glad.
verses.textLatin: Huic David, quando terra ejus restituta est. Dominus regnavit: exsultet terra; lætentur insulæ multæ.

verses.text: Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the establishment of his throne.
verses.textLatin: Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus; justitia et judicium correctio sedis ejus.

verses.text: A fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about.
verses.textLatin: Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus.

verses.text: His lightnings have shone forth to the world: the earth saw and trembled.
verses.textLatin: Illuxerunt fulgura ejus orbi terræ; vidit, et commota est terra.

verses.text: The mountains melted like wax, at the presence of the Lord: at the presence of the Lord of all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini; a facie Domini omnis terra.

verses.text: The heavens declared his justice: and all people saw his glory.
verses.textLatin: Annuntiaverunt cæli justitiam ejus, et viderunt omnes populi gloriam ejus.

verses.text: Let them be all confounded that adore graven things, and that glory in their idols. Adore him, all you his angels:
verses.textLatin: Confundantur omnes qui adorant sculptilia, et qui gloriantur in simulacris suis. Adorate eum omnes angeli ejus.

verses.text: Sion heard, and was glad. And the daughters of Juda rejoiced, because of thy judgments, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Audivit, et lætata est Sion, et exsultaverunt filiæ Judæ propter judicia tua, Domine.

verses.text: For thou art the most high Lord over all the earth: thou art exalted exceedingly above all gods.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam tu Dominus altissimus super omnem terram; nimis exaltatus es super omnes deos.

verses.text: You that love the Lord, hate evil: the Lord preserveth the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligitis Dominum, odite malum: custodit Dominus animas sanctorum suorum; de manu peccatoris liberabit eos.

verses.text: Light is risen to the just, and joy to the right of heart.
verses.textLatin: Lux orta est justo, et rectis corde lætitia.

verses.text: Rejoice, ye just, in the Lord: and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.
verses.textLatin: Lætamini, justi, in Domino, et confitemini memoriæ sanctificationis ejus.

verses.text: A psalm for David himself. Sing ye to the Lord a new canticle: because he hath done wonderful things. His right hand hath wrought for him salvation, and his arm is holy.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus ipsi David. Cantate Domino canticum novum, quia mirabilia fecit. Salvavit sibi dextera ejus, et brachium sanctum ejus.

verses.text: The Lord hath made known his salvation: he hath revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Notum fecit Dominus salutare suum; in conspectu gentium revelavit justitiam suam.

verses.text: He hath remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
verses.textLatin: Recordatus est misericordiæ suæ, et veritatis suæ domui Israël. Viderunt omnes termini terræ salutare Dei nostri.

verses.text: Sing joyfully to God, all the earth; make melody, rejoice and sing.
verses.textLatin: Jubilate Deo, omnis terra; cantate, et exsultate, et psallite.

verses.text: Sing praise to the Lord on the harp, on the harp, and with the voice of a psalm:
verses.textLatin: Psallite Domino in cithara; in cithara et voce psalmi;

verses.text: with long trumpets, and sound of cornet. Make a joyful noise before the Lord our king:
verses.textLatin: in tubis ductilibus, et voce tubæ corneæ. Jubilate in conspectu regis Domini:

verses.text: let the sea be moved and the fullness thereof: the world and they that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: moveatur mare, et plenitudo ejus; orbis terrarum, et qui habitant in eo.

verses.text: The rivers shall clap their hands, the mountains shall rejoice together
verses.textLatin: Flumina plaudent manu; simul montes exsultabunt

verses.text: at the presence of the Lord: because he cometh to judge the earth. He shall judge the world with justice, and the people with equity.
verses.textLatin: a conspectu Domini: quoniam venit judicare terram. Judicabit orbem terrarum in justitia, et populos in æquitate.

verses.text: A psalm for David himself. The Lord hath reigned, let the people be angry: he that sitteth on the cherubims: let the earth be moved.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus ipsi David. Dominus regnavit: irascantur populi; qui sedet super cherubim: moveatur terra.

verses.text: The lord is great in Sion, and high above all people.
verses.textLatin: Dominus in Sion magnus, et excelsus super omnes populos.

verses.text: Let them give praise to thy great name: for it is terrible and holy:
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur nomini tuo magno, quoniam terribile et sanctum est,

verses.text: and the king’s honour loveth judgment. Thou hast prepared directions: thou hast done judgment and justice in Jacob.
verses.textLatin: et honor regis judicium diligit. Tu parasti directiones; judicium et justitiam in Jacob tu fecisti.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore his footstool, for it is holy.
verses.textLatin: Exaltate Dominum Deum nostrum, et adorate scabellum pedum ejus, quoniam sanctum est.

verses.text: Moses and Aaron among his priests: and Samuel among them that call upon his name. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them:
verses.textLatin: Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus ejus, et Samuel inter eos qui invocant nomen ejus: invocabant Dominum, et ipse exaudiebat eos;

verses.text: he spoke to them in the pillar of the cloud. They kept his testimonies, and the commandment which he gave them.
verses.textLatin: in columna nubis loquebatur ad eos. Custodiebant testimonia ejus, et præceptum quod dedit illis.

verses.text: Thou didst hear them, O Lord our God: thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus noster, tu exaudiebas eos; Deus, tu propitius fuisti eis, et ulciscens in omnes adinventiones eorum.

verses.text: Exalt ye the Lord our God, and adore at his holy mountain: for the Lord our God is holy.
verses.textLatin: Exaltate Dominum Deum nostrum, et adorate in monte sancto ejus, quoniam sanctus Dominus Deus noster.

verses.text: A psalm of praise.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus in confessione.

verses.text: Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: serve ye the Lord with gladness. Come in before his presence with exceeding great joy.
verses.textLatin: Jubilate Deo, omnis terra; servite Domino in lætitia. Introite in conspectu ejus in exsultatione.

verses.text: Know ye that the Lord he is God: he made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
verses.textLatin: Scitote quoniam Dominus ipse est Deus; ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos: populus ejus, et oves pascuæ ejus.

verses.text: Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him. Praise ye his name:
verses.textLatin: Introite portas ejus in confessione; atria ejus in hymnis: confitemini illi. Laudate nomen ejus,

verses.text: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, and his truth to generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: quoniam suavis est Dominus, in æternum misericordia ejus, et usque in generationem et generationem veritas ejus.

verses.text: A psalm for David himself. Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee, O Lord: I will sing,
verses.textLatin: Psalmus ipsi David. Misericordiam et judicium cantabo tibi, Domine; psallam,

verses.text: and I will understand in the unspotted way, when thou shalt come to me. I walked in the innocence of my heart, in the midst of my house.
verses.textLatin: et intelligam in via immaculata: quando venies ad me? Perambulabam in innocentia cordis mei, in medio domus meæ.

verses.text: I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: I hated the workers of iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Non proponebam ante oculos meos rem injustam; facientes prævaricationes odivi; non adhæsit mihi

verses.text: The perverse heart did not cleave to me: and the malignant, that turned aside from me, I would not know.
verses.textLatin: cor pravum; declinantem a me malignum non cognoscebam.

verses.text: The man that in private detracted his neighbour, him did I persecute. With him that had a proud eye, and an unsatiable heart, I would not eat.
verses.textLatin: Detrahentem secreto proximo suo, hunc persequebar: superbo oculo, et insatiabili corde, cum hoc non edebam.

verses.text: My eyes were upon the faithful of the earth, to sit with me: the man that walked in the perfect way, he served me.
verses.textLatin: Oculi mei ad fideles terræ, ut sedeant mecum; ambulans in via immaculata, hic mihi ministrabat.

verses.text: He that worketh pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: he that speaketh unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.
verses.textLatin: Non habitabit in medio domus meæ qui facit superbiam; qui loquitur iniqua non direxit in conspectu oculorum meorum.

verses.text: In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: that I might cut off all the workers of iniquity from the city of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: In matutino interficiebam omnes peccatores terræ, ut disperderem de civitate Domini omnes operantes iniquitatem.

verses.text: The prayer of the poor man, when he was anxious, and poured out his supplication before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Oratio pauperis, cum anxius fuerit, et in conspectu Domini effuderit precem suam.

verses.text: Hear, O Lord, my prayer: and let my cry come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Domine, exaudi orationem meam, et clamor meus ad te veniat.

verses.text: Turn not away thy face from me: in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me. In what day soever I shall call upon thee, hear me speedily.
verses.textLatin: Non avertas faciem tuam a me: in quacumque die tribulor, inclina ad me aurem tuam; in quacumque die invocavero te, velociter exaudi me.

verses.text: For my days are vanished like smoke: and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.
verses.textLatin: Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei, et ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt.

verses.text: I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: because I forgot to eat my bread.
verses.textLatin: Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum, quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum.

verses.text: Through the voice of my groaning, my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.
verses.textLatin: A voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ.

verses.text: I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: I am like a night raven in the house.
verses.textLatin: Similis factus sum pellicano solitudinis; factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio.

verses.text: I have watched, and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.
verses.textLatin: Vigilavi, et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto.

verses.text: All the day long my enemies reproached me: and they that praised me did swear against me.
verses.textLatin: Tota die exprobrabant mihi inimici mei, et qui laudabant me adversum me jurabant:

verses.text: For I did eat ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping.
verses.textLatin: quia cinerem tamquam panem manducabam, et potum meum cum fletu miscebam,

verses.text: Because of thy anger and indignation: for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.
verses.textLatin: a facie iræ et indignationis tuæ: quia elevans allisisti me.

verses.text: My days have declined like a shadow, and I am withered like grass.
verses.textLatin: Dies mei sicut umbra declinaverunt, et ego sicut fœnum arui.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever: and thy memorial to all generations.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanes, et memoriale tuum in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come.
verses.textLatin: Tu exsurgens misereberis Sion, quia tempus miserendi ejus, quia venit tempus:

verses.text: For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants: and they shall have pity on the earth thereof.
verses.textLatin: quoniam placuerunt servis tuis lapides ejus, et terræ ejus miserebuntur.

verses.text: All the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, and all the kings of the earth thy glory.
verses.textLatin: Et timebunt gentes nomen tuum, Domine, et omnes reges terræ gloriam tuam:

verses.text: For the Lord hath built up Sion: and he shall be seen in his glory.
verses.textLatin: quia ædificavit Dominus Sion, et videbitur in gloria sua.

verses.text: He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble: and he hath not despised their petition.
verses.textLatin: Respexit in orationem humilium et non sprevit precem eorum.

verses.text: Let these things be written unto another generation: and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Scribantur hæc in generatione altera, et populus qui creabitur laudabit Dominum.

verses.text: Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary: from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Quia prospexit de excelso sancto suo; Dominus de cælo in terram aspexit:

verses.text: That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters: that he might release the children of the slain:
verses.textLatin: ut audiret gemitus compeditorum; ut solveret filios interemptorum:

verses.text: That they may declare the name of the Lord in Sion: and his praise in Jerusalem;
verses.textLatin: ut annuntient in Sion nomen Domini, et laudem ejus in Jerusalem:

verses.text: When the people assemble together, and kings, to serve the Lord.
verses.textLatin: in conveniendo populos in unum, et reges, ut serviant Domino.

verses.text: He answered him in the way of his strength: Declare unto me the fewness of my days.
verses.textLatin: Respondit ei in via virtutis suæ: Paucitatem dierum meorum nuntia mihi:

verses.text: Call me not away in the midst of my days: thy years are unto generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: ne revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum, in generationem et generationem anni tui.

verses.text: In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: and the heavens are the works of thy hands.
verses.textLatin: Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti, et opera manuum tuarum sunt cæli.

verses.text: They shall perish but thou remainest: and all of them shall grow old like a garment: And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi peribunt, tu autem permanes; et omnes sicut vestimentum veterascent. Et sicut opertorium mutabis eos, et mutabuntur;

verses.text: But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.
verses.textLatin: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non deficient.

verses.text: The children of thy servants shall continue and their seed shall be directed for ever.
verses.textLatin: Filii servorum tuorum habitabunt, et semen eorum in sæculum dirigetur.

verses.text: For David himself.  Bless the Lord, O my soul: and let all that is within me bless his holy name.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi David. Benedic, anima mea, Domino, et omnia quæ intra me sunt nomini sancto ejus.

verses.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and never forget all he hath done for thee.
verses.textLatin: Benedic, anima mea, Domino, et noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus.

verses.text: Who forgiveth all thy iniquities: who healeth all thy diseases.
verses.textLatin: Qui propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis; qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas:

verses.text: Who redeemeth thy life from destruction: who crowneth thee with mercy and compassion.
verses.textLatin: qui redimit de interitu vitam tuam; qui coronat te in misericordia et miserationibus:

verses.text: Who satisfieth thy desire with good things: thy youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s.
verses.textLatin: qui replet in bonis desiderium tuum; renovabitur ut aquilæ juventus tua:

verses.text: The Lord doth mercies, and judgment for all that suffer wrong.
verses.textLatin: faciens misericordias Dominus, et judicium omnibus injuriam patientibus.

verses.text: He hath made his ways known to Moses: his wills to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Notas fecit vias suas Moysi; filiis Israël voluntates suas.

verses.text: The Lord is compassionate and merciful: longsuffering and plenteous in mercy.
verses.textLatin: Miserator et misericors Dominus: longanimis, et multum misericors.

verses.text: He will not always be angry: nor will he threaten for ever.
verses.textLatin: Non in perpetuum irascetur, neque in æternum comminabitur.

verses.text: He hath not dealt with us according to our sins: nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis, neque secundum iniquitates nostras retribuit nobis.

verses.text: For according to the height of the heaven above the earth: he hath strengthened his mercy towards them that fear him.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam secundum altitudinem cæli a terra, corroboravit misericordiam suam super timentes se;

verses.text: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our iniquities from us.
verses.textLatin: quantum distat ortus ab occidente, longe fecit a nobis iniquitates nostras.

verses.text: As a father hath compassion on his children, so hath the Lord compassion on them that fear him:
verses.textLatin: Quomodo miseretur pater filiorum, misertus est Dominus timentibus se.

verses.text: for he knoweth our frame. He remembereth that we are dust:
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ipse cognovit figmentum nostrum; recordatus est quoniam pulvis sumus.

verses.text: man’s days are as grass, as the flower of the field so shall he flourish.
verses.textLatin: Homo, sicut fœnum dies ejus; tamquam flos agri, sic efflorebit:

verses.text: For the spirit shall pass in him, and he shall not be: and he shall know his place no more.
verses.textLatin: quoniam spiritus pertransibit in illo, et non subsistet, et non cognoscet amplius locum suum.

verses.text: But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity and unto eternity upon them that fear him: And his justice unto children’s children,
verses.textLatin: Misericordia autem Domini ab æterno, et usque in æternum super timentes eum. Et justitia illius in filios filiorum,

verses.text: to such as keep his covenant, And are mindful of his commandments to do them.
verses.textLatin: his qui servant testamentum ejus, et memores sunt mandatorum ipsius ad faciendum ea.

verses.text: The Lord hath prepared his throne in heaven: and his kingdom shall rule over all.
verses.textLatin: Dominus in cælo paravit sedem suam, et regnum ipsius omnibus dominabitur.

verses.text: Bless the Lord, all ye his angels: you that are mighty in strength, and execute his word, hearkening to the voice of his orders.
verses.textLatin: Benedicite Domino, omnes angeli ejus: potentes virtute, facientes verbum illius, ad audiendam vocem sermonum ejus.

verses.text: Bless the Lord, all ye his hosts: you ministers of his that do his will.
verses.textLatin: Benedicite Domino, omnes virtutes ejus; ministri ejus, qui facitis voluntatem ejus.

verses.text: Bless the Lord, all his works: in every place of his dominion, O my soul, bless thou the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Benedicite Domino, omnia opera ejus: in omni loco dominationis ejus, benedic, anima mea, Domino.

verses.text: For David himself. Bless the Lord, O my soul: O Lord my God, thou art exceedingly great. Thou hast put on praise and beauty:
verses.textLatin: Ipsi David. Benedic, anima mea, Domino: Domine Deus meus, magnificatus es vehementer. Confessionem et decorem induisti,

verses.text: and art clothed with light as with a garment. Who stretchest out the heaven like a pavilion:
verses.textLatin: amictus lumine sicut vestimento. Extendens cælum sicut pellem,

verses.text: who coverest the higher rooms thereof with water. Who makest the clouds thy chariot: who walkest upon the wings of the winds.
verses.textLatin: qui tegis aquis superiora ejus: qui ponis nubem ascensum tuum; qui ambulas super pennas ventorum:

verses.text: Who makest thy angels spirits: and thy ministers a burning fire.
verses.textLatin: qui facis angelos tuos spiritus, et ministros tuos ignem urentem.

verses.text: Who hast founded the earth upon its own bases: it shall not be moved for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Qui fundasti terram super stabilitatem suam: non inclinabitur in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: The deep like a garment is its clothing: above the mountains shall the waters stand.
verses.textLatin: Abyssus sicut vestimentum amictus ejus; super montes stabunt aquæ.

verses.text: At thy rebuke they shall flee: at the voice of thy thunder they shall fear.
verses.textLatin: Ab increpatione tua fugient; a voce tonitrui tui formidabunt.

verses.text: The mountains ascend, and the plains descend into the place which thou hast founded for them.
verses.textLatin: Ascendunt montes, et descendunt campi, in locum quem fundasti eis.

verses.text: Thou hast set a bound which they shall not pass over; neither shall they return to cover the earth.
verses.textLatin: Terminum posuisti quem non transgredientur, neque convertentur operire terram.

verses.text: Thou sendest forth springs in the vales: between the midst of the hills the waters shall pass.
verses.textLatin: Qui emittis fontes in convallibus; inter medium montium pertransibunt aquæ.

verses.text: All the beasts of the field shall drink: the wild asses shall expect in their thirst.
verses.textLatin: Potabunt omnes bestiæ agri; expectabunt onagri in siti sua.

verses.text: Over them the birds of the air shall dwell: from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices.
verses.textLatin: Super ea volucres cæli habitabunt; de medio petrarum dabunt voces.

verses.text: Thou waterest the hills from thy upper rooms: the earth shall be filled with the fruit of thy works:
verses.textLatin: Rigans montes de superioribus suis; de fructu operum tuorum satiabitur terra:

verses.text: Bringing forth grass for cattle, and herb for the service of men. That thou mayst bring bread out of the earth:
verses.textLatin: producens fœnum jumentis, et herbam servituti hominum, ut educas panem de terra,

verses.text: and that wine may cheer the heart of man. That he may make the face cheerful with oil: and that bread may strengthen man’s heart.
verses.textLatin: et vinum lætificet cor hominis: ut exhilaret faciem in oleo, et panis cor hominis confirmet.

verses.text: The trees of the field shall be filled, and the cedars of Libanus which he hath planted:
verses.textLatin: Saturabuntur ligna campi, et cedri Libani quas plantavit:

verses.text: there the sparrows shall make their nests. The highest of them is the house of the heron.
verses.textLatin: illic passeres nidificabunt: herodii domus dux est eorum.

verses.text: The high hills are a refuge for the harts, the rock for the irchins.
verses.textLatin: Montes excelsi cervis; petra refugium herinaciis.

verses.text: He hath made the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.
verses.textLatin: Fecit lunam in tempora; sol cognovit occasum suum.

verses.text: Thou hast appointed darkness, and it is night: in it shall all the beasts of the woods go about:
verses.textLatin: Posuisti tenebras, et facta est nox; in ipsa pertransibunt omnes bestiæ silvæ:

verses.text: The young lions roaring after their prey, and seeking their meat from God.
verses.textLatin: catuli leonum rugientes ut rapiant, et quærant a Deo escam sibi.

verses.text: The sun ariseth, and they are gathered together: and they shall lie down in their dens.
verses.textLatin: Ortus est sol, et congregati sunt, et in cubilibus suis collocabuntur.

verses.text: Man shall go forth to his work, and to his labour until the evening.
verses.textLatin: Exibit homo ad opus suum, et ad operationem suam usque ad vesperum.

verses.text: How great are thy works, O Lord ? thou hast made all things in wisdom: the earth is filled with thy riches.
verses.textLatin: Quam magnificata sunt opera tua, Domine! omnia in sapientia fecisti; impleta est terra possessione tua.

verses.text: So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms: there are creeping things without number: Creatures little and great.
verses.textLatin: Hoc mare magnum et spatiosum manibus; illic reptilia quorum non est numerus: animalia pusilla cum magnis.

verses.text: There the ships shall go. This sea dragon which thou hast formed to play therein.
verses.textLatin: Illic naves pertransibunt; draco iste quem formasti ad illudendum ei.

verses.text: All expect of thee that thou give them food in season.
verses.textLatin: Omnia a te expectant ut des illis escam in tempore.

verses.text: What thou givest to them they shall gather up: when thou openest thy hand, they shall all be filled with good.
verses.textLatin: Dante te illis, colligent; aperiente te manum tuam, omnia implebuntur bonitate.

verses.text: But if thou turnest away thy face, they shall be troubled: thou shalt take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall return to their dust.
verses.textLatin: Avertente autem te faciem, turbabuntur; auferes spiritum eorum, et deficient, et in pulverem suum revertentur.

verses.text: Thou shalt send forth thy spirit, and they shall be created: and thou shalt renew the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Emittes spiritum tuum, et creabuntur, et renovabis faciem terræ.

verses.text: May the glory of the Lord endure for ever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works.
verses.textLatin: Sit gloria Domini in sæculum; lætabitur Dominus in operibus suis.

verses.text: He looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble: he toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.
verses.textLatin: Qui respicit terram, et facit eam tremere; qui tangit montes, et fumigant.

verses.text: I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
verses.textLatin: Cantabo Domino in vita mea; psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum.

verses.text: Let my speech be acceptable to him: but I will take delight in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Jucundum sit ei eloquium meum; ego vero delectabor in Domino.

verses.text: Let sinners be consumed out of the earth, and the unjust, so that they be no more: O my soul, bless thou the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Deficiant peccatores a terra, et iniqui, ita ut non sint. Benedic, anima mea, Domino.

verses.text: Give  glory to the Lord, and call upon his name: declare his deeds among the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino, et invocate nomen ejus; annuntiate inter gentes opera ejus.

verses.text: Sing to him, yea sing praises to him: relate all his wondrous works.
verses.textLatin: Cantate ei, et psallite ei; narrate omnia mirabilia ejus.

verses.text: Glory ye in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Laudamini in nomine sancto ejus; lætetur cor quærentium Dominum.

verses.text: Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened: seek his face evermore.
verses.textLatin: Quærite Dominum, et confirmamini; quærite faciem ejus semper.

verses.text: Remember his marvellous works which he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Mementote mirabilium ejus quæ fecit; prodigia ejus, et judicia oris ejus:

verses.text: O ye seed of Abraham his servant; ye sons of Jacob his chosen.
verses.textLatin: semen Abraham servi ejus; filii Jacob electi ejus.

verses.text: He is the Lord our God: his judgments are in all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Ipse Dominus Deus noster; in universa terra judicia ejus.

verses.text: He hath remembered his covenant for ever: the word which he commanded to a thousand generations.
verses.textLatin: Memor fuit in sæculum testamenti sui; verbi quod mandavit in mille generationes:

verses.text: Which he made to Abraham; and his oath to Isaac:
verses.textLatin: quod disposuit ad Abraham, et juramenti sui ad Isaac:

verses.text: And he appointed the same to Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting testament:
verses.textLatin: et statuit illud Jacob in præceptum, et Israël in testamentum æternum,

verses.text: Saying: To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, the lot of your inheritance.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Tibi dabo terram Chanaan, funiculum hæreditatis vestræ:

verses.text: When they were but a small number: yea very few, and sojourners therein:
verses.textLatin: cum essent numero brevi, paucissimi, et incolæ ejus.

verses.text: And they passed from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
verses.textLatin: Et pertransierunt de gente in gentem, et de regno ad populum alterum.

verses.text: He suffered no man to hurt them: and he reproved kings for their sakes.
verses.textLatin: Non reliquit hominem nocere eis: et corripuit pro eis reges.

verses.text: Touch ye not my anointed: and do no evil to my prophets.
verses.textLatin: Nolite tangere christos meos, et in prophetis meis nolite malignari.

verses.text: And he called a famine upon the land: and he broke in pieces all the support of bread.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit famem super terram, et omne firmamentum panis contrivit.

verses.text: He sent a man before them: Joseph, who was sold for a slave.
verses.textLatin: Misit ante eos virum: in servum venumdatus est, Joseph.

verses.text: They humbled his feet in fetters: the iron pierced his soul,
verses.textLatin: Humiliaverunt in compedibus pedes ejus; ferrum pertransiit animam ejus:

verses.text: until his word came. The word of the Lord inflamed him.
verses.textLatin: donec veniret verbum ejus. Eloquium Domini inflammavit eum.

verses.text: The king sent, and he released him: the ruler of the people, and he set him at liberty.
verses.textLatin: Misit rex, et solvit eum; princeps populorum, et dimisit eum.

verses.text: He made him master of his house, and ruler of all his possession.
verses.textLatin: Constituit eum dominum domus suæ, et principem omnis possessionis suæ:

verses.text: That he might instruct his princes as himself, and teach his ancients wisdom.
verses.textLatin: ut erudiret principes ejus sicut semetipsum, et senes ejus prudentiam doceret.

verses.text: And Israel went into Egypt: and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Cham.
verses.textLatin: Et intravit Israël in Ægyptum, et Jacob accola fuit in terra Cham.

verses.text: And he increased his people exceedingly: and strengthened them over their enemies.
verses.textLatin: Et auxit populum suum vehementer, et firmavit eum super inimicos ejus.

verses.text: He turned their heart to hate his people: and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
verses.textLatin: Convertit cor eorum, ut odirent populum ejus, et dolum facerent in servos ejus.

verses.text: He sent Moses his servant: Aaron the man whom he had chosen.
verses.textLatin: Misit Moysen servum suum; Aaron quem elegit ipsum.

verses.text: He gave them power to shew his signs, and his wonders in the land of Cham.
verses.textLatin: Posuit in eis verba signorum suorum, et prodigiorum in terra Cham.

verses.text: He sent darkness, and made it obscure: and grieved not his words.
verses.textLatin: Misit tenebras, et obscuravit; et non exacerbavit sermones suos.

verses.text: He turned their waters into blood, and destroyed their fish.
verses.textLatin: Convertit aquas eorum in sanguinem, et occidit pisces eorum.

verses.text: Their land brought forth frogs, in the inner chambers of their kings.
verses.textLatin: Edidit terra eorum ranas in penetralibus regum ipsorum.

verses.text: He spoke, and there came divers sorts of flies and sciniphs in all their coasts.
verses.textLatin: Dixit, et venit cœnomyia et ciniphes in omnibus finibus eorum.

verses.text: He gave them hail for rain, a burning fire in the land.
verses.textLatin: Posuit pluvias eorum grandinem: ignem comburentem in terra ipsorum.

verses.text: And he destroyed their vineyards and their fig trees: and he broke in pieces the trees of their coasts.
verses.textLatin: Et percussit vineas eorum, et ficulneas eorum, et contrivit lignum finium eorum.

verses.text: He spoke, and the locust came, and the bruchus, of which there was no number.
verses.textLatin: Dixit, et venit locusta, et bruchus cujus non erat numerus:

verses.text: And they devoured all the grass in their land, and consumed all the fruit of their ground.
verses.textLatin: et comedit omne fœnum in terra eorum, et comedit omnem fructum terræ eorum.

verses.text: And he slew all the firstborn in their land: the firstfruits of all their labour.
verses.textLatin: Et percussit omne primogenitum in terra eorum, primitias omnis laboris eorum.

verses.text: And he brought them out with silver and gold: and there was not among their tribes one that was feeble.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit eos cum argento et auro, et non erat in tribubus eorum infirmus.

verses.text: Egypt was glad when they departed: for the fear of them lay upon them.
verses.textLatin: Lætata est Ægyptus in profectione eorum, quia incubuit timor eorum super eos.

verses.text: He spread a cloud for their protection, and fire to give them light in the night.
verses.textLatin: Expandit nubem in protectionem eorum, et ignem ut luceret eis per noctem.

verses.text: They asked, and the quail came: and he filled them with the bread of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Petierunt, et venit coturnix, et pane cæli saturavit eos.

verses.text: He opened the rock, and waters flowed: rivers ran down in the dry land.
verses.textLatin: Dirupit petram, et fluxerunt aquæ: abierunt in sicco flumina.

verses.text: Because he remembered his holy word, which he had spoken to his servant Abraham.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui, quod habuit ad Abraham puerum suum.

verses.text: And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit populum suum in exsultatione, et electos suos in lætitia.

verses.text: And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles: and they possessed the labours of the people:
verses.textLatin: Et dedit illis regiones gentium, et labores populorum possederunt:

verses.text: That they might observe his justifications, and seek after his law.
verses.textLatin: ut custodiant justificationes ejus, et legem ejus requirant.

verses.text: Give  glory to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? who shall set forth all his praises?
verses.textLatin: Quis loquetur potentias Domini; auditas faciet omnes laudes ejus?

verses.text: Blessed are they that keep judgment, and do justice at all times.
verses.textLatin: Beati qui custodiunt judicium, et faciunt justitiam in omni tempore.

verses.text: Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people: visit us with thy salvation.
verses.textLatin: Memento nostri, Domine, in beneplacito populi tui; visita nos in salutari tuo:

verses.text: That we may see the good of thy chosen, that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation: that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance.
verses.textLatin: ad videndum in bonitate electorum tuorum; ad lætandum in lætitia gentis tuæ: ut lauderis cum hæreditate tua.

verses.text: We have sinned with our fathers: we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Peccavimus cum patribus nostris: injuste egimus; iniquitatem fecimus.

verses.text: Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt: they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies: And they provoked to wrath going up to the sea, even the Red Sea.
verses.textLatin: Patres nostri in Ægypto non intellexerunt mirabilia tua; non fuerunt memores multitudinis misericordiæ tuæ. Et irritaverunt ascendentes in mare, mare Rubrum;

verses.text: And he saved them for his own name’s sake: that he might make his power known.
verses.textLatin: et salvavit eos propter nomen suum, ut notam faceret potentiam suam.

verses.text: And he rebuked the Red Sea and it was dried up: and he led them through the depths, as in a wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Et increpuit mare Rubrum et exsiccatum est, et deduxit eos in abyssis sicut in deserto.

verses.text: And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them: and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Et salvavit eos de manu odientium, et redemit eos de manu inimici.

verses.text: And the water covered them that afflicted them: there was not one of them left.
verses.textLatin: Et operuit aqua tribulantes eos; unus ex eis non remansit.

verses.text: And they believed his words: and they sang his praises.
verses.textLatin: Et crediderunt verbis ejus, et laudaverunt laudem ejus.

verses.text: They had quickly done, they forgot his works: and they waited not for his counsel.
verses.textLatin: Cito fecerunt; obliti sunt operum ejus: et non sustinuerunt consilium ejus.

verses.text: And they coveted their desire in the desert: and they tempted God in the place without water.
verses.textLatin: Et concupierunt concupiscentiam in deserto, et tentaverunt Deum in inaquoso.

verses.text: And he gave them their request: and sent fulness into their souls.
verses.textLatin: Et dedit eis petitionem ipsorum, et misit saturitatem in animas eorum.

verses.text: And they provoked Moses in the camp, Aaron the holy one of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et irritaverunt Moysen in castris; Aaron, sanctum Domini.

verses.text: The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan: and covered the congregation of Abiron.
verses.textLatin: Aperta est terra, et deglutivit Dathan, et operuit super congregationem Abiron.

verses.text: And a fire was kindled in their congregation: the flame burned the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Et exarsit ignis in synagoga eorum: flamma combussit peccatores.

verses.text: They made also a calf in Horeb: and they adored the graven thing.
verses.textLatin: Et fecerunt vitulum in Horeb, et adoraverunt sculptile.

verses.text: And they changed their glory into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass.
verses.textLatin: Et mutaverunt gloriam suam in similitudinem vituli comedentis fœnum.

verses.text: They forgot God, who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt,
verses.textLatin: Obliti sunt Deum qui salvavit eos; qui fecit magnalia in Ægypto,

verses.text: wondrous works in the land of Cham: terrible things in the Red Sea.
verses.textLatin: mirabilia in terra Cham, terribilia in mari Rubro.

verses.text: And he said that he would destroy them: had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach: To turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ut disperderet eos, si non Moyses, electus ejus, stetisset in confractione in conspectu ejus, ut averteret iram ejus, ne disperderet eos.

verses.text: And they set at nought the desirable land. They believed not his word,
verses.textLatin: Et pro nihilo habuerunt terram desiderabilem; non crediderunt verbo ejus.

verses.text: and they murmured in their tents: they hearkened not to the voice of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et murmuraverunt in tabernaculis suis; non exaudierunt vocem Domini.

verses.text: And he lifted up his hand over them: to overthrow them in the desert;
verses.textLatin: Et elevavit manum suam super eos ut prosterneret eos in deserto:

verses.text: And to cast down their seed among the nations, and to scatter them in the countries.
verses.textLatin: et ut dejiceret semen eorum in nationibus, et dispergeret eos in regionibus.

verses.text: They also were initiated to Beelphegor: and ate the sacrifices of the dead.
verses.textLatin: Et initiati sunt Beelphegor, et comederunt sacrificia mortuorum.

verses.text: And they provoked him with their inventions: and destruction was multiplied among them.
verses.textLatin: Et irritaverunt eum in adinventionibus suis, et multiplicata est in eis ruina.

verses.text: Then Phinees stood up, and pacified him: and the slaughter ceased.
verses.textLatin: Et stetit Phinees, et placavit, et cessavit quassatio.

verses.text: And it was reputed to him unto justice, to generation and generation for evermore.
verses.textLatin: Et reputatum est ei in justitiam, in generationem et generationem usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: They provoked him also at the waters of contradiction: and Moses was afflicted for their sakes:
verses.textLatin: Et irritaverunt eum ad aquas contradictionis, et vexatus est Moyses propter eos:

verses.text: because they exasperated his spirit. And he distinguished with his lips.
verses.textLatin: quia exacerbaverunt spiritum ejus, et distinxit in labiis suis.

verses.text: They did not destroy the nations of which the Lord spoke unto them.
verses.textLatin: Non disperdiderunt gentes quas dixit Dominus illis:

verses.text: And they were mingled among the heathens, and learned their works:
verses.textLatin: et commisti sunt inter gentes, et didicerunt opera eorum;

verses.text: and served their idols, and it became a stumbling-block to them.
verses.textLatin: et servierunt sculptilibus eorum, et factum est illis in scandalum.

verses.text: And they sacrificed their sons, and their daughters to devils.
verses.textLatin: Et immolaverunt filios suos et filias suas dæmoniis.

verses.text: And they shed innocent blood: the blood of their sons and of their daughters which they sacrificed to the idols of Chanaan. And the land was polluted with blood,
verses.textLatin: Et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem, sanguinem filiorum suorum et filiarum suarum, quas sacrificaverunt sculptilibus Chanaan. Et infecta est terra in sanguinibus,

verses.text: and was defiled with their works: and they went aside after their own inventions.
verses.textLatin: et contaminata est in operibus eorum: et fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis.

verses.text: And the Lord was exceedingly angry with his people: and he abhorred his inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus est furore Dominus in populum suum, et abominatus est hæreditatem suam.

verses.text: And he delivered them into the hands of the nations: and they that hated them had dominion over them.
verses.textLatin: Et tradidit eos in manus gentium; et dominati sunt eorum qui oderunt eos.

verses.text: And their enemies afflicted them: and they were humbled under their hands:
verses.textLatin: Et tribulaverunt eos inimici eorum, et humiliati sunt sub manibus eorum;

verses.text: many times did he deliver them. But they provoked him with their counsel: and they were brought low by their iniquities.
verses.textLatin: sæpe liberavit eos. Ipsi autem exacerbaverunt eum in consilio suo, et humiliati sunt in iniquitatibus suis.

verses.text: And he saw when they were in tribulation: and he heard their prayer.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit cum tribularentur, et audivit orationem eorum.

verses.text: And he was mindful of his covenant: and repented according to the multitude of his mercies.
verses.textLatin: Et memor fuit testamenti sui, et pœnituit eum secundum multitudinem misericordiæ suæ:

verses.text: And he gave them unto mercies, in the sight of all those that had made them captives.
verses.textLatin: et dedit eos in misericordias, in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos.

verses.text: Save us, O Lord, our God: and gather us from among the nations: That we may give thanks to thy holy name, and may glory in thy praise.
verses.textLatin: Salvos nos fac, Domine Deus noster, et congrega nos de nationibus: ut confiteamur nomini sancto tuo, et gloriemur in laude tua.

verses.text: Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say: So be it, so be it.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus Deus Israël, a sæculo et usque in sæculum; et dicet omnis populus: Fiat, fiat.

verses.text: Give  glory to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Let them say so that have been redeemed by the Lord, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy: and gathered out of the countries.
verses.textLatin: Dicant qui redempti sunt a Domino, quos redemit de manu inimici, et de regionibus congregavit eos,

verses.text: From the rising and from the setting of the sun, from the north and from the sea.
verses.textLatin: a solis ortu, et occasu, ab aquilone, et mari.

verses.text: They wandered in a wilderness, in a place without water: they found not the way of a city for their habitation.
verses.textLatin: Erraverunt in solitudine, in inaquoso; viam civitatis habitaculi non invenerunt.

verses.text: They were hungry and thirsty: their soul fainted in them.
verses.textLatin: Esurientes et sitientes, anima eorum in ipsis defecit.

verses.text: And they cried to the Lord in their tribulation: and he delivered them out of their distresses.
verses.textLatin: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum cum tribularentur, et de necessitatibus eorum eripuit eos;

verses.text: And he led them into the right way, that they might go to a city of habitation.
verses.textLatin: et deduxit eos in viam rectam, ut irent in civitatem habitationis.

verses.text: Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: and his wonderful works to the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum.

verses.text: For he hath satisfied the empty soul, and hath filled the hungry soul with good things.
verses.textLatin: Quia satiavit animam inanem, et animam esurientem satiavit bonis.

verses.text: Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death: bound in want and in iron.
verses.textLatin: Sedentes in tenebris et umbra mortis; vinctos in mendicitate et ferro.

verses.text: Because they had exasperated the words of God: and provoked the counsel of the most High:
verses.textLatin: Quia exacerbaverunt eloquia Dei, et consilium Altissimi irritaverunt.

verses.text: And their heart was humbled with labours: they were weakened, and there was none to help them.
verses.textLatin: Et humiliatum est in laboribus cor eorum; infirmati sunt, nec fuit qui adjuvaret.

verses.text: Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction: and he delivered them out of their distresses.
verses.textLatin: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum cum tribularentur; et de necessitatibus eorum liberavit eos.

verses.text: And he brought them out of darkness, and the shadow of death; and broke their bonds in sunder.
verses.textLatin: Et eduxit eos de tenebris et umbra mortis, et vincula eorum dirupit.

verses.text: Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, and his wonderful works to the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum.

verses.text: Because he hath broken gates of brass, and burst iron bars.
verses.textLatin: Quia contrivit portas æreas, et vectes ferreos confregit.

verses.text: He took them out of the way of their iniquity: for they were brought low for their injustices.
verses.textLatin: Suscepit eos de via iniquitatis eorum; propter injustitias enim suas humiliati sunt.

verses.text: Their soul abhorred all manner of meat: and they drew nigh even to the gates of death.
verses.textLatin: Omnem escam abominata est anima eorum, et appropinquaverunt usque ad portas mortis.

verses.text: And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: and he delivered them out of their distresses.
verses.textLatin: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum cum tribularentur, et de necessitatibus eorum liberavit eos.

verses.text: He sent his word, and healed them: and delivered them from their destructions.
verses.textLatin: Misit verbum suum, et sanavit eos, et eripuit eos de interitionibus eorum.

verses.text: Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: and his wonderful works to the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum.

verses.text: And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise: and declare his works with joy.
verses.textLatin: Et sacrificent sacrificium laudis, et annuntient opera ejus in exsultatione.

verses.text: They that go down to the sea in ships, doing business in the great waters:
verses.textLatin: Qui descendunt mare in navibus, facientes operationem in aquis multis:

verses.text: These have seen the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep.
verses.textLatin: ipsi viderunt opera Domini, et mirabilia ejus in profundo.

verses.text: He said the word, and there arose a storm of wind: and the waves thereof were lifted up.
verses.textLatin: Dixit, et stetit spiritus procellæ, et exaltati sunt fluctus ejus.

verses.text: They mount up to the heavens, and they go down to the depths: their soul pined away with evils.
verses.textLatin: Ascendunt usque ad cælos, et descendunt usque ad abyssos; anima eorum in malis tabescebat.

verses.text: They were troubled, and reeled like a drunken man; and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
verses.textLatin: Turbati sunt, et moti sunt sicut ebrius, et omnis sapientia eorum devorata est.

verses.text: And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: and he brought them out of their distresses.
verses.textLatin: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum cum tribularentur; et de necessitatibus eorum eduxit eos.

verses.text: And he turned the storm into a breeze: and its waves were still.
verses.textLatin: Et statuit procellam ejus in auram, et siluerunt fluctus ejus.

verses.text: And they rejoiced because they were still: and he brought them to the haven which they wished for.
verses.textLatin: Et lætati sunt quia siluerunt; et deduxit eos in portum voluntatis eorum.

verses.text: Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, and his wonderful works to the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur Domino misericordiæ ejus, et mirabilia ejus filiis hominum.

verses.text: And let them exalt him in the church of the people: and praise him in the chair of the ancients.
verses.textLatin: Et exaltent eum in ecclesia plebis, et in cathedra seniorum laudent eum.

verses.text: He hath turned rivers into a wilderness: and the sources of waters into dry ground:
verses.textLatin: Posuit flumina in desertum, et exitus aquarum in sitim;

verses.text: A fruitful land into barrenness, for the wickedness of them that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: terram fructiferam in salsuginem, a malitia inhabitantium in ea.

verses.text: He hath turned a wilderness into pools of waters, and a dry land into water springs.
verses.textLatin: Posuit desertum in stagna aquarum, et terram sine aqua in exitus aquarum.

verses.text: And hath placed there the hungry; and they made a city for their habitation.
verses.textLatin: Et collocavit illic esurientes, et constituerunt civitatem habitationis:

verses.text: And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards: and they yielded fruit of birth.
verses.textLatin: et seminaverunt agros et plantaverunt vineas, et fecerunt fructum nativitatis.

verses.text: And he blessed them, and they were multiplied exceedingly: and their cattle he suffered not to decrease.
verses.textLatin: Et benedixit eis, et multiplicati sunt nimis; et jumenta eorum non minoravit.

verses.text: Then they were brought to be few: and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils and sorrow.
verses.textLatin: Et pauci facti sunt et vexati sunt, a tribulatione malorum et dolore.

verses.text: Contempt was poured forth upon their princes: and he caused them to wander where there was no passing, and out of the way.
verses.textLatin: Effusa est contemptio super principes: et errare fecit eos in invio, et non in via.

verses.text: And he helped the poor out of poverty: and made him families like a flock of sheep.
verses.textLatin: Et adjuvit pauperem de inopia, et posuit sicut oves familias.

verses.text: The just shall see, and shall rejoice, and all iniquity shall stop her mouth.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt recti, et lætabuntur; et omnis iniquitas oppilabit os suum.

verses.text: Who is wise, and will keep these things; and will understand the mercies of the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Quis sapiens, et custodiet hæc, et intelliget misericordias Domini?

verses.text: A canticle of a psalm for David himself.
verses.textLatin: Canticum Psalmi, ipsi David.

verses.text: My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: I will sing, and will give praise, with my glory.
verses.textLatin: Paratum cor meum, Deus, paratum cor meum; cantabo, et psallam in gloria mea.

verses.text: Arise, my glory; arise, psaltery and harp: I will arise in the morning early.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, gloria mea; exsurge, psalterium et cithara; exsurgam diluculo.

verses.text: I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: and I will sing unto thee among the nations.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi in populis, Domine, et psallam tibi in nationibus:

verses.text: For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth even unto the clouds.
verses.textLatin: quia magna est super cælos misericordia tua, et usque ad nubes veritas tua.

verses.text: Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth:
verses.textLatin: Exaltare super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram gloria tua:

verses.text: that thy beloved may be delivered. Save with thy right hand and hear me.
verses.textLatin: ut liberentur dilecti tui. Salvum fac dextera tua, et exaudi me.

verses.text: God hath spoken in his holiness. I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: Deus locutus est in sancto suo: Exsultabo, et dividam Sichimam; et convallem tabernaculorum dimetiar.

verses.text: Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: and Ephraim the protection of my head. Juda is my king:
verses.textLatin: Meus est Galaad, et meus est Manasses, et Ephraim susceptio capitis mei. Juda rex meus;

verses.text: Moab the pot of my hope. Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: the aliens are become my friends.
verses.textLatin: Moab lebes spei meæ: in Idumæam extendam calceamentum meum; mihi alienigenæ amici facti sunt.

verses.text: Who will bring me into the strong city? who will lead me into Edom?
verses.textLatin: Quis deducet me in civitatem munitam? quis deducet me usque in Idumæam?

verses.text: Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?
verses.textLatin: nonne tu, Deus, qui repulisti nos? et non exibis, Deus, in virtutibus nostris?

verses.text: O grant us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man.
verses.textLatin: Da nobis auxilium de tribulatione, quia vana salus hominis.

verses.text: Through God we shall do mightily: and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
verses.textLatin: In Deo faciemus virtutem; et ipse ad nihilum deducet inimicos nostros.

verses.text: Unto the end, a psalm for David.
verses.textLatin: In finem. Psalmus David.

verses.text: O God, be not thou silent in my praise: for the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me.
verses.textLatin: Deus, laudem meam ne tacueris, quia os peccatoris et os dolosi super me apertum est.

verses.text: They have spoken against me with deceitful tongues; and they have compassed me about with words of hatred; and have fought against me without cause.
verses.textLatin: Locuti sunt adversum me lingua dolosa, et sermonibus odii circumdederunt me: et expugnaverunt me gratis.

verses.text: Instead of making me a return of love, they detracted me: but I gave myself to prayer.
verses.textLatin: Pro eo ut me diligerent, detrahebant mihi; ego autem orabam.

verses.text: And they repaid me evil for good: and hatred for my love.
verses.textLatin: Et posuerunt adversum me mala pro bonis, et odium pro dilectione mea.

verses.text: Set thou the sinner over him: and may the devil stand at his right hand.
verses.textLatin: Constitue super eum peccatorem, et diabolus stet a dextris ejus.

verses.text: When he is judged, may he go out condemned; and may his prayer be turned to sin.
verses.textLatin: Cum judicatur, exeat condemnatus; et oratio ejus fiat in peccatum.

verses.text: May his days be few: and his bishopric let another take.
verses.textLatin: Fiant dies ejus pauci, et episcopatum ejus accipiat alter.

verses.text: May his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
verses.textLatin: Fiant filii ejus orphani, et uxor ejus vidua.

verses.text: Let his children be carried about vagabonds, and beg; and let them be cast out of their dwellings.
verses.textLatin: Nutantes transferantur filii ejus et mendicent, et ejiciantur de habitationibus suis.

verses.text: May the usurer search all his substance: and let strangers plunder his labours.
verses.textLatin: Scrutetur fœnerator omnem substantiam ejus, et diripiant alieni labores ejus.

verses.text: May there be none to help him: nor none to pity his fatherless offspring.
verses.textLatin: Non sit illi adjutor, nec sit qui misereatur pupillis ejus.

verses.text: May his posterity be cut off; in one generation may his name be blotted out.
verses.textLatin: Fiant nati ejus in interitum; in generatione una deleatur nomen ejus.

verses.text: May the iniquity of his fathers be remembered in the sight of the Lord: and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
verses.textLatin: In memoriam redeat iniquitas patrum ejus in conspectu Domini, et peccatum matris ejus non deleatur.

verses.text: May they be before the Lord continually, and let the memory of them perish from the earth:
verses.textLatin: Fiant contra Dominum semper, et dispereat de terra memoria eorum:

verses.text: because he remembered not to shew mercy,
verses.textLatin: pro eo quod non est recordatus facere misericordiam,

verses.text: But persecuted the poor man and the beggar; and the broken in heart, to put him to death.
verses.textLatin: et persecutus est hominem inopem et mendicum, et compunctum corde, mortificare.

verses.text: And he loved cursing, and it shall come unto him: and he would not have blessing, and it shall be far from him. And he put on cursing, like a garment: and it went in like water into his entrails, and like oil in his bones.
verses.textLatin: Et dilexit maledictionem, et veniet ei; et noluit benedictionem, et elongabitur ab eo. Et induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum; et intravit sicut aqua in interiora ejus, et sicut oleum in ossibus ejus.

verses.text: May it be unto him like a garment which covereth him; and like a girdle with which he is girded continually.
verses.textLatin: Fiat ei sicut vestimentum quo operitur, et sicut zona qua semper præcingitur.

verses.text: This is the work of them who detract me before the Lord; and who speak evils against my soul.
verses.textLatin: Hoc opus eorum qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum, et qui loquuntur mala adversus animam meam.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, do with me for thy name’s sake: because thy mercy is sweet. Do thou deliver me,
verses.textLatin: Et tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum propter nomen tuum, quia suavis est misericordia tua.

verses.text: for I am poor and needy, and my heart is troubled within me.
verses.textLatin: Libera me, quia egenus et pauper ego sum, et cor meum conturbatum est intra me.

verses.text: I am taken away like the shadow when it declineth: and I am shaken off as locusts.
verses.textLatin: Sicut umbra cum declinat ablatus sum, et excussus sum sicut locustæ.

verses.text: My knees are weakened through fasting: and my flesh is changed for oil.
verses.textLatin: Genua mea infirmata sunt a jejunio, et caro mea immutata est propter oleum.

verses.text: And I am become a reproach to them: they saw me and they shaked their heads.
verses.textLatin: Et ego factus sum opprobrium illis; viderunt me, et moverunt capita sua.

verses.text: Help me, O Lord my God; save me according to thy mercy.
verses.textLatin: Adjuva me, Domine Deus meus; salvum me fac secundum misericordiam tuam.

verses.text: And let them know that this is thy hand: and that thou, O Lord, hast done it.
verses.textLatin: Et sciant quia manus tua hæc, et tu, Domine, fecisti eam.

verses.text: They will curse and thou wilt bless: let them that rise up against me be confounded: but thy servant shall rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Maledicent illi, et tu benedices: qui insurgunt in me confundantur; servus autem tuus lætabitur.

verses.text: Let them that detract me be clothed with shame: and let them be covered with their confusion as with a double cloak.
verses.textLatin: Induantur qui detrahunt mihi pudore, et operiantur sicut diploide confusione sua.

verses.text: I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: and in the midst of many I will praise him.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo, et in medio multorum laudabo eum:

verses.text: Because he hath stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from persecutors.
verses.textLatin: quia astitit a dextris pauperis, ut salvam faceret a persequentibus animam meam.

verses.text: A psalm for David. The Lord said to my Lord: Sit thou at my right hand: Until I make thy enemies thy footstool.
verses.textLatin: Psalmus David. Dixit Dominus Domino meo: Sede a dextris meis, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum.

verses.text: The Lord will send forth the sceptre of thy power out of Sion: rule thou in the midst of thy enemies.
verses.textLatin: Virgam virtutis tuæ emittet Dominus ex Sion: dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum.

verses.text: With thee is the principality in the day of thy strength: in the brightness of the saints: from the womb before the day star I begot thee.
verses.textLatin: Tecum principium in die virtutis tuæ in splendoribus sanctorum: ex utero, ante luciferum, genui te.

verses.text: The Lord hath sworn, and he will not repent: Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.
verses.textLatin: Juravit Dominus, et non pœnitebit eum: Tu es sacerdos in æternum secundum ordinem Melchisedech.

verses.text: The Lord at thy right hand hath broken kings in the day of his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Dominus a dextris tuis; confregit in die iræ suæ reges.

verses.text: He shall judge among nations, he shall fill ruins: he shall crush the heads in the land of many.
verses.textLatin: Judicabit in nationibus, implebit ruinas; conquassabit capita in terra multorum.

verses.text: He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head.
verses.textLatin: De torrente in via bibet; propterea exaltabit caput.

verses.text: I  will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart; in the council of the just, and in the congregation.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo, in consilio justorum, et congregatione.

verses.text: Great are the works of the Lord: sought out according to all his wills.
verses.textLatin: Magna opera Domini: exquisita in omnes voluntates ejus.

verses.text: His work is praise and magnificence: and his justice continueth for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Confessio et magnificentia opus ejus, et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works, being a merciful and gracious Lord:
verses.textLatin: Memoriam fecit mirabilium suorum, misericors et miserator Dominus.

verses.text: he hath given food to them that fear him. He will be mindful for ever of his covenant:
verses.textLatin: Escam dedit timentibus se; memor erit in sæculum testamenti sui.

verses.text: he will shew forth to his people the power of his works.
verses.textLatin: Virtutem operum suorum annuntiabit populo suo,

verses.text: That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles: the works of his hands are truth and judgment.
verses.textLatin: ut det illis hæreditatem gentium. Opera manuum ejus veritas et judicium.

verses.text: All his commandments are faithful: confirmed for ever and ever, made in truth and equity.
verses.textLatin: Fidelia omnia mandata ejus, confirmata in sæculum sæculi, facta in veritate et æquitate.

verses.text: He hath sent redemption to his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever. Holy and terrible is his name:
verses.textLatin: Redemptionem misit populo suo; mandavit in æternum testamentum suum. Sanctum et terribile nomen ejus.

verses.text: the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. A good understanding to all that do it: his praise continueth for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Initium sapientiæ timor Domini; intellectus bonus omnibus facientibus eum: laudatio ejus manet in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: Blessed  is the man that feareth the Lord: he shall delight exceedingly in his commandments.
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir qui timet Dominum: in mandatis ejus volet nimis.

verses.text: His seed shall be mighty upon earth: the generation of the righteous shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Potens in terra erit semen ejus; generatio rectorum benedicetur.

verses.text: Glory and wealth shall be in his house: and his justice remaineth for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Gloria et divitiæ in domo ejus, et justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: To the righteous a light is risen up in darkness: he is merciful, and compassionate and just.
verses.textLatin: Exortum est in tenebris lumen rectis: misericors, et miserator, et justus.

verses.text: Acceptable is the man that sheweth mercy and lendeth: he shall order his words with judgment:
verses.textLatin: Jucundus homo qui miseretur et commodat; disponet sermones suos in judicio:

verses.text: because he shall not be moved for ever.
verses.textLatin: quia in æternum non commovebitur.

verses.text: The just shall be in everlasting remembrance: he shall not fear the evil hearing. His heart is ready to hope in the Lord:
verses.textLatin: In memoria æterna erit justus; ab auditione mala non timebit. Paratum cor ejus sperare in Domino,

verses.text: his heart is strengthened, he shall not be moved until he look over his enemies.
verses.textLatin: confirmatum est cor ejus; non commovebitur donec despiciat inimicos suos.

verses.text: He hath distributed, he hath given to the poor: his justice remaineth for ever and ever: his horn shall be exalted in glory.
verses.textLatin: Dispersit, dedit pauperibus; justitia ejus manet in sæculum sæculi: cornu ejus exaltabitur in gloria.

verses.text: The wicked shall see, and shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away: the desire of the wicked shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Peccator videbit, et irascetur; dentibus suis fremet et tabescet: desiderium peccatorum peribit.

verses.text: Praise  the Lord, ye children: praise ye the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Laudate, pueri, Dominum; laudate nomen Domini.

verses.text: Blessed be the name of the Lord, from henceforth now and for ever.
verses.textLatin: Sit nomen Domini benedictum ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum.

verses.text: From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.
verses.textLatin: A solis ortu usque ad occasum laudabile nomen Domini.

verses.text: The Lord is high above all nations; and his glory above the heavens.
verses.textLatin: Excelsus super omnes gentes Dominus, et super cælos gloria ejus.

verses.text: Who is as the Lord our God, who dwelleth on high:
verses.textLatin: Quis sicut Dominus Deus noster, qui in altis habitat,

verses.text: and looketh down on the low things in heaven and in earth?
verses.textLatin: et humilia respicit in cælo et in terra?

verses.text: Raising up the needy from the earth, and lifting up the poor out of the dunghill:
verses.textLatin: Suscitans a terra inopem, et de stercore erigens pauperem:

verses.text: That he may place him with princes, with the princes of his people.
verses.textLatin: ut collocet eum cum principibus, cum principibus populi sui.

verses.text: Who maketh a barren woman to dwell in a house, the joyful mother of children.
verses.textLatin: Qui habitare facit sterilem in domo, matrem filiorum lætantem.

verses.text: When  Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarous people:
verses.textLatin: In exitu Israël de Ægypto, domus Jacob de populo barbaro,

verses.text: Judea was made his sanctuary, Israel his dominion.
verses.textLatin: facta est Judæa sanctificatio ejus; Israël potestas ejus.

verses.text: The sea saw and fled: Jordan was turned back.
verses.textLatin: Mare vidit, et fugit; Jordanis conversus est retrorsum.

verses.text: The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like the lambs of the flock.
verses.textLatin: Montes exsultaverunt ut arietes, et colles sicut agni ovium.

verses.text: What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou didst flee: and thou, O Jordan, that thou wast turned back?
verses.textLatin: Quid est tibi, mare, quod fugisti? et tu, Jordanis, quia conversus es retrorsum?

verses.text: Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams, and ye hills, like lambs of the flock?
verses.textLatin: montes, exsultastis sicut arietes? et colles, sicut agni ovium?

verses.text: At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved, at the presence of the God of Jacob:
verses.textLatin: A facie Domini mota est terra, a facie Dei Jacob:

verses.text: Who turned the rock into pools of water, and the stony hill into fountains of waters.
verses.textLatin: qui convertit petram in stagna aquarum, et rupem in fontes aquarum.

verses.text: Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory.
verses.textLatin: Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam:

verses.text: For thy mercy, and for thy truth’s sake: lest the Gentiles should say: Where is their God?
verses.textLatin: super misericordia tua et veritate tua; nequando dicant gentes: Ubi est Deus eorum?

verses.text: But our God is in heaven: he hath done all things whatsoever he would.
verses.textLatin: Deus autem noster in cælo; omnia quæcumque voluit fecit.

verses.text: The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, the works of the hands of men.
verses.textLatin: Simulacra gentium argentum et aurum, opera manuum hominum.

verses.text: They have mouths and speak not: they have eyes and see not.
verses.textLatin: Os habent, et non loquentur; oculos habent, et non videbunt.

verses.text: They have ears and hear not: they have noses and smell not.
verses.textLatin: Aures habent, et non audient; nares habent, et non odorabunt.

verses.text: They have hands and feel not: they have feet and walk not: neither shall they cry out through their throat.
verses.textLatin: Manus habent, et non palpabunt; pedes habent, et non ambulabunt; non clamabunt in gutture suo.

verses.text: Let them that make them become like unto them: and all such as trust in them.
verses.textLatin: Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui confidunt in eis.

verses.text: The house of Israel hath hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
verses.textLatin: Domus Israël speravit in Domino; adjutor eorum et protector eorum est.

verses.text: The house of Aaron hath hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
verses.textLatin: Domus Aaron speravit in Domino; adjutor eorum et protector eorum est.

verses.text: They that fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector.
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum speraverunt in Domino; adjutor eorum et protector eorum est.

verses.text: The Lord hath been mindful of us, and hath blessed us. He hath blessed the house of Israel: he hath blessed the house of Aaron.
verses.textLatin: Dominus memor fuit nostri, et benedixit nobis. Benedixit domui Israël; benedixit domui Aaron.

verses.text: He hath blessed all that fear the Lord, both little and great.
verses.textLatin: Benedixit omnibus qui timent Dominum, pusillis cum majoribus.

verses.text: May the Lord add blessings upon you: upon you, and upon your children.
verses.textLatin: Adjiciat Dominus super vos, super vos et super filios vestros.

verses.text: Blessed be you of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
verses.textLatin: Benedicti vos a Domino, qui fecit cælum et terram.

verses.text: The heaven of heaven is the Lord’s: but the earth he has given to the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Cælum cæli Domino; terram autem dedit filiis hominum.

verses.text: The dead shall not praise thee, O Lord: nor any of them that go down to hell.
verses.textLatin: Non mortui laudabunt te, Domine, neque omnes qui descendunt in infernum:

verses.text: But we that live bless the Lord: from this time now and for ever.
verses.textLatin: sed nos qui vivimus, benedicimus Domino, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum.

verses.text: I  have loved, because the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Dilexi, quoniam exaudiet Dominus vocem orationis meæ.

verses.text: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me: and in my days I will call upon him.
verses.textLatin: Quia inclinavit aurem suam mihi, et in diebus meis invocabo.

verses.text: The sorrows of death have compassed me: and the perils of hell have found me. I met with trouble and sorrow:
verses.textLatin: Circumdederunt me dolores mortis; et pericula inferni invenerunt me. Tribulationem et dolorem inveni,

verses.text: and I called upon the name of the Lord. O Lord, deliver my soul.
verses.textLatin: et nomen Domini invocavi: o Domine, libera animam meam.

verses.text: The Lord is merciful and just, and our God sheweth mercy.
verses.textLatin: Misericors Dominus et justus, et Deus noster miseretur.

verses.text: The Lord is the keeper of little ones: I was humbled, and he delivered me.
verses.textLatin: Custodiens parvulos Dominus; humiliatus sum, et liberavit me.

verses.text: Turn, O my soul, into thy rest: for the Lord hath been bountiful to thee.
verses.textLatin: Convertere, anima mea, in requiem tuam, quia Dominus benefecit tibi:

verses.text: For he hath delivered my soul from death: my eyes from tears, my feet from falling.
verses.textLatin: quia eripuit animam meam de morte, oculos meos a lacrimis, pedes meos a lapsu.

verses.text: I will please the Lord in the land of the living.
verses.textLatin: Placebo Domino in regione vivorum.

verses.text: I have believed, therefore have I spoken; but I have been humbled exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Credidi, propter quod locutus sum; ego autem humiliatus sum nimis.

verses.text: I said in my excess: Every man is a liar.
verses.textLatin: Ego dixi in excessu meo: Omnis homo mendax.

verses.text: What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me?
verses.textLatin: Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi?

verses.text: I will take the chalice of salvation; and I will call upon the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Calicem salutaris accipiam, et nomen Domini invocabo.

verses.text: I will pay my vows to the Lord before all his people:
verses.textLatin: Vota mea Domino reddam coram omni populo ejus.

verses.text: precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints.
verses.textLatin: Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum ejus.

verses.text: O Lord, for I am thy servant: I am thy servant, and the son of thy handmaid. Thou hast broken my bonds:
verses.textLatin: O Domine, quia ego servus tuus; ego servus tuus, et filius ancillæ tuæ. Dirupisti vincula mea:

verses.text: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise, and I will call upon the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: tibi sacrificabo hostiam laudis, et nomen Domini invocabo.

verses.text: I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all his people:
verses.textLatin: Vota mea Domino reddam in conspectu omnis populi ejus;

verses.text: in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: in atriis domus Domini, in medio tui, Jerusalem.

verses.text: O  praise the Lord, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people.
verses.textLatin: Laudate Dominum, omnes gentes; laudate eum, omnes populi.

verses.text: For his mercy is confirmed upon us: and the truth of the Lord remaineth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam confirmata est super nos misericordia ejus, et veritas Domini manet in æternum.

verses.text: Give  praise to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Let Israel now say, that he is good: that his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Dicat nunc Israël: Quoniam bonus, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Let the house of Aaron now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Dicat nunc domus Aaron: Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Let them that fear the Lord now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Dicant nunc qui timent Dominum: Quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: In my trouble I called upon the Lord: and the Lord heard me, and enlarged me.
verses.textLatin: De tribulatione invocavi Dominum, et exaudivit me in latitudine Dominus.

verses.text: The Lord is my helper: I will not fear what man can do unto me.
verses.textLatin: Dominus mihi adjutor; non timebo quid faciat mihi homo.

verses.text: The Lord is my helper: and I will look over my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Dominus mihi adjutor, et ego despiciam inimicos meos.

verses.text: It is good to confide in the Lord, rather than to have confidence in man.
verses.textLatin: Bonum est confidere in Domino, quam confidere in homine.

verses.text: It is good to trust in the Lord, rather than to trust in princes.
verses.textLatin: Bonum est sperare in Domino, quam sperare in principibus.

verses.text: All nations compassed me about; and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.
verses.textLatin: Omnes gentes circuierunt me, et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos.

verses.text: Surrounding me they compassed me about: and in the name of the Lord I have been revenged on them.
verses.textLatin: Circumdantes circumdederunt me, et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos.

verses.text: They surrounded me like bees, and they burned like fire among thorns: and in the name of the Lord I was revenged on them.
verses.textLatin: Circumdederunt me sicut apes, et exarserunt sicut ignis in spinis: et in nomine Domini, quia ultus sum in eos.

verses.text: Being pushed I was overturned that I might fall: but the Lord supported me.
verses.textLatin: Impulsus eversus sum, ut caderem, et Dominus suscepit me.
