verses.textLatin: et in misericordia tua disperdes inimicos meos, et perdes omnes qui tribulant animam meam, quoniam ego servus tuus sum.

verses.text: Blessed  be the Lord my God, who teacheth my hands to fight, and my fingers to war.
verses.textLatin: Benedictus Dominus Deus meus, qui docet manus meas ad prælium, et digitos meos ad bellum.

verses.text: My mercy, and my refuge: my support, and my deliverer: My protector, and I have hoped in him: who subdueth my people under me.
verses.textLatin: Misericordia mea et refugium meum; susceptor meus et liberator meus; protector meus, et in ipso speravi, qui subdit populum meum sub me.

verses.text: Lord, what is man, that thou art made known to him? or the son of man, that thou makest account of him?
verses.textLatin: Domine, quid est homo, quia innotuisti ei? aut filius hominis, quia reputas eum?

verses.text: Man is like to vanity: his days pass away like a shadow.
verses.textLatin: Homo vanitati similis factus est; dies ejus sicut umbra prætereunt.

verses.text: Lord, bow down thy heavens and descend: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.
verses.textLatin: Domine, inclina cælos tuos, et descende; tange montes, et fumigabunt.

verses.text: Send forth lightning, and thou shalt scatter them: shoot out thy arrows, and thou shalt trouble them.
verses.textLatin: Fulgura coruscationem, et dissipabis eos; emitte sagittas tuas, et conturbabis eos.

verses.text: Put forth thy hand from on high, take me out, and deliver me from many waters: from the hand of strange children:
verses.textLatin: Emitte manum tuam de alto: eripe me, et libera me de aquis multis, de manu filiorum alienorum:

verses.text: Whose mouth hath spoken vanity: and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: quorum os locutum est vanitatem, et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis.

verses.text: To thee, O God, I will sing a new canticle: on the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings I will sing praises to thee.
verses.textLatin: Deus, canticum novum cantabo tibi; in psalterio decachordo psallam tibi.

verses.text: Who givest salvation to kings: who hast redeemed thy servant David from the malicious sword:
verses.textLatin: Qui das salutem regibus, qui redemisti David servum tuum de gladio maligno,

verses.text: Deliver me, And rescue me out of the hand of strange children; whose mouth hath spoken vanity: and their right hand is the right hand of iniquity:
verses.textLatin: eripe me, et erue me de manu filiorum alienorum, quorum os locutum est vanitatem, et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis.

verses.text: Whose sons are as new plants in their youth: Their daughters decked out, adorned round about after the similitude of a temple:
verses.textLatin: Quorum filii sicut novellæ plantationes in juventute sua; filiæ eorum compositæ, circumornatæ ut similitudo templi.

verses.text: Their storehouses full, flowing out of this into that. Their sheep fruitful in young, abounding in their goings forth:
verses.textLatin: Promptuaria eorum plena, eructantia ex hoc in illud; oves eorum fœtosæ, abundantes in egressibus suis;

verses.text: their oxen fat. There is no breach of wall, nor passage, nor crying out in their streets.
verses.textLatin: boves eorum crassæ. Non est ruina maceriæ, neque transitus, neque clamor in plateis eorum.

verses.text: They have called the people happy, that hath these things: but happy is that people whose God is the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Beatum dixerunt populum cui hæc sunt; beatus populus cujus Dominus Deus ejus.

verses.text: I  will extol thee, O God my king: and I will bless thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Exaltabo te, Deus meus rex, et benedicam nomini tuo in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: Every day will I bless thee: and I will praise thy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Per singulos dies benedicam tibi, et laudabo nomen tuum in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised: and of his greatness there is no end.
verses.textLatin: Magnus Dominus, et laudabilis nimis, et magnitudinis ejus non est finis.

verses.text: Generation and generation shall praise thy works: and they shall declare thy power.
verses.textLatin: Generatio et generatio laudabit opera tua, et potentiam tuam pronuntiabunt.

verses.text: They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of thy holiness: and shall tell thy wondrous works.
verses.textLatin: Magnificentiam gloriæ sanctitatis tuæ loquentur, et mirabilia tua narrabunt.

verses.text: And they shall speak of the might of thy terrible acts: and shall declare thy greatness.
verses.textLatin: Et virtutem terribilium tuorum dicent, et magnitudinem tuam narrabunt.

verses.text: They shall publish the memory of the abundance of thy sweetness: and shall rejoice in thy justice.
verses.textLatin: Memoriam abundantiæ suavitatis tuæ eructabunt, et justitia tua exsultabunt.

verses.text: The Lord is gracious and merciful: patient and plenteous in mercy.
verses.textLatin: Miserator et misericors Dominus: patiens, et multum misericors.

verses.text: The Lord is sweet to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.
verses.textLatin: Suavis Dominus universis, et miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus.

verses.text: Let all thy works, O lord, praise thee: and let thy saints bless thee.
verses.textLatin: Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua, et sancti tui benedicant tibi.

verses.text: They shall speak of the glory of thy kingdom: and shall tell of thy power:
verses.textLatin: Gloriam regni tui dicent, et potentiam tuam loquentur:

verses.text: To make thy might known to the sons of men: and the glory of the magnificence of thy kingdom.
verses.textLatin: ut notam faciant filiis hominum potentiam tuam, et gloriam magnificentiæ regni tui.

verses.text: Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages: and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations. The Lord is faithful in all his words: and holy in all his works.
verses.textLatin: Regnum tuum regnum omnium sæculorum; et dominatio tua in omni generatione et generationem. Fidelis Dominus in omnibus verbis suis, et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis.

verses.text: The Lord lifteth up all that fall: and setteth up all that are cast down.
verses.textLatin: Allevat Dominus omnes qui corruunt, et erigit omnes elisos.

verses.text: The eyes of all hope in thee, O Lord: and thou givest them meat in due season.
verses.textLatin: Oculi omnium in te sperant, Domine, et tu das escam illorum in tempore opportuno.

verses.text: Thou openest thy hand, and fillest with blessing every living creature.
verses.textLatin: Aperis tu manum tuam, et imples omne animal benedictione.

verses.text: The Lord is just in all his ways: and holy in all his works.
verses.textLatin: Justus Dominus in omnibus viis suis, et sanctus in omnibus operibus suis.

verses.text: The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him: to all that call upon him in truth.
verses.textLatin: Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate.

verses.text: He will do the will of them that fear him: and he will hear their prayer, and save them.
verses.textLatin: Voluntatem timentium se faciet, et deprecationem eorum exaudiet, et salvos faciet eos.

verses.text: The Lord keepeth all them that love him; but all the wicked he will destroy.
verses.textLatin: Custodit Dominus omnes diligentes se, et omnes peccatores disperdet.

verses.text: My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name for ever; yea, for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Laudationem Domini loquetur os meum; et benedicat omnis caro nomini sancto ejus in sæculum, et in sæculum sæculi.

verses.text: Alleluia, of Aggeus and Zacharias.
verses.textLatin: Alleluja, Aggæi et Zachariæ.

verses.text: Praise the Lord, O my soul, in my life I will praise the Lord: I will sing to my God as long as I shall be. Put not your trust in princes:
verses.textLatin: Lauda, anima mea, Dominum. Laudabo Dominum in vita mea; psallam Deo meo quamdiu fuero. Nolite confidere in principibus,

verses.text: in the children of men, in whom there is no salvation.
verses.textLatin: in filiis hominum, in quibus non est salus.

verses.text: His spirit shall go forth, and he shall return into his earth: in that day all their thoughts shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Exibit spiritus ejus, et revertetur in terram suam; in illa die peribunt omnes cogitationes eorum.

verses.text: Blessed is he who hath the God of Jacob for his helper, whose hope is in the Lord his God:
verses.textLatin: Beatus cujus Deus Jacob adjutor ejus, spes ejus in Domino Deo ipsius:

verses.text: who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all things that are in them.
verses.textLatin: qui fecit cælum et terram, mare, et omnia quæ in eis sunt.

verses.text: Who keepeth truth for ever: who executeth judgment for them that suffer wrong: who giveth food to the hungry. The Lord looseth them that are fettered:
verses.textLatin: Qui custodit veritatem in sæculum; facit judicium injuriam patientibus; dat escam esurientibus. Dominus solvit compeditos;

verses.text: the Lord enlighteneth the blind. The Lord lifteth up them that are cast down: the Lord loveth the just.
verses.textLatin: Dominus illuminat cæcos. Dominus erigit elisos; Dominus diligit justos.

verses.text: The Lord keepeth the strangers, he will support the fatherless and the widow: and the ways of sinners he will destroy.
verses.textLatin: Dominus custodit advenas, pupillum et viduam suscipiet, et vias peccatorum disperdet.

verses.text: The Lord shall reign for ever: thy God, O Sion, unto generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Regnabit Dominus in sæcula; Deus tuus, Sion, in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: Praise  ye the Lord, because psalm is good: to our God be joyful and comely praise.
verses.textLatin: Laudate Dominum, quoniam bonus est psalmus; Deo nostro sit jucunda, decoraque laudatio.

verses.text: The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem: he will gather together the dispersed of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Ædificans Jerusalem Dominus, dispersiones Israëlis congregabit:

verses.text: Who healeth the broken of heart, and bindeth up their bruises.
verses.textLatin: qui sanat contritos corde, et alligat contritiones eorum;

verses.text: Who telleth the number of the stars: and calleth them all by their names.
verses.textLatin: qui numerat multitudinem stellarum, et omnibus eis nomina vocat.

verses.text: Great is our Lord, and great is his power: and of his wisdom there is no number.
verses.textLatin: Magnus Dominus noster, et magna virtus ejus, et sapientiæ ejus non est numerus.

verses.text: The Lord lifteth up the meek, and bringeth the wicked down even to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Suscipiens mansuetos Dominus; humilians autem peccatores usque ad terram.

verses.text: Sing ye to the Lord with praise: sing to our God upon the harp.
verses.textLatin: Præcinite Domino in confessione; psallite Deo nostro in cithara.

verses.text: Who covereth the heaven with clouds, and prepareth rain for the earth. Who maketh grass to grow on the mountains, and herbs for the service of men.
verses.textLatin: Qui operit cælum nubibus, et parat terræ pluviam; qui producit in montibus fœnum, et herbam servituti hominum;

verses.text: Who giveth to beasts their food: and to the young ravens that call upon him.
verses.textLatin: qui dat jumentis escam ipsorum, et pullis corvorum invocantibus eum.

verses.text: He shall not delight in the strength of the horse: nor take pleasure in the legs of a man.
verses.textLatin: Non in fortitudine equi voluntatem habebit, nec in tibiis viri beneplacitum erit ei.

verses.text: The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him: and in them that hope in his mercy.
verses.textLatin: Beneplacitum est Domino super timentes eum, et in eis qui sperant super misericordia ejus.

verses.text: Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem: praise thy God, O Sion.
verses.textLatin: Lauda, Jerusalem, Dominum; lauda Deum tuum, Sion.

verses.text: Because he hath strengthened the bolts of thy gates, he hath blessed thy children within thee.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam confortavit seras portarum tuarum; benedixit filiis tuis in te.

verses.text: Who hath placed peace in thy borders: and filleth thee with the fat of corn.
verses.textLatin: Qui posuit fines tuos pacem, et adipe frumenti satiat te.

verses.text: Who sendeth forth his speech to the earth: his word runneth swiftly.
verses.textLatin: Qui emittit eloquium suum terræ: velociter currit sermo ejus.

verses.text: Who giveth snow like wool: scattereth mists like ashes.
verses.textLatin: Qui dat nivem sicut lanam; nebulam sicut cinerem spargit.

verses.text: He sendeth his crystal like morsels: who shall stand before the face of his cold?
verses.textLatin: Mittit crystallum suam sicut buccellas: ante faciem frigoris ejus quis sustinebit?

verses.text: He shall send out his word, and shall melt them: his wind shall blow, and the waters shall run.
verses.textLatin: Emittet verbum suum, et liquefaciet ea; flabit spiritus ejus, et fluent aquæ.

verses.text: Who declareth his word to Jacob: his justices and his judgments to Israel.
verses.textLatin: Qui annuntiat verbum suum Jacob, justitias et judicia sua Israël.

verses.text: He hath not done in like manner to every nation: and his judgments he hath not made manifest to them. Alleluia.
verses.textLatin: Non fecit taliter omni nationi, et judicia sua non manifestavit eis. Alleluja.

verses.text: Praise  ye the Lord from the heavens: praise ye him in the high places.
verses.textLatin: Laudate Dominum de cælis; laudate eum in excelsis.

verses.text: Praise ye him, all his angels, praise ye him, all his hosts.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum, omnes angeli ejus; laudate eum, omnes virtutes ejus.

verses.text: Praise ye him, O sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars and light.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum, sol et luna; laudate eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

verses.text: Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: and let all the waters that are above the heavens
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum, cæli cælorum; et aquæ omnes quæ super cælos sunt,

verses.text: praise the name of the Lord. For he spoke, and they were made: he commanded, and they were created.
verses.textLatin: laudent nomen Domini. Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt; ipse mandavit, et creata sunt.

verses.text: He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.
verses.textLatin: Statuit ea in æternum, et in sæculum sæculi; præceptum posuit, et non præteribit.

verses.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, ye dragons, and all ye deeps:
verses.textLatin: Laudate Dominum de terra, dracones et omnes abyssi;

verses.text: Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds, which fulfil his word:
verses.textLatin: ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, quæ faciunt verbum ejus;

verses.text: Mountains and all hills, fruitful trees and all cedars:
verses.textLatin: montes, et omnes colles; ligna fructifera, et omnes cedri;

verses.text: Beasts and all cattle: serpents and feathered fowls:
verses.textLatin: bestiæ, et universa pecora; serpentes, et volucres pennatæ;

verses.text: Kings of the earth and all people: princes and all judges of the earth:
verses.textLatin: reges terræ et omnes populi; principes et omnes judices terræ;

verses.text: Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord:
verses.textLatin: juvenes et virgines; senes cum junioribus, laudent nomen Domini:

verses.text: for his name alone is exalted.
verses.textLatin: quia exaltatum est nomen ejus solius.

verses.text: The praise of him is above heaven and earth: and he hath exalted the horn of his people. A hymn to all his saints to the children of Israel, a people approaching to him. Alleluia.
verses.textLatin: Confessio ejus super cælum et terram; et exaltavit cornu populi sui. Hymnus omnibus sanctis ejus; filiis Israël, populo appropinquanti sibi. Alleluja.

verses.text: Sing  ye to the Lord a new canticle: let his praise be in the church of the saints.
verses.textLatin: Cantate Domino canticum novum; laus ejus in ecclesia sanctorum.

verses.text: Let Israel rejoice in him that made him: and let the children of Sion be joyful in their king.
verses.textLatin: Lætetur Israël in eo qui fecit eum, et filii Sion exsultent in rege suo.

verses.text: Let them praise his name in choir: let them sing to him with the timbrel and the psaltery.
verses.textLatin: Laudent nomen ejus in choro; in tympano et psalterio psallant ei.

verses.text: For the Lord is well pleased with his people: and he will exalt the meek unto salvation.
verses.textLatin: Quia beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo, et exaltabit mansuetos in salutem.

verses.text: The saints shall rejoice in glory: they shall be joyful in their beds.
verses.textLatin: Exsultabunt sancti in gloria; lætabuntur in cubilibus suis.

verses.text: The high praises of God shall be in their mouth: and two-edged swords in their hands:
verses.textLatin: Exaltationes Dei in gutture eorum, et gladii ancipites in manibus eorum:

verses.text: To execute vengeance upon the nations, chastisements among the people:
verses.textLatin: ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus, increpationes in populis;

verses.text: To bind their kings with fetters, and their nobles with manacles of iron.
verses.textLatin: ad alligandos reges eorum in compedibus, et nobiles eorum in manicis ferreis;

verses.text: To execute upon them the judgment that is written: this glory is to all his saints. Alleluia.
verses.textLatin: ut faciant in eis judicium conscriptum: gloria hæc est omnibus sanctis ejus. Alleluja.

verses.text: Praise  ye the Lord in his holy places: praise ye him in the firmament of his power.
verses.textLatin: Laudate Dominum in sanctis ejus; laudate eum in firmamento virtutis ejus.

verses.text: Praise ye him for his mighty acts: praise ye him according to the multitude of his greatness.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum in virtutibus ejus; laudate eum secundum multitudinem magnitudinis ejus.

verses.text: Praise him with the sound of trumpet: praise him with psaltery and harp.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum in sono tubæ; laudate eum in psalterio et cithara.

verses.text: Praise him with timbrel and choir: praise him with strings and organs.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum in tympano et choro; laudate eum in chordis et organo.

verses.text: Praise him on high sounding cymbals: praise him on cymbals of joy: let every spirit praise the Lord. Alleluia.
verses.textLatin: Laudate eum in cymbalis benesonantibus; laudate eum in cymbalis jubilationis.
Omnis spiritus laudet Dominum! Alleluja.

verses.text: The  parables of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel,
verses.textLatin: Parabolæ Salomonis, filii David, regis Israël,

verses.text: To know wisdom, and instruction:
verses.textLatin: ad sciendam sapientiam et disciplinam;

verses.text: To understand the words of prudence: and to receive the instruction of doctrine, justice, and judgment, and equity:
verses.textLatin: ad intelligenda verba prudentiæ, et suscipiendam eruditionem doctrinæ, justitiam, et judicium, et æquitatem:

verses.text: To give subtilty to little ones, to the young man knowledge and understanding.
verses.textLatin: ut detur parvulis astutia, adolescenti scientia et intellectus.

verses.text: A wise man shall hear, and shall be wiser: and he that understandeth, shall possess governments.
verses.textLatin: Audiens sapiens, sapientior erit, et intelligens gubernacula possidebit.

verses.text: He shall understand a parable, and the interpretation, the words of the wise, and their mysterious sayings.
verses.textLatin: Animadvertet parabolam et interpretationem, verba sapientum et ænigmata eorum.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Fools despise wisdom and instruction.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini principium sapientiæ; sapientiam atque doctrinam stulti despiciunt.

verses.text: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:
verses.textLatin: Audi, fili mi, disciplinam patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ:

verses.text: That grace may be added to thy head, and a chain of gold to thy neck.
verses.textLatin: ut addatur gratia capiti tuo, et torques collo tuo.

verses.text: My son, if sinners shall entice thee, consent not to them.
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, si te lactaverint peccatores, ne acquiescas eis.

verses.text: If they shall say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares for the innocent without cause:
verses.textLatin: Si dixerint: Veni nobiscum, insidiemur sanguini; abscondamus tendiculas contra insontem frustra;

verses.text: Let us swallow him up alive like hell, and whole as one that goeth down into the pit.
verses.textLatin: deglutiamus eum sicut infernus viventem, et integrum quasi descendentem in lacum;

verses.text: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoils.
verses.textLatin: omnem pretiosam substantiam reperiemus; implebimus domos nostras spoliis:

verses.text: Cast in thy lot with us, let us all have one purse.
verses.textLatin: sortem mitte nobiscum, marsupium unum sit omnium nostrum:

verses.text: My son, walk not thou with them, restrain thy foot from their paths.
verses.textLatin: fili mi, ne ambules cum eis; prohibe pedem tuum a semitis eorum:

verses.text: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.
verses.textLatin: pedes enim illorum ad malum currunt, et festinant ut effundant sanguinem.

verses.text: But a net is spread in vain before the eyes of them that have wings.
verses.textLatin: Frustra autem jacitur rete ante oculos pennatorum.

verses.text: And they themselves lie in wait for their own blood, and practise deceits against their own souls.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi quoque contra sanguinem suum insidiantur, et moliuntur fraudes contra animas suas.

verses.text: So the ways of every covetous man destroy the souls of the possessors.
verses.textLatin: Sic semitæ omnis avari: animas possidentium rapiunt.

verses.text: Wisdom preacheth abroad, she uttereth her voice in the streets:
verses.textLatin: Sapientia foris prædicat; in plateis dat vocem suam:

verses.text: At the head of multitudes she crieth out, in the entrance of the gates of the city she uttereth her words, saying:
verses.textLatin: in capite turbarum clamitat; in foribus portarum urbis profert verba sua, dicens:

verses.text: O children, how long will you love childishness, and fools covet those things which are hurtful to themselves, and the unwise hate knowledge?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, parvuli, diligitis infantiam, et stulti ea quæ sibi sunt noxia cupient, et imprudentes odibunt scientiam?

verses.text: Turn ye at my reproof: behold I will utter my spirit to you, and will shew you my words.
verses.textLatin: convertimini ad correptionem meam. En proferam vobis spiritum meum, et ostendam vobis verba mea.

verses.text: Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded.
verses.textLatin: Quia vocavi, et renuistis; extendi manum meam, et non fuit qui aspiceret:

verses.text: You have despised all my counsel, and have neglected my reprehensions.
verses.textLatin: despexistis omne consilium meum, et increpationes meas neglexistis.

verses.text: I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared.
verses.textLatin: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo cum vobis id quod timebatis advenerit.

verses.text: When sudden calamity shall fall on you, and destruction, as a tempest, shall be at hand: when tribulation and distress shall come upon you:
verses.textLatin: Cum irruerit repentina calamitas, et interitus quasi tempestas ingruerit; quando venerit super vos tribulatio et angustia:

verses.text: Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning and shall not find me:
verses.textLatin: tunc invocabunt me, et non exaudiam; mane consurgent, et non invenient me:

verses.text: Because they have hated instruction, and received not the fear of the Lord,
verses.textLatin: eo quod exosam habuerint disciplinam, et timorem Domini non susceperint,

verses.text: Nor consented to my counsel, but despised all my reproof.
verses.textLatin: nec acquieverint consilio meo, et detraxerint universæ correptioni meæ.

verses.text: Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way, and shall be filled with their own devices.
verses.textLatin: Comedent igitur fructus viæ suæ, suisque consiliis saturabuntur.

verses.text: The turning away of little ones shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Aversio parvulorum interficiet eos, et prosperitas stultorum perdet illos.

verses.text: But he that shall hear me, shall rest without terror, and shall enjoy abundance, without fear of evils.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem me audierit, absque terrore requiescet, et abundantia perfruetur, timore malorum sublato.

verses.text: My  son, if thou wilt receive my words, and wilt hide my commandments with thee,
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, si susceperis sermones meos, et mandata mea absconderis penes te:

verses.text: That thy ear may hearken to wisdom: incline thy heart to know prudence:
verses.textLatin: ut audiat sapientiam auris tua, inclina cor tuum ad cognoscendam prudentiam.

verses.text: For if thou shalt call for wisdom, and incline thy heart to prudence:
verses.textLatin: Si enim sapientiam invocaveris, et inclinaveris cor tuum prudentiæ;

verses.text: If thou shalt seek her as money, and shalt dig for her as for a treasure:
verses.textLatin: si quæsieris eam quasi pecuniam, et sicut thesauros effoderis illam:

verses.text: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and shalt find the knowledge of God.
verses.textLatin: tunc intelliges timorem Domini, et scientiam Dei invenies,

verses.text: Because the Lord giveth wisdom: and out of his mouth cometh prudence and knowledge.
verses.textLatin: quia Dominus dat sapientiam, et ex ore ejus prudentia et scientia.

verses.text: He will keep the salvation of the righteous, and protect them that walk in simplicity.
verses.textLatin: Custodiet rectorum salutem, et proteget gradientes simpliciter,

verses.text: Keeping the paths of justice, and guarding the ways of saints.
verses.textLatin: servans semitas justitiæ, et vias sanctorum custodiens.

verses.text: Then shalt thou understand justice, and judgment, and equity, and every good path.
verses.textLatin: Tunc intelliges justitiam, et judicium, et æquitatem, et omnem semitam bonam.

verses.text: If wisdom shall enter into thy heart, and knowledge please thy soul:
verses.textLatin: Si intraverit sapientia cor tuum, et scientia animæ tuæ placuerit,

verses.text: Counsel shall keep thee, and prudence shall preserve thee,
verses.textLatin: consilium custodiet te, et prudentia servabit te:

verses.text: That thou mayst be delivered from the evil way, and from the man that speaketh perverse things:
verses.textLatin: ut eruaris a via mala, et ab homine qui perversa loquitur;

verses.text: Who leave the right way, and walk by dark ways:
verses.textLatin: qui relinquunt iter rectum, et ambulant per vias tenebrosas;

verses.text: Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in most wicked things:
verses.textLatin: qui lætantur cum malefecerint, et exsultant in rebus pessimis;

verses.text: Whose ways are perverse, and their steps infamous.
verses.textLatin: quorum viæ perversæ sunt, et infames gressus eorum.

verses.text: That thou mayst be delivered from the strange women, and from the stranger, who softeneth her words:
verses.textLatin: Ut eruaris a muliere aliena, et ab extranea quæ mollit sermones suos,

verses.text: And forsaketh the guide of her youth,
verses.textLatin: et relinquit ducem pubertatis suæ,

verses.text: And hath forgotten the covenant of her God: for her house inclineth unto death, and her paths to hell.
verses.textLatin: et pacti Dei sui oblita est. Inclinata est enim ad mortem domus ejus, et ad inferos semitæ ipsius.

verses.text: None that go in unto her shall return again, neither shall they take hold of the paths of life,
verses.textLatin: Omnes qui ingrediuntur ad eam non revertentur, nec apprehendent semitas vitæ.

verses.text: That thou mayst walk in a good way: and mayst keep the paths of the just.
verses.textLatin: Ut ambules in via bona, et calles justorum custodias:

verses.text: For they that are upright shall dwell in the earth, and the simple shall continue in it.
verses.textLatin: qui enim recti sunt habitabunt in terra, et simplices permanebunt in ea;

verses.text: But the wicked shall be destroyed from the earth: and they that do unjustly shall be taken away from it.
verses.textLatin: impii vero de terra perdentur, et qui inique agunt auferentur ex ea.

verses.text: My  son, forget not my law, and let thy heart keep my commandments.
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, ne obliviscaris legis meæ, et præcepta mea cor tuum custodiat:

verses.text: For they shall add to thee length of days, and years of life and peace.
verses.textLatin: longitudinem enim dierum, et annos vitæ, et pacem, apponent tibi.

verses.text: Let not mercy and truth leave thee, put them about thy neck, and write them in the tables of thy heart:
verses.textLatin: Misericordia et veritas te non deserant; circumda eas gutturi tuo, et describe in tabulis cordis tui:

verses.text: And thou shalt find grace and good understanding before God and men.
verses.textLatin: et invenies gratiam, et disciplinam bonam, coram Deo et hominibus.

verses.text: Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence.
verses.textLatin: Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo, et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ.

verses.text: In all thy ways think on him, and he will direct thy steps.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus viis tuis cogita illum, et ipse diriget gressus tuos.

verses.text: Be not wise in thy own conceit: fear God, and depart from evil:
verses.textLatin: Ne sis sapiens apud temetipsum; time Deum, et recede a malo:

verses.text: For it shall be health to thy navel, and moistening to thy bones.
verses.textLatin: sanitas quippe erit umbilico tuo, et irrigatio ossium tuorum.

verses.text: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits:
verses.textLatin: Honora Dominum de tua substantia, et de primitiis omnium frugum tuarum da ei:

verses.text: And thy barns shall be filled with abundance, and thy presses shall run over with wine.
verses.textLatin: et implebuntur horrea tua saturitate, et vino torcularia tua redundabunt.

verses.text: My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him:
verses.textLatin: Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, nec deficias cum ab eo corriperis:

verses.text: For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself.
verses.textLatin: quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi.

verses.text: Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom and is rich in prudence:
verses.textLatin: Beatus homo qui invenit sapientiam, et qui affluit prudentia.

verses.text: The purchasing thereof is better than the merchandise of silver, and her fruit than the chiefest and purest gold:
verses.textLatin: Melior est acquisitio ejus negotiatione argenti, et auri primi et purissimi fructus ejus.

verses.text: She is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared with her.
verses.textLatin: Pretiosior est cunctis opibus, et omnia quæ desiderantur huic non valent comparari.

verses.text: Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory.
verses.textLatin: Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus, et in sinistra illius divitiæ et gloria.

verses.text: Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable.
verses.textLatin: Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ, et omnes semitæ illius pacificæ.

verses.text: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her: and he that shall retain her is blessed.
verses.textLatin: Lignum vitæ est his qui apprehenderint eam, et qui tenuerit eam beatus.

verses.text: The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence.
verses.textLatin: Dominus sapientia fundavit terram; stabilivit cælos prudentia.

verses.text: By his wisdom the depths have broken out, and the clouds grow thick with dew.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia illius eruperunt abyssi, et nubes rore concrescunt.

verses.text: My son, let not these things depart from thy eyes: keep the law and counsel:
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, ne effluant hæc ab oculis tuis. Custodi legem atque consilium,

verses.text: And there shall be life to thy soul, and grace to thy mouth.
verses.textLatin: et erit vita animæ tuæ, et gratia faucibus tuis.

verses.text: Then shalt thou walk confidently in thy way, and thy foot shall not stumble:
verses.textLatin: Tunc ambulabis fiducialiter in via tua, et pes tuus non impinget.

verses.text: If thou sleep, thou shalt not fear: thou shalt rest, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
verses.textLatin: Si dormieris, non timebis; quiesces, et suavis erit somnus tuus.

verses.text: Be not afraid of sudden fear, nor of the power of the wicked falling upon thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne paveas repentino terrore, et irruentes tibi potentias impiorum.

verses.text: For the Lord will be at thy side, and will keep thy foot that thou be not taken.
verses.textLatin: Dominus enim erit in latere tuo, et custodiet pedem tuum, ne capiaris.

verses.text: Do not withhold him from doing good, who is able: if thou art able, do good thyself also.
verses.textLatin: Noli prohibere benefacere eum qui potest: si vales, et ipse benefac.

verses.text: Say not to thy friend: Go, and come again: and to morrow I will give to thee: when thou canst give at present.
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas amico tuo: Vade, et revertere: cras dabo tibi: cum statim possis dare.

verses.text: Practise not evil against thy friend, when he hath confidence in thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne moliaris amico tuo malum, cum ille in te habeat fiduciam.

verses.text: Strive not against a man without cause, when he hath done thee no evil.
verses.textLatin: Ne contendas adversus hominem frustra, cum ipse tibi nihil mali fecerit.

verses.text: Envy not the unjust man, and do not follow his ways:
verses.textLatin: Ne æmuleris hominem injustum, nec imiteris vias ejus:

verses.text: For every mocker is an abomination to the Lord, and his communication is with the simple.
verses.textLatin: quia abominatio Domini est omnis illusor, et cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus.

verses.text: Want is from the Lord in the house of the wicked: but the habitations of the just shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Egestas a Domino in domo impii; habitacula autem justorum benedicentur.

verses.text: He shall scorn the scorners, and to the meek he will give grace.
verses.textLatin: Ipse deludet illusores, et mansuetis dabit gratiam.

verses.text: The wise shall possess glory: the promotion of fools is disgrace.
verses.textLatin: Gloriam sapientes possidebunt; stultorum exaltatio ignominia.

verses.text: Hear,  ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend that you may know prudence.
verses.textLatin: Audite, filii, disciplinam patris, et attendite ut sciatis prudentiam.

verses.text: I will give you a good gift, forsake not my law.
verses.textLatin: Donum bonum tribuam vobis: legem meam ne derelinquatis.

verses.text: For I also was my father’s son, tender and as an only son in the sight of my mother:
verses.textLatin: Nam et ego filius fui patris mei, tenellus et unigenitus coram matre mea.

verses.text: And he taught me, and said: Let thy heart receive my words, keep my commandments, and thou shalt live.
verses.textLatin: Et docebat me, atque dicebat: Suscipiat verba mea cor tuum; custodi præcepta mea, et vives.

verses.text: Get wisdom, get prudence: forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Posside sapientiam, posside prudentiam: ne obliviscaris, neque declines a verbis oris mei.

verses.text: Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee: love her, and she shall preserve thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne dimittas eam, et custodiet te: dilige eam, et conservabit te.

verses.text: The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all thy possession purchase prudence.
verses.textLatin: Principium sapientiæ: posside sapientiam, et in omni possessione tua acquire prudentiam.

verses.text: Take hold on her, and she shall exalt thee: thou shalt be glorified by her, when thou shalt embrace her.
verses.textLatin: Arripe illam, et exaltabit te; glorificaberis ab ea cum eam fueris amplexatus.

verses.text: She shall give to thy head increase of graces, and protect thee with a noble crown.
verses.textLatin: Dabit capiti tuo augmenta gratiarum, et corona inclyta proteget te.

verses.text: Hear, O my son, and receive my words, that years of life may be multiplied to thee.
verses.textLatin: Audi, fili mi, et suscipe verba mea, ut multiplicentur tibi anni vitæ.

verses.text: I will shew thee the way of wisdom, I will lead thee by the paths of equity:
verses.textLatin: Viam sapientiæ monstrabo tibi; ducam te per semitas æquitatis:

verses.text: Which when thou shalt have entered, thy steps shall not be straitened, and when thou runnest thou shalt not meet a stumblingblock.
verses.textLatin: quas cum ingressus fueris, non arctabuntur gressus tui, et currens non habebis offendiculum.

verses.text: Take hold on instruction, leave it not: keep it, because it is thy life.
verses.textLatin: Tene disciplinam, ne dimittas eam; custodi illam, quia ipsa est vita tua.

verses.text: Be not delighted in the paths of the wicked, neither let the way of evil men please thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne delecteris in semitis impiorum, nec tibi placeat malorum via.

verses.text: Flee from it, pass not by it: go aside, and forsake it.
verses.textLatin: Fuge ab ea, nec transeas per illam; declina, et desere eam.

verses.text: For they sleep not except they have done evil: and their sleep is taken away unless they have made some to fall.
verses.textLatin: Non enim dormiunt nisi malefecerint, et rapitur somnus ab eis nisi supplantaverint.

verses.text: They eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Comedunt panem impietatis, et vinum iniquitatis bibunt.

verses.text: But the path of the just, as a shining light, goeth forwards and increaseth even to perfect day.
verses.textLatin: Justorum autem semita quasi lux splendens procedit, et crescit usque ad perfectam diem.

verses.text: The way of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall.
verses.textLatin: Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruant.

verses.text: My son, hearken to my words, and incline thy ear to my sayings.
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, ausculta sermones meos, et ad eloquia mea inclina aurem tuam.

verses.text: Let them not depart from thy eyes, keep them in the midst of thy heart:
verses.textLatin: Ne recedant ab oculis tuis: custodi ea in medio cordis tui:

verses.text: For they are life to those that find them, and health to all flesh.
verses.textLatin: vita enim sunt invenientibus ea, et universæ carni sanitas.

verses.text: With all watchfulness keep thy heart, because life issueth out from it.
verses.textLatin: Omni custodia serva cor tuum, quia ex ipso vita procedit.

verses.text: Remove from thee a froward mouth, and let detracting lips be far from thee.
verses.textLatin: Remove a te os pravum, et detrahentia labia sint procul a te.

verses.text: Let thy eyes look straight on, and let thy eyelids go before thy steps.
verses.textLatin: Oculi tui recta videant, et palpebræ tuæ præcedant gressus tuos.

verses.text: Make straight the path for thy feet, and all thy ways shall be established.
verses.textLatin: Dirige semitam pedibus tuis, et omnes viæ tuæ stabilientur.

verses.text: Decline not to the right hand, nor to the left: turn away thy foot from evil. For the Lord knoweth the ways that are on the right hand: but those are perverse which are on the left hand. But he will make thy courses straight, he will bring forward thy ways in peace.
verses.textLatin: Ne declines ad dexteram neque ad sinistram; averte pedem tuum a malo: vias enim quæ a dextris sunt novit Dominus: perversæ vero sunt quæ a sinistris sunt. Ipse autem rectos faciet cursus tuos, itinera autem tua in pace producet.

verses.text: My  son, attend to my wisdom, and incline thy ear to my prudence.
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, attende ad sapientiam meam, et prudentiæ meæ inclina aurem tuam:

verses.text: That thou mayst keep thoughts, and thy lips may preserve instruction. Mind not the deceit of a woman.
verses.textLatin: ut custodias cogitationes, et disciplinam labia tua conservent. Ne attendas fallaciæ mulieris;

verses.text: For the lips of a harlot are like a honeycomb dropping, and her throat is smoother than oil.
verses.textLatin: favus enim distillans labia meretricis, et nitidius oleo guttur ejus:

verses.text: But her end is bitter as wormwood, and sharp as a two-edged sword.
verses.textLatin: novissima autem illius amara quasi absinthium, et acuta quasi gladius biceps.

verses.text: Her feet go down into death, and her steps go in as far as hell.
verses.textLatin: Pedes ejus descendunt in mortem, et ad inferos gressus illius penetrant.

verses.text: They walk not by the path of life, her steps are wandering, and unaccountable.
verses.textLatin: Per semitam vitæ non ambulant; vagi sunt gressus ejus et investigabiles.

verses.text: Now therefore, my son, hear me, and depart not from the words of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo fili mi, audi me, et ne recedas a verbis oris mei.

verses.text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the doors of her house.
verses.textLatin: Longe fac ab ea viam tuam, et ne appropinques foribus domus ejus.

verses.text: Give not thy honour to strangers, and thy years to the cruel.
verses.textLatin: Ne des alienis honorem tuum, et annos tuos crudeli:

verses.text: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, and thy labours be in another man’s house,
verses.textLatin: ne forte implentur extranei viribus tuis, et labores tui sint in domo aliena,

verses.text: And thou mourn at the last, when thou shalt have spent thy flesh and thy body, and say:
verses.textLatin: et gemas in novissimis, quando consumpseris carnes tuas et corpus tuum, et dicas:

verses.text: Why have I hated instruction, and my heart consented not to reproof,
verses.textLatin: Cur detestatus sum disciplinam, et increpationibus non acquievit cor meum,

verses.text: And have not heard the voice of them that taught me, and have not inclined my ear to masters?
verses.textLatin: nec audivi vocem docentium me, et magistris non inclinavi aurem meam?

verses.text: I have almost been in all evil, in the midst of the church and of the congregation.
verses.textLatin: pene fui in omni malo, in medio ecclesiæ et synagogæ.

verses.text: Drink water out of thy own cistern, and the streams of thy own well:
verses.textLatin: Bibe aquam de cisterna tua, et fluenta putei tui;

verses.text: Let thy fountains be conveyed abroad, and in the streets divide thy waters.
verses.textLatin: deriventur fontes tui foras, et in plateis aquas tuas divide.

verses.text: Keep them to thyself alone, neither let strangers be partakers with thee.
verses.textLatin: Habeto eas solus, nec sint alieni participes tui.

verses.text: Let thy vein be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of thy youth:
verses.textLatin: Sit vena tua benedicta, et lætare cum muliere adolescentiæ tuæ.

verses.text: Let her be thy dearest hind, and most agreeable fawn: let her breasts inebriate thee at all times; be thou delighted continually with her love.
verses.textLatin: Cerva carissima, et gratissimus hinnulus: ubera ejus inebrient te in omni tempore; in amore ejus delectare jugiter.

verses.text: Why art thou seduced, my son, by a strange woman, and art cherished in the bosom of another?
verses.textLatin: Quare seduceris, fili mi, ab aliena, et foveris in sinu alterius?

verses.text: The Lord beholdeth the ways of man, and considereth all his steps.
verses.textLatin: Respicit Dominus vias hominis, et omnes gressus ejus considerat.

verses.text: His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins.
verses.textLatin: Iniquitates suas capiunt impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur.

verses.text: He shall die, because he hath not received instruction, and in the multitude of his folly he shall be deceived.
verses.textLatin: Ipse morietur, quia non habuit disciplinam, et in multitudine stultitiæ suæ decipietur.

verses.text: My  son, if thou be surety for thy friend, thou hast engaged fast thy hand to a stranger.
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, si spoponderis pro amico tuo, defixisti apud extraneum manum tuam:

verses.text: Thou art ensnared with the words of thy mouth, and caught with thy own words.
verses.textLatin: illaqueatus es verbis oris tui, et captus propriis sermonibus.

verses.text: Do therefore, my son, what I say, and deliver thyself: because thou art fallen into the hand of thy neighbour. Run about, make haste, stir up thy friend:
verses.textLatin: Fac ergo quod dico, fili mi, et temetipsum libera, quia incidisti in manum proximi tui. Discurre, festina, suscita amicum tuum.

verses.text: Give not sleep to thy eyes, neither let thy eyelids slumber.
verses.textLatin: Ne dederis somnum oculis tuis, nec dormitent palpebræ tuæ.

verses.text: Deliver thyself as a doe from the hand, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
verses.textLatin: Eruere quasi damula de manu, et quasi avis de manu aucupis.

verses.text: Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider her ways, and learn wisdom:
verses.textLatin: Vade ad formicam, o piger, et considera vias ejus, et disce sapientiam.

verses.text: Which, although she hath no guide, nor master, nor captain,
verses.textLatin: Quæ cum non habeat ducem, nec præceptorem, nec principem,

verses.text: Provideth her meat for herself in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
verses.textLatin: parat in æstate cibum sibi, et congregat in messe quod comedat.

verses.text: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou rise out of thy sleep?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, piger, dormies? quando consurges e somno tuo?

verses.text: Thou wilt sleep a little, thou wilt slumber a little, thou wilt fold thy hands a little to sleep:
verses.textLatin: Paululum dormies, paululum dormitabis, paululum conseres manus ut dormias;

verses.text: And want shall come upon thee, as a traveller, and poverty as a man armed. But if thou be diligent, thy harvest shall come as a fountain, and want shall flee far from thee.
verses.textLatin: et veniet tibi quasi viator egestas, et pauperies quasi vir armatus. Si vero impiger fueris, veniet ut fons messis tua, et egestas longe fugiet a te.

verses.text: A man that is an apostate, an unprofitable man, walketh with a perverse mouth,
verses.textLatin: Homo apostata, vir inutilis, graditur ore perverso;

verses.text: He winketh with the eyes, presseth with the foot, speaketh with the finger.
verses.textLatin: annuit oculis, terit pede, digito loquitur,

verses.text: With a wicked heart he deviseth evil, and at all times he soweth discord.
verses.textLatin: pravo corde machinatur malum, et omni tempore jurgia seminat.

verses.text: To such a one his destruction shall presently come, and he shall suddenly be destroyed, and shall no longer have any remedy.
verses.textLatin: Huic extemplo veniet perditio sua, et subito conteretur, nec habebit ultra medicinam.

verses.text: Six things there are, which the Lord hateth, and the seventh his soul detesteth:
verses.textLatin: Sex sunt quæ odit Dominus, et septimum detestatur anima ejus:

verses.text: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
verses.textLatin: oculos sublimes, linguam mendacem, manus effundentes innoxium sanguinem,

verses.text: A heart that deviseth wicked plots, feet that are swift to run into mischief,
verses.textLatin: cor machinans cogitationes pessimas, pedes veloces ad currendum in malum,

verses.text: A deceitful witness that uttereth lies, and him that soweth discord among brethren.
verses.textLatin: proferentem mendacia testem fallacem, et eum qui seminat inter fratres discordias.

verses.text: My son, keep the commandments of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.
verses.textLatin: Conserva, fili mi, præcepta patris tui, et ne dimittas legem matris tuæ.

verses.text: Bind them in thy heart continually, and put them about thy neck.
verses.textLatin: Liga ea in corde tuo jugiter, et circumda gutturi tuo.

verses.text: When thou walkest, let them go with thee: when thou sleepest, let them keep thee; and when thou awakest, talk with them.
verses.textLatin: Cum ambulaveris, gradiantur tecum; cum dormieris, custodiant te: et evigilans loquere cum eis.

verses.text: Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:
verses.textLatin: Quia mandatum lucerna est, et lex lux, et via vitæ increpatio disciplinæ:

verses.text: That they may keep thee from the evil woman, and from the flattering tongue of the stranger.
verses.textLatin: ut custodiant te a muliere mala, et a blanda lingua extraneæ.

verses.text: Let not thy heart covet her beauty, be not caught with her winks:
verses.textLatin: Non concupiscat pulchritudinem ejus cor tuum, nec capiaris nutibus illius:

verses.text: For the price of a harlot is scarce one loaf: but the woman catcheth the precious soul of a man.
verses.textLatin: pretium enim scorti vix est unius panis, mulier autem viri pretiosam animam capit.

verses.text: Can a man hide fire in his bosom, and his garments not burn?
verses.textLatin: Numquid potest homo abscondere ignem in sinu suo, ut vestimenta illius non ardeant?

verses.text: Or can he walk upon hot coals, and his feet not be burnt?
verses.textLatin: aut ambulare super prunas, ut non comburantur plantæ ejus?

verses.text: So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife, shall not be clean when he shall touch her.
verses.textLatin: sic qui ingreditur ad mulierem proximi sui, non erit mundus cum tetigerit eam.

verses.text: The fault is not so great when a man hath stolen: for he stealeth to fill his hungry soul:
verses.textLatin: Non grandis est culpa cum quis furatus fuerit: furatur enim ut esurientem impleat animam;

verses.text: And if he be taken he shall restore sevenfold, and shall give up all the substance of his house.
verses.textLatin: deprehensus quoque reddet septuplum, et omnem substantiam domus suæ tradet.

verses.text: But he that is an adulterer, for the folly of his heart shall destroy his own soul:
verses.textLatin: Qui autem adulter est, propter cordis inopiam perdet animam suam;

verses.text: He gathereth to himself shame and dishonour, and his reproach shall not be blotted out:
verses.textLatin: turpitudinem et ignominiam congregat sibi, et opprobrium illius non delebitur:

verses.text: Because the jealousy and rage of the husband will not spare in the day of revenge,
verses.textLatin: quia zelus et furor viri non parcet in die vindictæ,

verses.text: Nor will he yield to any man’s prayers, nor will he accept for satisfaction ever so many gifts.
verses.textLatin: nec acquiescet cujusquam precibus, nec suscipiet pro redemptione dona plurima.

verses.text: My  son, keep my words, and lay up my precepts with thee. Son,
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, custodi sermones meos, et præcepta mea reconde tibi. Fili,

verses.text: Keep my commandments, and thou shalt live: and my law as the apple of thy eye:
verses.textLatin: serva mandata mea, et vives; et legem meam quasi pupillam oculi tui:

verses.text: Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart.
verses.textLatin: liga eam in digitis tuis, scribe illam in tabulis cordis tui.

verses.text: Say to wisdom: Thou art my sister: and call prudence thy friend,
verses.textLatin: Dic sapientiæ: Soror mea es, et prudentiam voca amicam tuam:

verses.text: That she may keep thee from the woman that is not thine, and from the stranger who sweeteneth her words.
verses.textLatin: ut custodiant te a muliere extranea, et ab aliena quæ verba sua dulcia facit.

verses.text: For I look out of the window of my house through the lattice,
verses.textLatin: De fenestra enim domus meæ per cancellos prospexi,

verses.text: And I see little ones, I behold a foolish young man,
verses.textLatin: et video parvulos; considero vecordem juvenem,

verses.text: Who passeth through the street by the corner, and goeth nigh the way of her house.
verses.textLatin: qui transit per plateam juxta angulum et prope viam domus illius graditur:

verses.text: In the dark, when it grows late, in the darkness and obscurity of the night,
verses.textLatin: in obscuro, advesperascente die, in noctis tenebris et caligine.

verses.text: And behold a woman meeteth him in harlot’s attire prepared to deceive souls; talkative and wandering,
verses.textLatin: Et ecce occurrit illi mulier ornatu meretricio, præparata ad capiendas animas: garrula et vaga,

verses.text: Not bearing to be quiet, not able to abide still at home,
verses.textLatin: quietis impatiens, nec valens in domo consistere pedibus suis;

verses.text: Now abroad, now in the streets, now lying in wait near the corners.
verses.textLatin: nunc foris, nunc in plateis, nunc juxta angulos insidians.

verses.text: And catching the young man, she kisseth him, and with an impudent face, flattereth, saying:
verses.textLatin: Apprehensumque deosculatur juvenem, et procaci vultu blanditur, dicens:

verses.text: I vowed victims for prosperity, this day I have paid my vows.
verses.textLatin: Victimas pro salute vovi; hodie reddidi vota mea:

verses.text: Therefore I am come out to meet thee, desirous to see thee, and I have found thee.
verses.textLatin: idcirco egressa sum in occursum tuum, desiderans te videre, et reperi.

verses.text: I have woven my bed with cords, I have covered it with painted tapestry, brought from Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Intexui funibus lectulum meum; stravi tapetibus pictis ex Ægypto:

verses.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
verses.textLatin: aspersi cubile meum myrrha, et aloë, et cinnamomo.

verses.text: Come, let us be inebriated with the breasts, and let us enjoy the desired embraces, till the day appear.
verses.textLatin: Veni, inebriemur uberibus, et fruamur cupitis amplexibus donec illucescat dies.

verses.text: For my husband is not at home, he is gone a very long journey.
verses.textLatin: Non est enim vir in domo sua: abiit via longissima:

verses.text: He took with him a bag of money: he will return home the day of the full moon.
verses.textLatin: sacculum pecuniæ secum tulit; in die plenæ lunæ reversurus est in domum suam.

verses.text: She entangled him with many words, and drew him away with the flattery of her lips.
verses.textLatin: Irretivit eum multis sermonibus, et blanditiis labiorum protraxit illum.

verses.text: Immediately he followeth her as an ox led to be a victim, and as a lamb playing the wanton, and not knowing that he is drawn like a fool to bonds,
verses.textLatin: Statim eam sequitur quasi bos ductus ad victimam, et quasi agnus lasciviens, et ignorans quod ad vincula stultus trahatur:

verses.text: Till the arrow pierce his liver: as if a bird should make haste to the snare, and knoweth not that his life is in danger.
verses.textLatin: donec transfigat sagitta jecur ejus, velut si avis festinet ad laqueum, et nescit quod de periculo animæ illius agitur.

verses.text: Now therefore, my son, hear me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, fili mi, audi me, et attende verbis oris mei.

verses.text: Let not thy mind be drawn away in her ways: neither be thou deceived with her paths.
verses.textLatin: Ne abstrahatur in viis illius mens tua, neque decipiaris semitis ejus;

verses.text: For she hath cast down many wounded, and the strongest have been slain by her.
verses.textLatin: multos enim vulneratos dejecit, et fortissimi quique interfecti sunt ab ea.

verses.text: Her house is the way to hell, reaching even to the inner chambers of death.
verses.textLatin: Viæ inferi domus ejus, penetrantes in interiora mortis.

verses.text: Doth  not wisdom cry aloud, and prudence put forth her voice?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non sapientia clamitat, et prudentia dat vocem suam?

verses.text: Standing in the top of the highest places by the way, in the midst of the paths,
verses.textLatin: In summis excelsisque verticibus supra viam, in mediis semitis stans,

verses.text: Beside the gates of the city, in the very doors she speaketh, saying:
verses.textLatin: juxta portas civitatis, in ipsis foribus loquitur, dicens:

verses.text: O ye men, to you I call, and my voice is to the sons of men.
verses.textLatin: O viri, ad vos clamito, et vox mea ad filios hominum.

verses.text: O little ones, understand subtilty, and ye unwise, take notice.
verses.textLatin: Intelligite, parvuli, astutiam, et insipientes, animadvertite.

verses.text: Hear, for I will speak of great things: and my lips shall be opened to preach right things.
verses.textLatin: Audite, quoniam de rebus magnis locutura sum, et aperientur labia mea ut recta prædicent.

verses.text: My mouth shall meditate truth, and my lips shall hate wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Veritatem meditabitur guttur meum, et labia mea detestabuntur impium.

verses.text: All my words are just, there is nothing wicked nor perverse in them.
verses.textLatin: Justi sunt omnes sermones mei: non est in eis pravum quid, neque perversum;

verses.text: They are right to them that understand, and just to them that find knowledge.
verses.textLatin: recti sunt intelligentibus, et æqui invenientibus scientiam.

verses.text: Receive my instruction, and not money: choose knowledge rather than gold.
verses.textLatin: Accipite disciplinam meam, et non pecuniam; doctrinam magis quam aurum eligite:

verses.text: For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and whatsoever may be desired cannot be compared to it.
verses.textLatin: melior est enim sapientia cunctis pretiosissimis, et omne desiderabile ei non potest comparari.

verses.text: I wisdom dwell in counsel, and am present in learned thoughts.
verses.textLatin: Ego sapientia, habito in consilio, et eruditis intersum cogitationibus.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord hateth evil: I hate arrogance, and pride, and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini odit malum: arrogantiam, et superbiam, et viam pravam, et os bilingue, detestor.

verses.text: Counsel and equity is mine, prudence is mine, strength is mine.
verses.textLatin: Meum est consilium et æquitas; mea est prudentia, mea est fortitudo.

verses.text: By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things,
verses.textLatin: Per me reges regnant, et legum conditores justa decernunt;

verses.text: By me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice.
verses.textLatin: per me principes imperant, et potentes decernunt justitiam.

verses.text: I love them that love me: and they that in the morning early watch for me, shall find me.
verses.textLatin: Ego diligentes me diligo, et qui mane vigilant ad me, invenient me.

verses.text: With me are riches and glory, glorious riches and justice.
verses.textLatin: Mecum sunt divitiæ et gloria, opes superbæ et justitia.

verses.text: For my fruit is better than gold and the precious stone, and my blossoms than choice silver.
verses.textLatin: Melior est enim fructus meus auro et lapide pretioso, et genimina mea argento electo.

verses.text: I walk in the way of justice, in the midst of the paths of judgment,
verses.textLatin: In viis justitiæ ambulo, in medio semitarum judicii:

verses.text: That I may enrich them that love me, and may fill their treasures.
verses.textLatin: ut ditem diligentes me, et thesauros eorum repleam.

verses.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Dominus possedit me in initio viarum suarum antequam quidquam faceret a principio.

verses.text: I was set up from eternity, and of old before the earth was made.
verses.textLatin: Ab æterno ordinata sum, et ex antiquis antequam terra fieret.

verses.text: The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived, neither had the fountains of waters as yet sprung out:
verses.textLatin: Nondum erant abyssi, et ego jam concepta eram: necdum fontes aquarum eruperant,

verses.text: The mountains with their huge bulk had not as yet been established: before the hills I was brought forth:
verses.textLatin: necdum montes gravi mole constiterant: ante colles ego parturiebar.

verses.text: He had not yet made the earth, nor the rivers, nor the poles of the world.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc terram non fecerat, et flumina, et cardines orbis terræ.

verses.text: When he prepared the heavens, I was present: when with a certain law and compass he enclosed the depths:
verses.textLatin: Quando præparabat cælos, aderam; quando certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos;

verses.text: When he established the sky above, and poised the fountains of waters:
verses.textLatin: quando æthera firmabat sursum, et librabat fontes aquarum;

verses.text: When he compassed the sea with its bounds, and set a law to the waters that they should not pass their limits: when he balanced the foundations of the earth;
verses.textLatin: quando circumdabat mari terminum suum, et legem ponebat aquis, ne transirent fines suos; quando appendebat fundamenta terræ:

verses.text: I was with him forming all things: and was delighted every day, playing before him at all times;
verses.textLatin: cum eo eram, cuncta componens. Et delectabar per singulos dies, ludens coram eo omni tempore,

verses.text: Playing in the world: and my delights were to be with the children of men.
verses.textLatin: ludens in orbe terrarum; et deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum.

verses.text: Now therefore, ye children, hear me: Blessed are they that keep my ways.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, filii, audite me: beati qui custodiunt vias meas.

verses.text: Hear instruction and be wise, and refuse it not.
verses.textLatin: Audite disciplinam, et estote sapientes, et nolite abjicere eam.

verses.text: Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth daily at my gates, and waiteth at the posts of my doors.
verses.textLatin: Beatus homo qui audit me, et qui vigilat ad fores meas quotidie, et observat ad postes ostii mei.

verses.text: He that shall find me, shall find life, and shall have salvation from the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Qui me invenerit, inveniet vitam, et hauriet salutem a Domino.

verses.text: But he that shall sin against me, shall hurt his own soul. All that hate me love death.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem in me peccaverit, lædet animam suam; omnes qui me oderunt diligunt mortem.

verses.text: Wisdom  hath built herself a house, she hath hewn her out seven pillars.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia ædificavit sibi domum: excidit columnas septem.

verses.text: She hath slain her victims, mingled her wine, and set forth her table.
verses.textLatin: Immolavit victimas suas, miscuit vinum, et proposuit mensam suam.

verses.text: She hath sent her maids to invite to the tower, and to the walls of the city:
verses.textLatin: Misit ancillas suas ut vocarent ad arcem et ad mœnia civitatis.

verses.text: Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me. And to the unwise she said:
verses.textLatin: Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me. Et insipientibus locuta est:

verses.text: Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you.
verses.textLatin: Venite, comedite panem meum, et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis.

verses.text: Forsake childishness, and live, and walk by the ways of prudence.
verses.textLatin: Relinquite infantiam, et vivite, et ambulate per vias prudentiæ.

verses.text: He that teacheth a scorner, doth an injury to himself: and he that rebuketh a wicked man, getteth himself a blot.
verses.textLatin: Qui erudit derisorem, ipse injuriam sibi facit, et qui arguit impium, sibi maculam generat.

verses.text: Rebuke not a scorner lest he hate thee. Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.
verses.textLatin: Noli arguere derisorem, ne oderit te: argue sapientem, et diliget te.

verses.text: Give an occasion to a wise man, and wisdom shall be added to him. Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it.
verses.textLatin: Da sapienti occasionem, et addetur ei sapientia; doce justum, et festinabit accipere.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is prudence.
verses.textLatin: Principium sapientiæ timor Domini, et scientia sanctorum prudentia.

verses.text: For by me shall thy days be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to thee.
verses.textLatin: Per me enim multiplicabuntur dies tui, et addentur tibi anni vitæ.

verses.text: If thou be wise, thou shalt be so to thyself: and if a scorner, thou alone shalt bear the evil.
verses.textLatin: Si sapiens fueris, tibimetipsi eris; si autem illusor, solus portabis malum.

verses.text: A foolish woman and clamorous, and full of allurements, and knowing nothing at all,
verses.textLatin: Mulier stulta et clamosa, plenaque illecebris, et nihil omnino sciens,

verses.text: Sat at the door of her house, upon a seat, in a high place of the city,
verses.textLatin: sedit in foribus domus suæ, super sellam in excelso urbis loco,

verses.text: To call them that pass by the way, and go on their journey:
verses.textLatin: ut vocaret transeuntes per viam, et pergentes itinere suo:

verses.text: He that is a little one, let him turn to me. And to the fool she said:
verses.textLatin: Qui est parvulus declinet ad me. Et vecordi locuta est:

verses.text: Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant.
verses.textLatin: Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior.

verses.text: And he did not know that giants are there, and that her guests are in the depths of hell.
verses.textLatin: Et ignoravit quod ibi sint gigantes, et in profundis inferni convivæ ejus.

verses.text: A  wise son maketh the father glad: but a foolish son is the sorrow of his mother.
verses.textLatin: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem, filius vero stultus mœstitia est matris suæ.

verses.text: Treasures of wickedness shall profit nothing: but justice shall deliver from death.
verses.textLatin: Nil proderunt thesauri impietatis, justitia vero liberabit a morte.

verses.text: The Lord will not afflict the soul of the just with famine, and he will disappoint the deceitful practices of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Non affliget Dominus fame animam justi, et insidias impiorum subvertet.

verses.text: The slothful hand hath wrought poverty: but the hand of the industrious getteth riches. He that trusteth to lies feedeth the winds: and the same runneth after birds that fly away.
verses.textLatin: Egestatem operata est manus remissa; manus autem fortium divitias parat. Qui nititur mendaciis, hic pascit ventos; idem autem ipse sequitur aves volantes.

verses.text: He that gathered in the harvest, is a wise son: but he that snorteth in the summer, is the son of confusion.
verses.textLatin: Qui congregat in messe, filius sapiens est; qui autem stertit æstate, filius confusionis.

verses.text: The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but iniquity covereth the mouth of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio Domini super caput justi; os autem impiorum operit iniquitas.

verses.text: The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot.
verses.textLatin: Memoria justi cum laudibus, et nomen impiorum putrescet.

verses.text: The wise of heart receiveth precepts: a fool is beaten with lips.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens corde præcepta suscipit; stultus cæditur labiis.

verses.text: He that walketh sincerely, walketh confidently: but he that perverteth his ways, shall be manifest.
verses.textLatin: Qui ambulat simpliciter ambulat confidenter; qui autem depravat vias suas manifestus erit.

verses.text: He that winketh with the eye shall cause sorrow: and the foolish in lips shall be beaten.
verses.textLatin: Qui annuit oculo dabit dolorem; et stultus labiis verberabitur.

verses.text: The mouth of the just is a vein of life: and the mouth of the wicked covereth iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Vena vitæ os justi, et os impiorum operit iniquitatem.

verses.text: Hatred stirreth up strifes: and charity covereth all sins.
verses.textLatin: Odium suscitat rixas, et universa delicta operit caritas.

verses.text: In the lips of the wise is wisdom found: and a rod on the back of him that wanteth sense.
verses.textLatin: In labiis sapientis invenitur sapientia, et virga in dorso ejus qui indiget corde.

verses.text: Wise men lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the fool is next to confusion.
verses.textLatin: Sapientes abscondunt scientiam; os autem stulti confusioni proximum est.

verses.text: The substance of a rich man is the city of his strength: the fear of the poor is their poverty.
verses.textLatin: Substantia divitis, urbs fortitudinis ejus; pavor pauperum egestas eorum.

verses.text: The work of the just is unto life: but the fruit of the wicked, unto sin.
verses.textLatin: Opus justi ad vitam, fructus autem impii ad peccatum.

verses.text: The way of life, to him that observeth correction: but he that forsaketh reproofs goeth astray.
verses.textLatin: Via vitæ custodienti disciplinam; qui autem increpationes relinquit, errat.

verses.text: Lying lips hide hatred: he that uttereth reproach is foolish.
verses.textLatin: Abscondunt odium labia mendacia; qui profert contumeliam, insipiens est.

verses.text: In the multitude of words there shall not want sin: but he that refraineth his lips is most wise.
verses.textLatin: In multiloquio non deerit peccatum, qui autem moderatur labia sua prudentissimus est.

verses.text: The tongue of the just is as choice silver: but the heart of the wicked is nothing worth.
verses.textLatin: Argentum electum lingua justi; cor autem impiorum pro nihilo.

verses.text: The lips of the just teach many: but they that are ignorant, shall die in the want of understanding.
verses.textLatin: Labia justi erudiunt plurimos; qui autem indocti sunt in cordis egestate morientur.

verses.text: The blessing of the Lord maketh men rich: neither shall affliction be joined to them.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio Domini divites facit, nec sociabitur eis afflictio.

verses.text: A fool worketh mischief as it were for sport: but wisdom is prudence to a man.
verses.textLatin: Quasi per risum stultus operatur scelus, sapientia autem est viro prudentia.

verses.text: That which the wicked feareth, shall come upon him: to the just their desire shall be given.
verses.textLatin: Quod timet impius veniet super eum; desiderium suum justus dabitur.

verses.text: As a tempest that passeth, so the wicked shall be no more: but the just is as an everlasting foundation.
verses.textLatin: Quasi tempestas transiens non erit impius; justus autem quasi fundamentum sempiternum.

verses.text: As vinegar to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to them that sent him.
verses.textLatin: Sicut acetum dentibus, et fumus oculis, sic piger his qui miserunt eum.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord shall prolong days: and the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini apponet dies, et anni impiorum breviabuntur.

verses.text: The expectation of the just is joy; but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Exspectatio justorum lætitia, spes autem impiorum peribit.

verses.text: The strength of the upright is the way of the Lord: and fear to them that work evil.
verses.textLatin: Fortitudo simplicis via Domini, et pavor his qui operantur malum.

verses.text: The just shall never be moved: but the wicked shall not dwell on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Justus in æternum non commovebitur, impii autem non habitabunt super terram.

verses.text: The mouth of the just shall bring forth wisdom: the tongue of the perverse shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Os justi parturiet sapientiam; lingua pravorum peribit.

verses.text: The lips of the just consider what is acceptable: and the mouth of the wicked uttereth perverse things.
verses.textLatin: Labia justi considerant placita, et os impiorum perversa.

verses.text: A  DECEITFUL balance is an abomination before the Lord: and a just weight is his will.
verses.textLatin: Statera dolosa abominatio est apud Dominum, et pondus æquum voluntas ejus.

verses.text: Where pride is, there also shall be reproach: but where humility is, there also is wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Ubi fuerit superbia, ibi erit et contumelia; ubi autem est humilitas, ibi et sapientia.

verses.text: The simplicity of the just shall guide them: and the deceitfulness of the wicked shall destroy them.
verses.textLatin: Simplicitas justorum diriget eos, et supplantatio perversorum vastabit illos.

verses.text: Riches shall not profit in the day of revenge: but justice shall deliver from death.
verses.textLatin: Non proderunt divitiæ in die ultionis; justitia autem liberabit a morte.

verses.text: The justice of the upright shall make his way prosperous: and the wicked man shall fall by his own wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Justitia simplicis diriget viam ejus, et in impietate sua corruet impius.

verses.text: The justice of the righteous shall deliver them: and the unjust shall be caught in their own snares.
verses.textLatin: Justitia rectorum liberabit eos, et in insidiis suis capientur iniqui.

verses.text: When the wicked man is dead, there shall be no hope any more: and the expectation of the solicitous shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Mortuo homine impio, nulla erit ultra spes, et exspectatio sollicitorum peribit.

verses.text: The just is delivered out of distress: and the wicked shall be given up for him.
verses.textLatin: Justus de angustia liberatus est, et tradetur impius pro eo.

verses.text: The dissembler with his mouth deceiveth his friend: but the just shall be delivered by knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Simulator ore decipit amicum suum; justi autem liberabuntur scientia.

verses.text: When it goeth well with the just the city shall rejoice: and when the wicked perish there shall be praise.
verses.textLatin: In bonis justorum exsultabit civitas, et in perditione impiorum erit laudatio.

verses.text: By the blessing of the just the city shall be exalted: and by the mouth of the wicked it shall be overthrown.
verses.textLatin: Benedictione justorum exaltabitur civitas, et ore impiorum subvertetur.

verses.text: He that despiseth his friend, is mean of heart: but the wise man will hold his peace.
verses.textLatin: Qui despicit amicum suum indigens corde est; vir autem prudens tacebit.

verses.text: He that walketh deceitfully, revealeth secrets: but he that is faithful, concealeth the thing committed to him by his friend.
verses.textLatin: Qui ambulat fraudulenter, revelat arcana; qui autem fidelis est animi, celat amici commissum.

verses.text: Where there is no governor, the people shall fall: but there is safety where there is much counsel.
verses.textLatin: Ubi non est gubernator, populus corruet; salus autem, ubi multa consilia.

verses.text: He shall be afflicted with evil, that is surety for a stranger: but he that is aware of the snares, shall be secure.
verses.textLatin: Affligetur malo qui fidem facit pro extraneo; qui autem cavet laqueos securus erit.

verses.text: A gracious woman shall find glory: and the strong shall have riches.
verses.textLatin: Mulier gratiosa inveniet gloriam, et robusti habebunt divitias.

verses.text: A merciful man doth good to his own soul: but he that is cruel casteth off even his own kindred.
verses.textLatin: Benefacit animæ suæ vir misericors; qui autem crudelis est, etiam propinquos abjicit.

verses.text: The wicked maketh an unsteady work: but to him that soweth justice, there is a faithful reward.
verses.textLatin: Impius facit opus instabile, seminanti autem justitiam merces fidelis.

verses.text: Clemency prepareth life: and the pursuing of evil things, death.
verses.textLatin: Clementia præparat vitam, et sectatio malorum mortem.

verses.text: A perverse heart is abominable to the Lord: and his will is in them that walk sincerely.
verses.textLatin: Abominabile Domino cor pravum, et voluntas ejus in iis qui simpliciter ambulant.

verses.text: Hand in hand the evil man shall not be innocent: but the seed of the just shall be saved.
verses.textLatin: Manus in manu non erit innocens malus; semen autem justorum salvabitur.

verses.text: A golden ring in a swine’s snout, a woman fair and foolish.
verses.textLatin: Circulus aureus in naribus suis, mulier pulchra et fatua.

verses.text: The desire of the just is all good: the expectation of the wicked is indignation.
verses.textLatin: Desiderium justorum omne bonum est; præstolatio impiorum furor.

verses.text: Some distribute their own goods, and grow richer: others take away what is not their own, and are always in want.
verses.textLatin: Alii dividunt propria, et ditiores fiunt; alii rapiunt non sua, et semper in egestate sunt.

verses.text: The soul which blesseth, shall be made fat: and he that inebriateth, shall be inebriated also himself.
verses.textLatin: Anima quæ benedicit impinguabitur, et qui inebriat, ipse quoque inebriabitur.

verses.text: He that hideth up corn, shall be cursed among the people: but a blessing upon the head of them that sell.
verses.textLatin: Qui abscondit frumenta maledicetur in populis; benedictio autem super caput vendentium.

verses.text: Well doth he rise early who seeketh good things; but he that seeketh after evil things shall be oppressed by them.
verses.textLatin: Bene consurgit diluculo qui quærit bona; qui autem investigator malorum est, opprimetur ab eis.

verses.text: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the just shall spring up as a green leaf.
verses.textLatin: Qui confidit in divitiis suis corruet: justi autem quasi virens folium germinabunt.

verses.text: He that troubleth his own house, shall inherit the winds: and the fool shall serve the wise.
verses.textLatin: Qui conturbat domum suam possidebit ventos, et qui stultus est serviet sapienti.

verses.text: The fruit of the just man is a tree of life: and he that gaineth souls, is wise.
verses.textLatin: Fructus justi lignum vitæ, et qui suscipit animas sapiens est.

verses.text: If the just man receive in the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner.
verses.textLatin: Si justus in terra recipit, quanto magis impius et peccator!

verses.text: He  that loveth correction, loveth knowledge: but he that hateth reproof is foolish.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligit disciplinam diligit scientiam; qui autem odit increpationes insipiens est.

verses.text: He that is good, shall draw grace from the Lord: but he that trusteth in his own devices doth wickedly.
verses.textLatin: Qui bonus est hauriet gratiam a Domino; qui autem confidit in cogitationibus suis impie agit.

verses.text: Men shall not be strengthened by wickedness: and the root of the just shall not be moved.
verses.textLatin: Non roborabitur homo ex impietate, et radix justorum non commovebitur.

verses.text: A diligent woman is a crown to her husband: and she that doth things worthy of confusion, is a rottenness in his bones.
verses.textLatin: Mulier diligens corona est viro suo; et putredo in ossibus ejus, quæ confusione res dignas gerit.

verses.text: The thoughts of the just are judgments: and the counsels of the wicked are deceitful.
