verses.textLatin: Cogitationes justorum judicia, et consilia impiorum fraudulenta.

verses.text: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood: the mouth of the just shall deliver them.
verses.textLatin: Verba impiorum insidiantur sanguini; os justorum liberabit eos.

verses.text: Turn the wicked, and they shall not be: but the house of the just shall stand firm.
verses.textLatin: Verte impios, et non erunt; domus autem justorum permanebit.

verses.text: A man shall be known by his learning: but he that is vain and foolish, shall be exposed to contempt.
verses.textLatin: Doctrina sua noscetur vir; qui autem vanus et excors est patebit contemptui.

verses.text: Better is the poor man that provideth for himself, than he that is glorious and wanteth bread.
verses.textLatin: Melior est pauper et sufficiens sibi quam gloriosus et indigens pane.

verses.text: The just regardeth the lives of his beasts: but the bowels of the wicked are cruel.
verses.textLatin: Novit justus jumentorum suorum animas; viscera autem impiorum crudelia.

verses.text: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that pursueth idleness is very foolish. He that is delighted in passing his time over wine, leaveth a reproach in his strong holds.
verses.textLatin: Qui operatur terram suam satiabitur panibus; qui autem sectatur otium stultissimus est. Qui suavis est in vini demorationibus, in suis munitionibus relinquit contumeliam.

verses.text: The desire of the wicked is the fortification of evil men: but the root of the just shall prosper.
verses.textLatin: Desiderium impii munimentum est pessimorum; radix autem justorum proficiet.

verses.text: For the sins of the lips, ruin draweth nigh to the evil man: but the just shall escape out of distress.
verses.textLatin: Propter peccata labiorum ruina proximat malo; effugiet autem justus de angustia.

verses.text: By the fruit of his own mouth shall a man be filled with good things, and according to the works of his hands it shall be repaid him.
verses.textLatin: De fructu oris sui unusquisque replebitur bonis, et juxta opera manuum suarum retribuetur ei.

verses.text: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsels.
verses.textLatin: Via stulti recta in oculis ejus; qui autem sapiens est audit consilia.

verses.text: A fool immediately sheweth his anger: but he that dissembleth injuries is wise.
verses.textLatin: Fatuus statim indicat iram suam; qui autem dissimulat injuriam callidus est.

verses.text: He that speaketh that which he knoweth, sheweth forth justice: but he that lieth, is a deceitful witness.
verses.textLatin: Qui quod novit loquitur, index justitiæ est; qui autem mentitur, testis est fraudulentus.

verses.text: There is that promiseth, and is pricked as it were with a sword of conscience: but the tongue of the wise is health.
verses.textLatin: Est qui promittit, et quasi gladio pungitur conscientiæ: lingua autem sapientium sanitas est.

verses.text: The lip of truth shall be steadfast for ever: but he that is a hasty witness, frameth a lying tongue.
verses.textLatin: Labium veritatis firmum erit in perpetuum; qui autem testis est repentinus, concinnat linguam mendacii.

verses.text: Deceit is in the heart of them that think evil things: but joy followeth them that take counsels of peace.
verses.textLatin: Dolus in corde cogitantium mala; qui autem pacis ineunt consilia, sequitur eos gaudium.

verses.text: Whatsoever shall befall the just man, it shall not make him sad: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief.
verses.textLatin: Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit: impii autem replebuntur malo.

verses.text: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord: but they that deal faithfully please him.
verses.textLatin: Abominatio est Domino labia mendacia; qui autem fideliter agunt placent ei.

verses.text: A cautious man concealeth knowledge: and the heart of fools publisheth folly.
verses.textLatin: Homo versatus celat scientiam, et cor insipientium provocat stultitiam.

verses.text: The hand of the valiant shall bear rule: but that which is slothful, shall be under tribute.
verses.textLatin: Manus fortium dominabitur; quæ autem remissa est, tributis serviet.

verses.text: Grief in the heart of a man shall bring him low, but with a good word he shall be made glad.
verses.textLatin: Mœror in corde viri humiliabit illum, et sermone bono lætificabitur.

verses.text: He that neglecteth a loss for the sake of a friend, is just: but the way of the wicked shall deceive them.
verses.textLatin: Qui negligit damnum propter amicum, justus est; iter autem impiorum decipiet eos.

verses.text: The deceitful man shall not find gain: but the substance of a just man shall be precious gold.
verses.textLatin: Non inveniet fraudulentus lucrum, et substantia hominis erit auri pretium.

verses.text: In the path of justice is life: but the by-way leadeth to death.
verses.textLatin: In semita justitiæ vita; iter autem devium ducit ad mortem.

verses.text: A  WISE son heareth the doctrine of his father: but he that is a scorner, heareth not when he is reproved.
verses.textLatin: Filius sapiens doctrina patris; qui autem illusor est non audit cum arguitur.

verses.text: Of the fruit of his own mouth shall a man be filled with good things: but the soul of transgressors is wicked.
verses.textLatin: De fructu oris sui homo satiabitur bonis: anima autem prævaricatorum iniqua.

verses.text: He that keepeth his mouth, keepeth his soul: but he that hath no guard on his speech shall meet with evils.
verses.textLatin: Qui custodit os suum custodit animam suam; qui autem inconsideratus est ad loquendum, sentiet mala.

verses.text: The sluggard willeth and willeth not: but the soul of them that work, shall be made fat.
verses.textLatin: Vult et non vult piger; anima autem operantium impinguabitur.

verses.text: The just shall hate a lying word: but the wicked confoundeth, and shall be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Verbum mendax justus detestabitur; impius autem confundit, et confundetur.

verses.text: Justice keepeth the way of the innocent: but wickedness overthroweth the sinner.
verses.textLatin: Justitia custodit innocentis viam, impietas autem peccatorem supplantat.

verses.text: One is as it were rich, when he hath nothing: and another is as it were poor, when he hath great riches.
verses.textLatin: Est quasi dives, cum nihil habeat, et est quasi pauper, cum in multis divitiis sit.

verses.text: The ransom of a man’s life are his riches: but he that is poor beareth not reprehension.
verses.textLatin: Redemptio animæ viri divitiæ suæ; qui autem pauper est, increpationem non sustinet.

verses.text: The light of the just giveth joy: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
verses.textLatin: Lux justorum lætificat: lucerna autem impiorum extinguetur.

verses.text: Among the proud there are always contentions: but they that do all things with counsel, are ruled by wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Inter superbos semper jurgia sunt; qui autem agunt omnia cum consilio, reguntur sapientia.

verses.text: Substance got in haste shall be diminished: but that which by little and little is gathered with the hand shall increase.
verses.textLatin: Substantia festinata minuetur; quæ autem paulatim colligitur manu, multiplicabitur.

verses.text: Hope that is deferred afflicteth the soul: desire when it cometh is a tree of life.
verses.textLatin: Spes quæ differtur affligit animam; lignum vitæ desiderium veniens.

verses.text: Whosoever speaketh ill of any thing, bindeth himself for the time to come: but he that feareth the commandment, shall dwell in peace. Deceitful souls go astray in sins: the just are merciful, and shew mercy.
verses.textLatin: Qui detrahit alicui rei, ipse se in futurum obligat; qui autem timet præceptum, in pace versabitur. Animæ dolosæ errant in peccatis: justi autem misericordes sunt, et miserantur.

verses.text: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, that he may decline from the ruin of death.
verses.textLatin: Lex sapientis fons vitæ, ut declinet a ruina mortis.

verses.text: Good instruction shall give grace: in the way of scorners is a deep pit.
verses.textLatin: Doctrina bona dabit gratiam; in itinere contemptorum vorago.

verses.text: The prudent man doth all things with counsel: but he that is a fool, layeth open his folly.
verses.textLatin: Astutus omnia agit cum consilio; qui autem fatuus est aperit stultitiam.

verses.text: The messenger of the wicked shall fall into mischief: but a faithful ambassador is health.
verses.textLatin: Nuntius impii cadet in malum; legatus autem fidelis, sanitas.

verses.text: Poverty and shame to him that refuseth instruction: but he that yieldeth to reproof, shall be glorified.
verses.textLatin: Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti glorificabitur.

verses.text: The desire that is accomplished, delighteth the soul: fools hate them that flee from evil things.
verses.textLatin: Desiderium si compleatur delectat animam; detestantur stulti eos qui fugiunt mala.

verses.text: He that walketh with the wise, shall be wise: a friend of fools shall become like to them.
verses.textLatin: Qui cum sapientibus graditur sapiens erit; amicus stultorum similis efficietur.

verses.text: Evil pursueth sinners: and to the just good shall be repaid.
verses.textLatin: Peccatores persequitur malum, et justis retribuentur bona.

verses.text: The good man leaveth heirs, sons, and grandsons: and the substance of the sinner is kept for the just.
verses.textLatin: Bonus reliquit hæredes filios et nepotes, et custoditur justo substantia peccatoris.

verses.text: Much food is in the tillage of fathers: but for others it is gathered without judgment.
verses.textLatin: Multi cibi in novalibus patrum, et aliis congregantur absque judicio.

verses.text: He that spareth the rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him correcteth him betimes.
verses.textLatin: Qui parcit virgæ odit filium suum; qui autem diligit illum instanter erudit.

verses.text: The just eateth and filleth his soul: but the belly of the wicked is never to be filled.
verses.textLatin: Justus comedit et replet animam suam; venter autem impiorum insaturabilis.

verses.text: A  WISE woman buildeth her house: but the foolish will pull down with her hands that also which is built.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens mulier ædificat domum suam; insipiens exstructam quoque manibus destruet.

verses.text: He that walketh in the right way, and feareth God, is despised by him that goeth by an infamous way.
verses.textLatin: Ambulans recto itinere, et timens Deum, despicitur ab eo qui infami graditur via.

verses.text: In the mouth of a fool is the rod of pride: but the lips of the wise preserve them.
verses.textLatin: In ore stulti virga superbiæ; labia autem sapientium custodiunt eos.

verses.text: Where there are no oxen, the crib is empty: but where there is much corn, there the strength of the ox is manifest.
verses.textLatin: Ubi non sunt boves, præsepe vacuum est; ubi autem plurimæ segetes, ibi manifesta est fortitudo bovis.

verses.text: A faithful witness will not lie: but a deceitful witness uttereth a lie.
verses.textLatin: Testis fidelis non mentitur; profert autem mendacium dolosus testis.

verses.text: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: the learning of the wise is easy.
verses.textLatin: Quærit derisor sapientiam, et non invenit; doctrina prudentium facilis.

verses.text: Go against a foolish man, and he knoweth not the lips of prudence.
verses.textLatin: Vade contra virum stultum, et nescit labia prudentiæ.

verses.text: The wisdom of a discreet man is to understand his way: and the imprudence of fools erreth.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia callidi est intelligere viam suam, et imprudentia stultorum errans.

verses.text: A fool will laugh at sin, but among the just grace shall abide.
verses.textLatin: Stultus illudet peccatum, et inter justos morabitur gratia.

verses.text: The heart that knoweth the bitterness of his own soul, in his joy the stranger shall not intermeddle.
verses.textLatin: Cor quod novit amaritudinem animæ suæ, in gaudio ejus non miscebitur extraneus.

verses.text: The house of the wicked shall be destroyed: but the tabernacles of the just shall flourish.
verses.textLatin: Domus impiorum delebitur: tabernacula vero justorum germinabunt.

verses.text: There is a way which seemeth just to a man: but the ends thereof lead to death.
verses.textLatin: Est via quæ videtur homini justa, novissima autem ejus deducunt ad mortem.

verses.text: Laughter shall be mingled with sorrow, and mourning taketh hold of the end of joy.
verses.textLatin: Risus dolore miscebitur, et extrema gaudii luctus occupat.

verses.text: A fool shall be filled with his own ways, and the good man shall be above him.
verses.textLatin: Viis suis replebitur stultus, et super eum erit vir bonus.

verses.text: The innocent believeth every word: the discreet man considereth his steps. No good shall come to the deceitful son: but the wise servant shall prosper in his dealings, and his way shall be made straight.
verses.textLatin: Innocens credit omni verbo; astutus considerat gressus suos. Filio doloso nihil erit boni; servo autem sapienti prosperi erunt actus, et dirigetur via ejus.

verses.text: A wise man feareth and declineth from evil: the fool leapeth over and is confident.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens timet, et declinat a malo; stultus transilit, et confidit.

verses.text: The impatient man shall work folly: and the crafty man is hateful.
verses.textLatin: Impatiens operabitur stultitiam, et vir versutus odiosus est.

verses.text: The childish shall possess folly, and the prudent shall look for knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Possidebunt parvuli stultitiam, et exspectabunt astuti scientiam.

verses.text: The evil shall fall down before the good: and the wicked before the gates of the just.
verses.textLatin: Jacebunt mali ante bonos, et impii ante portas justorum.

verses.text: The poor man shall be hateful even to his own neighbour: but the friends of the rich are many.
verses.textLatin: Etiam proximo suo pauper odiosus erit: amici vero divitum multi.

verses.text: He that despiseth his neighbour, sinneth: but he that sheweth mercy to the poor, shall be blessed. He that believeth in the Lord, loveth mercy.
verses.textLatin: Qui despicit proximum suum peccat; qui autem miseretur pauperis beatus erit. Qui credit in Domino misericordiam diligit.

verses.text: They err that work evil: but mercy and truth prepare good things.
verses.textLatin: Errant qui operantur malum; misericordia et veritas præparant bona.

verses.text: In much work there shall be abundance: but where there are many words, there is oftentimes want.
verses.textLatin: In omni opere erit abundantia; ubi autem verba sunt plurima, ibi frequenter egestas.

verses.text: The crown of the wise is their riches: the folly of fools, imprudence.
verses.textLatin: Corona sapientium divitiæ eorum; fatuitas stultorum imprudentia.

verses.text: A faithful witness delivereth souls: and the double dealer uttereth lies.
verses.textLatin: Liberat animas testis fidelis, et profert mendacia versipellis.

verses.text: In the fear of the Lord is confidence of strength, and there shall be hope for his children.
verses.textLatin: In timore Domini fiducia fortitudinis, et filiis ejus erit spes.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, to decline from the ruin of death.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini fons vitæ, ut declinent a ruina mortis.

verses.text: In the multitude of people is the dignity of the king: and in the small number of people the dishonour of the prince.
verses.textLatin: In multitudine populi dignitas regis, et in paucitate plebis ignominia principis.

verses.text: He that is patient, is governed with much wisdom: but he that is impatient, exalteth his folly.
verses.textLatin: Qui patiens est multa gubernatur prudentia; qui autem impatiens est exaltat stultitiam suam.

verses.text: Soundness of heart is the life of the flesh: but envy is the rottenness of the bones.
verses.textLatin: Vita carnium sanitas cordis; putredo ossium invidia.

verses.text: He that oppresseth the poor, upbraideth his Maker: but he that hath pity on the poor, honoureth him.
verses.textLatin: Qui calumniatur egentem exprobrat factori ejus; honorat autem eum qui miseretur pauperis.

verses.text: The wicked man shall be driven out in his wickedness: but the just hath hope in his death.
verses.textLatin: In malitia sua expelletur impius: sperat autem justus in morte sua.

verses.text: In the heart of the prudent resteth wisdom, and it shall instruct all the ignorant.
verses.textLatin: In corde prudentis requiescit sapientia, et indoctos quosque erudiet.

verses.text: Justice exalteth a nation: but sin maketh nations miserable.
verses.textLatin: Justitia elevat gentem; miseros autem facit populos peccatum.

verses.text: A wise servant is acceptable to the king: he that is good for nothing shall feel his anger.
verses.textLatin: Acceptus est regi minister intelligens; iracundiam ejus inutilis sustinebit.

verses.text: A  MILD answer breaketh wrath: but a harsh word stirreth up fury.
verses.textLatin: Responsio mollis frangit iram; sermo durus suscitat furorem.

verses.text: The tongue of the wise adorneth knowledge: but the mouth of fools bubbleth out folly.
verses.textLatin: Lingua sapientium ornat scientiam; os fatuorum ebullit stultitiam.

verses.text: The eyes of the Lord in every place behold the good and the evil.
verses.textLatin: In omni loco, oculi Domini contemplantur bonos et malos.

verses.text: A peaceable tongue is a tree of life: but that which is immoderate, shall crush the spirit.
verses.textLatin: Lingua placabilis lignum vitæ; quæ autem immoderata est conteret spiritum.

verses.text: A fool laugheth at the instruction of his father: but he that regardeth reproofs shall become prudent. In abundant justice there is the greatest strength: but the devices of the wicked shall be rooted out.
verses.textLatin: Stultus irridet disciplinam patris sui; qui autem custodit increpationes astutior fiet. In abundanti justitia virtus maxima est: cogitationes autem impiorum eradicabuntur.

verses.text: The house of the just is very much strength: and in the fruits of the wicked is trouble.
verses.textLatin: Domus justi plurima fortitudo, et in fructibus impii conturbatio.

verses.text: The lips of the wise shall disperse knowledge: the heart of fools shall be unlike.
verses.textLatin: Labia sapientium disseminabunt scientiam; cor stultorum dissimile erit.

verses.text: The victims of the wicked are abominable to the Lord: the vows of the just are acceptable.
verses.textLatin: Victimæ impiorum abominabiles Domino; vota justorum placabilia.

verses.text: The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: he that followeth justice is beloved by him.
verses.textLatin: Abominatio est Domino via impii; qui sequitur justitiam diligitur ab eo.

verses.text: Instruction is grievous to him that forsaketh the way of life: he that hateth reproof shall die.
verses.textLatin: Doctrina mala deserenti viam vitæ; qui increpationes odit, morietur.

verses.text: Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more the hearts of the children of men?
verses.textLatin: Infernus et perditio coram Domino; quanto magis corda filiorum hominum!

verses.text: A corrupt man loveth not one that reproveth him: nor will he go to the wise.
verses.textLatin: Non amat pestilens eum qui se corripit, nec ad sapientes graditur.

verses.text: A glad heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by grief of mind the spirit is cast down.
verses.textLatin: Cor gaudens exhilarat faciem; in mœrore animi dejicitur spiritus.

verses.text: The heart of the wise seeketh instruction: and the mouth of fools feedeth on foolishness.
verses.textLatin: Cor sapientis quærit doctrinam, et os stultorum pascitur imperitia.

verses.text: All the days of the poor are evil: a secure mind is like a continual feast.
verses.textLatin: Omnes dies pauperis, mali; secura mens quasi juge convivium.

verses.text: Better is a little with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without content.
verses.textLatin: Melius est parum cum timore Domini, quam thesauri magni et insatiabiles.

verses.text: It is better to be invited to herbs with love, than to a fatted calf with hatred.
verses.textLatin: Melius est vocari ad olera cum caritate, quam ad vitulum saginatum cum odio.

verses.text: A passionate man stirreth up strifes: he that is patient appeaseth those that are stirred up.
verses.textLatin: Vir iracundus provocat rixas; qui patiens est mitigat suscitatas.

verses.text: The way of the slothful is as a hedge of thorns; the way of the just is without offence.
verses.textLatin: Iter pigrorum quasi sepes spinarum; via justorum absque offendiculo.

verses.text: A wise son maketh a father joyful: but the foolish man despiseth his mother.
verses.textLatin: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem, et stultus homo despicit matrem suam.

verses.text: Folly is joy to the fool: and the wise man maketh straight his steps.
verses.textLatin: Stultitia gaudium stulto, et vir prudens dirigit gressus suos.

verses.text: Designs are brought to nothing where there is no counsel: but where there are many counsellors, they are established.
verses.textLatin: Dissipantur cogitationes ubi non est consilium; ubi vero sunt plures consiliarii, confirmantur.

verses.text: A man rejoiceth in the sentence of his mouth: and a word in due time is best.
verses.textLatin: Lætatur homo in sententia oris sui, et sermo opportunus est optimus.

verses.text: The path of life is above for the wise, that he may decline from the lowest hell.
verses.textLatin: Semita vitæ super eruditum, ut declinet de inferno novissimo.

verses.text: The Lord will destroy the house of the proud: and will strengthen the borders of the widow.
verses.textLatin: Domum superborum demolietur Dominus, et firmos faciet terminos viduæ.

verses.text: Evil thoughts are an abomination to the Lord: and pure words most beautiful shall be confirmed by him.
verses.textLatin: Abominatio Domini cogitationes malæ, et purus sermo pulcherrimus firmabitur ab eo.

verses.text: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house: but he that hateth bribes shall live. By mercy and faith sins are purged away: and by the fear of the Lord every one declineth from evil.
verses.textLatin: Conturbat domum suam qui sectatur avaritiam; qui autem odit munera, vivet. Per misericordiam et fidem purgantur peccata: per timorem autem Domini declinat omnis a malo.

verses.text: The mind of the just studieth obedience: the mouth of the wicked overfloweth with evils.
verses.textLatin: Mens justi meditatur obedientiam; os impiorum redundat malis.

verses.text: The Lord is far from the wicked: and he will hear the prayers of the just.
verses.textLatin: Longe est Dominus ab impiis, et orationes justorum exaudiet.

verses.text: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the soul: a good name maketh the bones fat.
verses.textLatin: Lux oculorum lætificat animam; fama bona impinguat ossa.

verses.text: The ear that heareth the reproofs of life, shall abide in the midst of the wise.
verses.textLatin: Auris quæ audit increpationes vitæ in medio sapientium commorabitur.

verses.text: He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that yieldeth to reproof possesseth understanding.
verses.textLatin: Qui abjicit disciplinam despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus possessor est cordis.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the lesson of wisdom: and humility goeth before glory.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini disciplina sapientiæ, et gloriam præcedit humilitas.

verses.text: It is the part of man to prepare the soul: and of the Lord to govern the tongue.
verses.textLatin: Hominis est animam præparare, et Domini gubernare linguam.

verses.text: All the ways of a man are open to his eyes: the Lord is the weigher of spirits.
verses.textLatin: Omnes viæ hominis patent oculis ejus; spirituum ponderator est Dominus.

verses.text: Lay open thy works to the Lord: and thy thoughts shall be directed.
verses.textLatin: Revela Domino opera tua, et dirigentur cogitationes tuæ.

verses.text: The Lord hath made all things for himself: the wicked also for the evil day.
verses.textLatin: Universa propter semetipsum operatus est Dominus; impium quoque ad diem malum.

verses.text: Every proud man is an abomination to the Lord: though hand should be joined to hand, he is not innocent. The beginning of a good way is to do justice; and this is more acceptable with God, than to offer sacrifices.
verses.textLatin: Abominatio Domini est omnis arrogans; etiamsi manus ad manum fuerit, non est innocens. Initium viæ bonæ facere justitiam; accepta est autem apud Deum magis quam immolare hostias.

verses.text: By mercy and truth iniquity is redeemed: and by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.
verses.textLatin: Misericordia et veritate redimitur iniquitas, et in timore Domini declinatur a malo.

verses.text: When the ways of man shall please the Lord, he will convert even his enemies to peace.
verses.textLatin: Cum placuerint Domino viæ hominis, inimicos quoque ejus convertet ad pacem.

verses.text: Better is a little with justice, than great revenues with iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Melius est parum cum justitia quam multi fructus cum iniquitate.

verses.text: The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps.
verses.textLatin: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Domini est dirigere gressus ejus.

verses.text: Divination is in the lips of the king, his mouth shall not err in judgment.
verses.textLatin: Divinatio in labiis regis; in judicio non errabit os ejus.

verses.text: Weight and balance are judgments of the Lord: and his work all the weights of the bag.
verses.textLatin: Pondus et statera judicia Domini sunt, et opera ejus omnes lapides sacculi.

verses.text: They that act wickedly are abominable to the king: for the throne is established by justice.
verses.textLatin: Abominabiles regi qui agunt impie, quoniam justitia firmatur solium.

verses.text: Just lips are the delight of kings: he that speaketh right things shall be loved.
verses.textLatin: Voluntas regum labia justa; qui recta loquitur diligetur.

verses.text: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death: and the wise man will pacify it.
verses.textLatin: Indignatio regis nuntii mortis, et vir sapiens placabit eam.

verses.text: In the cheerfulness of the king’s countenance is life: and his clemency is like the latter rain.
verses.textLatin: In hilaritate vultus regis vita, et clementia ejus quasi imber serotinus.

verses.text: Get wisdom, because it is better than gold: and purchase prudence, for it is more precious than silver.
verses.textLatin: Posside sapientiam, quia auro melior est, et acquire prudentiam, quia pretiosior est argento.

verses.text: The path of the just departeth from evils: he that keepeth his soul keepeth his way.
verses.textLatin: Semita justorum declinat mala; custos animæ suæ servat viam suam.

verses.text: Pride goeth before destruction: and the spirit is lifted up before a fall.
verses.textLatin: Contritionem præcedit superbia, et ante ruinam exaltatur spiritus.

verses.text: It is better to be humbled with the meek, than to divide spoils with the proud.
verses.textLatin: Melius est humiliari cum mitibus quam dividere spolia cum superbis.

verses.text: The learned in word shall find good things: and he that trusteth in the Lord is blessed.
verses.textLatin: Eruditus in verbo reperiet bona, et qui sperat in Domino beatus est.

verses.text: The wise in heart shall be called prudent: and he that is sweet in words shall attain to greater things.
verses.textLatin: Qui sapiens est corde appellabitur prudens, et qui dulcis eloquio majora percipiet.

verses.text: Knowledge is a fountain of life to him that possesseth it: the instruction of fools is foolishness.
verses.textLatin: Fons vitæ eruditio possidentis; doctrina stultorum fatuitas.

verses.text: The heart of the wise shall instruct his mouth: and shall add grace to his lips.
verses.textLatin: Cor sapientis erudiet os ejus, et labiis ejus addet gratiam.

verses.text: Well ordered words are as a honeycomb: sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
verses.textLatin: Favus mellis composita verba; dulcedo animæ sanitas ossium.

verses.text: There is a way that seemeth to a man right: and the ends thereof lead to death.
verses.textLatin: Est via quæ videtur homini recta, et novissima ejus ducunt ad mortem.

verses.text: The soul of him that laboureth, laboureth for himself, because his mouth hath obliged him to it.
verses.textLatin: Anima laborantis laborat sibi, quia compulit eum os suum.

verses.text: The wicked man diggeth evil, and in his lips is a burning fire.
verses.textLatin: Vir impius fodit malum, et in labiis ejus ignis ardescit.

verses.text: A perverse man stirreth up quarrels: and one full of words separateth princes.
verses.textLatin: Homo perversus suscitat lites, et verbosus separat principes.

verses.text: An unjust man allureth his friend: and leadeth him into a way that is not good.
verses.textLatin: Vir iniquus lactat amicum suum, et ducit eum per viam non bonam.

verses.text: He that with fixed eyes deviseth wicked things, biting his lips, bringeth evil to pass.
verses.textLatin: Qui attonitis oculis cogitat prava, mordens labia sua perficit malum.

verses.text: Old age is a crown of dignity, when it is found in the ways of justice.
verses.textLatin: Corona dignitatis senectus, quæ in viis justitiæ reperietur.

verses.text: The patient man is better than the valiant: and he that ruleth his spirit, than he that taketh cities.
verses.textLatin: Melior est patiens viro forti, et qui dominatur animo suo expugnatore urbium.

verses.text: Lots are cast into the lap, but they are disposed of by the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sortes mittuntur in sinum, sed a Domino temperantur.

verses.text: Better  is a dry morsel with joy, than a house full of victims with strife.
verses.textLatin: Melior est buccella sicca cum gaudio quam domus plena victimis cum jurgio.

verses.text: A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons, and shall divide the inheritance among the brethren.
verses.textLatin: Servus sapiens dominabitur filiis stultis, et inter fratres hæreditatem dividet.

verses.text: As silver is tried by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord trieth the hearts.
verses.textLatin: Sicut igne probatur argentum et aurum camino, ita corda probat Dominus.

verses.text: The evil man obeyeth an unjust tongue: and the deceitful hearkeneth to lying lips.
verses.textLatin: Malus obedit linguæ iniquæ, et fallax obtemperat labiis mendacibus.

verses.text: He that despiseth the poor, reproacheth his Maker; and he that rejoiceth at another man’s ruin, shall not be unpunished.
verses.textLatin: Qui despicit pauperem exprobrat factori ejus, et qui ruina lætatur alterius non erit impunitus.

verses.text: Children’s children are the crown of old men: and the glory of children are their fathers.
verses.textLatin: Corona senum filii filiorum, et gloria filiorum patres eorum.

verses.text: Eloquent words do not become a fool, nor lying lips a prince.
verses.textLatin: Non decent stultum verba composita, nec principem labium mentiens.

verses.text: The expectation of him that expecteth, is a most acceptable jewel: whithersoever he turneth himself, he understandeth wisely.
verses.textLatin: Gemma gratissima exspectatio præstolantis; quocumque se vertit, prudenter intelligit.

verses.text: He that concealeth a transgression, seeketh friendships: he that repeateth it again, separateth friends.
verses.textLatin: Qui celat delictum quærit amicitias; qui altero sermone repetit, separat fœderatos.

verses.text: A reproof availeth more with a wise man, than a hundred stripes with a fool.
verses.textLatin: Plus proficit correptio apud prudentem, quam centum plagæ apud stultum.

verses.text: An evil man always seeketh quarrels: but a cruel angel shall be sent against him.
verses.textLatin: Semper jurgia quærit malus: angelus autem crudelis mittetur contra eum.

verses.text: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her whelps, than a fool trusting in his own folly.
verses.textLatin: Expedit magis ursæ occurrere raptis fœtibus, quam fatuo confidenti in stultitia sua.

verses.text: He that rendereth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
verses.textLatin: Qui reddit mala pro bonis, non recedet malum de domo ejus.

verses.text: The beginning of quarrels is as when one letteth out water: before he suffereth reproach he forsaketh judgment.
verses.textLatin: Qui dimittit aquam caput est jurgiorum, et antequam patiatur contumeliam judicium deserit.

verses.text: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, both are abominable before God.
verses.textLatin: Qui justificat impium, et qui condemnat justum, abominabilis est uterque apud Deum.

verses.text: What doth it avail a fool to have riches, seeing he cannot buy wisdom? He that maketh his house high, seeketh a downfall: and he that refuseth to learn, shall fall into evils.
verses.textLatin: Quid prodest stulto habere divitias, cum sapientiam emere non possit? Qui altum facit domum suam quærit ruinam, et qui evitat discere incidet in mala.

verses.text: He that is a friend loveth at all times: and a brother is proved in distress.
verses.textLatin: Omni tempore diligit qui amicus est, et frater in angustiis comprobatur.

verses.text: A foolish man will clap hands, when he is surety for his friend.
verses.textLatin: Stultus homo plaudet manibus, cum spoponderit pro amico suo.

verses.text: He that studieth discords, loveth quarrels: and he that exalteth his door, seeketh ruin.
verses.textLatin: Qui meditatur discordias diligit rixas, et qui exaltat ostium quærit ruinam.

verses.text: He that is of a perverse heart, shall not find good: and he that perverteth his tongue, shall fall into evil.
verses.textLatin: Qui perversi cordis est non inveniet bonum, et qui vertit linguam incidet in malum.

verses.text: A fool is born to his own disgrace: and even his father shall not rejoice in a fool.
verses.textLatin: Natus est stultus in ignominiam suam; sed nec pater in fatuo lætabitur.

verses.text: A joyful mind maketh age flourishing: a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones.
verses.textLatin: Animus gaudens ætatem floridam facit; spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa.

verses.text: The wicked man taketh gifts out of the bosom, that he may pervert the paths of judgment.
verses.textLatin: Munera de sinu impius accipit, ut pervertat semitas judicii.

verses.text: Wisdom shineth in the face of the wise: the eyes of fools are in the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: In facie prudentis lucet sapientia; oculi stultorum in finibus terræ.

verses.text: A foolish son is the anger of the father: and the sorrow of the mother that bore him.
verses.textLatin: Ira patris filius stultus, et dolor matris quæ genuit eum.

verses.text: It is no good thing to do hurt to the just: nor to strike the prince, who judgeth right.
verses.textLatin: Non est bonum damnum inferre justo, nec percutere principem qui recta judicat.

verses.text: He that setteth bounds to his words, is knowing and wise: and the man of understanding is of a precious spirit.
verses.textLatin: Qui moderatur sermones suos doctus et prudens est, et pretiosi spiritus vir eruditus.

verses.text: Even a fool, if he will hold his peace shall be counted wise: and if he close his lips, a man of understanding.
verses.textLatin: Stultus quoque, si tacuerit, sapiens reputabitur, et si compresserit labia sua, intelligens.

verses.text: He  that hath a mind to depart from a friend seeketh occasions: he shall ever be subject to reproach.
verses.textLatin: Occasiones quærit qui vult recedere ab amico: omni tempore erit exprobrabilis.

verses.text: A fool receiveth not the words of prudence: unless thou say those things which are in his heart.
verses.textLatin: Non recipit stultus verba prudentiæ, nisi ea dixeris quæ versantur in corde ejus.

verses.text: The wicked man when he is come into the depth of sins, contemneth: but ignominy and reproach follow him.
verses.textLatin: Impius, cum in profundum venerit peccatorum, contemnit; sed sequitur eum ignominia et opprobrium.

verses.text: Words from the mouth of a man are as deep water: and the fountain of wisdom as an overflowing stream.
verses.textLatin: Aqua profunda verba ex ore viri, et torrens redundans fons sapientiæ.

verses.text: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to decline from the truth of judgment.
verses.textLatin: Accipere personam impii non est bonum, ut declines a veritate judicii.

verses.text: The lips of a fool intermeddle with strife: and his mouth provoketh quarrels.
verses.textLatin: Labia stulti miscent se rixis, et os ejus jurgia provocat.

verses.text: The mouth of a fool is his destruction: and his lips are the ruin of his soul.
verses.textLatin: Os stulti contritio ejus, et labia ipsius ruina animæ ejus.

verses.text: The words of the double tongued are as if they were harmless: and they reach even to the inner parts of the bowels. Fear casteth down the slothful: and the souls of the effeminate shall be hungry.
verses.textLatin: Verba bilinguis quasi simplicia, et ipsa perveniunt usque ad interiora ventris. Pigrum dejicit timor; animæ autem effeminatorum esurient.

verses.text: He that is loose and slack in his work, is the brother of him that wasteth his own works.
verses.textLatin: Qui mollis et dissolutus est in opere suo frater est sua opera dissipantis.

verses.text: The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runneth to it, and shall be exalted.
verses.textLatin: Turris fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus, et exaltabitur.

verses.text: The substance of the rich man is the city of his strength, and as a strong wall compassing him about.
verses.textLatin: Substantia divitis urbs roboris ejus, et quasi murus validus circumdans eum.

verses.text: Before destruction, the heart of a man is exalted: and before he be glorified, it is humbled.
verses.textLatin: Antequam conteratur, exaltatur cor hominis, et antequam glorificetur, humiliatur.

verses.text: He that answereth before he heareth sheweth himself to be a fool, and worthy of confusion.
verses.textLatin: Qui prius respondet quam audiat, stultum se esse demonstrat, et confusione dignum.

verses.text: The spirit of a man upholdeth his infirmity: but a spirit that is easily angered, who can bear?
verses.textLatin: Spiritus viri sustentat imbecillitatem suam; spiritum vero ad irascendum facilem quis poterit sustinere?

verses.text: A wise heart shall acquire knowledge: and the ear of the wise seeketh instruction.
verses.textLatin: Cor prudens possidebit scientiam, et auris sapientium quærit doctrinam.

verses.text: A man’s gift enlargeth his way, and maketh him room before princes.
verses.textLatin: Donum hominis dilatat viam ejus, et ante principes spatium ei facit.

verses.text: The just is first accuser of himself: his friend cometh, and shall search him.
verses.textLatin: Justus prior est accusator sui: venit amicus ejus, et investigabit eum.

verses.text: The lot suppresseth contentions, and determineth even between the mighty.
verses.textLatin: Contradictiones comprimit sors, et inter potentes quoque dijudicat.

verses.text: A brother that is helped by his brother, is like a strong city: and judgments are like the bars of cities.
verses.textLatin: Frater qui adjuvatur a fratre quasi civitas firma, et judicia quasi vectes urbium.

verses.text: Of the fruit of a man’s mouth shall his belly be satisfied: and the offspring of his lips shall fill him.
verses.textLatin: De fructu oris viri replebitur venter ejus, et genimina labiorum ipsius saturabunt eum.

verses.text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: they that love it, shall eat the fruits thereof.
verses.textLatin: Mors et vita in manu linguæ; qui diligunt eam comedent fructus ejus.

verses.text: He that hath found a good wife, hath found a good thing, and shall receive a pleasure from the Lord. He that driveth away a good wife, driveth away a good thing: but he that keepeth an adulteress, is foolish and wicked.
verses.textLatin: Qui invenit mulierem bonam invenit bonum, et hauriet jucunditatem a Domino. Qui expellit mulierem bonam expellit bonum; qui autem tenet adulteram stultus est et impius.

verses.text: The poor will speak with supplications, and the rich will speak roughly.
verses.textLatin: Cum obsecrationibus loquetur pauper, et dives effabitur rigide.

verses.text: A man amiable in society, shall be more friendly than a brother.
verses.textLatin: Vir amabilis ad societatem magis amicus erit quam frater.

verses.text: Better  is the poor man, that walketh in his simplicity, than a rich man that is perverse in his lips, and unwise.
verses.textLatin: Melior est pauper qui ambulat in simplicitate sua quam dives torquens labia sua, et insipiens.

verses.text: Where there is no knowledge of the soul, there is no good: and he that is hasty with his feet shall stumble.
verses.textLatin: Ubi non est scientia animæ, non est bonum, et qui festinus est pedibus offendet.

verses.text: The folly of a man supplanteth his steps: and he fretteth in his mind against God.
verses.textLatin: Stultitia hominis supplantat gressus ejus, et contra Deum fervet animo suo.

verses.text: Riches make many friends: but from the poor man, even they whom he had, depart.
verses.textLatin: Divitiæ addunt amicos plurimos; a paupere autem et hi quos habuit separantur.

verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished: and he that speaketh lies shall not escape.
verses.textLatin: Testis falsus non erit impunitus, et qui mendacia loquitur non effugiet.

verses.text: Many honour the person of him that is mighty, and are friends of him that giveth gifts.
verses.textLatin: Multi colunt personam potentis, et amici sunt dona tribuentis.

verses.text: The brethren of the poor man hate him: moreover also his friends have departed far from him. He that followeth after words only, shall have nothing.
verses.textLatin: Fratres hominis pauperis oderunt eum; insuper et amici procul recesserunt ab eo. Qui tantum verba sectatur nihil habebit;

verses.text: But he that possesseth a mind, loveth his own soul, and he that keepeth prudence shall find good things.
verses.textLatin: qui autem possessor est mentis diligit animam suam, et custos prudentiæ inveniet bona.

verses.text: A false witness shall not be unpunished: and he that speaketh lies, shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Falsus testis non erit impunitus, et qui loquitur mendacia peribit.

verses.text: Delicacies are not seemly for a fool: nor for a servant to have rule over princes.
verses.textLatin: Non decent stultum deliciæ, nec servum dominari principibus.

verses.text: The learning of a man is known by patience: and his glory is to pass over wrongs.
verses.textLatin: Doctrina viri per patientiam noscitur, et gloria ejus est iniqua prætergredi.

verses.text: As the roaring of a lion, so also is the anger of a king: and his cheerfulness as the dew upon the grass.
verses.textLatin: Sicut fremitus leonis, ita et regis ira, et sicut ros super herbam, ita et hilaritas ejus.

verses.text: A foolish son is the grief of his father: and a wrangling wife is like a roof continually dropping through.
verses.textLatin: Dolor patris filius stultus, et tecta jugiter perstillantia litigiosa mulier.

verses.text: House and riches are given by parents: but a prudent wife is properly from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Domus et divitiæ dantur a parentibus; a Domino autem proprie uxor prudens.

verses.text: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep, and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
verses.textLatin: Pigredo immittit soporem, et anima dissoluta esuriet.

verses.text: He that keepeth the commandment, keepeth his own soul: but he that neglecteth his own way, shall die.
verses.textLatin: Qui custodit mandatum custodit animam suam; qui autem negligit viam suam mortificabitur.

verses.text: He that hath mercy on the poor, lendeth to the Lord: and he will repay him.
verses.textLatin: Fœneratur Domino qui miseretur pauperis, et vicissitudinem suam reddet ei.

verses.text: Chastise thy son, despair not: but to the killing of him set not thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Erudi filium tuum; ne desperes: ad interfectionem autem ejus ne ponas animam tuam.

verses.text: He that is impatient, shall suffer damage: and when he shall take away he shall add another thing.
verses.textLatin: Qui impatiens est sustinebit damnum, et cum rapuerit, aliud apponet.

verses.text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayst be wise in thy latter end.
verses.textLatin: Audi consilium, et suscipe disciplinam, ut sis sapiens in novissimis tuis.

verses.text: There are many thoughts in the heart of a man: but the will of the Lord shall stand firm.
verses.textLatin: Multæ cogitationes in corde viri; voluntas autem Domini permanebit.

verses.text: A needy man is merciful: and better is the poor than the lying man.
verses.textLatin: Homo indigens misericors est, et melior est pauper quam vir mendax.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is unto life: and he shall abide in fulness without being visited with evil.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini ad vitam, et in plenitudine commorabitur absque visitatione pessima.

verses.text: The slothful hideth his hand under his armpit, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Abscondit piger manum suam sub ascella, nec ad os suum applicat eam.

verses.text: The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser: but if thou rebuke a wise man he will understand discipline.
verses.textLatin: Pestilente flagellato stultus sapientior erit; si autem corripueris sapientem, intelliget disciplinam.

verses.text: He that afflicteth his father, and chaseth away his mother, is infamous and unhappy.
verses.textLatin: Qui affligit patrem, et fugat matrem, ignominiosus est et infelix.

verses.text: Cease not, O my son, to hear instruction, and be not ignorant of the words of knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Non cesses, fili, audire doctrinam, nec ignores sermones scientiæ.

verses.text: An unjust witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Testis iniquus deridet judicium, et os impiorum devorat iniquitatem.

verses.text: Judgments are prepared for scorners: and striking hammers for the bodies of fools.
verses.textLatin: Parata sunt derisoribus judicia, et mallei percutientes stultorum corporibus.

verses.text: Wine  is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness riotous: whosoever is delighted therewith shall not be wise.
verses.textLatin: Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas: quicumque his delectatur non erit sapiens.

verses.text: As the roaring of a lion, so also is the dread of a king: he that provoketh him, sinneth against his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Sicut rugitus leonis, ita et terror regis: qui provocat eum peccat in animam suam.

verses.text: It is an honour for a man to separate himself from quarrels: but all fools are meddling with reproaches.
verses.textLatin: Honor est homini qui separat se a contentionibus; omnes autem stulti miscentur contumeliis.

verses.text: Because of the cold the sluggard would not plough: he shall beg therefore in the summer, and it shall not be given him.
verses.textLatin: Propter frigus piger arare noluit; mendicabit ergo æstate, et non dabitur illi.

verses.text: Counsel in the heart of a man is like deep water: but a wise man will draw it out.
verses.textLatin: Sicut aqua profunda, sic consilium in corde viri; sed homo sapiens exhauriet illud.

verses.text: Many men are called merciful: but who shall find a faithful man?
verses.textLatin: Multi homines misericordes vocantur; virum autem fidelem quis inveniet?

verses.text: The just that walketh in his simplicity, shall leave behind him blessed children.
verses.textLatin: Justus qui ambulat in simplicitate sua beatos post se filios derelinquet.

verses.text: The king, that sitteth on the throne of judgment, scattereth away all evil with his look.
verses.textLatin: Rex qui sedet in solio judicii dissipat omne malum intuitu suo.

verses.text: Who can say: My heart is clean, I am pure from sin?
verses.textLatin: Quis potest dicere: Mundum est cor meum; purus sum a peccato?

verses.text: Diverse weights and diverse measures, both are abominable before God.
verses.textLatin: Pondus et pondus, mensura et mensura: utrumque abominabile est apud Deum.

verses.text: By his inclinations a child is known, if his works be clean and right.
verses.textLatin: Ex studiis suis intelligitur puer, si munda et recta sint opera ejus.

verses.text: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the Lord hath made them both.
verses.textLatin: Aurem audientem, et oculum videntem: Dominus fecit utrumque.

verses.text: Love not sleep, lest poverty oppress thee: open thy eyes, and be filled with bread.
verses.textLatin: Noli diligere somnum, ne te egestas opprimat: aperi oculos tuos, et saturare panibus.

verses.text: It is nought, it is nought, saith every buyer: and when he is gone away, then he will boast.
verses.textLatin: Malum est, malum est, dicit omnis emptor; et cum recesserit, tunc gloriabitur.

verses.text: There is gold, and a multitude of jewels: but the lips of knowledge are a precious vessel.
verses.textLatin: Est aurum et multitudo gemmarum, et vas pretiosum labia scientiæ.

verses.text: Take away the garment of him that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for strangers.
verses.textLatin: Tolle vestimentum ejus qui fidejussor extitit alieni, et pro extraneis aufer pignus ab eo.

verses.text: The bread of lying is sweet to a man: but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
verses.textLatin: Suavis est homini panis mendacii, et postea implebitur os ejus calculo.

verses.text: Designs are strengthened by counsels: and wars are to be managed by governments.
verses.textLatin: Cogitationes consiliis roborantur, et gubernaculis tractanda sunt bella.

verses.text: Meddle not with him that revealeth secrets, and walketh deceitfully, and openeth wide his lips.
verses.textLatin: Ei qui revelat mysteria, et ambulat fraudulenter, et dilatat labia sua, ne commiscearis.

verses.text: He that curseth his father, and mother, his lamp shall be put out in the midst of darkness.
verses.textLatin: Qui maledicit patri suo et matri, extinguetur lucerna ejus in mediis tenebris:

verses.text: The inheritance gotten hastily in the beginning, in the end shall be without a blessing.
verses.textLatin: hæreditas ad quam festinatur in principio, in novissimo benedictione carebit.

verses.text: Say not: I will return evil: wait for the Lord and he will deliver thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas: Reddam malum: exspecta Dominum, et liberabit te.

verses.text: Diverse weights are an abomination before the Lord: a deceitful balance is not good.
verses.textLatin: Abominatio est apud Dominum pondus et pondus; statera dolosa non est bona.

verses.text: The steps of man are guided by the Lord: but who is the man that can understand his own way?
verses.textLatin: A Domino diriguntur gressus viri: quis autem hominum intelligere potest viam suam?

verses.text: It is ruin to a man to devour holy ones, and after vows to retract.
verses.textLatin: Ruina est homini devorare sanctos, et post vota retractare.

verses.text: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth over them the wheel.
verses.textLatin: Dissipat impios rex sapiens, et incurvat super eos fornicem.

verses.text: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the Lord, which searcheth all the hidden things of the bowels.
verses.textLatin: Lucerna Domini spiraculum hominis, quæ investigat omnia secreta ventris.

verses.text: Mercy and truth preserve the king, and his throne is strengthened by clemency.
verses.textLatin: Misericordia et veritas custodiunt regem, et roboratur clementia thronus ejus.

verses.text: The joy of young men is their strength: and the dignity of old men, their grey hairs.
verses.textLatin: Exsultatio juvenum fortitudo eorum, et dignitas senum canities.

verses.text: The blueness of a wound shall wipe away evils: and stripes in the more inward parts of the belly.
verses.textLatin: Livor vulneris absterget mala, et plagæ in secretioribus ventris.

verses.text: As  the divisions of waters, so the heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord: whithersoever he will he shall turn it.
verses.textLatin: Sicut divisiones aquarum, ita cor regis in manu Domini: quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud.

verses.text: Every way of a man seemeth right to himself: but the Lord weigheth the hearts.
verses.textLatin: Omnis via viri recta sibi videtur: appendit autem corda Dominus.

verses.text: To do mercy and judgment, pleaseth the Lord more than victims.
verses.textLatin: Facere misericordiam et judicium magis placet Domino quam victimæ.

verses.text: Haughtiness of the eyes is the enlarging of the heart: the lamp of the wicked is sin.
verses.textLatin: Exaltatio oculorum est dilatatio cordis; lucerna impiorum peccatum.

verses.text: The thoughts of the industrious always bring forth abundance: but every sluggard is always in want.
verses.textLatin: Cogitationes robusti semper in abundantia; omnis autem piger semper in egestate est.

verses.text: He that gathereth treasures by a lying tongue, is vain and foolish, and shall stumble upon the snares of death.
verses.textLatin: Qui congregat thesauros lingua mendacii vanus et excors est, et impingetur ad laqueos mortis.

verses.text: The robberies of the wicked shall be their downfall, because they would not do judgment.
verses.textLatin: Rapinæ impiorum detrahent eos, quia noluerunt facere judicium.

verses.text: The perverse way of a man is strange: but as for him that is pure, his work is right.
verses.textLatin: Perversa via viri aliena est; qui autem mundus est, rectum opus ejus.

verses.text: It is better to sit in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman, and in a common house.
verses.textLatin: Melius est sedere in angulo domatis, quam cum muliere litigiosa, et in domo communi.

verses.text: The soul of the wicked desireth evil, he will not have pity on his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Anima impii desiderat malum: non miserebitur proximo suo.

verses.text: When a pestilent man is punished, the little one will be wiser: and if he follow the wise, he will receive knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Mulctato pestilente, sapientior erit parvulus, et si sectetur sapientem, sumet scientiam.

verses.text: The just considereth seriously the house of the wicked, that he may withdraw the wicked from evil.
verses.textLatin: Excogitat justus de domo impii, ut detrahat impios a malo.

verses.text: He that stoppeth his ear against the cry of the poor, shall also cry himself and shall not be heard.
verses.textLatin: Qui obturat aurem suam ad clamorem pauperis, et ipse clamabit, et non exaudietur.

verses.text: A secret present quencheth anger: and a gift in the bosom the greatest wrath.
verses.textLatin: Munus absconditum extinguit iras, et donum in sinu indignationem maximam.

verses.text: It is joy to the just to do judgment: and dread to them that work iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Gaudium justo est facere judicium, et pavor operantibus iniquitatem.

verses.text: A man that shall wander out of the way of doctrine, shall abide in the company of the giants.
verses.textLatin: Vir qui erraverit a via doctrinæ in cœtu gigantum commorabitur.

verses.text: He that loveth good cheer, shall be in want: he that loveth wine, and fat things, shall not be rich.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligit epulas in egestate erit; qui amat vinum et pinguia non ditabitur.

verses.text: The wicked is delivered up for the just: and the unjust for the righteous.
verses.textLatin: Pro justo datur impius, et pro rectis iniquus.

verses.text: It is better to dwell in a wilderness, than with a quarrelsome and passionate woman.
verses.textLatin: Melius est habitare in terra deserta quam cum muliere rixosa et iracunda.

verses.text: There is a treasure to be desired, and oil in the dwelling of the just: and the foolish man shall spend it.
verses.textLatin: Thesaurus desiderabilis, et oleum in habitaculo justi: et imprudens homo dissipabit illud.

verses.text: He that followeth justice and mercy, shall find life, justice, and glory.
verses.textLatin: Qui sequitur justitiam et misericordiam inveniet vitam, justitiam, et gloriam.

verses.text: The wise man hath scaled the city of the strong, and hath cast down the strength of the confidence thereof.
verses.textLatin: Civitatem fortium ascendit sapiens, et destruxit robur fiduciæ ejus.

verses.text: He that keepeth his mouth and his tongue, keepeth his soul from distress.
verses.textLatin: Qui custodit os suum et linguam suam custodit ab angustiis animam suam.

verses.text: The proud and the arrogant is called ignorant, who in anger worketh pride.
verses.textLatin: Superbus et arrogans vocatur indoctus, qui in ira operatur superbiam.

verses.text: Desires kill the slothful: for his hands have refused to work at all.
verses.textLatin: Desideria occidunt pigrum: noluerunt enim quidquam manus ejus operari.

verses.text: He longeth and desireth all the day: but he that is just, will give, and will not cease.
verses.textLatin: Tota die concupiscit et desiderat; qui autem justus est, tribuet, et non cessabit.

verses.text: The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable, because they are offered of wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Hostiæ impiorum abominabiles, quia offeruntur ex scelere.

verses.text: A lying witness shall perish: an obedient man shall speak of victory.
verses.textLatin: Testis mendax peribit; vir obediens loquetur victoriam.

verses.text: The wicked man impudently hardeneth his face: but he that is righteous, correcteth his way.
verses.textLatin: Vir impius procaciter obfirmat vultum suum; qui autem rectus est corrigit viam suam.

verses.text: There is no wisdom, there is no prudence, there is no counsel against the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum.

verses.text: The horse is prepared for the day of battle: but the Lord giveth safety.
verses.textLatin: Equus paratur ad diem belli; Dominus autem salutem tribuit.

verses.text: A  GOOD name is better than great riches: and good favour is above silver and gold.
verses.textLatin: Melius est nomen bonum quam divitiæ multæ; super argentum et aurum gratia bona.

verses.text: The rich and poor have met one another: the Lord is the maker of them both.
verses.textLatin: Dives et pauper obviaverunt sibi: utriusque operator est Dominus.

verses.text: The prudent man saw the evil, and hid himself: the simple passed on, and suffered loss.
verses.textLatin: Callidus vidit malum, et abscondit se; innocens pertransiit, et afflictus est damno.

verses.text: The fruit of humility is the fear of the Lord, riches and glory and life.
verses.textLatin: Finis modestiæ timor Domini, divitiæ, et gloria, et vita.

verses.text: Arms and swords are in the way of the perverse: but he that keepeth his own soul departeth far from them.
verses.textLatin: Arma et gladii in via perversi; custos autem animæ suæ longe recedit ab eis.

verses.text: It is a proverb: A young man according to his way, even when he is old he will not depart from it.
verses.textLatin: Proverbium est: adolescens juxta viam suam; etiam cum senuerit, non recedet ab ea.

verses.text: The rich ruleth over the poor: and the borrower is servant to him that lendeth.
verses.textLatin: Dives pauperibus imperat, et qui accipit mutuum servus est fœnerantis.

verses.text: He that soweth iniquity shall reap evils, and with the rod of his anger he shall be consumed.
verses.textLatin: Qui seminat iniquitatem metet mala, et virga iræ suæ consummabitur.

verses.text: He that is inclined to mercy shall be blessed: for of his bread he hath given to the poor. He that maketh presents shall purchase victory and honour: but he carrieth away the souls of the receivers.
verses.textLatin: Qui pronus est ad misericordiam benedicetur: de panibus enim suis dedit pauperi. Victoriam et honorem acquiret qui dat munera; animam autem aufert accipientium.

verses.text: Cast out the scoffer, and contention shall go out with him, and quarrels and reproaches shall cease.
verses.textLatin: Ejice derisorem, et exibit cum eo jurgium, cessabuntque causæ et contumeliæ.

verses.text: He that loveth cleanness of heart, for the grace of his lips shall have the king for his friend.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligit cordis munditiam, propter gratiam labiorum suorum habebit amicum regem.

verses.text: The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge: and the words of the unjust are overthrown.
verses.textLatin: Oculi Domini custodiunt scientiam, et supplantantur verba iniqui.

verses.text: The slothful man saith: There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the midst of the streets.
verses.textLatin: Dicit piger: Leo est foris; in medio platearum occidendus sum.

verses.text: The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit: he whom the Lord is angry with, shall fall into it.
verses.textLatin: Fovea profunda os alienæ: cui iratus est Dominus, incidet in eam.

verses.text: Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, and the rod of correction shall drive it away.
verses.textLatin: Stultitia colligata est in corde pueri, et virga disciplinæ fugabit eam.

verses.text: He that oppresseth the poor, to increase his own riches, shall himself give to one that is richer, and shall be in need.
verses.textLatin: Qui calumniatur pauperem ut augeat divitias suas, dabit ipse ditiori, et egebit.

verses.text: Incline thy ear, and hear the words of the wise: and apply thy heart to my doctrine:
verses.textLatin: Inclina aurem tuam, et audi verba sapientium: appone autem cor ad doctrinam meam,

verses.text: Which shall be beautiful for thee, if thou keep it in thy bowels, and it shall flow in thy lips:
verses.textLatin: quæ pulchra erit tibi cum servaveris eam in ventre tuo, et redundabit in labiis tuis:

verses.text: That thy trust may be in the Lord, wherefore I have also shewn it to thee this day.
verses.textLatin: ut sit in Domino fiducia tua, unde et ostendi eam tibi hodie.

verses.text: Behold I have described it to thee three manner of ways, in thoughts and knowledge:
verses.textLatin: Ecce descripsi eam tibi tripliciter, in cogitationibus et scientia:

verses.text: That I might shew thee the certainty, and the words of truth, to answer out of these to them that sent thee.
verses.textLatin: ut ostenderem tibi firmitatem et eloquia veritatis, respondere ex his illis qui miserunt te.

verses.text: Do no violence to the poor, because he is poor: and do not oppress the needy in the gate:
verses.textLatin: Non facias violentiam pauperi quia pauper est, neque conteras egenum in porta:

verses.text: Because the Lord will judge his cause, and will afflict them that have afflicted his soul.
verses.textLatin: quia judicabit Dominus causam ejus, et configet eos qui confixerunt animam ejus.

verses.text: Be not a friend to an angry man, and do not walk with a furious man:
verses.textLatin: Noli esse amicus homini iracundo, neque ambules cum viro furioso:

verses.text: Lest perhaps thou learn his ways, and take scandal to thy soul.
verses.textLatin: ne forte discas semitas ejus, et sumas scandalum animæ tuæ.

verses.text: Be not with them that fasten down their hands, and that offer themselves sureties for debts:
verses.textLatin: Noli esse cum his qui defigunt manus suas, et qui vades se offerunt pro debitis:

verses.text: For if thou have not wherewith to restore, what cause is there, that he should take the covering from thy bed?
verses.textLatin: si enim non habes unde restituas, quid causæ est ut tollat operimentum de cubili tuo?

verses.text: Pass not beyond the ancient bounds which thy fathers have set.
verses.textLatin: Ne transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui.

verses.text: Hast thou seen a man swift in his work? he shall stand before kings, and shall not be before those that are obscure.
verses.textLatin: Vidisti virum velocem in opere suo? coram regibus stabit, nec erit ante ignobiles.

verses.text: When  thou shalt sit to eat with a prince, consider diligently what is set before thy face:
verses.textLatin: Quando sederis ut comedas cum principe, diligenter attende quæ apposita sunt ante faciem tuam.

verses.text: And put a knife to thy throat, if it be so that thou have thy soul in thy own power.
verses.textLatin: Et statue cultrum in gutture tuo: si tamen habes in potestate animam tuam.

verses.text: Be not desirous of his meats, in which is the bread of deceit.
verses.textLatin: Ne desideres de cibis ejus, in quo est panis mendacii.

verses.text: Labour not to be rich: but set bounds to thy prudence.
verses.textLatin: Noli laborare ut diteris, sed prudentiæ tuæ pone modum.

verses.text: Lift not up thy eyes to riches which thou canst not have: because they shall make themselves wings like those of an eagle, and shall fly towards heaven.
verses.textLatin: Ne erigas oculos tuos ad opes quas non potes habere, quia facient sibi pennas quasi aquilæ, et volabunt in cælum.

verses.text: Eat not with an envious man, and desire not his meats:
verses.textLatin: Ne comedas cum homine invido, et ne desideres cibos ejus:

verses.text: Because like a soothsayer, and diviner, he thinketh that which he knoweth not. Eat and drink, will he say to thee: and his mind is not with thee.
verses.textLatin: quoniam in similitudinem arioli et conjectoris æstimat quod ignorat. Comede et bibe, dicet tibi; et mens ejus non est tecum.

verses.text: The meats which thou hadst eaten, thou shalt vomit up: and shalt loose thy beautiful words.
verses.textLatin: Cibos quos comederas evomes, et perdes pulchros sermones tuos.

verses.text: Speak not in the ears of fools: because they will despise the instruction of thy speech.
verses.textLatin: In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, qui despicient doctrinam eloquii tui.

verses.text: Touch not the bounds of little ones: and enter not into the field of the fatherless:
verses.textLatin: Ne attingas parvulorum terminos, et agrum pupillorum ne introëas:

verses.text: For their near kinsman is strong: and he will judge their cause against thee.
verses.textLatin: propinquus enim illorum fortis est, et ipse judicabit contra te causam illorum.

verses.text: Let thy heart apply itself to instruction: and thy ears to words of knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Ingrediatur ad doctrinam cor tuum, et aures tuæ ad verba scientiæ.

verses.text: Withhold not correction from a child: for if thou strike him with the rod, he shall not die.
verses.textLatin: Noli subtrahere a puero disciplinam: si enim percusseris eum virga, non morietur.

verses.text: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and deliver his soul from hell.
verses.textLatin: Tu virga percuties eum, et animam ejus de inferno liberabis.

verses.text: My son, if thy mind be wise, my heart shall rejoice with thee:
verses.textLatin: Fili mi, si sapiens fuerit animus tuus, gaudebit tecum cor meum:

verses.text: And my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips shall speak what is right.
verses.textLatin: et exsultabunt renes mei, cum locuta fuerint rectum labia tua.

verses.text: Let not thy heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long:
verses.textLatin: Non æmuletur cor tuum peccatores, sed in timore Domini esto tota die:

verses.text: Because thou shalt have hope in the latter end, and thy expectation shall not be taken away.
verses.textLatin: quia habebis spem in novissimo, et præstolatio tua non auferetur.

verses.text: Hear thou, my son, and be wise: and guide thy mind in the way.
verses.textLatin: Audi, fili mi, et esto sapiens, et dirige in via animum tuum.

verses.text: Be not in the feasts of great drinkers, nor in their revellings, who contribute flesh to eat:
verses.textLatin: Noli esse in conviviis potatorum, nec in comessationibus eorum qui carnes ad vescendum conferunt:

verses.text: Because they that give themselves to drinking, and that club together shall be consumed; and drowsiness shall be clothed with rags.
verses.textLatin: quia vacantes potibus et dantes symbola consumentur, et vestietur pannis dormitatio.

verses.text: Hearken to thy father, that begot thee: and despise not thy mother when she is old.
verses.textLatin: Audi patrem tuum, qui genuit te, et ne contemnas cum senuerit mater tua.

verses.text: Buy truth, and do not sell wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
verses.textLatin: Veritatem eme, et noli vendere sapientiam, et doctrinam, et intelligentiam.

verses.text: The father of the just rejoiceth greatly: he that hath begotten a wise son, shall have joy in him.
verses.textLatin: Exsultat gaudio pater justi; qui sapientem genuit, lætabitur in eo.

verses.text: Let thy father, and thy mother be joyful, and let her rejoice that bore thee.
verses.textLatin: Gaudeat pater tuus et mater tua, et exsultet quæ genuit te.

verses.text: My son, give me thy heart: and let thy eyes keep my ways.
verses.textLatin: Præbe, fili mi, cor tuum mihi, et oculi tui vias meas custodiant.

verses.text: For a harlot is a deep ditch: and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
verses.textLatin: Fovea enim profunda est meretrix, et puteus angustus aliena.

verses.text: She lieth in wait in the way as a robber, and him whom she shall see unwary, she will kill.
verses.textLatin: Insidiatur in via quasi latro, et quos incautos viderit, interficiet.

verses.text: Who hath woe? whose father hath woe? who hath contentions? who falls into pits? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
verses.textLatin: Cui væ? cujus patri væ? cui rixæ? cui foveæ? cui sine causa vulnera? cui suffusio oculorum?

verses.text: Surely they that pass their time in wine, and study to drink off their cups.
verses.textLatin: nonne his qui commorantur in vino, et student calicibus epotandis?

verses.text: Look not upon the wine when it is yellow, when the colour thereof shineth in the glass: it goeth in pleasantly,
verses.textLatin: Ne intuearis vinum quando flavescit, cum splenduerit in vitro color ejus: ingreditur blande,

verses.text: But in the end, it will bite like a snake, and will spread abroad poison like a basilisk.
verses.textLatin: sed in novissimo mordebit ut coluber, et sicut regulus venena diffundet.

verses.text: Thy eyes shall behold strange women, and thy heart shall utter perverse things.
verses.textLatin: Oculi tui videbunt extraneas, et cor tuum loquetur perversa.

verses.text: And thou shalt be as one sleeping in the midst of the sea, and as a pilot fast asleep, when the stern is lost.
verses.textLatin: Et eris sicut dormiens in medio mari, et quasi sopitus gubernator, amisso clavo.

verses.text: And thou shalt say: They have beaten me, but I was not sensible of pain: they drew me, and I felt not: when shall I awake, and find wine again?
verses.textLatin: Et dices: Verberaverunt me, sed non dolui; traxerunt me, et ego non sensi. Quando evigilabo, et rursus vina reperiam?

verses.text: Seek  not to be like evil men, neither desire to be with them:
verses.textLatin: Ne æmuleris viros malos, nec desideres esse cum eis:

verses.text: Because their mind studieth robberies, and their lips speak deceits.
verses.textLatin: quia rapinas meditatur mens eorum, et fraudes labia eorum loquuntur.

verses.text: By wisdom the house shall be built, and by prudence it shall be strengthened.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia ædificabitur domus, et prudentia roborabitur.

verses.text: By instruction the storerooms shall be filled with all precious and most beautiful wealth.
verses.textLatin: In doctrina replebuntur cellaria, universa substantia pretiosa et pulcherrima.

verses.text: A wise man is strong: and a knowing man, stout and valiant.
verses.textLatin: Vir sapiens fortis est, et vir doctus robustus et validus:

verses.text: Because war is managed by due ordering: and there shall be safety where there are many counsels.
verses.textLatin: quia cum dispositione initur bellum, et erit salus ubi multa consilia sunt.

verses.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool, in the gate he shall not open his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Excelsa stulto sapientia; in porta non aperiet os suum.

verses.text: He that deviseth to do evils, shall be called a fool.
verses.textLatin: Qui cogitat mala facere stultus vocabitur:

verses.text: The thought of a fool is sin: and the detracter is the abomination of men.
verses.textLatin: cogitatio stulti peccatum est, et abominatio hominum detractor.

verses.text: If thou lose hope being weary in the day of distress, thy strength shall be diminished.
verses.textLatin: Si desperaveris lassus in die angustiæ, imminuetur fortitudo tua.

verses.text: Deliver them that are led to death: and those that are drawn to death forbear not to deliver.
verses.textLatin: Erue eos qui ducuntur ad mortem, et qui trahuntur ad interitum, liberare ne cesses.

verses.text: If thou say: I have not strength enough: he that seeth into the heart, he understandeth, and nothing deceiveth the keeper of thy soul, and he shall render to a man according to his works.
verses.textLatin: Si dixeris: Vires non suppetunt; qui inspector est cordis ipse intelligit: et servatorem animæ tuæ nihil fallit, reddetque homini juxta opera sua.

verses.text: Eat honey, my son, because it is good, and the honeycomb most sweet to thy throat:
verses.textLatin: Comede, fili mi, mel, quia bonum est, et favum dulcissimum gutturi tuo.

verses.text: So also is the doctrine of wisdom to thy soul: which when thou hast found, thou shalt have hope in the end, and thy hope shall not perish.
verses.textLatin: Sic et doctrina sapientiæ animæ tuæ: quam cum inveneris, habebis in novissimis spem, et spes tua non peribit.

verses.text: Lie not in wait, nor seek after wickedness in the house of the just, nor spoil his rest.
verses.textLatin: Ne insidieris, et quæras impietatem in domo justi, neque vastes requiem ejus.

verses.text: For a just man shall fall seven times and shall rise again: but the wicked shall fall down into evil.
verses.textLatin: Septies enim cadet justus, et resurget: impii autem corruent in malum.

verses.text: When thy enemy shall fall, be not glad, and in his ruin let not thy heart rejoice:
verses.textLatin: Cum ceciderit inimicus tuus ne gaudeas, et in ruina ejus ne exsultet cor tuum:

verses.text: Lest the Lord see, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
verses.textLatin: ne forte videat Dominus, et displiceat ei, et auferat ab eo iram suam.

verses.text: Contend not with the wicked, nor seek to be like the ungodly:
verses.textLatin: Ne contendas cum pessimis, nec æmuleris impios:

verses.text: For evil men have no hope of things to come, and the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
verses.textLatin: quoniam non habent futurorum spem mali, et lucerna impiorum extinguetur.

verses.text: My son, fear the Lord and the king: and have nothing to do with detractors.
verses.textLatin: Time Dominum, fili mi, et regem, et cum detractoribus non commiscearis:

verses.text: For their destruction shall rise suddenly: and who knoweth the ruin of both?
verses.textLatin: quoniam repente consurget perditio eorum, et ruinam utriusque quis novit?

verses.text: These things also to the wise: It is not good to have respect to persons in judgment.
verses.textLatin: Hæc quoque sapientibus. Cognoscere personam in judicio non est bonum.

verses.text: They that say to the wicked man: Thou art just: shall be cursed by the people, and the tribes shall abhor them.
verses.textLatin: Qui dicunt impio: Justus es: maledicent eis populi, et detestabuntur eos tribus.

verses.text: They that rebuke him, shall be praised: and a blessing shall come upon them.
verses.textLatin: Qui arguunt eum laudabuntur, et super ipsos veniet benedictio.

verses.text: He shall kiss the lips, who answereth right words.
verses.textLatin: Labia deosculabitur qui recta verba respondet.

verses.text: Prepare thy work without, and diligently till thy ground: that afterward thou mayst build thy house.
verses.textLatin: Præpara foris opus tuum, et diligenter exerce agrum tuum, ut postea ædifices domum tuam.

verses.text: Be not witness without cause against thy neighbour: and deceive not any man with thy lips.
verses.textLatin: Ne sis testis frustra contra proximum tuum, nec lactes quemquam labiis tuis.

verses.text: Say not: I will do to him as he hath done to me: I will render to every one according to his work.
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas: Quomodo fecit mihi, sic faciam ei; reddam unicuique secundum opus suum.

verses.text: I passed by the field of the slothful man, and by the vineyard of the foolish man:
verses.textLatin: Per agrum hominis pigri transivi, et per vineam viri stulti:

verses.text: And behold it was all filled with nettles, and thorns had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall was broken down.
verses.textLatin: et ecce totum repleverant urticæ, et operuerant superficiem ejus spinæ, et maceria lapidum destructa erat.

verses.text: Which when I had seen, I laid it up in my heart, and by the example I received instruction.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum vidissem, posui in corde meo, et exemplo didici disciplinam.

verses.text: Thou wilt sleep a little, said I, thou wilt slumber a little, thou wilt fold thy hands a little to rest:
verses.textLatin: Parum, inquam, dormies, modicum dormitabis; pauxillum manus conseres ut quiescas:

verses.text: And poverty shall come to thee as a runner, and beggary as an armed man.
verses.textLatin: et veniet tibi quasi cursor egestas, et mendicitas quasi vir armatus.

verses.text: These  are also parables of Solomon, which the men of Ezechias king of Juda copied out.
verses.textLatin: Hæ quoque parabolæ Salomonis, quas transtulerunt viri Ezechiæ regis Juda.

verses.text: It is the glory of God to conceal the word, and the glory of kings to search out the speech.
verses.textLatin: Gloria Dei est celare verbum, et gloria regum investigare sermonem.

verses.text: The heaven above, and the earth beneath, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.textLatin: Cælum sursum, et terra deorsum, et cor regum inscrutabile.

verses.text: Take away the rust from silver, and there shall come forth a most pure vessel:
verses.textLatin: Aufer rubiginem de argento, et egredietur vas purissimum.

verses.text: Take away wickedness from the face of the king, and his throne shall be established with justice.
verses.textLatin: Aufer impietatem de vultu regis, et firmabitur justitia thronus ejus.

verses.text: Appear not glorious before the king, and stand not in the place of great men.
verses.textLatin: Ne gloriosus appareas coram rege, et in loco magnorum ne steteris.

verses.text: For it is better that it should be said to thee: Come up hither; than that thou shouldst be humbled before the prince.
verses.textLatin: Melius est enim ut dicatur tibi: Ascende huc, quam ut humilieris coram principe.

verses.text: The things which thy eyes have seen, utter not hastily in a quarrel: lest afterward thou mayst not be able to make amends, when thou hast dishonoured thy friend.
verses.textLatin: Quæ viderunt oculi tui ne proferas in jurgio cito, ne postea emendare non possis, cum dehonestaveris amicum tuum.

verses.text: Treat thy cause with thy friend, and discover not the secret to a stranger:
verses.textLatin: Causam tuam tracta cum amico tuo, et secretum extraneo ne reveles:

verses.text: Lest he insult over thee, when he hath heard it, and cease not to upbraid thee. Grace and friendship deliver a man: keep these for thyself, lest thou fall under reproach.
