verses.textLatin: Omnia hæc consideravi, et dedi cor meum in cunctis operibus quæ fiunt sub sole. Interdum dominatur homo homini in malum suum.

verses.text: I saw the wicked buried: who also when they were yet living were in the holy place, and were praised in the city as men of just works: but this also is vanity.
verses.textLatin: Vidi impios sepultos, qui etiam cum adhuc viverent in loco sancto erant, et laudabantur in civitate quasi justorum operum. Sed et hoc vanitas est.

verses.text: For because sentence is not speedily pronounced against the evil, the children of men commit evils without any fear.
verses.textLatin: Etenim quia non profertur cito contra malos sententia, absque timore ullo filii hominum perpetrant mala.

verses.text: But though a sinner do evil a hundred times, and by patience be borne withal, I know from thence that it shall be well with them that fear God, who dread his face.
verses.textLatin: Attamen peccator ex eo quod centies facit malum, et per patientiam sustentatur; ego cognovi quod erit bonum timentibus Deum, qui verentur faciem ejus.

verses.text: But let it not be well with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged, but as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus, sed quasi umbra transeant qui non timent faciem Domini.

verses.text: There is also another vanity, which is done upon the earth. There are just men to whom evils happen, as though they had done the works of the wicked: and there are wicked men, who are as secure, as though they had the deeds of the just: but this also I judge most vain.
verses.textLatin: Est et alia vanitas quæ fit super terram: sunt justi quibus mala proveniunt quasi opera egerint impiorum: et sunt impii qui ita securi sunt quasi justorum facta habeant. Sed et hoc vanissimum judico.

verses.text: Therefore I commended mirth, because there was no good for a man under the sun, but to eat, and drink, and be merry, and that he should take nothing else with him of his labour in the days of his life, which God hath given him under the sun.
verses.textLatin: Laudavi igitur lætitiam; quod non esset homini bonum sub sole, nisi quod comederet, et biberet, atque gauderet, et hoc solum secum auferret de labore suo, in diebus vitæ suæ quos dedit ei Deus sub sole.

verses.text: And I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to understand the distraction that is upon earth: for there are some that day and night take no sleep with their eyes.
verses.textLatin: Et apposui cor meum ut scirem sapientiam, et intelligerem distentionem quæ versatur in terra. Est homo qui diebus et noctibus somnum non capit oculis.

verses.text: And I understood that man can find no reason of all those works of God that are done under the sun: and the more he shall labour to seek, so much the less shall he find: yea, though the wise man shall say, that he knoweth it, he shall not be able to find it.
verses.textLatin: Et intellexi quod omnium operum Dei nullam possit homo invenire rationem eorum quæ fiunt sub sole; et quanto plus laboraverit ad quærendum, tanto minus inveniat: etiam si dixerit sapiens se nosse, non poterit reperire.

verses.text: All  these things have I considered in my heart, that I might carefully understand them: there are just men and wise men, and their works are in the hand of God: and yet man knoweth not whether he be worthy of love, or hatred:
verses.textLatin: Omnia hæc tractavi in corde meo, ut curiose intelligerem. Sunt justi atque sapientes, et opera eorum in manu Dei; et tamen nescit homo utrum amore an odio dignus sit.

verses.text: But all things are kept uncertain for the time to come, because all things equally happen to the just and to the wicked, to the good and to the evil, to the clean and to the unclean, to him that offereth victims, and to him that despiseth sacrifices. As the good is, so also is the sinner: as the perjured, so he also that sweareth truth.
verses.textLatin: Sed omnia in futurum servantur incerta, eo quod universa æque eveniant justo et impio, bono et malo, mundo et immundo, immolanti victimas et sacrificia contemnenti. Sicut bonus, sic et peccator; ut perjurus, ita et ille qui verum dejerat.

verses.text: This is a very great evil among all things that are done under the sun, that the same things happen to all men: whereby also the hearts of the children of men are filled with evil, and with contempt while they live, and afterwards they shall be brought down to hell.
verses.textLatin: Hoc est pessimum inter omnia quæ sub sole fiunt: quia eadem cunctis eveniunt. Unde et corda filiorum hominum implentur malitia et contemptu in vita sua, et post hæc ad inferos deducentur.

verses.text: There is no man that liveth always, or that hopeth for this: a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.textLatin: Nemo est qui semper vivat, et qui hujus rei habeat fiduciam; melior est canis vivus leone mortuo.

verses.text: For the living know that they shall die, but the dead know nothing more, neither have they a reward any more: for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.textLatin: Viventes enim sciunt se esse morituros; mortui vero nihil noverunt amplius, nec habent ultra mercedem, quia oblivioni tradita est memoria eorum.

verses.text: Their love also, and their hatred, and their envy are all perished, neither have they any part in this world, and in the work that is done under the sun.
verses.textLatin: Amor quoque, et odium, et invidiæ simul perierunt; nec habent partem in hoc sæculo, et in opere quod sub sole geritur.

verses.text: Go then, and eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with gladness: because thy works please God.
verses.textLatin: Vade ergo, et comede in lætitia panem tuum, et bibe cum gaudio vinum tuum, quia Deo placent opera tua.

verses.text: At all times let thy garments be white, and let not oil depart from thy head.
verses.textLatin: Omni tempore sint vestimenta tua candida, et oleum de capite tuo non deficiat.

verses.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest, all the days of thy unsteady life, which are given to thee under the sun, all the time of thy vanity: for this is thy portion in life, and in thy labour wherewith thou labourest under the sun.
verses.textLatin: Perfruere vita cum uxore quam diligis, cunctis diebus vitæ instabilitatis tuæ, qui dati sunt tibi sub sole omni tempore vanitatis tuæ: hæc est enim pars in vita et in labore tuo quo laboras sub sole.

verses.text: Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly: for neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom, nor knowledge shall be in hell, whither thou art hastening.
verses.textLatin: Quodcumque facere potest manus tua, instanter operare, quia nec opus, nec ratio, nec sapientia, nec scientia erunt apud inferos, quo tu properas.

verses.text: I turned me to another thing, and I saw that under the sun, the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the learned, nor favour to the skilful: but time and chance in all.
verses.textLatin: Verti me ad aliud, et vidi sub sole nec velocium esse cursum, nec fortium bellum, nec sapientium panem, nec doctorum divitias, nec artificum gratiam; sed tempus casumque in omnibus.

verses.text: Man knoweth not his own end: but as fishes are taken with the hook, and as birds are caught with the snare, so men are taken in the evil time, when it shall suddenly come upon them.
verses.textLatin: Nescit homo finem suum; sed sicut pisces capiuntur hamo, et sicut aves laqueo comprehenduntur, sic capiuntur homines in tempore malo, cum eis extemplo supervenerit.

verses.text: This wisdom also I have seen under the sun, and it seemed to me to be very great:
verses.textLatin: Hanc quoque sub sole vidi sapientiam, et probavi maximam:

verses.text: A little city, and few men in it: there came against it a great king, and invested it, and built bulwarks round about it, and the siege was perfect.
verses.textLatin: civitas parva, et pauci in ea viri; venit contra eam rex magnus, et vallavit eam, exstruxitque munitiones per gyrum, et perfecta est obsidio.

verses.text: Now there was found in it a man poor and wise, and he delivered the city by his wisdom, and no man afterward remembered that poor man.
verses.textLatin: Inventusque est in ea vir pauper et sapiens, et liberavit urbem per sapientiam suam; et nullus deinceps recordatus est hominis illius pauperis.

verses.text: And I said that wisdom is better than strength: how then is the wisdom of the poor man slighted, and his words not heard?
verses.textLatin: Et dicebam ego meliorem esse sapientiam fortitudine. Quomodo ergo sapientia pauperis contempta est, et verba ejus non sunt audita?

verses.text: The words of the wise are heard in silence, more than the cry of a prince among fools.
verses.textLatin: Verba sapientium audiuntur in silentio, plus quam clamor principis inter stultos.

verses.text: Better is wisdom, than weapons of war: and he that shall offend in one, shall lose many good things.
verses.textLatin: Melior est sapientia quam arma bellica; et qui in uno peccaverit, multa bona perdet.

verses.text: Dying  flies spoil the sweetness of the ointment. Wisdom and glory is more precious than a small and shortlived folly.
verses.textLatin: Muscæ morientes perdunt suavitatem unguenti. Pretiosior est sapientia et gloria, parva et ad tempus stultitia.

verses.text: The heart of a wise man is in his right hand, and the heart of a fool is in his left hand.
verses.textLatin: Cor sapientis in dextera ejus, et cor stulti in sinistra illius.

verses.text: Yea, and the fool when he walketh in the way, whereas he himself is a fool, esteemeth all men fools.
verses.textLatin: Sed et in via stultus ambulans, cum ipse insipiens sit, omnes stultos æstimat.

verses.text: If the spirit of him that hath power, ascend upon thee, leave not thy place: because care will make the greatest sins to cease.
verses.textLatin: Si spiritus potestatem habentis ascenderit super te, locum tuum ne demiseris, quia curatio faciet cessare peccata maxima.

verses.text: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as it were by an error proceeding from the face of the prince:
verses.textLatin: Est malum quod vidi sub sole, quasi per errorem egrediens a facie principis:

verses.text: A fool set in high dignity, and the rich sitting beneath.
verses.textLatin: positum stultum in dignitate sublimi, et divites sedere deorsum.

verses.text: I have seen servants upon horses: and princes walking on the ground as servants.
verses.textLatin: Vidi servos in equis, et principes ambulantes super terram quasi servos.

verses.text: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.textLatin: Qui fodit foveam incidet in eam, et qui dissipat sepem mordebit eum coluber.

verses.text: He that removeth stones, shall be hurt by them: and he that cutteth trees, shall be wounded by them.
verses.textLatin: Qui transfert lapides affligetur in eis, et qui scindit ligna vulnerabitur ab eis.

verses.text: If the iron be blunt, and be not as before, but be made blunt, with much labour it shall be sharpened: and after industry shall follow wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Si retusum fuerit ferrum, et hoc non ut prius, sed hebetatum fuerit, multo labore exacuetur, et post industriam sequetur sapientia.

verses.text: If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly.
verses.textLatin: Si mordeat serpens in silentio, nihil eo minus habet qui occulte detrahit.

verses.text: The words of the mouth of a wise man are grace: but the lips of a fool shall throw him down headlong.
verses.textLatin: Verba oris sapientis gratia, et labia insipientis præcipitabunt eum;

verses.text: The beginning of his words is folly, and the end of his talk is a mischievous error.
verses.textLatin: initium verborum ejus stultitia, et novissimum oris illius error pessimus.

verses.text: A fool multiplieth words. A man cannot tell what hath been before him: and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.textLatin: Stultus verba multiplicat. Ignorat homo quid ante se fuerit; et quid post se futurum sit, quis ei poterit indicare?

verses.text: The labour of fools shall afflict them that know not how to go to the city.
verses.textLatin: Labor stultorum affliget eos, qui nesciunt in urbem pergere.

verses.text: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and when the princes eat in the morning.
verses.textLatin: Væ tibi, terra, cujus rex puer est, et cujus principes mane comedunt.

verses.text: Blessed is the land, whose king is noble, and whose princes eat in due season for refreshment, and not for riotousness.
verses.textLatin: Beata terra cujus rex nobilis est, et cujus principes vescuntur in tempore suo, ad reficiendum, et non ad luxuriam.

verses.text: By slothfulness a building shall be brought down, and through the weakness of hands, the house shall drop through.
verses.textLatin: In pigritiis humiliabitur contignatio, et in infirmitate manuum perstillabit domus.

verses.text: For laughter they make bread, and wine that the living may feast: and all things obey money.
verses.textLatin: In risum faciunt panem et vinum ut epulentur viventes; et pecuniæ obediunt omnia.

verses.text: Detract not the king, no not in thy thought; and speak not evil of the rich man in thy private chamber: because even the birds of the air will carry thy voice, and he that hath wings will tell what thou hast said.
verses.textLatin: In cogitatione tua regi ne detrahas, et in secreto cubiculi tui ne maledixeris diviti: quia et aves cæli portabunt vocem tuam, et qui habet pennas annuntiabit sententiam.

verses.text: Cast  thy bread upon the running waters: for after a long time thou shalt find it again.
verses.textLatin: Mitte panem tuum super transeuntes aquas, quia post tempora multa invenies illum.

verses.text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight: for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Da partem septem necnon et octo, quia ignoras quid futurum sit mali super terram.

verses.text: If the clouds be full, they will pour out rain upon the earth. If the tree fall to the south, or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be.
verses.textLatin: Si repletæ fuerint nubes, imbrem super terram effundent. Si ceciderit lignum ad austrum aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit.

verses.text: He that observeth the wind, shall not sow: and he that considereth the clouds, shall never reap.
verses.textLatin: Qui observat ventum non seminat; et qui considerat nubes numquam metet.

verses.text: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones are joined together in the womb of her that is with child: so thou knowest not the works of God, who is the maker of all.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo ignoras quæ sit via spiritus, et qua ratione compingantur ossa in ventre prægnantis, sic nescis opera Dei, qui fabricator est omnium.

verses.text: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening let not thy hand cease: for thou knowest not which may rather spring up, this or that: and if both together, it shall be the better.
verses.textLatin: Mane semina semen tuum, et vespere ne cesset manus tua: quia nescis quid magis oriatur, hoc aut illud; et si utrumque simul, melius erit.

verses.text: The light is sweet, and it is delightful for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.textLatin: Dulce lumen, et delectabile est oculis videre solem.

verses.text: If a man live many years, and have rejoiced in them all, he must remember the darksome time, and the many days: which when they shall come, the things past shall be accused of vanity.
verses.textLatin: Si annis multis vixerit homo, et in his omnibus lætatus fuerit, meminisse debet tenebrosi temporis, et dierum multorum, qui cum venerint, vanitatis arguentur præterita.

verses.text: Rejoice therefore, O young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart be in that which is good in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart, and in the sight of thy eyes: and know that for all these God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.textLatin: Lætare ergo, juvenis, in adolescentia tua, et in bono sit cor tuum in diebus juventutis tuæ: et ambula in viis cordis tui, et in intuitu oculorum tuorum, et scito quod pro omnibus his adducet te Deus in judicium.

verses.text: Remove anger from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh. For youth and pleasure are vain.
verses.textLatin: Aufer iram a corde tuo, et amove malitiam a carne tua: adolescentia enim et voluptas vana sunt.

verses.text: Remember  thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the time of affliction come, and the years draw nigh of which thou shalt say: They please me not:
verses.textLatin: Memento Creatoris tui in diebus juventutis tuæ, antequam veniat tempus afflictionis, et appropinquent anni de quibus dicas: Non mihi placent;

verses.text: Before the sun, and the light, and the moon, and the stars be darkened, and the clouds return after the rain:
verses.textLatin: antequam tenebrescat sol, et lumen, et luna, et stellæ, et revertantur nubes post pluviam;

verses.text: When the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall stagger, and the grinders shall be idle in a small number, and they that look through the holes shall be darkened:
verses.textLatin: quando commovebuntur custodes domus, et nutabunt viri fortissimi, et otiosæ erunt molentes in minuto numero, et tenebrescent videntes per foramina;

verses.text: And they shall shut the doors in the street, when the grinder’s voice shall be low, and they shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of music shall grow deaf.
verses.textLatin: et claudent ostia in platea, in humilitate vocis molentis, et consurgent ad vocem volucris, et obsurdescent omnes filiæ carminis:

verses.text: And they shall fear high things, and they shall be afraid in the way, the almond tree shall flourish, the locust shall be made fat, and the caper tree shall be destroyed: because man shall go into the house of his eternity, and the mourners shall go round about in the street.
verses.textLatin: excelsa quoque timebunt, et formidabunt in via. Florebit amygdalus, impinguabitur locusta, et dissipabitur capparis, quoniam ibit homo in domum æternitatis suæ, et circuibunt in platea plangentes.

verses.text: Before the silver cord be broken, and the golden fillet shrink back, and the pitcher be crushed at the fountain, and the wheel be broken upon the cistern,
verses.textLatin: Antequam rumpatur funiculus argenteus, et recurrat vitta aurea, et conteratur hydria super fontem, et confringatur rota super cisternam,

verses.text: And the dust return into its earth, from whence it was, and the spirit return to God, who gave it.
verses.textLatin: et revertatur pulvis in terram suam unde erat, et spiritus redeat ad Deum, qui dedit illum.

verses.text: Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes, and all things are vanity.
verses.textLatin: Vanitas vanitatum, dixit Ecclesiastes, et omnia vanitas.

verses.text: And whereas Ecclesiastes was very wise, he taught the people, and declared the things that he had done: and seeking out, he set forth many parables.
verses.textLatin: Cumque esset sapientissimus Ecclesiastes, docuit populum, et enarravit quæ fecerat; et investigans composuit parabolas multas.

verses.text: He sought profitable words, and wrote words most right, and full of truth.
verses.textLatin: Quæsivit verba utilia, et conscripsit sermones rectissimos ac veritate plenos.

verses.text: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails deeply fastened in, which by the counsel of masters are given from one shepherd.
verses.textLatin: Verba sapientium sicut stimuli, et quasi clavi in altum defixi, quæ per magistrorum consilium data sunt a pastore uno.

verses.text: More than these, my son, require not. Of making many books there is no end: and much study is an affliction of the flesh.
verses.textLatin: His amplius, fili mi, ne requiras. Faciendi plures libros nullus est finis; frequensque meditatio, carnis afflictio est.

verses.text: Let us all hear together the conclusion of the discourse. Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is all man:
verses.textLatin: Finem loquendi pariter omnes audiamus. Deum time, et mandata ejus observa: hoc est enim omnis homo,

verses.text: And all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil.
verses.textLatin: et cuncta quæ fiunt adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum, sive malum illud sit.

verses.text: Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth: for thy breasts are better than wine,
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Osculetur me osculo oris sui; quia meliora sunt ubera tua vino,

verses.text: Smelling sweet of the best ointments. Thy name is as oil poured out: therefore young maidens have loved thee.
verses.textLatin: Chorus adolescentularum fragrantia unguentis optimis. Oleum effusum nomen tuum; ideo adolescentulæ dilexerunt te.

verses.text: Draw me: we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments. The king hath brought me into his storerooms: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, remembering thy breasts more than wine: the rightous love thee.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Trahe me, post te curremus in odorem unguentorum tuorum. Introduxit me rex in cellaria sua; exsultabimus et lætabimur in te, memores uberum tuorum super vinum. Recti diligunt te.

verses.text: I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Cedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Nigra sum, sed formosa, filiæ Jerusalem, sicut tabernacula Cedar, sicut pelles Salomonis.

verses.text: Do not consider me that I am brown, because the sun hath altered my colour: the sons of my mother have fought against me, they have made me the keeper in the vineyards: my vineyard I have not kept.
verses.textLatin: Nolite me considerare quod fusca sim, quia decoloravit me sol. Filii matris meæ pugnaverunt contra me; posuerunt me custodem in vineis: vineam meam non custodivi.

verses.text: Shew me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou liest in the midday, lest I begin to wander after the flocks of thy companions.
verses.textLatin: Indica mihi, quem diligit anima mea, ubi pascas, ubi cubes in meridie, ne vagari incipiam post greges sodalium tuorum.

verses.text: If thou know not thyself, O fairest among women, go forth, and follow after the steps of the flocks, and feed thy kids beside the tents of the shepherds.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Si ignoras te, o pulcherrima inter mulieres, egredere, et abi post vestigia gregum, et pasce hædos tuos juxta tabernacula pastorum.

verses.text: To my company of horsemen, in Pharao’s chariots, have I likened thee, O my love.
verses.textLatin: Equitatui meo in curribus Pharaonis assimilavi te, amica mea.

verses.text: Thy cheeks are beautiful as the turtledove’s, thy neck as jewels.
verses.textLatin: Pulchræ sunt genæ tuæ sicut turturis; collum tuum sicut monilia.

verses.text: We will make thee chains of gold, inlaid with silver.
verses.textLatin: Murenulas aureas faciemus tibi, vermiculatas argento.

verses.text: While the king was at his repose, my spikenard sent forth the odour thereof.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Dum esset rex in accubitu suo, nardus mea dedit odorem suum.

verses.text: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts.
verses.textLatin: Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi; inter ubera mea commorabitur.

verses.text: A cluster of cypress my love is to me, in the vineyards of Engaddi.
verses.textLatin: Botrus cypri dilectus meus mihi in vineis Engaddi.

verses.text: Behold thou art fair, O my love, behold thou art fair, thy eyes are as those of doves.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Ecce tu pulchra es, amica mea! ecce tu pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum.

verses.text: Behold thou art fair, my beloved, and comely. Our bed is flourishing.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Ecce tu pulcher es, dilecte mi, et decorus! Lectulus noster floridus.

verses.text: The beams of our houses are of cedar, our rafters of cypress trees.
verses.textLatin: Tigna domorum nostrarum cedrina, laquearia nostra cypressina.

verses.text: I am the flower of the field, and the lily of the valleys.
verses.textLatin: Ego flos campi, et lilium convallium.

verses.text: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Sicut lilium inter spinas, sic amica mea inter filias.

verses.text: As the apple tree among the trees of the woods, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow, whom I desired: and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Sicut malus inter ligna silvarum, sic dilectus meus inter filios. Sub umbra illius quem desideraveram sedi, et fructus ejus dulcis gutturi meo.

verses.text: He brought me into the cellar of wine, he set in order charity in me.
verses.textLatin: Introduxit me in cellam vinariam; ordinavit in me caritatem.

verses.text: Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love.
verses.textLatin: Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo.

verses.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
verses.textLatin: Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.

verses.text: I adjure you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and the harts of the field, that you stir not up, nor make the beloved to awake, till she please.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit.

verses.text: The voice of my beloved, behold he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping over the hills.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Vox dilecti mei; ecce iste venit, saliens in montibus, transiliens colles.

verses.text: My beloved is like a roe, or a young hart. Behold he standeth behind our wall, looking through the windows, looking through the lattices.
verses.textLatin: Similis est dilectus meus capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum. En ipse stat post parietem nostrum, respiciens per fenestras, prospiciens per cancellos.

verses.text: Behold my beloved speaketh to me: Arise, make haste, my love, my dove, my beautiful one, and come.
verses.textLatin: En dilectus meus loquitur mihi. Sponsus Surge, propera, amica mea, columba mea, formosa mea, et veni:

verses.text: For winter is now past, the rain is over and gone.
verses.textLatin: jam enim hiems transiit; imber abiit, et recessit.

verses.text: The flowers have appeared in our land, the time of pruning is come: the voice of the turtle is heard in our land:
verses.textLatin: Flores apparuerunt in terra nostra; tempus putationis advenit: vox turturis audita est in terra nostra;

verses.text: The fig tree hath put forth her green figs: the vines in flower yield their sweet smell. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come:
verses.textLatin: ficus protulit grossos suos; vineæ florentes dederunt odorem suum. Surge, amica mea, speciosa mea, et veni:

verses.text: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow places of the wall, shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely.
verses.textLatin: columba mea, in foraminibus petræ, in caverna maceriæ, ostende mihi faciem tuam, sonet vox tua in auribus meis: vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora.

verses.text: Catch us the little foxes that destroy the vines: for our vineyard hath flourished.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Capite nobis vulpes parvulas quæ demoliuntur vineas: nam vinea nostra floruit.

verses.text: My beloved to me, and I to him who feedeth among the lilies,
verses.textLatin: Dilectus meus mihi, et ego illi, qui pascitur inter lilia,

verses.text: Till the day break, and the shadows retire. Return: be like, my beloved, to a roe, or to a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
verses.textLatin: donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbræ. Revertere; similis esto, dilecte mi, capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum super montes Bether.

verses.text: In my bed by night I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, and found him not.
verses.textLatin: In lectulo meo, per noctes, quæsivi quem diligit anima mea: quæsivi illum, et non inveni.

verses.text: I will rise, and will go about the city: in the streets and the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, and I found him not.
verses.textLatin: Surgam, et circuibo civitatem: per vicos et plateas quæram quem diligit anima mea: quæsivi illum, et non inveni.

verses.text: The watchmen who keep the city, found me: Have you seen him, whom my soul loveth?
verses.textLatin: Invenerunt me vigiles qui custodiunt civitatem: Num quem diligit anima mea vidistis?

verses.text: When I had a little passed by them, I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him: and I will not let him go, till I bring him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that bore me.
verses.textLatin: Paululum cum pertransissem eos, inveni quem diligit anima mea: tenui eum, nec dimittam, donec introducam illum in domum matris meæ, et in cubiculum genetricis meæ.

verses.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes and the harts of the fields, that you stir not up, nor awake my beloved, till she please.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.

verses.text: Who is she that goeth up by the desert, as a pillar of smoke of aromatical spices, of myrrh, and frankincense, and of all the powders of the perfumer?
verses.textLatin: Chorus Quæ est ista quæ ascendit per desertum sicut virgula fumi ex aromatibus myrrhæ, et thuris, et universi pulveris pigmentarii?

verses.text: Behold threescore valiant ones of the most valiant of Israel, surrounded the bed of Solomon?
verses.textLatin: En lectulum Salomonis sexaginta fortes ambiunt ex fortissimis Israël,

verses.text: All holding swords, and most expert in war: every man’s sword upon his thigh, because of fears in the night.
verses.textLatin: omnes tenentes gladios, et ad bella doctissimi: uniuscujusque ensis super femur suum propter timores nocturnos.

verses.text: King Solomon hath made him a litter of the wood of Libanus:
verses.textLatin: Ferculum fecit sibi rex Salomon de lignis Libani;

verses.text: The pillars thereof he made of silver, the seat of gold, the going up of purple: the midst he covered with charity for the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: columnas ejus fecit argenteas, reclinatorium aureum, ascensum purpureum; media caritate constravit, propter filias Jerusalem.

verses.text: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and see king Solomon in the diadem, wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the joy of his heart.
verses.textLatin: Egredimini et videte, filiæ Sion, regem Salomonem in diademate quo coronavit illum mater sua in die desponsationis illius, et in die lætitiæ cordis ejus.

verses.text: How beautiful art thou, my love, how beautiful art thou! thy eyes are doves’ eyes, besides what is hid within. Thy hair is as flocks of goats, which come up from mount Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Quam pulchra es, amica mea! quam pulchra es! Oculi tui columbarum, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet. Capilli tui sicut greges caprarum quæ ascenderunt de monte Galaad.

verses.text: Thy teeth as flocks of sheep, that are shorn, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.
verses.textLatin: Dentes tui sicut greges tonsarum quæ ascenderunt de lavacro; omnes gemellis fœtibus, et sterilis non est inter eas.

verses.text: Thy lips are as a scarlet lace: and thy speech sweet. Thy cheeks are as a piece of a pomegranate, besides that which lieth hid within.
verses.textLatin: Sicut vitta coccinea labia tua, et eloquium tuum dulce. Sicut fragmen mali punici, ita genæ tuæ, absque eo quod intrinsecus latet.

verses.text: Thy neck is as the tower of David, which is built with bulwarks: a thousand bucklers hang upon it, all the armour of valiant men.
verses.textLatin: Sicut turris David collum tuum, quæ ædificata est cum propugnaculis; mille clypei pendent ex ea, omnis armatura fortium.

verses.text: Thy two breasts like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
verses.textLatin: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, capreæ gemelli, qui pascuntur in liliis.

verses.text: Till the day break, and the shadows retire, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
verses.textLatin: Donec aspiret dies, et inclinentur umbræ, vadam ad montem myrrhæ, et ad collem thuris.

verses.text: Thou art all fair, O my love, and there is not a spot in thee.
verses.textLatin: Tota pulchra es, amica mea, et macula non est in te.

verses.text: Come from Libanus, my spouse, come from Libanus, come: thou shalt be crowned from the top of Amana, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.textLatin: Veni de Libano, sponsa mea: veni de Libano, veni, coronaberis: de capite Amana, de vertice Sanir et Hermon, de cubilibus leonum, de montibus pardorum.

verses.text: Thou hast wounded my heart, my sister, my spouse, thou hast wounded my heart with one of thy eyes, and with one hair of thy neck.
verses.textLatin: Vulnerasti cor meum, soror mea, sponsa; vulnerasti cor meum in uno oculorum tuorum, et in uno crine colli tui.

verses.text: How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister, my spouse! thy breasts are more beautiful than wine, and the sweet smell of thy ointments above all aromatical spices.
verses.textLatin: Quam pulchræ sunt mammæ tuæ, soror mea sponsa! pulchriora sunt ubera tua vino, et odor unguentorum tuorum super omnia aromata.

verses.text: Thy lips, my spouse, are as a dropping honeycomb, honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments, as the smell of frankincense.
verses.textLatin: Favus distillans labia tua, sponsa; mel et lac sub lingua tua: et odor vestimentorum tuorum sicut odor thuris.

verses.text: My sister, my spouse, is a garden enclosed, a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed up.
verses.textLatin: Hortus conclusus soror mea, sponsa, hortus conclusus, fons signatus.

verses.text: Thy plants are a paradise of pomegranates with the fruits of the orchard. Cypress with spikenard.
verses.textLatin: Emissiones tuæ paradisus malorum punicorum, cum pomorum fructibus, cypri cum nardo.

verses.text: Spikenard and saffron, sweet cane and cinnamon, with all the trees of Libanus, myrrh and aloes with all the chief perfumes.
verses.textLatin: Nardus et crocus, fistula et cinnamomum, cum universis lignis Libani; myrrha et aloë, cum omnibus primis unguentis.

verses.text: The fountain of gardens: the well of living waters, which run with a strong stream from Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Fons hortorum, puteus aquarum viventium, quæ fluunt impetu de Libano.

verses.text: Arise, O north wind, and come, O south wind, blow through my garden, and let the aromatical spices thereof flow.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Surge, aquilo, et veni, auster: perfla hortum meum, et fluant aromata illius.

verses.text: Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat the fruit of his apple trees. I am come into my garden, O my sister, my spouse, I have gathered my myrrh, with my aromatical spices: I have eaten the honeycomb with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved.
verses.textLatin: Veniat dilectus meus in hortum suum, et comedat fructum pomorum suorum. Sponsus Veni in hortum meum, soror mea, sponsa; messui myrrham meam cum aromatibus meis; comedi favum cum melle meo; bibi vinum meum cum lacte meo; comedite, amici, et bibite, et inebriamini, carissimi.

verses.text: I sleep, and my heart watcheth: the voice of my beloved knocking: Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is full of dew, and my locks of the drops of the nights.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Ego dormio, et cor meum vigilat. Vox dilecti mei pulsantis: Sponsus Aperi mihi, soror mea, amica mea, columba mea, immaculata mea, quia caput meum plenum est rore, et cincinni mei guttis noctium.

verses.text: I have put off my garment, how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet, how shall I defile them?
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Expoliavi me tunica mea: quomodo induar illa? lavi pedes meos: quomodo inquinabo illos?

verses.text: My beloved put his hand through the key hole, and my bowels were moved at his touch.
verses.textLatin: Dilectus meus misit manum suam per foramen, et venter meus intremuit ad tactum ejus.

verses.text: I arose up to open to my beloved: my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of the choicest myrrh.
verses.textLatin: Surrexi ut aperirem dilecto meo; manus meæ stillaverunt myrrham, et digiti mei pleni myrrha probatissima.

verses.text: I opened the bolt of my door to my beloved: but he had turned aside, and was gone. My soul melted when he spoke: I sought him, and found him not: I called, and he did not answer me.
verses.textLatin: Pessulum ostii mei aperui dilecto meo, at ille declinaverat, atque transierat. Anima mea liquefacta est, ut locutus est; quæsivi, et non inveni illum; vocavi, et non respondit mihi.

verses.text: The keepers that go about the city found me: they struck me: and wounded me: the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.textLatin: Invenerunt me custodes qui circumeunt civitatem; percusserunt me, et vulneraverunt me. Tulerunt pallium meum mihi custodes murorum.

verses.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, that you tell him that I languish with love.
verses.textLatin: Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, si inveneritis dilectum meum, ut nuntietis ei quia amore langueo.

verses.text: What manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, O thou most beautiful among women? what manner of one is thy beloved of the beloved, that thou hast so adjured us?
verses.textLatin: Chorus Qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, o pulcherrima mulierum? qualis est dilectus tuus ex dilecto, quia sic adjurasti nos?

verses.text: My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus; electus ex millibus.

verses.text: His head is as the finest gold: his locks as branches of palm trees, black as a raven.
verses.textLatin: Caput ejus aurum optimum; comæ ejus sicut elatæ palmarum, nigræ quasi corvus.

verses.text: His eyes as doves upon brooks of waters, which are washed with milk, and sit beside the plentiful streams.
verses.textLatin: Oculi ejus sicut columbæ super rivulos aquarum, quæ lacte sunt lotæ, et resident juxta fluenta plenissima.

verses.text: His cheeks are as beds of aromatical spices set by the perfumers. His lips are as lilies dropping choice myrrh.
verses.textLatin: Genæ illius sicut areolæ aromatum, consitæ a pigmentariis. Labia ejus lilia, distillantia myrrham primam.

verses.text: His hands are turned and as of gold, full of hyacinths. His belly as of ivory, set with sapphires.
verses.textLatin: Manus illius tornatiles, aureæ, plenæ hyacinthis. Venter ejus eburneus, distinctus sapphiris.

verses.text: His legs as pillars of marble, that are set upon bases of gold. His form as of Libanus, excellent as the cedars.
verses.textLatin: Crura illius columnæ marmoreæ quæ fundatæ sunt super bases aureas. Species ejus ut Libani, electus ut cedri.

verses.text: His throat most sweet, and he is all lovely: such is my beloved, and he is my friend, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Guttur illius suavissimum, et totus desiderabilis. Talis est dilectus meus, et ipse est amicus meus, filiæ Jerusalem.

verses.text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou most beautiful among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside, and we will seek him with thee?
verses.textLatin: Chorus Quo abiit dilectus tuus, o pulcherrima mulierum? quo declinavit dilectus tuus? et quæremus eum tecum.

verses.text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the bed of aromatical spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Dilectus meus descendit in hortum suum ad areolam aromatum, ut pascatur in hortis, et lilia colligat.

verses.text: I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, who feedeth among the lilies.
verses.textLatin: Ego dilecto meo, et dilectus meus mihi, qui pascitur inter lilia.

verses.text: Thou art beautiful, O my love, sweet and comely as Jerusalem: terrible as an army set in array.
verses.textLatin: SponsusPulchra es, amica mea; suavis, et decora sicut Jerusalem; terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata.

verses.text: Turn away thy eyes from me, for they have made me flee away. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Averte oculos tuos a me, quia ipsi me avolare fecerunt. Capilli tui sicut grex caprarum quæ apparuerunt de Galaad.

verses.text: Thy teeth as a flock of sheep, which come up from the washing, all with twins, and there is none barren among them.
verses.textLatin: Dentes tui sicut grex ovium quæ ascenderunt de lavacro: omnes gemellis fœtibus, et sterilis non est in eis.

verses.text: Thy cheeks are as the bark of a pomegranate, beside what is hidden within thee.
verses.textLatin: Sicut cortex mali punici, sic genæ tuæ, absque occultis tuis.

verses.text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and young maidens without number.
verses.textLatin: Sexaginta sunt reginæ, et octoginta concubinæ, et adolescentularum non est numerus.

verses.text: One is my dove, my perfect one is but one, she is the only one of her mother, the chosen of her that bore her. The daughters saw her, and declared her most blessed: the queens and concubines, and they praised her.
verses.textLatin: Una est columba mea, perfecta mea, una est matris suæ, electa genetrici suæ. Viderunt eam filiæ, et beatissimam prædicaverunt; reginæ et concubinæ, et laudaverunt eam.

verses.text: Who is she that cometh forth as the morning rising, fair as the moon, bright as the sun, terrible as an army set in array?
verses.textLatin: Quæ est ista quæ progreditur quasi aurora consurgens, pulchra ut luna, electa ut sol, terribilis ut castrorum acies ordinata?

verses.text: I went down into the garden of nuts, to see the fruits of the valleys, and to look if the vineyard had flourished, and the pomegranates budded.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Descendi in hortum nucum, ut viderem poma convallium, et inspicerem si floruisset vinea, et germinassent mala punica.

verses.text: I knew not: my soul troubled me for the chariots of Aminadab.
verses.textLatin: Nescivi: anima mea conturbavit me, propter quadrigas Aminadab.

verses.text: Return, return, O Sulamitess: return, return that we may behold thee.
verses.textLatin: Chorus Revertere, revertere, Sulamitis! revertere, revertere ut intueamur te.

verses.text: What  shalt thou see in the Sulamitess but the companies of camps? How beautiful are thy steps in shoes, O prince’s daughter! The joints of thy thighs are like jewels, that are made by the hand of a skilful workman.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Quid videbis in Sulamite, nisi choros castrorum? Chorus Quam pulchri sunt gressus tui in calceamentis, filia principis! Juncturæ femorum tuorum sicut monilia quæ fabricata sunt manu artificis.

verses.text: Thy navel is like a round bowl never wanting cups. Thy belly is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
verses.textLatin: Umbilicus tuus crater tornatilis, numquam indigens poculis. Venter tuus sicut acervus tritici vallatus liliis.

verses.text: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
verses.textLatin: Duo ubera tua sicut duo hinnuli, gemelli capreæ.

verses.text: Thy neck as a tower of ivory. Thy eyes like the fishpools in Hesebon, which are in the gate of the daughter of the multitude. Thy nose is as the tower of Libanus, that looketh toward Damascus.
verses.textLatin: Collum tuum sicut turris eburnea; oculi tui sicut piscinæ in Hesebon quæ sunt in porta filiæ multitudinis. Nasus tuus sicut turris Libani, quæ respicit contra Damascum.

verses.text: Thy head is like Carmel: and the hairs of thy head as the purple of the king bound in the channels.
verses.textLatin: Caput tuum ut Carmelus; et comæ capitis tui sicut purpura regis vincta canalibus.

verses.text: How beautiful art thou, and how comely, my dearest, in delights!
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Quam pulchra es, et quam decora, carissima, in deliciis!

verses.text: Thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
verses.textLatin: Statura tua assimilata est palmæ, et ubera tua botris.

verses.text: I said: I will go up into the palm tree, and will take hold of the fruit thereof: and thy breasts shall be as the clusters of the vine: and the odour of thy mouth like apples.
verses.textLatin: Dixi: Ascendam in palmam, et apprehendam fructus ejus; et erunt ubera tua sicut botri vineæ, et odor oris tui sicut malorum.

verses.text: Thy throat like the best wine, worthy for my beloved to drink, and for his lips and his teeth to ruminate.
verses.textLatin: Guttur tuum sicut vinum optimum, dignum dilecto meo ad potandum, labiisque et dentibus illius ad ruminandum.

verses.text: I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus.

verses.text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field, let us abide in the villages.
verses.textLatin: Veni, dilecte mi, egrediamur in agrum, commoremur in villis.

verses.text: Let us get up early to the vineyards, let us see if the vineyard flourish, if the flowers be ready to bring forth fruits, if the pomegranates flourish: there will I give thee my breasts.
verses.textLatin: Mane surgamus ad vineas: videamus si floruit vinea, si flores fructus parturiunt, si floruerunt mala punica; ibi dabo tibi ubera mea.

verses.text: The mandrakes give a smell. In our gates are all fruits: the new and the old, my beloved, I have kept for thee.
verses.textLatin: Mandragoræ dederunt odorem in portis nostris omnia poma: nova et vetera, dilecte mi, servavi tibi.

verses.text: Who  shall give thee to me for my brother, sucking the breasts of my mother, that I may find thee without, and kiss thee, and now no man may despise me?
verses.textLatin: Quis mihi det te fratrem meum, sugentem ubera matris meæ, ut inveniam te foris, et deosculer te, et jam me nemo despiciat?

verses.text: I will take hold of thee, and bring thee into my mother’s house: there thou shalt teach me, and I will give thee a cup of spiced wine and new wine of my pomegranates.
verses.textLatin: Apprehendam te, et ducam in domum matris meæ: ibi me docebis, et dabo tibi poculum ex vino condito, et mustum malorum granatorum meorum.

verses.text: His left hand under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
verses.textLatin: Læva ejus sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me.

verses.text: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that you stir not up, nor awake my love till she please.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Adjuro vos, filiæ Jerusalem, ne suscitetis, neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, donec ipsa velit.

verses.text: Who is this that cometh up from the desert, flowing with delights, leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple tree I raised thee up: there thy mother was corrupted, there she was defloured that bore thee.
verses.textLatin: Chorus Quæ est ista quæ ascendit de deserto, deliciis affluens, innixa super dilectum suum? Sponsus Sub arbore malo suscitavi te; ibi corrupta est mater tua, ibi violata est genitrix tua.

verses.text: Put me as a seal upon thy heart, as a seal upon thy arm, for love is strong as death, jealousy as hard as hell, the lamps thereof are fire and flames.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Pone me ut signaculum super cor tuum, ut signaculum super brachium tuum, quia fortis est ut mors dilectio, dura sicut infernus æmulatio: lampades ejus lampades ignis atque flammarum.

verses.text: Many waters cannot quench charity, neither can the floods drown it: if a man should give all the substance of his house for love, he shall despise it as nothing.
verses.textLatin: Aquæ multæ non potuerunt extinguere caritatem, nec flumina obruent illam. Si dederit homo omnem substantiam domus suæ pro dilectione, quasi nihil despiciet eam.

verses.text: Our sister is little, and hath no breasts. What shall we do to our sister in the day when she is to be spoken to?
verses.textLatin: Chorus Fratrum Soror nostra parva, et ubera non habet; quid faciemus sorori nostræ in die quando alloquenda est?

verses.text: If she be a wall: let us build upon it bulwarks of silver: if she be a door, let us join it together with boards of cedar.
verses.textLatin: Si murus est, ædificemus super eum propugnacula argentea; si ostium est, compingamus illud tabulis cedrinis.

verses.text: I am a wall: and my breasts are as a tower since I am become in his presence as one finding peace.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Ego murus, et ubera mea sicut turris, ex quo facta sum coram eo, quasi pacem reperiens.

verses.text: The peaceable had a vineyard, in that which hath people: he let out the same to keepers, every man bringeth for the fruit thereof a thousand pieces of silver.
verses.textLatin: Chorus Fratrum Vinea fuit pacifico in ea quæ habet populos: tradidit eam custodibus; vir affert pro fructu ejus mille argenteos.

verses.text: My vineyard is before me. A thousand are for thee, the peaceable, and two hundred for them that keep the fruit thereof.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Vinea mea coram me est. Mille tui pacifici, et ducenti his qui custodiunt fructus ejus.

verses.text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the friends hearken: make me hear thy voice.
verses.textLatin: Sponsus Quæ habitas in hortis, amici auscultant; fac me audire vocem tuam.

verses.text: Flee away, O my beloved, and be like to the roe, and to the young hart upon the mountains of aromatical spices.
verses.textLatin: Sponsa Fuge, dilecte mi, et assimilare capreæ, hinnuloque cervorum super montes aromatum.

verses.text: Love  justice, you that are the judges of the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart.
verses.textLatin: Diligite justitiam, qui judicatis terram. Sentite de Domino in bonitate, et in simplicitate cordis quærite illum:

verses.text: For he is found by them that tempt him not: and he sheweth himself to them that have faith in him.
verses.textLatin: quoniam invenitur ab his qui non tentant illum, apparet autem eis qui fidem habent in illum.

verses.text: For perverse thoughts separate from God: and his power, when it is tried, reproveth the unwise:
verses.textLatin: Perversæ enim cogitationes separant a Deo; probata autem virtus corripit insipientes.

verses.text: For wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam in malevolam animam non introibit sapientia, nec habitabit in corpore subdito peccatis.

verses.text: For the Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from the deceitful, and will withdraw himself from thoughts that are without understanding, and he shall not abide when iniquity cometh in.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus enim sanctus disciplinæ effugiet fictum, et auferet se a cogitationibus quæ sunt sine intellectu, et corripietur a superveniente iniquitate.

verses.text: For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not acquit the evil speaker from his lips: for God is witness of his reins, and he is a true searcher of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
verses.textLatin: Benignus est enim spiritus sapientiæ, et non liberabit maledicum a labiis suis: quoniam renum illius testis est Deus, et cordis illius scrutator est verus, et linguæ ejus auditor.

verses.text: For the Spirit of the Lord hath filled the whole world: and that, which containeth all things, hath knowledge of the voice.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam spiritus Domini replevit orbem terrarum, et hoc quod continet omnia, scientiam habet vocis.

verses.text: Therefore he that speaketh unjust things cannot be hid, neither shall the chastising judgment pass him by.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc qui loquitur iniqua non potest latere, nec præteriet illum corripiens judicium.

verses.text: For inquisition shall be made into the thoughts of the ungodly; and the hearing of his words shall come to God, to the chastising of his iniquities.
verses.textLatin: In cogitationibus enim impii interrogatio erit; sermonum autem illius auditio ad Deum veniet, ad correptionem iniquitatum illius.

verses.text: For the ear of jealousy heareth all things, and the tumult of murmuring shall not be hid.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam auris zeli audit omnia, et tumultus murmurationum non abscondetur.

verses.text: Keep yourselves therefore from murmuring, which profiteth nothing, and refrain your tongue from detraction, for an obscure speech shall not go for nought: and the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul.
verses.textLatin: Custodite ergo vos a murmuratione quæ nihil prodest, et a detractione parcite linguæ: quoniam sermo obscurus in vacuum non ibit, os autem quod mentitur occidit animam.

verses.text: Seek not death in the error of your life, neither procure ye destruction by the works of your hands.
verses.textLatin: Nolite zelare mortem in errore vitæ vestræ, neque acquiratis perditionem in operibus manuum vestrarum.

verses.text: For God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum.

verses.text: For he created all things that they might be: and he made the nations of the earth for health: and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor kingdom of hell upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Creavit enim ut essent omnia, et sanabiles fecit nationes orbis terrarum: et non est in illis medicamentum exterminii, nec inferorum regnum in terra.

verses.text: For justice is perpetual and immortal.
verses.textLatin: Justitia enim perpetua est, et immortalis.

verses.text: But the wicked with works and words have called it to them: and esteeming it a friend have fallen away, and have made a covenant with it: because they are worthy to be of the part thereof.
verses.textLatin: Impii autem manibus et verbis accersierunt illam, et æstimantes illam amicam, defluxerunt; et sponsiones posuerunt ad illam, quoniam digni sunt qui sint ex parte illius.

verses.text: For  they have said, reasoning with themselves, but not right: The time of our life is short and tedious, and in the end of a man there is no remedy, and no man hath been known to have returned from hell:
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt enim cogitantes apud se non recte: Exiguum et cum tædio est tempus vitæ nostræ, et non est refrigerium in fine hominis, et non est qui agnitus sit reversus ab inferis.

verses.text: For we are born of nothing, and after this we shall be as if we had not been: for the breath in our nostrils is smoke: and speech a spark to move our heart,
verses.textLatin: Quia ex nihilo nati sumus, et post hoc erimus tamquam non fuerimus. Quoniam fumus flatus est in naribus nostris, et sermo scintilla ad commovendum cor nostrum:

verses.text: Which being put out, our body shall be ashes, and our spirit shall be poured abroad as soft air, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, which is driven away by the beams of the sun, and overpowered with the heat thereof:
verses.textLatin: qua extincta, cinis erit corpus nostrum, et spiritus diffundetur tamquam mollis aër; et transibit vita nostra tamquam vestigium nubis, et sicut nebula dissolvetur quæ fugata est a radiis solis, et a calore illius aggravata.

verses.text: And our name in time shall be forgotten, and no man shall have any remembrance of our works.
verses.textLatin: Et nomen nostrum oblivionem accipiet per tempus, et nemo memoriam habebit operum nostrorum.

verses.text: For our time is as the passing of a shadow, and there is no going back of our end: for it is fast sealed, and no man returneth.
verses.textLatin: Umbræ enim transitus est tempus nostrum, et non est reversio finis nostri: quoniam consignata est, et nemo revertitur.

verses.text: Come therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth.
verses.textLatin: Venite ergo, et fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tamquam in juventute celeriter.

verses.text: Let us fill ourselves with costly wine, and ointments: and let not the flower of the time pass by us.
verses.textLatin: Vino pretioso et unguentis nos impleamus, et non prætereat nos flos temporis.

verses.text: Let us crown ourselves with roses, before they be withered: let no meadow escape our riot.
verses.textLatin: Coronemus nos rosis antequam marcescant; nullum pratum sit quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra:

verses.text: Let none of us go without his part in luxury: let us everywhere leave tokens of joy: for this is our portion, and this our lot.
verses.textLatin: nemo nostrum exsors sit luxuriæ nostræ. Ubique relinquamus signa lætitiæ, quoniam hæc est pars nostra, et hæc est sors.

verses.text: Let us oppress the poor just man, and not spare the widow, nor honour the ancient grey hairs of the aged.
verses.textLatin: Opprimamus pauperem justum, et non parcamus viduæ, nec veterani revereamur canos multi temporis:

verses.text: But let our strength be the law of justice: for that which is feeble, is found to be nothing worth.
verses.textLatin: sit autem fortitudo nostra lex justitiæ; quod enim infirmum est, inutile invenitur.

verses.text: Let us therefore lie in wait for the just, because he is not for our turn, and he is contrary to our doings, and upbraideth us with transgressions of the law, and divulgeth against us the sins of our way of life.
verses.textLatin: Circumveniamus ergo justum, quoniam inutilis est nobis, et contrarius est operibus nostris, et improperat nobis peccata legis, et diffamat in nos peccata disciplinæ nostræ.

verses.text: He boasteth that he hath the knowledge of God, and calleth himself the son of God.
verses.textLatin: Promittit se scientiam Dei habere, et filium Dei se nominat.

verses.text: He is become a censurer of our thoughts.
verses.textLatin: Factus est nobis in traductionem cogitationum nostrarum.

verses.text: He is grievous unto us, even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, and his ways are very different.
verses.textLatin: Gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum, quoniam dissimilis est aliis vita illius, et immutatæ sunt viæ ejus.

verses.text: We are esteemed by him as triflers, and he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness, and he preferreth the latter end of the just, and glorieth that he hath God for his father.
verses.textLatin: Tamquam nugaces æstimati sumus ab illo, et abstinet se a viis nostris tamquam ab immunditiis, et præfert novissima justorum, et gloriatur patrem se habere Deum.

verses.text: Let us see then if his words be true, and let us prove what shall happen to him, and we shall know what his end shall be.
verses.textLatin: Videamus ergo si sermones illius veri sint, et tentemus quæ ventura sunt illi, et sciemus quæ erunt novissima illius.

verses.text: For if he be the true son of God, he will defend him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Si enim est verus filius Dei, suscipiet illum, et liberabit eum de manibus contrariorum.

verses.text: Let us examine him by outrages and tortures, that we may know his meekness and try his patience.
verses.textLatin: Contumelia et tormento interrogemus eum, ut sciamus reverentiam ejus, et probemus patientiam illius.

verses.text: Let us condemn him to a most shameful death: for there shall be respect had unto him by his words.
verses.textLatin: Morte turpissima condemnemus eum; erit enim ei respectus ex sermonibus illius.

verses.text: These things they thought, and were deceived: for their own malice blinded them.
verses.textLatin: Hæc cogitaverunt, et erraverunt: excæcavit enim illos malitia eorum.

verses.text: And they knew not the secrets of God, nor hoped for the wages of justice, nor esteemed the honour of holy souls.
verses.textLatin: Et nescierunt sacramenta Dei: neque mercedem speraverunt justitiæ, nec judicaverunt honorem animarum sanctarum.

verses.text: For God created man incorruptible, and to the image of his own likeness he made him.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam Deus creavit hominem inexterminabilem, et ad imaginem similitudinis suæ fecit illum.

verses.text: But by the envy of the devil, death came into the world:
verses.textLatin: Invidia autem diaboli mors introivit in orbem terrarum:

verses.text: And they follow him that are of his side.
verses.textLatin: imitantur autem illum qui sunt ex parte illius.

verses.text: But  the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them.
verses.textLatin: Justorum autem animæ in manu Dei sunt, et non tanget illos tormentum mortis.

verses.text: In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure was taken for misery:
verses.textLatin: Visi sunt oculis insipientium mori, et æstimata est afflictio exitus illorum,

verses.text: And their going away from us, for utter destruction: but they are in peace.
verses.textLatin: et quod a nobis est iter exterminium; illi autem sunt in pace:

verses.text: And though in the sight of men they suffered torments, their hope is full of immortality.
verses.textLatin: etsi coram hominibus tormenta passi sunt, spes illorum immortalitate plena est.

verses.text: Afflicted in few things, in many they shall be well rewarded: because God hath tried them, and found them worthy of himself.
verses.textLatin: In paucis vexati sunt, in multis bene disponentur, quoniam Deus tentavit eos, et invenit illos dignos se.

verses.text: As gold in the furnace he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust he hath received them, and in time there shall be respect had to them.
verses.textLatin: Tamquam aurum in fornace probavit illos, et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos, et in tempore erit respectus illorum.

verses.text: The just shall shine, and shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds.
verses.textLatin: Fulgebunt justi et tamquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent.

verses.text: They shall judge nations, and rule over people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
verses.textLatin: Judicabunt nationes, et dominabuntur populis, et regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum.

verses.text: They that trust in him, shall understand the truth: and they that are faithful in love shall rest in him: for grace and peace is to his elect.
verses.textLatin: Qui confidunt in illo intelligent veritatem, et fideles in dilectione acquiescent illi, quoniam donum et pax est electis ejus.

verses.text: But the wicked shall be punished according to their own devices: who have neglected the just, and have revolted from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Impii autem secundum quæ cogitaverunt correptionem habebunt: qui neglexerunt justum, et a Domino recesserunt.

verses.text: For he that rejecteth wisdom, and discipline, is unhappy: and their hope is vain, and their labours without fruit, and their works unprofitable.
verses.textLatin: Sapientiam enim et disciplinam qui abjicit infelix est: et vacua est spes illorum, et labores sine fructu, et inutilia opera eorum.

verses.text: Their wives are foolish, and their children wicked.
verses.textLatin: Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt, et nequissimi filii eorum.

verses.text: Their offspring is cursed: for happy is the barren: and the undefiled, that hath not known bed in sin: she shall have fruit in the visitation of holy souls.
verses.textLatin: Maledicta creatura eorum, quoniam felix est sterilis; et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit thorum in delicto, habebit fructum in respectione animarum sanctarum;

verses.text: And the eunuch, that hath not wrought iniquity with his hands, nor thought wicked things against God: for the precious gift of faith shall be given to him, and a most acceptable lot in the temple of God.
verses.textLatin: et spado qui non operatus est per manus suas iniquitatem, nec cogitavit adversus Deum nequissima: dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum, et sors in templo Dei acceptissima.

verses.text: For the fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of wisdom never faileth.
verses.textLatin: Bonorum enim laborum gloriosus est fructus, et quæ non concidat radix sapientiæ.

verses.text: But the children of adulterers shall not come to perfection, and the seed of the unlawful bed shall be rooted out.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem adulterorum in inconsummatione erunt, et ab iniquo thoro semen exterminabitur.

verses.text: And if they live long, they shall be nothing regarded, and their last old age shall be without honour.
verses.textLatin: Et si quidem longæ vitæ erunt, in nihilum computabuntur, et sine honore erit novissima senectus illorum:

verses.text: And if they die quickly, they shall have no hope, nor speech of comfort in the day of trial.
verses.textLatin: et si celerius defuncti fuerint, non habebunt spem, nec in die agnitionis allocutionem.

verses.text: For dreadful are the ends of a wicked race.
verses.textLatin: Nationis enim iniquæ diræ sunt consummationes.

verses.text: O  HOW beautiful is the chaste generation with glory: for the memory thereof is immortal: because it is known both with God and with men.
verses.textLatin: O quam pulchra est casta generatio, cum claritate! immortalis est enim memoria illius, quoniam et apud Deum nota est, et apud homines.

verses.text: When it is present, they imitate it: and they desire it when it hath withdrawn itself, and it triumpheth crowned for ever, winning the reward of undefiled conflicts.
verses.textLatin: Cum præsens est, imitantur illam, et desiderant eam cum se eduxerit; et in perpetuum coronata triumphat, incoinquinatorum certaminum præmium vincens.

verses.text: But the multiplied brood of the wicked shall not thrive, and bastard slips shall not take deep root, nor any fast foundation.
verses.textLatin: Multigena autem impiorum multitudo non erit utilis, et spuria vitulamina non dabunt radices altas, nec stabile firmamentum collocabunt.

verses.text: And if they flourish in branches for a time, yet standing not fast, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.
verses.textLatin: Etsi in ramis in tempore germinaverint, infirmiter posita, a vento commovebuntur, et a nimietate ventorum eradicabuntur.

verses.text: For the branches not being perfect, shall be broken, and their fruits shall be unprofitable, and sour to eat, and fit for nothing.
verses.textLatin: Confringentur enim rami inconsummati; et fructus illorum inutiles et acerbi ad manducandum, et ad nihilum apti.

verses.text: For the children that are born of unlawful beds, are witnesses of wickedness against their parents in their trial.
verses.textLatin: Ex iniquis enim somnis filii qui nascuntur, testes sunt nequitiæ adversus parentes in interrogatione sua.

verses.text: But the just man, if he be prevented with death, shall be in rest.
verses.textLatin: Justus autem si morte præoccupatus fuerit, in refrigerio erit;

verses.text: For venerable old age is not that of long time, nor counted by the number of years: but the understanding of a man is grey hairs.
verses.textLatin: senectus enim venerabilis est non diuturna, neque annorum numero computata: cani autem sunt sensus hominis,

verses.text: And a spotless life is old age.
verses.textLatin: et ætas senectutis vita immaculata.

verses.text: He pleased God and was beloved, and living among sinners he was translated.
verses.textLatin: Placens Deo factus est dilectus, et vivens inter peccatores translatus est.

verses.text: He was taken away lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.
verses.textLatin: Raptus est, ne malitia mutaret intellectum ejus, aut ne fictio deciperet animam illius.

verses.text: For the bewitching of vanity obscureth good things, and the wandering of concupiscence overturneth the innocent mind.
verses.textLatin: Fascinatio enim nugacitatis obscurat bona, et inconstantia concupiscentiæ transvertit sensum sine malitia.

verses.text: Being made perfect in a short space, he fulfilled a long time:
verses.textLatin: Consummatus in brevi, explevit tempora multa;

verses.text: For his soul pleased God: therefore he hastened to bring him out of the midst of iniquities: but the people see this, and understand not, nor lay up such things in their hearts:
verses.textLatin: placita enim erat Deo anima illius: propter hoc properavit educere illum de medio iniquitatum. Populi autem videntes, et non intelligentes, nec ponentes in præcordiis talia,

verses.text: That the grace of God, and his mercy is with his saints, and that he hath respect to his chosen.
verses.textLatin: quoniam gratia Dei et misericordia est in sanctos ejus, et respectus in electos illius.

verses.text: But the just that is dead, condemneth the wicked that are living, and youth soon ended, the long life of the unjust.
verses.textLatin: Condemnat autem justus mortuus vivos impios, et juventus celerius consummata longam vitam injusti.

verses.text: For they shall see the end of the wise man, and shall not understand what God hath designed for him, and why the Lord hath set him in safety.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt enim finem sapientis, et non intelligent quid cogitaverit de illo Deus, et quare munierit illum Dominus.

verses.text: They shall see him, and shall despise him: but the Lord shall laugh them to scorn.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt, et contemnent eum; illos autem Dominus irridebit.

verses.text: And they shall fall after this without honour, and be a reproach among the dead for ever: for he shall burst them puffed up and speechless, and shall shake them from the foundations, and they shall be utterly laid waste: they shall be in sorrow, and their memory shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt post hæc decidentes sine honore, et in contumelia inter mortuos in perpetuum: quoniam disrumpet illos inflatos sine voce, et commovebit illos a fundamentis, et usque ad supremum desolabuntur, et erunt gementes, et memoria illorum peribit.

verses.text: They shall come with fear at the thought of their sins, and their iniquities shall stand against them to convict them.
verses.textLatin: Venient in cogitatione peccatorum suorum timidi, et traducent illos ex adverso iniquitates ipsorum.

verses.text: Then  shall the just stand with great constancy against those that have afflicted them, and taken away their labours.
verses.textLatin: Tunc stabunt justi in magna constantia adversus eos qui se angustiaverunt, et qui abstulerunt labores eorum.

verses.text: These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear, and shall be amazed at the suddenness of their unexpected salvation.
verses.textLatin: Videntes turbabuntur timore horribili, et mirabuntur in subitatione insperatæ salutis;

verses.text: Saying within themselves, repenting, and groaning for anguish of spirit: These are they, whom we had some time in derision, and for a parable of reproach.
verses.textLatin: dicentes intra se, pœnitentiam agentes, et præ angustia spiritus gementes: Hi sunt quos habuimus aliquando in derisum, et in similitudinem improperii.

verses.text: We fools esteemed their life madness, and their end without honour.
verses.textLatin: Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam, et finem illorum sine honore;

verses.text: Behold how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints.
verses.textLatin: ecce quomodo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter sanctos sors illorum est.

verses.text: Therefore we have erred from the way of truth, and the light of justice hath not shined unto us, and the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us.
verses.textLatin: Ergo erravimus a via veritatis, et justitiæ lumen non luxit nobis, et sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis.

verses.text: We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways, but the way of the Lord we have not known.
verses.textLatin: Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles: viam autem Domini ignoravimus.

verses.text: What hath pride profited us? or what advantage hath the boasting of riches brought us?
verses.textLatin: Quid nobis profuit superbia? aut divitiarum jactantia quid contulit nobis?

verses.text: All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on,
verses.textLatin: Transierunt omnia illa tamquam umbra, et tamquam nuntius percurrens,

verses.text: And as a ship that passeth through the waves: whereof when it is gone by, the trace cannot be found, nor the path of its keel in the waters:
verses.textLatin: et tamquam navis quæ pertransit fluctuantem aquam, cujus cum præterierit non est vestigium invenire, neque semitam carinæ illius in fluctibus;

verses.text: Or as when a bird flieth through the air, of the passage of which no mark can be found, but only the sound of the wings beating the light air, and parting it by the force of her flight; she moved her wings, and hath flown through, and there is no mark found afterwards of her way:
verses.textLatin: aut tamquam avis quæ transvolat in aëre, cujus nullum invenitur argumentum itineris, sed tantum sonitus alarum verberans levem ventum, et scindens per vim itineris aërem: commotis alis transvolavit, et post hoc nullum signum invenitur itineris illius;

verses.text: Or as when an arrow is shot at a mark, the divided air presently cometh together again, so that the passage thereof is not known:
verses.textLatin: aut tamquam sagitta emissa in locum destinatum, divisus aër continuo in se reclusus est, ut ignoretur transitus illius:

verses.text: So we also being born, forthwith ceased to be: and have been able to shew no mark of virtue: but are consumed in our wickedness.
verses.textLatin: sic et nos nati continuo desivimus esse; et virtutis quidem nullum signum valuimus ostendere, in malignitate autem nostra consumpti sumus.

verses.text: Such things as these the sinners said in hell:
verses.textLatin: Talia dixerunt in inferno hi qui peccaverunt:

verses.text: For the hope of the wicked is as dust, which is blown away with the wind, and as a thin froth which is dispersed by the storm: and a smoke that is scattered abroad by the wind: and as the remembrance of a guest of one day that passeth by.
verses.textLatin: quoniam spes impii tamquam lanugo est quæ a vento tollitur, et tamquam spuma gracilis quæ a procella dispergitur, et tamquam fumus qui a vento diffusus est, et tamquam memoria hospitis unius diei prætereuntis.

verses.text: But the just shall live for evermore: and their reward is with the Lord, and the care of them with the most High.
verses.textLatin: Justi autem in perpetuum vivent, et apud Dominum est merces eorum, et cogitatio illorum apud Altissimum.

verses.text: Therefore shall they receive a kingdom of glory, and a crown of beauty at the hand of the Lord: for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his holy arm he will defend them.
verses.textLatin: Ideo accipient regnum decoris, et diadema speciei de manu Domini: quoniam dextera sua teget eos, et brachio sancto suo defendet illos.

verses.text: And his zeal will take armour, and he will arm the creature for the revenge of his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Accipiet armaturam zelus illius, et armabit creaturam ad ultionem inimicorum.

verses.text: He will put on justice as a breastplate, and will take true judgment instead of a helmet.
verses.textLatin: Induet pro thorace justitiam, et accipiet pro galea judicium certum;

verses.text: He will take equity for an invincible shield:
verses.textLatin: sumet scutum inexpugnabile æquitatem.

verses.text: And he will sharpen his severe wrath for a spear, and the whole world shall fight with him against the unwise.
verses.textLatin: Acuet autem duram iram in lanceam, et pugnabit cum illo orbis terrarum contra insensatos.

verses.text: Then shafts of lightning shall go directly from the clouds, as from a bow well bent, they shall be shot out, and shall fly to the mark.
verses.textLatin: Ibunt directe emissiones fulgurum, et tamquam a bene curvato arcu nubium exterminabuntur, et ad certum locum insilient.

verses.text: And thick hail shall be cast upon them from the stone casting wrath: the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the rivers shall run together in a terrible manner.
verses.textLatin: Et a petrosa ira plenæ mittentur grandines; excandescet in illos aqua maris, et flumina concurrent duriter.

verses.text: A mighty wind shall stand up against them, and as a whirlwind shall divide them: and their iniquity shall bring all the earth to a desert, and wickedness shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty.
verses.textLatin: Contra illos stabit spiritus virtutis, et tamquam turbo venti dividet illos; et ad eremum perducet omnem terram iniquitas illorum, et malignitas evertet sedes potentium.

verses.text: Wisdom  is better than strength, and a wise man is better than a strong man.
verses.textLatin: Melior est sapientia quam vires, et vir prudens quam fortis.

verses.text: Hear therefore, ye kings, and understand learn: ye that are judges of the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Audite ergo, reges, et intelligite; discite, judices finium terræ.

verses.text: Give ear, you that rule the people, and that please yourselves in multitudes of nations:
verses.textLatin: Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines, et placetis vobis in turbis nationum.

verses.text: For power is given you by the Lord, and strength by the most High, who will examine your works, and search out your thoughts:
verses.textLatin: Quoniam data est a Domino potestas vobis, et virtus ab Altissimo: qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes scrutabitur.

verses.text: Because being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged rightly, nor kept the law of justice, nor walked according to the will of God.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam cum essetis ministri regni illius, non recte judicastis, nec custodistis legem justitiæ, neque secundum voluntatem Dei ambulastis.

verses.text: Horribly and speedily will he appear to you: for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule.
verses.textLatin: Horrende et cito apparebit vobis, quoniam judicium durissimum his qui præsunt fiet.

verses.text: For to him that is little, mercy is granted: but the mighty shall be mightily tormented.
verses.textLatin: Exiguo enim conceditur misericordia; potentes autem potenter tormenta patientur.

verses.text: For God will not except any man’s person, neither will he stand in awe of any man’s greatness: for he made the little and the great, and he hath equally care of all.
verses.textLatin: Non enim subtrahet personam cujusquam Deus, nec verebitur magnitudinem ejus cujusquam, quoniam pusillum et magnum ipse fecit, et æqualiter cura est illi de omnibus.

verses.text: But a greater punishment is ready for the more mighty.
verses.textLatin: Fortioribus autem fortior instat cruciatio.

verses.text: To you, therefore, O kings, are these my words, that you may learn wisdom, and not fall from it.
verses.textLatin: Ad vos ergo, reges, sunt hi sermones mei: ut discatis sapientiam, et non excidatis.

verses.text: For they that have kept just things justly, shall be justified: and they that have learned these things, shall find what to answer.
verses.textLatin: Qui enim custodierint justa juste, justificabuntur; et qui didicerint ista, invenient quid respondeant.

verses.text: Covet ye therefore my words, and love them, and you shall have instruction.
