verses.text: For as thou didst punish the adversaries: so thou didst also encourage and glorify us.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim læsisti adversarios, sic et nos provocans magnificasti.

verses.text: For the just children of good men were offering sacrifice secretly, and they unanimously ordered a law of justice: that the just should receive both good and evil alike, singing now the praises of the fathers.
verses.textLatin: Absconse enim sacrificabant justi pueri bonorum, et justitiæ legem in concordia disposuerunt; similiter et bona et mala recepturos justos, patrum jam decantantes laudes.

verses.text: But on the other side there sounded an ill according cry of the enemies, and a lamentable mourning was heard for the children that were bewailed.
verses.textLatin: Resonabat autem inconveniens inimicorum vox, et flebilis audiebatur planctus ploratorum infantium.

verses.text: And the servant suffered the same punishment as the master, and a common man suffered in like manner as the king.
verses.textLatin: Simili autem pœna servus cum domino afflictus est, et popularis homo regi similia passus.

verses.text: So all alike had innumerable dead, with one kind of death. Neither were the living sufficient to bury them; for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Similiter ergo omnes, uno nomine mortis, mortuos habebant innumerabiles: nec enim ad sepeliendum vivi sufficiebant, quoniam uno momento quæ erat præclarior natio illorum exterminata est.

verses.text: For whereas they would not believe any thing before by reason of the enchantments, then first upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged the people to be of God.
verses.textLatin: De omnibus enim non credentes, propter veneficia; tunc vero primum cum fuit exterminium primogenitorum, spoponderunt populum Dei esse.

verses.text: For while all things were in quiet silence, and the night was in the midst of her course,
verses.textLatin: Cum enim quietum silentium contineret omnia, et nox in suo cursu medium iter haberet,

verses.text: Thy almighty word leapt down from heaven from thy royal throne, as a fierce conqueror into the midst of the land of destruction,
verses.textLatin: omnipotens sermo tuus de cælo, a regalibus sedibus, durus debellator in mediam exterminii terram prosilivit,

verses.text: With a sharp sword carrying thy unfeigned commandment, and he stood and filled all things with death, and standing on the earth reached even to heaven.
verses.textLatin: gladius acutus insimulatum imperium tuum portans: et stans, replevit omnia morte, et usque ad cælum attingebat stans in terra.

verses.text: Then suddenly visions of evil dreams troubled them, and fears unlooked for came upon them.
verses.textLatin: Tunc continuo visus somniorum malorum turbaverunt illos, et timores supervenerunt insperati.

verses.text: And one thrown here, another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death.
verses.textLatin: Et alius alibi projectus semivivus, propter quam moriebatur causam demonstrabat mortis.

verses.text: For the visions that troubled them foreshewed these things, lest they should perish and not know why they suffered these evils.
verses.textLatin: Visiones enim quæ illos turbaverunt hæc præmonebant, ne inscii quare mala patiebantur perirent.

verses.text: But the just also were afterwards touched by an assault of death, and there was a disturbance of the multitude in the wilderness: but thy wrath did not long continue.
verses.textLatin: Tetigit autem tunc et justos tentatio mortis, et commotio in eremo facta est multitudinis: sed non diu permansit ira tua.

verses.text: For a blameless man made haste to pray for the people, bringing forth the shield of his ministry, prayer, and by incense making supplication, withstood the wrath, and put an end to the calamity, shewing that he was thy servant.
verses.textLatin: Prosperans enim homo sine querela deprecari pro populis, proferens servitutis suæ scutum, orationem et per incensum deprecationem allegans, restitit iræ, et finem imposuit necessitati, ostendens quoniam tuus est famulus.

verses.text: And he overcame the disturbance, not by strength of body nor with force of arms, but with a word he subdued him that punished them, alleging the oaths and covenant made with the fathers.
verses.textLatin: Vicit autem turbas non in virtute corporis, nec armaturæ potentia: sed verbo illum qui se vexabat subjecit, juramenta parentum et testamentum commemorans.

verses.text: For when they were now fallen down dead by heaps one upon another, he stood between and stayed the assault, and cut off the way to the living.
verses.textLatin: Cum enim jam acervatim cecidissent super alterutrum mortui, interstitit, et amputavit impetum, et divisit illam quæ ad vivos ducebat viam.

verses.text: For in the priestly robe which he wore, was the whole world: and in the four rows of the stones the glory of the fathers was graven, and thy majesty was written upon the diadem of his head.
verses.textLatin: In veste enim poderis quam habebat, totus erat orbis terrarum; et parentum magnalia in quatuor ordinibus lapidum erant sculpta, et magnificentia tua in diademate capitis illius sculpta erat.
His autem cessit qui exterminabat, et hæc extimuit: erat enim sola tentatio iræ sufficiens.

verses.text: But  as to the wicked, even to the end there came upon them wrath without mercy. For he knew before also what they would do:
verses.textLatin: Impiis autem usque in novissimum sine misericordia ira supervenit. Præsciebat enim et futura illorum:

verses.text: For when they had given them leave to depart, and had sent them away with great care, they repented, and pursued after them.
verses.textLatin: quoniam cum ipsi permisissent ut se educerent, et cum magna sollicitudine præmisissent illos, consequebantur illos, pœnitentia acti.

verses.text: For whilst they were yet mourning, and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they took up another foolish device: and pursued them as fugitives whom they had pressed to be gone:
verses.textLatin: Adhuc enim inter manus habentes luctum, et deplorantes ad monumenta mortuorum, aliam sibi assumpserunt cogitationem inscientiæ, et quos rogantes projecerant, hos tamquam fugitivos persequebantur.

verses.text: For a necessity, of which they were worthy, brought them to this end: and they lost the remembrance of those things which had happened, that their punishment might fill up what was wanting to their torments:
verses.textLatin: Ducebat enim illos ad hunc finem digna necessitas; et horum quæ acciderant commemorationem amittebant, ut quæ deerant tormentis repleret punitio:

verses.text: And that thy people might wonderfully pass through, but they might find a new death.
verses.textLatin: et populus quidem tuus mirabiliter transiret, illi autem novam mortem invenirent.

verses.text: For every creature according to its kind was fashioned again as from the beginning, obeying thy commandments, that thy children might be kept without hurt.
verses.textLatin: Omnis enim creatura ad suum genus ab initio refigurabatur, deserviens tuis præceptis, ut pueri tui custodirentur illæsi.

verses.text: For a cloud overshadowed their camp, and where water was before, dry land appeared, and in the Red Sea a way without hinderance, and out of the great deep a springing field:
verses.textLatin: Nam nubes castra eorum obumbrabat, et ex aqua quæ ante erat, terra arida apparuit, et in mari Rubro via sine impedimento, et campus germinans de profundo nimio:

verses.text: Through which all the nation passed which was protected with thy hand, seeing thy miracles and wonders.
verses.textLatin: per quem omnis natio transivit quæ tegebatur tua manu, videntes tua mirabilia et monstra.

verses.text: For they fed on their food like horses, and they skipped like lambs, praising thee, O Lord, who hadst delivered them.
verses.textLatin: Tamquam enim equi depaverunt escam, et tamquam agni exsultaverunt, magnificantes te, Domine, qui liberasti illos.

verses.text: For they were yet mindful of those things which had been done in the time of their sojourning, how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, and how the river cast up a multitude of frogs instead of fishes.
verses.textLatin: Memores enim erant adhuc eorum quæ in incolatu illorum facta fuerant: quemadmodum pro natione animalium eduxit terra muscas, et pro piscibus eructavit fluvius multitudinem ranarum.

verses.text: And at length they saw a new generation of birds, when being led by their appetite they asked for delicate meats.
verses.textLatin: Novissime autem viderunt novam creaturam avium, cum, adducti concupiscentia, postulaverunt escas epulationis.

verses.text: For to satisfy their desire, the quail came up to them from the sea: and punishments came upon the sinners, not without foregoing signs by the force of thunders: for they suffered justly according to their own wickedness.
verses.textLatin: In allocutione enim desiderii ascendit illis de mari ortygometra: et vexationes peccatoribus supervenerunt, non sine illis quæ ante facta erant argumentis per vim fulminum: juste enim patiebantur secundum suas nequitias.

verses.text: For they exercised a more detestable inhospitality than any: others indeed received not strangers unknown to them, but these brought their guests into bondage that had deserved well of them.
verses.textLatin: Etenim detestabiliorem inhospitalitatem instituerunt: alii quidem ignotos non recipiebant advenas; alii autem bonos hospites in servitutem redigebant.

verses.text: And not only so, but in another respect also they were worse: for the others against their will received the strangers.
verses.textLatin: Et non solum hæc, sed et alius quidam respectus illorum erat, quoniam inviti recipiebant extraneos.

verses.text: But these grievously afflicted them whom they had received with joy, and who lived under the same laws.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem cum lætitia receperunt hos qui eisdem usi erant justitiis, sævissimis afflixerunt doloribus.

verses.text: But they were struck with blindness: as those others were at the doors of the just man, when they were covered with sudden darkness, and every one sought the passage of his own door.
verses.textLatin: Percussi sunt autem cæcitate: sicut illi in foribus justi, cum subitaneis cooperti essent tenebris, unusquisque transitum ostii sui quærebat.

verses.text: For while the elements are changed in themselves, as in an instrument the sound of the quality is changed, yet all keep their sound: which may clearly be perceived by the very sight.
verses.textLatin: In se enim elementa dum convertuntur, sicut in organo qualitatis sonus immutatur, et omnia suum sonum custodiunt: unde æstimari ex ipso visu certo potest.

verses.text: For the things of the land were turned into things of the water: and the things before swam in the water passed upon the land.
verses.textLatin: Agrestia enim in aquatica convertebantur, et quæcumque erant natantia, in terram transibant.

verses.text: The fire had power in water above its own virtue, and the water forgot its quenching nature.
verses.textLatin: Ignis in aqua valebat supra suam virtutem, et aqua extinguentis naturæ obliviscebatur.

verses.text: On the other side, the flames wasted not the flesh of corruptible animals walking therein, neither did they melt that good food, which was apt to melt as ice. For in all things thou didst magnify thy people, O Lord, and didst honour them, and didst not despise them, but didst assist them at all times, and in every place.
verses.textLatin: Flammæ e contrario corruptibilium animalium non vexaverunt carnes coambulantium, nec dissolvebant illam, quæ facile dissolvebatur sicut glacies, bonam escam. In omnibus enim magnificasti populum tuum, Domine, et honorasti, et non despexisti, in omni tempore et in omni loco assistens eis.

verses.text: All  wisdom is from the Lord God, and hath been always with him, and is before all time.
verses.textLatin: Omnis sapientia a Domino Deo est: et cum illo fuit semper, et est ante ævum.

verses.text: Who hath numbered the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of the world? Who hath measured the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss?
verses.textLatin: Arenam maris, et pluviæ guttas, et dies sæculi, quis dinumeravit? altitudinem cæli, et latitudinem terræ, et profundum abyssi, quis dimensus est?

verses.text: Who hath searched out the wisdom of God that goeth before all things?
verses.textLatin: sapientiam Dei præcedentem omnia, quis investigavit?

verses.text: Wisdom hath been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
verses.textLatin: Prior omnium creata est sapientia, et intellectus prudentiæ ab ævo.

verses.text: The word of God on high is the fountain of wisdom, and her ways are everlasting commandments.
verses.textLatin: Fons sapientiæ verbum Dei in excelsis, et ingressus illius mandata æterna.

verses.text: To whom hath the root of wisdom been revealed, and who hath known her wise counsels?
verses.textLatin: Radix sapientiæ cui revelata est? et astutias illius quis agnovit?

verses.text: To whom hath the discipline of wisdom been revealed and made manifest? and who hath understood the multiplicity of her steps?
verses.textLatin: disciplina sapientiæ cui revelata est et manifestata? et multiplicationem ingressus illius quis intellexit?

verses.text: There is one most high Creator Almighty, and a powerful king, and greatly to be feared, who sitteth upon his throne, and is the God of dominion.
verses.textLatin: Unus est altissimus, Creator omnipotens, et rex potens et metuendus nimis, sedens super thronum illius, et dominans Deus.

verses.text: He created her in the Holy Ghost, and saw her, and numbered her, and measured her.
verses.textLatin: Ipse creavit illam in Spiritu Sancto, et vidit, et dinumeravit, et mensus est:

verses.text: And he poured her out upon all his works, and upon all flesh according to his gift, and hath given her to them that love him.
verses.textLatin: et effudit illam super omnia opera sua, et super omnem carnem, secundum datum suum, et præbuit illam diligentibus se.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of joy.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini gloria, et gloriatio, et lætitia, et corona exsultationis.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart, and shall give joy, and gladness, and length of days.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini delectabit cor, et dabit lætitiam, et gaudium, et longitudinem dierum.

verses.text: With him that feareth the Lord, it shall go well in the latter end, and in the day of his death he shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Timenti Dominum bene erit in extremis, et in die defunctionis suæ benedicetur.

verses.text: The love of God is honourable wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Dilectio Dei honorabilis sapientia:

verses.text: And they to whom she shall shew herself love her by the sight, and by the knowledge of her great works.
verses.textLatin: quibus autem apparuerit in visu diligunt eam in visione, et in agnitione magnalium suorum.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and was created with the faithful in the womb, it walketh with chosen women, and is known with the just and faithful.
verses.textLatin: Initium sapientiæ timor Domini: et cum fidelibus in vulva concreatus est: cum electis feminis graditur, et cum justis et fidelibus agnoscitur.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the religiousness of knowledge.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini scientiæ religiositas:

verses.text: Religiousness shall keep and justify the heart, it shall give joy and gladness.
verses.textLatin: religiositas custodiet et justificabit cor; jucunditatem atque gaudium dabit.

verses.text: It shall go well with him that feareth the Lord, and in the days of his end he shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Timenti Dominum bene erit, et in diebus consummationis illius benedicetur.

verses.text: To fear God is the fulness of wisdom, and fulness is from the fruits thereof.
verses.textLatin: Plenitudo sapientiæ est timere Deum, et plenitudo a fructibus illius.

verses.text: She shall fill all her house with her increase, and the storehouses with her treasures.
verses.textLatin: Omnem domum illius implebit a generationibus, et receptacula a thesauris illius.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, filling up peace and the fruit of salvation:
verses.textLatin: Corona sapientiæ timor Domini, replens pacem et salutis fructum:

verses.text: And it hath seen, and numbered her: but both are the gifts of God.
verses.textLatin: et vidit, et dinumeravit eam: utraque autem sunt dona Dei.

verses.text: Wisdom shall distribute knowledge, and understanding of prudence: and exalteth the glory of them that hold her.
verses.textLatin: Scientiam et intellectum prudentiæ sapientia compartietur, et gloriam tenentium se exaltat.

verses.text: The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord: and the branches thereof are long-lived.
verses.textLatin: Radix sapientiæ est timere Dominum, et rami illius longævi.

verses.text: In the treasures of wisdom is understanding, and religiousness of knowledge: but to sinners wisdom is an abomination.
verses.textLatin: In thesauris sapientiæ intellectus et scientiæ religiositas: execratio autem peccatoribus sapientia.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord driveth out sin:
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini expellit peccatum:

verses.text: For he that is without fear, cannot be justified: for the wrath of his high spirits is his ruin.
verses.textLatin: nam qui sine timore est non poterit justificari: iracundia enim animositatis illius subversio illius est.

verses.text: A patient man shall bear for a time, and afterwards joy shall be restored to him.
verses.textLatin: Usque in tempus sustinebit patiens, et postea redditio jucunditatis.

verses.text: A good understanding will hide his words for a time, and the lips of many shall declare his wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Bonus sensus usque in tempus abscondet verba illius, et labia multorum enarrabunt sensum illius.

verses.text: In the treasures of wisdom is the signification of discipline:
verses.textLatin: In thesauris sapientiæ significatio disciplinæ:

verses.text: But the worship of God is an abomination to a sinner.
verses.textLatin: execratio autem peccatori cultura Dei.

verses.text: Son, if thou desire wisdom, keep justice, and God will give her to thee.
verses.textLatin: Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, conserva justitiam, et Deus præbebit illam tibi.

verses.text: For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline: and that which is agreeable to him,
verses.textLatin: Sapientia enim et disciplina timor Domini: et quod beneplacitum est illi,

verses.text: Is faith, and meekness: and he will fill up his treasures.
verses.textLatin: fides et mansuetudo, et adimplebit thesauros illius.

verses.text: Be not incredulous to the fear of the Lord: and come not to him with a double heart.
verses.textLatin: Ne sis incredibilis timori Domini, et ne accesseris ad illum duplici corde.

verses.text: Be not a hypocrite in the sight of men, and let not thy lips be a stumblingblock to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne fueris hypocrita in conspectu hominum, et non scandalizeris in labiis tuis.

verses.text: Watch over them, lest thou fall, and bring dishonour upon thy soul,
verses.textLatin: Attende in illis, ne forte cadas, et adducas animæ tuæ inhonorationem:

verses.text: And God discover thy secrets, and cast thee down in the midst of the congregation.
verses.textLatin: et revelet Deus absconsa tua, et in medio synagogæ elidat te:

verses.text: Because thou camest to the Lord wickedly, and thy heart is full of guile and deceit.
verses.textLatin: quoniam accessisti maligne ad Dominum, et cor tuum plenum est dolo et fallacia.

verses.text: Son,  when thou comest to the service of God, stand in justice and in fear, and prepare thy soul for temptation.
verses.textLatin: Fili, accedens ad servitutem Dei sta in justitia et timore, et præpara animam tuam ad tentationem.

verses.text: Humble thy heart, and endure: incline thy ear, and receive the words of understanding: and make not haste in the time of clouds.
verses.textLatin: Deprime cor tuum, et sustine: inclina aurem tuam, et suscipe verba intellectus: et ne festines in tempore obductionis.

verses.text: Wait on God with patience: join thyself to God, and endure, that thy life may be increased in the latter end.
verses.textLatin: Sustine sustentationes Dei: conjungere Deo, et sustine, ut crescat in novissimo vita tua.

verses.text: Take all that shall be brought upon thee: and in thy sorrow endure, and in thy humiliation keep patience.
verses.textLatin: Omne quod tibi applicitum fuerit accipe: et in dolore sustine, et in humilitate tua patientiam habe:

verses.text: For gold and silver are tried in the fire, but acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
verses.textLatin: quoniam in igne probatur aurum et argentum, homines vero receptibiles in camino humiliationis.

verses.text: Believe God, and he will recover thee: and direct thy way, and trust in him. Keep his fear, and grow old therein.
verses.textLatin: Crede Deo, et recuperabit te: et dirige viam tuam, et spera in illum: serva timorem illius, et in illo veterasce.

verses.text: Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy: and go not aside from him, lest ye fall.
verses.textLatin: Metuentes Dominum, sustinete misericordiam ejus: et non deflectatis ab illo, ne cadatis.

verses.text: Ye that fear the Lord, believe him: and your reward shall not be made void.
verses.textLatin: Qui timetis Dominum, credite illi, et non evacuabitur merces vestra.

verses.text: Ye that fear the Lord, hope in him: and mercy shall come to you for your delight.
verses.textLatin: Qui timetis Dominum, sperate in illum, et in oblectationem veniet vobis misericordia.

verses.text: Ye that fear the Lord, love him, and your hearts shall be enlightened.
verses.textLatin: Qui timetis Dominum, diligite illum, et illuminabuntur corda vestra.

verses.text: My children behold the generations of men: and know ye that no one hath hoped in the Lord, and hath been confounded.
verses.textLatin: Respicite, filii, nationes hominum: et scitote quia nullus speravit in Domino et confusus est.

verses.text: For who hath continued in his commandment, and hath been forsaken? or who hath called upon him, and he despised him?
verses.textLatin: Quis enim permansit in mandatis ejus, et derelictus est? aut quis invocavit eum, et despexit illum?

verses.text: For God is compassionate and merciful, and will forgive sins in the day of tribulation: and he is a protector to all that seek him in truth.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam pius et misericors est Deus, et remittet in die tribulationis peccata, et protector est omnibus exquirentibus se in veritate.

verses.text: Woe to them that are of a double heart and to wicked lips, and to the hands that do evil, and to the sinner that goeth on the earth two ways.
verses.textLatin: Væ duplici corde, et labiis scelestis, et manibus malefacientibus, et peccatori terram ingredienti duabus viis!

verses.text: Woe to them that are fainthearted, who believe not God: and therefore they shall not be protected by him.
verses.textLatin: Væ dissolutis corde, qui non credunt Deo, et ideo non protegentur ab eo!

verses.text: Woe to them that have lost patience, and that have forsaken the right ways, and have gone aside into crooked ways.
verses.textLatin: Væ his qui perdiderunt sustinentiam, et qui dereliquerunt vias rectas, et diverterunt in vias pravas!

verses.text: And what will they do, when the Lord shall begin to examine?
verses.textLatin: Et quid facient cum inspicere cœperit Dominus?

verses.text: They that fear the Lord, will not be incredulous to his word: and they that love him, will keep his way.
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum non erunt incredibiles verbo illius: et qui diligunt illum conservabunt viam illius.

verses.text: They that fear the Lord, will seek after the things that are well pleasing to him: and they that love him, shall be filled with his law.
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum inquirent quæ beneplacita sunt ei, et qui diligunt eum replebuntur lege ipsius.

verses.text: They that fear the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and in his sight will sanctify their souls,
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum præparabunt corda sua, et in conspectu illius sanctificabunt animas suas.

verses.text: They that fear the Lord, keep his commandments, and will have patience even until his visitation,
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum custodiunt mandata illius, et patientiam habebunt usque ad inspectionem illius,

verses.text: Saying: If we do not penance, we shall fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men.
verses.textLatin: dicentes: Si pœnitentiam non egerimus, incidemus in manus Domini, et non in manus hominum.

verses.text: For according to his greatness, so also is his mercy with him.
verses.textLatin: Secundum enim magnitudinem ipsius, sic et misericordia illius cum ipso est.

verses.text: The  sons of wisdom are the church of the just: and their generation, obedience and love.
verses.textLatin: Filii sapientiæ ecclesia justorum, et natio illorum obedientia et dilectio.

verses.text: Children, hear the judgment of your father, and so do that you may be saved.
verses.textLatin: Judicium patris audite, filii, et sic facite, ut salvi sitis.

verses.text: For God hath made the father honourable to the children: and seeking the judgment of the mothers, hath confirmed it upon the children.
verses.textLatin: Deus enim honoravit patrem in filiis: et judicium matris exquirens, firmavit in filios.

verses.text: He that loveth God, shall obtain pardon for his sins by prayer, and shall refrain himself from them, and shall be heard in the prayer of days.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligit Deum exorabit pro peccatis, et continebit se ab illis, et in oratione dierum exaudietur.

verses.text: And he that honoureth his mother is as one that layeth up a treasure.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut qui thesaurizat, ita et qui honorificat matrem suam.

verses.text: He that honoureth his father shall have joy in his own children, and in the day of his prayer he shall be heard.
verses.textLatin: Qui honorat patrem suum jucundabitur in filiis, et in die orationis suæ exaudietur.

verses.text: He that honoureth his father shall enjoy a long life: and he that obeyeth the father, shall be a comfort to his mother.
verses.textLatin: Qui honorat patrem suum vita vivet longiore, et qui obedit patri refrigerabit matrem.

verses.text: He that feareth the Lord, honoureth his parents, and will serve them as his masters that brought him into the world.
verses.textLatin: Qui timet Dominum honorat parentes, et quasi dominis serviet his qui se genuerunt.

verses.text: Honour thy father, in work and word, and all patience,
verses.textLatin: In opere, et sermone, et omni patientia, honora patrem tuum,

verses.text: That a blessing may come upon thee from him, and his blessing may remain in the latter end.
verses.textLatin: ut superveniat tibi benedictio ab eo, et benedictio illius in novissimo maneat.

verses.text: The father’s blessing establisheth the houses of the children: but the mother’s curse rooteth up the foundation.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio patris firmat domos filiorum: maledictio autem matris eradicat fundamenta.

verses.text: Glory not in the dishonour of thy father: for his shame is no glory to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ne glorieris in contumelia patris tui: non enim est tibi gloria ejus confusio.

verses.text: For the glory of a man is from the honour of his father, and a father without honour is the disgrace of the son.
verses.textLatin: Gloria enim hominis ex honore patris sui, et dedecus filii pater sine honore.

verses.text: Son, support the old age of thy father, and grieve him not in his life;
verses.textLatin: Fili, suscipe senectam patris tui, et non contristes eum in vita illius:

verses.text: And if his understanding fail, have patience with him, and despise him not when thou art in thy strength: for the relieving of the father shall not be forgotten.
verses.textLatin: et si defecerit sensu, veniam da, et ne spernas eum in virtute tua: eleemosyna enim patris non erit in oblivione.

verses.text: For good shall be repaid to thee for the sin of thy mother.
verses.textLatin: Nam pro peccato matris restituetur tibi bonum:

verses.text: And in justice thou shalt be built up, and in the day of affliction thou shalt be remembered: and thy sins shall melt away as the ice in the fair warm weather.
verses.textLatin: et in justitia ædificabitur tibi, et in die tribulationis commemorabitur tui, et sicut in sereno glacies, solventur peccata tua.

verses.text: Of what an evil fame is he that forsaketh his father: and he is cursed of God that angereth his mother.
verses.textLatin: Quam malæ famæ est qui derelinquit patrem, et est maledictus a Deo qui exasperat matrem!

verses.text: My son, do thy works in meekness, and thou shalt be beloved above the glory of men.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in mansuetudine opera tua perfice, et super hominum gloriam diligeris.

verses.text: The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things, and thou shalt find grace before God:
verses.textLatin: Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam:

verses.text: For great is the power of God alone, and he is honoured by the humble.
verses.textLatin: quoniam magna potentia Dei solius, et ab humilibus honoratur.

verses.text: Seek not the things that are too high for thee, and search not into things above thy ability: but the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always, and in many of his works be not curious.
verses.textLatin: Altiora te ne quæsieris, et fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris: sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper, et in pluribus operibus ejus ne fueris curiosus.

verses.text: For it is not necessary for thee to see with thy eyes those things that are hid.
verses.textLatin: Non est enim tibi necessarium ea, quæ abscondita sunt, videre oculis tuis.

verses.text: In unnecessary matters be not over curious, and in many of his works thou shalt not be inquisitive.
verses.textLatin: In supervacuis rebus noli scrutari multipliciter, et in pluribus operibus ejus non eris curiosus.

verses.text: For many things are shewn to thee above the understanding of men.
verses.textLatin: Plurima enim super sensum hominum ostensa sunt tibi:

verses.text: And the suspicion of them hath deceived many, and hath detained their minds in vanity.
verses.textLatin: multos quoque supplantavit suspicio illorum, et in vanitate detinuit sensus illorum.

verses.text: A hard heart shall fear evil at the last: and he that loveth danger shall perish in it.
verses.textLatin: Cor durum habebit male in novissimo, et qui amat periculum in illo peribit.

verses.text: A heart that goeth two ways shall not have success, and the perverse of heart shall be scandalized therein.
verses.textLatin: Cor ingrediens duas vias non habebit successus, et pravus corde in illis scandalizabitur.

verses.text: A wicked heart shall be laden with sorrows, and the sinner will add sin to sin.
verses.textLatin: Cor nequam gravabitur in doloribus, et peccator adjiciet ad peccandum.

verses.text: The congregation of the proud shall not be healed: for the plant of wickedness shall take root in them, and it shall not be perceived.
verses.textLatin: Synagogæ superborum non erit sanitas, frutex enim peccati radicabitur in illis, et non intelligetur.

verses.text: The heart of the wise is understood in wisdom, and a good ear will hear wisdom with all desire.
verses.textLatin: Cor sapientis intelligitur in sapientia, et auris bona audiet cum omni concupiscentia sapientiam.

verses.text: A wise heart, and which hath understanding, will abstain from sins, and in the works of justice shall have success.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens cor et intelligibile abstinebit se a peccatis, et in operibus justitiæ successus habebit.

verses.text: Water quencheth a flaming fire, and alms resisteth sins:
verses.textLatin: Ignem ardentem exstinguit aqua, et eleemosyna resistit peccatis:

verses.text: And God provideth for him that sheweth favour: he remembereth him afterwards, and in the time of his fall he shall find a sure stay.
verses.textLatin: et Deus prospector est ejus qui reddit gratiam: meminit ejus in posterum, et in tempore casus sui inveniet firmamentum.

verses.text: Son,  defraud not the poor of alms, and turn not away thy eyes from the poor.
verses.textLatin: Fili, eleemosynam pauperis ne defraudes, et oculos tuos ne transvertas a paupere.

verses.text: Despise not the hungry soul: and provoke not the poor in his want.
verses.textLatin: Animam esurientem ne despexeris, et non exasperes pauperem in inopia sua.

verses.text: Afflict not the heart of the needy, and defer not to give to him that is in distress.
verses.textLatin: Cor inopis ne afflixeris, et non protrahas datum angustianti.

verses.text: Reject not the petition of the afflicted: and turn not away thy face from the needy.
verses.textLatin: Rogationem contribulati ne abjicias, et non avertas faciem tuam ab egeno.

verses.text: Turn not away thy eyes from the poor for fear of anger: and leave not to them that ask of thee to curse thee behind thy back.
verses.textLatin: Ab inope ne avertas oculos tuos propter iram: et non relinquas quærentibus tibi retro maledicere.

verses.text: For the prayer of him that curseth thee in the bitterness of his soul, shall be heard, for he that made him will hear him.
verses.textLatin: Maledicentis enim tibi in amaritudine animæ, exaudietur deprecatio illius: exaudiet autem eum qui fecit illum.

verses.text: Make thyself affable to the congregation of the poor, and humble thy soul to the ancient, and bow thy head to a great man.
verses.textLatin: Congregationi pauperum affabilem te facito: et presbytero humilia animam tuam, et magnato humilia caput tuum.

verses.text: Bow down thy ear cheerfully to the poor, and pay what thou owest, and answer him peaceable words with mildness.
verses.textLatin: Declina pauperi sine tristitia aurem tuam, et redde debitum tuum, et responde illi pacifica in mansuetudine.

verses.text: Deliver him that suffereth wrong out of the hand of the proud: and be not fainthearted in thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Libera eum qui injuriam patitur de manu superbi, et non acide feras in anima tua.

verses.text: In judging be merciful to the fatherless as a father, and as a husband to their mother.
verses.textLatin: In judicando esto pupillis misericors ut pater, et pro viro matri illorum:

verses.text: And thou shalt be as the obedient son of the most High, and he will have mercy on thee more than a mother.
verses.textLatin: et eris tu velut filius Altissimi obediens, et miserebitur tui magis quam mater.

verses.text: Wisdom inspireth life into her children, and protecteth them that seek after her, and will go before them in the way of justice.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia filiis suis vitam inspirat: et suscipit inquirentes se, et præibit in via justitiæ.

verses.text: And he that loveth her, loveth life: and they that watch for her, shall embrace her sweetness.
verses.textLatin: Et qui illam diligit, diligit vitam, et qui vigilaverint ad illam complectentur placorem ejus.

verses.text: They that hold her fast, shall inherit life: and whithersoever she entereth, God will give a blessing.
verses.textLatin: Qui tenuerint illam, vitam hæreditabunt: et quo introibit benedicet Deus.

verses.text: They that serve her, shall be servants to the holy one: and God loveth them that love her.
verses.textLatin: Qui serviunt ei obsequentes erunt sancto: et eos qui diligunt illam, diligit Deus.

verses.text: He that hearkeneth to her, shall judge nations: and he that looketh upon her, shall remain secure.
verses.textLatin: Qui audit illam judicabit gentes: et qui intuetur illam permanebit confidens.

verses.text: If he trust to her, he shall inherit her, and his generation shall be in assurance.
verses.textLatin: Si crediderit ei, hæreditabit illam, et erunt in confirmatione creaturæ illius:

verses.text: For she walketh with him in temptation, and at the first she chooseth him.
verses.textLatin: quoniam in tentatione ambulat cum eo, et in primis eligit eum.

verses.text: She will bring upon him fear and dread and trial: and she will scourge him with the affliction of her discipline, till she try him by her laws, and trust his soul.
verses.textLatin: Timorem, et metum, et probationem inducet super illum: et cruciabit illum in tribulatione doctrinæ suæ, donec tentet eum in cogitationibus suis, et credat animæ illius.

verses.text: Then she will strengthen him, and make a straight way to him, and give him joy,
verses.textLatin: Et firmabit illum, et iter adducet directum ad illum, et lætificabit illum:

verses.text: And will disclose her secrets to him, and will heap upon him treasures of knowledge and understanding of justice.
verses.textLatin: et denudabit absconsa sua illi, et thesaurizabit super illum scientiam et intellectum justitiæ.

verses.text: But if he go astray, she will forsake him, and deliver him into the hands of his enemy.
verses.textLatin: Si autem oberraverit, derelinquet eum, et tradet eum in manus inimici sui.

verses.text: Son, observe the time, and fly from evil.
verses.textLatin: Fili, conserva tempus, et devita a malo.

verses.text: For thy soul be not ashamed to say the truth.
verses.textLatin: Pro anima tua ne confundaris dicere verum:

verses.text: For there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame that bringeth glory and grace.
verses.textLatin: est enim confusio adducens peccatum, et est confusio adducens gloriam et gratiam.

verses.text: Accept no person against thy own person, nor against thy soul a lie.
verses.textLatin: Ne accipias faciem adversus faciem tuam, nec adversus animam tuam mendacium.

verses.text: Reverence not thy neighbour in his fall:
verses.textLatin: Ne reverearis proximum tuum in casu suo,

verses.text: And refrain not to speak in the time of salvation. Hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.
verses.textLatin: nec retineas verbum in tempore salutis. Non abscondas sapientiam tuam in decore suo:

verses.text: For by the tongue wisdom is discerned: and understanding, and knowledge, and learning by the word of the wise, and steadfastness in the works of justice.
verses.textLatin: in lingua enim sapientia dignoscitur: et sensus, et scientia, et doctrina in verbo sensati, et firmamentum in operibus justitiæ.

verses.text: In nowise speak against the truth, but be ashamed of the lie of thy ignorance.
verses.textLatin: Non contradicas verbo veritatis ullo modo, et de mendacio ineruditionis tuæ confundere.

verses.text: Be not ashamed to confess thy sins, but submit not thyself to every man for sin.
verses.textLatin: Non confundaris confiteri peccata tua, et ne subjicias te omni homini pro peccato.

verses.text: Resist not against the face of the mighty, and do not strive against the stream of the river.
verses.textLatin: Noli resistere contra faciem potentis, nec coneris contra ictum fluvii.

verses.text: Strive for justice for thy soul, and even unto death fight for justice, and God will overthrow thy enemies for thee.
verses.textLatin: Pro justitia agonizare pro anima tua, et usque ad mortem certa pro justitia: et Deus expugnabit pro te inimicos tuos.

verses.text: Be not hasty in thy tongue: and slack and remiss in thy works.
verses.textLatin: Noli citatus esse in lingua tua, et inutilis, et remissus in operibus tuis.

verses.text: Be not as a lion in thy house, terrifying them of thy household, and oppressing them that are under thee.
verses.textLatin: Noli esse sicut leo in domo tua, evertens domesticos tuos, et opprimens subjectos tibi.

verses.text: Let not thy hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when thou shouldst give.
verses.textLatin: Non sit porrecta manus tua ad accipiendum, et ad dandum collecta.

verses.text: Set  not thy heart upon unjust possessions, and say not: I have enough to live on: for it shall be of no service in the time of vengeance and darkness.
verses.textLatin: Noli attendere ad possessiones iniquas, et ne dixeris: Est mihi sufficiens vita: nihil enim proderit in tempore vindictæ et obductionis.

verses.text: Follow not in thy strength the desires of thy heart:
verses.textLatin: Ne sequaris in fortitudine tua concupiscentiam cordis tui,

verses.text: And say not: How mighty am I? and who shall bring me under for my deeds? for God will surely take revenge.
verses.textLatin: et ne dixeris: Quomodo potui? aut, Quis me subjiciet propter facta mea? Deus enim vindicans vindicabit.

verses.text: Say not: I have sinned, and what harm hath befallen me? for the most High is a patient rewarder.
verses.textLatin: Ne dixeris: Peccavi: et quid mihi accidit triste? Altissimus enim est patiens redditor.

verses.text: Be not without fear about sin forgiven, and add not sin upon sin:
verses.textLatin: De propitiatio peccato noli esse sine metu, neque adjicias peccatum super peccatum.

verses.text: And say not: The mercy of the Lord is great, he will have mercy on the multitude of my sins.
verses.textLatin: Et ne dicas: Miseratio Domini magna est, multitudinis peccatorum meorum miserebitur:

verses.text: For mercy and wrath quickly come from him, and his wrath looketh upon sinners.
verses.textLatin: misericordia enim et ira ab illo cito proximant, et in peccatores respicit ira illius.

verses.text: Delay not to be converted to the Lord, and defer it not from day to day.
verses.textLatin: Non tardes converti ad Dominum, et ne differas de die in diem:

verses.text: For his wrath shall come on a sudden, and in the time of vengeance he will destroy thee.
verses.textLatin: subito enim veniet ira illius, et in tempore vindictæ disperdet te.

verses.text: Be not anxious for goods unjustly gotten: for they shall not profit thee in the day of calamity and revenge.
verses.textLatin: Noli anxius esse in divitiis injustis: non enim proderunt tibi in die obductionis et vindictæ.

verses.text: Winnow not with every wind, and go not into every way: for so is every sinner proved by a double tongue.
verses.textLatin: Non ventiles te in omnem ventum, et non eas in omnem viam: sic enim omnis peccator probatur in duplici lingua.

verses.text: Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of thy judgment, and in knowledge, and let the word of peace and justice keep with thee.
verses.textLatin: Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui et scientia: et prosequatur te verbum pacis et justitiæ.

verses.text: Be meek to hear the word, that thou mayst understand: and return a true answer with wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Esto mansuetus ad audiendum verbum, ut intelligas, et cum sapientia proferas responsum verum.

verses.text: If thou have understanding, answer thy neighbour: but if not, let thy hand be upon thy mouth, lest thou be surprised in an unskilful word, and be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Si est tibi intellectus, responde proximo: sin autem, sit manus tua super os tuum, ne capiaris in verbo indisciplinato, et confundaris.

verses.text: Honour and glory is in the word of the wise, but the tongue of the fool is his ruin.
verses.textLatin: Honor et gloria in sermone sensati: lingua vero imprudentis subversio est ipsius.

verses.text: Be not called a whisperer, and be not taken in thy tongue, and confounded.
verses.textLatin: Non appelleris susurro, et lingua tua ne capiaris et confundaris:

verses.text: For confusion and repentance is upon a thief, and an evil mark of disgrace upon the double tongued, but to the whisperer hatred, and enmity, and reproach.
verses.textLatin: super furem enim est confusio et pœnitentia, et denotatio pessima super bilinguem: susurratori autem odium, et inimicitia, et contumelia.

verses.text: Justify alike the small and the great.
verses.textLatin: Justifica pusillum et magnum similiter.

verses.text: Instead  of a friend become not an enemy to thy neighbour: for an evil man shall inherit reproach and shame, so shall every sinner that is envious and double tongued.
verses.textLatin: Noli fieri pro amico inimicus proximo: improperium enim et contumeliam malus hæreditabit: et omnis peccator invidus et bilinguis.

verses.text: Extol not thyself in the thoughts of thy soul like a bull: lest thy strength be quashed by folly,
verses.textLatin: Non te extollas in cogitatione animæ tuæ velut taurus, ne forte elidatur virtus tua per stultitiam:

verses.text: And it eat up thy leaves, and destroy thy fruit, and thou be left as a dry tree in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: et folia tua comedat, et fructus tuos perdat, et relinquaris velut lignum aridum in eremo.

verses.text: For a wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and maketh him to be a joy to his enemies, and shall lead him into the lot of the wicked.
verses.textLatin: Anima enim nequam disperdet qui se habet, et in gaudium inimicis dat illum, et deducet in sortem impiorum.

verses.text: A sweet word multiplieth friends, and appeaseth enemies, and a gracious tongue in a good man aboundeth.
verses.textLatin: Verbum dulce multiplicat amicos et mitigat inimicos, et lingua eucharis in bono homine abundat.

verses.text: Be in peace with many, but let one of a thousand be thy counsellor.
verses.textLatin: Multi pacifici sint tibi: et consiliarius sit tibi unus de mille.

verses.text: If thou wouldst get a friend, try him before thou takest him, and do not credit him easily.
verses.textLatin: Si possides amicum, in tentatione posside eum, et ne facile credas ei.

verses.text: For there is a friend for his own occasion, and he will not abide in the day of thy trouble.
verses.textLatin: Est enim amicus secundum tempus suum, et non permanebit in die tribulationis.

verses.text: And there is a friend that turneth to enmity; and there is a friend that will disclose hatred and strife and reproaches.
verses.textLatin: Et est amicus qui convertitur ad inimicitiam, et est amicus qui odium et rixam et convitia denudabit.

verses.text: And there is a friend a companion at the table, and he will not abide in the day of distress.
verses.textLatin: Est autem amicus socius mensæ, et non permanebit in die necessitatis.

verses.text: A friend if he continue steadfast, shall be to thee as thyself, and shall act with confidence among them of thy household.
verses.textLatin: Amicus si permanserit fixus, erit tibi quasi coæqualis, et in domesticis tuis fiducialiter aget.

verses.text: If he humble himself before thee, and hide himself from thy face, thou shalt have unanimous friendship for good.
verses.textLatin: Si humiliaverit se contra te, et a facie tua absconderit se, unanimem habebis amicitiam bonam.

verses.text: Separate thyself from thy enemies, and take heed of thy friends.
verses.textLatin: Ab inimicis tuis separare, et ab amicis tuis attende.

verses.text: A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found him, hath found a treasure.
verses.textLatin: Amicus fidelis protectio fortis: qui autem invenit illum, invenit thesaurum.

verses.text: Nothing can be compared to a faithful friend, and no weight of gold and silver is able to countervail the goodness of his fidelity.
verses.textLatin: Amico fideli nulla est comparatio, et non est digna ponderatio auri et argenti contra bonitatem fidei illius.

verses.text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life and immortality: and they that fear the Lord, shall find him.
verses.textLatin: Amicus fidelis medicamentum vitæ et immortalitatis: et qui metuunt Dominum, invenient illum.

verses.text: He that feareth God, shall likewise have good friendship: because according to him shall his friend be.
verses.textLatin: Qui timet Deum æque habebit amicitiam bonam, quoniam secundum illum erit amicus illius.

verses.text: My son, from thy youth up receive instruction, and even to thy grey hairs thou shalt find wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Fili, a juventute tua excipe doctrinam, et usque ad canos invenies sapientiam.

verses.text: Come to her as one that plougheth, and soweth, and wait for her good fruits:
verses.textLatin: Quasi is qui arat et seminat accede ad eam, et sustine bonos fructus illius.

verses.text: For in working about her thou shalt labour a little, and shalt quickly eat of her fruits.
verses.textLatin: In opere enim ipsius exiguum laborabis, et cito edes de generationibus illius.

verses.text: How very unpleasant is wisdom to the unlearned, and the unwise will not continue with her.
verses.textLatin: Quam aspera est nimium sapientia indoctis hominibus! et non permanebit in illa excors.

verses.text: She shall be to them as a mighty stone of trial, and they will cast her from them before it be long.
verses.textLatin: Quasi lapidis virtus probatio erit in illis: et non demorabuntur projicere illam.

verses.text: For the wisdom of doctrine is according to her name, and she is not manifest unto many, but with them to whom she is known, she continueth even to the sight of God.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia enim doctrinæ secundum nomen est ejus, et non est multis manifestata: quibus autem cognita est, permanet usque ad conspectum Dei.

verses.text: Give ear, my son, and take wise counsel, and cast not away my advice.
verses.textLatin: Audi, fili, et accipe consilium intellectus, et ne abjicias consilium meum.

verses.text: Put thy feet into her fetters, and thy neck into her chains:
verses.textLatin: Injice pedem tuum in compedes illius, et in torques illius collum tuum.

verses.text: Bow down thy shoulder, and bear her, and be not grieved with her bands.
verses.textLatin: Subjice humerum tuum, et porta illam, et ne acedieris vinculis ejus.

verses.text: Come to her with all thy mind, and keep her ways with all thy power.
verses.textLatin: In omni animo tuo accede ad illam, et in omni virtute tua conserva vias ejus.

verses.text: Search for her, and she shall be made known to thee, and when thou hast gotten her, let her not go:
verses.textLatin: Investiga illam, et manifestabitur tibi: et continens factus, ne derelinquas eam:

verses.text: For in the latter end thou shalt find rest in her, and she shall be turned to thy joy.
verses.textLatin: in novissimis enim invenies requiem in ea, et convertetur tibi in oblectationem.

verses.text: Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for thee, and a firm foundation, and her chain a robe of glory:
verses.textLatin: Et erunt tibi compedes ejus in protectionem fortitudinis et bases virtutis, et torques illius in stolam gloriæ:

verses.text: For in her is the beauty of life, and her bands are a healthful binding.
verses.textLatin: decor enim vitæ est in illa, et vincula illius alligatura salutaris.

verses.text: Thou shalt put her on as a robe of glory, and thou shalt set her upon thee as a crown of joy.
verses.textLatin: Stolam gloriæ indues eam, et coronam gratulationis superpones tibi.

verses.text: My son, if thou wilt attend to me, thou shalt learn: and if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be wise.
verses.textLatin: Fili, si attenderis mihi, disces: et si accommodaveris animum tuum, sapiens eris.

verses.text: If thou wilt incline thy ear, thou shalt receive instruction: and if thou love to hear, thou shalt be wise.
verses.textLatin: Si inclinaveris aurem tuam, excipies doctrinam: et si dilexeris audire, sapiens eris.

verses.text: Stand in the multitude of ancients that are wise, and join thyself from thy heart to their wisdom, that thou mayst hear every discourse of God, and the sayings of praise may not escape thee.
verses.textLatin: In multitudine presbyterorum prudentium sta, et sapientiæ illorum ex corde conjungere, ut omnem narrationem Dei possis audire, et proverbia laudis non effugiant a te.

verses.text: And if thou see a man of understanding, go to him early in the morning, and let thy foot wear the steps of his doors.
verses.textLatin: Et si videris sensatum, evigila ad eum, et gradus ostiorum illius exterat pes tuus.

verses.text: Let thy thoughts be upon the precepts of God, and meditate continually on his commandments: and he will give thee a heart, and the desire of wisdom shall be given to thee.
verses.textLatin: Cogitatum tuum habe in præceptis Dei, et in mandatis illius maxime assiduus esto: et ipse dabit tibi cor, et concupiscentia sapientiæ dabitur tibi.

verses.text: Do  no evils, and no evils shall lay hold of thee.
verses.textLatin: Noli facere mala, et non te apprehendent:

verses.text: Depart from the unjust, and evils shall depart from thee.
verses.textLatin: discede ab iniquo, et deficient mala abs te.

verses.text: My son, sow not evils in the furrows of injustice, and thou shalt not reap them sevenfold.
verses.textLatin: Fili, non semines mala in sulcis injustitiæ, et non metes ea in septuplum.

verses.text: Seek not of the Lord a pre-eminence, nor of the king the seat of honour.
verses.textLatin: Noli quærere a Domino ducatum, neque a rege cathedram honoris.

verses.text: Justify not thyself before God, for he knoweth the heart: and desire not to appear wise before the king.
verses.textLatin: Non te justifices ante Deum, quoniam agnitor cordis ipse est: et penes regem noli velle videri sapiens.

verses.text: Seek not to be made a judge, unless thou have strength enough to extirpate iniquities: lest thou fear the person of the powerful, and lay a stumblingblock for thy integrity.
verses.textLatin: Noli quærere fieri judex, nisi valeas virtute irrumpere iniquitates: ne forte extimescas faciem potentis, et ponas scandalum in æquitate tua.

verses.text: Offend not against the multitude of a city, neither cast thyself in upon the people,
verses.textLatin: Non pecces in multitudinem civitatis, nec te immittas in populum:

verses.text: Nor bind sin to sin: for even in one thou shalt not be unpunished.
verses.textLatin: neque alliges duplicia peccata, nec enim in uno eris immunis.

verses.text: Be not fainthearted in thy mind:
verses.textLatin: Noli esse pusillanimis in animo tuo:

verses.text: Neglect not to pray, and to give alms.
verses.textLatin: exorare et facere eleemosynam ne despicias.

verses.text: Say not: God will have respect to the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer to the most high God, he will accept my offerings.
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas: In multitudine munerum meorum respiciet Deus, et offerente me Deo altissimo, munera mea suscipiet.

verses.text: Laugh no man to scorn in the bitterness of his soul: for there is one that humbleth and exalteth, God who seeth all.
verses.textLatin: Non irrideas hominem in amaritudine animæ: est enim qui humiliat et exaltat circumspector Deus.

verses.text: Devise not a lie against thy brother: neither do the like against thy friend.
verses.textLatin: Noli amare mendacium adversus fratrem tuum, neque in amicum similiter facias.

verses.text: Be not willing to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.
verses.textLatin: Noli velle mentiri omne mendacium: assiduitas enim illius non est bona.

verses.text: Be not full of words in a multitude of ancients, and repeat not the word in thy prayer.
verses.textLatin: Noli verbosus esse in multitudine presbyterorum, et non iteres verbum in oratione tua.

verses.text: Hate not laborious works, nor husbandry ordained by the most High.
verses.textLatin: Non oderis laboriosa opera, et rusticationem creatam ab Altissimo.

verses.text: Number not thyself among the multitude of the disorderly.
verses.textLatin: Non te reputes in multitudine indisciplinatorum.

verses.text: Remember wrath, for it will not tarry long.
verses.textLatin: Memento iræ, quoniam non tardabit.

verses.text: Humble thy spirit very much: for the vengeance on the flesh of the ungodly is fire and worms.
verses.textLatin: Humilia valde spiritum tuum, quoniam vindicta carnis impii ignis et vermis.

verses.text: Do not transgress against thy friend deferring money, nor despise thy dear brother for the sake of gold.
verses.textLatin: Noli prævaricari in amicum pecuniam differentem, neque fratrem carissimum auro spreveris.

verses.text: Depart not from a wise and good wife, whom thou hast gotten in the fear of the Lord: for the grace of her modesty is above gold.
verses.textLatin: Noli discedere a muliere sensata et bona, quam sortitus es in timore Domini: gratia enim verecundiæ illius super aurum.

verses.text: Hurt not the servant that worketh faithfully, nor the hired man that giveth thee his life.
verses.textLatin: Non lædas servum in veritate operantem, neque mercenarium dantem animam suam.

verses.text: Let a wise servant be dear to thee as thy own soul, defraud him not of liberty, nor leave him needy.
verses.textLatin: Servus sensatus sit tibi dilectus quasi anima tua: non defraudes illum libertate, neque inopem derelinquas illum.

verses.text: Hast thou cattle? have an eye to them: and if they be for thy profit, keep them with thee.
verses.textLatin: Pecora tibi sunt, attende illis: et si sunt utilia, perseverent apud te.

verses.text: Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their childhood.
verses.textLatin: Filii tibi sunt? erudi illos, et curva illos a pueritia illorum.

verses.text: Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thy countenance gay towards them.
verses.textLatin: Filiæ tibi sunt? serva corpus illarum, et non ostendas hilarem faciem tuam ad illas.

verses.text: Marry thy daughter well, and thou shalt do a great work, and give her to a wise man.
verses.textLatin: Trade filiam, et grande opus feceris: et homini sensato da illam.

verses.text: If thou hast a wife according to thy soul, cast her not off: and to her that is hateful, trust not thyself. With thy whole heart,
verses.textLatin: Mulier si est tibi secundum animam tuam, non projicias illam: et odibili non credas te. In toto corde tuo

verses.text: Honour thy father, and forget not the groanings of thy mother:
verses.textLatin: honora patrem tuum, et gemitus matris tuæ ne obliviscaris:

verses.text: Remember that thou hadst not been born but through them: and make a return to them as they have done for thee.
verses.textLatin: memento quoniam nisi per illos natus non fuisses: et retribue illis, quomodo et illi tibi.

verses.text: With all thy soul fear the Lord, and reverence his priests.
verses.textLatin: In tota anima tua time Dominum, et sacerdotes illius sanctifica.

verses.text: With all thy strength love him that made thee: and forsake not his ministers.
verses.textLatin: In omni virtute tua dilige eum qui te fecit, et ministros ejus ne derelinquas.

verses.text: Honour God with all thy soul, and give honour to the priests, and purify thyself with thy arms.
verses.textLatin: Honora Deum ex tota anima tua, et honorifica sacerdotes, et propurga te cum brachiis.

verses.text: Give them their portion, as it is commanded thee, of the firstfruits and of purifications: and for thy negligences purify thyself with a few.
verses.textLatin: Da illis partem, sicut mandatum est tibi, primitiarum et purgationis, et de negligentia tua purga te cum paucis.

verses.text: Offer to the Lord the gift of thy shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things:
verses.textLatin: Datum brachiorum tuorum, et sacrificium sanctificationis offeres Domino, et initia sanctorum.

verses.text: And stretch out thy hand to the poor, that thy expiation and thy blessing may be perfected.
verses.textLatin: Et pauperi porrige manum tuam, ut perficiatur propitiatio et benedictio tua.

verses.text: A gift hath grace in the sight of all the living, and restrain not grace from the dead.
verses.textLatin: Gratia dati in conspectu omnis viventis, et mortuo non prohibeas gratiam.

verses.text: Be not wanting in comforting them that weep, and walk with them that mourn.
verses.textLatin: Non desis plorantibus in consolatione, et cum lugentibus ambula.

verses.text: Be not slow to visit the sick: for by these things thou shalt be confirmed in love.
verses.textLatin: Non te pigeat visitare infirmum: ex his enim in dilectione firmaberis.

verses.text: In all thy works remember thy last end, and thou shalt never sin.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus operibus tuis memorare novissima tua, et in æternum non peccabis.

verses.text: Strive  not with a powerful man, lest thou fall into his hands.
verses.textLatin: Non litiges cum homine potente, ne forte incidas in manus illius.

verses.text: Contend not with a rich man, lest he bring an action against thee.
verses.textLatin: Non contendas cum viro locuplete, ne forte contra te constituat litem tibi:

verses.text: For gold and silver hath destroyed many, and hath reached even to the heart of kings, and perverted them.
verses.textLatin: multos enim perdidit aurum et argentum, et usque ad cor regum extendit et convertit.

verses.text: Strive not with a man that is full of tongue, and heap not wood upon his fire.
verses.textLatin: Non litiges cum homine linguato, et non strues in ignem illius ligna.

verses.text: Communicate not with an ignorant man, lest he speak ill of thy family.
verses.textLatin: Non communices homini indocto, ne male de progenie tua loquatur.

verses.text: Despise not a man that turneth away from sin, nor reproach him therewith: remember that we are all worthy of reproof.
verses.textLatin: Ne despicias hominem avertentem se a peccato, neque improperes ei: memento quoniam omnes in correptione sumus.

verses.text: Despise not a man in his old age; for we also shall become old.
verses.textLatin: Ne spernas hominem in sua senectute, etenim ex nobis senescunt.

verses.text: Rejoice not at the death of thy enemy; knowing that we all die, and are not willing that others should rejoice at our death.
verses.textLatin: Noli de mortuo inimico tuo gaudere: sciens quoniam omnes morimur, et in gaudium nolumus venire.

verses.text: Despise not the discourse of them that are ancient and wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs.
verses.textLatin: Ne despicias narrationem presbyterorum sapientium, et in proverbiis eorum conversare:

verses.text: For of them thou shalt learn wisdom, and instruction of understanding, and to serve great men without blame.
verses.textLatin: ab ipsis enim disces sapientiam et doctrinam intellectus, et servire magnatis sine querela.

verses.text: Let not the discourse of the ancients escape thee, for they have learned of their fathers:
verses.textLatin: Non te prætereat narratio seniorum, ipsi enim didicerunt a patribus suis:

verses.text: For of them thou shalt learn understanding, and to give an answer in time of need.
verses.textLatin: quoniam ab ipsis disces intellectum, et in tempore necessitatis dare responsum.

verses.text: Kindle not the coals of sinners by rebuking them, lest thou be burnt with the flame of the fire of their sins.
verses.textLatin: Non incendas carbones peccatorum arguens eos, et ne incendaris flamma ignis peccatorum illorum.

verses.text: Stand not against the face of an injurious person, lest he sit as a spy to entrap thee in thy words.
verses.textLatin: Ne contra faciem stes contumeliosi, ne sedeat quasi insidiator ori tuo.

verses.text: Lend not to a man that is mightier than thyself: and if thou lendest, count it as lost.
verses.textLatin: Noli fœnerari homini fortiori te: quod si fœneraveris, quasi perditum habe.

verses.text: Be not surety above thy power: and if thou be surety, think as if thou wert to pay it.
verses.textLatin: Non spondeas super virtutem tuam: quod si spoponderis, quasi restituens cogita.

verses.text: Judge not against a judge: for he judgeth according to that which is just.
verses.textLatin: Non judices contra judicem, quoniam secundum quod justum est judicat.

verses.text: Go not on the way with a bold man, lest he burden thee with his evils: for he goeth according to his own will, and thou shalt perish together with his folly.
verses.textLatin: Cum audace non eas in via, ne forte gravet mala sua in te: ipse enim secundum voluntatem suam vadit, et simul cum stultitia illius peries.

verses.text: Quarrel not with a passionate man, and go not into the desert with a bold man: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no help he will overthrow thee.
verses.textLatin: Cum iracundo non facias rixam, et cum audace non eas in desertum: quoniam quasi nihil est ante illum sanguis, et ubi non est adjutorium, elidet te.

verses.text: Advise not with fools, for they cannot love but such things as please them.
verses.textLatin: Cum fatuis consilium non habeas: non enim poterunt diligere nisi quæ eis placent.

verses.text: Before a stranger do no matter of counsel: for thou knowest not what he will bring forth.
verses.textLatin: Coram extraneo ne facias consilium: nescis enim quid pariet.

verses.text: Open not thy heart to every man: lest he repay thee with an evil turn, and speak reproachfully to thee.
verses.textLatin: Non omni homini cor tuum manifestes, ne forte inferat tibi gratiam falsam, et convicietur tibi.

verses.text: Be  not jealous over the wife of thy bosom, lest she shew in thy regard the malice of a wicked lesson.
verses.textLatin: Non zeles mulierem sinus tui, ne ostendat super te malitiam doctrinæ nequam.

verses.text: Give not the power of thy soul to a woman, lest she enter upon thy strength, and thou be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Non des mulieri potestatem animæ tuæ, ne ingrediatur in virtutem tuam, et confundaris.

verses.text: Look not upon a woman that hath a mind for many: lest thou fall into her snares.
verses.textLatin: Ne respicias mulierem multivolam, ne forte incidas in laqueos illius.

verses.text: Use not much the company of her that is a dancer, and hearken not to her, lest thou perish by the force of her charms.
verses.textLatin: Cum saltatrice ne assiduus sis, nec audias illam, ne forte pereas in efficacia illius.

verses.text: Gaze not upon a maiden, lest her beauty be a stumblingblock to thee.
verses.textLatin: Virginem ne conspicias, ne forte scandalizeris in decore illius.

verses.text: Give not thy soul to harlots in any point: lest thou destroy thyself and thy inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Ne des fornicariis animam tuam in ullo, ne perdas te et hæreditatem tuam.

verses.text: Look not round about thee in the ways of the city, nor wander up and down in the streets thereof.
verses.textLatin: Noli circumspicere in vicis civitatis, nec oberraveris in plateis illius.

verses.text: Turn away thy face from a woman dressed up, and gaze not about upon another’s beauty.
verses.textLatin: Averte faciem tuam a muliere compta, et ne circumspicias speciem alienam.

verses.text: For many have perished by the beauty of a woman, and hereby lust is enkindled as a fire.
verses.textLatin: Propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt: et ex hoc concupiscentia quasi ignis exardescit.

verses.text: Every woman that is a harlot, shall be trodden upon as dung in the way.
verses.textLatin: Omnis mulier quæ est fornicaria, quasi stercus in via conculcabitur.

verses.text: Many by admiring the beauty of another man’s wife, have become reprobate, for her conversation burneth as fire.
verses.textLatin: Speciem mulieris alienæ multi admirati, reprobi facti sunt: colloquium enim illius quasi ignis exardescit.

verses.text: Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor repose upon the bed with her:
verses.textLatin: Cum aliena muliere ne sedeas omnino, nec accumbas cum ea super cubitum:

verses.text: And strive not with her over wine, lest thy heart decline towards her and by thy blood thou fall into destruction.
verses.textLatin: et non alterceris cum illa in vino, ne forte declinet cor tuum in illam, et sanguine tuo labaris in perditionem.

verses.text: Forsake not an old friend, for the new will not be like to him.
verses.textLatin: Ne derelinquas amicum antiquum: novus enim non erit similis illi.

verses.text: A new friend is as new wine: it shall grow old, and thou shalt drink it with pleasure.
verses.textLatin: Vinum novum amicus novus: veterascet, et cum suavitate bibes illud.

verses.text: Envy not the glory and riches of a sinner: for thou knowest not what his ruin shall be.
verses.textLatin: Non zeles gloriam et opes peccatoris: non enim scis quæ futura sit illius subversio.

verses.text: Be not pleased with the wrong done by the unjust, knowing that even to hell the wicked shall not please.
verses.textLatin: Non placeat tibi injuria injustorum, sciens quoniam usque ad inferos non placebit impius.

verses.text: Keep thee far from the man that hath power to kill, so thou shalt not suspect the fear of death.
verses.textLatin: Longe abesto ab homine potestatem habente occidendi, et non suspicaberis timorem mortis.

verses.text: And if thou come to him, commit no fault, lest he take away thy life.
verses.textLatin: Et si accesseris ad illum, noli aliquid committere, ne forte auferat vitam tuam.

verses.text: Know it to be a communication with death: for thou art going in the midst of snares, and walking upon the arms of them that are grieved.
verses.textLatin: Communionem mortis scito, quoniam in medio laqueorum ingredieris, et super dolentium arma ambulabis.

verses.text: According to thy power beware of thy neighbour, and treat with the wise and prudent.
verses.textLatin: Secundum virtutem tuam cave te a proximo tuo, et cum sapientibus et prudentibus tracta.

verses.text: Let just men be thy guests, and let thy glory be in the fear of God.
verses.textLatin: Viri justi sint tibi convivæ, et in timore Dei sit tibi gloriatio:

verses.text: And let the thought of God be in thy mind, and all thy discourse on the commandments of the Highest.
verses.textLatin: et in sensu sit tibi cogitatus Dei, et omnis enarratio tua in præceptis Altissimi.

verses.text: Works shall be praised for the hand of the artificers, and the prince of the people for the wisdom of his speech, but the word of the ancients for the sense.
verses.textLatin: In manu artificum opera laudabuntur, et princeps populi in sapientia sermonis sui, in sensu vero seniorum verbum.

verses.text: A man full of tongue is terrible in his city, and he that is rash in his word shall be hateful.
verses.textLatin: Terribilis est in civitate sua homo linguosus: et temerarius in verbo suo odibilis erit.

verses.text: A wise judge shall judge his people, and the government of a prudent man shall be steady.
verses.textLatin: Judex sapiens judicabit populum suum, et principatus sensati stabilis erit.

verses.text: As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus: et qualis rector est civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea.

verses.text: An unwise king shall be the ruin of his people: and cities shall be inhabited through the prudence of the rulers.
verses.textLatin: Rex insipiens perdet populum suum: et civitates inhabitabuntur per sensum potentium.

verses.text: The power of the earth is in the hand of God, and in his time he will raise up a profitable ruler over it.
verses.textLatin: In manu Dei potestas terræ: et utilem rectorem suscitabit in tempus super illam.

verses.text: The prosperity of man is in the hand of God, and upon the person of the scribe he shall lay his honour.
verses.textLatin: In manu Dei prosperitas hominis, et super faciem scribæ imponet honorem suum.

verses.text: Remember not any injury done thee by thy neighbour, and do thou nothing by deeds of injury.
verses.textLatin: Omnis injuriæ proximi ne memineris, et nihil agas in operibus injuriæ.

verses.text: Pride is hateful before God and men: and all iniquity of nations is execrable.
verses.textLatin: Odibilis coram Deo est et hominibus superbia, et execrabilis omnis iniquitas gentium.

verses.text: A kingdom is translated from one people to another, because of injustices, and wrongs, and injuries, and divers deceits.
verses.textLatin: Regnum a gente in gentem transfertur propter injustitias, et injurias, et contumelias, et diversos dolos.

verses.text: But nothing is more wicked than the covetous man. Why is earth, and ashes proud?
verses.textLatin: Avaro autem nihil est scelestius. Quid superbit terra et cinis?

verses.text: There is not a more wicked thing than to love money: for such a one setteth even his own soul to sale: because while he liveth he hath cast away his bowels.
verses.textLatin: Nihil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam: hic enim et animam suam venalem habet, quoniam in vita sua projecit intima sua.

verses.text: All power is of short life. A long sickness is troublesome to the physician.
verses.textLatin: Omnis potentatus brevis vita; languor prolixior gravat medicum.

verses.text: The physician cutteth off a short sickness: so also a king is to day, and to morrow he shall die.
verses.textLatin: Brevem languorem præcidit medicus: sic et rex hodie est, et cras morietur.

verses.text: For when a man shall die, he shall inherit serpents, and beasts, and worms.
verses.textLatin: Cum enim morietur homo, hæreditabit serpentes, et bestias, et vermes.

verses.text: The beginning of the pride of man, is to fall off from God:
verses.textLatin: Initium superbiæ hominis apostatare a Deo:

verses.text: Because his heart is departed from him that made him: for pride is the beginning of all sin: he that holdeth it, shall be filled with maledictions, and it shall ruin him in the end.
verses.textLatin: quoniam ab eo qui fecit illum recessit cor ejus, quoniam initium omnis peccati est superbia. Qui tenuerit illam adimplebitur maledictis, et subvertet eum in finem.

verses.text: Therefore hath the Lord disgraced the assemblies of the wicked, and hath utterly destroyed them.
verses.textLatin: Propterea exhonoravit Dominus conventus malorum, et destruxit eos usque in finem.

verses.text: God hath overturned the thrones of proud princes, and hath set up the meek in their stead.
verses.textLatin: Sedes ducum superborum destruxit Deus, et sedere fecit mites pro eis.

verses.text: God hath made the roots of proud nations to wither, and hath planted the humble of these nations.
verses.textLatin: Radices gentium superbarum arefecit Deus, et plantavit humiles ex ipsis gentibus.

verses.text: The Lord hath overthrown the lands of the Gentiles, and hath destroyed them even to the foundation.
verses.textLatin: Terras gentium evertit Dominus, et perdidit eas usque ad fundamentum.

verses.text: He hath made some of them to wither away, and hath destroyed them, and hath made the memory of them to cease from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Arefecit ex ipsis, et disperdidit eos, et cessare fecit memoriam eorum a terra.

verses.text: God hath abolished the memory of the proud, and hath preserved the memory of them that are humble in mind.
verses.textLatin: Memoria superborum perdidit Deus, et reliquit memoriam humilium sensu.

verses.text: Pride was not made for men: nor wrath for the race of women.
verses.textLatin: Non est creata hominibus superbia, neque iracundia nationi mulierum.

verses.text: That seed of men shall be honoured, which feareth God: but that seed shall be dishonoured, which transgresseth the commandments of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Semen hominum honorabitur hoc, quod timet Deum: semen autem hoc exhonorabitur, quod præterit mandata Domini.

verses.text: In the midst of brethren their chief is honourable: so shall they that fear the Lord, be in his eyes.
verses.textLatin: In medio fratrum rector illorum in honore: et qui timent Dominum erunt in oculis illius.

verses.text: The fear of God is the glory of the rich, and of the honourable, and of the poor.
verses.textLatin: Gloria divitum, honoratorum, et pauperum, timor Dei est.

verses.text: Despise not a just man that is poor, and do not magnify a sinful man that is rich.
verses.textLatin: Noli despicere hominem justum pauperem, et noli magnificare virum peccatorem divitem.

verses.text: The great man, and the judge, and the mighty is in honour: and there is none greater than he that feareth God.
verses.textLatin: Magnus, et judex, et potens est in honore: et non est major illo qui timet Deum.

verses.text: They that are free shall serve a servant that is wise: and a man that is prudent and well instructed will not murmur when he is reproved; and he that is ignorant, shall not be honoured.
verses.textLatin: Servo sensato liberi servient: et vir prudens et disciplinatus non murmurabit correptus, et inscius non honorabitur.

verses.text: Extol not thyself in doing thy work, and linger not in the time of distress:
verses.textLatin: Noli extollere te in faciendo opere tuo, et noli cunctari in tempore angustiæ.

verses.text: Better is he that laboureth, and aboundeth in all things, than he that boasteth himself and wanteth bread.
verses.textLatin: Melior est qui operatur et abundat in omnibus, quam qui gloriatur et eget pane.

verses.text: My son, keep thy soul in meekness, and give it honour according to its desert.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in mansuetudine serva animam tuam, et da illi honorem secundum meritum suum.

verses.text: Who will justify him that sinneth against his own soul? and who will honour him that dishonoureth his own soul?
verses.textLatin: Peccantem in animam suam quis justificabit? et quis honorificabit exhonorantem animam suam?

verses.text: The poor man is glorified by his discipline and fear: and there is a man that is honoured for his wealth.
verses.textLatin: Pauper gloriatur per disciplinam et timorem suum: et est homo qui honorificatur propter substantiam suam.

verses.text: But he that is glorified in poverty, how much more in wealth? and he that is glorified in wealth, let him fear poverty.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem gloriatur in paupertate, quanto magis in substantia! et qui gloriatur in substantia, paupertatem vereatur.

verses.text: T  HE wisdom of the humble shall exalt his head, and shall make him sit in the midst of great men.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia humiliati exaltabit caput illius, et in medio magnatorum consedere illum faciet.

verses.text: Praise not a man for his beauty, neither despise a man for his look.
verses.textLatin: Non laudes virum in specie sua, neque spernas hominem in visu suo.

verses.text: The bee is small among flying things, but her fruit hath the chiefest sweetness.
verses.textLatin: Brevis in volatilibus est apis, et initium dulcoris habet fructus illius.

verses.text: Glory not in apparel at any time, and be not exalted in the day of thy honour: for the works of the Highest only are wonderful, and his works are glorious, and secret, and hidden.
verses.textLatin: In vestitu ne glorieris umquam, nec in die honoris tui extollaris: quoniam mirabilia opera Altissimi solius, et gloriosa, et absconsa, et invisa opera illius.

verses.text: Many tyrants have sat on the throne, and he whom no man would think on, hath worn the crown.
verses.textLatin: Multi tyranni sederunt in throno: et insuspicabilis portavit diadema.

verses.text: Many mighty men have been greatly brought down, and the glorious have been delivered into the hand of others.
verses.textLatin: Multi potentes oppressi sunt valide, et gloriosi traditi sunt in manus alterorum.

verses.text: Before thou inquire, blame no man: and when thou hast inquired, reprove justly.
verses.textLatin: Priusquam interroges, ne vituperes quemquam: et cum interrogaveris, corripe juste.

verses.text: Before thou hear, answer not a word: and interrupt not others in the midst of their discourse.
verses.textLatin: Priusquam audias, ne respondeas verbum: et in medio sermonum ne adjicias loqui.

verses.text: Strive not in a matter which doth not concern thee, and sit not in judgment with sinners.
verses.textLatin: De ea re quæ te non molestat, ne certeris: et in judicio peccantium ne consistas.
