verses.text: My son, meddle not with many matters: and if thou be rich, thou shalt not be free from sin: for if thou pursue after thou shalt not overtake: and if thou run before thou shalt not escape.
verses.textLatin: Fili, ne in multis sint actus tui: et si dives fueris, non eris immunis a delicto. Si enim secutus fueris, non apprehendes: et non effugies, si præcucurreris.

verses.text: There is an ungodly man that laboureth, and maketh haste, and is in sorrow, and is so much the more in want.
verses.textLatin: Est homo laborans et festinans, et dolens: impius, et tanto magis non abundabit.

verses.text: Again, there is an inactive man that wanteth help, is very weak in ability, and full of poverty:
verses.textLatin: Est homo marcidus egens recuperatione, plus deficiens virtute, et abundans paupertate:

verses.text: Yet the eye of God hath looked upon him for good, and hath lifted him up from his low estate, and hath exalted his head: and many have wondered at him, and have glorified God.
verses.textLatin: et oculus Dei respexit illum in bono, et erexit eum ab humilitate ipsius, et exaltavit caput ejus: et mirati sunt in illo multi, et honoraverunt Deum.

verses.text: Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and riches, are from God.
verses.textLatin: Bona et mala, vita et mors, paupertas et honestas, a Deo sunt:

verses.text: Wisdom and discipline, and the knowledge of the law are with God. Love and the ways of good things are with him.
verses.textLatin: sapientia, et disciplina, et scientia legis, apud Deum: dilectio, et viæ bonorum, apud ipsum.

verses.text: Error and darkness are created with sinners: and they that glory in evil things, grow old in evil.
verses.textLatin: Error et tenebræ peccatoribus concreata sunt: qui autem exsultant in malis consenescunt in malo.

verses.text: The gift of God abideth with the just, and his advancement shall have success for ever.
verses.textLatin: Datio Dei permanet justis, et profectus illius successus habebit in æternum.

verses.text: There is one that is enriched by living sparingly, and this is the portion of his reward.
verses.textLatin: Est qui locupletatur parce agendo, et hæc est pars mercedis illius.

verses.text: In that he saith: I have found me rest, and now I will eat of my goods alone:
verses.textLatin: In eo quod dicit: Inveni requiem mihi, et nunc manducabo de bonis meis solus:

verses.text: And he knoweth not what time shall pass, and that death approacheth, and that he must leave all to others, and shall die.
verses.textLatin: et nescit quod tempus præteriet, et mors appropinquet, et relinquat omnia aliis, et morietur.

verses.text: Be steadfast in thy covenant, and be conversant therein, and grow old in the work of thy commandments.
verses.textLatin: Sta in testamento tuo, et in illo colloquere, et in opere mandatorum tuorum veterasce.

verses.text: Abide not in the works of sinners. But trust in God, and stay in thy place.
verses.textLatin: Ne manseris in operibus peccatorum: confide autem in Deo, et mane in loco tuo.

verses.text: For it is easy in the eyes of God on a sudden to make the poor man rich.
verses.textLatin: Facile est enim in oculis Dei subito honestare pauperem.

verses.text: The blessing of God maketh haste to reward the just, and in a swift hour his blessing beareth fruit.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio Dei in mercedem justi festinat, et in hora veloci processus illius fructificat.

verses.text: Say not: What need I, and what good shall I have by this?
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas: Quid est mihi opus? et quæ erunt mihi ex hoc bona?

verses.text: Say not: I am sufficient for myself: and what shall I be made worse by this?
verses.textLatin: Ne dicas: Sufficiens mihi sum: et quid ex hoc pessimabor?

verses.text: In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils: and in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things:
verses.textLatin: In die bonorum ne immemor sis malorum, et in die malorum ne immemor sis bonorum:

verses.text: For it is easy before God in the day of death to reward every one according to his ways.
verses.textLatin: quoniam facile est coram Deo in die obitus retribuere unicuique secundum vias suas.

verses.text: The affliction of an hour maketh one forget great delights, and in the end of a man is the disclosing of his works.
verses.textLatin: Malitia horæ oblivionem facit luxuriæ magnæ, et in fine hominis denudatio operum illius.

verses.text: Praise not any man before death, for a man is known by his children.
verses.textLatin: Ante mortem ne laudes hominem quemquam: quoniam in filiis suis agnoscitur vir.

verses.text: Bring not every man into thy house: for many are the snares of the deceitful.
verses.textLatin: Non omnem hominem inducas in domum tuam: multæ enim sunt insidiæ dolosi.

verses.text: For as corrupted bowels send forth stinking breath, and as the partridge is brought into the cage, and as the roe into the snare: so also is the heart of the proud, and as a spy that looketh on the fall of his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim eructant præcordia fœtentium, et sicut perdix inducitur in caveam, et ut caprea in laqueum: sic et cor superborum, et sicut prospector videns casum proximi sui.

verses.text: For he lieth in wait and turneth good into evil, and on the elect he will lay a blot.
verses.textLatin: Bona enim in mala convertens insidiatur, et in electis imponet maculam.

verses.text: Of one spark cometh a great fire, and of one deceitful man much blood: and a sinful man lieth in wait for blood.
verses.textLatin: A scintilla una augetur ignis, et ab uno doloso augetur sanguis: homo vero peccator sanguini insidiatur.

verses.text: Take heed to thyself of a mischievous man, for he worketh evils: lest he bring upon thee reproach for ever.
verses.textLatin: Attende tibi a pestifero, fabricat enim mala, ne inducat super te subsannationem in perpetuum.

verses.text: Receive a stranger in, and he shall overthrow thee with a whirlwind, and shall turn thee out of thy own.
verses.textLatin: Admitte ad te alienigenam: et subvertet te in turbine, et abalienabit te a tuis propriis.

verses.text: If  thou do good, know to whom thou dost it, and there shall be much thanks for thy good deeds.
verses.textLatin: Si benefeceris, scito cui feceris, et erit gratia in bonis tuis multa.

verses.text: Do good to the just, and thou shalt find great recompense: and if not of him, assuredly of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Benefac justo, et invenies retributionem magnam: et si non ab ipso, certe a Domino.

verses.text: For there is no good for him that is always occupied in evil, and that giveth no alms: for the Highest hateth sinners, and hath mercy on the penitent.
verses.textLatin: Non est enim ei bene qui assiduus est in malis, et eleemosynas non danti: quoniam et Altissimus odio habet peccatores, et misertus est pœnitentibus.

verses.text: Give to the merciful and uphold not the sinner: God will repay vengeance to the ungodly and to sinners, and keep them against the day of vengeance.
verses.textLatin: Da misericordi, et ne suscipias peccatorem: et impiis et peccatoribus reddet vindictam, custodiens eos in diem vindictæ.

verses.text: Give to the good, and receive not a sinner.
verses.textLatin: Da bono, et non receperis peccatorem.

verses.text: Do good to the humble, and give not to the ungodly: hold back thy bread, and give it not to him, lest thereby he overmaster thee.
verses.textLatin: Benefac humili, et non dederis impio: prohibe panes illi dari, ne in ipsis potentior te sit:

verses.text: For thou shalt receive twice as much evil for all the good thou shalt have done to him: for the Highest also hateth sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
verses.textLatin: nam duplicia mala invenies in omnibus bonis quæcumque feceris illi, quoniam et Altissimus odio habet peccatores, et impiis reddet vindictam.

verses.text: A friend shall not be known in prosperity, and an enemy shall not be hidden in adversity.
verses.textLatin: Non agnoscetur in bonis amicus, et non abscondetur in malis inimicus.

verses.text: In the prosperity of a man, his enemies are grieved: and a friend is known in his adversity.
verses.textLatin: In bonis viri, inimici illius in tristitia: et in malitia illius, amicus agnitus est.

verses.text: Never trust thy enemy: for as a brass pot his wickedness rusteth:
verses.textLatin: Non credas inimico tuo in æternum: sicut enim æramentum æruginat nequitia illius:

verses.text: Though he humble himself and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him.
verses.textLatin: et si humiliatus vadat curvus, adjice animum tuum, et custodi te ab illo.

verses.text: Set him not by thee, neither let him sit on thy right hand, lest he turn into thy place, and seek to take thy seat: and at the last thou acknowledge my words, and be pricked with my sayings.
verses.textLatin: Non statuas illum penes te, nec sedeat ad dexteram tuam, ne forte conversus in locum tuum, inquirat cathedram tuam, et in novissimo agnosces verba mea, et in sermonibus meis stimuleris.

verses.text: Who will pity an enchanter struck by a serpent, or any that come near wild beasts? so is it with him that keepeth company with a wicked man, and is involved in his sins.
verses.textLatin: Quis miserebitur incantatori a serpente percusso, et omnibus qui appropiant bestiis? et sic qui comitatur cum viro iniquo, et obvolutus est in peccatis ejus.

verses.text: For an hour he will abide with thee: but if thou begin to decline, he will not endure it.
verses.textLatin: Una hora tecum permanebit: si autem declinaveris, non supportabit.

verses.text: An enemy speaketh sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he lieth in wait, to throw thee into a pit.
verses.textLatin: In labiis suis indulcat inimicus, et in corde suo insidiatur ut subvertat te in foveam.

verses.text: An enemy weepeth with his eyes: but if he find an opportunity he will not be satisfied with blood:
verses.textLatin: In oculis suis lacrimatur inimicus, et si invenerit tempus, non satiabitur sanguine.

verses.text: And if evils come upon thee, thou shalt find him there first.
verses.textLatin: Et si incurrerint tibi mala, invenies eum illic priorem.

verses.text: An enemy hath tears in his eyes, and while he pretendeth to help thee, will undermine thy feet.
verses.textLatin: In oculis suis lacrimatur inimicus, et quasi adjuvans suffodiet plantas tuas.

verses.text: He will shake his head, and clap his hands, and whisper much, and change his countenance.
verses.textLatin: Caput suum movebit, et plaudet manu, et multa susurrans commutabit vultum suum.

verses.text: He  that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled with it: and he that hath fellowship with the proud, shall put on pride.
verses.textLatin: Qui tetigerit picem inquinabitur ab ea: et qui communicaverit superbo induet superbiam.

verses.text: He shall take a burden upon him that hath fellowship with one more honourable than himself. And have no fellowship with one that is richer than thyself.
verses.textLatin: Pondus super se tollat qui honestiori se communicat, et ditiori te ne socius fueris.

verses.text: What agreement shall the earthen pot have with the kettle? for if they knock one against the other, it shall be broken.
verses.textLatin: Quid communicabit cacabus ad ollam? quando enim se colliserint, confringetur.

verses.text: The rich man hath done wrong, and yet he will fume: but the poor is wronged and must hold his peace.
verses.textLatin: Dives injuste egit, et fremet: pauper autem læsus tacebit.

verses.text: If thou give, he will make use of thee: and if thou have nothing, he will forsake thee.
verses.textLatin: Si largitus fueris, assumet te: et si non habueris, derelinquet te.

verses.text: If thou have any thing, he will live with thee, and will make thee bare, and he will not be sorry for thee.
verses.textLatin: Si habes, convivet tecum, et evacuabit te: et ipse non dolebit super te.

verses.text: If he have need of thee he will deceive thee, and smiling upon thee will put thee in hope; he will speak thee fair, and will say: What wantest thou?
verses.textLatin: Si necessarius illi fueris, supplantabit te, et subridens spem dabit, narrans tibi bona, et dicet: Quid opus est tibi?

verses.text: And he will shame thee by his meats, till he have drawn thee dry twice or thrice, and at last he will laugh at thee: and afterward when he seeth thee, he will forsake thee, and shake his head at thee.
verses.textLatin: Et confundet te in cibis suis, donec te exinaniat bis et ter: et in novissimo deridebit te, et postea videns derelinquet te, et caput suum movebit ad te.

verses.text: Humble thyself to God, and wait for his hands.
verses.textLatin: Humiliare Deo, et exspecta manus ejus.

verses.text: Beware that thou be not deceived into folly, and be humbled.
verses.textLatin: Attende ne seductus in stultitiam humilieris.

verses.text: Be not lowly in thy wisdom, lest being humbled thou be deceived into folly.
verses.textLatin: Noli esse humilis in sapientia tua, ne humiliatus in stultitiam seducaris.

verses.text: If thou be invited by one that is mightier, withdraw thyself: for so he will invite thee the more.
verses.textLatin: Advocatus a potentiore, discede: ex hoc enim magis te advocabit.

verses.text: Be not troublesome to him, lest thou be put back: and keep not far from him, lest thou be forgotten.
verses.textLatin: Ne improbus sis, ne impingaris: et ne longe sis ab eo, ne eas in oblivionem.

verses.text: Affect not to speak with him as an equal: and believe not his many words: for by much talk he will sift thee, and smiling will examine thee concerning thy secrets.
verses.textLatin: Ne retineas ex æquo loqui cum illo, nec credas multis verbis illius: ex multa enim loquela tentabit te, et subridens interrogabit te de absconditis tuis.

verses.text: His cruel mind will lay up thy words: and he will not spare to do thee hurt, and to cast thee into prison.
verses.textLatin: Immitis animus illius conservabit verba tua: et non parcet de malitia, et de vinculis.

verses.text: Take heed to thyself, and attend diligently to what thou hearest: for thou walkest in danger of thy ruin.
verses.textLatin: Cave tibi, et attende diligenter auditui tuo, quoniam cum subversione tua ambulas:

verses.text: When thou hearest those things, see as it were in sleep, and thou shalt awake.
verses.textLatin: audiens vero illa, quasi in somnis vide, et vigilabis.

verses.text: Love God all thy life, and call upon him for thy salvation.
verses.textLatin: Omni vita tua dilige Deum, et invoca illum in salute tua.

verses.text: Every beast loveth its like: so also every man him that is nearest to himself.
verses.textLatin: Omne animal diligit simile sibi, sic et omnis homo proximum sibi.

verses.text: All flesh shall consort with the like to itself, and every man shall associate himself to his like.
verses.textLatin: Omnis caro ad similem sibi conjungetur, et omnis homo simili sui sociabitur.

verses.text: If the wolf shall at any time have fellowship with the lamb, so the sinner with the just.
verses.textLatin: Si communicabit lupus agno aliquando, sic peccator justo.

verses.text: What fellowship hath a holy man with a dog, or what part hath the rich with the poor?
verses.textLatin: Quæ communicatio sancto homini ad canem? aut quæ pars diviti ad pauperem?

verses.text: The wild ass is the lion’s prey in the desert: so also the poor are devoured by the rich.
verses.textLatin: Venatio leonis onager in eremo: sic et pascua divitum sunt pauperes.

verses.text: And as humility is an abomination to the proud: so also the rich man abhorreth the poor.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut abominatio est superbo humilitas, sic et execratio divitis pauper.

verses.text: When a rich man is shaken, he is kept up by his friends: but when a poor man is fallen down, he is thrust away even by his acquaintance.
verses.textLatin: Dives commotus confirmatur ab amicis suis: humilis autem cum ceciderit, expelletur et a notis.

verses.text: When a rich man hath been deceived, he hath many helpers: he hath spoken proud things, and they have justified him.
verses.textLatin: Diviti decepto multi recuperatores: locutus est superbia, et justificaverunt illum.

verses.text: The poor man was deceived, and he is rebuked also: he hath spoken wisely, and could have no place.
verses.textLatin: Humilis deceptus est, insuper et arguitur: locutus est sensate, et non est datus ei locus.

verses.text: The rich man spoke, and all held their peace, and what he said they extol even to the clouds.
verses.textLatin: Dives locutus est, et omnes tacuerunt, et verbum illius usque ad nubes perducent.

verses.text: The poor man spoke, and they say: Who is this? and if he stumble, they will overthrow him.
verses.textLatin: Pauper locutus est, et dicunt: Quis est hic? et si offenderit, subvertent illum.

verses.text: Riches are good to him that hath no sin in his conscience: and poverty is very wicked in the mouth of the ungodly.
verses.textLatin: Bona est substantia cui non est peccatum in conscientia: et nequissima paupertas in ore impii.

verses.text: The heart of a man changeth his countenance, either for good, or for evil.
verses.textLatin: Cor hominis immutat faciem illius, sive in bona, sive in mala.

verses.text: The token of a good heart, and a good countenance thou shalt hardly find, and with labour.
verses.textLatin: Vestigium cordis boni et faciem bonam difficile invenies, et cum labore.

verses.text: Blessed  is the man that hath not slipped by a word out of his mouth, and is not pricked with the remorse of sin.
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir qui non est lapsus verbo ex ore suo, et non est stimulatus in tristitia delicti.

verses.text: Happy is he that hath had no sadness of his mind, and who is not fallen from his hope.
verses.textLatin: Felix qui non habuit animi sui tristitiam, et non excidit a spe sua.

verses.text: Riches are not comely for a covetous man and a niggard, and what should an envious man do with gold?
verses.textLatin: Viro cupido et tenaci sine ratione est substantia: et homini livido ad quid aurum?

verses.text: He that gathereth together by wronging his own soul, gathereth for others, and another will squander away his goods in rioting.
verses.textLatin: Qui acervat ex animo suo injuste, aliis congregat, et in bonis illius alius luxuriabitur.

verses.text: He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? and he shall not take pleasure in his goods.
verses.textLatin: Qui sibi nequam est, cui alii bonus erit? et non jucundabitur in bonis suis.

verses.text: There is none worse than he that envieth himself, and this is the reward of his wickedness:
verses.textLatin: Qui sibi invidet, nihil est illo nequius: et hæc redditio est malitiæ illius.

verses.text: And if he do good, he doth it ignorantly, and unwillingly: and at the last he discovereth his wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Et si bene fecerit, ignoranter et non volens facit: et in novissimo manifestat malitiam suam.

verses.text: The eye of the envious is wicked: and he turneth away his face, and despiseth his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Nequam est oculus lividi: et avertens faciem suam, et despiciens animam suam.

verses.text: The eye of the covetous man is insatiable in his portion of iniquity: he will not be satisfied till he consume his own soul, drying it up.
verses.textLatin: Insatiabilis oculus cupidi in parte iniquitatis: non satiabitur donec consumat arefaciens animam suam.

verses.text: An evil eye is towards evil things: and he shall not have his fill of bread, but shall be needy and pensive at his own table.
verses.textLatin: Oculus malus ad mala, et non saturabitur pane, sed indigens et in tristitia erit super mensam suam.

verses.text: My son, if thou have any thing, do good to thyself, and offer to God worthy offerings.
verses.textLatin: Fili, si habes, benefac tecum, et Deo dignas oblationes offer.

verses.text: Remember that death is not slow, and that the covenant of hell hath been shewn to thee: for the covenant of this world shall surely die.
verses.textLatin: Memor esto quoniam mors non tardat, et testamentum inferorum, quia demonstratum est tibi: testamentum enim hujus mundi morte morietur.

verses.text: Do good to thy friend before thou die, and according to thy ability, stretching out thy hand give to the poor.
verses.textLatin: Ante mortem benefac amico tuo, et secundum vires tuas exporrigens da pauperi.

verses.text: Defraud not thyself of the good day, and let not the part of a good gift overpass thee.
verses.textLatin: Non defrauderis a die bono, et particula boni doni non te prætereat.

verses.text: Shalt thou not leave to others to divide by lot thy sorrows and labours?
verses.textLatin: Nonne aliis relinques dolores et labores tuos in divisione sortis?

verses.text: Give and take, and justify thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Da et accipe, et justifica animam tuam.

verses.text: Before thy death work justice: for in hell there is no finding food.
verses.textLatin: Ante obitum tuum operare justitiam, quoniam non est apud inferos invenire cibum.

verses.text: All flesh shall fade as grass, and as the leaf that springeth out on a green tree.
verses.textLatin: Omnis caro sicut fœnum veterascet, et sicut folium fructificans in arbore viridi.

verses.text: Some grow, and some fall off: so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.
verses.textLatin: Alia generantur, et alia dejiciuntur: sic generatio carnis et sanguinis, alia finitur, et alia nascitur.

verses.text: Every work that is corruptible shall fail in the end: and the worker thereof shall go with it.
verses.textLatin: Omne opus corruptibile in fine deficiet, et qui illud operatur ibit cum illo.

verses.text: And every excellent work shall be justified: and the worker thereof shall be honoured therein.
verses.textLatin: Et omne opus electum justificabitur, et qui operatur illud honorabitur in illo.

verses.text: Blessed is the man that shall continue in wisdom, and that shall meditate in his justice, and in his mind shall think of the all seeing eye of God.
verses.textLatin: Beatus vir qui in sapientia morabitur, et qui in justitia sua meditabitur, et in sensu cogitabit circumspectionem Dei:

verses.text: He that considereth her ways in his heart, and hath understanding in her secrets, who goeth after her as one that traceth, and stayeth in her ways.
verses.textLatin: qui excogitat vias illius in corde suo, et in absconditis suis intelligens, vadens post illam quasi investigator, et in viis illius consistens:

verses.text: He who looketh in at her windows, and hearkeneth at her door:
verses.textLatin: qui respicit per fenestras illius, et in januis illius audiens:

verses.text: He that lodgeth near her house, and fastening a pin in her walls shall set up his tent high unto her, where good things shall rest in his lodging for ever.
verses.textLatin: qui requiescit juxta domum illius, et in parietibus illius figens palum, statuet casulam suam ad manus illius, et requiescent in casula illius bona per ævum.

verses.text: He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches:
verses.textLatin: Statuet filios suos sub tegmine illius, et sub ramis ejus morabitur.

verses.text: He shall be protected under her covering from the heat, and shall rest in her glory.
verses.textLatin: Protegetur sub tegmine illius a fervore, et in gloria ejus requiescet.

verses.text: He  that feareth God, will do good: and he that possesseth justice, shall lay hold on her,
verses.textLatin: Qui timet Deum faciet bona, et qui continens est justitiæ apprehendet illam:

verses.text: And she will meet him as an honourable mother, and will receive him as a wife married of a virgin.
verses.textLatin: et obviabit illi quasi mater honorificata, et quasi mulier a virginitate suscipiet illum.

verses.text: With the bread of life and understanding, she shall feed him, and give him the water of wholesome wisdom to drink: and she shall be made strong in him, and he shall not be moved.
verses.textLatin: Cibabit illum pane vitæ et intellectus, et aqua sapientiæ salutaris potabit illum: et firmabitur in illo, et non flectetur:

verses.text: And she shall hold him fast, and he shall not be confounded: and she shall exalt him among his neighbours.
verses.textLatin: et continebit illum, et non confundetur: et exaltabit illum apud proximos suos,

verses.text: And in the midst of the church she shall open his mouth, and shall fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and shall clothe him with a robe of glory.
verses.textLatin: et in medio ecclesiæ aperiet os ejus, et adimplebit illum spiritu sapientiæ et intellectus, et stola gloriæ vestiet illum.

verses.text: She shall heap upon him a treasure of joy and gladness, and shall cause him to inherit an everlasting name.
verses.textLatin: Jucunditatem et exsultationem thesaurizabit super illum, et nomine æterno hæreditabit illum.

verses.text: But foolish men shall not obtain her, and wise men shall meet her, foolish men shall not see her: for she is far from pride and deceit.
verses.textLatin: Homines stulti non apprehendent illam, et homines sensati obviabunt illi. Homines stulti non videbunt eam: longe enim abest a superbia et dolo.

verses.text: Lying men shall be mindful of her: but men that speak truth shall be found with her, and shall advance, even till they come to the sight of God.
verses.textLatin: Viri mendaces non erunt illius memores: et viri veraces invenientur in illa, et successum habebunt usque ad inspectionem Dei.

verses.text: Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner:
verses.textLatin: Non est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris,

verses.text: For wisdom came forth from God: for praise shall be with the wisdom of God, and shall abound in a faithful mouth, and the sovereign Lord will give praise unto it.
verses.textLatin: quoniam a Deo profecta est sapientia. Sapientiæ enim Dei astabit laus, et in ore fideli abundabit, et Dominator dabit eam illi.

verses.text: Say not: It is through God, that she is not with me: for do not thou the things that he hateth.
verses.textLatin: Non dixeris: Per Deum abest: quæ enim odit ne feceris.

verses.text: Say not: He hath caused me to err: for he hath no need of wicked men.
verses.textLatin: Non dicas: Ille me implanavit: non enim necessarii sunt ei homines impii.

verses.text: The Lord hateth all abomination of error, and they that fear him shall not love it.
verses.textLatin: Omne execramentum erroris odit Dominus, et non erit amabile timentibus eum.

verses.text: God made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his own counsel.
verses.textLatin: Deus ab initio constituit hominem, et reliquit illum in manu consilii sui:

verses.text: He added his commandments and precepts.
verses.textLatin: adjecit mandata et præcepta sua.

verses.text: If thou wilt keep the commandments and perform acceptable fidelity for ever, they shall preserve thee.
verses.textLatin: Si volueris mandata servare, conservabunt te, et in perpetuum fidem placitam facere.

verses.text: He hath set water and fire before thee: stretch forth thy hand to which thou wilt.
verses.textLatin: Apposuit tibi aquam et ignem, ad quod volueris porrige manum tuam.

verses.text: Before man is life and death, good and evil, that which he shall choose shall be given him:
verses.textLatin: Ante hominem vita et mors, bonum et malum: quod placuerit ei dabitur illi:

verses.text: For the wisdom of God is great, and he is strong in power, seeing all men without ceasing.
verses.textLatin: quoniam multa sapientia Dei, et fortis in potentia, videns omnes sine intermissione.

verses.text: The eyes of the Lord are towards them that fear him, and he knoweth all the work of man.
verses.textLatin: Oculi Domini ad timentes eum, et ipse agnoscit omnem operam hominis.

verses.text: He hath commanded no man to do wickedly, and he hath given no man license to sin:
verses.textLatin: Nemini mandavit impie agere, et nemini dedit spatium peccandi:

verses.text: For he desireth not a multitude of faithless and unprofitable children.
verses.textLatin: non enim concupiscit multitudinem filiorum infidelium et inutilium.

verses.text: Rejoice  not in ungodly children, if they be multiplied: neither be delighted in them, if the fear of God be not with them.
verses.textLatin: Ne jucunderis in filiis impiis, si multiplicentur: nec oblecteris super ipsos, si non est timor Dei in illis.

verses.text: Trust not to their life, and respect not their labours.
verses.textLatin: Non credas vitæ illorum, et ne respexeris in labores eorum.

verses.text: For better is one that feareth God, than a thousand ungodly children.
verses.textLatin: Melior est enim unus timens Deum, quam mille filii impii:

verses.text: And it is better to die without children, than to leave ungodly children.
verses.textLatin: et utile est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere filios impios.

verses.text: By one that is wise a country shall be inhabited, the tribe of the ungodly shall become desolate.
verses.textLatin: Ab uno sensato inhabitabitur patria: tribus impiorum deseretur.

verses.text: Many such things hath my eyes seen, and greater things than these my ear hath heard.
verses.textLatin: Multa talia vidit oculis meus, et fortiora horum audivit auris mea.

verses.text: In the congregation of sinners a fire shall be kindled, and in an unbelieving nation wrath shall flame out.
verses.textLatin: In synagoga peccantium exardebit ignis, et in gente incredibili exardescet ira.

verses.text: The ancient giants did not obtain pardon for their sins, who were destroyed trusting to their own strength:
verses.textLatin: Non exoraverunt pro peccatis suis antiqui gigantes, qui destructi sunt confidentes suæ virtuti.

verses.text: And he spared not the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for the pride of their word.
verses.textLatin: Et non pepercit peregrinationi Lot, et execratus est eos præ superbia verbi illorum.

verses.text: He had not pity on them, destroying the whole nation that extolled themselves in their sins.
verses.textLatin: Non misertus est illis, gentem totam perdens, et extollentem se in peccatis suis.

verses.text: So did he with the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their heart: and if one had been stiffnecked, it is a wonder if he had escaped unpunished:
verses.textLatin: Et sicut sexcenta millia peditum, qui congregati sunt in duritia cordis sui: et si unus fuisset cervicatus, mirum si fuisset immunis.

verses.text: For mercy and wrath are with him. He is mighty to forgive, and to pour out indignation:
verses.textLatin: Misericordia enim et ira est cum illo: potens exoratio, et effundens iram.

verses.text: According as his mercy is, so his correction judgeth a man according to his works.
verses.textLatin: Secundum misericordiam suam, sic correptio illius homines secundum opera sua judicat.

verses.text: The sinner shall not escape in his rapines, and the patience of him that sheweth mercy shall not be put off.
verses.textLatin: Non effugiet in rapina peccator, et non retardabit sufferentia misericordiam facientis.

verses.text: All mercy shall make a place for every man according to the merit of his works, and according to the wisdom of his sojournment.
verses.textLatin: Omnis misericordia faciet locum unicuique, secundum meritum operum suorum, et secundum intellectum peregrinationis ipsius.

verses.text: Say not: I shall be hidden from God, and who shall remember me from on high?
verses.textLatin: Non dicas: A Deo abscondar: et ex summo, quis mei memorabitur?

verses.text: In such a multitude I shall not be known: for what is my soul in such an immense creation?
verses.textLatin: in populo magno non agnoscar: quæ est enim anima mea in tam immensa creatura?

verses.text: Behold the heaven, and the heavens of heavens, the deep, and all the earth, and the things that are in them, shall be moved in his sight,
verses.textLatin: Ecce cælum et cæli cælorum, abyssus, et universa terra, et quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu illius commovebuntur.

verses.text: The mountains also, and the hills, and the foundations of the earth: when God shall look upon them, they shall be shaken with trembling.
verses.textLatin: Montes simul, et colles, et fundamenta terræ, cum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur.

verses.text: And in all these things the heart is senseless: and every heart is understood by him.
verses.textLatin: Et in omnibus his insensatum est cor, et omne cor intelligitur ab illo.

verses.text: And his ways who shall understand, and the storm, which no eye of man shall see?
verses.textLatin: Et vias illius quis intelligit, et procellam quam nec oculus videbit hominis?

verses.text: For many of his works are hidden: but the works of his justice who shall declare? or who shall endure? for the testament is far from some, and the examination of all is in the end.
verses.textLatin: Nam plurima illius opera sunt in absconsis: sed opera justitiæ ejus quis enuntiabit, aut quis sustinebit? longe enim est testamentum a quibusdam, et interrogatio omnium in consummatione est.

verses.text: He that wanteth understanding thinketh vain things: and the foolish, and erring man, thinketh foolish things.
verses.textLatin: Qui minoratur corde cogitat inania, et vir imprudens et errans cogitat stulta.

verses.text: Hearken to me, my son, and learn the discipline of understanding, and attend to my words in thy heart.
verses.textLatin: Audi me, fili, et disce disciplinam sensus, et in verbis meis attende in corde tuo:

verses.text: And I will shew forth good doctrine in equity, and will seek to declare wisdom: and attend to my words in thy heart, whilst with equity of spirit I tell thee the virtues that God hath put upon his works from the beginning, and I shew forth in truth his knowledge.
verses.textLatin: et dicam in æquitate disciplinam, et scrutabor enarrare sapientiam: et in verbis meis attende in corde tuo, et dico in æquitate spiritus virtutes quas posuit Deus in opera sua ab initio, et in veritate enuntio scientiam ejus.

verses.text: The works of God are done in judgment from the beginning, and from the making of them he distinguished their parts, and their beginnings in their generations.
verses.textLatin: In judicio Dei opera ejus ab initio, et ab institutione ipsorum distinxit partes illorum, et initia eorum in gentibus suis.

verses.text: He beautified their works for ever, they have neither hungered, nor laboured, and they have not ceased from their works.
verses.textLatin: Ornavit in æternum opera illorum: nec esurierunt, nec laboraverunt, et non destiterunt ab operibus suis.

verses.text: Nor shall any of them straiten his neighbour at any time.
verses.textLatin: Unusquisque proximum sibi non angustiabit in æternum:

verses.text: Be not thou incredulous to his word.
verses.textLatin: non sis incredibilis verbo illius.

verses.text: After this God looked upon the earth, and filled it with his goods.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc Deus in terram respexit, et implevit illam bonis suis:

verses.text: The soul of every living thing hath shewn forth before the face thereof, and into it they return again.
verses.textLatin: anima omnis vitalis denuntiavit ante faciem ipsius, et in ipsam iterum reversio illorum.

verses.text: God  created man of the earth, and made him after his own image.
verses.textLatin: Deus creavit de terra hominem, et secundum imaginem suam fecit illum:

verses.text: And he turned him into it again, and clothed him with strength according to himself.
verses.textLatin: et iterum convertit illum in ipsam, et secundum se vestivit illum virtute.

verses.text: He gave him the number of his days and time, and gave him power over all things that are upon the earth.
verses.textLatin: Numerum dierum et tempus dedit illi, et dedit illi potestatem eorum quæ sunt super terram.

verses.text: He put the fear of him upon all flesh, and he had dominion over beasts and fowls.
verses.textLatin: Posuit timorem illius super omnem carnem, et dominatus est bestiarum et volatilium.

verses.text: He created of him a helpmate like to himself: he gave them counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, and ears, and a heart to devise: and he filled them with the knowledge of understanding.
verses.textLatin: Creavit ex ipso adjutorium simile sibi: consilium, et linguam, et oculos, et aures, et cor dedit illis excogitandi, et disciplina intellectus replevit illos.

verses.text: He created in them the science of the spirit, he fired their heart with wisdom, and shewed them both good and evil.
verses.textLatin: Creavit illis scientiam spiritus, sensu implevit cor illorum, et mala et bona ostendit illis.

verses.text: He set his eye upon their hearts to shew them the greatness of his works:
verses.textLatin: Posuit oculum suum super corda illorum, ostendere illis magnalia operum suorum:

verses.text: That they might praise the name which he hath sanctified: and glory in his wondrous act that they might declare the glorious things of his works.
verses.textLatin: ut nomen sanctificationis collaudent, et gloriari in mirabilibus illius; ut magnalia enarrent operum ejus.

verses.text: Moreover he gave them instructions, and the law of life for an inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Addidit illis disciplinam, et legem vitæ hæreditavit illos.

verses.text: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and he shewed them his justice and judgments.
verses.textLatin: Testamentum æternum constituit cum illis, et justitiam et judicia sua ostendit illis.

verses.text: And their eye saw the majesty of his glory, and their ears heard his glorious voice, and he said to them: Beware of all iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Et magnalia honoris ejus vidit oculus illorum, et honorem vocis audierunt aures illorum. Et dixit illis: Attendite ab omni iniquo.

verses.text: And he gave to every one of them commandment concerning his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Et mandavit illis unicuique de proximo suo.

verses.text: Their ways are always before him, they are not hidden from his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Viæ illorum coram ipso sunt semper: non sunt absconsæ ab oculis ipsius.

verses.text: Over every nation he set a ruler.
verses.textLatin: In unamquamque gentem præposuit rectorem:

verses.text: And Israel was made the manifest portion of God.
verses.textLatin: et pars Dei Israël facta est manifesta.

verses.text: And all their works are as the sun in the sight of God: and his eyes are continually upon their ways.
verses.textLatin: Et omnia opera illorum velut sol in conspectu Dei: et oculi ejus sine intermissione inspicientes in viis eorum.

verses.text: Their covenants were not hid by their iniquity, and all their iniquities are in the sight of God.
verses.textLatin: Non sunt absconsa testamenta per iniquitatem illorum, et omnes iniquitates eorum in conspectu Dei.

verses.text: The alms of a man is as a signet with him, and shall preserve the grace of a man as the apple of the eye:
verses.textLatin: Eleemosyna viri quasi signaculum cum ipso, et gratiam hominis quasi pupillam conservabit.

verses.text: And afterward he shall rise up, and shall render them their reward, to every one upon their own head, and shall turn them down into the bowels of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et postea resurget, et retribuet illis retributionem, unicuique in caput ipsorum, et convertet in interiores partes terræ.

verses.text: But to the penitent he hath given the way of justice, and he hath strengthened them that were fainting in patience, and hath appointed to them the lot of truth.
verses.textLatin: Pœnitentibus autem dedit viam justitiæ, et confirmavit deficientes sustinere, et destinavit illis sortem veritatis.

verses.text: Turn to the Lord, and forsake thy sins:
verses.textLatin: Convertere ad Dominum, et relinque peccata tua:

verses.text: Make thy prayer before the face of the Lord, and offend less.
verses.textLatin: precare ante faciem Domini, et minue offendicula.

verses.text: Return to the Lord, and turn away from thy injustice, and greatly hate abomination.
verses.textLatin: Revertere ad Dominum, et avertere ab injustitia tua, et nimis odito execrationem:

verses.text: And know the justices and judgments of God, and stand firm in the lot set before thee, and in prayer to the most high God.
verses.textLatin: et cognosce justitias et judicia Dei, et sta in sorte propositionis, et orationis altissimi Dei.

verses.text: Go to the side of the holy age, with them that live and give praise to God.
verses.textLatin: In partes vade sæculi sancti, cum vivis et dantibus confessionem Deo.

verses.text: Tarry not in the error of the ungodly, give glory before death. Praise perisheth from the dead as nothing.
verses.textLatin: Non demoreris in errore impiorum: ante mortem confitere: a mortuo, quasi nihil, perit confessio.

verses.text: Give thanks whilst thou art living, whilst thou art alive and in health thou shalt give thanks, and shalt praise God, and shalt glory in his mercies.
verses.textLatin: Confiteberis vivens, vivus et sanus confiteberis: et laudabis Deum, et gloriaberis in miserationibus illius.

verses.text: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his forgiveness to them that turn to him !
verses.textLatin: Quam magna misericordia Domini, et propitiatio illius convertentibus ad se!

verses.text: For all things cannot be in men, because the son of man is not immortal, and they are delighted with the vanity of evil.
verses.textLatin: Nec enim omnia possunt esse in hominibus, quoniam non est immortalis filius hominis, et in vanitate malitiæ placuerunt.

verses.text: What is brighter than the sun; yet it shall be eclipsed. Or what is more wicked than that which flesh and blood hath invented? and this shall be reproved.
verses.textLatin: Quid lucidius sole? et hic deficiet; aut quid nequius quam quod excogitavit caro et sanguis? et hoc arguetur.

verses.text: He beholdeth the power of the height of heaven: and all men are earth and ashes.
verses.textLatin: Virtutem altitudinis cæli ipse conspicit: et omnes homines terra et cinis.

verses.text: He  that liveth for ever created all things together. God only shall be justified, and he remaineth an invincible king for ever.
verses.textLatin: Qui vivet in æternum creavit omnia simul. Deus solus justificabitur, et manet invictus rex in æternum.

verses.text: Who is able to declare his works?
verses.textLatin: Quis sufficit enarrare opera illius?

verses.text: For who shall search out his glorious acts?
verses.textLatin: quis enim investigabit magnalia ejus?

verses.text: And who shall show forth the power of his majesty? or who shall be able to declare his mercy?
verses.textLatin: virtutem autem magnitudinis ejus quis enuntiabit? aut quis adjiciet enarrare misericordiam ejus?

verses.text: Nothing may be taken away, nor added, neither is it possible to find out the glorious works of God.
verses.textLatin: Non est minuere neque adjicere, nec est invenire magnalia Dei.

verses.text: When a man hath done, then shall he begin: and when he leaveth off, he shall be at a loss.
verses.textLatin: Cum consummaverit homo, tunc incipiet: et cum quieverit, aporiabitur.

verses.text: What is man, and what is his grace? and what is his good, or what is his evil?
verses.textLatin: Quid est homo? et quæ est gratia illius? et quid bonum aut quid nequam illius?

verses.text: The number of the days of men at the most are a hundred years: as a drop of water of the sea are they esteemed: and as a pebble of the sand, so are a few years compared to eternity.
verses.textLatin: Numerus dierum hominum, ut multum centum anni, quasi gutta aquæ maris deputati sunt: et sicut calculus arenæ, sic exigui anni in die ævi.

verses.text: Therefore God is patient in them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc patiens est Deus in illis, et effundit super eos misericordiam suam.

verses.text: He hath seen the presumption of their heart that it is wicked, and hath known their end that it is evil.
verses.textLatin: Vidit præsumptionem cordis eorum, quoniam mala est: et cognovit subversionem illorum, quoniam nequam est.

verses.text: Therefore hath he filled up his mercy in their favour, and hath shewn them the way of justice.
verses.textLatin: Ideo adimplevit propitiationem suam in illis, et ostendit eis viam æquitatis.

verses.text: The compassion of man is toward his neighbour: but the mercy of God is upon all flesh.
verses.textLatin: Miseratio hominis circa proximum suum: misericordia autem Dei super omnem carnem.

verses.text: He hath mercy, and teacheth, and correcteth, as a shepherd doth his flock.
verses.textLatin: Qui misericordiam habet, docet et erudit quasi pastor gregem suum.

verses.text: He hath mercy on him that receiveth the discipline of mercy, and that maketh haste in his judgments.
verses.textLatin: Miseretur excipientis doctrinam miserationis, et qui festinat in judiciis ejus.

verses.text: My son, in thy good deeds, make no complaint, and when thou givest any thing, add not grief by an evil word.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in bonis non des querelam, et in omni dato non des tristitiam verbi mali.

verses.text: Shall not the dew assuage the heat? so also the good word is better than the gift.
verses.textLatin: Nonne ardorem refrigerabit ros? sic et verbum melius quam datum.

verses.text: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a justified man.
verses.textLatin: Nonne ecce verbum super datum bonum? sed utraque cum homine justificato.

verses.text: A fool will upbraid bitterly: and a gift of one ill taught consumeth the eyes.
verses.textLatin: Stultus acriter improperabit: et datus indisciplinati tabescere facit oculos.

verses.text: Before judgment prepare thee justice, and learn before thou speak.
verses.textLatin: Ante judicium para justitiam tibi, et antequam loquaris, disce.

verses.text: Before sickness take a medicine, and before judgment examine thyself, and thou shalt find mercy in the sight of God.
verses.textLatin: Ante languorem adhibe medicinam: et ante judicium interroga teipsum, et in conspectu Dei invenies propitiationem.

verses.text: Humble thyself before thou art sick, and in the time of sickness shew thy conversation.
verses.textLatin: Ante languorem humilia te, et in tempore infirmitatis ostende conversationem tuam.

verses.text: Let nothing hinder thee from praying always, and be not afraid to be justified even to death: for the reward of God continueth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Non impediaris orare semper, et ne verearis usque ad mortem justificari, quoniam merces Dei manet in æternum.

verses.text: Before prayer prepare thy soul: and be not as a man that tempteth God.
verses.textLatin: Ante orationem præpara animam tuam, et noli esse quasi homo qui tentat Deum.

verses.text: Remember the wrath that shall be at the last day, and the time of repaying when he shall turn away his face.
verses.textLatin: Memento iræ in die consummationis, et tempus retributionis in conversatione faciei.

verses.text: Remember poverty in the time of abundance, and the necessities of poverty in the day of riches.
verses.textLatin: Memento paupertatis in tempore abundantiæ, et necessitatum paupertatis in die divitiarum.

verses.text: From the morning until the evening the time shall be changed, and all these are swift in the eyes of God.
verses.textLatin: A mane usque ad vesperam immutabitur tempus, et hæc omnia citata in oculis Dei.

verses.text: A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the days of sins will beware of sloth.
verses.textLatin: Homo sapiens in omnibus metuet, et in diebus delictorum attendet ab inertia.

verses.text: Every man of understanding knoweth wisdom, and will give praise to him that findeth her.
verses.textLatin: Omnis astutus agnoscit sapientiam, et invenienti eam dabit confessionem.

verses.text: They that were of good understanding in words, have also done wisely themselves: and have understood truth and justice, and have poured forth proverbs and judgments.
verses.textLatin: Sensati in verbis et ipsi sapienter egerunt, et intellexerunt veritatem et justitiam, et impluerunt proverbia et judicia.

verses.text: Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will.
verses.textLatin: Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere.

verses.text: If thou give to thy soul her desires, she will make thee a joy to thy enemies.
verses.textLatin: Si præstes animæ tuæ concupiscentias ejus, faciat te in gaudium inimicis tuis.

verses.text: Take no pleasure in riotous assemblies, be they ever so small: for their concertation is continual.
verses.textLatin: Ne oblecteris in turbis nec in modicis: assidua enim est commissio illorum.

verses.text: Make not thyself poor by borrowing to contribute to feasts when thou hast nothing in thy purse: for thou shalt be an enemy to thy own life.
verses.textLatin: Ne fueris mediocris in contentione ex fœnore, et est tibi nihil in sacculo: eris enim invidus vitæ tuæ.

verses.text: A  WORKMAN that is a drunkard shall not be rich: and he that contemneth small things, shall fall by little and little.
verses.textLatin: Operarius ebriosus non locupletabitur: et qui spernit modica paulatim decidet.

verses.text: Wine and women make wise men fall off, and shall rebuke the prudent:
verses.textLatin: Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt sapientes, et arguent sensatos.

verses.text: And he that joineth himself to harlots, will be wicked. Rottenness and worms shall inherit him, and he shall be lifted up for a greater example, and his soul shall be taken away out of the number.
verses.textLatin: Et qui se jungit fornicariis erit nequam: putredo et vermes hæreditabunt illum: et extolletur in exemplum majus, et tolletur de numero anima ejus.

verses.text: He that is hasty to give credit, is light of heart, and shall be lessened: and he that sinneth against his own soul, shall be despised.
verses.textLatin: Qui credit cito levis corde est, et minorabitur: et qui delinquit in animam suam, insuper habebitur.

verses.text: He that rejoiceth in iniquity, shall be censured, and he that hateth chastisement, shall have less life: and he that hateth babbling, extinguisheth evil.
verses.textLatin: Qui gaudet iniquitate, denotabitur: et qui odit correptionem, minuetur vita: et qui odit loquacitatem, extinguit malitiam.

verses.text: He that sinneth against his own soul, shall repent: and he that is delighted with wickedness, shall be condemned.
verses.textLatin: Qui peccat in animam suam, pœnitebit: et qui jucundatur in malitia, denotabitur.

verses.text: Rehearse not again a wicked and harsh word, and thou shalt not fare the worse.
verses.textLatin: Ne iteres verbum nequam et durum, et non minoraberis.

verses.text: Tell not thy mind to friend or foe: and if there be a sin with thee, disclose it not.
verses.textLatin: Amico et inimico noli narrare sensum tuum: et si est tibi delictum, noli denudare:

verses.text: For he will hearken to thee, and will watch thee, and as it were defending thy sin he will hate thee, and so will he be with thee always.
verses.textLatin: audiet enim te, et custodiet te, et quasi defendens peccatum, odiet te, et sic aderit tibi semper.

verses.text: Hast thou heard a word against thy neighbour? let it die within thee, trusting that it will not burst thee.
verses.textLatin: Audisti verbum adversus proximum tuum? commoriatur in te, fidens quoniam non te dirumpet.

verses.text: At the hearing of a word the fool is in travail, as a woman groaning in the bringing forth a child.
verses.textLatin: A facie verbi parturit fatuus, tamquam gemitus partus infantis.

verses.text: As an arrow that sticketh in a man’s thigh: so is a word in the heart of a fool.
verses.textLatin: Sagitta infixa femori carnis, sic verbum in corde stulti.

verses.text: Reprove a friend, lest he may not have understood, and say: I did it not: or if he did it, that he may do it no more.
verses.textLatin: Corripe amicum, ne forte non intellexerit, et dicat: Non feci: aut, si fecerit, ne iterum addat facere.

verses.text: Reprove thy neighbour, for it may be he hath not said it: and if he hath said it, that he may not say it again.
verses.textLatin: Corripe proximum, ne forte non dixerit: et si dixerit, ne forte iteret.

verses.text: Admonish thy friend: for there is often a fault committed.
verses.textLatin: Corripe amicum, sæpe enim fit commissio:

verses.text: And believe not every word. There is one, that slippeth with the tongue, but not from his heart.
verses.textLatin: et non omni verbo credas. Est qui labitur lingua, sed non ex animo:

verses.text: For who is there that hath not offended with his tongue? Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him.
verses.textLatin: quis est enim qui non deliquerit in lingua sua? Corripe proximum antequam commineris,

verses.text: And give place to the fear of the most High: for the fear of God is all wisdom, and therein is to fear God, and the disposition of the law is in all wisdom.
verses.textLatin: et da locum timori Altissimi: quia omnis sapientia timor Dei, et in illa timere Deum, et in omni sapientia dispositio legis.

verses.text: But the learning of wickedness is not wisdom: and the device of sinners is not prudence.
verses.textLatin: Et non est sapientia nequitiæ disciplina, et non est cogitatus peccatorum prudentia.

verses.text: There is a subtle wickedness, and the same is detestable: and there is a man that is foolish, wanting in wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Est nequitia, et in ipsa execratio, et est insipiens qui minuitur sapientia.

verses.text: Better is a man that hath less wisdom, and wanteth understanding, with the fear of God, than he that aboundeth in understanding, and transgresseth the law of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Melior est homo qui minuitur sapientia, et deficiens sensu, in timore, quam qui abundat sensu, et transgreditur legem Altissimi.

verses.text: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust.
verses.textLatin: Est solertia certa, et ipsa iniqua:

verses.text: And there is one that uttereth an exact word telling the truth. There is one that humbleth himself wickedly, and his interior is full of deceit:
verses.textLatin: et est qui emittit verbum certum enarrans veritatem. Est qui nequiter humiliat se, et interiora ejus plena sunt dolo:

verses.text: And there is one that submitteth himself exceedingly with a great lowliness: and there is one that casteth down his countenance, and maketh as if he did not see that which is unknown:
verses.textLatin: et est qui se nimium submittit a multa humilitate: et est qui inclinat faciem suam, et fingit se non videre quod ignoratum est:

verses.text: And if he be hindered from sinning for want of power, if he shall find opportunity to do evil, he will do it.
verses.textLatin: et si ab imbecillitate virium vetetur peccare, si invenerit tempus malefaciendi, malefaciet.

verses.text: A man is known by his look, and a wise man, when thou meetest him, is known by his countenance.
verses.textLatin: Ex visu cognoscitur vir, et ab occursu faciei cognoscitur sensatus.

verses.text: The attire of the body, and the laughter of the teeth, and the gait of the man, shew what he is.
verses.textLatin: Amictus corporis, et risus dentium, et ingressus hominis, enuntiant de illo.

verses.text: There is a lying rebuke in the anger of an injurious man: and there is a judgment that is not allowed to be good: and there is one that holdeth his peace, he is wise.
verses.textLatin: Est correptio mendax in ira contumeliosi, et est judicium quod non probatur esse bonum: et est tacens, et ipse est prudens.

verses.text: How  much better is it to reprove, than to be angry, and not to hinder him that confesseth in prayer.
verses.textLatin: Quam bonum est arguere, quam irasci, et confitentem in oratione non prohibere!

verses.text: The lust of an eunuch shall deflour a young maiden:
verses.textLatin: Concupiscentia spadonis devirginabit juvenculam:

verses.text: So is he that by violence executeth unjust judgment.
verses.textLatin: sic qui facit per vim judicium iniquum.

verses.text: How good is it, when thou art reproved, to shew repentance! for so thou shalt escape wilful sin.
verses.textLatin: Quam bonum est correptum manifestare pœnitentiam! sic enim effugies voluntarium peccatum.

verses.text: There is one that holdeth his peace, that is found wise: and there is another that is hateful, that is bold in speech.
verses.textLatin: Est tacens qui invenitur sapiens: et est odibilis qui procax est ad loquendum.

verses.text: There is one that holdeth his peace, because he knoweth not what to say: and there is another that holdeth his peace, knowing the proper time.
verses.textLatin: Est tacens non habens sensum loquelæ: et est tacens sciens tempus aptum.

verses.text: A wise man will hold his peace till he see opportunity: but a babbler, and a fool will regard no time.
verses.textLatin: Homo sapiens tacebit usque ad tempus: lascivus autem et imprudens non servabunt tempus.

verses.text: He that useth many words shall hurt his own soul: and he that taketh authority to himself unjustly shall be hated.
verses.textLatin: Qui multis utitur verbis lædet animam suam: et qui potestatem sibi sumit injuste, odietur.

verses.text: There is success in evil things to a man without discipline, and there is a finding that turneth to loss.
verses.textLatin: Est processio in malis viro indisciplinato, et est inventio in detrimentum.

verses.text: There is a gift that is not profitable: and there is a gift, the recompense of which is double.
verses.textLatin: Est datum quod non est utile, et est datum cujus retributio duplex.

verses.text: There is an abasement because of glory: and there is one that shall lift up his head from a low estate.
verses.textLatin: Est propter gloriam minoratio, et est qui ab humilitate levabit caput.

verses.text: There is that buyeth much for a small price, and restoreth the same sevenfold.
verses.textLatin: Est qui multa redimat modico pretio, et restituens ea in septuplum.

verses.text: A man wise in words shall make himself beloved: but the graces of fools shall be poured out.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens in verbis seipsum amabilem facit: gratiæ autem fatuorum effundentur.

verses.text: The gift of the fool shall do thee no good: for his eyes are sevenfold.
verses.textLatin: Datus insipientis non erit utilis tibi: oculi enim illius septemplices sunt.

verses.text: He will give a few things, and upbraid much: and the opening of his mouth is the kindling of a fire.
verses.textLatin: Exigua dabit, et multa improperabit: et apertio oris illius inflammatio est.

verses.text: To day a man lendeth, and to morrow he asketh it again: such a man as this is hateful.
verses.textLatin: Hodie fœneratur quis, et cras expetit: odibilis est homo hujusmodi.

verses.text: A fool shall have no friend, and there shall be no thanks for his good deeds.
verses.textLatin: Fatuo non erit amicus, et non erit gratia bonis illius:

verses.text: For they that eat his bread, are of a false tongue. How often, and how many will laugh him to scorn!
verses.textLatin: qui enim edunt panem illius, falsæ linguæ sunt. Quoties et quanti irridebunt eum!

verses.text: For he doth not distribute with right understanding that which was to be had: in like manner also that which was not to be had.
verses.textLatin: neque enim quod habendum erat directo sensu distribuit; similiter et quod non erat habendum.

verses.text: The slipping of a false tongue is as one that falleth on the pavement: so the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
verses.textLatin: Lapsus falsæ linguæ quasi qui in pavimento cadens: sic casus malorum festinanter veniet.

verses.text: A man without grace is as a vain fable, it shall be continually in the mouth of the unwise.
verses.textLatin: Homo acharis quasi fabula vana, in ore indisciplinatorum assidua erit.

verses.text: A parable coming out of a fool’s mouth shall be rejected: for he doth not speak it in due season.
verses.textLatin: Ex ore fatui reprobabitur parabola: non enim dicit illam in tempore suo.

verses.text: There is that is hindered from sinning through want, and in his rest he shall be pricked.
verses.textLatin: Est qui vetatur peccare præ inopia, et in requie sua stimulabitur.

verses.text: There is that will destroy his own soul through shamefacedness, and by occasion of an unwise person he will destroy it: and by respect of person he will destroy himself.
verses.textLatin: Est qui perdet animam suam præ confusione, et ab imprudenti persona perdet eam: personæ autem acceptione perdet se.

verses.text: There is that for bashfulness promiseth to his friend, and maketh him his enemy for nothing.
verses.textLatin: Est qui præ confusione promittit amico, et lucratus est eum inimicum gratis.

verses.text: A lie is a foul blot in a man, and yet it will be continually in the mouth of men without discipline.
verses.textLatin: Opprobrium nequam in homine mendacium: et in ore indisciplinatorum assidue erit.

verses.text: A thief is better than a man that is always lying: but both of them shall inherit destruction.
verses.textLatin: Potior fur quam assiduitas viri mendacis: perditionem autem ambo hæreditabunt.

verses.text: The manners of lying men are without honour: and their confusion is with them without ceasing.
verses.textLatin: Mores hominum mendacium sine honore, et confusio illorum cum ipsis sine intermissione.

verses.text: A wise man shall advance himself with his words, and a prudent man shall please the great ones.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens in verbis producet seipsum, et homo prudens placebit magnatis.

verses.text: He that tilleth his land shall make a high heap of corn: and he that worketh justice shall be exalted: and he that pleaseth great men shall escape iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Qui operatur terram suam inaltabit acervum frugum, et qui operatur justitiam, ipse exaltabitur: qui vero placet magnatis effugiet iniquitatem.

verses.text: Presents and gifts blind the eyes of judges, and make them dumb in the mouth, so that they cannot correct.
verses.textLatin: Xenia et dona excæcant oculos judicum, et quasi mutus, in ore avertit correptiones eorum.

verses.text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is not seen: what profit is there in them both?
verses.textLatin: Sapientia absconsa, et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?

verses.text: Better is he that hideth his folly, than the man that hideth his wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Melior est qui celat insipientiam suam, quam homo qui abscondit sapientiam suam.

verses.text: My  son, hast thou sinned? do so no more: but for thy former sins also pray that they may be forgiven thee.
verses.textLatin: Fili, peccasti, non adjicias iterum: sed et de pristinis deprecare, ut tibi dimittantur.

verses.text: Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent: for if thou comest near them, they will take hold of thee.
verses.textLatin: Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata: et si accesseris ad illa, suscipient te.

verses.text: The teeth thereof are the teeth of a lion, killing the souls of men.
verses.textLatin: Dentes leonis dentes ejus, interficientes animas hominum.

verses.text: All iniquity is like a two-edged sword, there is no remedy for the wound thereof.
verses.textLatin: Quasi rhomphæa bis acuta omnis iniquitas: plagæ illius non est sanitas.

verses.text: Injuries and wrongs will waste riches: and the house that is very rich shall be brought to nothing by pride: so the substance of the proud shall be rooted out.
verses.textLatin: Objurgatio et injuriæ annullabunt substantiam, et domus quæ nimis locuples est annullabitur superbia: sic substantia superbi eradicabitur.

verses.text: The prayer out of the mouth of the poor shall reach the ears of God, and judgment shall come for him speedily.
verses.textLatin: Deprecatio pauperis ex ore usque ad aures ejus perveniet, et judicium festinato adveniet illi.

verses.text: He that hateth to be reproved walketh in the trace of a sinner: and he that feareth God will turn to his own heart.
verses.textLatin: Qui odit correptionem vestigium est peccatoris, et qui timet Deum convertetur ad cor suum.

verses.text: He that is mighty by a bold tongue is known afar off, but a wise man knoweth to slip by him.
verses.textLatin: Notus a longe potens lingua audaci, et sensatus scit labi se ab ipso.

verses.text: He that buildeth his house at other men’s charges, is as he that gathereth himself stones to build in the winter.
verses.textLatin: Qui ædificat domum suam impendiis alienis, quasi qui colligat lapides suos in hieme.

verses.text: The congregation of sinners is like tow heaped together, and the end of them is a flame of fire.
verses.textLatin: Stupa collecta synagoga peccantium, et consummatio illorum flamma ignis.

verses.text: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, and in their end is hell, and darkness, and pains.
verses.textLatin: Via peccatorum complanata lapidibus: et in fine illorum inferi, et tenebræ, et pœnæ.

verses.text: He that keepeth justice shall get the understanding thereof.
verses.textLatin: Qui custodit justitiam, continebit sensum ejus.

verses.text: The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding.
verses.textLatin: Consummatio timoris Dei, sapientia et sensus.

verses.text: He that is not wise in good, will not be taught.
verses.textLatin: Non erudietur qui non est sapiens in bono.

verses.text: But there is a wisdom that aboundeth in evil: and there is no understanding where there is bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Est autem sapientia quæ abundat in malo, et non est sensus ubi est amaritudo.

verses.text: The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood, and his counsel continueth like a fountain of life.
verses.textLatin: Scientia sapientis tamquam inundatio abundabit, et consilium illius sicut fons vitæ permanet.

verses.text: The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel, and no wisdom at all shall it hold.
verses.textLatin: Cor fatui quasi vas confractum, et omnem sapientiam non tenebit.

verses.text: A man of sense will praise every wise word he shall hear, and will apply it to himself: the luxurious man hath heard it, and it shall displease him, and he will cast it behind his back.
verses.textLatin: Verbum sapiens quodcumque audierit scius, laudabit, et ad se adjiciet: audivit luxuriosus, et displicebit illi, et projiciet illud post dorsum suum.

verses.text: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but in the lips of the wise, grace shall be found.
verses.textLatin: Narratio fatui quasi sarcina in via: nam in labiis sensati invenietur gratia.

verses.text: The mouth of the prudent is sought after in the church, and they will think upon his words in their hearts.
verses.textLatin: Os prudentis quæritur in ecclesia, et verba illius cogitabunt in cordibus suis.

verses.text: As a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as words without sense.
verses.textLatin: Tamquam domus exterminata, sic fatuo sapientia: et scientia insensati inenarrabilia verba.

verses.text: Doctrine to a fool is as fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand.
verses.textLatin: Compedes in pedibus, stulto doctrina: et quasi vincula manuum super manum dextram.

verses.text: A fool lifteth up his voice in laughter: but a wise man will scarce laugh low to himself.
verses.textLatin: Fatuus in risu exaltat vocem suam: vir autem sapiens vix tacite ridebit.

verses.text: Learning to the prudent is as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet upon his right arm.
verses.textLatin: Ornamentum aureum prudenti doctrina, et quasi brachiale in brachio dextro.

verses.text: The foot of a fool is soon in his neighbour’s house: but a man of experience will be abashed at the person of the mighty.
verses.textLatin: Pes fatui facilis in domum proximi: et homo peritus confundetur a persona potentis.

verses.text: A fool will peep through the window into the house: but he that is well taught will stand without.
verses.textLatin: Stultus a fenestra respiciet in domum: vir autem eruditus foris stabit.

verses.text: It is the folly of a man to hearken at the door: and a wise man will be grieved with the disgrace.
verses.textLatin: Stultitia hominis auscultare per ostium: et prudens gravabitur contumelia.

verses.text: The lips of the unwise will be telling foolish things: but the words of the wise shall be weighed in a balance.
verses.textLatin: Labia imprudentium stulta narrabunt; verba autem prudentium statera ponderabuntur.

verses.text: The heart of fools is in their mouth: and the mouth of wise men is in their heart.
verses.textLatin: In ore fatuorum cor illorum, et in corde sapientium os illorum.

verses.text: While the ungodly curseth the devil, he curseth his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Dum maledicit impius diabolum, maledicit ipse animam suam.

verses.text: The talebearer shall defile his own soul, and shall be hated by all: and he that shall abide with him shall be hateful: the silent and wise man shall be honoured.
verses.textLatin: Susurro coinquinabit animam suam, et in omnibus odietur, et qui cum eo manserit odiosus erit: tacitus et sensatus honorabitur.

verses.text: The  sluggard is pelted with a dirty stone, and all men will speak of his disgrace.
verses.textLatin: In lapide luteo lapidatus est piger: et omnes loquentur super aspernationem illius.

verses.text: The sluggard is pelted with the dung of oxen: and every one that toucheth him will shake his hands.
verses.textLatin: De stercore boum lapidatus est piger: et omnis qui tetigerit eum excutiet manus.

verses.text: A son ill taught is the confusion of the father: and a foolish daughter shall be to his loss.
verses.textLatin: Confusio patris est de filio indisciplinato: filia autem in deminoratione fiet.

verses.text: A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that confoundeth, becometh a disgrace to her father.
verses.textLatin: Filia prudens hæreditas viro suo: nam quæ confundit, in contumeliam fit genitoris.

verses.text: She that is bold shameth both her father and husband, and will not be inferior to the ungodly: and shall be disgraced by them both.
verses.textLatin: Patrem et virum confundit audax, et ab impiis non minorabitur: ab utrisque autem inhonorabitur.

verses.text: A tale out of time is like music in mourning: but the stripes and instruction of wisdom are never out of time.
verses.textLatin: Musica in luctu importuna narratio: flagella et doctrina in omni tempore sapientia.

verses.text: He that teacheth a fool, is like one that glueth a potsherd together.
verses.textLatin: Qui docet fatuum, quasi qui conglutinat testam.

verses.text: He that telleth a word to him that heareth not, is like one that waketh a man out of a deep sleep.
verses.textLatin: Qui narrat verbum non audienti, quasi qui excitat dormientem de gravi somno.

verses.text: He speaketh with one that is asleep, who uttereth wisdom to a fool: and in the end of the discourse he saith: Who is this?
verses.textLatin: Cum dormiente loquitur qui enarrat stulto sapientiam: et in fine narrationis dicit: Quis est hic?

verses.text: Weep for the dead, for his light hath failed: and weep for the fool, for his understanding faileth.
verses.textLatin: Supra mortuum plora, defecit enim lux ejus: et supra fatuum plora, defecit enim sensus.

verses.text: Weep but a little for the dead, for he is at rest.
verses.textLatin: Modicum plora super mortuum, quoniam requievit:

verses.text: For the wicked life of a wicked fool is worse than death.
verses.textLatin: nequissimi enim nequissima vita super mortem fatui.

verses.text: The mourning for the dead is seven days: but for a fool and an ungodly man all the days of their life.
verses.textLatin: Luctus mortui septem dies: fatui autem et impii omnes dies vitæ illorum.

verses.text: Talk not much with a fool, and go not with him that hath no sense.
verses.textLatin: Cum stulto ne multum loquaris, et cum insensato ne abieris.

verses.text: Keep thyself from him, that thou mayst not have trouble, and thou shalt not be defiled with his sin.
verses.textLatin: Serva te ab illo, ut non molestiam habeas, et non coinquinaberis peccato illius.

verses.text: Turn away from him, and thou shalt find rest, and shalt not be wearied out with his folly.
verses.textLatin: Deflecte ab illo, et invenies requiem, et non acediaberis in stultitia illius.

verses.text: What is heavier than lead? and what other name hath he but fool?
verses.textLatin: Super plumbum quid gravabitur? et quod illi aliud nomen quam fatuus?

verses.text: Sand and salt, and a mass of iron is easier to bear, than a man without sense, that is both foolish and wicked.
verses.textLatin: Arenam, et salem, et massam ferri facilius est ferre quam hominem imprudentem, et fatuum, et impium.

verses.text: A frame of wood bound together in the foundation of a building, shall not be loosed: so neither shall the heart that is established by advised counsel.
verses.textLatin: Loramentum ligneum colligatum in fundamento ædificii non dissolvetur, sic et cor confirmatum in cogitatione consilii.

verses.text: The thought of him that is wise at all times, shall not be depraved by fear.
verses.textLatin: Cogitatus sensati in omni tempore metu non depravabitur.

verses.text: As pales set in high places, and plasterings made without cost, will not stand against the face of the wind:
verses.textLatin: Sicut pali in excelsis, et cæmenta sine impensa posita, contra faciem venti non permanebunt:

verses.text: So also a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool shall not resist against the violence of fear.
verses.textLatin: sic et cor timidum in cogitatione stulti contra impetum timoris non resistet.

verses.text: As a fearful heart in the thought of a fool at all times will not fear, so neither shall he that continueth always in the commandments of God.
verses.textLatin: Sicut cor trepidum in cogitatione fatui omni tempore non metuet, sic et qui in præceptis Dei permanet semper.

verses.text: He that pricketh the eye, bringeth out tears: and he that pricketh the heart, bringeth forth resentment.
verses.textLatin: Pungens oculum deducit lacrimas, et qui pungit cor profert sensum.

verses.text: He that flingeth a stone at birds, shall drive them away: so he that upbraideth his friend, breaketh friendship.
verses.textLatin: Mittens lapidem in volatilia, dejiciet illa: sic et qui conviciatur amico, dissolvit amicitiam.

verses.text: Although thou hast drawn a sword at a friend, despair not: for there may be a returning. To a friend,
verses.textLatin: Ad amicum etsi produxeris gladium, non desperes: est enim regressus. Ad amicum

verses.text: If thou hast opened a sad mouth, fear not, for there may be a reconciliation: except upbraiding, and reproach, and pride, and disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for in all these cases a friend will flee away.
verses.textLatin: si aperueris os triste, non timeas: est enim concordatio: excepto convitio, et improperio, et superbia, et mysterii revelatione, et plaga dolosa: in his omnibus effugiet amicus.

verses.text: Keep fidelity with a friend in his poverty, that in his prosperity also thou mayst rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Fidem posside cum amico in paupertate illius, ut et in bonis illius læteris.

verses.text: In the time of his trouble continue faithful to him, that thou mayst also be heir with him in his inheritance.
verses.textLatin: In tempore tribulationis illius permane illi fidelis, ut et in hæreditate illius cohæres sis.

verses.text: As the vapour of a chimney, and the smoke of the fire goeth up before the fire: so also injurious words, and reproaches, and threats, before blood.
verses.textLatin: Ante ignem camini vapor et fumus ignis inaltatur: sic et ante sanguinem maledicta, et contumeliæ, et minæ.

verses.text: I will not be ashamed to salute a friend, neither will I hide myself from his face: and if any evil happen to me by him, I will bear it.
verses.textLatin: Amicum salutare non confundar, a facie illius non me abscondam: et si mala mihi evenerint per illum, sustinebo.

verses.text: But every one that shall hear it, will beware of him.
verses.textLatin: Omnis qui audiet cavebit se ab eo.

verses.text: Who will set a guard before my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, that I fall not by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
verses.textLatin: Quis dabit ori meo custodiam, et super labia mea signaculum certum, ut non cadam ab ipsis, et lingua mea perdat me?

verses.text: O Lord, father, and sovereign ruler of my life, leave me not to their counsel: nor suffer me to fall by them.
verses.textLatin: Domine, pater et dominator vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in consilio eorum, nec sinas me cadere in illis.

verses.text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not in their ignorances, and that their sins may not appear:
verses.textLatin: Quis superponet in cogitatu meo flagella, et in corde meo doctrinam sapientiæ, ut ignorationibus eorum non parcant mihi, et non appareant delicta eorum,

verses.text: Lest my ignorances increase, and my offences be multiplied, and my sins abound, and I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me?
verses.textLatin: et ne adincrescant ignorantiæ meæ, et multiplicentur delicta mea, et peccata mea abundent, et incidam in conspectu adversariorum meorum, et gaudeat super me inimicus meus?

verses.text: O Lord, father, and God of my life, leave me not to their devices.
verses.textLatin: Domine, pater et Deus vitæ meæ, ne derelinquas me in cogitatu illorum.

verses.text: Give me not haughtiness of my eyes, and turn away from me all coveting.
verses.textLatin: Extollentiam oculorum meorum ne dederis mihi, et omne desiderium averte a me.

verses.text: Take from me the greediness of the belly, and let not the lusts of the flesh take hold of me, and give me not over to a shameless and foolish mind.
verses.textLatin: Aufer a me ventris concupiscentias, et concubitus concupiscentiæ ne apprehendant me, et animæ irreverenti et infrunitæ ne tradas me.

verses.text: Hear, O ye children, the discipline of the mouth, and he that will keep it shall not perish by his lips, nor be brought to fall into most wicked works.
verses.textLatin: Doctrinam oris audite, filii: et qui custodierit illam non periet labiis, nec scandalizabitur in operibus nequissimis.

verses.text: A sinner is caught in his own vanity, and the proud and the evil speakers shall fall thereby.
verses.textLatin: In vanitate sua apprehenditur peccator: et superbus et maledicus scandalizabitur in illis.

verses.text: Let not thy mouth be accustomed to swearing: for in it there are many falls.
verses.textLatin: Jurationi non assuescat os tuum: multi enim casus in illa.

verses.text: And let not the naming of God be usual in thy mouth, and meddle not with the names of saints, for thou shalt not escape free from them.
verses.textLatin: Nominatio vero Dei non sit assidua in ore tuo, et nominibus sanctorum non admiscearis, quoniam non erit immunis ab eis.

verses.text: For as a slave daily put to the question, is never without a blue mark: so every one that sweareth, and nameth, shall not be wholly pure from sin.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim servus interrogatus assidue a livore non minuitur, sic omnis jurans et nominans in toto a peccato non purgabitur.

verses.text: A man that sweareth much, shall be filled with iniquity, and a scourge shall not depart from his house.
verses.textLatin: Vir multum jurans implebitur iniquitate, et non discedet a domo illius plaga.

verses.text: And if he make it void, his sin shall be upon him, and if he dissemble it, he offendeth double:
verses.textLatin: Et si frustraverit, delictum illius super ipsum erit: et si dissimulaverit, delinquit dupliciter:

verses.text: And if he swear in vain, he shall not be justified: for his house shall be filled with his punishment.
