verses.textLatin: et si in vacuum juraverit, non justificabitur: replebitur enim retributione domus illius.

verses.text: There is also another speech opposite to death, let it not be found in the inheritance of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Est et alia loquela contraria morti: non inveniatur in hæreditate Jacob.

verses.text: For from the merciful all these things shall be taken away, and they shall not wallow in sins.
verses.textLatin: Etenim a misericordibus omnia hæc auferentur, et in delictis non volutabuntur.

verses.text: Let not thy mouth be accustomed to indiscreet speech: for therein is the word of sin.
verses.textLatin: Indisciplinatæ loquelæ non assuescat os tuum: est enim in illa verbum peccati.

verses.text: Remember thy father and thy mother, for thou sittest in the midst of great men:
verses.textLatin: Memento patris et matris tuæ: in medio enim magnatorum consistis:

verses.text: Lest God forget thee in their sight, and thou, by thy daily custom be infatuated and suffer reproach: and wish that thou hadst not been born, and curse the day of thy nativity.
verses.textLatin: ne forte obliviscatur te Deus in conspectu illorum, et assiduitate tua infatuatus, improperium patiaris, et maluisses non nasci, et diem nativitatis tuæ maledicas.

verses.text: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will never be corrected all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: Homo assuetus in verbis improperii in omnibus diebus suis non erudietur.

verses.text: Two sorts of men multiply sins, and the third bringeth wrath and destruction.
verses.textLatin: Duo genera abundant in peccatis, et tertium adducit iram et perditionem.

verses.text: A hot soul is a burning fire, it will never be quenched, till it devour some thing.
verses.textLatin: Anima calida quasi ignis ardens, non extinguetur donec aliquid glutiat:

verses.text: And a man that is wicked in the mouth of his flesh, will not leave off till he hath kindled a fire.
verses.textLatin: et homo nequam in ore carnis suæ non desinet donec incendat ignem.

verses.text: To a man that is a fornicator all bread is sweet, he will not be weary of sinning unto the end.
verses.textLatin: Homini fornicario omnis panis dulcis: non fatigabitur transgrediens usque ad finem.

verses.text: Every man that passeth beyond his own bed, despising his own soul, and saying: Who seeth me?
verses.textLatin: Omnis homo qui transgreditur lectum suum, contemnens in animam suam, et dicens: Quis me videt?

verses.text: Darkness compasseth me about, and the walls cover me, and no man seeth me: whom do I fear? the most High will not remember my sins.
verses.textLatin: Tenebræ circumdant me, et parietes cooperiunt me, et nemo circumspicit me: quem vereor? delictorum meorum non memorabitur Altissimus.

verses.text: And he understandeth not that his eye seeth all things, for such a man’s fear driveth him from the fear of God, and the eyes of men fearing him:
verses.textLatin: Et non intelligit quoniam omnia videt oculus illius, quoniam expellit a se timorem Dei hujusmodi hominis timor, et oculi hominum timentes illum:

verses.text: And he knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men, and the bottom of the deep, and looking into the hearts of men, into the most hidden parts.
verses.textLatin: et non cognovit quoniam oculi Domini multo plus lucidiores sunt super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum, et profundum abyssi, et hominum corda, intuentes in absconditas partes.

verses.text: For all things were known to the Lord God, before they were created: so also after they were perfected he beholdeth all things.
verses.textLatin: Domino enim Deo antequam crearentur omnia sunt agnita: sic et post perfectum respicit omnia.

verses.text: This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and he shall be chased as a colt: and where he suspected not, he shall be taken.
verses.textLatin: Hic in plateis civitatis vindicabitur, et quasi pullus equinus fugabitur, et ubi non speravit apprehendetur.

verses.text: And he shall be in disgrace with all men, because he understood not the fear of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et erit dedecus omnibus, eo quod non intellexerit timorem Domini.

verses.text: So every woman also that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another:
verses.textLatin: Sic et mulier omnis relinquens virum suum, et statuens hæreditatem ex alieno matrimonio:

verses.text: For first she hath been unfaithful to the law of the most High: and secondly, she hath offended against her husband: thirdly, she hath fornicated in adultery, and hath gotten her children of another man.
verses.textLatin: primo enim in lege Altissimi incredibilis fuit: secundo in virum suum deliquit: tertio in adulterio fornicata est, et ex alio viro filios statuit sibi.

verses.text: This woman shall be brought into the assembly, and inquisition shall be made of her children.
verses.textLatin: Hæc in ecclesiam adducetur, et in filios ejus respicietur:

verses.text: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.
verses.textLatin: non tradent filii ejus radices, et rami ejus non dabunt fructum:

verses.text: She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her infamy shall not be blotted out.
verses.textLatin: derelinquet in maledictum memoriam ejus, et dedecus illius non delebitur.

verses.text: And they that remain shall know, that there is nothing better than the fear of God: and that there is nothing sweeter than to have regard to the commandments of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et agnoscent qui derelicti sunt, quoniam nihil melius est quam timor Dei, et nihil dulcius quam respicere in mandatis Domini.

verses.text: It is great glory to follow the Lord: for length of days shall be received from him.
verses.textLatin: Gloria magna est sequi Dominum: longitudo enim dierum assumetur ab eo.

verses.text: Wisdom  shall praise her own self, and shall be honoured in God, and shall glory in the midst of her people,
verses.textLatin: Sapientia laudabit animam suam, et in Deo honorabitur, et in medio populi sui gloriabitur,

verses.text: And shall open her mouth in the churches of the most High, and shall glorify herself in the sight of his power,
verses.textLatin: et in ecclesiis Altissimi aperiet os suum, et in conspectu virtutis illius gloriabitur,

verses.text: And in the midst of her own people she shall be exalted, and shall be admired in the holy assembly.
verses.textLatin: et in medio populi sui exaltabitur, et in plenitudine sancta admirabitur,

verses.text: And in the multitude of the elect she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed, saying:
verses.textLatin: et in multitudine electorum habebit laudem, et inter benedictos benedicetur, dicens:

verses.text: I came out of the mouth of the most High, the firstborn before all creatures:
verses.textLatin: Ego ex ore Altissimi prodivi, primogenita ante omnem creaturam.

verses.text: I made that in the heavens there should rise light that never faileth, and as a cloud I covered all the earth:
verses.textLatin: Ego feci in cælis ut oriretur lumen indeficiens, et sicut nebula texi omnem terram.

verses.text: I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of a cloud.
verses.textLatin: Ego in altissimis habitavi, et thronus meus in columna nubis.

verses.text: I alone have compassed the circuit of heaven, and have penetrated into the bottom of the deep, and have walked in the waves of the sea,
verses.textLatin: Gyrum cæli circuivi sola, et profundum abyssi penetravi: in fluctibus maris ambulavi.

verses.text: And have stood in all the earth: and in every people,
verses.textLatin: Et in omni terra steti: et in omni populo,

verses.text: And in every nation I have had the chief rule:
verses.textLatin: et in omni gente primatum habui:

verses.text: And by my power I have trodden under my feet the hearts of all the high and low: and in all these I sought rest, and I shall abide in the inheritance of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et omnium excellentium et humilium corda virtute calcavi. Et in his omnibus requiem quæsivi, et in hæreditate Domini morabor.

verses.text: Then the creator of all things commanded, and said to me: and he that made me, rested in my tabernacle,
verses.textLatin: Tunc præcepit, et dixit mihi Creator omnium: et qui creavit me, requievit in tabernaculo meo.

verses.text: And he said to me: Let thy dwelling be in Jacob, and thy inheritance in Israel, and take root in my elect.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit mihi: In Jacob inhabita, et in Israël hæreditare, et in electis meis mitte radices.

verses.text: From the beginning, and before the world, was I created, and unto the world to come I shall not cease to be, and in the holy dwelling place I have ministered before him.
verses.textLatin: Ab initio et ante sæcula creata sum, et usque ad futurum sæculum non desinam: et in habitatione sancta coram ipso ministravi.

verses.text: And so was I established in Sion, and in the holy city likewise I rested, and my power was in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et sic in Sion firmata sum, et in civitate sanctificata similiter requievi, et in Jerusalem potestas mea.

verses.text: And I took root in an honourable people, and in the portion of my God his inheritance, and my abode is in the full assembly of saints.
verses.textLatin: Et radicavi in populo honorificato, et in parte Dei mei hæreditas illius, et in plenitudine sanctorum detentio mea.

verses.text: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree on mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: Quasi cedrus exaltata sum in Libano, et quasi cypressus in monte Sion:

verses.text: I was exalted like a palm tree in Cades, and as a rose plant in Jericho:
verses.textLatin: quasi palma exaltata sum in Cades, et quasi plantatio rosæ in Jericho:

verses.text: As a fair olive tree in the plains, and as a plane tree by the water in the streets, was I exalted.
verses.textLatin: quasi oliva speciosa in campis, et quasi platanus exaltata sum juxta aquam in plateis.

verses.text: I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon, and aromatical balm: I yielded a sweet odour like the best myrrh:
verses.textLatin: Sicut cinnamomum et balsamum aromatizans odorem dedi; quasi myrrha electa dedi suavitatem odoris:

verses.text: And I perfumed my dwelling as storax, and galbanum, and onyx, and aloes, and as the frankincense not cut, and my odour is as the purest balm.
verses.textLatin: et quasi storax, et galbanus, et ungula, et gutta, et quasi Libanus non incisus vaporavi habitationem meam, et quasi balsamum non mistum odor meus.

verses.text: I have stretched out my branches as the turpentine tree, and my branches are of honour and grace.
verses.textLatin: Ego quasi terebinthus extendi ramos meos, et rami mei honoris et gratiæ.

verses.text: As the vine I have brought forth a pleasant odour: and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
verses.textLatin: Ego quasi vitis fructificavi suavitatem odoris: et flores mei fructus honoris et honestatis.

verses.text: I am the mother of fair love, and of fear, and of knowledge, and of holy hope.
verses.textLatin: Ego mater pulchræ dilectionis, et timoris, et agnitionis, et sanctæ spei.

verses.text: In me is all grace of the way and of the truth, in me is all hope of life and of virtue.
verses.textLatin: In me gratia omnis viæ et veritatis: in me omnis spes vitæ et virtutis.

verses.text: Come over to me, all ye that desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
verses.textLatin: Transite ad me, omnes qui concupiscitis me, et a generationibus meis implemini:

verses.text: For my spirit is sweet above honey, and my inheritance above honey and the honeycomb.
verses.textLatin: spiritus enim meus super mel dulcis, et hæreditas mea super mel et favum.

verses.text: My memory is unto everlasting generations.
verses.textLatin: Memoria mea in generatione sæculorum.

verses.text: They that eat me, shall yet hunger: and they that drink me, shall yet thirst.
verses.textLatin: Qui edunt me, adhuc esurient, et qui bibunt me, adhuc sitient.

verses.text: He that hearkeneth to me, shall not be confounded: and they that work by me, shall not sin.
verses.textLatin: Qui audit me non confundetur, et qui operantur in me non peccabunt:

verses.text: They that explain me shall have life everlasting.
verses.textLatin: qui elucidant me, vitam æternam habebunt.

verses.text: All these things are the book of life, and the covenant of the most High, and the knowledge of truth.
verses.textLatin: Hæc omnia liber vitæ, et testamentum Altissimi, et agnitio veritatis.

verses.text: Moses commanded a law in the precepts of justices, and an inheritance to the house of Jacob, and the promises to Israel.
verses.textLatin: Legem mandavit Moyses in præceptis justitiarum, et hæreditatem domui Jacob, et Israël promissiones.

verses.text: He appointed to David his servant to raise up of him a most mighty king, and sitting on the throne of glory for ever.
verses.textLatin: Posuit David, puero suo, excitare regem ex ipso fortissimum, et in throno honoris sedentem in sempiternum.

verses.text: Who filleth up wisdom as the Phison, and as the Tigris in the days of the new fruits.
verses.textLatin: Qui implet quasi Phison sapientiam, et sicut Tigris in diebus novorum:

verses.text: Who maketh understanding to abound as the Euphrates, who multiplieth it as the Jordan in the time of harvest.
verses.textLatin: qui adimplet quasi Euphrates sensum, qui multiplicat quasi Jordanis in tempore messis:

verses.text: Who sendeth knowledge as the light, and riseth up as Gehon in the time of the vintage.
verses.textLatin: qui mittit disciplinam sicut lucem, et assistens quasi Gehon in die vindemiæ.

verses.text: Who first hath perfect knowledge of her, and a weaker shall not search her out.
verses.textLatin: Qui perficit primus scire ipsam, et infirmior non investigabit eam.

verses.text: For her thoughts are more vast than the sea, and her counsels more deep than the great ocean.
verses.textLatin: A mari enim abundavit cogitatio ejus, et consilium illius ab abysso magna.

verses.text: I, wisdom, have poured out rivers.
verses.textLatin: Ego sapientiam effudi flumina:

verses.text: I, like a brook out of a river of a mighty water; I, like a channel of a river, and like an aqueduct, came out of paradise.
verses.textLatin: ego quasi trames aquæ immensæ de fluvio: ego quasi fluvii dioryx, et sicut aquæductus exivi de paradiso.

verses.text: I said: I will water my garden of plants, and I will water abundantly the fruits of my meadow.
verses.textLatin: Dixi: Rigabo hortum meum plantationum, et inebriabo prati mei fructum.

verses.text: And behold my brook became a great river, and my river came near to a sea:
verses.textLatin: Et ecce factus est mihi trames abundans, et fluvius meus appropinquavit ad mare:

verses.text: For I make doctrine to shine forth to all as the morning light, and I will declare it afar off.
verses.textLatin: quoniam doctrinam quasi antelucanum illumino omnibus, et enarrabo illam usque ad longinquum.

verses.text: I will penetrate to all the lower parts of the earth, and will behold all that sleep, and will enlighten all that hope in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Penetrabo omnes inferiores partes terræ, et inspiciam omnes dormientes, et illuminabo omnes sperantes in Domino.

verses.text: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and will leave it to them that seek wisdom, and will not cease to instruct their offspring even to the holy age.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc doctrinam quasi prophetiam effundam, et relinquam illam quærentibus sapientiam, et non desinam in progenies illorum usque in ævum sanctum.

verses.text: See ye that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all that seek out the truth.
verses.textLatin: Videte quoniam non soli mihi laboravi, sed omnibus exquirentibus veritatem.

verses.text: With  three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and men:
verses.textLatin: In tribus placitum est spiritui meo, quæ sunt probata coram Deo et hominibus:

verses.text: The concord of brethren, and the love of neighbours, and man and wife that agree well together.
verses.textLatin: concordia fratrum, et amor proximorum, et vir et mulier bene sibi consentientes.

verses.text: Three sorts my soul hateth, and I am greatly grieved at their life:
verses.textLatin: Tres species odivit anima mea, et aggravor valde animæ illorum:

verses.text: A poor man that is proud: a rich man that is a liar: an old man that is a fool, and doting.
verses.textLatin: pauperem superbum, divitem mendacem, senem fatuum et insensatum.

verses.text: The things that thou hast not gathered in thy youth, how shalt thou find them in thy old age?
verses.textLatin: Quæ in juventute tua non congregasti, quomodo in senectute tua invenies?

verses.text: O how comely is judgment for a grey head, and for ancients to know counsel!
verses.textLatin: Quam speciosum canitiei judicium, et presbyteris cognoscere consilium!

verses.text: O how comely is wisdom for the aged, and understanding and counsel to men of honour!
verses.textLatin: Quam speciosa veteranis sapientia, et gloriosus intellectus et consilium!

verses.text: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of God is their glory.
verses.textLatin: Corona senum multa peritia, et gloria illorum timor Dei.

verses.text: Nine things that are not to be imagined by the heart have I magnified, and the tenth I will utter to men with my tongue.
verses.textLatin: Novem insuspicabilia cordis magnificavi: et decimum dicam in lingua hominibus:

verses.text: A man that hath joy of his children: and he that liveth and seeth the fall of his enemies.
verses.textLatin: homo qui jucundatur in filiis, vivens et videns subversionem inimicorum suorum.

verses.text: Blessed is he that dwelleth with a wise woman, and that hath not slipped with his tongue, and that hath not served such as are unworthy of him.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui habitat cum muliere sensata, et qui lingua sua non est lapsus, et qui non servivit indignis se.

verses.text: Blessed is he that findeth a true friend, and that declareth justice to an ear that heareth.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui invenit amicum verum, et qui enarrat justitiam auri audienti.

verses.text: How great is he that findeth wisdom and knowledge! but there is none above him that feareth the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Quam magnus qui invenit sapientiam et scientiam! sed non est super timentem Dominum.

verses.text: The fear of God hath set itself above all things:
verses.textLatin: Timor Dei super omnia se superposuit.

verses.text: Blessed is the man, to whom it is given to have the fear of God: he that holdeth it, to whom shall he be likened?
verses.textLatin: Beatus homo cui donatum est habere timorem Dei: qui tenet illum, cui assimilabitur?

verses.text: The fear of God is the beginning of his love: and the beginning of faith is to be fast joined unto it.
verses.textLatin: Timor Dei initium dilectionis ejus: fidei autem initium agglutinandum est ei.

verses.text: The sadness of the heart is every plague: and the wickedness of a woman is all evil.
verses.textLatin: Omnis plaga tristitia cordis est, et omnis malitia nequitia mulieris.

verses.text: And a man will choose any plague, but the plague of the heart:
verses.textLatin: Et omnem plagam, et non plagam videbit cordis:

verses.text: And any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman:
verses.textLatin: et omnem nequitiam, et non nequitiam mulieris:

verses.text: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate him:
verses.textLatin: et omnem obductum, et non obductum odientium:

verses.text: And any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
verses.textLatin: et omnem vindictam, et non vindictam inimicorum.

verses.text: There is no head worse than the head of a serpent:
verses.textLatin: Non est caput nequius super caput colubri,

verses.text: And there is no anger above the anger of a woman. It will be more agreeable to abide with a lion and a dragon, than to dwell with a wicked woman.
verses.textLatin: et non est ira super iram mulieris. Commorari leoni et draconi placebit, quam habitare cum muliere nequam.

verses.text: The wickedness of a woman changeth her face: and she darkeneth her countenance as a bear: and sheweth it like sackcloth. In the midst of her neighbours,
verses.textLatin: Nequitia mulieris immutat faciem ejus: et obcæcat vultum suum tamquam ursus, et quasi saccum ostendit. In medio proximorum ejus

verses.text: Her husband groaned, and hearing he sighed a little.
verses.textLatin: ingemuit vir ejus, et audiens suspiravit modicum.

verses.text: All malice is short to the malice of a woman, let the lot of sinners fall upon her.
verses.textLatin: Brevis omnis malitia super malitiam mulieris: sors peccatorum cadat super illam.

verses.text: As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of tongue to a quiet man.
verses.textLatin: Sicut ascensus arenosus in pedibus veterani, sic mulier linguata homini quieto.

verses.text: Look not upon a woman’s beauty, and desire not a woman for beauty.
verses.textLatin: Ne respicias in mulieris speciem, et non concupiscas mulierem in specie.

verses.text: A woman’s anger, and impudence, and confusion is great.
verses.textLatin: Mulieris ira, et irreverentia, et confusio magna.

verses.text: A woman, if she have superiority, is contrary to her husband.
verses.textLatin: Mulier si primatum habeat, contraria est viro suo.

verses.text: A wicked woman abateth the courage, and maketh a heavy countenance, and a wounded heart.
verses.textLatin: Cor humile, et facies tristis, et plaga cordis, mulier nequam.

verses.text: Feeble hands, and disjointed knees, a woman that doth not make her husband happy.
verses.textLatin: Manus debiles et genua dissoluta, mulier quæ non beatificat virum suum.

verses.text: From the woman came the beginning of sin, and by her we all die.
verses.textLatin: A muliere initium factum est peccati, et per illam omnes morimur.

verses.text: Give no issue to thy water, no, not a little: nor to a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad.
verses.textLatin: Non des aquæ tuæ exitum, nec modicum: nec mulieri nequam veniam prodeundi.

verses.text: If she walk not at thy hand, she will confound thee in the sight of thy enemies.
verses.textLatin: Si non ambulaverit ad manum tuam, confundet te in conspectu inimicorum.

verses.text: Cut her off from thy flesh, lest she always abuse thee.
verses.textLatin: A carnibus tuis abscinde illam, ne semper te abutatur.

verses.text: Happy  is the husband of a good wife: for the number of his years is double.
verses.textLatin: Mulieris bonæ beatus vir: numerus enim annorum illius duplex.

verses.text: A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.
verses.textLatin: Mulier fortis oblectat virum suum, et annos vitæ illius in pace implebit.

verses.text: A good wife is a good portion, she shall be given in the portion of them that fear God, to a man for his good deeds.
verses.textLatin: Pars bona mulier bona, in parte timentium Deum dabitur viro pro factis bonis:

verses.text: Rich or poor, if his heart is good, his countenance shall be cheerful at all times.
verses.textLatin: divitis autem et pauperis cor bonum, in omni tempore vultus illorum hilaris.

verses.text: Of three things my heart hath been afraid, and at the fourth my face hath trembled:
verses.textLatin: A tribus timuit cor meum, et in quarto facies mea metuit:

verses.text: The accusation of a city, and the gathering together of the people:
verses.textLatin: delaturam civitatis, et collectionem populi:

verses.text: And a false calumny, all are more grievous than death.
verses.textLatin: calumniam mendacem super mortem omnia gravia:

verses.text: A jealous woman is the grief and mourning of the heart.
verses.textLatin: dolor cordis et luctus, mulier zelotypa.

verses.text: With a jealous woman is a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.
verses.textLatin: In muliere zelotypa flagellum linguæ, omnibus communicans.

verses.text: As a yoke of oxen that is moved to and fro, so also is a wicked woman: he that hath hold of her, is as he that taketh hold of a scorpion.
verses.textLatin: Sicut boum jugum quod movetur, ita et mulier nequam: qui tenet illam quasi qui apprehendit scorpionem.

verses.text: A drunken woman is a great wrath: and her reproach and shame shall not be hid.
verses.textLatin: Mulier ebriosa ira magna, et contumelia: et turpitudo illius non tegetur.

verses.text: The fornication of a woman shall be known by the haughtiness of her eyes, and by her eyelids.
verses.textLatin: Fornicatio mulieris in extollentia oculorum, et in palpebris illius agnoscetur.

verses.text: On a daughter that turneth not away herself, set a strict watch: lest finding an opportunity she abuse herself.
verses.textLatin: In filia non avertente se, firma custodiam, ne inventa occasione utatur se.

verses.text: Take heed of the impudence of her eyes, and wonder not if she slight thee.
verses.textLatin: Ab omni irreverentia oculorum ejus cave, et ne mireris si te neglexerit.

verses.text: She will open her mouth as a thirsty traveller to the fountain, and will drink of every water near her, and will sit down by every hedge, and open her quiver against every arrow, until she fail.
verses.textLatin: Sicut viator sitiens ad fontem os aperiet, et ab omni aqua proxima bibet, et contra omnem palum sedebit, et contra omnem sagittam aperiet pharetram donec deficiat.

verses.text: The grace of a diligent woman shall delight her husband, and shall fat his bones.
verses.textLatin: Gratia mulieris sedulæ delectabit virum suum, et ossa illius impinguabit.

verses.text: Her discipline is the gift of God.
verses.textLatin: Disciplina illius datum Dei est.

verses.text: Such is a wise and silent woman, and there is nothing so much worth as a well instructed soul.
verses.textLatin: Mulier sensata et tacita, non est immutatio eruditæ animæ.

verses.text: A holy and shamefaced woman is grace upon grace.
verses.textLatin: Gratia super gratiam mulier sancta et pudorata.

verses.text: And no price is worthy of a continent soul.
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem ponderatio non est digna continentis animæ.

verses.text: As the sun when it riseth to the world in the high places of God, so is the beauty of a good wife for the ornament of her house.
verses.textLatin: Sicut sol oriens mundo in altissimis Dei, sic mulieris bonæ species in ornamentum domus ejus.

verses.text: As the lamp shining upon the holy candlestick, so is the beauty of the face in a ripe age,
verses.textLatin: Lucerna splendens super candelabrum sanctum, et species faciei super ætatem stabilem.

verses.text: As golden pillars upon bases of silver, so are the firm feet upon the soles of a steady woman.
verses.textLatin: Columnæ aureæ super bases argenteas, et pedes firmi super plantas stabilis mulieris.

verses.text: As everlasting foundations upon a solid rock, so the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman.
verses.textLatin: Fundamenta æterna supra petram solidam, et mandata Dei in corde mulieris sanctæ.

verses.text: At two things my heart is grieved, and the third bringeth anger upon me.
verses.textLatin: In duobus contristatum est cor meum, et in tertio iracundia mihi advenit:

verses.text: A man of war fainting through poverty: and a man of sense despised:
verses.textLatin: vir bellator deficiens per inopiam; et vir sensatus contemptus;

verses.text: And he that passeth over from justice to sin, God hath prepared such an one for the sword.
verses.textLatin: et qui transgreditur a justitia ad peccatum: Deus paravit eum ad rhomphæam.

verses.text: Two sorts of callings have appeared to me hard and dangerous: a merchant is hardly free from negligence: and a huckster shall not be justified from the sins of the lips.
verses.textLatin: Duæ species difficiles et periculosæ mihi apparuerunt: difficile exuitur negotians a negligentia, et non justificabitur caupo a peccatis labiorum.

verses.text: Through  poverty many have sinned: and he that seeketh to be enriched, turneth away his eye.
verses.textLatin: Propter inopiam multi deliquerunt: et qui quærit locupletari avertit oculum suum.

verses.text: As a stake sticketh fast in the midst of the joining of stones, so also in the midst of selling and buying, sin shall stick fast.
verses.textLatin: Sicut in medio compaginis lapidum palus figitur, sic et inter medium venditionis et emptionis angustiabitur peccatum:

verses.text: Sin shall be destroyed with the sinner.
verses.textLatin: conteretur cum delinquente delictum.

verses.text: Unless thou hold thyself diligently in the fear of the Lord, thy house shall quickly be overthrown.
verses.textLatin: Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua.

verses.text: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the dust will remain: so will the perplexity of a man in his thoughts.
verses.textLatin: Sicut in percussura cribri remanebit pulvis, sic aporia hominis in cogitatu illius.

verses.text: The furnace trieth the potter’s vessels, and the trial of affliction just men.
verses.textLatin: Vasa figuli probat fornax, et homines justos tentatio tribulationis.

verses.text: As the dressing of a tree sheweth the fruit thereof, so a word out of the thought of the heart of man.
verses.textLatin: Sicut rusticatio de ligno ostendit fructum illius, sic verbum ex cogitatu cordis hominis.

verses.text: Praise not a man before he speaketh, for this is the trial of men.
verses.textLatin: Ante sermonem non laudes virum: hæc enim tentatio est hominum.

verses.text: If thou followest justice, thou shalt obtain her: and shalt put her on as a long robe of honour, and thou shalt dwell with her: and she shall protect thee for ever, and in the day of acknowledgment thou shalt find a strong foundation.
verses.textLatin: Si sequaris justitiam, apprehendes illam, et indues quasi poderem honoris: et inhabitabis cum ea, et proteget te in sempiternum, et in die agnitionis invenies firmamentum.

verses.text: Birds resort unto their like: so truth will return to them that practise her.
verses.textLatin: Volatilia ad sibi similia conveniunt: et veritas ad eos qui operantur illam revertetur.

verses.text: The lion always lieth in wait for prey: so do sins for them that work iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Leo venationi insidiatur semper: sic peccata operantibus iniquitates.

verses.text: A holy man continueth in wisdom as the sun: but a fool is changed as the moon.
verses.textLatin: Homo sanctus in sapientia manet sicut sol: nam stultus sicut luna mutatur.

verses.text: In the midst of the unwise keep in the word till its time: but be continually among men that think.
verses.textLatin: In medio insensatorum serva verbum tempori: in medio autem cogitantium assiduus esto.

verses.text: The discourse of sinners is hateful, and their laughter is at the pleasures of sin.
verses.textLatin: Narratio peccantium odiosa, et risus illorum in deliciis peccati.

verses.text: The speech that sweareth much shall make the hair of the head stand upright: and its irreverence shall make one stop his ears.
verses.textLatin: Loquela multum jurans horripilationem capiti statuet, et irreverentia ipsius obturatio aurium.

verses.text: In the quarrels of the road is the shedding of blood: and their cursing is a grievous hearing.
verses.textLatin: Effusio sanguinis in rixa superborum, et maledictio illorum auditus gravis.

verses.text: He that discloseth the secret of a friend loseth his credit, and shall never find a friend to his mind.
verses.textLatin: Qui denudat arcana amici fidem perdit, et non inveniet amicum ad animum suum.

verses.text: Love thy neighbour, and be joined to him with fidelity.
verses.textLatin: Dilige proximum, et conjungere fide cum illo.

verses.text: But if thou discover his secrets, follow no more after him.
verses.textLatin: Quod si denudaveris absconsa illius, non persequeris post eum.

verses.text: For as a man that destroyeth his friend, so also is he that destroyeth the friendship of his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim homo qui perdit amicum suum, sic et qui perdit amicitiam proximi sui.

verses.text: And as one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so hast thou let thy neighbour go, and thou shalt not get him again.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut qui dimittit avem de manu sua, sic dereliquisti proximum tuum, et non eum capies.

verses.text: Follow after him no more, for he is gone afar off, he is fled, as a roe escaped out of the snare because his soul is wounded.
verses.textLatin: Non illum sequaris, quoniam longe abest: effugit enim quasi caprea de laqueo, quoniam vulnerata est anima ejus:

verses.text: Thou canst no more bind him up. And of a curse there is reconciliation:
verses.textLatin: ultra eum non poteris colligare. Et maledicti est concordatio:

verses.text: But to disclose the secrets of a friend, leaveth no hope to an unhappy soul.
verses.textLatin: denudare autem amici mysteria, desperatio est animæ infelicis.

verses.text: He that winketh with the eye forgeth wicked things, and no man will cast him off:
verses.textLatin: Annuens oculo fabricat iniqua, et nemo eum abjiciet.

verses.text: In the sight of thy eyes he will sweeten his mouth, and will admire thy words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and on thy words he will lay a stumblingblock.
verses.textLatin: In conspectu oculorum tuorum condulcabit os suum, et super sermones tuos admirabitur: novissime autem pervertet os suum, et in verbis tuis dabit scandalum.

verses.text: I have hated many things but not like him, and the Lord will hate him.
verses.textLatin: Multa odivi, et non coæquavi ei, et Dominus odiet illum.

verses.text: If one cast a stone on high, it will fall upon his own head: and the deceitful stroke will wound the deceitful.
verses.textLatin: Qui in altum mittit lapidem, super caput ejus cadet: et plaga dolosa dolosi dividet vulnera.

verses.text: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that setteth a stone for his neighbour, shall stumble upon it: and he that layeth a snare for another, shall perish in it.
verses.textLatin: Et qui foveam fodit incidet in eam: et qui statuit lapidem proximo offendet in eo: et qui laqueum alii ponit, peribit in illo.

verses.text: A mischievous counsel shall be rolled back upon the author, and he shall not know from whence it cometh to him.
verses.textLatin: Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non agnoscet unde adveniat illi.

verses.text: Mockery and reproach are of the proud, and vengeance as a lion shall lie in wait for him.
verses.textLatin: Illusio et improperium superborum, et vindicta sicut leo insidiabitur illi.

verses.text: They shall perish in a snare that are delighted with the fall of the just: and sorrow shall consume them before they die.
verses.textLatin: Laqueo peribunt qui oblectantur casu justorum, dolor autem consumet illos antequam moriantur.

verses.text: Anger and fury are both of them abominable, and the sinful man shall be subject to them.
verses.textLatin: Ira et furor utraque execrabilia sunt, et vir peccator continens erit illorum.

verses.text: He  that seeketh to revenge himself, shall find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
verses.textLatin: Qui vindicari vult, a Domino inveniet vindictam, et peccata illius servans servabit.

verses.text: Forgive thy neighbour if he hath hurt thee: and then shall thy sins be forgiven to thee when thou prayest.
verses.textLatin: Relinque proximo tuo nocenti te, et tunc deprecanti tibi peccata solventur.

verses.text: Man to man reserveth anger, and doth he seek remedy of God?
verses.textLatin: Homo homini reservat iram, et a Deo quærit medelam:

verses.text: He hath no mercy on a man like himself, and doth he entreat for his own sins?
verses.textLatin: in hominem similem sibi non habet misericordiam, et de peccatis suis deprecatur.

verses.text: He that is but flesh, nourisheth anger, and doth he ask forgiveness of God? who shall obtain pardon for his sins?
verses.textLatin: Ipse cum caro sit reservat iram, et propitiationem petit a Deo: quis exorabit pro delictis illius?

verses.text: Remember thy last things, and let enmity cease:
verses.textLatin: Memento novissimorum, et desine inimicari:

verses.text: For corruption and death hang over in his commandments.
verses.textLatin: tabitudo enim et mors imminent in mandatis ejus.

verses.text: Remember the fear of God, and be not angry with thy neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Memorare timorem Dei, et non irascaris proximo.

verses.text: Remember the covenant of the most High, and overlook the ignorance of thy neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Memorare testamentum Altissimi, et despice ignorantiam proximi.

verses.text: Refrain from strife, and thou shalt diminish thy sins.
verses.textLatin: Abstine te a lite, et minues peccata.

verses.text: For a passionate man kindleth strife, and a sinful man will trouble his friends, and bring in debate in the midst of them that are at peace.
verses.textLatin: Homo enim iracundus incendit litem, et vir peccator turbabit amicos, et in medio pacem habentium immittet inimicitiam.

verses.text: For as the wood of the forest is, so the fire burneth, and as a man’s strength is, so shall his anger be, and according to his riches he shall increase his anger.
verses.textLatin: Secundum enim ligna silvæ sic ignis exardescit: et secundum virtutem hominis sic iracundia illius erit, et secundum substantiam suam exaltabit iram suam.

verses.text: A hasty contention kindleth a fire: and a hasty quarrel sheddeth blood: and a tongue that beareth witness bringeth death.
verses.textLatin: Certamen festinatum incendit ignem, et lis festinans effundit sanguinem: et lingua testificans adducit mortem.

verses.text: If thou blow the spark, it shall burn as a fire: and if thou spit upon it, it shall be quenched: both come out of the mouth.
verses.textLatin: Si sufflaveris in scintillam, quasi ignis exardebit: et si exspueris super illam, extinguetur: utraque ex ore proficiscuntur.

verses.text: The whisperer and the double tongue is accursed: for he hath troubled many that were at peace.
verses.textLatin: Susurro et bilinguis maledictus, multos enim turbabit pacem habentes.

verses.text: The tongue of a third person hath disquieted many, and scattered them from nation to nation.
verses.textLatin: Lingua tertia multos commovit, et dispersit illos de gente in gentem.

verses.text: It hath destroyed the strong cities of the rich, and hath overthrown the houses of great men.
verses.textLatin: Civitates muratas divitum destruxit, et domus magnatorum effodit.

verses.text: It hath cut in pieces the forces of people, and undone strong nations.
verses.textLatin: Virtutes populorum concidit, et gentes fortes dissolvit.

verses.text: The tongue of a third person hath cast out valiant women, and deprived them of their labours.
verses.textLatin: Lingua tertia mulieres viratas ejecit, et privavit illas laboribus suis.

verses.text: He that hearkeneth to it, shall never have rest, neither shall he have a friend in whom he may repose.
verses.textLatin: Qui respicit illam non habebit requiem, nec habebit amicum in quo requiescat.

verses.text: The stroke of a whip maketh a blue mark: but the stroke of the tongue will break the bones.
verses.textLatin: Flagelli plaga livorem facit: plaga autem linguæ comminuet ossa.

verses.text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as have perished by their own tongue.
verses.textLatin: Multi ceciderunt in ore gladii: sed non sic quasi qui interierunt per linguam suam.

verses.text: Blessed is he that is defended from a wicked tongue, that hath not passed into the wrath thereof, and that hath not drawn the yoke thereof, and hath not been bound in its bands.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui tectus est a lingua nequam, qui in iracundiam illius non transivit, et qui non attraxit jugum illius, et in vinculis ejus non est ligatus:

verses.text: For its yoke is a yoke of iron: and its bands are bands of brass.
verses.textLatin: jugum enim illius jugum ferreum est, et vinculum illius vinculum æreum est;

verses.text: The death thereof is a most evil death: and hell is preferable to it.
verses.textLatin: mors illius mors nequissima: et utilis potius infernus quam illa.

verses.text: Its continuance shall not be for a long time, but it shall possess the ways of the unjust: and the just shall not be burnt with its flame.
verses.textLatin: Perseverantia illius non permanebit, sed obtinebit vias injustorum, et in flamma sua non comburet justos.

verses.text: They that forsake God shall fall into it, and it shall burn in them, and shall not be quenched, and it shall be sent upon them as a lion, and as a leopard it shall tear them.
verses.textLatin: Qui relinquunt Deum incident in illam, et exardebit in illis, et non extinguetur, et immittetur in illos quasi leo, et quasi pardus lædet illos.

verses.text: Hedge in thy ears with thorns, hear not a wicked tongue, and make doors and bars to thy mouth.
verses.textLatin: Sepi aures tuas spinis: linguam nequam noli audire: et ori tuo facito ostia et seras.

verses.text: Melt down thy gold and silver, and make a balance for thy words, and a just bridle for thy mouth:
verses.textLatin: Aurum tuum et argentum tuum confla, et verbis tuis facito stateram, et frenos ori tuo rectos:

verses.text: And take heed lest thou slip with thy tongue, and fall in the sight of thy enemies who lie in wait for thee, and thy fall be incurable unto death.
verses.textLatin: et attende ne forte labaris in lingua, et cadas in conspectu inimicorum insidiantium tibi, et sit casus tuus insanabilis in mortem.

verses.text: He  that sheweth mercy, lendeth to his neighbour: and he that is stronger in hand, keepeth the commandments.
verses.textLatin: Qui facit misericordiam fœneratur proximo suo: et qui prævalet manu mandata servat.

verses.text: Lend to thy neighbour in the time of his need, and pay thou thy neighbour again in due time.
verses.textLatin: Fœnerare proximo tuo in tempore necessitatis illius: et iterum redde proximo in tempore suo.

verses.text: Keep thy word, and deal faithfully with him: and thou shalt always find that which is necessary for thee.
verses.textLatin: Confirma verbum, et fideliter age cum illo: et in omni tempore invenies quod tibi necessarium est.

verses.text: Many have looked upon a thing lent as a thing found, and have given trouble to them that helped them.
verses.textLatin: Multi quasi inventionem æstimaverunt fœnus, et præstiterunt molestiam his qui se adjuverunt.

verses.text: Till they receive, they kiss the hands of the lender, and in promises they humble their voice:
verses.textLatin: Donec accipiant, osculantur manus dantis, et in promissionibus humiliant vocem suam:

verses.text: But when they should repay, they will ask time, and will return tedious and murmuring words, and will complain of the time:
verses.textLatin: et in tempore redditionis postulabit tempus, et loquetur verba tædii et murmurationum, et tempus causabitur.

verses.text: And if he be able to pay, he will stand off, he will scarce pay one half, and will count it as if he had found it:
verses.textLatin: Si autem potuerit reddere, adversabitur: solidi vix reddet dimidium, et computabit illud quasi inventionem:

verses.text: But if not, he will defraud him of his money, and he shall get him for an enemy without cause.
verses.textLatin: sin autem, fraudabit illum pecunia sua, et possidebit illum inimicum gratis:

verses.text: And he will pay him with reproaches and curses, and instead of honour and good turn will repay him injuries.
verses.textLatin: et convitia et maledicta reddet illi, et pro honore et beneficio reddet illi contumeliam.

verses.text: Many have refused to lend, not out of wickedness, but they were afraid to be defrauded without cause.
verses.textLatin: Multi non causa nequitiæ non fœnerati sunt, sed fraudari gratis timuerunt.

verses.text: But yet towards the poor be thou more hearty, and delay not to shew him mercy.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen super humilem animo fortior esto, et pro eleemosyna non trahas illum.

verses.text: Help the poor because of the commandment: and send him not away empty handed because of his poverty.
verses.textLatin: Propter mandatum assume pauperem, et propter inopiam ejus ne dimittas eum vacuum.

verses.text: Lose thy money for thy brother and thy friend: and hide it not under a stone to be lost.
verses.textLatin: Perde pecuniam propter fratrem et amicum tuum, et non abscondas illam sub lapide in perditionem.

verses.text: Place thy treasure in the commandments of the most High, and it shall bring thee more profit than gold.
verses.textLatin: Pone thesaurum tuum in præceptis Altissimi, et proderit tibi magis quam aurum.

verses.text: Shut up alms in the heart of the poor, and it shall obtain help for thee against all evil.
verses.textLatin: Conclude eleemosynam in corde pauperis, et hæc pro te exorabit ab omni malo.

verses.text: Better than the shield of the mighty, and better than the spear:
verses.textLatin: 17 18 Super scutum potentis et super lanceam adversus inimicum tuum pugnabit.

verses.text: A good man is surety for his neighbour: and he that hath lost shame, will leave him to himself.
verses.textLatin: Vir bonus fidem facit pro proximo suo: et qui perdiderit confusionem derelinquet sibi.

verses.text: Forget not the kindness of thy surety: for he hath given his life for thee.
verses.textLatin: Gratiam fidejussoris ne obliviscaris: dedit enim pro te animam suam.

verses.text: The sinner and the unclean fleeth from his surety.
verses.textLatin: Repromissorem fugit peccator et immundus.

verses.text: A sinner attributeth to himself the goods of his surety: and he that is of an unthankful mind will leave him that delivered him.
verses.textLatin: Bona repromissoris sibi ascribit peccator: et ingratus sensu derelinquet liberantem se.

verses.text: A man is surety for his neighbour: and when he hath lost all shame, he shall forsake him.
verses.textLatin: Vir repromittit de proximo suo: et cum perdiderit reverentiam, derelinquetur ab eo.

verses.text: Evil suretyship hath undone many of good estate, and hath tossed them as a wave of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Repromissio nequissima multos perdidit dirigentes, et commovit illos quasi fluctus maris.

verses.text: It hath made powerful men to go from place to place round about, and they have wandered in strange countries.
verses.textLatin: Viros potentes gyrans migrare fecit, et vagati sunt in gentibus alienis.

verses.text: A sinner that transgresseth the commandment of the Lord, shall fall into an evil suretyship: and he that undertaketh many things, shall fall into judgment.
verses.textLatin: Peccator transgrediens mandatum Domini incidet in promissionem nequam: et qui conatur multa agere incidet in judicium.

verses.text: Recover thy neighbour according to thy power, and take heed to thyself that thou fall not.
verses.textLatin: Recupera proximum secundum virtutem tuam, et attende tibi ne incidas.

verses.text: The chief thing for man’s life is water and bread, and clothing, and a house to cover shame.
verses.textLatin: Initium vitæ hominis, aqua et panis, et vestimentum, et domus protegens turpitudinem.

verses.text: Better is the poor man’s fare under a roof of boards, than sumptuous cheer abroad in another man’s house.
verses.textLatin: Melior est victus pauperis sub tegmine asserum quam epulæ splendidæ in peregre sine domicilio.

verses.text: Be contented with little instead of much, and thou shalt not hear the reproach of going abroad.
verses.textLatin: Minimum pro magno placeat tibi, et improperium peregrinationis non audies.

verses.text: It is a miserable life to go as a guest from house to house: for where a man is a stranger, he shall not deal confidently, nor open his mouth.
verses.textLatin: Vita nequam hospitandi de domo in domum: et ubi hospitabitur non fiducialiter aget, nec aperiet os.

verses.text: He shall entertain and feed, and give drink to the unthankful, and moreover he shall hear bitter words.
verses.textLatin: Hospitabitur, et pascet, et potabit ingratos, et ad hæc amara audiet:

verses.text: Go, stranger, and furnish the table, and give others to eat what thou hast in thy hand.
verses.textLatin: transi, hospes, et orna mensam, et quæ in manu habes ciba ceteros.

verses.text: Give place to the honourable presence of my friends: for I want my house, my brother being to be lodged with me.
verses.textLatin: Exi a facie honoris amicorum meorum: necessitudine domus meæ hospitio mihi factus est frater.

verses.text: These things are grievous to a man of understanding: the upbraiding of houseroom, and the reproaching of the lender.
verses.textLatin: Gravia hæc homini habenti sensum: correptio domus, et improperium fœneratoris.

verses.text: He  that loveth his son, frequently chastiseth him, that he may rejoice in his latter end, and not grope after the doors of his neighbours.
verses.textLatin: Qui diligit filium suum assiduat illi flagella, ut lætetur in novissimo suo, et non palpet proximorum ostia.

verses.text: He that instructeth his son shall be praised in him, and shall glory in him in the midst of them of his household.
verses.textLatin: Qui docet filium suum laudabitur in illo, et in medio domesticorum in illo gloriabitur.

verses.text: He that teacheth his son, maketh his enemy jealous, and in the midst of his friends he shall glory in him.
verses.textLatin: Qui docet filium suum in zelum mittit inimicum, et in medio amicorum gloriabitur in illo.

verses.text: His father is dead, and he is as if he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself.
verses.textLatin: Mortuus est pater ejus, et quasi non est mortuus: similem enim reliquit sibi post se.

verses.text: While he lived he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died he was not sorrowful, neither was he confounded before his enemies.
verses.textLatin: In vita sua vidit, et lætatus est in illo: in obitu suo non est contristatus, nec confusus est coram inimicis:

verses.text: For he left behind him a defender of his house against his enemies, and one that will requite kindness to his friends.
verses.textLatin: reliquit enim defensorem domus contra inimicos, et amicis reddentem gratiam.

verses.text: For the souls of his sons he shall bind up his wounds, and at every cry his bowels shall be troubled.
verses.textLatin: Pro animabus filiorum colligabit vulnera sua, et super omnem vocem turbabuntur viscera ejus.

verses.text: A horse not broken becometh stubborn, and a child left to himself will become headstrong.
verses.textLatin: Equus indomitus evadit durus, et filius remissus evadet præceps.

verses.text: Give thy son his way, and he shall make thee afraid: play with him, and he shall make thee sorrowful.
verses.textLatin: Lacta filium, et paventem te faciet: lude cum eo, et contristabit te.

verses.text: Laugh not with him, lest thou have sorrow, and at the last thy teeth be set on edge.
verses.textLatin: Non corrideas illi, ne doleas, et in novissimo obstupescent dentes tui.

verses.text: Give him not liberty in his youth, and wink not at his devices.
verses.textLatin: Non des illi potestatem in juventute, et ne despicias cogitatus illius.

verses.text: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat his sides while he is a child, lest he grow stubborn, and regard thee not, and so be a sorrow of heart to thee.
verses.textLatin: Curva cervicem ejus in juventute, et tunde latera ejus dum infans est, ne forte induret, et non credat tibi, et erit tibi dolor animæ.

verses.text: Instruct thy son, and labour about him, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence to thee.
verses.textLatin: Doce filium tuum, et operare in illo, ne in turpitudinem illius offendas.

verses.text: Better is a poor man who is sound, and strong of constitution, than a rich man who is weak and afflicted with evils.
verses.textLatin: Melior est pauper sanus, et fortis viribus, quam dives imbecillis et flagellatus malitia.

verses.text: Health of the soul in holiness of justice, is better than all gold and silver: and a sound body, than immense revenues.
verses.textLatin: Salus animæ in sanctitate justitiæ melior est omni auro et argento: et corpus validum quam census immensus.

verses.text: There is no riches above the riches of the health of the body: and there is no pleasure above the joy of the heart.
verses.textLatin: Non est census super censum salutis corporis, et non est oblectamentum super cordis gaudium.

verses.text: Better is death than a bitter life: and everlasting rest, than continual sickness.
verses.textLatin: Melior est mors quam vita amara, et requies æterna quam languor perseverans.

verses.text: Good things that are hidden in a mouth that is shut, are as messes of meat set about a grave.
verses.textLatin: Bona abscondita in ore clauso, quasi appositiones epularum circumpositæ sepulchro.

verses.text: What good shall an offering do to an idol? for it can neither eat, nor smell:
verses.textLatin: Quid proderit libatio idolo? nec enim manducabit, nec odorabit.

verses.text: So is he that is persecuted by the Lord, bearing the reward of his iniquity:
verses.textLatin: Sic qui effugatur a Domino, portans mercedes iniquitatis:

verses.text: He seeth with his eyes, and groaneth, as an eunuch embracing a virgin, and sighing.
verses.textLatin: videns oculis et ingemiscens, sicut spado complectens virginem, et suspirans.

verses.text: Give not up thy soul to sadness, and afflict not thyself in thy own counsel.
verses.textLatin: Tristitiam non des animæ tuæ, et non affligas temetipsum in consilio tuo.

verses.text: The joyfulness of the heart, is the life of a man, and a never failing treasure of holiness: and the joy of a man is length of life.
verses.textLatin: Jucunditas cordis, hæc est vita hominis, et thesaurus sine defectione sanctitatis: et exsultatio viri est longævitas.

verses.text: Have pity on thy own soul, pleasing God, and contain thyself: gather up thy heart in his holiness: and drive away sadness far from thee.
verses.textLatin: Miserere animæ tuæ placens Deo, et contine: congrega cor tuum in sanctitate ejus, et tristitiam longe repelle a te.

verses.text: For sadness hath killed many, and there is no profit in it.
verses.textLatin: Multos enim occidit tristitia, et non est utilitas in illa.

verses.text: Envy and anger shorten a man’s days, and pensiveness will bring old age before the time.
verses.textLatin: Zelus et iracundia minuunt dies, et ante tempus senectam adducet cogitatus.

verses.text: A cheerful and good heart is always feasting: for his banquets are prepared with diligence.
verses.textLatin: Splendidum cor et bonum in epulis est: epulæ enim illius diligenter fiunt.

verses.text: Watching  for riches consumeth the flesh, and the thought thereof driveth away sleep.
verses.textLatin: Vigilia honestatis tabefaciet carnes, et cogitatus illius auferet somnum.

verses.text: The thinking beforehand turneth away the understanding, and a grievous sickness maketh the soul sober.
verses.textLatin: Cogitatus præscientiæ avertit sensum, et infirmitas gravis sobriam facit animam.

verses.text: The rich man hath laboured in gathering riches together, and when he resteth he shall be filled with his goods.
verses.textLatin: Laboravit dives in congregatione substantiæ, et in requie sua replebitur bonis suis.

verses.text: The poor man hath laboured in his low way of life, and in the end he is still poor.
verses.textLatin: Laboravit pauper in diminutione victus, et in fine inops fit.

verses.text: He that loveth gold, shall not be justified: and he that followeth after corruption, shall be filled with it.
verses.textLatin: Qui aurum diligit non justificabitur, et qui insequitur consumptionem replebitur ex ea.

verses.text: Many have been brought to fall for gold, and the beauty thereof hath been their ruin.
verses.textLatin: Multi dati sunt in auri casus, et facta est in specie ipsius perditio illorum.

verses.text: Gold is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it: woe to them that eagerly follow after it, and every fool shall perish by it.
verses.textLatin: Lignum offensionis est aurum sacrificantium: væ illis qui sectantur illud! et omnis imprudens deperiet in illo.

verses.text: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures.
verses.textLatin: Beatus dives qui inventus est sine macula, et qui post aurum non abiit, nec speravit in pecunia et thesauris.

verses.text: Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.
verses.textLatin: Quis est hic? et laudabimus eum: fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua.

verses.text: Who hath been tried thereby, and made perfect, he shall have glory everlasting. He that could have transgressed, and hath not transgressed: and could do evil things, and hath not done them:
verses.textLatin: Qui probatus est in illo, et perfectus est, erit illi gloria æterna: qui potuit transgredi, et non est transgressus; facere mala, et non fecit.

verses.text: Therefore are his goods established in the Lord, and all the church of the saints shall declare his alms.
verses.textLatin: Ideo stabilita sunt bona illius in Domino, et eleemosynas illius enarrabit omnis ecclesia sanctorum.

verses.text: Art thou set at a great table? be not the first to open thy mouth upon it.
verses.textLatin: Supra mensam magnam sedisti? non aperias super illam faucem tuam prior.

verses.text: Say not: There are many things which are upon it.
verses.textLatin: Non dicas sic: Multa sunt, quæ super illam sunt.

verses.text: Remember that a wicked eye is evil.
verses.textLatin: Memento quoniam malus est oculus nequam.

verses.text: What is created more wicked than an eye? therefore shall it weep over all the face when it shall see.
verses.textLatin: Nequius oculo quid creatum est? ideo ab omni facie sua lacrimabitur, cum viderit.

verses.text: Stretch not out thy hand first, lest being disgraced with envy thou be put to confusion.
verses.textLatin: Ne extendas manum tuam prior, et invidia contaminatus erubescas.

verses.text: Be not hasty in a feast.
verses.textLatin: Ne comprimaris in convivio.

verses.text: Judge of the disposition of thy neighbour by thyself.
verses.textLatin: Intellige quæ sunt proximi tui ex teipso.

verses.text: Use as a frugal man the things that are set before thee: lest if thou eatest much, thou be hated.
verses.textLatin: Utere quasi homo frugi his quæ tibi apponuntur: ne, cum manducas multum, odio habearis.

verses.text: Leave off first, for manners’ sake: and exceed not, lest thou offend.
verses.textLatin: Cessa prior causa disciplinæ: et noli nimius esse, ne forte offendas.

verses.text: And if thou sittest among many, reach not thy hand out first of all: and be not the first to ask for drink.
verses.textLatin: Et si in medio multorum sedisti, prior illis ne extendas manum tuam, nec prior poscas bibere.

verses.text: How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught, and in sleeping thou shalt not be uneasy with it, and thou shalt feel no pain.
verses.textLatin: Quam sufficiens est homini erudito vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, et non senties dolorem.

verses.text: Watching, and choler, and gripes, are with an intemperate man:
verses.textLatin: Vigilia, cholera et tortura viro infrunito,

verses.text: Sound and wholesome sleep with a moderate man: he shall sleep till morning, and his soul shall be delighted with him.
verses.textLatin: somnus sanitatis in homine parco: dormiet usque mane, et anima illius cum ipso delectabitur.

verses.text: And if thou hast been forced to eat much, arise, go out, and vomit: and it shall refresh thee, and thou shalt not bring sickness upon thy body.
verses.textLatin: Et si coactus fueris in edendo multum, surge e medio, evome, et refrigerabit te, et non adduces corpori tuo infirmitatem.

verses.text: Hear me, my son, and despise me not: and in the end thou shalt find my words.
verses.textLatin: Audi me, fili, et ne spernas me, et in novissimo invenies verba mea.

verses.text: In all thy works be quick, and no infirmity shall come to thee.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus operibus tuis esto velox, et omnis infirmitas non occurret tibi.

verses.text: The lips of many shall bless him that is liberal of his bread, and the testimony of his truth is faithful.
verses.textLatin: Splendidum in panibus benedicent labia multorum, et testimonium veritatis illius fidele.

verses.text: Against him that is niggardly of his bread, the city will murmur, and the testimony of his niggardliness is true.
verses.textLatin: Nequissimo in pane murmurabit civitas, et testimonium nequitiæ illius verum est.

verses.text: Challenge not them that love wine: for wine hath destroyed very many.
verses.textLatin: Diligentes in vino noli provocare: multos enim exterminavit vinum.

verses.text: Fire trieth hard iron: so wine drunk to excess shall rebuke the hearts of the proud.
verses.textLatin: Ignis probat ferrum durum: sic vinum corda superborum arguet in ebrietate potatum.

verses.text: Wine taken with sobriety is equal life to men: if thou drink it moderately, thou shalt be sober.
verses.textLatin: Æqua vita hominibus vinum in sobrietate: si bibas illud moderate, eris sobrius.

verses.text: What is his life, who is diminished with wine?
verses.textLatin: Quæ vita est ei qui minuitur vino?

verses.text: What taketh away life? death.
verses.textLatin: Quid defraudat vitam? mors.

verses.text: Wine was created from the beginning to make men joyful, and not to make them drunk.
verses.textLatin: Vinum in jucunditatem creatum est, et non in ebrietatem ab initio.

verses.text: Wine drunken with moderation is the joy of the soul and the heart.
verses.textLatin: Exsultatio animæ et cordis vinum moderate potatum.

verses.text: Sober drinking is health to soul and body.
verses.textLatin: Sanitas est animæ et corpori sobrius potus.

verses.text: Wine drunken with excess raiseth quarrels, and wrath, and many ruins.
verses.textLatin: Vinum multum potatum irritationem, et iram, et ruinas multas facit.

verses.text: Wine drunken with excess is bitterness of the soul.
verses.textLatin: Amaritudo animæ vinum multum potatum.

verses.text: The heat of drunkenness is the stumblingblock of the fool, lessening strength and causing wounds.
verses.textLatin: Ebrietatis animositas, imprudentis offensio, minorans virtutem, et faciens vulnera.

verses.text: Rebuke not thy neighbour in a banquet of wine: and despise him not in his mirth.
verses.textLatin: In convivio vini non arguas proximum, et non despicias eum in jucunditate illius.

verses.text: Speak not to him words of reproach: and press him not in demanding again.
verses.textLatin: Verba improperii non dicas illi, et non premas illum repetendo.

verses.text: Have  they made thee ruler? be not lifted up: be among them as one of them.
verses.textLatin: Rectorem te posuerunt? noli extolli: esto in illis quasi unus ex ipsis.

verses.text: Have care of them, and so sit down, and when thou hast acquitted thyself of all thy charge, take thy place:
verses.textLatin: Curam illorum habe, et sic conside, et omni cura tua explicita recumbe:

verses.text: That thou mayst rejoice for them, and receive a crown as an ornament of grace, and get the honour of the contribution.
verses.textLatin: ut læteris propter illos, et ornamentum gratiæ accipias coronam, et dignationem consequaris corrogationis.

verses.text: Speak, thou that art elder: for it becometh thee,
verses.textLatin: Loquere major natu: decet enim te

verses.text: To speak the first word with careful knowledge, and hinder not music.
verses.textLatin: primum verbum diligenti scientia, et non impedias musicam.

verses.text: Where there is no hearing, pour not out words, and be not lifted up out of season with thy wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Ubi auditus non est, non effundas sermonem, et importune noli extolli in sapientia tua.

verses.text: A concert of music in a banquet of wine is as a carbuncle set in gold.
verses.textLatin: Gemmula carbunculi in ornamento auri, et comparatio musicorum in convivio vini.

verses.text: As a signet of an emerald in a work of gold: so is the melody of music with pleasant and moderate wine.
verses.textLatin: Sicut in fabricatione auri signum est smaragdi, sic numerus musicorum in jucundo et moderato vino.

verses.text: Hear in silence, and for thy reverence good grace shall come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Audi tacens, et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.

verses.text: Young man, scarcely speak in thy own cause.
verses.textLatin: Adolescens, loquere in tua causa vix.

verses.text: If thou be asked twice, let thy answer be short.
verses.textLatin: Si bis interrogatus fueris, habeat caput responsum tuum.

verses.text: In many things be as if thou wert ignorant, and hear in silence and withal seeking.
verses.textLatin: In multis esto quasi inscius, et audi tacens simul et quærens.

verses.text: In the company of great men take not upon thee: and when the ancients are present, speak not much.
verses.textLatin: In medio magnatorum non præsumas: et ubi sunt senes non multum loquaris.

verses.text: Before a storm goeth lightning: and before shamefacedness goeth favour: and for thy reverence good grace shall come to thee.
verses.textLatin: Ante grandinem præibit coruscatio: et ante verecundiam præibit gratia, et pro reverentia accedet tibi bona gratia.

verses.text: And at the time of rising be not slack: but be first to run home to thy house, and there withdraw thyself, and there take thy pastime.
verses.textLatin: Et hora surgendi non te trices: præcurre autem prior in domum tuam, et illic avocare, et illic lude,

verses.text: And do what thou hast a mind, but not in sin or proud speech.
verses.textLatin: et age conceptiones tuas, et non in delictis et verbo superbo:

verses.text: And for all these things bless the Lord, that made thee, and that replenisheth thee with all his good things.
verses.textLatin: et super his omnibus benedicito Dominum, qui fecit, et inebriantem te ab omnibus bonis suis.

verses.text: He that feareth the Lord, will receive his discipline: and they that will seek him early, shall find a blessing.
verses.textLatin: Qui timet Dominum excipiet doctrinam ejus: et qui vigilaverint ad illum invenient benedictionem.

verses.text: He that seeketh the law, shall be filled with it: and he that dealeth deceitfully, shall meet with a stumblingblock therein.
verses.textLatin: Qui quærit legem replebitur ab ea, et qui insidiose agit scandalizabitur in ea.

verses.text: They that fear the Lord, shall find just judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
verses.textLatin: Qui timent Dominum invenient judicium justum, et justitias quasi lumen accendent.

verses.text: A sinful man will flee reproof, and will find an excuse according to his will.
verses.textLatin: Peccator homo vitabit correptionem, et secundum voluntatem suam inveniet comparationem.

verses.text: A man of counsel will not neglect understanding, a strange and proud man will not dread fear:
verses.textLatin: Vir consilii non disperdet intelligentiam: alienus et superbus non pertimescet timorem:

verses.text: Even after he hath done with fear without counsel, he shall be controlled by the things of his own seeking.
verses.textLatin: etiam postquam fecit cum eo sine consilio, et suis insectationibus arguetur.

verses.text: My son, do thou nothing without counsel, and thou shalt not repent when thou hast done.
verses.textLatin: Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis.

verses.text: Go not in the way of ruin, and thou shalt not stumble against the stones: trust not thyself to a rugged way, lest thou set a stumblingblock to thy soul.
verses.textLatin: In via ruinæ non eas, et non offendes in lapides: nec credas te viæ laboriosæ, ne ponas animæ tuæ scandalum.

verses.text: And beware of thy own children, and take heed of them of thy household.
verses.textLatin: Et a filiis tuis cave, et a domesticis tuis attende.

verses.text: In every work of thine regard thy soul in faith: for this is the keeping of the commandments.
verses.textLatin: In omni opere tuo crede ex fide animæ tuæ, hoc est enim conservatio mandatorum.

verses.text: He that believeth God, taketh heed to the commandments: and he that trusteth in him, shall fare never the worse.
verses.textLatin: Qui credit Deo attendit mandatis: et qui confidit in illo non minorabitur.

verses.text: No  evils shall happen to him that feareth the Lord, but in temptation God will keep him, and deliver him from evils.
verses.textLatin: Timenti Dominum non occurrent mala: sed in tentatione Deus illum conservabit, et liberabit a malis. Sapiens non odit mandata et justitias,

verses.text: A wise man hateth not the commandments and justices, and he shall not be dashed in pieces as a ship in a storm.
verses.textLatin: et non illidetur quasi in procella navis.

verses.text: A man of understanding is faithful to the law of God, and the law is faithful to him.
verses.textLatin: Homo sensatus credit legi Dei, et lex illi fidelis.

verses.text: He that cleareth up a question, shall prepare what to say, and so having prayed he shall be heard, and shall keep discipline, and then he shall answer.
verses.textLatin: Qui interrogationem manifestat parabit verbum, et sic deprecatus exaudietur: et conservabit disciplinam, et tunc respondebit.

verses.text: The heart of a fool is as a wheel of a cart: and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.
verses.textLatin: Præcordia fatui quasi rota carri, et quasi axis versatilis cogitatus illius.

verses.text: A friend that is a mocker, is like a stallion horse: he neigheth under every one that sitteth upon him.
verses.textLatin: Equus emissarius, sic et amicus subsannator: sub omni supra sedente hinnit.

verses.text: Why doth one day excel another, and one light another, and one year another year, when all come of the sun?
verses.textLatin: Quare dies diem superat, et iterum lux lucem, et annus annum a sole?

verses.text: By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished, the sun being made, and keeping his commandment.
verses.textLatin: A Domini scientia separati sunt, facto sole, et præceptum custodiente.

verses.text: And he ordered the seasons, and holidays of them, and in them they celebrated festivals at an hour.
verses.textLatin: Et immutavit tempora, et dies festos ipsorum, et in illis dies festos celebraverunt ad horam.

verses.text: Some of them God made high and great days, and some of them he put in the number of ordinary days. And all men are from the ground, and out of the earth, from whence Adam was created.
verses.textLatin: Ex ipsis exaltavit et magnificavit Deus, et ex ipsis posuit in numerum dierum: et omnes homines de solo et ex terra unde creatus est Adam.

verses.text: With much knowledge the Lord hath divided them and diversified their ways.
verses.textLatin: In multitudine disciplinæ Dominus separavit eos, et immutavit vias eorum.

verses.text: Some of them hath he blessed, and exalted: and some of them hath he sanctified, and set near himself: and some of them hath he cursed and brought low, and turned them from their station.
verses.textLatin: Ex ipsis benedixit et exaltavit, et ex ipsis sanctificavit, et ad se applicavit, et ex ipsis maledixit, et humiliavit, et convertit illos a separatione ipsorum.

verses.text: As the potter’s clay is in his hand, to fashion and order it:
verses.textLatin: Quasi lutum figuli in manu ipsius, plasmare illud et disponere.

verses.text: All his ways are according to his ordering: so man is in the hand of him that made him, and he will render to him according to his judgment.
verses.textLatin: Omnes viæ ejus secundum dispositionem ejus: sic homo in manu illius qui se fecit, et reddet illi secundum judicium suum.

verses.text: Good is set against evil, and life against death: so also is the sinner against a just man. And so look upon all the works of the most High. Two and two, and one against another.
verses.textLatin: Contra malum bonum est, et contra mortem vita: sic et contra virum justum peccator, et sic intuere in omnia opera Altissimi, duo et duo, et unum contra unum.

verses.text: And I awaked last of all, and as one that gathereth after the grapegatherers.
verses.textLatin: Et ego novissimus evigilavi, et quasi qui colligit acinos post vindemiatores.

verses.text: In the blessing of God I also have hoped: and as one that gathereth grapes, have I filled the winepress.
verses.textLatin: In benedictione Dei et ipse speravi, et quasi qui vindemiat replevi torcular.

verses.text: See that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all that seek discipline.
verses.textLatin: Respicite quoniam non mihi soli laboravi, sed omnibus exquirentibus disciplinam.

verses.text: Hear me, ye great men, and all ye people, and hearken with your ears, ye rulers of the church.
verses.textLatin: Audite me, magnates et omnes populi: et rectores ecclesiæ, auribus percipite.

verses.text: Give not to son or wife, brother or friend, power over thee while thou livest; and give not thy estate to another, lest thou repent, and thou entreat for the same.
verses.textLatin: Filio et mulieri, fratri et amico, non des potestatem super te in vita tua: et non dederis alii possessionem tuam, ne forte pœniteat te, et depreceris pro illis.

verses.text: As long as thou livest, and hast breath in thee, let no man change thee.
verses.textLatin: Dum adhuc superes et aspiras, non immutabit te omnis caro.

verses.text: For it is better that thy children should ask of thee, than that thou look toward the hands of thy children.
verses.textLatin: Melius est enim ut filii tui te rogent, quam te respicere in manus filiorum tuorum.

verses.text: In all thy works keep the pre-eminence.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus operibus tuis præcellens esto.

verses.text: Let no stain sully thy glory. In the time when thou shalt end the days of thy life, and in the time of thy decease, distribute thy inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Ne dederis maculam in gloria tua. In die consummationis dierum vitæ tuæ, et in tempore exitus tui, distribue hæreditatem tuam.

verses.text: Fodder, and a wand, and a burden are for an ass: bread, and correction, and work for a slave.
verses.textLatin: Cibaria, et virga, et onus asino: panis, et disciplina, et opus servo.

verses.text: He worketh under correction, and seeketh to rest: let his hands be idle, and he seeketh liberty.
verses.textLatin: Operatur in disciplina, et quærit requiescere: laxa manus illi, et quærit libertatem.

verses.text: The yoke and the thong bend a stiff neck, and continual labours bow a slave.
verses.textLatin: Jugum et lorum curvant collum durum, et servum inclinant operationes assiduæ.

verses.text: Torture and fetters are for a malicious slave: send him to work, that he be not idle:
verses.textLatin: Servo malevolo tortura et compedes: mitte illum in operationem, ne vacet:

verses.text: For idleness hath taught much evil.
verses.textLatin: multam enim malitiam docuit otiositas.

verses.text: Set him to work: for so it is fit for him. And if he be not obedient, bring him down with fetters, but be not excessive towards any one: and do no grievous thing without judgment.
verses.textLatin: In opera constitue eum: sic enim condecet illum. Quod si non obaudierit, curva illum compedibus, et non amplifices super omnem carnem: verum sine judicio nihil facias grave.

verses.text: If thou have a faithful servant, let him be to thee as thy own soul: treat him as a brother: because in the blood of thy soul thou hast gotten him.
verses.textLatin: Si est tibi servus fidelis, sit tibi quasi anima tua: quasi fratrem sic eum tracta, quoniam in sanguine animæ comparasti illum.

verses.text: If thou hurt him unjustly, he will run away:
verses.textLatin: Si læseris eum injuste, in fugam convertetur:

verses.text: And if he rise up and depart, thou knowest not whom to ask, and in what way to seek him.
verses.textLatin: et si extollens discesserit, quem quæras et in qua via quæras illum nescis.

verses.text: The  hopes of a man that is void of understanding are vain and deceitful: and dreams lift up fools.
verses.textLatin: Vana spes et mendacium viro insensato: et somnia extollunt imprudentes.

verses.text: The man that giveth heed to lying visions, is like to him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.
verses.textLatin: Quasi qui apprehendit umbram et persequitur ventum, sic et qui attendit ad visa mendacia.

verses.text: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another: as when a man’s likeness is before the face of a man.
verses.textLatin: Hoc secundum hoc visio somniorum, ante faciem hominis similitudo hominis.

verses.text: What can be made clean by the unclean? and what truth can come from that which is false?
verses.textLatin: Ab immundo, quid mundabitur? et a mendace, quid verum dicetur?

verses.text: Deceitful divinations and lying omens and the dreams of evildoers, are vanity:
verses.textLatin: Divinatio erroris, et auguria mendacia, et somnia malefacientium, vanitas est:

verses.text: And the heart fancieth as that of a woman in travail: except it be a vision sent forth from the most High, set not thy heart upon them.
verses.textLatin: et sicut parturientis, cor tuum phantasias patitur. Nisi ab Altissimo fuerit emissa visitatio, ne dederis in illis cor tuum:

verses.text: For dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
verses.textLatin: multos enim errare fecerunt somnia, et exciderunt sperantes in illis.

verses.text: The word of the law shall be fulfilled without a lie, and wisdom shall be made plain in the mouth of the faithful.
verses.textLatin: Sine mendacio consummabitur verbum legis, et sapientia in ore fidelis complanabitur.

verses.text: What doth he know, that hath not been tried? A man that hath much experience, shall think of many things: and he that hath learned many things, shall shew forth understanding.
verses.textLatin: Qui non est tentatus quid scit? vir in multis expertus cogitabit multa: et qui multa didicit enarrabit intellectum.

verses.text: He that hath no experience, knoweth little: and he that hath been experienced in many things, multiplieth prudence.
verses.textLatin: Qui non est expertus pauca recognoscit: qui autem in multis factus est, multiplicat malitiam.

verses.text: He that hath not been tried, what manner of things doth he know? he that hath been surprised, shall abound with subtlety.
verses.textLatin: Qui tentatus non est qualia scit? qui implanatus est abundabit nequitia.

verses.text: I have seen many things by travelling, and many customs of things.
verses.textLatin: Multa vidi errando, et plurimas verborum consuetudines.

verses.text: Sometimes I have been in danger of death for these things, and I have been delivered by the grace of God.
verses.textLatin: Aliquoties usque ad mortem periclitatus sum horum causa, et liberatus sum gratia Dei.

verses.text: The spirit of those that fear God, is sought after, and by his regard shall be blessed.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus timentium Deum quæritur, et in respectu illius benedicetur.

verses.text: For their hope is on him that saveth them, and the eyes of God are upon them that love him.
verses.textLatin: Spes enim illorum in salvantem illos, et oculi Dei in diligentes se.

verses.text: He that feareth the Lord shall tremble at nothing, and shall not be afraid: for he is his hope.
verses.textLatin: Qui timet Dominum nihil trepidabit: et non pavebit, quoniam ipse est spes ejus.

verses.text: The soul of him that feareth the Lord is blessed.
verses.textLatin: Timentis Dominum, beata est anima ejus.
