verses.text: To whom doth he look, and who is his strength?
verses.textLatin: Ad quem respicit, et quis est fortitudo ejus?

verses.text: The eyes of the Lord are upon them that fear him, he is their powerful protector, and strong stay, a defence from the heat, and a cover from the sun at noon,
verses.textLatin: Oculi Domini super timentes eum: protector potentiæ, firmamentum virtutis, tegimen ardoris, et umbraculum meridiani:

verses.text: A preservation from stumbling, and a help from falling; he raiseth up the soul, and enlighteneth the eyes, and giveth health, and life, and blessing.
verses.textLatin: deprecatio offensionis, et adjutorium casus: exaltans animam, et illuminans oculos, dans sanitatem, et vitam, et benedictionem.

verses.text: The offering of him that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, is stained, and the mockeries of the unjust are not acceptable.
verses.textLatin: Immolantis ex iniquo oblatio est maculata, et non sunt beneplacitæ subsannationes injustorum.

verses.text: The Lord is only for them that wait upon him in the way of truth and justice.
verses.textLatin: Dominus solus sustinentibus se in via veritatis et justitiæ.

verses.text: The most High approveth not the gifts of the wicked: neither hath he respect to the oblations of the unjust, nor will he be pacified for sins by the multitude of their sacrifices.
verses.textLatin: Dona iniquorum non probat Altissimus, nec respicit in oblationes iniquorum, nec in multitudine sacrificiorum eorum propitiabitur peccatis.

verses.text: He that offereth sacrifice of the goods of the poor, is as one that sacrificeth the son in the presence of his father.
verses.textLatin: Qui offert sacrificium ex substantia pauperum, quasi qui victimat filium in conspectu patris sui.

verses.text: The bread of the needy, is the life of the poor: he that defraudeth them thereof, is a man of blood.
verses.textLatin: Panis egentium vita pauperum est: qui defraudat illum homo sanguinis est.

verses.text: He that taketh away the bread gotten by sweat, is like him that killeth his neighbour.
verses.textLatin: Qui aufert in sudore panem, quasi qui occidit proximum suum.

verses.text: He that sheddeth blood, and he that defraudeth the laborer of his hire, are brothers.
verses.textLatin: Qui effundit sanguinem, et qui fraudem facit mercenario, fratres sunt.

verses.text: When one buildeth up, and another pulleth down: what profit have they but the labour?
verses.textLatin: Unus ædificans, et unus destruens: quid prodest illis, nisi labor?

verses.text: When one prayeth, and another curseth: whose voice will God hear?
verses.textLatin: Unus orans, et unus maledicens: cujus vocem exaudiet Deus?

verses.text: He that washeth himself after touching the dead, if he toucheth him again, what doth his washing avail?
verses.textLatin: Qui baptizatur a mortuo, et iterum tangit eum, quid proficit lavatio illius?

verses.text: So a man that fasteth for his sins, and doth the same again, what doth his humbling himself profit him? who will hear his prayer?
verses.textLatin: Sic homo qui jejunat in peccatis suis, et iterum eadem faciens: quid proficit humiliando se? orationem illius quis exaudiet?

verses.text: He  that keepeth the law, multiplieth offerings.
verses.textLatin: Qui conservat legem multiplicat oblationem.

verses.text: It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Sacrificium salutare est attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate.

verses.text: And to depart from injustice, is to offer a propitiatory sacrifice for injustices, and a begging of pardon for sins.
verses.textLatin: Et propitiationem litare sacrificii super injustitias: et deprecatio pro peccatis, recedere ab injustitia.

verses.text: He shall return thanks, that offereth fine flour: and he that doth mercy, offereth sacrifice.
verses.textLatin: Retribuet gratiam qui offert similaginem: et qui facit misericordiam offert sacrificium.

verses.text: To depart from iniquity is that which pleaseth the Lord, and to depart from injustice, is an entreaty for sins.
verses.textLatin: Beneplacitum est Domino recedere ab iniquitate: et deprecatio pro peccatis recedere ab injustitia.

verses.text: Thou shalt not appear empty in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non apparebis ante conspectum Domini vacuus:

verses.text: For all these things are to be done because of the commandment of God.
verses.textLatin: hæc enim omnia propter mandatum Dei fiunt.

verses.text: The oblation of the just maketh the altar fat, and is an odour of sweetness in the sight of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Oblatio justi impinguat altare, et odor suavitatis est in conspectu Altissimi.

verses.text: The sacrifice of the just is acceptable, and the Lord will not forget the memorial thereof.
verses.textLatin: Sacrificium justi acceptum est, et memoriam ejus non obliviscetur Dominus.

verses.text: Give glory to God with a good heart: and diminish not the firstfruits of thy hands.
verses.textLatin: Bono animo gloriam redde Deo, et non minuas primitias manuum tuarum.

verses.text: In every gift shew a cheerful countenance, and sanctify thy tithes with joy.
verses.textLatin: In omni dato hilarem fac vultum tuum, et in exsultatione sanctifica decimas tuas.

verses.text: Give to the most High according to what he hath given to thee, and with a good eye do according to the ability of thy hands:
verses.textLatin: Da Altissimo secundum datum ejus, et in bono oculo adinventionem facito manuum tuarum,

verses.text: For the Lord maketh recompense, and will give thee seven times as much.
verses.textLatin: quoniam Dominus retribuens est, et septies tantum reddet tibi.

verses.text: Do not offer wicked gifts, for such he will not receive.
verses.textLatin: Noli offerre munera prava, non enim suscipiet illa.

verses.text: And look not upon an unjust sacrifice, for the Lord is judge, and there is not with him respect of person.
verses.textLatin: Et noli inspicere sacrificum injustum, quoniam Dominus judex est, et non est apud illum gloria personæ.

verses.text: The Lord will not accept any person against a poor man, and he will hear the prayer of him that is wronged.
verses.textLatin: Non accipiet Dominus personam in pauperem, et deprecationem læsi exaudiet.

verses.text: He will not despise the prayers of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.
verses.textLatin: Non despiciet preces pupilli, nec viduam, si effundat loquelam gemitus.

verses.text: Do not the widow’s tears run down the cheek, and her cry against him that causeth them to fall?
verses.textLatin: Nonne lacrimæ viduæ ad maxillam descendunt, et exclamatio ejus super deducentem eas?

verses.text: For from the cheek they go up even to heaven, and the Lord that heareth will not be delighted with them.
verses.textLatin: A maxilla enim ascendunt usque ad cælum, et Dominus exauditor non delectabitur in illis.

verses.text: He that adoreth God with joy, shall be accepted, and his prayer shall approach even to the clouds.
verses.textLatin: Qui adorat Deum in oblectatione suscipietur, et deprecatio illius usque ad nubes propinquabit.

verses.text: The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds: and till it come nigh he will not be comforted: and he will not depart till the most High behold.
verses.textLatin: Oratio humiliantis se nubes penetrabit, et donec propinquet non consolabitur, et non discedet donec Altissimus aspiciat.

verses.text: And the Lord will not be slack, but will judge for the just, and will do judgment: and the Almighty will not have patience with them, that he may crush their back:
verses.textLatin: Et Dominus non elongabit: et judicabit justos, et faciet judicium: et Fortissimus non habebit in illis patientiam, ut contribulet dorsum ipsorum:

verses.text: And he will repay vengeance to the Gentiles, till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptres of the unjust,
verses.textLatin: et gentibus reddet vindictam, donec tollat plenitudinem superborum, et sceptra iniquorum contribulet:

verses.text: Till he have rendered to men according to their deeds: and according to the works of Adam, and according to his presumption,
verses.textLatin: donec reddat hominibus secundum actus suos, et secundum opera Adæ, et secundum præsumptionem illius:

verses.text: Till he have judged the cause of his people, and he shall delight the just with his mercy.
verses.textLatin: donec judicet judicium plebis suæ, et oblectabit justos misericordia sua.

verses.text: The mercy of God is beautiful in the time of affliction, as a cloud of rain in the time of drought.
verses.textLatin: Speciosa misericordia Dei in tempore tribulationis, quasi nubes pluviæ in tempore siccitatis.

verses.text: Have  mercy upon us, O God of all, and behold us, and shew us the light of thy mercies:
verses.textLatin: Miserere nostri, Deus omnium, et respice nos, et ostende nobis lucem miserationum tuarum:

verses.text: And send thy fear upon the nations, that have not sought after thee: that they may know that there is no God beside thee, and that they may shew forth thy wonders.
verses.textLatin: et immitte timorem tuum super gentes quæ non exquisierunt te, ut cognoscant quia non est deus nisi tu, et enarrent magnalia tua.

verses.text: Lift up thy hand over the strange nations, that they may see thy power.
verses.textLatin: Alleva manum tuam super gentes alienas, ut videant potentiam tuam.

verses.text: For as thou hast been sanctified in us in their sight, so thou shalt be magnified among them in our presence,
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim in conspectu eorum sanctificatus es in nobis, sic in conspectu nostro magnificaberis in eis:

verses.text: That they may know thee, as we also have known thee, that there is no God beside thee, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: ut cognoscant te, sicut et nos cognovimus quoniam non est deus præter te, Domine.

verses.text: Renew thy signs, and work new miracles.
verses.textLatin: Innova signa, et immuta mirabilia.

verses.text: Glorify thy hand, and thy right arm.
verses.textLatin: Glorifica manum et brachium dextrum.

verses.text: Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath.
verses.textLatin: Excita furorem, et effunde iram.

verses.text: Take away the adversary, and crush the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Tolle adversarium, et afflige inimicum.

verses.text: Hasten the time, and remember the end, that they may declare thy wonderful works.
verses.textLatin: Festina tempus, et memento finis, ut enarrent mirabilia tua.

verses.text: Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire: and let them perish that oppress thy people.
verses.textLatin: In ira flammæ devoretur qui salvatur: et qui pessimant plebem tuam inveniant perditionem.

verses.text: Crush the head of the princes of the enemies that say: There is no other beside us.
verses.textLatin: Contere caput principum inimicorum, dicentium: Non est alius præter nos.

verses.text: Gather together all the tribes of Jacob: that they may know that there is no God besides thee, and may declare thy great works: and thou shalt inherit them as from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Congrega omnes tribus Jacob, ut cognoscant quia non est deus nisi tu, et enarrent magnalia tua, et hæreditabis eos sicut ab initio.

verses.text: Have mercy on thy people, upon whom thy name is invoked: and upon Israel, whom thou hast raised up to be thy firstborn.
verses.textLatin: Miserere plebi tuæ, super quam invocatum est nomen tuum, et Israël quem coæquasti primogenito tuo.

verses.text: Have mercy on Jerusalem, the city which thou hast sanctified, the city of thy rest.
verses.textLatin: Miserere civitati sanctificationis tuæ, Jerusalem, civitati requiei tuæ.

verses.text: Fill Sion with thy unspeakable words, and thy people with thy glory.
verses.textLatin: Reple Sion inenarrabilibus verbis tuis, et gloria tua populum tuum.

verses.text: Give testimony to them that are thy creatures from the beginning, and raise up the prophecies which the former prophets spoke in thy name.
verses.textLatin: Da testimonium his qui ab initio creaturæ tuæ sunt, et suscita prædicationes quas locuti sunt in nomine tuo prophetæ priores.

verses.text: Reward them that patiently wait for thee, that thy prophets may be found faithful: and hear the prayers of thy servants,
verses.textLatin: Da mercedem sustinentibus te, ut prophetæ tui fideles inveniantur: et exaudi orationes servorum tuorum,

verses.text: According to the blessing of Aaron over thy people, and direct us into the way of justice, and let all know that dwell upon the earth, that thou art God the beholder of all ages.
verses.textLatin: secundum benedictionem Aaron de populo tuo: et dirige nos in viam justitiæ, et sciant omnes qui habitant terram quia tu es Deus conspector sæculorum.

verses.text: The belly will devour all meat, yet one is better than another.
verses.textLatin: Omnem escam manducabit venter: et est cibus cibo melior.

verses.text: The palate tasteth venison and the wise heart false speeches.
verses.textLatin: Fauces contingunt cibum feræ, et cor sensatum verba mendacia.

verses.text: A perverse heart will cause grief, and a man of experience will resist it.
verses.textLatin: Cor pravum dabit tristitiam, et homo peritus resistet illi.

verses.text: A woman will receive every man: yet one daughter is better than another.
verses.textLatin: Omnem masculum excipiet mulier: et est filia melior filia.

verses.text: The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance of her husband, and a man desireth nothing more.
verses.textLatin: Species mulieris exhilarat faciem viri sui, et super omnem concupiscentiam hominis superducit desiderium.

verses.text: If she have a tongue that can cure, and likewise mitigate and shew mercy: her husband is not like other men.
verses.textLatin: Si est lingua curationis, est et mitigationis et misericordiæ: non est vir illius secundum filios hominum.

verses.text: He that possesseth a good wife, beginneth a possession: she is a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest.
verses.textLatin: Qui possidet mulierem bonam inchoat possessionem: adjutorium secundum illum est, et columna ut requies.

verses.text: Where there is no hedge, the possession shall be spoiled: and where there is no wife, he mourneth that is in want.
verses.textLatin: Ubi non est sepes, diripietur possessio: et ubi non est mulier, ingemiscit egens.

verses.text: Who will trust him that hath no rest, and that lodgeth wheresoever the night taketh him, as a robber well appointed, that skippeth from city to city.
verses.textLatin: Quis credit ei qui non habet nidum, et deflectens ubicumque obscuraverit, quasi succinctus latro exiliens de civitate in civitatem?

verses.text: Every  friend will say: I also am his friend: but there is a friend, that is only a friend in name. Is not this a grief even to death?
verses.textLatin: Omnis amicus dicet: Et ego amicitiam copulavi: sed est amicus solo nomine amicus. Nonne tristitia inest usque ad mortem?

verses.text: But a companion and a friend shall be turned to an enemy.
verses.textLatin: sodalis autem et amicus ad inimicitiam convertentur.

verses.text: O wicked presumption, whence camest thou to cover the earth with thy malice, and deceitfulness?
verses.textLatin: O præsumptio nequissima, unde creata es cooperire aridam malitia et dolositate illius?

verses.text: There is a companion who rejoiceth with his friend in his joys, but in the time of trouble, he will be against him.
verses.textLatin: Sodalis amico conjucundatur in oblectationibus, et in tempore tribulationis adversarius erit.

verses.text: There is a companion who condoleth with his friend for his belly’s sake, and he will take up a shield against the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Sodalis amico condolet causa ventris, et contra hostem accipiet scutum.

verses.text: Forget not thy friend in thy mind, and be not unmindful of him in thy riches.
verses.textLatin: Non obliviscaris amici tui in animo tuo, et non immemor sis illius in opibus tuis.

verses.text: Consult not with him that layeth a snare for thee, and hide thy counsel from them that envy thee.
verses.textLatin: Noli consiliari cum eo qui tibi insidiatur, et a zelantibus te absconde consilium.

verses.text: Every counsellor giveth out counsel, but there is one that is a counsellor for himself.
verses.textLatin: Omnis consiliarius prodit consilium, sed est consiliarius in semetipso.

verses.text: Beware of a counsellor. And know before what need he hath: for he will devise to his own mind:
verses.textLatin: A consiliario serva animam tuam: prius scito quæ sit illius necessitas: et ipse enim animo suo cogitabit:

verses.text: Lest he thrust a stake into the ground, and say to thee:
verses.textLatin: ne forte mittat sudem in terram, et dicat tibi:

verses.text: Thy way is good; and then stand on the other side to see what shall befall thee.
verses.textLatin: Bona est via tua: et stet e contrario videre quid tibi eveniat.

verses.text: Treat not with a man without religion concerning holiness, nor with an unjust man concerning justice, nor with a woman touching her of whom she is jealous, nor with a coward concerning war, nor with a merchant about traffic, nor with a buyer of selling, nor with an envious man of giving thanks,
verses.textLatin: Cum viro irreligioso tracta de sanctitate, et cum injusto de justitia, et cum muliere de ea quæ æmulatur, cum timido de bello, cum negotiatore de trajectione, cum emptore de venditione, cum viro livido de gratiis agendis,

verses.text: Nor with the ungodly of piety, nor with the dishonest of honesty, nor with the field laborer of every work,
verses.textLatin: cum impio de pietate, cum inhonesto de honestate, cum operario agrario de omni opere,

verses.text: Nor with him that worketh by the year of the finishing of the year, nor with an idle servant of much business: give no heed to these in any matter of counsel.
verses.textLatin: cum operario annuali de consummatione anni, cum servo pigro de multa operatione. Non attendas his in omni consilio:

verses.text: But be continually with a holy man, whomsoever thou shalt know to observe the fear of God,
verses.textLatin: sed cum viro sancto assiduus esto, quemcumque cognoveris observantem timorem Dei:

verses.text: Whose soul is according to thy own soul: and who, when thou shalt stumble in the dark, will be sorry for thee.
verses.textLatin: cujus anima est secundum animam tuam, et qui, cum titubaveris in tenebris, condolebit tibi.

verses.text: And establish within thyself a heart of good counsel: for there is no other thing of more worth to thee than it.
verses.textLatin: Cor boni consilii statue tecum: non est enim tibi aliud pluris illo.

verses.text: The soul of a holy man discovereth sometimes true things, more than seven watchmen that sit in a high place to watch.
verses.textLatin: Anima viri sancti enuntiat aliquando vera, quam septem circumspectores sedentes in excelso ad speculandum.

verses.text: But above all these things pray to the most High, that he may direct thy way in truth.
verses.textLatin: Et in his omnibus deprecare Altissimum, ut dirigat in veritate viam tuam.

verses.text: In all thy works let the true word go before thee, and steady counsel before every action.
verses.textLatin: Ante omnia opera verbum verax præcedat te, et ante omnem actum consilium stabile.

verses.text: A wicked word shall change the heart: out of which four manner of things arise, good and evil, life and death: and the tongue is continually the ruler of them. There is a man that is subtle and a teacher of many, and yet is unprofitable to his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Verbum nequam immutabit cor: ex quo partes quatuor oriuntur: bonum et malum, vita et mors: et dominatrix illorum est assidua lingua. Est vir astutus multorum eruditor, et animæ suæ inutilis est.

verses.text: A skilful man hath taught many, and is sweet to his own soul.
verses.textLatin: Vir peritus multos erudivit, et animæ suæ suavis est.

verses.text: He that speaketh sophistically, is hateful: he shall be destitute of every thing.
verses.textLatin: Qui sophistice loquitur odibilis est: in omni re defraudabitur.

verses.text: Grace is not given him from the Lord: for he is deprived of all wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Non est illi data a Domino gratia, omni enim sapientia defraudatus est.

verses.text: There is a wise man that is wise to his own soul: and the fruit of his understanding is commendable.
verses.textLatin: Est sapiens animæ suæ sapiens, et fructus sensus illius laudabilis.

verses.text: A wise man instructeth his own people, and the fruits of his understanding are faithful.
verses.textLatin: Vir sapiens plebem suam erudit, et fructus sensus illius fideles sunt.

verses.text: A wise man shall be filled with blessings, and they that see shall praise him.
verses.textLatin: Vir sapiens implebitur benedictionibus, et videntes illum laudabunt.

verses.text: The life of a man is in the number of his days: but the days of Israel are innumerable.
verses.textLatin: Vita viri in numero dierum: dies autem Israël innumerabiles sunt.

verses.text: A wise man shall inherit honour among his people, and his name shall live for ever.
verses.textLatin: Sapiens in populo hæreditabit honorem, et nomen illius erit vivens in æternum.

verses.text: My son, prove thy soul in thy life: and if it be wicked, give it no power:
verses.textLatin: Fili, in vita tua tenta animam tuam, et si fuerit nequam non des illi potestatem:

verses.text: For all things are not expedient for all, and every kind pleaseth not every soul.
verses.textLatin: non enim omnia omnibus expediunt, et non omni animæ omne genus placet.

verses.text: Be not greedy in any feasting, and pour not out thyself upon any meat:
verses.textLatin: Noli avidus esse in omni epulatione, et non te effundas super omnem escam:

verses.text: For in many meats there will be sickness, and greediness will turn to choler.
verses.textLatin: in multis enim escis erit infirmitas, et aviditas appropinquabit usque ad choleram.

verses.text: By surfeiting many have perished: but he that is temperate, shall prolong life.
verses.textLatin: Propter crapulam multi obierunt: qui autem abstinens est adjiciet vitam.

verses.text: Honour  the physician for the need thou hast of him: for the most High hath created him.
verses.textLatin: Honora medicum propter necessitatem: etenim illum creavit Altissimus.

verses.text: For all healing is from God, and he shall receive gifts of the king.
verses.textLatin: A Deo est enim omnis medela, et a rege accipiet donationem.

verses.text: The skill of the physician shall lift up his head, and in the sight of great men he shall be praised.
verses.textLatin: Disciplina medici exaltabit caput illius, et in conspectu magnatorum collaudabitur.

verses.text: The most High hath created medicines out of the earth, and a wise man will not abhor them.
verses.textLatin: Altissimus creavit de terra medicamenta, et vir prudens non abhorrebit illa.

verses.text: Was not bitter water made sweet with wood?
verses.textLatin: Nonne a ligno indulcata est aqua amara?

verses.text: The virtue of these things is come to the knowledge of men, and the most High hath given knowledge to men, that he may be honoured in his wonders.
verses.textLatin: Ad agnitionem hominum virtus illorum: et dedit hominibus scientiam Altissimus, honorari in mirabilibus suis.

verses.text: By these he shall cure and shall allay their pains, and of these the apothecary shall make sweet confections, and shall make up ointments of health, and of his works there shall be no end.
verses.textLatin: In his curans mitigabit dolorem: et unguentarius faciet pigmenta suavitatis, et unctiones conficiet sanitatis: et non consummabuntur opera ejus.

verses.text: For the peace of God is over all the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Pax enim Dei super faciem terræ.

verses.text: My son, in thy sickness neglect not thyself, but pray to the Lord, and he shall heal thee.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in tua infirmitate ne despicias teipsum: sed ora Dominum, et ipse curabit te.

verses.text: Turn away from sin and order thy hands aright, and cleanse thy heart from all offence.
verses.textLatin: Averte a delicto, et dirige manus, et ab omni delicto munda cor tuum.

verses.text: Give a sweet savour, and a memorial of fine flour, and make a fat offering, and then give place to the physician.
verses.textLatin: Da suavitatem et memoriam similaginis, et impingua oblationem, et da locum medico:

verses.text: For the Lord created him: and let him not depart from thee, for his works are necessary.
verses.textLatin: etenim illum Dominus creavit, et non discedat a te, quia opera ejus sunt necessaria.

verses.text: For there is a time when thou must fall into their hands:
verses.textLatin: Est enim tempus quando in manus illorum incurras:

verses.text: And they shall beseech the Lord, that he would prosper what they give for ease and remedy, for their conversation.
verses.textLatin: ipsi vero Dominum deprecabuntur, ut dirigat requiem eorum, et sanitatem, propter conversationem illorum.

verses.text: He that sinneth in the sight of his Maker, shall fall into the hands of the physician.
verses.textLatin: Qui delinquit in conspectu ejus qui fecit eum, incidet in manus medici.

verses.text: My son, shed tears over the dead, and begin to lament as if thou hadst suffered some great harm, and according to judgment cover his body, and neglect not his burial.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in mortuum produc lacrimas, et quasi dira passus incipe plorare: et secundum judicium contege corpus illius, et non despicias sepulturam illius.

verses.text: And for fear of being ill spoken of weep bitterly for a day, and then comfort thyself in thy sadness.
verses.textLatin: Propter delaturam autem amare fer luctum illius uno die, et consolare propter tristitiam:

verses.text: And make mourning for him according to his merit for a day, or two, for fear of detraction.
verses.textLatin: et fac luctum secundum meritum ejus uno die, vel duobus, propter detractionem:

verses.text: For of sadness cometh death, and it overwhelmeth the strength, and the sorrow of the heart boweth down the neck.
verses.textLatin: a tristitia enim festinat mors, et cooperit virtutem, et tristitia cordis flectit cervicem.

verses.text: In withdrawing aside sorrow remaineth: and the substance of the poor is according to his heart.
verses.textLatin: In abductione permanet tristitia, et substantia inopis secundum cor ejus.

verses.text: Give not up thy heart to sadness, but drive it from thee: and remember the latter end.
verses.textLatin: Ne dederis in tristitia cor tuum, sed repelle eam a te, et memento novissimorum.

verses.text: Forget it not: for there is no returning, and thou shalt do him no good, and shalt hurt thyself.
verses.textLatin: Noli oblivisci, neque enim est conversio: et huic nihil proderis, et teipsum pessimabis.

verses.text: Remember my judgment: for thine also shall be so: yesterday for me, and to day for thee.
verses.textLatin: Memor esto judicii mei: sic enim erit et tuum: mihi heri, et tibi hodie.

verses.text: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest, and comfort him in the departing of his spirit.
verses.textLatin: In requie mortui requiescere fac memoriam ejus, et consolare illum in exitu spiritus sui.

verses.text: The wisdom of a scribe cometh by his time of leisure: and he that is less in action, shall receive wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Sapientia scribæ in tempore vacuitatis, et qui minoratur actu sapientiam percipiet, qua sapientia replebitur.

verses.text: With what wisdom shall he be furnished that holdeth the plough, and that glorieth in the goad, that driveth the oxen therewith, and is occupied in their labours, and his whole talk is about the offspring of bulls?
verses.textLatin: Qui tenet aratrum, et qui gloriatur in jaculo, stimulo boves agitat, et conversatur in operibus eorum, et enarratio ejus in filiis taurorum.

verses.text: He shall give his mind to turn up furrows, and his care is to give the kine fodder.
verses.textLatin: Cor suum dabit ad versandos sulcos, et vigilia ejus in sagina vaccarum.

verses.text: So every craftsman and workmaster that laboureth night and day, he who maketh graven seals, and by his continual diligence varieth the figure: he shall give his mind to the resemblance of the picture, and by his watching shall finish the work.
verses.textLatin: Sic omnis faber et architectus, qui noctem tamquam diem transigit: qui sculpit signacula sculptilia, et assiduitas ejus variat picturam: cor suum dabit in similitudinem picturæ, et vigilia sua perficiet opus.

verses.text: So doth the smith sitting by the anvil and considering the iron work. The vapour of the fire wasteth his flesh, and he fighteth with the heat of the furnace.
verses.textLatin: Sic faber ferrarius sedens juxta incudem, et considerans opus ferri: vapor ignis uret carnes ejus, et in calore fornacis concertatur.

verses.text: The noise of the hammer is always in his ears, and his eye is upon the pattern of the vessel he maketh.
verses.textLatin: Vox mallei innovat aurem ejus, et contra similitudinem vasis oculus ejus.

verses.text: He setteth his mind to finish his work, and his watching to polish them to perfection.
verses.textLatin: Cor suum dabit in consummationem operum, et vigilia sua ornabit in perfectionem.

verses.text: So doth the potter sitting at his work, turning the wheel about with his feet, who is always carefully set to his work, and maketh all his work by number:
verses.textLatin: Sic figulus sedens ad opus suum, convertens pedibus suis rotam, qui in sollicitudine positus est semper propter opus suum, et in numero est omnis operatio ejus.

verses.text: He fashioneth the clay with his arm, and boweth down his strength before his feet:
verses.textLatin: In brachio suo formabit lutum, et ante pedes suos curvabit virtutem suam.

verses.text: He shall give his mind to finish the glazing, and his watching to make clean the furnace.
verses.textLatin: Cor suum dabit ut consummet linitionem, et vigilia sua mundabit fornacem.

verses.text: All these trust to their hands, and every one is wise in his own art.
verses.textLatin: Omnes hi in manibus suis speraverunt, et unusquisque in arte sua sapiens est.

verses.text: Without these a city is not built.
verses.textLatin: Sine his omnibus non ædificatur civitas,

verses.text: And they shall not dwell, nor walk about therein, and they shall not go up into the assembly.
verses.textLatin: et non inhabitabunt, nec inambulabunt, et in ecclesiam non transilient.

verses.text: Upon the judges’ seat they shall not sit, and the ordinance of judgment they shall not understand, neither shall they declare discipline and judgment, and they shall not be found where parables are spoken:
verses.textLatin: Super sellam judicis non sedebunt, et testamentum judicii non intelligent, neque palam facient disciplinam et judicium, et in parabolis non invenientur:

verses.text: But they shall strengthen the state of the world, and their prayer shall be in the work of their craft, applying their soul, and searching in the law of the most High.
verses.textLatin: sed creaturam ævi confirmabunt: et deprecatio illorum in operatione artis, accomodantes animam suam, et conquirentes in lege Altissimi.

verses.text: The  wise man will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients, and will be occupied in the prophets.
verses.textLatin: Sapientiam omnium antiquorum exquiret sapiens, et in prophetis vacabit.

verses.text: He will keep the sayings of renowned men, and will enter withal into the subtilties of parables.
verses.textLatin: Narrationem virorum nominatorum conservabit, et in versutias parabolarum simul introibit.

verses.text: He will search out the hidden meanings of proverbs, and will be conversant in the secrets of parables.
verses.textLatin: Occulta proverbiorum exquiret, et in absconditis parabolarum conversabitur.

verses.text: He shall serve among great men, and appear before the governor.
verses.textLatin: In medio magnatorum ministrabit, et in conspectu præsidis apparebit.

verses.text: He shall pass into strange countries: for he shall try good and evil among men.
verses.textLatin: In terram alienigenarum gentium pertransiet: bona enim et mala in hominibus tentabit.

verses.text: He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and he will pray in the sight of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Cor suum tradet ad vigilandum diluculo ad Dominum, qui fecit illum, et in conspectu Altissimi deprecabitur.

verses.text: He will open his mouth in prayer, and will make supplication for his sins.
verses.textLatin: Aperiet os suum in oratione, et pro delictis suis deprecabitur.

verses.text: For if it shall please the great Lord, he will fill him with the spirit of understanding:
verses.textLatin: Si enim Dominus magnus voluerit, spiritu intelligentiæ replebit illum:

verses.text: And he will pour forth the words of his wisdom as showers, and in his prayer he will confess to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et ipse tamquam imbres mittet eloquia sapientiæ suæ, et in oratione confitebitur Domino:

verses.text: And he shall direct his counsel, and his knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.
verses.textLatin: et ipse diriget consilium ejus, et disciplinam, et in absconditis suis consiliabitur.

verses.text: He shall shew forth the discipline he hath learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ipse palam faciet disciplinam doctrinæ suæ, et in lege testamenti Domini gloriabitur.

verses.text: Many shall praise his wisdom, and it shall never be forgotten.
verses.textLatin: Collaudabunt multi sapientiam ejus, et usque in sæculum non delebitur.

verses.text: The memory of him shall not depart away, and his name shall be in request from generation to generation.
verses.textLatin: Non recedet memoria ejus, et nomen ejus requiretur a generatione in generationem.

verses.text: Nations shall declare his wisdom, and the church shall shew forth his praise.
verses.textLatin: Sapientiam ejus enarrabunt gentes, et laudem ejus enuntiabit ecclesia.

verses.text: If he continue, he shall leave a name above a thousand: and if he rest, it shall be to his advantage.
verses.textLatin: Si permanserit, nomen derelinquet plus quam mille: et si requieverit, proderit illi.

verses.text: I will yet meditate that I may declare: for I am filled as with a holy transport.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc consiliabor ut enarrem: ut furore enim repletus sum.

verses.text: By a voice he saith: Hear me, ye divine offspring, and bud forth as the rose planted by the brooks of waters.
verses.textLatin: In voce dicit: Obaudite me, divini fructus, et quasi rosa plantata super rivos aquarum fructificate.

verses.text: Give ye a sweet odour as frankincense.
verses.textLatin: Quasi Libanus odorem suavitatis habete.

verses.text: Send forth flowers, as the lily, and yield a smell, and bring forth leaves in grace, and praise with canticles, and bless the Lord in his works.
verses.textLatin: Florete flores quasi lilium: et date odorem, et frondete in gratiam: et collaudate canticum, et benedicite Dominum in operibus suis.

verses.text: Magnify his name, and give glory to him with the voice of your lips, and with the canticles of your mouths, and with harps, and in praising him, you shall say in this manner:
verses.textLatin: Date nomini ejus magnificentiam, et confitemini illi in voce labiorum vestrorum, et in canticis labiorum, et citharis: et sic dicetis in confessione:

verses.text: All the works of the Lord are exceeding good.
verses.textLatin: Opera Domini universa bona valde.

verses.text: At his word the waters stood as a heap: and at the words of his mouth the receptacles of waters:
verses.textLatin: In verbo ejus stetit aqua sicut congeries: et in sermone oris illius sicut exceptoria aquarum:

verses.text: For at his commandment favour is shewn, and there is no diminishing of his salvation.
verses.textLatin: quoniam in præcepto ipsius placor fit, et non est minoratio in salute ipsius.

verses.text: The works of all flesh are before him, and there is nothing hid from his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Opera omnis carnis coram illo, et non est quidquam absconditum ab oculis ejus.

verses.text: He seeth from eternity to eternity, and there is nothing wonderful before him.
verses.textLatin: A sæculo usque in sæculum respicit, et nihil est mirabile in conspectu ejus.

verses.text: There is no saying: What is this, or what is that? for all things shall be sought in their time.
verses.textLatin: Non est dicere: Quid est hoc, aut quid est istud? omnia enim in tempore suo quærentur.

verses.text: His blessing hath overflowed like a river.
verses.textLatin: Benedictio illius quasi fluvius inundavit.

verses.text: And as a flood hath watered the earth; so shall his wrath inherit the nations, that have not sought after him:
verses.textLatin: Quomodo cataclysmus aridam inebriavit, sic ira ipsius gentes quæ non exquisierunt eum hæreditabit.

verses.text: Even as he turned the waters into a dry land, and the earth was made dry: and his ways were made plain for their journey: so to sinners they are stumblingblocks in his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo convertit aquas in siccitatem, et siccata est terra, et viæ illius viis illorum directæ sunt, sic peccatoribus offensiones in ira ejus.

verses.text: Good things were created for the good from the beginning, so for the wicked, good and evil things.
verses.textLatin: Bona bonis creata sunt ab initio: sic nequissimis bona et mala.

verses.text: The principal things necessary for the life of men, are water, fire, and iron, salt, milk, and bread of flour, and honey, and the cluster of the grape, and oil, and clothing.
verses.textLatin: Initium necessariæ rei vitæ hominum, aqua, ignis, et ferrum, sal, lac, et panis similagineus, et mel, et botrus uvæ, et oleum, et vestimentum.

verses.text: All these things shall be for good to the holy, so to the sinners and the ungodly they shall be turned into evil.
verses.textLatin: Hæc omnia sanctis in bona, sic et impiis et peccatoribus in mala convertentur.

verses.text: There are spirits that are created for vengeance, and in their fury they lay on grievous torments.
verses.textLatin: Sunt spiritus qui ad vindictam creati sunt, et in furore suo confirmaverunt tormenta sua.

verses.text: In the time of destruction they shall pour out their force: and they shall appease the wrath of him that made them.
verses.textLatin: In tempore consummationis effundent virtutem, et furorem ejus qui fecit illos placabunt.

verses.text: Fire, hail, famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance.
verses.textLatin: Ignis, grando, fames, et mors, omnia hæc ad vindictam creata sunt:

verses.text: The teeth of beasts, and scorpions, and serpents, and the sword taking vengeance upon the ungodly unto destruction.
verses.textLatin: bestiarum dentes, et scorpii, et serpentes, et rhomphæa vindicans in exterminium impios.

verses.text: In his commandments they shall feast, and they shall be ready upon earth when need is, and when their time is come they shall not transgress his word.
verses.textLatin: In mandatis ejus epulabuntur: et super terram in necessitatem præparabuntur, et in temporibus suis non præterient verbum.

verses.text: Therefore from the beginning I was resolved, and I have meditated, and thought on these things and left them in writing,
verses.textLatin: Propterea ab initio confirmatus sum, et consiliatus sum, et cogitavi, et scripta dimisi.

verses.text: All the works of the Lord are good, and he will furnish every work in due time.
verses.textLatin: Omnia opera Domini bona, et omne opus hora sua subministrabit.

verses.text: It is not to be said: This is worse than that: for all shall be well approved in their time.
verses.textLatin: Non est dicere: Hoc illo nequius est: omnia enim in tempore suo comprobabuntur.

verses.text: Now therefore with the whole heart and mouth praise ye him, and bless the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc in omni corde et ore collaudate, et benedicite nomen Domini.

verses.text: Great  labour is created for all men, and a heavy yoke is upon the children of Adam, from the day of their coming out of their mother’s womb, until the day of their burial into the mother of all.
verses.textLatin: Occupatio magna creata est omnibus hominibus, et jugum grave super filios Adam, a die exitus de ventre matris eorum usque in diem sepulturæ in matrem omnium.

verses.text: Their thoughts, and fears of the heart, their imagination of things to come, and the day of their end:
verses.textLatin: Cogitationes eorum, et timores cordis, adinventio exspectationis, et dies finitionis,

verses.text: From him that sitteth on a glorious throne, unto him that is humbled in earth and ashes:
verses.textLatin: a residente super sedem gloriosam, usque ad humiliatum in terra et cinere:

verses.text: From him that weareth purple, and beareth the crown, even to him that is covered with rough linen: wrath, envy, trouble, unquietness, and the fear of death, continual anger, and strife,
verses.textLatin: ab eo qui utitur hyacintho et portat coronam, usque ad eum qui operitur lino crudo: furor, zelus, tumultus, fluctuatio, et timor mortis, iracundia perseverans, et contentio:

verses.text: And in the time of rest upon his bed, the sleep of the night changeth his knowledge.
verses.textLatin: et in tempore refectionis in cubili, somnus noctis immutat scientiam ejus.

verses.text: A little and as nothing is his rest, and afterward in sleep, as in the day of keeping watch.
verses.textLatin: Modicum tamquam nihil in requie, et ab eo in somnis, quasi in die respectus.

verses.text: He is troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he had escaped in the day of battle. In the time of his safety he rose up, and wondereth that there is no fear:
verses.textLatin: Conturbatus est in visu cordis sui, tamquam qui evaserit in die belli: in tempore salutis suæ exsurrexit, et admirans ad nullum timorem:

verses.text: Such things happen to all flesh, from man even to beast, and upon sinners are sevenfold more.
verses.textLatin: cum omni carne, ab homine usque ad pecus, et super peccatores septuplum.

verses.text: Moreover, death, and bloodshed, strife, and sword, oppressions, famine, and affliction, and scourges:
verses.textLatin: Ad hæc mors, sanguis, contentio, et rhomphæa, oppressiones, fames, et contritio, et flagella:

verses.text: All these things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.
verses.textLatin: super iniquos creata sunt hæc omnia: et propter illos factus est cataclysmus.

verses.text: All things that are of the earth, shall return to the earth again, and all waters shall return to the sea.
verses.textLatin: Omnia quæ de terra sunt in terram convertentur, et omnes aquæ in mare revertentur.

verses.text: All bribery, and injustice shall be blotted out, and fidelity shall stand for ever.
verses.textLatin: Omne munus et iniquitas delebitur, et fides in sæculum stabit.

verses.text: The riches of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall pass away with a noise like a great thunder in rain.
verses.textLatin: Substantiæ injustorum sicut fluvius siccabuntur, et sicut tonitruum magnum in pluvia personabunt.

verses.text: While he openeth his hands he shall rejoice: but transgressors shall pine away in the end.
verses.textLatin: In aperiendo manus suas lætabitur: sic prævaricatores in consummatione tabescent.

verses.text: The offspring of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches, and make a noise as unclean roots upon the top of a rock.
verses.textLatin: Nepotes impiorum non multiplicabunt ramos: et radices immundæ super cacumen petræ sonant.

verses.text: The weed growing over every water, and at the bank of the river, shall be pulled up before all grass.
verses.textLatin: Super omnem aquam viriditas, et ad oram fluminis ante omne fœnum evelletur.

verses.text: Grace is like a paradise in blessings, and mercy remaineth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Gratia sicut paradisus in benedictionibus, et misericordia in sæculum permanet.

verses.text: The life of a laborer that is content with what he hath, shall be sweet, and in it thou shalt find a treasure.
verses.textLatin: Vita sibi sufficientis operarii condulcabitur, et in ea invenies thesaurum.

verses.text: Children, and the building of a city shall establish a name, but a blameless wife shall be counted above them both.
verses.textLatin: Filii et ædificatio civitatis confirmabit nomen: et super hæc mulier immaculata computabitur.

verses.text: Wine and music rejoice the heart, but the love of wisdom is above them both.
verses.textLatin: Vinum et musica lætificant cor: et super utraque dilectio sapientiæ.

verses.text: The flute and the psaltery make a sweet melody, but a pleasant tongue is above them both.
verses.textLatin: Tibiæ et psalterium suavem faciunt melodiam: et super utraque lingua suavis.

verses.text: Thy eye desireth favour and beauty, but more than these green sown fields.
verses.textLatin: Gratiam et speciem desiderabit oculus tuus: et super hæc virides sationes.

verses.text: A friend and companion meeting together in season, but above them both is a wife with her husband.
verses.textLatin: Amicus et sodalis in tempore convenientes, et super utrosque mulier cum viro.

verses.text: Brethren are a help in the time of trouble, but mercy shall deliver more than they.
verses.textLatin: Fratres in adjutorium in tempore tribulationis: et super eos misericordia liberabit.

verses.text: Gold and silver make the feet stand sure: but wise counsel is above them both.
verses.textLatin: Aurum et argentum est constitutio pedum: et super utrumque consilium beneplacitum.

verses.text: Riches and strength lift up the heart: but above these is the fear of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Facultates et virtutes exaltant cor, et super hæc timor Domini.

verses.text: There is no want in the fear of the Lord, and it needeth not to seek for help.
verses.textLatin: Non est in timore Domini minoratio: et non est in eo inquirere adjutorium.

verses.text: The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing, and they have covered it above all glory.
verses.textLatin: Timor Domini sicut paradisus benedictionis, et super omnem gloriam operuerunt illum.

verses.text: My son, in thy lifetime be not indigent: for it is better to die than to want.
verses.textLatin: Fili, in tempore vitæ tuæ ne indigeas: melius est enim mori quam indigere.

verses.text: The life of him that looketh toward another man’s table is not to be counted a life: for he feedeth his soul with another man’s meat.
verses.textLatin: Vir respiciens in mensam alienam, non est vita ejus in cogitatione victus: alit enim animam suam cibis alienis:

verses.text: But a man, well instructed and taught, will look to himself.
verses.textLatin: vir autem disciplinatus et eruditus custodiet se.

verses.text: Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the unwise, but in his belly there shall burn a fire.
verses.textLatin: In ore imprudentis condulcabitur inopia, et in ventre ejus ignis ardebit.

verses.text: O  DEATH, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that hath peace in his possessions!
verses.textLatin: O mors, quam amara est memoria tua homini pacem habenti in substantiis suis:

verses.text: To a man that is at rest, and whose ways are prosperous in all things, and that is yet able to take meat!
verses.textLatin: viro quieto, et cujus viæ directæ sunt in omnibus, et adhuc valenti accipere cibum!

verses.text: O death, thy sentence is welcome to the man that is in need, and to him whose strength faileth:
verses.textLatin: O mors, bonum est judicium tuum homini indigenti, et qui minoratur viribus,

verses.text: Who is in a decrepit age, and that is in care about all things, and to the distrustful that loseth patience!
verses.textLatin: defecto ætate, et cui de omnibus cura est, et incredibili, qui perdit patientiam!

verses.text: Fear not the sentence of death. Remember what things have been before thee, and what shall come after thee: this sentence is from the Lord upon all flesh.
verses.textLatin: Noli metuere judicium mortis: memento quæ ante te fuerunt, et quæ superventura sunt tibi: hoc judicium a Domino omni carni.

verses.text: And what shall come upon thee by the good pleasure of the most High? whether ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
verses.textLatin: Et quid superveniet tibi in beneplacito Altissimi? sive decem, sive centum, sive mille anni:

verses.text: For among the dead there is no accusing of life.
verses.textLatin: non est enim in inferno accusatio vitæ.

verses.text: The children of sinners become children of abominations, and they that converse near the houses of the ungodly.
verses.textLatin: Filii abominationum fiunt filii peccatorum, et qui conversantur secus domos impiorum.

verses.text: The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, and with their posterity shall be a perpetual reproach.
verses.textLatin: Filiorum peccatorum periet hæreditas, et cum semine illorum assiduitas opprobrii.

verses.text: The children will complain of an ungodly father, because for his sake they are in reproach.
verses.textLatin: De patre impio queruntur filii, quoniam propter illum sunt in opprobrio.

verses.text: Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the most high Lord.
verses.textLatin: Væ vobis, viri impii, qui dereliquistis legem Domini Altissimi!

verses.text: And if you be born, you shall be born in malediction: and if you die, in malediction shall be your portion.
verses.textLatin: Et si nati fueritis, in maledictione nascemini: et si mortui fueritis, in maledictione erit pars vestra.

verses.text: All things that are of the earth, shall return into the earth: so the ungodly shall from malediction to destruction.
verses.textLatin: Omnia quæ de terra sunt in terram convertentur: sic impii a maledicto in perditionem.

verses.text: The mourning of men is about their body, but the name of the ungodly shall be blotted out.
verses.textLatin: Luctus hominum in corpore ipsorum: nomen autem impiorum delebitur.

verses.text: Take care of a good name: for this shall continue with thee, more than a thousand treasures precious and great.
verses.textLatin: Curam habe de bono nomine: hoc enim magis permanebit tibi quam mille thesauri pretiosi et magni.

verses.text: A good life hath its number of days: but a good name shall continue for ever.
verses.textLatin: Bonæ vitæ numerus dierum: bonum autem nomen permanebit in ævum.

verses.text: My children, keep discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?
verses.textLatin: Disciplinam in pace conservate, filii: sapientia enim abscondita, et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?

verses.text: Better is the man that hideth his folly, than the man that hideth his wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Melior est homo qui abscondit stultitiam suam, quam homo qui abscondit sapientiam suam.

verses.text: Wherefore have a shame of these things I am now going to speak of.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen reveremini in his quæ procedunt de ore meo:

verses.text: For it is not good to keep all shame facedness: and all things do not please all men in opinion.
verses.textLatin: non est enim bonum omnem reverentiam observare, et non omnia omnibus bene placent in fide.

verses.text: Be ashamed of fornication before father and mother: and of a lie before a governor and a man in power:
verses.textLatin: Erubescite a patre et a matre de fornicatione: et a præsidente et a potente de mendacio:

verses.text: Of an offence before a prince, and a judge: of iniquity before a congregation and a people:
verses.textLatin: a principe et a judice de delicto: a synagoga et plebe de iniquitate:

verses.text: Of injustice before a companion and friend: and in regard to the place where thou dwellest,
verses.textLatin: a socio et amico de injustitia, et de loco in quo habitas:

verses.text: Of theft, and of the truth of God, and the covenant: of leaning with thy elbow over meat, and of deceit in giving and taking:
verses.textLatin: de furto, de veritate Dei, et testamento: de discubitu in panibus, et ab obfuscatione dati et accepti:

verses.text: Of silence before them that salute thee: of looking upon a harlot: and of turning away thy face from thy kinsman.
verses.textLatin: a salutantibus de silentio, a respectu mulieris fornicariæ, et ab aversione vultus cognati.

verses.text: Turn not away thy face from thy neighbour, and of taking away a portion and not restoring.
verses.textLatin: Ne avertas faciem a proximo tuo, et ab auferendo partem et non restituendo.

verses.text: Gaze not upon another man’s wife, and be not inquisitive after his handmaid, and approach not her bed.
verses.textLatin: Ne respicias mulierem alieni viri, et ne scruteris ancillam ejus, neque steteris ad lectum ejus.

verses.text: Be ashamed of upbraiding speeches before friends: and after thou hast given, upbraid not.
verses.textLatin: Ab amicis de sermonibus improperii: et cum dederis, ne improperes.

verses.text: Repeat  not the word which thou hast heard, and disclose not the thing that is secret; so shalt thou be truly without confusion, and shalt find favour before all men: be not ashamed of any of these things, and accept no person to sin thereby:
verses.textLatin: Non duplices sermonem auditus de revelatione sermonis absconditi: et eris vere sine confusione, et invenies gratiam in conspectu omnium hominum. Ne pro his omnibus confundaris, et ne accipias personam ut delinquas:

verses.text: Of the law of the most High, and of his covenant, and of judgment to justify the ungodly:
verses.textLatin: de lege Altissimi, et testamento, et de judicio justificare impium,

verses.text: Of the affair of companions and travellers, and of the gift of the inheritance of friends:
verses.textLatin: de verbo sociorum et viatorum, et de datione hæreditatis amicorum,

verses.text: Of exactness of balance and weights, of getting much or little:
verses.textLatin: de æqualitate stateræ et ponderum, de acquisitione multorum et paucorum,

verses.text: Of the corruption of buying, and of merchants, and of much correction of children, and to make the side of a wicked slave to bleed.
verses.textLatin: de corruptione emptionis et negotiatorum, et de multa disciplina filiorum, et servo pessimo latus sanguinare.

verses.text: Sure keeping is good over a wicked wife.
verses.textLatin: Super mulierem nequam bonum est signum.

verses.text: Where there are many hands, shut up, and deliver all things in number, and weight: and put all in writing that thou givest out or receivest in.
verses.textLatin: Ubi manus multæ sunt, claude: et quodcumque trades, numera et appende: datum vero et acceptum omne describe.

verses.text: Be not ashamed to inform the unwise and foolish, and the aged, that are judged by young men: and thou shalt be well instructed in all things, and well approved in the sight of all men living.
verses.textLatin: De disciplina insensati et fatui, et de senioribus qui judicantur ab adolescentibus: et eris eruditus in omnibus, et probabilis in conspectu omnium vivorum.

verses.text: The father waketh for the daughter when no man knoweth, and the care for her taketh away his sleep, when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age, and when she is married, lest she should be hateful:
verses.textLatin: Filia patris abscondita est vigilia, et sollicitudo ejus aufert somnum: ne forte in adolescentia sua adulta efficiatur, et cum viro commorata odibilis fiat:

verses.text: In her virginity, lest she should be corrupted, and be found with child in her father’s house: and having a husband, lest she should misbehave herself, or at the least become barren.
verses.textLatin: nequando polluatur in virginitate sua, et in paternis suis gravida inveniatur: ne forte cum viro commorata transgrediatur, aut certe sterilis efficiatur.

verses.text: Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter: lest at anytime she make thee become a laughingstock to thy enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and she make thee ashamed before all the multitude.
verses.textLatin: Super filiam luxuriosam confirma custodiam, nequando faciat te in opprobrium venire inimicis, a detractione in civitate, et objectione plebis, et confundat te in multitudine populi.

verses.text: Behold not everybody’s beauty: and tarry not among women.
verses.textLatin: Omni homini noli intendere in specie, et in medio mulierum noli commorari:

verses.text: For from garments cometh a moth, and from a woman the iniquity of a man.
verses.textLatin: de vestimentis enim procedit tinea, et a muliere iniquitas viri.

verses.text: For better is the iniquity of a man, than a woman doing a good turn, and a woman bringing shame and reproach.
verses.textLatin: Melior est enim iniquitas viri quam mulier benefaciens, et mulier confundens in opprobrium.

verses.text: I will now remember the works of the Lord, and I will declare the things I have seen. By the words of the Lord are his works.
verses.textLatin: Memor ero igitur operum Domini, et quæ vidi annuntiabo. In sermonibus Domini opera ejus.

verses.text: The sun giving light hath looked upon all things, and full of the glory of the Lord is his work.
verses.textLatin: Sol illuminans per omnia respexit, et gloria Domini plenum est opus ejus.

verses.text: Hath not the Lord made the saints to declare all his wonderful works, which the Lord Almighty hath firmly settled to be established for his glory?
verses.textLatin: Nonne Dominus fecit sanctos enarrare omnia mirabilia sua, quæ confirmavit Dominus omnipotens stabiliri in gloria sua?

verses.text: He hath searched out the deep, and the heart of men: and considered their crafty devices.
verses.textLatin: Abyssum et cor hominum investigavit, et in astutia eorum excogitavit.

verses.text: For the Lord knoweth all knowledge, and hath beheld the signs of the world, he declareth the things that are past, and the things that are to come, and revealeth the traces of hidden things.
verses.textLatin: Cognovit enim Dominus omnem scientiam, et inspexit in signum ævi, annuntians quæ præterierunt et quæ superventura sunt, revelans vestigia occultorum.

verses.text: No thought escapeth him, and no word can hide itself from him.
verses.textLatin: Non præterit illum omnis cogitatus, et non abscondit se ab eo ullus sermo.

verses.text: He hath beautified the glorious works of his wisdom: and he is from eternity to eternity, and to him nothing may be added,
verses.textLatin: Magnalia sapientiæ suæ decoravit, qui est ante sæculum et usque in sæculum: neque adjectum est,

verses.text: Nor can he be diminished, and he hath no need of any counsellor.
verses.textLatin: neque minuitur, et non eget alicujus consilio.

verses.text: O how desirable are all his works, and what we can know is but as a spark!
verses.textLatin: Quam desiderabilia omnia opera ejus! et tamquam scintilla quæ est considerare!

verses.text: All these things live, and remain for ever, and for every use all things obey him.
verses.textLatin: Omnia hæc vivunt, et manent in sæculum, et in omni necessitate omnia obaudiunt ei.

verses.text: All things are double, one against another, and he hath made nothing defective.
verses.textLatin: Omnia duplicia, unum contra unum, et non fecit quidquam deesse.

verses.text: He hath established the good things of every one. And who shall be filled with beholding his glory?
verses.textLatin: Uniuscujusque confirmavit bona: et quis satiabitur videns gloriam ejus?

verses.text: The  firmament on high is his beauty, the beauty of heaven with its glorious shew.
verses.textLatin: Altitudinis firmamentum pulchritudo ejus est, species cæli in visione gloriæ.

verses.text: The sun when he appeareth shewing forth at his rising, an admirable instrument, the work of the most High.
verses.textLatin: Sol in aspectu annuntians in exitu, vas admirabile, opus Excelsi.

verses.text: At noon he burneth the earth, and who can abide his burning heat? As one keeping a furnace in the works of heat:
verses.textLatin: In meridiano exurit terram, et in conspectu ardoris ejus quis poterit sustinere? fornacem custodiens in operibus ardoris:

verses.text: The sun three times as much, burneth the mountains, breathing out fiery vapours, and shining with his beams, he blindeth the eyes.
verses.textLatin: tripliciter sol exurens montes, radios igneos exsufflans, et refulgens radiis suis obcæcat oculos.

verses.text: Great is the Lord that made him, and at his words he hath hastened his course.
verses.textLatin: Magnus Dominus qui fecit illum, et in sermonibus ejus festinavit iter.

verses.text: And the moon in all in her season, is for a declaration of times and a sign of the world.
verses.textLatin: Et luna in omnibus in tempore suo, ostensio temporis, et signum ævi.

verses.text: From the moon is the sign of the festival day, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.
verses.textLatin: A luna signum diei festi: luminare quod minuitur in consummatione.

verses.text: The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her perfection.
verses.textLatin: Mensis secundum nomen ejus est, crescens mirabiliter in consummatione.

verses.text: Being an instrument of the armies on high, shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven.
verses.textLatin: Vas castrorum in excelsis, in firmamento cæli resplendens gloriose.

verses.text: The glory of the stars is the beauty of heaven; the Lord enlighteneth the world on high.
verses.textLatin: Species cæli gloria stellarum: mundum illuminans in excelsis Dominus.

verses.text: By the words of the holy one they shall stand in judgment, and shall never fall in their watches.
verses.textLatin: In verbis Sancti stabunt ad judicium, et non deficient in vigiliis suis.

verses.text: Look upon the rainbow, and bless him that made it: it is very beautiful in its brightness.
verses.textLatin: Vide arcum, et benedic eum qui fecit illum: valde speciosus est in splendore suo.

verses.text: It encompasseth the heaven about with the circle of its glory, the hands of the most High have displayed it.
verses.textLatin: Gyravit cælum in circuitu gloriæ suæ: manus Excelsi aperuerunt illum.

verses.text: By his commandment he maketh the snow to fall apace, and sendeth forth swiftly the lightnings of his judgment.
verses.textLatin: Imperio suo acceleravit nivem, et accelerat coruscationes emittere judicii sui.

verses.text: Through this are the treasures opened, and the clouds fly out like birds.
verses.textLatin: Propterea aperti sunt thesauri, et evolaverunt nebulæ sicut aves.

verses.text: By his greatness he hath fixed the clouds, and the hailstones are broken.
verses.textLatin: In magnitudine sua posuit nubes, et confracti sunt lapides grandinis.

verses.text: At his sight shall the mountains be shaken, and at his will the south wind shall blow.
verses.textLatin: In conspectu ejus commovebuntur montes, et in voluntate ejus aspirabit notus.

verses.text: The noise of his thunder shall strike the earth, so doth the northern storm, and the whirlwind:
verses.textLatin: Vox tonitrui ejus verberavit terram, tempestas aquilonis, et congregatio spiritus:

verses.text: And as the birds lighting upon the earth, he scattereth snow, and the falling thereof, is as the coming down of locusts.
verses.textLatin: et sicut avis deponens ad sedendum, aspergit nivem, et sicut locusta demergens descensus ejus.

verses.text: The eye admireth at the beauty of the whiteness thereof, and the heart is astonished at the shower thereof.
verses.textLatin: Pulchritudinem candoris ejus admirabitur oculus, et super imbrem ejus expavescet cor.

verses.text: He shall pour frost as salt upon the earth: and when it freezeth, it shall become like the tops of thistles.
verses.textLatin: Gelu sicut salem effundet super terram: et dum gelaverit, fiet tamquam cacumina tribuli.

verses.text: The cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into crystal; upon every gathering together of waters it shall rest, and shall clothe the waters as a breastplate.
verses.textLatin: Frigidus ventus aquilo flavit, et gelavit crystallus ab aqua: super omnem congregationem aquarum requiescet, et sicut lorica induet se aquis:

verses.text: And it shall devour the mountains, and burn the wilderness, and consume all that is green as with fire.
verses.textLatin: et devorabit montes, et exuret desertum, et extinguet viride, sicut igne.

verses.text: A present remedy of all is the speedy coming of a cloud, and a dew that meeteth it, by the heat that cometh, shall overpower it.
verses.textLatin: Medicina omnium in festinatione nebulæ: et ros obvians ab ardore venienti humilem efficiet eum.

verses.text: At his word the wind is still, and with his thought he appeaseth the deep, and the Lord hath planted islands therein.
verses.textLatin: In sermone ejus siluit ventus, et cogitatione sua placavit abyssum: et plantavit in illa Dominus insulas.

verses.text: Let them that sail on the sea, tell the dangers thereof: and when we hear with our ears, we shall admire.
verses.textLatin: Qui navigant mare enarrent pericula ejus, et audientes auribus nostris admirabimur.

verses.text: There are great and wonderful works: a variety of beasts, and of all living things, and the monstrous creatures of whales.
verses.textLatin: Illic præclara opera et mirabilia, varia bestiarum genera, et omnium pecorum, et creatura belluarum.

verses.text: Through him is established the end of their journey, and by his word all things are regulated.
verses.textLatin: Propter ipsum confirmatus est itineris finis, et in sermone ejus composita sunt omnia.

verses.text: We shall say much, and yet shall want words: but the sum of our words is, He is all.
verses.textLatin: Multa dicemus, et deficiemus in verbis: consummatio autem sermonum ipse est in omnibus.

verses.text: What shall we be able to do to glorify him? for the Almighty himself is above all his works.
verses.textLatin: Gloriantes ad quid valebimus? ipse enim omnipotens super omnia opera sua.

verses.text: The Lord is terrible, and exceeding great, and his power is admirable.
verses.textLatin: Terribilis Dominus, et magnus vehementer, et mirabilis potentia ipsius.

verses.text: Glorify the Lord as much as ever you can, for he will yet far exceed, and his magnificence is wonderful.
verses.textLatin: Glorificantes Dominum quantumcumque potueritis, supervalebit enim adhuc: et admirabilis magnificentia ejus.

verses.text: Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can: for he is above all praise.
verses.textLatin: Benedicentes Dominum, exaltate illum quantum potestis: major enim est omni laude.

verses.text: When you exalt him put forth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can never go far enough.
verses.textLatin: Exaltantes eum, replemini virtute, ne laboretis, non enim comprehendetis.

verses.text: Who shall see him, and declare him? and who shall magnify him as he is from the beginning?
verses.textLatin: Quis videbit eum et enarrabit? et quis magnificabit eum sicut est ab initio?

verses.text: There are many things hidden from us that are greater than these: for we have seen but a few of his works.
verses.textLatin: Multa abscondita sunt majora his: pauca enim vidimus operum ejus.

verses.text: But the Lord hath made all things, and to the godly he hath given wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Omnia autem Dominus fecit, et pie agentibus dedit sapientiam.

verses.text: Let  us now praise men of renown, and our fathers in their generation.
verses.textLatin: Laudemus viros gloriosos, et parentes nostros in generatione sua.

verses.text: The Lord hath wrought great glory through his magnificence from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Multam gloriam fecit Dominus: magnificentia sua a sæculo.

verses.text: Such as have borne rule in their dominions, men of great power, and endued with their wisdom, shewing forth in the prophets the dignity of prophets,
verses.textLatin: Dominantes in potestatibus suis, homines magni virtute et prudentia sua præditi, nuntiantes in prophetis dignitatem prophetarum:

verses.text: And ruling over the present people, and by the strength of wisdom instructing the people in most holy words.
verses.textLatin: et imperantes in præsenti populo, et virtute prudentiæ populis sanctissima verba:

verses.text: Such as by their skill sought out musical tunes, and published canticles of the scriptures.
verses.textLatin: in peritia sua requirentes modos musicos, et narrantes carmina Scripturarum:

verses.text: Rich men in virtue, studying beautifulness: living at peace in their houses.
verses.textLatin: homines divites in virtute, pulchritudinis studium habentes, pacificantes in domibus suis.

verses.text: All these have gained glory in their generations, and were praised in their days.
verses.textLatin: Omnes isti in generationibus gentis suæ gloriam adepti sunt, et in diebus suis habentur in laudibus.

verses.text: They that were born of them have left a name behind them, that their praises might be related:
verses.textLatin: Qui de illis nati sunt reliquerunt nomen narrandi laudes eorum.

verses.text: And there are some, of whom there is no memorial: who are perished, as if they had never been: and are become as if they had never been born, and their children with them.
verses.textLatin: Et sunt quorum non est memoria: perierunt quasi qui non fuerint: et nati sunt quasi non nati, et filii ipsorum cum ipsis.

verses.text: But these were men of mercy, whose godly deeds have not failed:
verses.textLatin: Sed illi viri misericordiæ sunt, quorum pietates non defuerunt.

verses.text: Good things continue with their seed,
verses.textLatin: Cum semine eorum permanent bona:

verses.text: Their posterity are a holy inheritance, and their seed hath stood in the covenants.
verses.textLatin: hæreditas sancta nepotes eorum, et in testamentis stetit semen eorum:

verses.text: And their children for their sakes remain for ever: their seed and their glory shall not be forsaken.
verses.textLatin: et filii eorum propter illos usque in æternum manent: semen eorum et gloria eorum non derelinquetur.

verses.text: Their bodies are buried in peace, and their name liveth unto generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Corpora ipsorum in pace sepulta sunt, et nomen eorum vivit in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: Let the people shew forth their wisdom, and the church declare their praise.
verses.textLatin: Sapientiam ipsorum narrent populi, et laudem eorum nuntiet ecclesia.

verses.text: Henoch pleased God, and was translated into paradise, that he may give repentance to the nations.
verses.textLatin: Enoch placuit Deo, et translatus est in paradisum, ut det gentibus pœnitentiam.

verses.text: Noe was found perfect, just, and in the time of wrath he was made a reconciliation.
verses.textLatin: Noë inventus est perfectus, justus, et in tempore iracundiæ factus est reconciliatio.

verses.text: Therefore was there a remnant left to the earth, when the flood came.
verses.textLatin: Ideo dimissum est reliquum terræ, cum factum est diluvium.

verses.text: The covenants of the world were made with him, that all flesh should no more be destroyed with the flood.
verses.textLatin: Testamenta sæculi posita sunt apud illum, ne deleri possit diluvio omnis caro.

verses.text: Abraham was the great father of a multitude of nations, and there was not found the like to him in glory, who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him.
verses.textLatin: Abraham magnus pater multitudinis gentium, et non est inventus similis illi in gloria: qui conservavit legem Excelsi, et fuit in testamento cum illo.

verses.text: In his flesh he established the covenant, and in temptation he was found faithful.
verses.textLatin: In carne ejus stare fecit testamentum, et in tentatione inventus est fidelis.

verses.text: Therefore by an oath he gave him glory in his posterity, that he should increase as the dust of the earth,
verses.textLatin: Ideo jurejurando dedit illi gloriam in gente sua, crescere illum quasi terræ cumulum,

verses.text: And that he would exalt his seed as the stars, and they should inherit from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth.
verses.textLatin: et ut stellas exaltare semen ejus, et hæreditare illos a mari usque ad mare, et a flumine usque ad terminos terræ.

verses.text: And he did in like manner with Isaac for the sake of Abraham his father.
verses.textLatin: Et in Isaac eodem modo fecit, propter Abraham patrem ejus.

verses.text: The Lord gave him the blessing of all nations, and confirmed his covenant upon the head of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Benedictionem omnium gentium dedit illi Dominus, et testamentum confirmavit super caput Jacob.

verses.text: He acknowledged him in his blessings, and gave him an inheritance, and divided him his portion in twelve tribes.
verses.textLatin: Agnovit eum in benedictionibus suis, et dedit illi hæreditatem, et divisit illi partem in tribubus duodecim.

verses.text: And he preserved for him men of mercy, that found grace in the eyes of all flesh.
verses.textLatin: Et conservavit illi homines misericordiæ, invenientes gratiam in oculis omnis carnis.

verses.text: Moses  was beloved of God, and men: whose memory is in benediction.
verses.textLatin: Dilectus Deo et hominibus Moyses, cujus memoria in benedictione est.

verses.text: He made him like the saints in glory, and magnified him in the fear of his enemies, and with his words he made prodigies to cease.
verses.textLatin: Similem illum fecit in gloria sanctorum, et magnificavit eum in timore inimicorum, et in verbis suis monstra placavit.

verses.text: He glorified him in the sight of kings, and gave him commandments in the sight of his people, and shewed him his glory.
verses.textLatin: Glorificavit illum in conspectu regum, et jussit illi coram populo suo, et ostendit illi gloriam suam.

verses.text: He sanctified him in his faith, and meekness, and chose him out of all flesh.
verses.textLatin: In fide et lenitate ipsius sanctum fecit illum, et elegit eum ex omni carne.

verses.text: For he heard him, and his voice, and brought him into a cloud.
verses.textLatin: Audivit enim eum, et vocem ipsius, et induxit illum in nubem.

verses.text: And he gave him commandments before his face, and a law of life and instruction, that he might teach Jacob his covenant, and Israel his judgments.
verses.textLatin: Et dedit illi coram præcepta, et legem vitæ et disciplinæ, docere Jacob testamentum suum, et judicia sua Israël.

verses.text: He exalted Aaron his brother, and like to himself of the tribe of Levi:
verses.textLatin: Excelsum fecit Aaron fratrem ejus, et similem sibi, de tribu Levi.

verses.text: He made an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him the priesthood of the nation, and made him blessed in glory,
verses.textLatin: Statuit ei testamentum æternum, et dedit illi sacerdotium gentis, et beatificavit illum in gloria:

verses.text: And he girded him about with a glorious girdle, and clothed him with a robe of glory, and crowned him with majestic attire.
verses.textLatin: et circumcinxit eum zona gloriæ, et induit eum stolam gloriæ, et coronavit eum in vasis virtutis.

verses.text: He put upon him a garment to the feet, and breeches, and an ephod, and he compassed him with many little bells of gold all round about,
verses.textLatin: Circumpedes, et femoralia, et humerale posuit ei: et cinxit illum tintinnabulis aureis plurimis in gyro:

verses.text: That as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple, for a memorial to the children of his people.
verses.textLatin: dare sonitum in incessu suo, auditum facere sonitum in templo in memoriam filiis gentis suæ.

verses.text: He gave him a holy robe of gold, and blue, and purple, a woven work of a wise man, endued with judgment and truth:
verses.textLatin: Stolam sanctam auro, et hyacintho, et purpura, opus textile viri sapientis, judicio et veritate præditi:

verses.text: Of twisted scarlet the work of an artist, with precious stones cut and set in gold, and graven by the work of a lapidary for a memorial, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.textLatin: torto cocco opus artificis gemmis pretiosis figuratis in ligatura auri, et opere lapidarii sculptis, in memoriam secundum numerum tribuum Israël.

verses.text: And a crown of gold upon his mitre wherein was engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour: a work of power, and delightful to the eyes for its beauty.
verses.textLatin: Corona aurea super mitram ejus expressa signo sanctitatis, et gloria honoris: opus virtutis, et desideria oculorum ornata.

verses.text: Before him there were none so beautiful, even from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Sic pulchra ante ipsum non fuerunt talia usque ad originem.

verses.text: No stranger was ever clothed with them, but only his children alone, and his grandchildren for ever.
verses.textLatin: Non est indutus illa alienigena aliquis, sed tantum filii ipsius soli, et nepotes ejus per omne tempus.

verses.text: His sacrifices were consumed with fire every day.
verses.textLatin: Sacrificia ipsius consumpta sunt igne quotidie.

verses.text: Moses filled his hands and anointed him with holy oil.
verses.textLatin: Complevit Moyses manus ejus, et unxit illum oleo sancto.

verses.text: This was made to him for an everlasting testament, and to his seed as the days of heaven, to execute the office of the priesthood, and to have praise, and to glorify his people in his name.
verses.textLatin: Factum est illi in testamentum æternum, et semini ejus, sicut dies cæli, fungi sacerdotio, et habere laudem, et glorificare populum suum in nomine ejus.

verses.text: He chose him out of all men living, to offer sacrifice to God, incense, and a good savour, for a memorial to make reconciliation for his people:
verses.textLatin: Ipsum elegit ab omni vivente, offerre sacrificium Deo, incensum, et bonum odorem, in memoriam placare pro populo suo:

verses.text: And he gave him power in his commandments, in the covenants of his judgments, that he should teach Jacob his testimonies, and give light to Israel in his law.
verses.textLatin: et dedit illi in præceptis suis potestatem, in testamentis judiciorum: docere Jacob testimonia, et in lege sua lucem dare Israël.

verses.text: And strangers stood up against him, and through envy the men that were with Dathan and Abiron, compassed him about in the wilderness, and the congregation of Core in their wrath.
verses.textLatin: Quia contra illum steterunt alieni, et propter invidiam circumdederunt illum homines in deserto, qui erant cum Dathan et Abiron, et congregatio Core in iracundia.

verses.text: The Lord God saw and it pleased him not, and they were consumed in his wrathful indignation.
verses.textLatin: Vidit Dominus Deus, et non placuit illi, et consumpti sunt in impetu iracundiæ.

verses.text: He wrought wonders upon them, and consumed them with a flame of fire.
verses.textLatin: Fecit illis monstra, et consumpsit illos in flamma ignis.

verses.text: And he added glory to Aaron, and gave him an inheritance, and divided unto him the firstfruits of the increase of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et addidit Aaron gloriam, et dedit illi hæreditatem, et primitias frugum terræ divisit illi.

verses.text: He prepared them bread in the first place unto fulness: for the sacrifices also of the Lord they shall eat, which he gave to him, and to his seed.
verses.textLatin: Panem ipsis in primis paravit in satietatem: nam et sacrificia Domini edent, quæ dedit illi et semini ejus.
