verses.text: But he shall not inherit among the people in the land, and he hath no portion among the people: for he himself is his portion and inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Ceterum in terra gentes non hæreditabit, et pars non est illi in gente: ipse est enim pars ejus, et hæreditas.

verses.text: Phinees the son of Eleazar is the third in glory, by imitating him in the fear of the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Phinees, filius Eleazari, tertius in gloria est, imitando eum in timore Domini,

verses.text: And he stood up in the shameful fall of the people: in the goodness and readiness of his soul he appeased God for Israel.
verses.textLatin: et stare in reverentia gentis: in bonitate et alacritate animæ suæ placuit Deo pro Israël.

verses.text: Therefore he made to him a covenant of peace, to be the prince of the sanctuary, and of his people, that the dignity of priesthood should be to him and to his seed for ever.
verses.textLatin: Ideo statuit illi testamentum pacis, principem sanctorum et gentis suæ, ut sit illi et semini ejus sacerdotii dignitas in æternum.

verses.text: And a covenant to David the king, the son of Jesse of the tribe of Juda, an inheritance to him and to his seed, that he might give wisdom into our heart to judge his people in justice, that their good things might not be abolished, and he made their glory in their nation everlasting.
verses.textLatin: Et testamentum David regi filio Jesse de tribu Juda, hæreditas ipsi et semini ejus: ut daret sapientiam in cor nostrum, judicare gentem suam in justitia, ne abolerentur bona ipsorum: et gloriam ipsorum in gentem eorum æternam fecit.

verses.text: Valiant  in war was Jesus the son of Nave, who was successor of Moses among the prophets, who was great according to his name,
verses.textLatin: Fortis in bello Jesus Nave, successor Moysi in prophetis, qui fuit magnus secundum nomen suum,

verses.text: Very great for the saving the elect of God, to overthrow the enemies that rose up against them, that he might get the inheritance for Israel.
verses.textLatin: maximus in salutem electorum Dei, expugnare insurgentes hostes, ut consequeretur hæreditatem Israël.

verses.text: How great glory did he gain when he lifted up his hands, and stretched out swords against the cities?
verses.textLatin: Quam gloriam adeptus est in tollendo manus suas, et jactando contra civitates rhomphæas!

verses.text: Who before him hath so resisted? for the Lord himself brought the enemies.
verses.textLatin: Quis ante illum sic restitit? nam hostes ipse Dominus perduxit.

verses.text: Was not the sun stopped in his anger, and one day made as two?
verses.textLatin: An non in iracundia ejus impeditus est sol, et una dies facta est quasi duo?

verses.text: He called upon the most high Sovereign when the enemies assaulted him on every side, and the great and holy God heard him by hailstones of exceeding great force.
verses.textLatin: Invocavit Altissimum potentem, in oppugnando inimicos undique: et audivit illum magnus et sanctus Deus, in saxis grandinis virtutis valde fortis.

verses.text: He made a violent assault against the nation of his enemies, and in the descent he destroyed the adversaries.
verses.textLatin: Impetum fecit contra gentem hostilem, et in descensu perdidit contrarios:

verses.text: That the nations might know his power, that it is not easy to fight against God. And he followed the mighty one:
verses.textLatin: ut cognoscant gentes potentiam ejus, quia contra Deum pugnare non est facile. Et secutus est a tergo potentis:

verses.text: And in the days of Moses he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephone, in standing against the enemy, and withholding the people from sins, and appeasing the wicked murmuring.
verses.textLatin: et in diebus Moysi misericordiam fecit, ipse, et Caleb filius Jephone, stare contra hostem, et prohibere gentem a peccatis, et perfringere murmur malitiæ.

verses.text: And they two being appointed, were delivered out of the danger from among the number of six hundred thousand men on foot, to bring them into their inheritance, into the land that floweth with milk and honey.
verses.textLatin: Et ipsi duo constituti a periculo liberati sunt a numero sexcentorum millium peditum, inducere illos in hæreditatem, in terram quæ manat lac et mel.

verses.text: And the Lord gave strength also to Caleb, and his strength continued even to his old age, so that he went up to the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an inheritance:
verses.textLatin: Et dedit Dominus ipsi Caleb fortitudinem, et usque in senectutem permansit illi virtus, ut ascenderet in excelsum terræ locum, et semen ipsius obtinuit hæreditatem,

verses.text: That all the children of Israel might see, that it is good to obey the holy God.
verses.textLatin: ut viderent omnes filii Israël quia bonum est obsequi sancto Deo.

verses.text: Then all the judges, every one by name, whose heart was not corrupted: who turned not away from the Lord,
verses.textLatin: Et judices singuli suo nomine, quorum non est corruptum cor, qui non aversi sunt a Domino,

verses.text: That their memory might be blessed, and their bones spring up out of their place,
verses.textLatin: ut sit memoria illorum in benedictione, et ossa eorum pullulent de loco suo:

verses.text: And their name continue for ever, the glory of the holy men remaining unto their children.
verses.textLatin: et nomen eorum permaneat in æternum, permanens ad filios illorum, sanctorum virorum gloria.

verses.text: Samuel the prophet of the Lord, the beloved of the Lord his God, established a new government, and anointed princes over his people.
verses.textLatin: Dilectus a Domino Deo suo Samuel, propheta Domini, renovavit imperium, et unxit principes in gente sua.

verses.text: By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the God of Jacob beheld, and by his fidelity he was proved a prophet.
verses.textLatin: In lege Domini congregationem judicavit, et vidit Deus Jacob: et in fide sua probatus est propheta,

verses.text: And he was known to be faithful in his words, because he saw the God of light:
verses.textLatin: et cognitus est in verbis suis fidelis, quia vidit Deum lucis.

verses.text: And called upon the name of the Lord Almighty, in fighting against the enemies who beset him on every side, when he offered a lamb without blemish.
verses.textLatin: Et invocavit Dominum omnipotentem, in oppugnando hostes circumstantes undique, in oblatione agni inviolati.

verses.text: And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.
verses.textLatin: Et intonuit de cælo Dominus, et in sonitu magno auditam fecit vocem suam:

verses.text: And he crushed the princes of the Tyrians, and all the lords of the Philistines:
verses.textLatin: et contrivit principes Tyriorum, et omnes duces Philisthiim:

verses.text: And before the time of the end of his life in the world, he protested before the Lord, and his anointed: money, or any thing else, even to a shoe, he had not taken of any man, and no man did accuse him.
verses.textLatin: et ante tempus finis vitæ suæ et sæculi, testimonium præbuit in conspectu Domini et christi: pecunias et usque ad calceamenta ab omni carne non accepit, et non accusavit illum homo.

verses.text: And after this he slept, and he made known to the king, and shewed him the end of his life, and he lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy to blot out the wickedness of the nation.
verses.textLatin: Et post hoc dormivit: et notum fecit regi, et ostendit illi finem vitæ suæ: et exaltavit vocem suam de terra in prophetia, delere impietatem gentis.

verses.text: Then  Nathan the prophet arose in the days of David.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc surrexit Nathan, propheta in diebus David.

verses.text: And as the fat taken away from the flesh, so was David chosen from among the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et quasi adeps separatus a carne, sic David a filiis Israël.

verses.text: He played with lions as with lambs: and with bears he did in like manner as with the lambs of the flock, in his youth.
verses.textLatin: Cum leonibus lusit quasi cum agnis, et in ursis similiter fecit sicut in agnis ovium, in juventute sua.

verses.text: Did not he kill the giant, and take away reproach from his people?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non occidit gigantem, et abstulit opprobrium de gente?

verses.text: In lifting up his hand, with the stone in the sling he beat down the boasting of Goliath:
verses.textLatin: In tollendo manum, saxo fundæ dejecit exsultationem Goliæ:

verses.text: For he called upon the Lord the Almighty, and he gave strength in his right hand, to take away the mighty warrior, and to set up the horn of his nation.
verses.textLatin: nam invocavit Dominum omnipotentem, et dedit in dextera ejus tollere hominem fortem in bello, et exaltare cornu gentis suæ.

verses.text: So in ten thousand did he glorify him, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in offering to him a crown of glory:
verses.textLatin: Sic in decem millibus glorificavit eum: et laudavit eum in benedictionibus Domini, in offerendo illi coronam gloriæ:

verses.text: For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and extirpated the Philistines the adversaries unto this day: he broke their horn for ever.
verses.textLatin: contrivit enim inimicos undique, et extirpavit Philisthiim contrarios usque in hodiernum diem: contrivit cornu ipsorum usque in æternum.

verses.text: In all his works he gave thanks to the holy one, and to the most High, with words of glory.
verses.textLatin: In omni opere dedit confessionem Sancto, et Excelso in verbo gloriæ.

verses.text: With his whole heart he praised the Lord, and loved God that made him: and he gave him power against his enemies:
verses.textLatin: De omni corde suo laudavit Dominum: et dilexit Deum, qui fecit illum, et dedit illi contra inimicos potentiam:

verses.text: And he set singers before the altar, and by their voices he made sweet melody.
verses.textLatin: et stare fecit cantores contra altare, et in sono eorum dulces fecit modos.

verses.text: And to the festivals he added beauty, and set in order the solemn times even to the end of his life, that they should praise the holy name of the Lord, and magnify the holiness of God in the morning.
verses.textLatin: Et dedit in celebrationibus decus, et ornavit tempora usque ad consummationem vitæ, ut laudarent nomen sanctum Domini, et amplificarent mane Dei sanctitatem.

verses.text: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: and he gave him a covenant of the kingdom, and a throne of glory in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Dominus purgavit peccata ipsius, et exaltavit in æternum cornu ejus: et dedit illi testamentum regni, et sedem gloriæ in Israël.

verses.text: After him arose up a wise son, and for his sake he cast down all the power of the enemies.
verses.textLatin: Post ipsum surrexit filius sensatus, et propter illum dejecit omnem potentiam inimicorum.

verses.text: Solomon reigned in days of peace, and God brought all his enemies under him, that he might build a house in his name, and prepare a sanctuary for ever: O how wise wast thou in thy youth!
verses.textLatin: Salomon imperavit in diebus pacis, cui subjecit Deus omnes hostes, ut conderet domum in nomine suo, et pararet sanctitatem in sempiternum. Quemadmodum eruditus es in juventute tua,

verses.text: And thou wast filled as a river with wisdom, and thy soul covered the earth.
verses.textLatin: et impletus es, quasi flumen, sapientia, et terram retexit anima tua.

verses.text: And thou didst multiply riddles in parables: thy name went abroad to the islands far off, and thou wast beloved in thy peace.
verses.textLatin: Et replesti in comparationibus ænigmata: ad insulas longe divulgatum est nomen tuum, et dilectus es in pace tua.

verses.text: The countries wondered at thee for thy canticles, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations,
verses.textLatin: In cantilenis, et proverbiis, et comparationibus, et interpretationibus, miratæ sunt terræ:

verses.text: And at the name of the Lord God, whose surname is, God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et in nomine Domini Dei, cui est cognomen Deus Israël.

verses.text: Thou didst gather gold as copper, and didst multiply silver as lead,
verses.textLatin: Collegisti quasi auricalcum aurum, et ut plumbum complesti argentum:

verses.text: And thou didst bow thyself to women: and by thy body thou wast brought under subjection.
verses.textLatin: et inclinasti femora tua mulieribus: potestatem habuisti in corpore tuo.

verses.text: Thou hast stained thy glory, and defiled thy seed so as to bring wrath upon thy children, and to have thy folly kindled,
verses.textLatin: Dedisti maculam in gloria tua, et profanasti semen tuum, inducere iracundiam ad liberos tuos, et incitari stultitiam tuam:

verses.text: That thou shouldst make the kingdom to be divided, and out of Ephraim a rebellious kingdom to rule.
verses.textLatin: ut faceres imperium bipartitum, et ex Ephraim imperare imperium durum.

verses.text: But God will not leave off his mercy, and he will not destroy, nor abolish his own works, neither will he cut up by the roots the offspring of his elect: and he will not utterly take away the seed of him that loveth the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Deus autem non derelinquet misericordiam suam: et non corrumpet, nec delebit opera sua, neque perdet a stirpe nepotes electi sui, et semen ejus qui diligit Dominum non corrumpet.

verses.text: Wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and to David of the same stock.
verses.textLatin: Dedit autem reliquum Jacob, et David de ipsa stirpe.

verses.text: And Solomon had an end with his fathers.
verses.textLatin: Et finem habuit Salomon cum patribus suis.

verses.text: And he left behind him of his seed, the folly of the nation,
verses.textLatin: Et dereliquit post se de semine suo, gentis stultitiam,

verses.text: Even Roboam that had little wisdom, who turned away the people through his counsel:
verses.textLatin: et imminutum a prudentia, Roboam, qui avertit gentem consilio suo:

verses.text: And Jeroboam the son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin, and their sins were multiplied exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: et Jeroboam filium Nabat, qui peccare fecit Israël, et dedit viam peccandi Ephraim: et plurima redundaverunt peccata ipsorum.

verses.text: They removed them far away from their land.
verses.textLatin: Valde averterunt illos a terra sua.

verses.text: And they sought out all iniquities, till vengeance came upon them, and put an end to all their sins.
verses.textLatin: Et quæsivit omnes nequitias, usque dum perveniret ad illos defensio, et ab omnibus peccatis liberavit eos.

verses.text: And  Elias the prophet stood up, as a fire, and his word burnt like a torch.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit Elias propheta quasi ignis, et verbum ipsius quasi facula ardebat.

verses.text: He brought a famine upon them, and they that provoked him in their envy, were reduced to a small number, for they could not endure the commandments of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui induxit in illos famem: et irritantes illum invidia sua pauci facti sunt: non enim poterant sustinere præcepta Domini.

verses.text: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and he brought down fire from heaven thrice.
verses.textLatin: Verbo Domini continuit cælum, et dejecit de cælo ignem ter.

verses.text: Thus was Elias magnified in his wondrous works. And who can glory like to thee?
verses.textLatin: Sic amplificatus est Elias in mirabilibus suis. Et quis potest similiter sic gloriari tibi?

verses.text: Who raisedst up a dead man from below, from the lot of death, by the word of the Lord God.
verses.textLatin: qui sustulisti mortuum ab inferis de sorte mortis, in verbo Domini Dei:

verses.text: Who broughtest down kings to destruction, and brokest easily their power in pieces, and the glorious from their bed.
verses.textLatin: qui dejecisti reges ad pernicem, et confregisti facile potentiam ipsorum, et gloriosos de lecto suo:

verses.text: Who heardest judgment in Sina, and in Horeb the judgments of vengeance.
verses.textLatin: qui audis in Sina judicium, et in Horeb judicia defensionis:

verses.text: Who anointedst kings to penance, and madest prophets successors after thee.
verses.textLatin: qui ungis reges ad pœnitentiam, et prophetas facis successores post te:

verses.text: Who wast taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.
verses.textLatin: qui receptus es in turbine ignis, in curru equorum igneorum:

verses.text: Who art registered in the judgments of times to appease the wrath of the Lord, to reconcile the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: qui scriptus es in judiciis temporum, lenire iracundiam Domini, conciliare cor patris ad filium, et restituere tribus Jacob.

verses.text: Blessed are they that saw thee, and were honoured with thy friendship.
verses.textLatin: Beati sunt qui te viderunt, et in amicitia tua decorati sunt.

verses.text: For we live only in our life, but after death our name shall not be such.
verses.textLatin: Nam nos vita vivimus tantum: post mortem autem non erit tale nomen nostrum.

verses.text: Elias was indeed covered with the whirlwind, and his spirit was filled up in Eliseus: in his days he feared not the prince, and no man was more powerful than he.
verses.textLatin: Elias quidem in turbine tectus est, et in Eliseo completus est spiritus ejus: in diebus suis non pertimuit principem, et potentia nemo vicit illum:

verses.text: No word could overcome him, and after death his body prophesied.
verses.textLatin: nec superavit illum verbum aliquod, et mortuum prophetavit corpus ejus.

verses.text: In his life he did great wonders, and in death he wrought miracles.
verses.textLatin: In vita sua fecit monstra, et in morte mirabilia operatus est.

verses.text: For all this the people repented not, neither did they depart from their sins till they were cast out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus istis non pœnituit populus, et non recesserunt a peccatis suis, usque dum ejecti sunt de terra sua, et dispersi sunt in omnem terram:

verses.text: And there was left but a small people, and a prince in the house of David.
verses.textLatin: et relicta est gens perpauca, et princeps in domo David.

verses.text: Some of these did that which pleased God: but others committed many sins.
verses.textLatin: Quidam ipsorum fecerunt quod placeret Deo: alii autem multa commiserunt peccata.

verses.text: Ezechias fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof, and he digged a rock with iron, and made a well for water.
verses.textLatin: Ezechias munivit civitatem suam, et induxit in medium ipsius aquam: et fodit ferro rupem, et ædificavit ad aquam puteum.

verses.text: In his days Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabsaces, and lifted up his hand against them, and he stretched out his hand against Sion, and became proud through his power.
verses.textLatin: In diebus ipsius ascendit Sennacherib, et misit Rabsacen, et sustulit manum suam contra illos: et extulit manum suam in Sion, et superbus factus est potentia sua.

verses.text: Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they were in pain as women in travail.
verses.textLatin: Tunc mota sunt corda et manus ipsorum: et doluerunt quasi parturientes mulieres.

verses.text: And they called upon the Lord who is merciful, and spreading their hands, they lifted them up to heaven: and the holy Lord God quickly heard their voice.
verses.textLatin: Et invocaverunt Dominum misericordem, et expandentes manus suas extulerunt ad cælum: et Sanctus, Dominus Deus, audivit cito vocem ipsorum.

verses.text: He was not mindful of their sins, neither did he deliver them up to their enemies, but he purified them by the hand of Isaias, the holy prophet.
verses.textLatin: Non est commemoratus peccatorum illorum, neque dedit illos inimicis suis: sed purgavit eos in manu Isaiæ sancti prophetæ.

verses.text: He overthrew the army of the Assyrians, and the angel of the Lord destroyed them.
verses.textLatin: Dejecit castra Assyriorum, et contrivit illos angelus Domini:

verses.text: For Ezechias did that which pleased God, and walked valiantly in the way of David his father, which Isaias, the great prophet, and faithful in the sight of God, had commanded him.
verses.textLatin: nam fecit Ezechias quod placuit Deo, et fortiter ivit in via David patris sui, quam mandavit illi Isaias, propheta magnus, et fidelis in conspectu Dei.

verses.text: In his days the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king’s life.
verses.textLatin: In diebus ipsius retro rediit sol, et addidit regi vitam.

verses.text: With a great spirit he saw the things that are to come to pass at last, and comforted the mourners in Sion.
verses.textLatin: Spiritu magno vidit ultima, et consolatus est lugentes in Sion usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: He shewed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things before they came.
verses.textLatin: Ostendit futura, et abscondita antequam evenirent.

verses.text: The  memory of Josias is like the composition of a sweet smell made by the art of a perfumer:
verses.textLatin: Memoria Josiæ in compositionem odoris facta opus pigmentarii.

verses.text: His remembrance shall be sweet as honey in every mouth, and as music at a banquet of wine.
verses.textLatin: In omni ore quasi mel indulcabitur ejus memoria, et ut musica in convivio vini.

verses.text: He was directed by God unto the repentance of the nation, and he took away the abominations of wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Ipse est directus divinitus in pœnitentiam gentis, et tulit abominationes impietatis.

verses.text: And he directed his heart towards the Lord, and in the days of sinners he strengthened godliness.
verses.textLatin: Et gubernavit ad Dominum cor ipsius, et in diebus peccatorum corroboravit pietatem.

verses.text: Except David, and Ezechias and Josias, all committed sin.
verses.textLatin: Præter David et Ezechiam et Josiam, omnes peccatum commiserunt:

verses.text: For the kings of Juda forsook the law of the most High, and despised the fear of God.
verses.textLatin: nam reliquerunt legem Altissimi reges Juda, et contempserunt timorem Dei.

verses.text: So they gave their kingdom to others, and their glory to a strange nation,
verses.textLatin: Dederunt enim regnum suum aliis, et gloriam suam alienigenæ genti.

verses.text: They burnt the chosen city of holiness, and made the streets thereof desolate according to the prediction of Jeremias.
verses.textLatin: Incenderunt electam sanctitatis civitatem, et desertas fecerunt vias ipsius in manu Jeremiæ.

verses.text: For they treated him evil, who was consecrated a prophet from his mother’s womb, to overthrow, and pluck up, and destroy, and to build again, and renew.
verses.textLatin: Nam male tractaverunt illum qui a ventre matris consecratus est propheta, evertere, et eruere, et perdere, et iterum ædificare, et renovare:

verses.text: It was Ezechiel that saw the glorious vision, which was shewn him upon the chariot of cherubims.
verses.textLatin: Ezechiel, qui vidit conspectum gloriæ quam ostendit illi in curru cherubim.

verses.text: For he made mention of the enemies under the figure of rain, and of doing good to them that shewed right ways.
verses.textLatin: Nam commemoratus est inimicorum in imbre, benefacere illis qui ostenderunt rectas vias.

verses.text: And may the bones of the twelve prophets spring up out of their place: for they strengthened Jacob, and redeemed themselves by strong faith.
verses.textLatin: Et duodecim prophetarum ossa pullulent de loco suo: nam corroboraverunt Jacob, et redemerunt se in fide virtutis.

verses.text: How shall we magnify Zorobabel? for he was as a signet on the right hand;
verses.textLatin: Quomodo amplificemus Zorobabel? nam et ipse quasi signum in dextera manu:

verses.text: In like manner Jesus the son of Josedec who in their days built the house, and set up a holy temple to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
verses.textLatin: sic et Jesum filium Josedec, qui in diebus suis ædificaverunt domum, et exaltaverunt templum sanctum Domino, paratum in gloriam sempiternam.

verses.text: And let Nehemias be a long time remembered, who raised up for us our walls that were cast down, and set up the gates and the bars, who rebuilt our houses.
verses.textLatin: Et Nehemias in memoriam multi temporis, qui erexit nobis muros eversos, et stare fecit portas et seras, qui erexit domos nostras.

verses.text: No man was born upon earth like Henoch: for he also was taken up from the earth.
verses.textLatin: Nemo natus est in terra qualis Henoch, nam et ipse receptus est a terra:

verses.text: Nor as Joseph, who was a man born prince of his brethren, the support of his family, the ruler of his brethren, the stay of the people:
verses.textLatin: neque ut Joseph, qui natus est homo princeps fratrum, firmamentum gentis, rector fratrum, stabilimentum populi:

verses.text: And his bones were visited, and after death they prophesied.
verses.textLatin: et ossa ipsius visitata sunt, et post mortem prophetaverunt.

verses.text: Seth and Sem obtained glory among men: and above every soul Adam in the beginning,
verses.textLatin: Seth et Sem apud homines gloriam adepti sunt, et super omnem animam in origine Adam.

verses.text: Simon  the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life propped up the house, and in his days fortified the temple.
verses.textLatin: Simon, Oniæ filius, sacerdos magnus, qui in vita sua suffulsit domum, et in diebus suis corroboravit templum.

verses.text: By him also the height of the temple was founded, the double building and the high walls of the temple.
verses.textLatin: Templi etiam altitudo ab ipso fundata est, duplex ædificatio, et excelsi parietes templi.

verses.text: In his days the wells of water flowed out, and they were filled as the sea above measure.
verses.textLatin: In diebus ipsius emanaverunt putei aquarum, et quasi mare adimpleti sunt supra modum.

verses.text: He took care of his nation, and delivered it from destruction.
verses.textLatin: Qui curavit gentem suam, et liberavit eam a perditione:

verses.text: He prevailed to enlarge the city, and obtained glory in his conversation with the people: and enlarged the entrance of the house and the court.
verses.textLatin: qui prævaluit amplificare civitatem, qui adeptus est gloriam in conversatione gentis, et ingressum domus et atrii amplificavit.

verses.text: He shone in his days as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full.
verses.textLatin: Quasi stella matutina in medio nebulæ, et quasi luna plena, in diebus suis lucet:

verses.text: And as the sun when it shineth, so did he shine in the temple of God.
verses.textLatin: et quasi sol refulgens, sic ille effulsit in templo Dei.

verses.text: And as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds, and as the flower of roses in the days of the spring, and as the lilies that are on the brink of the water, and as the sweet smelling frankincense in the time of summer.
verses.textLatin: Quasi arcus refulgens inter nebulas gloriæ, et quasi flos rosarum in diebus vernis, et quasi lilia quæ sunt in transitu aquæ, et quasi thus redolens in diebus æstatis:

verses.text: As a bright fire, and frankincense burning in the fire.
verses.textLatin: quasi ignis effulgens, et thus ardens in igne:

verses.text: As a massy vessel of gold, adorned with every precious stone.
verses.textLatin: quasi vas auri solidum, ornatum omni lapide pretioso:

verses.text: As an olive tree budding forth, and a cypress tree rearing itself on high, when he put on the robe of glory, and was clothed with the perfection of power.
verses.textLatin: quasi oliva pullulans, et cypressus in altitudinem se extollens, in accipiendo ipsum stolam gloriæ, et vestiri eum in consummationem virtutis.

verses.text: When he went up to the holy altar, he honoured the vesture of holiness.
verses.textLatin: In ascensu altaris sancti gloriam dedit sanctitatis amictum.

verses.text: And when he took the portions out of the hands of the priests, he himself stood by the altar. And about him was the ring of his brethren: and as the cedar planted in mount Libanus,
verses.textLatin: In accipiendo autem partes de manu sacerdotum, et ipse stans juxta aram: et circa illum corona fratrum: quasi plantatio cedri in monte Libano,

verses.text: And as branches of palm trees, they stood round about him, and all the sons of Aaron in their glory.
verses.textLatin: sic circa illum steterunt quasi rami palmæ: et omnes filii Aaron in gloria sua.

verses.text: And the oblation of the Lord was in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel: and finishing his service, on the altar, to honour the offering of the most high King,
verses.textLatin: Oblatio autem Domini in manibus ipsorum coram omni synagoga Israël: et consummatione fungens in ara, amplificare oblationem excelsi Regis,

verses.text: He stretched forth his hand to make a libation, and offered of the blood of the grape.
verses.textLatin: porrexit manum suam in libatione, et libavit de sanguine uvæ.

verses.text: He poured out at the foot of the altar a divine odour to the most high Prince.
verses.textLatin: Effudit in fundamento altaris odorem divinum excelso Principi.

verses.text: Then the sons of Aaron shouted, they sounded with beaten trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard for a remembrance before God.
verses.textLatin: Tunc exclamaverunt filii Aaron, in tubis productilibus sonuerunt: et auditam fecerunt vocem magnam in memoriam coram Deo.

verses.text: Then all the people together made haste, and fell down to the earth upon their faces, to adore the Lord their God, and to pray to the Almighty God the most High.
verses.textLatin: Tunc omnis populus simul properaverunt, et ceciderunt in faciem super terram, adorare Dominum Deum suum, et dare preces omnipotenti Deo excelso.

verses.text: And the singers lifted up their voices, and in the great house the sound of sweet melody was increased.
verses.textLatin: Et amplificaverunt psallentes in vocibus suis, et in magna domo auctus est sonus suavitatis plenus.

verses.text: And the people in prayer besought the Lord the most High, until the worship of the Lord was perfected, and they had finished their office.
verses.textLatin: Et rogavit populus Dominum excelsum in prece, usque dum perfectus est honor Domini, et munus suum perfecerunt.

verses.text: Then coming down, he lifted up his hands over all the congregation of the children of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips, and to glory in his name:
verses.textLatin: Tunc descendens, manus suas extulit in omne congregationem filiorum Israël, dare gloriam Deo a labiis suis, et in nomine ipsius gloriari:

verses.text: And he repeated his prayer, willing to shew the power of God.
verses.textLatin: et iteravit orationem suam, volens ostendere virtutem Dei.

verses.text: And now pray ye to the God of all, who hath done great things in all the earth, who hath increased our days from our mother’s womb, and hath done with us according to his mercy.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc orate Deum omnium, qui magna fecit in omni terra, qui auxit dies nostros a ventre matris nostræ, et fecit nobiscum secundum suam misericordiam:

verses.text: May he grant us joyfulness of heart, and that there be peace in our days in Israel for ever:
verses.textLatin: det nobis jucunditatem cordis, et fieri pacem in diebus nostris in Israël per dies sempiternos:

verses.text: That Israel may believe that the mercy of God is with us, to deliver us in his days.
verses.textLatin: credere Israël nobiscum esse Dei misericordiam, ut liberet nos in diebus suis.

verses.text: There are two nations which my soul abhorreth: and the third is no nation, which I hate:
verses.textLatin: Duas gentes odit anima mea: tertia autem non est gens quam oderim:

verses.text: They that sit on mount Seir, and the Philistines, and the foolish people that dwell in Sichem.
verses.textLatin: qui sedent in monte Seir, et Philisthiim, et stultus populus qui habitat in Sichimis.

verses.text: Jesus the son of Sirach, of Jerusalem, hath written in this book the doctrine of wisdom and instruction, who renewed wisdom from his heart.
verses.textLatin: Doctrinam sapientiæ et disciplinæ scripsit in codice isto Jesus, filius Sirach, Jerosolymita, qui renovavit sapientiam de corde suo.

verses.text: Blessed is he that is conversant in these good things and he that layeth them up in his heart, shall be wise always.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui in istis versatur bonis: qui ponit illa in corde suo, sapiens erit semper.

verses.text: For if he do them, he shall be strong to do all things: because the light of God guideth his steps.
verses.textLatin: Si enim hæc fecerit, ad omnia valebit, quia lux Dei vestigium ejus est.

verses.text: A  PRAYER of Jesus the son of Sirach. I will give glory to thee, O Lord, O King, and I will praise thee, O God my Saviour.
verses.textLatin: Oratio Jesu filii Sirach. Confitebor tibi, Domine rex, et collaudabo te Deum salvatorem meum.

verses.text: I will give glory to thy name: for thou hast been a helper and protector to me.
verses.textLatin: Confitebor nomini tuo, quoniam adjutor et protector factus es mihi,

verses.text: And hast preserved my body from destruction, from the snare of an unjust tongue, and from the lips of them that forge lies, and in the sight of them that stood by, thou hast been my helper.
verses.textLatin: et liberasti corpus meum a perditione: a laqueo linguæ iniquæ, et a labiis operantium mendacium: et in conspectu astantium factus es mihi adjutor.

verses.text: And thou hast delivered me, according to the multitude of the mercy of thy name, from them that did roar, prepared to devour.
verses.textLatin: Et liberasti me, secundum multitudinem misericordiæ nominis tui, a rugientibus præparatis ad escam:

verses.text: Out of the hands of them that sought my life, and from the gates of afflictions, which compassed me about:
verses.textLatin: de manibus quærentium animam meam, et de portis tribulationum quæ circumdederunt me;

verses.text: From the oppression of the flame which surrounded me, and in the midst of the fire I was not burnt.
verses.textLatin: a pressura flammæ quæ circumdedit me, et in medio ignis non sum æstuatus;

verses.text: From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, from an unjust king, and from a slanderous tongue:
verses.textLatin: de altitudine ventris inferi, et a lingua coinquinata, et a verbo mendacii, a rege iniquo, et a lingua injusta.

verses.text: My soul shall praise the Lord even to death.
verses.textLatin: Laudabit usque ad mortem anima mea Dominum,

verses.text: And my life was drawing near to hell beneath.
verses.textLatin: et vita mea appropinquans erat in inferno deorsum.

verses.text: They compassed me on every side, and there was no one that would help me. I looked for the succour of men, and there was none.
verses.textLatin: Circumdederunt me undique, et non erat qui adjuvaret: respiciens eram ad adjutorium hominum, et non erat.

verses.text: I remembered thy mercy, O Lord, and thy works, which are from the beginning of the world.
verses.textLatin: Memoratus sum misericordiæ tuæ Domine, et operationis tuæ, quæ a sæculo sunt:

verses.text: How thou deliverest them that wait for thee, O Lord, and savest them out of the hands of the nations.
verses.textLatin: quoniam eruis sustinentes te, Domine, et liberas eos de manibus gentium.

verses.text: Thou hast exalted my dwelling place upon the earth and I have prayed for death to pass away.
verses.textLatin: Exaltasti super terram habitationem meam, et pro morte defluente deprecatus sum.

verses.text: I called upon the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud without help.
verses.textLatin: Invocavi Dominum patrem Domini mei, ut non derelinquat me in die tribulationis meæ, et in tempore superborum, sine adjutorio.

verses.text: I will praise thy name continually, and will praise it with thanksgiving, and my prayer was heard.
verses.textLatin: Laudabo nomen tuum assidue, et collaudabo illud in confessione: et exaudita est oratio mea,

verses.text: And thou hast saved me from destruction, and hast delivered me from the evil time.
verses.textLatin: et liberasti me de perditione, et eripuisti me de tempore iniquo.

verses.text: Therefore I will give thanks, and praise thee, and bless the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Propterea confitebor, et laudem dicam tibi, et benedicam nomini Domini.

verses.text: When I was yet young, before I wandered about, I sought for wisdom openly in my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Cum adhuc junior essem, priusquam oberrarem, quæsivi sapientiam palam in oratione mea.

verses.text: I prayed for her before the temple, and unto the very end I will seek after her, and she flourished as a grape soon ripe.
verses.textLatin: Ante templum postulabam pro illis, et usque in novissimis inquiram eam: et effloruit tamquam præcox uva.

verses.text: My heart delighted in her, my foot walked in the right way, from my youth up I sought after her.
verses.textLatin: Lætatum est cor meum in ea: ambulavit pes meus iter rectum: a juventute mea investigabam eam.

verses.text: I bowed down my ear a little, and received her.
verses.textLatin: Inclinavi modico aurem meam, et excepi illam.

verses.text: I found much wisdom in myself, and I profited much therein.
verses.textLatin: Multam inveni in meipso sapientiam, et multum profeci in ea.

verses.text: To him that giveth me wisdom, will I give glory.
verses.textLatin: Danti mihi sapientiam dabo gloriam:

verses.text: For I have determined to follow her: I have had a zeal for good, and shall not be confounded.
verses.textLatin: consiliatus sum enim ut facerem illam. Zelatus sum bonum, et non confundar.

verses.text: My soul hath wrestled for her, and in doing it I have been confirmed.
verses.textLatin: Colluctata est anima mea in illa, et in faciendo eam confirmatus sum.

verses.text: I stretched forth my hands on high, and I bewailed my ignorance of her.
verses.textLatin: Manus meas extendi in altum, et insipientiam ejus luxi;

verses.text: I directed my soul to her, and in knowledge I found her.
verses.textLatin: animam meam direxi ad illam, et in agnitione inveni eam.

verses.text: I possessed my heart with her from the beginning: therefore I shall not be forsaken.
verses.textLatin: Possedi cum ipsa cor ab initio: propter hoc, non derelinquar.

verses.text: My entrails were troubled in seeking her: therefore shall I possess a good possession.
verses.textLatin: Venter meus conturbatus est quærendo illam: propterea bonam possidebo possessionem.

verses.text: The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward: and with it I will praise him.
verses.textLatin: Dedit mihi Dominus linguam mercedem meam, et in ipsa laudabo eum.

verses.text: Draw near to me, ye unlearned, and gather yourselves together into the house of discipline.
verses.textLatin: Appropiate ad me, indocti, et congregate vos in domum disciplinæ.

verses.text: Why are ye slow? and what do you say of these things? your souls are exceeding thirsty.
verses.textLatin: Quid adhuc retardatis? et quid dicitis in his? animæ vestræ sitiunt vehementer.

verses.text: I have opened my mouth, and have spoken: buy her for yourselves without silver,
verses.textLatin: Aperui os meum, et locutus sum: Comparate vobis sine argento,

verses.text: And submit your neck to the yoke, and let your soul receive discipline: for she is near at hand to be found.
verses.textLatin: et collum vestrum subjicite jugo: et suscipiat anima vestra disciplinam: in proximo est enim invenire eam.

verses.text: Behold with your eyes how I have laboured a little, and have found much rest to myself.
verses.textLatin: Videte oculis vestris, quia modicum laboravi, et inveni mihi multam requiem.

verses.text: Receive ye discipline as a great sum of money, and possess abundance of gold by her.
verses.textLatin: Assumite disciplinam in multo numero argenti, et copiosum aurum possidete in ea.

verses.text: Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and you shall not be confounded in his praise.
verses.textLatin: Lætetur anima vestra in misericordia ejus, et non confundemini in laude ipsius.

verses.text: The  vision of Isaias the son of Amos, which he saw concerning Juda and Jerusalem in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Visio Isaiæ, filii Amos, quam vidit super Judam et Jerusalem, in diebus Oziæ, Joathan, Achaz, et Ezechiæ, regum Juda.

verses.text: Hear, O ye heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord hath spoken. I have brought up children, and exalted them: but they have despised me.
verses.textLatin: Audite, cæli, et auribus percipe, terra, quoniam Dominus locutus est. Filios enutrivi, et exaltavi; ipsi autem spreverunt me.

verses.text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood.
verses.textLatin: Cognovit bos possessorem suum, et asinus præsepe domini sui; Israël autem me non cognovit, et populus meus non intellexit.

verses.text: Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a wicked seed, ungracious children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backwards.
verses.textLatin: Væ genti peccatrici, populo gravi iniquitate, semini nequam, filiis sceleratis! dereliquerunt Dominum; blasphemaverunt Sanctum Israël; abalienati sunt retrorsum.

verses.text: For what shall I strike you any more, you that increase transgression? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart is sad.
verses.textLatin: Super quo percutiam vos ultra, addentes prævaricationem? omne caput languidum, et omne cor mœrens.

verses.text: From the sole of the foot unto the top of the head, there is no soundness therein: wounds and bruises and swelling sores: they are not bound up, nor dressed, nor fomented with oil.
verses.textLatin: A planta pedis usque ad verticem, non est in eo sanitas; vulnus, et livor, et plaga tumens, non est circumligata, nec curata medicamine, neque fota oleo.

verses.text: Your land is desolate, your cities are burnt with fire: your country strangers devour before your face, and it shall be desolate as when wasted by enemies.
verses.textLatin: Terra vestra deserta; civitates vestræ succensæ igni: regionem vestram coram vobis alieni devorant, et desolabitur sicut in vastitate hostili.

verses.text: And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard, and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, and as a city that is laid waste.
verses.textLatin: Et derelinquetur filia Sion ut umbraculum in vinea, et sicut tugurium in cucumerario, et sicut civitas quæ vastatur.

verses.text: Except the Lord of hosts had left us seed, we had been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrha.
verses.textLatin: Nisi Dominus exercituum reliquisset nobis semen, quasi Sodoma fuissemus, et quasi Gomorrha similes essemus.

verses.text: Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give ear to the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrha.
verses.textLatin: Audite verbum Domini, principes Sodomorum; percipite auribus legem Dei nostri, populus Gomorrhæ.

verses.text: To what purpose do you offer me the multitude of your victims, saith the Lord? I am full, I desire not holocausts of rams, and fat of fatlings, and blood of calves, and lambs, and buck goats.
verses.textLatin: Quo mihi multitudinem victimarum vestrarum? dicit Dominus. Plenus sum: holocausta arietum, et adipem pinguium, et sanguinem vitulorum et agnorum et hircorum, nolui.

verses.text: When you came to appear before me, who required these things at your hands, that you should walk in my courts?
verses.textLatin: Cum veniretis ante conspectum meum, quis quæsivit hæc de manibus vestris, ut ambularetis in atriis meis?

verses.text: Offer sacrifice no more in vain: incense is an abomination to me. The new moons, and the sabbaths, and other festivals I will not abide, your assemblies are wicked.
verses.textLatin: Ne offeratis ultra sacrificium frustra: incensum abominatio est mihi. Neomeniam et sabbatum, et festivitates alias, non feram; iniqui sunt cœtus vestri.

verses.text: My soul hateth your new moons, and your solemnities: they are become troublesome to me, I am weary of bearing them.
verses.textLatin: Calendas vestras, et solemnitates vestras odivit anima mea: facta sunt mihi molesta; laboravi sustinens.

verses.text: And when you stretch forth your hands, I will turn away my eyes from you: and when you multiply prayer, I will not hear: for your hands are full of blood.
verses.textLatin: Et cum extenderitis manus vestras, avertam oculos meos a vobis, et cum multiplicaveritis orationem, non exaudiam: manus enim vestræ sanguine plenæ sunt.

verses.text: Wash yourselves, be clean, take away the evil of your devices from my eyes: cease to do perversely,
verses.textLatin: Lavamini, mundi estote; auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis: quiescite agere perverse,

verses.text: Learn to do well: seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge for the fatherless, defend the widow.
verses.textLatin: discite benefacere; quærite judicium, subvenite oppresso, judicate pupillo, defendite viduam.

verses.text: And then come, and accuse me, saith the Lord: if your sins be as scarlet, they shall be made as white as snow: and if they be red as crimson, they shall be white as wool.
verses.textLatin: Et venite, et arguite me, dicit Dominus. Si fuerint peccata vestra ut coccinum, quasi nix dealbabuntur; et si fuerint rubra quasi vermiculus, velut lana alba erunt.

verses.text: If you be willing, and will hearken to me, you shall eat the good things of the land.
verses.textLatin: Si volueritis, et audieritis me, bona terræ comeditis.

verses.text: But if you will not, and will provoke me to wrath: the sword shall devour you because the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.
verses.textLatin: Quod si nolueritis, et me ad iracundiam provocaveritis, gladius devorabit vos, quia os Domini locutum est.

verses.text: How is the faithful city, that was full of judgment, become a harlot? justice dwelt in it, but now murderers.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo facta est meretrix civitas fidelis, plena judicii? justitia habitavit in ea, nunc autem homicidæ.

verses.text: Thy silver is turned into dross: thy wine is mingled with water.
verses.textLatin: Argentum tuum versum est in scoriam; vinum tuum mistum est aqua.

verses.text: Thy princes are faithless, companions of thieves: they all love bribes, they run after rewards. They judge not for the fatherless: and the widow’s cause cometh not in to them.
verses.textLatin: Principes tui infideles, socii furum. Omnes diligunt munera, sequuntur retributiones. Pupillo non judicant, et causa viduæ non ingreditur ad illos.

verses.text: Therefore saith the Lord the God of hosts, the mighty one of Israel: Ah! I will comfort myself over my adversaries: and I will be revenged of my enemies.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc ait Dominus, Deus exercituum, Fortis Israël: Heu! consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis.

verses.text: And I will turn my hand to thee, and I will clean purge away thy dross, and I will take away all thy tin.
verses.textLatin: Et convertam manum meam ad te, et excoquam ad puram scoriam tuam, et auferam omne stannum tuum.

verses.text: And I will restore thy judges as they were before, and thy counsellors as of old. After this thou shalt be called the city of the just, a faithful city.
verses.textLatin: Et restituam judices tuos ut fuerunt prius, et consiliarios tuos sicut antiquitus; post hæc vocaberis civitas justi, urbs fidelis.

verses.text: Sion shall be redeemed in judgment, and they shall bring her back in justice.
verses.textLatin: Sion in judicio redimetur, et reducent eam in justitia.

verses.text: And he shall destroy the wicked, and the sinners together: and they that have forsaken the Lord, shall be consumed.
verses.textLatin: Et conteret scelestos, et peccatores simul; et qui dereliquerunt Dominum consumentur.

verses.text: For they shall be confounded for the idols, to which they have sacrificed: and you shall be ashamed of the gardens which you have chosen.
verses.textLatin: Confundentur enim ab idolis quibus sacrificaverunt, et erubescetis super hortis quos elegeratis,

verses.text: When you shall be as an oak with the leaves falling off, and as a garden without water.
verses.textLatin: cum fueritis velut quercus defluentibus foliis, et velut hortus absque aqua.

verses.text: And your strength shall be as the ashes of tow, and your work as a spark: and both shall burn together, and there shall be none to quench it.
verses.textLatin: Et erit fortitudo vestra ut favilla stuppæ, et opus vestrum quasi scintilla, et succendetur utrumque simul, et non erit qui extinguat.

verses.text: The  word that Isaias the son of Amos saw, concerning Juda and Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Verbum quod vidit Isaias, filius Amos, super Juda et Jerusalem.

verses.text: And in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all nations shall flow unto it.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in novissimis diebus: præparatus mons domus Domini in vertice montium, et elevabitur super colles; et fluent ad eum omnes gentes,

verses.text: And many people shall go, and say: Come and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et ibunt populi multi, et dicent: Venite, et ascendamus ad montem Domini, et ad domum Dei Jacob; et docebit nos vias suas, et ambulabimus in semitis ejus, quia de Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem.

verses.text: And he shall judge the Gentiles, and rebuke many people: and they shall turn their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into sickles: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they be exercised any more to war.
verses.textLatin: Et judicabit gentes, et arguet populos multos; et conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces. Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium.

verses.text: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Domus Jacob, venite, et ambulemus in lumine Domini.

verses.text: For thou hast cast off thy people, the house of Jacob: because they are filled as in times past, and have had soothsayers as the Philistines, and have adhered to strange children.
verses.textLatin: Projecisti enim populum tuum, domum Jacob, quia repleti sunt ut olim, et augeres habuerunt ut Philisthiim, et pueris alienis adhæserunt.

verses.text: Their land is filled with silver and gold: and there is no end of their treasures.
verses.textLatin: Repleta est terra argento et auro, et non est finis thesaurorum ejus.

verses.text: And their land is filled with horses: and their chariots are innumerable. Their land also is full of idols: they have adored the work of their own hands, which their own fingers have made.
verses.textLatin: Et repleta est terra ejus equis, et innumerabiles quadrigæ ejus. Et repleta est terra ejus idolis; opus manuum suarum adoraverunt, quod fecerunt digiti eorum.

verses.text: And man hath bowed himself down, and man hath been debased: therefore forgive them not.
verses.textLatin: Et incurvavit se homo, et humiliatus est vir; ne ergo dimittas eis.

verses.text: Enter thou into the rock, and hide thee in the pit from the face of the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty.
verses.textLatin: Ingredere in petram, et abscondere in fossa humo a facie timoris Domini, et a gloria majestatis ejus.

verses.text: The lofty eyes of man are humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be made to stoop: and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
verses.textLatin: Oculi sublimes hominis humiliati sunt, et incurvabitur altitudo virorum; exaltabitur autem Dominus solus in die illa.

verses.text: Because the day of the Lord of hosts shall be upon every one that is proud and highminded, and upon every one that is arrogant, and he shall be humbled.
verses.textLatin: Quia dies Domini exercituum super omnem superbum, et excelsum, et super omnem arrogantem, et humiliabitur;

verses.text: And upon all the tall and lofty cedars of Libanus, and upon all the oaks of Basan.
verses.textLatin: et super omnes cedros Libani sublimes et erectas, et super omnes quercus Basan,

verses.text: And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the elevated hills.
verses.textLatin: et super omnes montes excelsos, et super omnes colles elevatos,

verses.text: And upon every high tower, and every fenced wall.
verses.textLatin: et super omnem turrim excelsam, et super omnem murum munitum,

verses.text: And upon all the ships of Tharsis, and upon all that is fair to behold.
verses.textLatin: et super omnes naves Tharsis, et super omne quod visu pulchrum est,

verses.text: And the loftiness of men shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be humbled, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
verses.textLatin: et incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum, et elevabitur Dominus solus in die illa;

verses.text: And idols shall be utterly destroyed.
verses.textLatin: et idola penitus conterentur;

verses.text: And they shall go into the holes of rocks, and into the caves of the earth from the face of the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall rise up to strike the earth.
verses.textLatin: et introibunt in speluncas petrarum, et in voragines terræ, a facie formidinis Domini et a gloria majestatis ejus, cum surrexerit percutere terram.

verses.text: In that day a man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which he had made for himself to adore, moles and bats.
verses.textLatin: In die illa projiciet homo idola argenti sui, et simulacra auri sui, quæ fecerat sibi ut adoraret, talpas et vespertiliones.

verses.text: And he shall go into the clefts of rocks, and into the holes of stones from the face of the fear of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall rise up to strike the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et ingreditur scissuras petrarum et in cavernas saxorum, a facie formidinis Domini, et a gloria majestatis ejus, cum surrexerit percutere terram.

verses.text: Cease ye therefore from the man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for he is reputed high.
verses.textLatin: Quiescite ergo ab homine, cujus spiritus in naribus ejus est, quia excelsus reputatus est ipse.

verses.text: For  behold the sovereign the Lord of hosts shall take away from Jerusalem, and from Juda the valiant and the strong, the whole strength of bread, and the whole strength of water.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim Dominator, Dominus exercituum, auferet a Jerusalem et a Juda validum et fortem, omne robur panis, et omne robor aquæ;

verses.text: The strong man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the cunning man, and the ancient.
verses.textLatin: fortem, et virum bellatorem, judicem, et prophetam, et ariolum, et senem;

verses.text: The captain over fifty, and the honourable in countenance, and the counsellor, and the architect, and the skilful in eloquent speech.
verses.textLatin: principem super quinquaginta, et honorabilem vultu et consiliarium, et sapientem de architectis, et prudentem eloquii mystici.

verses.text: And I will give children to be their princes, and the effeminate shall rule over them.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo pueros principes eorum, et effeminati dominabuntur eis;

verses.text: And the people shall rush one upon another, and every man against his neighbour: the child shall make a tumult against the ancient, and the base against the honourable.
verses.textLatin: et irruet populus, vir ad virum, et unusquisque ad proximum suum; tumultuabitur puer contra senem, et ignobilis contra nobilem.

verses.text: For a man shall take hold of his brother, one of the house of his father, saying: Thou hast a garment, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand.
verses.textLatin: Apprehendet enim vir fratrem suum, domesticum patris sui: Vestimentum tibi est, princeps esto noster, ruina autem hæc sub manu tua.

verses.text: In that day he shall answer, saying: I am no healer, and in my house there is no bread, nor clothing: make me not ruler of the people.
verses.textLatin: Respondebit in die illa, dicens: Non sum medicus, et in domo mea non est panis neque vestimentum: nolite constituere me principem populi.

verses.text: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Juda is fallen: because their tongue, and their devices are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his majesty.
verses.textLatin: Ruit enim Jerusalem, et Judas concidit, quia lingua eorum et adinventiones eorum contra Dominum, ut provocarent oculos majestatis ejus.

verses.text: The shew of their countenance hath answered them: and they have proclaimed abroad their sin as Sodom, and they have not hid it: woe to their souls, for evils are rendered to them.
verses.textLatin: Agnitio vultus eorum respondit eis; et peccatum suum quasi Sodoma prædicaverunt, nec absconderunt. Væ animæ eorum, quoniam reddita sunt eis mala!

verses.text: Say to the just man that it is well, for he shall eat the fruit of his doings.
verses.textLatin: Dicite justo quoniam bene, quoniam fructum adinventionum suarum comedet.

verses.text: Woe to the wicked unto evil: for the reward of his hands shall be given him.
verses.textLatin: Væ impio in malum! retributio enim manuum ejus fiet ei.

verses.text: As for my people, their oppressors have stripped them, and women have ruled over them. O my people, they that call thee blessed, the same deceive thee, and destroy the way of thy steps.
verses.textLatin: Populum meum exactores sui spoliaverunt, et mulieres dominatæ sunt eis. Popule meus, qui te beatum dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, et viam gressuum tuorum dissipant.

verses.text: The Lord standeth up to judge, and he standeth to judge the people.
verses.textLatin: Stat ad judicandum Dominus, et stat ad judicandos populos.

verses.text: The Lord will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and its princes: for you have devoured the vineyard, and the spoil of the poor is in your house.
verses.textLatin: Dominus ad judicium veniet cum senibus populi sui, et principibus ejus; vos enim depasti estis vineam, et rapina pauperis in domo vestra.

verses.text: Why do you consume my people, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord the God of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Quare atteritis populum meum, et facies pauperum commolitis? dicit Dominus Deus exercituum.

verses.text: And the Lord said: Because the daughters of Sion are haughty, and have walked with stretched out necks, and wanton glances of their eyes, and made a noise as they walked with their feet and moved in a set pace:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus: Pro eo quod elevatæ sunt filiæ Sion, et ambulaverunt extento collo, et nutibus oculorum ibant, et plaudebant, ambulabant pedibus suis, et composito gradu incedebant;

verses.text: The Lord will make bald the crown of the head of the daughters of Sion, and the Lord will discover their hair.
verses.textLatin: decalvabit Dominus verticem filiarum Sion, et Dominus crinem earum nudabit.

verses.text: In that day the Lord will take away the ornaments of shoes, and little moons,
verses.textLatin: In die illa auferet Dominus ornamentum calceamentum,

verses.text: And chains and necklaces, and bracelets, and bonnets,
verses.textLatin: et lunulas, et torques, et monilia, et armillas, et mitras,

verses.text: And bodkins, and ornaments of the legs, and tablets, and sweet balls, and earrings,
verses.textLatin: et discriminalia, et periscelidas, et murenulas, et olfactoriola, et inaures,

verses.text: And rings, and jewels hanging on the forehead,
verses.textLatin: et annulos, et gemmas in fronte pendentes,

verses.text: And changes of apparel, and short cloaks, and fine linen, and crisping pins,
verses.textLatin: et mutatoria, et palliola, et linteamina, et acus,

verses.text: And looking-glasses, and lawns, and headbands, and fine veils.
verses.textLatin: et specula, et sindones, et vittas, et theristra.

verses.text: And instead of a sweet smell there shall be stench, and instead of a girdle, a cord, and instead of curled hair, baldness, and instead of a stomacher, haircloth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit pro suavi odore fœtor, et pro zona funiculus, et pro crispanti crine calvitium, et pro fascia pectorali cilicium.

verses.text: Thy fairest men also shall fall by the sword, and thy valiant ones in battle.
verses.textLatin: Pulcherrimi quoque viri tui gladio cadent, et fortes tui in prælio.

verses.text: And her gates shall lament and mourn, and she shall sit desolate on the ground.
verses.textLatin: Et mœrebunt atque lugebunt portæ ejus, et desolata in terra sedebit.

verses.text: And  in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying: We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, take away our reproach.
verses.textLatin: Et apprehendent septem mulieres virum unum in die illa, dicentes: Panem nostrum comedemus, et vestimentis nostris operiemur: tantummodo invocetur nomen tuum super nos; aufer opprobrium nostrum.

verses.text: In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth shall be high, and a great joy to them that shall have escaped of Israel.
verses.textLatin: In die illa, erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria, et fructus terræ sublimis, et exsultatio his qui salvati fuerint de Israël.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall be left in Sion, and that shall remain in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, every one that is written in life in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: omnis qui relictus fuerit in Sion, et residuus in Jerusalem, Sanctus vocabitur, omnis qui scriptus est in vita in Jerusalem.

verses.text: If the Lord shall wash away the filth of the daughters of Sion, and shall wash away the blood of Jerusalem out of the midst thereof, by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
verses.textLatin: Si abluerit Dominus sordes filiarum Sion, et sanguinem Jerusalem laverit de medio ejus, in spiritu judicii, et spiritu ardoris.

verses.text: And the Lord will create upon every place of mount Sion, and where he is called upon, a cloud by day, and a smoke and the brightness of a flaming fire in the night: for over all the glory shall be a protection.
verses.textLatin: Et creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Sion, et ubi invocatus est, nubem per diem et fumum, et splendorem ignis flammantis in nocte: super omnem enim gloriam protectio.

verses.text: And there shall be a tabernacle for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a security and covert from the whirlwind, and from rain.
verses.textLatin: Et tabernaculum erit in umbraculum, diei ab æstu, et in securitatem et absconsionem a turbine et a pluvia.

verses.text: I will sing to my beloved the canticle of my cousin concerning his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a hill in a fruitful place.
verses.textLatin: Cantabo dilecto meo canticum patruelis mei vineæ suæ. Vinea facta est dilecto meo in cornu filio olei.

verses.text: And he fenced it in, and picked the stones out of it, and planted it with the choicest vines, and built a tower in the midst thereof, and set up a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.
verses.textLatin: Et sepivit eam, et lapides elegit ex illa, et plantavit eam electam; et ædificavit turrim in medio ejus, et torcular exstruxit in ea; et exspectavit ut faceret uvas, et fecit labruscas.

verses.text: And now, O ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and ye men of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, habitatores Jerusalem et viri Juda, judicate inter me et vineam meam.

verses.text: What is there that I ought to do more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it? was it that I looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it hath brought forth wild grapes?
verses.textLatin: Quid est quod debui ultra facere vineæ meæ, et non feci ei? an quod exspectavi ut faceret uvas, et fecit labruscas?

verses.text: And now I will shew you what I will do to my vineyard. I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be wasted: I will break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc ostendam vobis quid ego faciam vineæ meæ: auferam sepem ejus, et erit in direptionem; diruam maceriam ejus, et erit in conculcationem.

verses.text: And I will make it desolate: it shall not be pruned, and it shall not be digged: but briers and thorns shall come up: and I will command the clouds to rain no rain upon it.
verses.textLatin: Et ponam eam desertam; non putabitur et non fodietur: et ascendent vepres et spinæ, et nubibus mandabo ne pluant super eam imbrem.

verses.text: For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel: and the man of Juda, his pleasant plant: and I looked that he should do judgment, and behold iniquity: and do justice, and behold a cry.
verses.textLatin: Vinea enim Domini exercituum domus Israël est; et vir Juda germen ejus delectabile: et exspectavi ut faceret judicium, et ecce iniquitas; et justitiam, et ecce clamor.

verses.text: Woe to you that join house to house and lay field to field, even to the end of the place: shall you alone dwell in the midst of the earth?
verses.textLatin: Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulatis usque ad terminum loci! Numquid habitabitis vos soli in medio terræ?

verses.text: These things are in my ears, saith the Lord of hosts: Unless many great and fair houses shall become desolate, without an inhabitant.
verses.textLatin: In auribus meis sunt hæc, dicit Dominus exercituum; nisi domus multæ desertæ fuerint, grandes et pulchræ, absque habitatore.

verses.text: For ten acres of vineyard shall yield one little measure, and thirty bushels of seed shall yield three bushels.
verses.textLatin: Decem enim jugera vinearum facient lagunculam unam, et triginta modii sementis facient modios tres.

verses.text: Woe to you that rise up early in the morning to follow drunkenness, and to drink till the evening, to be inflamed with wine.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui consurgitis mane ad ebrietatem sectandam, et potandum usque ad vesperam, ut vino æstuetis!

verses.text: The harp, and the lyre, and the timbrel, and the pipe, and wine are in your feasts: and the work of the Lord you regard not, nor do you consider the works of his hands.
verses.textLatin: Cithara, et lyra, et tympanum, et tibia, et vinum in conviviis vestris; et opus Domini non respicitis, nec opera manuum ejus consideratis.

verses.text: Therefore is my people led away captive, because they had not knowledge, and their nobles have perished with famine, and their multitude were dried up with thirst.
verses.textLatin: Propterea captivus ductus est populus meus, quia non habuit scientiam, et nobiles ejus interierunt fame, et multitudo ejus siti exaruit.

verses.text: Therefore hath hell enlarged her soul, and opened her mouth without any bounds, and their strong ones, and their people, and their high and glorious ones shall go down into it.
verses.textLatin: Propterea dilatavit infernus animam suam, et aperuit os suum absque ullo termino; et descendent fortes ejus, et populus ejus, et sublimes gloriosique ejus, ad eum.

verses.text: And man shall be brought down, and man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be brought low.
verses.textLatin: Et incurvabitur homo, et humiliabitur vir, et oculi sublimium deprimentur.

verses.text: And the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy God shall be sanctified in justice.
verses.textLatin: Et exaltabitur Dominus exercituum in judicio; et Deus sanctus sanctificabitur in justitia.

verses.text: And the lambs shall feed according to their order, and strangers shall eat the deserts turned into fruitfulness.
verses.textLatin: Et pascentur agni juxta ordinem suum, et deserta in ubertatem versa advenæ comedent.

verses.text: Woe to you that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as the rope of a cart.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum!

verses.text: That say: Let him make haste, and let his work come quickly, that we may see it: and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, that we may know it.
verses.textLatin: qui dicitis: Festinet, et cito veniat opus ejus, ut videamus; et appropiet, et veniat consilium sancti Israël, et sciemus illud!

verses.text: Woe to you that call evil good, and good evil: that put darkness for light, and light for darkness: that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, et bonum malum; ponentes tenebras lucem, et lucem tenebras; ponentes amarum in dulce, et dulce in amarum!

verses.text: Woe to you that are wise in your own eyes, and prudent in your own conceits.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui sapientes estis in oculis vestris, et coram vobismetipsis prudentes.

verses.text: Woe to you that are mighty to drink wine, and stout men at drunkenness.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui potentes estis ad bibendum vinum, et viri fortes ad miscendam ebrietatem!

verses.text: That justify the wicked for gifts, and take away the justice of the just from him.
verses.textLatin: qui justificatis impium pro muneribus, et justitiam justi aufertis ab eo!

verses.text: Therefore as the tongue of the fire devoureth the stubble, and the heat of the flame consumeth it: so shall their root be as ashes, and their bud shall go up as dust: for they have cast away the law of the Lord of hosts, and have blasphemed the word of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc, sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis, et calor flammæ exurit, sic radix eorum quasi favilla erit, et germen eorum ut pulvis ascendet; abjecerunt enim legem Domini exercituum, et eloquium sancti Israël blasphemaverunt.

verses.text: Therefore is the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, and he hath stretched out his hand upon them, and struck them: and the mountains were troubled, and their carcasses became as dung in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.textLatin: Ideo iratus est furor Domini in populum suum, et extendit manum suam super eum, et percussit eum: et conturbati sunt montes, et facta sunt morticina eorum quasi stercus in medio platearum. In his omnibus non est adversus furor ejus, sed adhuc manus ejus extenta.

verses.text: And he will lift up a sign to the nations afar off, and will whistle to them from the ends of the earth: and behold they shall come with speed swiftly.
verses.textLatin: Et elevabit signum in nationibus procul, et sibilabit ad eum de finibus terræ: et ecce festinus velociter veniet.

verses.text: There is none that shall faint, nor labour among them: they shall not slumber nor sleep, neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken.
verses.textLatin: Non est deficiens neque laborans in eo; non dormitabit, neque dormiet; neque solvetur cingulum renum ejus, nec rumpetur corrigia calceamenti ejus.

verses.text: Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are bent. The hoofs of their horses shall be like the flint, and their wheels like the violence of a tempest.
verses.textLatin: Sagittæ ejus acutæ, et omnes arcus ejus extenti. Ungulæ equorum ejus ut silex, et rotæ ejus quasi impetus tempestatis.

verses.text: Their roaring like that of a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yea they shall roar, and take hold of the prey, and they shall keep fast hold of it, and there shall be none to deliver it.
verses.textLatin: Rugitus ejus ut leonis; rugiet ut catuli leonum: et frendet, et tenebit prædam, et amplexabitur, et non erit qui eruat.

verses.text: And they shall make a noise against them that day, like the roaring of the sea; we shall look towards the land, and behold darkness of tribulation, and the light is darkened with the mist thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et sonabit super eum in die illa sicut sonitus maris: aspiciemus in terram, et ecce tenebræ tribulationis, et lux obtenebrata est in caligine ejus.

verses.text: In  the year that king Ozias died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated: and his train filled the temple.
verses.textLatin: In anno quo mortuus est rex Ozias, vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum et elevatum; et ea quæ sub ipso erant replebant templum.

verses.text: Upon it stood the seraphims: the one had six wings, and the other had six wings: with two they covered his face, and with two they covered his feet, and with two they flew.
verses.textLatin: Seraphim stabant super illud: sex alæ uni, et sex alæ alteri; duabus velabant faciem ejus, et duabus velabant pedes ejus, et duabus volabant.

verses.text: And they cried one to another, and said: Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts, all the earth is full of his glory.
verses.textLatin: Et clamabant alter ad alterum, et dicebant: Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus Dominus, Deus exercituum; plena est omnis terra gloria ejus.

verses.text: And the lintels of the doors were moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.textLatin: Et commota sunt superliminaria cardinum a voce clamantis, et domus repleta est fumo.

verses.text: And I said: Woe is me, because I have held my peace; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people that hath unclean lips, and I have seen with my eyes the King the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Væ mihi, quia tacui, quia vir pollutus labiis ego sum, et in medio populi polluta labia habentis ego habito, et regem Dominum exercituum vidi oculis meis.

verses.text: And one of the seraphims flew to me, and in his hand was a live coal, which he had taken with the tongs off the altar.
verses.textLatin: Et volavit ad me unus de seraphim, et in manu ejus calculus, quem forcipe tulerat de altari,

verses.text: And he touched my mouth, and said: Behold this hath touched thy lips, and thy iniquities shall be taken away, and thy sin shall be cleansed.
verses.textLatin: et tetigit os meum, et dixit: Ecce tetigit hoc labia tua, et auferetur iniquitas tua, et peccatum tuum mundabitur.

verses.text: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: Whom shall I send? and who shall go for us? And I said: Lo, here am I, send me.
verses.textLatin: Et audivi vocem Domini dicentis: Quem mittam? et quis ibit nobis? Et dixi: Ecce ego, mitte me.

verses.text: And he said: Go, and thou shalt say to this people: Hearing, hear, and understand not: and see the vision, and know it not.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Vade, et dices populo huic: Audite audientes, et nolite intelligere; et videte visionem, et nolite cognoscere.

verses.text: Blind the heart of this people, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes: lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted and I heal them.
verses.textLatin: Excæca cor populi hujus, et aures ejus aggrava, et oculos ejus claude: ne forte videat oculis suis, et auribus suis audiat, et corde suo intelligat, et convertatur, et sanem eum.

verses.text: And I said: How long, O Lord? And he said: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land shall be left desolate.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Usquequo, Domine? Et dixit: Donec desolentur civitates absque habitatore, et domus sine homine, et terra relinquetur deserta.

verses.text: And the Lord shall remove men far away, and she shall be multiplied that was left in the midst of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et longe faciet Dominus homines, et multiplicabitur quæ derelicta fuerat in medio terræ.

verses.text: And there shall be still a tithing therein, and she shall turn, and shall be made a show as a turpentine tree, and as an oak that spreadeth its branches: that which shall stand therein, shall be a holy seed.
verses.textLatin: Et adhuc in ea decimatio, et convertetur, et erit in ostensionem sicut terebinthus, et sicut quercus quæ expandit ramos suos; semen sanctum erit id quod steterit in ea.

verses.text: And  it came to pass in the days of Achaz the son of Joathan, the son of Ozias, king of Juda, that Rasin king of Syria, and Phacee the son of Romelia king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem, to fight against it: but they could not prevail over it.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est in diebus Achaz, filii Joathan, filii Oziæ, regis Juda, ascendit Rasin, rex Syriæ, et Phacee, filius Romeliæ, rex Israël, in Jerusalem, ad præliandum contra eam: et non potuerunt

verses.text: And they told the house of David, saying: Syria hath rested upon Ephraim, and his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the woods are moved with the wind.
verses.textLatin: debellare eam. Et nuntiaverunt domui David, dicentes: Requievit Syria super Ephraim. Et commotum est cor ejus, et cor populi ejus, sicut moventur ligna silvarum a facie venti.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Isaias: Go forth to meet Achaz, thou and Jasub thy son that is left, to the conduit of the upper pool, in the way of the fuller’s field.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Isaiam: Egredere in occursum Achaz, tu et qui derelictus est Jasub, filius tuus, ad extremum aquæductus piscinæ superioris in via agri Fullonis;

verses.text: And thou shalt say to him: See thou be quiet: fear not, and let not thy heart be afraid of the two tails of these firebrands, smoking with the wrath of the fury of Rasin king of Syria, and of the son of Romelia.
verses.textLatin: et dices ad eum: Vide ut sileas; noli timere, et cor tuum ne formidet a duabus caudis titionum fumigantium istorum, in ira furoris Rasin, regis Syriæ, et filii Romeliæ;

verses.text: Because Syria hath taken counsel against thee, unto the evil of Ephraim and the son of Romelia, saying:
verses.textLatin: eo quod consilium inierit contra te Syria in malum, Ephraim, et filius Romeliæ, dicentes:

verses.text: Let us go up to Juda, and rouse it up, and draw it away to us, and make the son of Tabeel king in the midst thereof.
verses.textLatin: Ascendamus ad Judam, et suscitemus eum, et avellamus eum ad nos, et ponamus regem in medio ejus filium Tabeel.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God: It shall not stand, and this shall not be.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Non stabit, et non erit istud;

verses.text: But the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rasin: and within threescore and five years, Ephraim shall cease to be a people:
verses.textLatin: sed caput Syriæ Damascus, et caput Damasci Rasin; et adhuc sexaginta et quinque anni, et desinet Ephraim esse populus;

verses.text: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria the son of Romelia. If you will not believe, you shall not continue.
verses.textLatin: et caput Ephraim Samaria, et caput Samariæ filius Romeliæ. Si non credideritis, non permanebitis.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke again to Achaz, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et adjecit Dominus loqui ad Achaz, dicens:

verses.text: Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God, either unto the depth of hell, or unto the height above.
verses.textLatin: Pete tibi signum a Domino Deo tuo, in profundum inferni, sive in excelsum supra.
