verses.text: And Achaz said: I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Achaz: Non petam, et non tentabo Dominum.

verses.text: And he said: Hear ye therefore, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to be grievous to men, that you are grievous to my God also?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Audite ergo, domus David. Numquid parum vobis est molestos esse hominibus, quia molesti estis et Deo meo?

verses.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign. Behold a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc dabit Dominus ipse vobis signum: ecce virgo concipiet, et pariet filium, et vocabitur nomen ejus Emmanuel.

verses.text: He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know to refuse the evil, and to choose the good.
verses.textLatin: Butyrum et mel comedet, ut sciat reprobare malum, et eligere bonum.

verses.text: For before the child know to refuse the evil, and to choose the good, the land which thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of the face of her two kings.
verses.textLatin: Quia antequam sciat puer reprobare malum et eligere bonum, derelinquetur terra quam tu detestaris a facie duorum regum suorum.

verses.text: The Lord shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon the house of thy father, days that have not come since the time of the separation of Ephraim from Juda with the king of the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: Adducet Dominus super te, et super populum tuum, et super domum patris tui, dies qui non venerunt a diebus separationis Ephraim a Juda, cum rege Assyriorum.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall hiss for the fly, that is in the uttermost parts of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: sibilabit Dominus muscæ quæ est in extremo fluminum Ægypti, et api quæ est in terra Assur;

verses.text: And they shall come, and shall all of them rest in the torrents of the valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and upon all places set with shrubs, and in all hollow places.
verses.textLatin: et venient, et requiescent omnes in torrentibus vallium, et in cavernis petrarum, et in omnibus frutetis, et in universis foraminibus.

verses.text: In that day the Lord shall shave with a razor that is hired by them that are beyond the river, by the king of the Assyrians, the head and the hairs of the feet, and the whole beard.
verses.textLatin: In die illa radet Dominus in novacula conducta in his qui trans flumen sunt, in rege Assyriorum, caput et pilos pedum, et barbam universam.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man shall nourish a young cow, and two sheep.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: nutriet homo vaccam boum, et duas oves,

verses.text: And for the abundance of milk he shall eat butter: for butter and honey shall every one eat that shall be left in the midst of the land.
verses.textLatin: et præ ubertate lactis comedet butyrum; butyrum enim et mel manducabit omnis qui relictus fuerit in medio terræ.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place where there were a thousand vines, at a thousand pieces of silver, shall become thorns and briers.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: omnis locus ubi fuerint mille vites, mille argenteis, in spinas et in vepres erunt.

verses.text: With arrows and with bows they shall go in thither: for briers and thorns shall be in all the land.
verses.textLatin: Cum sagittis et arcu ingredientur illuc: vepres enim et spinæ erunt in universa terra.

verses.text: And as for all the hills that shall be raked with a rake, the fear of thorns and briers shall not come thither, but they shall be for the ox to feed on, and the lesser cattle to tread upon.
verses.textLatin: Et omnes montes qui in sarculo sarrientur, non veniet illuc terror spinarum et veprium: et erit in pascua bovis, et in conculcationem pecoris.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to me: Take thee a great book, and write in it with a man’s pen. Take away the spoils with speed, quickly take the prey.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad me: Sume tibi librum grandem, et scribe in eo stylo hominis: Velociter spolia detrahe, cito prædare.

verses.text: And I took unto me faithful witnesses, Urias the priest, and Zacharias the son of Barachias.
verses.textLatin: Et adhibui mihi testes fideles, Uriam sacerdotem, et Zachariam, filium Barachiæ:

verses.text: And I went to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: Call his name, Hasten to take away the spoils: Make hast to take away the prey.
verses.textLatin: et accessi ad prophetissam, et concepit, et peperit filium. Et dixit Dominus ad me: Voca nomen ejus: Accelera spolia detrahere; Festina prædari:

verses.text: For before the child know to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus, and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: quia antequam sciat puer vocare patrem suum et matrem suam, auferetur fortitudo Damasci, et spolia Samariæ, coram rege Assyriorum.

verses.text: And the Lord spoke to me again, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et adjecit Dominus loqui ad me adhuc, dicens:

verses.text: Forasmuch as this people hath cast away the waters of Siloe, that go with silence, and hath rather taken Rasin, and the son of Romelia:
verses.textLatin: Pro eo quod abjecit populus iste aquas Siloë, quæ vadunt cum silentio, et assumpsit magis Rasin, et filium Romeliæ:

verses.text: Therefore behold the Lord will bring upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of the Assyrians, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and shall overflow all his banks,
verses.textLatin: propter hoc ecce Dominus adducet super eos aquas fluminis fortes et multas, regem Assyriorum, et omnem gloriam ejus, et ascendet super omnes rivos ejus, et fluet super universas ripas ejus;

verses.text: And shall pass through Juda, overflowing, and going over shall reach even to the neck. And the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Emmanuel.
verses.textLatin: et ibit per Judam, inundans, et transiens: usque ad collum veniet. Et erit extensio alarum ejus implens latitudinem terræ tuæ, o Emmanuel!

verses.text: Gather yourselves together, O ye people, and be overcome, and give ear, all ye lands afar off: strengthen yourselves, and be overcome, gird yourselves, and be overcome.
verses.textLatin: Congregamini, populi, et vincimini; et audite, universæ procul terræ: confortamini, et vincimini; accingite vos, et vincimini.

verses.text: Take counsel together, and it shall be defeated: speak a word, and it shall not be done: because God is with us.
verses.textLatin: Inite consilium, et dissipabitur; loquimini verbum, et non fiet: quia nobiscum Deus.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord to me: As he hath taught me, with a strong arm, that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying:
verses.textLatin: Hæc enim ait Dominus ad me: Sicut in manu forti erudivit me, ne irem in via populi hujus, dicens:

verses.text: Say ye not: A conspiracy: for all that this people speaketh, is a conspiracy: neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid.
verses.textLatin: Non dicatis: Conjuratio; omnia enim quæ loquitur populus iste, conjuratio est: et timorem ejus ne timeatis, neque paveatis.

verses.text: Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.
verses.textLatin: Dominum exercituum ipsum sanctificate; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester:

verses.text: And he shall be a sanctification to you. But for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offence to the two houses of Israel, for a snare and a ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et erit vobis in sanctificationem; in lapidem autem offensionis, et in petram scandali, duabus domibus Israël; in laqueum et in ruinam habitantibus Jerusalem.

verses.text: And very many of them shall stumble and fall, and shall be broken in pieces, and shall be snared, and taken.
verses.textLatin: Et offendent ex eis plurimi, et cadent, et conterentur, et irretientur, et capientur.

verses.text: Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.
verses.textLatin: Liga testimonium, signa legem in discipulis meis.

verses.text: And I will wait for the Lord, who hath hid his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him.
verses.textLatin: Et exspectabo Dominum qui abscondit faciem suam a domo Jacob, et præstolabor eum.

verses.text: Behold I and my children, whom the Lord hath given me for a sign, and for a wonder in Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwelleth in mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego et pueri mei quos dedit mihi Dominus in signum, et in portentum Israël a Domino exercituum, qui habitat in monte Sion:

verses.text: And when they shall say to you: Seek of pythons, and of diviners, who mutter in their enchantments: should not the people seek of their God, for the living of the dead?
verses.textLatin: et cum dixerint ad vos: Quærite a pythonibus et a divinis qui strident in incantationibus suis: numquid non populus a Deo suo requiret, pro vivis a mortuis?

verses.text: To the law rather, and to the testimony. And if they speak not according to this word, they shall not have the morning light.
verses.textLatin: ad legem magis et ad testimonium. Quod si non dixerint juxta verbum hoc, non erit eis matutina lux.

verses.text: And they shall pass by it, they shall fall, and be hungry: and when they shall be hungry, they will be angry, and curse their king, and their God, and look upwards.
verses.textLatin: Et transibit per eam, corruet, et esuriet; et cum esurierit, irascetur. Et maledicet regi suo, et Deo suo, et suscipiet sursum,

verses.text: And they shall look to the earth, and behold trouble and darkness, weakness and distress, and a mist following them, and they cannot fly away from their distress.
verses.textLatin: et ad terram intuebitur; et ecce tribulatio et tenebræ, dissolutio et angustia, et caligo persequens, et non poterit avolare de angustia sua.

verses.text: At  the first time the land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephtali was lightly touched: and at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan of the Galilee of the Gentiles was heavily loaded.
verses.textLatin: Primo tempore alleviata est terra Zabulon et terra Nephthali: et novissimo aggravata est via maris trans Jordanem Galilææ gentium.

verses.text: The people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: to them that dwelt in the region of the shadow of death, light is risen.
verses.textLatin: Populus qui ambulabat in tenebris, vidit lucem magnam; habitantibus in regione umbræ mortis, lux orta est eis.

verses.text: Thou hast multiplied the nation, and hast not increased the joy. They shall rejoice before thee, as they that rejoice in the harvest, as conquerors rejoice after taking a prey, when they divide the spoils.
verses.textLatin: Multiplicasti gentem, et non magnificasti lætitiam. Lætabuntur coram te, sicut qui lætantur in messe; sicut exsultant victores capta præda, quando dividunt spolia.

verses.text: For the yoke of their burden, and the rod of their shoulder, and the sceptre of their oppressor thou hast overcome, as in the day of Madian.
verses.textLatin: Jugum enim oneris ejus, et virgam humeri ejus, et sceptrum exactoris ejus superasti, sicut in die Madian.

verses.text: For every violent taking of spoils, with tumult, and garment mingled with blood, shall be burnt, and be fuel for the fire.
verses.textLatin: Quia omnis violentia prædatio cum tumultu, et vestimentum mistum sanguine, erit in combustionem, et cibus ignis.

verses.text: For a CHILD IS BORN to us, and a son is given to us, and the government is upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called, Wonderful, Counsellor, God the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace.
verses.textLatin: Parvulus enim natus est nobis, et filius datus est nobis, et factus est principatus super humerum ejus: et vocabitur nomen ejus, Admirabilis, Consiliarius, Deus, Fortis, Pater futuri sæculi, Princeps pacis.

verses.text: His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace: he shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom; to establish it and strengthen it with judgment and with justice, from henceforth and for ever: the zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.
verses.textLatin: Multiplicabitur ejus imperium, et pacis non erit finis; super solium David, et super regnum ejus sedebit, ut confirmet illud et corroboret in judicio et justitia, amodo et usque in sempiternum: zelus Domini exercituum faciet hoc.

verses.text: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.
verses.textLatin: Verbum misit Dominus in Jacob, et cecidit in Israël.

verses.text: And all the people of Ephraim shall know, and the inhabitants of Samaria that say in the pride and haughtiness of their heart:
verses.textLatin: Et sciet omnis populus Ephraim, et habitantes Samariam, in superbia et magnitudine cordis dicentes:

verses.text: The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with square stones: they have cut down the sycamores, but we will change them for cedars.
verses.textLatin: Lateres ceciderunt, sed quadris lapidibus ædificabimus; sycomoros succiderunt, sed cedros immutabimus.

verses.text: And the Lord shall set up the enemies of Rasin over him, and shall bring on his enemies in a crowd:
verses.textLatin: Et elevabit Dominus hostes Rasin super eum, et inimicos ejus in tumultum vertet.

verses.text: The Syrians from the east, and the Philistines from the west: and they shall devour Israel with open mouth. For all this his indignation is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.textLatin: Syriam ab oriente, et Philisthiim ab occidente; et devorabunt Israël toto ore. In omnibus his non est aversus furor ejus, sed adhuc manus ejus extenta.

verses.text: And the people are not returned to him who hath struck them, and have not sought after the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum exercituum non inquisierunt.

verses.text: And the Lord shall destroy out of Israel the head and the tail, him that bendeth down, and him that holdeth back, in one day.
verses.textLatin: Et disperdet Dominus ab Israël caput et caudam, incurvantem et refrenantem, die una.

verses.text: The aged and honourable, he is the head: and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.
verses.textLatin: Longævus et honorabilis, ipse est caput; et propheta docens mendacium, ipse est cauda.

verses.text: And they that call this people blessed, shall cause them to err: and they that are called blessed, shall be thrown down headlong.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt qui beatificant populum istum, seducentes; et qui beatificantur, præcipitati.

verses.text: Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men: neither shall he have mercy on their fatherless, and widows: for every one is a hypocrite and wicked, and every mouth hath spoken folly. For all this his indignation is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc super adolescentulis ejus non lætabitur Dominus, et pupillorum ejus et viduarum non miserebitur: quia omnis hypocrita est et nequam, et universum os locutum est stultitiam; in omnibus his non est aversus furor ejus, sed adhuc manus ejus extenta.

verses.text: For wickedness is kindled as a fire, it shall devour the brier and the thorn: and shall kindle in the thicket of the forest, and it shall be wrapped up in smoke ascending on high.
verses.textLatin: Succensa est enim quasi ignis impietas: veprem et spinam vorabit, et succendetur in densitate saltus, et convolvetur superbia fumi.

verses.text: By the wrath of the Lord of hosts the land is troubled, and the people shall be as fuel for the fire: no man shall spare his brother.
verses.textLatin: In ira Domini exercituum conturbata est terra, et erit populus quasi esca ignis; vir fratri suo non parcet.

verses.text: And he shall turn to the right hand, and shall be hungry: and shall eat on the left hand, and shall not be filled: every one shall eat the flesh of his own arm: Manasses Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasses, and they together shall be against Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et declinabit ad dexteram, et esuriet; et comedet ad sinistram, et non saturabitur; unusquisque carnem brachii sui vorabit: Manasses Ephraim, et Ephraim Manassen; simul ipsi contra Judam.

verses.text: After all these things his indignation is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.textLatin: In omnibus his non est aversus furor ejus, sed adhuc manus ejus extenta.

verses.text: Woe  to them that make wicked laws: and when they write, write injustice:
verses.textLatin: Væ qui condunt leges iniquas, et scribentes injustitiam scripserunt,

verses.text: To oppress the poor in judgment, and do violence to the cause of the humble of my people: that widows might be their prey, and that they might rob the fatherless.
verses.textLatin: ut opprimerent in judicio pauperes, et vim facerent causæ humilium populi mei; ut essent viduæ præda eorum, et pupillos diriperent.

verses.text: What will you do in the day of visitation, and of the calamity which cometh from afar? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory?
verses.textLatin: Quid facietis in die visitationis, et calamitatis de longe venientis? ad cujus confugietis auxilium? et ubi derelinquetis gloriam vestram,

verses.text: That you be not bowed down under the bond, and fall with the slain? In all these things his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.textLatin: ne incurvemini sub vinculo, et cum interfectis cadatis? Super omnibus his non est aversus furor ejus, sed adhuc manus ejus extenta.

verses.text: Woe to the Assyrian, he is the rod and the staff of my anger, and my indignation is in their hands.
verses.textLatin: Væ Assur! virga furoris mei et baculus ipse est; in manu eorum indignatio mea.

verses.text: I will send him to a deceitful nation, and I will give him a charge against the people of my wrath, to take away the spoils, and to lay hold on the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
verses.textLatin: Ad gentem fallacem mittam eum, et contra populum furoris mei mandabo illi, ut auferat spolia, et diripiat prædam, et ponat illum in conculcationem quasi lutum platearum.

verses.text: But he shall not take it so, and his heart shall not think so: but his heart shall be set to destroy, and to cut off nations not a few.
verses.textLatin: Ipse autem non sic arbitrabitur, et cor ejus non ita existimabit; sed ad conterendum erit cor ejus, et ad internecionem gentium non paucarum.

verses.text: For he shall say:
verses.textLatin: Dicet enim:

verses.text: Are not my princes as so many kings? is not Calano as Charcamis: and Emath as Arphad? is not Samaria as Damascus?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non principes mei simul reges sunt? numquid non ut Charcamis, sic Calano? et ut Arphad, sic Emath? numquid non ut Damascus, sic Samaria?

verses.text: As my hand hath found the kingdoms of the idol, so also their idols of Jerusalem, and of Samaria.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo invenit manus mea regna idoli, sic et simulacra eorum de Jerusalem et de Samaria.

verses.text: Shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non sicut feci Samariæ et idolis ejus, sic faciam Jerusalem et simulacris ejus?

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that when the Lord shall have performed all his works in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem, I will visit the fruit of the proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of the haughtiness of his eyes.
verses.textLatin: Et erit, cum impleverit Dominus cuncta opera sua in monte Sion et in Jerusalem, visitabo super fructum magnifici cordis regis Assur, et super gloriam altitudinis oculorum ejus.

verses.text: For he hath said: By the strength of my own hand I have done it, and by my own wisdom I have understood: and I have removed the bounds of the people, and have taken the spoils of the princes, and as a mighty man hath pulled down them that sat on high.
verses.textLatin: Dixit enim: In fortitudine manus meæ feci, et in sapientia mea intellexi; et abstuli terminos populorum, et principes eorum deprædatus sum, et detraxi quasi potens in sublimi residentes.

verses.text: And my hand hath found the strength of the people as a nest; and as eggs are gathered, that are left, so have I gathered all the earth: and there was none that moved the wing, or opened the mouth, or made the least noise.
verses.textLatin: Et invenit quasi nidum manus mea fortitudinem populorum; et sicut colliguntur ova quæ derelicta sunt, sic universam terram ego congregavi; et non fuit qui moveret pennam, et aperiret os, et ganniret.

verses.text: Shall the axe boast itself against him that cutteth with it? or shall the saw exalt itself against him by whom it is drawn? as if a rod should lift itself up against him that lifteth it up, and a staff exalt itself, which is but wood.
verses.textLatin: Numquid gloriabitur securis contra eum qui secat in ea? aut exaltabitur serra contra eum a quo trahitur? Quomodo si elevetur virga contra elevantem se, et exaltetur baculus, qui utique lignum est.

verses.text: Therefore the sovereign Lord, the Lord of hosts, shall send leanness among his fat ones: and under his glory shall be kindled a burning, as it were the burning of a fire.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc mittet Dominator, Dominus exercituum, in pinguibus ejus tenuitatem; et subtus gloriam ejus succensa ardebit quasi combustio ignis.

verses.text: And the light of Israel shall be as a fire, and the Holy One thereof as a flame: and his thorns and his briers shall be set on fire, and shall be devoured in one day.
verses.textLatin: Et erit lumen Israël in igne, et Sanctus ejus in flamma; et succendetur, et devorabitur spina ejus et vepres in die una.

verses.text: And the glory of his forest, and of his beautiful hill, shall be consumed from the soul even to the flesh, and he shall run away through fear.
verses.textLatin: Et gloria saltus ejus, et carmeli ejus, ab anima usque ad carnem consumetur; et erit terrore profugus.

verses.text: And they that remain of the trees of his forest shall be so few, that they shall easily be numbered, and a child shall write them down.
verses.textLatin: Et reliquiæ ligni saltus ejus præ paucitate numerabuntur, et puer scribet eos.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Israel, and they that shall escape of the house of Jacob, shall lean no more upon him that striketh them: but they shall lean upon the Lord the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: non adjiciet residuum Israël, et hi qui fugerint de domo Jacob, inniti super eo qui percutit eos; sed innitetur super Dominum, Sanctum Israël, in veritate.

verses.text: The remnant shall be converted, the remnant, I say, of Jacob, to the mighty God.
verses.textLatin: Reliquiæ convertentur; reliquiæ, inquam, Jacob ad Deum fortem.

verses.text: For if thy people, O Israel, shall be as the sand of the sea, a remnant of them shall be converted, the consumption abridged shall overflow with justice.
verses.textLatin: Si enim fuerit populus tuus, Israël, quasi arena maris, reliquiæ convertentur ex eo; consummatio abbreviata inundabit justitiam.

verses.text: For the Lord God of hosts shall make a consumption, and an abridgment in the midst of all the land.
verses.textLatin: Consummationem enim et abbreviationem Dominus Deus exercituum faciet in medio omnis terræ.

verses.text: Therefore, thus saith the Lord the God of hosts: O my people that dwellest in Sion, be not afraid of the Assyrian: he shall strike thee with his rod, and he shall lift up his staff over thee in the way of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc, hæc dicit Dominus Deus exercituum: Noli timere, populus meus, habitator Sion, ab Assur: in virga percutiet te, et baculum suum levabit super te, in via Ægypti.

verses.text: For yet a little and a very little while, and my indignation shall cease, and my wrath shall be upon their wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc enim paululum modicumque, et consummabitur indignatio et furor meus super scelus eorum.

verses.text: And the Lord of hosts shall raise up a scourge against him, according to the slaughter of Madian in the rock of Oreb, and his rod over the sea, and he shall lift it up in the way of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et suscitabit super eum Dominus exercituum flagellum, juxta plagam Madian in petra Oreb: et virgam suam super mare, et levabit eam in via Ægypti.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke from off thy neck, and the yoke shall putrify at the presence of the oil.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: auferetur onus ejus de humero tuo et jugum ejus de collo tuo, et computrescet jugum a facie olei.

verses.text: He shall come into Aiath, he shall pass into Magron: at Machmas he shall lay up his carriages.
verses.textLatin: Veniet in Ajath, transibit in Magron, apud Machmas commendabit vasa sua.

verses.text: They have passed in haste, Gaba is our lodging: Rama was astonished, Gabaath of Saul fled away.
verses.textLatin: Transierunt cursim, Gaba sedes nostra; obstupuit Rama, Gabaath Saulis fugit.

verses.text: Lift up thy voice, O daughter of Gallim, attend, O Laisa, poor Anathoth.
verses.textLatin: Hinni voce tua, filia Gallim, attende Laisa, paupercula Anathoth.

verses.text: Medemena is removed: ye inhabitants of Gabim, take courage.
verses.textLatin: Migravit Medemena; habitatores Gabim, confortamini.

verses.text: It is yet day enough, to remain in Nobe: he shall shake his hand against the mountain of the daughter of Sion, the hill of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc dies est ut in Nobe stetur; agitabit manum suam super montem filiæ Sion, collem Jerusalem.

verses.text: Behold the sovereign Lord of hosts shall break the earthen vessel with terror, and the tall of stature shall be cut down, and the lofty shall be humbled.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Dominator, Dominus exercituum, confringet lagunculam in terrore; et excelsi statura succidentur, et sublimes humiliabuntur.

verses.text: And the thickets of the forest shall be cut down with iron, and Libanus with its high ones shall fall.
verses.textLatin: Et subvertentur condensa saltus ferro; et Libanus cum excelsis cadet.

verses.text: And  there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root.
verses.textLatin: Et egredietur virga de radice Jesse, et flos de radice ejus ascendet.

verses.text: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, the spirit of counsel, and of fortitude, the spirit of knowledge, and of godliness.
verses.textLatin: Et requiescet super eum spiritus Domini: spiritus sapientiæ et intellectus, spiritus consilii et fortitudinis, spiritus scientiæ et pietatis;

verses.text: And he shall be filled with the spirit of the fear of the Lord. He shall not judge according to the sight of the eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of the ears.
verses.textLatin: et replebit eum spiritus timoris Domini. Non secundum visionem oculorum judicabit, neque secundum auditum aurium arguet;

verses.text: But he shall judge the poor with justice, and shall reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.
verses.textLatin: sed judicabit in justitia pauperes, et arguet in æquitate pro mansuetis terræ; et percutiet terram virga oris sui, et spiritu labiorum suorum interficiet impium.

verses.text: And justice shall be the girdle of his loins: and faith the girdle of his reins.
verses.textLatin: Et erit justitia cingulum lumborum ejus, et fides cinctorium renum ejus.

verses.text: The wolf shall dwell with the lamb: and the leopard shall lie down with the kid: the calf and the lion, and the sheep shall abide together, and a little child shall lead them.
verses.textLatin: Habitabit lupus cum agno, et pardus cum hædo accubabit; vitulus, et leo, et ovis, simul morabuntur, et puer parvulus minabit eos.

verses.text: The calf and the bear shall feed: their young ones shall rest together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
verses.textLatin: Vitulus et ursus pascentur, simul requiescent catuli eorum; et leo quasi bos comedet paleas.

verses.text: And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp: and the weaned child shall thrust his hand into the den of the basilisk.
verses.textLatin: Et delectabitur infans ab ubere super foramine aspidis; et in caverna reguli qui ablactatus fuerit manum suam mittet.

verses.text: They shall not hurt, nor shall they kill in all my holy mountain, for the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Non nocebunt, et non occident in universo monte sancto meo, quia repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes.

verses.text: In that day the root of Jesse, who standeth for an ensign of the people, him the Gentiles shall beseech, and his sepulchre shall be glorious.
verses.textLatin: In die illa radix Jesse, qui stat in signum populorum, ipsum gentes deprecabuntur, et erit sepulchrum ejus gloriosum.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand the second time to possess the remnant of his people, which shall be left from the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Phetros, and from Ethiopia, and from Elam, and from Sennaar, and from Emath, and from the islands of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: adjiciet Dominus secundo manum suam ad possidendum residuum populi sui, quod relinquetur ab Assyriis, et ab Ægypto, et a Phetros, et ab Æthiopia, et ab Ælam, et a Sennaar, et ab Emath, et ab insulis maris.

verses.text: And he shall set up a standard unto the nations, and shall assemble the fugitives of Israel, and shall gather together the dispersed of Juda from the four quarters of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et levabit signum in nationes, et congregabit profugos Israël, et dispersos Juda colliget a quatuor plagis terræ.

verses.text: And the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Juda shall perish: Ephraim shall not envy Juda, and Juda shall not fight against Ephraim.
verses.textLatin: Et auferetur zelus Ephraim, et hostes Juda peribunt; Ephraim non æmulabitur Judam, et Judas non pugnabit contra Ephraim.

verses.text: But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines by the sea, they together shall spoil the children of the east: Edom, and Moab shall be under the rule of their hand, and the children of Ammon shall be obedient.
verses.textLatin: Et volabunt in humeros Philisthiim per mare, simul prædabuntur filios orientis; Idumæa et Moab præceptum manus eorum, et filii Ammon obedientes erunt.

verses.text: And the Lord shall lay waste the tongue of the sea of Egypt, and shall lift up his hand over the river in the strength of his spirit: and he shall strike it in the seven streams, so that men may pass through it in their shoes.
verses.textLatin: Et desolabit Dominus linguam maris Ægypti, et levabit manum suam super flumen in fortitudine spiritus sui; et percutiet eum in septem rivis, ita ut transeant per eum calceati.

verses.text: And there shall be a highway for the remnant of my people, which shall be left from the Assyrians: as there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et erit via residuo populo meo qui relinquetur ab Assyriis, sicut fuit Israëli in die illa qua ascendit de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And  thou shalt say in that day: I will give thanks to thee, O Lord, for thou wast angry with me: thy wrath is turned away, and thou hast comforted me.
verses.textLatin: Et dices in die illa: Confitebor tibi, Domine, quoniam iratus es mihi; conversus est furor tuus, et consolatus es me.

verses.text: Behold, God is my saviour, I will deal confidently, and will not fear: because the Lord is my strength, and my praise, and he is become my salvation.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Deus salvator meus; fiducialiter agam, et non timebo: quia fortitudo mea et laus mea Dominus, et factus est mihi in salutem.

verses.text: You shall draw waters with joy out of the saviour’s fountains:
verses.textLatin: Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus salvatoris.

verses.text: And you shall say in that day: Praise ye the Lord, and call upon his name: make his works known among the people: remember that his name is high.
verses.textLatin: Et dicetis in die illa: Confitemini Domino et invocate nomen ejus; notas facite in populis adinventiones ejus; mementote quoniam excelsum est nomen ejus.

verses.text: Sing ye to the Lord, for he hath done great things: shew this forth in all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Cantate Domino, quoniam magnifice fecit; annuntiate hoc in universa terra.

verses.text: Rejoice, and praise, O thou habitation of Sion: for great is he that is in the midst of thee, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Exsulta et lauda, habitatio Sion, quia magnus in medio tui Sanctus Israël.

verses.text: The burden of Babylon, which Isaias the son of Amos saw.
verses.textLatin: Onus Babylonis, quod vidit Isaias, filius Amos.

verses.text: Upon the dark mountain lift ye up a banner, exalt the voice, lift up the hand, and let the rulers go into the gates.
verses.textLatin: Super montem caliginosum levate signum: exaltate vocem, levate manum, et ingrediantur portas duces.

verses.text: I have commanded my sanctified ones, and have called my strong ones in my wrath, them that rejoice in my glory.
verses.textLatin: Ego mandavi sanctificatis meis, et vocavi fortes meos in ira mea, exsultantes in gloria mea.

verses.text: The noise of a multitude in the mountains, as it were of many people, the noise of the sound of kings, of nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts hath given charge to the troops of war.
verses.textLatin: Vox multitudinis in montibus, quasi populorum frequentium; vox sonitus regum, gentium congregatarum. Dominus exercituum præcepit militiæ belli,

verses.text: To them that come from a country afar off, from the end of heaven: the Lord and the instruments of his wrath, to destroy the whole land.
verses.textLatin: venientibus de terra procul, a summitate cæli; Dominus, et vasa furoris ejus, ut disperdat omnem terram.

verses.text: Howl ye, for the day of the Lord is near: it shall come as a destruction from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ululate, quia prope est dies Domini; quasi vastitas a Domino veniet.

verses.text: Therefore shall all hands be faint, and every heart of man shall melt,
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc omnes manus dissolventur, et omne cor hominis contabescet,

verses.text: And shall be broken. Gripings and pains shall take hold of them, they shall be in pain as a woman in labour. Every one shall be amazed at his neighbour, their countenances shall be as faces burnt.
verses.textLatin: et conteretur. Torsiones et dolores tenebunt; quasi parturiens dolebunt: unusquisque ad proximum suum stupebit, facies combustæ vultus eorum.

verses.text: Behold, the day of the Lord shall come, a cruel day, and full of indignation, and of wrath, and fury, to lay the land desolate, and to destroy the sinners thereof out of it.
verses.textLatin: Ecce dies Domini veniet, crudelis, et indignationis plenus, et iræ, furorisque, ad ponendam terram in solitudinem, et peccatores ejus conterendos de ea.

verses.text: For the stars of heaven, and their brightness shall not display their light: the sun shall be darkened in his rising, and the moon shall not shine with her light.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam stellæ cæli, et splendor earum, non expandent lumen suum; obtenebratus est sol in ortu suo, et luna non splendebit in lumine suo.

verses.text: And I will visit the evils of the world, and against the wicked for their iniquity: and I will make the pride of infidels to cease, and will bring down the arrogancy of the mighty.
verses.textLatin: Et visitabo super orbis mala, et contra impios iniquitatem eorum; et quiescere faciam superbiam infidelium, et arrogantiam fortium humiliabo.

verses.text: A man shall be more precious than gold, yea a man than the finest of gold.
verses.textLatin: Pretiosior erit vir auro, et homo mundo obrizo.

verses.text: For this I will trouble the heaven: and the earth shall be moved out of her place, for the indignation of the Lord of hosts, and for the day of his fierce wrath.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc cælum turbabo; et movebitur terra de loco suo, propter indignationem Domini exercituum, et propter diem iræ furoris ejus.

verses.text: And they shall be as a doe fleeing away, and as a sheep: and there shall be none to gather them together: every man shall turn to his own people, and every one shall flee to his own land.
verses.textLatin: Et erit quasi damula fugiens, et quasi ovis, et non erit qui congreget. Unusquisque ad populum suum convertetur, et singuli ad terram suam fugient.

verses.text: Every one that shall be found, shall be slain: and every one that shall come to their aid, shall fall by the sword.
verses.textLatin: Omnis qui inventus fuerit occidetur, et omnis qui supervenerit cadet in gladio;

verses.text: Their infants shall be dashed in pieces before their eyes: their houses shall be pillaged, and their wives shall be ravished.
verses.textLatin: infantes eorum allidentur in oculis eorum, diripientur domus eorum, et uxores eorum violabuntur.

verses.text: Behold I will stir up the Medes against them, who shall not seek silver, nor desire gold:
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego suscitabo super eos Medos, qui argentum non quærant, nec aurum velint;

verses.text: But with their arrows they shall kill the children, and shall have no pity upon the sucklings of the womb, and their eye shall not spare their sons.
verses.textLatin: sed sagittis parvulos interficient, et lactantibus uteris non miserebuntur, et super filios non parcet oculus eorum.

verses.text: And that Babylon, glorious among kingdoms, the famous pride of the Chaldeans, shall be even as the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrha.
verses.textLatin: Et erit Babylon illa gloriosa in regnis, inclyta superbia Chaldæorum, sicut subvertit Dominus Sodomam et Gomorrham.

verses.text: It shall no more be inhabited for ever, and it shall not be founded unto generation and generation: neither shall the Arabian pitch his tents there, nor shall shepherds rest there.
verses.textLatin: Non habitabitur usque in finem, et non fundabitur usque ad generationem et generationem; nec ponet ibi tentoria Arabs, nec pastores requiescent ibi.

verses.text: But wild beasts shall rest there, and their houses shall be filled with serpents, and ostriches shall dwell there, and the hairy ones shall dance there:
verses.textLatin: Sed requiescent ibi bestiæ, et replebuntur domus eorum draconibus, et habitabunt ibi struthiones, et pilosi saltabunt ibi;

verses.text: And owls shall answer one another there, in the houses thereof, and sirens in the temples of pleasure.
verses.textLatin: et respondebunt ibi ululæ in ædibus ejus, et sirenes in delubris voluptatis.

verses.text: Her  time is near at hand, and her days shall not be prolonged. For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose out of Israel, and will make them rest upon their own ground: and the stranger shall be joined with them, and shall adhere to the house of Jacob.
verses.textLatin: Prope est ut veniat tempus ejus, et dies ejus non elongabuntur. Miserebitur enim Dominus Jacob, et eliget adhuc de Israël, et requiescere eos faciet super humum suam; adjungetur advena ad eos, et adhærebit domui Jacob.

verses.text: And the people shall take them, and bring them into their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall make them captives that had taken them, and shall subdue their oppressors.
verses.textLatin: Et tenebunt eos populi, et adducent eos in locum suum; et possidebit eos domus Israël super terram Domini in servos et ancillas: et erunt capientes eos qui se ceperant, et subjicient exactores suos.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that when God shall give thee rest from thy labour, and from thy vexation, and from the hard bondage, wherewith thou didst serve before,
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: cum requiem dederit tibi Deus a labore tuo, et a concussione tua, et a servitute dura qua ante servisti,

verses.text: Thou shalt take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and shalt say: How is the oppressor come to nothing, the tribute hath ceased?
verses.textLatin: sumes parabolam istam contra regem Babylonis, et dices: Quomodo cessavit exactor; quievit tributum?

verses.text: The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers,
verses.textLatin: Contrivit Dominus baculum impiorum, virgam dominantium,

verses.text: That struck the people in wrath with an incurable wound, that brought nations under in fury, that persecuted in a cruel manner.
verses.textLatin: cædentem populos in indignatione plaga insanabili, subjicientem in furore gentes, persequentem crudeliter.

verses.text: The whole earth is quiet and still, it is glad and hath rejoiced.
verses.textLatin: Conquievit et siluit omnis terra, gavisa est et exsultavit;

verses.text: The fir trees also have rejoiced over thee, and the cedars of Libanus, saying: Since thou hast slept, there hath none come up to cut us down.
verses.textLatin: abietes quoque lætatæ sunt super te, et cedri Libani: ex quo dormisti, non ascendet qui succidat nos.

verses.text: Hell below was in an uproar to meet thee at thy coming, it stirred up the giants for thee. All the princes of the earth are risen up from their thrones, all the princes of nations.
verses.textLatin: Infernus subter conturbatus est in occursum adventus tui; suscitavit tibi gigantes. Omnes principes terræ surrexerunt de soliis suis, omnes principes nationum.

verses.text: All shall answer, and say to thee: Thou also art wounded as well as we, thou art become like unto us.
verses.textLatin: Universi respondebunt, et dicent tibi: Et tu vulneratus es sicut et nos; nostri similis effectus es.

verses.text: Thy pride is brought down to hell, thy carcass is fallen down: under thee shall the moth be strewed, and worms shall be thy covering.
verses.textLatin: Detracta est ad inferos superbia tua, concidit cadaver tuum; subter te sternetur tinea, et operimentum tuum erunt vermes.

verses.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, who didst rise in the morning? how art thou fallen to the earth, that didst wound the nations?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo cecidisti de cælo, Lucifer, qui mane oriebaris? corruisti in terram, qui vulnerabas gentes?

verses.text: And thou saidst in thy heart: I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God, I will sit in the mountain of the covenant, in the sides of the north.
verses.textLatin: Qui dicebas in corde tuo: In cælum conscendam, super astra Dei exaltabo solium meum; sedebo in monte testamenti, in lateribus aquilonis;

verses.text: I will ascend above the height of the clouds, I will be like the most High.
verses.textLatin: ascendam super altitudinem nubium, similis ero Altissimo?

verses.text: But yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, into the depth of the pit.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen ad infernum detraheris, in profundum laci.

verses.text: They that shall see thee, shall turn toward thee, and behold thee. Is this the man that troubled the earth, that shook kingdoms,
verses.textLatin: Qui te viderint, ad te inclinabuntur, teque prospicient: Numquid iste est vir qui conturbavit terram, qui concussit regna,

verses.text: That made the world a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof, that opened not the prison to his prisoners?
verses.textLatin: qui posuit orbem desertum, et urbes ejus destruxit, vinctis ejus non aperuit carcerem?

verses.text: All the kings of the nations have all of them slept in glory, every one in his own house.
verses.textLatin: Omnes reges gentium universi dormierunt in gloria, vir in domo sua;

verses.text: But thou art cast out of thy grave, as an unprofitable branch defiled, and wrapped up among them that were slain by the sword, and art gone down to the bottom of the pit, as a rotten carcass.
verses.textLatin: tu autem projectus es de sepulchro tuo, quasi stirps inutilis pollutus, et obvolutus cum his qui interfecti sunt gladio, et descenderunt ad fundamenta laci, quasi cadaver putridum.

verses.text: Thou shalt not keep company with them, even in burial: for thou hast destroyed thy land, thou hast slain thy people: the seed of the wicked shall not be named for ever.
verses.textLatin: Non habebis consortium, neque cum eis in sepultura; tu enim terram tuam disperdidisti, tu populum tuum occidisti: non vocabitur in æternum semen pessimorum.

verses.text: Prepare his children for slaughter for the iniquity of their fathers: they shall not rise up, nor inherit the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.
verses.textLatin: Præparate filios ejus occisioni, in iniquitate patrum suorum: non consurgent, nec hæreditabunt terram, neque implebunt faciem orbis civitatum.

verses.text: And I will rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will destroy the name of Babylon, and the remains, and the bud, and the offspring, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et consurgam super eos, dicit Dominus exercituum; et perdam Babylonis nomen, et reliquias, et germen, et progeniem, dicit Dominus;

verses.text: And I will make it a possession for the ericius and pools of waters, and I will sweep it and wear it out with a besom, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: et ponam eam in possessionem ericii, et in paludes aquarum, et scopabo eam in scopa terens, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: The Lord of hosts hath sworn, saying: Surely as I have thought, so shall it be: and as I have purposed,
verses.textLatin: Juravit Dominus exercituum, dicens: Si non, ut putavi, ita erit; et quomodo mente tractavi,

verses.text: So shall it fall out: That I will destroy the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot: and his yoke shall be taken away from them, and his burden shall be taken off their shoulder.
verses.textLatin: sic eveniet: ut conteram Assyrium in terra mea, et in montibus meis conculcem eum; et auferetur ab eis jugum ejus, et onus illius ab humero eorum tolletur.

verses.text: This is the counsel, that I have purposed upon all the earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all nations.
verses.textLatin: Hoc consilium quod cogitavi super omnem terram; et hæc est manus extenta super universas gentes.

verses.text: For the Lord of hosts hath decreed, and who can disannul it? and his hand is stretched out: and who shall turn it away?
verses.textLatin: Dominus enim exercituum decrevit; et quis poterit infirmare? et manus ejus extenta; et quis avertet eam?

verses.text: In the year that king Achaz died, was this burden:
verses.textLatin: In anno quo mortuus est rex Achaz, factum est onus istud:

verses.text: Rejoice not thou, whole Philistia, that the rod of him that struck thee is broken in pieces: for out of the root of the serpent shall come forth a basilisk, and his seed shall swallow the bird.
verses.textLatin: Ne lætaris, Philisthæa omnis tu, quoniam comminuta est virga percussoris tui; de radice enim colubri egredietur regulus, et semen ejus absorbens volucrem.

verses.text: And the firstborn of the poor shall be fed, and the poor shall rest with confidence: and I will make thy root perish with famine, and I will kill thy remnant.
verses.textLatin: Et pascentur primogeniti pauperum, et pauperes fiducialiter requiescent; et interire faciam in fame radicem tuam, et reliquias tuas interficiam.

verses.text: Howl, O gate; cry, O city: all Philistia is thrown down: for a smoke shall come from the north, and there is none that shall escape his troop.
verses.textLatin: Ulula, porta; clama civitas; prostrata est Philisthæa omnis; ab aquilone enim fumus veniet, et non est qui effugiet agmen ejus.

verses.text: And what shall be answered to the messengers of the nations? That the Lord hath founded Sion, and the poor of his people shall hope in him.
verses.textLatin: Et quid respondebitur nuntiis gentis? Quia Dominus fundavit Sion, et in ipso sperabunt pauperes populi ejus.

verses.text: The  burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, it is silent: because the wall of Moab is destroyed in the night, it is silent.
verses.textLatin: Onus Moab. Quia nocte vastata est Ar Moab, conticuit; quia nocte vastatus est murus Moab, conticuit.

verses.text: The house is gone up, and Dibon to the high places to mourn over Nabo, and over Medaba, Moab hath howled: on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard shall be shaven.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit domus, et Dibon ad excelsa, in planctum super Nabo; et super Medaba, Moab ululavit; in cunctis capitibus ejus calvitium, et omnis barba radetur.

verses.text: In their streets they are girded with sackcloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their streets all shall howl and come down weeping.
verses.textLatin: In triviis ejus accincti sunt sacco; super tecta ejus et in plateis ejus omnis ululatus descendit in fletum.

verses.text: Hesebon shall cry, and Eleale, their voice is heard even to Jasa. For this shall the well appointed men of Moab howl, his soul shall howl to itself.
verses.textLatin: Clamabit Hesebon et Eleale, usque Jasa audita est vox eorum; super hoc expediti Moab ululabunt, anima ejus ululabit sibi.

verses.text: My heart shall cry to Moab, the bars thereof shall flee unto Segor a heifer of three years old: for by the ascent of Luith they shall go up weeping: and in the way of Oronaim they shall lift up a cry of destruction.
verses.textLatin: Cor meum ad Moab clamabit; vectes ejus usque ad Segor, vitulam conternantem; per ascensum enim Luith flens ascendet, et in via Oronaim clamorem contritionis levabunt.

verses.text: For the waters of Nemrim shall be desolate, for the grass is withered away, the spring is faded, all the greenness is perished.
verses.textLatin: Aquæ enim Nemrim desertæ erunt, quia aruit herba, defecit germen, viror omnis interiit.

verses.text: According to the greatness of their work, is their visitation also: they shall lead them to the torrent of the willows.
verses.textLatin: Secundum magnitudinem operis, et visitatio eorum: ad torrentem Salicum ducent eos.

verses.text: For the cry is gone round about the border of Moab: the howling thereof unto Gallim, and unto the well of Elim the cry thereof.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam circuivit clamor terminum Moab; usque ad Gallim ululatus ejus, et usque ad puteum Elim clamor ejus.

verses.text: For the waters of Dibon are filled with blood: for I will bring more upon Dibon: the lion upon them that shall flee of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land.
verses.textLatin: Quia aquæ Dibon repletæ sunt sanguine; ponam enim super Dibon additamenta; his qui fugerint de Moab leonem, et reliquiis terræ.

verses.text: Send  forth, O Lord, the lamb, the ruler of the earth, from Petra of the desert, to the mount of the daughter of Sion.
verses.textLatin: Emitte agnum, Domine, dominatorem terræ, de petra deserti ad montem filiæ Sion.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that as a bird fleeing away, and as young ones flying out of the nest, so shall the daughters of Moab be in the passage of Arnon.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: sicut avis fugiens, et pulli de nido avolantes, sic erunt filiæ Moab in transcensu Arnon.

verses.text: Take counsel, gather a council: make thy shadow as the night in the midday: hide them that flee, and betray not them that wander about.
verses.textLatin: Ini consilium, coge concilium; pone quasi noctem umbram tuam in meridie; absconde fugientes, et vagos ne prodas.

verses.text: My fugitives shall dwell with thee: O Moab, be thou a covert to them from the face of the destroyer: for the dust is at an end, the wretch is consumed: he hath failed, that trod the earth under foot.
verses.textLatin: Habitabunt apud te profugi mei; Moab, esto latibulum eorum a facie vastatoris: finitus est enim pulvis, consummatus est miser, defecit qui conculcabat terram.

verses.text: And a throne shall be prepared in mercy, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment and quickly rendering that which is just.
verses.textLatin: Et præparabitur in misericordia solium, et sedebit super illud in veritate in tabernaculo David, judicans et quærens judicium, et velociter reddens quod justum est.

verses.text: We have heard of the pride of Moab, he is exceeding proud: his pride and his arrogancy, and his indignation is more than his strength.
verses.textLatin: Audivimus superbiam Moab: superbus est valde; superbia ejus, et arrogantia ejus, et indignatio ejus plus quam fortitudo ejus.

verses.text: Therefore shall Moab howl to Moab, every one shall howl: to them that rejoice upon the brick walls, tell ye their stripes.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco ululabit Moab ad Moab; universus ululabit: his qui lætantur super muros cocti lateris, loquimini plagas suas.

verses.text: For the suburbs of Hesebon are desolate, and the lords of the nations have destroyed the vineyard of Sabama: the branches thereof have reached even to Jazer: they have wandered in the wilderness, the branches thereof are left, they are gone over the sea.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam suburbana Hesebon deserta sunt, et vineam Sabama domini gentium exciderunt: flagella ejus usque ad Jazer pervenerunt, erraverunt in deserto; propagines ejus relictæ sunt, transierunt mare.

verses.text: Therefore I will lament with the weeping of Jazer the vineyard of Sabama: I will water thee with my tears, O Hesebon, and Eleale: for the voice of the treaders hath rushed in upon thy vintage, and upon thy harvest.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc plorabo in fletu Jazer vineam Sabama; inebriabo de lacrima mea, Hesebon et Eleale, quoniam super vindemiam tuam et super messem tuam vox calcantium irruit.

verses.text: And gladness and joy shall be taken away from Carmel, and there shall be no rejoicing nor shouting in the vineyards. He shall not tread out wine in the press that was wont to tread it out: the voice of the treaders I have taken away.
verses.textLatin: Et auferetur lætitia et exsultatio de Carmelo, et in vineis non exsultabit neque jubilabit. Vinum in torculari non calcabit qui calcare consueverat; vocem calcantium abstuli.

verses.text: Wherefore my bowels shall sound like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for the brick wall.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc venter meus ad Moab quasi cithara sonabit, et viscera mea ad murum cocti lateris.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, when it is seen that Moab is wearied on his high places, that he shall go in to his sanctuaries to pray, and shall not prevail.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: cum apparuerit quod laboravit Moab super excelsis suis, ingredietur ad sancta sua ut obsecret, et non valebit.

verses.text: This is the word, that the Lord spoke to Moab from that time:
verses.textLatin: Hoc verbum quod locutus est Dominus ad Moab ex tunc.

verses.text: And now the Lord hath spoken, saying: In three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be taken away for all the multitude of the people, and it shall be left small and feeble, not many.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc locutus est Dominus, dicens: In tribus annis, quasi anni mercenarii, auferetur gloria Moab super omni populo multo, et relinquetur parvus et modicus, nequaquam multus.

verses.text: The  burden of Damascus. Behold Damascus shall cease to be a city, and shall be as a ruinous heap of stones.
verses.textLatin: Onus Damasci. Ecce Damascus desinet esse civitas, et erit sicut acervus lapidum in ruina.

verses.text: The cities of Aroer shall be left for flocks, and they shall rest there, and there shall be none to make them afraid.
verses.textLatin: Derelictæ civitates Aroër gregibus erunt, et requiescent ibi, et non erit qui exterreat.

verses.text: And aid shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus: and the remnant of Syria shall be as the glory of the children of Israel: saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et cessabit adjutorium ab Ephraim, et regnum a Damasco; et reliquiæ Syriæ sicut gloria filiorum Israël erunt, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall grow lean.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: attenuabitur gloria Jacob, et pinguedo carnis ejus marcescet.

verses.text: And it shall be as when one gathereth in the harvest that which remaineth, and his arm shall gather the ears of corn: and it shall be as he that seeketh ears in the vale of Raphaim.
verses.textLatin: Et erit sicut congregans in messe quod restiterit, et brachium ejus spicas leget; et erit sicut quærens spicas in valle Raphaim.

verses.text: And the fruit thereof that shall be left upon it, shall be as one cluster of grapes, and as the shaking of the olive tree, two or three berries in the top of a bough, or four or five upon the top of the tree, saith the Lord the God of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et relinquetur in eo sicut racemus et sicut excussio oleæ duarum vel trium olivarum in summitate rami, sive quatuor aut quinque in cacuminibus ejus fructus ejus, dicit Dominus Deus Israël.

verses.text: In that day man shall bow down himself to his Maker, and his eyes shall look to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.textLatin: In die illa inclinabitur homo ad factorem suum, et oculi ejus ad Sanctum Israël respicient;

verses.text: And he shall not look to the altars which his hands made: and he shall not have respect to the things that his fingers wrought, such as groves and temples.
verses.textLatin: et non inclinabitur ad altaria quæ fecerunt manus ejus; et quæ operati sunt digiti ejus non respiciet lucos et delubra.

verses.text: In that day his strong cities shall be forsaken, as the ploughs, and the corn that were left before the face of the children of Israel, and thou shalt be desolate.
verses.textLatin: In die illa erunt civitates fortitudinis ejus derelictæ sicut aratra, et segetes quæ derelictæ sunt a facie filiorum Israël; et eris deserta.

verses.text: Because thou hast forgotten God thy saviour, and hast not remembered thy strong helper: therefore shalt thou plant good plants, and shalt sow strange seed.
verses.textLatin: Quia oblitus es Dei salvatoris tui, et fortis adjutoris tui non es recordata: propterea plantabis plantationem fidelem, et germen alienum seminabis;

verses.text: In the day of thy planting shall be the wild grape, and in the morning thy seed shall flourish: the harvest is taken away in the day of inheritance, and shall grieve thee much.
verses.textLatin: in die plantationis tuæ labrusca, et mane semen tuum florebit; ablata est messis in die hæreditatis, et dolebit graviter.

verses.text: Woe to the multitude of many people, like the multitude of the roaring sea: and the tumult of crowds, like the noise of many waters.
verses.textLatin: Væ multitudini populorum multorum, ut multitudo maris sonantis; et tumultus turbarum, sicut sonitus aquarum multarum.

verses.text: Nations shall make a noise like the noise of waters overflowing, but he shall rebuke him, and he shall flee far off: and he shall be carried away as the dust of the mountains before the wind, and as a whirlwind before a tempest.
verses.textLatin: Sonabunt populi sicut sonitus aquarum inundantium, et increpabit eum, et fugiet procul; et rapietur sicut pulvis montium a facie venti, et sicut turbo coram tempestate.

verses.text: In the time of the evening, behold there shall be trouble: the morning shall come, and he shall not be: this is the portion of them that have wasted us, and the lot of them that spoiled us.
verses.textLatin: In tempore vespere, et ecce turbatio; in matutino, et non subsistet. Hæc est pars eorum qui vastaverunt nos, et sors diripientium nos.

verses.text: Woe  to the land, the winged cymbal, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
verses.textLatin: Væ terræ cymbalo alarum, quæ est trans flumina Æthiopiæ,

verses.text: That sendeth ambassadors by the sea, and in vessels of bulrushes upon the waters. Go, ye swift angels, to a nation rent and torn in pieces: to a terrible people, after which there is no other: to a nation expecting and trodden underfoot, whose land the rivers have spoiled.
verses.textLatin: qui mittit in mare legatos, et in vasis papyri super aquas. Ite, angeli veloces, ad gentem convulsam et dilaceratam; ad populum terribilem, post quem non est alius; ad gentem exspectantem et conculcatam, cujus diripuerunt flumina terram ejus.

verses.text: All ye inhabitants of the world, who dwell on the earth, when the sign shall be lifted up on the mountains, you shall see, and you shall hear the sound of the trumpet.
verses.textLatin: Omnes habitatores orbis, qui moramini in terra, cum elevatum fuerit signum in montibus, videbitis, et clangorem tubæ audietis.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord to me: I will take my rest, and consider in my place, as the noon light is clear, and as a cloud of dew in the day of harvest.
verses.textLatin: Quia hæc dicit Dominus ad me: Quiescam et considerabo in loco meo, sicut meridiana lux clara est, et sicut nubes roris in die messis.

verses.text: For before the harvest it was all flourishing, and it shall bud without perfect ripeness, and the sprigs thereof shall be cut off with pruning hooks: and what is left shall be cut away and shaken out.
verses.textLatin: Ante messem enim totus effloruit, et immatura perfectio germinabit; et præcidentur ramusculi ejus falcibus, et quæ derelicta fuerint abscindentur et excutientur.

verses.text: And they shall be left together to the birds of the mountains, and the beasts of the earth: and the fowls shall be upon them all the summer, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them.
verses.textLatin: Et relinquentur simul avibus montium et bestiis terræ; et æstate perpetua erunt super eum volucres, et omnes bestiæ terræ super illum hiemabunt.

verses.text: At that time shall a present be brought to the Lord of hosts, from a people rent and torn in pieces: from a terrible people, after which there hath been no other: from a nation expecting, expecting and trodden under foot, whose land the rivers have spoiled, to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, to mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: In tempore illo deferetur munus Domino exercituum a populo divulso et dilacerato, a populo terribili, post quem non fuit alius; a gente exspectante, exspectante et conculcata, cujus diripuerunt flumina terram ejus; ad locum nominis Domini exercituum, montem Sion.

verses.text: The  burden of Egypt. Behold the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud, and will enter into Egypt, and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst thereof.
verses.textLatin: Onus Ægypti. Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, et ingredietur Ægyptum, et commovebuntur simulacra Ægypti a facie ejus, et cor Ægypti tabescet in medio ejus,

verses.text: And I will set the Egyptians to fight against the Egyptians: and they shall fight brother against brother, and friend against friend, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
verses.textLatin: et concurrere faciam Ægyptios adversus Ægyptios; et pugnabit vir contra fratrem suum, et vir contra amicum suum, civitas adversus civitatem, regnum adversus regnum.

verses.text: And the spirit of Egypt shall be broken in the bowels thereof, and I will cast down their counsel: and they shall consult their idols, and their diviners, and their wizards, and soothsayers.
verses.textLatin: Et dirumpetur spiritus Ægypti in visceribus ejus, et consilium ejus præcipitabo; et interrogabunt simulacra sua, et divinos suos, et pythones, et ariolos.

verses.text: And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of cruel masters, and a strong king shall rule over them, saith the Lord the God of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et tradam Ægyptum in manu dominorum crudelium, et rex fortis dominabitur eorum, ait Dominus Deus exercituum.

verses.text: And the water of the sea shall be dried up, and the river shall be wasted and dry.
verses.textLatin: Et arescet aqua de mari, et fluvius desolabitur atque siccabitur.

verses.text: And the rivers shall fail: the streams of the banks shall be diminished, and be dried up. The reed and the bulrush shall wither away.
verses.textLatin: Et deficient flumina, attenuabuntur et siccabuntur rivi aggerum, calamus et juncus marcescet.

verses.text: The channel of the river shall be laid bare from its fountain, and every thing sown by the water shall be dried up, it shall wither away, and shall be no more.
verses.textLatin: Nudabitur alveus rivi a fonte suo, et omnis sementis irrigua siccabitur, arescet, et non erit.

verses.text: The fishers also shall mourn, and all that cast a hook into the river shall lament, and they that spread nets upon the waters shall languish away.
verses.textLatin: Et mœrebunt piscatores, et lugebunt omnes mittentes in flumen hamum; et expandentes rete super faciem aquarum emarcescent.

verses.text: They shall be confounded that wrought in flax, combing and weaving fine linen.
verses.textLatin: Confundentur qui operabantur linum, pectentes et texentes subtilia.

verses.text: And its watery places shall be dry, all they shall mourn that made pools to take fishes.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt irrigua ejus flaccentia: omnes qui faciebant lacunas ad capiendos pisces.

verses.text: The princes of Tanis are become fools, the wise counsellors of Pharao have given foolish counsel: how will you say to Pharao: I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?
verses.textLatin: Stulti principes Taneos, sapientes consiliarii Pharaonis dederunt consilium insipiens. Quomodo dicetis Pharaoni: Filius sapientium ego, filius regum antiquorum?

verses.text: Where are now thy wise men? let them tell thee, and shew what the Lord of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Ubi nunc sunt sapientes tui? annuntient tibi, et indicent quid cogitaverit Dominus exercituum super Ægyptum.

verses.text: The princes of Tanis are become fools, the princes of Memphis are gone astray, they have deceived Egypt, the stay of the people thereof.
verses.textLatin: Stulti facti sunt principes Taneos, emarcuerunt principes Mempheos; deceperunt Ægyptum, angulum populorum ejus.

verses.text: The Lord hath mingled in the midst thereof the spirit of giddiness: and they have caused Egypt to err in all its works, as a drunken man staggereth and vomiteth.
verses.textLatin: Dominus miscuit in medio ejus spiritum vertiginis; et errare fecerunt Ægyptum in omni opere suo, sicut errat ebrius et vomens.

verses.text: And there shall be no work for Egypt, to make head or tail, him that bendeth down, or that holdeth back.
verses.textLatin: Et non erit Ægypto opus quod faciat caput et caudam, incurvantem et refrenantem.

verses.text: In that day Egypt shall be like unto women, and they shall be amazed, and afraid, because of the moving of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shall move over it.
verses.textLatin: In die illa erit Ægyptus quasi mulieres; et stupebunt, et timebunt a facie commotionis manus Domini exercituum, quam ipse movebit super eam.

verses.text: And the land of Juda shall be a terror to Egypt: every one that shall remember it shall tremble because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he hath determined concerning it.
verses.textLatin: Et erit terra Juda Ægypto in pavorem; omnis qui illius fuerit recordatus pavebit a facie consilii Domini exercituum, quod ipse cogitavit super eam.

verses.text: In that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt, speaking the language of Chanaan, and swearing by the Lord of hosts: one shall be called the city of the sun.
verses.textLatin: In die illa erunt quinque civitates in terra Ægypti loquentes lingua Chanaan, et jurantes per Dominum exercituum: Civitas solis vocabitur una.

verses.text: In that day there shall be an altar of the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a monument of the Lord at the borders thereof:
verses.textLatin: In die illa erit altare Domini in medio terræ Ægypti, et titulus Domini juxta terminum ejus.

verses.text: It shall be for a sign, and for a testimony to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt. For they shall cry to the Lord because of the oppressor, and he shall send them a Saviour and a defender to deliver them.
verses.textLatin: Erit in signum et in testimonium Domino exercituum in terra Ægypti; clamabunt enim ad Dominum a facie tribulationis, et mittet eis salvatorem et propugnatorem qui liberet eos.

verses.text: And the Lord shall be known by Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day, and shall worship him with sacrifices and offerings: and they shall make vows to the Lord, and perform them.
verses.textLatin: Et cognoscetur Dominus ab Ægypto, et cognoscent Ægyptii Dominum in die illa; et colent eum in hostiis et in muneribus; et vota vovebunt Domino, et solvent.

verses.text: And the Lord shall strike Egypt with a scourge, and shall heal it, and they shall return to the Lord, and he shall be pacified towards them, and heal them.
verses.textLatin: Et percutiet Dominus Ægyptum plaga, et sanabit eam; et revertentur ad Dominum, et placabitur eis, et sanabit eos.

verses.text: In that day there shall be a way from Egypt to the Assyrians, and the Assyrian shall enter into Egypt, and the Egyptian to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians shall serve the Assyrian.
verses.textLatin: In die illa erit via de Ægypto in Assyrios; et intrabit Assyrius Ægyptum, et Ægyptius in Assyrios, et servient Ægyptii Assur.

verses.text: In that day shall Israel be the third to the Egyptian and the Assyrian: a blessing in the midst of the land,
verses.textLatin: In die illa erit Israël tertius Ægyptio et Assyrio; benedictio in medio terræ

verses.text: Which the Lord of hosts hath blessed, saying: Blessed be my people of Egypt, and the work of my hands to the Assyrian: but Israel is my inheritance.
verses.textLatin: cui benedixit Dominus exercituum, dicens: Benedictus populus meus Ægypti, et opus manuum mearum Assyrio; hæreditas autem mea Israël.

verses.text: In  the year that Tharthan entered into Azotus, when Sargon the king of the Assyrians had sent him, and he had fought against Azotus, and had taken it:
verses.textLatin: In anno quo ingressus est Thathan in Azotum, cum misisset eum Sargon, rex Assyriorum, et pugnasset contra Azotum, et cepisset eam:

verses.text: At that same time the Lord spoke by the hand of Isaias the son of Amos, saying: Go, and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and take off thy shoes from thy feet. And he did so, and went naked, and barefoot.
verses.textLatin: in tempore illo locutus est Dominus in manu Isaiæ, filii Amos, dicens: Vade, et solve saccum de lumbis tuis, et calceamenta tua tolle de pedibus tuis. Et fecit sic, vadens nudus et discalceatus.

verses.text: And the Lord said: As my servant Isaias hath walked, naked and barefoot, it shall be a sign and a wonder of three years upon Egypt, and upon Ethiopia,
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus: Sicut ambulavit servus meus Isaias nudus et discalceatus, trium annorum signum et portentum erit super Ægyptum et super Æthiopiam;

verses.text: So shall the king of the Assyrians lead away the prisoners of Egypt, and the captivity of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered to the shame of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: sic minabit rex Assyriorum captivitatem Ægypti, et transmigrationem Æthiopiæ, juvenum et senum, nudam et discalceatam, discoopertis natibus, ad ignominiam Ægypti.

verses.text: And they shall be afraid, and ashamed of Ethiopia their hope, and of Egypt their glory.
verses.textLatin: Et timebunt, et confundentur ab Æthiopia spe sua, et ab Ægypto gloria sua.

verses.text: And the inhabitants of this isle shall say in that day: Lo this was our hope, to whom we fled for help, to deliver us from the face of the king of the Assyrians: and how shall we be able to escape?
verses.textLatin: Et dicet habitator insulæ hujus in die illa: Ecce hæc erat spes nostra, ad quos confugimus in auxilium, ut liberarent nos a facie regis Assyriorum: et quomodo effugere poterimus nos?

verses.text: The burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds come from the south, it cometh from the desert from a terrible land.
verses.textLatin: Onus deserti maris. Sicut turbines ab africo veniunt, de deserto venit, de terra horribili.

verses.text: A grievous vision is told me: he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully: and he that is a spoiler, spoileth. Go up, O Elam, besiege, O Mede: I have made all the mourning thereof to cease.
verses.textLatin: Visio dura nuntiata est mihi: qui incredulus est infideliter agit; et qui depopulator est vastat. Ascende, Ælam; obside, Mede; omnem gemitum ejus cessare feci.

verses.text: Therefore are my loins filled with pain, anguish hath taken hold of me, as the anguish of a woman in labour: I fell down at the hearing of it, I was troubled at the seeing of it.
verses.textLatin: Propterea repleti sunt lumbi mei dolore; angustia possedit me sicut angustia parturientis; corrui cum audirem, conturbatus sum cum viderem.

verses.text: My heart failed, darkness amazed me: Babylon my beloved is become a wonder to me.
verses.textLatin: Emarcuit cor meum; tenebræ stupefecerunt me: Babylon dilecta mea posita est mihi in miraculum.

verses.text: Prepare the table, behold in the watchtower them that eat and drink: arise, ye princes, take up the shield.
verses.textLatin: Pone mensam, contemplare in specula comedentes et bibentes: surgite, principes, arripite clypeum.

verses.text: For thus hath the Lord said to me: Go, and set a watchman: and whatsoever he shall see, let him tell.
verses.textLatin: Hæc enim dixit mihi Dominus: Vade, et pone speculatorem, et quodcumque viderit annuntiet.

verses.text: And he saw a chariot with two horsemen, a rider upon an ass, and a rider upon a camel: and he beheld them diligently with much heed.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit currum duorum equitum, ascensorem asini, et ascensorem cameli; et contemplatus est diligenter multo intuitu.

verses.text: And a lion cried out: I am upon the watchtower of the Lord, standing continually by day: and I am upon my ward, standing whole nights.
verses.textLatin: Et clamavit leo: Super speculam Domini ego sum, stans jugiter per diem; et super custodiam meam ego sum, stans totis noctibus.

verses.text: Behold this man cometh, the rider upon the chariot with two horsemen, and he answered, and said: Babylon is fallen, she is fallen, and all the graven gods thereof are broken unto the ground.
verses.textLatin: Ecce iste venit ascensor vir bigæ equitum; et respondit, et dixit: Cecidit, cecidit Babylon, et omnia sculptilia deorum ejus contrita sunt in terram.

verses.text: O my thrashing, and the children of my floor, that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared unto you.
verses.textLatin: Tritura mea et filii areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino exercituum, Deo Israël, annuntiavi vobis.

verses.text: The burden of Duma calleth to me out of Seir: Watchman, what of the night? watchman, what of the night?
verses.textLatin: Onus Duma. Ad me clamat ex Seir: Custos, quid de nocte? custos, quid de nocte?

verses.text: The watchman said: The morning cometh, also the night: if you seek, seek: return, come.
verses.textLatin: Dixit custos: Venit mane et nox; si quæritis, quærite; convertimini, venite.

verses.text: The burden in Arabia. In the forest at evening you shall sleep, in the paths of Dedanim.
verses.textLatin: Onus in Arabia. In saltu ad vesperam dormietis, in semitis Dedanim.

verses.text: Meeting the thirsty bring him water, you that inhabit the land of the south, meet with bread him that fleeth.
verses.textLatin: Occurrentes sitienti ferte aquam, qui habitatis terram austri; cum panibus occurrite fugienti.

verses.text: For they are fled from before the swords, from the sword that hung over them, from the bent bow, from the face of a grievous battle.
verses.textLatin: A facie enim gladiorum fugerunt, a facie gladii imminentis, a facie arcus extenti, a facie gravis prælii.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord to me: Within a year, according to the years of a hireling, all the glory of Cedar shall be taken away.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam hæc dicit Dominus ad me: Adhuc in uno anno, quasi in anno mercenarii, et auferetur omnis gloria Cedar.

verses.text: And the residue of the number of strong archers of the children of Cedar shall be diminished: for the Lord the God of Israel hath spoken it.
verses.textLatin: Et reliquiæ numeri sagittariorum fortium de filiis Cedar imminuentur; Dominus enim Deus Israël locutus est.

verses.text: The burden of the valley of vision. What aileth thee also, that thou too art wholly gone up to the housetops?
verses.textLatin: Onus vallis Visionis. Quidnam quoque tibi est, quia ascendisti et tu omnis in tecta?

verses.text: Full of clamour, a populous city, a joyous city: thy slain are not slain by the sword, nor dead in battle.
verses.textLatin: Clamoris plena, urbs frequens, civitas exsultans; interfecti tui, non interfecti gladio, nec mortui in bello.

verses.text: All the princes are fled together, and are bound hard: all that were found, are bound together, they are fled far off.
verses.textLatin: Cuncti principes tui fugerunt simul dureque ligati sunt; omnes qui inventi sunt vincti sunt pariter; procul fugerunt.

verses.text: Therefore have I said: Depart from me, I will weep bitterly: labour not to comfort me, for the devastation of the daughter of my people.
verses.textLatin: Propterea dixi: Recedite a me: amare flebo; nolite incumbere ut consolemini me super vastitate filiæ populi mei;

verses.text: For it is a day of slaughter and of treading down, and of weeping to the Lord the God of hosts in the valley of vision, searching the wall, and magnificent upon the mountain.
verses.textLatin: dies enim interfectionis, et conculcationis, et fletuum, Domino Deo exercituum, in valle Visionis, scrutans murum, et magnificus super montem.

verses.text: And Elam took the quiver, the chariot of the horseman, and the shield was taken down from the wall.
verses.textLatin: Et Ælam sumpsit pharetram, currum hominis equitis, et parietem nudavit clypeus.

verses.text: And thy choice valleys shall be full of chariots, and the horsemen shall place themselves in the gate.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt electæ valles tuæ plenæ quadrigarum, et equites ponent sedes suas in porta.

verses.text: And the covering of Juda shall be discovered, and thou shalt see in that day the armoury of the house of the forest.
verses.textLatin: Et revelabitur operimentum Judæ, et videbis in die illa armamentarium domus saltus.

verses.text: And you shall see the breaches of the city of David, that they are many: and you have gathered together the waters of the lower pool,
verses.textLatin: Et scissuras civitatis David videbitis, quia multiplicatæ sunt; et congregastis aquas piscinæ inferioris,

verses.text: And have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and broken down houses to fortify the wall.
verses.textLatin: et domos Jerusalem numerastis, et destruxistis domos ad muniendum murum.
