verses.text: And you made a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool: and you have not looked up to the maker thereof, nor regarded him even at a distance, that wrought it long ago.
verses.textLatin: Et lacum fecistis inter duos muros ad aquam piscinæ veteris; et non suspexistis ad eum qui fecerat eam, et operatorem ejus de longe non vidistis.

verses.text: And the Lord, the God of hosts, in that day shall call to weeping, and to mourning, to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
verses.textLatin: Et vocabit Dominus Deus exercituum in die illa ad fletum, et ad planctum, ad calvitium, et ad cingulum sacci;

verses.text: And behold joy and gladness, killing calves, and slaying rams, eating flesh, and drinking wine: Let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die.
verses.textLatin: et ecce gaudium et lætitia, occidere vitulos et jugulare arietes, comedere carnes, et bibere vinum: comedamus et bibamus, cras enim moriemur.

verses.text: And the voice of the Lord of hosts was revealed in my ears: Surely this iniquity shall not be forgiven you till you die, saith the Lord God of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et revelata est in auribus meis vox Domini exercituum: Si dimittetur iniquitas hæc vobis donec moriamini, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God of hosts: Go, get thee in to him that dwelleth in the tabernacle, to Sobna who is over the temple: and thou shalt say to him:
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus exercituum: Vade, ingredere ad eum qui habitat in tabernaculo, ad Sobnam, præpositum templi, et dices ad eum:

verses.text: What dost thou here, or as if thou wert somebody here? for thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, thou hast hewed out a monument carefully in a high place, a dwelling for thyself in a rock.
verses.textLatin: Quid tu hic, aut quasi quis hic? quia excidisti tibi hic sepulchrum, excidisti in excelso memoriale diligenter, in petra tabernaculum tibi.

verses.text: Behold the Lord will cause thee to be carried away, as a cock is carried away, and he will lift thee up as a garment.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Dominus asportari te faciet, sicut asportatur gallus gallinaceus; et quasi amictum, sic sublevabit te.

verses.text: He will crown thee with a crown of tribulation, he will toss thee like a ball into a large and spacious country: there shalt thou die, and there shall the chariot of thy glory be, the shame of the house of thy Lord.
verses.textLatin: Coronas coronabit te tribulatione; quasi pilam mittet te in terram latam et spatiosam; ibi morieris, et ibi erit currus gloriæ tuæ, ignominia domus domini tui.

verses.text: And I will drive thee out from thy station, and depose thee from thy ministry.
verses.textLatin: Et expellam te de statione tua, et de ministerio tuo deponam te.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliacim the son of Helcias,
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: vocabo servum meum Eliacim, filium Helciæ,

verses.text: And I will clothe him with thy robe, and will strengthen him with thy girdle, and will give thy power into his hand: and he shall be as a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Juda.
verses.textLatin: et induam illum tunica tua, et cingulo tuo confortabo eum, et potestatem tuam dabo in manu ejus; et erit quasi pater habitantibus Jerusalem et domui Juda.

verses.text: And I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder: and he shall open, and none shall shut: and he shall shut, and none shall open.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo clavem domus David super humerum ejus; et aperiet, et non erit qui claudat; et claudet, et non erit qui aperiat.

verses.text: And I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place, and he shall be for a throne of glory to the house of his father.
verses.textLatin: Et figam illum paxillum in loco fideli, et erit in solium gloriæ domui patris ejus.

verses.text: And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father’s house, divers kinds of vessels, every little vessel, from the vessels of cups even to every instrument of music.
verses.textLatin: Et suspendent super eum omnem gloriam domus patris ejus; vasorum diversa genera, omne vas parvulum, a vasis craterarum usque ad omne vas musicorum.

verses.text: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, shall the peg be removed, that was fastened in the sure place: and it shall be broken and shall fall: and that which hung thereon, shall perish, because the Lord hath spoken it.
verses.textLatin: In die illa, dicit Dominus exercituum, auferetur paxillus qui fixus fuerat in loco fideli, et frangetur, et cadet, et peribit quod pependerat in eo, quia Dominus locutus est.

verses.text: The  burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of the sea, for the house is destroyed, from whence they were wont to come: from the land of Cethim it is revealed to them.
verses.textLatin: Onus Tyri. Ululate, naves maris, quia vastata est domus unde venire consueverant: de terra Cethim revelatum est eis.

verses.text: Be silent, you that dwell in the island: the merchants of Sidon passing over the sea, have filled thee.
verses.textLatin: Tacete, qui habitatis in insula; negotiatores Sidonis, transfretantes mare, repleverunt te.

verses.text: The seed of the Nile in many waters, the harvest of the river is her revenue: and she is become the mart of the nations.
verses.textLatin: In aquis multis semen Nili; messis fluminis fruges ejus: et facta est negotiatio gentium.

verses.text: Be thou ashamed, O Sidon: for the sea speaketh, even the strength of the sea, saying: I have not been in labour, nor have I brought forth, nor have I nourished up young men, nor brought up virgins.
verses.textLatin: Erubesce, Sidon; ait enim mare, fortitudo maris, dicens: Non parturivi, et non peperi, et non enutrivi juvenes, nec ad incrementum perduxi virgines.

verses.text: When it shall be heard in Egypt, they will be sorry when they shall hear of Tyre:
verses.textLatin: Cum auditum fuerit in Ægypto, dolebunt cum audierint de Tiro.

verses.text: Pass over the seas, howl, ye inhabitants of the island.
verses.textLatin: Transite maria, ululate, qui habitatis in insula!

verses.text: Is not this your city, which gloried from of old in her antiquity? her feet shall carry her afar off to sojourn.
verses.textLatin: Numquid non vestra hæc est, quæ gloriabatur a diebus pristinis in antiquitate sua? Ducent eam pedes sui longe ad peregrinandum.

verses.text: Who hath taken this counsel against Tyre, that was formerly crowned, whose merchants were princes, and her traders the nobles of the earth?
verses.textLatin: Quis cogitavit hoc super Tyrum quondam coronatam, cujus negotiatores principes, institores ejus inclyti terræ?

verses.text: The Lord of hosts hath designed it, to pull down the pride of all glory, and bring to disgrace all the glorious ones of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Dominus exercituum cogitavit hoc, ut detraheret superbiam omnis gloriæ, et ad ignominiam deduceret universos inclytos terræ.

verses.text: Pass thy land as a river, O daughter of the sea, thou hast a girdle no more.
verses.textLatin: Transi terram tuam quasi flumen, filia maris! non est cingulum ultra tibi.

verses.text: He stretched out his hand over the sea, he troubled kingdoms: the Lord hath given a charge against Chanaan, to destroy the strong ones thereof.
verses.textLatin: Manum suam extendit super mare; conturbavit regna. Dominus mandavit adversus Chanaan, ut contereret fortes ejus;

verses.text: And he said: Thou shalt glory no more, O virgin daughter of Sidon, who art oppressed: arise and sail over to Cethim, there also thou shalt have no rest.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Non adjicies ultra ut glorieris, calumniam sustinens virgo filia Sidonis: in Cethim consurgens transfreta: ibi quoque non erit requies tibi.

verses.text: Behold the land of the Chaldeans, there was not such a people, the Assyrian founded it: they have led away the strong ones thereof into captivity, they have destroyed the houses thereof, they have brought it to ruin.
verses.textLatin: Ecce terra Chaldæorum, talis populus non fuit: Assur fundavit eam; in captivitatem traduxerunt robustos ejus, suffoderunt domos ejus, posuerunt eam in ruinam.

verses.text: Howl, O ye ships of the sea, for your strength is laid waste.
verses.textLatin: Ululate, naves maris, quia devastata est fortitudo vestra.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day that thou, O Tyre, shalt be forgotten, seventy years, according to the days of one king: but after seventy years, there shall be unto Tyre as the song of a harlot.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: in oblivione eris, o Tyre! septuaginta annis, sicut dies regis unius; post septuaginta autem annos erit Tyro quasi canticum meretricis:

verses.text: Take a harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten: sing well, sing many a song, that thou mayst be remembered.
verses.textLatin: Sume citharam, circui civitatem, meretrix oblivioni tradita: bene cane, frequenta canticum, ut memoria tui sit.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass after seventy years, that the Lord will visit Tyre, and will bring her back again to her traffic: and she shall commit fornication again with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit post septuaginta annos: visitabit Dominus Tyrum, et reducet eam ad mercedes suas, et rursum fornicabitur cum universis regnis terræ super faciem terræ;

verses.text: And her merchandise and her hire shall be sanctified to the Lord: they shall not be kept in store, nor laid up: for her merchandise shall be for them that shall dwell before the Lord, that they may eat unto fulness, and be clothed for a continuance.
verses.textLatin: et erunt negotiationes ejus et mercedes ejus sanctificatæ Domino: non condentur neque reponentur, quia his qui habitaverint coram Domino erit negotiatio ejus, ut manducent in saturitatem, et vestiantur usque ad vetustatem.

verses.text: Behold  the Lord shall lay waste the earth, and shall strip it, and shall afflict the face thereof, and scatter abroad the inhabitants thereof.
verses.textLatin: Ecce Dominus dissipabit terram: et nudabit eam, et affliget faciem ejus, et disperget habitatores ejus.

verses.text: And it shall be as with the people, so with the priest: and as with the servant, so with his master: as with the handmaid, so with her mistress: as with the buyer, so with the seller: as with the lender, so with the borrower: as with him that calleth for his money, so with him that oweth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos; et sicut servus, sic dominus ejus; sicut ancilla, sic domina ejus; sicut emens, sic ille qui vendit; sicut fœnerator, sic is qui mutuum accipit; sicut qui repetit, sic qui debet.

verses.text: With desolation shall the earth be laid waste, and it shall be utterly spoiled: for the Lord hath spoken this word.
verses.textLatin: Dissipatione dissipabitur terra, et direptione prædabitur; Dominus enim locutus est verbum hoc.

verses.text: The earth mourned, and faded away, and is weakened: the world faded away, the height of the people of the earth is weakened.
verses.textLatin: Luxit, et defluxit terra, et infirmata est; defluxit orbis, infirmata est altitudo populi terræ.

verses.text: And the earth is infected by the inhabitants thereof: because they have transgressed the laws, they have changed the ordinance, they have broken the everlasting covenant.
verses.textLatin: Et terra infecta est ab habitatoribus suis, quia transgressi sunt leges, mutaverunt jus, dissipaverunt fœdus sempiternum.

verses.text: Therefore shall a curse devour the earth, and the inhabitants thereof shall sin: and therefore they that dwell therein shall be mad, and few men shall be left.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc maledictio vorabit terram, et peccabunt habitatores ejus; ideoque insanient cultores ejus, et relinquentur homines pauci.

verses.text: The vintage hath mourned, the vine hath languished away, all the merryhearted have sighed.
verses.textLatin: Luxit vindemia, infirmata est vitis, ingemuerunt omnes qui lætabantur corde;

verses.text: The mirth of timbrels hath ceased, the noise of them that rejoice is ended, the melody of the harp is silent.
verses.textLatin: cessavit gaudium tympanorum, quievit sonitus lætantium, conticuit dulcedo citharæ.

verses.text: They shall not drink wine with a song: the drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.
verses.textLatin: Cum cantico non bibent vinum; amara erit potio bibentibus illam.

verses.text: The city of vanity is broken down, every house is shut up, no man cometh in.
verses.textLatin: Attrita est civitas vanitatis, clausa est omnis domus, nullo introëunte.

verses.text: There shall be a crying for wine in the streets: all mirth is forsaken: the joy of the earth is gone away.
verses.textLatin: Clamor erit super vino in plateis, deserta est omnia lætitia, translatum est gaudium terræ.

verses.text: Desolation is left in the city, and calamity shall oppress the gates.
verses.textLatin: Relicta est in urbe solitudo, et calamitas opprimet portas.

verses.text: For it shall be thus in the midst of the earth, in the midst of the people, as if a few olives, that remain, should be shaken out of the olive tree: or grapes, when the vintage is ended.
verses.textLatin: Quia hæc erunt in medio terræ in medio populorum, quomodo si paucæ olivæ quæ remanserunt excutiantur ex olea et racemi, cum fuerit finita vindemia.

verses.text: These shall lift up their voice, and shall give praise: when the Lord shall be glorified, they shall make a joyful noise from the sea.
verses.textLatin: Hi levabunt vocem suam, atque laudabunt: cum glorificatus fuerit Dominus, hinnient de mari.

verses.text: Therefore glorify ye the Lord in instruction: the name of the Lord God of Israel in the islands of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc in doctrinis glorificate Dominum; in insulis maris nomen Domini Dei Israël.

verses.text: From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one. And I said: My secret to myself, my secret to myself, woe is me: the prevaricators have prevaricated, and with the prevarication of transgressors they have prevaricated.
verses.textLatin: A finibus terræ laudes audivimus, gloriam Justi. Et dixi: Secretum meum mihi, secretum meum mihi. Væ mihi! prævaricantes prævaricati sunt, et prævaricatione transgressorum prævaricati sunt.

verses.text: Fear, and the pit, and the snare are upon thee, O thou inhabitant of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Formido, et fovea, et laqueus super te, qui habitator es terræ.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that he that shall flee from the noise of the fear, shall fall into the pit: and he that shall rid himself out of the pit, shall be taken in the snare: for the flood-gates from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: qui fugerit a voce formidinis cadet in foveam; et qui se explicaverit de fovea tenebitur laqueo; quia cataractæ de excelsis apertæ sunt et concutientur fundamenta terræ.

verses.text: With breaking shall the earth be broken, with crushing shall the earth be crushed, with trembling shall the earth be moved.
verses.textLatin: Confractione confringetur terra, contritione conteretur terra, commotione commovebitur terra;

verses.text: With shaking shall the earth be shaken as a drunken man, and shall be removed as the tent of one night: and the iniquity thereof shall be heavy upon it, and it shall fall, and not rise again.
verses.textLatin: agitatione agitabitur terra sicut ebrius, et auferetur quasi tabernaculum unius noctis; et gravabit eam iniquitas sua, et corruet, et non adjiciet ut resurgat.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that in that day the Lord shall visit upon the host of heaven on high, and upon the kings of the earth, on the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: in die illa visitabit Dominus super militiam cæli in excelso, et super reges terræ qui sunt super terram;

verses.text: And they shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle into the pit, and they shall be shut up there in prison: and after many days they shall be visited.
verses.textLatin: et congregabuntur in congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur ibi in carcere, et post multos dies visitabuntur.

verses.text: And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem, and shall be glorified in the sight of his ancients.
verses.textLatin: Et erubescet luna, et confundetur sol, cum regnaverit Dominus exercituum in monte Sion et in Jerusalem et in conspectu senum suorum fuerit glorificatus.

verses.text: O  LORD, thou art my God, I will exalt thee, and give glory to thy name: for thou hast done wonderful things, thy designs of old faithful, amen.
verses.textLatin: Domine, Deus meus es tu; exaltabo te, et confitebor nomini tuo: quoniam fecisti mirabilia, cogitationes antiquas fideles. Amen.

verses.text: For thou hast reduced the city to a heap, the strong city to ruin, the house of strangers, to be no city, and to be no more built up for ever.
verses.textLatin: Quia posuisti civitatem in tumulum, urbem fortem in ruinam, domum alienorum: ut non sit civitas, et in sempiternum non ædificetur.

verses.text: Therefore shall a strong people praise thee, the city of mighty nations shall fear thee.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc laudabit te populus fortis; civitas gentium robustarum timebit te:

verses.text: Because thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress: a refuge from the whirlwind, a shadow from the heat. For the blast of the mighty is like a whirlwind beating against a wall.
verses.textLatin: quia factus es fortitudo pauperi, fortitudo egeno in tribulatione sua, spes a turbine, umbraculum ab æstu; spiritus enim robustorum quasi turbo impellens parietem.

verses.text: Thou shalt bring down the tumult of strangers, as heat in thirst: and as with heat under a burning cloud, thou shalt make the branch of the mighty to wither away.
verses.textLatin: Sicut æstus in siti, tumultum alienorum humiliabis; et quasi calore sub nube torrente, propaginem fortium marcescere facies.

verses.text: And the Lord of hosts shall make unto all people in this mountain, a feast of fat things, a feast of wine, of fat things full of marrow, of wine purified from the lees.
verses.textLatin: Et faciet Dominus exercituum omnibus populis in monte hoc convivium pinguium, convivium vindemiæ, pinguium medullatorum, vindemiæ defæcatæ.

verses.text: And he shall destroy in this mountain the face of the bond with which all people were tied, and the web that he began over all nations.
verses.textLatin: Et præcipitabit in monte isto faciem vinculi colligati super omnes populos, et telam quam orditus est super omnes nationes.

verses.text: He shall cast death down headlong for ever: and the Lord God shall wipe away tears from every face, and the reproach of his people he shall take away from off the whole earth: for the Lord hath spoken it.
verses.textLatin: Præcipitabit mortem in sempiternum; et auferet Dominus Deus lacrimam ab omni facie, et opprobrium populi sui auferet de universa terra: quia Dominus locutus est.

verses.text: And they shall say in that day: Lo, this is our God, we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the Lord, we have patiently waited for him, we shall rejoice and be joyful in his salvation.
verses.textLatin: Et dicet in die illa: Ecce Deus noster iste; exspectavimus eum, et salvabit nos; iste Dominus, sustinuimus eum: exsultabimus, et lætabimur in salutari ejus.

verses.text: For the hand of the Lord shall rest in this mountain: and Moab shall be trodden down under him, as straw is broken in pieces with the wain.
verses.textLatin: Quia requiescet manus Domini in monte isto; et triturabitur Moab sub eo, sicuti teruntur paleæ in plaustro.

verses.text: And he shall stretch forth his hands under him, as he that swimmeth stretcheth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down his glory with the dashing of his hands.
verses.textLatin: Et extendet manus suas sub eo sicut extendit natans ad natandum; et humiliabit gloriam ejus cum allisione manuum ejus.

verses.text: And the bulwarks of thy high walls shall fall, and be brought low, and shall be pulled down to the ground, even to the dust.
verses.textLatin: Et munimenta sublimium murorum tuorum concident, et humiliabuntur, et detrahentur in terram usque ad pulverem.

verses.text: In  that day shall this canticle be sung in the land of Juda. Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein.
verses.textLatin: In die illa cantabitur canticum istud in terra Juda: Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Sion; salvator ponetur in ea murus et antemurale.

verses.text: Open ye the gates, and let the just nation, that keepeth the truth, enter in.
verses.textLatin: Aperite portas, et ingrediatur gens justa, custodiens veritatem.

verses.text: The old error is passed away: thou wilt keep peace: peace, because we have hoped in thee.
verses.textLatin: Vetus error abiit: servabis pacem; pacem, quia in te speravimus.

verses.text: You have hoped in the Lord for evermore, in the Lord God mighty for ever.
verses.textLatin: Sperastis in Domino in sæculis æternis; in Domino Deo forti in perpetuum.

verses.text: For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low. He shall bring it down even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust.
verses.textLatin: Quia incurvabit habitantes in excelso; civitatem sublimem humiliabit: humiliabit eam usque ad terram, detrahet eam usque ad pulverem.

verses.text: The foot shall tread it down, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy.
verses.textLatin: Conculcabit eam pes, pedes pauperis, gressus egenorum.

verses.text: The way of the just is right, the path of the just is right to walk in.
verses.textLatin: Semita justi recta est, rectus callis justi ad ambulandum.

verses.text: And in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, we have patiently waited for thee: thy name, and thy remembrance are the desire of the soul.
verses.textLatin: Et in semita judiciorum tuorum, Domine, sustinuimus te: nomen tuum et memoriale tuum in desiderio animæ.

verses.text: My soul hath desired thee in the night: yea, and with my spirit within me in the morning early I will watch to thee. When thou shalt do thy judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice.
verses.textLatin: Anima mea desideravit te in nocte, sed et spiritu meo in præcordiis meis de mane vigilabo ad te. Cum feceris judicia tua in terra, justitiam discent habitatores orbis.

verses.text: Let us have pity on the wicked, but he will not learn justice: in the land of the saints he hath done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Misereamur impio, et non discet justitiam; in terra sanctorum iniqua gessit, et non videbit gloriam Domini.

verses.text: Lord, let thy hand be exalted, and let them not see: let the envious people see, and be confounded: and let fire devour thy enemies.
verses.textLatin: Domine, exaltetur manus tua, et non videant; videant, et confundantur zelantes populi; et ignis hostes tuos devoret.

verses.text: Lord, thou wilt give us peace: for thou hast wrought all our works for us.
verses.textLatin: Domine, dabis pacem nobis: omnia enim opera nostra operatus es nobis.

verses.text: O Lord our God, other lords besides thee have had dominion over us, only in thee let us remember thy name.
verses.textLatin: Domine Deus noster, possederunt nos domini absque te; tantum in te recordemur nominis tui.

verses.text: Let not the dead live, let not the giants rise again: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and hast destroyed all their memory.
verses.textLatin: Morientes non vivant, gigantes non resurgant: propterea visitasti et contrivisti eos, et perdidisti omnem memoriam eorum.

verses.text: Thou hast been favourable to the nation, O Lord, thou hast been favourable to the nation: art thou glorified? thou hast removed all the ends of the earth far off.
verses.textLatin: Indulsisti genti, Domine, indulsisti genti, numquid glorificatus es? elongasti omnes terminos terræ.

verses.text: Lord, they have sought after thee in distress, in the tribulation of murmuring thy instruction was with them.
verses.textLatin: Domine, in angustia requisierunt te, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis.

verses.text: As a woman with child, when she draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs: so are we become in thy presence, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sicut quæ concipit, cum appropinquaverit ad partum, dolens clamat in doloribus suis, sic facti sumus a facie tua, Domine.

verses.text: We have conceived, and been as it were in labour, and have brought forth wind: we have not wrought salvation on the earth, therefore the inhabitants of the earth have not fallen.
verses.textLatin: Concepimus, et quasi parturivimus, et peperimus spiritum. Salutes non fecimus in terra; ideo non ceciderunt habitatores terræ.

verses.text: Thy dead men shall live, my slain shall rise again: awake, and give praise, ye that dwell in the dust: for thy dew is the dew of the light: and the land of the giants thou shalt pull down into ruin.
verses.textLatin: Vivent mortui tui, interfecti mei resurgent. Expergiscimini, et laudate, qui habitatis in pulvere, quia ros lucis ros tuus, et terram gigantum detrahes in ruinam.

verses.text: Go, my people, enter into thy chambers, shut thy doors upon thee, hide thyself a little for a moment, until the indignation pass away.
verses.textLatin: Vade, populus meus, intra in cubicula tua; claude ostia tua super te, abscondere modicum ad momentum, donec pertranseat indignatio.

verses.text: For behold the Lord will come out of his place, to visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth against him: and the earth shall disclose her blood, and shall cover her slain no more.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim Dominus egredietur de loco suo, ut visitet iniquitatem habitatoris terræ contra eum; et revelabit terra sanguinem suum, et non operiet ultra interfectos suos.

verses.text: In that day the Lord with his hard, and great, and strong sword shall visit leviathan the bar serpent, and leviathan the crooked serpent, and shall slay the whale that is in the sea.
verses.textLatin: In die illa visitabit Dominus in gladio suo duro, et grandi, et forti, super Leviathan, serpentem vectem, et super Leviathan, serpentem tortuosum, et occidet cetum qui in mari est.

verses.text: In that day there shall be singing to the vineyard of pure wine.
verses.textLatin: In die illa vinea meri cantabit ei.

verses.text: I am the Lord that keep it, I will suddenly give it drink: lest any hurt come to it, I keep it night and day.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus qui servo eam; repente propinabo ei. Ne forte visitetur contra eam, nocte et die servo eam.

verses.text: There is no indignation in me: who shall make me a thorn and a brier in battle: shall I march against it, shall I set it on fire together?
verses.textLatin: Indignatio non est mihi. Quis dabit me spinam et veprem in prælio? gradiar super eam, succendam eam pariter.

verses.text: Or rather shall it take hold of my strength, shall it make peace with me, shall it make peace with me?
verses.textLatin: An potius tenebit fortitudinem meam? faciet pacem mihi, pacem faciet mihi.

verses.text: When they shall rush in unto Jacob, Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed.
verses.textLatin: Qui ingrediuntur impetu ad Jacob, florebit et germinabit Israël, et implebunt faciem orbis semine.

verses.text: Hath he struck him according to the stroke of him that struck him? or is he slain, as he killed them that were slain by him?
verses.textLatin: Numquid juxta plagam percutientis se percussit eum? aut sicut occidit interfectos ejus, sic occisus est?

verses.text: In measure against measure, when it shall be cast off, thou shalt judge it. He hath meditated with his severe spirit in the day of heat.
verses.textLatin: In mensura contra mensuram, cum abjecta fuerit, judicabis eam; meditatus est in spiritu suo duro per diem æstus.

verses.text: Therefore upon this shall the iniquity of the house of Jacob be forgiven: and this is all the fruit, that the sin thereof should be taken away, when he shall have made all the stones of the altar, as burnt stones broken in pieces, the groves and temples shall not stand.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco super hoc dimittetur iniquitas domui Jacob; et iste omnis fructus: ut auferatur peccatum ejus, cum posuerit omnes lapides altaris sicut lapides cineris allisos: non stabunt luci et delubra.

verses.text: For the strong city shall be desolate, the beautiful city shall be forsaken, and shall be left as a wilderness: there the calf shall feed, and there shall he lie down, and shall consume its branches.
verses.textLatin: Civitas enim munita desolata erit; speciosa relinquetur, et dimittetur quasi desertum; ibi pascetur vitulus, et ibi accubabit, et consumet summitates ejus.

verses.text: Its harvest shall be destroyed with drought, women shall come and teach it: for it is not a wise people, therefore he that made it, shall not have mercy on it: and he that formed it, shall not spare it.
verses.textLatin: In siccitate messes illius conterentur. Mulieres venientes, et docentes eam; non est enim populus sapiens: propterea non miserebitur ejus qui fecit eum, et qui formavit eum non parcet ei.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that in that day the Lord will strike from the channel of the river even to the torrent of Egypt, and you shall be gathered together one by one, O ye children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: in die illa percutiet Dominus ab alveo fluminis usque ad torrentem Ægypti; et vos congregabimini unus et unus, filii Israël.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that in that day a noise shall be made with a great trumpet, and they that were lost, shall come from the land of the Assyrians, and they that were outcasts in the land of Egypt, and they shall adore the Lord in the holy mount in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: in die illa clangetur in tuba magna; et venient qui perditi fuerant de terra Assyriorum, et qui ejecti erant in terra Ægypti, et adorabunt Dominum in monte sancto in Jerusalem.

verses.text: Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the fading flower the glory of his joy, who were on the head of the fat valley, staggering with wine.
verses.textLatin: Væ coronæ superbiæ, ebriis Ephraim, et flori decidenti, gloriæ exsultationis ejus, qui erant in vertice vallis pinguissimæ, errantes a vino.

verses.text: Behold the Lord is mighty and strong, as a storm of hail: a destroying whirlwind, as the violence of many waters overflowing, and sent forth upon a spacious land.
verses.textLatin: Ecce validus et fortis Dominus sicut impetus grandinis; turbo confringens, sicut impetus aquarum multarum inundantium et emissarum super terram spatiosam.

verses.text: The crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim shall be trodden under feet.
verses.textLatin: Pedibus conculcabitur corona superbiæ ebriorum Ephraim.

verses.text: And the fading flower the glory of his joy, who is on the head of the fat valley, shall be as a hasty fruit before the ripeness of autumn: which when he that seeth it shall behold, as soon as he taketh it in his hand, he will eat it up.
verses.textLatin: Et erit flos decidens gloriæ exsultationis ejus, qui est super verticem vallis pinguium, quasi temporaneum ante maturitatem autumni, quod, cum aspexerit videns, statim ut manu tenuerit, devorabit illud.

verses.text: In that day the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory, and a garland of joy to the residue of his people:
verses.textLatin: In die illa erit Dominus exercituum corona gloriæ, et sertum exsultationis residuo populi sui;

verses.text: And a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and strength to them that return out of the battle to the gate.
verses.textLatin: et spiritus judicii sedenti super judicium, et fortitudo revertentibus de bello ad portam.

verses.text: But these also have been ignorant through wine, and through drunkenness have erred: the priest and the prophet have been ignorant through drunkenness, they are swallowed up with wine, they have gone astray in drunkenness, they have not known him that seeth, they have been ignorant of judgment.
verses.textLatin: Verum hi quoque præ vino nescierunt, et præ ebrietate erraverunt; sacerdos et propheta nescierunt præ ebrietate; absorpti sunt a vino, erraverunt in ebrietate, nescierunt videntem, ignoraverunt judicium.

verses.text: For all tables were full of vomit and filth, so that there was no more place.
verses.textLatin: Omnes enim mensæ repletæ sunt vomitu sordiumque, ita ut non esset ultra locus.

verses.text: Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand the hearing? them that are weaned from the milk, that are drawn away from the breasts.
verses.textLatin: Quem docebit scientiam? et quem intelligere faciet auditum? Ablactatos a lacte, avulsos ab uberibus.

verses.text: For command, command again; command, command again; expect, expect again; expect, expect again: a little there, a little there.
verses.textLatin: Quia manda, remanda; manda, remanda; exspecta, reexspecta; exspecta, reexspecta; modicum ibi, modicum ibi.

verses.text: For with the speech of lips, and with another tongue he will speak to this people.
verses.textLatin: In loquela enim labii, et lingua altera loquetur ad populum istum.

verses.text: To whom he said: This is my rest, refresh the weary, and this is my refreshing: and they would not hear.
verses.textLatin: Cui dixit: Hæc est requies mea, reficite lassum; et hoc est meum refrigerium: et noluerunt audire.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord shall be to them: Command, command again; command, command again; expect, expect again; expect, expect again: a little there, a little there: that they may go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.
verses.textLatin: Et erit eis verbum Domini: Manda, remanda; manda, remanda; exspecta, reexspecta; exspecta, reexspecta; modicum ibi, modicum ibi; ut vadant, et cadant retrorsum, et conterantur, et illaqueentur, et capiantur.

verses.text: Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, ye scornful men, who rule over my people that is in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc audite verbum Domini, viri illusores, qui dominamini super populum meum, qui est in Jerusalem.

verses.text: For you have said: We have entered into a league with death, and we have made a covenant with hell. When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come upon us: for we have placed our hope in lies, and by falsehood we are protected.
verses.textLatin: Dixistis enim: Percussimus fœdus cum morte, et cum inferno fecimus pactum: flagellum inundans cum transierit, non veniet super nos quia posuimus mendacium spem nostram, et mendacio protecti sumus.

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Behold I will lay a stone in the foundations of Sion, a tried stone, a corner stone, a precious stone, founded in the foundation. He that believeth, let him not hasten.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Ecce ego mittam in fundamentis Sion lapidem, lapidem probatum, angularem, pretiosum, in fundamento fundatum; qui crediderit, non festinet.

verses.text: And I will set judgment in weight, and justice in measure: and hail shall overturn the hope of falsehood: and waters shall overflow its protection.
verses.textLatin: Et ponam in pondere judicium, et justitiam in mensura; et subvertet grando spem mendacii, et protectionem aquæ inundabunt.

verses.text: And your league with death shall be abolished, and your covenant with hell shall not stand: when the overflowing scourge shall pass, you shall be trodden down by it.
verses.textLatin: Et delebitur fœdus vestrum cum morte, et pactum vestrum cum inferno non stabit: flagellum inundans cum transierit, eritis ei in conculcationem.

verses.text: Whensoever it shall pass through, it shall take you away: because in the morning early it shall pass through, in the day and in the night, and vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear.
verses.textLatin: Quandocumque pertransierit, tollet vos, quoniam in mane diluculo pertransibit in die et in nocte; et tantummodo sola vexatio intellectum dabit auditui.

verses.text: For the bed is straitened, so that one must fall out, and a short covering cannot cover both.
verses.textLatin: Coangustatum est enim stratum, ita ut alter decidat; et pallium breve utrumque operire non potest.

verses.text: For the Lord shall stand up as in the mountain of divisions: he shall be angry as in the valley which is in Gabaon: that he may do his work, his strange work: that he may perform his work, his work is strange to him.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim in monte divisionum stabit Dominus; sicut in valle quæ est in Gabaon irascetur, ut faciat opus suum, alienum opus ejus: ut operetur opus suum, peregrinum est opus ejus ab eo.

verses.text: And now do not mock, lest your bonds be tied strait. For I have heard of the Lord the God of hosts a consumption and a cutting short upon all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc nolite illudere, ne forte constringantur vincula vestra; consummationem enim et abbreviationem audivi a Domino Deo exercituum, super universam terram.

verses.text: Give ear, and hear my voice, hearken, and hear my speech.
verses.textLatin: Auribus percipite, et audite vocem meam: attendite, et audite eloquium meum.

verses.text: Shall the ploughman plough all the day to sow, shall he open and harrow his ground?
verses.textLatin: Numquid tota die arabit arans ut serat? proscindet et sarriet humum suam?

verses.text: Will he not, when he hath made plain the surface thereof, sow gith, and scatter cummin, and put wheat in order, and barley, and millet, and vetches in their bounds?
verses.textLatin: Nonne cum adæquaverit faciem ejus, seret gith et cyminum sparget? et ponet triticum per ordinem, et hordeum, et milium, et viciam in finibus suis?

verses.text: For he will instruct him in judgment: his God will teach him.
verses.textLatin: Et erudiet illum in judicio; Deus suus docebit illum.

verses.text: For gith shall not be thrashed with saws, neither shall the cart wheel turn about upon cummin: but gith shall be beaten out with a rod, and cummin with a staff.
verses.textLatin: Non enim in serris triturabitur gith, nec rota plaustri super cyminum circuibit; sed in virga excutietur gith, et cyminum in baculo.

verses.text: But bread corn shall be broken small: but the thrasher shall not thrash it for ever, neither shall the cart wheel hurt it, nor break it with its teeth.
verses.textLatin: Panis autem comminuetur; verum non in perpetuum triturans triturabit illum, neque vexabit eum rota plaustri, neque ungulis suis comminuet eum.

verses.text: This also is come forth from the Lord God of hosts, to make his counsel wonderful, and magnify justice.
verses.textLatin: Et hoc a Domino Deo exercituum exivit, ut mirabile faceret consilium, et magnificaret justitiam.

verses.text: Woe to Ariel, to Ariel the city which David took: year is added to year: the solemnities are at an end.
verses.textLatin: Væ Ariel, Ariel civitas, quam expugnavit David! additus est annus ad annum: solemnitates evolutæ sunt.

verses.text: And I will make a trench about Ariel, and it shall be in sorrow and mourning, and it shall be to me as Ariel.
verses.textLatin: Et circumvallabo Ariel, et erit tristis et mœrens, et erit mihi quasi Ariel.

verses.text: And I will make a circle round about thee, and will cast up a rampart against thee, and raise up bulwarks to besiege thee.
verses.textLatin: Et circumdabo quasi sphæram in circuitu tuo, et jaciam contra te aggerem, et munimenta ponam in obsidionem tuam.

verses.text: Thou shalt be brought down, thou shall speak out of the earth, and thy speech shall be heard out of the ground: and thy voice shall be from the earth like that of the python, and out of the ground thy speech shall mutter.
verses.textLatin: Humiliaberis, de terra loqueris, et de humo audietur eloquium tuum; et erit quasi pythonis de terra vox tua, et de humo eloquium tuum mussitabit.

verses.text: And the multitude of them that fan thee, shall be like small dust: and as ashes passing away, the multitude of them that have prevailed against thee.
verses.textLatin: Et erit sicut pulvis tenuis multitudo ventilantium te, et sicut favilla pertransiens multitudo eorum qui contra te prævaluerunt;

verses.text: And it shall be at an instant suddenly. A visitation shall come from the Lord of hosts in thunder, and with earthquake, and with a great noise of whirlwind and tempest, and with the flame of devouring fire.
verses.textLatin: eritque repente confestim. A Domino exercituum visitabitur in tonitruo, et commotione terræ, et voce magna turbinis et tempestatis, et flammæ ignis devorantis.

verses.text: And the multitude of all nations that have fought against Ariel, shall be as the dream of a vision by night, and all that have fought, and besieged and prevailed against it.
verses.textLatin: Et erit sicut somnium visionis nocturnæ multitudo omnium gentium quæ dimicaverunt contra Ariel, et omnes qui militaverunt, et obsederunt, et prævaluerunt adversus eam.

verses.text: And as he that is hungry dreameth, and eateth, but when he is awake, his soul is empty: and as he that is thirsty dreameth, and drinketh, and after he is awake, is yet faint with thirst, and his soul is empty: so shall be the multitude of all the Gentiles, that have fought against mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut somniat esuriens, et comedit, cum autem fuerit expergefactus, vacua est anima ejus; et sicut somniat sitiens et bibit, et postquam fuerit expergefactus, lassus adhuc sitit, et anima ejus vacua est: sic erit multitudo omnium gentium quæ dimicaverunt contra montem Sion.

verses.text: Be astonished, and wonder, waver, and stagger: be drunk, and not with wine: stagger, and not with drunkenness.
verses.textLatin: Obstupescite et admiramini; fluctuate et vacillate; inebriamini, et non a vino; movemini, et non ab ebrietate.

verses.text: For the Lord hath mingled for you the spirit of a deep sleep, he will shut up your eyes, he will cover your prophets and princes, that see visions.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam miscuit vobis Dominus spiritum soporis; claudet oculos vestros: prophetas et principes vestros, qui vident visiones, operiet.

verses.text: And the vision of all shall be unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which when they shall deliver to one that is learned, they shall say: Read this: and he shall answer: I cannot, for it is sealed.
verses.textLatin: Et erit vobis visio omnium sicut verba libri signati, quem cum dederint scienti litteras, dicent: Lege istum: et respondebit: Non possum, signatus est enim.

verses.text: And the book shall be given to one that knoweth no letters, and it shall be said to him: Read: and he shall answer: I know no letters.
verses.textLatin: Et dabitur liber nescienti litteras, diceturque ei: Lege; et respondebit: Nescio litteras.

verses.text: And the Lord said: Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips glorify me, but their heart is far from me, and they have feared me with the commandment and doctrines of men:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus: Eo quod appropinquat populus iste ore suo, et labiis suis glorificat me, cor autem ejus longe est a me, et timuerunt me mandato hominum et doctrinis,

verses.text: Therefore behold I will proceed to cause an admiration in this people, by a great and wonderful miracle: for wisdom shall perish from their wise men, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.
verses.textLatin: ideo ecce ego addam ut admirationem faciam populo huic miraculo grandi et stupendo; peribit enim sapientia a sapientibus ejus, et intellectus prudentium ejus abscondetur.

verses.text: Woe to you that are deep of heart, to hide your counsel from the Lord: and their works are in the dark, and they say: Who seeth us, and who knoweth us?
verses.textLatin: Væ qui profundi estis corde, ut a Domino abscondatis consilium; quorum sunt in tenebris opera, et dicunt: Quis videt nos? et quis novit nos?

verses.text: This thought of yours is perverse: as if the clay should think against the potter, and the work should say to the maker thereof: Thou madest me not: or the thing framed should say to him that fashioned it: Thou understandest not.
verses.textLatin: Perversa est hæc vestra cogitatio; quasi si lutum contra figulum cogitet, et dicat opus factori suo: Non fecisti me; et figmentum dicat fictori suo: Non intelligis.

verses.text: Is it not yet a very little while, and Libanus shall be turned into charmel, and charmel shall be esteemed as a forest?
verses.textLatin: Nonne adhuc in modico et in brevi convertetur Libanus in carmel, et carmel in saltum reputabitur?

verses.text: And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of darkness and obscurity the eyes of the blind shall see.
verses.textLatin: Et audient in die illa surdi verba libri, et de tenebris et caligine oculi cæcorum videbunt.

verses.text: And the meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et addent mites in Domino lætitiam, et pauperes homines in Sancto Israël exsultabunt;

verses.text: For he that did prevail hath failed, the scorner is consumed, and they are all cut off that watched for iniquity:
verses.textLatin: quoniam defecit qui prævalebat, consummatus est illusor, et succisi sunt omnes qui vigilabant super iniquitatem,

verses.text: That made men sin by word, and supplanted him that reproved them in the gate, and declined in vain from the just.
verses.textLatin: qui peccare faciebant homines in verbo, et arguentem in porta supplantabant, et declinaverunt frustra a justo.

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord to the house of Jacob, he that redeemed Abraham: Jacob shall not now be confounded, neither shall his countenance now be ashamed:
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc, hæc dicit Dominus ad domum Jacob, qui redemit Abraham: Non modo confundetur Jacob, nec modo vultus ejus erubescet;

verses.text: But when he shall see his children, the work of my hands in the midst of him sanctifying my name, and they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall glorify the God of Israel:
verses.textLatin: sed cum viderit filios suos, opera manuum mearum in medio sui sanctificantes nomen meum, et sanctificabunt Sanctum Jacob, et Deum Israël prædicabunt;

verses.text: And they that erred in spirit, shall know understanding, and they that murmured, shall learn the law.
verses.textLatin: et scient errantes spiritu intellectum, et mussitatores discent legem.

verses.text: Woe  to you, apostate children, saith the Lord, that you would take counsel, and not of me: and would begin a web, and not by my spirit, that you might add sin upon sin:
verses.textLatin: Væ filii desertores, dicit Dominus, ut faceretis consilium, et non ex me, et ordiremini telam, et non per spiritum meum, ut adderetis peccatum super peccatum;

verses.text: Who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth, hoping for help in the strength of Pharao, and trusting in the shadow of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: qui ambulatis ut descendatis in Ægyptum, et os meum non interrogastis, sperantes auxilium in fortitudine Pharaonis, et habentes fiduciam in umbra Ægypti!

verses.text: And the strength of Pharao shall be to your confusion, and the confidence of the shadow of Egypt to your shame.
verses.textLatin: Et erit vobis fortitudo Pharaonis in confusionem, et fiducia umbræ Ægypti in ignominiam.

verses.text: For thy princes were in Tanis, and thy messengers came even to Hanes.
verses.textLatin: Erant enim in Tani principes tui, et nuntii tui usque ad Hanes pervenerunt.

verses.text: They were all confounded at a people that could not profit them: they were no help, nor to any profit, but to confusion and to reproach.
verses.textLatin: Omnes confusi sunt super populo qui eis prodesse non potuit: non fuerunt in auxilium et in aliquam utilitatem, sed in confusionem et in opprobrium.

verses.text: The burden of the beasts of the south. In a land of trouble and distress, from whence come the lioness, and the lion, the viper and the flying basilisk, they carry their riches upon the shoulders of beasts, and their treasures upon the bunches of camels to a people that shall not be able to profit them.
verses.textLatin: Onus jumentorum austri. In terra tribulationis et angustiæ leæna, et leo ex eis, vipera et regulus volans; portantes super humeros jumentorum divitias suas, et super gibbum camelorum thesauros suos, ad populum qui eis prodesse non poterit.

verses.text: For Egypt shall help in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I cried concerning this: It is pride only, sit still.
verses.textLatin: Ægyptus enim frustra et vane auxiliabitur. Ideo clamavi super hoc: Superbia tantum est, quiesce.

verses.text: Now therefore go in and write for them upon box, and note it diligently in a book, and it shall be in the latter days for a testimony for ever.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo ingressus, scribe ei super buxum, et in libro diligenter exara illud, et erit in die novissimo in testimonium usque in æternum.

verses.text: For it is a people that provoketh to wrath, and lying children, children that will not hear the law of God.
verses.textLatin: Populus enim ad iracundiam provocans est: et filii mendaces, filii nolentes audire legem Dei;

verses.text: Who say to the seers: See not: and to them that behold: Behold not for us those things that are right: speak unto us pleasant things, see errors for us.
verses.textLatin: qui dicunt videntibus: Nolite videre, et aspicientibus: Nolite aspicere nobis ea quæ recta sunt; loquimini nobis placentia: videte nobis errores.

verses.text: Take away from me the way, turn away the path from me, let the Holy One of Israel cease from before us.
verses.textLatin: Auferte a me viam; declinate a me semitam; cesset a facie nostra Sanctus Israël.

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel: Because you have rejected this word, and have trusted in oppression and tumult, and have leaned upon it:
verses.textLatin: Propterea hæc dicit Sanctus Israël: Pro eo quod reprobastis verbum hoc, et sperastis in calumnia et in tumultu, et innixi estis super eo;

verses.text: Therefore shall this iniquity be to you as a breach that falleth, and is found wanting in a high wall, for the destruction thereof shall come on a sudden, when it is not looked for.
verses.textLatin: propterea erit vobis iniquitas hæc sicut interruptio cadens, et requisita in muro excelso, quoniam subito, dum non speratur, veniet contritio ejus.

verses.text: And it shall be broken small, as the potter’s vessel is broken all to pieces with mighty breaking, and there shall not a sherd be found of the pieces thereof, wherein a little fire may be carried from the hearth, or a little water be drawn out of the pit.
verses.textLatin: Et comminuetur sicut conteritur lagena figuli contritione pervalida, et non invenietur de fragmentis ejus testa in qua portetur igniculus de incendio, aut hauriatur parum aquæ de fovea.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord God the Holy One of Israel: If you return and be quiet, you shall be saved: in silence and in hope shall your strength be. And you would not:
verses.textLatin: Quia hæc dicit Dominus Deus, Sanctus Israël: Si revertamini et quiescatis, salvi eritis; in silentio et in spe erit fortitudo vestra. Et noluistis,

verses.text: But have said: No, but we will flee to horses: therefore shall you flee. And we will mount upon swift ones: therefore shall they be swifter that shall pursue after you.
verses.textLatin: et dixistis: Nequaquam, sed ad equos fugiemus: ideo fugietis; et: Super veloces ascendemus: ideo velociores erunt qui persequentur vos.

verses.text: A thousand men shall flee for fear of one: and for fear of five shall you flee, till you be left as the mast of ship on the top of a mountain, and as an ensign upon a hill.
verses.textLatin: Mille homines a facie terroris unius; et a facie terroris quinque fugietis, donec relinquamini quasi malus navis in vertice montis, et quasi signum super collem.

verses.text: Therefore the Lord waiteth that he may have mercy on you: and therefore shall he be exalted sparing you: because the Lord is the God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.
verses.textLatin: Propterea exspectat Dominus ut misereatur vestri; et ideo exaltabitur parcens vobis, quia Deus judicii Dominus: beati omnes qui exspectant eum!

verses.text: For the people of Sion shall dwell in Jerusalem: weeping thou shalt not weep, he will surely have pity on thee: at the voice of thy cry, as soon as he shall hear, he will answer thee.
verses.textLatin: Populus enim Sion habitabit in Jerusalem: plorans nequaquam plorabis: miserans miserebitur tui, ad vocem clamoris tui: statim ut audierit, respondebit tibi.

verses.text: And the Lord will give you spare bread, and short water: and will not cause thy teacher to flee away from thee any more, and thy eyes shall see thy teacher.
verses.textLatin: Et dabit vobis Dominus panem arctum, et aquam brevem; et non faciet avolare a te ultra doctorem tuum; et erunt oculi tui videntes præceptorem tuum.

verses.text: And thy ears shall hear the word of one admonishing thee behind thy back: This is the way, walk ye in it: and go not aside neither to the right hand, nor to the left.
verses.textLatin: Et aures tuæ audient verbum post tergum monentis: Hæc est via; ambulate in ea, et non declinetis neque ad dexteram, neque ad sinistram.

verses.text: And thou shalt defile the plates of thy graven things of silver, and the garment of thy molten things of gold, and shalt cast them away as the uncleanness of a menstruous woman. Thou shalt say to it: Get thee hence.
verses.textLatin: Et contaminabis laminas sculptilium argenti tui, et vestimentum conflatilis auri tui, et disperges ea sicut immunditiam menstruatæ. Egredere, dices ei.

verses.text: And rain shall be given to thy seed, wheresoever thou shalt sow in the land: and the bread of the corn of the land shall be most plentiful, and fat. The lamb in that day shall feed at large in thy possession:
verses.textLatin: Et dabitur pluvia semini tuo, ubicumque seminaveris in terra, et panis frugum terræ erit uberrimus et pinguis; pascetur in possessione tua in die illo agnus spatiose,

verses.text: And thy oxen, and the ass colts that till the ground, shall eat mingled provender as it was winnowed in the floor.
verses.textLatin: et tauri tui, et pulli asinorum, qui operantur terram, commistum migma comedent sicut in area ventilatum est.

verses.text: And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every elevated hill rivers of running waters in the day of the slaughter of many, when the tower shall fall.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt super omnem montem excelsum, et super omnem collem elevatum, rivi currentium aquarum, in die interfectionis multorum, cum ceciderint turres:

verses.text: And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days: in the day when the Lord shall bind up the wound of his people, and shall heal the stroke of their wound.
verses.textLatin: et erit lux lunæ sicut lux solis, et lux solis erit septempliciter sicut lux septem dierum, in die qua alligaverit Dominus vulnus populi sui, et percussuram plagæ ejus sanaverit.

verses.text: Behold the name of the Lord cometh from afar, his wrath burneth, and is heavy to bear: his lips are filled with indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire.
verses.textLatin: Ecce nomen Domini venit de longinquo, ardens furor ejus, et gravis ad portandum; labia ejus repleta sunt indignatione, et lingua ejus quasi ignis devorans.

verses.text: His breath as a torrent overflowing even to the midst of the neck, to destroy the nations unto nothing, and the bridle of error that was in the jaws of the people.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus ejus velut torrens inundans usque ad medium colli, ad perdendas gentes in nihilum, et frenum erroris quod erat in maxillis populorum.

verses.text: You shall have a song as in the night of the sanctified solemnity, and joy of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe, to come into the mountain of the Lord, to the Mighty One of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Canticum erit vobis sicut nox sanctificatæ solemnitatis, et lætitia cordis sicut qui pergit cum tibia, ut intret in montem Domini ad Fortem Israël.

verses.text: And the Lord shall make the glory of his voice to be heard, and shall shew the terror of his arm, in the threatening of wrath, and the flame of devouring fire: he shall crush to pieces with whirlwind, and hailstones.
verses.textLatin: Et auditam faciet Dominus gloriam vocis suæ, et terrorem brachii sui ostendet in comminatione furoris, et flamma ignis devorantis: allidet in turbine, et in lapide grandinis.

verses.text: For at the voice of the Lord the Assyrian shall fear being struck with the rod.
verses.textLatin: A voce enim Domini pavebit Assur virga percussus.

verses.text: And the passage of the rod shall be strongly grounded, which the Lord shall make to rest upon him with timbrels and harps, and in great battles he shall overthrow them.
verses.textLatin: Et erit transitus virgæ fundatus, quam requiescere faciet Dominus super eum in tympanis et citharis; et in bellis præcipuis expugnabit eos.

verses.text: For Topheth is prepared from yesterday, prepared by the king, deep, and wide. The nourishment thereof is fire and much wood: the breath of the Lord as a torrent of brimstone kindling it.
verses.textLatin: Præparata est enim ab heri Topheth, a rege præparata, profunda, et dilatata. Nutrimenta ejus, ignis et ligna multa; flatus Domini sicut torrens sulphuris succendens eam.

verses.text: Woe  to them that go down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses, and putting their confidence in chariots, because they are many: and in horsemen, because they are very strong: and have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel, and have not sought after the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui descendunt in Ægyptum ad auxilium, in equis sperantes, et habentes fiduciam super quadrigis, quia multæ sunt; et super equitibus, quia prævalidi nimis; et non sunt confisi super Sanctum Israël, et Dominum non requisierunt!

verses.text: But he that is the wise one hath brought evil, and hath not removed his words: and he will rise up against the house of the wicked, and against the aid of them that work iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Ipse autem sapiens adduxit malum, et verba sua non abstulit; et consurget contra domum pessimorum, et contra auxilium operantium iniquitatem.

verses.text: Egypt is man, and not God: and their horses, flesh, and not spirit: and the Lord shall put down his hand, and the helper shall fall, and he that is helped shall fall, and they shall all be confounded together.
verses.textLatin: Ægyptus homo, et non deus; et equi eorum caro, et non spiritus; et Dominus inclinabit manum suam, et corruet auxiliator, et cadet cui præstatur auxilium, simulque omnes consumentur.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord to me: Like as the lion roareth, and the lion’s whelp upon his prey, and when a multitude of shepherds shall come against him, he will not fear at their voice, nor be afraid of their multitude: so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight upon mount Sion, and upon the hill thereof.
verses.textLatin: Quia hæc dicit Dominus ad me: Quomodo si rugiat leo et catulus leonis super prædam suam; et cum occurrerit ei multitudo pastorum, a voce eorum non formidabit, et a multitudine eorum non pavebit: sic descendet Dominus exercituum ut prælietur super montem Sion et super collem ejus.

verses.text: As birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem, protecting and delivering, passing over and saving.
verses.textLatin: Sicut aves volantes, sic proteget Dominus exercituum Jerusalem, protegens et liberans, transiens et salvans.

verses.text: Return as you had deeply revolted, O children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Convertimini, sicut in profundum recesseratis, filii Israël.

verses.text: For in that day a man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your hands have made for you to sin.
verses.textLatin: In die enim illa abjiciet vir idola argenti sui, et idola auri sui, quæ fecerunt vobis manus vestræ in peccatum.

verses.text: And the Assyrian shall fall by the sword not of a man, and the sword not of a man shall devour him, and he shall flee not at the face of the sword: and his young men shall be tributaries.
verses.textLatin: Et cadet Assur in gladio non viri, et gladius non hominis vorabit eum: et fugiet non a facie gladii, et juvenes ejus vectigales erunt.

verses.text: And his strength shall pass away with dread, and his princes fleeing shall be afraid: the Lord hath said it, whose fire is in Sion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et fortitudo ejus a terrore transibit, et pavebunt fugientes principes ejus, dixit Dominus: cujus ignis est in Sion et caminus ejus in Jerusalem.

verses.text: Behold  a king shall reign in justice, and princes shall rule in judgment.
verses.textLatin: Ecce in justitia regnabit rex, et principes in judicio præerunt.

verses.text: And a man shall be as when one is hid from the wind, and hideth himself from a storm, as rivers of waters in drought, and the shadow of a rock that standeth out in a desert land.
verses.textLatin: Et erit vir sicut qui absconditur a vento, et celat se a tempestate; sicut rivi aquarum in siti, et umbra petræ prominentis in terra deserta.

verses.text: The eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken diligently.
verses.textLatin: Non caligabunt oculi videntium, et aures audientium diligenter auscultabunt.

verses.text: And the heart of fools shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers shall speak readily and plain.
verses.textLatin: Et cor stultorum intelliget scientiam, et lingua balborum velociter loquetur et plane.

verses.text: The fool shall no more be called prince: neither shall the deceitful be called great:
verses.textLatin: Non vocabitur ultra is qui insipiens est, princeps, neque fraudulentus appellabitur major;

verses.text: For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise hypocrisy, and speak to the Lord deceitfully, and to make empty the soul of the hungry, and take away drink from the thirsty.
verses.textLatin: stultus enim fatua loquetur, et cor ejus faciet iniquitatem, ut perficiat simulationem, et loquatur ad Dominum fraudulenter, et vacuam faciat animam esurientis, et potum sitienti auferat.

verses.text: The vessels of the deceitful are most wicked: for he hath framed devices to destroy the meek, with lying words, when the poor man speaketh judgment.
verses.textLatin: Fraudulenti vasa pessima sunt; ipse enim cogitationes concinnavit ad perdendos mites in sermone mendacii, cum loqueretur pauper judicium.

verses.text: But the prince will devise such things as are worthy of a prince, and he shall stand above the rulers.
verses.textLatin: Princeps vero ea quæ digna sunt principe cogitabit, et ipse super duces stabit.

verses.text: Rise up, ye rich women, and hear my voice: ye confident daughters, give ear to my speech.
verses.textLatin: Mulieres opulentæ, surgite, et audite vocem meam; filiæ confidentes, percipite auribus eloquium meum.

verses.text: For after days and a year, you that are confident shall be troubled: for the vintage is at an end, the gathering shall come no more.
verses.textLatin: Post dies enim et annum, vos conturbabimini confidentes; consummata est enim vindemia, collectio ultra non veniet.

verses.text: Be astonished, ye rich women, be troubled, ye confident ones: strip you, and be confounded, gird your loins.
verses.textLatin: Obstupescite, opulentæ; conturbamini, confidentes: exuite vos et confundimini; accingite lumbos vestros.

verses.text: Mourn for your breasts, for the delightful country, for the fruitful vineyard.
verses.textLatin: Super ubera plangite, super regione desiderabili, super vinea fertili.

verses.text: Upon the land of my people shall thorns and briers come up: how much more upon all the houses of joy, of the city that rejoiced?
verses.textLatin: Super humum populi mei spinæ et vepres ascendent: quanto magis super omnes domos gaudii civitatis exultantis!

verses.text: For the house is forsaken, the multitude of the city is left, darkness and obscurity are come upon its dens for ever. A joy of wild asses, the pastures of flocks,
verses.textLatin: Domus enim dimissa est, multitudo urbis relicta est, tenebræ et palpatio factæ sunt super speluncas usque in æternum; gaudium onagrorum, pascua gregum.

verses.text: Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high: and the desert shall be as a charmel, and charmel shall be counted for a forest.
verses.textLatin: Donec effundatur super nos spiritus de excelso, et erit desertum in carmel, et carmel in saltum reputabitur.

verses.text: An judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and justice shall sit in charmel.
verses.textLatin: Et habitabit in solitudine judicium, et justitia in carmel sedebit.

verses.text: And the work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice quietness, and security for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et erit opus justitiæ pax, et cultus justitiæ silentium, et securitas usque in sempiternum.

verses.text: And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest.
verses.textLatin: Et sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis, et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta.

verses.text: But hail shall be in the descent of the forest, and the city shall be made very low.
verses.textLatin: Grando autem in descensione saltus, et humilitate humiliabitur civitas.

verses.text: Blessed are ye that sow upon all waters, sending thither the foot of the ox and the ass.
verses.textLatin: Beati qui seminatis super omnes aquas, immittentes pedem bovis et asini.

verses.text: Woe to thee that spoilest, shalt not thou thyself also be spoiled? and thou that despisest, shalt not thyself also be despised? when thou shalt have made an end of spoiling, thou shalt be spoiled: when being wearied thou shalt cease to despise, thou shalt be despised.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui prædaris! nonne et ipse prædaberis? et qui spernis, nonne et ipse sperneris? Cum consummaveris deprædationem, deprædaberis; cum fatigatus desieris contemnere, contemneris.

verses.text: O Lord, have mercy on us: for we have waited for thee: be thou our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of trouble.
verses.textLatin: Domine, miserere nostri, te enim exspectavimus; esto brachium nostrum in mane, et salus nostra in tempore tribulationis.

verses.text: At the voice of the angel the people fled, and at the lifting up thyself the nations are scattered.
verses.textLatin: A voce angeli fugerunt populi, et ab exaltatione tua dispersæ sunt gentes.

verses.text: And your spoils shall be gathered together as the locusts are gathered, as when the ditches are full of them.
verses.textLatin: Et congregabuntur spolia vestra sicut colligitur bruchus, velut cum fossæ plenæ fuerint de eo.

verses.text: The Lord is magnified, for he hath dwelt on high: he hath filled Sion with judgment and justice.
verses.textLatin: Magnificatus est Dominus, quoniam habitavit in excelso; implevit Sion judicio et justitia.

verses.text: And there shall be faith in thy times: riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
verses.textLatin: Et erit fides in temporibus tuis: divitiæ salutis sapientia et scientia; timor Domini ipse est thesaurus ejus.

verses.text: Behold they that see shall cry without, the angels of peace shall weep bitterly.
verses.textLatin: Ecce videntes clamabunt foris; angeli pacis amare flebunt.

verses.text: The ways are made desolate, no one passeth by the road, the covenant is made void, he hath rejected the cities, he hath not regarded the men.
verses.textLatin: Dissipatæ sunt viæ, cessavit transiens per semitam: irritum factum est pactum, projecit civitates, non reputavit homines.

verses.text: The land hath mourned, and languished: Libanus is confounded, and become foul, and Saron is become as a desert: and Basan and Carmel are shaken.
verses.textLatin: Luxit et elanguit terra; confusus est Libanus, et obsorduit: et factus est Saron sicut desertum, et concussa est Basan, et Carmelus.

verses.text: Now will I rise up, saith the Lord: now will I be exalted, now will I lift up myself.
verses.textLatin: Nunc consurgam, dicit Dominus; nunc exaltabor, nunc sublevabor.

verses.text: You shall conceive heat, you shall bring forth stubble: your breath as fire shall devour you.
verses.textLatin: Concipietis ardorem, parietis stipulam; spiritus vester ut ignis vorabit vos.

verses.text: And the people shall be as ashes after a fire, as a bundle of thorns they shall be burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: Et erunt populi quasi de incendio cinis; spinæ congregatæ igni comburentur.

verses.text: Hear, you that are far off, what I have done, and you that are near know my strength.
verses.textLatin: Audite, qui longe estis, quæ fecerim; et cognoscite, vicini, fortitudinem meam.

verses.text: The sinners in Sion are afraid, trembling hath seized upon the hypocrites. Which of you can dwell with devouring fire? which of you shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
verses.textLatin: Conterriti sunt in Sion peccatores; possedit tremor hypocritas. Quis poterit habitare de vobis cum igne devorante? quis habitabit ex vobis cum ardoribus sempiternis?

verses.text: He that walketh in justices, and speaketh truth, that casteth away avarice by oppression, and shaketh his hands from all bribes, that stoppeth his ears lest he hear blood, and shutteth his eyes that he may see no evil.
verses.textLatin: Qui ambulat in justitiis et loquitur veritatem, qui projicit avaritiam ex calumnia, et excutit manus suas ab omni munere, qui obturat aures suas ne audiat sanguinem, et claudit oculos suos ne videat malum.

verses.text: He shall dwell on high, the fortifications of rocks shall be his highness: bread is given him, his waters are sure.
verses.textLatin: Iste in excelsis habitabit; munimenta saxorum sublimitas ejus: panis ei datus est, aquæ ejus fideles sunt.

verses.text: His eyes shall see the king in his beauty, they shall see the land far off.
verses.textLatin: Regem in decore suo videbunt oculi ejus, cernent terram de longe.

verses.text: Thy heart shall meditate fear: where is the learned? where is he that pondereth the words of the law? where is the teacher of little ones?
verses.textLatin: Cor tuum meditabitur timorem: ubi est litteratus? ubi legis verba ponderans? ubi doctor parvulorum?

verses.text: The shameless people thou shalt not see, the people of profound speech: so that thou canst not understand the eloquence of his tongue, in whom there is no wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Populum impudentem non videbis, populum alti sermonis, ita ut non possis intelligere disertitudinem linguæ ejus, in quo nulla est sapientia.

verses.text: Look upon Sion the city of our solemnity: thy eyes shall see Jerusalem, a rich habitation, a tabernacle that cannot be removed: neither shall the nails thereof be taken away for ever, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken:
verses.textLatin: Respice, Sion, civitatem solemnitatis nostræ: oculi tui videbunt Jerusalem, habitationem opulentam, tabernaculum quod nequaquam transferri poterit; nec auferentur clavi ejus in sempiternum, et omnes funiculi ejus non rumpentur:

verses.text: Because only there our Lord is magnificent: a place of rivers, very broad and spacious streams: no ship with oars shall pass by it, neither shall the great galley pass through it.
verses.textLatin: quia solummodo ibi magnificus est Dominus noster: locus fluviorum rivi latissimi et patentes: non transibit per eum navis remigum, neque trieris magna transgredietur eum.

verses.text: For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king: he will save us.
verses.textLatin: Dominus enim judex noster, Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster, ipse salvabit nos.

verses.text: Thy tacklings are loosed, and they shall be of no strength: thy mast shall be in such condition, that thou shalt not be able to spread the flag. Then shall the spoils of much prey be divided: the lame shall take the spoil.
verses.textLatin: Laxati sunt funiculi tui, et non prævalebunt; sic erit malus tuus ut dilatare signum non queas. Tunc dividentur spolia prædarum multarum; claudi diripient rapinam.

verses.text: Neither shall he that is near, say: I am feeble. The people that dwell therein, shall have their iniquity taken away from them.
verses.textLatin: Nec dicet vicinus: Elangui; populus qui habitat in ea, auferetur ab eo iniquitas.

verses.text: Come  near, ye Gentiles, and hear, and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear, and all that is therein, the world, and every thing that cometh forth of it.
verses.textLatin: Accedite, gentes, et audite; et populi, attendite: audiat terra, et plenitudo ejus; orbis, et omne germen ejus.

verses.text: For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath killed them, and delivered them to slaughter.
verses.textLatin: Quia indignatio Domini super omnes gentes, et furor super universam militiam eorum: interfecit eos, et dedit eos in occisionem.

verses.text: Their slain shall be cast forth, and out of their carcasses shall rise a stink: the mountains shall be melted with their blood.
verses.textLatin: Interfecti eorum projicientur, et de cadaveribus eorum ascendet fœtor; tabescent montes a sanguine eorum.

verses.text: And all the host of the heavens shall pine away, and the heavens shall be folded together as a book: and all their host shall fall down as the leaf falleth from the vine, and from the fig tree.
verses.textLatin: Et tabescet omnis militia cælorum, et complicabuntur sicut liber cæli: et omnis militia eorum defluet, sicut defluit folium de vinea et de ficu.

verses.text: For my sword is inebriated in heaven: behold it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my slaughter unto judgment.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam inebriatus est in cælo gladius meus; ecce super Idumæam descendet, et super populum interfectionis meæ, ad judicium.

verses.text: The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made thick with the blood of lambs and buck goats, with the blood of rams full of marrow: for there is a victim of the Lord in Bosra and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
verses.textLatin: Gladius Domini repletus est sanguine, incrassatus est adipe, de sanguine agnorum et hircorum, de sanguine medullatorum arietum: victima enim Domini in Bosra, et interfectio magna in terra Edom.

verses.text: And the unicorns shall go down with them, and the bulls with the mighty: their land shall be soaked with blood, and their ground with the fat of fat ones.
verses.textLatin: Et descendent unicornes cum eis, et tauri cum potentibus; inebriabitur terra eorum sanguine, et humus eorum adipe pinguium.

verses.text: For it is the day of the vengeance of the Lord, the year of recompenses of the judgment of Sion.
verses.textLatin: Quia dies ultionis Domini, annus retributionum judicii Sion.

verses.text: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the ground thereof into brimstone: and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.
verses.textLatin: Et convertentur torrentes ejus in picem, et humus ejus in sulphur; et erit terra ejus in picem ardentem.

verses.text: Night and day it shall not be quenched, the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste, none shall pass through it for ever and ever.
verses.textLatin: Nocte et die non extinguetur, in sempiternum ascendet fumus ejus, a generatione in generationem desolabitur, in sæcula sæculorum non erit transiens per eam.

verses.text: The bittern and ericius shall possess it: and the ibis and the raven shall dwell in it: and a line shall be stretched out upon it, to bring it to nothing, and a plummet, unto desolation.
verses.textLatin: Et possidebunt illam onocrotalus et ericius; ibis et corvus habitabunt in ea: et extendetur super eam mensura, ut redigatur ad nihilum, et perpendiculum in desolationem.

verses.text: The nobles thereof shall not be there: they shall call rather upon the king, and all the princes thereof shall be nothing.
verses.textLatin: Nobiles ejus non erunt ibi; regem potius invocabunt, et omnes principes ejus erunt in nihilum.

verses.text: And thorns and nettles shall grow up in its houses, and the thistle in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be the habitation of dragons, and the pasture of ostriches.
verses.textLatin: Et orientur in domibus ejus spinæ et urticæ, et paliurus in munitionibus ejus; et erit cubile draconum, et pascua struthionum.

verses.text: And demons and monsters shall meet, and the hairy ones shall cry out one to another, there hath the lamia lain down, and found rest for herself.
verses.textLatin: Et occurrent dæmonia onocentauris, et pilosus clamabit alter ad alterum; ibi cubavit lamia, et invenit sibi requiem.

verses.text: There hath the ericius had its hole, and brought up its young ones, and hath dug round about, and cherished them in the shadow thereof: thither are the kites gathered together one to another.
verses.textLatin: Ibi habuit foveam ericius, et enutrivit catulos, et circumfodit, et fovit in umbra ejus; illuc congregati sunt milvi, alter ad alterum.

verses.text: Search ye diligently in the book of the Lord, and read: not one of them was wanting, one hath not sought for the other: for that which proceedeth out of my mouth, he hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.
verses.textLatin: Requirite diligenter in libro Domini, et legite: Unum ex eis non defuit, alter alterum non quæsivit; quia quod ex ore meo procedit, ille mandavit, et spiritus ejus ipse congregavit ea.

verses.text: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it to them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation they shall dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Et ipse misit eis sortem, et manus ejus divisit eam illis in mensuram: usque in æternum possidebunt eam; in generationem et generationem habitabunt in ea.

verses.text: The  land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice, and shall flourish like the lily.
verses.textLatin: Lætabitur deserta et invia, et exsultabit solitudo, et florebit quasi lilium.

verses.text: It shall bud forth and blossom, and shall rejoice with joy and praise: the glory of Libanus is given to it: the beauty of Carmel, and Saron, they shall see the glory of the Lord, and the beauty of our God.
verses.textLatin: Germinans germinabit, et exsultabit lætabunda et laudans: gloria Libani data est ei, decor Carmeli et Saron; ipsi videbunt gloriam Domini, et decorem Dei nostri.

verses.text: Strengthen ye the feeble hands, and confirm the weak knees.
verses.textLatin: Confortate manus dissolutas, et genua debilia roborate.

verses.text: Say to the fainthearted: Take courage, and fear not: behold your God will bring the revenge of recompense: God himself will come and will save you.
