verses.text: We are confounded, because we have heard reproach: shame hath covered our faces: because strangers are come upon the sanctuaries of the house of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Confusi sumus, quoniam audivimus opprobrium: operuit ignominia facies nostras, quia venerunt alieni super sanctificationem domus Domini.

verses.text: Therefore behold the days come, saith the Lord, and I will visit her graven things, and in all her land the wounded shall groan:
verses.textLatin: Propterea ecce dies veniunt, ait Dominus, et visitabo super sculptilia ejus, et in omni terra ejus mugiet vulneratus.

verses.text: If Babylon should mount up to heaven, and establish her strength on high: from me there should come spoilers upon her, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Si ascenderit Babylon in cælum, et firmaverit in excelso robur suum, a me venient vastatores ejus, ait Dominus.

verses.text: The noise of a cry from Babylon, and great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans:
verses.textLatin: Vox clamoris de Babylone, et contritio magna de terra Chaldæorum:

verses.text: Because the Lord hath laid Babylon waste, and destroyed out of her the great voice: and their wave shall roar like many waters: their voice hath made a noise:
verses.textLatin: quoniam vastavit Dominus Babylonem, et perdidit ex ea vocem magnam: et sonabunt fluctus eorum quasi aquæ multæ; dedit sonitum vox eorum:

verses.text: Because the spoiler is come upon her, that is, upon Babylon, and her valiant men are taken, and their bow is weakened, because the Lord, who is a strong revenger, will surely repay.
verses.textLatin: quia venit super eam, id est super Babylonem, prædo, et apprehensi sunt fortes ejus, et emarcuit arcus eorum, quia fortis ultor Dominus reddens retribuet.

verses.text: And I will make her princes drunk, and her wise men, and her captains, and her rulers, and her valiant men: and they shall sleep an everlasting sleep, and shall awake no more, saith the king whose name is Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et inebriabo principes ejus, et sapientes ejus, et duces ejus, et magistratus ejus, et fortes ejus: et dormient somnum sempiternum, et non expergiscentur, ait Rex (Dominus exercituum nomen ejus).

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: That broad wall of Babylon shall be utterly broken down, and her high gates shall be burnt with fire, and the labours of the people shall come to nothing, and of the nations shall go to the fire, and shall perish.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Murus Babylonis ille latissimus suffossione suffodietur, et portæ ejus excelsæ igni comburentur, et labores populorum ad nihilum, et gentium in ignem erunt, et disperibunt.

verses.text: The word that Jeremias the prophet commanded Saraias the son of Nerias, the son of Maasias, when he went with king Sedecias to Babylon, in the fourth year of his reign: now Saraias was chief over the prophecy.
verses.textLatin: Verbum quod præcepit Jeremias propheta Saraiæ filio Neriæ filii Maasiæ, cum pergeret cum Sedecia rege in Babylonem, in anno quarto regni ejus: Saraias autem erat princeps prophetiæ.

verses.text: And Jeremias wrote in one book all the evil that was to come upon Babylon: all these words that are written against Babylon.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit Jeremias omne malum quod venturum erat super Babylonem, in libro uno: omnia verba hæc quæ scripta sunt contra Babylonem.

verses.text: And Jeremias said to Saraias: When thou shalt come into Babylon, and shalt see, and shalt read all these words,
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Jeremias ad Saraiam: Cum veneris in Babylonem, et videris, et legeris omnia verba hæc,

verses.text: Thou shalt say: O Lord, thou hast spoken against this place to destroy it: so that there should be neither man nor beast to dwell therein, and that it should be desolate for ever.
verses.textLatin: dices: Domine, tu locutus es contra locum istum, ut disperderes eum, ne sit qui in eo habitet, ab homine usque ad pecus, et ut sit perpetua solitudo.

verses.text: And when thou shalt have made an end of reading this book, thou shalt tie a stone to it, and shalt throw it into the midst of the Euphrates:
verses.textLatin: Cumque compleveris legere librum istum, ligabis ad eum lapidem, et projicies illum in medium Euphraten,

verses.text: And thou shalt say: Thus shall Babylon sink, and she shall not rise up from the affliction that I will bring upon her, and she shall be utterly destroyed. Thus far are the words of Jeremias.
verses.textLatin: et dices: Sic submergetur Babylon, et non consurget a facie afflictionis quam ego adduco super eam, et dissolvetur. Hucusque verba Jeremiæ.

verses.text: Sedecias  was one and twenty years old when he began to reign: and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem: and the name of his mother was Amital, the daughter of Jeremias of Lobna.
verses.textLatin: Filius viginti et unius anni erat Sedecias cum regnare cœpisset, et undecim annis regnavit in Jerusalem. Et nomen matris ejus Amital filia Jeremiæ de Lobna.

verses.text: And he did that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Joakim had done.
verses.textLatin: Et fecit malum in oculis Domini, juxta omnia quæ fecerat Joakim,

verses.text: For the wrath of the Lord was against Jerusalem, and against Juda, till he cast them out from his presence: and Sedecias revolted from the king of Babylon.
verses.textLatin: quoniam furor Domini erat in Jerusalem et in Juda, usquequo projiceret eos a facie sua: et recessit Sedecias a rege Babylonis.

verses.text: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, the tenth day of the month, that Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and they besieged it, and built forts against it round about.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem in anno nono regni ejus, in mense decimo, decima mensis, venit Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis, ipse et omnis exercitus ejus, adversus Jerusalem: et obsederunt eam, et ædificaverunt contra eam munitiones in circuitu.

verses.text: And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Sedecias.
verses.textLatin: Et fuit civitas obsessa usque ad undecimum annum regis Sedeciæ.

verses.text: And in the fourth month, the ninth day of the month, a famine overpowered the city: and there was no food for the people of the land.
verses.textLatin: Mense autem quarto, nona mensis, obtinuit fames civitatem, et non erant alimenta populo terræ.

verses.text: And the city was broken up, and the men of war fled, and went out of the city in the night by the way of the gate that is between the two walls, and leadeth to the king’s garden, (the Chaldeans besieging the city round about,) and they went by the way that leadeth to the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Et dirupta est civitas, et omnes viri bellatores ejus fugerunt, exieruntque de civitate nocte, per viam portæ quæ est inter duos muros, et ducit ad hortum regis, Chaldæis obsidentibus urbem in gyro, et abierunt per viam quæ ducit in eremum.

verses.text: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king: and they overtook Sedecias in the desert which is near Jericho: and all his companions were scattered from him.
verses.textLatin: Persecutus est autem Chadæorum exercitus regem, et apprehenderunt Sedeciam in deserto quod est juxta Jericho: et omnis comitatus ejus diffugit ab eo.

verses.text: And when they had taken the king, they carried him to the king of Babylon to Reblatha, which is in the land of Emath: and he gave judgment upon him.
verses.textLatin: Cumque comprehendissent regem, adduxerunt eum ad regem Babylonis in Reblatha, quæ est in terra Emath, et locutus est ad eum judicia.

verses.text: And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Sedecias before his eyes: and he slew all the princes of Juda in Reblatha.
verses.textLatin: Et jugulavit rex Babylonis filios Sedeciæ in oculis ejus, sed et omnes principes Juda occidit in Reblatha.

verses.text: And he put out the eyes of Sedecias, and bound him with fetters, and the king of Babylon brought him into Babylon, and he put him in prison till the day of his death.
verses.textLatin: Et oculos Sedeciæ eruit, et vinxit eum compedibus, et adduxit eum rex Babylonis in Babylonem, et posuit eum in domo carceris usque ad diem mortis ejus.

verses.text: And in the fifth month, the tenth day of the month, the same is the nineteenth year of Nabuchodonosor, king of Babylon, came Nabuzardan the general of the army, who stood before the king of Babylon in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: In mense autem quinto, decima mensis, ipse est annus nonusdecimus Nabuchodonosor regis Babylonis, venit Nabuzardan princeps militiæ, qui stabat coram rege Babylonis, in Jerusalem,

verses.text: And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: et incendit domum Domini, et domum regis, et omnes domos Jerusalem: et omnem domum magnam igni combussit:

verses.text: And all the army of the Chaldeans that were with the general broke down all the wall of Jerusalem round about.
verses.textLatin: et totum murum Jerusalem per circuitum destruxit cunctus exercitus Chaldæorum qui erat cum magistro militiæ.

verses.text: But Nabuzardan the general carried away captives some of the poor people, and of the rest of the common sort who remained in the city, and of the fugitives that were fled over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
verses.textLatin: De pauperibus autem populi, et de reliquo vulgo quod remanserat in civitate, et de perfugis qui transfugerant ad regem Babylonis, et ceteros de multitudine transtulit Nabuzardan princeps militiæ.

verses.text: But of the poor of the land, Nabuzardan the general left some for vinedressers, and for husbandmen.
verses.textLatin: De pauperibus vero terræ reliquit Nabuzardan princeps militiæ vinitores et agricolas.

verses.text: The Chaldeans also broke in pieces the brazen pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the sea of brass that was in the house of the Lord: and they carried all the brass of them to Babylon.
verses.textLatin: Columnas quoque æreas quæ erant in domo Domini, et bases, et mare æneum quod erat in domo Domini, confregerunt Chaldæi, et tulerunt omne æs eorum in Babylonem,

verses.text: And they took the caldrons, and the fleshhooks, and the psalteries, and the bowls, and the little mortars, and all the brazen vessels that had been used in the ministry: and
verses.textLatin: et lebetes, et creagras, et psalteria, et phialas, et mortariola, et omnia vasa ærea quæ in ministerio fuerant, tulerunt:

verses.text: The general took away the pitchers, and the censers, and the pots, and the basins, and the candlesticks, and the mortars, and the cups: as many as were of gold, in gold: and as many as were of silver, in silver:
verses.textLatin: et hydrias, et thymiamateria, et urceos, et pelves, et candelabra, et mortaria, et cyathos, quotquot aurea, aurea, et quotquot argentea, argentea, tulit magister militiæ:

verses.text: And the two pillars, and one sea, and twelve oxen of brass that were under the bases, which king Solomon had made in the house of the Lord: there was no weight of the brass of all these vessels.
verses.textLatin: et columnas duas, et mare unum, et vitulos duodecim æreos qui erant sub basibus quas fecerat rex Salomon in domo Domini. Non erat pondus æris omnium horum vasorum.

verses.text: And concerning the pillars, one pillar was eighteen cubits high: and a cord of twelve cubits compassed it about: but the thickness thereof was four fingers, and it was hollow within.
verses.textLatin: De columnis autem decem et octo cubiti altitudinis erant in columna una, et funiculus duodecim cubitorum circuibat eam: porro grossitudo ejus quatuor digitorum, et intrinsecus cava erat.

verses.text: And chapiters of brass were upon both: and the height of one chapiter was five cubits: and network, and pomegranates were upon the chapiters round about, all of brass. The same of the second pillar, and the pomegranates.
verses.textLatin: Et capitella super utramque ærea: altitudo capitelli unius quinque cubitorum, et retiacula et malogranata super coronam in circuitu, omnia ærea: similiter columnæ secundæ, et malogranata.

verses.text: And there were ninety-six pomegranates hanging down: and the pomegranates being a hundred in all, were compassed with network.
verses.textLatin: Et fuerunt malogranata nonaginta sex dependentia: et omnia malogranata centum, retiaculis circumdabantur.

verses.text: And the general took Saraias the chief priest, and Sophonias the second priest, and the three keepers of the entry.
verses.textLatin: Et tulit magister militiæ Saraiam sacerdotem primum, et Sophoniam sacerdotem secundum, et tres custodes vestibuli:

verses.text: He also took out of the city one eunuch that was chief over the men of war: and seven men of them that were near the king’s person, that were found in the city: and a scribe, an officer of the army who exercised the young soldiers: and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the midst of the city.
verses.textLatin: et de civitate tulit eunuchum unum, qui erat præpositus super viros bellatores: et septem viros de his qui videbant faciem regis, qui inventi sunt in civitate: et scribam principem militum, qui probabat tyrones: et sexaginta viros de populo terræ, qui inventi sunt in medio civitatis.

verses.text: And Nabuzardan the general took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon, to Reblatha.
verses.textLatin: Tulit autem eos Nabuzardan magister militiæ, et duxit eos ad regem Babylonis in Reblatha:

verses.text: And the king of Babylon struck them, and put them to death in Reblatha, in the land of Emath: and Juda was carried away captive out of his land.
verses.textLatin: et percussit eos rex Babylonis, et interfecit eos in Reblatha in terra Emath: et translatus est Juda de terra sua.

verses.text: This is the people whom Nabuchodonosor carried away captive: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews.
verses.textLatin: Iste est populus quem transtulit Nabuchodonosor: in anno septimo, Judæos tria millia et viginti tres:

verses.text: In the eighteenth year of Nabuchodonosor, eight hundred and thirty-two souls from Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: in anno octavodecimo Nabuchodonosor, de Jerusalem animas octingentas triginta duas:

verses.text: In the three and twentieth year of Nabuchodonosor, Nabuzardan the general carried away of the Jews seven hundred and forty-five souls. So all the souls were four thousand six hundred.
verses.textLatin: in anno vigesimo tertio Nabuchodonosor, transtulit Nabuzardan magister militiæ animas Judæorum septingentas quadraginta quinque. Omnes ergo animæ, quatuor millia sexcentæ.

verses.text: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Joachin king of Juda, in the twelfth month, the five and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Joachin king of Juda, and brought him forth out of prison.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est in trigesimo septimo anno transmigrationis Joachin regis Juda, duodecimo mense, vigesima quinta mensis, elevavit Evilmerodach rex Babylonis, ipso anno regni sui, caput Joachin regis Juda, et eduxit eum de domo carceris.

verses.text: And he spoke kindly to him, and he set his throne above the thrones of the kings that were with him in Babylon.
verses.textLatin: Et locutus est cum eo bona, et posuit thronum ejus super thronos regum qui erant post se in Babylone.

verses.text: And he changed his prison garments, and he ate bread before him always all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: Et mutavit vestimenta carceris ejus, et comedebat panem coram eo semper cunctis diebus vitæ suæ.

verses.text: And for his diet a continual provision was allowed him by the king of Babylon, every day a portion, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: Et cibaria ejus, cibaria perpetua dabantur ei a rege Babylonis, statuta per singulos dies, usque ad diem mortis suæ, cunctis diebus vitæ ejus.

verses.text: Aleph. How doth the city sit solitary that was full of people! how is the mistress of the Gentiles become as a widow: the princes of provinces made tributary!
verses.textLatin: Aleph Quomodo sedet sola civitas plena populo! Facta est quasi vidua domina gentium; princeps provinciarum facta est sub tributo.

verses.text: Beth. Weeping she hath wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: there is none to comfort her among all them that were dear to her: all her friends have despised her, and are become her enemies.
verses.textLatin: Beth Plorans ploravit in nocte, et lacrimæ ejus in maxillis ejus: non est qui consoletur eam ex omnibus caris ejus; omnes amici ejus spreverunt eam, et facti sunt ei inimici.

verses.text: Ghimel. Juda hath removed her dwelling place because of her affliction, and the greatness of her bondage: she hath dwelt among the nations, and she hath found no rest: all her persecutors have taken her in the midst of straits.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Migravit Judas propter afflictionem, et multitudinem servitutis; habitavit inter gentes, nec invenit requiem: omnes persecutores ejus apprehenderunt eam inter angustias.

verses.text: Daleth. The ways of Sion mourn, because there are none that come to the solemn feast: all her gates are broken down: her priests sigh: her virgins are in affliction, and she is oppressed with bitterness.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Viæ Sion lugent, eo quod non sint qui veniant ad solemnitatem: omnes portæ ejus destructæ, sacerdotes ejus gementes; virgines ejus squalidæ, et ipsa oppressa amaritudine.

verses.text: He. Her adversaries are become her lords, her enemies are enriched: because the Lord hath spoken against her for the multitude of her iniquities: her children are led into captivity: before the face of the oppressor.
verses.textLatin: He Facti sunt hostes ejus in capite; inimici ejus locupletati sunt: quia Dominus locutus est super eam propter multitudinem iniquitatum ejus. Parvuli ejus ducti sunt in captivitatem ante faciem tribulantis.

verses.text: Vau. And from the daughter of Sion all her beauty is departed: her princes are become like rams that find no pastures: and they are gone away without strength before the face of the pursuer.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et egressus est a filia Sion omnis decor ejus; facti sunt principes ejus velut arietes non invenientes pascua, et abierunt absque fortitudine ante faciem subsequentis.

verses.text: Zain. Jerusalem hath remembered the days of her affliction, and prevarication of all her desirable things which she had from the days of old, when her people fell in the enemy’s hand, and there was no helper: the enemies have seen her, and have mocked at her sabbaths.
verses.textLatin: Zain Recordata est Jerusalem dierum afflictionis suæ, et prævaricationis, omnium desiderabilium suorum, quæ habuerat a diebus antiquis, cum caderet populus ejus in manu hostili, et non esset auxiliator: viderunt eam hostes, et deriserunt sabbata ejus.

verses.text: Heth. Jerusalem hath grievously sinned, therefore is she become unstable: all that honoured her have despised her, because they have seen her shame: but she sighed and turned backward.
verses.textLatin: Heth Peccatum peccavit Jerusalem, propterea instabilis facta est; omnes qui glorificabant eam spreverunt illam, quia viderunt ignominiam ejus: ipsa autem gemens conversa est retrorsum.

verses.text: Teth. Her filthiness is on her feet, and she hath not remembered her end: she is wonderfully cast down, not having a comforter: behold, O Lord, my affliction, because the enemy is lifted up.
verses.textLatin: Teth Sordes ejus in pedibus ejus, nec recordata est finis sui; deposita est vehementer, non habens consolatorem. Vide, Domine, afflictionem meam, quoniam erectus est inimicus.

verses.text: Jod. The enemy hath put out his hand to all her desirable things: for she hath seen the Gentiles enter into her sanctuary, of whom thou gavest commandment that they should not enter into thy church.
verses.textLatin: Jod Manum suam misit hostis ad omnia desiderabilia ejus, quia vidit gentes ingressas sanctuarium suum, de quibus præceperas ne intrarent in ecclesiam tuam.

verses.text: Caph. All her people sigh, they seek bread: they have given all their precious things for food to relieve the soul: see, O Lord, and consider, for I am become vile.
verses.textLatin: Caph Omnis populus ejus gemens, et quærens panem; dederunt pretiosa quæque pro cibo ad refocillandam animam. Vide, Domine, et considera quoniam facta sum vilis!

verses.text: Lamed. O all ye that pass by the way, attend, and see if there be any sorrow like to my sorrow: for he hath made a vintage of me, as the Lord spoke in the day of his fierce anger.
verses.textLatin: Lamed O vos omnes qui transitis per viam, attendite, et videte si est dolor sicut dolor meus! quoniam vindemiavit me, ut locutus est Dominus, in die iræ furoris sui.

verses.text: Mem. From above he hath sent fire into my bones, and hath chastised me: he hath spread a net for my feet, he hath turned me back: he hath made me desolate, wasted with sorrow all the day long.
verses.textLatin: Mem De excelso misit ignem in ossibus meis, et erudivit me: expandit rete pedibus meis, convertit me retrorsum; posuit me desolatam, tota die mœrore confectam.

verses.text: Nun. The yoke of my iniquities hath watched: they are folded together in his hand, and put upon my neck: my strength is weakened: the Lord hath delivered me into a hand, out of which I am not able to rise.
verses.textLatin: Nun Vigilavit jugum iniquitatum mearum; in manu ejus convolutæ sunt, et impositæ collo meo. Infirmata est virtus mea: dedit me Dominus in manu de qua non potero surgere.

verses.text: Samech. The Lord hath taken away all my mighty men out of the midst of me: he hath called against me the time, to destroy my chosen men: the Lord hath trodden the winepress for the virgin daughter of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Samech Abstulit omnes magnificos meos Dominus de medio mei; vocavit adversum me tempus ut contereret electos meos. Torcular calcavit Dominus virgini filiæ Juda.

verses.text: Ain. Therefore do I weep, and my eyes run down with water: because the comforter, the relief of my soul, is far from me: my children are desolate because the enemy hath prevailed.
verses.textLatin: Ain Idcirco ego plorans, et oculus meus deducens aquas, quia longe factus est a me consolator, convertens animam meam. Facti sunt filii mei perditi, quoniam invaluit inimicus.

verses.text: Phe. Sion hath spread forth her hands, there is none to comfort her: the Lord hath commanded against Jacob, his enemies are round about him: Jerusalem is as a menstruous woman among them.
verses.textLatin: Phe Expandit Sion manus suas; non est qui consoletur eam. Mandavit Dominus adversum Jacob in circuitu ejus hostes ejus; facta est Jerusalem quasi polluta menstruis inter eos.

verses.text: Sade. The Lord is just, for I have provoked his mouth to wrath: hear, I pray you, all ye people, and see my sorrow: my virgins, and my young men are gone into captivity.
verses.textLatin: Sade Justus est Dominus, quia os ejus ad iracundiam provocavi. Audite, obsecro, universi populi, et videte dolorem meum: virgines meæ et juvenes mei abierunt in captivitatem.

verses.text: Coph. I called for my friends, but they deceived me: my priests and my ancients pined away in the city: while they sought their food, to relieve their souls.
verses.textLatin: Coph Vocavi amicos meos, et ipsi deceperunt me; sacerdotes mei et senes mei in urbe consumpti sunt, quia quæsierunt cibum sibi ut refocillarent animam suam.

verses.text: Res. Behold, O Lord, for I am in distress, my bowels are troubled: my heart is turned within me, for I am full of bitterness: abroad the sword destroyeth, and at home there is death alike.
verses.textLatin: ResVide, Domine, quoniam tribulor: conturbatus est venter meus, subversum est cor meum in memetipsa, quoniam amaritudine plena sum. Foris interfecit gladius, et domi mors similis est.

verses.text: Sin. They have heard that I sigh, and there is none to comfort me: all my enemies have heard of my evil, they have rejoiced that thou hast done it: thou hast brought a day of consolation, and they shall be like unto me.
verses.textLatin: Sin Audierunt quia ingemisco ego, et non est qui consoletur me; omnes inimici mei audierunt malum meum, lætati sunt quoniam tu fecisti: adduxisti diem consolationis, et fient similes mei.

verses.text: Thau. Let all their evil be present before thee: and make vintage of them, as thou hast made vintage of me for all my iniquities: for my sighs are many, and my heart is sorrowful.
verses.textLatin: Thau Ingrediatur omne malum eorum coram te: et vindemia eos, sicut vindemiasti me propter omnes iniquitates meas: multi enim gemitus mei, et cor meum mœrens.

verses.text: Aleph. How hath the Lord covered with obscurity the daughter of Sion in his wrath! how hath he cast down from heaven to the earth the glorious one of Israel, and hath not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger!
verses.textLatin: Aleph Quomodo obtexit caligine in furore suo Dominus filiam Sion; projecit de cælo in terram inclytam Israël, et non est recordatus scabelli pedum suorum in die furoris sui!

verses.text: Beth. The Lord hath cast down headlong, and hath not spared, all that was beautiful in Jacob: he hath destroyed in his wrath the strong holds of the virgin of Juda, and brought them down to the ground: he hath made the kingdom unclean, and the princes thereof.
verses.textLatin: Beth Præcipitavit Dominus, nec pepercit omnia speciosa Jacob: destruxit in furore suo munitiones virginis Juda, et dejecit in terram; polluit regnum et principes ejus.

verses.text: Ghimel. He hath broken in his fierce anger all the horn of Israel: he hath drawn back his right hand from before the enemy: and he hath kindled in Jacob as it were a flaming fire devouring round about.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Confregit in ira furoris sui omne cornu Israël; avertit retrorsum dexteram suam a facie inimici, et succendit in Jacob quasi ignem flammæ devorantis in gyro.

verses.text: Daleth. He hath bent his bow as an enemy, he hath fixed his right hand as an adversary: and he hath killed all that was fair to behold in the tabernacle of the daughter of Sion, he hath poured out his indignation like fire.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Tetendit arcum suum quasi inimicus, firmavit dexteram suam quasi hostis, et occidit omne quod pulchrum erat visu in tabernaculo filiæ Sion; effudit quasi ignem indignationem suam.

verses.text: He. The Lord is become as an enemy: he hath cast down Israel headlong, he hath overthrown all the walls thereof: he hath destroyed his strong holds, and hath multiplied in the daughter of Juda the afflicted, both men and women.
verses.textLatin: He Factus est Dominus velut inimicus, præcipitavit Israël: præcipitavit omnia mœnia ejus, dissipavit munitiones ejus, et replevit in filia Juda humiliatum et humiliatam.

verses.text: Vau. And he hath destroyed his tent as a garden, he hath thrown down his tabernacle: the Lord hath caused feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Sion: and hath delivered up king and priest to reproach, and to the indignation of his wrath.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et dissipavit quasi hortum tentorium suum; demolitus est tabernaculum suum. Oblivioni tradidit Dominus in Sion festivitatem et sabbatum; et in opprobrium, et in indignationem furoris sui, regem et sacerdotem.

verses.text: Zain. The Lord hath cast off his altar, he hath cursed his sanctuary: he hath delivered the walls of the towers thereof into the hand of the enemy: they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as in the day of a solemn feast.
verses.textLatin: Zain Repulit Dominus altare suum; maledixit sanctificationi suæ: tradidit in manu inimici muros turrium ejus. Vocem dederunt in domo Domini sicut in die solemni.

verses.text: Heth. The Lord hath purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Sion: he hath stretched out his line, and hath not withdrawn his hand from destroying: and the bulwark hath mourned, and the wall hath been destroyed together.
verses.textLatin: Heth Cogitavit Dominus dissipare murum filiæ Sion; tetendit funiculum suum, et non avertit manum suam a perditione: luxitque antemurale, et murus pariter dissipatus est.

verses.text: Teth. Her gates are sunk into the ground: he hath destroyed, and broken her bars: her king and her princes are among the Gentiles: the law is no more, and her prophets have found no vision from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Teth Defixæ sunt in terra portæ ejus, perdidit et contrivit vectes ejus; regem ejus et principes ejus in gentibus: non est lex, et prophetæ ejus non invenerunt visionem a Domino.

verses.text: Jod. The ancients of the daughter of Sion sit upon the ground, they have held their peace: they have sprinkled their heads with dust, they are girded with haircloth, the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Jod Sederunt in terra, conticuerunt senes filiæ Sion; consperserunt cinere capita sua, accincti sunt ciliciis: abjecerunt in terram capita sua virgines Jerusalem.

verses.text: Caph. My eyes have failed with weeping, my bowels are troubled: my liver is poured out upon the earth, for the destruction of the daughter of my people, when the children, and the sucklings, fainted away in the streets of the city.
verses.textLatin: Caph Defecerunt præ lacrimis oculi mei, conturbata sunt viscera mea; effusum est in terra jecur meum super contritione filiæ populi mei, cum deficeret parvulus et lactens in plateis oppidi.

verses.text: Lamed. They said to their mothers: Where is corn and wine? when they fainted away as the wounded in the streets of the city: when they breathed out their souls in the bosoms of their mothers.
verses.textLatin: Lamed Matribus suis dixerunt: Ubi est triticum et vinum? cum deficerent quasi vulnerati in plateis civitatis, cum exhalarent animas suas in sinu matrum suarum.

verses.text: Mem. To what shall I compare thee? or to what shall I liken thee, O daughter of Jerusalem? to what shall I equal thee, that I may comfort thee, O virgin daughter of Sion? for great as the sea is thy destruction: who shall heal thee?
verses.textLatin: Mem Cui comparabo te, vel cui assimilabo te, filia Jerusalem? cui exæquabo te, et consolabor te, virgo, filia Sion? magna est enim velut mare contritio tua: quis medebitur tui?

verses.text: Nun. Thy prophets have seen false and foolish things for thee: and they have not laid open thy iniquity, to excite thee to penance: but they have seen for thee false revelations and banishments.
verses.textLatin: Nun Prophetæ tui viderunt tibi falsa et stulta; nec aperiebant iniquitatem tuam, ut te ad pœnitentiam provocarent; viderunt autem tibi assumptiones falsas, et ejectiones.

verses.text: Samech. All they that passed by the way have clapped their hands at thee: they have hissed, and wagged their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem, saying: Is this the city of perfect beauty, the joy of all the earth?
verses.textLatin: Samech Plauserunt super te manibus omnes transeuntes per viam; sibilaverunt et moverunt caput suum super filiam Jerusalem: Hæccine est urbs, dicentes, perfecti decoris, gaudium universæ terræ?

verses.text: Phe. All thy enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they have hissed, and gnashed with the teeth, and have said: We will swallow her up: lo, this is the day which we looked for: we have found it, we have seen it.
verses.textLatin: Phe Aperuerunt super te os suum omnes inimici tui: sibilaverunt, et fremuerunt dentibus, et dixerunt: Devorabimus: en ista est dies quam exspectabamus; invenimus, vidimus.

verses.text: Ain. The Lord hath done that which he purposed, he hath fulfilled his word, which he commanded in the days of old: he hath destroyed, and hath not spared, and he hath caused the enemy to rejoice over thee, and hath set up the horn of thy adversaries.
verses.textLatin: Ain Fecit Dominus quæ cogitavit; complevit sermonem suum, quem præceperat a diebus antiquis: destruxit, et non pepercit, et lætificavit super te inimicum, et exaltavit cornu hostium tuorum.

verses.text: Sade. Their heart cried to the Lord upon the walls of the daughter of Sion: Let tears run down like a torrent day and night: give thyself no rest, and let not the apple of thy eye cease.
verses.textLatin: Sade Clamavit cor eorum ad Dominum super muros filiæ Sion: Deduc quasi torrentem lacrimas per diem et noctem; non des requiem tibi, neque taceat pupilla oculi tui.

verses.text: Coph. Arise, give praise in the night, in the beginning of the watches: pour out thy heart like water before the face of the Lord: lift up thy hands to him for the life of thy little children, that have fainted for hunger at the top of all the streets.
verses.textLatin: Coph Consurge, lauda in nocte, in principio vigiliarum; effunde sicut aquam cor tuum ante conspectum Domini: leva ad eum manus tuas pro anima parvulorum tuorum, qui defecerunt in fame in capite omnium compitorum.

verses.text: Res. Behold, O Lord, and consider whom thou hast thus dealt with: shall women then eat their own fruit, their children of a span long? shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Res Vide, Domine, et considera quem vindemiaveris ita. Ergone comedent mulieres fructum suum, parvulos ad mensuram palmæ? si occiditur in sanctuario Domini sacerdos et propheta?

verses.text: Sin. The child and the old man lie without on the ground: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword: thou hast slain them in the day of thy wrath: thou hast killed, and shewn them no pity.
verses.textLatin: Sin Jacuerunt in terra foris puer et senex; virgines meæ et juvenes mei ceciderunt in gladio: interfecisti in die furoris tui, percussisti, nec misertus es.

verses.text: Thau. Thou hast called as to a festival, those that should terrify me round about, and there was none in the day of the wrath of the Lord that escaped and was left: those that I brought up, and nourished, my enemy hath consumed them.
verses.textLatin: Thau Vocasti quasi ad diem solemnem, qui terrerent me de circuitu; et non fuit in die furoris Domini qui effugeret, et relinqueretur: quos educavi et enutrivi, inimicus meus consumpsit eos.

verses.text: Aleph. I AM the man that see my poverty by the rod of his indignation.
verses.textLatin: Aleph Ego vir videns paupertatem meam in virga indignationis ejus.

verses.text: Aleph. He hath led me, and brought me into darkness, and not into light.
verses.textLatin: Aleph Me minavit, et adduxit in tenebras, et non in lucem.

verses.text: Aleph. Only against me he hath turned, and turned again his hand all the day.
verses.textLatin: Aleph Tantum in me vertit et convertit manum suam tota die.

verses.text: Beth. My skin and my flesh he hath made old, he hath broken my bones.
verses.textLatin: Beth Vetustam fecit pellem meam et carnem meam; contrivit ossa mea.

verses.text: Beth. He hath built round about me, and he hath compassed me with gall and labour.
verses.textLatin: Beth Ædificavit in gyro meo, et circumdedit me felle et labore.

verses.text: Beth. He hath set me in dark places as those that are dead for ever.
verses.textLatin: Beth In tenebrosis collocavit me, quasi mortuos sempiternos.

verses.text: Ghimel. He hath built against me round about, that I may not get out: he hath made my fetters heavy.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Circumædificavit adversum me, ut non egrediar; aggravavit compedem meum.

verses.text: Ghimel. Yea, and when I cry, and entreat, he hath shut out my prayer.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Sed et cum clamavero, et rogavero, exclusit orationem meam.

verses.text: Ghimel. He hath shut up my ways with square stones, he hath turned my paths upside down.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Conclusit vias meas lapidibus quadris; semitas meas subvertit.

verses.text: Daleth. He is become to me as a bear lying in wait: as a lion in secret places.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Ursus insidians factus est mihi, leo in absconditis.

verses.text: Daleth. He hath turned aside my paths, and hath broken me in pieces, he hath made me desolate.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Semitas meas subvertit, et confregit me; posuit me desolatam.

verses.text: Daleth. He hath bent his bow, and set me as a mark for his arrows.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Tetendit arcum suum, et posuit me quasi signum ad sagittam.

verses.text: He. He hath shot into my reins the daughters of his quiver.
verses.textLatin: He Misit in renibus meis filias pharetræ suæ.

verses.text: He. I am made a derision to all my people, their song all the day long.
verses.textLatin: He Factus sum in derisum omni populo meo, canticum eorum tota die.

verses.text: He. He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath inebriated me with wormwood.
verses.textLatin: He Replevit me amaritudinibus; inebriavit me absinthio.

verses.text: Vau. And he hath broken my teeth one by one, he hath fed me with ashes.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et fregit ad numerum dentes meos; cibavit me cinere.

verses.text: Vau. And my soul is removed far off from peace, I have forgotten good things.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et repulsa est a pace anima mea; oblitus sum bonorum.

verses.text: Vau. And I said: My end and my hope is perished from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et dixi: Periit finis meus, et spes mea a Domino.

verses.text: Zain. Remember my poverty, and transgression, the wormwood, and the gall.
verses.textLatin: Zain Recordare paupertatis, et transgressionis meæ, absinthii et fellis.

verses.text: Zain. I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me.
verses.textLatin: Zain Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea.

verses.text: Zain. These things I shall think over in my heart, therefore will I hope.
verses.textLatin: Zain Hæc recolens in corde meo, ideo sperabo.

verses.text: Heth. The mercies of the Lord that we are not consumed: because his commiserations have not failed.
verses.textLatin: Heth Misericordiæ Domini, quia non sumus consumpti; quia non defecerunt miserationes ejus.

verses.text: Heth. They are new every morning, great is thy faithfulness.
verses.textLatin: Heth Novi diluculo, multa est fides tua.

verses.text: Heth. The Lord is my portion, said my soul: therefore will I wait for him.
verses.textLatin: Heth Pars mea Dominus, dixit anima mea; propterea exspectabo eum.

verses.text: Teth. The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him.
verses.textLatin: Teth Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in eum, animæ quærenti illum.

verses.text: Teth. It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of God.
verses.textLatin: Teth Bonum est præstolari cum silentio salutare Dei.

verses.text: Teth. It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke from his youth.
verses.textLatin: Teth Bonum est viro cum portaverit jugum ab adolescentia sua.

verses.text: Jod. He shall sit solitary, and hold his peace: because he hath taken it up upon himself.
verses.textLatin: Jod Sedebit solitarius, et tacebit, quia levavit super se.

verses.text: Jod. He shall put his mouth in the dust, if so be there may be hope.
verses.textLatin: Jod Ponet in pulvere os suum, si forte sit spes.

verses.text: Jod. He shall give his cheek to him that striketh him, he shall be filled with reproaches.
verses.textLatin: Jod Dabit percutienti se maxillam: saturabitur opprobriis.

verses.text: Caph. For the Lord will not cast off for ever.
verses.textLatin: Caph Quia non repellet in sempiternum Dominus.

verses.text: Caph. For if he hath cast off, he will also have mercy, according to the multitude of his mercies.
verses.textLatin: Caph Quia si abjecit, et miserebitur, secundum multitudinem misericordiarum suarum.

verses.text: Caph. For he hath not willingly afflicted, nor cast off the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Caph Non enim humiliavit ex corde suo et abjecit filios hominum.

verses.text: Lamed. To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the land,
verses.textLatin: Lamed Ut conteret sub pedibus suis omnes vinctos terræ.

verses.text: Lamed. To turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the most High,
verses.textLatin: Lamed Ut declinaret judicium viri in conspectu vultus Altissimi.

verses.text: Lamed. To destroy a man wrongfully in his judgment, the Lord hath not approved.
verses.textLatin: Lamed Ut perverteret hominem in judicio suo; Dominus ignoravit.

verses.text: Mem. Who is he that hath commanded a thing to be done, when the Lord commandeth it not?
verses.textLatin: Mem Quis est iste qui dixit ut fieret, Domino non jubente?

verses.text: Mem. Shall not both evil and good proceed out of the mouth of the Highest?
verses.textLatin: Mem Ex ore Altissimi non egredientur nec mala nec bona?

verses.text: Mem. Why hath a living man murmured, man suffering for his sins?
verses.textLatin: Mem Quid murmuravit homo vivens, vir pro peccatis suis?

verses.text: Nun. Let us search our ways, and seek, and return to the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Nun Scrutemur vias nostras, et quæramus, et revertamur ad Dominum.

verses.text: Nun. Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens.
verses.textLatin: Nun Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cælos.

verses.text: Nun. We have done wickedly, and provoked thee to wrath: therefore thou art inexorable.
verses.textLatin: Nun Nos inique egimus, et ad iracundiam provocavimus; idcirco tu inexorabilis es.

verses.text: Samech. Thou hast covered in thy wrath, and hast struck us: thou hast killed and hast not spared.
verses.textLatin: Samech Operuisti in furore, et percussisti nos; occidisti, nec pepercisti.

verses.text: Samech. Thou hast set a cloud before thee, that our prayer may not pass through.
verses.textLatin: Samech Opposuisti nubem tibi, ne transeat oratio.

verses.text: Samech. Thou hast made me as an outcast, and refuse in the midst of the people.
verses.textLatin: Samech Eradicationem et abjectionem posuisti me in medio populorum.

verses.text: Phe. All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
verses.textLatin: Phe Aperuerunt super nos os suum omnes inimici.

verses.text: Phe. Prophecy is become to us a fear, and a snare, and destruction.
verses.textLatin: Phe Formido et laqueus facta est nobis vaticinatio, et contritio.

verses.text: Phe. My eye hath run down with streams of water, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
verses.textLatin: Phe Divisiones aquarum deduxit oculus meus, in contritione filiæ populi mei.

verses.text: Ain. My eye is afflicted, and hath not been quiet, because there was no rest:
verses.textLatin: Ain Oculus meus afflictus est, nec tacuit, eo quod non esset requies.

verses.text: Ain. Till the Lord regarded and looked down from the heavens.
verses.textLatin: Ain Donec respiceret et videret Dominus de cælis.

verses.text: Ain. My eye hath wasted my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
verses.textLatin: Ain Oculus meus deprædatus est animam meam in cunctis filiabus urbis meæ.

verses.text: Sade. My enemies have chased me and caught me like a bird, without cause.
verses.textLatin: Sade Venatione ceperunt me quasi avem inimici mei gratis.

verses.text: Sade. My life is fallen into the pit, and they have laid a stone over me.
verses.textLatin: Sade Lapsa est in lacum vita mea, et posuerunt lapidem super me.

verses.text: Sade. Waters have flowed over my head: I said: I am cut off.
verses.textLatin: Sade Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum; dixi: Perii.

verses.text: Coph. I have called upon thy name, O Lord, from the lowest pit.
verses.textLatin: Coph Invocavi nomen tuum, Domine, de lacu novissimo.

verses.text: Coph. Thou hast heard my voice: turn not away thy ear from my sighs, and cries.
verses.textLatin: Coph Vocem meam audisti; ne avertas aurem tuam a singultu meo et clamoribus.

verses.text: Coph. Thou drewest near in the day, when I called upon thee, thou saidst: Fear not.
verses.textLatin: Coph Appropinquasti in die quando invocavi te; dixisti: Ne timeas.

verses.text: Res. Thou hast judged, O Lord, the cause of my soul, thou the Redeemer of my life.
verses.textLatin: Res Judicasti, Domine, causam animæ meæ, redemptor vitæ meæ.

verses.text: Res. Thou hast seen, O Lord, their iniquity against me: judge thou my judgment.
verses.textLatin: Res Vidisti, Domine, iniquitatem illorum adversum me: judica judicium meum.

verses.text: Res. Thou hast seen all their fury, and all their thoughts against me.
verses.textLatin: Res Vidisti omnem furorem, universas cogitationes eorum adversum me.

verses.text: Sin. Thou hast heard their reproach, O Lord, all their imaginations against me.
verses.textLatin: Sin Audisti opprobrium eorum, Domine, omnes cogitationes eorum adversum me.

verses.text: Sin. The lips of them that rise up against me: and their devices against me all the day.
verses.textLatin: Sin Labia insurgentium mihi, et meditationes eorum adversum me tota die.

verses.text: Sin. Behold their sitting down, and their rising up, I am their song.
verses.textLatin: Sin Sessionem eorum et resurrectionem eorum vide; ego sum psalmus eorum.

verses.text: Thau. Thou shalt render them a recompense, O Lord, according to the works of their hands.
verses.textLatin: Thau Redes eis vicem, Domine, juxta opera manuum suarum.

verses.text: Thau. Thou shalt give them a buckler of heart, thy labour.
verses.textLatin: Thau Dabis eis scutum cordis, laborem tuum.

verses.text: Thau. Thou shalt persecute them in anger, and shalt destroy them from under the heavens, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Thau Persequeris in furore, et conteres eos sub cælis, Domine.

verses.text: Aleph. How is the gold become dim, the finest colour is changed, the stones of the sanctuary are scattered in the top of every street?
verses.textLatin: Aleph Quomodo obscuratum est aurum, mutatus est color optimus! dispersi sunt lapides sanctuarii in capite omnium platearum!

verses.text: Beth. The noble sons of Sion, and they that were clothed with the best gold: how are they esteemed as earthen vessels, the work of the potter’s hands?
verses.textLatin: Beth Filii Sion inclyti, et amicti auro primo: quomodo reputati sunt in vasa testea, opus manuum figuli!

verses.text: Ghimel. Even the sea monsters have drawn out the breast, they have given suck to their young: the daughter of my people is cruel, like the ostrich in the desert.
verses.textLatin: Ghimel Sed et lamiæ nudaverunt mammam, lactaverunt catulos suos: filia populi mei crudelis quasi struthio in deserto.

verses.text: Daleth. The tongue of the sucking child hath stuck to the roof of his mouth for thirst: the little ones have asked for bread, and there was none to break it unto them.
verses.textLatin: Daleth Adhæsit lingua lactentis ad palatum ejus in siti; parvuli petierunt panem, et non erat qui frangeret eis.

verses.text: He. They that were fed delicately have died in the streets; they that were brought up in scarlet have embraced the dung.
verses.textLatin: He Qui vescebantur voluptuose, interierunt in viis; qui nutriebantur in croceis, amplexati sunt stercora.

verses.text: Vau. And the iniquity of the daughter of my people is made greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and hands took nothing in her.
verses.textLatin: Vau Et major effecta est iniquitas filiæ populi mei peccato Sodomorum, quæ subversa est in momento, et non ceperunt in ea manus.

verses.text: Zain. Her Nazarites were whiter than snow, purer than milk, more ruddy than the old ivory, fairer than the sapphire.
verses.textLatin: Zain Candidiores Nazaræi ejus nive, nitidiores lacte, rubicundiores ebore antiquo, sapphiro pulchriores.

verses.text: Heth. Their face is now made blacker than coals, and they are not known in the streets: their skin hath stuck to their bones, it is withered, and is become like wood.
verses.textLatin: Heth Denigrata est super carbones facies eorum et non sunt cogniti in plateis; adhæsit cutis eorum ossibus: aruit, et facta est quasi lignum.

verses.text: Teth. It was better with them that were slain by the sword, than with them that died with hunger: for these pined away being consumed for want of the fruits of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Teth Melius fuit occisis gladio quam interfectis fame, quoniam isti extabuerunt consumpti a sterilitate terræ.

verses.text: Jod. The hands of the pitiful women have sodden their own children: they were their meat in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
verses.textLatin: Jod Manus mulierum misericordium coxerunt filios suos; facti sunt cibus earum in contritione filiæ populi mei.

verses.text: Caph. The Lord hath accomplished his wrath, he hath poured out his fierce anger: and he hath kindled a fire in Sion, and it hath devoured the foundations thereof.
verses.textLatin: Caph Complevit Dominus furorem suum, effudit iram indignationis suæ: et succendit ignem in Sion, et devoravit fundamenta ejus.

verses.text: Lamed. The kings of the earth, and all the inhabitants of the world would not have believed, that the adversary and the enemy should enter in by the gates of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Lamed Non crediderunt reges terræ, et universi habitatores orbis, quoniam ingrederetur hostis et inimicus per portas Jerusalem.

verses.text: Mem. For the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her.
verses.textLatin: Mem Propter peccata prophetarum ejus, et iniquitates sacerdotum ejus, qui effuderunt in medio ejus sanguinem justorum.

verses.text: Nun. They have wandered as blind men in the streets, they were defiled with blood: and when they could not help walking in it, they held up their skirts.
verses.textLatin: Nun Erraverunt cæci in plateis, polluti sunt in sanguine; cumque non possent, tenuerunt lacinias suas.

verses.text: Samech. Depart you that are defiled, they cried out to them: Depart, get ye hence, touch not: for they quarrelled, and being removed, they said among the Gentiles: He will no more dwell among them.
verses.textLatin: Samech Recedite polluti, clamaverunt eis; recedite, abite, nolite tangere: jurgati quippe sunt, et commoti dixerunt inter gentes: Non addet ultra ut habitet in eis.

verses.text: Phe. The face of the Lord hath divided them, he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, neither had they pity on the ancient.
verses.textLatin: Phe Facies Domini divisit eos, non addet ut respiciat eos; facies sacerdotum non erubuerunt, neque senum miserti sunt.

verses.text: Ain. While we were yet standing, our eyes failed, expecting help for us in vain, when we looked attentively towards a nation that was not able to save.
verses.textLatin: Ain Cum adhuc subsisteremus, defecerunt oculi nostri ad auxilium nostrum vanum; cum respiceremus attenti ad gentem quæ salvare non poterat.

verses.text: Sade. Our steps have slipped in the way of our streets, our end draweth near: our days are fulfilled, for our end is come.
verses.textLatin: Sade Lubricaverunt vestigia nostra in itinere platearum nostrarum; appropinquavit finis noster, completi sunt dies nostri, quia venit finis noster.

verses.text: Coph. Our persecutors were swifter than the eagles of the air: they pursued us upon the mountains, they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Coph Velociores fuerunt persecutores nostri aquilis cæli; super montes persecuti sunt nos, in deserto insidiati sunt nobis.

verses.text: Res. The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins: to whom we said: Under thy shadow we shall live among the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Res Spiritus oris nostri, christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris, cui diximus: In umbra tua vivemus in gentibus.

verses.text: Sin. Rejoice, and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Hus: to thee also shall the cup come, thou shalt be made drunk, and naked.
verses.textLatin: Sin Gaude et lætare, filia Edom, quæ habitas in terra Hus! ad te quoque perveniet calix: inebriaberis, atque nudaberis.

verses.text: Thau. Thy iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Sion, he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he hath visited thy iniquity, O daughter of Edom, he hath discovered thy sins.
verses.textLatin: Thau Completa est iniquitas tua, filia Sion: non addet ultra ut transmigret te. Visitavit iniquitatem tuam, filia Edom; discooperuit peccata tua.

verses.text: Remember,  O Lord, what is come upon us: consider and behold our reproach.
verses.textLatin: Recordare, Domine, quid acciderit nobis; intuere et respice opprobrium nostrum.

verses.text: Our inheritance is turned to aliens: our houses to strangers.
verses.textLatin: Hæreditas nostra versa est ad alienos, domus nostræ ad extraneos.

verses.text: We are become orphans without a father: our mothers are as widows.
verses.textLatin: Pupilli facti sumus absque patre, matres nostræ quasi viduæ.

verses.text: We have drunk our water for money: we have bought our wood.
verses.textLatin: Aquam nostram pecunia bibimus; ligna nostra pretio comparavimus.

verses.text: We were dragged by the necks, we were weary and no rest was given us.
verses.textLatin: Cervicibus nostris minabamur, lassis non dabatur requies.

verses.text: We have given our hand to Egypt, and to the Assyrians, that we might be satisfied with bread.
verses.textLatin: Ægypto dedimus manum et Assyriis, ut saturaremur pane.

verses.text: Our fathers have sinned, and are not: and we have borne their iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Patres nostri peccaverunt, et non sunt: et nos iniquitates eorum portavimus.

verses.text: Servants have ruled over us: there was none to redeem us out of their hand.
verses.textLatin: Servi dominati sunt nostri: non fuit qui redimeret de manu eorum.

verses.text: We fetched our bread at the peril of our lives, because of the sword in the desert.
verses.textLatin: In animabus nostris afferebamus panem nobis, a facie gladii in deserto.

verses.text: Our skin was burnt as an oven, by reason of the violence of the famine.
verses.textLatin: Pellis nostra quasi clibanus exusta est, a facie tempestatum famis.

verses.text: They oppressed the women in Sion, and the virgins in the cities of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Mulieres in Sion humiliaverunt, et virgines in civitatibus Juda.

verses.text: The princes were hanged up by their hand: they did not respect the persons of the ancient.
verses.textLatin: Principes manu suspensi sunt; facies senum non erubuerunt.

verses.text: They abused the young men indecently: and the children fell under the wood.
verses.textLatin: Adolescentibus impudice abusi sunt, et pueri in ligno corruerunt.

verses.text: The ancients have ceased from the gates: the young men from the choir of the singers.
verses.textLatin: Senes defecerunt de portis, juvenes de choro psallentium.

verses.text: The joy of our heart is ceased, our dancing is turned into mourning.
verses.textLatin: Defecit gaudium cordis nostri; versus est in luctum chorus noster.

verses.text: The crown is fallen from our head woe to us, because we have sinned.
verses.textLatin: Cecidit corona capitis nostri: væ nobis, quia peccavimus!

verses.text: Therefore is our heart sorrowful, therefore are our eyes become dim,
verses.textLatin: Propterea mœstum factum est cor nostrum; ideo contenebrati sunt oculi nostri,

verses.text: For mount Sion, because it is destroyed, foxes have walked upon it.
verses.textLatin: propter montem Sion quia disperiit; vulpes ambulaverunt in eo.

verses.text: But thou, O Lord, shalt remain for ever, thy throne from generation to generation.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, Domine, in æternum permanebis, solium tuum in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: Why wilt thou forget us for ever? why wilt thou forsake us for a long time?
verses.textLatin: Quare in perpetuum oblivisceris nostri, derelinques nos in longitudine dierum?

verses.text: Convert us, O Lord, to thee, and we shall be converted: renew our days, as from the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Converte nos, Domine, ad te, et convertemur; innova dies nostros, sicut a principio.

verses.text: But thou hast utterly rejected us, thou art exceedingly angry with us.
verses.textLatin: Sed projiciens repulisti nos: iratus es contra nos vehementer.

verses.text: And  these are the words of the book, which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maasias, the son of Sedecias, the son of Sedei, the son Helcias, wrote in Babylonia.
verses.textLatin: Et hæc verba libri quæ scripsit Baruch filius Neriæ, filii Maasiæ, filii Sedeciæ, filii Sedei, filii Helciæ, in Babylonia,

verses.text: In the fifth year, in the seventh day of the month, at the time that the Chaldeans took Jerusalem, and burnt it with fire.
verses.textLatin: in anno quinto, in septimo die mensis, in tempore quo ceperunt Chaldæi Jerusalem, et succenderunt eam igni.

verses.text: And Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias the son of Joakim king of Juda, and in the hearing of all the people that came to hear the book.
verses.textLatin: Et legit Baruch verba libri hujus ad aures Jechoniæ filii Joakim regis Juda, et ad aures universi populi venientis ad librum,

verses.text: And in the hearing of the nobles, the sons of the kings, and in the hearing of the ancients, and in the hearing of the people, from the least even to the greatest of them that dwelt in Babylonia, by the river Sedi.
verses.textLatin: et ad aures potentium, filiorum regum, et ad aures presbyterorum, et ad aures populi, a minimo usque ad maximum eorum, omnium habitantium in Babylonia, ad flumen Sodi.

verses.text: And when they heard it they wept, and fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Qui audientes plorabant, et jejunabant, et orabant in conspectu Domini.

verses.text: And they made a collection of money, according to every man’s power.
verses.textLatin: Et collegerunt pecuniam, secundum quod potuit uniuscujusque manus,

verses.text: And they sent it to Jerusalem to Joakim the priest, the son of Helcias, the son of Salom, and to the priests, and to all the people, that were found with him in Jerusalem:
verses.textLatin: et miserunt in Jerusalem ad Joakim filium Helciæ filii Salom sacerdotem, et ad sacerdotes, et ad omnem populum qui inventi sunt cum eo in Jerusalem:

verses.text: At the time when he received the vessels of the temple of the Lord, which had been taken away out of the temple, to return them into the land of Juda the tenth day of the month Sivan, the silver vessels, which Sedecias the son of Josias king of Juda had made,
verses.textLatin: cum acciperet vasa templi Domini, quæ ablata fuerant de templo, revocare in terram Juda, decima die mensis Sivan, vasa argentea quæ fecit Sedecias filius Josiæ rex Juda,

verses.text: After that Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon had carried away Jechonias, and the princes, and all the powerful men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought them bound to Babylon.
verses.textLatin: posteaquam cepisset Nabuchodonosor rex Babylonis Jechoniam, et principes, et cunctos potentes, et populum terræ, ab Jerusalem, et duxit eos vinctos in Babylonem.

verses.text: And they said: Behold we have sent you money, buy with it holocausts, and frankincense, and make meat offerings, and offerings for sin at the altar of the Lord our God:
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt: Ecce misimus ad vos pecunias, de quibus emite holocautomata et thus: et facite manna, et offerte pro peccato, ad aram Domini Dei nostri:

verses.text: And pray ye for the life of Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon, and for the life of Balthasar his son, that their days may be upon earth as the days of heaven:
verses.textLatin: et orate pro vita Nabuchodonosor regis Babylonis, et pro vita Baltassar filii ejus, ut sint dies eorum sicut dies cæli super terram:

verses.text: And that the Lord may give us strength, and enlighten our eyes, that we may live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Balthasar his son, and may serve them many days, and may find favour in their sight.
verses.textLatin: et ut det Dominus virtutem nobis, et illuminet oculos nostros, ut vivamus sub umbra Nabuchodonosor regis Babylonis, et sub umbra Baltassar filii ejus, et serviamus eis multis diebus, et inveniamus gratiam in conspectu eorum.

verses.text: And pray ye for us to the Lord our God: for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his wrath is not turned away from us even to this day.
verses.textLatin: Et pro nobis ipsis orate ad Dominum Deum nostrum, quia peccavimus Domino Deo nostro, et non est aversus furor ejus a nobis usque in hunc diem.

verses.text: And read ye this book, which we have sent to you to be read in the temple of the Lord, on feasts, and proper days.
verses.textLatin: Et legite librum istum quem misimus ad vos recitari in templo Domini, in die solemni et in die opportuno:

verses.text: And you shall say: To the Lord our God belongeth justice, but to us confusion of our face: as it is come to pass at this day to all Juda, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
verses.textLatin: et dicetis: Domino Deo nostro justitia, nobis autem confusio faciei nostræ, sicut est dies hæc omni Juda, et habitantibus in Jerusalem:

verses.text: To our kings, and to our princes, and to our priests, and to our prophets, and to our fathers.
verses.textLatin: regibus nostris, et principibus nostris, et sacerdotibus nostris, et prophetis nostris, et patribus nostris.

verses.text: We have sinned before the Lord our God, and have not believed him, nor put our trust in him:
verses.textLatin: Peccavimus ante Dominum Deum nostrum, et non credidimus, diffidentes in eum:

verses.text: And we were not obedient to him, and we have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his commandments, which he hath given us.
verses.textLatin: et non fuimus subjectibiles illi, et non audivimus vocem Domini Dei nostri, ut ambularemus in mandatis ejus, quæ dedit nobis.

verses.text: From the day that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, even to this day, we were disobedient to the Lord our God: and going astray we turned away from hearing his voice.
verses.textLatin: A die qua eduxit patres nostros de terra Ægypti, usque ad diem hanc, eramus incredibiles ad Dominum Deum nostrum: et dissipati recessimus, ne audiremus vocem ipsius:

verses.text: And many evils have cleaved to us, and the curses which the Lord foretold by Moses his servant: who brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day.
verses.textLatin: et adhæserunt nobis multa mala et maledictiones quæ constituit Dominus Moysi servo suo, qui eduxit patres nostros de terra Ægypti, dare nobis terram fluentem lac et mel, sicut hodierna die.

verses.text: And we have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord our God according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us:
verses.textLatin: Et non audivimus vocem Domini Dei nostri, secundum omnia verba prophetarum quos misit ad nos:

verses.text: And we have gone away every man after the inclinations of his own wicked heart, to serve strange gods, and to do evil in the sight of the Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: et abivimus unusquisque in sensum cordis nostri maligni, operari diis alienis, facientes mala ante oculos Domini Dei nostri.

verses.text: Wherefore  the Lord our God hath made good his word, that he spoke to us, and to our judges that have judged Israel, and to our kings, and to our princes, and to all Israel and Juda:
verses.textLatin: Propter quod statuit Dominus Deus noster verbum suum, quod locutus est ad nos, et ad judices nostros qui judicaverunt Israël, et ad reges nostros, et ad principes nostros, et ad omnem Israël et Juda:

verses.text: That the Lord would bring upon us great evils, such as never happened under heaven, as they have come to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that are written in the law of Moses:
verses.textLatin: ut adduceret Dominus super nos mala magna, quæ non sunt facta sub cælo quemadmodum facta sunt in Jerusalem, secundum quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysi,

verses.text: That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter.
verses.textLatin: et manducaret homo carnes filii sui et carnes filiæ suæ.

verses.text: And he hath delivered them up to be under the hand of all the kings that are round about us, to be a reproach, and desolation among all the people, among whom the Lord hath scattered us.
verses.textLatin: Et dedit eos sub manu regum omnium qui sunt in circuitu nostro, in improperium et in desolationem in omnibus populis in quibus nos dispersit Dominus:

verses.text: And we are brought under, and are not uppermost: because we have sinned against the Lord our God, by not obeying his voice.
verses.textLatin: et facti sumus subtus, et non supra, quia peccavimus Domino Deo nostro, non obaudiendo voci ipsius.

verses.text: To the Lord our God belongeth justice: but to us, and to our fathers confusion of face, as at this day.
verses.textLatin: Domino Deo nostro justitia, nobis autem et patribus nostris confusio faciei, sicut est dies hæc:

verses.text: For the Lord hath pronounced against us all these evils that are come upon us:
verses.textLatin: quia locutus est Dominus super nos omnia mala hæc quæ venerunt super nos:

verses.text: And we have not entreated the face of the Lord our God, that we might return every one of us from our most wicked ways.
verses.textLatin: et non sumus deprecati faciem Domini Dei nostri, ut reverteremur unusquisque nostrum a viis nostris pessimis.

verses.text: And the Lord hath watched over us for evil, and hath brought it upon us: for the Lord is just in all his works which he hath commanded us:
verses.textLatin: Et vigilavit Dominus in malis, et adduxit ea super nos: quia justus est Dominus in omnibus operibus suis quæ mandavit nobis,

verses.text: And we have not hearkened to his voice to walk in the commandments of the Lord which he hath set before us.
verses.textLatin: et non audivimus vocem ipsius ut iremus in præceptis Domini, quæ dedit ante faciem nostram.

verses.text: And now, O Lord God of Israel, who hast brought thy people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand, and with signs, and with wonders, and with thy great power, and with a mighty arm, and hast made thee a name as at this day,
verses.textLatin: Et nunc, Domine Deus Israël, qui eduxisti populum tuum de terra Ægypti in manu valida, et in signis, et in prodigiis, et in virtute tua magna, et in brachio excelso, et fecisti tibi nomen sicut est dies iste:

verses.text: We have sinned, we have done wickedly, we have acted unjustly, O Lord our God, against all thy justices.
verses.textLatin: peccavimus, impie egimus, inique gessimus, Domine Deus noster, in omnibus justitiis tuis.

verses.text: Let thy wrath be turned away from us: for we are left a few among the nations where thou hast scattered us.
verses.textLatin: Avertatur ira tua a nobis, quia derelicti sumus pauci inter gentes ubi dispersisti nos.

verses.text: Hear, O Lord, our prayers, and our petitions, and deliver us for thy own sake: and grant that we may find favour in the sight of them that have led us away:
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Domine, preces nostras et orationes nostras, et educ nos propter te, et da nobis invenire gratiam ante faciem eorum qui nos abduxerunt:

verses.text: That all the earth may know that thou art the Lord our God, and that thy name is called upon Israel, and upon his posterity.
verses.textLatin: ut sciat omnis terra quia tu es Dominus Deus noster, et quia nomen tuum invocatum est super Israël, et super genus ipsius.

verses.text: Look down upon us, O Lord, from thy holy house, and incline thy ear, and hear us.
verses.textLatin: Respice, Domine, de domo sancta tua in nos, et inclina aurem tuam, et exaudi nos.

verses.text: Open thy eyes, and behold: for the dead that are in hell, whose spirit is taken away from their bowels, shall not give glory and justice to the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Aperi oculos tuos et vide: quia non mortui qui sunt in inferno, quorum spiritus acceptus est a visceribus suis, dabunt honorem et justificationem Domino:

verses.text: But the soul that is sorrowful for the greatness of evil she hath done, and goeth bowed down, and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul giveth glory and justice to thee the Lord.
verses.textLatin: sed anima quæ tristis est super magnitudine mali, et incedit curva et infirma, et oculi deficientes, et anima esuriens, dat tibi gloriam et justitiam Domino.

verses.text: For it is not for the justices of our fathers that we pour out our prayers, and beg mercy in thy sight, O Lord our God:
verses.textLatin: Quia non secundum justitias patrum nostrorum nos fundimus preces et petimus misericordiam ante conspectum tuum, Domine Deus noster:

verses.text: But because thou hast sent out thy wrath, and thy indignation upon us, as thou hast spoken by the hand of thy servants the prophets, saying:
verses.textLatin: sed quia misisti iram tuam et furorem tuum super nos, sicut locutus es in manu puerorum tuorum prophetarum, dicens:

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: Bow down your shoulder, and your neck, and serve the king of Babylon: and you shall remain in the land which I have given to your fathers.
verses.textLatin: Sic dicit Dominus: Inclinate humerum vestrum et cervicem vestram, et opera facite regi Babylonis, et sedebitis in terra quam dedi patribus vestris.

verses.text: But if you will not hearken to the voice of the Lord your God, to serve the king of Babylon: I will cause you to depart out of the cities of Juda, and from without Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Quod si non audieritis vocem Domini Dei vestri, operari regi Babyloniæ, defectionem vestram faciam de civitatibus Juda, et a foris Jerusalem,

verses.text: And I will take away from you the voice of mirth, and the voice of joy, and the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, and all the land shall be without any footstep of inhabitants.
verses.textLatin: et auferam a vobis vocem jucunditatis et vocem gaudii, et vocem sponsi et vocem sponsæ, et erit omnis terra sine vestigio ab inhabitantibus eam.

verses.text: And they hearkened not to thy voice, to serve the king of Babylon: and thou hast made good thy words, which thou spokest by the hands of thy servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings, and the bones of our fathers should be removed out of their place:
verses.textLatin: Et non audierunt vocem tuam, ut operarentur regi Babylonis: et statuisti verba tua, quæ locutus es in manibus puerorum tuorum prophetarum, ut transferrentur ossa regum nostrorum et ossa patrum nostrorum de loco suo:

verses.text: And behold they are cast out to the heat of the sun, and to the frost of the night: and they have died in grievous pains, by famine, and by the sword, and in banishment.
verses.textLatin: et ecce projecta sunt in calore solis et in gelu noctis, et mortui sunt in doloribus pessimis, in fame et in gladio, et in emissione.

verses.text: And thou hast made the temple, in which thy name was called upon, as it is at this day, for the iniquity of the house of Israel, and the house of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et posuisti templum in quo invocatum est nomen tuum in ipso sicut hæc dies, propter iniquitatem domus Israël et domus Juda.

verses.text: And thou hast dealt with us, O Lord our God, according to all thy goodness, and according to all that great mercy of thine:
verses.textLatin: Et fecisti in nobis, Domine Deus noster, secundum omnem bonitatem tuam et secundum omnem miserationem tuam illam magnam:

verses.text: As thou spokest by the hand of thy servant Moses, in the day when thou didst command him to write thy law before the children of Israel,
verses.textLatin: sicut locutus es in manu pueri tui Moysi, in die qua præcepisti ei scribere legem tuam coram filiis Israël,

verses.text: Saying: If you will not hear my voice, this great multitude shall be turned into a very small number among the nations, where I will scatter them:
verses.textLatin: dicens: Si non audieritis vocem meam, multitudo hæc magna convertetur in minimam inter gentes, quo ego eos dispergam:

verses.text: For I know that the people will not hear me, for they are a people of a stiff neck: but they shall turn to their heart in the land of their captivity:
verses.textLatin: quia scio quod me non audiet populus: populus est enim dura cervice. Et convertetur ad cor suum in terra captivitatis suæ,

verses.text: And they shall know that I am the Lord their God: and I will give them a heart, and they shall understand: and ears, and they shall hear.
verses.textLatin: et scient quia ego sum Dominus Deus eorum: et dabo eis cor, et intelligent; aures, et audient:

verses.text: And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and shall be mindful of my name.
verses.textLatin: et laudabunt me in terra captivitatis suæ, et memores erunt nominis mei,

verses.text: And they shall turn away themselves from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, that sinned against me.
verses.textLatin: et avertent se a dorso suo duro, et a malignitatibus suis: quia reminiscentur viam patrum suorum, qui peccaverunt in me.

verses.text: And I will bring them back again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be masters thereof: and I will multiply them, and they shall not be diminished.
verses.textLatin: Et revocabo illos in terram quam juravi patribus eorum, Abraham, Isaac, et Jacob: et dominabuntur ejus, et multiplicabo eos, et non minorabuntur:

verses.text: And I will make with them another covenant that shall be everlasting, to be their God, and they shall be my people: and I will no more remove my people, the children of Israel, out of the land that I have given them.
verses.textLatin: et statuam illis testamentum alterum sempiternum, ut sim illis in Deum, et ipsi erunt mihi in populum: et non movebo amplius populum meum, filios Israël, a terra quam dedi illis.

verses.text: And  now, O Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, the soul in anguish, and the troubled spirit crieth to thee:
verses.textLatin: Et nunc, Domine omnipotens, Deus Israël, anima in angustiis, et spiritus anxius clamat ad te.

verses.text: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy, for thou art a merciful God, and have pity on us: for we have sinned before thee.
verses.textLatin: Audi, Domine, et miserere, quia Deus es misericors: et miserere nostri, quia peccavimus ante te:

verses.text: For thou remainest for ever, and shall we perish everlastingly?
verses.textLatin: quia tu sedes in sempiternum, et nos, peribimus in ævum?

verses.text: O Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead of Israel, and of their children, that have sinned before thee, and have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord their God, wherefore evils have cleaved fast to us.
verses.textLatin: Domine omnipotens, Deus Israël, audi nunc orationem mortuorum Israël, et filiorum ipsorum qui peccaverunt ante te, et non audierunt vocem Domini Dei sui, et agglutinata sunt nobis mala.

verses.text: Remember not the iniquities of our fathers, but think upon thy hand, and upon thy name at this time:
verses.textLatin: Noli meminisse iniquitatum patrum nostrorum, sed memento manus tuæ et nominis tui in tempore isto:

verses.text: For thou art the Lord our God, and we will praise thee, O Lord:
verses.textLatin: quia tu es Dominus Deus noster, et laudabimus te, Domine:

verses.text: Because for this end thou hast put thy fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon thy name, and praise thee in our captivity, for we are converted from the iniquity of our fathers, who sinned before thee.
verses.textLatin: quia propter hoc dedisti timorem tuum in cordibus nostris, et ut invocemus nomen tuum, et laudemus te in captivitate nostra, quia convertimur ab iniquitate patrum nostrorum, qui peccaverunt ante te.

verses.text: And behold we are at this day in our captivity, whereby thou hast scattered us to be a reproach, and a curse, and an offence, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, who departed from thee, O Lord our God.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce nos in captivitate nostra sumus hodie, qua nos dispersisti in improperium, et in maledictum, et in peccatum, secundum omnes iniquitates patrum nostrorum, qui recesserunt a te, Domine Deus noster.

verses.text: Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life: give ear, that thou mayst learn wisdom.
verses.textLatin: Audi, Israël, mandata vitæ: auribus percipe, ut scias prudentiam.

verses.text: How happeneth it, O Israel, that thou art in thy enemies’ land?
verses.textLatin: Quid est, Israël, quod in terra inimicorum es,

verses.text: Thou art grown old in a strange country, thou art defiled with the dead: thou art counted with them that go down into hell.
verses.textLatin: inveterasti in terra aliena, coinquinatus es cum mortuis, deputatus es cum descendentibus in infernum?

verses.text: Thou hast forsaken the fountain of wisdom:
verses.textLatin: Dereliquisti fontem sapientiæ:

verses.text: For if thou hadst walked in the way of God, thou hadst surely dwelt in peace for ever.
verses.textLatin: nam si in via Dei ambulasses, habitasses utique in pace sempiterna.

verses.text: Learn where is wisdom, where is strength, where is understanding: that thou mayst know also where is length of days and life, where is the light of the eyes, and peace.
verses.textLatin: Disce ubi sit prudentia, ubi sit virtus, ubi sit intellectus, ut scias simul ubi sit longiturnitas vitæ et victus, ubi sit lumen oculorum, et pax.

verses.text: Who hath found out her place? and who hath gone in to her treasures?
verses.textLatin: Quis invenit locum ejus? et quis intravit in thesauros ejus?

verses.text: Where are the princes of the nations, and they that rule over the beasts that are upon the earth?
verses.textLatin: Ubi sunt principes gentium, et qui dominantur super bestias quæ sunt super terram?

verses.text: That take their diversion with the birds of the air.
verses.textLatin: qui in avibus cæli ludunt,

verses.text: That hoard up silver and gold, wherein men trust, and there is no end of their getting? who work in silver and are solicitous, and their works are unsearchable.
verses.textLatin: qui argentum thesaurizant, et aurum, in quo confidunt homines, et non est finis acquisitionis eorum? qui argentum fabricant, et solliciti sunt, nec est inventio operum illorum?

verses.text: They are cut off, and are gone down to hell, and others are risen up in their place.
verses.textLatin: Exterminati sunt, et ad inferos descenderunt, et alii loco eorum surrexerunt.

verses.text: Young men have seen the light, and dwelt upon the earth: but the way of knowledge they have not known,
verses.textLatin: Juvenes viderunt lumen, et habitaverunt super terram, viam autem disciplinæ ignoraverunt,

verses.text: Nor have they understood the paths thereof, neither have their children received it, it is far from their face.
verses.textLatin: neque intellexerunt semitas ejus, neque filii eorum susceperunt eam: a facie ipsorum longe facta est;

verses.text: It hath not been heard of in the land of Chanaan, neither hath it been seen in Theman.
verses.textLatin: non est audita in terra Chanaan, neque visa est in Theman.

verses.text: The children of Agar also, that search after the wisdom that is of the earth, the merchants of Merrha, and of Theman, and the tellers of fables, and searchers of prudence and understanding: but the way of wisdom they have not known, neither have they remembered her paths.
