verses.textLatin: Filii quoque Agar, qui exquirunt prudentiam quæ de terra est, negotiatores Merrhæ et Theman, et fabulatores, et exquisitores prudentiæ et intelligentiæ: viam autem sapientiæ nescierunt, neque commemorati sunt semitas ejus.

verses.text: O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how vast is the place of his possession!
verses.textLatin: O Israël, quam magna est domus Dei, et ingens locus possessionis ejus!

verses.text: It is great, and hath no end: it is high and immense.
verses.textLatin: magnus est, et non habet finem: excelsus, et immensus.

verses.text: There were the giants, those renowned men that were from the beginning, of great stature, expert in war.
verses.textLatin: Ibi fuerunt gigantes nominati illi, qui ab initio fuerunt, statura magna, scientes bellum.

verses.text: The Lord chose not them, neither did they find the way of knowledge: therefore did they perish.
verses.textLatin: Non hos elegit Dominus, neque viam disciplinæ invenerunt: propterea perierunt,

verses.text: And because they had not wisdom, they perished through their folly.
verses.textLatin: et quoniam non habuerunt sapientiam, interierunt propter suam insipientiam.

verses.text: Who hath gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
verses.textLatin: Quis ascendit in cælum, et accepit eam, et eduxit eam de nubibus?

verses.text: Who hath passed over the sea, and found her, and brought her preferably to chosen gold?
verses.textLatin: Quis transfretavit mare, et invenit illam, et attulit illam super aurum electum?

verses.text: There is none that is able to know her ways, nor that can search out her paths:
verses.textLatin: Non est qui possit scire vias ejus, neque qui exquirat semitas ejus:

verses.text: But he that knoweth all things, knoweth her, and hath found her out with his understanding: he that prepared the earth for evermore, and filled it with cattle and fourfooted beasts:
verses.textLatin: sed qui scit universa novit eam, et adinvenit eam prudentia sua qui præparavit terram in æterno tempore: et replevit eam pecudibus et quadrupedibus

verses.text: He that sendeth forth light, and it goeth: and hath called it, and it obeyeth him with trembling.
verses.textLatin: qui emittit lumen, et vadit, et vocavit illud, et obedit illi in tremore.

verses.text: And the stars have given light in their watches, and rejoiced:
verses.textLatin: Stellæ autem dederunt lumen in custodiis suis, et lætatæ sunt:

verses.text: They were called, and they said: Here we are: and with cheerfulness they have shined forth to him that made them.
verses.textLatin: vocatæ sunt, et dixerunt: Adsumus, et luxerunt ei cum jucunditate, qui fecit illas.

verses.text: This is our God, and there shall no other be accounted of in comparison of him.
verses.textLatin: Hic est Deus noster, et non æstimabitur alius adversus eum.

verses.text: He found out all the way of knowledge, and gave it to Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.
verses.textLatin: Hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ, et tradidit illam Jacob puero suo, et Israël dilecto suo.

verses.text: Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est.

verses.text: This  is the book of the commandments of God, and the law, that is for ever: all they that keep it, shall come to life: but they that have forsaken it, to death.
verses.textLatin: Hic liber mandatorum Dei, et lex quæ est in æternum: omnes qui tenent eam pervenient ad vitam: qui autem dereliquerunt eam, in mortem.

verses.text: Return, O Jacob, and take hold of it, walk in the way by its brightness, in the presence of the light thereof.
verses.textLatin: Convertere, Jacob, et apprehende eam: ambula per viam ad splendorem ejus contra lumen ejus.

verses.text: Give not thy honour to another, nor thy dignity to a strange nation.
verses.textLatin: Ne tradas alteri gloriam tuam, et dignitatem tuam genti alienæ.

verses.text: We are happy, O Israel: because the things that are pleasing to God, are made known to us.
verses.textLatin: Beati sumus, Israël, quia quæ Deo placent manifesta sunt nobis.

verses.text: Be of good comfort, O people of God, the memorial of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Animæquior esto, populus Dei, memorabilis Israël:

verses.text: You have been sold to the Gentiles, not for your destruction: but because you provoked God to wrath, you are delivered to your adversaries.
verses.textLatin: venundati estis gentibus non in perditionem: sed propter quod in ira ad iracundiam provocastis Deum, traditi estis adversariis.

verses.text: For you have provoked him who made you, the eternal God, offering sacrifice to devils, and not to God.
verses.textLatin: Exacerbastis enim eum qui fecit vos, Deum æternum, immolantes dæmoniis, et non Deo.

verses.text: For you have forgotten God, who brought you up, and you have grieved Jerusalem that nursed you.
verses.textLatin: Obliti enim estis Deum qui nutrivit vos, et contristastis nutricem vestram Jerusalem.

verses.text: For she saw the wrath of God coming upon you, and she said: Give ear, all you that dwell near Sion, for God hath brought upon me great mourning:
verses.textLatin: Vidit enim iracundiam a Deo venientem vobis, et dixit: Audite, confines Sion: adduxit enim mihi Deus luctum magnum.

verses.text: For I have seen the captivity of my people, of my sons, and my daughters, which the Eternal hath brought upon them.
verses.textLatin: Vidi enim captivitatem populi mei, filiorum meorum et filiarum, quam superduxit illis Æternus.

verses.text: For I nourished them with joy: but I sent them away with weeping and mourning.
verses.textLatin: Nutrivi enim illos cum jucunditate; dimisi autem illos cum fletu et luctu.

verses.text: Let no man rejoice over me, a widow, and desolate: I am forsaken of many for the sins of my children, because they departed from the law of God.
verses.textLatin: Nemo gaudeat super me viduam et desolatam: a multis derelicta sum propter peccata filiorum meorum, quia declinaverunt a lege Dei.

verses.text: And they have not known his justices, nor walked by the ways of God’s commandments, neither have they entered by the paths of his truth and justice.
verses.textLatin: Justitias autem ipsius nescierunt, nec ambulaverunt per vias mandatorum Dei, neque per semitas veritatis ejus cum justitia ingressi sunt.

verses.text: Let them that dwell about Sion come, and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal hath brought upon them.
verses.textLatin: Veniant confines Sion, et memorentur captivitatem filiorum et filiarum mearum, quam superduxit illis Æternus.

verses.text: For he hath brought a nation upon them from afar, a wicked nation, and of a strange tongue:
verses.textLatin: Adduxit enim super illos gentem de longinquo, gentem improbam, et alterius linguæ,

verses.text: Who have neither reverenced the ancient, nor pitied children, and have carried away the beloved of the widow, and have left me all alone without children.
verses.textLatin: qui non sunt reveriti senem, neque puerorum miserti sunt, et abduxerunt dilectos viduæ, et a filiis unicam desolaverunt.

verses.text: But as for me, what help can I give you?
verses.textLatin: Ego autem, quid possum adjuvare vos?

verses.text: But he that hath brought the evils upon you, he will deliver you out of the hands of your enemies.
verses.textLatin: qui enim adduxit super vos mala, ipse vos eripiet de manibus inimicorum vestrorum.

verses.text: Go your way, my children, go your way: for I am left alone.
verses.textLatin: Ambulate, filii, ambulate: ego enim derelicta sum sola.

verses.text: I have put off the robe of peace, and have put upon me the sackcloth of supplication, and I will cry to the most High in my days.
verses.textLatin: Exui me stola pacis, indui autem me sacco obsecrationis, et clamabo ad Altissimum in diebus meis.

verses.text: Be of good comfort, my children, cry to the Lord, and he will deliver you out of the hand of the princes your enemies.
verses.textLatin: Animæquiores estote, filii; clamate ad Dominum, et eripiet vos de manu principum inimicorum.

verses.text: For my hope is in the Eternal that he will save you: and joy is come upon me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall come to you from our everlasting Saviour.
verses.textLatin: Ego enim speravi in æternum salutem vestram, et venit mihi gaudium a Sancto, super misericordia quæ veniet vobis ab æterno salutari nostro.

verses.text: For I sent you forth with mourning and weeping: but the Lord will bring you back to me with joy and gladness for ever.
verses.textLatin: Emisi enim vos cum luctu et ploratu: reducet autem vos mihi Dominus cum gaudio et jucunditate in sempiternum.

verses.text: For as the neighbours of Sion have now seen your captivity from God: so shall they also shortly see your salvation from God, which shall come upon you with great honour, and everlasting glory.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim viderunt vicinæ Sion captivitatem vestram a Deo, sic videbunt et in celeritate salutem vestram a Deo, quæ superveniet vobis cum honore magno et splendore æterno.

verses.text: My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you: for thy enemy hath persecuted thee, but thou shalt quickly see his destruction: and thou shalt get up upon his neck.
verses.textLatin: Filii, patienter sustinete iram quæ supervenit vobis: persecutus est enim te inimicus tuus: sed cito videbis perditionem ipsius, et super cervices ipsius ascendes.

verses.text: My delicate ones have walked rough ways, for they were taken away as a flock made a prey by the enemies.
verses.textLatin: Delicati mei ambulaverunt vias asperas: ducti sunt enim ut grex direptus ab inimicis.

verses.text: Be of good comfort, my children, and cry to the Lord: for you shall be remembered by him that hath led you away.
verses.textLatin: Animæquiores estote, filii, et proclamate ad Dominum: erit enim memoria vestra ab eo qui duxit vos.

verses.text: For as it was your mind to go astray from God; so when you return again you shall seek him ten times as much.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim fuit sensus vester ut erraretis a Deo, decies tantum iterum convertentes requiretis eum:

verses.text: For he that hath brought evils upon you, shall bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation.
verses.textLatin: qui enim induxit vobis mala, ipse rursum adducet vobis sempiternam jucunditatem cum salute vestra.

verses.text: Be of good heart, O Jerusalem: for he exhorteth thee, that named thee.
verses.textLatin: Animæquior esto, Jerusalem: exhortatur enim te, qui te nominavit.

verses.text: The wicked that have afflicted thee, shall perish: and they that have rejoiced at thy ruin, shall be punished.
verses.textLatin: Nocentes peribunt, qui te vexaverunt: et qui gratulati sunt in tua ruina, punientur.

verses.text: The cities which thy children have served, shall be punished: and she that received thy sons.
verses.textLatin: Civitates quibus servierunt filii tui, punientur, et quæ accepit filios tuos.

verses.text: For as she rejoiced at thy ruin, and was glad of thy fall: so shall she be grieved for her own desolation.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim gavisa est in tua ruina, et lætata est in casu tuo, sic contristabitur in sua desolatione,

verses.text: And the joy of her multitude shall be cut off: and her gladness shall be turned to mourning.
verses.textLatin: et amputabitur exsultatio multitudinis ejus, et gaudimonium ejus erit in luctum.

verses.text: For fire shall come upon her from the Eternal, long to endure, and she shall be inhabited by devils for a great time.
verses.textLatin: Ignis enim superveniet ei ab Æterno in longiturnis diebus, et habitabitur a dæmoniis in multitudine temporis.

verses.text: Look about thee, O Jerusalem, towards the east, and behold the joy that cometh to thee from God.
verses.textLatin: Circumspice, Jerusalem, ad orientem, et vide jucunditatem a Deo tibi venientem.

verses.text: For behold thy children come, whom thou sentest away scattered, they come gathered together from the east even to the west, at the word of the Holy One rejoicing for the honour of God.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim veniunt filii tui, quos dimisisti dispersos: veniunt collecti ab oriente usque ad occidentem, in verbo Sancti, gaudentes in honorem Dei.

verses.text: Put  off, O Jerusalem, the garment of thy mourning, and affliction: and put on the beauty, and honour of that everlasting glory which thou hast from God.
verses.textLatin: Exue te, Jerusalem, stola luctus et vexationis tuæ, et indue te decore, et honore ejus, quæ a Deo tibi est, sempiternæ gloriæ.

verses.text: God will clothe thee with the double garment of justice, and will set a crown on thy head of everlasting honour.
verses.textLatin: Circumdabit te Deus diploide justitiæ, et imponet mitram capiti honoris æterni.

verses.text: For God will shew his brightness in thee, to every one under heaven.
verses.textLatin: Deus enim ostendet splendorem suum in te, omni qui sub cælo est.

verses.text: For thy name shall be named to thee by God for ever: the peace of justice, and honour of piety.
verses.textLatin: Nominabitur enim tibi nomen tuum a Deo in sempiternum: pax justitiæ, et honor pietatis.

verses.text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high: and look about towards the east, and behold thy children gathered together from the rising to the setting sun, by the word of the Holy One rejoicing in the remembrance of God.
verses.textLatin: Exsurge, Jerusalem, et sta in excelso: et circumspice ad orientem, et vide collectos filios tuos ab oriente sole usque ad occidentem, in verbo Sancti, gaudentes Dei memoria.

verses.text: For they went out from thee on foot, led by the enemies: but the Lord will bring them to thee exalted with honour as children of the kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Exierunt enim abs te pedibus ducti ab inimicis: adducet autem illos Dominus ad te portatos in honore sicut filios regni:

verses.text: For God hath appointed to bring down every high mountain, and the everlasting rocks, and to fill up the valleys to make them even with the ground: that Israel may walk diligently to the honour of God.
verses.textLatin: constituit enim Deus humiliare omnem montem excelsum et rupes perennes, et convalles replere in æqualitatem terræ, ut ambulet Israël diligenter in honorem Dei.

verses.text: Moreover the woods, and every sweetsmelling tree have overshadowed Israel by the commandment of God.
verses.textLatin: Obumbraverunt autem et silvæ, et omne lignum suavitatis Israël ex mandato Dei.

verses.text: For God will bring Israel with joy in the light of his majesty, with mercy, and justice, that cometh from him.
verses.textLatin: Adducet enim Deus Israël cum jucunditate in lumine majestatis suæ, cum misericordia et justitia quæ est ex ipso.

verses.text: For  the sins that you have committed before God, you shall be carried away captives into Babylon by Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon.
verses.textLatin: Propter peccata quæ peccastis ante Deum, abducemini in Babyloniam captivi a Nabuchodonosor rege Babylonis.

verses.text: And when you are come into Babylon, you shall be there many years, and for a long time, even to seven generations: and after that I will bring you away from thence with peace.
verses.textLatin: Ingressi itaque in Babylonem, eritis ibi annis plurimis, et temporibus longis, usque ad generationes septem: post hoc autem educam vos inde cum pace.

verses.text: But now, you shall see in Babylon gods of gold, and of silver, and of stone, and of wood borne upon shoulders, causing fear to the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Nunc autem videbitis in Babylonia deos aureos et argenteos, et lapideos et ligneos, in humeris portari, ostentantes metum gentibus.

verses.text: Beware therefore that you imitate not the doings of others, and be afraid, and the fear of them should seize upon you.
verses.textLatin: Videte ergo ne et vos similes efficiamini factis alienis, et metuatis, et metus vos capiat in ipsis.

verses.text: But when you see the multitude behind, and before, adoring them, say you in your hearts: Thou oughtest to be adored, O Lord.
verses.textLatin: Visa itaque turba de retro et ab ante, adorantes dicite in cordibus vestris: Te oportet adorari, Domine.

verses.text: For my angel is with you: And I myself will demand an account of your souls.
verses.textLatin: Angelus enim meus vobiscum est: ipse autem exquiram animas vestras.

verses.text: For their tongue that is polished by the craftsman, and themselves laid over with gold and silver, are false things, and they cannot speak.
verses.textLatin: Nam lingua ipsorum polita a fabro; ipsa etiam inaurata et inargentata: falsa sunt, et non possunt loqui.

verses.text: And as if it were for a maiden that loveth to go gay: so do they take gold and make them up.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut virgini amanti ornamenta, ita accepto auro fabricati sunt.

verses.text: Their gods have golden crowns upon their heads: whereof the priests secretly convey away from them gold, and silver, and bestow it on themselves.
verses.textLatin: Coronas certe aureas habent super capita sua dii illorum: unde subtrahunt sacerdotes ab eis aurum et argentum, et erogant illud in semetipsos.

verses.text: Yea and they give thereof to prostitutes, and they dress out harlots: and again when they receive it of the harlots, they adorn their gods.
verses.textLatin: Dant autem et ex ipso prostitutis, et meretrices ornant: et iterum cum receperint illud a meretricibus, ornant deos suos.

verses.text: And these gods cannot defend themselves from the rust, and the moth.
verses.textLatin: Hi autem non liberantur ab ærugine et tinea.

verses.text: But when they have covered them with a purple garment, they wipe their face because of the dust of the house, which is very much among them.
verses.textLatin: Opertis autem illis veste purpurea, extergunt faciem ipsorum propter pulverem domus qui est plurimus inter eos.

verses.text: This holdeth a sceptre as a man, as a judge of the country, but cannot put to death one that offendeth him.
verses.textLatin: Sceptrum autem habet ut homo, sicut judex regionis, qui in se peccantem non interficit.

verses.text: And this hath in his hand a sword, or an axe, but cannot save himself from war, or from robbers, whereby be it known to you, that they are not gods.
verses.textLatin: Habet etiam in manu gladium et securim, se autem de bello et a latronibus non liberat. Unde vobis notum sit quia non sunt dii:

verses.text: Therefore fear them not. For as a vessel that a man uses when it is broken becometh useless, even so are their gods:
verses.textLatin: non ergo timueritis eos. Sicut enim vas hominis confractum inutile efficitur, tales sunt et dii illorum.

verses.text: When they are placed in the house, their eyes are full of dust by the feet of them that go in.
verses.textLatin: Constitutis illis in domo, oculi eorum pleni sunt pulvere a pedibus introëuntium.

verses.text: And as the gates are made sure on every side upon one that hath offended the king, or like a dead man carried to the grave, so do the priests secure the doors with bars and locks, lest they be stripped by thieves.
verses.textLatin: Et sicut alicui qui regem offendit circumseptæ sunt januæ, aut sicut ad sepulchrum adductum mortuum: ita tutantur sacerdotes ostia clausuris et seris, ne a latronibus expolientur.

verses.text: They light candles to them, and in great number, of which they cannot see one: but they are like beams in the house.
verses.textLatin: Lucernas accendunt illis, et quidem multas, ex quibus nullam videre possunt: sunt autem sicut trabes in domo.

verses.text: And they say that the creeping things which are of the earth, gnaw their hearts, while they eat them and their garments, and they feel it not.
verses.textLatin: Corda vero eorum dicunt elingere serpentes qui de terra sunt, dum comedunt eos, et vestimentum ipsorum, et non sentiunt.

verses.text: Their faces are black with the smoke that is made in the house.
verses.textLatin: Nigræ fiunt facies eorum a fumo qui in domo fit.

verses.text: Owls, and swallows, and other birds fly upon their bodies, and upon their heads, and cats in like manner.
verses.textLatin: Supra corpus eorum et supra caput eorum volant noctuæ, et hirundines, et aves etiam, similiter et cattæ.

verses.text: Whereby you may know that they are no gods. Therefore fear them not.
verses.textLatin: Unde sciatis quia non sunt dii: ne ergo timueritis eos.

verses.text: The gold also which they have, is for shew, but except a man wipe off the rust, they will not shine: for neither when they were molten, did they feel it.
verses.textLatin: Aurum etiam quod habent ad speciem est: nisi aliquis exterserit æruginem, non fulgebunt: neque enim dum conflarentur, sentiebant.

verses.text: Men buy them at a high price, whereas there is no breath in them.
verses.textLatin: Ex omni pretio empta sunt, in quibus spiritus non inest ipsis.

verses.text: And having not the use of feet they are carried upon shoulders, declaring to men how vile they are. Be they confounded also that worship them.
verses.textLatin: Sine pedibus, in humeris portantur, ostentantes ignobilitatem suam hominibus: confundantur etiam qui colunt ea.

verses.text: Therefore if they fall to the ground, they rise not up again of themselves, nor if a man set them upright, will they stand by themselves, but their gifts shall be set before them, as to the dead.
verses.textLatin: Propterea si ceciderint in terram, a semetipsis non consurgunt: neque si quis eum statuerit rectum, per semetipsum stabit: sed sicut mortuis munera eorum illis apponentur.

verses.text: The things that are sacrificed to them, their priests sell and abuse: in like manner also their wives take part of them, but give nothing of it either to the sick, or to the poor.
verses.textLatin: Hostias illorum vendunt sacerdotes ipsorum, et abutuntur: similiter et mulieres eorum decerpentes, neque infirmo, neque mendicanti, aliquid impertiunt.

verses.text: The childbearing and menstruous women touch their sacrifices: knowing therefore by these things that they are not gods, fear them not.
verses.textLatin: De sacrificiis eorum fœtæ et menstruatæ contingunt. Sciens itaque ex his quia non sunt dii, ne timeatis eos.

verses.text: For how can they be called gods? because women set offerings before the gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood:
verses.textLatin: Unde enim vocantur dii? quia mulieres apponunt diis argenteis, et aureis, et ligneis:

verses.text: And priests sit in their temples, having their garments rent, and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing upon their heads.
verses.textLatin: et in domibus eorum sacerdotes sedent habentes tunicas scissas, et capita et barbam rasam, quorum capita nuda sunt.

verses.text: And they roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead.
verses.textLatin: Rugiunt autem clamantes contra deos suos sicut in cœna mortui.

verses.text: The priests take away their garments, and clothe their wives and their children.
verses.textLatin: Vestimenta eorum auferunt sacerdotes, et vestiunt uxores suas et filios suos.

verses.text: And whether it be evil that one doth unto them, or good, they are not able to recompense it: neither can they set up a king nor put him down:
verses.textLatin: Neque si quid mali patiuntur ab aliquo, neque si quid boni, poterunt retribuere: neque regem constituere possunt, neque auferre.

verses.text: In like manner they can neither give riches, nor requite evil. If a man make a vow to them, and perform it not, they cannot require it.
verses.textLatin: Similiter neque dare divitias possunt, neque malum retribuere. Si quis illis votum voverit et non reddiderit, neque hoc requirunt.

verses.text: They cannot deliver a man from death nor save the weak from the mighty.
verses.textLatin: Hominem a morte non liberant, neque infirmum a potentiori eripiunt.

verses.text: They cannot restore the blind man to his sight: nor deliver a man from distress.
verses.textLatin: Hominem cæcum ad visum non restituunt; de necessitate hominem non liberabunt.

verses.text: They shall not pity the widow, nor do good to the fatherless.
verses.textLatin: Viduæ non miserebuntur, neque orphanis benefacient.

verses.text: Their gods, of wood, and of stone, and of gold, and of silver, are like the stones that are hewn out of the mountains: and they that worship them shall be confounded.
verses.textLatin: Lapidibus de monte similes sunt dii illorum, lignei, et lapidei, et aurei, et argentei: qui autem colunt ea, confundentur.

verses.text: How then is it to be supposed, or to be said, that they are gods?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo ergo æstimandum est aut dicendum illos esse deos?

verses.text: Even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them: who when they hear of one dumb that cannot speak, they present him to Bel, entreating him, that he may speak,
verses.textLatin: Adhuc enim ipsis Chaldæis non honorantibus ea: qui cum audierint mutum non posse loqui, offerunt illud ad Bel, postulantes ab eo loqui:

verses.text: As though they could be sensible that have no motion themselves: and they, when they shall perceive this, will leave them: for their gods themselves have no sense.
verses.textLatin: quasi possint sentire qui non habent motum! Et ipsi, cum intellexerint, relinquent ea: sensum enim non habent ipsi dii illorum.

verses.text: The women also with cords about them, sit in the ways, burning olive stones.
verses.textLatin: Mulieres autem circumdatæ funibus in viis sedent, succendentes ossa olivarum:

verses.text: And when any one of them, drawn away by some passenger, lieth with him, she upbraideth her neighbour, that she was not thought as worthy as herself, nor her cord broken.
verses.textLatin: cum autem aliqua ex ipsis, attracta ab aliquo transeunte, dormierit cum eo, proximæ suæ exprobrat quod ea non sit digna habita, sicut ipsa, neque funis ejus diruptus sit.

verses.text: But all things that are done about them, are false: how is it then to be thought, or to be said, that they are gods?
verses.textLatin: Omnia autem quæ illi fiunt, falsa sunt: quomodo æstimandum aut dicendum est illos esse deos?

verses.text: And they are made by workmen, and by goldsmiths. They shall be nothing else but what the priests will have them to be.
verses.textLatin: A fabris autem et ab aurificibus facta sunt: nihil aliud erunt, nisi id quod volunt esse sacerdotes.

verses.text: For the artificers themselves that make them, are of no long continuance. Can those things then that are made by them be gods?
verses.textLatin: Artifices etiam ipsi, qui ea faciunt, non sunt multi temporis: numquid ergo possunt ea, quæ fabricata sunt ab ipsis, esse dii?

verses.text: But they have left false things and reproach to them that come after.
verses.textLatin: Reliquerunt autem falsa et opprobrium postea futuris.

verses.text: For when war cometh upon them, or evils, the priests consult with themselves where they may hide themselves with them.
verses.textLatin: Nam cum supervenerit illis prælium et mala, cogitant sacerdotes apud se ubi se abscondant cum illis.

verses.text: How then can they be thought to be gods, that can neither deliver themselves from war, nor save themselves from evils?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo ergo sentiri debeant quoniam dii sunt, qui nec de bello se liberant, neque de malis se eripiunt?

verses.text: For seeing they are but of wood, and laid over with gold, and with silver, it shall be known hereafter that they are false things, by all nations and kings: and it shall be manifest that they are no gods, but the work of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God in them.
verses.textLatin: Nam cum sint lignea, inaurata et inargentata, scietur postea quia falsa sunt ab universis gentibus et regibus: quæ manifesta sunt quia non sunt dii, sed opera manuum hominum, et nullum Dei opus cum illis.

verses.text: Whence therefore is it known that they are not gods, but the work of men’s hands, and no work of God is in them?
verses.textLatin: Unde ergo notum est quia non sunt dii, sed opera manuum hominum, et nullum Dei opus in ipsis est.

verses.text: They cannot set up a king over the land, nor give rain to men.
verses.textLatin: Regem regioni non suscitant, neque pluviam hominibus dabunt.

verses.text: They determine no causes, nor deliver countries from oppression; because they can do nothing, and are as daws between heaven and earth.
verses.textLatin: Judicium quoque non discernent, neque regiones liberabunt ab injuria, quia nihil possunt, sicut corniculæ inter medium cæli et terræ.

verses.text: For when fire shall fall upon the house of these gods of wood, and of silver, and of gold, their priests indeed will flee away, and be saved: but they themselves shall be burnt in the midst like beams.
verses.textLatin: Etenim cum inciderit ignis in domum deorum ligneorum, argenteorum et aureorum, sacerdotes quidem ipsorum fugient, et liberabuntur: ipsi vero sicut trabes in medio comburentur.

verses.text: And they cannot withstand a king and war. How then can it be supposed, or admitted that they are gods?
verses.textLatin: Regi autem et bello non resistent. Quomodo ergo æstimandum est aut recipiendum quia dii sunt?

verses.text: Neither are these gods of wood, and of stone, and laid over with gold, and with silver, able to deliver themselves from thieves or robbers: they that are stronger than them
verses.textLatin: Non a furibus, neque a latronibus se liberabunt dii lignei, et lapidei, et inaurati, et inargentati: quibus hi qui fortiores sunt,

verses.text: Shall take from them the gold, and silver, and the raiment wherewith they are clothed, and shall go their way, neither shall they help themselves.
verses.textLatin: aurum et argentum, et vestimentum quo operti sunt, auferent illis, et abibunt, nec sibi auxilium ferent.

verses.text: Therefore it is better to be a king that sheweth his power: or else a profitable vessel in the house, with which the owner thereof will be well satisfied: or a door in the house, to keep things safe that are therein, than such false gods.
verses.textLatin: Itaque melius est esse regem ostentantem virtutem suam, aut vas in domo utile, in quo gloriabitur qui possidet illud, vel ostium in domo, quod custodit quæ in ipsa sunt, quam falsi dii.

verses.text: The sun, and the moon, and the stars being bright, and sent forth for profitable uses, are obedient.
verses.textLatin: Sol quidem et luna ac sidera, cum sint splendida et emissa ad utilitates, obaudiunt:

verses.text: In like manner the lightning, when it breaketh forth, is easy to be seen: and after the same manner the wind bloweth in every country.
verses.textLatin: similiter et fulgur cum apparuerit, perspicuum est: idipsum autem et spiritus in omni regione spirat:

verses.text: And the clouds when God commandeth them to go over the whole world, do that which is commanded them.
verses.textLatin: et nubes, quibus cum imperatum fuerit a Deo perambulare universum orbem, perficiunt quod imperatum est eis:

verses.text: The fire also being sent from above to consume mountains and woods, doth as it is commanded. But these neither in shew, nor in power are like to any one of them.
verses.textLatin: ignis etiam missus desuper, ut consumat montes et silvas, facit quod præceptum est ei: hæc autem neque speciebus, neque virtutibus, uni eorum similia sunt.

verses.text: Wherefore it is neither to be thought, nor to be said, that they are gods: since they are neither able to judge causes, nor to do any good to men.
verses.textLatin: Unde neque existimandum est, neque dicendum illos esse deos, quando non possunt neque judicium judicare, neque quidquam facere hominibus.

verses.text: Knowing therefore that they are not gods, fear them not.
verses.textLatin: Scientes itaque quia non sunt dii, ne ergo timueritis eos.

verses.text: For neither can they curse kings, nor bless them.
verses.textLatin: Neque enim regibus maledicent, neque benedicent.

verses.text: Neither do they shew signs in the heaven to the nations, nor shine as the sun, nor give light as the moon.
verses.textLatin: Signa etiam in cælo gentibus non ostendunt: neque ut sol lucebunt, neque illuminabunt ut luna.

verses.text: Beasts are better than they, which can fly under a covert, and help themselves.
verses.textLatin: Bestiæ meliores sunt illis, quæ possunt fugere sub tectum ac prodesse sibi.

verses.text: Therefore there is no manner of appearance that they are gods: so fear them not.
verses.textLatin: Nullo itaque modo nobis est manifestum quia sunt dii: propter quod ne timeatis eos.

verses.text: For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers keepeth nothing, so are their gods of wood, and of silver, and laid over with gold.
verses.textLatin: Nam sicut in cucumerario formido nihil custodit, ita sunt dii illorum lignei, et argentei, et inaurati.

verses.text: They are no better than a white thorn in a garden, upon which every bird sitteth. In like manner also their gods of wood, and laid over with gold, and with silver, are like to a dead body cast forth in the dark.
verses.textLatin: Eodem modo et in horto spina alba, supra quam omnis avis sedet, similiter et mortuo projecto in tenebris, similes sunt dii illorum lignei, et inaurati, et inargentati.

verses.text: By the purple also and the scarlet which are motheaten upon them, you shall know that they are not gods. And they themselves at last are consumed, and shall be a reproach in the country.
verses.textLatin: A purpura quoque et murice, quæ supra illos tineant, scietis itaque quia non sunt dii: ipsi etiam postremo comeduntur, et erunt opprobrium in regione.

verses.text: Better therefore is the just man that hath no idols: for he shall be far from reproach.
verses.textLatin: Melior est homo justus qui non habet simulacra, nam erit longe ab opprobriis.

verses.text: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, when I was in the midst of the captives by the river Chobar, the heavens were opened, and I saw the visions of God.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est in trigesimo anno, in quarto, in quinta mensis, cum essem in medio captivorum juxta fluvium Chobar, aperti sunt cæli, et vidi visiones Dei.

verses.text: On the fifth day of the month, the same was the fifth year of the captivity of king Joachin,
verses.textLatin: In quinta mensis, ipse est annus quintus transmigrationis regis Joachin,

verses.text: The word of the Lord came to Ezechiel the priest the son of Buzi in the land of the Chadeans, by the river Chobar: and the hand of the Lord was there upon him.
verses.textLatin: factum est verbum Domini ad Ezechielem filium Buzi sacerdotem, in terra Chaldæorum, secus flumen Chobar: et facta est super eum ibi manus Domini.

verses.text: And I saw, and behold a whirlwind came out of the north: and a great cloud,and a fire infolding it, and brightness was about it: and out of the midst thereof, that is, out of the midst of the fire, as it were the resemblance of amber:
verses.textLatin: Et vidi, et ecce ventus turbinis veniebat ab aquilone, et nubes magna, et ignis involvens, et splendor in circuitu ejus: et de medio ejus, quasi species electri, id est, de medio ignis:

verses.text: And in the midst thereof the likeness of four living creatures: and this was their appearance: there was the likeness of a man in them.
verses.textLatin: et in medio ejus similitudo quatuor animalium. Et hic aspectus eorum, similitudo hominis in eis.

verses.text: Every one had four faces, and every one four wings.
verses.textLatin: Quatuor facies uni, et quatuor pennæ uni.

verses.text: Their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their foot was like the sole of a calf’s foot, and they sparkled like the appearance of glowing brass.
verses.textLatin: Pedes eorum, pedes recti, et planta pedis eorum quasi planta pedis vituli: et scintillæ quasi aspectus æris candentis.

verses.text: And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides: and they had faces, and wings on the four sides,
verses.textLatin: Et manus hominis sub pennis eorum, in quatuor partibus: et facies et pennas per quatuor partes habebant.

verses.text: And the wings of one were joined to the wings of another. They turned not when they went: but every one went straight forward.
verses.textLatin: Junctæque erant pennæ eorum alterius ad alterum: non revertebantur cum incederent, sed unumquodque ante faciem suam gradiebatur.

verses.text: And as for the likeness of their faces: there was the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side of all the four: and the face of an ox, on the left side of all the four: and the face of an eagle over all the four.
verses.textLatin: Similitudo autem vultus eorum, facies hominis et facies leonis a dextris ipsorum quatuor, facies autem bovis a sinistris ipsorum quatuor, et facies aquilæ desuper ipsorum quatuor.

verses.text: And their faces, and their wings were stretched upward: two wings of every one were joined, and two covered their bodies:
verses.textLatin: Facies eorum et pennæ eorum extentæ desuper: duæ pennæ singulorum jungebantur, et duæ tegebant corpora eorum.

verses.text: And every one of them went straight forward: whither the impulse of the spirit was to go, thither they went: and they turned not when they went.
verses.textLatin: Et unumquodque eorum coram facie sua ambulabat: ubi erat impetus spiritus, illuc gradiebantur, nec revertebantur cum ambularent.

verses.text: And as for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like that of burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. This was the vision running to and fro in the midst of the living creatures, a bright fire, and lightning going forth from the fire.
verses.textLatin: Et similitudo animalium, aspectus eorum quasi carbonum ignis ardentium, et quasi aspectus lampadarum: hæc erat visio discurrens in medio animalium, splendor ignis, et de igne fulgur egrediens.

verses.text: And the living creatures ran and returned like flashes of lightning.
verses.textLatin: Et animalia ibant et revertebantur, in similitudinem fulguris coruscantis.

verses.text: Now as I beheld the living creatures, there appeared upon the earth by the living creatures one wheel with four faces.
verses.textLatin: Cumque aspicerem animalia, apparuit rota una super terram juxta animalia, habens quatuor facies.

verses.text: And the appearance of the wheels, and the work of them was like the appearance of the sea: and the four had all one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the midst of a wheel.
verses.textLatin: Et aspectus rotarum et opus earum quasi visio maris: et una similitudo ipsarum quatuor: et aspectus earum et opera quasi sit rota in medio rotæ.

verses.text: When they went, they went by their four parts: and they turned not when they went.
verses.textLatin: Per quatuor partes earum euntes ibant, et non revertebantur cum ambularent.

verses.text: The wheels had also a size, and a height, and a dreadful appearance: and the whole body was full of eyes round about all the four.
verses.textLatin: Statura quoque erat rotis, et altitudo, et horribilis aspectus: et totum corpus oculis plenum in circuitu ipsarum quatuor.

verses.text: And when the living creatures went, the wheels also went together by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels also were lifted up with them.
verses.textLatin: Cumque ambularent animalia, ambulabant pariter et rotæ juxta ea: et cum elevarentur animalia de terra, elevabantur simul et rotæ.

verses.text: Withersoever the spirit went, thither as the spirit went the wheels also were lifted up withal, and followed it: for the spirit of life was in the wheels.
verses.textLatin: Quocumque ibat spiritus, illuc, eunte spiritu, et rotæ pariter elevabantur sequentes eum: spiritus enim vitæ erat in rotis.

verses.text: When those went these went, and when those stood these stood, and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels also were lifted up together, and followed them: for the spirit of life was in the wheels.
verses.textLatin: Cum euntibus ibant, et cum stantibus stabant: et cum elevatis a terra, pariter elevabantur et rotæ sequentes ea, quia spiritus vitæ erat in rotis.

verses.text: And over the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of the firmament, as the appearance of crystal terrible to behold, and stretched out over their heads above.
verses.textLatin: Et similitudo super capita animalium firmamenti, quasi aspectus crystalli horribilis, et extenti super capita eorum desuper.

verses.text: And under the firmament were their wings straight, the one toward the other, every one with two wings covered his body, and the other was covered in like manner.
verses.textLatin: Sub firmamento autem pennæ eorum rectæ alterius ad alterum: unumquodque duabus alis velabat corpus suum, et alterum similiter velabatur.

verses.text: And I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of many waters, as it were the voice of the most high God: when they walked, it was like the voice of a multitude, like the noise of an army, and when they stood, their wings were let down.
verses.textLatin: Et audiebam sonum alarum, quasi sonum aquarum multarum, quasi sonum sublimis Dei: cum ambularent, quasi sonus erat multitudinis ut sonus castrorum: cumque starent, demittebantur pennæ eorum.

verses.text: For when a voice came from above the firmament, that was over their heads, they stood, and let down their wings.
verses.textLatin: Nam cum fieret vox super firmamentum quod erat super caput eorum, stabant, et submittebant alas suas.

verses.text: And above the firmament that was over their heads, was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of the sapphire stone, and upon the likeness of the throne, was a likeness as of the appearance of a man above upon it.
verses.textLatin: Et super firmamentum quod erat imminens capiti eorum, quasi aspectus lapidis sapphiri similitudo throni: et super similitudinem throni similitudo quasi aspectus hominis desuper.

verses.text: And I saw as it were the resemblance of amber as the appearance of fire within it round about: from his loins and upward, and from his loins downward, I saw as it were the resemblance of fire shining round about.
verses.textLatin: Et vidi quasi speciem electri, velut aspectum ignis, intrinsecus ejus per circuitum: a lumbis ejus et desuper, et a lumbis ejus usque deorsum, vidi quasi speciem ignis splendentis in circuitu,

verses.text: As the appearance of the rainbow when it is in a cloud on a rainy day: this was the appearance of the brightness round about.
verses.textLatin: velut aspectum arcus cum fuerit in nube in die pluviæ. Hic erat aspectus splendoris per gyrum.

verses.text: This  was the vision of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And I saw, and I fell upon my face, and I heard the voice of one that spoke. And he said to me: Son of man, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak to thee.
verses.textLatin: Hæc visio similitudinis gloriæ Domini. Et vidi, et cecidi in faciem meam, et audivi vocem loquentis, et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, sta super pedes tuos, et loquar tecum.

verses.text: And the spirit entered into me after that he spoke to me, and he set me upon my feet: and I heard him speaking to me,
verses.textLatin: Et ingressus est in me spiritus postquam locutus est mihi, et statuit me supra pedes meos: et audivi loquentem ad me,

verses.text: And saying: Son of man, I send thee to the children of Israel, to a rebellious people, that hath revolted from me, they, and their fathers, have transgressed my covenant even unto this day.
verses.textLatin: et dicentem: Fili hominis, mitto ego te ad filios Israël, ad gentes apostatrices quæ recesserunt a me: ipsi et patres eorum prævaricati sunt pactum meum usque ad diem hanc:

verses.text: And they to whom I send thee are children of a hard face, and of an obstinate heart: and thou shalt say to them: Thus saith the Lord God:
verses.textLatin: et filii dura facie et indomabili corde sunt, ad quos ego mitto te. Et dices ad eos: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus:

verses.text: If so be they at least will hear, and if so be they will forbear, for they are a provoking house: and they shall know that there hath been a prophet in the midst of them.
verses.textLatin: si forte vel ipsi audiant, et si forte quiescant, quoniam domus exasperans est: et scient quia propheta fuerit in medio eorum.

verses.text: And thou, O son of man, fear not, neither be thou afraid of their words: for thou art among unbelievers and destroyers, and thou dwellest with scorpions. Fear not their words, neither be thou dismayed at their looks: for they are a provoking house.
verses.textLatin: Tu ergo, fili hominis, ne timeas eos, neque sermones eorum metuas, quoniam increduli et subversores sunt tecum, et cum scorpionibus habitas. Verba eorum ne timeas, et vultus eorum ne formides, quia domus exasperans est.

verses.text: And thou shalt speak my words to them, if perhaps they will hear, and forbear: for they provoke me to anger.
verses.textLatin: Loqueris ergo verba mea ad eos, si forte audiant, et quiescant: quoniam irritatores sunt.

verses.text: But thou, O son of man, hear all that I say to thee: and do not thou provoke me, as that house provoketh me: open thy mouth, and eat what I give thee.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, fili hominis, audi quæcumque loquor ad te, et noli esse exasperans, sicut domus exasperatrix est: aperi os tuum, et comede quæcumque ego do tibi.

verses.text: And I looked, and behold, a hand was sent to me, wherein was a book rolled up: and he spread it before me, and it was written within and without: and there were written in it lamentations, and canticles, and woe.
verses.textLatin: Et vidi: et ecce manus missa ad me, in qua erat involutus liber: et expandit illum coram me, qui erat scriptus intus et foris: et scriptæ erant in eo lamentationes, et carmen, et væ.

verses.text: And he said to me: Son of man, eat all that thou shalt find: eat this book, and go speak to the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, quodcumque inveneris, comede: comede volumen istud, et vadens loquere ad filios Israël.

verses.text: And I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat that book:
verses.textLatin: Et aperui os meum, et cibavit me volumine illo:

verses.text: And he said to me: Son of man, thy belly shall eat, and thy bowels shall be filled with this book, which I give thee. And I did eat it: and it was sweet as honey in my mouth.
verses.textLatin: et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, venter tuus comedet, et viscera tua complebuntur volumine isto quod ego do tibi. Et comedi illud, et factum est in ore meo sicut mel dulce.

verses.text: And he said to me: Son of man, go to the house of Israel, and thou shalt speak my words to them.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, vade ad domum Israël, et loqueris verba mea ad eos.

verses.text: For thou art not sent to a people of a profound speech, and of an unknown tongue, but to the house of Israel:
verses.textLatin: Non enim ad populum profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ tu mitteris ad domum Israël:

verses.text: Nor to many nations of a strange speech, and of an unknown tongue, whose words thou canst not understand: and if thou wert sent to them, they would hearken to thee.
verses.textLatin: neque ad populos multos profundi sermonis et ignotæ linguæ, quorum non possis audire sermones: et si ad illos mittereris, ipsi audirent te:

verses.text: But the house of Israel will not hearken to thee: because they will not hearken to me: for all the house of Israel are of a hard forehead and an obstinate heart.
verses.textLatin: domus autem Israël nolunt audire te, quia nolunt audire me: omnis quippe domus Israël attrita fronte est, et duro corde.

verses.text: Behold I have made thy face stronger than their faces: and thy forehead harder than their foreheads.
verses.textLatin: Ecce dedi faciem tuam valentiorem faciebus eorum, et frontem tuam duriorem frontibus eorum:

verses.text: I have made thy face like an adamant and like flint: fear them not, neither be thou dismayed at their presence: for they are a provoking house.
verses.textLatin: ut adamantem et ut silicem dedi faciem tuam: ne timeas eos, neque metuas a facie eorum, quia domus exasperans est.

verses.text: And he said to me: Son of man, receive in thy heart, and hear with thy ears, all the words that I speak to thee:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, omnes sermones meos quos ego loquor ad te, assume in corde tuo, et auribus tuis audi:

verses.text: And go get thee in to them of the captivity, to the children of thy people, and thou shalt speak to them, and shalt say to them: Thus saith the Lord: If so be they will hear and will forbear.
verses.textLatin: et vade, ingredere ad transmigrationem, ad filios populi tui, et loqueris ad eos: et dices eis: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: si forte audiant et quiescant.

verses.text: And the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great commotion, saying: Blessed be the glory of the Lord, from his place.
verses.textLatin: Et assumpsit me spiritus, et audivi post me vocem commotionis magnæ: Benedicta gloria Domini de loco suo:

verses.text: And the noise of the wings of the living creatures striking one against another, and the noise of the wheels following the living creatures, and the noise of a great commotion.
verses.textLatin: et vocem alarum animalium percutientium alteram ad alteram, et vocem rotarum sequentium animalia, et vocem commotionis magnæ.

verses.text: The spirit also lifted me, and took me up: and I went away in bitterness in the indignation of my spirit: for the hand of the Lord was with me, strengthening me.
verses.textLatin: Spiritus quoque levavit me, et assumpsit me: et abii amarus in indignatione spiritus mei: manus enim Domini erat mecum, confortans me.

verses.text: And I came to them of the captivity, to the heap of new corn, to them that dwelt by the river Chobar, and I sat where they sat: and I remained there seven days mourning in the midst of them.
verses.textLatin: Et veni ad transmigrationem, ad acervum novarum frugum, ad eos qui habitabant juxta flumen Chobar: et sedi ubi illi sedebant, et mansi ibi septem diebus mœrens in medio eorum.

verses.text: And at the end of seven days the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.textLatin: Cum autem pertransissent septem dies, factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens:

verses.text: Son of man, I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel: and thou shalt hear the word out of my mouth, and shalt tell it them from me.
verses.textLatin: Fili hominis, speculatorem dedi te domui Israël, et audies de ore meo verbum, et annuntiabis eis ex me.

verses.text: If, when I say to the wicked, Thou shalt surely die: thou declare it not to him, nor speak to him, that he may be converted from his wicked way, and live: the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at thy hand.
verses.textLatin: Si, dicente me ad impium: Morte morieris, non annuntiaveris ei, neque locutus fueris ut avertatur a via sua impia et vivat, ipse impius in iniquitate sua morietur, sanguinem autem ejus de manu tua requiram.

verses.text: But if thou give warning to the wicked, and he be not converted from his wickedness, and from his evil way: he indeed shall die in his iniquity, but thou hast delivered thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Si autem tu annuntiaveris impio, et ille non fuerit conversus ab impietate sua et a via sua impia, ipse quidem in iniquitate sua morietur: tu autem animam tuam liberasti.

verses.text: Moreover if the just man shall turn away from his justice, and shall commit iniquity: I will lay a stumblingblock before him, he shall die, because thou hast not given him warning: he shall die in his sin, and his justices which he hath done, shall not be remembered: but I will require his blood at thy hand.
verses.textLatin: Sed et si conversus justus a justitia sua fuerit, et fecerit iniquitatem, ponam offendiculum coram eo: ipse morietur quia non annuntiasti ei. In peccato suo morietur, et non erunt in memoria justitiæ ejus quas fecit: sanguinem vero ejus de manu tua requiram.

verses.text: But if thou warn the just man, that the just may not sin, and he doth not sin: living he shall live, because thou hast warned him, and thou hast delivered thy soul.
verses.textLatin: Si autem tu annuntiaveris justo ut non peccet justus, et ille non peccaverit, vivens vivet, quia annuntiasti ei, et tu animam tuam liberasti.

verses.text: And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he said to me: Rise and go forth into the plain, and there I will speak to thee.
verses.textLatin: Et facta est super me manus Domini, et dixit ad me: Surgens egredere in campum, et ibi loquar tecum.

verses.text: And I rose up, and went forth into the plain: and behold the glory of the Lord stood there, like the glory which I saw by the river Chobar: and I fell upon my face.
verses.textLatin: Et surgens egressus sum in campum: et ecce ibi gloria Domini stabat, quasi gloria quam vidi juxta fluvium Chobar: et cecidi in faciem meam.

verses.text: And the spirit entered into me, and set me upon my feet: and he spoke to me, and said to me: Go in; and shut thyself up in the midst of thy house.
verses.textLatin: Et ingressus est in me spiritus, et statuit me super pedes meos, et locutus est mihi, et dixit ad me: Ingredere, et includere in medio domus tuæ.

verses.text: And thou, O son of man, behold they shall put bands upon thee, and they shall bind thee with them: and thou shalt not go forth from the midst of them.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, fili hominis, ecce data sunt super te vincula, et ligabunt te in eis, et non egredieris de medio eorum.

verses.text: And I will make thy tongue stick fast to the roof of thy mouth, and thou shalt be dumb, and not as a man that reproveth: because they are a provoking house.
verses.textLatin: Et linguam tuam adhærere faciam palato tuo, et eris mutus, nec quasi vir objurgans, quia domus exasperans est.

verses.text: But when I shall speak to thee, I will open thy mouth, and thou shalt say to them: Thus saith the Lord God: He that heareth, let him hear: and he that forbeareth, let him forbear: for they are a provoking house.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem locutus fuero tibi, aperiam os tuum, et dices ad eos: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Qui audit, audiat, et qui quiescit, quiescat: quia domus exasperans est.

verses.text: And  thou, O son of man, take thee a tile, and lay it before thee: and draw upon it the plan of the city of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, fili hominis, sume tibi laterem, et pones eum coram te, et describes in eo civitatem Jerusalem.

verses.text: And lay siege against it, and build forts, and cast up a mount, and set a camp against it, and place battering rams round about it.
verses.textLatin: Et ordinabis adversus eam obsidionem, et ædificabis munitiones, et comportabis aggerem, et dabis contra eam castra, et pones arietes in gyro.

verses.text: And take unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city: and set thy face resolutely against it, and it shall be besieged, and thou shalt lay siege against it: it is a sign to the house of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et tu sume tibi sartaginem ferream, et pones eam in murum ferreum inter te et inter civitatem: et obfirmabis faciem tuam ad eam, et erit in obsidionem, et circumdabis eam: signum est domui Israël.

verses.text: And thou shalt sleep upon thy left side, and shalt lay the iniquities of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of the days that thou shalt sleep upon it, and thou shalt take upon thee their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Et tu dormies super latus tuum sinistrum, et pones iniquitates domus Israël super eo, numero dierum quibus dormies super illud: et assumes iniquitatem eorum.

verses.text: And I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days three hundred and ninety days: and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem dedi tibi annos iniquitatis eorum, numero dierum trecentos et nonaginta dies: et portabis iniquitatem domus Israël.

verses.text: And when thou hast accomplished this, thou shalt sleep again upon thy right side, and thou shalt take upon thee the iniquity of the house of Juda forty days: a day for a year, yea, a day for a year I have appointed to thee.
verses.textLatin: Et cum compleveris hæc, dormies super latus tuum dexterum secundo, et assumes iniquitatem domus Juda quadraginta diebus: diem pro anno, diem, inquam, pro anno, dedi tibi.

verses.text: And thou shalt turn thy face to the siege of Jerusalem, and thy arm shall be stretched out: and thou shalt prophesy against it.
verses.textLatin: Et ad obsidionem Jerusalem convertes faciem tuam, et brachium tuum erit extentum: et prophetabis adversus eam.

verses.text: Behold I have encompassed thee with bands: and thou shalt not turn thyself from one side to the other, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege.
verses.textLatin: Ecce circumdedi te vinculis: et non te convertes a latere tuo in latus aliud, donec compleas dies obsidionis tuæ.

verses.text: And take to thee wheat and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and fitches, and put them in one vessel, and make thee bread thereof according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon thy side: three hundred and ninety days shalt thou eat thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, sume tibi frumentum, et hordeum, et fabam, et lentem, et milium, et viciam: et mittes ea in vas unum, et facies tibi panes numero dierum quibus dormies super latus tuum: trecentis et nonaginta diebus comedes illud.

verses.text: And thy meat that thou shalt eat, shall be in weight twenty staters a day: from time to time thou shalt eat it.
verses.textLatin: Cibus autem tuus, quo vesceris, erit in pondere viginti stateres in die: a tempore usque ad tempus comedes illud.

verses.text: And thou shalt drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin: from time to time thou shalt drink it,
verses.textLatin: Et aquam in mensura bibes, sextam partem hin: a tempore usque ad tempus bibes illud.

verses.text: And thou shalt eat it as barley bread baked under the ashes: and thou shalt cover it, in their sight, with the dung that cometh out of a man.
verses.textLatin: Et quasi subcinericium hordeaceum comedes illud, et stercore quod egreditur de homine operies illud in oculis eorum.

verses.text: And the Lord said: So shall the children of Israel eat their bread all filthy among the nations whither I will cast them out.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus: Sic comedent filii Israël panem suum pollutum inter gentes ad quas ejiciam eos. Et dixi:

verses.text: And I said: Ah, ah, ah, O Lord God, behold my soul hath not been defiled, and from my infancy even till now, I have not eaten any thing that died of itself, or was torn by beasts, and no unclean flesh hath entered into my mouth.
verses.textLatin: A, a, a, Domine Deus, ecce anima mea non est polluta: et morticinum, et laceratum a bestiis non comedi ab infantia mea usque nunc, et non est ingressa in os meum omnis caro immunda.

verses.text: And he said to me: Behold I have given thee neat’s dung for man’s dung, and thou shalt make thy bread therewith.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Ecce dedi tibi fimum boum pro stercoribus humanis, et facies panem tuum in eo.

verses.text: And he said to me: Son of man: Behold, I will break in pieces the staff of bread in Jerusalem: and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care: and they shall drink water by measure, and in distress.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Fili hominis, ecce ego conteram baculum panis in Jerusalem, et comedent panem in pondere et in sollicitudine, et aquam in mensura et in angustia bibent,

verses.text: So that when bread and water fail, every man may fall against his brother, and they may pine away in their iniquities.
verses.textLatin: ut deficientibus pane et aqua, corruat unusquisque ad fratrem suum, et contabescant in iniquitatibus suis.

verses.text: And  thou, son of man, take thee a sharp knife that shaveth the hair: and cause it to pass over thy head, and over thy beard: and take thee a balance to weigh in, and divide the hair.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, fili hominis, sume tibi gladium acutum, radentem pilos, et assumes eum et duces per caput tuum et per barbam tuam, et assumes tibi stateram ponderis et divides eos.

verses.text: A third part thou shalt burn with fire in the midst of the city, according to the fulfilling of the days of the siege: and thou shalt take a third part, and cut it in pieces with the knife all round about: and the other third part thou shalt scatter in the wind, and I will draw out the sword after them.
verses.textLatin: Tertiam partem igni combures in medio civitatis, juxta completionem dierum obsidionis, et assumes tertiam partem, et concides gladio in circuitu ejus: tertiam vero aliam disperges in ventum, et gladium nudabo post eos.

verses.text: And thou shalt take thereof a small number: and shalt bind them in the skirt of thy cloak.
verses.textLatin: Et sumes inde parvum numerum, et ligabis eos in summitate pallii tui:

verses.text: And thou shalt take of them again, and shalt cast them in the midst of the fire, and shalt burn them with fire: and out of it shall come forth a fire into all the house of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et ex eis rursum tolles, et projicies eos in medio ignis, et combures eos igni, et ex eo egredietur ignis in omnem domum Israël.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God: This is Jerusalem, I have set her in the midst of the nations, and the countries round about her.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Ista est Jerusalem: in medio gentium posui eam, et in circuitu ejus terras.

verses.text: And she hath despised my judgments, so as to be more wicked than the Gentiles; and my commandments, more than the countries that are round about her: for they have cast off my judgments, and have not walked in my commandments.
verses.textLatin: Et contempsit judicia mea, ut plus esset impia quam gentes, et præcepta mea ultra quam terræ quæ in circuitu ejus sunt: judicia enim mea projecerunt, et in præceptis meis non ambulaverunt.

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Because you have surpassed the Gentiles that are round about you, and have not walked in my commandments, and have not kept my judgments, and have not done according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you:
verses.textLatin: Idcirco hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Quia superastis gentes quæ in circuitu vestro sunt, et in præceptis meis non ambulastis, et judicia mea non fecistis, et juxta judicia gentium quæ in circuitu vestro sunt non estis operati,

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Behold I come against thee, and I myself will execute judgments in the midst of thee in the sight of the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: ideo hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Ecce ego ad te, et ipse ego faciam in medio tui judicia in oculis gentium:

verses.text: And I will do in thee that which I have not done: and the like to which I will do no more, because of all thy abominations.
verses.textLatin: et faciam in te quod non feci, et quibus similia ultra non faciam, propter omnes abominationes tuas.

verses.text: Therefore the fathers shall eat the sons in the midst of thee, and the sons shall eat their fathers: and I will execute judgments in thee, and I will scatter thy whole remnant into every wind.
verses.textLatin: Ideo patres comedent filios in medio tui, et filii comedent patres suos: et faciam in te judicia, et ventilabo universas reliquias tuas in omnem ventum.

verses.text: Therefore as I live, saith the Lord God: Because thou hast violated my sanctuary with all thy offences, and with all thy abominations: I will also break thee in pieces, and my eye shall not spare, and I will not have any pity.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco vivo ego, dicit Dominus Deus, nisi pro eo quod sanctum meum violasti in omnibus offensionibus tuis et in cunctis abominationibus tuis, ego quoque confringam: et non parcet oculus meus, et non miserebor.

verses.text: A third part of thee shall die with the pestilence, and shall be consumed with famine in the midst of thee: and a third part of thee shall fall by the sword round about thee: and a third part of thee will I scatter into every wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
verses.textLatin: Tertia pars tui peste morietur, et fame consumetur in medio tui, et tertia pars tui in gladio cadet in circuitu tuo: tertiam vero partem tuam in omnem ventum dispergam, et gladium evaginabo post eos.

verses.text: And I will accomplish my fury, and will cause my indignation to rest upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the Lord have spoken it in my zeal, when I shall have accomplished my indignation in them.
verses.textLatin: Et complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam in eis, et consolabor: et scient quia ego Dominus locutus sum in zelo meo, cum implevero indignationem meam in eis.

verses.text: And I will make thee desolate, and a reproach among the nations that are round about thee, in the sight of every one that passeth by.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo te in desertum, et in opprobrium gentibus quæ in circuitu tuo sunt, in conspectu omnis prætereuntis:

verses.text: And thou shalt be a reproach, and a scoff, an example, and an astonishment amongst the nations that are round about thee, when I shall have executed judgments in thee in anger, and in indignation, and in wrathful rebukes.
verses.textLatin: et eris opprobrium et blasphemia, exemplum et stupor in gentibus quæ in circuitu tuo sunt, cum fecero in te judicia in furore, et in indignatione, et in increpationibus iræ.

verses.text: I the Lord have spoken it: When I shall send upon them the grievous arrows of famine, which shall bring death, and which I will send to destroy you: and I will gather together famine against you: and I will break among you the staff of bread.
verses.textLatin: Ego Dominus locutus sum: quando misero sagittas famis pessimas in eos, quæ erunt mortiferæ, et quas mittam ut disperdam vos: et famem congregabo super vos, et conteram in vobis baculum panis:

verses.text: And I will send in upon you famine, and evil beasts unto utter destruction: and pestilence, and blood shall pass through thee, and I will bring in the sword upon thee. I the Lord have spoken it.
verses.textLatin: et immittam in vos famem et bestias pessimas, usque ad internecionem: et pestilentia et sanguis transibunt per te, et gladium inducam super te. Ego Dominus locutus sum.

verses.text: And  the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et factus est sermo Domini ad me, dicens:

verses.text: Son of man, set thy face towards the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them.
verses.textLatin: Fili hominis, pone faciem tuam ad montes Israël, et prophetabis ad eos,

verses.text: And say: Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus saith the Lord God to the mountains, and to the hills, and to the rocks, and the valleys: Behold, I will bring upon you the sword, and I will destroy your high places.
verses.textLatin: et dices: Montes Israël, audite verbum Domini Dei. Hæc dicit Dominus Deus montibus et collibus, rupibus et vallibus: Ecce ego inducam super vos gladium, et disperdam excelsa vestra,

verses.text: And I will throw down your altars, and your idols shall be broken in pieces: and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
verses.textLatin: et demoliar aras vestras, et confringentur simulacra vestra, et dejiciam interfectos vestros ante idola vestra:

verses.text: And I will lay the dead carcasses of the children of Israel before your idols: and I will scatter your bones round about your altars,
verses.textLatin: et dabo cadavera filiorum Israël ante faciem simulacrorum vestrorum, et dispergam ossa vestra circum aras vestras:

verses.text: In all your dwelling places. The cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be thrown down, and destroyed, and your altars shall be abolished, and shall be broken in pieces: and your idols shall be no more, and your temples shall be destroyed, and your works shall be defaced.
verses.textLatin: in omnibus habitationibus vestris urbes desertæ erunt, et excelsa demolientur et dissipabuntur: et interibunt aræ vestræ, et confringentur, et cessabunt idola vestra, et conterentur delubra vestra, et delebuntur opera vestra:

verses.text: And the slain shall fall in the midst of you: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et cadet interfectus in medio vestri, et scietis quia ego sum Dominus.

verses.text: And I will leave in you some that shall escape the sword among the nations, when I shall have scattered you through the countries.
verses.textLatin: Et relinquam in vobis eos qui fugerint gladium in gentibus, cum dispersero vos in terris:

verses.text: And they that are saved of you shall remember me amongst the nations to which they are carried captives: because I have broken their heart that was faithless, and revolted from me: and their eyes that went a fornicating after their idols: and they shall be displeased with themselves because of the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.
verses.textLatin: et recordabuntur mei liberati vestri in gentibus ad quas captivi ducti sunt: quia contrivi cor eorum fornicans et recedens a me, et oculos eorum fornicantes post idola sua: et displicebunt sibimet super malis quæ fecerunt in universis abominationibus suis.

verses.text: And they shall know that I the Lord have not spoken in vain that I would do this evil to them.
verses.textLatin: Et scient quia ego Dominus non frustra locutus sum, ut facerem eis malum hoc.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God: Strike with thy hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say: Alas, for all the abominations of the evils of the house of Israel: for they shall fall by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Percute manum tuam et allide pedem tuum, et dic: Heu! ad omnes abominationes malorum domus Israël: quia gladio, fame et peste ruituri sunt.

verses.text: He that is far off shall die of the pestilence: and he that is near, shall fall by the sword: and he that remaineth, and is besieged, shall die by the famine: and I will accomplish my indignation upon them.
verses.textLatin: Qui longe est, peste morietur: qui autem prope, gladio corruet: et qui relictus fuerit et obsessus, fame morietur: et complebo indignationem meam in eis.

verses.text: And you shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain shall be amongst your idols, round about your altars, in every high hill, and on all the tops of mountains, and under every woody tree, and under every thick oak, the place where they burnt sweet smelling frankincense to all their idols.
verses.textLatin: Et scietis quia ego Dominus, cum fuerint interfecti vestri in medio idolorum vestrorum, in circuitu ararum vestrarum, in omni colle excelso, et in cunctis summitatibus montium, et subtus omne lignum nemorosum, et subtus universam quercum frondosam, locum ubi accenderunt thura redolentia universis idolis suis.

verses.text: And I will stretch forth my hand upon them: and I will make the land desolate, and abandoned from the desert of Deblatha in all their dwelling places: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et extendam manum meam super eos: et faciam terram desolatam et destitutam, a deserto Deblatha, in omnibus habitationibus eorum: et scient quia ego Dominus.

verses.text: And  the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et factus est sermo Domini ad me, dicens:

verses.text: And thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God to the land of Israel: The end is come, the end is come upon the four quarters of the land.
verses.textLatin: Et tu, fili hominis, hæc dicit Dominus Deus terræ Israël: Finis venit: venit finis super quatuor plagas terræ.

verses.text: Now is an end come upon thee, and I will send my wrath upon thee, and I will judge thee according to thy ways: and I will set all thy abominations against thee.
verses.textLatin: Nunc finis super te, et immittam furorem meum in te: et judicabo te juxta vias tuas, et ponam contra te omnes abominationes tuas.

verses.text: And my eye shall not spare thee, and I will shew thee no pity: but I will lay thy ways upon thee, and thy abominations shall be in the midst of thee: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et non parcet oculus meus super te, et non miserebor: sed vias tuas ponam super te, et abominationes tuæ in medio tui erunt, et scietis quia ego Dominus.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord God: One affliction, behold an affliction is come.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Afflictio una, afflictio ecce venit.

verses.text: An end is come, the end is come, it hath awaked against thee: behold it is come.
verses.textLatin: Finis venit, venit finis: evigilavit adversum te, ecce venit.

verses.text: Destruction is come upon thee that dwellest in the land: the time is come, the day of slaughter is near, and not of the joy of mountains.
verses.textLatin: Venit contritio super te, qui habitas in terra: venit tempus, prope est dies occisionis, et non gloriæ montium.

verses.text: Now very shortly I will pour out my wrath upon thee, and I will accomplish my anger in thee: and I will judge thee according to thy ways, and I will lay upon thee all thy crimes.
verses.textLatin: Nunc de propinquo effundam iram meam super te, et complebo furorem meum in te: et judicabo te juxta vias tuas, et imponam tibi omnia scelera tua,

verses.text: And my eye shall not spare, neither will I shew mercy: but I will lay thy ways upon thee, and thy abominations shall be in the midst of thee: and you shall know that I am the Lord that strike.
verses.textLatin: et non parcet oculus meus, nec miserebor: sed vias tuas imponam tibi, et abominationes tuæ in medio tui erunt, et scietis quia ego sum Dominus percutiens.

verses.text: Behold the day, behold it is come: destruction is gone forth, the rod hath blossomed, pride hath budded.
verses.textLatin: Ecce dies, ecce venit: egressa est contritio, floruit virga, germinavit superbia,

verses.text: Iniquity is risen up into a rod of impiety: nothing of them shall remain, nor of their people, nor of the noise of them: and there shall be no rest among them.
verses.textLatin: iniquitas surrexit in virga impietatis: non ex eis, et non ex populo, neque ex sonitu eorum: et non erit requies in eis.

verses.text: The time is come, the day is at hand: let not the buyer rejoice: nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the people thereof.
verses.textLatin: Venit tempus, appropinquavit dies: qui emit, non lætetur, et qui vendit, non lugeat: quia ira super omnem populum ejus.

verses.text: For the seller shall not return to that which he hath sold, although their life be yet among the living. For the vision which regardeth all the multitude thereof, shall not go back: neither shall man be strengthened in the iniquity of his life.
verses.textLatin: Quia qui vendit, ad id quod vendidit non revertetur: et adhuc in viventibus vita eorum: visio enim ad omnem multitudinem ejus non regredietur, et vir in iniquitate vitæ suæ non confortabitur.

verses.text: Blow the trumpet, let all be made ready, yet there is none to go to the battle: for my wrath shall be upon all the people thereof.
verses.textLatin: Canite tuba, præparentur omnes: et non est qui vadat ad prælium: ira enim mea super universum populum ejus.

verses.text: The sword without: and the pestilence, and the famine within: he that is in the field shall die by the sword: and they that are in the city, shall be devoured by the pestilence, and the famine.
verses.textLatin: Gladium foris, et pestis et fames intrinsecus: qui in agro est, gladio morietur, et qui in civitate, pestilentia et fame devorabuntur.

verses.text: And such of them as shall flee shall escape: and they shall be in the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them trembling, every one for his iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Et salvabuntur qui fugerint ex eis: et erunt in montibus quasi columbæ convallium omnes trepidi, unusquisque in iniquitate sua.

verses.text: All hands shall be made feeble, and all knees shall run with water.
verses.textLatin: Omnes manus dissolventur, et omnia genua fluent aquis.

verses.text: And they shall gird themselves with haircloth, and fear shall cover them,and shame shall be upon every face, and baldness upon all their heads.
verses.textLatin: Et accingent se ciliciis, et operiet eos formido: et in omni facie confusio, et in universis capitibus eorum calvitium.

verses.text: Their silver shall be cast forth, and their gold shall become a dunghill. Their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord. They shall not satisfy their soul, and their bellies shall not be filled: because it hath been the stumblingblock of their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Argentum eorum foras projicietur, et aurum eorum in sterquilinium erit: argentum eorum et aurum eorum non valebit liberare eos in die furoris Domini: animam suam non saturabunt, et ventres eorum non implebuntur, quia scandalum iniquitatis eorum factum est.

verses.text: And they have turned the ornament of their jewels into pride, and have made of it the images of their abominations, and idols: therefore I have made it an uncleanness to them.
verses.textLatin: Et ornamentum monilium suorum in superbiam posuerunt, et imagines abominationum suarum et simulacrorum fecerunt ex eo: propter hoc dedi eis illud in immunditiam.

verses.text: And I will give it into the hands of strangers for spoil, and to the wicked of the earth for a prey, and they shall defile it.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo illud in manus alienorum ad diripiendum, et impiis terræ in prædam, et contaminabunt illud.

verses.text: And I will turn away my face from them, and they shall violate my secret place: and robbers shall enter into it, and defile it.
verses.textLatin: Et avertam faciem meam ab eis, et violabunt arcanum meum: et introibunt in illud emissarii, et contaminabunt illud.

verses.text: Make a shutting up: for the land is full of the judgment of blood, and the city is full of iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Fac conclusionem, quoniam terra plena est judicio sanguinum, et civitas plena iniquitate.

verses.text: And I will bring the worst of the nations, and they shall possess their houses: and I will make the pride of the mighty to cease, and they shall possess their sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Et adducam pessimos de gentibus, et possidebunt domos eorum: et quiescere faciam superbiam potentium, et possidebunt sanctuaria eorum.

verses.text: When distress cometh upon them, they will seek for peace and there shall be none.
verses.textLatin: Angustia superveniente, requirent pacem, et non erit.

verses.text: Trouble shall come upon trouble, and rumour upon rumour, and they shall seek a vision of the prophet, and the law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the ancients.
verses.textLatin: Conturbatio super conturbationem veniet, et auditus super auditum: et quærent visionem de propheta, et lex peribit a sacerdote, et consilium a senioribus.

verses.text: The king shall mourn, and the prince shall be clothed with sorrow, and the hands of the people of the land shall be troubled. I will do to them according to their way, and will judge them according to their judgments: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
