verses.text: We have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly, and have revolted: and we have gone aside from thy commandments, and thy judgments.
verses.textLatin: peccavimus, iniquitatem fecimus, impie egimus, et recessimus: et declinavimus a mandatis tuis ac judiciis.

verses.text: We have not hearkened to thy servants the prophets, that have spoken in thy name to our kings, to our princes, to our fathers, and to all the people of the land.
verses.textLatin: Non obedivimus servis tuis prophetis, qui locuti sunt in nomine tuo regibus nostris, principibus nostris, patribus nostris, omnique populo terræ.

verses.text: To thee, O Lord, justice: but to us confusion of face, as at this day to the men of Juda, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, to them that are near, and to them that are far off in all the countries whither thou hast driven them, for their iniquities by which they have sinned against thee.
verses.textLatin: Tibi, Domine, justitia: nobis autem confusio faciei, sicut est hodie viro Juda, et habitatoribus Jerusalem, et omni Israël, his qui prope sunt, et his qui procul in universis terris, ad quas ejecisti eos propter iniquitates eorum, in quibus peccaverunt in te.

verses.text: O Lord, to us belongeth confusion of face, to our princes, and to our fathers that have sinned.
verses.textLatin: Domine, nobis confusio faciei, regibus nostris, principibus nostris, et patribus nostris, qui peccaverunt.

verses.text: But to thee, the Lord our God, mercy and forgiveness, for we have departed from thee:
verses.textLatin: Tibi autem Domino Deo nostro misericordia et propitiatio, quia recessimus a te,

verses.text: And we have not hearkened to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his law, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.
verses.textLatin: et non audivimus vocem Domini Dei nostri ut ambularemus in lege ejus, quam posuit nobis per servos suos prophetas.

verses.text: And all Israel have transgressed thy law, and have turned away from hearing thy voice, and the malediction, and the curse, which is written in the book of Moses the servant of God, is fallen upon us, because we have sinned against him.
verses.textLatin: Et omnis Israël prævaricati sunt legem tuam, et declinaverunt ne audirent vocem tuam: et stillavit super nos maledictio et detestatio quæ scripta est in libro Moysi servi Dei, quia peccavimus ei.

verses.text: And he hath confirmed his words which he spoke against us, and against our princes that judged us, that he would bring in upon us a great evil, such as never was under all the heaven, according to that which hath been done in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et statuit sermones suos, quos locutus est super nos et super principes nostros, qui judicaverunt nos, ut superinduceret in nos magnum malum, quale numquam fuit sub omni cælo, secundum quod factum est in Jerusalem.

verses.text: As it is written in the law of Moses, all this evil is come upon us: and we entreated not thy face, O Lord our God, that we might turn from our iniquities, and think on thy truth.
verses.textLatin: Sicut scriptum est in lege Moysi, omne malum hoc venit super nos: et non rogavimus faciem tuam, Domine Deus noster, ut reverteremur ab iniquitatibus nostris, et cogitaremus veritatem tuam.

verses.text: And the Lord hath watched upon the evil, and hath brought it upon us: the Lord our God is just in all his works which he hath done: for we have not hearkened to his voice.
verses.textLatin: Et vigilavit Dominus super malitiam, et adduxit eam super nos. Justus Dominus Deus noster in omnibus operibus suis, quæ fecit: non enim audivimus vocem ejus.

verses.text: And now, O Lord our God, who hast brought forth thy people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand, and hast made thee a name as at this day: we have sinned, we have committed iniquity,
verses.textLatin: Et nunc Domine Deus noster, qui eduxisti populum tuum de terra Ægypti in manu forti, et fecisti tibi nomen secundum diem hanc: peccavimus, iniquitatem fecimus.

verses.text: O Lord, against all thy justice: let thy wrath and thy indignation be turned away, I beseech thee, from thy city Jerusalem, and from thy holy mountain. For by reason of our sins, and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem, and thy people are a reproach to all that are round about us.
verses.textLatin: Domine, in omnem justitiam tuam avertatur, obsecro, ira tua et furor tuus a civitate tua Jerusalem, et monte sancto tuo. Propter peccata enim nostra, et iniquitates patrum nostrorum, Jerusalem et populus tuus in opprobrium sunt omnibus per circuitum nostrum.

verses.text: Now therefore, O our God, hear the supplication of thy servant, and his prayers: and shew thy face upon thy sanctuary which is desolate, for thy own sake.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo exaudi, Deus noster, orationem servi tui, et preces ejus: et ostende faciem tuam super sanctuarium tuum, quod desertum est propter temetipsum.

verses.text: Incline, O my God, thy ear, and hear: open thy eyes, and see our desolation, and the city upon which thy name is called: for it is not for our justifications that we present our prayers before thy face, but for the multitude of thy tender mercies.
verses.textLatin: Inclina, Deus meus, aurem tuam, et audi: aperi oculos tuos, et vide desolationem nostram, et civitatem super quam invocatum est nomen tuum: neque enim in justificationibus nostris prosternimus preces ante faciem tuam, sed in miserationibus tuis multis.

verses.text: O Lord, hear: O Lord, be appeased: hearken and do: delay not for thy own sake, O my God: because thy name is invocated upon thy city, and upon thy people.
verses.textLatin: Exaudi, Domine; placare Domine: attende et fac: ne moreris propter temetipsum, Deus meus, quia nomen tuum invocatum est super civitatem et super populum tuum.

verses.text: Now while I was yet speaking, and praying, and confessing my sins, and the sins of my people of Israel, and presenting my supplications in the sight of my God, for the holy mountain of my God:
verses.textLatin: Cumque adhuc loquerer, et orarem, et confiterer peccata mea, et peccata populi mei Israël, et prosternerem preces meas in conspectu Dei mei, pro monte sancto Dei mei:

verses.text: As I was yet speaking in prayer, behold the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, flying swiftly touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice.
verses.textLatin: adhuc me loquente in oratione, ecce vir Gabriel, quem videram in visione a principio, cito volans tetigit me in tempore sacrificii vespertini.

verses.text: And he instructed me, and spoke to me, and said: O Daniel, I am now come forth to teach thee, and that thou mightest understand.
verses.textLatin: Et docuit me, et locutus est mihi, dixitque: Daniel, nunc egressus sum ut docerem te, et intelligeres.

verses.text: From the beginning of thy prayers the word came forth: and I am come to shew it to thee, because thou art a man of desires: therefore do thou mark the word, and understand the vision.
verses.textLatin: Ab exordio precum tuarum egressus est sermo: ego autem veni ut indicarem tibi, quia vir desideriorum es: tu ergo animadverte sermonem, et intellige visionem.

verses.text: Seventy weeks are shortened upon thy people, and upon thy holy city, that transgression may be finished, and sin may have an end, and iniquity may be abolished; and everlasting justice may be brought; and vision and prophecy may be fulfilled; and the saint of saints may be anointed.
verses.textLatin: Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum et super urbem sanctam tuam, ut consummetur prævaricatio, et finem accipiat peccatum, et deleatur iniquitas, et adducatur justitia sempiterna, et impleatur visio et prophetia, et ungatur Sanctus sanctorum.

verses.text: Know thou therefore, and take notice: that from the going forth of the word, to build up Jerusalem again, unto Christ the prince, there shall be seven weeks, and sixty-two weeks: and the street shall be built again, and the walls in straitness of times.
verses.textLatin: Scito ergo, et animadverte: ab exitu sermonis, ut iterum ædificetur Jerusalem, usque ad christum ducem, hebdomades septem, et hebdomades sexaginta duæ erunt: et rursum ædificabitur platea, et muri in angustia temporum.

verses.text: And after sixty-two weeks Christ shall be slain: and the people that shall deny him shall not be his. And a people with their leader that shall come, shall destroy the city and the sanctuary: and the end thereof shall be waste, and after the end of the war the appointed desolation.
verses.textLatin: Et post hebdomades sexaginta duas occidetur christus: et non erit ejus populus qui eum negaturus est. Et civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo: et finis ejus vastitas, et post finem belli statuta desolatio.

verses.text: And he shall confirm the covenant with many, in one week: and in the half of the week the victim and the sacrifice shall fail: and there shall be in the temple the abomination of desolation: and the desolation shall continue even to the consummation, and to the end.
verses.textLatin: Confirmabit autem pactum multis hebdomada una: et in dimidio hebdomadis deficiet hostia et sacrificium: et erit in templo abominatio desolationis: et usque ad consummationem et finem perseverabit desolatio.

verses.text: In  the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel surnamed Baltassar, and a true word, and great strength: and he understood the word: for there is need of understanding in a vision.
verses.textLatin: Anno tertio Cyri regis Persarum, verbum revelatum est Danieli cognomento Baltassar, et verbum verum, et fortitudo magna: intellexitque sermonem: intelligentia enim est opus in visione.

verses.text: In those days I Daniel mourned the days of three weeks.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis ego Daniel lugebam trium hebdomadarum diebus:

verses.text: I ate no desirable bread, and neither flesh, nor wine entered into my mouth, neither was I anointed with ointment: till the days of three weeks were accomplished.
verses.textLatin: panem desiderabilem non comedi, et caro et vinum non introierunt in os meum, sed neque unguento unctus sum, donec complerentur trium hebdomadarum dies.

verses.text: And in the four and twentieth day of the first month I was by the great river which is the Tigris.
verses.textLatin: Die autem vigesima et quarta mensis primi, eram juxta fluvium magnum, qui est Tigris.

verses.text: And I lifted up my eyes, and I saw: and behold a man clothed in linen, and his loins were girded with the finest gold:
verses.textLatin: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi: et ecce vir unus vestitus lineis, et renes ejus accincti auro obrizo:

verses.text: And his body was like the chrysolite, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as a burning lamp: and his arms, and all downward even to the feet, like in appearance to glittering brass: and the voice of his word like the voice of a multitude.
verses.textLatin: et corpus ejus quasi chrysolithus, et facies ejus velut species fulguris, et oculi ejus ut lampas ardens: et brachia ejus, et quæ deorsum sunt usque ad pedes, quasi species æris candentis: et vox sermonum ejus ut vox multitudinis.

verses.text: And I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me saw it not: but an exceeding great terror fell upon them, and they fled away, and hid themselves.
verses.textLatin: Vidi autem ego Daniel solus visionem: porro viri qui erant mecum non viderunt, sed terror nimius irruit super eos, et fugerunt in absconditum.

verses.text: And I being left alone saw this great vision: and there remained no strength in me, and the appearance of my countenance was changed in me, and I fainted away, and retained no strength.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem relictus solus vidi visionem grandem hanc: et non remansit in me fortitudo, sed et species mea immutata est in me, et emarcui, nec habui quidquam virium.

verses.text: And I heard the voice of his words: and when I heard, I lay in a consternation, upon my face, and my face was close to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Et audivi vocem sermonum ejus: et audiens jacebam consternatus super faciem meam, et vultus meus hærebat terræ.

verses.text: And behold a hand touched me, and lifted me up upon my knees, and upon the joints of my hands.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce manus tetigit me, et erexit me super genua mea, et super articulos manuum mearum.

verses.text: And he said to me: Daniel, thou man of desires, understand the words that I speak to thee, and stand upright: for I am sent now to thee. And when he had said this word to me, I stood trembling.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Daniel vir desideriorum, intellige verba quæ ego loquor ad te, et sta in gradu tuo: nunc enim sum missus ad te. Cumque dixisset mihi sermonem istum, steti tremens.

verses.text: And he said to me: Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thy heart to understand, to afflict thyself in the sight of thy God, thy words have been heard: and I am come for thy words.
verses.textLatin: Et ait ad me: Noli metuere, Daniel: quia ex die primo, quo posuisti cor tuum ad intelligendum ut te affligeres in conspectu Dei tui, exaudita sunt verba tua: et ego veni propter sermones tuos.

verses.text: But the prince of the kingdom of the Persians resisted me one and twenty days: and behold Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there by the king of the Persians.
verses.textLatin: Princeps autem regni Persarum restitit mihi viginti et uno diebus: et ecce Michaël, unus de principibus primis, venit in adjutorium meum, et ego remansi ibi juxta regem Persarum.

verses.text: But I am come to teach thee what things shall befall thy people in the latter days, for as yet the vision is for days.
verses.textLatin: Veni autem ut docerem te quæ ventura sunt populo tuo in novissimis diebus, quoniam adhuc visio in dies.

verses.text: And when he was speaking such words to me, I cast down my countenance to the ground, and held my peace.
verses.textLatin: Cumque loqueretur mihi hujuscemodi verbis, dejeci vultum meum ad terram, et tacui.

verses.text: And behold, as it were the likeness of a son of man touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spoke, and said to him that stood before me: O my Lord, at the sight of thee my joints are loosed, and no strength hath remained in me.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce quasi similitudo filii hominis tetigit labia mea: et aperiens os meum locutus sum, et dixi ad eum, qui stabat contra me: Domine mi, in visione tua dissolutæ sunt compages meæ, et nihil in me remansit virium.

verses.text: And how can the servant of my lord speak with my lord? for no strength remaineth in me, moreover my breath is stopped.
verses.textLatin: Et quomodo poterit servus domini mei loqui cum domino meo? nihil enim in me remansit virium, sed et halitus meus intercluditur.

verses.text: Therefore he that looked like a man touched me again, and strengthened me.
verses.textLatin: Rursum ergo tetigit me quasi visio hominis, et confortavit me,

verses.text: And he said: Fear not, O man of desires, peace be to thee: take courage and be strong. And when he spoke to me, I grew strong: and I said: Speak, O my lord, for thou hast strengthened me.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Noli timere, vir desideriorum: pax tibi: confortare, et esto robustus. Cumque loqueretur mecum, convalui, et dixi: Loquere, domine mi, quia confortasti me.

verses.text: And he said: Dost thou know wherefore I am come to thee? and now I will return, to fight against the prince of the Persians. When I went forth, there appeared the prince of the Greeks coming.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Numquid scis quare venerim ad te? et nunc revertar ut prælier adversum principem Persarum. Cum ego egrederer, apparuit princeps Græcorum veniens.

verses.text: But I will tell thee what is set down in the scripture of truth: and none is my helper in all these things, but Michael your prince.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen annuntiabo tibi quod expressum est in scriptura veritatis: et nemo est adjutor meus in omnibus his, nisi Michaël princeps vester.

verses.text: And  from the first year of Darius the Mede I stood up that he might be strengthened and confirmed.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem ab anno primo Darii Medi stabam ut confortaretur et roboraretur.

verses.text: And now I will shew thee the truth. Behold there shall stand yet three kings in Persia, and the fourth shall be enriched exceedingly above them all: and when he shall be grown mighty by his riches, he shall stir up all against the kingdom of Greece.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc veritatem annuntiabo tibi. Ecce adhuc tres reges stabunt in Perside, et quartus ditabitur opibus nimiis super omnes: et cum invaluerit divitiis suis, concitabit omnes adversum regnum Græciæ.

verses.text: But there shall rise up a strong king, and shall rule with great power: and he shall do what he pleaseth.
verses.textLatin: Surget vero rex fortis, et dominabitur potestate multa, et faciet quod placuerit ei.

verses.text: And when he shall come to his height, his kingdom shall be broken, and it shall be divided towards the four winds of the heaven: but not to his posterity, nor according to his power with which he ruled. For his kingdom shall be rent in pieces, even for strangers, beside these.
verses.textLatin: Et cum steterit, conteretur regnum ejus, et dividetur in quatuor ventos cæli: sed non in posteros ejus, neque secundum potentiam illius, qua dominatus est: lacerabitur enim regnum ejus etiam in externos, exceptis his.

verses.text: And the king of the south shall be strengthened, and one of his princes shall prevail over him, and he shall rule with great power: for his dominion shall be great.
verses.textLatin: Et confortabitur rex austri: et de principibus ejus prævalebit super eum, et dominabitur ditione: multa enim dominatio ejus.

verses.text: And after the end of years they shall be in league together: and the daughter of the king of the south shall come to the king of the north to make friendship, but she shall not obtain the strength of the arm, neither shall her seed stand: and she shall be given up, and her young men that brought her, and they that strengthened her in these times.
verses.textLatin: Et post finem annorum fœderabuntur: filiaque regis austri veniet ad regem aquilonis facere amicitiam, et non obtinebit fortitudinem brachii, nec stabit semen ejus: et tradetur ipsa, et qui adduxerunt eam adolescentes ejus, et qui confortabant eam in temporibus.

verses.text: And a plant of the bud of her roots shall stand up: and he shall come with an army, and shall enter into the province of the king of the north: and he shall abuse them, and shall prevail.
verses.textLatin: Et stabit de germine radicum ejus plantatio: et veniet cum exercitu, et ingredietur provinciam regis aquilonis: et abutetur eis, et obtinebit.

verses.text: And he shall also carry away captive into Egypt their gods, and their graven things, and their precious vessels of gold and silver: he shall prevail against the king of the north.
verses.textLatin: Insuper et deos eorum, et sculptilia, vasa quoque pretiosa argenti et auri, captiva ducet in Ægyptum: ipse prævalebit adversus regem aquilonis.

verses.text: And the king of the south shall enter into the kingdom, and shall return to his own land.
verses.textLatin: Et intrabit in regnum rex austri, et revertetur ad terram suam.

verses.text: And his sons shall be provoked, and they shall assemble a multitude of great forces: and he shall come with haste like a flood: and he shall return and be stirred up, and he shall join battle with his forces.
verses.textLatin: Filii autem ejus provocabuntur, et congregabunt multitudinem exercituum plurimorum: et veniet properans, et inundans: et revertetur, et concitabitur, et congredietur cum robore ejus.

verses.text: And the king of the south being provoked shall go forth, and shall fight against the king of the north, and shall prepare an exceeding great multitude, and a multitude shall be given into his hands.
verses.textLatin: Et provocatus rex austri egredietur, et pugnabit adversus regem aquilonis, et præparabit multitudinem nimiam, et dabitur multitudo in manu ejus.

verses.text: And he shall take a multitude, and his heart shall be lifted up, and he shall cast down many thousands: but he shall not prevail.
verses.textLatin: Et capiet multitudinem, et exaltabitur cor ejus, et dejiciet multa millia, sed non prævalebit.

verses.text: For the king of the north shall return and shall prepare a multitude much greater than before: and in the end of times and years, he shall come in haste with a great army, and much riches.
verses.textLatin: Convertetur enim rex aquilonis, et præparabit multitudinem multo majorem quam prius: et in fine temporum annorumque veniet properans cum exercitu magno, et opibus nimiis.

verses.text: And in those times many shall rise up against the king of the south, and the children of prevaricators of thy people shall lift up themselves to fulfil the vision, and they shall fall.
verses.textLatin: Et in temporibus illis multi consurgent adversus regem austri: filii quoque prævaricatorum populi tui extollentur ut impleant visionem, et corruent.

verses.text: And the king of the north shall come, and shall cast up a mount, and shall take the best fenced cities: and the arms of the south shall not withstand, and his chosen ones shall rise up to resist, and they shall not have strength.
verses.textLatin: Et venit rex aquilonis, et comportabit aggerem, et capiet urbes munitissimas: et brachia austri non sustinebunt, et consurgent electi ejus ad resistendum, et non erit fortitudo.

verses.text: And he shall come upon him and do according to his pleasure, and there shall be none to stand against his face: and he shall stand in the glorious land, and it shall be consumed by his hand.
verses.textLatin: Et faciet veniens super eum juxta placitum suum, et non erit qui stet contra faciem ejus: et stabit in terra inclyta, et consumetur in manu ejus.

verses.text: And he shall set his face to come to possess all his kingdom, and he shall make upright conditions with him: and he shall give him a daughter of women, to overthrow it: and she shall not stand, neither shall she be for him.
verses.textLatin: Et ponet faciem suam ut veniat ad tenendum universum regnum ejus, et recta faciet cum eo: et filiam feminarum dabit ei, ut evertat illud: et non stabit, nec illius erit.

verses.text: And he shall turn his face to the islands, and shall take many: and he shall cause the prince of his reproach to cease, and his reproach shall be turned upon him.
verses.textLatin: Et convertet faciem suam ad insulas, et capiet multas: et cessare faciet principem opprobrii sui, et opprobrium ejus convertetur in eum.

verses.text: And he shall turn his face to the empire of his own land, and he shall stumble, and fall, and shall not be found.
verses.textLatin: Et convertet faciem suam ad imperium terræ suæ, et impinget, et corruet, et non invenietur.

verses.text: And there shall stand up in his place, one most vile, and unworthy of kingly honour: and in a few days he shall be destroyed, not in rage nor in battle.
verses.textLatin: Et stabit in loco ejus vilissimus, et indignus decore regio: et in paucis diebus conteretur, non in furore, nec in prælio.

verses.text: And there shall stand up in his place one despised, and the kingly honour shall not be given him: and he shall come privately, and shall obtain the kingdom by fraud.
verses.textLatin: Et stabit in loco ejus despectus, et non tribuetur ei honor regius: et veniet clam, et obtinebit regnum in fraudulentia.

verses.text: And the arms of the fighter shall be overcome before his face, and shall be broken; yea also the prince of the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Et brachia pugnantis expugnabuntur a facie ejus, et conterentur: insuper et dux fœderis.

verses.text: And after friendships, he will deal deceitfully with him: and he shall go up, and shall overcome with a small people.
verses.textLatin: Et post amicitias, cum eo faciet dolum: et ascendet, et superabit in modico populo.

verses.text: And he shall enter into rich and plentiful cities: and he shall do that which his fathers never did, nor his fathers’ fathers: he shall scatter their spoils, and their prey, and their riches, and shall forecast devices against the best fenced places: and this until a time.
verses.textLatin: Et abundantes, et uberes urbes ingredietur: et faciet quæ non fecerunt patres ejus, et patres patrum ejus: rapinas, et prædam, et divitias eorum dissipabit, et contra firmissimas cogitationes inibit: et hoc usque ad tempus.

verses.text: And his strength and his heart shall be stirred up against the king of the south with a great army: and the king of the south shall be stirred up to battle with many and very strong succours: and they shall not stand, for they shall form designs against him.
verses.textLatin: Et concitabitur fortitudo ejus, et cor ejus adversum regem austri in exercitu magno: et rex austri provocabitur ad bellum multis auxiliis, et fortibus nimis: et non stabunt, quia inibunt adversus eum consilia.

verses.text: And they that eat bread with him, shall destroy him, and his army shall be overthrown: and many shall fall down slain.
verses.textLatin: Et comedentes panem cum eo, conterent illum, exercitusque ejus opprimetur: et cadent interfecti plurimi.

verses.text: And the heart of the two kings shall be to do evil, and they shall speak lies at one table, and they shall not prosper: because as yet the end is unto another time.
verses.textLatin: Duorum quoque regum cor erit ut malefaciant, et ad mensam unam mendacium loquentur: et non proficient, quia adhuc finis in aliud tempus.

verses.text: And he shall return into his land with much riches: and his heart shall be against the holy covenant, and he shall succeed and shall return into his own land.
verses.textLatin: Et revertetur in terram suam cum opibus multis: et cor ejus adversum testamentum sanctum, et faciet, et revertetur in terram suam.

verses.text: At the time appointed he shall return, and he shall come to the south, but the latter time shall not be like the former.
verses.textLatin: Statuto tempore revertetur, et veniet ad austrum: et non erit priori simile novissimum.

verses.text: And the galleys and the Romans shall come upon him, and he shall be struck, and shall return, and shall have indignation against the covenant of the sanctuary, and he shall succeed: and he shall return and shall devise against them that have forsaken the covenant of the sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Et venient super eum trieres, et Romani: et percutietur, et revertetur, et indignabitur contra testamentum sanctuarii, et faciet: reverteturque, et cogitabit adversum eos qui dereliquerunt testamentum sanctuarii.

verses.text: And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall defile the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the continual sacrifice, and they shall place there the abomination unto desolation.
verses.textLatin: Et brachia ex eo stabunt, et polluent sanctuarium fortitudinis, et auferent juge sacrificium: et dabunt abominationem in desolationem.

verses.text: And such as deal wickedly against the covenant shall deceitfully dissemble: but the people that know their God shall prevail and succeed.
verses.textLatin: Et impii in testamentum simulabunt fraudulenter: populus autem sciens Deum suum, obtinebit, et faciet.

verses.text: And they that are learned among the people shall teach many: and they shall fall by the sword, and by fire, and by captivity, and by spoil for many days.
verses.textLatin: Et docti in populo docebunt plurimos: et ruent in gladio, et in flamma, et in captivitate, et in rapina dierum.

verses.text: And when they shall have fallen they shall be relieved with a small help: and many shall be joined to them deceitfully.
verses.textLatin: Cumque corruerint, sublevabuntur auxilio parvulo: et applicabuntur eis plurimi fraudulenter.

verses.text: And some of the learned shall fall, that they may be tried, and may be chosen, and made white even to the appointed time, because yet there shall be another time.
verses.textLatin: Et de eruditis ruent, ut conflentur, et eligantur, et dealbentur usque ad tempus præfinitum: quia adhuc aliud tempus erit.

verses.text: And the king shall do according to his will, and he shall be lifted up, and shall magnify himself against every god: and he shall speak great things against the God of gods, and shall prosper, till the wrath be accomplished. For the determination is made.
verses.textLatin: Et faciet juxta voluntatem suam rex, et elevabitur, et magnificabitur adversus omnem deum: et adversus Deum deorum loquetur magnifica, et dirigetur, donec compleatur iracundia: perpetrata quippe est definitio.

verses.text: And he shall make no account of the God of his fathers: and he shall follow the lust of women, and he shall not regard any gods: for he shall rise up against all things.
verses.textLatin: Et Deum patrum suorum non reputabit: et erit in concupiscentiis feminarum, nec quemquam deorum curabit, quia adversum universa consurget.

verses.text: But he shall worship the god Maozim in his place: and a god whom his fathers knew not, he shall worship with gold, and silver, and precious stones, and things of great price.
verses.textLatin: Deum autem Maozim in loco suo venerabitur: et deum, quem ignoraverunt patres ejus, colet auro, et argento, et lapide pretioso, rebusque pretiosis.

verses.text: And he shall do this to fortify Maozim with a strange god, whom he hath acknowledged, and he shall increase glory and shall give them power over many, and shall divide the land gratis.
verses.textLatin: Et faciet ut muniat Maozim cum deo alieno, quem cognovit, et multiplicabit gloriam, et dabit eis potestatem in multis, et terram dividet gratuito.

verses.text: And at the time prefixed the king of the south shall fight against him, and the king of the north shall come against him like a tempest, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with a great navy, and he shall enter into the countries, and shall destroy, and pass through.
verses.textLatin: Et in tempore præfinito præliabitur adversus eum rex austri, et quasi tempestas veniet contra illum rex aquilonis in curribus, et in equitibus, et in classe magna, et ingredietur terras, et conteret, et pertransiet.

verses.text: And he shall enter into the glorious land, and many shall fall: and these only shall be saved out of his hand, Edom, and Moab, and the principality of the children of Ammon.
verses.textLatin: Et introibit in terram gloriosam, et multæ corruent: hæ autem solæ salvabuntur de manu ejus, Edom, et Moab, et principium filiorum Ammon.

verses.text: And he shall lay his hand upon the lands: and the land of Egypt shall not escape.
verses.textLatin: Et mittet manum suam in terras: et terra Ægypti non effugiet.

verses.text: And he shall have power over the treasures of gold, and of silver, and all the precious things of Egypt: and he shall pass through Libya, and Ethiopia.
verses.textLatin: Et dominabitur thesaurorum auri, et argenti, et in omnibus pretiosis Ægypti: per Libyam quoque, et Æthiopiam transibit.

verses.text: And tidings out of the east, and out of the north shall trouble him: and he shall come with a great multitude to destroy and slay many.
verses.textLatin: Et fama turbabit eum ab oriente et ab aquilone: et veniet in multitudine magna ut conterat et interficiat plurimos.

verses.text: And he shall fix his tabernacle Apadno between the seas, upon a glorious and holy mountain: and he shall come even to the top thereof, and none shall help him.
verses.textLatin: Et figet tabernaculum suum Apadno inter maria, super montem inclytum et sanctum: et veniet usque ad summitatem ejus, et nemo auxiliabitur ei.

verses.text: But  at that time shall Michael rise up, the great prince, who standeth for the children of thy people: and a time shall come such as never was from the time that nations began even until that time. And at that time shall thy people be saved, every one that shall be found written in the book.
verses.textLatin: In tempore autem illo consurget Michaël princeps magnus, qui stat pro filiis populi tui: et veniet tempus quale non fuit ab eo ex quo gentes esse cœperunt usque ad tempus illud. Et in tempore illo salvabitur populus tuus, omnis qui inventus fuerit scriptus in libro.

verses.text: And many of those that sleep in the dust of the earth, shall awake: some unto life everlasting, and others unto reproach, to see it always.
verses.textLatin: Et multi de his qui dormiunt in terræ pulvere evigilabunt, alii in vitam æternam, et alii in opprobrium ut videant semper.

verses.text: But they that are learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem docti fuerint, fulgebunt quasi splendor firmamenti: et qui ad justitiam erudiunt multos, quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates.

verses.text: But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time appointed: many shall pass over, and knowledge shall be manifold.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem Daniel, claude sermones, et signa librum usque ad tempus statutum: plurimi pertransibunt, et multiplex erit scientia.

verses.text: And I Daniel looked, and behold as it were two others stood: one on this side upon the bank of the river, and another on that side, on the other bank of the river.
verses.textLatin: Et vidi ego Daniel, et ecce quasi duo alii stabant: unus hinc super ripam fluminis, et alius inde ex altera ripa fluminis.

verses.text: And I said to the man that was clothed in linen, that stood upon the waters of the river: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?
verses.textLatin: Et dixi viro qui erat indutus lineis, qui stabat super aquas fluminis: Usquequo finis horum mirabilium?

verses.text: And I heard the man that was clothed in linen, that stood upon the waters of the river: when he had lifted up his right hand, and his left hand to heaven, and had sworn, by him that liveth for ever, that it should be unto a time, and times, and half a time. And when the scattering of the band of the holy people shall be accomplished, all these things shall be finished.
verses.textLatin: Et audivi virum qui indutus erat lineis, qui stabat super aquas fluminis, cum elevasset dexteram et sinistram suam in cælum, et jurasset per viventem in æternum, quia in tempus, et tempora, et dimidium temporis. Et cum completa fuerit dispersio manus populi sancti, complebuntur universa hæc.

verses.text: And I heard, and understood not. And I said: O my lord, what shall be after these things?
verses.textLatin: Et ego audivi, et non intellexi. Et dixi: Domine mi, quid erit post hæc?

verses.text: And he said: Go, Daniel, because the words are shut up, and sealed until the appointed time.
verses.textLatin: Et ait: Vade, Daniel, quia clausi sunt signatique sermones usque ad præfinitum tempus.

verses.text: Many shall be chosen, and made white, and shall be tried as fire: and the wicked shall deal wickedly, and none of the wicked shall understand, but the learned shall understand.
verses.textLatin: Eligentur, et dealbabuntur, et quasi ignis probabuntur multi: et impie agent impii, neque intelligent omnes impii: porro docti intelligent.

verses.text: And from the time when the continual sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination unto desolation shall be set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred ninety days.
verses.textLatin: Et a tempore cum ablatum fuerit juge sacrificium, et posita fuerit abominatio in desolationem, dies mille ducenti nonaginta.

verses.text: Blessed is he that waiteth, and cometh unto a thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
verses.textLatin: Beatus qui exspectat, et pervenit usque ad dies mille trecentos triginta quinque.

verses.text: But go thou thy ways until the time appointed: and thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot unto the end of the days.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem vade ad præfinitum: et requiesces, et stabis in sorte tua in finem dierum.

verses.text: Now  there was a man that dwelt in Babylon, and his name was Joakim:
verses.textLatin: Et erat vir habitans in Babylone, et nomen ejus Joakim:

verses.text: And he took a wife whose name was Susanna, the daughter of Helcias, a very beautiful woman, and one that feared God.
verses.textLatin: et accepit uxorem nomine Susannam, filiam Helciæ, pulchram nimis, et timentem Deum:

verses.text: For her parents being just, had instructed their daughter according to the law of Moses.
verses.textLatin: parentes enim illius, cum essent justi, erudierunt filiam suam secundum legem Moysi.

verses.text: Now Joakim was very rich, and had an orchard near his house: and the Jews resorted to him, because he was the most honourable of them all.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Joakim dives valde, et erat ei pomarium vicinum domui suæ: et ad ipsum confluebant Judæi, eo quod esset honorabilior omnium.

verses.text: And there were two of the ancients of the people appointed judges that year, of whom the Lord said: Iniquity came out from Babylon from the ancient judges, that seemed to govern the people.
verses.textLatin: Et constituti sunt de populo duo senes judices in illo anno, de quibus locutus est Dominus: Quia egressa est iniquitas de Babylone a senioribus judicibus, qui videbantur regere populum.

verses.text: These men frequented the house of Joakim, and all that had any matters of judgment came to them.
verses.textLatin: Isti frequentabant domum Joakim, et veniebant ad eos omnes qui habebant judicia.

verses.text: And when the people departed away at noon, Susanna went in, and walked in her husband’s orchard.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem populus revertisset per meridiem, ingrediebatur Susanna, et deambulabat in pomario viri sui.

verses.text: And the old men saw her going in every day, and walking: and they were inflamed with lust towards her:
verses.textLatin: Et videbant eam senes quotidie ingredientem et deambulantem, et exarserunt in concupiscentiam ejus:

verses.text: And they perverted their own mind and turned away their eyes that they might not look unto heaven, nor remember just judgments.
verses.textLatin: et everterunt sensum suum, et declinaverunt oculos suos ut non viderent cælum, neque recordarentur judiciorum justorum.

verses.text: So they were both wounded with the love of her, yet they did not make known their grief one to the other:
verses.textLatin: Erant ergo ambo vulnerati amore ejus, nec indicaverunt sibi vicissim dolorem suum:

verses.text: For they were ashamed to declare to one another their lust, being desirous to have to do with her.
verses.textLatin: erubescebant enim indicare sibi concupiscentiam suam, volentes concumbere cum ea.

verses.text: And they watched carefully every day to see her. And one said to the other:
verses.textLatin: Et observabant quotidie sollicitius videre eam. Dixitque alter ad alterum:

verses.text: Let us now go home, for it is dinner time. So going out they departed one from another.
verses.textLatin: Eamus domum, quia hora prandii est. Et egressi, recesserunt a se.

verses.text: And turning back again, they came both to the same place: and asking one another the cause, they acknowledged their lust; and then they agreed upon a time, when they might find her alone.
verses.textLatin: Cumque revertissent, venerunt in unum: et sciscitantes ab invicem causam, confessi sunt concupiscentiam suam: et tunc in communi statuerunt tempus quando eam possent invenire solam.

verses.text: And it fell out, as they watched a fit day, she went in on a time, as yesterday and the day before, with two maids only, and was desirous to wash herself in the orchard: for it was hot weather.
verses.textLatin: Factum est autem, cum observarent diem aptum, ingressa est aliquando sicut heri et nudiustertius, cum duabus solis puellis, voluitque lavari in pomario: æstus quippe erat:

verses.text: And there was nobody there, but the two old men that had hid themselves and were beholding her.
verses.textLatin: et non erat ibi quisquam, præter duos senes absconditos, et contemplantes eam.

verses.text: So she said to the maids: Bring me oil, and washing balls, and shut the doors of the orchard, that I may wash me.
verses.textLatin: Dixit ergo puellis: Afferte mihi oleum, et smigmata, et ostia pomarii claudite, ut laver.

verses.text: And they did as she bade them: and they shut the doors of the orchard, and went out by a back door to fetch what she had commanded them, and they knew not that the elders were hid within.
verses.textLatin: Et fecerunt sicut præceperat: clauseruntque ostia pomarii, et egressæ sunt per posticum ut afferrent quæ jusserat; nesciebantque senes intus esse absconditos.

verses.text: Now when the maids were gone forth, the two elders arose, and ran to her, and said:
verses.textLatin: Cum autem egressæ essent puellæ, surrexerunt duo senes, et accurrerunt ad eam, et dixerunt:

verses.text: Behold the doors of the orchard are shut, and nobody seeth us, and we are in love with thee: wherefore consent to us, and lie with us.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ostia pomarii clausa sunt, et nemo nos videt, et nos in concupiscentia tui sumus: quam ob rem assentire nobis, et commiscere nobiscum.

verses.text: But if thou wilt not, we will bear witness against thee, that a young man was with thee, and therefore thou didst send away thy maids from thee.
verses.textLatin: Quod si nolueris, dicemus contra te testimonium, quod fuerit tecum juvenis, et ob hanc causam emiseris puellas a te.

verses.text: Susanna sighed, and said: I am straitened on every side: for if I do this thing, it is death to me: and if I do it not, I shall not escape your hands.
verses.textLatin: Ingemuit Susanna, et ait: Angustiæ sunt mihi undique: si enim hoc egero, mors mihi est: si autem non egero, non effugiam manus vestras.

verses.text: But it is better for me to fall into your hands without doing it, than to sin in the sight of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Sed melius est mihi absque opere incidere in manus vestras, quam peccare in conspectu Domini.

verses.text: With that Susanna cried out with a loud voice: and the elders also cried out against her.
verses.textLatin: Et exclamavit voce magna Susanna: exclamaverunt autem et senes adversus eam.

verses.text: And one of them ran to the door of the orchard, and opened it.
verses.textLatin: Et cucurrit unus ad ostia pomarii, et aperuit.

verses.text: So when the servants of the house heard the cry in the orchard, they rushed in by the back door to see what was the matter.
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo audissent clamorem famuli domus in pomario, irruerunt per posticum ut viderent quidnam esset.

verses.text: But after the old men had spoken, the servants were greatly ashamed: for never had there been any such word said of Susanna. And on the next day,
verses.textLatin: Postquam autem senes locuti sunt, erubuerunt servi vehementer, quia numquam dictus fuerat sermo hujuscemodi de Susanna. Et facta est dies crastina.

verses.text: When the people were come to Joakim her husband, the two elders also came full of wicked device against Susanna, to put her to death.
verses.textLatin: Cumque venisset populus ad Joakim virum ejus, venerunt et duo presbyteri, pleni iniqua cogitatione adversus Susannam ut interficerent eam.

verses.text: And they said before the people: Send to Susanna daughter of Helcias the wife of Joakim. And presently they sent.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt coram populo: Mittite ad Susannam filiam Helciæ uxorem Joakim. Et statim miserunt.

verses.text: And she came with her parents, and children, and all her kindred.
verses.textLatin: Et venit cum parentibus, et filiis, et universis cognatis suis.

verses.text: Now Susanna was exceeding delicate, and beautiful to behold.
verses.textLatin: Porro Susanna erat delicata nimis, et pulchra specie.

verses.text: But those wicked men commanded that her face should be uncovered, (for she was covered,) that so at least they might be satisfied with her beauty.
verses.textLatin: At iniqui illi jusserunt ut discooperiretur (erat enim cooperta), ut vel sic satiarentur decore ejus.

verses.text: Therefore her friends and all her acquaintance wept.
verses.textLatin: Flebant igitur sui, et omnes qui noverant eam.

verses.text: But the two elders rising up in the midst of the people, laid their hands upon her head.
verses.textLatin: Consurgentes autem duo presbyteri in medio populi, posuerunt manus suas super caput ejus.

verses.text: And she weeping looked up to heaven, for her heart had confidence in the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Quæ flens suspexit ad cælum: erat enim cor ejus fiduciam habens in Domino.

verses.text: And the elders said: As we walked in the orchard alone, this woman came in with two maids, and shut the doors of the orchard, and sent away the maids from her.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt presbyteri: Cum deambularemus in pomario soli, ingressa est hæc cum duabus puellis: et clausit ostia pomarii, et dimisit a se puellas.

verses.text: Then a young man that was there hid came to her, and lay with her.
verses.textLatin: Venitque ad eam adolescens, qui erat absconditus, et concubuit cum ea.

verses.text: But we that were in a corner of the orchard, seeing this wickedness, ran up to them, and we saw them lie together.
verses.textLatin: Porro nos cum essemus in angulo pomarii, videntes iniquitatem, cucurrimus ad eos, et vidimus eos pariter commisceri.

verses.text: And him indeed we could not take, because he was stronger than us, and opening the doors he leaped out:
verses.textLatin: Et illum quidem non quivimus comprehendere, quia fortior nobis erat, et apertis ostiis exilivit:

verses.text: But having taken this woman, we asked who the young man was, but she would not tell us: of this thing we are witnesses.
verses.textLatin: hanc autem cum apprehendissemus, interrogavimus, quisnam esset adolescens, et noluit indicare nobis: hujus rei testes sumus.

verses.text: The multitude believed them as being the elders and the judges of the people, and they condemned her to death.
verses.textLatin: Credidit eis multitudo quasi senibus et judicibus populi, et condemnaverunt eam ad mortem.

verses.text: Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice, and said: O eternal God, who knowest hidden things, who knowest all things before they come to pass,
verses.textLatin: Exclamavit autem voce magna Susanna, et dixit: Deus æterne, qui absconditorum es cognitor, qui nosti omnia antequam fiant,

verses.text: Thou knowest that they have borne false witness against me: and behold I must die, whereas I have done none of these things, which these men have maliciously forged against me.
verses.textLatin: tu scis quoniam falsum testimonium tulerunt contra me: et ecce morior, cum nihil horum fecerim, quæ isti malitiose composuerunt adversum me.

verses.text: And the Lord heard her voice.
verses.textLatin: Exaudivit autem Dominus vocem ejus.

verses.text: And when she was led to be put to death, the Lord raised up the holy spirit of a young boy, whose name was Daniel.
verses.textLatin: Cumque duceretur ad mortem, suscitavit Dominus spiritum sanctum pueri junioris, cujus nomen Daniel:

verses.text: And he cried out with a loud voice: I am clear from the blood of this woman.
verses.textLatin: et exclamavit voce magna: Mundus ego sum a sanguine hujus.

verses.text: Then all the people turning themselves towards him, said: What meaneth this word that thou hast spoken?
verses.textLatin: Et conversus omnis populus ad eum, dixit: Quis est iste sermo, quem tu locutus es?

verses.text: But he standing in the midst of them, said: Are ye so foolish, ye children of Israel, that without examination or knowledge of the truth, you have condemned a daughter of Israel?
verses.textLatin: Qui cum staret in medio eorum, ait: Sic fatui filii Israël, non judicantes, neque quod verum est cognoscentes, condemnastis filiam Israël?

verses.text: Return to judgment, for they have borne false witness against her.
verses.textLatin: revertimini ad judicium, quia falsum testimonium locuti sunt adversus eam.

verses.text: So all the people turned again in haste, and the old men said to him: Come, and sit thou down among us, and shew it us: seeing God hath given thee the honour of old age.
verses.textLatin: Reversus est ergo populus cum festinatione, et dixerunt ei senes: Veni, et sede in medio nostrum, et indica nobis: quia tibi Deus dedit honorem senectutis.

verses.text: And Daniel said to the people: Separate these two far from one another, and I will examine them.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad eos Daniel: Separate illos ab invicem procul, et dijudicabo eos.

verses.text: So when they were put asunder one from the other, he called one of them, and said to him: O thou that art grown old in evil days, now are thy sins come out, which thou hast committed before:
verses.textLatin: Cum ergo divisi essent alter ab altero, vocavit unum de eis, et dixit ad eum: Inveterate dierum malorum, nunc venerunt peccata tua, quæ operabaris prius:

verses.text: In judging unjust judgments, oppressing the innocent, and letting the guilty to go free, whereas the Lord saith: The innocent and the just thou shalt not kill.
verses.textLatin: judicans judicia injusta, innocentes opprimens, et dimittens noxios, dicente Domino: Innocentem et justum non interficies.

verses.text: Now then, if thou sawest her, tell me under what tree thou sawest them conversing together. He said: Under a mastic tree.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, si vidisti eam, dic sub qua arbore videris eos colloquentes sibi. Qui ait: Sub schino.

verses.text: And Daniel said: Well hast thou lied against thy own head: for behold the angel of God having received the sentence of him, shall cut thee in two.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Daniel: Recte mentitus es in caput tuum: ecce enim angelus Dei, accepta sententia ab eo, scindet te medium.

verses.text: And having put him aside, he commanded that the other should come, and he said to him: O thou seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda, beauty hath deceived thee, and lust hath perverted thy heart:
verses.textLatin: Et, amoto eo, jussit venire alium, et dixit ei: Semen Chanaan, et non Juda, species decepit te, et concupiscentia subvertit cor tuum:

verses.text: Thus did you do to the daughters of Israel, and they for fear conversed with you: but a daughter of Juda would not abide your wickedness.
verses.textLatin: sic faciebatis filiabus Israël, et illæ timentes loquebantur vobis: sed filia Juda non sustinuit iniquitatem vestram.

verses.text: Now therefore tell me, under what tree didst thou take them conversing together. And he answered: Under a holm tree.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, dic mihi sub qua arbore comprehenderis eos loquentes sibi. Qui ait: Sub prino.

verses.text: And Daniel said to him: Well hast thou also lied against thy own head: for the angel of the Lord waiteth with a sword to cut thee in two, and to destroy you.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem ei Daniel: Recte mentitus es et tu in caput tuum: manet enim angelus Domini, gladium habens, ut secet te medium, et interficiat vos.

verses.text: With that all the assembly cried out with a loud voice, and they blessed God, who saveth them that trust in him.
verses.textLatin: Exclamavit itaque omnis cœtus voce magna, et benedixerunt Deum, qui salvat sperantes in se.

verses.text: And they rose up against the two elders, (for Daniel had convicted them of false witness by their own mouth,) and they did to them as they had maliciously dealt against their neighbour,
verses.textLatin: Et consurrexerunt adversus duos presbyteros (convicerat enim eos Daniel ex ore suo falsum dixisse testimonium), feceruntque eis sicut male egerant adversus proximum,

verses.text: To fulfil the law of Moses: and they put them to death, and innocent blood was saved in that day.
verses.textLatin: ut facerent secundum legem Moysi. Et interfecerunt eos, et salvatus est sanguis innoxius in die illa.

verses.text: But Helcias and his wife praised God, for their daughter Susanna, with Joakim her husband, and all her kindred, because there was no dishonesty found in her.
verses.textLatin: Helcias autem et uxor ejus laudaverunt Deum pro filia sua Susanna cum Joakim marito ejus, et cognatis omnibus, quia non esset inventa in ea res turpis.

verses.text: And Daniel became great in the sight of the people from that day, and thenceforward.
verses.textLatin: Daniel autem factus est magnus in conspectu populi a die illa, et deinceps.

verses.text: And king Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Et rex Astyages appositus est ad patres suos, et suscepit Cyrus Perses regnum ejus.

verses.text: And Daniel was the king’s guest, and was honoured above all his friends.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Daniel conviva regis, et honoratus super omnes amicos ejus.

verses.text: Now the Babylonians had an idol called Bel: and there were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and sixty vessels of wine.
verses.textLatin: Erat quoque idolum apud Babylonios nomine Bel: et impendebantur in eo per dies singulos similæ artabæ duodecim, et oves quadraginta, vinique amphoræ sex.

verses.text: The king also worshipped him, and went every day to adore him: but Daniel adored his God. And the king said to him: Why dost thou not adore Bel?
verses.textLatin: Rex quoque colebat eum, et ibat per singulos dies adorare eum: porro Daniel adorabat Deum suum. Dixitque ei rex: Quare non adoras Bel?

verses.text: And he answered, and said to him: Because I do not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, that created heaven and earth, and hath power over all flesh.
verses.textLatin: Qui respondens ait ei: Quia non colo idola manufacta, sed viventem Deum, qui creavit cælum, et terram, et habet potestatem omnis carnis.

verses.text: And the king said to him: Doth not Bel seem to thee to be a living god? Seest thou not how much he eateth and drinketh every day?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit rex ad eum: Non videtur tibi esse Bel vivens deus? an non vides quanta comedat et bibat quotidie?

verses.text: Then Daniel smiled and said: O king, be not deceived: for this is but clay within, and brass without, neither hath he eaten at any time.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Daniel arridens: Ne erres, rex: iste enim intrinsecus luteus est, et forinsecus æreus, neque comedit aliquando.

verses.text: And the king being angry called for his priests, and said to them: If you tell me not, who it is that eateth up these expenses, you shall die.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus rex vocavit sacerdotes ejus, et ait eis: Nisi dixeritis mihi quis est qui comedat impensas has, moriemini.

verses.text: But if you can shew that Bel eateth these things, Daniel shall die, because he hath blasphemed against Bel. And Daniel said to the king: Be it done according to thy word.
verses.textLatin: Si autem ostenderitis quoniam Bel comedat hæc, morietur Daniel, quia blasphemavit in Bel. Et dixit Daniel regi: Fiat juxta verbum tuum.

verses.text: Now the priests of Bel were seventy, beside their wives, and little ones, and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
verses.textLatin: Erant autem sacerdotes Bel septuaginta, exceptis uxoribus, et parvulis, et filiis. Et venit rex cum Daniele in templum Bel.

verses.text: And the priests of Bel said: Behold we go out: and do thou, O king, set on the meats, and make ready the wine, and shut the door fast, and seal it with thy own ring:
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt sacerdotes Bel: Ecce nos egredimur foras: et tu, rex, pone escas, et vinum misce, et claude ostium, et signa annulo tuo:

verses.text: And when thou comest in the morning, if thou findest not that Bel hath eaten up all, we will suffer death, or else Daniel that hath lied against us.
verses.textLatin: et cum ingressus fueris mane, nisi inveneris omnia comesta a Bel, morte moriemur, vel Daniel qui mentitus est adversum nos.

verses.text: And they little regarded it, because they had made under the table a secret entrance, and they always came in by it, and consumed those things.
verses.textLatin: Contemnebant autem, quia fecerant sub mensa absconditum introitum, et per illum ingrediebantur semper, et devorabant ea.

verses.text: So it came to pass after they were gone out, the king set the meats before Bel: and Daniel commanded his servants, and they brought ashes, and he sifted them all over the temple before the king: and going forth they shut the door, and having sealed it with the king’s ring, they departed.
verses.textLatin: Factum est igitur postquam egressi sunt illi, rex posuit cibos ante Bel: præcepit Daniel pueris suis, et attulerunt cinerem, et cribravit per totum templum coram rege: et egressi clauserunt ostium, et signantes annulo regis abierunt.

verses.text: But the priests went in by night, according to their custom, with their wives and their children: and they ate and drank up all.
verses.textLatin: Sacerdotes autem ingressi sunt nocte juxta consuetudinem suam, et uxores et filii eorum, et comederunt omnia, et biberunt.

verses.text: And the king arose early in the morning, and Daniel with him.
verses.textLatin: Surrexit autem rex primo diluculo, et Daniel cum eo.

verses.text: And the king said: Are the seals whole, Daniel? And he answered: They are whole, O king.
verses.textLatin: Et ait rex: Salvane sunt signacula, Daniel? Qui respondit: Salva, rex.

verses.text: And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked upon the table, and cried out with a loud voice: Great art thou, O Bel, and there is not any deceit with thee.
verses.textLatin: Statimque cum aperuisset ostium, intuitus rex mensam, exclamavit voce magna: Magnus es, Bel, et non est apud te dolus quisquam.

verses.text: And Daniel laughed: and he held the king that he should not go in: and he said: Behold the pavement, mark whose footsteps these are.
verses.textLatin: Et risit Daniel, et tenuit regem ne ingrederetur intro: et dixit: Ecce pavimentum: animadverte cujus vestigia sint hæc.

verses.text: And the king said: I see the footsteps of men, and women, and children. And the king was angry.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit rex: Video vestigia virorum, et mulierum, et infantium. Et iratus est rex.

verses.text: Then he took the priests, and their wives, and their children: and they shewed him the private doors by which they came in, and consumed the things that were on the table.
verses.textLatin: Tunc apprehendit sacerdotes, et uxores, et filios eorum: et ostenderunt ei abscondita ostiola, per quæ ingrediebantur, et consumebant quæ erant super mensam.

verses.text: The king therefore put them to death, and delivered Bel into the power of Daniel: who destroyed him, and his temple.
verses.textLatin: Occidit ergo illos rex, et tradidit Bel in potestatem Danielis: qui subvertit eum, et templum ejus.

verses.text: And there was a great dragon in that place, and the Babylonians worshipped him.
verses.textLatin: Et erat draco magnus in loco illo, et colebant eum Babylonii.

verses.text: And the king said to Daniel: Behold thou canst not say now, that this is not a living god: adore him therefore.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit rex Danieli: Ecce nunc non potes dicere quia iste non sit deus vivens: adora ergo eum.

verses.text: And Daniel said: I adore the Lord my God: for he is the living God: but that is no living god.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Daniel: Dominum Deum meum adoro, quia ipse est Deus vivens: iste autem non est deus vivens.

verses.text: But give me leave, O king, and I will kill this dragon without sword or club. And the king said: I give thee leave.
verses.textLatin: Tu autem, rex, da mihi potestatem, et interficiam draconem absque gladio et fuste. Et ait rex: Do tibi.

verses.text: Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and boiled them together: and he made lumps, and put them into the dragon’s mouth, and the dragon burst asunder. And he said: Behold him whom you worshipped.
verses.textLatin: Tulit ergo Daniel picem, et adipem, et pilos, et coxit pariter: fecitque massas, et dedit in os draconis, et diruptus est draco. Et dixit: Ecce quem colebatis.

verses.text: And when the Babylonians had heard this, they took great indignation: and being gathered together against the king, they said: The king is become a Jew. He hath destroyed Bel, he hath killed the dragon, and he hath put the priests to death.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum audissent Babylonii, indignati sunt vehementer: et congregati adversum regem, dixerunt: Judæus factus est rex: Bel destruxit, draconem interfecit, et sacerdotes occidit.

verses.text: And they came to the king, and said: Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy thee and thy house.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt cum venissent ad regem: Trade nobis Danielem, alioquin interficiemus te, et domum tuam.

verses.text: And the king saw that they pressed upon him violently: and being constrained by necessity he delivered Daniel to them.
verses.textLatin: Vidit ergo rex quod irruerent in eum vehementer: et necessitate compulsus, tradidit eis Danielem.

verses.text: And they cast him into the den of lions, and he was there six days.
verses.textLatin: Qui miserunt eum in lacum leonum, et erat ibi diebus sex.

verses.text: And in the den there were seven lions, and they had given to them two carcasses every day, and two sheep: but then they were not given unto them, that they might devour Daniel.
verses.textLatin: Porro in lacu erant leones septem, et dabantur eis duo corpora quotidie, et duæ oves: et tunc non data sunt eis, ut devorarent Danielem.

verses.text: Now there was in Judea a prophet called Habacuc, and he had boiled pottage, and had broken bread in a bowl: and was going into the field, to carry it to the reapers.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem Habacuc propheta in Judæa, et ipse coxerat pulmentum, et intriverat panes in alveolo: et ibat in campum ut ferret messoribus.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord said to Habacuc: Carry the dinner which thou hast into Babylon to Daniel, who is in the lions’ den.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque angelus Domini ad Habacuc: Fer prandium quod habes in Babylonem Danieli, qui est in lacu leonum.

verses.text: And Habacuc said: Lord, I never saw Babylon, nor do I know the den.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Habacuc: Domine, Babylonem non vidi, et lacum nescio.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord took him by the top of his head, and carried him by the hair of his head, and set him in Babylon over the den in the force of his spirit.
verses.textLatin: Et apprehendit eum angelus Domini in vertice ejus, et portavit eum capillo capitis sui, posuitque eum in Babylone supra lacum in impetu spiritus sui.

verses.text: And Habacuc cried, saying: O Daniel, thou servant of God, take the dinner that God hath sent thee.
verses.textLatin: Et clamavit Habacuc, dicens: Daniel serve Dei, tolle prandium quod misit tibi Deus.

verses.text: And Daniel said: Thou hast remembered me, O God, and thou hast not forsaken them that love thee.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Daniel: Recordatus es mei, Deus, et non dereliquisti diligentes te.

verses.text: And Daniel arose and ate. And the angel of the Lord presently set Habacuc again in his own place.
verses.textLatin: Surgensque Daniel comedit. Porro angelus Domini restituit Habacuc confestim in loco suo.

verses.text: And upon the seventh day the king came to bewail Daniel: and he came to the den, and looked in, and behold Daniel was sitting in the midst of the lions.
verses.textLatin: Venit ergo rex die septimo ut lugeret Danielem: et venit ad lacum, et introspexit, et ecce Daniel sedens in medio leonum.

verses.text: And the king cried out with a loud voice, saying: Great art thou, O Lord the God of Daniel. And he drew him out of the lions’ den.
verses.textLatin: Et exclamavit voce magna rex, dicens: Magnus es, Domine Deus Danielis. Et extraxit eum de lacu leonum.

verses.text: But those that had been the cause of his destruction, he cast into the den, and they were devoured in a moment before him.
verses.textLatin: Porro illos, qui perditionis ejus causa fuerant, intromisit in lacum, et devorati sunt in momento coram eo.

verses.text: Then the king said: Let all the inhabitants of the whole earth fear the God of Daniel: for he is the Saviour, working signs, and wonders in the earth: who hath delivered Daniel out of the lions’ den.
verses.textLatin: Tunc rex ait: Paveant omnes habitantes in universa terra Deum Danielis: quia ipse est salvator, faciens signa et mirabilia in terra: qui liberavit Danielem de lacu leonum.

verses.text: The  word of the Lord, that came to Osee the son of Beeri, in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias kings of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Verbum Domini, quod factum est ad Osee, filium Beeri, in diebus Oziæ, Joathan, Achaz, Ezechiæ, regum Juda; et in diebus Jeroboam, filii Joas, regis Israël.

verses.text: The beginning of the Lord’s speaking by Osee: and the Lord said to Osee: Go, take thee a wife of fornications, and have of her children of fornications: for the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Principium loquendi Domino in Osee. Et dixit Dominus ad Osee: Vade, sume tibi uxorem fornicationum, et fac tibi filios fornicationum, quia fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino.

verses.text: So he went, and took Gomer the daughter of Debelaim: and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit, et accepit Gomer, filiam Debelaim: et concepit, et peperit ei filium.

verses.text: And the Lord said to him: Call his name Jezrahel: for yet a little while, and I will visit the blood of Jezrahel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad eum: Voca nomen ejus Jezrahel, quoniam adhuc modicum, et visitabo sanguinem Jezrahel super domum Jehu, et quiescere faciam regnum domus Israël.

verses.text: And in that day I will break in pieces the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezrahel.
verses.textLatin: Et in illa die conteram arcum Israël in valle Jezrahel.

verses.text: And she conceived again, and bore a daughter, and he said to him: Call her name, Without mercy: for I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them.
verses.textLatin: Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filiam. Et dixit ei: Voca nomen ejus, Absque misericordia, quia non addam ultra misereri domui Israël, sed oblivione obliviscar eorum.

verses.text: And I will have mercy on the house of Juda, and I will save them by the Lord their God: and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, nor by horses, nor by horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Et domui Juda miserebor, et salvabo eos in Domino Deo suo; et non salvabo eos in arcu et gladio, et in bello, et in equis, et in equitibus.

verses.text: And she weaned her that was called Without mercy. And she conceived, and bore a son.
verses.textLatin: Et ablactavit eam quæ erat Absque misericordia. Et concepit, et peperit filium.

verses.text: And he said: Call his name, Not my people: for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus, quia vos non populus meus, et ego non ero vester.

verses.text: And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, that is without measure, and shall not be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God.
verses.textLatin: Et erit numerus filiorum Israël quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est, et non numerabitur. Et erit in loco ubi dicetur eis: Non populus meus vos: dicetur eis: Filii Dei viventis.

verses.text: And the children of Juda, and the children of Israel shall be gathered together: and they shall appoint themselves one head, and shall come up out of the land: for great is the day of Jezrahel.
verses.textLatin: Et congregabuntur filii Juda et filii Israël pariter; et ponent sibimet caput unum, et ascendent de terra, quia magnus dies Jezrahel.

verses.text: Say ye to your brethren: You are my people, and to your sister: Thou hast obtained mercy.
verses.textLatin: Dicite fratribus vestris: Populus meus; et sorori vestræ: Misericordiam consecuta.

verses.text: Judge your mother, judge her: because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts.
verses.textLatin: Judicate matrem vestram, judicate, quoniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus. Auferat fornicationes suas a facie sua, et adulteria sua de medio uberum suorum;

verses.text: Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was born: and I will make her as a wilderness, and will set her as a land that none can pass through, and will kill her with drought.
verses.textLatin: ne forte expoliem eam nudam, et statuam eam secundum diem nativitatis suæ, et ponam eam quasi solitudinem, et statuam eam velut terram inviam, et interficiam eam siti.

verses.text: And I will not have mercy on her children: for they are the children of fornications.
verses.textLatin: Et filiorum illius non miserebor, quoniam filii fornicationum sunt.

verses.text: For their mother hath committed fornication, she that conceived them is covered with shame: for she said: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, my oil, and my drink.
verses.textLatin: Quia fornicata est mater eorum, confusa est quæ concepit eos; quia dixit: Vadam post amatores meos, qui dant panes mihi, et aquas meas, lanam meam, et linum meum, oleum meum, et potum meum.

verses.text: Wherefore behold I will hedge up thy way with thorns, and I will stop it up with a wall, and she shall not find her paths.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc ecce ego sepiam viam tuam spinis, et sepiam eam maceria, et semitas suas non inveniet.

verses.text: And she shall follow after her lovers, and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them, and shall not find, and she shall say: I will go, and return to my first husband, because it was better with me then, than now.
verses.textLatin: Et sequetur amatores suos, et non apprehendet eos; et quæret eos, et non inveniet: et dicet: Vadam, et revertar ad virum meum priorem, quia bene mihi erat tunc magis quam nunc.

verses.text: And she did not know that I gave her corn and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver, and gold, which they have used in the service of Baal.
verses.textLatin: Et hæc nescivit, quia ego dedi ei frumentum, et vinum, et oleum, et argentum multiplicavi ei, et aurum, quæ fecerunt Baal.

verses.text: Therefore will I return, and take away my corn in its season, and my wine in its season, and I will set at liberty my wool, and my flax, which covered her disgrace.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco convertar, et sumam frumentum meum in tempore suo, et vinum meum in tempore suo. Et liberabo lanam meam et linum meum, quæ operiebant ignominiam ejus.

verses.text: And now I will lay open her folly in the eyes of her lovers: and no man shall deliver her out of my hand:
verses.textLatin: Et nunc revelabo stultitiam ejus in oculis amatorum ejus; et vir non eruet eam de manu mea;

verses.text: And I will cause all her mirth to cease, her solemnities, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her festival times.
verses.textLatin: et cessare faciam omne gaudium ejus, solemnitatem ejus, neomeniam ejus, sabbatum ejus, et omnia festa tempora ejus.

verses.text: And I will destroy her vines, and her fig trees, of which she said: These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me: and I will make her as a forest, and the beasts of the field shall devour her.
verses.textLatin: Et corrumpam vineam ejus, et ficum ejus, de quibus dixit: Mercedes hæ meæ sunt, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei; et ponam eam in saltum, et comedet eam bestia agri.

verses.text: And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim, to whom she burnt incense, and decked herself out with her earrings, and with her jewels, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et visitabo super eam dies Baalim, quibus accendebat incensum, et ornabatur in aure sua, et monili suo. Et ibat post amatores suos, et mei obliviscebatur, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Therefore, behold I will allure her, and will lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc ecce ego lactabo eam, et ducam eam in solitudinem, et loquar ad cor ejus.

verses.text: And I will give her vinedressers out of the same place, and the valley of Achor for an opening of hope: and she shall sing there according to the days of her youth, and according to the days of her coming up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo ei vinitores ejus ex eodem loco, et vallem Achor, ad aperiendam spem; et canet ibi juxta dies juventutis suæ, et juxta dies ascensionis suæ de terra Ægypti.

verses.text: And it shall be in that day, saith the Lord, That she shall call me: My husband, and she shall call me no more Baali.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa, ait Dominus: vocabit me, Vir meus, et non vocabit me ultra Baali.

verses.text: And I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and she shall no more remember their name.
verses.textLatin: Et auferam nomina Baalim de ore ejus, et non recordabitur ultra nominis eorum.

verses.text: And in that day I will make a covenant with them, with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air, and with the creeping things of the earth: and I will destroy the bow, and the sword, and war out of the land: and I will make them sleep secure.
verses.textLatin: Et percutiam cum eis fœdus in die illa, cum bestia agri, et cum volucre cæli, et cum reptili terræ; et arcum, et gladium, et bellum conteram de terra, et dormire eos faciam fiducialiter.

verses.text: And I will espouse thee to me for ever: and I will espouse thee to me in justice, and judgment, and in mercy, and in commiserations.
verses.textLatin: Et sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum; et sponsabo te mihi in justitia, et judicio, et in misericordia, et in miserationibus.

verses.text: And I will espouse thee to me in faith: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et sponsabo te mihi in fide; et scies quia ego Dominus.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day: I will hear, saith the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: exaudiam, dicit Dominus, exaudiam cælos, et illi exaudient terram.

verses.text: And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil, and these shall hear Jezrahel.
verses.textLatin: Et terra exaudiet triticum, et vinum, et oleum, et hæc exaudient Jezrahel.

verses.text: And I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercy on her that was without mercy.
verses.textLatin: Et seminabo eam mihi in terra, et miserebor ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia.

verses.text: And I will say to that which was not my people: Thou art my people: and they shall say: Thou art my God.
verses.textLatin: Et dicam Non populo meo: Populus meus es tu; et ipse dicet: Deus meus es tu.

verses.text: And  the Lord said to me: Go yet again, and love a woman beloved of her friend, and an adulteress: as the Lord loveth the children of Israel, and they look to strange gods, and love the husks of the grapes.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad me: Adhuc vade, et dilige mulierem dilectam amico et adulteram, sicut diligit Dominus filios Israël, et ipsi respiciunt ad deos alienos, et diligunt vinacia uvarum.

verses.text: And I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for a core of barley, and for half a core of barley.
verses.textLatin: Et fodi eam mihi quindecim argenteis, et coro hordei, et dimidio coro hordæi.

verses.text: And I said to her: Thou shalt wait for me many days: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be no man’s, and I also will wait for thee.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi ad eam: Dies multos exspectabis me; non fornicaberis, et non eris viro; sed et ego exspectabo te.

verses.text: For the children of Israel shall sit many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without altar, and without ephod, and without theraphim.
verses.textLatin: Quia dies multos sedebunt filii Israël sine rege, et sine principe, et sine sacrificio, et sine altari, et sine ephod, et sine theraphim.

verses.text: And after this the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the Lord their God, and David their king: and they shall fear the Lord, and his goodness in the last days.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc revertentur filii Israël, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum: et pavebunt ad Dominum, et ad bonum ejus, in novissimo dierum.

verses.text: Hear  the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel, for the Lord shall enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the land: for there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land.
verses.textLatin: Audite verbum Domini, filii Israël, quia judicium Domino cum habitatoribus terræ: non est enim veritas, et non est misericordia, et non est scientia Dei in terra.

verses.text: Cursing, and lying, and killing, and theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood hath touched blood.
verses.textLatin: Maledictum, et mendacium, et homicidium, et furtum, et adulterium inundaverunt, et sanguis sanguinem tetigit.

verses.text: Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth in it shall languish with the heat of the field, and with the fowls of the air: yea, the fishes of the sea also shall be gathered together.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc lugebit terra, et infirmabitur omnis qui habitat in ea, in bestia agri, et in volucre cæli; sed et pisces maris congregabuntur.

verses.text: But yet let not any man judge: and let not a man be rebuked: for thy people are as they that contradict the priest.
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen unusquisque non judicet, et non arguatur vir: populus enim tuus sicut hi qui contradicunt sacerdoti.

verses.text: And thou shalt fall to day, and the prophet also shall fall with thee: in the night I have made thy mother to be silent.
verses.textLatin: Et corrues hodie, et corruet etiam propheta tecum. Nocte tacere feci matrem tuam.

verses.text: My people have been silent, because they had no knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me: and thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I also will forget thy children.
verses.textLatin: Conticuit populus meus, eo quod non habuerit scientiam: quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi; et oblita es legis Dei tui, obliviscar filiorum tuorum et ego.

verses.text: According to the multitude of them so have they sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame.
verses.textLatin: Secundum multitudinem eorum sic peccaverunt mihi: gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo.

verses.text: They shall eat the sins of my people, and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Peccata populi mei comedent, et ad iniquitatem eorum sublevabunt animas eorum.

verses.text: And there shall be like people like priest: and I will visit their ways upon them, and I will repay them their devices.
verses.textLatin: Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos; et visitabo super eum vias ejus, et cogitationes ejus reddam ei.

verses.text: And they shall eat and shall not be filled: they have committed fornication, and have not ceased: because they have forsaken the Lord in not observing his law.
