verses.textLatin: Et comedent, et non saturabuntur; fornicati sunt, et non cessaverunt: quoniam Dominum dereliquerunt in non custodiendo.

verses.text: Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness take away the understanding.
verses.textLatin: Fornicatio, et vinum, et ebrietas auferunt cor.

verses.text: My people have consulted their stocks, and their staff hath declared unto them: for the spirit of fornication hath deceived them, and they have committed fornication against their God.
verses.textLatin: Populus meus in ligno suo interrogavit, et baculus ejus annuntiavit ei; spiritus enim fornicationum decepit eos, et fornicati sunt a Deo suo.

verses.text: They offered sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burnt incense upon the hills: under the oak, and the poplar, and the turpentine tree, because the shadow thereof was good: therefore shall your daughters commit fornication, and your spouses shall be adulteresses.
verses.textLatin: Super capita montium sacrificabant, et super colles ascendebant thymiama; subtus quercum, et populum, et terebinthum, quia bona erat umbra ejus; ideo fornicabuntur filiæ vestræ, et sponsæ vestræ adulteræ erunt.

verses.text: I will not visit upon your daughters when they shall commit fornication, and upon your spouses when they shall commit adultery: because themselves conversed with harlots, and offered sacrifice with the effeminate, and the people that doth not understand shall be beaten.
verses.textLatin: Non visitabo super filias vestras cum fuerint fornicatæ, et super sponsas vestras cum adulteraverint, quoniam ipsi cum meretricibus conversabantur, et cum effeminatis sacrificabant; et populus non intelligens vapulabit.

verses.text: If thou play the harlot, O Israel, at least let not Juda offend: and go ye not into Galgal, and come not up into Bethaven, and do not swear: The Lord liveth.
verses.textLatin: Si fornicaris tu, Israël, non delinquat saltem Juda; et nolite ingredi in Galgala, et ne ascenderitis in Bethaven, neque juraveritis: Vivit Dominus!

verses.text: For Israel hath gone astray like a wanton heifer: now will the Lord feed them, as a lamb in a spacious place.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam sicut vacca lasciviens declinavit Israël; nunc pascet eos Dominus, quasi agnum in latitudine.

verses.text: Ephraim is a partaker with idols, let him alone.
verses.textLatin: Particeps idolorum Ephraim: dimitte eum.

verses.text: Their banquet is separated, they have gone astray by fornication: they that should have protected them have loved to bring shame upon them.
verses.textLatin: Separatum est convivium eorum; fornicatione fornicati sunt: dilexerunt afferre ignominiam protectores ejus.

verses.text: The wind hath bound them up in its wings, and they shall be confounded because of their sacrifices.
verses.textLatin: Ligavit eum spiritus in alis suis, et confundentur a sacrificiis suis.

verses.text: Hear ye this, O priests, and hearken, O ye house of Israel, and give ear, O house of the king: for there is a judgment against you, because you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over, and a net spread upon Thabor.
verses.textLatin: Audite hoc, sacerdotes,  et attendite, domus Israël, et domus regis, auscultate: quia vobis judicium est, quoniam laqueus facti estis speculationi, et rete expansum super Thabor.

verses.text: And you have turned aside victims into the depth: and I am the teacher of them all.
verses.textLatin: Et victimas declinastis in profundum; et ego eruditor omnium eorum.

verses.text: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now Ephraim hath committed fornication, Israel is defiled.
verses.textLatin: Ego scio Ephraim, et Israël non est absconditus a me: quia nunc fornicatus est Ephraim; contaminatus est Israël.

verses.text: They will not set their thoughts to return to their God: for the spirit of fornication is in the midst of them, and they have not known the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non dabunt cogitationes suas ut revertantur ad Deum suum, quia spiritus fornicationum in medio eorum, et Dominum non cognoverunt.

verses.text: And the pride of Israel shall answer in his face: and Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity, Juda also shall fall with them.
verses.textLatin: Et respondebit arrogantia Israël in facie ejus, et Israël et Ephraim ruent in iniquitate sua: ruet etiam Judas cum eis.

verses.text: With their flocks, and with their herds, they shall go to seek the Lord, and shall not find him: he is withdrawn from them.
verses.textLatin: In gregibus suis et in armentis suis vadent ad quærendum Dominum, et non invenient: ablatus est ab eis.

verses.text: They have transgressed against the Lord, for they have begotten children that are strangers: now shall a month devour them with their portions.
verses.textLatin: In Dominum prævaricati sunt, quia filios alienos genuerunt: nunc devorabit eos mensis, cum partibus suis.

verses.text: Blow ye the cornet in Gabaa, the trumpet in Rama: howl ye in Bethaven, behind thy back, O Benjamin.
verses.textLatin: Clangite buccina in Gabaa, tuba in Rama; ululate in Bethaven, post tergum tuum, Benjamin.

verses.text: Ephraim shall be in desolation in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel I have shewn that which shall surely be.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim in desolatione erit in die correptionis; in tribubus Israël ostendi fidem.

verses.text: The princes of Juda are become as they that take up the bound: I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.
verses.textLatin: Facti sunt principes Juda quasi assumentes terminum; super eos effundam quasi aquam iram meam.

verses.text: Ephraim is under oppression, and broken in judgment: because he began to go after filthiness.
verses.textLatin: Calumniam patiens est Ephraim, fractus judicio, quoniam cœpit abire post sordes.

verses.text: And I will be like a moth to Ephraim: and like rottenness to the house of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et ego quasi tinea Ephraim, et quasi putredo domui Juda.

verses.text: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Juda his band: and Ephraim went to the Assyrian, and sent to the avenging king: and he shall not be able to heal you, neither shall he be able to take off the band from you.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Ephraim languorem suum, et Juda vinculum suum; et abiit Ephraim ad Assur, et misit ad regem ultorem: et ipse non poterit sanare vos, nec solvere poterit a vobis vinculum.

verses.text: For I will be like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a lion’s whelp to the house of Juda: I, I will catch, and go: I will take away, and there is none that can rescue.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam ego quasi leæna Ephraim, et quasi catulus leonis domui Juda. Ego, ego capiam, et vadam; tollam, et non est qui eruat.

verses.text: I will go and return to my place: until you are consumed, and seek my face.
verses.textLatin: Vadens revertar ad locum meum, donec deficiatis, et quæratis faciem meam.

verses.text: In  their affliction they will rise early to me: Come, and let us return to the Lord:
verses.textLatin: In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me: Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum,

verses.text: For he hath taken us, and he will heal us: he will strike, and he will cure us.
verses.textLatin: quia ipse cepit, et sanabit nos; percutiet, et curabit nos.

verses.text: He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on, that we may know the Lord. His going forth is prepared as the morning light, and he will come to us as the early and the latter rain to the earth.
verses.textLatin: Vivificabit nos post duos dies; in die tertia suscitabit nos, et vivemus in conspectu ejus. Sciemus, sequemurque ut cognoscamus Dominum: quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus, et veniet quasi imber nobis temporaneus et serotinus terræ.

verses.text: What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim? what shall I do to thee, O Juda? your mercy is as a morning cloud, and as the dew that goeth away in the morning.
verses.textLatin: Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? quid faciam tibi, Juda? misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina, et quasi ros mane pertransiens.

verses.text: For this reason have I hewed them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and thy judgments shall go forth as the light.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc dolavi in prophetis; occidi eos in verbis oris mei: et judicia tua quasi lux egredientur.

verses.text: For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice: and the knowledge of God more than holocausts.
verses.textLatin: Quia misericordiam volui, et non sacrificium; et scientiam Dei plus quam holocausta.

verses.text: But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant, there have they dealt treacherously against me.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi autem sicut Adam transgressi sunt pactum: ibi prævaricati sunt in me.

verses.text: Galaad is a city of workers of idols, supplanted with blood.
verses.textLatin: Galaad civitas operantium idolum, supplantata sanguine.

verses.text: And like the jaws of highway robbers, they conspire with the priests who murder in the way those that pass out of Sichem: for they have wrought wickedness.
verses.textLatin: Et quasi fauces virorum latronum, particeps sacerdotum, in via interficientium pergentes de Sichem: quia scelus operati sunt.

verses.text: I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel: the fornications of Ephraim there: Israel is defiled.
verses.textLatin: In domo Israël vidi horrendum: ibi fornicationes Ephraim, contaminatus est Israël.

verses.text: And thou also, O Juda, set thee a harvest, when I shall bring back the captivity of my people.
verses.textLatin: Sed et Juda, pone messem tibi, cum convertero captivitatem populi mei.

verses.text: When  I would have healed Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria, for they have committed falsehood, and the thief is come in to steal, the robber is without.
verses.textLatin: Cum sanare vellem Israël, revelata est iniquitas Ephraim, et malitia Samariæ, quia operati sunt mendacium; et fur ingressus est spolians, latrunculus foris.

verses.text: And lest they may say in their hearts, that I remember all their wickedness: their own devices now have beset them about, they have been done before my face.
verses.textLatin: Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ: coram facie mea factæ sunt.

verses.text: They have made the king glad with their wickedness: and the princes with their lies.
verses.textLatin: In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, et in mendaciis suis principes.

verses.text: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker: the city rested a little from the mingling of the leaven, till the whole was leavened.
verses.textLatin: Omnes adulterantes, quasi clibanus succensus a coquente; quievit paululum civitas a commistione fermenti, donec fermentaretur totum.

verses.text: The day of our king, the princes began to be mad with wine: he stretched out his hand with scorners.
verses.textLatin: Dies regis nostri: cœperunt principes furere a vino; extendit manum suam cum illusoribus.

verses.text: Because they have applied their heart like an oven, when he laid snares for them: he slept all the night baking them, in the morning he himself was heated as a flaming fire.
verses.textLatin: Quia applicuerunt quasi clibanum cor suum, cum insidiaretur eis; tota nocte dormivit coquens eos: mane ipse succensus quasi ignis flammæ.

verses.text: They were all heated like an oven, and have devoured their judges: all their kings have fallen: there is none amongst them that calleth unto me.
verses.textLatin: Omnes calefacti sunt quasi clibanus, et devoraverunt judices suos: omnes reges eorum ceciderunt; non est qui clamat in eis ad me.

verses.text: Ephraim himself is mixed among the nations: Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes, that is not turned.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim in populis ipse commiscebatur; Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, qui non reversatur.

verses.text: Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knew it not: yea, grey hairs also are spread about upon him, and he is ignorant of it.
verses.textLatin: Comederunt alieni robur ejus, et ipse nescivit; sed et cani effusi sunt in eo, et ipse ignoravit.

verses.text: And the pride of Israel shall be humbled before his face: and they have not returned to the Lord their God, nor have they sought him in all these.
verses.textLatin: Et humiliabitur superbia Israël in facie ejus; nec reversi sunt ad Dominum Deum suum, et non quæsierunt eum in omnibus his.

verses.text: And Ephraim is become as a dove that is decoyed, not having a heart: they called upon Egypt, they went to the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: Et factus est Ephraim quasi columba seducta non habens cor. Ægyptum invocabant; ad Assyrios abierunt.

verses.text: And when they shall go, I will spread my net upon them: I will bring them down as the fowl of the air, I will strike them as their congregation hath heard.
verses.textLatin: Et cum profecti fuerint, expandam super eos rete meum: quasi volucrem cæli detraham eos; cædam eos secundum auditionem cœtus eorum.

verses.text: Woe to them, for they have departed from me: they shall be wasted because they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they have spoken lies against me.
verses.textLatin: Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me! vastabuntur, quia prævaricati sunt in me, et ego redemi eos, et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia.

verses.text: And they have not cried to me with their heart, but they howled in their beds: they have thought upon wheat and wine, they are departed from me.
verses.textLatin: Et non clamaverunt ad me in corde suo, sed ululabant in cubilibus suis: super triticum et vinum ruminabant; recesserunt a me.

verses.text: And I have chastised them, and strengthened their arms: and they have imagined evil against me.
verses.textLatin: Et ego erudivi eos, et confortavi brachia eorum, et in me cogitaverunt malitiam.

verses.text: They returned, that they might be without yoke: they became like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword, for the rage of their tongue. This is their derision in the land of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Reversi sunt ut essent absque jugo; facti sunt quasi arcus dolosus: cadent in gladio principes eorum, a furore linguæ suæ. Ista subsannatio eorum in terra Ægypti.

verses.text: Let  there be a trumpet in thy throat like an eagle upon the house of the Lord: because they have transgressed my covenant, and have violated my law.
verses.textLatin: In gutture tuo sit tuba quasi aquila super domum Domini, pro eo quod transgressi sunt fœdus meum, et legem meam prævaricati sunt.

verses.text: They shall call upon me: O my God, we, Israel, know thee.
verses.textLatin: Me invocabunt: Deus meus, cognovimus te Israël.

verses.text: Israel hath cast off the thing that is good, the enemy shall pursue him.
verses.textLatin: Projecit Israël bonum: inimicus persequetur eum.

verses.text: They have reigned, but not by me: they have been princes, and I knew not: of their silver, and their gold they have made idols to themselves, that they might perish.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi regnaverunt, et non ex me; principes exstiterunt, et non cognovi: argentum suum et aurum suum fecerunt sibi idola, ut interirent.

verses.text: Thy calf, O Samaria, is cast off, my wrath is kindled against them. How long will they be incapable of being cleansed?
verses.textLatin: Projectus est vitulus tuus, Samaria; iratus est furor meus in eos. Usquequo non poterunt emundari?

verses.text: For itself also is the invention of Israel: a workman made it, and it is no god: for the calf of Samaria shall be turned to spiders’ webs.
verses.textLatin: Quia ex Israël et ipse est: artifex fecit illum, et non est deus; quoniam in aranearum telas erit vitulus Samariæ.

verses.text: For they shall sow wind, and reap a whirlwind, there is no standing stalk in it, the bud shall yield no meal; and if it should yield, strangers shall eat it.
verses.textLatin: Quia ventum seminabunt, et turbinem metent: culmus stans non est in eo; germen non faciet farinam: quod etsi fecerit, alieni comedent eam.

verses.text: Israel is swallowed up: now is he become among the nations like an unclean vessel.
verses.textLatin: Devoratus est Israël; nunc factus est in nationibus quasi vas immundum.

verses.text: For they are gone up to Assyria, a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath given gifts to his lovers.
verses.textLatin: Quia ipsi ascenderunt ad Assur, onager solitarius sibi; Ephraim munera dederunt amatoribus.

verses.text: But even though they shall have hired the nations, now will I gather them together: and they shall rest a while from the burden of the king, and the princes.
verses.textLatin: Sed et cum mercede conduxerint nationes, nunc congregabo eos, et quiescent paulisper ab onere regis et principum.

verses.text: Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin: altars are become to him unto sin.
verses.textLatin: Quia multiplicavit Ephraim altaria ad peccandum; factæ sunt ei aræ in delictum.

verses.text: I shall write to him my manifold laws, which have been accounted as foreign.
verses.textLatin: Scribam ei multiplices leges meas, quæ velut alienæ computatæ sunt.

verses.text: They shall offer victims, they shall sacrifice flesh, and shall eat it, and the Lord will not receive them: now will he remember their iniquity, and will visit their sins: they shall return to Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Hostias offerent, immolabunt carnes et comedent, et Dominus non suscipiet eas: nunc recordabitur iniquitatis eorum, et visitabit peccata eorum: ipsi in Ægyptum convertentur.

verses.text: And Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and hath built temples: and Juda hath built many fenced cities: and I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall devour the houses thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et oblitus est Israël factoris sui, et ædificavit delubra; et Judas multiplicavit urbes munitas; et mittam ignem in civitates ejus, et devorabit ædes illius.

verses.text: Rejoice  not, O Israel: rejoice not as the nations do: for thou hast committed fornication against thy God, thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor.
verses.textLatin: Noli lætari, Israël; noli exsultare sicut populi: quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo; dilexisti mercedem super omnes areas tritici.

verses.text: The floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the wine shall deceive them.
verses.textLatin: Area et torcular non pascet eos, et vinum mentietur eis:

verses.text: They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land: Ephraim is returned to Egypt, and hath eaten unclean things among the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: non habitabunt in terra Domini. Reversus est Ephraim in Ægyptum, et in Assyriis pollutum comedit.

verses.text: They shall not offer wine to the Lord, neither shall they please him: their sacrifices shall be like the bread of mourners: all that shall eat it shall be defiled: for their bread is life for their soul, it shall not enter into the house of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Non libabunt Domino vinum, et non placebunt ei. Sacrificia eorum quasi panis lugentium; omnes qui comedent eum, contaminabuntur: quia panis eorum animæ ipsorum: non intrabit in domum Domini.

verses.text: What will you do in the solemn day, in the day of the feast of the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Quid facietis in die solemni, in die festivitatis Domini?

verses.text: For behold they are gone because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them together, Memphis shall bury them: nettles shall inherit their beloved silver, the bur shall be in their tabernacles.
verses.textLatin: Ecce enim profecti sunt a vastitate: Ægyptus congregabit eos; Memphis sepeliet eos: desiderabile argentum eorum urtica hæreditabit, lappa in tabernaculis eorum.

verses.text: The days of visitation are come, the days of repaying are come: know ye, O Israel, that the prophet was foolish, the spiritual man was mad, for the multitude of thy iniquity, and the multitude of thy madness.
verses.textLatin: Venerunt dies visitationis, venerunt dies retributionis. Scitote, Israël, stultum prophetam, insanum virum spiritualem, propter multitudinem iniquitatis tuæ, et multitudinem amentiæ.

verses.text: The watchman of Ephraim was with my God: the prophet is become a snare of ruin upon all his ways, madness is in the house of his God.
verses.textLatin: Speculator Ephraim cum Deo meo, propheta laqueus ruinæ factus est super omnes vias ejus; insania in domo Dei ejus.

verses.text: They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa: he will remember their iniquity, and will visit their sin.
verses.textLatin: Profunde peccaverunt, sicut in diebus Gabaa. Recordabitur iniquitatis eorum, et visitabit peccata eorum.

verses.text: I found Israel like grapes in the desert, I saw their fathers like the firstfruits of the fig tree in the top thereof: but they went in to Beelphegor, and alienated themselves to that confusion, and became abominable, as those things were, which they loved.
verses.textLatin: Quasi uvas in deserto inveni Israël, quasi prima poma ficulneæ in cacumine ejus vidi patres eorum: ipsi autem intraverunt ad Beelphegor, et abalienati sunt in confusionem, et facti sunt abominabiles sicut ea quæ dilexerunt.

verses.text: As for Ephraim, their glory hath flown away like a bird from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim quasi avis avolavit; gloria eorum a partu, et ab utero, et a conceptu.

verses.text: And though they should bring up their children, I will make them without children among men: yea, and woe to them, when I shall depart from them.
verses.textLatin: Quod etsi enutrierint filios suos, absque liberis eos faciam in hominibus; sed et væ eis cum recessero ab eis!

verses.text: Ephraim, as I saw, was a Tyre founded in beauty: and Ephraim shall bring out his children to the murderer.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim, ut vidi, Tyrus erat fundata in pulchritudine; et Ephraim educet ad interfectorem filios suos.

verses.text: Give them, O Lord. What wilt thou give them? Give them a womb without children, and dry breasts.
verses.textLatin: Da eis, Domine. Quid dabis eis? da eis vulvam sine liberis, et ubera arentia.

verses.text: All their wickedness is in Galgal, for there I hated them: for the wickedness of their devices I will cast them forth out of my house: I will love them no more, all their princes are revolters.
verses.textLatin: Omnes nequitiæ eorum in Galgal, quia ibi exosos habui eos. Propter malitiam adinventionum eorum, de domo mea ejiciam eos; non addam ut diligam eos: omnes principes eorum recedentes.

verses.text: Ephraim is struck, their root is dried up, they shall yield no fruit. And if they should have issue, I will slay the best beloved fruit of their womb.
verses.textLatin: Percussus est Ephraim; radix eorum exsiccata est: fructum nequaquam facient, quod etsi genuerint, interficiam amantissima uteri eorum.

verses.text: My God will cast them away, because they hearkened not to him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.
verses.textLatin: Abjiciet eos Deus meus, quia non audierunt eum, et erunt vagi in nationibus.

verses.text: Israel  a vine full of branches, the fruit is agreeable to it: according to the multitude of his fruit he hath multiplied altars, according to the plenty of his land he hath abounded with idols.
verses.textLatin: Vitis frondosa Israël, fructus adæquatus est ei: secundum multitudinem fructus sui multiplicavit altaria, juxta ubertatem terræ suæ exuberavit simulacris.

verses.text: Their heart is divided: now they shall perish: he shall break down their idols, he shall destroy their altars.
verses.textLatin: Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt; ipse confringet simulacra eorum, depopulabitur aras eorum.

verses.text: For now they shall say: We have no king: because we fear not the Lord: and what shall a king do to us?
verses.textLatin: Quia nunc dicent: Non est rex nobis, non enim timemus Dominum; et rex quid faciet nobis?

verses.text: You speak words of an unprofitable vision, and you shall make a covenant: and judgment shall spring up as bitterness in the furrows of the field.
verses.textLatin: Loquimini verba visionis inutilis, et ferietis fœdus; et germinabit quasi amaritudo judicium super sulcos agri.

verses.text: The inhabitants of Samaria have worshipped the kine of Bethaven: for the people thereof have mourned over it, and the wardens of its temple that rejoiced over it in its glory because it is departed from it.
verses.textLatin: Vaccas Bethaven coluerunt habitatores Samariæ; quia luxit super eum populus ejus, et æditui ejus super eum exsultaverunt in gloria ejus, quia migravit ab eo.

verses.text: For itself also is carried into Assyria, a present to the avenging king: shame shall fall upon Ephraim, and Israel shall be confounded in his own will.
verses.textLatin: Siquidem et ipse in Assur delatus est, munus regi ultori. Confusio Ephraim capiet, et confundetur Israël in voluntate sua.

verses.text: Samaria hath made her king to pass as froth upon the face of the water.
verses.textLatin: Transire fecit Samaria regem suum quasi spumam super faciem aquæ.

verses.text: And the high places of the idol, the sin of Israel shall be destroyed: the bur and the thistle shall grow up over their altars: and they shall say to the mountains: Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us.
verses.textLatin: Et disperdentur excelsa idoli, peccatum Israël; lappa et tribulus ascendet super aras eorum: et dicent montibus: Operite nos, et collibus: Cadite super nos.

verses.text: From the days of Gabaa, Israel hath sinned, there they stood: the battle in Gabaa against the children of iniquity shall not overtake them.
verses.textLatin: Ex diebus Gabaa peccavit Israël; ibi steterunt. Non comprehendet eos in Gabaa prælium super filios iniquitatis.

verses.text: According to my desire I will chastise them: and the nations shall be gathered together against them, when they shall be chastised for their two iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Juxta desiderium meum corripiam eos: congregabuntur super eos populi, cum corripientur propter duas iniquitates suas.

verses.text: Ephraim is a heifer taught to love to tread out corn, but I passed over upon the beauty of her neck: I will ride upon Ephraim, Juda shall plough, Jacob shall break the furrows for himself.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim vitula docta diligere trituram, et ego transivi super pulchritudinem colli ejus: ascendam super Ephraim, arabit Judas; confringet sibi sulcos Jacob.

verses.text: Sow for yourselves in justice, and reap in the mouth of mercy, break up your fallow ground: but the time to seek the Lord is, when he shall come that shall teach you justice.
verses.textLatin: Seminate vobis in justitia, et metite in ore misericordiæ. Innovate vobis novale; tempus autem requirendi Dominum, cum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam.

verses.text: You have ploughed wickedness, you have reaped iniquity, you have eaten the fruit of lying: because thou hast trusted in thy ways, in the multitude of thy strong ones.
verses.textLatin: Arastis impietatem, iniquitatem messuistis: comedistis frugem mendacii, quia confisus es in viis tuis, in multitudine fortium tuorum.

verses.text: A tumult shall arise among thy people: and all thy fortresses shall be destroyed as Salmana was destroyed, by the house of him that judged Baal in the day of battle, the mother being dashed in pieces upon her children.
verses.textLatin: Consurget tumultus in populo tuo; et omnes munitiones tuæ vastabuntur, sicut vastatus est Salmana a domo ejus qui judicavit Baal in die prælii, matre super filios allisa.

verses.text: So hath Bethel done to you, because of the evil of your iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Sic fecit vobis Bethel, a facie malitiæ nequitiarum vestrarum.

verses.text: As the morning passeth, so hath the king of Israel passed away. Because Israel was a child, and I loved him: and I called my son out of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Sicut mane transiit, pertransiit rex Israël. Quia puer Israël, et dilexi eum; et ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum.

verses.text: As they called them, they went away from before their face: they offered victims to Baalim, and sacrificed to idols.
verses.textLatin: Vocaverunt eos, sic abierunt a facie eorum; Baalim immolabant, et simulacris sacrificabant.

verses.text: And I was like a foster father to Ephraim, I carried them in my arms: and they knew not that I healed them.
verses.textLatin: Et ego quasi nutritius Ephraim: portabam eos in brachiis meis, et nescierunt quod curarem eos.

verses.text: I will draw them with the cords of Adam, with the bands of love: and I will be to them as one that taketh off the yoke on their jaws: and I put his meat to him that he might eat.
verses.textLatin: In funiculis Adam traham eos, in vinculis caritatis; et ero eis quasi exaltans jugum super maxillas eorum, et declinavi ad eum ut vesceretur.

verses.text: He shall not return into the land of Egypt, but the Assyrian shall be his king: because they would not be converted.
verses.textLatin: Non revertetur in terram Ægypti, et Assur ipse rex ejus, quoniam noluerunt converti.

verses.text: The sword hath begun in his cities, and it shall consume his chosen men, and shall devour their heads.
verses.textLatin: Cœpit gladius in civitatibus ejus, et consumet electos ejus, et comedet capita eorum.

verses.text: And my people shall long for my return: but a yoke shall be put upon them together, which shall not be taken off.
verses.textLatin: Et populus meus pendebit ad reditum meum; jugum autem imponetur eis simul, quod non auferetur.

verses.text: How shall I deal with thee, O Ephraim, shall I protect thee, O Israel? how shall I make thee as Adama, shall I set thee as Seboim? my heart is turned within me, my repentance is stirred up.
verses.textLatin: Quomodo dabo te, Ephraim? protegam te, Israël? Quomodo dabo te sicut Adama, ponam te ut Seboim? Conversum est in me cor meum, pariter conturbata est pœnitudo mea.

verses.text: I will not execute the fierceness of my wrath: I will not return to destroy Ephraim: because I am God, and not man: the holy one in the midst of thee, and I will not enter into the city.
verses.textLatin: Non faciam furorem iræ meæ; non convertar ut disperdam Ephraim, quoniam Deus ego, et non homo; in medio tui sanctus, et non ingrediar civitatem.

verses.text: They shall walk after the Lord, he shall roar as a lion: because he shall roar, and the children of the sea shall fear.
verses.textLatin: Post Dominum ambulabunt; quasi leo rugiet, quia ipse rugiet, et formidabunt filii maris.

verses.text: And they shall fly away like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of the Assyrians: and I will place them in their own houses, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et avolabunt quasi avis ex Ægypto, et quasi columba de terra Assyriorum: et collocabo eos in domibus suis, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Ephraim hath compassed me about with denials, and the house of Israel with deceit: but Juda went down as a witness with God, and is faithful with the saints.
verses.textLatin: Circumdedit me in negatione Ephraim, et in dolo domus Israël; Judas autem testis descendit cum Deo, et cum sanctis fidelis.

verses.text: Ephraim  feedeth on the wind, and followeth the burning heat: all the day long he multiplied lies and desolation: and he hath made a covenant with the Assyrians, and carried oil into Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim pascit ventum, et sequitur æstum; tota die mendacium et vastitatem multiplicat: et fœdus cum Assyriis iniit, et oleum in Ægyptum ferebat.

verses.text: Therefore there is a judgment of the Lord with Juda, and a visitation for Jacob: he will render to him according to his ways, and according to his devices.
verses.textLatin: Judicium ergo Domini cum Juda, et visitatio super Jacob: juxta vias ejus, et juxta adinventiones ejus reddet ei.

verses.text: In the womb he supplanted his brother: and by his strength he had success with an angel.
verses.textLatin: In utero supplantavit fratrem suum, et in fortitudine sua directus est cum angelo.

verses.text: And he prevailed over the angel, and was strengthened: he wept, and made supplication to him: he found him in Bethel, and there he spoke with us.
verses.textLatin: Et invaluit ad angelum, et confortatus est; flevit, et rogavit eum. In Bethel invenit eum, et ibi locutus est nobiscum.

verses.text: Even the Lord the God of hosts, the Lord is his memorial.
verses.textLatin: Et Dominus Deus exercituum, Dominus memoriale ejus.

verses.text: Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and judgment, and hope in thy God always.
verses.textLatin: Et tu ad Deum tuum converteris; misericordiam et judicium custodi, et spera in Deo tuo semper.

verses.text: He is like Chanaan, there is a deceitful balance in his hand, he hath loved oppression.
verses.textLatin: Chanaan, in manu ejus statera dolosa, calumniam dilexit.

verses.text: And Ephraim said: But yet I am become rich, I have found me an idol: all my labours shall not find me the iniquity that I have committed.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Ephraim: Verumtamen dives effectus sum; inveni idolum mihi: omnes labores mei non invenient mihi iniquitatem quam peccavi.

verses.text: And I that am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, will yet cause thee to dwell in tabernacles, as in the days of the feast.
verses.textLatin: Et ego Dominus Deus tuus ex terra Ægypti: adhuc sedere te faciam in tabernaculis, sicut in diebus festivitatis.

verses.text: And I have spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and I have used similitudes by the ministry of the prophets.
verses.textLatin: Et locutus sum super prophetas, et ego visionem multiplicavi, et in manu prophetarum assimilatus sum.

verses.text: If Galaad be an idol, then in vain were they in Galgal offering sacrifices with bullocks: for their altars also are as heaps in the furrows of the field.
verses.textLatin: Si Galaad idolum, ergo frustra erant in Galgal bobus immolantes; nam et altaria eorum quasi acervi super sulcos agri.

verses.text: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and was a keeper for a wife.
verses.textLatin: Fugit Jacob in regionem Syriæ, et servivit Israël in uxorem, et in uxorem servavit.

verses.text: But the Lord by a prophet brought Israel out of Egypt: and he was preserved by a prophet.
verses.textLatin: In propheta autem eduxit Dominus Israël de Ægypto, et in propheta servatus est.

verses.text: Ephraim hath provoked me to wrath with his bitterness, and his blood shall come upon him, and his Lord will render his reproach unto him.
verses.textLatin: Ad iracundiam me provocavit Ephraim in amaritudinibus suis: et sanguis ejus super eum veniet, et opprobrium ejus restituet ei Dominus suus.

verses.text: When  Ephraim spoke, a horror seized Israel: and he sinned in Baal and died.
verses.textLatin: Loquente Ephraim, horror invasit Israël; et deliquit in Baal, et mortuus est.

verses.text: And now they have sinned more and more: and they have made to themselves a molten thing of their silver as the likeness of idols: the whole is the work of craftsmen: to these that say: Sacrifice men, ye that adore calves.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc addiderunt ad peccandum; feceruntque sibi conflatile de argento suo quasi similitudinem idolorum: factura artificum totum est: his ipsi dicunt: Immolate homines, vitulos adorantes.

verses.text: Therefore they shall be as a morning cloud, and as the early dew that passeth away, as the dust that is driven with a whirlwind out of the floor, and as the smoke out of the chimney.
verses.textLatin: Idcirco erunt quasi nubes matutina, et sicut ros matutinus præteriens; sicut pulvis turbine raptus ex area, et sicut fumus de fumario.

verses.text: But I am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt: and thou shalt know no God but me, and there is no saviour beside me.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem Dominus Deus tuus, ex terra Ægypti; et Deum absque me nescies, et salvator non est præter me.

verses.text: I knew thee in the desert, in the land of the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Ego cognovi te in deserto, in terra solitudinis.

verses.text: According to their pastures they were filled, and were made full: and they lifted up their heart, and have forgotten me.
verses.textLatin: Juxta pascua sua adimpleti sunt et saturati sunt; et levaverunt cor suum, et obliti sunt mei.

verses.text: And I will be to them as a lioness, as a leopard in the way of the Assyrians.
verses.textLatin: Et ego ero eis quasi leæna, sicut pardus in via Assyriorum.

verses.text: I will meet them as a bear that is robbed of her whelps, and I will rend the inner parts of their liver: and I will devour them there as a lion, the beast of the field shall tear them.
verses.textLatin: Occurram eis quasi ursa raptis catulis, et dirumpam interiora jecoris eorum, et consumam eos ibi quasi leo: bestia agri scindet eos.

verses.text: Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me.
verses.textLatin: Perditio tua, Israël: tantummodo in me auxilium tuum.

verses.text: Where is thy king? now especially let him save thee in all thy cities: and thy judges, of whom thou saidst: Give me kings and princes.
verses.textLatin: Ubi est rex tuus? maxime nunc salvet te in omnibus urbibus tuis; et judices tui, de quibus dixisti: Da mihi regem et principes.

verses.text: I will give thee a king in my wrath, and will take him away in my indignation.
verses.textLatin: Dabo tibi regem in furore meo, et auferam in indignatione mea.

verses.text: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up, his sin is hidden.
verses.textLatin: Colligata est iniquitas Ephraim; absconditum peccatum ejus.

verses.text: The sorrows of a woman in labour shall come upon him, he is an unwise son: for now he shall not stand in the breach of the children.
verses.textLatin: Dolores parturientis venient ei: ipse filius non sapiens: nunc enim non stabit in contritione filiorum.

verses.text: I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite: comfort is hidden from my eyes.
verses.textLatin: De manu mortis liberabo eos; de morte redimam eos. Ero mors tua, o mors! morsus tuus ero, inferne! consolatio abscondita est ab oculis meis.

verses.text: Because he shall make a separation between brothers: the Lord will bring a burning wind that shall rise from the desert, and it shall dry up his springs, and shall make his fountain desolate, and he shall carry off the treasure of every desirable vessel.
verses.textLatin: Quia ipse inter fratres dividet: adducet urentem ventum Dominus de deserto ascendentem, et siccabit venas ejus, et desolabit fontem ejus: et ipse diripiet thesaurum omnis vasis desiderabilis.

verses.text: Let Samaria perish, because she hath stirred up her God to bitterness: let them perish by the sword, let their little ones be dashed, and let the women with child be ripped up.
verses.textLatin: Pereat Samaria, quoniam ad amaritudinem concitavit Deum suum! in gladio pereant, parvuli eorum elidantur, et fœtæ ejus discindantur!

verses.text: Return, O Israel, to the Lord thy God: for thou hast fallen down by thy iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Convertere, Israël, ad Dominum Deum tuum, quoniam corruisti in iniquitate tua.

verses.text: Take with you words, and return to the Lord, and say to him: Take away all iniquity, and receive the good: and we will render the calves of our lips.
verses.textLatin: Tollite vobiscum verba, et convertimini ad Dominum; et dicite ei: Omnem aufer iniquitatem, accipe bonum, et reddemus vitulos labiorum nostrorum.

verses.text: Assyria shall not save us, we will not ride upon horses, neither will we say any more: The works of our hands are our gods, for thou wilt have mercy on the fatherless that is in thee.
verses.textLatin: Assur non salvabit nos: super equum non ascendemus, nec dicemus ultra, Dii nostri opera manuum nostrarum: quia ejus, qui in te est, misereberis pupilli.

verses.text: I will heal their breaches, I will love them freely: for my wrath is turned away from them.
verses.textLatin: Sanabo contritiones eorum; diligam eos spontanee: quia aversus est furor meus ab eis.

verses.text: I will be as the dew, Israel shall spring as the lily, and his root shall shoot forth as that of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Ero quasi ros; Israël germinabit sicut lilium, et erumpet radix ejus ut Libani.

verses.text: His branches shall spread, and his glory shall be as the olive tree: and his smell as that of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Ibunt rami ejus, et erit quasi oliva gloria ejus, et odor ejus ut Libani.

verses.text: They shall be converted that sit under his shadow: they shall live upon wheat, and they shall blossom as a vine: his memorial shall be as the wine of Libanus.
verses.textLatin: Convertentur sedentes in umbra ejus; vivent tritico, et germinabunt quasi vinea; memoriale ejus sicut vinum Libani.

verses.text: Ephraim shall say, What have I to do any more with idols? I will hear him, and I will make him flourish like a green fir tree: from me is thy fruit found.
verses.textLatin: Ephraim, quid mihi ultra idola? Ego exaudiam, et dirigam eum ego ut abietem virentem; ex me fructus tuus inventus est.

verses.text: Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know these things? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall in them.
verses.textLatin: Quis sapiens, et intelliget ista? intelligens, et sciet hæc? quia rectæ viæ Domini, et justi ambulabunt in eis; prævaricatores vero corruent in eis.

verses.text: The word of the Lord, that came to Joel, the son of Phatuel.
verses.textLatin: Verbum Domini, quod factum est ad Joël, filium Phatuel.

verses.text: Hear this, ye old men, and give ear, all ye inhabitants of the land: did this ever happen in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
verses.textLatin: Audite hoc, senes, et auribus percipite, omnes habitatores terræ: si factum est istud in diebus vestris, aut in diebus patrum vestrorum?

verses.text: Tell ye of this to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children to another generation.
verses.textLatin: Super hoc filiis vestris narrate, et filii vestri filiis suis, et filii eorum generationi alteræ.

verses.text: That which the palmerworm hath left, the locust hath eaten: and that which the locust hath left, the bruchus hath eaten: and that which the bruchus hath left, the mildew hath destroyed.
verses.textLatin: Residuum erucæ comedit locusta, et residuum locustæ comedit bruchus, et residuum bruchi comedit rubigo.

verses.text: Awake, ye that are drunk, and weep, and mourn all ye that take delight in drinking sweet wine: for it is cut off from your mouth.
verses.textLatin: Expergiscimini, ebrii, et flete et ululate, omnes qui bibitis vinum in dulcedine, quoniam periit ab ore vestro.

verses.text: For a nation come up upon my land, strong and without number: his teeth are like the teeth of a lion: and his cheek teeth as of a lion’s whelp.
verses.textLatin: Gens enim ascendit super terram meam, fortis et innumerabilis: dentes ejus ut dentes leonis, et molares ejus ut catuli leonis.

verses.text: He hath laid my vineyard waste, and hath pilled off the bark of my fig tree: he hath stripped it bare, and cast it away; the branches thereof are made white.
verses.textLatin: Posuit vineam meam in desertum, et ficum meam decorticavit; nudans spoliavit eam, et projecit: albi facti sunt rami ejus.

verses.text: Lament like a virgin girded with sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
verses.textLatin: Plange quasi virgo accincta sacco super virum pubertatis suæ.

verses.text: Sacrifice and libation is cut off from the house of the Lord: the priests, the Lord’s ministers, have mourned:
verses.textLatin: Periit sacrificium et libatio de domo Domini; luxerunt sacerdotes, ministri Domini.

verses.text: The country is destroyed, the ground hath mourned: for the corn is wasted, the wine is confounded, the oil hath languished.
verses.textLatin: Depopulata est regio, luxit humus, quoniam devastatum est triticum, confusum est vinum, elanguit oleum.

verses.text: The husbandmen are ashamed, the vinedressers have howled for the wheat, and for the barley, because the harvest of the field is perished.
verses.textLatin: Confusi sunt agricolæ, ululaverunt vinitores super frumento et hordeo, quia periit messis agri.

verses.text: The vineyard is confounded, and the fig tree hath languished: the pomegranate tree, and the palm tree, and the apple tree, and all the trees of the field are withered: because joy is withdrawn from the children of men.
verses.textLatin: Vinea confusa est, et ficus elanguit; malogranatum, et palma, et malum, et omnia ligna agri aruerunt, quia confusum est gaudium a filiis hominum.

verses.text: Gird yourselves, and lament, O ye priests, howl, ye ministers of the altars: go in, lie in sackcloth, ye ministers of my God: because sacrifice and libation is cut off from the house of your God.
verses.textLatin: Accingite vos, et plangite, sacerdotes: ululate, ministri altaris; ingredimini, cubate in sacco, ministri Dei mei, quoniam interiit de domo Dei vestri sacrificium et libatio.

verses.text: Sanctify ye a fast, call an assembly; gather together the ancients, all the inhabitants of the land into the house of your God: and cry ye to the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Sanctificate jejunium, vocate cœtum, congregate senes, omnes habitatores terræ in domum Dei vestri, et clamate ad Dominum:

verses.text: Ah, ah, ah, for the day: because the day of the Lord is at hand, and it shall come like destruction from the mighty.
verses.textLatin: A, a, a, diei! quia prope est dies Domini, et quasi vastitas a potente veniet.

verses.text: Is not your food cut off before your eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non coram oculis vestris alimenta perierunt de domo Dei nostri, lætitia et exsultatio?

verses.text: The beasts have rotted in their dung, the barns are destroyed, the storehouses are broken down: because the corn is confounded.
verses.textLatin: Computruerunt jumenta in stercore suo, demolita sunt horrea, dissipatæ sunt apothecæ, quoniam confusum est triticum.

verses.text: Why did the beasts groan, why did the herds of cattle low? because there is no pasture for them: yea, and the flocks of sheep are perished.
verses.textLatin: Quid ingemuit animal, mugierunt greges armenti? quia non est pascua eis; sed et greges pecorum disperierunt.

verses.text: To thee, O Lord, will I cry: because fire hath devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness: and the flame hath burnt all the trees of the country.
verses.textLatin: Ad te, Domine, clamabo, quia ignis comedit speciosa deserti, et flamma succendit omnia ligna regionis.

verses.text: Yea, and the beasts of the field have looked up to thee, as a garden bed that thirsteth after rain, for the springs of waters are dried up, and fire hath devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.
verses.textLatin: Sed et bestiæ agri, quasi area sitiens imbrem, suspexerunt ad te, quoniam exsiccati sunt fontes aquarum, et ignis devoravit speciosa deserti.

verses.text: Blow ye the trumpet in Sion, sound an alarm in my holy mountain, let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: because the day of the Lord cometh, because it is nigh at hand.
verses.textLatin: Canite tuba in Sion, ululate in monte sancto meo, conturbentur omnes habitatores terræ: quia venit dies Domini, quia prope est.

verses.text: A day of darkness, and of gloominess, a day of clouds and whirlwinds: a numerous and strong people as the morning spread upon the mountains: the like to it hath not been from the beginning, nor shall be after it even to the years of generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nubis et turbinis; quasi mane expansum super montes populus multus et fortis: similis ei non fuit a principio, et post eum non erit usque in annos generationis et generationis.

verses.text: Before the face thereof a devouring fire, and behind it a burning flame: the land is like a garden of pleasure before it, and behind it a desolate wilderness, neither is there any one that can escape it.
verses.textLatin: Ante faciem ejus ignis vorans, et post eum exurens flamma. Quasi hortus voluptatis terra coram eo, et post eum solitudo deserti, neque est qui effugiat eum.

verses.text: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses, and they shall run like horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Quasi aspectus equorum, aspectus eorum; et quasi equites, sic current.

verses.text: They shall leap like the noise of chariots upon the tops of mountains, like the noise of a flame of fire devouring the stubble, as a strong people prepared to battle.
verses.textLatin: Sicut sonitus quadrigarum super capita montium exilient, sicut sonitus flammæ ignis devorantis stipulam, velut populus fortis præparatus ad prælium.

verses.text: At their presence the people shall be in grievous pains: all faces shall be made like a kettle.
verses.textLatin: A facie ejus cruciabuntur populi; omnes vultus redigentur in ollam.

verses.text: They shall run like valiant men: like men of war they shall scale the wall: the men shall march every one on his way, and they shall not turn aside from their ranks.
verses.textLatin: Sicut fortes current; quasi viri bellatores ascendent murum: viri in viis suis gradientur, et non declinabunt a semitis suis.

verses.text: No one shall press upon his brother: they shall walk every one in his path: yea, and they shall fall through the windows, and shall take no harm.
verses.textLatin: Unusquisque fratrem suum non coarctabit, singuli in calle suo ambulabunt; sed et per fenestras cadent, et non demolientur.

verses.text: They shall enter into the city: they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up the houses, they shall come in at the windows as a thief.
verses.textLatin: Urbem ingredientur, in muro current, domos conscendent, per fenestras intrabunt quasi fur.

verses.text: At their presence the earth hath trembled, the heavens are moved: the sun and moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining.
verses.textLatin: A facie ejus contremuit terra, moti sunt cæli, sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum.

verses.text: And the Lord hath uttered his voice before the face of his army: for his armies are exceedingly great, for they are strong and execute his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible: and who can stand it?
verses.textLatin: Et Dominus dedit vocem suam ante faciem exercitus sui, quia multa sunt nimis castra ejus, quia fortia et facientia verbum ejus: magnus enim dies Domini, et terribilis valde, et quis sustinebit eum?

verses.text: Now therefore saith the Lord: Be converted to me with all your heart, in fasting, and in weeping, and in mourning.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, dicit Dominus, convertimini ad me in toto corde vestro, in jejunio, et in fletu, et in planctu.

verses.text: And rend your hearts, and not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, patient and rich in mercy, and ready to repent of the evil.
verses.textLatin: Et scindite corda vestra, et non vestimenta vestra; et convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrum, quia benignus et misericors est, patiens et multæ misericordiæ, et præstabilis super malitia.

verses.text: Who knoweth but he will return, and forgive, and leave a blessing behind him, sacrifice and libation to the Lord your God?
verses.textLatin: Quis scit si convertatur, et ignoscat, et relinquat post se benedictionem, sacrificium et libamen Domino Deo vestro?

verses.text: Blow the trumpet in Sion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly,
verses.textLatin: Canite tuba in Sion, sanctificate jejunium, vocate cœtum:

verses.text: Gather together the people, sanctify the church, assemble the ancients, gather together the little ones, and them that suck at the breasts: let the bridegroom go forth from his bed, and the bride out of her bride chamber.
verses.textLatin: congregate populum, sanctificate ecclesiam, coadunate senes, congregate parvulos, et sugentes ubera; egrediatur sponsus de cubili suo, et sponsa de thalamo suo.

verses.text: Between the porch and the altar the priests the Lord’s ministers shall weep, and shall say: Spare, O Lord, spare thy people: and give not thy inheritance to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them. Why should they say among the nations: Where is their God?
verses.textLatin: Inter vestibulum et altare plorabunt sacerdotes, ministri Domini, et dicent: Parce, Domine, parce populo tuo; et ne des hæreditatem tuam in opprobrium, ut dominentur eis nationes. Quare dicunt in populis: Ubi est Deus eorum?

verses.text: The Lord hath been zealous for his land, and hath spared his people.
verses.textLatin: Zelatus est Dominus terram suam, et pepercit populo suo.

verses.text: And the Lord answered and said to his people: Behold I will send you corn, and wine, and oil, and you shall be filled with them: and I will no more make you a reproach among the nations.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Dominus, et dixit populo suo: Ecce ego mittam vobis frumentum, et vinum, et oleum, et replebimini eis; et non dabo vos ultra opprobrium in gentibus.

verses.text: And I will remove far off from you the northern enemy: and I will drive him into a land unpassable, and desert, with his face towards the east sea, and his hinder part towards the utmost sea: and his stench shall ascend, and his rottenness shall go up, because he hath done proudly.
verses.textLatin: Et eum qui ab aquilone est procul faciam a vobis, et expellam eum in terram inviam et desertam: faciem ejus contra mare orientale, et extremum ejus ad mare novissimum: et ascendet fœtor ejus, et ascendet putredo ejus, quia superbe egit.

verses.text: Fear not, O land, be glad and rejoice: for the Lord hath done great things.
verses.textLatin: Noli timere, terra: exsulta, et lætare, quoniam magnificavit Dominus ut faceret.

verses.text: Fear not, ye beasts of the fields: for the beautiful places of the wilderness are sprung, for the tree hath brought forth its fruit, the fig tree, and the vine have yielded their strength.
verses.textLatin: Nolite timere, animalia regionis, quia germinaverunt speciosa deserti; quia lignum attulit fructum suum, ficus et vinea dederunt virtutem suam.

verses.text: And you, O children of Sion, rejoice, and be joyful in the Lord your God: because he hath given you a teacher of justice, and he will make the early and the latter rain to come down to you as in the beginning.
verses.textLatin: Et, filii Sion, exsultate, et lætamini in Domino Deo vestro, quia dedit vobis doctorem justitiæ, et descendere faciet ad vos imbrem matutinum et serotinum, sicut in principio.

verses.text: And the floors shall be filled with wheat, and the presses shall overflow with wine and oil.
verses.textLatin: Et implebuntur areæ frumento, et redundabunt torcularia vino et oleo.

verses.text: And I will restore to you the years which the locust, and the bruchus, and the mildew, and the palmerworm have eaten; my great host which I sent upon you.
verses.textLatin: Et reddam vobis annos, quos comedit locusta, bruchus, et rubigo, et eruca: fortitudo mea magna quam misi in vos.

verses.text: And you shall eat in plenty, and shall be filled: and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God, who hath done wonders with you, and my people shall not be confounded for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et comedetis vescentes, et saturabimini; et laudabitis nomen Domini Dei vestri, qui fecit mirabilia vobiscum; et non confundetur populus meus in sempiternum.

verses.text: And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel: and I am the Lord your God, and there is none besides: and my people shall not be confounded for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et scietis quia in medio Israël ego sum, et ego Dominus Deus vester, et non est amplius; et non confundetur populus meus in æternum.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass after this, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy: your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
verses.textLatin: Et erit post hæc: effundam spiritum meum super omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii vestri et filiæ vestræ: senes vestri somnia somniabunt, et juvenes vestri visiones videbunt.

verses.text: Moreover upon my servants and handmaids in those days I will pour forth my spirit.
verses.textLatin: Sed et super servos meos et ancillas in diebus illis effundam spiritum meum.

verses.text: And I will shew wonders in heaven; and in earth, blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke.
verses.textLatin: Et dabo prodigia in cælo et in terra, sanguinem, et ignem, et vaporem fumi.

verses.text: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood: before the great and dreadful day of the Lord doth come.
verses.textLatin: Sol convertetur in tenebras, et luna in sanguinem, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass, that every one that shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved: for in mount Sion, and in Jerusalem shall be salvation, as the Lord hath said, and in the residue whom the Lord shall call.
verses.textLatin: Et erit: omnis qui invocaverit nomen Domini, salvus erit: quia in monte Sion et in Jerusalem erit salvatio, sicut dixit Dominus, et in residuis quos Dominus vocaverit.

verses.text: For  behold in those days, and in that time when I shall bring back the captivity of Juda and Jerusalem:
verses.textLatin: Quia ecce in diebus illis, et in tempore illo, cum convertero captivitatem Juda et Jerusalem,

verses.text: I will gather together all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Josaphat: and I will plead with them there for my people, and for my inheritance Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and have parted my land.
verses.textLatin: congregabo omnes gentes, et deducam eas in vallem Josaphat; et disceptabo cum eis ibi super populo meo, et hæreditate mea Israël, quos disperserunt in nationibus, et terram meam diviserunt.

verses.text: And they have cast lots upon my people: and the boy they have put in the stews, and the girl they have sold for wine, that they might drink.
verses.textLatin: Et super populum meum miserunt sortem; et posuerunt puerum in prostibulo, et puellam vendiderunt pro vino ut biberent.

verses.text: But what have you to do with me, O Tyre, and Sidon, and all the coast of the Philistines? will you revenge yourselves on me? and if you revenge yourselves on me, I will very soon return you a recompense upon your own head.
verses.textLatin: Verum quid mihi et vobis, Tyrus et Sidon, et omnis terminus Palæstinorum? numquid ultionem vos reddetis mihi? et si ulciscimini vos contra me, cito velociter reddam vicissitudinem vobis super caput vestrum.

verses.text: For you have taken away my silver and my gold: and my desirable and most beautiful things you have carried into your temples.
verses.textLatin: Argentum enim meum et aurum tulistis, et desiderabilia mea et pulcherrima intulistis in delubra vestra.

verses.text: And the children of Juda, and the children of Jerusalem you have sold to the children of the Greeks, that you might remove them far off from their own country.
verses.textLatin: Et filios Juda et filios Jerusalem vendidistis filiis Græcorum, ut longe faceretis eos de finibus suis.

verses.text: Behold, I will raise them up out of the place wherein you have sold them: and I will return your recompense upon your own heads.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego suscitabo eos de loco in quo vendidistis eos, et convertam retributionem vestram in caput vestrum.

verses.text: And I will sell your sons, and your daughters by the hands of the children of Juda, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, a nation far off, for the Lord hath spoken it.
verses.textLatin: Et vendam filios vestros et filias vestras in manibus filiorum Juda, et venundabunt eos Sabæis, genti longinquæ, quia Dominus locutus est.

verses.text: Proclaim ye this among the nations: prepare war, rouse up the strong: let them come, let all the men of war come up.
verses.textLatin: Clamate hoc in gentibus, sanctificate bellum, suscitate robustos: accedant, ascendant omnes viri bellatores.

verses.text: Cut your ploughshares into swords, and your spades into spears. Let the weak say: I am strong.
verses.textLatin: Concidite aratra vestra in gladios, et ligones vestros in lanceas. Infirmus dicat: Quia fortis ego sum.

verses.text: Break forth, and come, all ye nations, from round about, and gather yourselves together: there will the Lord cause all thy strong ones to fall down.
verses.textLatin: Erumpite, et venite, omnes gentes de circuitu, et congregamini; ibi occumbere faciet Dominus robustos tuos.

verses.text: Let them arise, and let the nations come up into the valley of Josaphat: for there I will sit to judge all nations round about.
verses.textLatin: Consurgant, et ascendant gentes in vallem Josaphat, quia ibi sedebo ut judicem omnes gentes in circuitu.

verses.text: Put ye in the sickles, for the harvest is ripe: come and go down, for the press is full, the fats run over: for their wickedness is multiplied.
verses.textLatin: Mittite falces, quoniam maturavit messis; venite, et descendite, quia plenum est torcular, exuberant torcularia: quia multiplicata est malitia eorum.

verses.text: Nations, nations in the valley of destruction: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of destruction.
verses.textLatin: Populi, populi, in valle concisionis, quia juxta est dies Domini in valle concisionis.

verses.text: The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars have withdrawn their shining.
verses.textLatin: Sol et luna obtenebrati sunt, et stellæ retraxerunt splendorem suum.

verses.text: And the Lord shall roar out of Sion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem: and the heavens and the earth shall be moved, and the Lord shall be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et Dominus de Sion rugiet, et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam, et movebuntur cæli et terra; et Dominus spes populi sui, et fortitudo filiorum Israël.

verses.text: And you shall know that I am the Lord your God, dwelling in Sion my holy mountain: and Jerusalem shall be holy and strangers shall pass through it no more.
verses.textLatin: Et scietis quia ego Dominus Deus vester, habitans in Sion monte sancto meo; et erit Jerusalem sancta, et alieni non transibunt per eam amplius.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the mountains shall drop down sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk: and waters shall flow through all the rivers of Juda: and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord, and shall water the torrent of thorns.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa: stillabunt montes dulcedinem, et colles fluent lacte, et per omnes rivos Juda ibunt aquæ; et fons de domo Domini egredietur, et irrigabit torrentem spinarum.

verses.text: Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom a wilderness destroyed: because they have done unjustly against the children of Juda, and have shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.textLatin: Ægyptus in desolationem erit, et Idumæa in desertum perditionis, pro eo quod inique egerint in filios Juda, et effuderint sanguinem innocentem in terra sua.

verses.text: And Judea shall be inhabited for ever, and Jerusalem to generation and generation.
verses.textLatin: Et Judæa in æternum habitabitur, et Jerusalem in generationem et generationem.

verses.text: And I will cleanse their blood which I had not cleansed: and the Lord will dwell in Sion.
verses.textLatin: Et mundabo sanguinem eorum, quem non mundaveram; et Dominus commorabitur in Sion.

verses.text: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Thecua: which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Ozias king of Juda, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joas king of Israel two years before the earthquake.
verses.textLatin: Verba Amos, qui fuit in pastoribus de Thecue, quæ vidit super Israël in diebus Oziæ, regis Juda, et in diebus Jeroboam, filii Joas, regis Israël, ante duos annos terræmotus.

verses.text: And he said: The Lord will roar from Sion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem: and the beautiful places of the shepherds have mourned, and the top of Carmel is withered.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Dominus de Sion rugiet, et de Jerusalem dabit vocem suam; et luxerunt speciosa pastorum, et exsiccatus est vertex Carmeli.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Damascus, and for four I will not convert it: because they have thrashed Galaad with iron wains.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Damasci, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod trituraverint in plaustris ferreis Galaad.

verses.text: And I will send a fire into the house of Azael, and it shall devour the houses of Benadad.
verses.textLatin: Et mittam ignem in domum Azaël, et devorabit domos Benadad.

verses.text: And I will break the bar of Damascus: and I will cut off the inhabitants from the plain of the idol, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of pleasure: and the people of Syria shall be carried away to Cyrene, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et conteram vectem Damasci: et disperdam habitatorem de campo idoli, et tenentem sceptrum de domo voluptatis: et transferetur populus Syriæ Cyrenen, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Gaza, and for four I will not convert it: because they have carried away a perfect captivity to shut them up in Edom.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Gazæ, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod transtulerint captivitatem perfectam, ut concluderent eam in Idumæa.

verses.text: And I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, and it shall devour the houses thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et mittam ignem in murum Gazæ, et devorabit ædes ejus.

verses.text: And I will cut off the inhabitant from Azotus, and him that holdeth the sceptre from Ascalon: and I will turn my hand against Accaron, and the rest of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord God.
verses.textLatin: Et disperdam habitatorem de Azoto, et tenentem sceptrum de Ascalone: et convertam manum meam super Accaron, et peribunt reliqui Philisthinorum, dicit Dominus Deus.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four I will not convert it: because they have shut up an entire captivity in Edom, and have not remembered the covenant of brethren.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Tyri, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod concluserint captivitatem perfectam in Idumæa, et non sint recordati fœderis fratrum.

verses.text: And I will send a fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it shall devour the houses thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et mittam ignem in murum Tyri, et devorabit ædes ejus.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Edom, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath pursued his brother with the sword, and hath cast off all pity, and hath carried on his fury, and hath kept his wrath to the end.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Edom, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod persecutus sit in gladio fratrem suum, et violaverit misericordiam ejus, et tenuerit ultra furorem suum, et indignationem suam servaverit usque in finem.

verses.text: I will send a fire into Theman: and it shall devour the houses of Bosra.
verses.textLatin: Mittam ignem in Theman, et devorabit ædes Bosræ.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of the children of Ammon, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath ripped up the women with child of Galaad to enlarge his border.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus filiorum Ammon, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod dissecuerit prægnantes Galaad ad dilatandum terminum suum.

verses.text: And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabba: and it shall devour the houses thereof with shouting in the day of battle, and with a whirlwind in the day of trouble.
verses.textLatin: Et succendam ignem in muro Rabba, et devorabit ædes ejus in ululatu in die belli, et in turbine in die commotionis.

verses.text: And Melchom shall go into captivity, both he, and his princes together, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et ibit Melchom in captivitatem, ipse et principes ejus simul, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Thus  saith the Lord: For three crimes of Moab, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath burnt the bones of the king of Edom even to ashes.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Moab, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod incenderit ossa regis Idumææ usque ad cinerem.

verses.text: And I will send a fire into Moab, and it shall devour the houses of Carioth: and Moab shall die with a noise, with the sound of the trumpet:
verses.textLatin: Et mittam ignem in Moab, et devorabit ædes Carioth: et morietur in sonitu Moab, in clangore tubæ.

verses.text: And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all his princes with him, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et disperdam judicem de medio ejus, et omnes principes ejus interficiam cum eo, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Juda, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath cast away the law of the Lord, and hath not kept his commandments: for their idols have caused them to err, after which their fathers have walked.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Juda, et super quatuor non convertam eum, eo quod abjecerit legem Domini et mandata ejus non custodierit: deceperant enim eos idola sua, post quæ abierant patres eorum.

verses.text: And I will send a fire into Juda, and it shall devour the houses of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et mittam ignem in Juda, et devorabit ædes Jerusalem.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four I will not convert him: because he hath sold the just man for silver, and the poor man for a pair of shoes.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Super tribus sceleribus Israël, et super quatuor non convertam eum, pro eo quod vendiderit pro argento justum, et pauperem pro calceamentis.

verses.text: They bruise the heads of the poor upon the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the humble: and the son and his father have gone to the same young woman, to profane my holy name.
verses.textLatin: Qui conterunt super pulverem terræ capita pauperum, et viam humilium declinant: et filius ac pater ejus ierunt ad puellam, ut violarent nomen sanctum meum.

verses.text: And they sat down upon garments laid to pledge by every altar: and drank the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.
verses.textLatin: Et super vestimentis pignoratis accubuerunt juxta omne altare, et vinum damnatorum bibebant in domo Dei sui.

verses.text: Yet I cast out the Amorrhite before their face: whose height was like the height of cedars, and who was strong as an oak: and I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots beneath.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem exterminavi Amorrhæum a facie eorum, cujus altitudo, cedrorum altitudo ejus, et fortis ipse quasi quercus; et contrivi fructum ejus desuper, et radices ejus subter.

verses.text: It is I that brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and I led you forty years through the wilderness, that you might possess the land of the Amorrhite.
verses.textLatin: Ego sum qui ascendere vos feci de terra Ægypti, et duxi vos in deserto quadraginta annis, ut possideretis terram Amorrhæi.

verses.text: And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites. Is it not so, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord?
verses.textLatin: Et suscitavi de filiis vestris in prophetas, et de juvenibus vestris nazaræos. Numquid non ita est, filii Israël? dicit Dominus.

verses.text: And you will present wine to the Nazarites: and command the prophets, saying: Prophesy not.
verses.textLatin: Et propinabitis nazaræis vinum, et prophetis mandabitis, dicentes: Ne prophetetis.

verses.text: Behold, I will screak under you as a wain screaketh that is laden with hay.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego stridebo subter vos, sicut stridet plaustrum onustum fœno.

verses.text: And flight shall perish from the swift, and the valiant shall not possess his strength, neither shall the strong save his life.
verses.textLatin: Et peribit fuga a veloce, et fortis non obtinebit virtutem suam, et robustus non salvabit animam suam:

verses.text: And he that holdeth the bow shall not stand, and the swift of foot shall not escape, neither shall the rider of the horse save his life.
verses.textLatin: et tenens arcum non stabit, et velox pedibus suis non salvabitur, et ascensor equi non salvabit animam suam:

verses.text: And the stout of heart among the valiant shall flee away naked in that day, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: et robustus corde inter fortes nudus fugiet in illa die, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Hear  the word that the Lord hath spoken concerning you, O ye children of Israel: concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
verses.textLatin: Audite verbum quod locutus est Dominus super vos, filii Israël, super omnem cognationem quam eduxi de terra Ægypti, dicens:

verses.text: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore will I visit upon you all your iniquities.
verses.textLatin: Tantummodo vos cognovi ex omnibus cognationibus terræ; idcirco visitabo super vos omnes iniquitates vestras.

verses.text: Shall two walk together except they be agreed?
verses.textLatin: Numquid ambulabunt duo pariter, nisi convenerit eis?

verses.text: Will a lion roar in the forest, if he have no prey? will the lion’s whelp cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?
verses.textLatin: numquid rugiet leo in saltu, nisi habuerit prædam? numquid dabit catulus leonis vocem de cubili suo, nisi aliquid apprehenderit?

verses.text: Will the bird fall into the snare upon the earth, if there be no fowler? Shall the snare be taken up from the earth, before it hath taken somewhat?
verses.textLatin: numquid cadet avis in laqueum terræ absque aucupe? numquid auferetur laqueus de terra antequam quid ceperit?

verses.text: Shall the trumpet sound in a city, and the people not be afraid? Shall there be evil in a city, which the Lord hath not done?
verses.textLatin: si clanget tuba in civitate, et populus non expavescet? si erit malum in civitate, quod Dominus non fecerit?

verses.text: For the Lord God doth nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets.
verses.textLatin: Quia non facit Dominus Deus verbum, nisi revelaverit secretum suum ad servos suos prophetas.

verses.text: The lion shall roar, who will not fear? The Lord God hath spoken, who shall not prophesy?
verses.textLatin: Leo rugiet, quis non timebit? Dominus Deus locutus est, quis non prophetabit?

verses.text: Publish it in the houses of Azotus, and in the houses of the land of Egypt, and say: Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the many follies in the midst thereof, and them that suffer oppression in the inner rooms thereof.
verses.textLatin: Auditum facite in ædibus Azoti, et in ædibus terræ Ægypti, et dicite: Congregamini super montes Samariæ, et videte insanias multas in medio ejus, et calumniam patientes in penetralibus ejus.

verses.text: And they have not known to do the right thing, saith the Lord, storing up iniquity, and robberies in their houses.
verses.textLatin: Et nescierunt facere rectum, dicit Dominus, thesaurizantes iniquitatem et rapinas in ædibus suis.

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord God: The land shall be in tribulation, and shall be compassed about: and thy strength shall be taken away from thee, and thy houses shall be spoiled.
verses.textLatin: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus Deus: Tribulabitur et circuietur terra: et detrahetur ex te fortitudo tua, et diripientur ædes tuæ.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: As if a shepherd should get out of the lion’s mouth two legs, or the tip of the ear: so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria, in a piece of a bed, and in the couch of Damascus.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura, aut extremum auriculæ, sic eruentur filii Israël, qui habitant in Samaria in plaga lectuli, et in Damasci grabato.

verses.text: Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord the God of hosts:
verses.textLatin: Audite, et contestamini in domo Jacob, dicit Dominus Deus exercituum;

verses.text: That in the day when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel, I will visit upon him, and upon the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altars shall be cut off, and shall fall to the ground.
verses.textLatin: quia in die cum visitare cœpero prævaricationes Israël, super eum visitabo, et super altaria Bethel; et amputabuntur cornua altaris, et cadent in terram.

verses.text: And I will strike the winter house with the summer house: and the houses of ivory shall perish, and many houses shall be destroyed, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et percutiam domum hiemalem cum domo æstiva, et peribunt domus eburneæ, et dissipabuntur ædes multæ, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Hear this word, ye fat kine that are in the mountains of Samaria: you that oppress the needy, and crush the poor: that say to your masters: Bring, and we will drink.
verses.textLatin: Audite verbum hoc, vaccæ pingues, quæ estis in monte Samariæ, quæ calumniam facitis egenis et confringitis pauperes; quæ dicitis dominis vestris: Afferte, et bibemus.

verses.text: The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness, that lo, the days shall come upon you, when they shall lift you up on pikes, and what shall remain of you in boiling pots.
verses.textLatin: Juravit Dominus Deus in sancto suo, quia ecce dies venient super vos, et levabunt vos in contis, et reliquias vestras in ollis ferventibus.

verses.text: And you shall go out at the breaches one over against the other, and you shall be cast forth into Armon, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et per aperturas exibitis altera contra alteram, et projiciemini in Armon, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Come ye to Bethel, and do wickedly: to Galgal, and multiply transgressions: and bring in the morning your victims, your tithes in three days.
verses.textLatin: Venite ad Bethel, et impie agite; ad Galgalam, et multiplicate prævaricationem: et afferte mane victimas vestras, tribus diebus decimas vestras.

verses.text: And offer a sacrifice of praise with leaven: and call free offerings, and proclaim it: for so you would do, O children of Israel, saith the Lord God.
verses.textLatin: Et sacrificate de fermentato laudem, et vocate voluntarias oblationes, et annuntiate; sic enim voluistis, filii Israël, dicit Dominus Deus.

verses.text: Whereupon I also have given you dulness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet you have not returned to me, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Unde et ego dedi vobis stuporem dentium in cunctis urbibus vestris, et indigentiam panum in omnibus locis vestris; et non estis reversi ad me, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: I also have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon: and the piece whereupon I rained not, withered.
