verses.textLatin: Et aspiciet inimica mea, et operietur confusione, quæ dicit ad me: Ubi est Dominus Deus tuus? Oculi mei videbunt in eam: nunc erit in conculcationem ut lutum platearum.

verses.text: The day shall come, that thy walls may be built up: in that day shall the law be far removed.
verses.textLatin: Dies, ut ædificentur maceriæ tuæ; in die illa longe fiet lex.

verses.text: In that day they shall come even from Assyria to thee, and to the fortified cities: and from the fortified cities even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
verses.textLatin: In die illa et usque ad te veniet de Assur, et usque ad civitates munitas, et a civitatibus munitis usque ad flumen, et ad mare de mari, et ad montem de monte.

verses.text: And the land shall be made desolate, because of the inhabitants thereof, and for the fruit of their devices.
verses.textLatin: Et terra erit in desolationem propter habitatores suos, et propter fructum cogitationum eorum.

verses.text: Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thy inheritance, them that dwell alone in the forest, in the midst of Carmel: they shall feed in Basan and Galaad according to the days of old.
verses.textLatin: Pasce populum tuum in virga tua, gregem hæreditatis tuæ, habitantes solos, in saltu, in medio Carmeli. Pascentur Basan et Galaad juxta dies antiquos.

verses.text: According to the days of thy coming out of the land of Egypt I will shew him wonders.
verses.textLatin: Secundum dies egressionis tuæ de terra Ægypti, ostendam ei mirabilia.

verses.text: The nations shall see, and shall be confounded at all their strength: they shall put the hand upon the mouth, their ears shall be deaf.
verses.textLatin: Videbunt gentes, et confundentur super omni fortitudine sua. Ponent manum super os, aures eorum surdæ erunt.

verses.text: They shall lick the dust like serpents, as the creeping things of the earth, they shall be disturbed in their houses: they shall dread the Lord our God, and shall fear thee.
verses.textLatin: Lingent pulverem sicut serpentes; velut reptilia terræ perturbabuntur in ædibus suis. Dominum Deum nostrum formidabunt, et timebunt te.

verses.text: Who is a God like to thee, who takest away iniquity, and passest by the sin of the remnant of thy inheritance? he will send his fury in no more, because he delighteth in mercy.
verses.textLatin: Quis, Deus, similis tui, qui aufers iniquitatem, et transis peccatum reliquiarum hæreditatis tuæ? Non immittet ultra furorem suum, quoniam volens misericordiam est.

verses.text: He will turn again, and have mercy on us: he will put away our iniquities: and he will cast all our sins into the bottom of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Revertetur, et miserebitur nostri; deponet iniquitates nostras, et projiciet in profundum maris omnia peccata nostra.

verses.text: Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, the mercy to Abraham: which thou hast sworn to our fathers from the days of old.
verses.textLatin: Dabis veritatem Jacob, misericordiam Abraham, quæ jurasti patribus nostris a diebus antiquis.

verses.text: The  burden of Ninive. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elcesite.
verses.textLatin: Onus Ninive. Liber visionis Nahum Elcesæi.

verses.text: The Lord is a jealous God, and a revenger: the Lord is a revenger, and hath wrath: the Lord taketh vengeance on his adversaries, and he is angry with his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Deus æmulator, et ulciscens Dominus: ulciscens Dominus, et habens furorem: ulciscens Dominus in hostes suos, et irascens ipse inimicis suis.

verses.text: The Lord is patient, and great in power, and will not cleanse and acquit the guilty. The Lord’s ways are in a tempest, and a whirlwind, and clouds are the dust of his feet.
verses.textLatin: Dominus patiens, et magnus fortitudine, et mundans non faciet innocentem. Dominus in tempestate et turbine viæ ejus, et nebulæ pulvis pedum ejus.

verses.text: He rebuketh the sea, and drieth it up: and bringeth all the rivers to be a desert. Basan languisheth and Carmel: and the flower of Libanus fadeth away.
verses.textLatin: Increpans mare, et exsiccans illud, et omnia flumina ad desertum deducens. Infirmatus est Basan et Carmelus, et flos Libani elanguit.

verses.text: The mountains tremble at him, and the hills are made desolate: and the earth hath quaked at his presence, and the world, and all that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Montes commoti sunt ab eo, et colles desolati sunt: et contremuit terra a facie ejus, et orbis, et omnes habitantes in eo.

verses.text: Who can stand before the face of his indignation? and who shall resist in the fierceness of his anger? his indignation is poured out like fire: and the rocks are melted by him.
verses.textLatin: Ante faciem indignationis ejus quis stabit? et quis resistet in ira furoris ejus? Indignatio ejus effusa est ut ignis, et petræ dissolutæ sunt ab eo.

verses.text: The Lord is good and giveth strength in the day of trouble: and knoweth them that hope in him.
verses.textLatin: Bonus Dominus, et confortans in die tribulationis, et sciens sperantes in se.

verses.text: But with a flood that passeth by, he will make an utter end of the place thereof: and darkness shall pursue his enemies.
verses.textLatin: Et in diluvio prætereunte consummationem faciet loci ejus, et inimicos ejus persequentur tenebræ.

verses.text: What do ye devise against the Lord? he will make an utter end: there shall not rise a double affliction.
verses.textLatin: Quid cogitatis contra Dominum? Consummationem ipse faciet: non consurget duplex tribulatio,

verses.text: For as thorns embrace one another: so while they are feasting and drinking together, they shall be consumed as stubble that is fully dry.
verses.textLatin: quia sicut spinæ se invicem complectuntur, sic convivium eorum pariter potantium; consumentur quasi stipula ariditate plena.

verses.text: Out of thee shall come forth one that imagineth evil against the Lord, contriving treachery in his mind.
verses.textLatin: Ex te exibit cogitans contra Dominum malitiam, mente pertractans prævaricationem.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord: Though they were perfect: and many of them so, yet thus shall they be cut off, and he shall pass: I have afflicted thee, and I will afflict thee no more.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus: Si perfecti fuerint, et ita plures, sic quoque attondentur, et pertransibit: afflixi te, et non affligam te ultra.

verses.text: And now I will break in pieces his rod with which he struck thy back, and Iwill burst thy bonds asunder.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc conteram virgam ejus de dorso tuo, et vincula tua disrumpam.

verses.text: And the Lord will give a commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name shall be sown: I will destroy the graven and molten thing out of the house of thy God, I will make it thy grave, for thou art disgraced.
verses.textLatin: Et præcipiet super te Dominus; non seminabitur ex nomine tuo amplius: de domo Dei tui interficiam sculptile, et conflatile; ponam sepulchrum tuum, quia inhonoratus es.

verses.text: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, and that preacheth peace: O Juda, keep thy festivals, and pay thy vows: for Belial shall no more pass through thee again, he is utterly cut off.
verses.textLatin: Ecce super montes pedes evangelizantis, et annuntiantis pacem. Celebra, Juda, festivitates tuas, et redde vota tua, quia non adjiciet ultra ut pertranseat in te Belial: universus interiit.

verses.text: He  is come up that shall destroy before thy face, that shall keep the siege: watch the way, fortify thy loins, strengthen thy power exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Ascendit qui dispergat coram te, qui custodiat obsidionem: contemplare viam, conforta lumbos, robora virtutem valde.

verses.text: For the Lord hath rendered the pride of Jacob, as the pride of Israel: because the spoilers have laid them waste, and have marred their vine branches.
verses.textLatin: Quia reddidit Dominus superbiam Jacob, sicut superbiam Israël; quia vastatores dissipaverunt eos, et propagines eorum corruperunt.

verses.text: The shield of his mighty men is like fire, the men of the army are clad in scarlet, the reins of the chariot are flaming in the day of his preparation, and the drivers are stupefied.
verses.textLatin: Clypeus fortium ejus ignitus, viri exercitus in coccineis; igneæ habenæ currus in die præparationis ejus, et agitatores consopiti sunt.

verses.text: They are in confusion in the ways, the chariots jostle one against another in the streets: their looks are like torches, like lightning running to and fro.
verses.textLatin: In itineribus conturbati sunt; quadrigæ collisæ sunt in plateis: aspectus eorum quasi lampades, quasi fulgura discurrentia.

verses.text: He will muster up his valiant men, they shall stumble in their march: they shall quickly get upon the walls thereof: and a covering shall be prepared.
verses.textLatin: Recordabitur fortium suorum; ruent in itineribus suis: velociter ascendent muros ejus, et præparabitur umbraculum.

verses.text: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the temple is thrown down to the ground.
verses.textLatin: Portæ fluviorum apertæ sunt, et templum ad solum dirutum.

verses.text: And the soldier is led away captive: and her bondwomen were led away mourning as doves, murmuring in their hearts.
verses.textLatin: Et miles captivus abductus est, et ancillæ ejus minabantur gementes ut columbæ, murmurantes in cordibus suis.

verses.text: And as for Ninive, her waters are like a great pool, but the men flee away. They cry: Stand, stand, but there is none that will return back.
verses.textLatin: Et Ninive quasi piscina aquarum aquæ ejus; ipsi vero fugerunt. State, state! et non est qui revertatur.

verses.text: Take ye the spoil of the silver, take the spoil of the gold: for there is no end of the riches of all the precious furniture.
verses.textLatin: Diripite argentum, diripite aurum: et non est finis divitiarum ex omnibus vasis desiderabilibus.

verses.text: She is destroyed, and rent, and torn: the heart melteth, and the knees fail, and all the loins lose their strength: and the faces of them all are as the blackness of a kettle.
verses.textLatin: Dissipata est, et scissa, et dilacerata; et cor tabescens, et dissolutio geniculorum, et defectio in cunctis renibus, et facies omnium eorum sicut nigredo ollæ.

verses.text: Where is now the dwelling of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, to which the lion went, to enter in thither, the young lion, and there was none to make them afraid?
verses.textLatin: Ubi est habitaculum leonum, et pascua catulorum leonum, ad quam ivit leo ut ingrederetur illuc catulus leonis, et non est qui exterreat?

verses.text: The lion caught enough for his whelps, and killed for his lionesses: and he filled his holes with prey, and his denwith rapine.
verses.textLatin: Leo cepit sufficienter catulis suis, et necavit leænis suis, et implevit præda speluncas suas, et cubile suum rapina.

verses.text: Behold I come against thee, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will burn thy chariots even to smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey out of the land, and the voice of thy messengers shall be heard no more.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego ad te, dicit Dominus exercituum, et succendam usque ad fumum quadrigas tuas, et leunculos tuos comedet gladius, et exterminabo de terra prædam tuam, et non audietur ultra vox nuntiorum tuorum.

verses.text: Woe  to thee, O city of blood, all full of lies and violence: rapine shall not depart from thee.
verses.textLatin: Væ civitas sanguinum, universa mendacii dilaceratione plena! non recedet a te rapina.

verses.text: The noise of the whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the neighing horse, and of the running chariot, and of the horsemen coming up,
verses.textLatin: Vox flagelli, et vox impetus rotæ, et equi frementis, et quadrigæ ferventis, et equitis ascendentis,

verses.text: And of the shining sword, and of the glittering spear, and of a multitude slain, and of a grievous destruction: and there is no end of carcasses, and they shall fall down on their dead bodies.
verses.textLatin: et micantis gladii, et fulgurantis hastæ, et multitudinis interfectæ, et gravis ruinæ; nec est finis cadaverum, et corruent in corporibus suis.

verses.text: Because of the multitude of the fornications of the harlot that was beautiful and agreeable, and that made use of witchcraft, that sold nations through her fornications, and families through her witchcrafts.
verses.textLatin: Propter multitudinem fornicationum meretricis speciosæ, et gratæ, et habentis maleficia, quæ vendidit gentes in fornicationibus suis, et familias in maleficiis suis.

verses.text: Behold I come against thee, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will discover thy shame to thy face, and will shew thy nakedness to the nations, and thy shame to kingdoms.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego ad te, dicit Dominus exercituum, et revelabo pudenda tua in facie tua; et ostendam gentibus nuditatem tuam, et regnis ignominiam tuam.

verses.text: And I will cast abominations upon thee, and will disgrace thee, and will make an example of thee.
verses.textLatin: Et projiciam super te abominationes, et contumeliis te afficiam, et ponam te in exemplum.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass that every one that shall see thee, shall flee from thee, and shall say: Ninive is laid waste: who shall bemoan thee? whence shall Iseek a comforter for thee?
verses.textLatin: Et erit: omnis qui viderit te resiliet a te, et dicet: Vastata est Ninive. Quis commovebit super te caput? unde quæram consolatorem tibi?

verses.text: Art thou better than the populous Alexandria, that dwelleth among therivers? waters are round about it: the sea is its riches, the waters are its walls.
verses.textLatin: Numquid melior es Alexandria populorum, quæ habitat in fluminibus? aquæ in circuitu ejus; cujus divitiæ, mare; aquæ, muri ejus.

verses.text: Ethiopia and Egypt were the strength thereof, and there is no end: Africa and the Libyans were thy helpers.
verses.textLatin: Æthiopia fortitudo ejus, et Ægyptus, et non est finis; Africa et Libyes fuerunt in auxilio tuo.

verses.text: Yet she also was removed and carried into captivity: her young children were dashed in pieces at the top of every street, and they cast lots upon her nobles, and all her great men were bound in fetters.
verses.textLatin: Sed et ipsa in transmigrationem ducta est in captivitatem: parvuli ejus elisi sunt in capite omnium viarum, et super inclytos ejus miserunt sortem, et omnes optimates ejus confixi sunt in compedibus.

verses.text: Therefore thou also shalt be made drunk, and shalt be despised: and thou shalt seek help from the enemy.
verses.textLatin: Et tu ergo inebriaberis, et eris despecta: et tu quæres auxilium ab inimico.

verses.text: All thy strong holds shall be like fig trees with their green figs: if they be shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.textLatin: Omnes munitiones tuæ sicut ficus cum grossis suis: si concussæ fuerint, cadent in os comedentis.

verses.text: Behold thy people in the midst of thee are women: the gates of thy land shall be set wide open to thy enemies, the fire shall devour thy bars.
verses.textLatin: Ecce populus tuus mulieres in medio tui: inimicis tuis adapertione pandentur portæ terræ tuæ, devorabit ignis vectes tuos.

verses.text: Draw thee water for the siege, build up thy bulwarks: go into the clay, and tread, work it and make brick.
verses.textLatin: Aquam propter obsidionem hauri tibi: exstrue munitiones tuas, intra in lutum, et calca, subigens tene laterem.

verses.text: There shall the fire devour thee: thou shalt perish by the sword, it shall devour thee like the bruchus: assemble together like the bruchus, make thyself many like the locust.
verses.textLatin: Ibi comedet te ignis, peribis gladio, devorabit te ut bruchus: congregare ut bruchus, multiplicare ut locusta.

verses.text: Thou hast multiplied thy merchandises above the stars of heaven: the bruchus hath spread himself and flown away.
verses.textLatin: Plures fecisti negotiationes tuas quam stellæ sint cæli; bruchus expansus est, et avolavit.

verses.text: Thy guards are like the locusts: and thy little ones like the locusts of locusts which swarm on the hedges in the day of cold: the sun arose, and they flew away, and their place was not known where they were.
verses.textLatin: Custodes tui quasi locustæ, et parvuli tui quasi locustæ locustarum, quæ considunt in sepibus in die frigoris: sol ortus est, et avolaverunt, et non est cognitus locus earum ubi fuerint.

verses.text: Thy shepherds have slumbered, O king of Assyria, thy princes shall be buried: thy people are hid in the mountains, and there is none to gather themtogether.
verses.textLatin: Dormitaverunt pastores tui, rex Assur, sepelientur principes tui: latitavit populus tuus in montibus, et non est qui congreget.

verses.text: Thy destruction is not hidden, thy wound is grievous: all that have heard the fame of thee, have clapped their hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
verses.textLatin: Non est obscura contritio tua; pessima est plaga tua. Omnes qui audierunt auditionem tuam compresserunt manum super te: quia super quem non transiit malitia tua semper?

verses.text: The burden that Habacuc the prophet saw.
verses.textLatin: Onus quod vidit Habacuc propheta.

verses.text: How long, O Lord, shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear? shall I cry out to thee suffering violence, and thou wilt not save?
verses.textLatin: Usquequo, Domine, clamabo, et non exaudies? vociferabor ad te, vim patiens, et non salvabis?

verses.text: Why hast thou shewn me iniquity and grievance, to see rapine and injustice before me? and there is a judgment, but opposition is more powerful.
verses.textLatin: Quare ostendisti mihi iniquitatem et laborem, videre prædam et injustitiam contra me? Et factum est judicium, et contradictio potentior.

verses.text: Therefore the law is torn in pieces, and judgment cometh not to the end:because the wicked prevaileth against the just, therefore wrong judgment goeth forth.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc lacerata est lex, et non pervenit usque ad finem judicium; quia impius prævalet adversus justum, propterea egreditur judicium perversum.

verses.text: Behold ye among the nations, and see: wonder, and be astonished: for a work is done in your days, which no man will believe when it shall be told.
verses.textLatin: Aspicite in gentibus, et videte; admiramini, et obstupescite: quia opus factum est in diebus vestris, quod nemo credet cum narrabitur.

verses.text: For behold, I will raise up the Chaldeans, a bitter and swift nation, marching upon the breadth of the earth, to possess the dwelling places that are not their own.
verses.textLatin: Quia ecce ego suscitabo Chaldæos, gentem amaram et velocem, ambulantem super latitudinem terræ, ut possideat tabernacula non sua.

verses.text: They are dreadful, and terrible: from themselves shall their judgment, and their burden proceed.
verses.textLatin: Horribilis et terribilis est: ex semetipsa judicium et onus ejus egredietur.

verses.text: Their horses are lighter than leopards, and swifter than evening wolves; and their horsemen shall be spread abroad: for their horsemen shall come from afar, they shall fly as an eagle that maketh haste to eat.
verses.textLatin: Leviores pardis equi ejus, et velociores lupis vespertinis: et diffundentur equites ejus: equites namque ejus de longe venient; volabunt quasi aquila festinans ad comedendum.

verses.text: They shall all come to the prey, their face is like a burning wind: and they shall gather together captives as the sand.
verses.textLatin: Omnes ad prædam venient, facies eorum ventus urens; et congregabit quasi arenam captivitatem.

verses.text: And their prince shall triumph over kings, and princes shall be his laughingstock: and he shall laugh at every strong hold, and shall cast up a mount, and shall take it.
verses.textLatin: Et ipse de regibus triumphabit, et tyranni ridiculi ejus erunt; ipse super omnem munitionem ridebit, et comportabit aggerem, et capiet eam.

verses.text: Then shall his spirit be changed, and he shall pass, and fall: this is his strength of his god.
verses.textLatin: Tunc mutabitur spiritus, et pertransibit, et corruet: hæc est fortitudo ejus dei sui.

verses.text: Wast thou not from the beginning, O Lord my God, my holy one, and we shall not die? Lord, thou hast appointed him for judgment: and made him strong for correction.
verses.textLatin: Numquid non tu a principio, Domine, Deus meus, sancte meus, et non moriemur? Domine, in judicium posuisti eum, et fortem, ut corriperes, fundasti eum.

verses.text: Thy eyes are too pure to behold evil, and thou canst not look on iniquity. Why lookest thou upon them that do unjust things, and holdest thy peace when the wicked devoureth the man that is more just than himself?
verses.textLatin: Mundi sunt oculi tui, ne videas malum, et respicere ad iniquitatem non poteris. Quare respicis super iniqua agentes, et taces devorante impio justiorem se?

verses.text: And thou wilt make men as the fishes of the sea, and as the creeping things that have no ruler.
verses.textLatin: Et facies homines quasi pisces maris, et quasi reptile non habens principem.

verses.text: He lifted up all them with his hook, he drew them in his drag, and gathered them into his net: for this he will be glad and rejoice.
verses.textLatin: Totum in hamo sublevavit, traxit illud in sagena sua, et congregavit in rete suum. Super hoc lætabitur, et exsultabit.

verses.text: Therefore will he offer victims to his drag, and he will sacrifice to his net: because through them his portion is made fat, and his meat dainty.
verses.textLatin: Propterea immolabit sagenæ suæ, et sacrificabit reti suo, quia in ipsis incrassata est pars ejus, et cibus ejus electus.

verses.text: For this cause therefore he spreadeth his net, and will not spare continually to slay the nations.
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc ergo expandit sagenam suam, et semper interficere gentes non parcet.

verses.text: I will stand upon my watch, and fix my foot upon the tower: and I will watch, to see what will be said to me, and what I may answer to him that reproveth me.
verses.textLatin: Super custodiam meam stabo, et figam gradum super munitionem: et contemplabor ut videam quid dicatur mihi, et quid respondeam ad arguentem me.

verses.text: And the Lord answered me, and said: Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables: that he that readeth it may run over it.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit mihi Dominus, et dixit: Scribe visum, et explana eum super tabulas, ut percurrat qui legerit eum.

verses.text: For as yet the vision is far off, and it shall appear at the end, and shall not lie: if it make any delay, wait for it: for it shall surely come, and it shall not be slack.
verses.textLatin: Quia adhuc visus procul; et apparebit in finem, et non mentietur: si moram fecerit, exspecta illum, quia veniens veniet, et non tardabit.

verses.text: Behold, he that is unbelieving, his soul shall not be right in himself: but the just shall live in his faith.
verses.textLatin: Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso; justus autem in fide sua vivet.

verses.text: And as wine deceiveth him that drinketh it: so shall the proud man be, and he shall not be honoured: who hath enlarged his desire like hell: and is himself like death, and he is never satisfied: but will gather together unto him all nations, and heap together unto him all people.
verses.textLatin: Et quomodo vinum potantem decipit, sic erit vir superbus, et non decorabitur: qui dilatavit quasi infernus animam suam, et ipse quasi mors, et non adimpletur: et congregabit ad se omnes gentes, et coacervabit ad se omnes populos.

verses.text: Shall not all these take up a parableagainst him, and a dark speech concerning him: and it shall be said: Woe to him that heapeth together that which is not his own? how long also doth he load himself with thick clay?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non omnes isti super eum parabolam sument, et loquelam ænigmatum ejus, et dicetur: Væ ei qui multiplicat non sua? usquequo et aggravat contra se densum lutum?

verses.text: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee: and they be stirred up that shall tear thee, and thou shalt be a spoil to them?
verses.textLatin: Numquid non repente consurgent qui mordeant te, et suscitabuntur lacerantes te, et eris in rapinam eis?

verses.text: Because thou hast spoiled many nations, all that shall be left of the people shall spoil thee: because of men’s blood, and for the iniquity of the land, of the city, and of all that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Quia tu spoliasti gentes multas, spoliabunt te omnes qui reliqui fuerint de populis, propter sanguinem hominis, et iniquitatem terræ, civitatis, et omnium habitantium in ea.

verses.text: Woe to him that gathereth together an evil covetousness to his house, that his nest may be on high, and thinketh he may be delivered out of the hand of evil.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui congregat avaritiam malam domui suæ, ut sit in excelso nidus ejus, et liberari se putat de manu mali!

verses.text: Thou hast devised confusion to thyhouse, thou hast cut off many people, and thy soul hath sinned.
verses.textLatin: Cogitasti confusionem domui tuæ; concidisti populos multos, et peccavit anima tua.

verses.text: For the stone shall cry out of the wall: and the timber that is between the joints of the building, shall answer.
verses.textLatin: Quia lapis de pariete clamabit, et lignum, quod inter juncturas ædificiorum est, respondebit.

verses.text: Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and prepareth a city by iniquity.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui ædificat civitatem in sanguinibus, et præparat urbem in iniquitate!

verses.text: Are not these things from the Lord of hosts? for the people shall labour in a great fire: and the nations in vain, and they shall faint.
verses.textLatin: Numquid non hæc sunt a Domino exercituum? laborabunt enim populi in multo igne, et gentes in vacuum, et deficient.

verses.text: For the earth shall be filled, that men may know the glory of the Lord, as waters covering the sea.
verses.textLatin: Quia replebitur terra, ut cognoscant gloriam Domini, quasi aquæ operientes mare.

verses.text: Woe to him that giveth drink to his friend, and presenteth his gall, and maketh him drunk, that he may behold his nakedness.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui potum dat amico suo mittens fel suum, et inebrians ut aspiciat nuditatem ejus!

verses.text: Thou art filled with shame instead of glory: drink thou also, and fall fast asleep: the cup of the right hand of the Lord shall compass thee, and shameful vomiting shall be on thy glory.
verses.textLatin: Repletus es ignominia pro gloria; bibe tu quoque, et consopire. Circumdabit te calix dexteræ Domini, et vomitus ignominiæ super gloriam tuam.

verses.text: For the iniquity of Libanus shall cover thee, and the ravaging of beasts shall terrify them because of the blood of men, and the iniquity of the land, and of the city, and of all that dwell therein.
verses.textLatin: Quia iniquitas Libani operiet te, et vastitas animalium deterrebit eos de sanguinibus hominum, et iniquitate terræ, et civitatis, et omnium habitantium in ea.

verses.text: What doth the graven thing avail, because the maker thereof hath graven it, a molten, and a false image? because the forger thereof hath trusted in a thing of his own forging, to make dumb idols.
verses.textLatin: Quid prodest sculptile, quia sculpsit illud fictor suus, conflatile, et imaginem falsam? quia speravit in figmento fictor ejus, ut faceret simulacra muta.

verses.text: Woe to him that saith to wood: Awake: to the dumb stone: Arise: can it teach? Behold, it is laid over with gold, and silver, and there is no spirit in the bowels thereof.
verses.textLatin: Væ qui dicit ligno: Expergiscere; Surge, lapidi tacenti! Numquid ipse docere poterit? ecce iste coopertus est auro et argento, et omnis spiritus non est in visceribus ejus.

verses.text: But the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.
verses.textLatin: Dominus autem in templo sancto suo: sileat a facie ejus omnis terra!

verses.text: A PRAYER OF HABACUC THE PROPHET FOR IGNORANCES.
verses.textLatin: ORATIO HABACUC PROPHETÆ, PRO IGNORANTIIS.

verses.text: O Lord, I have heard thy hearing, and was afraid. O Lord, thy work, in the midst of the years bring it to life: In the midst of the years thou shalt make it known: when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy.
verses.textLatin: Domine, audivi auditionem tuam, et timui. Domine, opus tuum, in medio annorum vivifica illud; in medio annorum notum facies: cum iratus fueris, misericordiæ recordaberis.

verses.text: God will come from the south, and the holy one from mount Pharan: His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.
verses.textLatin: Deus ab austro veniet, et Sanctus de monte Pharan: operuit cælos gloria ejus, et laudis ejus plena est terra.

verses.text: His brightness shall be as the light: horns are in his hands: There is his strength hid:
verses.textLatin: Splendor ejus ut lux erit, cornua in manibus ejus: ibi abscondita est fortitudo ejus.

verses.text: Death shall go before his face. And the devil shall go forth before his feet.
verses.textLatin: Ante faciem ejus ibit mors, et egredietur diabolus ante pedes ejus.

verses.text: He stood and measured the earth. He beheld, and melted the nations: and the ancient mountains were crushed to pieces. The hills of the world were bowed down by the journeys of his eternity.
verses.textLatin: Stetit, et mensus est terram; aspexit, et dissolvit gentes, et contriti sunt montes sæculi: incurvati sunt colles mundi ab itineribus æternitatis ejus.

verses.text: I saw the tents of Ethiopia for their iniquity, the curtains of the land of Madian shall be troubled.
verses.textLatin: Pro iniquitate vidi tentoria Æthiopiæ; turbabuntur pelles terræ Madian.

verses.text: Wast thou angry, O Lord, with the rivers? or was thy wrath upon the rivers? or thy indignation in the sea? Who will ride upon thy horses: and thy chariots are salvation.
verses.textLatin: Numquid in fluminibus iratus es, Domine? aut in fluminibus furor tuus? vel in mari indignatio tua? Qui ascendes super equos tuos, et quadrigæ tuæ salvatio.

verses.text: Thou wilt surely take up thy bow: according to the oaths which thou hast spoken to the tribes. Thou wilt divide the rivers of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Suscitans suscitabis arcum tuum, juramenta tribubus quæ locutus es; fluvios scindes terræ.

verses.text: The mountains saw thee, and were grieved: the great body of waters passed away. The deep put forth its voice: the deep lifted up its hands.
verses.textLatin: Viderunt te, et doluerunt montes; gurges aquarum transiit: dedit abyssus vocem suam; altitudo manus suas levavit.

verses.text: The sun and the moon stood still in their habitation, in the light of thy arrows, they shall go in the brightness of thy glittering spear.
verses.textLatin: Sol et luna steterunt in habitaculo suo: in luce sagittarum tuarum ibunt, in splendore fulgurantis hastæ tuæ.

verses.text: In thy anger thou wilt tread the earth under foot: in thy wrath thou wilt astonish the nations.
verses.textLatin: In fremitu conculcabis terram; in furore obstupefacies gentes.

verses.text: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people: for salvation with thy Christ. Thou struckest the head of the house of the wicked: thou hast laid bare his foundation even to the neck.
verses.textLatin: Egressus es in salutem populi tui, in salutem cum christo tuo: percussisti caput de domo impii, denudasti fundamentum ejus usque ad collum.

verses.text: Thou hast cursed his sceptres, the head of his warriors, them that came out as a whirlwind to scatter me. Their joy was like that of him that devoureth the poor man in secret.
verses.textLatin: Maledixisti sceptris ejus, capiti bellatorum ejus, venientibus ut turbo ad dispergendum me: exsultatio eorum, sicut ejus qui devorat pauperem in abscondito.

verses.text: Thou madest a way in the sea for thy horses, in the mud of many waters.
verses.textLatin: Viam fecisti in mari equis tuis, in luto aquarum multarum.

verses.text: I have heard and my bowels were troubled: my lips trembled at the voice. Let rottenness enter into my bones, and swarm under me. That I may rest in the day of tribulation: that I may go up to our people that are girded.
verses.textLatin: Audivi, et conturbatus est venter meus; a voce contremuerunt labia mea. Ingrediatur putredo in ossibus meis, et subter me scateat: ut requiescam in die tribulationis, ut ascendam ad populum accinctum nostrum.

verses.text: For the fig tree shall not blossom: and there shall be no spring in the vines. The labour of the olive tree shall fail: and the fields shall yield no food: the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls.
verses.textLatin: Ficus enim non florebit, et non erit germen in vineis; mentietur opus olivæ, et arva non afferent cibum: abscindetur de ovili pecus, et non erit armentum in præsepibus.

verses.text: But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus.
verses.textLatin: Ego autem in Domino gaudebo; et exsultabo in Deo Jesu meo.

verses.text: The Lord God is my strength: and he will make my feet like the feet of harts: and he the conqueror will lead me upon my high places singing psalms.
verses.textLatin: Deus Dominus fortitudo mea, et ponet pedes meos quasi cervorum: et super excelsa mea deducet me victor in psalmis canentem.

verses.text: The  word of the Lord that came to Sophonias the son of Chusi, the son of Godolias, the son of Amarias, the son of Ezechias, in the days of Josias, the son of Amon king of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Sophoniam, filium Chusi, filii Godoliæ, filii Amariæ, filii Ezeciæ, in diebus Josiæ, filii Amon, regis Judæ.

verses.text: Gathering, I will gather together allthings from off the face of the land, saith the Lord:
verses.textLatin: Congregans congregabo omnia a facie terræ, dicit Dominus:

verses.text: I will gather man, and beast, I will gather the birds of the air, and the fishes of he sea: and the ungodly shall meet with ruin: and I will destroy men from off the face of the land, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: congregans hominem et pecus, congregans volatilia cæli et pisces maris: et ruinæ impiorum erunt, et disperdam homines a facie terræ, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: And I will stretch out my hand upon Juda, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and I will destroy out of this place the remnant of Baal, and the names of the wardens of the temples with the priests:
verses.textLatin: Et extendam manum meam super Judam et super omnes habitantes Jerusalem: et disperdam de loco hoc reliquias Baal, et nomina ædituorum cum sacerdotibus;

verses.text: And them that worship the host of heaven upon the tops of houses, and them that adore, and swear by the Lord, and swear by Melchom.
verses.textLatin: et eos qui adorant super tecta militiam cæli, et adorant et jurant in Domino, et jurant in Melchom;

verses.text: And them that turn away from following after the Lord, and that have not sought the Lord, nor searched after him.
verses.textLatin: et qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini, et qui non quæsierunt Dominum, nec investigaverunt eum.

verses.text: Be silent before the face of the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is near, for the Lord hath prepared a victim, he hath sanctified his guests.
verses.textLatin: Silete a facie Domini Dei, quia juxta est dies Domini: quia præparavit Dominus hostiam; sanctificavit vocatos suos.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in the day of the victim of the Lord, that I will visit upon the princes, and upon the king’s sons, and upon all such as are clothed with strange apparel:
verses.textLatin: Et erit: in die hostiæ Domini, visitabo super principes, et super filios regis, et super omnes qui induti sunt veste peregrina;

verses.text: And I will visit in that day upon every one that entereth arrogantly over thethreshold: them that fill the house of the Lord their God with iniquity and deceit.
verses.textLatin: et visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur super limen in die illa, qui complent domum Domini Dei sui iniquitate et dolo.

verses.text: And there shall be in that day, saith the Lord, the noise of a cry from the fish gate, and a howling from the Second, and a great destruction from the hills.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus, vox clamoris a porta piscium, et ululatus a Secunda, et contritio magna a collibus.

verses.text: Howl, ye inhabitants of the Morter. All the people of Chanaan is hush, all are cut off that were wrapped up in silver.
verses.textLatin: Ululate, habitatores Pilæ: conticuit omnis populus Chanaan, disperierunt omnes involuti argento.

verses.text: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and will visit upon the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their hearts: The Lord will not do good, nor will he do evil.
verses.textLatin: Et erit in tempore illo: scrutabor Jerusalem in lucernis, et visitabo super viros defixos in fæcibus suis, qui dicunt in cordibus suis: Non faciet bene Dominus, et non faciet male.

verses.text: And their strength shall become a booty, and their houses as a desert: and they shall build houses, and shall not dwell in them: and they shall plant vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them.
verses.textLatin: Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem, et domus eorum in desertum: et ædificabunt domos, et non habitabunt; et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum.

verses.text: The great day of the Lord is near, it is near and exceeding swift: the voice of the day of the Lord is bitter, the mighty man shall there meet with tribulation.
verses.textLatin: Juxta est dies Domini magnus: juxta est, et velox nimis. Vox diei Domini amara: tribulabitur ibi fortis.

verses.text: That day is a day of wrath, a day of tribulation and distress, a day of calamity and misery, a day of darkness and obscurity, a day of clouds and whirlwinds,
verses.textLatin: Dies iræ dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ, dies tenebrarum et caliginis, dies nebulæ et turbinis,

verses.text: A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities, and against the high bulwarks.
verses.textLatin: dies tubæ et clangoris super civitates munitas, et super angulos excelsos.

verses.text: And I will distress men, and they shall walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord: and theirblood shall be poured out as earth, and their bodies as dung.
verses.textLatin: Et tribulabo homines, et ambulabunt ut cæci, quia Domino peccaverunt; et effundetur sanguis eorum sicut humus, et corpora eorum sicut stercora.

verses.text: Neither shall their silver and their gold be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord: all the land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy, for he shall make even a speedy destruction of all them that dwell in the land.
verses.textLatin: Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos in die iræ Domini : in igne zeli ejus devorabitur omnis terra, quia consummationem cum festinatione faciet cunctis habitantibus terram.

verses.text: Assemble  yourselves together, be gathered together, O nation not worthy to be loved:
verses.textLatin: Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos in die iræ Domini: in igne zeli ejus devorabitur omnis terra, quia consummationem cum festinatione faciet cunctis habitantibus terram.

verses.text: Before the decree bring forth the day as dust passing away, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s indignation come upon you.
verses.textLatin: Convenite, congregamini, gens non amabilis,

verses.text: Seek the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, you that have wrought his judgment: seek the just, seek the meek: if by any means you may be hid in the day of the Lord’s indignation.
verses.textLatin: priusquam pariat jussio quasi pulverem transeuntem diem, antequam veniat super vos ira furoris Domini, antequam veniat super vos dies indignationis Domini.

verses.text: For Gaza shall be destroyed, and Ascalon shall be a desert, they shall cast out Azotus at noonday, and Accaron shall be rooted up.
verses.textLatin: Quærite Dominum, omnes mansueti terræ, qui judicium ejus estis operati; quærite justum, quærite mansuetum, si quomodo abscondamini in die furoris Domini.

verses.text: Woe to you that inhabit the sea coast, O nation of reprobates: the word of the Lord upon you, O Chanaan, the land of the Philistines, and I will destroy thee, so that there shall not be an inhabitant.
verses.textLatin: Quia Gaza destructa erit, et Ascalon in desertum: Azotum in meridie ejicient, et Accaron eradicabitur.

verses.text: And the sea coast shall be the resting place of shepherds, and folds for cattle:
verses.textLatin: Væ qui habitatis funiculum maris, gens perditorum! verbum Domini super vos, Chanaan, terra Philisthinorum; et disperdam te, ita ut non sit inhabitator.

verses.text: And it shall be the portion of him that shall remain of the house of Juda, there they shall feed: in the houses of Ascalon they shall rest in the evening: because the Lord their God will visit them, and bring back their captivity.
verses.textLatin: Et erit funiculus maris requies pastorum, et caulæ pecorum;

verses.text: I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the blasphemies of the children ofAmmon, with which they reproached my people, and have magnified themselves upon their borders.
verses.textLatin: et erit funiculus ejus qui remanserit de domo Juda: ibi pascentur, in domibus Ascalonis ad vesperam requiescent, quia visitabit eos Dominus Deus eorum, et avertet captivitatem eorum.

verses.text: Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts the God of Israel, Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrha, the dryness of thorns, and heaps of salt, and a desert even for ever: the remnant of my people shall make a spoil of them, and the residue of my nation shall possess them.
verses.textLatin: Audivi opprobrium Moab, et blasphemias filiorum Ammon, quæ exprobraverunt populo meo, et magnificati sunt super terminos eorum.

verses.text: This shall befall them for their pride: because they have blasphemed, and have been magnified against the people of the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Propterea vivo ego, dicit Dominus exercituum, Deus Israël, quia Moab ut Sodoma erit, et filii Ammon quasi Gomorrha: siccitas spinarum, et acervi salis, et desertum usque in æternum: reliquiæ populi mei diripient eos, et residui gentis meæ possidebunt illos.

verses.text: The Lord shall be terrible upon them, and shall consume all the gods of the earth: and they shall adore him every man from his own place, all the islands of the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Hoc eis eveniet pro superbia sua, quia blasphemaverunt et magnificati sunt super populum Domini exercituum.

verses.text: You Ethiopians, also shall be slain with my sword.
verses.textLatin: Horribilis Dominus super eos, et attenuabit omnes deos terræ: et adorabunt eum viri de loco suo, omnes insulæ gentium.

verses.text: And he will stretch out his hand upon the north, and will destroy Assyria: and he will make the beautiful city a wilderness, and as a place not passable, and as a desert.
verses.textLatin: Sed et vos, Æthiopes, interfecti gladio meo eritis.

verses.text: And flocks shall lie down in the midst thereof, all the beasts of the nations: and the bittern and the urchin shall lodge in the threshold thereof: thevoice of the singing bird in the window, the raven on the upper post, for I will consume her strength.
verses.textLatin: Et extendet manum suam super aquilonem, et perdet Assur, et ponet speciosam in solitudinem, et in invium, et quasi desertum.

verses.text: This is the glorious city that dwelt insecurity: that said in her heart: I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desert, a place for beasts to lie down in? every one that passeth by her, shall hiss, and wag his hand.
verses.textLatin: Et accubabunt in medio ejus greges, omnes bestiæ gentium; et onocrotalus et ericius in liminibus ejus morabuntur: vox cantantis in fenestra, corvus in superliminari, quoniam attenuabo robur ejus.

verses.text: Woe  to the provoking and redeemed city, the dove.
verses.textLatin: Hæc est civitas gloriosa habitans in confidentia, quæ dicebat in corde suo: Ego sum, et extra me non est alia amplius: quomodo facta est in desertum cubile bestiæ? omnis qui transit per eam sibilabit, et movebit manum suam.

verses.text: She hath not hearkened to the voice, neither hath she received discipline: she hath not trusted in the Lord, she drew not near to her God.
verses.textLatin: Væ provocatrix, et redempta civitas, columba!

verses.text: Her princes are in the midst of her as roaring lions: her judges are evening wolves, they left nothing for the morning.
verses.textLatin: non audivit vocem, et non suscepit disciplinam; in Domino non est confisa, ad Deum suum non appropinquavit.

verses.text: Her prophets are senseless, men without faith: her priests have polluted the sanctuary, they have acted unjustly against the law.
verses.textLatin: Principes ejus in medio ejus quasi leones rugientes; judices ejus lupi vespere, non relinquebant in mane.

verses.text: The just Lord is in the midst thereof, he will not do iniquity: in the morning, in the morning he will bring his judgment to light, and it shall not be hid: but the wicked man hath not known shame.
verses.textLatin: Prophetæ ejus vesani, viri infideles; sacerdotes ejus polluerunt sanctum, injuste egerunt contra legem.

verses.text: I have destroyed the nations, and their towers are beaten down: I have made their ways desert, so that there is none that passeth by: their cities are desolate, there is not a man remaining, nor any inhabitant.
verses.textLatin: Dominus justus in medio ejus non faciet iniquitatem; mane, mane judicium suum dabit in lucem, et non abscondetur; nescivit autem iniquus confusionem.

verses.text: I said: Surely thou wilt fear me, thou wilt receive correction: and her dwelling shall not perish, for all things wherein I have visited her: but they rose earlyand corrupted all their thoughts.
verses.textLatin: Disperdidi gentes, et dissipati sunt anguli earum; desertas feci vias eorum, dum non est qui transeat; desolatæ sunt civitates eorum, non remanente viro, neque ullo habitatore.

verses.text: Wherefore expect me, saith the Lord, in the day of my resurrection that is to come, for my judgment is to assemble the Gentiles, and to gather the kingdoms: and to pour upon them my indignation, all my fierce anger: for with the fire of my jealousy shall all the earth be devoured.
verses.textLatin: Dixi: Attamen timebis me, suscipies disciplinam; et non peribit habitaculum ejus, propter omnia in quibus visitavi eam: verumtamen diluculo surgentes corruperunt omnes cogitationes suas.

verses.text: Because then I will restore to the people a chosen lip, that all may call upon the name of the Lord, and may serve him with one shoulder.
verses.textLatin: Quapropter exspecta me, dicit Dominus, in die resurrectionis meæ in futurum: quia judicium meum ut congregem gentes, et colligam regna, et effundam super eos indignationem meam, omnem iram furoris mei: in igne enim zeli mei devorabitur omnis terra.

verses.text: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, shall my suppliants, the children of my dispersed people, bring me an offering.
verses.textLatin: Quia tunc reddam populis labium electum, ut invocent omnes in nomine Domini, et serviant ei humero uno.

verses.text: In that day thou shalt not be ashamed for all thy doings, wherein thou hast transgressed against me for then I will take away out of the midst of thee thy proud boasters, and thou shalt no more be lifted up because of my holy mountain.
verses.textLatin: Ultra flumina Æthiopiæ, inde supplices mei; filii dispersorum meorum deferent munus mihi.

verses.text: And I will leave in the midst of thee a poor and needy people: and they shall hope in the name of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: In die illa non confunderis super cunctis adinventionibus tuis, quibus prævaricata es in me, quia tunc auferam de medio tui magniloquos superbiæ tuæ, et non adjicies exaltari amplius in monte sancto meo.

verses.text: The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth: for they shall feed, and shall lie down, and there shall be none to make them afraid.
verses.textLatin: Et derelinquam in medio tui populum pauperem et egenum: et sperabunt in nomine Domini.

verses.text: Give praise, O daughter of Sion: shout, O Israel: be glad, and rejoice with all thy heart, O daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Reliquiæ Israël non facient iniquitatem, nec loquentur mendacium, et non invenietur in ore eorum lingua dolosa, quoniam ipsi pascentur, et accubabunt, et non erit qui exterreat.

verses.text: The Lord hath taken away thy judgment, he hath turned away thy enemies: the king of Israel, the Lord, is in the midst of thee, thou shalt fear evil no more.
verses.textLatin: Lauda, filia Sion; jubila, Israël: lætare, et exsulta in omni corde, filia Jerusalem.

verses.text: In that day it shall be said to Jerusalem: Fear not: to Sion: Let not thy hands be weakened.
verses.textLatin: Abstulit Dominus judicium tuum; avertit inimicos tuos. Rex Israël Dominus in medio tui: non timebis malum ultra.

verses.text: The Lord thy God in the midst of thee is mighty, he will save: he will rejoice over thee with gladness, he will be silent in his love, he will be joyful over thee in praise.
verses.textLatin: In die illa dicetur Jerusalem: Noli timere; Sion: Non dissolvantur manus tuæ.

verses.text: The triflers that were departed from the law, I will gather together, because they were of thee: that thou mayest nomore suffer reproach for them.
verses.textLatin: Dominus Deus tuus in medio tui fortis, ipse salvabit: gaudebit super te in lætitia, silebit in dilectione sua, exsultabit super te in laude.

verses.text: Behold I will cut off all that have afflicted thee at that time: and I will save her that halteth, and will gather her that was cast out: and I will get them praise, and a name, in all the land where they had been put to confusion.
verses.textLatin: Nugas, qui a lege recesserant, congregabo, quia ex te erant: ut non ultra habeas super eis opprobrium.

verses.text: At that time, when I will bring you: and at the time that I will gather you: for I will give you a name, and praise among all the people of the earth, when I shall have brought back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ecce ego interficiam omnes qui afflixerunt te in tempore illo: et salvabo claudicantem, et eam quæ ejecta fuerat congregabo: et ponam eos in laudem, et in nomen, in omni terra confusionis eorum,

verses.text: In  the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet, to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, governor of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, saying:
verses.textLatin: In anno secundo Darii regis, in mense sexto, in die una mensis, factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, ad Zorobabel, filium Salathiel, ducem Juda, et ad Jesum, filium Josedec, sacerdotem magnum, dicens:

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: This people saith: The time is not yet come for building the house of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Hæc ait Dominus exercituum, dicens: Populus iste dicit: Nondum venit tempus domus Domini ædificandæ.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, dicens:

verses.text: Is it time for you to dwell in ceiled houses, and this house lie desolate?
verses.textLatin: Numquid tempus vobis est ut habitetis in domibus laqueatis, et domus ista deserta?

verses.text: And now thus saith the Lord of hosts: Set your hearts to consider your ways.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras.

verses.text: You have sowed much, and brought in little: you have eaten, but have not had enough: you have drunk, but have not been filled with drink: you have clothed yourselves, but have not been warmed: and he that hath earned wages, put them into a bag with holes.
verses.textLatin: Seminastis multum, et intulistis parum; comedistis, et non estis satiati; bibistis, et non estis inebriati; operuistis vos, et non estis calefacti; et qui mercedes congregavit, misit eas in sacculum pertusum.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Set your hearts upon your ways:
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Ponite corda vestra super vias vestras;

verses.text: Go up to the mountain, bring timber, and build the house: and it shall be acceptable to me, and I shall be glorified, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: ascendite in montem, portate ligna, et ædificate domum: et acceptabilis mihi erit, et glorificabor, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: You have looked for more, and behold it became less, and you brought it home, and I blowed it away: why, saith the Lord of hosts? because my house is desolate, and you make haste every man to his own house.
verses.textLatin: Respexistis ad amplius, et ecce factum est minus; et intulistis in domum, et exsufflavi illud: quam ob causam? dicit Dominus exercituum: quia domus mea deserta est, et vos festinatis unusquisque in domum suam.

verses.text: Therefore the heavens over you were stayed from giving dew, and the earth was hindered from yielding her fruits:
verses.textLatin: Propter hoc super vos prohibiti sunt cæli ne darent rorem, et terra prohibita est ne daret germen suum:

verses.text: And I called for a drought upon the land, and upon the mountains, and upon the corn, and upon the wine, and upon the oil, and upon all that the ground bringeth forth, and upon men, and upon beasts, and upon all the labour of the hands.
verses.textLatin: et vocavi siccitatem super terram, et super montes, et super triticum, et super vinum, et super oleum, et quæcumque profert humus, et super homines, et super jumenta, et super omnem laborem manuum.

verses.text: Then Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and all the remnant of the people hearkened to the voice of the Lord their God, and to the words of Aggeus the prophet, as the Lord their God sent him to them: and the people feared before the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Zorobabel, filius Salathiel, et Jesus, filius Josedec, sacerdos magnus, et omnes reliquiæ populi, vocem Domini Dei sui, et verba Aggæi prophetæ, sicut misit eum Dominus Deus eorum ad eos, et timuit populus a facie Domini.

verses.text: And Aggeus the messenger of the Lord, as one of the messengers of the Lord, spoke, saying to the people: I am with you, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Aggæus, nuntius Domini de nuntiis Domini, populo dicens: Ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zorobabel the son of Salathiel governor of Juda, and the spirit of Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people: and they went in, and did the work in the house of the Lord of hosts their God.
verses.textLatin: Et suscitavit Dominus spiritum Zorobabel, filii Salathiel, ducis Juda, et spiritum Jesu, filii Josedec, sacerdotis magni, et spiritum reliquorum de omni populo: et ingressi sunt, et faciebant opus in domo Domini exercituum, Dei sui.

verses.text: In  the four and twentieth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king, they began.
verses.textLatin: In die vigesima et quarta mensis, in sexto mense, in anno secundo Darii regis.

verses.text: And in the seventh month, the word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet, saying:
verses.textLatin: In septimo mense, vigesima et prima mensis, factum est verbum Domini in manu Aggæi prophetæ, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel the governor of Juda, and to Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and to the rest of the people, saying:
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad Zorobabel, filium Salathiel, ducem Juda, et ad Jesum, filium Josedec, sacerdotem magnum, et ad reliquos populi, dicens:

verses.text: Who is left among you, that saw this house in its first glory? and how do you see it now? is it not in comparison to thatas nothing in your eyes?
verses.textLatin: Quis in vobis est derelictus, qui vidit domum istam in gloria sua prima? et quid vos videtis hanc nunc? numquid non ita est, quasi non sit in oculis vestris?

verses.text: Yet now take courage, O Zorobabel, saith the Lord, and take courage, O Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and take courage, all ye people of the land, saith the Lord of hosts: and perform (for I am with you, saith the Lord of hosts)
verses.textLatin: Et nunc confortare, Zorobabel, dicit Dominus; et confortare, Jesu, fili Josedec, sacerdos magne; et confortare, omnis populus terræ, dicit Dominus exercituum: et facite (quoniam ego vobiscum sum, dicit Dominus exercituum)

verses.text: The word that I covenanted with you when you came out of the land of Egypt: and my spirit shall be in the midst of you: fear not.
verses.textLatin: verbum quod pepigi vobiscum cum egrederemini de terra Ægypti: et spiritus meus erit in medio vestrum: nolite timere.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord of hosts: Yet one little while, and I will move the heaven and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land.
verses.textLatin: Quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Adhuc unum modicum est, et ego commovebo cælum, et terram, et mare, et aridam.

verses.text: And I will move all nations: AND THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME: and I will fill this house with glory: saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et movebo omnes gentes, et veniet desideratus cunctis gentibus: et implebo domum istam gloria, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Meum est argentum, et meum est aurum, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first, saith the Lord of hosts: and in this place I will give peace, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Magna erit gloria domus istius novissimæ plus quam primæ, dicit Dominus exercituum: et in loco isto dabo pacem, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: In the four and twentieth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius the king, the word of the Lord came to Aggeus the prophet, saying:
verses.textLatin: In vigesima et quarta noni mensis, in anno secundo Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Aggæum prophetam, dicens:

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Ask the priests the law, saying:
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Interroga sacerdotes legem, dicens:

verses.text: If a man carry sanctified flesh in the skirt of his garment, and touch with his skirt, bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any meat: shall it be sanctified? And the priests answered, and said: No.
verses.textLatin: Si tulerit homo carnem sanctificatam in ora vestimenti sui, et tetigerit de summitate ejus panem, aut pulmentum, aut vinum, aut oleum, aut omnem cibum, numquid sanctificabitur? Respondentes autem sacerdotes, dixerunt: Non.

verses.text: And Aggeus said: If one that is unclean by occasion of a soul touch any of all these things, shall it be defiled? And the priests answered, and said: It shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Aggæus: Si tetigerit pollutus in anima ex omnibus his, numquid contaminabitur? Et responderunt sacerdotes, et dixerunt: Contaminabitur.

verses.text: And Aggeus answered, and said: So is this people, and so is this nation before my face, saith the Lord, and so is all the work of their hands: and all that they have offered there, shall be defiled.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Aggæus, et dixit: Sic populus iste, et sic gens ista ante faciem meam, dicit Dominus, et sic omne opus manuum eorum: et omnia quæ obtulerunt ibi, contaminata erunt.

verses.text: And now consider in your hearts, from this day and upward, before there was a stone laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc ponite corda vestra a die hac et supra, antequam poneretur lapis super lapidem in templo Domini.

verses.text: When you went to a heap of twenty bushels, and they became ten: and you went into the press, to press out fifty vessels, and they became twenty.
verses.textLatin: Cum accederetis ad acervum viginti modiorum, et fierent decem; et intraretis ad torcular, ut exprimeretis quinquaginta lagenas, et fiebant viginti.

verses.text: I struck you with a blasting wind, and all the works of your hand with the mildew and with hail, yet there was none among you that returned to me, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Percussi vos vento urente, et aurugine, et grandine omnia opera manuum vestrarum: et non fuit in vobis qui reverteretur ad me, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: Set your hearts from this day, and henceforward, from the four and twentieth day of the ninth month: from the day that the foundations of the temple of the Lord were laid, and lay it up in your hearts.
verses.textLatin: Ponite corda vestra ex die ista, et in futurum, a die vigesima et quarta noni mensis: a die qua fundamenta jacta sunt templi Domini, ponite super cor vestrum.

verses.text: Is the seed as yet sprung up? or hath the vine, and the fig tree, and the pomegranate, and the olive tree as yet flourished? from this day I will bless you.
verses.textLatin: Numquid jam semen in germine est, et adhuc vinea, et ficus, et malogranatum, et lignum olivæ non floruit? ex die ista benedicam.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord came a second time to Aggeus in the four and twentieth day of the month, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et factum est verbum Domini secundo ad Aggæum in vigesima et quarta mensis, dicens:

verses.text: Speak to Zorobabel the governor of Juda, saying: I will move both heaven and earth.
verses.textLatin: Loquere ad Zorobabel ducem Juda, dicens: Ego movebo cælum pariter et terram,

verses.text: And I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms, and will destroy the strength of the kingdom of the Gentiles: and I will overthrow the chariot, and him that rideth therein: and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother.
verses.textLatin: et subvertam solium regnorum, et conteram fortitudinem regni gentium: et subvertam quadrigam et ascensorem ejus, et descendent equi, et ascensores eorum, vir in gladio fratris sui.

verses.text: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts, I will take thee, O Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, my servant, saith the Lord, and will make thee as a signet, for I have chosen thee, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: In die illa, dicit Dominus exercituum, assumam te, Zorobabel, fili Salathiel, serve meus, dicit Dominus: et ponam te quasi signaculum, quia te elegi, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: In  the eighth month, in the second year of king Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, the son of Addo, the prophet, saying:
verses.textLatin: Omnis autem cognatio ejus et omnis generatio ejus in bona vita et in sancta conversatione permansit, ita ut accepti essent tam Deo quam hominibus, et cunctis habitantibus in terra.

verses.text: The Lord hath been exceeding angry with your fathers.
verses.textLatin: In mense octavo, in anno secundo Darii regis, factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ filii Addo prophetam, dicens:

verses.text: And thou shalt say to them: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Turn ye to me, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will turn to you, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Iratus est Dominus super patres vestros iracundia.

verses.text: Be not as your fathers, to whom the former prophets have cried, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: Turn ye from your evil ways, and from your wicked thoughts: but they did not give ear, neither did they hearken to me, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et dices ad eos: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Convertimini ad me, ait Dominus exercituum, et convertar ad vos, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: Your fathers, where are they? and the prophets, shall they live always?
verses.textLatin: Ne sitis sicut patres vestri, ad quos clamabant prophetæ priores, dicentes: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Convertimini de viis vestris malis, et de cogitationibus vestris pessimis: et non audierunt, neque attenderunt ad me, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: But yet my words, and my ordinances, which I gave in charge to my servants the prophets, did they not take hold of your fathers, and they returned, and said: As the Lord of hosts thought to do to us according to our ways, and according to our devices, so he hath done to us.
verses.textLatin: Patres vestri, ubi sunt? et prophetæ numquid in sempiternum vivent?

verses.text: In the four and twentieth day of the eleventh month which is called Sabath, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, the son of Addo, the prophet, saying:
verses.textLatin: Verumtamen verba mea, et legitima mea, quæ mandavi servis meis prophetis, numquid non comprehenderunt patres vestros, et conversi sunt, et dixerunt: Sicut cogitavit Dominus exercituum facere nobis secundum vias nostras, et secundum adinventiones nostras, fecit nobis?

verses.text: I saw by night, and behold a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees, that were in the bottom: and behind him were horses, red, speckled, and white.
verses.textLatin: In die vigesima et quarta undecimi mensis Sabath, in anno secundo Darii, factum est verbum Domini ad Zachariam filium Barachiæ filii Addo prophetam, dicens:

verses.text: And I said: What are these, my Lord? and the angel that spoke in me, said to me: I will shew thee what these are:
verses.textLatin: Vidi per noctem, et ecce vir ascendens super equum rufum, et ipse stabat inter myrteta, quæ erant in profundo, et post eum equi rufi, varii, et albi.

verses.text: And the man that stood among the myrtle trees answered, and said: These are they, whom the Lord hath sent to walk through the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Quid sunt isti, domine mi? Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me: Ego ostendam tibi quid sint hæc.

verses.text: And they answered the angel of the Lord, that stood among the myrtle trees, and said: We have walked through the earth, and behold all the earth is inhabited, and is at rest.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit vir qui stabat inter myrteta, et dixit: Isti sunt quos misit Dominus ut perambulent terram.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord answered, and said: O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda, with which thou hast been angry? this is now the seventieth year.
verses.textLatin: Et responderunt angelo Domini, qui stabat inter myrteta, et dixerunt: Perambulavimus terram, et ecce omnis terra habitatur, et quiescit.

verses.text: And the Lord answered the angel, that spoke in me, good words, comfortable words.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit angelus Domini, et dixit: Domine exercituum, usquequo tu non misereberis Jerusalem, et urbium Juda, quibus iratus es? iste jam septuagesimus annus est.

verses.text: And the angel that spoke in me, said to me: Cry thou, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I am zealous for Jerusalem, and Sion with a great zeal.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Dominus angelo qui loquebatur in me verba bona, verba consolatoria.

verses.text: And I am angry with a great anger with the wealthy nations: for I was angry a little, but they helped forward the evil.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me angelus qui loquebatur in me: Clama, dicens: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Zelatus sum Jerusalem et Sion zelo magno,

verses.text: Therefore thus saith the Lord: I will return to Jerusalem in mercies: my house shall be built in it, saith the Lord of hosts: and the building line shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et ira magna ego irascor super gentes opulentas, quia ego iratus sum parum, ipsi vero adjuverunt in malum.

verses.text: Cry yet, saying: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: My cities shall yet flow with good things: and the Lord will yet comfort Sion, and he will yet choose Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Propterea hæc dicit Dominus: Revertar ad Jerusalem in misericordiis, et domus mea ædificabitur in ea, ait Dominus exercituum, et perpendiculum extendetur super Jerusalem.

verses.text: And I lifted up my eyes, and saw: and behold four horns.
verses.textLatin: Adhuc clama, dicens: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Adhuc affluent civitates meæ bonis, et consolabitur adhuc Dominus Sion, et eliget adhuc Jerusalem.

verses.text: And I said to the angel that spoke in me: What are these? And he said to me: These are the horns that have scattered Juda, and Israel, and Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi, et ecce quatuor cornua.

verses.text: And the Lord shewed me four smiths.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi ad angelum qui loquebatur in me: Quid sunt hæc? Et dixit ad me: Hæc sunt cornua quæ ventilaverunt Judam, et Israël, et Jerusalem.

verses.text: And I said: What come these to do? and he spoke, saying: These are the horns which have scattered Juda every man apart, and none of them lifted up his head: and these are come to fray them, to cast down the horns of the nations, that have lifted up the horn upon the land of Juda to scatter it.
verses.textLatin: Et ostendit mihi Dominus quatuor fabros.

verses.text: And  I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold a man, with a measuring line in his hand.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Quid isti veniunt facere? Qui ait, dicens: Hæc sunt cornua quæ ventilaverunt Judam per singulos viros, et nemo eorum levavit caput suum: et venerunt isti deterrere ea, ut dejiciant cornua gentium, quæ levaverunt cornu super terram Juda ut dispergerent eam.

verses.text: And I said: Whither goest thou? and he said to me: To measure Jerusalem, and to see how great is the breadth thereof, and how great the length thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et levavi oculos meos, et vidi, et ecce vir, et in manu ejus funiculus mensorum.

verses.text: And behold the angel that spoke in me went forth, and another angel went out to meet him.
verses.textLatin: Et dixi: Quo tu vadis? Et dixit ad me: Ut metiar Jerusalem, et videam quanta sit latitudo ejus, et quanta longitudo ejus.

verses.text: And he said to him: Run, speak to this young man, saying: Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls, by reason of the multitude of men, and of the beasts in the midst thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce angelus qui loquebatur in me egrediebatur, et angelus alius egrediebatur in occursum ejus:

verses.text: And I will be to it, saith the Lord, a wall of fire round about: and I will be in glory in the midst thereof.
verses.textLatin: et dixit ad eum: Curre, loquere ad puerum istum, dicens: Absque muro habitabitur Jerusalem, præ multitudine hominum et jumentorum in medio ejus.

verses.text: O, O flee ye out of the land of the north, saith the Lord, for I have scattered you into the four winds of heaven, saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et ego ero ei, ait Dominus, murus ignis in circuitu, et in gloria ero in medio ejus.

verses.text: O Sion, flee, thou that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon:
verses.textLatin: O, o, fugite de terra aquilonis, dicit Dominus, quoniam in quatuor ventos cæli dispersi vos, dicit Dominus.

verses.text: For thus saith the Lord of hosts: After the glory he hath sent me to the nations that have robbed you: for he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye:
verses.textLatin: O Sion! fuge, quæ habitas apud filiam Babylonis:

verses.text: For behold I lift up my hand upon them, and they shall be a prey to those that served them: and you shall know that the Lord of hosts sent me.
verses.textLatin: quia hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Post gloriam misit me ad gentes quæ spoliaverunt vos: qui enim tetigerit vos, tangit pupillam oculi mei:

verses.text: Sing praise, and rejoice, O daughter of Sion: for behold I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee: saith the Lord.
verses.textLatin: quia ecce ego levo manum meam super eos, et erunt prædæ his qui serviebant sibi: et cognoscetis quia Dominus exercituum misit me.

verses.text: And many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and they shall be my people, and I will dwell in the midst of thee: and thou shalt know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me to thee.
verses.textLatin: Lauda et lætare, filia Sion, quia ecce ego venio, et habitabo in medio tui, ait Dominus.

verses.text: And the Lord shall possess Juda his portion in the sanctified land: and he shall yet choose Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et applicabuntur gentes multæ ad Dominum in die illa, et erunt mihi in populum, et habitabo in medio tui: et scies quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad te.

verses.text: Let all flesh be silent at the presence of the Lord: for he is risen up out of his holy habitation.
verses.textLatin: Et possidebit Dominus Judam partem suam in terra sanctificata, et eliget adhuc Jerusalem.

verses.text: And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord: and Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary.
verses.textLatin: Sileat omnis caro a facie Domini, quia consurrexit de habitaculo sancto suo.

verses.text: And the Lord said to Satan: The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan: and the Lord that chose Jerusalem rebuke thee: Is not this a brand plucked out of the fire?
verses.textLatin: Et ostendit mihi Dominus Jesum sacerdotem magnum, stantem coram angelo Domini: et Satan stabat a dextris ejus ut adversaretur ei.

verses.text: And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments: and he stood before the face of the angel.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Dominus ad Satan: Increpet Dominus in te, Satan! et increpet Dominus in te, qui elegit Jerusalem! numquid non iste torris est erutus de igne?

verses.text: Who answered, and said to them that stood before him, saying: Take away the filthy garments from him. And he said to him: Behold I have taken away thy iniquity, and have clothed thee with change of garments.
verses.textLatin: Et Jesus erat indutus vestibus sordidis, et stabat ante faciem angeli.

verses.text: And he said: Put a clean mitre upon his head: and they put a clean mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments, and the angel of the Lord stood.
verses.textLatin: Qui respondit, et ait ad eos qui stabant coram se, dicens: Auferte vestimenta sordida ab eo. Et dixit ad eum: Ecce abstuli a te iniquitatem tuam, et indui te mutatoriis.

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord protested to Jesus, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et dixit: Ponite cidarim mundam super caput ejus. Et posuerunt cidarim mundam super caput ejus, et induerunt eum vestibus: et angelus Domini stabat.

verses.text: Thus saith the Lord of hosts: If thou wilt walk in my ways, and keep my charge, thou also shalt judge my house, and shalt keep my courts, and I will give thee some of them that are now present here to walk with thee.
verses.textLatin: Et contestabatur angelus Domini Jesum, dicens:

verses.text: Hear, O Jesus thou high priest, thou and thy friends that dwell before thee, for they are portending men: for behold I WILL BRING MY SERVANT THE ORIENT.
verses.textLatin: Hæc dicit Dominus exercituum: Si in viis meis ambulaveris, et custodiam meam custodieris, tu quoque judicabis domum meam, et custodies atria mea, et dabo tibi ambulantes de his qui nunc hic assistunt.

verses.text: For behold the stone that I have laid before Jesus: upon one stone there are seven eyes: behold I will grave the graving thereof, saith the Lord of hosts: and I will take away the iniquity of that land in one day.
verses.textLatin: Audi, Jesu sacerdos magne, tu et amici tui, qui habitant coram te, quia viri portendentes sunt: ecce enim ego adducam servum meum Orientem.

verses.text: In that day, saith the Lord of hosts,every man shall call his friend under the vine and under the fig tree.
verses.textLatin: Quia ecce lapis quem dedi coram Jesu: super lapidem unum septem oculi sunt: ecce ego cælabo sculpturam ejus, ait Dominus exercituum, et auferam iniquitatem terræ illius in die una.

verses.text: And  the angel that spoke in me came again: and he waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep.
verses.textLatin: In die illa, dicit Dominus exercituum, vocabit vir amicum suum subter vitem et subter ficum.

verses.text: And he said to me: What seest thou? And I said: I have looked, and behold a candlestick all of gold, and its lamp upon the top of it: and the seven lights thereof upon it: and seven funnels for the lights that were upon the top thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est angelus qui loquebatur in me, et suscitavit me quasi virum qui suscitatur de somno suo.

verses.text: And two olive trees over it: one upon the right side of the lamp, and the other upon the left side thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad me: Quid tu vides? Et dixi: Vidi, et ecce candelabrum aureum totum, et lampas ejus super caput ipsius, et septem lucernæ ejus super illud, et septem infusoria lucernis quæ erant super caput ejus.

verses.text: And I answered, and said to the angel that spoke in me, saying: What are these things, my lord?
verses.textLatin: Et duæ olivæ super illud: una a dextris lampadis, et una a sinistris ejus.

verses.text: And the angel that spoke in me answered, and said to me: Knowest thou not what these things are? And I said: No, my lord.
verses.textLatin: Et respondi, et aio ad angelum qui loquebatur in me, dicens: Quid sunt hæc, domine mi?

verses.text: And he answered, and spoke to me, saying: This is the word of the Lord to Zorobabel, saying: Not with an army, nor by might, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit angelus qui loquebatur in me, et dixit ad me: Numquid nescis quid sunt hæc? Et dixi: Non, domine mi.

verses.text: Who art thou, O great mountain, before Zorobabel? thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring out the chief stone, and shall give equal grace to the grace thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit, et ait ad me, dicens: Hoc est verbum Domini ad Zorobabel, dicens: Non in exercitu, nec in robore, sed in spiritu meo, dicit Dominus exercituum.

verses.text: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
verses.textLatin: Quis tu, mons magne, coram Zorobabel? In planum: et educet lapidem primarium, et exæquabit gratiam gratiæ ejus.

verses.text: The hands of Zorobabel have laid the foundations of this house, and his hands shall finish it: and you shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me to you.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est verbum Domini ad me, dicens:

verses.text: For who hath despised little days? and they shall rejoice, and shall see the tin plummet in the hand of Zorobabel. These are the seven eyes of the Lord, that run to and fro through the whole earth.
verses.textLatin: Manus Zorobabel fundaverunt domum istam, et manus ejus perficient eam: et scietis quia Dominus exercituum misit me ad vos.

verses.text: And I answered, and said to him: What are these two olive trees upon the right side of the candlestick, and upon the left side thereof ?
