verses.textLatin: Sanctificatio ejus desolata est sicut solitudo; dies festi ejus conversi sunt in luctum, sabbata ejus in opprobrium, honores ejus in nihilum.

verses.text: Her dishonour was increased according to her glory, and her excellency was turned into mourning.
verses.textLatin: Secundum gloriam ejus multiplicata est ignominia ejus, et sublimitas ejus conversa est in luctum.

verses.text: And king Antiochus wrote to all his kingdom, that all the people should be one: and every one should leave his own law.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit rex Antiochus omni regno suo ut esset omnis populus unus: et relinqueret unusquisque legem suam.

verses.text: And all nations consented according to the word of king Antiochus.
verses.textLatin: Et consenserunt omnes gentes secundum verbum regis Antiochi:

verses.text: And many of Israel consented to his service, and they sacrificed to idols, and profaned the sabbath.
verses.textLatin: et multi ex Israël consenserunt servituti ejus, et sacrificaverunt idolis, et coinquinaverunt sabbatum.

verses.text: And the king sent letters by the hands of messengers to Jerusalem, and to all the cities of Juda: that they should follow the law of the nations of the earth,
verses.textLatin: Et misit rex libros per manus nuntiorum in Jerusalem, et in omnes civitates Juda, ut sequerentur leges gentium terræ,

verses.text: And should forbid holocausts and sacrifices, and atonements to be made in the temple of God.
verses.textLatin: et prohiberent holocausta et sacrificia, et placationes fieri in templo Dei,

verses.text: And should prohibit the sabbath, and the festival days, to be celebrated.
verses.textLatin: et prohiberent celebrari sabbatum, et dies solemnes:

verses.text: And he commanded the holy places to be profaned, and the holy people of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et jussit coinquinari sancta, et sanctum populum Israël.

verses.text: And he commanded altars to be built, and temples, and idols, and swine’s flesh to be immolated, and unclean beasts.
verses.textLatin: Et jussit ædificari aras, et templa, et idola, et immolari carnes suillas, et pecora communia,

verses.text: And that they should leave their children uncircumcised, and let their souls be defiled with all uncleannesses, and abominations, to the end that they should forget the law, and should change all the justifications of God.
verses.textLatin: et relinquere filios suos incircumcisos, et coinquinari animas eorum in omnibus immundis, et abominationibus, ita ut obliviscerentur legem, et immutarent omnes justificationes Dei:

verses.text: And that whosoever would not do according to the word of king Antiochus should be put to death.
verses.textLatin: et quicumque non fecissent secundum verbum regis Antiochi, morerentur.

verses.text: According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom, and he appointed rulers over the people that should force them to do these things.
verses.textLatin: Secundum omnia verba hæc scripsit omni regno suo: et præposuit principes populo, qui hæc fieri cogerent.

verses.text: And they commanded the cities of Juda to sacrifice.
verses.textLatin: Et jusserunt civitatibus Juda sacrificare.

verses.text: Then many of the people were gathered to them that had forsaken the law of the Lord: and they committed evils in the land:
verses.textLatin: Et congregati sunt multi de populo ad eos qui dereliquerant legem Domini, et fecerunt mala super terram:

verses.text: And they drove away the people of Israel into lurking holes, and into the secret places of fugitives.
verses.textLatin: et effugaverunt populum Israël in abditis, et in absconditis fugitivorum locis.

verses.text: On the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundred and forty-fifth year, king Antiochus set up the abominable idol of desolation upon the altar of God, and they built altars throughout all the cities of Juda round about:
verses.textLatin: Die quintadecima mensis Casleu, quinto et quadragesimo et centesimo anno, ædificavit rex Antiochus abominandum idolum desolationis super altare Dei, et per universas civitates Juda in circuitu ædificaverunt aras:

verses.text: And they burnt incense, and sacrificed at the doors of the houses, and in the streets.
verses.textLatin: et ante januas domorum et in plateis incendebant thura, et sacrificabant:

verses.text: And they cut in pieces, and burnt with fire the books of the law of God:
verses.textLatin: et libros legis Dei combusserunt igni, scindentes eos:

verses.text: And every one with whom the books of the testament of the Lord were found, and whosoever observed the law of the Lord, they put to death, according to the edict of the king.
verses.textLatin: et apud quemcumque inveniebantur libri testamenti Domini, et quicumque observabat legem Domini, secundum edictum regis trucidabant eum.

verses.text: Thus by their power did they deal with the people of Israel, that were found in the cities month after month.
verses.textLatin: In virtute sua faciebant hæc populo Israël, qui inveniebatur in omni mense et mense in civitatibus.

verses.text: And on the five and twentieth day of the month they sacrificed upon the altar of the idol that was over against the altar of God.
verses.textLatin: Et quinta et vigesima die mensis sacrificabant super aram, quæ erat contra altare.

verses.text: Now the women that circumcised their children, were slain according to the commandment of king Antiochus.
verses.textLatin: Et mulieres, quæ circumcidebant filios suos, trucidabantur secundum jussum regis Antiochi,

verses.text: And they hanged the children about their necks in all their houses: and those that had circumcised them, they put to death.
verses.textLatin: et suspendebant pueros a cervicibus per universas domos eorum: et eos, qui circumciderant illos, trucidabant.

verses.text: And many of the people of Israel determined with themselves, that they would not eat unclean things: and they chose rather to die than to be defiled with unclean meats.
verses.textLatin: Et multi de populo Israël definierunt apud se, ut non manducarent immunda: et elegerunt magis mori, quam cibis coinquinari immundis:

verses.text: And they would not break the holy law of God, and they were put to death:
verses.textLatin: et noluerunt infringere legem Dei sanctam, et trucidati sunt:

verses.text: And there was very great wrath upon the people.
verses.textLatin: et facta est ira magna super populum valde.

verses.text: In  those days arose Mathathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and he abode in the mountain of Modin.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis surrexit Mathathias filius Joannis filii Simeonis, sacerdos ex filiis Joarib, ab Jerusalem, et consedit in monte Modin:

verses.text: And he had five sons: John who was surnamed Gaddis:
verses.textLatin: et habebat filios quinque, Joannem, qui cognominabatur Gaddis:

verses.text: And Simon, who was surnamed Thasi:
verses.textLatin: et Simonem, qui cognominabatur Thasi:

verses.text: And Judas, who was called Machabeus:
verses.textLatin: et Judam, qui vocabatur Machabæus:

verses.text: And Eleazar, who was surnamed Abaron: and Jonathan, who was surnamed Apphus.
verses.textLatin: et Eleazarum, qui cognominabatur Abaron: et Jonathan, qui cognominabatur Apphus:

verses.text: These saw the evils that were done in the people of Juda, and in Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: hi viderunt mala, quæ fiebant in populo Juda, et in Jerusalem.

verses.text: And Mathathias said: Woe is me, wherefore was I born to see the ruin of my people, and the ruin of the holy city, and to dwell there, when it is given into the hands of the enemies?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Mathathias: Væ mihi! ut quid natus sum videre contritionem populi mei, et contritionem civitatis sanctæ, et sedere illic, cum datur in manibus inimicorum?

verses.text: The holy places are come into the hands of strangers: her temple is become as a man without honour.
verses.textLatin: Sancta in manu extraneorum facta sunt: templum ejus sicut homo ignobilis.

verses.text: The vessels of her glory are carried away captive: her old men are murdered in the streets, and her young men are fallen by the sword of the enemies.
verses.textLatin: Vasa gloriæ ejus captiva abducta sunt: trucidati sunt senes ejus in plateis, et juvenes ejus ceciderunt in gladio inimicorum.

verses.text: What nation hath not inherited her kingdom, and gotten of her spoils?
verses.textLatin: Quæ gens non hæreditavit regnum ejus et non obtinuit spolia ejus?

verses.text: All her ornaments are taken away. She that was free is made a slave.
verses.textLatin: Omnis compositio ejus ablata est. Quæ erat libera, facta est ancilla.

verses.text: And behold our sanctuary, and our beauty, and our glory is laid waste, and the Gentiles have defiled them.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce sancta nostra, et pulchritudo nostra, et claritas nostra desolata est, et coinquinaverunt ea gentes.

verses.text: To what end then should we live any longer?
verses.textLatin: Quo ergo nobis adhuc vivere?

verses.text: And Mathathias and his sons rent their garments, and they covered themselves with haircloth, and made great lamentation.
verses.textLatin: Et scidit vestimenta sua Mathathias, et filii ejus: et operuerunt se ciliciis, et planxerunt valde.

verses.text: And they that were sent from king Antiochus came thither, to compel them that were fled into the city of Modin, to sacrifice, and to burn incense, and to depart from the law of God.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt illuc qui missi erant a rege Antiocho, ut cogerent eos, qui confugerant in civitatem Modin, immolare, et accendere thura, et a lege Dei discedere.

verses.text: And many of the people of Israel consented, and came to them: but Mathathias and his sons stood firm.
verses.textLatin: Et multi de populo Israël consentientes accesserunt ad eos: sed Mathathias et filii ejus constanter steterunt.

verses.text: And they that were sent from Antiochus, answering, said to Mathathias: Thou art a ruler, and an honourable, and great man in this city, and adorned with sons, and brethren.
verses.textLatin: Et respondentes qui missi erant ab Antiocho, dixerunt Mathathiæ: Princeps, et clarissimus et magnus es in hac civitate, et ornatus filiis et fratribus:

verses.text: Therefore come thou first, and obey the king’s commandment, as all nations have done, and the men of Juda, and they that remain in Jerusalem: and thou, and thy sons, shall be in the number of the king’s friends, and enriched with gold, and silver, and many presents.
verses.textLatin: ergo accede prior, et fac jussum regis, sicut fecerunt omnes gentes, et viri Juda, et qui remanserunt in Jerusalem: et eris tu, et filii tui, inter amicos regis, et amplificatus auro, et argento, et muneribus multis.

verses.text: Then Mathathias answered, and said with a loud voice: Although all nations obey king Antiochus, so as to depart every man from the service of the law of his fathers, and consent to his commandments:
verses.textLatin: Et respondit Mathathias, et dixit magna voce: Etsi omnes gentes regi Antiocho obediunt, ut discedat unusquisque a servitute legis patrum suorum, et consentiat mandatis ejus:

verses.text: I and my sons, and my brethren will obey the law of our fathers.
verses.textLatin: ego et filii mei, et fratres mei, obediemus legi patrum nostrorum:

verses.text: God be merciful unto us: it is not profitable for us to forsake the law, and the justices of God:
verses.textLatin: propitius sit nobis Deus: non est nobis utile relinquere legem, et justitias Dei:

verses.text: We will not hearken to the words of king Antiochus, neither will we sacrifice, and transgress the commandments of our law, to go another way.
verses.textLatin: non audiemus verba regis Antiochi, nec sacrificabimus transgredientes legis nostræ mandata, ut eamus altera via.

verses.text: Now as he left off speaking these words, there came a certain Jew in the sight of all to sacrifice to the idols upon the altar in the city of Modin, according to the king’s commandment.
verses.textLatin: Et ut cessavit loqui verba hæc, accessit quidam Judæus in omnium oculis sacrificare idolis super aram in civitate Modin, secundum jussum regis:

verses.text: And Mathathias saw and was grieved and his reins trembled, and his wrath was kindled according to the judgment of the law, and running upon him he slew him upon the altar:
verses.textLatin: et vidit Mathathias, et doluit, et contremuerunt renes ejus, et accensus est furor ejus secundum judicium legis, et insiliens trucidavit eum super aram:

verses.text: Moreover the man whom king Antiochus had sent, who compelled them to sacrifice, he slew at the same time, and pulled down the altar,
verses.textLatin: sed et virum, quem rex Antiochus miserat, qui cogebat immolare, occidit in ipso tempore, et aram destruxit:

verses.text: And shewed zeal for the law, as Phinees did by Zamri the son of Salomi.
verses.textLatin: et zelatus est legem, sicut fecit Phinees Zamri filio Salomi.

verses.text: And Mathathias cried out in the city with a loud voice, saying: Every one that hath zeal for the law, and maintaineth the testament, let him follow me.
verses.textLatin: Et exclamavit Mathathias voce magna in civitate, dicens: Omnis qui zelum habet legis, statuens testamentum, exeat post me.

verses.text: So he, and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that they had in the city.
verses.textLatin: Et fugit ipse, et filii ejus in montes, et reliquerunt quæcumque habebant in civitate.

verses.text: Then many that sought after judgment, and justice, went down into the desert:
verses.textLatin: Tunc descenderunt multi quærentes judicium, et justitiam, in desertum:

verses.text: And they abode there, they and their children, and their wives, and their cattle: because afflictions increased upon them.
verses.textLatin: et sederunt ibi ipsi, et filii eorum, et mulieres eorum, et pecora eorum: quoniam inundaverunt super eos mala.

verses.text: And it was told to the king’s men, and to the army that was in Jerusalem in the city of David, that certain men who had broken the king’s commandment, were gone away into the secret places in the wilderness, and that many were gone after them.
verses.textLatin: Et renuntiatum est viris regis, et exercitui qui erat in Jerusalem civitate David, quoniam discessissent viri quidam, qui dissipaverunt mandatum regis, in loca occulta in deserto, et abiissent post illos multi.

verses.text: And forthwith they went out towards them, and made war against them on the sabbath day,
verses.textLatin: Et statim perrexerunt ad eos, et constituerunt adversus eos prælium in die sabbatorum,

verses.text: And they said to them: Do you still resist? come forth, and do according to the edict of king Antiochus, and you shall live.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt ad eos: Resistitis et nunc adhuc? exite, et facite secundum verbum regis Antiochi, et vivetis.

verses.text: And they said: We will not come forth, neither will we obey the king’s edict, to profane the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Et dixerunt: Non exibimus, neque faciemus verbum regis, ut polluamus diem sabbatorum.

verses.text: And they made haste to give them battle.
verses.textLatin: Et concitaverunt adversus eos prælium.

verses.text: But they answered them not, neither did they cast a stone at them, nor stopped up the secret places,
verses.textLatin: Et non responderunt eis, nec lapidem miserunt in eos, nec oppilaverunt loca occulta,

verses.text: Saying: Let us all die in our innocency: and heaven and earth shall be witnesses for us, that you put us to death wrongfully.
verses.textLatin: dicentes: Moriamur omnes in simplicitate nostra: et testes erunt super nos cælum et terra, quod injuste perditis nos.

verses.text: So they gave them battle on the sabbath: and they were slain with their wives, and their children, and their cattle, to the number of a thousand persons.
verses.textLatin: Et intulerunt illis bellum sabbatis: et mortui sunt ipsi, et uxores eorum, et filii eorum, et pecora eorum usque ad mille animas hominum.

verses.text: And Mathathias and his friends heard of it, and they mourned for them exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Mathathias et amici ejus, et luctum habuerunt super eos valde.

verses.text: And every man said to his neighbour: If we shall all do as our brethren have done, and not fight against the heathens for our lives, and our justifications: they will now quickly root us out of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit vir proximo suo: Si omnes fecerimus sicut fratres nostri fecerunt, et non pugnaverimus adversus gentes pro animabus nostris et justificationibus nostris, nunc citius disperdent nos a terra.

verses.text: And they determined in that day, saying: Whosoever shall come up against us to fight on the sabbath day, we will fight against him: and we will not all die, as our brethren that were slain in the secret places.
verses.textLatin: Et cogitaverunt in die illa, dicentes: Omnis homo, quicumque venerit ad nos in bello die sabbatorum, pugnemus adversus eum: et non moriemur omnes, sicut mortui sunt fratres nostri in occultis.

verses.text: Then was assembled to them the congregation of the Assideans, the stoutest of Israel, every one that had a good will for the law.
verses.textLatin: Tunc congregata est ad eos synagoga Assidæorum fortis viribus ex Israël, omnis voluntarius in lege:

verses.text: And all they that fled from the evils, joined themselves to them, and were a support to them.
verses.textLatin: et omnes, qui fugiebant a malis, additi sunt ad eos, et facti sunt illis ad firmamentum.

verses.text: And they gathered an army, and slew the sinners in their wrath, and the wicked men in their indignation: and the rest fled to the nations for safety.
verses.textLatin: Et collegerunt exercitum, et percusserunt peccatores in ira sua, et viros iniquos in indignatione sua: et ceteri fugerunt ad nationes, ut evaderent.

verses.text: And Mathathias and his friends went round about, and they threw down the altars:
verses.textLatin: Et circuivit Mathathias et amici ejus, et destruxerunt aras:

verses.text: And they circumcised all the children whom they found in the confines of Israel that were uncircumcised: and they did valiantly.
verses.textLatin: et circumciderunt pueros incircumcisos quotquot invenerunt in finibus Israël: et in fortitudine.

verses.text: And they pursued after the children of pride, and the work prospered in their hands:
verses.textLatin: Et persecuti sunt filios superbiæ, et prosperatum est opus in manibus eorum:

verses.text: And they recovered the law out of the hands of the nations, and out of the hands of the kings: and they yielded not the horn to the sinner.
verses.textLatin: et obtinuerunt legem de manibus gentium, et de manibus regum, et non dederant cornu peccatori.

verses.text: Now the days drew near that Mathathias should die, and he said to his sons: Now hath pride and chastisement gotten strength, and the time of destruction, and the wrath of indignation:
verses.textLatin: Et appropinquaverunt dies Mathathiæ moriendi, et dixit filiis suis: Nunc confortata est superbia, et castigatio, et tempus eversionis, et ira indignationis.

verses.text: Now therefore, O my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, o filii, æmulatores estote legis, et date animas vestras pro testamento patrum vestrorum,

verses.text: And call to remembrance the works of the fathers, which they have done in their generations: and you shall receive great glory, and an everlasting name.
verses.textLatin: et mementote operum patrum, quæ fecerunt in generationibus suis: et accipietis gloriam magnam, et nomen æternum.

verses.text: Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was reputed to him unto justice?
verses.textLatin: Abraham nonne in tentatione inventus est fidelis, et reputatum est ei ad justitiam?

verses.text: Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment, and he was made lord of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: Joseph in tempore angustiæ suæ custodivit mandatum, et factus est dominus Ægypti.

verses.text: Phinees our father, by being fervent in the zeal of God, received the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.
verses.textLatin: Phinees pater noster, zelando zelum Dei, accepit testamentum sacerdotii æterni.

verses.text: Jesus, whilst he fulfilled the word, was made ruler in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Jesus dum implevit verbum, factus est dux in Israël.

verses.text: Caleb, for bearing witness before the congregation, received an inheritance.
verses.textLatin: Caleb dum testificatur in ecclesia, accepit hæreditatem.

verses.text: David by his mercy obtained the throne of an everlasting kingdom.
verses.textLatin: David in sua misericordia consecutus est sedem regni in sæcula.

verses.text: Elias, while he was full of zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven.
verses.textLatin: Elias, dum zelat zelum legis, receptus est in cælum.

verses.text: Ananias and Azarias and Misael by believing, were delivered out of the flame.
verses.textLatin: Ananias et Azarias et Misaël credentes, liberati sunt de flamma.

verses.text: Daniel in his innocency was delivered out of the mouth of the lions.
verses.textLatin: Daniel in sua simplicitate liberatus est de ore leonum.

verses.text: And thus consider through all generations: that none that trust in him fail in strength.
verses.textLatin: Et ita cogitate per generationem et generationem: quia omnes qui sperant in eum, non infirmantur.

verses.text: And fear not the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung, and worms:
verses.textLatin: Et a verbis viri peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus stercus et vermis est:

verses.text: To day he is lifted up, and to morrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his earth; and his thought is come to nothing.
verses.textLatin: hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur: quia conversus est in terram suam, et cogitatio ejus periit.

verses.text: You therefore, my sons, take courage, and behave manfully in the law: for by it you shall be glorious.
verses.textLatin: Vos ergo filii, confortamini, et viriliter agite in lege: quia in ipsa gloriosi eritis.

verses.text: And behold, I know that your brother Simon is a man of counsel: give ear to him always, and he shall be a father to you.
verses.textLatin: Et ecce Simon frater vester, scio quod vir consilii est: ipsum audite semper, et ipse erit vobis pater.

verses.text: And Judas Machabeus who is valiant and strong from his youth up, let him be the leader of your army, and he shall manage the war of the people.
verses.textLatin: Et Judas Machabæus, fortis viribus a juventute sua, sit vobis princeps militiæ, et ipse aget bellum populi.

verses.text: And you shall take to you all that observe the law: and revenge ye the wrong of your people.
verses.textLatin: Et adducetis ad vos omnes factores legis: et vindicate vindictam populi vestri.

verses.text: Render to the Gentiles their reward, and take heed to the precepts of the law.
verses.textLatin: Retribuite retributionem gentibus, et intendite in præceptum legis.

verses.text: And he blessed them, and was joined to his fathers.
verses.textLatin: Et benedixit eos, et appositus est ad patres suos.

verses.text: And he died in the hundred and forty-sixth year: and he was buried by his sons in the sepulchres of his fathers in Modin, and all Israel mourned for him with great mourning.
verses.textLatin: Et defunctus est anno centesimo et quadragesimo sexto: et sepultus est a filiis suis in sepulchris patrum suorum in Modin, et planxerunt eum omnis Israël planctu magno.

verses.text: Then  his son Judas, called Machabeus, rose up in his stead.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit Judas, qui vocabatur Machabæus, filius ejus, pro eo:

verses.text: And all his brethren helped him, and all they that had joined themselves to his father, and they fought with cheerfulness the battle of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et adjuvabant eum omnes fratres ejus, et universi qui se conjunxerant patri ejus, et præliabantur prælium Israël cum lætitia.

verses.text: And he got his people great honour, and put on a breastplate as a giant, and girt his warlike armour about him in battles, and protected the camp with his sword.
verses.textLatin: Et dilatavit gloriam populo suo, et induit se loricam sicut gigas, et succinxit se arma bellica sua in præliis, et protegebat castra gladio suo.

verses.text: In his acts he was like a lion, and like a lion’s whelp roaring for his prey.
verses.textLatin: Similis factus est leoni in operibus suis, et sicut catulus leonis rugiens in venatione.

verses.text: And he pursued the wicked and sought them out, and them that troubled his people he burnt with fire:
verses.textLatin: Et persecutus est iniquos perscrutans eos: et qui conturbabant populum suum, eos succendit flammis:

verses.text: And his enemies were driven away for fear of him, and all the workers of iniquity were troubled: and salvation prospered in his hand.
verses.textLatin: et repulsi sunt inimici ejus præ timore ejus, et omnes operarii iniquitatis conturbati sunt: et directa est salus in manu ejus.

verses.text: And he grieved many kings, and made Jacob glad with his works, and his memory is blessed for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et exacerbabat reges multos, et lætificabat Jacob in operibus suis, et in sæculum memoria ejus in benedictione.

verses.text: And he went through the cities of Juda, and destroyed the wicked out of them, and turned away wrath from Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et perambulavit civitates Juda, et perdidit impios ex eis, et avertit iram ab Israël.

verses.text: And he was renowned even to the utmost part of the earth, and he gathered them that were perishing.
verses.textLatin: Et nominatus est usque ad novissimum terræ, et congregavit pereuntes.

verses.text: And Apollonius gathered together the Gentiles, and a numerous and great army from Samaria, to make war against Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et congregavit Apollonius gentes, et a Samaria virtutem multam et magnam ad bellandum contra Israël.

verses.text: And Judas understood it, and went forth to meet him: and he overthrew him, and killed him: and many fell down slain, and the rest fled away.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Judas, et exiit obviam illi: et percussit, et occidit illum: et ceciderunt vulnerati multi, et reliqui fugerunt.

verses.text: And he took their spoils, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and fought with it all his lifetime.
verses.textLatin: Et accepit spolia eorum: et gladium Apollonii abstulit Judas, et erat pugnans in eo omnibus diebus.

verses.text: And Seron captain of the army of Syria heard that Judas had assembled a company of the faithful, and a congregation with him,
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Seron princeps exercitus Syriæ, quod congregavit Judas congregationem fidelium, et ecclesiam secum,

verses.text: And he said: I will get me a name, and will be glorified in the kingdom, and will overthrow Judas, and those that are with him, that have despised the edict of the king.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Faciam mihi nomen, et glorificabor in regno, et debellabo Judam, et eos qui cum ipso sunt, qui spernebant verbum regis.

verses.text: And he made himself ready: and the host of the wicked went up with him, strong succours, to be revenged of the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et præparavit se: et ascenderunt cum eo castra impiorum fortes auxiliarii ut facerent vindictam in filios Israël.

verses.text: And they approached even as far as Bethoron: and Judas went forth to meet him, with a small company.
verses.textLatin: Et appropinquaverunt usque ad Bethoron: et exivit Judas obviam illi cum paucis.

verses.text: But when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Judas: How shall we, being few, be able to fight against so great a multitude and so strong, and we are ready to faint with fasting to day?
verses.textLatin: Ut autem viderunt exercitum venientem sibi obviam, dixerunt Judæ: Quomodo poterimus pauci pugnare contra multitudinem tantam, et tam fortem, et nos fatigati sumus jejunio hodie?

verses.text: And Judas said: It is an easy matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few: and there is no difference in the sight of the God of heaven to deliver with a great multitude, or with a small company:
verses.textLatin: Et ait Judas: Facile est concludi multos in manus paucorum: et non est differentia in conspectu Dei cæli liberare in multis, et in paucis:

verses.text: For the success of war is not in the multitude of the army, but strength cometh from heaven.
verses.textLatin: quoniam non in multitudine exercitus victoria belli, sed de cælo fortitudo est.

verses.text: They come against us with an insolent multitude, and with pride, to destroy us, and our wives, and our children, and to take our spoils.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi veniunt ad nos in multitudine contumaci, et superbia, ut disperdant nos, et uxores nostras, et filios nostros, et ut spolient nos:

verses.text: But we will fight for our lives and our laws:
verses.textLatin: nos vero pugnabimus pro animabus nostris, et legibus nostris:

verses.text: And the Lord himself will overthrow them before our face: but as for you, fear them not.
verses.textLatin: et ipse Dominus conteret eos ante faciem nostram: vos autem ne timueritis eos.

verses.text: And as soon as he had made an end of speaking, he rushed suddenly upon them: and Seron and his host were overthrown before him:
verses.textLatin: Ut cessavit autem loqui, insiluit in eos subito: et contritus est Seron et exercitus ejus in conspectu ipsius:

verses.text: And he pursued him by the descent of Bethoron even to the plain, and there fell of them eight hundred men, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
verses.textLatin: et persecutus est eum in descensu Bethoron usque in campum, et ceciderunt ex eis octingenti viri, reliqui autem fugerunt in terram Philisthiim.

verses.text: And the fear of Judas and of his brethren, and the dread of them fell upon all the nations round about them.
verses.textLatin: Et cecidit timor Judæ ac fratrum ejus, et formido super omnes gentes in circuitu eorum:

verses.text: And his fame came to the king, and all nations told of the battles of Judas.
verses.textLatin: et pervenit ad regem nomen ejus, et de præliis Judæ narrabant omnes gentes.

verses.text: Now when king Antiochus heard these words, he was angry in his mind: and he sent and gathered the forces of all his kingdom, an exceeding strong army.
verses.textLatin: Ut audivit autem rex Antiochus sermones istos, iratus est animo: et misit, et congregavit exercitum universi regni sui, castra fortia valde:

verses.text: And he opened his treasury, and gave out pay to the army for a year: and he commanded them, that they should be ready for all things.
verses.textLatin: et aperuit ærarium suum, et dedit stipendia exercitui in annum: et mandavit illis ut essent parati ad omnia.

verses.text: And he perceived that the money of his treasures failed, and that the tributes of the country were small because of the dissension, and the evil that he had brought upon the land, that he might take away the laws of old times:
verses.textLatin: Et vidit quod defecit pecunia de thesauris suis, et tributa regionis modica propter dissensionem et plagam quam fecit in terra, ut tolleret legitima, quæ erant a primis diebus:

verses.text: And he feared that he should not have as formerly enough, for charges and gifts, which he had given before with a liberal hand: for he had abounded more than the kings that had been before him.
verses.textLatin: et timuit ne non haberet ut semel et bis, in sumptus et donaria, quæ dederat ante larga manu: et abundaverat super reges qui ante eum fuerant.

verses.text: And he was greatly perplexed in mind, and purposed to go into Persia, and to take tributes of the countries, and to gather much money.
verses.textLatin: Et consternatus erat animo valde, et cogitavit ire in Persidem, et accipere tributa regionum, et congregare argentum multum.

verses.text: And he left Lysias, a nobleman of the blood royal, to oversee the affairs of the kingdom, from the river Euphrates even to the river of Egypt:
verses.textLatin: Et reliquit Lysiam hominem nobilem de genere regali, super negotia regia, a flumine Euphrate usque ad flumen Ægypti,

verses.text: And to bring up his son Antiochus, till he came again.
verses.textLatin: et ut nutriret Antiochum filium suum, donec rediret.

verses.text: And he delivered to him half the army, and the elephants: and he gave him charge concerning all that he would have done, and concerning the inhabitants of Judea, and Jerusalem:
verses.textLatin: Et tradidit ei medium exercitum, et elephantos: et mandavit ei de omnibus quæ volebat, et de inhabitantibus Judæam, et Jerusalem:

verses.text: And that he should send an army against them, to destroy and root out the strength of Israel, and the remnant of Jerusalem, and to take away the memory of them from that place:
verses.textLatin: et ut mitteret ad eos exercitum ad conterendam et extirpandam virtutem Israël, et reliquias Jerusalem, et auferendam memoriam eorum de loco:

verses.text: And that he should settle strangers to dwell in all their coasts, and divide their land by lot.
verses.textLatin: et ut constitueret habitatores filios alienigenas in omnibus finibus eorum, et sorte distribueret terram eorum.

verses.text: So the king took the half of the army that remained, and went forth from Antioch the chief city of his kingdom, in the hundred and forty-seventh year: and he passed over the river Euphrates, and went through the higher countries.
verses.textLatin: Et rex assumpsit partem exercitus residui, et exivit ab Antiochia civitate regni sui anno centesimo et quadragesimo septimo: et transfretavit Euphraten flumen, et perambulabat superiores regiones.

verses.text: Then Lysias chose Ptolemee the son of Dorymenus, and Nicanor, and Gorgias, mighty men of the king’s friends.
verses.textLatin: Et elegit Lysias Ptolemæum filium Dorymini, et Nicanorem, et Gorgiam, viros potentes ex amicis regis:

verses.text: And he sent with them forty thousand men, and seven thousand horsemen: to go into the land of Juda, and to destroy it according to the king’s orders.
verses.textLatin: et misit cum eis quadraginta millia virorum, et septem millia equitum, ut venirent in terram Juda, et disperderent eam secundum verbum regis.

verses.text: So they went forth with all their power, and came, and pitched near Emmaus in the plain country.
verses.textLatin: Et processerunt cum universa virtute sua, et venerunt, et applicuerunt Emmaum in terra campestri.

verses.text: And the merchants of the countries heard the fame of them: and they took silver and gold in abundance, and servants: and they came into the camp, to buy the children of Israel for slaves: and there were joined to them the forces of Syria, and of the land of the strangers.
verses.textLatin: Et audierunt mercatores regionum nomen eorum: et acceperunt argentum, et aurum multum valde, et pueros, et venerunt in castra ut acciperent filios Israël in servos, et additi sunt ad eos exercitus Syriæ, et terræ alienigenarum.

verses.text: And Judas and his brethren saw that evils were multiplied, and that the armies approached to their borders: and they knew the orders the king had given to destroy the people and utterly abolish them.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Judas et fratres ejus, quia multiplicata sunt mala, et exercitus applicabant ad fines eorum: et cognoverunt verba regis, quæ mandavit populo facere in interitum et consummationem:

verses.text: And they said every man to his neighbour: Let us raise up the low condition of our people, and let us fight for our people, and our sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt unusquisque ad proximum suum: Erigamus dejectionem populi nostri, et pugnemus pro populo nostro, et sanctis nostris.

verses.text: And the assembly was gathered that they might be ready for battle: and that they might pray, and ask mercy and compassion.
verses.textLatin: Et congregatus est conventus ut essent parati in prælium, et ut orarent et peterent misericordiam et miserationes.

verses.text: Now Jerusalem was not inhabited, but was like a desert: there was none of her children that went in or out: and the sanctuary was trodden down: and the children of strangers were in the castle, there was the habitation of the Gentiles: and joy was taken away from Jacob, and the pipe and harp ceased there.
verses.textLatin: Et Jerusalem non habitabatur, sed erat sicut desertum: non erat qui ingrederetur et egrederetur de natis ejus. Et sanctum conculcabatur: et filii alienigenarum erant in arce; ibi erat habitatio gentium: et ablata est voluptas a Jacob, et defecit ibi tibia et cithara.

verses.text: And they assembled together, and came to Maspha over against Jerusalem: for in Maspha was a place of prayer heretofore in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et congregati sunt, et venerunt in Maspha contra Jerusalem, quia locus orationis erat in Maspha ante in Israël.

verses.text: And they fasted that day, and put on haircloth, and put ashes upon their heads: and they rent their garments:
verses.textLatin: Et jejunaverunt illa die, et induerunt se ciliciis, et cinerem imposuerunt capiti suo, et disciderunt vestimenta sua:

verses.text: And they laid open the books of the law, in which the Gentiles searched for the likeness of their idols:
verses.textLatin: et expanderunt libros legis, de quibus scrutabantur gentes similitudinem simulacrorum suorum:

verses.text: And they brought the priestly ornaments, and the firstfruits and tithes, and stirred up the Nazarites that had fulfilled their days:
verses.textLatin: et attulerunt ornamenta sacerdotalia, et primitias, et decimas: et suscitaverunt Nazaræos, qui impleverant dies,

verses.text: And they cried with a loud voice toward heaven, saying: What shall we do with these, and whither shall we carry them?
verses.textLatin: et clamaverunt voce magna in cælum, dicentes: Quid faciemus istis, et quo eos ducemus?

verses.text: For thy holies are trodden down, and are profaned, and thy priests are in mourning, and are brought low.
verses.textLatin: et sancta tua conculcata sunt, et contaminata sunt, et sacerdotes tui facti sunt in luctum, et in humilitatem:

verses.text: And behold the nations are come together against us to destroy us: thou knowest what they intend against us.
verses.textLatin: et ecce nationes convenerunt adversum nos ut nos disperdant: tu scis quæ cogitant in nos.

verses.text: How shall we be able to stand before their face, unless thou, O God, help us?
verses.textLatin: Quomodo poterimus subsistere ante faciem eorum, nisi tu, Deus, adjuves nos?

verses.text: Then they sounded with trumpets, and cried out with a loud voice.
verses.textLatin: Et tubis exclamaverunt voce magna.

verses.text: And after this Judas appointed captains over the people, over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc constituit Judas duces populi, tribunos, et centuriones, et pentacontarchos, et decuriones.

verses.text: And he said to them that were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, that they should return every man to his house, according to the law.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit his, qui ædificabant domos, et sponsabant uxores, et plantabant vineas, et formidolosis, ut redirent unusquisque in domum suam secundum legem.

verses.text: So they removed the camp, and pitched on the south side of Emmaus.
verses.textLatin: Et moverunt castra, et collocaverunt ad austrum Emmaum.

verses.text: And Judas said: Gird yourselves, and be valiant men, and be ready against the morning, that you may fight with these nations that are assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Judas: Accingimini, et estote filii potentes, et estote parati in mane, ut pugnetis adversus nationes has quæ convenerunt adversus nos disperdere nos, et sancta nostra:

verses.text: For it is better for us to die in battle, than to see the evils of our nation, and of the holies:
verses.textLatin: quoniam melius est nos mori in bello, quam videre mala gentis nostræ, et sanctorum.

verses.text: Nevertheless as it shall be the will of God in heaven so be it done.
verses.textLatin: Sicut autem fuerit voluntas in cælo, sic fiat.

verses.text: Then  Gorgias took five thousand men, and a thousand of the best horsemen: and they removed out of the camp by night.
verses.textLatin: Et assumpsit Gorgias quinque millia virorum, et mille equites electos: et moverunt castra nocte,

verses.text: That they might come upon the camp of the Jews, and strike them suddenly: and the men that were of the castle were their guides.
verses.textLatin: ut applicarent ad castra Judæorum, et percuterent eos subito: et filii, qui erant ex arce, erant illis duces.

verses.text: And Judas heard of it, and rose up, he and the valiant men, to attack the king’s forces that were in Emmaus.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Judas, et surrexit ipse et potentes percutere virtutem exercituum regis, qui erant in Emmaum:

verses.text: For as yet the army was dispersed from the camp.
verses.textLatin: adhuc enim dispersus erat exercitus a castris.

verses.text: And Gorgias came by night into the camp of Judas, and found no man, and he sought them in the mountains: for he said: These men flee from us.
verses.textLatin: Et venit Gorgias in castra Judæ noctu, et neminem invenit: et quærebat eos in montibus, quoniam dixit: Fugiunt hi a nobis.

verses.text: And when it was day, Judas shewed himself in the plain with three thousand men only, who neither had armour nor swords.
verses.textLatin: Et cum dies factus esset, apparuit Judas in campo cum tribus millibus virorum tantum, qui tegumenta et gladios non habebant:

verses.text: And they saw the camp of the Gentiles that it was strong, and the men in breastplates, and the horsemen round about them, and these were trained up to war.
verses.textLatin: et viderunt castra gentium valida, et loricatos et equitatus in circuitu eorum, et hi docti ad prælium.

verses.text: And Judas said to the men that were with him: Fear ye not their multitude, neither be ye afraid of their assault.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Judas viris, qui secum erant: Ne timueritis multitudinem eorum, et impetum eorum ne formidetis.

verses.text: Remember in what manner our fathers were saved in the Red Sea, when Pharao pursued them with a great army.
verses.textLatin: Mementote qualiter salvi facti sunt patres nostri in mari Rubro, cum sequeretur eos Pharao cum exercitu multo.

verses.text: And now let us cry to heaven: and the Lord will have mercy on us, and will remember the covenant of our fathers, and will destroy this army before our face this day:
verses.textLatin: Et nunc clamemus in cælum: et miserebitur nostri Dominus, et memor erit testamenti patrum nostrorum, et conteret exercitum istum ante faciem nostram hodie:

verses.text: And all nations shall know that there is one that redeemeth and delivereth Israel.
verses.textLatin: et scient omnes gentes quia est qui redimat et liberet Israël.

verses.text: And the strangers lifted up their eyes, and saw them coming against them.
verses.textLatin: Et elevaverunt alienigenæ oculos suos, et viderunt eos venientes ex adverso.

verses.text: And they went out of the camp to battle, and they that were with Judas sounded the trumpet.
verses.textLatin: Et exierunt de castris in prælium, et tuba cecinerunt hi qui erant cum Juda.

verses.text: And they joined battle: and the Gentiles were routed, and fled into the plain.
verses.textLatin: Et congressi sunt: et contritæ sunt gentes, et fugerunt in campum.

verses.text: But all the hindmost of them fell by the sword, and they pursued them as far as Gezeron, and even to the plains of Idumea, and of Azotus, and of Jamnia: and there fell of them to the number of three thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Novissimi autem omnes ceciderunt in gladio, et persecuti sunt eos usque Gezeron, et usque in campos Idumææ, et Azoti, et Jamniæ: et ceciderunt ex illis usque ad tria millia virorum.

verses.text: And Judas returned again with his army that followed him,
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Judas, et exercitus ejus sequens eum.

verses.text: And he said to the people: Be not greedy of the spoils: for there is war before us:
verses.textLatin: Dixitque ad populum: Non concupiscatis spolia: quia bellum contra nos est,

verses.text: And Gorgias and his army are near us in the mountain: but stand ye now against our enemies, and overthrow them, and you shall take the spoils afterwards with safety.
verses.textLatin: et Gorgias et exercitus ejus prope nos in monte: sed state nunc contra inimicos nostros, et expugnate eos, et sumetis postea spolia securi.

verses.text: And as Judas was speaking these words, behold part of them appeared looking forth from the mountain.
verses.textLatin: Et adhuc loquente Juda hæc, ecce apparuit pars quædam prospiciens de monte.

verses.text: And Gorgias saw that his men were put to flight, and that they had set fire to the camp: for the smoke that was seen declared what was done.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Gorgias quod in fugam conversi sunt sui, et succenderunt castra: fumus enim, qui videbatur, declarabat quod factum est.

verses.text: And when they had seen this, they were seized with great fear, seeing at the same time Judas and his army in the plain ready to fight.
verses.textLatin: Quibus illi conspectis timuerunt valde, aspicientes simul et Judam, et exercitum in campo paratum ad prælium.

verses.text: So they all fled away into the land of the strangers.
verses.textLatin: Et fugerunt omnes in campum alienigenarum:

verses.text: And Judas returned to take the spoils of the camp, and they got much gold, and silver, and blue silk, and purple of the sea, and great riches.
verses.textLatin: et Judas reversus est ad spolia castrorum, et acceperunt aurum multum, et argentum, et hyacinthinum, et purpuram marinam, et opes magnas.

verses.text: And returning home they sung a hymn, and blessed God in heaven, because he is good, because his mercy endureth for ever.
verses.textLatin: Et conversi, hymnum canebant, et benedicebant Deum in cælum, quoniam bonus est, quoniam in sæculum misericordia ejus.

verses.text: So Israel had a great deliverance that day.
verses.textLatin: Et facta est salus magna in Israël in die illa.

verses.text: And such of the strangers as escaped, went and told Lysias all that had happened.
verses.textLatin: Quicumque autem alienigenarum evaserunt, venerunt, et nuntiaverunt Lysiæ universa quæ acciderant.

verses.text: And when he heard these things, he was amazed and discouraged: because things had not succeeded in Israel according to his mind, and as the king had commanded.
verses.textLatin: Quibus ille auditis, consternatus animo deficiebat: quod non qualia voluit, talia contigerunt in Israël, et qualia mandavit rex.

verses.text: So the year following Lysias gathered together threescore thousand chosen men, and five thousand horsemen, that he might subdue them.
verses.textLatin: Et sequenti anno, congregavit Lysias virorum electorum sexaginta millia, et equitum quinque millia, ut debellaret eos.

verses.text: And they came into Judea, and pitched their tents in Bethoron, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt in Judæam, et castra posuerunt in Bethoron, et occurrit illis Judas cum decem millibus viris.

verses.text: And they saw that the army was strong, and he prayed, and said: Blessed art thou, O Saviour of Israel, who didst break the violence of the mighty by the hand of thy servant David, and didst deliver up the camp of the strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul and of his armourbearer.
verses.textLatin: Et viderunt exercitum fortem, et oravit, et dixit: Benedictus es, salvator Israël, qui contrivisti impetum potentis in manu servi tui David, et tradidisti castra alienigenarum in manu Jonathæ filii Saul, et armigeri ejus.

verses.text: Shut up this army in the hands of thy people Israel, and let them be confounded in their host and their horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Conclude exercitum istum in manu populi tui Israël, et confundantur in exercitu suo et equitibus.

verses.text: Strike them with fear, and cause the boldness of their strength to languish, and let them quake at their own destruction.
verses.textLatin: Da illis formidinem, et tabefac audaciam virtutis eorum, et commoveantur contritione sua.

verses.text: Cast them down with the sword of them that love thee: and let all that know thy name, praise thee with hymns.
verses.textLatin: Dejice illos gladio diligentium te: et collaudent te omnes, qui noverunt nomen tuum, in hymnis.

verses.text: And they joined battle: and there fell of the army of Lysias five thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Et commiserunt prælium: et ceciderunt de exercitu Lysiæ quinque millia virorum.

verses.text: And when Lysias saw that his men were put to flight, and how bold the Jews were, and that they were ready either to live, or to die manfully, he went to Antioch, and chose soldiers, that they might come again into Judea with greater numbers.
verses.textLatin: Videns autem Lysias fugam suorum, et Judæorum audaciam, et quod parati sunt aut vivere, aut mori fortiter, abiit Antiochiam, et elegit milites, ut multiplicati rursus venirent in Judæam.

verses.text: Then Judas, and his brethren said: Behold our enemies are discomfited: let us go up now to cleanse the holy places and to repair them.
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem Judas, et fratres ejus: Ecce contriti sunt inimici nostri: ascendamus nunc mundare sancta, et renovare.

verses.text: And all the army assembled together, and they went up into mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: Et congregatus est omnis exercitus, et ascenderunt in montem Sion.

verses.text: And they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burnt, and shrubs growing up in the courts as in a forest, or on the mountains, and the chambers joining to the temple thrown down.
verses.textLatin: Et viderunt sanctificationem desertam, et altare profanatum, et portas exustas, et in atriis virgulta nata sicut in saltu vel in montibus, et pastophoria diruta.

verses.text: And they rent their garments, and made great lamentation, and put ashes on their heads:
verses.textLatin: Et sciderunt vestimenta sua, et planxerunt planctu magno, et imposuerunt cinerem super caput suum,

verses.text: And they fell down to the ground on their faces, and they sounded with the trumpets of alarm, and they cried towards heaven.
verses.textLatin: et ceciderunt in faciem super terram, et exclamaverunt tubis signorum, et clamaverunt in cælum.

verses.text: Then Judas appointed men to fight against them that were in the castle, till they had cleansed the holy places.
verses.textLatin: Tunc ordinavit Judas viros ut pugnarent adversus eos qui erant in arce, donec emundarent sancta.

verses.text: And he chose priests without blemish, whose will was set upon the law of God:
verses.textLatin: Et elegit sacerdotes sine macula, voluntatem habentes in lege Dei:

verses.text: And they cleansed the holy places, and took away the stones that had been defiled into an unclean place.
verses.textLatin: et mundaverunt sancta, et tulerunt lapides contaminationis in locum immundum.

verses.text: And he considered about the altar of holocausts that had been profaned, what he should do with it.
verses.textLatin: Et cogitavit de altari holocaustorum, quod profanatum erat, quid de eo faceret.

verses.text: And a good counsel came into their minds, to pull it down: lest it should be a reproach to them, because the Gentiles had defiled it; so they threw it down.
verses.textLatin: Et incidit illis consilium bonum ut destruerent illud: ne forte illis esset in opprobrium, quia contaminaverunt illud gentes, et demoliti sunt illud.

verses.text: And they laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, till there should come a prophet, and give answer concerning them.
verses.textLatin: Et reposuerunt lapides in monte domus in loco apto, quoadusque veniret propheta, et responderet de eis.

verses.text: Then they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former:
verses.textLatin: Et acceperunt lapides integros secundum legem, et ædificaverunt altare novum secundum illud quod fuit prius:

verses.text: And they built up the holy places, and the things that were within the temple: and they sanctified the temple, and the courts.
verses.textLatin: et ædificaverunt sancta, et quæ intra domum erant intrinsecus: et ædem, et atria sanctificaverunt.

verses.text: And they made new holy vessels, and brought in the candlestick, and the altar of incense, and the table into the temple.
verses.textLatin: Et fecerunt vasa sancta nova, et intulerunt candelabrum, et altare incensorum, et mensam, in templum.

verses.text: And they put incense upon the altar, and lighted up the lamps that were upon the candlestick, and they gave light in the temple.
verses.textLatin: Et incensum posuerunt super altare, et accenderunt lucernas quæ super candelabrum erant, et lucebant in templo.

verses.text: And they set the loaves upon the table, and hung up the veils, and finished all the works that they had begun to make.
verses.textLatin: Et posuerunt super mensam panes, et appenderunt vela, et consummaverunt omnia opera quæ fecerant.

verses.text: And they arose before the morning on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month (which is the month of Casleu) in the hundred and forty-eighth year.
verses.textLatin: Et ante matutinum surrexerunt quinta et vigesima die mensis noni (hic est mensis Casleu) centesimi quadragesimi octavi anni:

verses.text: And they offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of holocausts which they had made.
verses.textLatin: et obtulerunt sacrificium secundum legem super altare holocaustorum novum, quod fecerunt.

verses.text: According to the time, and according to the day wherein the heathens had defiled it, in the same was it dedicated anew with canticles, and harps, and lutes, and cymbals.
verses.textLatin: Secundum tempus et secundum diem in qua contaminaverunt illud gentes, in ipsa renovatum est in canticis, et citharis, et cinyris, et in cymbalis.

verses.text: And all the people fell upon their faces, and adored, and blessed up to heaven, him that had prospered them.
verses.textLatin: Et cecidit omnis populus in faciem, et adoraverunt, et benedixerunt in cælum eum, qui prosperavit eis.

verses.text: And they kept the dedication of the altar eight days, and they offered holocausts with joy, and sacrifices of salvation, and of praise.
verses.textLatin: Et fecerunt dedicationem altaris diebus octo, et obtulerunt holocausta cum lætitia, et sacrificium salutaris et laudis.

verses.text: And they adorned the front of the temple with crowns of gold, and escutcheons, and they renewed the gates, and the chambers, and hanged doors upon them.
verses.textLatin: Et ornaverunt faciem templi coronis aureis et scutulis, et dedicaverunt portas et pastophoria, et imposuerunt eis januas.

verses.text: And there was exceeding great joy among the people, and the reproach of the Gentiles was turned away.
verses.textLatin: Et facta est lætitia in populo magna valde, et aversum est opprobrium gentium.

verses.text: And Judas, and his brethren, and all the church of Israel decreed, that the day of the dedication of the altar should be kept in its season from year to year for eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month of Casleu, with joy and gladness.
verses.textLatin: Et statuit Judas, et fratres ejus, et universa ecclesia Israël, ut agatur dies dedicationis altaris in temporibus suis ab anno in annum per dies octo a quinta et vigesima die mensis Casleu, cum lætitia et gaudio.

verses.text: They built up also at that time mount Sion, with high walls, and strong towers round about, lest the Gentiles should at any time come, and tread it down as they did before.
verses.textLatin: Et ædificaverunt in tempore illo montem Sion, et per circuitum muros altos et turres firmas, nequando venirent gentes, et conculcarent eum sicut antea fecerunt.

verses.text: And he placed a garrison there to keep it, and he fortified it to secure Bethsura, that the people might have a defence against Idumea.
verses.textLatin: Et collocavit illic exercitum, ut servarent eum, et munivit eum ad custodiendum Bethsuram, ut haberet populus munitionem contra faciem Idumææ.

verses.text: Now  it came to pass, when the nations round about heard that the altar and the sanctuary were built up as before, that they were exceeding angry.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, ut audierunt gentes in circuitu quia ædificatum est altare et sanctuarium sicut prius, iratæ sunt valde:

verses.text: And they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that were among them, and they began to kill some of the people, and to persecute them.
verses.textLatin: et cogitabant tollere genus Jacob, qui erant inter eos, et cœperunt occidere de populo, et persequi.

verses.text: Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea, and them that were in Acrabathane: because they beset the Israelites round about, and he made a great slaughter of them.
verses.textLatin: Et debellabat Judas filios Esau in Idumæa, et eos qui erant in Acrabathane, quia circumsedebant Israëlitas: et percussit eos plaga magna.

verses.text: And he remembered the malice of the children of Bean: who were a snare and a stumblingblock to the people, by lying in wait for them in the way.
verses.textLatin: Et recordatus est malitiam filiorum Bean, qui erant populo in laqueum et in scandalum, insidiantes ei in via.

verses.text: And they were shut up by him in towers, and he set upon them, and devoted them to utter destruction, and burnt their towers with fire, and all that were in them.
verses.textLatin: Et conclusi sunt ab eo in turribus, et applicuit ad eos, et anathematizavit eos, et incendit turres eorum igni cum omnibus qui in eis erant.

verses.text: Then he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found a mighty power, and much people, and Timotheus was their captain:
verses.textLatin: Et transivit ad filios Ammon, et invenit manum fortem, et populum copiosum, et Timotheum ducem ipsorum:

verses.text: And he fought many battles with them, and they were discomfited in their sight, and he smote them:
verses.textLatin: et commisit cum eis prælia multa, et contriti sunt in conspectu eorum, et percussit eos:

verses.text: And he took the city of Gazer and her towns, and returned into Judea.
verses.textLatin: et cepit Gazer civitatem et filias ejus, et reversus est in Judæam.

verses.text: And the Gentiles that were in Galaad, assembled themselves together against the Israelites that were in their quarters to destroy them: and they fled into the fortress of Datheman.
verses.textLatin: Et congregatæ sunt gentes quæ sunt in Galaad adversus Israëlitas, qui erant in finibus eorum, ut tollerent eos: et fugerunt in Datheman munitionem.

verses.text: And they sent letters to Judas and his brethren, saying: The heathens that are round about are gathered together against us, to destroy us:
verses.textLatin: Et miserunt litteras ad Judam et fratres ejus, dicentes: Congregatæ sunt adversum nos gentes per circuitum, ut nos auferant,

verses.text: And they are preparing to come, and to take the fortress into which we are fled: and Timotheus is the captain of their host.
verses.textLatin: et parant venire, et occupare munitionem, in quam confugimus: et Timotheus est dux exercitus eorum.

verses.text: Now therefore come, and deliver us out of their hands, for many of us are slain.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo veni, et eripe nos de manibus eorum, quia cecidit multitudo de nobis.

verses.text: And all our brethren that were in the places of Tubin, are killed: and they have carried away their wives, and their children, captives, and taken their spoils, and they have slain there almost a thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Et omnes fratres nostri, qui erant in locis Tubin, interfecti sunt: et captivas duxerunt uxores eorum, et natos, et spolia, et peremerunt illic fere mille viros.

verses.text: And while they were yet reading these letters, behold there came other messengers out of Galilee with their garments rent, who related according to these words:
verses.textLatin: Et adhuc epistolæ legebantur, et ecce alii nuntii venerunt de Galilæa conscissis tunicis, nuntiantes secundum verba hæc:

verses.text: Saying, that they of Ptolemais, and of Tyre, and of Sidon, were assembled against them, and all Galilee is filled with strangers, in order to consume us.
verses.textLatin: dicentes convenisse adversum se a Ptolemaida, et Tyro, et Sidone: et repleta est omnis Galilæa alienigenis, ut nos consumant.

verses.text: Now when Judas and the people heard these words, a great assembly met together to consider what they should do for their brethren that were in trouble, and were assaulted by them.
verses.textLatin: Ut audivit autem Judas et populus sermones istos, convenit ecclesia magna cogitare quid facerent fratribus suis, qui in tribulatione erant, et expugnabantur ab eis.

verses.text: And Judas said to Simon his brother: Choose thee men, and go, and deliver thy brethren in Galilee: and I, and my brother Jonathan will go into the country of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque Judas Simoni fratri suo: Elige tibi viros, et vade, et libera fratres tuos in Galilæa: ego autem et frater meus Jonathas ibimus in Galaaditim.

verses.text: And he left Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias captains of the people with the remnant of the army in Judea to keep it:
verses.textLatin: Et reliquit Josephum filium Zachariæ, et Azariam, duces populi, cum residuo exercitu in Judæa ad custodiam:

verses.text: And he commanded them, saying: Take ye the charge of this people: but make no war against the heathens, till we return.
verses.textLatin: et præcepit illis, dicens: Præestote populo huic: et nolite bellum committere adversum gentes, donec revertamur.

verses.text: Now three thousand men were allotted to Simon, to go into Galilee: and eight thousand to Judas to go into the land of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Et partiti sunt Simoni viri tria millia, ut iret in Galilæam: Judæ autem octo millia in Galaaditim.

verses.text: And Simon went into Galilee, and fought many battles with the heathens: and the heathens were discomfited before his face, and he pursued them even to the gate of Ptolemais.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit Simon in Galilæam, et commisit prælia multa cum gentibus: et contritæ sunt gentes a facie ejus, et persecutus est eos usque ad portam

verses.text: And there fell of the heathens almost three thousand men, and he took the spoils of them,
verses.textLatin: Ptolemaidis: et ceciderunt de gentibus fere tria millia virorum. Et accepit spolia eorum,

verses.text: And he took with him those that were in Galilee and in Arbatis with their wives, and children, and all that they had, and he brought them into Judea with great joy.
verses.textLatin: et assumpsit eos qui erant in Galilæa et in Arbatis, cum uxoribus, et natis, et omnibus quæ erant illis, et adduxit in Judæam cum lætitia magna.

verses.text: And Judas Machabeus, and Jonathan his brother passed over the Jordan, and went three days’ journey through the desert.
verses.textLatin: Et Judas Machabæus, et Jonathas frater ejus, transierunt Jordanem, et abierunt viam trium dierum per desertum.

verses.text: And the Nabutheans met them, and received them in a peaceable manner, and told them all that happened to their brethren in the land of Galaad,
verses.textLatin: Et occurrerunt eis Nabuthæi, et susceperunt eos pacifice, et narraverunt eis omnia quæ acciderant fratribus eorum in Galaaditide,

verses.text: And that many of them were shut up in Barasa, and in Bosor, and in Alima, and in Casphor, and in Mageth, and in Carnaim: all these strong and great cities.
verses.textLatin: et quia multi ex eis comprehensi sunt in Barasa, et Bosor, et in Alimis, et in Casphor, et Mageth, et Carnaim: hæ omnes civitates munitæ et magnæ.

verses.text: Yea, and that they were kept shut up in the rest of the cities of Galaad, and that they had appointed to bring their army on the morrow near to these cities, and to take them and to destroy them all in one day.
verses.textLatin: Sed et in ceteris civitatibus Galaaditidis tenentur comprehensi, et in crastinum constituerunt admovere exercitum civitatibus his, et comprehendere, et tollere eos in una die.

verses.text: Then Judas and his army suddenly turned their march into the desert, to Bosor, and took the city: and he slew every male by the edge of the sword, and took all their spoils, and burnt it with fire.
verses.textLatin: Et convertit Judas et exercitus ejus viam in desertum Bosor repente, et occupavit civitatem: et occidit omnem masculum in ore gladii, et accepit omnia spolia eorum, et succendit eam igni.

verses.text: And they removed from thence by night, and went till they came to the fortress.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexerunt inde nocte, et ibant usque ad munitionem.

verses.text: And it came to pass that early in the morning, when they lifted up their eyes, behold there were people without number, carrying ladders and engines to take the fortress, and assault them.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est diluculo, cum elevassent oculos suos, ecce populus multus, cujus non erat numerus, portantes scalas et machinas ut comprehenderent munitionem, et expugnarent eos.

verses.text: And Judas saw that the fight was begun, and the cry of the battle went up to heaven like a trumpet, and a great cry out of the city:
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Judas quia cœpit bellum, et clamor belli ascendit ad cælum sicut tuba, et clamor magnus de civitate:

verses.text: And he said to his host: Fight ye today for your brethren.
verses.textLatin: et dixit exercitui suo: Pugnate hodie pro fratribus vestris.

verses.text: And he came with three companies behind them, and they sounded their trumpets, and cried out in prayer.
verses.textLatin: Et venit tribus ordinibus post eos, et exclamaverunt tubis, et clamaverunt in oratione.

verses.text: And the host of Timotheus understood that it was Machabeus, and they fled away before his face: and they made a great slaughter of them: and there fell of them in that day almost eight thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Et cognoverunt castra Timothei quia Machabæus est, et refugerunt a facie ejus: et percusserunt eos plaga magna. Et ceciderunt ex eis in die illa fere octo millia virorum.

verses.text: And Judas turned aside to Maspha, and assaulted, and took it, and he slew every male thereof, and took the spoils thereof, and burnt it with fire.
verses.textLatin: Et divertit Judas in Maspha, et expugnavit, et cepit eam: et occidit omnem masculum ejus, et sumpsit spolia ejus, et succendit eam igni.

verses.text: From thence he marched, and took Casbon, and Mageth, and Bosor, and the rest of the cities of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Inde perrexit, et cepit Casbon, et Mageth, et Bosor, et reliquas civitates Galaaditidis.

verses.text: But after this Timotheus gathered another army, and camped over against Raphon beyond the torrent.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc autem verba congregavit Timotheus exercitum alium, et castra posuit contra Raphon trans torrentem.

verses.text: And Judas sent men to view the army: and they brought him word, saying: All the nations, that are round about us, are assembled unto him an army exceeding great:
verses.textLatin: Et misit Judas speculari exercitum: et renuntiaverunt ei, dicentes: Quia convenerunt ad eum omnes gentes quæ in circuitu nostro sunt, exercitus multus nimis:

verses.text: And they have hired the Arabians to help them, and they have pitched their tents beyond the torrent, ready to come to fight against thee. And Judas went to meet them.
verses.textLatin: et Arabas conduxerunt in auxilium sibi, et castra posuerunt trans torrentem, parati ad te venire in prælium. Et abiit Judas obviam illis.

verses.text: And Timotheus said to the captains of his army: When Judas and his army come near the torrent of water, if he pass over unto us first, we shall not be able to withstand him: for he will certainly prevail over us.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Timotheus principibus exercitus sui: Cum appropinquaverit Judas, et exercitus ejus, ad torrentem aquæ: si transierit ad nos prior, non poterimus sustinere eum, quia potens poterit adversum nos;

verses.text: But if he be afraid to pass over, and camp on the other side of the river, we will pass over to them and shall prevail against him.
verses.textLatin: si vero timuerit transire, et posuerit castra extra flumen, transfretamus ad eos, et poterimus adversus illum.

verses.text: Now when Judas came near the torrent of water, he set the scribes of the people by the torrent, and commanded them, saying: Suffer no man to stay behind: but let all come to the battle.
verses.textLatin: Ut autem appropinquavit Judas ad torrentem aquæ, statuit scribas populi secus torrentem, et mandavit eis, dicens: Neminem hominem reliqueritis, sed veniant omnes in prælium.

verses.text: And he passed over to them first, and all the people after him, and all the heathens were discomfited before them, and they threw away their weapons, and fled to the temple that was in Carnaim.
verses.textLatin: Et transfretavit ad illos prior, et omnis populus post eum, et contritæ sunt omnes gentes a facie eorum, et projecerunt arma sua, et fugerunt ad fanum, quod erat in Carnaim.

verses.text: And he took that city, and the temple he burnt with fire, with all things that were therein: and Carnaim was subdued, and could not stand against the face of Judas.
verses.textLatin: Et occupavit ipsam civitatem, et fanum succendit igni cum omnibus qui erant in ipso: et oppressa est Carnaim, et non potuit sustinere contra faciem Judæ.

verses.text: And Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the land of Galaad, from the least even to the greatest, and their wives, and children, and an army exceeding great, to come into the land of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et congregavit Judas universos Israëlitas, qui erant in Galaaditide, a minimo usque ad maximum, et uxores eorum, et natos, et exercitum magnum valde, ut venirent in terram Juda.

verses.text: And they came as far as Ephron: now this was a great city situate in the way, strongly fortified, and there was no means to turn from it on the right hand or on the left, but the way was through the midst of it.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt usque Ephron: et hæc civitas magna in ingressu posita, munita valde, et non erat declinare ab ea dextera vel sinistra, sed per mediam iter erat.

verses.text: And they that were in the city, shut themselves in, and stopped up the gates with stones: and Judas sent to them with peaceable words,
verses.textLatin: Et incluserunt se qui erant in civitate, et obstruxerunt portas lapidibus: et misit ad eos Judas verbis pacificis,

verses.text: Saying: Let us pass through your land, to go into our own country: and no man shall hurt you: we will only pass through on foot. But they would not open to them.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Transeamus per terram vestram, ut eamus in terram nostram: et nemo vobis nocebit, tantum pedibus transibimus. Et nolebant eis aperire.

verses.text: Then Judas commanded proclamation to be made in the camp, that they should make an assault every man in the place where he was.
verses.textLatin: Et præcepit Judas prædicare in castris, ut applicarent unusquisque in quo erat loco:

verses.text: And the men of the army drew near, and he assaulted that city all the day, and all the night, and the city was delivered into his hands:
verses.textLatin: et applicuerunt se viri virtutis, et oppugnavit civitatem illam tota die et tota nocte, et tradita est civitas in manu ejus:

verses.text: And they slew every male with the edge of the sword, and he razed the city, and took the spoils thereof, and passed through all the city over them that were slain.
verses.textLatin: et peremerunt omnem masculum in ore gladii, et eradicavit eam, et accepit spolia ejus: et transivit per totam civitatem super interfectos.

verses.text: Then they passed over the Jordan to the great plain that is over against Bethsan.
verses.textLatin: Et transgressi sunt Jordanem in campo magno, contra faciem Bethsan.

verses.text: And Judas gathered together the hindmost, and he exhorted the people all the way through, till they came into the land of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et erat Judas congregans extremos, et exhortabatur populum per totam viam, donec venirent in terram Juda:

verses.text: And they went up to mount Sion with joy and gladness, and offered holocausts, because not one of them was slain, till they had returned in peace.
verses.textLatin: et ascenderunt in montem Sion cum lætitia, et gaudio, et obtulerunt holocausta, quod nemo ex eis cecidisset donec reverterentur in pace.

verses.text: Now in the days that Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Galaad, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais,
verses.textLatin: Et in diebus quibus erat Judas et Jonathas in terra Galaad, et Simon frater ejus in Galilæa contra faciem Ptolemaidis,

verses.text: Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias captain of the soldiers, heard of the good success, and the battles that were fought.
verses.textLatin: audivit Josephus Zachariæ filius, et Azarias princeps virtutis, res bene gestas, et prælia quæ facta sunt,

verses.text: And he said: Let us also get us a name, and let us go fight against the Gentiles that are round about us.
verses.textLatin: et dixit: Faciamus et ipsi nobis nomen, et eamus pugnare adversus gentes quæ in circuitu nostro sunt.

verses.text: And he gave charge to them that were in his army, and they went towards Jamnia.
verses.textLatin: Et præcepit his qui erant in exercitu suo, et abierunt Jamniam.

verses.text: And Gorgias and his men went out of the city, to give them battle.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit Gorgias de civitate, et viri ejus obviam illis in pugnam.

verses.text: And Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, and were pursued unto the borders of Judea: and there fell, on that day, of the people of Israel about two thousand men, and there was a great overthrow of the people:
verses.textLatin: Et fugati sunt Josephus et Azarias usque in fines Judææ: et ceciderunt illo die de populo Israël ad duo millia viri, et facta est fuga magna in populo:

verses.text: Because they did not hearken to Judas, and his brethren, thinking that they should do manfully.
verses.textLatin: quia non audierunt Judam, et fratres ejus, existimantes fortiter se facturos.

verses.text: But they were not of the seed of those men by whom salvation was brought to Israel.
verses.textLatin: Ipsi autem non erant de semine virorum illorum, per quos salus facta est in Israël.

verses.text: And the men of Juda were magnified exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and of all the nations where their name was heard.
verses.textLatin: Et viri Juda magnificati sunt valde in conspectu omnis Israël, et gentium omnium ubi audiebatur nomen eorum.

verses.text: And the people assembled to them with joyful acclamations.
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt ad eos fausta acclamantes.

verses.text: Then Judas and his brethren went forth and attacked the children of Esau, in the land toward the south, and he took Chebron, and her towns: and he burnt the walls thereof and the towers all round it.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit Judas et fratres ejus, et expugnabant filios Esau in terra quæ ad austrum est, et percussit Chebron et filias ejus: et muros ejus, et turres succendit igni in circuitu.

verses.text: And he removed his camp to go into the land of the aliens, and he went through Samaria.
verses.textLatin: Et movit castra ut iret in terram alienigenarum, et perambulabat Samariam.

verses.text: In that day some priests fell in battle, while desiring to do manfully they went out unadvisedly to fight.
verses.textLatin: In die illa ceciderunt sacerdotes in bello, dum volunt fortiter facere, dum sine consilio exeunt in prælium.

verses.text: And Judas turned to Azotus into the land of the strangers, and he threw down their altars, and he burnt the statues of their gods with fire: and he took the spoils of the cities, and returned into the land of Juda.
verses.textLatin: Et declinavit Judas in Azotum in terram alienigenarum, et diruit aras eorum, et sculptilia deorum ipsorum succendit igni: et cepit spolia civitatum, et reversus est in terram Juda.

verses.text: Now  king Antiochus was going through the higher countries, and he heard that the city of Elymais in Persia was greatly renowned, and abounding in silver and gold.
verses.textLatin: Et rex Antiochus perambulabat superiores regiones, et audivit esse civitatem Elymaidem in Perside nobilissimam, et copiosam in argento et auro,

verses.text: And that there was in it a temple, exceeding rich: and coverings of gold, and breastplates, and shields which king Alexander, son of Philip the Macedonian that reigned first in Greece, had left there.
verses.textLatin: templumque in ea locuples valde, et illic velamina aurea, et loricæ, et scuta, quæ reliquit Alexander Philippi rex Macedo, qui regnavit primus in Græcia.

verses.text: Lo, he came, and sought to take the city and to pillage it: but he was not able, because the design was known to them that were in the city.
verses.textLatin: Et venit, et quærebat capere civitatem, et deprædari eam: et non potuit, quoniam innotuit sermo his qui erant in civitate:

verses.text: And they rose up against him in battle, and he fled away from thence, and departed with great sadness, and returned towards Babylonia.
verses.textLatin: et insurrexerunt in prælium, et fugit inde, et abiit cum tristitia magna, et reversus est in Babyloniam.

verses.text: And whilst he was in Persia, there came one that told him, how the armies that were in the land of Juda were put to flight:
verses.textLatin: Et venit qui nuntiaret ei in Perside, quia fugata sunt castra quæ erant in terra Juda:

verses.text: And that Lysias went with a very great power, and was put to flight before the face of the Jews, and that they were grown strong by the armour, and power, and store of spoils, which they had gotten out of the camps which they had destroyed:
verses.textLatin: et quia abiit Lysias cum virtute forti in primis, et fugatus est a facie Judæorum, et invaluerunt armis, et viribus, et spoliis multis, quæ ceperunt de castris, quæ exciderunt:

verses.text: And that they had thrown down the abomination which he had set up upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had compassed about the sanctuary with high walls as before, and Bethsura also his city.
verses.textLatin: et quia diruerunt abominationem, quam ædificaverat super altare quod erat in Jerusalem: et sanctificationem, sicut prius, circumdederunt muris excelsis, sed et Bethsuram civitatem suam.

verses.text: And it came to pass when the king heard these words, that he was struck with fear, and exceedingly moved: and he laid himself down upon his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not fallen out to him as he imagined.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est ut audivit rex sermones istos, expavit, et commotus est valde: et decidit in lectum, et incidit in languorem præ tristitia, quia non factum est ei sicut cogitabat.

verses.text: And he remained there many days: for great grief came more and more upon him, and he made account that he should die.
verses.textLatin: Et erat illic per dies multos, quia renovata est in eo tristitia magna, et arbitratus est se mori.
