verses.text: And he called for all his friends, and said to them: Sleep is gone from my eyes, and I am fallen away, and my heart is cast down for anxiety.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit omnes amicos suos, et dixit illis: Recessit somnus ab oculis meis, et concidi, et corrui corde præ sollicitudine:

verses.text: And I said in my heart: Into how much tribulation am I come, and into what floods of sorrow, wherein now I am: I that was pleasant and beloved in my power!
verses.textLatin: et dixi in corde meo: In quantam tribulationem deveni, et in quos fluctus tristitiæ, in qua nunc sum: qui jucundus eram, et dilectus in potestate mea!

verses.text: But now I remember the evils that I have done in Jerusalem, from whence also I took away all the spoils of gold, and of silver that were in it, and I sent to destroy the inhabitants of Juda without cause.
verses.textLatin: Nunc vero reminiscor malorum quæ feci in Jerusalem, unde et abstuli omnia spolia aurea et argentea quæ erant in ea, et misi auferre habitantes Judæam sine causa.

verses.text: I know therefore that for this cause these evils have found me: and behold I perish with great grief in a strange land.
verses.textLatin: Cognovi ergo quia propterea invenerunt me mala ista: et ecce pereo tristitia magna in terra aliena.

verses.text: Then he called Philip, one of his friends, and he made him regent over all his kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit Philippum, unum de amicis suis, et præposuit eum super universum regnum suum:

verses.text: And he gave him the crown, and his robe, and his ring, that he should go to Antiochus his son, and should bring him up for the kingdom.
verses.textLatin: et dedit ei diadema, et stolam suam, et annulum, ut adduceret Antiochum filium suum, et nutriret eum, et regnaret.

verses.text: So king Antiochus died there in the year one hundred and forty-nine.
verses.textLatin: Et mortuus est illic Antiochus rex anno centesimo quadragesimo nono.

verses.text: And Lysias understood that the king was dead, and he set up Antiochus his son to reign, whom he brought up young: and he called his name Eupator.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Lysias quoniam mortuus est rex, et constituit regnare Antiochum filium ejus, quem nutrivit adolescentem: et vocavit nomen ejus Eupator.

verses.text: Now they that were in the castle, had shut up the Israelites round about the holy places: and they were continually seeking their hurt, and to strengthen the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Et hi qui erant in arce, concluserant Israël in circuitu sanctorum: et quærebant eis mala semper, et firmamentum gentium.

verses.text: And Judas purposed to destroy them: and he called together all the people, to besiege them.
verses.textLatin: Et cogitavit Judas disperdere eos: et convocavit universum populum, ut obsiderent eos.

verses.text: And they came together, and besieged them in the year one hundred and fifty, and they made battering slings and engines.
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt simul, et obsederunt eos anno centesimo quinquagesimo, et fecerunt ballistas et machinas.

verses.text: And some of the besieged got out: and some wicked men of Israel joined themselves unto them.
verses.textLatin: Et exierunt quidam ex eis qui obsidebantur: et adjunxerunt se illis aliqui impii ex Israël,

verses.text: And they went to the king, and said: How long dost thou delay to execute the judgment, and to revenge our brethren?
verses.textLatin: et abierunt ad regem, et dixerunt: Quousque non facis judicium, et vindicas fratres nostros?

verses.text: We determined to serve thy father and to do according to his orders, and obey his edicts:
verses.textLatin: Nos decrevimus servire patri tuo, et ambulare in præceptis ejus, et obsequi edictis ejus:

verses.text: And for this they of our nation are alienated from us, and have slain as many of us as they could find, and have spoiled our inheritances.
verses.textLatin: et filii populi nostri propter hoc alienabant se a nobis, et quicumque inveniebantur ex nobis, interficiebantur, et hæreditates nostræ diripiebantur.

verses.text: Neither have they put forth their hand against us only, but also against all our borders.
verses.textLatin: Et non ad nos tantum extenderunt manum, sed et in omnes fines nostros:

verses.text: And behold they have approached this day to the castle of Jerusalem to take it, and they have fortified the strong hold of Bethsura:
verses.textLatin: et ecce applicuerunt hodie ad arcem Jerusalem occupare eam, et munitionem Bethsuram munierunt:

verses.text: And unless thou speedily prevent them, they will do greater things than these, and thou shalt not be able to subdue them.
verses.textLatin: et nisi præveneris eos velocius, majora quam hæc facient, et non poteris obtinere eos.

verses.text: Now when the king heard this, he was angry: and he called together all his friends, and the captains of his army, and them that were over the horsemen.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus est rex, ut hæc audivit: et convocavit omnes amicos suos, et principes exercitus sui, et eos qui super equites erant:

verses.text: There came also to him from other realms, and from the islands of the sea hired troops.
verses.textLatin: sed et de regnis aliis et de insulis maritimis venerunt ad eum exercitus conductitii.

verses.text: And the number of his army was an hundred thousand footmen, and twenty thousand horsemen, and thirty-two elephants, trained to battle.
verses.textLatin: Et erat numerus exercitus ejus, centum millia peditum, et viginti millia equitum, et elephanti triginta duo, docti ad prælium.

verses.text: And they went through Idumea, and approached to Bethsura, and fought many days, and they made engines: but they sallied forth and burnt them with fire, and fought manfully.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt per Idumæam, et applicuerunt ad Bethsuram, et pugnaverunt dies multos: et fecerunt machinas, et exierunt, et succenderunt eas igni, et pugnaverunt viriliter.

verses.text: And Judas departed from the castle, and removed the camp to Bethzacharam, over against the king’s camp.
verses.textLatin: Et recessit Judas ab arce, et movit castra ad Bethzacharam contra castra regis.

verses.text: And the king rose before it was light, and made his troops march on fiercely towards the way of Bethzacharam: and the armies made themselves ready for the battle, and they sounded the trumpets:
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit rex ante lucem, et concitavit exercitus in impetum contra viam Bethzacharam: et comparaverunt se exercitus in prælium, et tubis cecinerunt:

verses.text: And they shewed the elephants the blood of grapes, and mulberries to provoke them to fight.
verses.textLatin: et elephantis ostenderunt sanguinem uvæ et mori, ad acuendos eos in prælium:

verses.text: And they distributed the beasts by the legions: and there stood by every elephant a thousand men in coats of mail, and with helmets of brass on their heads: and five hundred horsemen set in order were chosen for every beast.
verses.textLatin: et diviserunt bestias per legiones, et astiterunt singulis elephantis mille viri in loricis concatenatis, et galeæ æreæ in capitibus eorum: et quingenti equites ordinati unicuique bestiæ electi erant.

verses.text: These before the time wheresoever the beast was, they were there: and whithersoever it went, they went, and they departed not from it.
verses.textLatin: Hi ante tempus, ubicumque erat bestia, ibi erant: et quocumque ibat, ibant, et non discedebant ab ea.

verses.text: And upon the beast, there were strong wooden towers, which covered every one of them: and engines upon them: and upon every one thirty-two valiant men, who fought from above; and an Indian to rule the beast.
verses.textLatin: Sed et turres ligneæ super eos firmæ protegentes super singulas bestias: et super eas machinæ: et super singulas viri virtutis triginta duo, qui pugnabant desuper: et Indus magister bestiæ.

verses.text: And the rest of the horsemen he placed on this side and on that side at the two wings, with trumpets to stir up the army, and to hasten them forward that stood thick together in the legions thereof.
verses.textLatin: Et residuum equitatum hinc et inde statuit in duas partes, tubis exercitum commovere, et perurgere constipatos in legionibus ejus.

verses.text: Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold, and of brass, the mountains glittered therewith, and they shone like lamps of fire.
verses.textLatin: Et ut refulsit sol in clypeos aureos et æreos, resplenduerunt montes ab eis, et resplenduerunt sicut lampades ignis.

verses.text: And part of the king’s army was distinguished by the high mountains, and the other part by the low places: and they marched on warily and orderly.
verses.textLatin: Et distincta est pars exercitus regis per montes excelsos, et alia per loca humilia: et ibant caute et ordinate.

verses.text: And all the inhabitants of the land were moved at the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the company, and the rattling of the armour, for the army was exceeding great and strong.
verses.textLatin: Et commovebantur omnes inhabitantes terram a voce multitudinis, et incessu turbæ, et collisione armorum: erat enim exercitus magnus valde, et fortis.

verses.text: And Judas and his army drew near for battle: and there fell of the king’s army six hundred men.
verses.textLatin: Et appropiavit Judas et exercitus ejus in prælium, et ceciderunt de exercitu regis sexcenti viri.

verses.text: And Eleazar the son of Saura saw one of the beasts harnessed with the king’s harness: and it was higher than the other beasts: and it seemed to him that the king was on it:
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Eleazar filius Saura unam de bestiis loricatam loricis regis: et erat eminens super ceteras bestias, et visum est ei quod in ea esset rex:

verses.text: And he exposed himself to deliver his people and to get himself an everlasting name.
verses.textLatin: et dedit se ut liberaret populum suum, et acquireret sibi nomen æternum.

verses.text: And he ran up to it boldly in the midst of the legion, killing on the right hand, and on the left, and they fell by him on this side and that side.
verses.textLatin: Et cucurrit ad eam audacter in medio legionis, interficiens a dextris et a sinistris, et cadebant ab eo huc atque illuc.

verses.text: And he went between the feet of the elephant, and put himself under it: and slew it, and it fell to the ground upon him, and he died there.
verses.textLatin: Et ivit sub pedes elephantis, et supposuit se ei, et occidit eum: et cecidit in terram super ipsum, et mortuus est illic.

verses.text: Then they seeing the strength of the king and the fierceness of his army, turned away from them.
verses.textLatin: Et videntes virtutem regis, et impetum exercitus ejus, diverterunt se ab eis.

verses.text: But the king’s army went up against them to Jerusalem: and the king’s army pitched their tents against Judea and mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: Castra autem regis ascenderunt contra eos in Jerusalem, et applicuerunt castra regis ad Judæam, et montem Sion.

verses.text: And he made peace with them that were in Bethsura: and they came forth out of the city, because they had no victuals, being shut up there, for it was the year of rest to the land.
verses.textLatin: Et fecit pacem cum his qui erant in Bethsura: et exierunt de civitate, quia non erant eis ibi alimenta conclusis, quia sabbata erant terræ.

verses.text: And the king took Bethsura: and he placed there a garrison to keep it.
verses.textLatin: Et comprehendit rex Bethsuram: et constituit illic custodiam servare eam.

verses.text: And he turned his army against the sanctuary for many days: and he set up there battering slings, and engines and instruments to cast fire, and engines to cast stones and javelins, and pieces to shoot arrows, and slings.
verses.textLatin: Et convertit castra ad locum sanctificationis dies multos: et statuit illic ballistas, et machinas, et ignis jacula, et tormenta ad lapides jactandos, et spicula, et scorpios ad mittendas sagittas, et fundibula.

verses.text: And they also made engines against their engines, and they fought for many days.
verses.textLatin: Fecerunt autem et ipsi machinas adversus machinas eorum, et pugnaverunt dies multos.

verses.text: But there were no victuals in the city, because it was the seventh year: and such as had stayed in Judea of them that came from among the nations, had eaten the residue of all that which had been stored up.
verses.textLatin: Escæ autem non erant in civitate, eo quod septimus annus esset: et qui remanserant in Judæa de gentibus, consumpserant reliquias eorum, quæ repositæ fuerant.

verses.text: And there remained in the holy places but a few, for the famine had prevailed over them: and they were dispersed every man to his own place.
verses.textLatin: Et remanserunt in sanctis viri pauci, quoniam obtinuerat eos fames: et dispersi sunt unusquisque in locum suum.

verses.text: Now Lysias heard that Philip, whom king Antiochus while he lived had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus, and to reign, to be king,
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Lysias quod Philippus, quem constituerat rex Antiochus cum adhuc viveret, ut nutriret Antiochum filium suum, et regnaret,

verses.text: Was returned from Persia, and Media, with the army that went with him, and that he sought to take upon him the affairs of the kingdom:
verses.textLatin: reversus esset a Perside et Media, et exercitus qui abierat cum ipso, et quia quærebat suscipere regni negotia:

verses.text: Wherefore he made haste to go, and say to the king and to the captains of the army: We decay daily, and our provision of victuals is small, and the place that we lay siege to is strong, and it lieth upon us to take order for the affairs of the kingdom.
verses.textLatin: festinavit ire, et dicere ad regem, et duces exercitus: Deficimus quotidie, et esca nobis modica est; et locus, quem obsidemus, est munitus, et incumbit nobis ordinare de regno.

verses.text: Now therefore let us come to an agreement with these men, and make peace with them and with all their nation.
verses.textLatin: Nunc itaque demus dextras hominibus istis, et faciamus cum illis pacem, et cum omni gente eorum:

verses.text: And let us covenant with them, that they may live according to their own laws as before. For because of our despising their laws, they have been provoked, and have done all these things.
verses.textLatin: et constituamus illis ut ambulent in legitimis suis sicut prius: propter legitima enim ipsorum, quæ despeximus, irati sunt, et fecerunt omnia hæc.

verses.text: And the proposal was acceptable in the sight of the king, and of the princes: and he sent to them to make peace: and they accepted of it.
verses.textLatin: Et placuit sermo in conspectu regis et principum: et misit ad eos pacem facere, et receperunt illam.

verses.text: And the king and the princes swore to them: and they came out of the strong hold.
verses.textLatin: Et juravit illis rex et principes, et exierunt de munitione.

verses.text: Then the king entered into mount Sion, and saw the strength of the place: and he quickly broke the oath that he had taken, and gave commandment to throw down the wall round about.
verses.textLatin: Et intravit rex montem Sion, et vidit munitionem loci: et rupit citius juramentum quod juravit, et mandavit destruere murum in gyro.

verses.text: And he departed in haste, and returned to Antioch, where he found Philip master of the city: and he fought against him, and took the city.
verses.textLatin: Et discessit festinanter, et reversus est Antiochiam, et invenit Philippum dominantem civitati: et pugnavit adversus eum, et occupavit civitatem.

verses.text: In  the hundred and fifty-first year Demetrius the son of Seleucus departed from the city of Rome, and came up with a few men into a city of the sea coast, and reigned there.
verses.textLatin: Anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo, exiit Demetrius Seleuci filius ab urbe Roma, et ascendit cum paucis viris in civitatem maritimam, et regnavit illic.

verses.text: And it came to pass, as he entered into the house of the kingdom of his fathers, that the army seized upon Antiochus, and Lysias, to bring them unto him.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, ut ingressus est domum regni patrum suorum, comprehendit exercitus Antiochum et Lysiam, ut adducerent eos ad eum.

verses.text: And when he knew it, he said: Let me not see their face.
verses.textLatin: Et res ei innotuit, et ait: Nolite mihi ostendere faciem eorum.

verses.text: So the army slew them. And Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom:
verses.textLatin: Et occidit eos exercitus. Et sedit Demetrius super sedem regni sui.

verses.text: And there came to him the wicked and ungodly men of Israel: and Alcimus was at the head of them, who desired to be made high priest.
verses.textLatin: Et venerunt ad eum viri iniqui et impii ex Israël: et Alcimus dux eorum, qui volebat fieri sacerdos.

verses.text: And they accused the people to the king, saying: Judas and his brethren have destroyed all thy friends, and he hath driven us out of our land.
verses.textLatin: Et accusaverunt populum apud regem, dicentes: Perdidit Judas et fratres ejus omnes amicos tuos, et nos dispersit de terra nostra.

verses.text: Now therefore send some man whom thou trustest, and let him go, and see all the havock he hath made amongst us, and in the king’s lands: and let him punish all his friends and their helpers.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo mitte virum, cui credis, ut eat, et videat exterminium omne quod fecit nobis, et regionibus regis: et puniat omnes amicos ejus, et adjutores eorum.

verses.text: Then the king chose Bacchides, one of his friends that ruled beyond the great river in the kingdom, and was faithful to the king: and he sent him,
verses.textLatin: Et elegit rex ex amicis suis Bacchidem, qui dominabatur trans flumen magnum in regno, et fidelem regi: et misit eum,

verses.text: To see the havock that Judas had made: and the wicked Alcimus he made high priest, and commanded him to take revenge upon the children of Israel.
verses.textLatin: ut videret exterminium quod fecit Judas: sed et Alcimum impium constituit in sacerdotium, et mandavit ei facere ultionem in filios Israël.

verses.text: And they arose, and came with a great army into the land of Juda: and they sent messengers, and spoke to Judas and his brethren with peaceable words deceitfully.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexerunt, et venerunt cum exercitu magno in terram Juda: et miserunt nuntios, et locuti sunt ad Judam et ad fratres ejus verbis pacificis in dolo.

verses.text: But they gave no heed to their words: for they saw that they were come with a great army.
verses.textLatin: Et non intenderunt sermonibus eorum: viderunt enim quia venerunt cum exercitu magno.

verses.text: Then there assembled to Alcimus and Bacchides a company of the scribes to require things that are just:
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt ad Alcimum et Bacchidem congregatio scribarum requirere quæ justa sunt:

verses.text: And first the Assideans that were among the children of Israel, and they sought peace of them.
verses.textLatin: et primi, Assidæi qui erant in filiis Israël: et exquirebant ab eis pacem.

verses.text: For they said: One that is a priest of the seed of Aaron is come, he will not deceive us.
verses.textLatin: Dixerunt enim: Homo sacerdos de semine Aaron venit; non decipiet nos:

verses.text: And he spoke to them peaceably: and he swore to them, saying: We will do you no harm nor your friends.
verses.textLatin: et locutus est cum eis verba pacifica, et juravit illis, dicens: Non inferemus vobis malum, neque amicis vestris.

verses.text: And they believed him. And he took threescore of them, and slew them in one day, according to the word that is written:
verses.textLatin: Et crediderunt ei: et comprehendit ex eis sexaginta viros, et occidit eos in una die, secundum verbum quod scriptum est:

verses.text: The flesh of thy saints, and the blood of them they have shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
verses.textLatin: Carnes sanctorum tuorum, et sanguinem ipsorum effuderunt in circuitu Jerusalem, et non erat qui sepeliret.

verses.text: Then fear and trembling fell upon all the people: for they said: There is no truth, nor justice among them: for they have broken the covenant, and the oath which they made.
verses.textLatin: Et incubuit timor et tremor in omnem populum: quia dixerunt: Non est veritas, et judicium in eis: transgressi sunt enim constitutum, et jusjurandum quod juraverunt.

verses.text: And Bacchides removed the camp from Jerusalem, and pitched in Bethzecha: and he sent, and took many of them that were fled away from him, and some of the people he killed, and threw them into a great pit.
verses.textLatin: Et movit Bacchides castra ab Jerusalem, et applicuit in Bethzecha: et misit, et comprehendit multos ex eis qui a se effugerant: et quosdam de populo mactavit, et in puteum magnum projecit.

verses.text: Then he committed the country to Alcimus, and left with him troops to help him. So Bacchides went away to the king:
verses.textLatin: Et commisit regionem Alcimo, et reliquit cum eo auxilium in adjutorium ipsi. Et abiit Bacchides ad regem:

verses.text: But Alcimus did what he could to maintain his chief priesthood.
verses.textLatin: et satis agebat Alcimus pro principatu sacerdotii sui:

verses.text: And they that disturbed the people resorted to him, and they got the land of Juda into their power, and did much hurt in Israel.
verses.textLatin: et convenerunt ad eum omnes, qui perturbabant populum suum, et obtinuerunt terram Juda, et fecerunt plagam magnam in Israël.

verses.text: And Judas saw all the evils that Alcimus, and they that were with him, did to the children of Israel, much more than the Gentiles.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Judas omnia mala quæ fecit Alcimus et qui cum eo erant filiis Israël, multo plus quam gentes:

verses.text: And he went out into all the coasts of Judea round about, and took vengeance upon the men that had revolted, and they ceased to go forth any more into the country.
verses.textLatin: et exiit in omnes fines Judææ in circuitu, et fecit vindictam in viros desertores, et cessaverunt ultra exire in regionem.

verses.text: And Alcimus saw that Judas, and they that were with him prevailed: and he knew that he could not stand against them, and he went back to the king, and accused them of many crimes.
verses.textLatin: Vidit autem Alcimus quod prævaluit Judas et qui cum eo erant, et cognovit quia non potest sustinere eos: et regressus est ad regem, et accusavit eos multis criminibus.

verses.text: And the king sent Nicanor one of his principal lords, who was a great enemy to Israel: and he commanded him to destroy the people.
verses.textLatin: Et misit rex Nicanorem, unum ex principibus suis nobilioribus, qui erat inimicitias exercens contra Israël: et mandavit ei evertere populum.

verses.text: And Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great army, and he sent to Judas and to his brethren deceitfully with friendly words,
verses.textLatin: Et venit Nicanor in Jerusalem cum exercitu magno, et misit ad Judam et ad fratres ejus verbis pacificis cum dolo,

verses.text: Saying: Let there be no fighting between me and you: I will come with a few men to see your faces with peace.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Non sit pugna inter me et vos: veniam cum viris paucis, ut videam facies vestras cum pace.

verses.text: And he came to Judas, and they saluted one another peaceably: and the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by force.
verses.textLatin: Et venit ad Judam, et salutaverunt se invicem pacifice: et hostes parati erant rapere Judam.

verses.text: And the thing was known to Judas that he was come to him with deceit: and he was much afraid of him, and would not see his face any more.
verses.textLatin: Et innotuit sermo Judæ quoniam cum dolo venerat ad eum: et conterritus est ab eo, et amplius noluit videre faciem ejus.

verses.text: And Nicanor knew that his counsel was discovered: and he went out to fight against Judas near Capharsalama.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Nicanor quoniam denudatum est consilium ejus: et exivit obviam Judæ in pugnam juxta Capharsalama.

verses.text: And there fell of Nicanor’s army almost five thousand men, and they fled into the city of David.
verses.textLatin: Et ceciderunt de Nicanoris exercitu fere quinque millia viri, et fugerunt in civitatem David.

verses.text: And after this Nicanor went up into mount Sion: and some of the priests and the people came out to salute him peaceably, and to shew him the holocausts that were offered for the king.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc verba ascendit Nicanor in montem Sion: et exierunt de sacerdotibus populi salutare eum in pace, et demonstrare ei holocautomata, quæ offerebantur pro rege.

verses.text: But he mocked and despised them, and abused them: and he spoke proudly,
verses.textLatin: Et irridens sprevit eos, et polluit: et locutus est superbe,

verses.text: And swore in anger, saying: Unless Judas and his army be delivered into my hands, as soon as ever I return in peace, I will burn this house. And he went out in a great rage.
verses.textLatin: et juravit cum ira, dicens: Nisi traditus fuerit Judas et exercitus ejus in manus meas, continuo cum regressus fuero in pace, succendam domum istam. Et exiit cum ira magna.

verses.text: And the priests went in, and stood before the face of the altar and the temple: and weeping, they said:
verses.textLatin: Et intraverunt sacerdotes, et steterunt ante faciem altaris et templi, et flentes dixerunt:

verses.text: Thou, O Lord, hast chosen this house for thy name to be called upon therein, that it might be a house of prayer and supplication for thy people.
verses.textLatin: Tu, Domine, elegisti domum istam ad invocandum nomen tuum in ea, ut esset domus orationis et obsecrationis populo tuo:

verses.text: Be avenged of this man, and his army, and let them fall by the sword: remember their blasphemies, and suffer them not to continue any longer.
verses.textLatin: fac vindictam in homine isto et exercitu ejus, et cadant in gladio: memento blasphemias eorum, et ne dederis eis ut permaneant.

verses.text: Then Nicanor went out from Jerusalem, and encamped near to Bethoron: and an army of Syria joined him.
verses.textLatin: Et exiit Nicanor ab Jerusalem, et castra applicuit ad Bethoron: et occurrit illi exercitus Syriæ.

verses.text: But Judas pitched in Adarsa with three thousand men: and Judas prayed, and said:
verses.textLatin: Et Judas applicuit in Adarsa cum tribus millibus viris: et oravit Judas, et dixit:

verses.text: O Lord, when they that were sent by king Sennacherib blasphemed thee, an angel went out, and slew of them a hundred and eighty-five thousand:
verses.textLatin: Qui missi erant a rege Sennacherib, Domine, quia blasphemaverunt te, exiit angelus, et percussit ex eis centum octoginta quinque millia:

verses.text: Even so destroy this army in our sight to day, and let the rest know that he hath spoken ill against thy sanctuary: and judge thou him according to his wickedness.
verses.textLatin: sic contere exercitum istum in conspectu nostro hodie: et sciant ceteri quia male locutus est super sancta tua: et judica illum secundum malitiam illius.

verses.text: And the armies joined battle on the thirteenth day of the month Adar: and the army of Nicanor was defeated, and he himself was first slain in the battle.
verses.textLatin: Et commiserunt exercitus prælium tertiadecima die mensis Adar: et contrita sunt castra Nicanoris, et cecidit ipse primus in prælio.

verses.text: And when his army saw that Nicanor was slain, they threw away their weapons, and fled:
verses.textLatin: Ut autem vidit exercitus ejus quia cecidisset Nicanor, projecerunt arma sua, et fugerunt:

verses.text: And they pursued after them one day’s journey from Adazer, even till ye come to Gazara, and they sounded the trumpets after them with signals.
verses.textLatin: et persecuti sunt eos viam unius diei ab Adazer usquequo veniatur in Gazara, et tubis cecinerunt post eos cum significationibus:

verses.text: And they went forth out of all the towns of Judea round about, and they pushed them with the horns, and they turned again to them, and they were all slain with the sword, and there was not left of them so much as one.
verses.textLatin: et exierunt de omnibus castellis Judææ in circuitu, et ventilabant eos cornibus, et convertebantur iterum ad eos, et ceciderunt omnes gladio, et non est relictus ex eis nec unus.

verses.text: And they took the spoils of them for a booty, and they cut off Nicanor’s head, and his right hand, which he had proudly stretched out, and they brought it, and hung it up over against Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et acceperunt spolia eorum in prædam: et caput Nicanoris amputaverunt, et dexteram ejus, quam extenderat superbe, et attulerunt, et suspenderunt contra Jerusalem.

verses.text: And the people rejoiced exceedingly, and they spent that day with great joy.
verses.textLatin: Et lætatus est populus valde, et egerunt diem illam in lætitia magna.

verses.text: And he ordained that this day should be kept every year, being the thirteenth of the month of Adar.
verses.textLatin: Et constituit agi omnibus annis diem istam tertiadecima die mensis Adar.

verses.text: And the land of Juda was quiet for a short time.
verses.textLatin: Et siluit terra Juda dies paucos.

verses.text: Now  Judas heard of the fame of the Romans, that they are powerful and strong, and willingly agree to all things that are requested of them: and that whosoever have come to them, they have made amity with them, and that they are mighty in power.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Judas nomen Romanorum, quia sunt potentes viribus, et acquiescunt ad omnia quæ postulantur ab eis, et quicumque accesserunt ad eos, statuerunt cum eis amicitias: et quia sunt potentes viribus.

verses.text: And they heard of their battles, and their noble acts, which they had done in Galatia, how they had conquered them, and brought them under tribute:
verses.textLatin: Et audierunt prælia eorum, et virtutes bonas, quas fecerunt in Galatia, quia obtinuerunt eos, et duxerunt sub tributum:

verses.text: And how great things they had done in the land of Spain, and that they had brought under their power the mines of silver and of gold that are there, and had gotten possession of all the place by their counsel and patience:
verses.textLatin: et quanta fecerunt in regione Hispaniæ, et quod in potestatem redegerunt metalla argenti et auri, quæ illic sunt, et possederunt omnem locum consilio suo, et patientia:

verses.text: And had conquered places that were very far off from them, and kings that came against them from the ends of the earth, and had overthrown them with great slaughter: and the rest pay them tribute every year.
verses.textLatin: locaque quæ longe erant valde ab eis, et reges, qui supervenerant eis ab extremis terræ, contriverunt, et percusserunt eos plaga magna: ceteri autem dant eis tributum omnibus annis.

verses.text: And that they had defeated in battle Philip, and Perses the king of the Ceteans, and the rest that had borne arms against them, and had conquered them:
verses.textLatin: Et Philippum et Persen Ceteorum regem, et ceteros qui adversum eos arma tulerant, contriverunt in bello, et obtinuerunt eos:

verses.text: And how Antiochus the great king of Asia, who went to fight against them having a hundred and twenty elephants with horsemen, and chariots, and a very great army, was routed by them:
verses.textLatin: et Antiochum magnum regem Asiæ, qui eis pugnam intulerat habens centum viginti elephantos, et equitatum, et currus, et exercitum magnum valde, contritum ab eis:

verses.text: And how they took him alive, and appointed to him, that both he and they that should reign after him, should pay a great tribute, and that he should give hostages, and that which was agreed upon,
verses.textLatin: et quia ceperunt eum vivum, et statuerunt ei ut daret ipse, et qui regnarent post ipsum, tributum magnum, et daret obsides, et constitutum,

verses.text: And the country of the Indians, and of the Medes, and of the Lydians, some of their best provinces: and those which they had taken from them they gave to king Eumenes.
verses.textLatin: et regionem Indorum, et Medos, et Lydos, de optimis regionibus eorum: et acceptas eas ab eis, dederunt Eumeni regi,

verses.text: And that they who were in Greece had a mind to go and to destroy them: and they had knowledge thereof,
verses.textLatin: et quia qui erant apud Helladam, voluerunt ire, et tollere eos: et innotuit sermo his,

verses.text: And they sent a general against them, and fought with them, and many of them were slain, and they carried away their wives and their children captives, and spoiled them, and took possession of their land, and threw down their walls, and brought them to be their servants unto this day.
verses.textLatin: et miserunt ad eos ducem unum, et pugnaverunt contra illos, et ceciderunt ex eis multi, et captivas duxerunt uxores eorum et filios, et diripuerunt eos, et terram eorum possederunt, et destruxerunt muros eorum, et in servitutem illos redegerunt usque in hunc diem:

verses.text: And the other kingdoms, and islands, that at any time had resisted them, they had destroyed and brought under their power.
verses.textLatin: et residua regna, et insulas, quæ aliquando restiterant illis, exterminaverunt, et in potestatem redegerunt.

verses.text: But with their friends, and such as relied upon them, they kept amity, and had conquered kingdoms that were near, and that were far off: for all that heard their name, were afraid of them.
verses.textLatin: Cum amicis autem suis, et qui in ipsis requiem habebant, conservaverunt amicitiam, et obtinuerunt regna, quæ erant proxima, et quæ erant longe: quia quicumque audiebant nomen eorum, timebant eos:

verses.text: That whom they had a mind to help to a kingdom, those reigned: and whom they would, they deposed from the kingdom: and they were greatly exalted.
verses.textLatin: quibus vero vellent auxilio esse ut regnarent, regnabant: quos autem vellent, regno deturbabant: et exaltati sunt valde.

verses.text: And none of all these wore a crown, or was clothed in purple, to be magnified thereby.
verses.textLatin: Et in omnibus istis nemo portabat diadema, nec induebatur purpura, ut magnificaretur in ea.

verses.text: And that they had made themselves a senate house, and consulted daily three hundred and twenty men, that sat in council always for the people, that they might do the things that were right.
verses.textLatin: Et quia curiam fecerunt sibi, et quotidie consulebant trecentos viginti consilium agentes semper de multitudine, ut quæ digna sunt, gerant:

verses.text: And that they committed their government to one man every year, to rule over all their country, and they all obey one, and there is no envy, nor jealousy amongst them.
verses.textLatin: et committunt uni homini magistratum suum per singulos annos dominari universæ terræ suæ, et omnes obediunt uni, et non est invidia, neque zelus inter eos.

verses.text: So Judas chose Eupolemus the son of John, the son of Jacob, and Jason the son of Eleazar, and he sent them to Rome to make a league of amity and confederacy with them.
verses.textLatin: Et elegit Judas Eupolemum filium Joannis filii Jacob, et Jasonem filium Eleazari, et misit eos Romam constituere cum illis amicitiam et societatem:

verses.text: And that they might take off from them the yoke of the Grecians, for they saw that they oppressed the kingdom of Israel with servitude.
verses.textLatin: et ut auferrent ab eis jugum Græcorum, quia viderunt quod in servitutem premerent regnum Israël.

verses.text: And they went to Rome, a very long journey, and they entered into the senate house, and said:
verses.textLatin: Et abierunt Romam viam multam valde, et introierunt curiam, et dixerunt:

verses.text: Judas Machabeus, and his brethren, and the people of the Jews have sent us to you, to make alliance and peace with you, and that we may be registered your confederates and friends.
verses.textLatin: Judas Machabæus, et fratres ejus, et populus Judæorum, miserunt nos ad vos statuere vobiscum societatem et pacem, et conscribere nos socios et amicos vestros.

verses.text: And the proposal was pleasing in their sight.
verses.textLatin: Et placuit sermo in conspectu eorum.

verses.text: And this is the copy of the writing that they wrote back again, graven in tables of brass, and sent to Jerusalem, that it might be with them there for a memorial of the peace and alliance.
verses.textLatin: Et hoc rescriptum est quod rescripserunt in tabulis æreis, et miserunt in Jerusalem, ut esset apud eos ibi memoriale pacis et societatis:

verses.text: GOOD SUCCESS BE TO THE ROMANS, and to the people of the Jews, by sea and by land for ever: and far be the sword and enemy from them.
verses.textLatin: Bene sit Romanis, et genti Judæorum, in mari et in terra in æternum: gladiusque et hostis procul sit ab eis.

verses.text: But if there come first any war upon the Romans, or any of their confederates, in all their dominions:
verses.textLatin: Quod si institerit bellum Romanis prius, aut omnibus sociis eorum in omni dominatione eorum,

verses.text: The nation of the Jews shall help them according as the time shall direct, with all their heart:
verses.textLatin: auxilium feret gens Judæorum, prout tempus dictaverit, corde pleno:

verses.text: Neither shall they give them, whilst they are fighting, or furnish them with wheat, or arms, or money, or ships, as it hath seemed good to the Romans: and they shall obey their orders, without taking any thing of them.
verses.textLatin: et præliantibus non dabunt, neque subministrabunt triticum, arma, pecuniam, naves, sicut placuit Romanis: et custodient mandata eorum, nihil ab eis accipientes.

verses.text: In like manner also if war shall come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall help them with all their heart, according as the time shall permit them.
verses.textLatin: Similiter autem et si genti Judæorum prius acciderit bellum, adjuvabunt Romani ex animo, prout eis tempus permiserit:

verses.text: And there shall not be given to them that come to their aid, either wheat, or arms, or money, or ships, as it hath seemed good to the Romans: and they shall observe their orders without deceit.
verses.textLatin: et adjuvantibus non dabitur triticum, arma, pecunia, naves, sicut placuit Romanis: et custodient mandata eorum absque dolo:

verses.text: According to these articles did the Romans covenant with the people of the Jews.
verses.textLatin: secundum hæc verba constituerunt Romani populo Judæorum.

verses.text: And if after this one party or the other shall have a mind to add to these articles, or take away any thing, they may do it at their pleasure: and whatsoever they shall add, or take away, shall be ratified.
verses.textLatin: Quod si post hæc verba hi aut illi addere aut demere ad hæc aliquid voluerint, facient ex proposito suo: et quæcumque addiderint, vel dempserint, rata erunt.

verses.text: Moreover concerning the evils that Demetrius the king hath done against them, we have written to him, saying: Why hast thou made thy yoke heavy upon our friends, and allies, the Jews?
verses.textLatin: Sed et de malis, quæ Demetrius rex fecit in eos, scripsimus ei, dicentes: Quare gravasti jugum tuum super amicos nostros, et socios Judæos?

verses.text: If therefore they come again to us complaining of thee, we will do them justice, and will make war against thee by sea and land.
verses.textLatin: si ergo iterum adierint nos, adversum te faciemus illis judicium, et pugnabimus tecum mari terraque.

verses.text: In  the mean time when Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his army were fallen in battle, he sent again Bacchides and Alcimus into Judea; and the right wing of his army with them.
verses.textLatin: Interea, ut audivit Demetrius quia cecidit Nicanor et exercitus ejus in prælio, apposuit Bacchidem et Alcimum rursum mittere in Judæam, et dextrum cornu cum illis.

verses.text: And they took the road that leadeth to Galgal, and they camped in Masaloth, which is in Arabella: and they made themselves masters of it, and slew many people.
verses.textLatin: Et abierunt viam quæ ducit in Galgala, et castra posuerunt in Masaloth, quæ est in Arbellis: et occupaverunt eam, et peremerunt animas hominum multas.

verses.text: In the first month of the hundred and fifty-second year they brought the army to Jerusalem:
verses.textLatin: In mense primo anni centesimi et quinquagesimi secundi, applicuerunt exercitum ad Jerusalem:

verses.text: And they arose, and went to Berea with twenty thousand men, and two thousand horsemen.
verses.textLatin: et surrexerunt, et abierunt in Beream viginti millia virorum, et duo millia equitum.

verses.text: Now Judas had pitched his tents in Laisa, and three thousand chosen men with him:
verses.textLatin: Et Judas posuerat castra in Laisa, et tria millia viri electi cum eo:

verses.text: And they saw the multitude of the army that they were many, and they were seized with great fear: and many withdrew themselves out of the camp, and there remained of them no more than eight hundred men.
verses.textLatin: et viderunt multitudinem exercitus, quia multi sunt, et timuerunt valde: et multi subtraxerunt se de castris, et non remanserunt ex eis nisi octingenti viri.

verses.text: And Judas saw that his army slipped away, and the battle pressed upon him, and his heart was cast down: because he had not time to gather them together, and he was discouraged.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Judas quod defluxit exercitus suus, et bellum perurgebat eum, et confractus est corde, quia non habebat tempus congregandi eos, et dissolutus est.

verses.text: Then he said to them that remained: Let us arise, and go against our enemies, if we may be able to fight against them.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit his qui residui erant: Surgamus, et eamus ad adversarios nostros, si poterimus pugnare adversus eos.

verses.text: But they dissuaded him, saying: We shall not be able, but let us save our lives now, and return to our brethren, and then we will fight against them: for we are but few.
verses.textLatin: Et avertebant eum, dicentes: Non poterimus, sed liberemus animas nostras modo, et revertamur ad fratres nostros, et tunc pugnabimus adversus eos: nos autem pauci sumus.

verses.text: Then Judas said: God forbid we should do this thing, and flee away from them: but if our time be come, let us die manfully for our brethren, and let us not stain our glory.
verses.textLatin: Et ait Judas: Absit istam rem facere ut fugiamus ab eis: et si appropiavit tempus nostrum, moriamur in virtute propter fratres nostros, et non inferamus crimen gloriæ nostræ.

verses.text: And the army removed out of the camp, and they stood over against them: and the horsemen were divided into two troops, and the slingers, and the archers went before the army, and they that were in the front were all men of valour.
verses.textLatin: Et movit exercitus de castris, et steterunt illis obviam: et divisi sunt equites in duas partes, et fundibularii et sagittarii præibant exercitum, et primi certaminis omnes potentes.

verses.text: And Bacchides was in the right wing, and the legion drew near on two sides, and they sounded the trumpets:
verses.textLatin: Bacchides autem erat in dextro cornu, et proximavit legio ex duabus partibus, et clamabant tubis:

verses.text: And they also that were on Judas side, even they also cried out, and the earth shook at the noise of the armies: and the battle was fought from morning even unto the evening.
verses.textLatin: exclamaverunt autem et hi qui erant ex parte Judæ etiam ipsi, et commota est terra a voce exercituum: et commissum est prælium a mane usque ad vesperam.

verses.text: And Judas perceived that the stronger part of the army of Bacchides was on the right side, and all the stout of heart came together with him:
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Judas quod firmior est pars exercitus Bacchidis in dextris, et convenerunt cum ipso omnes constantes corde:

verses.text: And the right wing was discomfited by them, and he pursued them even to the mount Azotus.
verses.textLatin: et contrita est dextera pars ab eis, et persecutus est eos usque ad montem Azoti.

verses.text: And they that were in the left wing saw that the right wing was discomfited, and they followed after Judas, and them that were with him, at their back:
verses.textLatin: Et qui in sinistro cornu erant, viderunt quod contritum est dextrum cornu, et secuti sunt post Judam, et eos qui cum ipso erant, a tergo:

verses.text: And the battle was hard fought, and there fell many wounded of the one side and of the other.
verses.textLatin: et ingravatum est prælium, et ceciderunt vulnerati multi ex his et ex illis.

verses.text: And Judas was slain, and the rest fled away.
verses.textLatin: Et Judas cecidit, et ceteri fugerunt.

verses.text: And Jonathan and Simon took Judas their brother, and buried him in the sepulchre of their fathers in the city of Modin.
verses.textLatin: Et Jonathas et Simon tulerunt Judam fratrem suum, et sepelierunt eum in sepulchro patrum suorum in civitate Modin.

verses.text: And all the people of Israel bewailed him with great lamentation, and they mourned for him many days.
verses.textLatin: Et fleverunt eum omnis populus Israël planctu magno, et lugebant dies multos,

verses.text: And said: How is the mighty man fallen, that saved the people of Israel!
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt: Quomodo cecidit potens, qui salvum faciebat populum Israël!

verses.text: But the rest of the words of the wars of Judas, and of the noble acts that he did, and of his greatness, are not written: for they were very many.
verses.textLatin: Et cetera verba bellorum Judæ, et virtutum, quas fecit, et magnitudinis ejus, non sunt descripta: multa enim erant valde.

verses.text: And it came to pass after the death of Judas, that the wicked began to put forth their heads in all the confines of Israel, and all the workers of iniquity rose up.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est: post obitum Judæ emerserunt iniqui in omnibus finibus Israël, et exorti sunt omnes qui operabantur iniquitatem.

verses.text: In those days there was a very great famine, and they and all their country yielded to Bacchides.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis facta est fames magna valde, et tradidit se Bacchidi omnis regio eorum cum ipsis.

verses.text: And Bacchides chose the wicked men, and made them lords of the country:
verses.textLatin: Et elegit Bacchides viros impios, et constituit eos dominos regionis:

verses.text: And they sought out, and made diligent search after the friends of Judas, and brought them to Bacchides, and he took vengeance of them, and abused them.
verses.textLatin: et exquirebant, et perscrutabantur amicos Judæ, et adducebant eos ad Bacchidem, et vindicabat in illos, et illudebat.

verses.text: And there was a great tribulation in Israel, such as was not since the day, that there was no prophet seen in Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et facta est tribulatio magna in Israël, qualis non fuit ex die qua non est visus propheta in Israël.

verses.text: And all the friends of Judas came together, and said to Jonathan:
verses.textLatin: Et congregati sunt omnes amici Judæ, et dixerunt Jonathæ:

verses.text: Since thy brother Judas died, there is not a man like him to go forth against our enemies, Bacchides, and them that are the enemies of our nation.
verses.textLatin: Ex quo frater tuus Judas defunctus est, vir similis ei non est, qui exeat contra inimicos nostros, Bacchidem et eos qui inimici sunt gentis nostræ.

verses.text: Now therefore we have chosen thee this day to be our prince, and captain in his stead to fight our battles.
verses.textLatin: Nunc itaque, te hodie elegimus esse pro eo nobis in principem, et ducem ad bellandum bellum nostrum.

verses.text: So Jonathan took upon him the government at that time, and rose up in the place of Judas his brother
verses.textLatin: Et suscepit Jonathas tempore illo principatum, et surrexit loco Judæ fratris sui.

verses.text: And Bacchides had knowledge of it, and sought to kill him.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Bacchides, et quærebat eum occidere.

verses.text: And Jonathan and Simon his brother, knew it, and all that were with them: and they fled into the desert of Thecua, and they pitched by the water of the lake Asphar,
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Jonathas, et Simon frater ejus, et omnes qui cum eo erant: et fugerunt in desertum Thecuæ et consederunt ad aquam lacus Asphar.

verses.text: And Bacchides understood it, and he came himself with all his army over the Jordan on the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Bacchides, et die sabbatorum venit ipse et omnis exercitus ejus trans Jordanem.

verses.text: And Jonathan sent his brother a captain of the people, to desire the Nabutheans his friends, that they would lend them their equipage, which was copious.
verses.textLatin: Et Jonathas misit fratrem suum ducem populi, et rogavit Nabuthæos amicos suos, ut commodarent illis apparatum suum, qui erat copiosus.

verses.text: And the children of Jambri came forth out of Madaba, and took John, and all that he had, and went away with them.
verses.textLatin: Et exierunt filii Jambri ex Madaba, et comprehenderunt Joannem et omnia quæ habebat, et abierunt habentes ea.

verses.text: After this it was told Jonathan, and Simon his brother, that the children of Jambri made a great marriage, and were bringing the bride out of Madaba, the daughter of one of the great princes of Chanaan, with great pomp.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc verba, renuntiatum est Jonathæ et Simoni fratri ejus, quia filii Jambri faciunt nuptias magnas, et ducunt sponsam ex Madaba filiam unius de magnis principibus Chanaan cum ambitione magna.

verses.text: And they remembered the blood of John their brother: and they went up, and hid themselves under the covert of the mountain.
verses.textLatin: Et recordati sunt sanguinis Joannis fratris sui: et ascenderunt, et absconderunt se sub tegumento montis.

verses.text: And they lifted up their eyes, and saw: and behold a tumult, and great preparation: and the bridegroom came forth, and his friends, and his brethren to meet them with timbrels, and musical instruments, and many weapons.
verses.textLatin: Et elevaverunt oculos suos, et viderunt: et ecce tumultus, et apparatus multus: et sponsus processit, et amici ejus, et fratres ejus obviam illis cum tympanis, et musicis, et armis multis.

verses.text: And they rose up against them from the place where they lay in ambush, and slew them, and there fell many wounded, and the rest fled into the mountains, and they took all their spoils:
verses.textLatin: Et surrexerunt ad eos ex insidiis, et occiderunt eos, et ceciderunt vulnerati multi, et residui fugerunt in montes: et acceperunt omnia spolia eorum:

verses.text: And the marriage was turned into mourning, and the noise of their musical instruments into lamentation.
verses.textLatin: et conversæ sunt nuptiæ in luctum, et vox musicorum ipsorum in lamentum.

verses.text: And they took revenge for the blood of their brother: and they returned to the bank of the Jordan.
verses.textLatin: Et vindicaverunt vindictam sanguinis fratris sui: et reversi sunt ad ripam Jordanis.

verses.text: And Bacchides heard it, and he came on the sabbath day even to the bank of the Jordan with a great power.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Bacchides, et venit die sabbatorum usque ad oram Jordanis in virtute magna.

verses.text: And Jonathan said to his company: Let us arise, and fight against our enemies: for it is not now as yesterday, and the day before.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit ad suos Jonathas: Surgamus, et pugnemus contra inimicos nostros: non est enim hodie sicut heri et nudiustertius:

verses.text: For behold the battle is before us, and the water of the Jordan on this side and on that side, and banks, and marshes, and woods: and there is no place for us to turn aside.
verses.textLatin: ecce enim bellum ex adverso, aqua vero Jordanis hinc et inde, et ripæ, et paludes, et saltus: et non est locus divertendi.

verses.text: Now therefore cry ye to heaven, that ye may be delivered from the hand of your enemies. And they joined battle.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo, clamate in cælum, ut liberemini de manu inimicorum vestrorum. Et commissum est bellum.

verses.text: And Jonathan stretched forth his hand to strike Bacchides, but he turned away from him backwards.
verses.textLatin: Et extendit Jonathas manum suam percutere Bacchidem, et divertit ab eo retro:

verses.text: And Jonathan, and they that were with him leaped into the Jordan, and swam over the Jordan to them:
verses.textLatin: et desiliit Jonathas, et qui cum eo erant, in Jordanem, et transnataverunt ad eos Jordanem.

verses.text: And there fell of Bacchides’ side that day a thousand men: and they returned to Jerusalem,
verses.textLatin: Et ceciderunt de parte Bacchidis die illa mille viri. Et reversi sunt in Jerusalem,

verses.text: And they built strong cities in Judea, the fortress that was in Jericho, and in Ammaus, and in Bethoron, and in Bethel, and Thamnata, and Phara, and Thopo, with high walls, and gates, and bars.
verses.textLatin: et ædificaverunt civitates munitas in Judæa, munitionem quæ erat in Jericho, et in Ammaum, et in Bethoron, et in Bethel, et Thamnata, et Phara, et Thopo muris excelsis, et portis, et seris.

verses.text: And he placed garrisons in them, that they might wage war against Israel:
verses.textLatin: Et posuit custodiam in eis, ut inimicitias exercerent in Israël:

verses.text: And he fortified the city of Bethsura, and Gazara, and the castle, and set garrisons in them, and provisions of victuals:
verses.textLatin: et munivit civitatem Bethsuram, et Gazaram, et arcem, et posuit in eis auxilia, et apparatum escarum:

verses.text: And he took the sons of the chief men of the country for hostages, and put them in the castle in Jerusalem in custody.
verses.textLatin: et accepit filios principum regionis obsides, et posuit eos in arce in Jerusalem in custodiam.

verses.text: Now in the year one hundred and fifty-three, the second month, Alcimus commanded the walls of the inner court of the sanctuary to be thrown down, and the works of the prophets to be destroyed: and he began to destroy.
verses.textLatin: Et anno centesimo quinquagesimo tertio, mense secundo, præcepit Alcimus destrui muros domus sanctæ interioris, et destrui opera prophetarum: et cœpit destruere.

verses.text: At that time Alcimus was struck: and his works were hindered, and his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsy, so that he could no more speak a word, nor give order concerning his house.
verses.textLatin: In tempore illo percussus est Alcimus: et impedita sunt opera illius, et occlusum est os ejus, et dissolutus est paralysi, nec ultra potuit loqui verbum, et mandare de domo sua.

verses.text: And Alcimus died at that time in great torment.
verses.textLatin: Et mortuus est Alcimus in tempore illo cum tormento magno.

verses.text: And Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead: and he returned to the king, and the land was quiet for two years.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Bacchides quoniam mortuus est Alcimus, et reversus est ad regem. Et siluit terra annis duobus.

verses.text: And all the wicked held a council, saying: Behold Jonathan, and they that are with him, dwell at ease, and without fear: now therefore let us bring Bacchides hither, and he shall take them all in one night.
verses.textLatin: Et cogitaverunt omnes iniqui, dicentes: Ecce Jonathas, et qui cum eo sunt, in silentio habitant confidenter: nunc ergo adducamus Bacchidem, et comprehendet eos omnes una nocte.

verses.text: So they went, and gave him counsel.
verses.textLatin: Et abierunt, et consilium ei dederunt.

verses.text: And he arose to come with a great army: and he sent secretly letters to his adherents that were in Judea, to seize upon Jonathan, and them that were with him: but they could not, for their design was known to them.
verses.textLatin: Et surrexit ut veniret cum exercitu multo: et misit occulte epistolas sociis suis qui erant in Judæa, ut comprehenderent Jonathan, et eos qui cum eo erant: sed non potuerunt, quia innotuit eis consilium eorum.

verses.text: And he apprehended of the men of the country, that were the principal authors of the mischief, fifty men, and slew them.
verses.textLatin: Et apprehendit de viris regionis, qui principes erant malitiæ, quinquaginta viros, et occidit eos:

verses.text: And Jonathan, and Simon, and they that were with him retired into Bethbessen, which is in the desert: and he repaired the breaches thereof, and they fortified it.
verses.textLatin: et secessit Jonathas, et Simon, et qui cum eo erant, in Bethbessen, quæ est in deserto: et exstruxit diruta ejus, et firmaverunt eam.

verses.text: And when Bacchides knew it, he gathered together all his multitude: and sent word to them that were of Judea.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Bacchides, et congregavit universam multitudinem suam: et his, qui de Judæa erant, denuntiavit.

verses.text: And he came, and camped above Bethbessen, and fought against it many days, and made engines.
verses.textLatin: Et venit, et castra posuit desuper Bethbessen: et oppugnavit eam dies multos, et fecit machinas.

verses.text: But Jonathan left his brother Simon in the city, and went forth into the country: and came with a number of men.
verses.textLatin: Et reliquit Jonathas Simonem fratrem suum in civitate, et exiit in regionem, et venit cum numero:

verses.text: And struck Odares, and his brethren, and the children of Phaseron in their tents, and he began to slay, and to increase in forces.
verses.textLatin: et percussit Odaren et fratres ejus, et filios Phaseron in tabernaculis ipsorum: et cœpit cædere, et crescere in virtutibus.

verses.text: But Simon and they that were with him, sallied out of the city, and burnt the engines,
verses.textLatin: Simon vero, et qui cum ipso erant, exierunt de civitate, et succenderunt machinas,

verses.text: And they fought against Bacchides, and he was discomfited by them: and they afflicted him exceedingly, for his counsel, and his enterprise was in vain.
verses.textLatin: et pugnaverunt contra Bacchidem, et contritus est ab eis: et afflixerunt eum valde, quoniam consilium ejus et congressus ejus erat inanis.

verses.text: And he was angry with the wicked men that had given him counsel to come into their country, and he slew many of them: and he purposed to return with the rest into their country.
verses.textLatin: Et iratus contra viros iniquos, qui ei consilium dederant ut veniret in regionem ipsorum, multos ex eis occidit: ipse autem cogitavit cum reliquis abire in regionem suam.

verses.text: And Jonathan had knowledge of it and he sent ambassadors to him to make peace with him, and to restore to him the prisoners.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Jonathas: et misit ad eum legatos componere pacem cum ipso, et reddere ei captivitatem.

verses.text: And he accepted it willingly, and did according to his words, and swore that he would do him no harm all the days of his life.
verses.textLatin: Et libenter accepit, et fecit secundum verba ejus, et juravit se nihil facturum ei mali omnibus diebus vitæ ejus.

verses.text: And he restored to him the prisoners which he before had taken out of the land of Juda: and he returned and went away into his own country, and he came no more into their borders.
verses.textLatin: Et reddidit ei captivitatem, quam prius erat prædatus de terra Juda: et conversus abiit in terram suam, et non apposuit amplius venire in fines ejus.

verses.text: So the sword ceased from Israel: and Jonathan dwelt in Machmas, and Jonathan began there to judge the people, and he destroyed the wicked out of Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et cessavit gladius ex Israël: et habitavit Jonathas in Machmas, et cœpit Jonathas ibi judicare populum, et exterminavit impios ex Israël.

verses.text: Now  in the hundred and sixtieth year Alexander the son of Antiochus, surnamed the Illustrious, came up and took Ptolemais, and they received him, and he reigned there.
verses.textLatin: Et anno centesimo sexagesimo, ascendit Alexander Antiochi filius, qui cognominatus est Nobilis, et occupavit Ptolemaidam: et receperunt eum, et regnavit illic.

verses.text: And king Demetrius heard of it, and gathered together an exceeding great army, and went forth against him to fight.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Demetrius rex, et congregavit exercitum copiosum valde, et exivit obviam illi in prælium.

verses.text: And Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan with peaceable words, to magnify him.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Demetrius epistolam ad Jonathan verbis pacificis, ut magnificaret eum.

verses.text: For he said: Let us first make a peace with him, before he make one with Alexander against us.
verses.textLatin: Dixit enim: Anticipemus facere pacem cum eo, priusquam faciat cum Alexandro adversum nos:

verses.text: For he will remember all the evils that we have done against him, and against his brother, and against his nation.
verses.textLatin: recordabitur enim omnium malorum, quæ fecimus in eum, et in fratrem ejus, et in gentem ejus.

verses.text: And he gave him authority to gather together an army, and to make arms, and that he should be his confederate: and the hostages that were in the castle, he commanded to be delivered to him.
verses.textLatin: Et dedit ei potestatem congregandi exercitum, et fabricare arma, et esse ipsum socium ejus: et obsides, qui erant in arce, jussit tradi ei.

verses.text: And Jonathan came to Jerusalem, and read the letters in the hearing of all the people, and of them that were in the castle.
verses.textLatin: Et venit Jonathas in Jerusalem, et legit epistolas in auditu omnis populi, et eorum qui in arce erant.

verses.text: And they were struck with great fear, because they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together an army.
verses.textLatin: Et timuerunt timore magno, quoniam audierunt quod dedit ei rex potestatem congregandi exercitum.

verses.text: And the hostages were delivered to Jonathan, and he restored them to their parents.
verses.textLatin: Et traditi sunt Jonathæ obsides, et reddidit eos parentibus suis:

verses.text: And Jonathan dwelt in Jerusalem, and began to build, and to repair the city.
verses.textLatin: et habitavit Jonathas in Jerusalem, et cœpit ædificare et innovare civitatem.

verses.text: And he ordered workmen to build the walls, and mount Sion round about with square stones for fortification: and so they did.
verses.textLatin: Et dixit facientibus opera ut exstruerent muros, et montem Sion in circuitu lapidibus quadratis ad munitionem: et ita fecerunt.

verses.text: And the strangers that were in the strong holds, which Bacchides had built, fled away.
verses.textLatin: Et fugerunt alienigenæ, qui erant in munitionibus quas Bacchides ædificaverat:

verses.text: And every man left his place, and departed into his own country:
verses.textLatin: et reliquit unusquisque locum suum, et abiit in terram suam:

verses.text: Only in Bethsura there remained some of them, that had forsaken the law, and the commandments of God: for this was a place of refuge for them.
verses.textLatin: tantum in Bethsura remanserunt aliqui ex his qui reliquerant legem et præcepta Dei: erat enim hæc eis ad refugium.

verses.text: And king Alexander heard of the promises that Demetrius had made Jonathan: and they told him of the battles, and the worthy acts that he, and his brethren had done, and the labours that they had endured.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Alexander rex promissa, quæ promisit Demetrius Jonathæ: et narraverunt ei prælia, et virtutes quas ipse fecit, et fratres ejus, et labores quos laboraverunt:

verses.text: And he said: Shall we find such another man? now therefore we will make him our friend and our confederate.
verses.textLatin: et ait: Numquid inveniemus aliquem virum talem? et nunc faciemus eum amicum, et socium nostrum.

verses.text: So he wrote a letter, and sent it to him according to these words, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit epistolam, et misit ei secundum hæc verba, dicens:

verses.text: King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Rex Alexander fratri Jonathæ salutem.

verses.text: We have heard of thee, that thou art a man of great power, and fit to be our friend:
verses.textLatin: Audivimus de te quod vir potens sis viribus, et aptus es ut sis amicus noster:

verses.text: Now therefore we make thee this day high priest of thy nation, and that thou be called the king’s friend, (and he sent him a purple robe, and a crown of gold,) and that thou be of one mind with us in our affairs, and keep friendship with us.
verses.textLatin: et nunc constituimus te hodie summum sacerdotem gentis tuæ, et ut amicus voceris regis (et misit ei purpuram, et coronam auream) et quæ nostra sunt sentias nobiscum, et conserves amicitias ad nos.

verses.text: Then Jonathan put on the holy vestment in the seventh month, in the year one hundred and threescore, at the feast day of the tabernacles: and he gathered together an army, and made a great number of arms.
verses.textLatin: Et induit se Jonathas stola sancta septimo mense, anno centesimo sexagesimo, in die solemni scenopegiæ: et congregavit exercitum, et fecit arma copiosa.

verses.text: And Demetrius heard these words, and was exceeding sorry, and said:
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Demetrius verba ista, et contristatus est nimis, et ait:

verses.text: What is this that we have done, that Alexander hath prevented us to gain the friendship of the Jews to strengthen himself?
verses.textLatin: Quid hoc fecimus, quod præoccupavit nos Alexander apprehendere amicitiam Judæorum ad munimen sui?

verses.text: I also will write to them words of request, and offer dignities, and gifts: that they may be with me to aid me.
verses.textLatin: scribam et ego illis verba deprecatoria, et dignitates, et dona, ut sint mecum in adjutorium.

verses.text: And he wrote to them in these words: King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit eis in hæc verba: Rex Demetrius genti Judæorum salutem.

verses.text: Whereas you have kept covenant with us, and have continued in our friendship, and have not joined with our enemies, we have heard of it, and are glad.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam servastis ad nos pactum, et mansistis in amicitia nostra, et non accessistis ad inimicos nostros, audivimus, et gavisi sumus.

verses.text: Wherefore now continue still to keep fidelity towards us, and we will reward you with good things, for what you have done in our behalf.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc perseverate adhuc conservare ad nos fidem, et retribuemus vobis bona pro his quæ fecistis nobiscum:

verses.text: And we will remit to you many charges, and will give you gifts.
verses.textLatin: et remittemus vobis præstationes multas, et dabimus vobis donationes.

verses.text: And now I free you, and all the Jews from tributes, and I release you from the customs of salt, and remit the crowns, and the thirds of the seed:
verses.textLatin: Et nunc absolvo vos et omnes Judæos a tributis, et pretia salis indulgeo, et coronas remitto, et tertias seminis:

verses.text: And the half of the fruit of trees, which is my share, I leave to you from this day forward, so that it shall not be taken of the land of Juda, and of the three cities that are added thereto out of Samaria and Galilee, from this day forth and for ever:
verses.textLatin: et dimidiam partem fructus ligni, quod est portionis meæ, relinquo vobis ex hodierno die, et deinceps, ne accipiatur a terra Juda, et a tribus civitatibus quæ additæ sunt illi ex Samaria et Galilæa; ex hodierna die et in totum tempus:

verses.text: And let Jerusalem be holy and free, with the borders thereof: and let the tenths, and tributes be for itself.
verses.textLatin: et Jerusalem sit sancta, et libera cum finibus suis: et decimæ et tributa ipsius sint.

verses.text: I yield up also the power of the castle that is in Jerusalem, and I give it to the high priest, to place therein such men as he shall choose to keep it.
verses.textLatin: Remitto etiam potestatem arcis, quæ est in Jerusalem: et do eam summo sacerdoti, ut constituat in ea viros quoscumque ipse elegerit, qui custodiant eam.

verses.text: And every soul of the Jews that hath been carried captive from the land of Juda in all my kingdom, I set at liberty freely, that all be discharged from tributes even of their cattle.
verses.textLatin: Et omnem animam Judæorum, quæ captiva est a terra Juda in omni regno meo, relinquo liberam gratis, ut omnes a tributis solvantur, etiam pecorum suorum.

verses.text: And I will that all the feasts, and the sabbaths, and the new moons, and the days appointed, and three days before the solemn day, and three days after the solemn day, be all days of immunity and freedom, for all the Jews that are in my kingdom:
verses.textLatin: Et omnes dies solemnes, et sabbata, et neomeniæ, et dies decreti, et tres dies ante diem solemnem, et tres dies post diem solemnem, sint omnes immunitatis et remissionis omnibus Judæis, qui sunt in regno meo:

verses.text: And no man shall have power to do any thing against them, or to molest any of them, in any cause.
verses.textLatin: et nemo habebit potestatem agere aliquid, et movere negotia adversus aliquem illorum in omni causa.

verses.text: And let there be enrolled in the king’s army to the number of thirty thousand of the Jews: and allowance shall be made them as is due to all the king’s forces, and certain of them shall be appointed to be in the fortresses of the great king:
verses.textLatin: Et ascribantur ex Judæis in exercitu regis ad triginta millia virorum: et dabuntur illis copiæ ut oportet omnibus exercitibus regis, et ex eis ordinabuntur qui sint in munitionibus regis magni:

verses.text: And some of them shall be set over the affairs of the kingdom, that are of trust, and let the governors be taken from among themselves, and let them walk in their own laws, as the king hath commanded in the land of Juda.
verses.textLatin: et ex his constituentur super negotia regni, quæ aguntur ex fide, et principes sint ex eis, et ambulent in legibus suis, sicut præcepit rex in terra Juda.

verses.text: And the three cities that are added to Judea, out of the country of Samaria, let them be accounted with Judea: that they may be under one, and obey no other authority but that of the high priest
verses.textLatin: Et tres civitates, quæ additæ sunt Judææ ex regione Samariæ, cum Judæa reputentur: ut sint sub uno, et non obediant alii potestati, nisi summi sacerdotis.

verses.text: Ptolemais, and the confines thereof, I give as a free gift to the holy places, that are in Jerusalem, for the necessary charges of the holy things.
verses.textLatin: Ptolemaida et confines ejus, quas dedi donum sanctis qui sunt in Jerusalem, ad necessarios sumptus sanctorum.

verses.text: And I give every year fifteen thousand sicles of silver out of the king’s accounts, of what belongs to me:
verses.textLatin: Et ego do singulis annis quindecim millia siclorum argenti de rationibus regis, quæ me contingunt:

verses.text: And all that is above, which they that were over the affairs the years before, had not paid, from this time they shall give it to the works of the house.
verses.textLatin: et omne quod reliquum fuerit, quod non reddiderant qui super negotia erant annis prioribus, ex hoc dabunt in opera domus.

verses.text: Moreover the five thousand sicles of silver which they received from the account of the holy places, every year, shall also belong to the priests that execute the ministry.
verses.textLatin: Et super hæc quinque millia siclorum argenti, quæ accipiebant de sanctorum ratione per singulos annos: et hæc ad sacerdotes pertineant, qui ministerio funguntur.

verses.text: And whosoever shall flee into the temple that is in Jerusalem, and in all the borders thereof, being indebted to the king for any matter, let them be set at liberty, and all that they have in my kingdom, let them have it free.
verses.textLatin: Et quicumque confugerint in templum quod est Jerosolymis, et in omnibus finibus ejus, obnoxii regi in omni negotio dimittantur, et universa quæ sunt eis in regno meo, libera habeant.

verses.text: For the building also, or repairing the works of the holy places, the charges shall be given out of the king’s revenues:
verses.textLatin: Et ad ædificanda vel restauranda opera sanctorum, sumptus dabuntur de ratione regis:

verses.text: For the building also of the walls of Jerusalem, and the fortifying thereof round about, the charges shall be given out of the king’s account, as also for the building of the walls in Judea.
verses.textLatin: et ad exstruendos muros Jerusalem, et communiendos in circuitu, sumptus dabuntur de ratione regis, et ad construendos muros in Judæa.

verses.text: Now when Jonathan, and the people heard these words, they gave no credit to them nor received them: because they remembered the great evil that he had done in Israel, for he had afflicted them exceedingly.
verses.textLatin: Ut audivit autem Jonathas et populus sermones istos, non crediderunt eis, nec receperunt eos: quia recordati sunt malitiæ magnæ, quam fecerat in Israël, et tribulaverat eos valde.

verses.text: And their inclinations were towards Alexander, because he had been the chief promoter of peace in their regard, and him they always helped.
verses.textLatin: Et complacuit eis in Alexandrum, quia ipse fuerat eis princeps sermonum pacis, et ipsi auxilium ferebant omnibus diebus.

verses.text: And king Alexander gathered together a great army, and moved his camp near to Demetrius.
verses.textLatin: Et congregavit rex Alexander exercitum magnum, et admovit castra contra Demetrium.

verses.text: And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled away, and Alexander pursued after him, and pressed them close.
verses.textLatin: Et commiserunt prælium duo reges, et fugit exercitus Demetrii, et insecutus est eum Alexander, et incubuit super eos.

verses.text: And the battle was hard fought till the sun went down: and Demetrius was slain that day.
verses.textLatin: Et invaluit prælium nimis, donec occidit sol: et cecidit Demetrius in die illa.

verses.text: And Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemee king of Egypt, with words to this effect, saying:
verses.textLatin: Et misit Alexander ad Ptolemæum regem Ægypti legatos secundum hæc verba, dicens:

verses.text: Forasmuch as I am returned into my kingdom, and am set in the throne of my ancestors, and have gotten the dominion, and have overthrown Demetrius, and possessed our country,
verses.textLatin: Quoniam regressus sum in regnum meum, et sedi in sede patrum meorum, et obtinui principatum, et contrivi Demetrium, et possedi regionem nostram,

verses.text: And have joined battle with him, and both he and his army have been destroyed by us, and we are placed in the throne of his kingdom:
verses.textLatin: et commisi pugnam cum eo, et contritus est ipse et castra ejus a nobis, et sedimus in sede regni ejus:

verses.text: Now therefore let us make friendship one with another: and give me now thy daughter to wife, and I will be thy son in law, and I will give both thee and her gifts worthy of thee.
verses.textLatin: et nunc statuamus ad invicem amicitiam: et da mihi filiam tuam uxorem, et ego ero gener tuus, et dabo tibi dona, et ipsi, digna te.

verses.text: And king Ptolemee answered, saying: Happy is the day wherein thou didst return to the land of thy fathers, and sattest in the throne of their kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Et respondit rex Ptolemæus, dicens: Felix dies, in qua reversus es ad terram patrum tuorum, et sedisti in sede regni eorum.

verses.text: And now I will do to thee as thou hast written: but meet me at Ptolemais, that we may see one another, and I may give her to thee as thou hast said.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc faciam tibi quod scripsisti: sed occurre mihi Ptolemaidam, ut videamus invicem nos, et spondeam tibi sicut dixisti.

verses.text: So Ptolemee went out of Egypt, with Cleopatra his daughter, and he came to Ptolemais in the hundred and sixty-second year.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit Ptolemæus de Ægypto, ipse et Cleopatra filia ejus, et venit Ptolemaidam anno centesimo sexagesimo secundo.

verses.text: And king Alexander met him, and he gave him his daughter Cleopatra: and he celebrated her marriage at Ptolemais, with great glory, after the manner of kings.
verses.textLatin: Et occurrit ei Alexander rex, et dedit ei Cleopatram filiam suam: et fecit nuptias ejus Ptolemaidæ, sicut reges in magna gloria.

verses.text: And king Alexander wrote to Jonathan, that he should come and meet him.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit rex Alexander Jonathæ, ut veniret obviam sibi.

verses.text: And he went honourably to Ptolemais, and he met there the two kings, and he gave them much silver, and gold, and presents: and he found favour in their sight.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit cum gloria Ptolemaidam, et occurrit ibi duobus regibus, et dedit illis argentum multum, et aurum, et dona: et invenit gratiam in conspectu eorum.

verses.text: And some pestilent men of Israel, men of a wicked life, assembled themselves against him to accuse him: and the king gave no heed to them.
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt adversus eum viri pestilentes ex Israël, viri iniqui interpellantes adversus eum: et non intendit ad eos rex.

verses.text: And he commanded that Jonathan’s garments should be taken off, and that he should be clothed with purple: and they did so. And the king made him sit by himself.
verses.textLatin: Et jussit spoliari Jonathan vestibus suis, et indui eum purpura: et ita fecerunt. Et collocavit eum rex sedere secum.

verses.text: And he said to his princes: Go out with him into the midst of the city, and make proclamation, that no man complain against him of any matter, and that no man trouble him for any manner of cause.
verses.textLatin: Dixitque principibus suis: Exite cum eo in medium civitatis, et prædicate, ut nemo adversus eum interpellet de ullo negotio, nec quisquam ei molestus sit de ulla ratione.

verses.text: So when his accusers saw his glory proclaimed, and him clothed with purple, they all fled away.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, ut viderunt qui interpellabant gloriam ejus, quæ prædicabatur, et opertum eum purpura, fugerunt omnes:

verses.text: And the king magnified him, and enrolled him amongst his chief friends, and made him governor and partaker of his dominion.
verses.textLatin: et magnificavit eum rex, et scripsit eum inter primos amicos, et posuit eum ducem, et participem principatus.

verses.text: And Jonathan returned into Jerusalem with peace and joy.
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Jonathas in Jerusalem cum pace et lætitia.

verses.text: In the year one hundred and sixty-five Demetrius the son of Demetrius came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
verses.textLatin: In anno centesimo sexagesimo quinto, venit Demetrius filius Demetrii a Creta in terram patrum suorum.

verses.text: And king Alexander heard of it, and was much troubled, and returned to Antioch.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Alexander rex, et contristatus est valde, et reversus est Antiochum.

verses.text: And king Demetrius made Apollonius his general, who was governor of Celesyria: and he gathered together a great army, and came to Jamnia: and he sent to Jonathan the high priest,
verses.textLatin: Et constituit Demetrius rex Apollonium ducem, qui præerat Cœlesyriæ: et congregavit exercitum magnum, et accessit ad Jamniam: et misit ad Jonathan summum sacerdotem,
