verses.text: Saying: Thou alone standest against us, and I am laughed at, and reproached, because thou shewest thy power against us in the mountains.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Tu solus resistis nobis: ego autem factus sum in derisum, et in opprobrium, propterea quia tu potestatem adversum nos exerces in montibus.

verses.text: Now therefore if thou trustest in thy forces, come down to us into the plain, and there let us try one another: for with me is the strength of war.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo si confidis in virtutibus tuis, descende ad nos in campum, et comparemus illic invicem: quia mecum est virtus bellorum.

verses.text: Ask, and learn who I am, and the rest that help me, who also say that your foot cannot stand before our face, for thy fathers have twice been put to flight in their own land:
verses.textLatin: Interroga, et disce quis sum ego, et ceteri qui auxilio sunt mihi, qui et dicunt quia non potest stare pes vester ante faciem nostram, quia bis in fugam conversi sunt patres tui in terra sua:

verses.text: And now how wilt thou be able to abide the horsemen, and so great an army in the plain, where there is no stone, nor rock, nor place to flee to?
verses.textLatin: et nunc quomodo poteris sustinere equitatum et exercitum tantum in campo, ubi non est lapis, neque saxum, neque locus fugiendi?

verses.text: Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, he was moved in his mind: and he chose ten thousand men, and went out of Jerusalem, and Simon his brother met him to help him.
verses.textLatin: Ut audivit autem Jonathas sermones Apollonii, motus est animo: et elegit decem millia virorum, et exiit ab Jerusalem, et occurrit ei Simon frater ejus in adjutorium:

verses.text: And they pitched their tents near Joppe, but they shut him out of the city: because a garrison of Apollonius was in Joppe, and he laid siege to it.
verses.textLatin: et applicuerunt castra in Joppen, et exclusit eum a civitate, quia custodia Apollonii Joppe erat: et oppugnavit eam.

verses.text: And they that were in the city being affrighted, opened the gates to him: so Jonathan took Joppe.
verses.textLatin: Et exterriti qui erant in civitate, aperuerunt ei, et obtinuit Jonathas Joppen.

verses.text: And Apollonius heard of it, and he took three thousand horsemen, and a great army.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Apollonius, et admovit tria millia equitum, et exercitum multum.

verses.text: And he went to Azotus as one that was making a journey, and immediately he went forth into the plain: because he had a great number of horsemen, and he trusted in them. And Jonathan followed after him to Azotus, and they joined battle.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit Azotum tamquam iter faciens, et statim exiit in campum, eo quod haberet multitudinem equitum, et confideret in eis. Et insecutus est eum Jonathas in Azotum, et commiserunt prælium.

verses.text: And Apollonius left privately in the camp a thousand horsemen behind them.
verses.textLatin: Et reliquit Apollonius in castris mille equites post eos occulte.

verses.text: And Jonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him, and they surrounded his army, and cast darts at the people from morning till evening.
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Jonathas quoniam insidiæ sunt post se, et circuierunt castra ejus, et jecerunt jacula in populum a mane usque ad vesperam.

verses.text: But the people stood still, as Jonathan had commanded them: and so their horses were fatigued.
verses.textLatin: Populus autem stabat, sicut præceperat Jonathas: et laboraverunt equi eorum.

verses.text: Then Simon drew forth his army, and attacked the legion: for the horsemen were wearied: and they were discomfited by him, and fled.
verses.textLatin: Et ejecit Simon exercitum suum, et commisit contra legionem: equites enim fatigati erant: et contriti sunt ab eo, et fugerunt.

verses.text: And they that were scattered about the plain, fled into Azotus, and went into Bethdagon their idol’s temple, there to save themselves.
verses.textLatin: Et qui dispersi sunt per campum, fugerunt in Azotum, et intraverunt in Bethdagon idolum suum, ut ibi se liberarent.

verses.text: But Jonathan set fire to Azotus, and the cities that were round about it, and took the spoils of them, and the temple of Dagon: and all them that were fled into it, he burnt with fire.
verses.textLatin: Et succendit Jonathas Azotum, et civitates quæ erant in circuitu ejus, et accepit spolia eorum, et templum Dagon: et omnes qui fugerunt in illud, succendit igni.

verses.text: So they that were slain by the sword, with them that were burnt, were almost eight thousand men.
verses.textLatin: Et fuerunt qui ceciderunt gladio, cum his qui succensi sunt, fere octo millia virorum.

verses.text: And Jonathan removed his army from thence, and camped against Ascalon: and they went out of the city to meet him with great honour.
verses.textLatin: Et movit inde Jonathas castra, et applicuit ea Ascalonem: et exierunt de civitate obviam illi in magna gloria.

verses.text: And Jonathan returned into Jerusalem with his people, having many spoils.
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Jonathas in Jerusalem cum suis, habentibus spolia multa.

verses.text: And it came to pass: when Alexander the king heard these words, that he honoured Jonathan yet more.
verses.textLatin: Et factum est, ut audivit Alexander rex sermones istos, addidit adhuc glorificare Jonathan.

verses.text: And he sent him a buckle of gold, as the custom is, to be given to such as are of the royal blood. And he gave him Accaron and all the borders thereof in possession.
verses.textLatin: Et misit ei fibulam auream, sicut consuetudo est dari cognatis regum. Et dedit ei Accaron, et omnes fines ejus, in possessionem.

verses.text: And  the king of Egypt gathered together an army, like the sand that lieth upon the sea shore, and many ships: and he sought to get the kingdom of Alexander by deceit, and join it to his own kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Et rex Ægypti congregavit exercitum, sicut arena quæ est circa oram maris, et naves multas: et quærebat obtinere regnum Alexandri dolo, et addere illud regno suo.

verses.text: And he went out into Syria with peaceable words, and they opened to him the cities, and met him: for king Alexander had ordered them to go forth to meet him, because he was his father in law.
verses.textLatin: Et exiit in Syriam verbis pacificis, et aperiebant ei civitates, et occurrebant ei: quia mandaverat Alexander rex exire ei obviam, eo quod socer suus esset.

verses.text: Now when Ptolemee entered into the cities, he put garrisons of soldiers in every city.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem introiret civitatem Ptolemæus, ponebat custodias militum in singulis civitatibus.

verses.text: And when he came near to Azotus, they shewed him the temple of Dagon that was burnt with fire, and Azotus, and the suburbs thereof that were destroyed, and the bodies that were cast abroad, and the graves of them that were slain in the battle, which they had made near the way.
verses.textLatin: Et ut appropiavit Azoto, ostenderunt ei templum Dagon succensum igni, et Azotum, et cetera ejus demolita, et corpora projecta, et eorum, qui cæsi erant in bello, tumulos quos fecerant secus viam.

verses.text: And they told the king that Jonathan had done these things, to make him odious: but the king held his peace.
verses.textLatin: Et narraverunt regi quia hæc fecit Jonathas, ut invidiam facerent ei: et tacuit rex.

verses.text: And Jonathan came to meet the king at Joppe with glory, and they saluted one another, and they lodged there.
verses.textLatin: Et occurrit Jonathas regi in Joppen cum gloria, et invicem se salutaverunt, et dormierunt illic.

verses.text: And Jonathan went with the king as far as the river, called Eleutherus: and he returned into Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit Jonathas cum rege usque ad fluvium qui vocatur Eleutherus: et reversus est in Jerusalem.

verses.text: And king Ptolemee got the dominion of the cities by the sea side, even to Seleucia, and he devised evil designs against Alexander.
verses.textLatin: Rex autem Ptolemæus obtinuit dominium civitatum usque Seleuciam maritimam, et cogitabat in Alexandrum consilia mala.

verses.text: And he sent ambassadors to Demetrius, saying: Come, let us make a league between us, and I will give thee my daughter whom Alexander hath, and thou shalt reign in the kingdom of thy father.
verses.textLatin: Et misit legatos ad Demetrium, dicens: Veni, componamus inter nos pactum, et dabo tibi filiam meam, quam habet Alexander, et regnabis in regno patris tui:

verses.text: For I repent that I have given him my daughter: for he hath sought to kill me.
verses.textLatin: pœnitet enim me quod dederim illi filiam meam: quæsivit enim me occidere.

verses.text: And he slandered him, because he coveted his kingdom.
verses.textLatin: Et vituperavit eum, propterea quod concupierat regnum ejus.

verses.text: And he took away his daughter, and gave her to Demetrius, and alienated himself from Alexander, and his enmities were made manifest.
verses.textLatin: Et abstulit filiam suam, et dedit eam Demetrio, et alienavit se ab Alexandro, et manifestæ sunt inimicitiæ ejus.

verses.text: And Ptolemee entered into Antioch, and set two crowns upon his head, that of Egypt, and that of Asia.
verses.textLatin: Et intravit Ptolemæus Antiochiam, et imposuit duo diademata capiti suo, Ægypti et Asiæ.

verses.text: Now king Alexander was in Cilicia at that time: because they that were in those places had rebelled.
verses.textLatin: Alexander autem rex erat in Cilicia illis temporibus: quia rebellabant qui erant in locis illis.

verses.text: And when Alexander heard of it, he came to give him battle, and king Ptolemee brought forth his army, and met him with a strong power, and put him to flight.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Alexander, et venit ad eum in bellum: et produxit Ptolemæus rex exercitum, et occurrit ei in manu valida, et fugavit eum.

verses.text: And Alexander fled into Arabia, there to be protected: and king Ptolemee was exalted.
verses.textLatin: Et fugit Alexander in Arabiam, ut ibi protegeretur: rex autem Ptolemæus exaltatus est.

verses.text: And Zabdiel the Arabian took off Alexander’s head, and sent it to Ptolemee.
verses.textLatin: Et abstulit Zabdiel Arabs caput Alexandri, et misit Ptolemæo.

verses.text: And king Ptolemee died the third day after: and they that were in the strong holds were destroyed by them that were within the camp.
verses.textLatin: Et rex Ptolemæus mortuus est in die tertia: et qui erant in munitionibus, perierunt ab his qui erant intra castra.

verses.text: And Demetrius reigned in the hundred and sixty-seventh year.
verses.textLatin: Et regnavit Demetrius anno centesimo sexagesimo septimo.

verses.text: In those days Jonathan gathered together them that were in Judea, to take the castle that was in Jerusalem: and they made many engines of war against it.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis congregavit Jonathas eos qui erant in Judæa, ut expugnarent arcem quæ est in Jerusalem: et fecerunt contra eam machinas multas.

verses.text: Then some wicked men that hated their own nation, went away to king Demetrius, and told him that Jonathan was besieging the castle.
verses.textLatin: Et abierunt quidam qui oderant gentem suam viri iniqui ad regem Demetrium, et renuntiaverunt ei quod Jonathas obsideret arcem.

verses.text: And when he heard it, he was angry: and forthwith he came to Ptolemais, and wrote to Jonathan, that he should not besiege the castle, but should come to him in haste, and speak to him.
verses.textLatin: Et ut audivit, iratus est: et statim venit ad Ptolemaidam, et scripsit Jonathæ ne obsideret arcem, sed occurreret sibi ad colloquium festinato.

verses.text: But when Jonathan heard this, he bade them besiege it still: and he chose some of the ancients of Israel, and of the priests, and put himself in danger.
verses.textLatin: Ut audivit autem Jonathas, jussit obsidere: et elegit de senioribus Israël, et de sacerdotibus, et dedit se periculo.

verses.text: And he took gold, and silver, and raiment, and many other presents, and went to the king to Ptolemais, and he found favour in his sight.
verses.textLatin: Et accepit aurum, et argentum, et vestem, et alia xenia multa, et abiit ad regem Ptolemaidam: et invenit gratiam in conspectu ejus,

verses.text: And certain wicked men of his nation made complaints against him.
verses.textLatin: et interpellabant adversus eum quidam iniqui ex gente sua.

verses.text: And the king treated him as his predecessors had done before: and he exalted him in the sight of all his friends.
verses.textLatin: Et fecit ei rex sicut fecerant ei qui ante eum fuerant: et exaltavit eum in conspectu omnium amicorum suorum,

verses.text: And he confirmed him in the high priesthood, and all the honours he had before, and he made him the chief of his friends.
verses.textLatin: et statuit ei principatum sacerdotii, et quæcumque alia habuit prius pretiosa, et fecit eum principem amicorum.

verses.text: And Jonathan requested of the king that he would make Judea free from tribute, and the three governments, and Samaria, and the confines thereof: and he promised him three hundred talents.
verses.textLatin: Et postulavit Jonathas a rege ut immunem faceret Judæam, et tres toparchias, et Samariam et confines ejus: et promisit ei talenta trecenta.

verses.text: And the king consented: and he wrote letters to Jonathan of all these things to this effect.
verses.textLatin: Et consensit rex: et scripsit Jonathæ epistolas de his omnibus, hunc modum continentes:

verses.text: King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan, and to the nation of the Jews, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Rex Demetrius fratri Jonathæ salutem, et genti Judæorum.

verses.text: We send you here a copy of the letter, which we have written to Lasthenes our parent concerning you, that you might know it.
verses.textLatin: Exemplum epistolæ, quam scripsimus Lastheni parenti nostro de vobis, misimus ad vos ut sciretis:

verses.text: King Demetrius to Lasthenes his parent, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Rex Demetrius Lastheni parenti salutem.

verses.text: We have determined to do good to the nation of the Jews who are our friends, and keep the things that are just with us, for their good will which they bear towards us.
verses.textLatin: Genti Judæorum amicis nostris, et conservantibus quæ justa sunt apud nos, decrevimus benefacere propter benignitatem ipsorum, quam erga nos habent.

verses.text: We have ratified therefore unto them all the borders of Judea, and the three cities, Apherema, Lydda, and Ramatha, which are added to Judea, out of Samaria, and all their confines, to be set apart to all them that sacrifice in Jerusalem, instead of the payments which the king received of them every year, and for the fruits of the land, and of the trees.
verses.textLatin: Statuimus ergo illis omnes fines Judææ, et tres civitates, Lydan, et Ramathan, quæ additæ sunt Judææ ex Samaria, et omnes confines earum, sequestrari omnibus sacrificantibus in Jerosolymis pro his quæ ab eis prius accipiebat rex per singulos annos, et pro fructibus terræ et pomorum.

verses.text: And as for other things that belonged to us of the tithes, and of the tributes, from this time we discharge them of them: the saltpans also, and the crowns that were presented to us.
verses.textLatin: Et alia quæ ad nos pertinebant decimarum et tributorum ex hoc tempore, remittimus eis: et areas salinarum, et coronas, quæ nobis deferebantur,

verses.text: We give all to them, and nothing hereof shall be revoked from this time forth and for ever.
verses.textLatin: omnia ipsis concedimus: et nihil horum irritum erit, ex hoc, et in omne tempus.

verses.text: Now therefore see that thou make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan, and set upon the holy mountain, in a conspicuous place.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo curate facere horum exemplum, et detur Jonathæ, et ponatur in monte sancto, in loco celebri.

verses.text: And king Demetrius seeing that the land was quiet before him, and nothing resisted him, sent away all his forces, every man to his own place, except the foreign army, which he had drawn together from the islands of the nations: so all the troops of his fathers hated him.
verses.textLatin: Et videns Demetrius rex quod siluit terra in conspectu suo, et nihil ei resistit, dimisit totum exercitum suum, unumquemque in locum suum, excepto peregrino exercitu, quem contraxit ab insulis gentium: et inimici erant ei omnes exercitus patrum ejus.

verses.text: Now there was one Tryphon who had been of Alexander’s party before: who seeing that all the army murmured against Demetrius, went to Emalchuel the Arabian, who brought up Antiochus the son of Alexander.
verses.textLatin: Tryphon autem erat quidam partium Alexandri prius: et vidit quoniam omnis exercitus murmurabat contra Demetrium, et ivit ad Emalchuel Arabem, qui nutriebat Antiochum filium Alexandri:

verses.text: And he pressed him much to deliver him to him, that he might be king in his father’s place: and he told him all that Demetrius had done, and how his soldiers hated him. And he remained there many days.
verses.textLatin: et assidebat ei, ut traderet eum ipsi, ut regnaret loco patris sui: et enuntiavit ei quanta fecit Demetrius, et inimicitias exercituum ejus adversus illum. Et mansit ibi diebus multis.

verses.text: And Jonathan sent to king Demetrius, desiring that he would cast out them that were in the castle in Jerusalem, and those that were in the strong holds: because they fought against Israel.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Jonathas ad Demetrium regem, ut ejiceret eos qui in arce erant in Jerusalem, et qui in præsidiis erant: quia impugnabant Israël.

verses.text: And Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying: I will not only do this for thee, and for thy people, but I will greatly honour thee, and thy nation, when opportunity shall serve.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Demetrius ad Jonathan, dicens: Non hæc tantum faciam tibi, et genti tuæ, sed gloria illustrabo te, et gentem tuam, cum fuerit opportunum.

verses.text: Now therefore thou shalt do well if thou send me men to help me: for all my army is gone from me.
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo recte feceris, si miseris in auxilium mihi viros: quia discessit omnis exercitus meus.

verses.text: And Jonathan sent him three thousand valiant men to Antioch: and they came to the king, and the king was very glad of their coming.
verses.textLatin: Et misit ei Jonathas tria millia virorum fortium Antiochiam: et venerunt ad regem, et delectatus est rex in adventu eorum.

verses.text: And they that were of the city assembled themselves together, to the number of a hundred and twenty thousand men, and would have killed the king.
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt qui erant de civitate, centum viginti millia virorum, et volebant interficere regem.

verses.text: And the king fled into the palace, and they of the city kept the passages of the city, and began to fight.
verses.textLatin: Et fugit rex in aulam: et occupaverunt qui erant de civitate, itinera civitatis, et cœperunt pugnare.

verses.text: And the king called the Jews to his assistance: and they came to him all at once, and they all dispersed themselves through the city.
verses.textLatin: Et vocavit rex Judæos in auxilium, et convenerunt omnes simul ad eum, et dispersi sunt omnes per civitatem:

verses.text: And they slew in that day a hundred thousand men, and they set fire to the city, and got many spoils that day, and delivered the king.
verses.textLatin: et occiderunt in illa die centum millia hominum, et succenderunt civitatem, et ceperunt spolia multa in die illa, et liberaverunt regem.

verses.text: And they that were of the city saw that the Jews had got the city as they would: and they were discouraged in their mind, and cried to the king, making supplication, and saying:
verses.textLatin: Et viderunt qui erant de civitate, quod obtinuissent Judæi civitatem sicut volebant: et infirmati sunt mente sua, et clamaverunt ad regem cum precibus, dicentes:

verses.text: Grant us peace, and let the Jews cease from assaulting us, and the city.
verses.textLatin: Da nobis dextras, et cessent Judæi oppugnare nos, et civitatem.

verses.text: And they threw down their arms, and made peace, and the Jews were glorified in the sight of the king, and in the sight of all that were in his realm, and were renowned throughout the kingdom, and returned to Jerusalem with many spoils.
verses.textLatin: Et projecerunt arma sua, et fecerunt pacem, et glorificati sunt Judæi in conspectu regis, et in conspectu omnium qui erant in regno ejus, et nominati sunt in regno: et regressi sunt in Jerusalem habentes spolia multa.

verses.text: So king Demetrius sat in the throne of his kingdom: and the land was quiet before him.
verses.textLatin: Et sedit Demetrius rex in sede regni sui: et siluit terra in conspectu ejus.

verses.text: And he falsified all whatsoever he had said, and alienated himself from Jonathan, and did not reward him according to the benefits he had received from him, but gave him great trouble.
verses.textLatin: Et mentitus est omnia quæcumque dixit, et abalienavit se a Jonatha, et non retribuit ei secundum beneficia quæ sibi tribuerat, et vexabat eum valde.

verses.text: And after this Tryphon returned, and with him Antiochus the young boy, who was made king, and put on the diadem.
verses.textLatin: Post hæc autem reversus est Tryphon, et Antiochus cum eo puer adolescens, et regnavit, et imposuit sibi diadema.

verses.text: And there assembled unto him all the hands which Demetrius had sent away, and they fought against Demetrius, who turned his back and fled.
verses.textLatin: Et congregati sunt ad eum omnes exercitus, quos disperserat Demetrius, et pugnaverunt contra eum: et fugit, et terga vertit.

verses.text: And Tryphon took the elephants, and made himself master of Antioch.
verses.textLatin: Et accepit Tryphon bestias, et obtinuit Antiochiam.

verses.text: And young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying: I confirm thee in the high priesthood, and I appoint thee ruler over the four cities, and to be one of the king’s friends.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsit Antiochus adolescens Jonathæ, dicens: Constituo tibi sacerdotium, et constituo te super quatuor civitates, ut sis de amicis regis.

verses.text: And he sent him vessels of gold for his service, and he gave him leave to drink in gold, and to be clothed in purple, and to wear a golden buckle:
verses.textLatin: Et misit illi vasa aurea in ministerium, et dedit ei potestatem bibendi in auro, et esse in purpura, et habere fibulam auream:

verses.text: And he made his brother Simon governor from the borders of Tyre even to the confines of Egypt.
verses.textLatin: et Simonem fratrem ejus constituit ducem a terminis Tyri usque ad fines Ægypti.

verses.text: Then Jonathan went forth and passed through the cities beyond the river: and all the forces of Syria gathered themselves to him to help him, and he came to Ascalon, and they met him honourably out of the city.
verses.textLatin: Et exiit Jonathas, et perambulabat trans flumen civitates: et congregatus est ad eum omnis exercitus Syriæ in auxilium, et venit Ascalonem, et occurrerunt ei honorifice de civitate.

verses.text: And he went from thence to Gaza: and they that were in Gaza shut him out: and he besieged it, and burnt all the suburbs round about, and took the spoils.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit inde Gazam: et concluserunt se qui erant Gazæ: et obsedit eam, et succendit quæ erant in circuitu civitatis, et prædatus est ea.

verses.text: And the men of Gaza made supplication to Jonathan, and he gave them the right hand: and he took their sons for hostages, and sent them to Jerusalem: and he went through the country as far as Damascus.
verses.textLatin: Et rogaverunt Gazenses Jonathan, et dedit illis dexteram: et accepit filios eorum obsides, et misit illos in Jerusalem: et perambulavit regionem usque Damascum.

verses.text: And Jonathan heard that the generals of Demetrius were come treacherously to Cades, which is in Galilee, with a great army, purposing to remove him from the affairs of the kingdom:
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Jonathas quod prævaricati sunt principes Demetrii in Cades, quæ est in Galilæa, cum exercitu multo, volentes eum removere a negotio regni:

verses.text: And he went against them: but left his brother Simon in the country.
verses.textLatin: et occurrit illis: fratrem autem suum Simonem reliquit intra provinciam.

verses.text: And Simon encamped against Bethsura, and assaulted it many days, and shut them up.
verses.textLatin: Et applicuit Simon ad Bethsuram, et expugnabat eam diebus multis, et conclusit eos.

verses.text: And they desired him to make peace, and he granted it them: and he cast them out from thence, and took the city, and placed a garrison in it.
verses.textLatin: Et postulaverunt ab eo dextras accipere, et dedit illis: et ejecit eos inde, et cepit civitatem, et posuit in ea præsidium.

verses.text: And Jonathan, and his army encamped by the water of Genesar, and before it was light they were ready in the plain of Asor.
verses.textLatin: Et Jonathas et castra ejus applicuerunt ad aquam Genesar, et ante lucem vigilaverunt in campo Asor:

verses.text: And behold the army of the strangers met him in the plain, and they laid an ambush for him in the mountains: but he went out against them.
verses.textLatin: et ecce castra alienigenarum occurrebant in campo, et tendebant ei insidias in montibus: ipse autem occurrit ex adverso.

verses.text: And they that lay in ambush rose out of their places, and joined battle.
verses.textLatin: Insidiæ vero exsurrexerunt de locis suis, et commiserunt prælium.

verses.text: And all that were on Jonathan’s side fled, and none was left of them, but Mathathias the son of Absalom, and Judas the son of Calphi, chief captain of the army.
verses.textLatin: Et fugerunt qui erant ex parte Jonathæ omnes, et nemo relictus est ex eis, nisi Mathathias filius Absolomi, et Judas filius Calphi, princeps militiæ exercitus.

verses.text: And Jonathan rent his garments, and cast earth upon his head, and prayed.
verses.textLatin: Et scidit Jonathas vestimenta sua, et posuit terram in capite suo, et oravit.

verses.text: And Jonathan turned again to them to battle, and he put them to flight, and they fought.
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Jonathas ad eos in prælium, et convertit eos in fugam, et pugnaverunt.

verses.text: And they of his part that fled saw this, and they turned again to him, and they all with him pursued the enemies even to Cades to their own camp, and they came even thither.
verses.textLatin: Et viderunt qui fugiebant partis illius, et reversi sunt ad eum, et insequebantur cum eo omnes usque Cades ad castra sua, et pervenerunt usque illuc:

verses.text: And there fell of the aliens in that day three thousand men: and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et ceciderunt de alienigenis in die illa tria millia virorum: et reversus est Jonathas in Jerusalem.

verses.text: And  Jonathan saw that the time served him, and he chose certain men and sent them to Rome, to confirm and to renew the amity with them:
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Jonathas quia tempus eum juvat, et elegit viros, et misit eos Romam statuere et renovare cum eis amicitiam:

verses.text: And he sent letters to the Spartans, and to other places according to the same form.
verses.textLatin: et ad Spartiatas, et ad alia loca misit epistolas secundum eamdem formam:

verses.text: And they went to Rome, and entered into the senate house, and said: Jonathan the high priest, and the nation of the Jews have sent us to renew the amity, and alliance as it was before.
verses.textLatin: et abierunt Romam, et intraverunt curiam, et dixerunt: Jonathas summus sacerdos, et gens Judæorum miserunt nos, ut renovaremus amicitiam et societatem secundum pristinum.

verses.text: And they gave them letters to their governors in every place, to conduct them into the land of Juda with peace.
verses.textLatin: Et dederunt illis epistolas ad ipsos per loca, ut deducerent eos in terram Juda cum pace.

verses.text: And this is a copy of the letters which Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
verses.textLatin: Et hoc est exemplum epistolarum, quas scripsit Jonathas Spartiatis:

verses.text: Jonathan the high priest, and the ancients of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to the Spartans, their brethren, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Jonathas summus sacerdos, et seniores gentis, et sacerdotes, et reliquus populus Judæorum, Spartiatis fratribus salutem.

verses.text: There were letters sent long ago to Onias the high priest from Arius who reigned then among you, to signify that you are our brethren, as the copy here underwritten doth specify.
verses.textLatin: Jampridem missæ erant epistolæ ad Oniam summum sacerdotem ab Ario, qui regnabat apud vos, quoniam estis fratres nostri, sicut rescriptum continet, quod subjectum est.

verses.text: And Onias received the ambassador with honour: and received the letters wherein there was mention made of the alliance, and amity.
verses.textLatin: Et suscepit Onias virum, qui missus fuerat, cum honore: et accepit epistolas, in quibus significabatur de societate et amicitia.

verses.text: We, though we needed none of these things, having for our comfort the holy books that are in our hands,
verses.textLatin: Nos cum nullo horum indigeremus, habentes solatio sanctos libros, qui sunt in manibus nostris,

verses.text: Chose rather to send to you to renew the brotherhood and friendship, lest we should become strangers to you altogether: for there is a long time passed since you sent to us.
verses.textLatin: maluimus mittere ad vos renovare fraternitatem et amicitiam, ne forte alieni efficiamur a vobis: multa enim tempora transierunt, ex quo misistis ad nos.

verses.text: We therefore at all times without ceasing, both in our festivals, and other days, wherein it is convenient, remember you in the sacrifices that we offer, and in our observances, as it is meet, and becoming to remember brethren.
verses.textLatin: Nos ergo in omni tempore sine intermissione in diebus solemnibus, et ceteris, quibus oportet, memores sumus vestri in sacrificiis quæ offerimus, et in observationibus, sicut fas est, et decet meminisse fratrum.

verses.text: And we rejoice at your glory.
verses.textLatin: Lætamur itaque de gloria vestra.

verses.text: But we have had many troubles and wars on every side, and the kings that are round about us, have fought against us.
verses.textLatin: Nos autem circumdederunt multæ tribulationes, et multa prælia, et impugnaverunt nos reges qui sunt in circuitu nostro.

verses.text: But we would not be troublesome to you, nor to the rest of our allies and friends in these wars.
verses.textLatin: Noluimus ergo vobis molesti esse, neque ceteris sociis et amicis nostris in his præliis:

verses.text: For we have had help from heaven, and we have been delivered, and our enemies are humbled.
verses.textLatin: habuimus enim de cælo auxilium, et liberati sumus nos, et humiliati sunt inimici nostri.

verses.text: We have chosen therefore Numenius the son of Antiochus, and Antipater the son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew with them the former amity and alliance.
verses.textLatin: Elegimus itaque Numenium Antiochi filium, et Antipatrem Jasonis filium, et misimus ad Romanos renovare cum eis amicitiam et societatem pristinam.

verses.text: And we have commanded them to go also to you, and to salute you, and to deliver you our letters, concerning the renewing of our brotherhood.
verses.textLatin: Mandavimus itaque eis ut veniant etiam ad vos, et salutent vos, et reddant vobis epistolas nostras de innovatione fraternitatis nostræ.

verses.text: And now you shall do well to give us an answer hereto.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc benefacietis respondentes nobis ad hæc.

verses.text: And this is the copy of the letter which he had sent to Onias:
verses.textLatin: Et hoc est rescriptum epistolarum quod miserat Oniæ:

verses.text: Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the high priest, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Arius rex Spartiatarum Oniæ sacerdoti magno salutem.

verses.text: It is found in writing concerning the Spartans, and the Jews, that they are brethren, and that they are of the stock of Abraham.
verses.textLatin: Inventum est in scriptura de Spartiatis, et Judæis, quoniam sunt fratres, et quod sunt de genere Abraham.

verses.text: And now since this is come to our knowledge, you do well to write to us of your prosperity.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc ex quo hæc cognovimus, benefacitis scribentes nobis de pace vestra.

verses.text: And we also have written back to you: That our cattle, and our possessions are yours: and yours, ours. We therefore have commanded that these things should be told you.
verses.textLatin: Sed et nos rescripsimus vobis: Pecora nostra, et possessiones nostræ, vestræ sunt: et vestræ, nostræ: mandavimus itaque hæc nuntiari vobis.

verses.text: Now Jonathan heard that the generals of Demetrius were come again with a greater army than before to fight against him.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Jonathas quoniam regressi sunt principes Demetrii cum exercitu multo supra quam prius, pugnare adversus eum:

verses.text: So he went out from Jerusalem, and met them in the land of Amath: for he gave them no time to enter into his country.
verses.textLatin: et exiit ab Jerusalem, et occurrit eis in Amathite regione: non enim dederat eis spatium ut ingrederentur regionem ejus.

verses.text: And he sent spies into their camp, and they came back and brought him word that they designed to come upon them in the night.
verses.textLatin: Et misit speculatores in castra eorum: et reversi renuntiaverunt quod constituunt supervenire illis nocte.

verses.text: And when the sun was set, Jonathan commanded his men to watch, and to be in arms all night long ready to fight, and he set sentinels round about the camp.
verses.textLatin: Cum occidisset autem sol, præcepit Jonathas suis vigilare, et esse in armis paratos ad pugnam tota nocte: et posuit custodes per circuitum castrorum.

verses.text: And the enemies heard that Jonathan and his men were ready for battle, and they were struck with fear, and dread in their heart: and they kindled fires in their camp.
verses.textLatin: Et audierunt adversarii quod paratus est Jonathas cum suis in bello: et timuerunt, et formidaverunt in corde suo: et accenderunt focos in castris suis.

verses.text: But Jonathan and they that were with him knew it not till the morning: for they saw the lights burning.
verses.textLatin: Jonathas autem, et qui cum eo erant, non cognoverunt usque mane: videbant autem luminaria ardentia,

verses.text: And Jonathan pursued after them, but overtook them not: for they had passed the river Eleutherus.
verses.textLatin: et secutus est eos Jonathas, et non comprehendit eos: transierant enim flumen Eleutherum.

verses.text: And Jonathan turned upon the Arabians that are called Zabadeans: and he defeated them, and took the spoils of them.
verses.textLatin: Et divertit Jonathas ad Arabas, qui vocantur Zabadæi: et percussit eos, et accepit spolia eorum.

verses.text: And he went forward, and came to Damascus, and passed through all that country.
verses.textLatin: Et junxit, et venit Damascum, et perambulabat omnem regionem illam.

verses.text: Simon also went forth, and came as far as Ascalon, and the neighbouring fortresses, and he turned aside to Joppe, and took possession of it,
verses.textLatin: Simon autem exiit, et venit usque ad Ascalonem, et ad proxima præsidia: et declinavit in Joppen, et occupavit eam

verses.text: (For he heard that they designed to deliver the hold to them that took part with Demetrius,) and he put a garrison there to keep it.
verses.textLatin: (audivit enim quod vellent præsidium tradere partibus Demetrii), et posuit ibi custodes ut custodirent eam.

verses.text: And Jonathan came back, and called together the ancients of the people, and he took a resolution with them to build fortresses in Judea,
verses.textLatin: Et reversus est Jonathas, et convocavit seniores populi, et cogitavit cum eis ædificare præsidia in Judæa,

verses.text: And to build up walls in Jerusalem, and raise a mount between the castle and the city, to separate it from the city, that so it might have no communication, and that they might neither buy nor sell.
verses.textLatin: et ædificare muros in Jerusalem, et exaltare altitudinem magnam inter medium arcis et civitatis, ut separaret eam a civitate, ut esset ipsa singulariter, et neque emant, neque vendant.

verses.text: And they came together to build up the city: for the wall that was upon the brook towards the east was broken down, and he repaired that which is called Caphetetha:
verses.textLatin: Et convenerunt ut ædificarent civitatem: et cecidit murus qui erat super torrentem ab ortu solis, et reparavit eum, qui vocatur Caphetetha:

verses.text: And Simon built Adiada in Sephela, and fortified it, and set up gates and bars.
verses.textLatin: et Simon ædificavit Adiada in Sephela, et munivit eam, et imposuit portas et seras.

verses.text: Now when Tryphon had conceived a design to make himself king of Asia, and to take the crown, and to stretch out his hand against king Antiochus:
verses.textLatin: Et cum cogitasset Tryphon regnare Asiæ, et assumere diadema, et extendere manum in Antiochum regem:

verses.text: Fearing lest Jonathan would not suffer him, but would fight against him: he sought to seize upon him, and to kill him. So he rose up and came to Bethsan.
verses.textLatin: timens ne forte non permitteret eum Jonathas, sed pugnaret adversus eum, quærebat comprehendere eum, et occidere. Et exsurgens abiit in Bethsan.

verses.text: And Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for battle, and came to Bethsan.
verses.textLatin: Et exivit Jonathas obviam illi cum quadraginta millibus virorum electorum in prælium, et venit Bethsan.

verses.text: Now when Tryphon saw that Jonathan came with a great army, he durst not stretch forth his hand against him,
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Tryphon quia venit Jonathas cum exercitu multo ut extenderet in eum manus: timuit,

verses.text: But received him with honour, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him presents: and he commanded his troops to obey him, as himself.
verses.textLatin: et excepit eum cum honore, et commendavit eum omnibus amicis suis, et dedit ei munera: et præcepit exercitibus suis ut obedirent ei, sicut sibi.

verses.text: And he said to Jonathan: Why hast thou troubled all the people, whereas we have no war?
verses.textLatin: Et dixit Jonathæ: Ut quid vexasti universum populum, cum bellum nobis non sit?

verses.text: Now therefore send them back to their own houses: and choose thee a few men that may be with thee, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I will deliver it to thee, and the rest of the strong holds, and the army, and all that have any charge, and I will return and go away: for this is the cause of my coming.
verses.textLatin: et nunc remitte eos in domos suas: elige autem tibi viros paucos, qui tecum sint, et veni mecum Ptolemaidam, et tradam eam tibi, et reliqua præsidia, et exercitum, et universos præpositos negotii: et conversus abibo: propterea enim veni.

verses.text: And Jonathan believed him, and did as he said: and sent away his army, and they departed into the land of Juda:
verses.textLatin: Et credidit ei, et fecit sicut dixit: et dimisit exercitum, et abierunt in terram Juda.

verses.text: But he kept with him three thousand men: of whom he sent two thousand into Galilee, and one thousand went with him.
verses.textLatin: Retinuit autem secum tria millia virorum: ex quibus remisit in Galilæam duo millia: mille autem venerunt cum eo.

verses.text: Now as soon as Jonathan entered into Ptolemais, they of Ptolemais shut the gates of the city, and took him: and all them that came in with him they slew with the sword.
verses.textLatin: Ut autem intravit Ptolemaidam Jonathas, clauserunt portas civitatis Ptolemenses, et comprehenderunt eum: et omnes qui cum eo intraverant, gladio interfecerunt.

verses.text: Then Tryphon sent an army and horsemen into Galilee, and into the great plain to destroy all Jonathan’s company.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Tryphon exercitum et equites in Galilæam et in campum magnum, ut perderent omnes socios Jonathæ.

verses.text: But they, when they understood that Jonathan and all that were with him were taken and slain, encouraged one another, and went out ready for battle.
verses.textLatin: At illi cum cognovissent quia comprehensus est Jonathas, et periit, et omnes qui cum eo erant, hortati sunt semetipsos, et exierunt parati in prælium.

verses.text: Then they that had come after them, seeing that they stood for their lives, returned back.
verses.textLatin: Et videntes hi qui insecuti fuerant, quia pro anima res est illis, reversi sunt:

verses.text: Whereupon they all came peaceably into the land of Juda. And they bewailed Jonathan, and them that had been with him, exceedingly: and Israel mourned with great lamentation.
verses.textLatin: illi autem venerunt omnes cum pace in terram Juda. Et planxerunt Jonathan, et eos qui cum ipso fuerant, valde: et luxit Israël luctu magno.

verses.text: Then all the heathens that were round about them, sought to destroy them. For they said:
verses.textLatin: Et quæsierunt omnes gentes quæ erant in circuitu eorum conterere eos: dixerunt enim:

verses.text: They have no prince, nor any to help them: now therefore let us make war upon them, and take away the memory of them from amongst men.
verses.textLatin: Non habent principem et adjuvantem: nunc ergo expugnemus illos, et tollamus de hominibus memoriam eorum.

verses.text: Now  Simon heard that Tryphon was gathering together a very great army, to invade the land of Juda, and to destroy it.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Simon quod congregavit Tryphon exercitum copiosum ut veniret in terram Juda, et attereret eam.

verses.text: And seeing that the people was in dread, and in fear, he went up to Jerusalem, and assembled the people:
verses.textLatin: Videns quia in tremore populus est, et in timore, ascendit Jerusalem, et congregavit populum:

verses.text: And exhorted them, saying: You know what great battles I and my brethren, and the house of my father, have fought for the laws, and the sanctuary, and the distresses that we have seen:
verses.textLatin: et adhortans dixit: Vos scitis quanta ego, et fratres mei, et domus patris mei, fecimus pro legibus et pro sanctis, prælia, et angustias quales vidimus:

verses.text: By reason whereof all my brethren have lost their lives for Israel’s sake, and I am left alone.
verses.textLatin: horum gratia perierunt fratres mei omnes propter Israël, et relictus sum ego solus.

verses.text: And now far be it from me to spare my life in any time of trouble: for I am not better than my brethren.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc non mihi contingat parcere animæ meæ in omni tempore tribulationis: non enim melior sum fratribus meis.

verses.text: I will avenge then my nation and the sanctuary, and our children, and wives: for all the heathens are gathered together to destroy us out of mere malice.
verses.textLatin: Vindicabo itaque gentem meam, et sancta, natos quoque nostros, et uxores: quia congregatæ sunt universæ gentes conterere nos inimicitiæ gratia.

verses.text: And the spirit of the people was enkindled as soon as they heard these words.
verses.textLatin: Et accensus est spiritus populi simul ut audivit sermones istos:

verses.text: And they answered with a loud voice, saying: Thou art our leader in the place of Judas, and Jonathan thy brother.
verses.textLatin: et responderunt voce magna, dicentes: Tu es dux noster loco Judæ, et Jonathæ fratris tui:

verses.text: Fight thou our battles, and we will do whatsoever thou shalt say to us.
verses.textLatin: pugna prælium nostrum: et omnia, quæcumque dixeris nobis, faciemus.

verses.text: So gathering together all the men of war, he made haste to finish all the walls of Jerusalem, and he fortified it round about.
verses.textLatin: Et congregans omnes viros bellatores, acceleravit consummare universos muros Jerusalem, et munivit eam in gyro.

verses.text: And he sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a new army into Joppe, and he cast out them that were in it, and himself remained there.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Jonathan filium Absalomi, et cum eo exercitum novum in Joppen, et ejectis his qui erant in ea, remansit illic ipse.

verses.text: And Tryphon removed from Ptolemais with a great army, to invade the land of Juda, and Jonathan was with him in custody.
verses.textLatin: Et movit Tryphon a Ptolemaida cum exercitu multo, ut veniret in terram Juda, et Jonathas cum eo in custodia.

verses.text: But Simon pitched in Addus, over against the plain.
verses.textLatin: Simon autem applicuit in Addus contra faciem campi.

verses.text: And when Tryphon understood that Simon was risen up in the place of his brother Jonathan, and that he meant to join battle with him, he sent messengers to him,
verses.textLatin: Et ut cognovit Tryphon quia surrexit Simon loco fratris sui Jonathæ, et quia commissurus esset cum eo prælium, misit ad eum legatos,

verses.text: Saying: We have detained thy brother Jonathan for the money that he owed in the king’s account, by reason of the affairs which he had the management of.
verses.textLatin: dicens: Pro argento, quod debebat frater tuus Jonathas in ratione regis propter negotia quæ habuit, detinuimus eum.

verses.text: But now send a hundred talents of silver, and his two sons for hostages, that when he is set at liberty he may not revolt from us, and we will release him.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc mitte argenti talenta centum, et duos filios ejus obsides, ut non dimissus fugiat a nobis, et remittemus eum.

verses.text: Now Simon knew that he spoke deceitfully to him, nevertheless he ordered the money, and the children to be sent: lest he should bring upon himself a great hatred of the people of Israel, who might have said:
verses.textLatin: Et cognovit Simon quia cum dolo loqueretur secum: jussit tamen dari argentum et pueros, ne inimicitiam magnam sumeret ad populum Israël, dicentem:

verses.text: Because he sent not the money, and the children, therefore is he lost.
verses.textLatin: Quia non misit ei argentum, et pueros, propterea periit.

verses.text: So he sent the children, and the hundred talents: and he lied, and did not let Jonathan go.
verses.textLatin: Et misit pueros, et centum talenta: et mentitus est, et non dimisit Jonathan.

verses.text: And after this Tryphon entered within the country, to destroy it: and they went about by the way that leadeth to Ador: and Simon and his army marched to every place whithersoever they went.
verses.textLatin: Et post hæc venit Tryphon intra regionem, ut contereret eam: et gyraverunt per viam quæ ducit Ador: et Simon et castra ejus ambulabant in omnem locum quocumque ibant.

verses.text: And they that were in the castle, sent messengers to Tryphon, that he should make haste to come through the desert, and send them victuals.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem in arce erant, miserunt ad Tryphonem legatos, ut festinaret venire per desertum, et mitteret illis alimonias.

verses.text: And Tryphon made ready all his horsemen to come that night: but there fell a very great snow, and he came not into the country of Galaad.
verses.textLatin: Et paravit Tryphon omnem equitatum, ut veniret illa nocte: erat autem nix multa valde, et non venit in Galaaditim.

verses.text: And when he approached to Bascama, he slew Jonathan and his sons there.
verses.textLatin: Et cum appropinquasset Bascaman, occidit Jonathan et filios ejus illic.

verses.text: And Tryphon returned, and went into his own country.
verses.textLatin: Et convertit Tryphon, et abiit in terram suam.

verses.text: And Simon sent, and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried them in Modin, in the city of his fathers.
verses.textLatin: Et misit Simon, et accepit ossa Jonathæ fratris sui, et sepelivit ea in Modin civitate patrum ejus.

verses.text: And all Israel bewailed him with great lamentation: and they mourned for him many days.
verses.textLatin: Et planxerunt eum omnis Israël planctu magno, et luxerunt eum dies multos.

verses.text: And Simon built over the sepulchre of his father and of his brethren, a building lofty to the sight, of polished stone behind and before:
verses.textLatin: Et ædificavit Simon super sepulchrum patris sui et fratrum suorum ædificium altum visu, lapide polito retro et ante.

verses.text: And he set up seven pyramids one against another for his father and his mother, and his four brethren:
verses.textLatin: Et statuit septem pyramidas, unam contra unam, patri et matri, et quatuor fratribus:

verses.text: And round about these he set great pillars: and upon the pillars arms for a perpetual memory: and by the arms ships carved, which might be seen by all that sailed on the sea.
verses.textLatin: et his circumposuit columnas magnas: et super columnas arma, ad memoriam æternam: et juxta arma naves sculptas, quæ viderentur ab omnibus navigantibus mare:

verses.text: This is the sepulchre that he made in Modin even unto this day.
verses.textLatin: hoc est sepulchrum, quod fecit in Modin usque in hunc diem.

verses.text: But Tryphon when he was upon a journey with the young king Antiochus, treacherously slew him.
verses.textLatin: Tryphon autem cum iter faceret cum Antiocho rege adolescente, dolo occidit eum:

verses.text: And he reigned in his place, and put on the crown of Asia: and brought great evils upon the land.
verses.textLatin: et regnavit loco ejus, et imposuit sibi diadema Asiæ, et fecit plagam magnam in terra.

verses.text: And Simon built up the strong holds of Judea, fortifying them with high towers, and great walls, and gates, and bars: and he stored up victuals in the fortresses.
verses.textLatin: Et ædificavit Simon præsidia Judææ, muniens ea turribus excelsis, et muris magnis, et portis, et seris: et posuit alimenta in munitionibus.

verses.text: And Simon chose men and sent to king Demetrius, to the end that he should grant an immunity to the land: for all that Tryphon did was to spoil.
verses.textLatin: Et elegit Simon viros, et misit ad Demetrium regem ut faceret remissionem regioni: quia actus omnes Tryphonis per direptionem fuerant gesti.

verses.text: And king Demetrius in answer to this request, wrote a letter in this manner:
verses.textLatin: Et Demetrius rex ad verba ista respondit ei, et scripsit epistolam talem:

verses.text: King Demetrius to Simon the high priest, and friend of kings, and to the ancients, and to the nation of the Jews, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Rex Demetrius Simoni summo sacerdoti et amico regum, et senioribus, et genti Judæorum, salutem.

verses.text: The golden crown, and the palm, which you sent, we have received: and we are ready to make a firm peace with you, and to write to the king’s chief officers to release you the things that we have released.
verses.textLatin: Coronam auream, et bahem, quam misistis, suscepimus: et parati sumus facere vobiscum pacem magnam, et scribere præpositis regis remittere vobis quæ indulsimus.

verses.text: For all that we have decreed in your favour, shall stand in force. The strong holds that you have built, shall be your own.
verses.textLatin: Quæcumque enim constituimus, vobis constant: munitiones, quas ædificastis, vobis sint:

verses.text: And as for any oversight or fault committed unto this day, we forgive it, and the crown which you owed: and if any other thing were taxed in Jerusalem, now let it not be taxed.
verses.textLatin: remittimus quoque ignorantias et peccata usque in hodiernum diem, et coronam quam debebatis: et si quid aliud erat tributarium in Jerusalem, jam non sit tributarium.

verses.text: And if any of you be fit to be enrolled among ours, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.
verses.textLatin: Et si qui ex vobis apti sunt conscribi inter nostros, conscribantur, et sit inter nos pax.

verses.text: In the year one hundred and seventy the yoke of the Gentiles was taken off from Israel.
verses.textLatin: Anno centesimo septuagesimo, ablatum est jugum gentium ab Israël.

verses.text: And the people of Israel began to write in the instruments, and public records, The first year under Simon the high priest, the great captain and prince of the Jews.
verses.textLatin: Et cœpit populus Israël scribere in tabulis, et gestis publicis, anno primo sub Simone summo sacerdote, magno duce, et principe Judæorum.

verses.text: In those days Simon besieged Gaza, and camped round about it, and he made engines, and set them to the city, and he struck one tower, and took it.
verses.textLatin: In diebus illis applicuit Simon ad Gazam, et circumdedit eam castris, et fecit machinas, et applicuit ad civitatem, et percussit turrem unam, et comprehendit eam.

verses.text: And they that were within the engine leaped into the city: and there was a great uproar in the city.
verses.textLatin: Et eruperant qui erant intra machinam in civitatem, et factus est motus magnus in civitate.

verses.text: And they that were in the city went up with their wives and children upon the wall, with their garments rent, and they cried with a loud voice, beseeching Simon to grant them peace.
verses.textLatin: Et ascenderunt qui erant in civitate cum uxoribus et filiis supra murum, scissis tunicis suis, et clamaverunt voce magna, postulantes a Simone dextras sibi dari,

verses.text: And they said: Deal not with us according to our evil deeds, but according to thy mercy.
verses.textLatin: et dixerunt: Non nobis reddas secundum malitias nostras, sed secundum misericordias tuas.

verses.text: And Simon being moved, did not destroy them: but yet he cast them out of the city, and cleansed the houses wherein there had been idols, and then he entered into it with hymns, blessing the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Et flexus Simon, non debellavit eos: ejecit tamen eos de civitate, et mundavit ædes in quibus fuerant simulacra, et tunc intravit in eam cum hymnis benedicens Dominum:

verses.text: And having cast out of it all uncleanness, he placed in it men that should observe the law: and he fortified it, and made it his habitation.
verses.textLatin: et ejecta ab ea omni immunditia, collocavit in ea viros qui legem facerent: et munivit eam, et fecit sibi habitationem.

verses.text: But they that were in the castle of Jerusalem were hindered from going out and coming into the country, and from buying and selling: and they were straitened with hunger, and many of them perished through famine.
verses.textLatin: Qui autem erant in arce Jerusalem, prohibebantur egredi et ingredi regionem, et emere ac vendere: et esurierunt valde, et multi ex eis fame perierunt,

verses.text: And they cried to Simon for peace, and he granted it to them: and he cast them out from thence, and cleansed the castle from uncleannesses.
verses.textLatin: et clamaverunt ad Simonem ut dextras acciperent: et dedit illis: et ejecit eos inde, et mundavit arcem a contaminationibus:

verses.text: And they entered into it the three and twentieth day of the second month, in the year one hundred and seventy-one, with thanksgiving, and branches of palm trees, and harps, and cymbals, and psalteries, and hymns, and canticles, because the great enemy was destroyed out of Israel.
verses.textLatin: et intraverunt in eam tertia et vigesima die secundi mensis, anno centesimo septuagesimo primo, cum laude, et ramis palmarum, et cinyris, et cymbalis, et nablis, et hymnis, et canticis, quia contritus est inimicus magnus ex Israël.

verses.text: And he ordained that these days should be kept every year with gladness.
verses.textLatin: Et constituit ut omnibus annis agerentur dies hi cum lætitia.

verses.text: And he fortified the mountain of the temple that was near the castle, and he dwelt there himself, and they that were with him.
verses.textLatin: Et munivit montem templi, qui erat secus arcem, et habitavit ibi ipse, et qui cum eo erant.

verses.text: And Simon saw that John his son was a valiant man for war: and he made him captain of all the forces: and he dwelt in Gazara.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit Simon Joannem filium suum, quod fortis prælii vir esset: et posuit eum ducem virtutum universarum: et habitavit in Gazaris.

verses.text: In  the year one hundred and seventy-two, king Demetrius assembled his army, and went into Media to get him succours to fight against Tryphon.
verses.textLatin: Anno centesimo septuagesimo secundo, congregavit rex Demetrius exercitum suum, et abiit in Mediam ad contrahenda sibi auxilia, ut expugnaret Tryphonem.

verses.text: And Arsaces the king of Persia and Media heard that Demetrius was entered within his borders, and he sent one of his princes to take him alive, and bring him to him.
verses.textLatin: Et audivit Arsaces rex Persidis et Mediæ, quia intravit Demetrius confines suos: et misit unum de principibus suis ut comprehenderet eum vivum, et adduceret eum ad se.

verses.text: And he went and defeated the army of Demetrius: and took him, and brought him to Arsaces, and he put him into custody.
verses.textLatin: Et abiit, et percussit castra Demetrii: et comprehendit eum, et duxit eum ad Arsacem, et posuit eum in custodiam.

verses.text: And all the land of Juda was at rest all the days of Simon, and he sought the good of his nation: and his power, and his glory pleased them well all his days.
verses.textLatin: Et siluit omnis terra Juda omnibus diebus Simonis, et quæsivit bona genti suæ: et placuit illis potestas ejus et gloria ejus omnibus diebus.

verses.text: And with all his glory he took Joppe for a haven, and made an entrance to the isles of the sea.
verses.textLatin: Et cum omni gloria sua accepit Joppen in portum, et fecit introitum in insulis maris.

verses.text: And he enlarged the bounds of his nation, and made himself master of the country.
verses.textLatin: Et dilatavit fines gentis suæ, et obtinuit regionem.

verses.text: And he gathered together a great number of captives, and had the dominion of Gazara, and of Bethsura, and of the castle: and took away all uncleanness out of it, and there was none that resisted him.
verses.textLatin: Et congregavit captivitatem multam, et dominatus est Gazaræ, et Bethsuræ, et arci: et abstulit immunditias ex ea, et non erat qui resisteret ei.

verses.text: And every man tilled his land with peace: and the land of Juda yielded her increase, and the trees of the fields their fruit.
verses.textLatin: Et unusquisque colebat terram suam cum pace: et terra Juda dabat fructus suos, et ligna camporum fructum suum.

verses.text: The ancient men sat all in the streets, and treated together of the good things of the land, and the young men put on them glory, and the robes of war.
verses.textLatin: Seniores in plateis sedebant omnes, et de bonis terræ tractabant, et juvenes induebant se gloriam, et stolas belli.

verses.text: And he provided victuals for the cities, and he appointed that they should be furnished with ammunition, so that the fame of his glory was renowned even to the end of the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et civitatibus tribuebat alimonias, et constituebat eas ut essent vasa munitionis quoadusque nominatum est nomen gloriæ ejus usque ad extremum terræ.

verses.text: He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy.
verses.textLatin: Fecit pacem super terram, et lætatus est Israël lætitia magna.

verses.text: And every man sat under his vine, and under his fig tree: and there was none to make them afraid.
verses.textLatin: Et sedit unusquisque sub vite sua, et sub ficulnea sua: et non erat qui eos terreret.

verses.text: There was none left in the land to fight against them: kings were discomfited in those days.
verses.textLatin: Defecit impugnans eos super terram: reges contriti sunt in diebus illis.

verses.text: And he strengthened all those of his people that were brought low, and he sought the law, and took away every unjust and wicked man.
verses.textLatin: Et confirmavit omnes humiles populi sui, et legem exquisivit, et abstulit omnem iniquum et malum:

verses.text: He glorified the sanctuary, and multiplied the vessels of the holy places.
verses.textLatin: sancta glorificavit, et multiplicavit vasa sanctorum.

verses.text: And it was heard at Rome, and as far as Sparta, that Jonathan was dead: and they were very sorry.
verses.textLatin: Et auditum est Romæ quia defunctus esset Jonathas, et usque in Spartiatas: et contristati sunt valde.

verses.text: But when they heard that Simon his brother was made high priest in his place, and was possessed of all the country, and the cities therein:
verses.textLatin: Ut audierunt autem quod Simon frater ejus factus esset summus sacerdos loco ejus, et ipse obtineret omnem regionem, et civitates in ea,

verses.text: They wrote to him in tables of brass, to renew the friendship and alliance which they had made with Judas, and with Jonathan his brethren.
verses.textLatin: scripserunt ad eum in tabulis æreis, ut renovarent amicitias et societatem quam fecerant cum Juda et cum Jonatha, fratribus ejus.

verses.text: And they were read before the assembly in Jerusalem. And this is the copy of the letters that the Spartans sent.
verses.textLatin: Et lectæ sunt in conspectu ecclesiæ in Jerusalem. Et hoc exemplum epistolarum, quas Spartiatæ miserunt:

verses.text: The princes and the cities of the Spartans to Simon the high priest, and to the ancients, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews their brethren, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Spartianorum principes et civitates, Simoni sacerdoti magno, et senioribus, et sacerdotibus, et reliquo populo Judæorum, fratribus, salutem.

verses.text: The ambassadors that were sent to our people, have told us of your glory, and honour, and joy: and we rejoiced at their coming.
verses.textLatin: Legati, qui missi sunt ad populum nostrum, nuntiaverunt nobis de vestra gloria, et honore, ac lætitia: et gavisi sumus in introitu eorum.

verses.text: And we registered what was said by them in the councils of the people in this manner: Numenius the son of Antiochus, and Antipater the son of Jason, ambassadors of the Jews, came to us to renew the former friendship with us.
verses.textLatin: Et scripsimus quæ ab eis erant dicta in conciliis populi, sic: Numenius Antiochi, et Antipater Jasonis filius, legati Judæorum, venerunt ad nos, renovantes nobiscum amicitiam pristinam.

verses.text: And it pleased the people to receive the men honourably, and to put a copy of their words in the public records, to be a memorial to the people of the Spartans. And we have written a copy of them to Simon the high priest.
verses.textLatin: Et placuit populo excipere viros gloriose, et ponere exemplum sermonum eorum in segregatis populi libris, ut sit ad memoriam populo Spartiatarum. Exemplum autem horum scripsimus Simoni magno sacerdoti.

verses.text: And after this Simon sent Numenius to Rome, with a great shield of gold of the weight of a thousand pounds, to confirm the league with them. And when the people of Rome had heard
verses.textLatin: Post hæc autem misit Simon Numenium Romam, habentem clypeum aureum magnum, pondo mnarum mille, ad statuendam cum eis societatem. Cum autem audisset populus Romanus

verses.text: These words, they said: What thanks shall we give to Simon, and his sons?
verses.textLatin: sermones istos, dixerunt: Quam gratiarum actionem reddemus Simoni, et filiis ejus?

verses.text: For he hath restored his brethren, and hath driven away in fight the enemies of Israel from them: and they decreed him liberty, and registered it in tables of brass, and set it upon pillars in mount Sion.
verses.textLatin: restituit enim ipse fratres suos, et expugnavit inimicos Israël ab eis, et statuerunt ei libertatem, et descripserunt in tabulis æreis, et posuerunt in titulis in monte Sion.

verses.text: And this is a copy of the writing: The eighteenth day of the month Elul, in the year one hundred and seventy-two, being the third year under Simon the high priest at Asaramel,
verses.textLatin: Et hoc est exemplum scripturæ: Octavadecima die mensis Elul, anno centesimo septuagesimo secundo, anno tertio sub Simone sacerdote magno in Asaramel,

verses.text: In a great assembly of the priests, and of the people, and the princes of the nation, and the ancients of the country, these things were notified: Forasmuch as there have often been wars in our country,
verses.textLatin: in conventu magno sacerdotum, et populi, et principum gentis, et seniorum regionis, nota facta sunt hæc: quoniam frequenter facta sunt prælia in regione nostra,

verses.text: And Simon the son of Mathathias of the children of Jarib, and his brethren have put themselves in danger, and resisted the enemies of their nation, for the maintenance of their holy places, and the law: and have raised their nation to great glory.
verses.textLatin: Simon autem Mathathiæ filius, ex filiis Jarib, et fratres ejus, dederunt se periculo, et restiterunt adversariis gentis suæ, ut starent sancta ipsorum, et lex: et gloria magna glorificaverunt gentem suam.

verses.text: And Jonathan gathered together his nation, and was made their high priest, and he was laid to his people.
verses.textLatin: Et congregavit Jonathas gentem suam, et factus est illis sacerdos magnus, et appositus est ad populum suum.

verses.text: And their enemies desired to tread down and destroy their country, and to stretch forth their hands against their holy places.
verses.textLatin: Et voluerunt inimici eorum calcare et atterere regionem ipsorum, et extendere manus in sancta eorum.

verses.text: Then Simon resisted and fought for his nation, and laid out much of his money, and armed the valiant men of his nation, and gave them wages:
verses.textLatin: Tunc restitit Simon, et pugnavit pro gente sua, et erogavit pecunias multas, et armavit viros virtutis gentis suæ, et dedit illis stipendia:

verses.text: And he fortified the cities of Judea, and Bethsura that lieth in the borders of Judea, where the armour of the enemies was before: and he placed there a garrison of Jews.
verses.textLatin: et munivit civitates Judææ, et Bethsuram, quæ erat in finibus Judææ, ubi erant arma hostium antea: et posuit illic præsidium viros Judæos.

verses.text: And he fortified Joppe which lieth by the sea: and Gazara, which bordereth upon Azotus, wherein the enemies dwelt before, and he placed Jews here: and furnished them with all things convenient for their reparation.
verses.textLatin: Et Joppen munivit, quæ erat ad mare, et Gazaram, quæ est in finibus Azoti, in qua hostes antea habitabant: et collocavit illic Judæos, et quæcumque apta erant ad correptionem eorum, posuit in eis.

verses.text: And the people seeing the acts of Simon, and to what glory he meant to bring his nation, made him their prince, and high priest, because he had done all these things, and for the justice, and faith, which he kept to his nation, and for that he sought by all means to advance his people.
verses.textLatin: Et vidit populus actum Simonis, et gloriam quam cogitabat facere genti suæ, et posuerunt eum ducem suum, et principem sacerdotum, eo quod ipse fecerat hæc omnia, et justitiam, et fidem, quam conservavit genti suæ, et exquisivit omni modo exaltare populum suum.

verses.text: And in his days things prospered in his hands, so that the heathens were taken away out of their country, and they also that were in the city of David in Jerusalem in the castle, out of which they issued forth, and profaned all places round about the sanctuary, and did much evil to its purity.
verses.textLatin: Et in diebus ejus prosperatum est in manibus ejus, ut tollerentur gentes de regione ipsorum, et qui in civitate David erant, in Jerusalem in arce, de qua procedebant, et contaminabant omnia quæ in circuitu sanctorum sunt, et inferebant plagam magnam castitati:

verses.text: And he placed therein Jews for the defence of the country, and of the city, and he raised up the walls of Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: et collocavit in ea viros Judæos ad tutamentum regionis, et civitatis, et exaltavit muros Jerusalem.

verses.text: And king Demetrius confirmed him in the high priesthood.
verses.textLatin: Et rex Demetrius statuit illi summum sacerdotium.

verses.text: According to these things he made him his friend, and glorified him with great glory.
verses.textLatin: Secundum hæc fecit eum amicum suum, et glorificavit eum gloria magna.

verses.text: For he had heard that the Romans had called the Jews their friends, and confederates, and brethren, and that they had received Simon’s ambassadors with honour:
verses.textLatin: Audivit enim quod appellati sunt Judæi a Romanis amici, et socii, et fratres, et quia susceperunt legatos Simonis gloriose,

verses.text: And that the Jews, and their priests, had consented that he should be their prince, and high priest for ever, till there should arise a faithful prophet:
verses.textLatin: et quia Judæi et sacerdotes eorum consenserunt eum esse ducem suum, et summum sacerdotem in æternum, donec surgat propheta fidelis:

verses.text: And that he should be chief over them, and that he should have the charge of the sanctuary, and that he should appoint rulers over their works, and over the country, and over the armour, and over the strong holds.
verses.textLatin: et ut sit super eos dux, et ut cura esset illi pro sanctis, et ut constitueret præpositos super opera eorum, et super regionem, et super arma, et super præsidia:

verses.text: And that he should have care of the holy places: and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all the writings in the country should be made in his name: and that he should be clothed with purple, and gold:
verses.textLatin: et cura sit illi de sanctis: et ut audiatur ab omnibus, et scribantur in nomine ejus omnes conscriptiones in regione: et ut operiatur purpura et auro:

verses.text: And that it should not be lawful for any of the people, or of the priests, to disannul any of these things, or to gainsay his words, or to call together an assembly in the country without him: or to be clothed with purple, or to wear a buckle of gold:
verses.textLatin: et ne liceat ulli ex populo et ex sacerdotibus irritum facere aliquid horum, et contradicere his quæ ab eo dicuntur, aut convocare conventum in regione sine ipso, et vestiri purpura, et uti fibula aurea:

verses.text: And whosoever shall do otherwise, or shall make void any of these things shall be punished.
verses.textLatin: qui autem fecerit extra hæc, aut irritum fecerit aliquid horum, reus erit.

verses.text: And it pleased all the people to establish Simon, and to do according to these words.
verses.textLatin: Et complacuit omni populo statuere Simonem, et facere secundum verba ista.

verses.text: And Simon accepted thereof, and was well pleased to execute the office of the high priesthood, and to be captain, and prince of the nation of the Jews, and of the priests, and to be chief over all.
verses.textLatin: Et suscepit Simon, et placuit ei ut summo sacerdotio fungeretur, et esset dux et princeps gentis Judæorum, et sacerdotum, et præesset omnibus.

verses.text: And they commanded that this writing should be put in tables of brass, and that they should be set up within the compass of the sanctuary, in a conspicuous place:
verses.textLatin: Et scripturam istam dixerunt ponere in tabulis æreis, et ponere eas in peribolo sanctorum, in loco celebri:

verses.text: And that a copy thereof should be put in the treasury, that Simon and his sons may have it.
verses.textLatin: exemplum autem eorum ponere in ærario, ut habeat Simon, et filii ejus.

verses.text: And  king Antiochus the son of Demetrius sent letters from the isles of the sea to Simon the priest, and prince of the nation of the Jews, and to all the people:
verses.textLatin: Et misit rex Antiochus filius Demetrii epistolas ab insulis maris Simoni sacerdoti, et principi gentis Judæorum, et universæ genti:

verses.text: And the contents were these: King Antiochus to Simon the high priest, and to the nation of the Jews, greeting.
verses.textLatin: et erant continentes hunc modum: Rex Antiochus Simoni sacerdoti magno, et genti Judæorum salutem.

verses.text: Forasmuch as certain pestilent men have usurped the kingdom of our fathers, and my purpose is to challenge the kingdom, and to restore it to its former estate: and I have chosen a great army, and have built ships of war.
verses.textLatin: Quoniam quidem pestilentes obtinuerunt regnum patrum nostrorum, volo autem vendicare regnum, et restituere illud sicut erat antea: et electam feci multitudinem exercitus, et feci naves bellicas.

verses.text: And I design to go through the country that I may take revenge of them that have destroyed our country, and that have made many cities desolate in my realm.
verses.textLatin: Volo autem procedere per regionem ut ulciscar in eos, qui corruperunt regionem nostram, et qui desolaverunt civitates multas in regno meo.

verses.text: Now therefore I confirm unto thee all the oblations which all the kings before me remitted to thee, and what other gifts soever they remitted to thee:
verses.textLatin: Nunc ergo statuo tibi omnes oblationes, quas remiserunt tibi ante me omnes reges, et quæcumque alia dona remiserunt tibi:

verses.text: And I give thee leave to coin thy own money in thy country:
verses.textLatin: et permitto tibi facere percussuram proprii numismatis in regione tua:

verses.text: And let Jerusalem be holy and free, and all the armour that hath been made, and the fortresses which thou hast built, and which thou keepest in thy hands, let them remain to thee.
verses.textLatin: Jerusalem autem sanctam esse, et liberam: et omnia arma, quæ fabricata sunt, et præsidia, quæ construxisti, quæ tenes, maneant tibi.

verses.text: And all that is due to the king, and what should be the king’s hereafter, from this present and for ever, is forgiven thee.
verses.textLatin: Et omne debitum regis, et quæ futura sunt regi, ex hoc et in totum tempus remittuntur tibi.

verses.text: And when we shall have recovered our kingdom, we will glorify thee, and thy nation, and the temple with great glory, so that your glory shall be made manifest in all the earth.
verses.textLatin: Cum autem obtinuerimus regnum nostrum, glorificabimus te, et gentem tuam, et templum, gloria magna, ita ut manifestetur gloria vestra in universa terra.

verses.text: In the year one hundred and seventy-four Antiochus entered into the land of his fathers, and all the forces assembled to him, so that few were left with Tryphon.
verses.textLatin: Anno centesimo septuagesimo quarto exiit Antiochus in terram patrum suorum, et convenerunt ad eum omnes exercitus, ita ut pauci relicti essent cum Tryphone.

verses.text: And king Antiochus pursued after him, and he fled along by the sea coast and came to Dora.
verses.textLatin: Et insecutus est eum Antiochus rex, et venit Doram fugiens per maritimam:

verses.text: For he perceived that evils were gathered together upon him, and his troops had forsaken him.
verses.textLatin: sciebat enim quod congregata sunt mala in eum, et reliquit eum exercitus:

verses.text: And Antiochus camped above Dora with a hundred and twenty thousand men of war, and eight thousand horsemen:
verses.textLatin: et applicuit Antiochus super Doram cum centum viginti millibus virorum belligeratorum, et octo millibus equitum:

verses.text: And he invested the city, and the ships drew near by sea: and they annoyed the city by land, and by sea, and suffered none to come in, or to go out.
verses.textLatin: et circuivit civitatem, et naves a mari accesserunt: et vexabant civitatem a terra et mari, et neminem sinebant ingredi vel egredi.

verses.text: And Numenius, and they that had been with him, came from the city of Rome, having letters written to the kings, and countries, the contents whereof were these:
verses.textLatin: Venit autem Numenius, et qui cum eo fuerant, ab urbe Roma, habentes epistolas regibus et regionibus scriptas, in quibus continebantur hæc:

verses.text: Lucius the consul of the Romans, to king Ptolemee, greeting.
verses.textLatin: Lucius consul Romanorum, Ptolemæo regi salutem.

verses.text: The ambassadors of the Jews our friends came to us, to renew the former friendship and alliance, being sent from Simon the high priest, and the people of the Jews.
verses.textLatin: Legati Judæorum venerunt ad nos amici nostri, renovantes pristinam amicitiam et societatem, missi a Simone principe sacerdotum et populo Judæorum.

verses.text: And they brought also a shield of gold of a thousand pounds.
verses.textLatin: Attulerunt autem et clypeum aureum mnarum mille.

verses.text: It hath seemed good therefore to us to write to the kings, and countries, that they should do them no harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or countries: and that they should give no aid to them that fight against them.
verses.textLatin: Placuit itaque nobis scribere regibus et regionibus, ut non inferant illis mala, neque impugnent eos, et civitates eorum, et regiones eorum: et ut non ferant auxilium pugnantibus adversus eos.

verses.text: And it hath seemed good to us to receive the shield of them.
verses.textLatin: Visum autem est nobis accipere ab eis clypeum.

verses.text: If therefore any pestilent men are fled out of their country to you, deliver them to Simon the high priest, that he may punish them according to their law.
verses.textLatin: Si qui ergo pestilentes refugerunt de regione ipsorum ad vos, tradite eos Simoni principi sacerdotum, ut vindicet in eos secundum legem suam.

verses.text: These same things were written to king Demetrius, and to Attalus, and to Ariarathes, and to Arsaces,
verses.textLatin: Hæc eadem scripta sunt Demetrio regi, et Attalo, et Ariarathi, et Arsaci,

verses.text: And to all the countries; and to Lampsacus, and to the Spartans, and to Delus, and Myndus, and Sicyon, and Caria, and Samus, and Pamphylia, and Lycia, and Alicarnassus, and Cos, and Side, and Aradus, and Rhodes, and Phaselis, and Gortyna, and Gnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
verses.textLatin: et in omnes regiones: et Lampsaco, et Spartiatis, et in Delum, et in Myndum, et in Sicyonem, et in Cariam, et in Samum, et in Pamphyliam, et in Lyciam, et in Alicarnassum, et in Coo, et in Siden, et in Aradon, et in Rhodum, et in Phaselidem, et in Gortynam, et Gnidum, et Cyprum, et Cyrenen.

verses.text: And they wrote a copy thereof to Simon the high priest, and to the people of the Jews.
verses.textLatin: Exemplum autem eorum scripserunt Simoni principi sacerdotum, et populo Judæorum.

verses.text: But king Antiochus moved his camp to Dora the second time, assaulting it continually, and making engines: and he shut up Tryphon, that he could not go out.
verses.textLatin: Antiochus autem rex applicuit castra in Doram secundo, admovens ei semper manus, et machinas faciens: et conclusit Tryphonem, ne procederet:

verses.text: And Simon sent to him two thousand chosen men to aid him, silver also, and gold, and abundance of furniture.
verses.textLatin: et misit ad eum Simon duo millia virorum electorum in auxilium, et argentum, et aurum, et vasa copiosa:

verses.text: And he would not receive them, but broke all the covenant that he had made with him before, and alienated himself from him.
verses.textLatin: et noluit ea accipere, sed rupit omnia, quæ pactus est cum eo antea, et alienavit se ab eo.

verses.text: And he sent to him Athenobius one of his friends, to treat with him, saying: You hold Joppe, and Gazara, and the castle that is in Jerusalem, which are cities of my kingdom:
