verses.text: Now there was in that place a tower fifty cubits high, having a heap of ashes on every side: this had a prospect steep down.
verses.textLatin: Erat autem in eodem loco turris quinquaginta cubitorum, aggestum undique habens cineris: hæc prospectum habebat in præceps.

verses.text: From thence he commanded the sacrilegious wretch to be thrown down into the ashes, all men thrusting him forward unto death.
verses.textLatin: Inde in cinerem dejici jussit sacrilegum, omnibus eum propellentibus ad interitum.

verses.text: And by such a law it happened that Menelaus the transgressor of the law was put to death: not having so much as burial in the earth.
verses.textLatin: Et tali lege prævaricatorem legis contigit mori, nec terræ dari Menelaum.

verses.text: And indeed very justly, for insomuch as he had committed many sins against the altar of God, the fire and ashes of which were holy: he was condemned to die in ashes.
verses.textLatin: Et quidem satis juste: nam quia multa erga aram Dei delicta commisit, cujus ignis et cinis erat sanctus: ipse in cineris morte damnatus est.

verses.text: But the king, with his mind full of rage, came on to shew himself worse to the Jews than his father was.
verses.textLatin: Sed rex mente effrenatus veniebat, nequiorem se patre suo Judæis ostensurus.

verses.text: Which, when Judas understood, he commanded the people to call upon the Lord day and night, that as he had always done, so now also he would help them:
verses.textLatin: Quibus Judas cognitis, præcepit populo ut die ac nocte Dominum invocarent, quo, sicut semper, et nunc adjuvaret eos,

verses.text: Because they were afraid to be deprived of the law, and of their country, and of the holy temple: and that he would not suffer the people, that had of late taken breath for a little while, to be again in subjection to blasphemous nations.
verses.textLatin: quippe qui lege, et patria, sanctoque templo privari vererentur: ac populum, qui nuper paululum respirasset, ne sineret blasphemis rursus nationibus subdi.

verses.text: So when they had all done this together, and had craved mercy of the Lord with weeping and fasting, lying prostrate on the ground for three days continually, Judas exhorted them to make themselves ready.
verses.textLatin: Omnibus itaque simul id facientibus, et petentibus a Domino misericordiam cum fletu et jejuniis, per triduum continuum prostratis, hortatus est eos Judas ut se præpararent.

verses.text: But he with the ancients determined, before the king should bring his army into Judea, and make himself master of the city, to go out, and to commit the event of the thing to the judgment of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Ipse vero cum senioribus cogitavit priusquam rex admoveret exercitum ad Judæam et obtineret civitatem, exire, et Domini judicio committere exitum rei.

verses.text: So committing all to God, the creator of the world, and having exhorted his people to fight manfully, and to stand up even to death for the laws, the temple, the city, their country, and citizens: he placed his army about Modin.
verses.textLatin: Dans itaque potestatem omnium Deo mundi creatori, et exhortatus suos ut fortiter dimicarent, et usque ad mortem pro legibus, templo, civitate, patria, et civibus starent, circa Modin exercitum constituit.

verses.text: And having given his company for a watchword, The victory of God, with most valiant chosen young men, he set upon the king’s quarter by night, and slew four thousand men in the camp, and the greatest of the elephants, with them that had been upon him,
verses.textLatin: Et dato signo suis Dei victoriæ, juvenibus fortissimis electis nocte aggressus aulam regiam, in castris interfecit viros quatuor millia, et maximum elephantorum cum his qui superpositi fuerant:

verses.text: And having filled the camp of the enemies with exceeding great fear and tumult, they went off with good success.
verses.textLatin: summoque metu ac perturbatione hostium castra replentes, rebus prospere gestis, abierunt.

verses.text: Now this was done at the break of day, by the protection and help of the Lord.
verses.textLatin: Hoc autem factum est die illucescente, adjuvante eum Domini protectione.

verses.text: But the king having taken a taste of the hardiness of the Jews, attempted to take the strong places by policy:
verses.textLatin: Sed rex, accepto gustu audaciæ Judæorum, arte difficultatem locorum tentabat:

verses.text: And he marched with his army to Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Jews: but he was repulsed, he failed, he lost his men.
verses.textLatin: et Bethsuræ, quæ erat Judæorum præsidium munitum, castra admovebat: sed fugabatur, impingebat, minorabatur.

verses.text: Now Judas sent necessaries to them that were within.
verses.textLatin: His autem qui intus erant, Judas necessaria mittebat.

verses.text: But Rhodocus, one of the Jews’ army, disclosed the secrets to the enemies, so he was sought out, and taken up, and put in prison.
verses.textLatin: Enuntiavit autem mysteria hostibus Rhodocus quidam de judaico exercitu, qui requisitus comprehensus est, et conclusus.

verses.text: Again the king treated with them that were in Bethsura: gave his right hand: took theirs: and went away.
verses.textLatin: Iterum rex sermonem habuit ad eos qui erant in Bethsuris: dextram dedit, accepit, abiit:

verses.text: He fought with Judas: and was overcome. And when he understood that Philip, who had been left over the affairs, had rebelled at Antioch, he was in a consternation of mind, and entreating the Jews, and yielding to them, he swore to all things that seemed reasonable, and, being reconciled, offered sacrifices, honoured the temple, and left gifts.
verses.textLatin: commisit cum Juda, superatus est. Ut autem cognovit rebellasse Philippum Antiochiæ, qui relictus erat super negotia, mente consternatus, Judæos deprecans, subditusque eis, jurat de omnibus quibus justum visum est: et reconciliatus obtulit sacrificium, honoravit templum, et munera posuit.

verses.text: He embraced Machabeus, and made him governor and prince from Ptolemais unto the Gerrenians.
verses.textLatin: Machabæum amplexatus est, et fecit eum a Ptolemaide usque ad Gerrenos ducem et principem.

verses.text: But when he was come to Ptolemais, the men of that city were much displeased with the conditions of the peace, being angry for fear they should break the covenant.
verses.textLatin: Ut autem venit Ptolemaidam, graviter ferebant Ptolemenses amicitiæ conventionem, indignantes ne forte fœdus irrumperent.

verses.text: Then Lysias went up to the judgment seat, and set forth the reason, and appeased the people, and returned to Antioch: and thus matters went with regard to the king’s coming and his return.
verses.textLatin: Tunc ascendit Lysias tribunal, et exposuit rationem, et populum sedavit, regressusque est Antiochiam: et hoc modo regis profectio et reditus processit.

verses.text: But  after the space of three years Judas, and they that were with him, understood that Demetrius, the son of Seleucus was come up with great power, and a navy by the haven of Tripolis to places proper for his purpose.
verses.textLatin: Sed post triennii tempus, cognovit Judas et qui cum eo erant Demetrium Seleuci cum multitudine valida et navibus per portam Tripolis ascendisse ad loca opportuna,

verses.text: And had made himself master of the countries against Antiochus, and his general, Lysias.
verses.textLatin: et tenuisse regiones adversus Antiochum, et ducem ejus Lysiam.

verses.text: Now one Alcimus, who had been chief priest, but had wilfully defiled himself in the time of mingling with the heathens, seeing that there was no safety for him, nor access to the altar,
verses.textLatin: Alcimus autem quidam, qui summus sacerdos fuerat, sed voluntarie coinquinatus est temporibus commistionis, considerans nullo modo sibi esse salutem neque accessum ad altare,

verses.text: Came to king Demetrius in the year one hundred and fifty, presenting unto him a crown of gold, and a palm, and besides these, some boughs which seemed to belong to the temple. And that day indeed he held his peace.
verses.textLatin: venit ad regem Demetrium centesimo quinquagesimo anno, offerens ei coronam auream et palmam, super hæc et thallos, qui templi esse videbantur. Et ipsa quidem die siluit.

verses.text: But having gotten a convenient time to further his madness, being called to counsel by Demetrius, and asked what the Jews relied upon, and what were their counsels,
verses.textLatin: Tempus autem opportunum dementiæ suæ nactus, convocatus a Demetrio ad consilium, et interrogatus quibus rebus et consiliis Judæi niterentur,

verses.text: He answered thereunto: They among the Jews that are called Assideans, of whom Judas Machabeus is captain, nourish wars, and raise seditions, and will not suffer the realm to be in peace.
verses.textLatin: respondit: Ipsi qui dicuntur Assidæi Judæorum, quibus præest Judas Machabæus, bella nutriunt, et seditiones movent, nec patiuntur regnum esse quietum:

verses.text: For I also being deprived of my ancestor’s glory (I mean of the high priesthood) am now come hither:
verses.textLatin: nam et ego defraudatus parentum gloria (dico autem summo sacerdotio) huc veni:

verses.text: Principally indeed out of fidelity to the king’s interests, but in the next place also to provide for the good of my countrymen: for all our nation suffereth much from the evil proceedings of those men.
verses.textLatin: primo quidem utilitatibus regis fidem servans, secundo autem etiam civibus consulens: nam illorum pravitate universum genus nostrum non minime vexatur.

verses.text: Wherefore, O king, seeing thou knowest all these things, take care, I beseech thee, both of the country, and of our nation, according to thy humanity which is known to all men,
verses.textLatin: Sed oro his singulis, o rex, cognitis, et regioni et generi, secundum humanitatem tuam pervulgatam omnibus, prospice:

verses.text: For as long as Judas liveth, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.
verses.textLatin: nam, quamdiu superest Judas, impossibile est pacem esse negotiis.

verses.text: Now when this man had spoken to this effect, the rest also of the king’s friends, who were enemies of Judas, incensed Demetrius against him.
verses.textLatin: Talibus autem ab hoc dictis, et ceteri amici hostiliter se habentes adversus Judam, inflammaverunt Demetrium.

verses.text: And forthwith he sent Nicanor, the commander over the elephants, governor into Judea:
verses.textLatin: Qui statim Nicanorem præpositum elephantorum ducem misit in Judæam:

verses.text: Giving him in charge, to take Judas himself: and disperse all them that were with him, and to make Alcimus the high priest of the great temple.
verses.textLatin: datis mandatis ut ipsum quidem Judam caperet: eos vero qui cum illo erant, dispergeret, et constitueret Alcimum maximi templi summum sacerdotem.

verses.text: Then the Gentiles who had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the miseries and calamities of the Jews to be the welfare of their affairs.
verses.textLatin: Tunc gentes quæ de Judæa fugerant Judam, gregatim se Nicanori miscebant, miserias et clades Judæorum prosperitates rerum suarum existimantes.

verses.text: Now when the Jews heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the nations were assembled against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him, who chose his people to keep them for ever, and who protected his portion by evident signs.
verses.textLatin: Audito itaque Judæi Nicanoris adventu, et conventu nationum, conspersi terra rogabant eum qui populum suum constituit, ut in æternum custodiret, quique suam portionem signis evidentibus protegit.

verses.text: Then at the commandment of their captain, they forthwith removed from the place where they were, and went to the town of Dessau, to meet them.
verses.textLatin: Imperante autem duce, statim inde moverunt, conveneruntque ad castellum Dessau.

verses.text: Now Simon the brother of Judas had joined battle with Nicanor, but was frightened with the sudden coming of the adversaries.
verses.textLatin: Simon vero frater Judæ commiserat cum Nicanore: sed conterritus est repentino adventu adversariorum.

verses.text: Nevertheless Nicanor hearing of the valour of Judas’s companions, and the greatness of courage with which they fought for their country, was afraid to try the matter by the sword.
verses.textLatin: Nicanor tamen, audiens virtutem comitum Judæ, et animi magnitudinem quam pro patriæ certaminibus habebant, sanguine judicium facere metuebat.

verses.text: Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotius, and Matthias before to present and receive the right hands.
verses.textLatin: Quam ob rem præmisit Posidonium, et Theodotium, et Matthiam, ut darent dextras atque acciperent.

verses.text: And when there had been a consultation thereupon, and the captain had acquainted the multitude with it, they were all of one mind to consent to covenants.
verses.textLatin: Et cum diu de his consilium ageretur, et ipse dux ad multitudinem retulisset, omnium una fuit sententia amicitiis annuere.

verses.text: So they appointed a day upon which they might commune together by themselves: and seats were brought out, and set for each one.
verses.textLatin: Itaque diem constituerunt, qua secreto inter se agerent: et singulis sellæ prolatæ sunt, et positæ.

verses.text: But Judas ordered men to be ready in convenient places, lest some mischief might be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made an agreeable conference.
verses.textLatin: Præcepit autem Judas armatos esse locis opportunis, ne forte ab hostibus repente mali aliquid oriretur: et congruum colloquium fecerunt.

verses.text: And Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no wrong, but sent away the flocks of the multitudes that had been gathered together.
verses.textLatin: Morabatur autem Nicanor Jerosolymis, nihilque inique agebat: gregesque turbarum quæ congregatæ fuerant, dimisit.

verses.text: And Judas was always dear to him from the heart, and he was well affected to the man.
verses.textLatin: Habebat autem Judam semper carum ex animo, et erat viro inclinatus.

verses.text: And he desired him to marry a wife, and to have children. So he married: he lived quietly, and they lived in common.
verses.textLatin: Rogavitque eum ducere uxorem, filiosque procreare. Nuptias fecit: quiete egit, communiterque vivebant.

verses.text: But Alcimus seeing the love they had one to another, and the covenants, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor assented to the foreign interest, for that he meant to make Judas, who was a traitor to the kingdom, his successor.
verses.textLatin: Alcimus autem, videns caritatem illorum ad invicem et conventiones, venit ad Demetrium, et dicebat Nicanorem rebus alienis assentire, Judamque regni insidiatorem successorem sibi destinasse.

verses.text: Then the king being in a rage and provoked with this man’s wicked accusations, wrote to Nicanor, signifying, that he was greatly displeased with the covenant of friendship: and that he commanded him nevertheless to send Machabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch.
verses.textLatin: Itaque rex exasperatus, et pessimis hujus criminationibus irritatus, scripsit Nicanori, dicens graviter quidem se ferre de amicitiæ conventione, jubere tamen Machabæum citius vinctum mittere Antiochiam.

verses.text: When this was known, Nicanor was in a consternation, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles that were agreed upon, having received no injury from the man.
verses.textLatin: Quibus cognitis, Nicanor consternabatur, et graviter ferebat, si ea quæ convenerant irrita faceret, nihil læsus a viro:

verses.text: But because he could not oppose the king, he watched an opportunity to comply with the orders
verses.textLatin: sed quia regi resistere non poterat, opportunitatem observabat qua præceptum perficeret.

verses.text: But when Machabeus perceived that Nicanor was more stern to him, and that when they met together as usual he behaved himself in a rough manner: and was sensible that this rough behaviour came not of good, he gathered together a few of his men, and hid himself from Nicanor.
verses.textLatin: At Machabæus, videns secum austerius agere Nicanorem, et consuetum occursum ferocius exhibentem, intelligens non ex bono esse austeritatem istam, paucis suorum congregatis, occultavit se a Nicanore.

verses.text: But he finding himself notably prevented by the man, came to the great and holy temple: and commanded the priests that were offering the accustomed sacrifices, to deliver him the man.
verses.textLatin: Quod cum ille cognovit, fortiter se a viro præventum, venit ad maximum et sanctissimum templum: et sacerdotibus solitas hostias offerentibus, jussit sibi tradi virum.

verses.text: And when they swore unto him, that they knew not where the man was whom he sought, he stretched out his hand to the temple,
verses.textLatin: Quibus cum juramento dicentibus nescire se ubi esset qui quærebatur, extendens manum ad templum,

verses.text: And swore, saying: Unless you deliver Judas prisoner to me, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and will beat down the altar, and I will dedicate this temple to Bacchus.
verses.textLatin: juravit, dicens: Nisi Judam mihi vinctum tradideritis, istud Dei fanum in planitiem deducam, et altare effodiam, et templum hoc Libero patri consecrabo.

verses.text: And when he had spoken thus he departed. But the priests stretching forth their hands to heaven, called upon him that was ever the defender of their nation, saying in this manner:
verses.textLatin: Et his dictis abiit. Sacerdotes autem protendentes manus in cælum, invocabant eum qui semper propugnator esset gentis ipsorum, hæc dicentes:

verses.text: Thou, O Lord of all things, who wantest nothing, wast pleased that the temple of thy habitation should be amongst us.
verses.textLatin: Tu, Domine universorum, qui nullius indiges, voluisti templum habitationis tuæ fieri in nobis.

verses.text: Therefore now, O Lord the holy of all holies, keep this house for ever undefiled which was lately cleansed.
verses.textLatin: Et nunc, Sancte sanctorum, omnium Domine, conserva in æternum impollutam domum istam, quæ nuper mundata est.

verses.text: Now Razias, one of the ancients of Jerusalem, was accused to Nicanor, a man that was a lover of the city, and of good report, who for his affection was called the father of the Jews.
verses.textLatin: Razias autem quidam de senioribus ab Jerosolymis delatus est Nicanori, vir amator civitatis, et bene audiens: qui pro affectu pater Judæorum appellabatur.

verses.text: This man, for a long time, had held fast his purpose of keeping himself pure in the Jews’ religion, and was ready to expose his body and life, that he might persevere therein.
verses.textLatin: Hic multis temporibus continentiæ propositum tenuit in Judaismo, corpusque et animam tradere contentus pro perseverantia.

verses.text: So Nicanor being willing to declare the hatred that he bore the Jews, sent five hundred soldiers to take him.
verses.textLatin: Volens autem Nicanor manifestare odium quod habebat in Judæos, misit milites quingentos ut eum comprehenderent.

verses.text: For he thought by insnaring him to hurt the Jews very much.
verses.textLatin: Putabat enim, si illum decepisset, se cladem Judæis maximam illaturum.

verses.text: Now as the multitude sought to rush into his house, and to break open the door, and to set fire to it, when he was ready to be taken, he struck himself with his sword:
verses.textLatin: Turbis autem irruere in domum ejus, et januam dirumpere: atque ignem admovere cupientibus, cum jam comprehenderetur, gladio se petiit,

verses.text: Choosing to die nobly rather than to fall into the hands of the wicked, and to suffer abuses unbecoming his noble birth.
verses.textLatin: eligens nobiliter mori potius quam subditus fieri peccatoribus, et contra natales suos indignis injuriis agi.

verses.text: But whereas through haste he missed of giving himself a sure wound, and the crowd was breaking into the doors, he ran boldly to the wall, and manfully threw himself down to the crowd:
verses.textLatin: Sed cum per festinationem non certo ictu plagam dedisset, et turbæ intra ostia irrumperent, recurrens audacter ad murum præcipitavit semetipsum viriliter in turbas:

verses.text: But they quickly making room for his fall, he came upon the midst of the neck.
verses.textLatin: quibus velociter locum dantibus casui ejus, venit per mediam cervicem.

verses.text: And as he had yet breath in him, being inflamed in mind he arose: and while his blood ran down with a great stream, and he was grievously wounded, he ran through the crowd:
verses.textLatin: Et cum adhuc spiraret, accensus animo, surrexit, et cum sanguis ejus magno fluxu deflueret, et gravissimis vulneribus esset saucius, cursu turbam pertransiit:

verses.text: And standing upon a steep rock, when he was now almost without blood, grasping his bowels with both hands, he cast them upon the throng, calling upon the Lord of life and spirit, to restore these to him again: and so he departed this life.
verses.textLatin: et stans supra quamdam petram præruptam, et jam exsanguis effectus, complexus intestina sua, utrisque manibus projecit super turbas, invocans dominatorem vitæ ac spiritus ut hæc illi iterum redderet: atque ita vita defunctus est.

verses.text: But  when Nicanor understood that Judas was in the places of Samaria, he purposed to set upon him with all violence on the sabbath day.
verses.textLatin: Nicanor autem, ut comperit Judam esse in locis Samariæ, cogitavit cum omni impetu die sabbati committere bellum.

verses.text: And when the Jews that were constrained to follow him, said: Do not act so fiercely and barbarously, but give honour to the day that is sanctified: and reverence him that beholdeth all things:
verses.textLatin: Judæis vero qui illum per necessitatem sequebantur, dicentibus: Ne ita ferociter et barbare feceris, sed honorem tribue diei sanctificationis, et honora eum qui universa conspicit:

verses.text: That unhappy man asked, if there were a mighty One in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept.
verses.textLatin: ille infelix interrogavit si est potens in cælo, qui imperavit agi diem sabbatorum.

verses.text: And when they answered: There is the living Lord himself in heaven, the mighty One, that commanded the seventh day to be kept,
verses.textLatin: Et respondentibus illis: Est Dominus vivus ipse in cælo potens, qui jussit agi septimam diem:

verses.text: Then he said: And I am mighty upon the earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king’s business. Nevertheless he prevailed not to accomplish his design.
verses.textLatin: at ille ait: Et ego potens sum super terram qui impero sumi arma, et negotia regis impleri. Tamen non obtinuit ut consilium perficeret.

verses.text: So Nicanor being puffed up with exceeding great pride, thought to set up a public monument of his victory over Judas.
verses.textLatin: Et Nicanor quidem cum summa superbia erectus, cogitaverat commune trophæum statuere de Juda.

verses.text: But Machabeus ever trusted with all hope that God would help them.
verses.textLatin: Machabæus autem semper confidebat cum omni spe auxilium sibi a Deo affuturum:

verses.text: And he exhorted his people not to fear the coming of the nations, but to remember the help they had before received from heaven, and now to hope for victory from the Almighty.
verses.textLatin: et hortabatur suos ne formidarent ad adventum nationum, sed in mente haberent adjutoria sibi facta de cælo, et nunc sperarent ab Omnipotente sibi affuturam victoriam.

verses.text: And speaking to them out of the law, and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles they had fought before, he made them more cheerful:
verses.textLatin: Et allocutus eos de lege et prophetis, admonens etiam certamina quæ fecerant prius, promptiores constituit eos:

verses.text: Then after he had encouraged them, he shewed withal the falsehood of the Gentiles, and their breach of oaths.
verses.textLatin: et ita animis eorum erectis simul ostendebat gentium fallaciam, et juramentorum prævaricationem.

verses.text: So he armed every one of them, not with defence of shield and spear, but with very good speeches and exhortations, and told them a dream worthy to be believed, whereby he rejoiced them all.
verses.textLatin: Singulos autem illorum armavit, non clypei et hastæ munitione, sed sermonibus optimis et exhortationibus, exposito digno fide somnio, per quod universos lætificavit.

verses.text: Now the vision was in this manner: Onias who had been high priest, a good and virtuous man, modest in his looks, gentle in his manners, and graceful in his speech, and who from a child was exercised in virtues, holding up his hands, prayed for all the people of the Jews:
verses.textLatin: Erat autem hujuscemodi visus: Oniam, qui fuerat summus sacerdos, virum bonum et benignum, verecundum visu, modestum moribus, et eloquio decorum, et qui a puero in virtutibus exercitatus sit, manus protendentem orare pro omni populo Judæorum.

verses.text: After this there appeared also another man, admirable for age, and glory, and environed with great beauty and majesty:
verses.textLatin: Post hoc apparuisse et alium virum ætate et gloria mirabilem, et magni decoris habitudine circa illum.

verses.text: Then Onias answering, said: This is a lover of his brethren, and of the people of Israel: this is he that prayeth much for the people, and for all the holy city, Jeremias the prophet of God.
verses.textLatin: Respondentem vero Oniam dixisse: Hic est fratrum amator, et populi Israël: hic est qui multum orat pro populo et universa sancta civitate, Jeremias propheta Dei.

verses.text: Whereupon Jeremias stretched forth his right hand, and gave to Judas a sword of gold, saying:
verses.textLatin: Extendisse autem Jeremiam dextram, et dedisse Judæ gladium aureum, dicentem:

verses.text: Take this holy sword a gift from God, wherewith thou shalt overthrow the adversaries of my people Israel.
verses.textLatin: Accipe sanctum gladium munus a Deo, in quo dejicies adversarios populi mei Israël.

verses.text: Thus being exhorted with the words of Judas, which were very good, and proper to stir up the courage, and strengthen the hearts of the young men, they resolved to fight, and to set upon them manfully: that valour might decide the matter, because the holy city and the temple were in danger.
verses.textLatin: Exhortati itaque Judæ sermonibus bonis valde, de quibus extolli posset impetus, et animi juvenum confortari, statuerunt dimicare et confligere fortiter: ut virtus de negotiis judicaret, eo quod civitas sancta et templum periclitarentur.

verses.text: For their concern was less for their wives, and children, and for their brethren, and kinsfolks: but their greatest and principal fear was for the holiness of the temple.
verses.textLatin: Erat enim pro uxoribus et filiis, itemque pro fratribus et cognatis, minor sollicitudo: maximus vero et primus pro sanctitate timor erat templi.

verses.text: And they also that were in the city, had no little concern for them that were to be engaged in battle.
verses.textLatin: Sed et eos qui in civitate erant, non minima sollicitudo habebat pro his qui congressuri erant.

verses.text: And now when all expected what judgment would be given, and the enemies were at hand, and the army was set in array, the beasts and the horsemen ranged in convenient places,
verses.textLatin: Et cum jam omnes sperarent judicium futurum, hostesque adessent atque exercitus esset ordinatus, bestiæ equitesque opportuno in loco compositi,

verses.text: Machabeus considering the coming of the multitude, and the divers preparations of armour, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretching out his hands to heaven, called upon the Lord, that worketh wonders, who giveth victory to them that are worthy, not according to the power of their arms, but according as it seemeth good to him.
verses.textLatin: considerans Machabæus adventum multitudinis, et apparatum varium armorum, et ferocitatem bestiarum, extendens manus in cælum, prodigia facientem Dominum invocavit, qui non secundum armorum potentiam, sed prout ipsi placet, dat dignis victoriam.

verses.text: And in his prayer he said after this manner: Thou, O Lord, who didst send thy angel in the time of Ezechias king of Juda, and didst kill a hundred and eighty-five thousand of the army of Sennacherib:
verses.textLatin: Dixit autem invocans hoc modo: Tu Domine, qui misisti angelum tuum sub Ezechia rege Juda, et interfecisti de castris Sennacherib centum octoginta quinque millia:

verses.text: Send now also, O Lord of heaven, thy good angel before us, for the fear and dread of the greatness of thy arm,
verses.textLatin: et nunc, dominator cælorum, mitte angelum tuum bonum ante nos in timore et tremore magnitudinis brachii tui,

verses.text: That they may be afraid, who come with blasphemy against thy holy people. And thus he concluded his prayer.
verses.textLatin: ut metuant qui cum blasphemia veniunt adversus sanctum populum tuum. Et hic quidem ita peroravit.

verses.text: But Nicanor, and they that were with him came forward, with trumpets and songs.
verses.textLatin: Nicanor autem et qui cum ipso erant, cum tubis et canticis admovebant.

verses.text: But Judas, and they that were with him, encountered them, calling upon God by prayers:
verses.textLatin: Judas vero et qui cum eo erant, invocato Deo, per orationes congressi sunt:

verses.text: So fighting with their hands, but praying to the Lord with their hearts, they slew no less than five and thirty thousand, being greatly cheered with the presence of God.
verses.textLatin: manu quidem pugnantes, sed Dominum cordibus orantes, prostraverunt non minus triginta quinque millia, præsentia Dei magnifice delectati.

verses.text: And when the battle was over, and they were returning with joy, they understood that Nicanor was slain in his armour.
verses.textLatin: Cumque cessassent, et cum gaudio redirent, cognoverunt Nicanorem ruisse cum armis suis.

verses.text: Then making a shout, and a great noise, they blessed the Almighty Lord in their own language.
verses.textLatin: Facto itaque clamore, et perturbatione excitata, patria voce omnipotentem Dominum benedicebant.

verses.text: And Judas, who was altogether ready, in body and mind, to die for his countrymen, commanded that Nicanor’s head, and his hand with the shoulder should be cut off, and carried to Jerusalem.
verses.textLatin: Præcepit autem Judas, qui per omnia corpore et animo mori pro civibus paratus erat, caput Nicanoris, et manum cum humero abscissam, Jerosolymam perferri.

verses.text: And when he was come thither, having called together his countrymen, and the priests to the altar, he sent also for them that were in the castle,
verses.textLatin: Quo cum pervenisset, convocatis contribulibus et sacerdotibus ad altare, accersiit et eos qui in arce erant.

verses.text: And shewing them the head of Nicanor, and the wicked hand, which he had stretched out, with proud boasts, against the holy house of the Almighty God,
verses.textLatin: Et ostenso capite Nicanoris, et manu nefaria quam extendens contra domum sanctam omnipotentis Dei magnifice gloriatus est.

verses.text: He commanded also, that the tongue of the wicked Nicanor, should be cut out and given by pieces to birds, and the hand of the furious man to be hanged up over against the temple.
verses.textLatin: Linguam etiam impii Nicanoris præcisam jussit particulatim avibus dari: manum autem dementis contra templum suspendi.

verses.text: Then all blessed the Lord of heaven, saying: Blessed be he that hath kept his own place undefiled.
verses.textLatin: Omnes igitur cæli benedixerunt Dominum, dicentes: Benedictus qui locum suum incontaminatum servavit.

verses.text: And he hung up Nicanor’s head in the top of the castle, that it might be an evident and manifest sign of the help of God.
verses.textLatin: Suspendit autem Nicanoris caput in summa arce, ut evidens esset, et manifestum signum auxilii Dei.

verses.text: And they all ordained by a common decree, by no means to let this day pass without solemnity:
verses.textLatin: Itaque omnes communi consilio decreverunt nullo modo diem istum absque celebritate præterire:

verses.text: But to celebrate the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, called, in the Syrian language, the day before Mardochias’ day.
verses.textLatin: habere autem celebritatem tertiadecima die mensis Adar, quod dicitur voce syriaca, pridie Mardochæi diei.

verses.text: So these things being done with relation to Nicanor, and from that time the city being possessed by the Hebrews, I also will here make an end of my narration.
verses.textLatin: Igitur his erga Nicanorem gestis, et ex illis temporibus ab Hebræis civitate possessa, ego quoque in his faciam finem sermonis.

verses.text: Which if I have done well, and as it becometh the history, it is what I desired: but if not so perfectly, it must be pardoned me.
verses.textLatin: Et si quidem bene, et ut historiæ competit, hoc et ipse velim: sin autem minus digne, concedendum est mihi.

verses.text: For as it is hurtful to drink always wine, or always water, but pleasant to use sometimes the one, and sometimes the other: so if the speech be always nicely framed, it will not be grateful to the readers. But here it shall be ended.
verses.textLatin: Sicut enim vinum semper bibere, aut semper aquam, contrarium est; alternis autem uti, delectabile: ita legentibus si semper exactus sit sermo, non erit gratus. Hic ergo erit consummatus.
